Other items like Tinkertech Gadget, Tinkertech Power Modification, Artificial Intelligence, and so on can be integrated into the frame if you desire.)
objects.title: Jar Mentality

objects.text:
Not only are you extremely weak, you are tiny too. For every selection your height and weight is 10% less than the average for your age group and species. Additionally the maximum amount of strength you can reach through training is reduced by 8% of the average per selection.

This will not necessarily make you look like a child upon close inspection though some may still assume at first glance.
objects.title: Runt

objects.text: You’re not just weak, you are terminally ill. Whether it be Cancer, Heart Disease or some obscure illness you are incurably sick. You cannot fix this with your starting powers but can gain something that will.
objects.title: Terminally Ill

addons.text: Your disease is lethal. This illness, incurable with current knowledge and treatments, will relentlessly weakens your body. With time, there may be hope for a remedy, but for now, you must endure the debilitating effects of this disease. The symptoms and weakness in your body becomes more pronounced each day, forcing you to adapt and persevere in the face of your grim prognosis.
addons.title: Lethal Disease

addons.text:
Your curse manifests as a disease that slowly breaks apart your body. Every time you use your powers, your body not only suffers for it, but the disease rapidly accelerates. Each use of your abilities takes a toll, causing your muscles to weaken, your bones to ache, and your very cells to deteriorate. The more you rely on your powers, the more severe the symptoms become. Your powers are also become increasingly difficult to control.

As the disease advances, you must grapple with the harsh reality of your condition. Each decision to use your abilities carries the weight of knowing it may hasten your decline, yet there are moments when you have no choice but to risk it.
addons.title: Cursed Disease

objects.text: Your poor constitution resulted in you getting infected by some kind of disease. It could be mundane or magical in nature, but it is currently incurable. A cure may eventually be discovered, until then, you must navigate life with this affliction, adapting to its challenges and finding ways to manage your symptoms as best as possible. Symptoms could include chronic fatigue, periodic fevers, intense muscle pain, and sporadic coughing fits. At times, your condition might flare up, leaving you bedridden and unable to perform even the simplest of tasks.
objects.title: Diseased

objects.text: Your hair must remain a certain length. If you cut it it will grow back to that length in seconds. At one purchase it must be shoulder length, at two it must reach your mid back, at three it must be hip length, at 4 it must reach your thighs and at 5 it must reach your ankles. You can style your hair in any way you wish as long as it remains at the length limit or longer. Using buns and braids is recommended to manage the length.
objects.title: Rapunzel, Rapunzel Let Down Your Hair

objects.text: One year after your arrival you will suffer a horrible unavoidable death, this death will be torturously painful and traumatic. If you have some method to revive yourself it will activate as normal but anyone who isn’t insane is guaranteed to be traumatized.
objects.title: It's Called Suffering

objects.text:
Languages, wonderful little things that allow communication between many, but unfortunately, the gift of learning them has been robbed from you. 

If you know no languages, once you start learning one you will become locked into it; essentially, that is the only language you will ever be able to learn, all others forever will be unintelligible gibberish for you. If you already know one or more languages, the same happens, except you are locked to those you already know.

This affects your ability to learn any power systems dependent on languages, but does not affect your ability to read body language, as it is not actually a language despite its name.
objects.title: Language Barrier

objects.text:
You wake up in a doctor's office in the middle of nowhere after being shot twice in the head and left for dead in a shallow grave outside of town, with no memory of why or how you got there. You don't remember your own name and only hazy fragments of your memories from the last few months remain. Luckily, this only has a very minor impact on your character and personality.

The only clues you have are the pair of bullets pulled out of your skull and some random trash the doctor found in your pockets. What happened during that time? Who tried to kill you and why? 

Will you seek the answers or leave the past behind? No matter which one you choose, you will encounter former friends and foes on your journey, clues about your past will surface, and the truth will come to light.

This drawback triggers between 6 to 8 months after your arrival in your chosen world. It adapts to your form if you are non-human.
objects.title: Vegas Sendoff

addons.text: Unfortunately for you, whatever miracle repaired the brain- or at least got it into semi-working condition- of the body you've found yourself in wasn't perfect. Now, not only are the memories of whatever person you've taken the place of damaged, but so are your own, to near the same extent even! Your personality may have taken some hits too- blending with the personality of whoever your body once was. If you're very lucky, or well adjusted, this might not give you a personality disorder!
addons.title: Mixed Minds

objects.text: Your point of insert/reincarnation is now the events of the Vegas Sendoff, where you wake up in the body on the doctor's table. The memories from your reincarnated life or inserted character are just as damaged, but whatever memories you bring with you are unaffected.
objects.title: New Soul, Whose This?

objects.text: You have an overinflated sense of your own worth, your new favorite pastime is making sure that you look your absolute best at all times.
objects.title: Narcissism

objects.text: You can’t find any motivation, sometimes you don’t even want to do anything. While not suicidal, sometimes you don’t feel like eating when you really need to. You need strong willpower to be able to live a normal life, but you will regularly just stop doing something halfway and have trouble starting something.
objects.title: Depression

addons.text: Your anxiety can reach a boiling point where you suffer from panic attacks either the closer you are to your deepest fear or your wavering confidence reaches a fever pitch, where often the course of action to prevent future attacks is avoidance, distraction, or the nurturing of maladaptive coping mechanisms.
addons.title: Panic Attacks

addons.text: “I learned courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. The brave man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear.” ― Nelson Mandela. Your fear propels you to conquer any doubt, insecurity, or hesitation and find the resolve to see it through; fear is now the awareness of danger, to fight and deal with this threat, hurdle, conflict, or obstacle despite the panic you experience boiling in your veins, facing what you’re afraid of relentlessly while gaining vigilance and precaution. You act in clarity under the most extreme horrors or traumatic experiences, allowing them to endure the extreme mental stress, dominating, mastering Fear’s power for your own.
addons.title: Courage

objects.text: You find yourself more bothered; tense, both angsty, and easily panicked in equal measure than normal. Your ever-present insecurities or doubts crept over you, a constant sense of doom or danger with no discernible direction permeates occasionally, and you’re skittish at best and high-strung at worst. The slightest bit of setback or inconvenience causes a downward spiral, with stressful environments your greatest enemy. A sense of apprehension or wariness spikes across any person you encounter.  You pace with almost a sense of contained franticness, a coiled spring, ever-vigilant, sweeping gazes. Deep-seated dread is your beloathed company.
objects.title: Anxiety: [Internally Screaming]

objects.text: You find yourself slightly more easily angered than usual. If you were normally calm and composed, then you'd find yourself making harsh retorts or giving others the cold shoulder a bit more often, while if you only had the emotional intelligence of a baby larva, then even the slightest insults toward yourself would fill you with fury.
objects.title: Wrath

addons.text: Your perpetual state of exhaustion transcends mere sleep; even when awake, fatigue is your constant companion. Oversleeping and indulging in frequent naps becomes second nature, offering temporary reprieve from the relentless weariness that weighs you down. Moments of wakefulness become fleeting interludes between bouts of slumber, each day blurring into a haze of drowsiness. The simple act of staying awake feels like a Herculean task, reserved only for essential activities such as nourishing your body with food, a chore that at times feels more burdensome than satisfying. This effect is diminished if Cure Curse was taken.
addons.title: Sin of Sloth

objects.text: You often find yourself falling victim to the siren call of procrastination, continually putting off tasks until the last possible moment. The weight of fatigue seems ever-present, sapping your energy and leaving you feeling lethargic. Motivation feels like a distant dream, elusive and fleeting, as you navigate through each day with a sense of inertia. Your pace is slow, your movements sluggish, as if the very essence of slothfulness has taken root within you.
objects.title: Slothful

addons.text:
Your Battle Junkie tendencies mesh well with your addictive relationship with your powers, now driven to a constant and insatiable drive to seek and incite conflict where you’ll be able to fully unleash them. This manifests into an inability to sit idle for prolonged periods of time, irritability, and a generally confrontational personality, giving the impression where you’re seeking problems or looking for a fight, which they’ll be right to judge.  

Aside from your withdrawal symptoms for a lack of use, the only way to scratch your itch is obvious: unbridled combat. Doesn’t matter how or where, as long as you let yourself go in the heat of battle, you can dull the draw of your passion for battle for a while.
addons.title: Battle Beast

objects.text: You find yourself caught in the grips of a fierce and addictive passion for battle. As a Battle Junkie, you are driven by an insatiable desire to engage in combat, constantly seeking out new challenges and victories. However, be warned, for the art of combat comes a massive dopamine hit comparable to hard drugs, be careful not to be addicted to violence.
objects.title: Battle Junkie

objects.text:
You’re, well… gloomy. There’s dark circles under your eyes, you always look exhausted and slightly unkempt, and there seems to be an aura around you that seems to make the light just a bit dimmer and the air just a touch chillier. You can still clean yourself up briefly, but it’ll be a lot of work and won’t last long.

You look absolutely ridiculous trying to wear bright and cheery colors, though on the bright side you could probably rock the goth-aesthetic effortlessly.
objects.title: Gloomy

objects.text: You are deathly afraid of something. A phobia so debilitating it almost stops you from functioning as any other person when closer to it. You are aware of it, yet you can’t help how frantic you feel about it. It could be anything, from insects, holes, and the ocean, to open spaces or large groups of people, etc. You panic at the mere sight of it and if you force the issue you might even faint.
objects.title: The Only Thing I Fear

addons.text: It seems you are quite the scaredy pants. In addition to your phobia, you are prone to fear and tend to avoid danger whenever possible, resulting in frequent retreats and reluctance to engage in risky situations. Your first choice is always to flee or freeze under pressure. You appear unreliable or untrustworthy, your instinct is to choose the safest, often less rewarding, path. You gain a tendency to hoard supplies for fear of future scarcity.
addons.title: Coward

addons.text: You are consumed by paranoia, constantly doubting everything and second-guessing every action and decision to the point of delusion. This intense mistrust affects all aspects of your life, making it difficult to distinguish between reality and your imagined fears. Your paranoia causes you to hesitate, suspecting traps or hidden dangers in every situation. You overanalyze every detail and delay crucial decisions, potentially causing you to miss opportunities or fall into traps your paranoia convinced you were there.
addons.title: Paranoid

objects.text: You struggle with confidence and making decisions, leading to frequent hesitation and second-guessing. You find it difficult to assert your opinions or make persuasive arguments, hindering leadership. Your indecision delays progress and may lead to missed opportunities or unintended consequences. Even your skill development is hindered by self-doubt, making it harder to decide which skills to improve.
objects.title: Indecisive Nature

objects.text: Your hunger for wealth is undeniable, insatiable, and unquenchable. You desire money and all things that can help you financially above all else. If you lack a strong will, you can abandon any morals in the face of the almighty dollar. Your sole focus is money, the means to your end. For you, the difficulty of a task is irrelevant; only the potential reward matters.
objects.title: Miser

objects.text: You are afflicted by a condition, known as compulsive spending, which makes it virtually impossible for you to save money. You simply cannot control your urges to spend and constantly feel the need to purchase items, whether necessary or not. This habit drains your finances, leaving you always wanting more money. It is a difficult condition to deal with, as it can lead to excessive debt and stress, and can negatively impact your social and personal relationships.
objects.title: Shopping Addiction

objects.text:
Old habits die hard, huh?—clinging to your being, stubbornly, burying their roots deep inside. From now on, you'll need to consciously and actively work on yourself if you wish to avoid slipping back into all your familiar pitfalls, vices, or bad habits. Any vice or detrimental behavior you possess—or develop—will become significantly more demanding to overcome. Without active effort, you'll unconsciously revert to these old patterns, making the process of breaking free more arduous and time-consuming than it would be for most.

This will inherently extend to addictions as well. In whatever form they may be, kicking an addiction will demand immense perseverance and determination, as the grip of dependency will feel heavier and more difficult to shake off than for others.
objects.title: Old Dog

objects.text:
Every time you utter a divine being's name in vain or say curse words, something terrible will happen to you.

(Lasts until you ascend to divinity and only with gods you are aware of, if you are atheist and say something like ‘dear god’, a random god will smite you "gently").
objects.title: Thou shalt not utter Lord's name in vain.

objects.text:
You are allergic to something. It might be dust, animals, food, material, substance, energy, etc.

Can be taken up to 10 times.
objects.title: Allergic

objects.text: You find it grueling to gain a reputation. Your accomplishments are often downplayed by others, usually crediting your successes to others and failures to you, and the public opinion about you is gonna be either somewhat poor or infamously bad. Anything you do can be reviled and ridiculed if left unchecked. A loss with this Drawback is probably going to be a humiliating affair, a win an exercise in pyrrhic futility. Impressions you leave behind are out of your control, being normally unflattering.
objects.title: Disreputable

objects.text: No matter what, you cannot keep your civilian identity secret. Perhaps your voice is recognized by a childhood friend and they tell everyone, or perhaps you're forced into revealing your identity to save someone's life. It doesn't matter how, but your civilian identity will be revealed one way or another within a month.
objects.title: Unmasked

objects.text:
You attract the interest of a local group (like the E88 and ABB, or the Ambassadors and the Teeth if you end up in Boston, etc.). They will either want to recruit you or eliminate you.

If you move locations you will inevitably attract the interest of another group. If you participate in dismantling that group, another will not appear.
objects.title: Wanted (Local)

objects.text:
You attract the interest of a group with national or international reach (like PRT, CUI, the Elite, etc.). They will either want to recruit you or eliminate you.

If you move locations you will inevitably attract the interest of another group. If you participate in dismantling that group, another will not appear.
objects.title: Wanted (Global)

objects.text:
You have caught the attention of a group, either possessing national or international reach into multiple parallel worlds of your setting (So for Earth Bet it would be parallel worlds like Aleph, Shin, Gimel, etc.), and have access to interdimensional Tinkertech or other means to travel to other alternate worlds.

This group, intrigued by your potential or threatened by your presence, seeks to recruit you for their purposes or eliminate any potential competition you may pose.
objects.title: Wanted (Parallel Worlds)

objects.text:
At some point, after you arrive, you will be wrongfully accused of a serious crime that you did not commit. You will be forced to go on the run and a manhunt will be instigated by the local law enforcement agencies such as the PRT. The seriousness of the crime and apparent evidence against you is strong enough that if you are caught, you will be found guilty and likely given life imprisonment or the death penalty if you undergo a fair trial.

You can potentially exonerate yourself if you gather enough evidence to prove or convince them of your innocence. Outside of Earth Bet, this drawback extends to you being wanted by the closest thing to a local government law enforcement agency within whatever world you choose, such as the Aurors in Harry Potter.
objects.title: Fugitive

objects.text:
Before, you were wrongfully accused of a crime you didn’t do. Now you have instead been forced to carry out the crime you are accused of, even if you were unwilling. The worst part? No one knows. To law enforcement, you are the same fugitive as before; only now the evidence is undeniable.

The precise way this Drawback manifests is up to you. Perhaps you were subject to a Master/Stranger effect or acting under extreme coercion and duress. Maybe you were being manipulated via chemical or psychological means, had your memories altered or were subjected to some other force. The end result, however, is the same.

Naturally, this makes it significantly harder to exonerate yourself. If you were controlled by a Master/Stranger effect or something similar, how well-known these influences are in the Setting will affect the ease of being acquitted. Even then, proving your innocence requires strong evidence and convincing others will be an uphill battle.

While you weren’t in full control of your actions, the weight of what has happened might still leave you grappling with intense guilt and trauma. Additionally, the social consequences may be just as severe as people's trust in you is shattered depending on the nature of the crime and its impact.

You can optionally choose to have committed this crime entirely of your own free will with no outside factors limiting your culpability.
objects.title: Blood-Stained Hands

objects.text:
You have been targeted by the Yàngbǎn or Gesellschaft to be kidnapped and indoctrinated. They will violate international sovereignty and attempt to kidnap you directly as a high-priority target. They will only begin to target you once you start to act as a cape (if you don't have powers yet you are safe).

If those groups have yet to form, they will, or another group with similar goals will form instead.
objects.title: CUI Summer Camp

objects.text:
The Perks <u>Blank</u>, <u>Trumped the Trump</u>, <u>All-Seeing Precognition</u>, and <u>Plot Armor</u> no longer work everywhere. Instead, they are limited to the multiverse cluster you start in.

If you choose the <u>Canon Earth Bet</u> or <u>AU Earth Bet</u> the range is limited to what the Entities can reach (10^80 universes). For <u>Crossover</u> and <u>AU Crossover</u>, it includes the multiverses of any settings you select. <u>Alternate Earth</u> contains the multiverse of your chosen destination(s).
objects.title: Some Terms and Conditions apply

objects.text: The Perks Blank, Trumped the Trump, Mental Barrier, and All-Seeing Precognition are no longer absolute or completely invincible. Your Perks can be sidestepped, and some other powers may be able to overcome them. However, these Perks still possess a high level of effectiveness in most situations, although their efficacy against higher-tier opponents may be reduced. For example, Contessa may not be able to path you, but she can simulate you like she does for Eidolon. If you take either Only A Sith Deals in Absolutes or Countdown, then its effects are only partially negated: For Only A Sith Deals in Absolutes, powers will still be absolutes even if they wouldn’t be otherwise, whereas your Perks will still be normal or even weakened to be no longer absolute. Additionally, you don't get to choose if your absolute power wins against another absolute power in any case; it just usually wins. For Countdown, rather than completely removing your drawbacks when its requirements are met, it would merely reduce them to a more manageable level, with them completely disappearing after time and/or effort, with all your Drawbacks (including this one) being removed after at maximum 10 years.
objects.title: No Such Thing as Absolutes

addons.text: It is now possible to pseudo-trigger your non-absolute powers back to being absolute. This does require you to have them trained back to their strength under No Such Thing As Absolute and of course, a traumatic event.
addons.title: Double Tap

addons.text: The growth for your Perks is now affected by any additional Drawback for Acclimation you have chosen. The speed at which your Perks grow from training and how much you need to train them will be the same as how much you need to do the same for powers. This does not mean that their growth is linked, it simply means they must both be equally trained.
addons.title: Same Start, Same Speed

addons.text: The enhancements made by Golden Perks also require additional training to achieve.
addons.title: From Lead to Gold

objects.text:
The Perks affected by <u>No Such Thing as Absolutes</u> have all been further reduced to only provide about half of their benefits alongside the Perks: <u>Powered Sustenance</u>, <u>Noctis Cape</u>, <u>Manton Protected</u>, <u>Accentuate the Positive</u>, <u>Eliminate the Negative</u>, and <u>Platinum Kryptonite</u>. With training, it is possible to restore them to their previous state. It is not possible to restore perks to an “absolute” state.

Perks such as <u>Powered Sustenance</u> and <u>Noctis Cape</u> will be reduced to simply needing fewer resources and generally better memory. They can be trained by fasting and mental exercises. Mental exercises will also be valid for perks like Mental Barrier.

Perks like <u>Blank</u>, <u>Only A Sith Deals in Absolutes</u>, and <u>Manton Protected</u> will require training with another person or minion to use the appropriate powers against you. The use of a minion will require it to have some measure of independence from you.
objects.title: Work for It

objects.text: Instead of having an indomitable will, you are very stubborn, to a degree that some would call you downright stupid. You are the type of person to keep throwing your head against a wall time and time again until the wall breaks or your head does, and even then, you will try throwing your head against the wall again. You will keep trying the same solution to the same problem, even if it doesn't work the first time and shows no chance of success.
objects.title: Definition of Insanity

addons.text: Maybe there's still a chance for you after all Your memories might be gone, but the impressions they had remain. Your Sixth Sense has become much more accurate in regards to things that had to do with Worm; such as getting a feeling of weal or woe towards canon characters, or feeling a sense of impending doom around May 5th, 2011. This also makes uncovering secrets much easier, with the connection between civilian and cape identities seeming to just click into place and finding the idea of an illuminati-esk organization as easy as interacting with a few major players. If you picked Countdown, your memories of Worm will slowly return, but not as knowledge of a web serial. Instead it will be revealed to you as knowledge of real people or events, slowly being given to you over the course of your Countdown. At the end, you can choose whether or not the source of this knowledge is revealed. If you selected both Countdown and Golden Perks, this knowledge will reveal itself with enough frequency and relevance to be considered a weak, albiet esoteric, Thinker power.
addons.title: Wildbow? That Sounds Familiar...

objects.text:
You forget everything you know about Worm. Why? You had a chance to save everything! Stop the bloodshed, and save the multiverse! Well, there's still a chance if you got Backup that you'll save everyone, or that you'll be powerful enough to save everyone by chance. Please don't pick this without Backup, especially not if you chose to arrive on April 8th, 2011!

You retain knowledge of your build, but the context behind some of your choices—why you picked certain perks or powers—is lost to you.

(Note: If you pick alternate Earth or crossover knowledge of whatever other worlds you chose will be erased from your knowledge.)
objects.title: Wildbow? Where have I heard that before?

objects.text:
You lose any meta-knowledge relevant to the powers you picked from the CYOA, except from what's directly granted by the powers themselves. For example, if you have shard powers, your knowledge of Worm power mechanics would be what's available to the public in-universe; the same goes for shardless powers, where your knowledge would either be non-existent or to the level of the average civilian or novice, depending on the power.

(This can, optionally, also extend to powers gained after the fact, through methods like copying or summoning, companions and other choices that have meta-knowledge attached.)
objects.title: Meta-Less Knight

objects.text: You forget everything from your current life. You are like a walking duckling who has no clue who or what everything is unless you have Wildbow's predictions. Any friends your current life made, any family, and even any enemies. You don't remember them.
objects.title: Clean Slate

objects.text: You forget a large part of everything from your first life EXCEPT Wildbow's predictions. While you forget a lot of facts such as the name of your parents or maybe even yourself, you still remember important key information like pets you had or key events that shaped your personality. While you no longer remember your past self, the memories you do have make it so you still retain your personality, goals, emotions, and overall identity.
objects.title: Half of Who I Am

objects.text: You forget everything from your first life EXCEPT Wildbow's predictions. Wow, that's some serious dedication. You don't remember your thoughts or feelings about Wildbow's predictions, just the facts. You retain knowledge of your build, but lose the personal context and feelings behind your choices—except those made specifically in response to Wildbow’s predictions.
objects.title: Selective Amnesia

objects.text: All the choices you made leading up to your dimensional displacement has been forgotten. Now you won't even remember all the extra help (and challenges) R.O.B. has given you for your journey. You will keep all the Perks, Drawbacks, Missions, Powers, Skills, and Items you have chosen but you will have to (re)discover yourself what exactly these are. You will still have a fated meeting with your Companions.
objects.title: What do you mean I did this to myself?

addons.text:
Your Amnesia fails to fully scrub the memory of your death from your mind, merely causing it to seem more like a persistent, weirdly realistic daydream than a straight up memory. 

Your conscious mind may have trouble remembering it fully, but your subconscious does not, leading to nightmares and instinctive discomfort whenever topics related to your death come up, as at least some part of your mind will be forced to relive that moment.
addons.title: Nightmares

objects.text:
Your transfer to this world wasn't quite a clean nap. Instead, whatever sparked your transfer to this world, an important catalyst for it was your traumatic death in the previous one.

You have a supernaturally clear memory of how you died and will find it difficult to fully suppress recalling it when related things come up.
objects.title: Truck-kun

objects.text: Your death was not only traumatic, it was also incredibly embarrassing as well, whether by it being easily avoidable, or even just being inherently comedic and mockable.
objects.title: Banana Peel

objects.text: You are incredibly annoying, cocky, and arrogant to your last breath. Most people garner actual hate and disgust for you and your attitude after a single sentence
objects.title: Smarmy Asshole

objects.text: You experience an unusual reflex occasionally, where your senses will invert, leading to temporary disorientation. Such as you may perceive colors as inverted, hear sounds in reverse, or even feel sensations like hot and cold swapped. These episodes can occur randomly and last for random durations.
objects.title: Inverted Controls

addons.text: Your power addiction is more akin to a compulsive need it needs to fulfil. Where once you could use it sparingly or use traditional rehabilitation techniques to mitigate it, it’s now more equivalent to a ceaseless hunger. Where Divergent Instincts might originally cause a power that allows you to revive from the dead might to make you purposely suppress survival instincts, now you would feel the need to die and revive repeatedly like a normal human needs to eat, becoming a true part of your biology.
addons.title: Instinctive Need

objects.title: Divergent Instincts

objects.text: You have an addiction to illegal substances, hindering your overall performance. The constant use of these drugs has diminished your mental capacity and cognitive abilities, reducing your mental capabilities and perception. This, in turn, makes it more difficult to perform critical tasks such as planning, strategizing, and executing complex plans. Furthermore, prolonged drug use has left your body in a state of dependency, causing you to experience painful and debilitating withdrawals when not using. During this time, your physical abilities are reduced, resulting in a decrease in strength, agility, and stamina.
objects.title: Druggie

addons.text:
Your friendly nature makes you a downright bacchanal drunk, jovial and prone to being the life of the party, the one to shout first and loudest, breaking out into laughter given the slightest excuse, and not hesitating in doing something silly to keep the mood up. This does on occasion lead to some rather poorly thought-out actions and moments of embarrassment the next morning, but usually nothing that would result in more than a bit of ribbing and some jokes at your expense for a few days.

Consequently you're less prone to drinking by yourself, however in return when in a group in a relaxed setting you'll find yourself itching to start a wild binge at the slightest excuse.
addons.title: Happy Drunk

addons.text: As a depressive drunk, you are prone to unpredictable and unstable moods. When under the influence of alcohol, you may experience bouts of sadness or hopelessness that can last hours or even days. You may have difficulty finding joy in things that used to bring you happiness. To cope with these negative emotions, you may turn to alcohol, leading to a vicious cycle of depression and drinking.
addons.title: Depressive Drunk

addons.text: As a reckless drunk, you have a tendency to make poor decisions, often leading to reckless behavior. You may be prone to accidents and mishaps, as you have trouble maintaining your composure and controlling your actions and emotions. You may also struggle with memory loss, as you may not remember events from the previous night, leading to difficulty in solving puzzles or remembering information.
addons.title: Reckless Drunk

addons.text: When drunk, your mood and demeanor will constantly and suddenly shift at the slightest or even seemingly no provocation whatsoever, flipping from happy, to raging, to sobbing, to back to happy within seconds. You can remain in one state for a while, only to suddenly shift completely in a heartbeat when something sets you off. You're probably going to give those drinking with you whiplash.
addons.title: Mercurial Drunk

addons.text: As a blackout drunk, you have a tendency to lose consciousness, memory, and control when drinking in excess. This can lead to unpredictable and reckless behavior, as well as a lack of awareness of your surroundings and poor decision-making. You may also struggle with memory loss, leaving gaps in your recollection of the previous night's events.
addons.title: Blackout Drunk

objects.text: You developed an addiction to alcohol, resulting in impaired judgment, reckless behavior, and an inability to perform certain tasks. You struggle with the need to drink, often consuming large amounts of alcohol in a short period of time. As a result, you experience physical and emotional consequences, including headaches, vomiting, and withdrawals.
objects.title: Alcoholic

objects.text:
Good news, you have a teleportation power. Bad news, it only works when no one is looking at you through mundane means and you can't control it. 

It's also global in scale.

This drawback only activates every 24 to 48 hours and, after this drawback triggers, you cannot teleport further than 10 kilometers from your landing spot for one hour.
objects.title: Ryoga Hibiki

objects.text:
Good news, you no longer teleport around the Earth at random. Bad news you now teleport across the multiverse at random.

You are stuck in the universe you arrive in for one hour, and when your hour is up you are returned to a random place near to where you were when the drawback activated. You will not be teleported somewhere where you instantly die, such as a volcano or space.  You can optionally choose to extend your stay at the destination beyond one hour for any amount of time up until the next time the drawback triggers.

The places you arrive have a 1 in 3 chance to be beneficial, such as inside Scrooge McDuck's vault, a 1 in 3 chance to be benign, such as a random street in King's Landing, and a 1 in 3 chance to be dangerous, such as Northrend or the Outlands in World of Warcraft.

This drawback wears off after 100 jumps and only activates once every 5 to 7 days. This interval can be increased with Power Tweak but it will increase the time you must stay at the destination proportionally. The base drawback, Ryoga Hibiki, expires at the same moment Reluctant Dimension Hopper does.

You can also activate this drawback yourself before the deadline up to once every 24 hours.
objects.title: Reluctant Dimension Hopper

objects.text: There's no place like home. The destinations you jump to are not completely disconnected anymore. They will instead be an alternate universe (AU) reflecting your starting universe. For example, say your first universe is Worm. The next world you might go to could be Earth Cheit. Perhaps you land in an AU where Danny Hebert triggered instead of his daughter. Or where an otherwise minor character has access to the Celestial Forge. Or perhaps in a version of Earth Bet where a Parahuman created and used a mass relay, notifying the Citadel. Maybe you go where Khonsu, Tohu, and Bohu are the first Endbringers to appear and Brockton Bay is designated as Quarantine Site 8. Or maybe even on an alien planet undergoing a cycle by another Entity. In other words, you now jump to worlds that are in the local multiverse, official "What-Ifs," fanfiction, crossovers, or any other AUs of your first universe so long as it is recognizably derived from the first universe's continuity, characters, or framework.
objects.title: No Place Like Home

objects.text: For the Adventurous! The destinations this drawback sends you to are more dangerous. You have 1 in 6 chance to arrive somewhere beneficial, a 1 in 3 chances to arrive somewhere benign, a 1 in 3 chance to be sent somewhere dangerous, and finally you have a 1 in 6 chance to be sent somewhere deadly like the jungles of Catachan or Commorragh in Warhammer 40k. The latter does not mean you will die immediately on arrival as you are guaranteed to have at least a chance to survive, but it will not be easy unless you are powerful. This drawback wears off after 75 jumps and only activates once every 10 to 15 days.
objects.title: Zelretch's Entertainment

objects.text: For the Adrenaline Junkies! The destinations this drawback sends you to are more dangerous. You have 1 in 6 chances to arrive somewhere benign, a 1 in 3 chance to be sent somewhere dangerous, and a 1 in 2 chance to be sent somewhere deadly. This drawback wears off after 50 jumps and only activates once every 20 to 30 days.
objects.title: Friend of the Doctor

objects.text: For the Mad The multiverse has grown tired of your tourism and has decided to make an example of you. Every jump is now a confrontation with mortality itself, and the fragile peace you once found between destinations has been revoked entirely. Every single time this drawback triggers, you are guaranteed to be sent somewhere deadly. This does not mean you will die immediately on arrival, as the universe still extends you the courtesy of a fighting chance, but you will find no purchase in safe harbors, no respite in quiet corners, only the certainty that wherever you land, existence itself is trying to kill you. This drawback wears off after 25 jumps and only activates once every 1 to 2 months.
objects.title: The Diavolo Special

addons.title: Duration Hunches
addons.text: You still do not know how long any of your involuntary journeys will last, but now when you are dropped in, you get a fairly solid hunch on if your stay will be on the shorter or longer side. Nothing precise enough to set a schedule, but sufficient to know if you should be looking for a snack, a place to spend the night, or a job to cover the expenses of your stay.

objects.text: Consistency is something many don't really appreciate until it's gone. For you, the consistency of your involuntary journeys has now vanished. Whenever you are sent to a new world, instead of staying there for exactly an hour the time you'll spend there is now completely randomized, ranging from one minute to one day. The randomization cannot be affected by Drawbacks, Perks, or Powers influencing luck or chance. You will have no idea how long your stay will be at entry, though you will be be able to feel your imminent return shortly before it happens, with shortly being a couple seconds with a minute's stay and a few minutes with a day's. Should you have Delayed Return Flight, the upper limit of the randomization moves to the next larger unit, meaning up to week with one selection, up to a month with two selections, and up to a year if you've chosen all three. Should you actually spend a year in another world, you'll get roughly a week's warning before your return.
objects.title: Excuse Me, When's the Train Coming?

objects.text:
Previously your involuntary trips would return you back home after an hour. Well, your stay has just been extended.

By selecting this Drawback once, it will now take an entire day before you are returned back home. Selecting it twice extends it to a week, while choosing it thrice now leaves you in whatever new world you found yourself in for an entire month.

The interval between jumps can still be increased like in Reluctant Dimension Hopper, the proportional increase in subsequent duration however now uses the increased duration as its baseline.
objects.title: Delayed Return Flight

addons.text: You can designate any dimension you have visited previously as your 'home' and the power will periodically send you there instead of your original dimension. This can be changed once a year at most.
addons.title: Home away from Home

objects.text: One-way ticket to anywhere but here. When you teleport, you now stay around for longer than an hour. In fact, you don’t return at all. Every jump will leave you stranded in a new dimension. You will also be stuck in this dimension for at least an hour and dimensional transportation power will not work during this time. You can choose to delay your next jump and remain at your destination for up to 12 months. Luckily, every 3 to 5 jumps you will be transported to your original dimension. You will be able to stay in your original dimension for the time it takes for your drawback to trigger again.
objects.title: Stranded

objects.text: This dimensional train has no brakes. This drawback never wears off. However, Friend of the Doctor, Zelretch's Entertainment and The Diavolo Special will downgrade into their lower danger variants when their specified amount of jumps is exhausted until they reach the level of Reluctant Dimension Hopper. After this happens, you can always choose to be sent to a higher danger destination on your next jump. Additionally, once the drawbacks have exhausted their mandatory jumps, you can extend your stays to any length of time up to 10 years.
objects.title: Never Ending Adventure

objects.text:
The randomness of your jumps has developed a stutter. Sometimes the multiverse isn't finished with you when your hour is up, and you find yourself falling again before you can catch your breath.

When your time in a destination ends, you have a 1 in 2 chance to immediately trigger another jump to a new location before you can return to your starting point. When that jump ends, you again have a 1 in 2 chance to jump again, and this pattern repeats endlessly until you finally fail the coin flip. These coin flips are always fair, no form of luck from either perks, drawbacks, powers or outside force can influence it. These chain jumps still only count as a single jump toward the total limit of your base drawback.

This drawback lasts for the duration of your base drawback and does not alter its activation schedule.
objects.title: Into the Rabbit Hole

objects.text: Rather than being reincarnated straight into the world you've chosen in Settings, you've instead reincarnated and lived a brand-new life in another, unrelated world entirely—only to then be dropped into the world originally meant for you. Optionally, you may choose the scenario of how you came to be there, whether it was a freak science accident, an enemy technique that threw you across worlds, or something stranger. Your history and perks are affected by this. If taken without Homecoming, you've simply been dropped off—your family remains in your Reincarnation world, and perks or items such as A Pencil. A Fucking Pencil! apply only there. If taken with Homecoming, you may decide how aspects such as your family, time spent, reputation, and possessions are affected across both worlds. Finally, you'll be dropped into the Location and Scenario chosen here; your Reincarnation world can also be anything you wish.
objects.title: Displaced

objects.text: Your origin is not something most would be proud of. You could be a villain's child or a villain's marriage partner. Either way, people will know and distrust you because of it.
objects.title: Infamous Origins

addons.text: Good news: your sibling now no longer sees themselves as your enemy, in fact they really love you. Bad news: your sibling really loves you. They have become your stalker, becoming obsessed with you. At absolute minimum they have a shrine devoted to you, if not an entire wall of pictures and paintings of you if they can get away with it. They still want to see you happy and succeed, the problem here being what extremes your sibling is willing to go to, which can range from embarrassing to dangerous. If you and someone else are in competition for something, even if it's something as minor as being class-president, your sibling could decide to start campaigning like you're running for office, bribe your classmates to vote for you, or they could decide that if the other contender were to suffer an unfortunate accident that leaves them hospitalized for months, you will win by default. And this is by no means restricted to small matters. Regardless of your chosen path in life, your sibling wants to see you shine dazzlingly brightly, regardless of the expense to anyone else. This could result in them being genuinely helpful by aiding in investigations, or leading to them stirring up trouble just so that you can be seen solving it. They might still take on the role as your Rival if they feel it's the best way to raise your image or help you grow, though they're just as likely to try to assassinate anyone ahead of you in public opinion. Seeing that your sibling is every bit as powerful as you are, you will have an extremely hard time trying to keep them from meddling in your life, and you must take care to strike an extremely careful balance with their obsession with you. If you neglect them too much, they will resort to more and more drastic schemes to gain your attention. If in contrast you are too careless in lavishing attention and praise on them, they may well decide you are at your happiest when with your beloved sibling and don't really need anyone else in the world... Good luck, you'll need it.
addons.title: Obsessive Sibling

addons.text: Your evil sibling also has a variant of your other sibling’s power. Not only that, thanks to some shard shenanigans, your regular sibling has had their own power rise to match both of yours. This will cause butterflies.
addons.title: Sibling Rivalry

objects.text:
You were not born into this world as an only child. It does not matter if they are your older brother, younger sister, or even identical twin. What does matter is that they have obtained an equal amount of power as you and have decided to use it for nefarious purposes. 

Your path in life will naturally cross theirs, and not in a good way. Should you become a hero, they will become one of your greatest foes. Become a villain yourself, they will become your strongest rival. Even being a rogue will get you in their crosshairs, as your business becomes one of their targets. 

Whether you can go back to a healthy sibling relationship is completely unknown. Only conflict is certain in your future.
objects.title: Evil Sibling

addons.text: You have subverted a portion of the family to align with your interests, thereby securing access to a significant portion of their assets. This includes valuable resources such as land, financial capital, and a loyal cadre of personnel, all bolstering your power within the family's hierarchy.
addons.title: Up and Coming Contender

addons.text: You may not be the rightful heir, but you are one of, if not the most influential person within the family. You have contacts with everyone within the family, and they owe you in different ways. You have people monitoring each one of your relatives, and you will always know in advance if they plan to attack or sabotage you.
addons.title: Seat At The Table

addons.text: You aren’t some nobody, you have a reputation. You are someone known. You are the rightful heir of the family. Your siblings or other relatives will obey you, unless the actual head of the family says otherwise. This doesn’t mean others won’t desire your place, it just means that they will not do so openly, and if enough evidence is shown that they are attacking you, the family will back you up.
addons.title: The Heir

addons.text: You aren’t some nobody, you have a reputation. You are someone known. You are the head of the family. Your siblings or other relatives will obey you. This doesn’t mean others won’t desire your place, it just means that they will not do so openly, and if you so feel like it, you can have them expelled from the family and hunted down.
addons.title: Godfather

addons.text: No matter the situation with your family, you will always have some allies. This can be a relative, a parent, or even another sibling. These allies will stand by your side through thick and thin, providing support and assistance whenever you need it. Their powers may mirror yours exactly or take on unique forms that complement your abilities, ensuring that you are never truly alone in your endeavors. This bond of shared strength and mutual support can help you navigate even the most challenging circumstances.
addons.title: Allies

addons.text: Your family isn't just any old crime family. No, they are the crème de la crème of the criminal underworld, holding one of the seats on the Council, deciding the future of crime on a global scale and shaping the course of history. Being part of the family means that, like it or not, you've been involved in your fair share of crimes, and you have seen some shit. How deep the rabbit hole goes for you depends on your position within the family, but needless to say, your slate is far from clean, even if the authorities have no proof that'll hold up in court. This will make it exponentially more difficult and dangerous to try to switch to the side of the angels, both because you're at least suspected to be involved in some very unsavory business and, because of your upbringing, you know a number of things that some very influential and dangerous people want to keep confidential.
addons.title: Spot on the Council

objects.text:
It isn’t just your siblings or parents that are villains, it is your entire extended family. You’re born as one of the children of the head of a notorious crime family. They rose to prominence during the time parahumans first started triggering with lies, deceit, and their newfound unrivaled power. 

Your attempts at being good will be seen with immense doubt from just about everyone, with most assuming you’re attempting to lull them into a sense of security before you strike. Your attempt at becoming a full-blown cape will also get you hit ordered by the family for your perceived betrayal. 

Attempting to stay in the family will still net a hit on your life because you're in line to be the next head, and EVERYBODY wants to be the next head. Trying to pass this on to one of your siblings to avoid the heat won’t work. More than likely, they are the ones who put the hit out in the first place. So, once you declare them the heir, you will have outlived your usefulness in their eyes. 

You WILL be caught up in a web of lies, deceit, and betrayal, whether you like it or not.
objects.title: The Family Business

addons.text:
The drawbacks weaken with each subsequent generation. Each new generation will experience the drawbacks more slowly, with the full effects taking longer to manifest. Over time, the severity of the drawbacks will also diminish, resulting in weaker manifestations. For instance, a drawback that would fully activate by the age of twenty-five in the first generation might take until thirty in the next generation, and the impact would be less severe. This gradual weakening continues with each generation, offering a glimmer of hope that the drawbacks might eventually fade away entirely.

You can optionally choose to make it that your ancestors also had the same drawbacks and thus created ways to manage them (such as specific medicine for the weak body drawback).
addons.title: Paid In Blood

objects.text: All personal drawbacks you suffer will now be inherited by your descendants and retroactively given to any other family member you have. Initially, these drawbacks will be weak but will fully activate by their twenty-fifth birthday. The order in which they receive the drawbacks progresses from the least dangerous and least lethal to the most dangerous and greatest consequence. For example, if you have the orphan drawback, your child will also become an orphan by the age of twenty-five. If a drawback is impossible to manifest directly, it will alter to achieve a similar effect; for instance, if both parents are immortal, the orphan drawback might cause the parents to disown the child or become lost in another dimension forever. Drawbacks that require time to be fulfilled, such as Acclimation, will manifest earlier.
objects.title: Bound By Blood

addons.text:
In the off-chance you reconcile with your dark reflection, admitting the faults and parts within yourself you fear to stomach or think about, inviting said self-reflection through a cathartic battle or much-needed discussion doubling as self-examination of one’s psyche, you’ve achieved what most people take their whole lives to accomplish for themselves: Individuation, the integration of the Psyche to a larger Whole. As your dark reflection was the Shadow you cast, it has returned to its proper place within your mind, subsumed yet distinct, an aspect ready for your beck and call, like a projection.

This additionally has internal and spiritual repercussions: you’re now distinct and fully connected from the World, that is, things as gaining value or attachment from groups (society, institutions, organization, parties, ideologies, etc.) and the innate self-absorption common in mankind has been now surpassed, as well a connectedness to the process of the Collective, getting a feel on how everything and everyone feels and reasons. How you act and move feels lighter, a weight gone from your shoulders, an all-embracing sense of direction or purpose derived from a clearer mind, and a mindset confused as enlightenment to some that might as well be.

We can’t live with ourselves at our worst; we can’t be a better version of ourselves till we make peace with those times we were the worst. That is when you give yourself the chance to be more than you could ever be.
addons.title: I Can Neither Live With You Nor Without You

objects.text: Somewhere out there, there’s another you lurking in the shadows, a warped reflection of yourself; all your negative traits brought to the surface, everything about yourself you hate or fear or disgust, every bad memory, vice and past mistake. This dark copy of yours has everything you do, from the exact same powers and skills to even perks and items, and is filled with a burning, singular desire that they are willing to pursue at any cost to themselves - not to defeat you, but rather to confront you about your flaws and bring them to light, to make you acknowledge and accept them. Despite the overwhelming drive, they are not “evil”, or even ruthless, unless you also happen to be; while antagonistic, they are still you, - in mind, body and soul, whether or not you agree with it - and they are fully willing to simply talk things out and be reasonable rather than resort to brute force. They still, in fact, share many of the same attachments and motives as yourself, and in times of crisis are fully willing to call a truce in the face of a greater threat, or compromise if the both of you are especially stubborn, but they will never stop at least keep trying until you’ve fully accepted all the worse aspects of yourself for what they are.
objects.title: Face Thyself

objects.text:
Instead of being a human, you will transform into a domesticated animal like a cat, dog, or snake.

If you don't choose Drop-In, your choices in Character Identity will determine who your first owner will be in this new life. Alternatively, your character identity (from Character-Insert or Reincarnation) can become the animal.

Perks or drawbacks that can only reasonably affect a human (such as Wealthy or Kill Order) will be passed on to those who care for you. This means if you change owners, the previous caregiver loses these perks or drawbacks, and they transfer to your current caregiver. However, this only applies if they cannot reasonably affect you so if for example you somehow gain enough notoriety as a cat or someone believes your cape power involves transforming into a cat, the Kill Order drawback could apply directly to you.
objects.title: I am a What!?

addons.text:
Your ‘inhuman’ features are now a part of your animal being. While still based on your powers, this has the capability of making your resemblance mythical. Your appearance still determines how favorable your mutations are. Becoming a disfigured Slime for instance may well end up with chunks of digesting matter churning inside you for all to see, while a beautiful phoenix is a creature of true majesty. While these can make you resemble something mythical, your powers still have to resemble a creature to be able to truly mimic it. 

If you're entering another world, your form can be one of the mundane animals from that world. Additionally, lucky mutations are liable to make you akin to a true mythical creature.
addons.title: Monstrous Fauna

addons.text: Thanks to your specific emphasis on retaining your humanity, any new instincts from your new form are considerably weakened. enough to tell you where they should be but far from the strength of true animal instincts.
addons.title: The Erudite Inhuman

addons.text:
Your incredible foresight... it boggles the mind. 

Thanks to your world's native inhabitancy of intelligent animals, you can choose, rather than having an 'owner' to take your human-specific perks and drawbacks, they will instead affect yourself, with society affecting perks instead affecting your relationship with your fellow citizens of the wild, or the greater public should animal co-operation become the order of the day.
addons.title: I'm The Master Now!

objects.text: Instead of being a domesticated animal, you’re not even that lucky. Now Instead of being reborn as a domesticated animal, you’re a wild creature such as a gorilla, tiger or even penguin. While this will no doubt be better for your physical capabilities, you can expect your ability to navigate human society to be greatly prohibited.
objects.title: Not Even That Lucky...

objects.text: It’s not enough that you are now an animal; you are an animal that doesn’t fit your surroundings. You could be a goldfish in a desert, a garden snake in the mountains, or a parrot in the sea. You must find a way to thrive, to find sustenance, shelter, and a way to exist in a habitat that was never meant for you. Powers can help negate this to a degree.
objects.title: Invasive Species

addons.text: You are among the few birdcage inmates who didn't manage to escape. The remaining inmates harbor varying degrees of enmity towards you. Similarly, some of the inmates who did escape also share this animosity.
addons.title: Caged

objects.text: The morning tomorrow of your arrival, somehow there will be a massive breakout at the Baumann Parahuman Center with practically all prisoners escaping, more than half of them will encounter you and find a reason to target you.
objects.title: Won't You Fly High, Free Bird

objects.text: It seems that building the biggest prison for Capes in the same country as a mass master cape was not a good idea, now, either by luck, power, cape, or an idiot wanting points, that idea just got the WORM treatment. Now Heartbreaker has some of its inmates as Thralls. In its own, that would be catastrophic—but among those under his sway are Teacher, a Trump who can distribute low-level Tinker and Thinker abilities, and Ingenue, a Trump capable of enhancing one aspect of a cape’s powers in exchange for weakening another. Now every Thrall under Heartbreaker control is more than just loyal—they’re low-level Thinkers and Tinkers, optimized and cross-boosted by Ingenue’s interference. The result: a city’s worth of empowered parahumans, unified, coordinated, and utterly devoted. This pushes Heartbreaker far outside anything the PRT can plausibly contain, akin to a containment style S-Class, but no plausible contingency is in place. Worse, Heartbreaker control is absolute. His power rewrites the physical and chemical structures of his victims, making “cures” effectively impossible—freeing someone would require re-mastering them into their original state. In practice, this means every Thrall is his, permanently, and the number only grows.
objects.title: IT GETS WORM

objects.text: You will harbor exceedingly high expectations for everything and everyone around you, yet you will inevitably face disappointment. You might expect your son to achieve A+++, but he only manages an A. You aspire for him to become a doctor, but he chooses to be a musician instead. You hope your best friend will always support your dreams, but they pursue their own path, leaving you feeling abandoned. You expect your sibling to uphold family traditions, but they reject them entirely. You believe your top student will win a prestigious scholarship, but they fall short. You purchase a new phone expecting it to be flawless, only to find it lagging frequently. This will push others around you away, as the weight of your expectations is too heavy for them to bear. The most frustrating part? Someone else unrelated to you will always meet or exceed your lofty expectations, as if to spite you.
objects.title: The Asian Parent

objects.text: You or your family is not very wealthy. If you're a CEO then your business is quickly going downhill, though you're not yet poor, just getting there with a lot of momentum.
objects.title: Poor

objects.text: You live on the streets or in the wild. Your whole family could be like this, or just you if you're an orphan.
objects.title: Homeless

addons.text: Seems that your source of wealth was actually lent by the shady group. Now besides the money you owe by taking this drawback, you also owe them the value of what you gained with Wealthy.
addons.title: Nefarious Sources

objects.text: Uh-oh, you are in deep trouble now. Seen you owe to some people the greatest power of them all… money. On the first selection you will owe a shady group (either the Elite, or whatever comparable group in your world) 50,000$ or the equivalent, with each selection increasing it ten times (500k, 5M, 50M, 500M). They charge 1% in interest per month. If you refuse to pay, they will send goons after you and your properties to cover their losses. You can beat them, but each time they will send stronger people after you, each time more stronger then the previous.
objects.title: Debt

objects.text: You tend to monologue. It's nothing overpowering, but if you don't actively go out of your way to not monologue, you're probably going to monologue after you feel you've won.
objects.title: Monologue

objects.text: You tend to not say much. It's nothing overpowering, but if you don't actively try to talk, you'll find yourself doing roundabout things like elaborate gestures or saying the bare minimum when spoken to.
objects.title: Silent Protagonist

addons.text: Your nicknames are incredibly catchy and will spread like wildfire, to the point where those you give nicknames to may become more accustomed to responding to your nickname than to their actual names.
addons.title: Catchy

addons.text: Your nicknames will generally be rather bland, going either by parts of their names, like calling someone named Trafalgar Traffy or Tra-guy, or physical traits, like calling a girl Ponytail after her preferred hairstyle.
addons.title: Uninspired

addons.text: Your nicknames tend to lean towards unflattering at best, like calling someone with droopy hair Mophead, if not being outright provocative or insulting, such as calling someone with a styled hairstyle Shitty Hair or someone with burnscars Fry-Face.
addons.title: Taunt

objects.text:
You are terrible with names. Horrible really, they seem to refuse to take hold in your memory. You know your own name, those of your parents and siblings if applicable, and perhaps those of your closest friends, but beyond that it will take forever to hammer a new name into your head and make it stick. You still know who people are and recognize them perfectly fine, it's just their names escape you.

In response, you resort to nicknames, as they stick in your mind perfectly fine. They can be generic with people you're not close to, most of your educators will be Teach' or Sir/Madam unless they're your favorite teacher, while friends generally get more thoughtful titles.

You will irritate people with this habit, especially in more formal settings, and if you're trying to get into demonology or other practices requiring something's True Name, either bring cheat-sheets or, even better, just don't.
objects.title: Nicknamer

objects.text: Assuming the Slaughterhouse 9 has formed, they're after you. Not to kill you or torture you, no, something worse: They have a vacancy and recruitment in mind, only for you. If the Slaughterhouse 9 has yet to form, they will, and they will survive long enough to try to recruit you. If you don't have powers yet, they will only come after you once you've triggered.
objects.title: Slaughterhouse 8

objects.text:
If the Slaughterhouse 9 have already formed, then they'll be guaranteed to successfully clone themselves and their former members. While there will in truth only be around 300 clones in total instead of 9000 they'll still be just as vicious, and they've all been implanted with the desire to subdue you and make you part of their ilk, not to mention that they're just as strong as their original selves, although with alternate expressions of their powers. Should they not be able to find you they'll go after whatever you hold dearest, they will cause chaos and mayhem to draw you out if they can't find you. If they do know where you are, then they'll come after you in groups of 9 one group at a time.

Should they not have formed yet, they will and they will manage to survive long enough to clone themselves. If you don't have powers yet, they will only come after you once you've triggered.
objects.title: Slaughterhouse 9000

objects.text:
For whatever reason, the Teeth (and consequently the Butcher) decided to make you their next leader. They will pursue and attack you relentlessly, all with the goal of possessing your mind and making you the next incarnation of the Butcher.

Should they die and fail to possess you, whether due to someone else killing them, your powers or perks making possession impossible, or another reason entirely, they will still not waver in their dedication, as each previous incarnation will pressure the new one into pursuing you with the same relentless drive.

You can overcome this drawback by killing the Butcher in such a way that they cannot possess another person, like destroying their shard, for example, agreeing to lead the teeth in such a way that the voices in the current Butcher's head will be content with, or helping the most recent incarnation overcome the maddening influence of the voices before they drive them completely insane.
objects.title: Jaws of the Butcher

objects.text: The first time you go to an Endbringer fight, the Endbringer will go slightly out of its way to kill you. Unless you show that you're very powerful, you won't be its main focus.
objects.title: Endbringer Target

objects.text: Endbringers now perceive you as a potential existential threat. Regardless of how many battles you’ve fought, they will always make killing you a priority—though not necessarily above all other targets. They may alter their tactics, adapt their attacks, and occasionally ignore more pressing strategic objectives to eliminate you. However, they will not pursue you beyond the battlefield or seek you out if you choose not to engage.
objects.title: Hostile Endbringers

objects.text: Endbringers now recognize you as an anomaly that must be erased. They will prioritize you above all other targets, even altering their attack locations to ensure you are within the destruction zone. They may reveal previously unseen abilities, escalate encounters beyond known limits, and share information between battles to adapt to your tactics. If they consider a great enough threat, pairs of Endbringers may coordinate their efforts, and in extreme cases strike together to eliminate you. While they will not accelerate their attack schedule, your presence guarantees a far deadlier fight for everyone involved.
objects.title: Singular Target

addons.text:
The compulsion you are placed under is no longer outright malicious. Now, the end goal of the plot you are a part of will be to free Simurgh from Eidolon's control.

While not inherently destructive, should you lack the necessary powers to sever the bond peacefully, you may still be forced to take drastic actions, such as a direct confrontation with Eidolon, for example.

Should you successfully free Simurgh from Eidolon's control, the drawback will be resolved.
addons.title: Path to Freedom

objects.text: A silent screech lies in the back of your mind. You are now an unwilling part of a Simurgh plot. Maybe you'll wind up thinking that the plot must go as closely to the canon as possible, causing you to never do something that could jeopardize the plot or even try to correct perceived deviations. Maybe you will attempt to "remove" any threat to your city and burn it down in the process. Whatever the case, it is almost certainly negative in nature. This power overrides <u>Mental Barrier</u> and <u>Blank</u>.
objects.title: Whispers In The Mind

objects.text: Regardless if you're immune to Master/Stranger powers or not, at some time after you gained powers, you will succumb to a master effect and be compelled to forget about it. You'll become a sleeper agent, compelled to perform certain actions or behaviors upon hearing a specific trigger phrase, chosen by the master. These actions will seem entirely "normal" to you and will be carried out accordingly, even if they would otherwise be deemed unusual or inappropriate, or they could "ask" them to be forgotten.
objects.title: Would You Kindly...

addons.text: The person who made you is in fact, Echidna herself. Your appearance has been altered, with your features being distorted, some overgrown and others undergrown. You will additionally be placed under a master effect which will cause you to hate your original and all they love as well as have minor protective desire for Echidna’s wellbeing.
addons.title: You Are The Clone

addons.text: Now instead of coming to consume you to mass produce clones, Noelle seeks to clone your powers and form in an effort to get her revenge.
addons.title: A Different Cause

objects.text:
Sooner or later, Noelle Meinhardt, later dubbed Echidna, will snap due to the constant maddening influence of her powers. At this point, she will hold you solely responsible for her current predicament and desire revenge above all else. If she manages to consume you and you lack protections of any kind, she will produce numerous clones of yourself, each possessing all your memories, a connection to a variant of your shard powers, and a burning hatred for you in particular. If she fails to catch you, she will try to gather as many parahumans as possible to overwhelm you with sheer numbers.

You may prevent this by healing Noelle before she completely loses her mind.
objects.title: Echidna Clone

objects.text: Glaistig Uaine never entered the Birdcage and has continued gathering powers, often targeting those with strong or interesting powers. She has become a boogeyman for Capes and is now regarded as even above Eidolon (as he is now). Whatever your powers, regardless of how strong or weak they are, she has decided to add you to her collection. You have about a week before Glaistig Uaine arrives so use that time to get familiar with your powers and the layout of the city.
objects.title: Fairy Goddess

objects.text:
Eidolon will learn, through one means or another like Thinker powers or Watchdog evaluation, that you are a worthy challenge for him. A Worthy Opponent. Anti-thinker perks cannot protect you against this. Even if you are a hero, he will find a way to challenge you.

And you better be able to provide an adequate challenge as Eidolon will be coming at you with all his might.
objects.title: You are the Worthy Opponent

objects.text: Eidolon will learn that he can restore his powers to their full strength by killing you. He will not give up and will not hesitate to exhaust his Shard to kill you.
objects.title: Chosen One

objects.text: At some point in the future, Saint and the Dragonslayers will become convinced that you will be a serious threat to humanity, even if you don't plan on doing anything big with AIs. Saint will use his remote access to Dragon's code combined with Teacher's granted skills to master her, forcing her to fight you as a high-priority target.
objects.title: Saintly Purge

objects.text:
You'll come to the attention of Teacher and he'll become convinced that you're a threat to his interests and an essential target for brainwashing.

You'll find him comparable to his peak in Ward, with a large, well-tuned organization of empowered thralls and Parahuman recruits, which is particularly well-suited for subterfuge and sabotage from afar. Depending on the timeline, he may never have entered the Birdcage in the first place, and has instead had a few years to grow his influence while safely tucked away on a far-away world.
objects.title: Compulsory Enrollment

objects.text:
Through some method, the Machine Army will learn about you, determining you as an existential threat to their survival. They will not stop at anything to collect you before dissecting you to determine how your powers work. They will ignore all existing rules and truces in their single-minded pursuit to capture you. The Machine Army is guaranteed to breach their containment zone in Eagleton.
 
Should you find yourself on an alternate Earth without the Machine Army, a threat analogous to them and just as dogmatic will be formed.
objects.title: Targeted for Termination

objects.text: Bonesaw has perfected the building of artificial cape amalgamations out of the corpses of her victims, now properly incorporate different powers into one body and not just combining them. By the time you arrive she has built almost a dozen artificial capes, some being enough to equal teams worth of capes. And she finds herself wanting you and your power for an artificial cape.
objects.title: Bonesaw's Army

objects.text: Bonesaw has now created what could be viewed as a proper magnum opus, an artificial cape on par with a member of the triumvirate that can combine or independently use its powers, this magnum opus also has an advanced brain and thinks for itself and acts independently of outside command. And she’s set it loose with the one goal of killing you. Bonesaw also has the capability to make more artificial capes on this level now
objects.title: Bonesaw's Opus

objects.text: Outside of battle, you're clumsy and forgetful. These can both be removed through your powers or through practice.
objects.title: Ditz

objects.text:
Your life is full of misunderstandings, almost like a comedy anime, without the comedic undertones while being prone to cause serious problems. Maybe a Hero might think you are committing a crime, the public blames you for a bank heist you incidentally went to open an account, or a Villain thinks you are responsible for killing their child. Almost all misunderstandings you’re personally involved in will have a detrimental price, to put it shortly.
(If you take Trouble Magnet as well… well get ready)
objects.title: Misunderstandings

objects.text: You will frequently be required to perform villainous acts or suffer escalating consequences. You are not required to succeed but an attempt with a reasonable possibility of success must be made. These tasks will require illegal acts to be performed, from theft and robbery to arson or even assassination. As long as you cooperate, what will be asked of you will test but not overstep your moral boundaries but will be inconvenient to your plans in some way. (Such as robbing a bank if you are trying to lay low.)
objects.title: Contractual Villainy

objects.text: The tasks you receive are no longer constrained by moral boundaries. Instead, they will slowly escalate and become more morally reprehensible until you reach depravities that would make even the Slaughterhouse Nine sick. (Or, more likely, recruit you.)
objects.title: I'm Altering the Deal

objects.text: You can't hold your alcohol. No matter the type of drink, your tolerance is so low anything gets you easily intoxicated. A single shot and you're slurring your words, stumbling, and likely making a fool of yourself. It might raise the likelihood of alcohol poisoning due to your low tolerance.
objects.title: Lightweight

objects.text:
Over time you will find Parahumans of opposing alignments and goals drawn to you like moths to a flame. This will happen at a rate of roughly one Normal Shard Parahuman per month, and an additional person with a Vital Shard appearing yearly. However the more powerful you are, the more rapidly enemies will rise to challenge you.
This Drawback will wear off after 10 years.
objects.title: Rogues Gallery

objects.text: Your body is anomalous, causing it to defy the conventional Manton Limit. For example, Vista's power won't recognize you as a living being, allowing her to warp the space your body occupies as if you weren't there. However, Crusader's ghost treats you as a living target, able to inflict harm upon you. In other words, you exist on the unfavorable side of the Manton Effect, where the usual rules and protections do not apply to you.
objects.title: Manton Unlimited

objects.text:
When it comes to irrelevant, everyday inconveniences, you have terrible luck. You will stub your toe more frequently, often arrive at a stoplight just as it turns red, will never win at bingo, and experience other such frustrations. 
This Drawback will wear off after 10 years.
objects.title: Inconsistent Minor Misfortune

objects.text:
You are slightly less lucky in all aspects. This is a very subtle, very small decrease, but affects even combat. This effect is twice as potent if you have any Perks or Powers that increase your luck. 
This Drawback will wear off after 10 years.
objects.title: Consistent Minor Misfortune

objects.text:
You will frequently find yourself the target of embarrassing accidents and situations. Your clothes may get damaged in the fight, you may accidentally lock yourself out of your apartment in nothing but a bath towel, and other staples of the genre.

This will not happen in situations where it would pose immediate danger to your life, but prepare for a world of shame.
objects.title: Fan Service Magnet

objects.text:
