Whenever you die a final death with no means of resurrection via your own powers or stay dead for more than a year voluntarily, you are sent back right to the beginning of your CYOA adventure, to the moment you first wake up in a new world. Only your memories and personality are carried over, and all the other progress is reset.

<small>Do note, that this Drawback does not come with the escape clause.</small>
objects.title: Eigo Kaiki

objects.text: You're not necessarily any less intelligent... you just care less. You're really bad at anything you're not significantly motivated to do.
objects.title: Shounen

objects.text: People will expect you to do small favors for them whenever you're not busy with something important. People might ask you to mow their lawn or save their cat from a tree. You can decline to do so, but most people will be offended by this.
objects.title: Servant

objects.text:
The death of your parents is all but inevitable; not long after your arrival, events will conspire to remove them permanently.

You can protect your parents by relocating them to another universe while you remain behind. However, this drawback will resume if you make meaningful contact again.

This drawback expires once you turn 18.
objects.title: Orphaned

objects.text: You now suffer from an incurable soul sickness for a week. While it won't kill you, it will make you want to rest your head for the week and not do anything.
objects.title: Sick

addons.text: While your physical body can be healed, for as long as you are under the effects of Soul Sickness you will feel a constant phantom pain where your injuries were located. These pains cannot be healed whatsoever, even mitigating it will be impossible. Others can’t heal it either.
addons.title: Spiritual Pains

objects.text: Your body is injured in some way. It could be a broken arm or even a gun wound. The injury must be serious enough to hinder you in some way, but not enough to be lethal. You cannot heal yourself of these injuries for a week, but can mitigate them to a degree. However, you can still be healed by others.
objects.title: Injured

objects.text: Even if you're not handicapped in the slightest, when you're in your civilian identity, people will think you're handicapped.
objects.title: Handicapped

addons.text: Whatever disabilities you have are now a part of your Case 53 form. You are beyond saving.
addons.title: Monster Cape

addons.text: The Injuries you sustained are now likely the cause of your disability. Lost an eye? Be prepared to enter with a bloody socket. Nerve damage? Perhaps a burn rides up the portion it resides in. This does not apply for disabilities that cannot reasonably come from physical damage.
addons.title: Grievous Injury

objects.text:
You now possess a disability which slightly impacts your day-to-day life. For example, this disability can range from, but is not limited to: minor deafness, partial vision loss, mild speech disorders, partial paralysis, minor genetic disorders, mild cognitive disabilities or limited amputations such as the loss of a single eye or section of a limb.

No powers you possess can outright heal your disability but can still potentially compensate for it. This drawback also doesn't stop others from being able to heal you.
objects.title: Minor Disability

addons.text: Whatever disabilities you have are now a part of your Case 53 form. You are beyond saving.
addons.title: Monster Cape

addons.text: The Injuries you sustained are now likely the cause of your disability. Blinded? Prepare for sharp pain and darkness. Lost an arm? Best pray you’re close to a healer… or at least a hospital. This does not apply for disabilities that cannot reasonably come from physical damage.
addons.title: Debilitating injury

objects.text:
You now possess a severe disability which strongly impacts your day-to-day life. For example, this disability can range from, but is not limited to: complete deafness, blindness, muteness, paraplegia, severe genetic and mental disorders or major amputations such as the loss of an entire limb.

No powers you possess can outright heal your disability but can still potentially compensate for it. This drawback also doesn't stop others from being able to heal you.
objects.title: Major Disability

objects.text:
Good news—everyone wants a piece of you. Bad news—this is meant quite literally.

Anything, from your blood to your flesh and everything else, is now tailored to be perfect for those that consume it. A vampire will find your blood tastier than that of any other human; a ghoul will find the flesh of others tasteless and bland after having a piece of you. And if you have Shardless or Esoteric Knowledge, this effect extends to any supernatural energies you possess for those who may feast on them.

While this will not affect those who do not appreciate the taste of human blood or flesh in the first place, those who do, like cannibals, ghouls, vampires, zombies, etc., will now instinctually understand that you are the best meal they will ever come across. How they react depends on their moral disposition, as well as their relation to you.
objects.title: Morsel

objects.text: Your empathy is muffled, with your emotional intelligence hampered, making it harder to see things from the perspective of others; on top of it all, any emotional response or general sentimentality is indirectly dulled, coming as aloof or wooden to other people.
objects.title: Cold Heart

objects.text:
You've a little quirk and urge to right perceived injustice, feeling compelled to do right by people and help them the best you can, even at the detriment of your own mental and physical well-being.

This urge won't be overwhelming at first, but the more you ignore it, the more it will build. Eventually, it will reach a breaking point when you witness someone in danger, and you won't be able to look away. You'll throw yourself in without hesitation or second thought, even if it means facing near-certain death.

That said, helping others in small but meaningful ways to brighten their day may ease this pressure. But be warned: if you turn your back on someone in need, especially under threat of death, this desire will swell to its absolute limits.
objects.title: No Rest for the Righteous

addons.text: You are quick to hate and hold grudges. If someone has ever slighted you, even if they did so unknowingly, you will remember. This can cumulate into you acting on this petty hatred, such as directly attacking them in retaliation, or doing something even more sinister which can result in the target dying or worst.
addons.title: Hatred

addons.text: Your pride and honor are among your most valuable traits. When challenged or making a promise, you feel compelled to follow through, no matter the personal cost to you. This commitment to your principles and your own self-worth is a strength, but it can also be a burden. You can never back down, never accept anything less that your best.
addons.title: Pride

addons.text: Your fear moves you to a careful and distrustful mien. Anything that flares your uneasiness is either avoided or reactively acted upon to “deal” with. Born out of a desire for self-preservation, you are compelled to assert control or compensate due to your dread. Disbelief and denial are the defense mechanisms you grapple with and struggle with. Having Courage turns this into a sense of carefulness and concern for people around you, a healthy skepticism that never passes to cynicism, and being capable of acknowledging your doubts and insecurities with passionate certainty.
addons.title: Fear

addons.text:
Your emotions can now reach a plateau, a point from which they can no longer increase and instead seem to cease. You can effectively achieve a stack integer overflow with your emotions, achieving a sort of harmonic state where you are able to focus on the task at hand.

This is rather dangerous due to it being extremely draining on you, with side effects including memory loss, depression, and even becoming completely comatose should you stay in this state too long. Unfortunately, your high emotional state makes this easier to achieve than it should. 

It does come with the benefit of enhanced problem solving, perception, and reflexes; meaning that you may end up needing to do this if the situation calls for it. Too bad that this simply increases the temptation to do this again and again, desperately trying to solve your problems as quickly as possible. You will need to be mindful of your emotions in the future to make sure that you don’t burn out and become an empty shell of who you once were.

If you have Healer, Well-Adjusted, or Inland Empire you will be able to recover from this faster to various degrees. Having I Can Fix Them or Inland Empire can even allow you to recover from total emotional burnout, preventing you from becoming a sociopath. While having either Well-Adjusted or Inland Empire can prevent you from permanently going into a coma, the threat will remain. You will simply become more aware of your limits and how to work around them.
addons.title: Threshold

objects.text: Your emotions run deep and often cloud your judgment, leading you to form quick and strong emotional attachments with others. For example, you might fall in love quickly and deeply, which can lead to heartbreak. Additionally, you might make decisions based on your emotions rather than logic, causing problems in your life. It’s hard for you to take a step back and think things through before following your intuition, and as your emotions tend to control you.
objects.title: Emotional

addons.text: You are guided by your desires, putting your own needs and wants above all else. Whether you are in the midst of a fierce battle or an intense negotiation, if you suddenly get a craving for fried chicken, you will simply drop everything and leave to satisfy your craving. Your impulsive and erratic behavior, driven by your desires, can be both unpredictable and dangerous. Nevertheless, you remain steadfast in your pursuit of personal pleasure, regardless of the consequences.
addons.title: Acting On A Whim

addons.text: Anyone can tell at first glance that you are like an open book. Any of your emotions are not only transmitted to others but also affect your body and appearance, changing by your current emotions. For example, burning anger will turn your hair into fire and your face into demonically terrifying, or happiness will give you a halo of light around you, making you a literal manifestation of the idiom "Shine with Happiness" making you look like an open book. Any attempts to lie, cunning, or deceive another person are doomed from the start as a thought. With this, it will be difficult for you to find companions and friends, and many will most likely leave you, but those who remain will be your best friends.
addons.title: Open Book

objects.text: You wear your heart on your sleeve, broadcasting your emotions and desires to the world with unmistakable clarity. Your emotions shine through, impossible to conceal even from the most dense people. Whether it be about you liking someone or you hating an activity, anyone can tell. There is no hiding your wants and desires; they're laid bare for all to witness.
objects.title: What Do You Desire

objects.text: You are an old-school man. If you are a hero, then you must be in a suit. If in normal life, then you must live without superpowers. You must differentiate your life between life as a cape and life as an ordinary citizen. You cannot knowingly reveal the secret of your civilian identity to others. You cannot use your powers in civilian identity.
objects.title: Keep The Secret

objects.text:
You have a dangerous habit of underestimating the threat certain people pose, and this always ends up biting you in the ass.

Major players are exempt from this. Instead, this drawback triggers whenever you go against lesser foes or threats.

Expect a lot of humiliation to come your way that could have been avoided. Be careful not to get yourself killed.
objects.title: Eh, I Can Take You

objects.text:
You tend to attract trouble or, more likely, trouble tends to find you. 

Even if you live a normal life, you will occasionally be involved in minor events that spice up your routine. These predicaments will rarely, if ever, completely disturb your life or put you in serious danger and your involvement in them will generally match your principles and morals. In most cases, the problems can be resolved without the use of violence on your part.

For example, the local police could ask you to assist with a mysterious murder if you’re known as a detective if not a P.I., additionally, your neighbors want help investigating the strange happenings around the block if you are heroically aligned or known as a helpful person. You might also uncover conspiracies or cabals by accident, like the school principal committing fraud or local Thinkers manipulating property prices.
objects.title: Trouble Magnet

objects.text:
The frequency, scope, and general ... oddness of the events you become involved with all increase. 

For example, you might find yourself at the center of an underground war between the Mafia and Yakuzas after you befriend the heiress to one of their clans at school, or you might get dragged into a long trip to uncover the dark secrets of the Golden Idol you received from a long lost acquaintance, or you might even discover that Medhall Corporation is working on a bioweapon to turn people into zombies.

The sky is very much not the limit and those adventures might get dangerous but never outside of your ability to solve — or at least survive — with your current skill set, powers, and allies.
objects.title: Wild Wasteland

objects.text:
You attract trouble. Even if you try to live a completely mundane life, you will get pulled into the schemes of others or strong parahumans will always find you and challenge you to a fight. Either way, your life will be interesting in the Chinese sense.

This could be considered a perk if you have a power that grows with the use or that gets significantly more useful with increased skill, but it ensures you're never overpowered.

If you're stronger than anyone in the setting, a Tinker might find themselves opening a portal between the universe you're in and one with stronger fighters.
objects.title: May you live in Interesting Times

objects.text:
Somehow, when getting involved — or dragged into — in strange plots, you often find yourself in the position of "damsel in distress," getting captured and taken hostage or prisoner; this applies regardless of gender.

Even if you have powers that would normally prevent this, you'll get knocked out by a blow to the head or put to sleep with some chloroform, then wake up somewhere else, usually restrained in some form or prevented from leaving. You can foil some of those plots but, at least some of the time, your kidnappers will get lucky.

Of course, once the deed is done, nothing stops you from rescuing yourself if you have the means to do so; even if your powers are unsuited to direct confrontation, there will be opportunities to leverage your social engineering or escape artist skills. You might convince a guard to unlock your handcuffs and brain them with a fire extinguisher, or fashion a lockpick out of a hairpin and use your stealth skills to escape. (Or teleport away, but that would be super boring.)

Either way, it will be an adventure. If you fail in your escape, your kidnappers will bring you back to your cell and add some extra security. After some time, your allies will come to your aid, or pay the ransom, and you'll get to go home.
objects.title: Kidnapping Magnet

objects.text:
Your life is now destined for a grand journey—a tale brimming with adventure, thrills, sorrows, joys, and terrors, with so much more in between, weaving together into a tapestry of unforgettable experiences.

While your role in fate's design is significant, it won't overshadow all others, nor will it pull everyone into your orbit. Instead, your life will be a balance of remarkable events and meaningful connections, filled with intrigue and excitement. However, please note that you won't have any plot armor to shield you through this journey; the stakes are very much real.

Even so, when the time comes for your grandest adventures to draw to a close and as you enter the quieter chapters of your life, the journey won't entirely fade. You'll continue to attract a subtle flow of intrigue and challenges—a touch of excitement just enough to keep your days vibrant. Yet amidst all this, leaving you enough peace and solitude to find true contentment in the quieter moments.
objects.title: Fated Journey

objects.text:
You have been blessed with the fate to live out your own story, with you as the protagonist. You will meet the most interesting people, be present for the most momentous events, and get to see the most amazing places around, all the while getting into no end of dangerous trouble, just like any other protagonist out there.

This practically guarantees that regardless of your desires, you will be drawn into and be a major player in the main story of any world you land in or visit, if there is any - and if it doesn't have any, fate will put you on a path that determines the future of the world, whether for better or for worse. This might sound amazing but know that this doesn't give you any plot armor, so there is nothing that guarantees your safety, and while you will have some downtime between adventures, you will inevitably get dragged back into another grandiose adventure.
objects.title: Child of Fate

objects.text:
Wow, you really must be a glutton for the strange, weird, and adventurous, aren't you? Well, you now have that in abundance.

You are going to see everything the Multiverse has to offer if you live that long, from the Reapers invading, Darkseid attacking whatever world you currently live in, to a rowdy and destructive group of mages crashing in your house, and Justice League randomly appearing in your current world, et cetera. You will never lack for any form of excitement.

This in essence makes your life a massive multi-crossover, where you will meet several characters not limited to franchises you know regardless of your current world, they will find you, and they will involve you in their nonsense, so I hope you're ready.

Note: If you take this and <u>Child of Fate</u>, you are in for a hell of a time.
objects.title: Mr. Regular

addons.text: Your Perks are also locked behind the same mechanism. Perhaps you’ll need an anti-scrying ritual for <u>Blank</u> or a new body made of power-disrupting metals for <u>Manton Protected</u>.
addons.title: From Scratch

addons.text: You don't just have to gain your Perks over time but actively work to improve them after you acquire them.
addons.title: Grind It Out

objects.text:
Rather than a singular event igniting your abilities, they’ve become linked to the ‘story’ you’re fated to live.

While at the start of your story you’ll only have access to the basest powers to your inciting incident, over time through gifted items, fortuitous encounter, arcane ritual, or eleventh-hour power-up, you’ll obtain them all. However, they will only come at the whim of the narrative.
objects.title: Kindling

objects.text:
The Fate of this world actively resists change, skewing probability and railroading events to produce the “Canon” outcome, as if the very world itself conspires against attempts to change things. While this may not have much impact in places far from the main “story” as it were, the closer you get to the action the more luck and probability distort to result in a specific outcome. 

While this may not sound so bad at first, you’ll find that any attempt to influence things for the better will result in pushback. For instance in Worm, if you try to kill Jack Slash to prevent him from triggering Golden Morning you will experience progressively more and more ludicrous events designed to prolong his existence until he can fulfil his role. 

Such is the strength of this affect that in order to kill him you would need to cut off every possible avenue of survival or escape no matter how unlikely, and even if you do kill him events will conspire to resurrect or clone him, and if you prevent all ways of that happening something else will come along to trigger Scion instead.

If you intend to change the Fate of this world, strap yourself in because you’re going to need to be on top of things 24/7 in order to get anything done.
objects.title: Chains of Fate

objects.text:
Your fate is now intertwined with the main plot of the world you first appear in. You will find yourself encountering canon characters more often, and events will conspire to encourage your participation in the main story.

For example, the Undersiders may bump into you while fleeing from Lung, you may be chosen as another member or a Jonin instructor of Team 7, etc. This drawback naturally expires when the main plot reaches its conclusion.
objects.title: Plotbound

objects.text: Plotbound now activates every time you enter a new universe, ensuring that you are forced to participate in the canon story. This does not affect universes you have previously visited, such as your home one, for example.
objects.title: Never Ending Story

objects.text:
Circumstances will always conspire, whether by having you trapped, preoccupied, distracted, or just sleeping in, from directly participating in major events of the original narrative. You can still interact with and influence the main canon characters, and even indirectly influence these events, but you will never be there for them.

This does not prevent you from having your own epic adventures and narratives. In fact, those will probably be what’s keeping you away from the main events of the original. Even in the case of massive world shaking or apocalyptic events, you will probably be stuck half a city or more away from the main characters dealing with your own fallout of those events.
objects.title: Slept Through It

objects.text: The Fallen believe you to be one of the Endbringers, possibly not believing you've yet to receive whatever divine wisdom causes the Endbringers to destroy cities every couple of months. They will worship you and try to get you to act like the Endbringers. Even if you don't take this, they might still come to this conclusion.
objects.title: Fallen Worship

objects.text: No one will believe you if you tell them about the entity or Cauldron unless you show them definite proof or they already know about what you're telling them. Powers like (Stranger) Truth overpowers this drawback.
objects.title: Tinfoil Hat

objects.text:
Now you can’t tell anyone any meta-knowledge without some kind of proof. This ranges from telling the Undersiders about Dinah or telling the PRT about Bakuda in advance. If you do, they won’t believe you.

This also makes it impossible for others to get this information, mind control or mind reading will not work as the information will temporarily just cease to exist.
objects.title: Conspiracy Theory

objects.text: Every negative event can impact your mental state, accumulating mental wounds that, if not properly healed, can cause significant damage. The more severe the event, the greater the damage, while mild events can cause mild to no damage. As mental damage accumulates, your thoughts gradually darken, worsening at certain points. Unhealed mental wounds will haunt you with flashbacks. After a certain amount of mental damage, a break can occur so severe that it turns a paragon of heroes into the most vile of villains. Once the Despair Event Horizon is passed, recovery becomes very difficult, though not impossible.
objects.title: Despair Event Horizon

objects.text:
You possess a major weakness or vulnerability to a particular thing. How it affects you is under your discretion but it must be highly detrimental, whether acting as an inhibitor, poison and/or causing some other form of harm.

For instance, like Kryptonite, you might find yourself weakening and losing your abilities in its presence. It could induce a crippling fatal flaw similar to an Achilles’ Heel or, like a werewolf under a full moon, force you into an uncontrollable berserk rage that causes you to go on a rampage.

This can be an element on the periodic table, the performance of a ritual or an object like the Bible. There is no hard requirement on how prevalent it must be, maybe even as ubiquitous as sunlight or fire, but it cannot be too difficult to feasibly acquire or use; such as an unattainable item or condition that can never be met.
objects.title: Arbitrary Weakness

objects.text:
You will follow the orders given to you by your superiors unless they clash personally with your morals or viewpoint e.g. you wouldn’t obey orders forcing you to kill innocent civilians if your standards defy this.

You also take legality into account where it’s harder to question or challenge orders you disagree with, although made legitimately or with the law supporting it i.e. if a despot were to seize power through legal means like an election, you would be more inclined to follow the orders of the new government than if they seized power through a violent coup.
objects.title: Just Following Orders

objects.text: You have a pragmatist mindset. Your plans and solutions do not always consider the human factor or the PR angle, even so, your ethics and morals still influence your plans. This makes working in a team somewhat difficult if the other members are less pragmatic than you, it depends on whether you are ready to compromise and accept the opinion of others or follow their plans.
objects.title: Pragmatist

objects.text:
You have an idealist mindset. Your plans and solutions are influenced by your values and vision of how things should be and do not always consider efficiency or feasibility.

You will likely reject utilitarian ideas if they conflict with your principles, though logistical and practical concerns can still influence your decision-making. This may make working in a team difficult if other members are less idealistic than you, it depends on whether you are ready to compromise with others on your ideals.
objects.title: Idealist

objects.text: You are unable to work with others in a meaningful way for any extended period of time unless you really put the effort in. Any team you join will inevitably either fall apart or kick you out. You must be genuinely attempting to work with the team for this to take effect, so no joining a gang with the intent of having them fall apart.
objects.title: Personality Conflict

objects.text: You must always try for a peaceful resolution before subduing an opponent by force. Your attempt at a peaceful resolution must be a true attempt but can be done in a simulation or have been undone by time travel. The resolution attempt should be proportional to the situation, you are not expected to solve a random ganger's family problems before arresting him for armed robbery.
objects.title: Mercy

objects.text: You can't help but make unnecessarily elaborate and dramatic plans. Maybe you steal an entire building just to steal an item inside, or maybe you only use a tank of sharks to kill your enemies. Regardless, your plans are more dramatic than pragmatic.
objects.title: Complexity Addiction

objects.text: You just suck at looking charismatic or good due to the horrendous fashion choices. Not only that, even when wearing normal clothing, you will somehow look a bit off, enough that people will subconsciously find you less attractive.
objects.title: Terrible Fashion

objects.text: Everyone, and I mean EVERYONE (including that cat by the end of the road), has at least a 50% chance of defeating you unless you are able to read their attack patterns, and time your attacks perfectly. This doesn't make enemies stronger, not really, rather it makes all combat more skill based than pure power based. This doesn’t change the fact that pure power can help you win, it just makes it that even with pure power there is a chance someone more skilled than you can snatch the win. This chance of losing does not accumulate with each opponent you are facing at once.
objects.title: Souls Game

objects.text: Your social life will suffer because of your Hero career. If you work for an organization, you'll be interrupted during your off-time for various "urgent" matters. Your candlelit dinner date might be interrupted by a villain attack or another emergency. None of the interruptions will put your secret identity at risk, if you have one, there will always be the opportunity to slip away discreetly or politely excuse yourself.
objects.title: Always on The Clock

objects.text: Your life is absolutely miserable, like there is some invisible force having a laugh at your misery.  Supervillains might attack and kill your loved one, You will struggle with work and earning money constantly at risk of being fired or entering poverty, or some guy or girl might come along and steal the love of your life from you. Being a hero is a sacrifice and your duty will take it pound of flesh from you but remember with great power comes great responsibility you will even make it out somehow.
objects.title: Parker Luck

objects.text: Two powerful people will be aware of you, the Entity/Entities, and either the choices the other person made, the CYOA you played, or the deal the third party gave you (depending on your Meta (Awareness) choice). One will be a paragon of heroism, the other self-interested villainy (though whether they are a 'Hero' or a 'Villain' is variable). The 'hero' will try to convince you to use your power for good, though that doesn't necessarily mean they care how you go about this (They don't care if you act the part of a Superhero or if you do humanitarian work instead). The 'villain' will try to convince you to use your power for selfishness and evil. Neither of them will attack you unless you choose the side of the other person.
objects.title: An Angel and Devil on My Shoulders

objects.text: You will inevitably have a kill order placed on your head by the PRT. Anybody in the world can murder you with no legal consequences whatsoever, and in fact, will be rewarded for doing so. Heroes especially will be gunning for you whenever they have a chance. All those unwritten rules that discourage actually killing someone in a Cape conflict no longer apply to you, and your opponents will be going all out.
objects.title: Kill Order

objects.text: You tend to really stand out to Thinkers. Any nearby Thinkers will feel the urge to use their powers more often, especially in your direction. Thinker powers tend to get a much better scan of you than they normally would, i.e. figuring out more details about you, where you are or what you’ve been up to, or getting more accurate predictions about your future or past, and receiving less mistakes and false assumptions. Stranger powers also become dulled as far as Thinkers are concerned.
objects.title: Noticeable

objects.text:
You can't help but add things absolutely no one will want. You promise something and vastly under-deliver. You are a complete buzzkill when it comes to making anything or everything.

You say you will create a sword that can annihilate continents, you will only end up putting in enough work to make a sword that barely damages a building.

Your promises are lies and you're probably a douchebag
objects.title: Overwatch 2

objects.text:
Your ability to traverse the Multiverse has been disabled and all forms of methods to get out of your initial world will fail. You must wait sometime before a successful jump to another universe is made.

It takes 1 year for the soul anchor to fade. Taking this option repeatedly multiplies it by 10 for a maximum of a billion years.
objects.title: A Little While Longer

objects.text:
You are metaphysically tethered to a specific Anchorpoint. If you do not select one, your starting Location becomes your Anchorpoint.

If your Anchorpoint is a city, the area of effect encompasses the entire city limits. If it is a non-urban location, such as a forest, mountain, or abandoned ruin, your influence extends over a radius of 12km centered around the chosen spot.

Your powers (from this CYOA) diminish the farther you travel from this area and the longer you are outside of it.  Re-entering the zone gradually restores your full strength.

Over time and with the growth of your powers the effective area of your Anchorpoint grows in size, allowing you greater range and freedom—but never complete detachment.
objects.title: Anchorpoint

objects.text: You are now physically incapable of leaving your Anchorpoint's domain. Invisible or metaphysical forces keep you within its boundary—step too close to the edge, and your body simply refuses to go farther. Vehicles break down, paths seem to loop, and sheer force fails. You gain increased power and control within your Anchorpoint, but the outside world becomes forever unreachable.
objects.title: Bound to the Land

objects.text: Being away from your Anchorpoint is no longer just disempowering, it becomes actively harmful. The moment you leave the area, you begin to experience nausea, dizziness, and pain. These symptoms worsen over time and with distance, eventually leading to permanent damage or death if you stay away too long. Your bond to your Anchorpoint becomes a vital tether—sever it, and you suffer the consequences.
objects.title: Soul Recoil

objects.text:
Scion/Zion is haunted by visions of his own death. For each time this drawback is taken, it half as much time for Zion to initiate Golden Morning until something sets him off (counting from the moment of your arrival). It could be that Jack gets the idea to influence him early, Zion realizes that humans are using the remains of his dead partner to create more Parahumans, or any number of other things. Now you are locked in, and nothing can change Zion. Even if you kill Jack Slash before he sets off Zion, he will still initiate Gold Morning after the correct amount of time has passed.

If taken on an Alternate Earth this instead changes the local doomsday scenario such as The Snap (MCU), The Reapers harvest of the universe(Mass Effect), or Voldemort's return and subsequent fall of Hogwarts(Harry Potter). 

If there's no existential threat present at all, a random one will appear and will act up in about a decade.
objects.title: Apocalypse Now

objects.text: It seems as though your transfer (or your empowerment, if you picked No Transfer) has destabilized your 'position' in space. While this isn't much of an issue on its own, it will cause any attempts to travel to other dimensions or universes to almost always fail catastrophically, at best sending you far away from your intended destination in that world, and at worst sending you to a completely different universe entirely. Thankfully, your initial transfer has anchored you to your chosen world, preventing this from interfering with any attempts to return, should the need arise. This flux will last for about 10 years before stabilizing.
objects.title: Dimensional Flux

objects.text: For each instance this option is taken, the power of all sapient beings will increase by 10%, excluding yourself. Each boost requires a month to take effect. Therefore, if all 10 boosts are taken, it will take 10 months for the full effect to manifest. It's important to note that these boosts are not cumulative, so if you take all 10 boosts, the final increase will be 100% rather than 259.37%. Optionally, you can choose to make the power boost retroactive. This makes it appear as if the characters were always this strong through various methods such as training, rituals, or simply being born stronger. The exact method will change to suit the world and/or character.
objects.title: Power Boost Additive

objects.text: For each instance this option is taken, the power of all sapient beings, excluding yourself, will increase cumulatively by 20%. Each boost requires a month to take effect. Therefore, if all 10 boosts are taken, it will take 10 months for the full effect to manifest, resulting in a total increase of approximately 619.17% (i.e., power multiplied by 1.2<sup>10</sup>≈6.1917) rather than a simple 200% increase. Optionally, you can choose to make the power boost retroactive. This makes it appear as if the characters were always this strong through various methods such as training, rituals, or simply being born stronger. The exact method will change to suit the world and/or character.
objects.title: Power Boost Multiplicative

objects.text: For each instance this option is taken, the power of all sapient beings, excluding yourself, will increase exponentially by 30%. Each boost requires a month to take effect. Therefore, if all 10 boosts are taken, it will take 10 months for the full effect to manifest, resulting in a total increase of approximately 2008% (i.e., power multiplied by e<sup>3</sup>≈20.09) rather than a simple 300% increase. Optionally, you can choose to make the power boost retroactive. This makes it appear as if the characters were always this strong through various methods such as training, rituals, or simply being born stronger. The exact method will change to suit the world and/or character.
objects.title: Power Boost Exponential

objects.text: Instead of it being retroactive or taking months for the full effect to manifest, the boost happens instantly when you appear in the world, quite possibly plunging the world into total chaos.
objects.title: Instant Boost

objects.text:
For each instance this option is taken the duration for each Power Boost to take affect is increased. Selecting it once will result in each Boost taking 3 months to take full effect. 6 months if selected twice and a whole year if taken 3 times. 

Therefor, if all 10 Boosts are taken the time it would take for all of them to take affect would be 30/60/120 months which equals 2.5/5/10 years respectivly.
objects.title: Delayed Power Boost

objects.text:
Whatever friends you make will turn on you, or die, or maybe they weren't your friends, to begin with. 
In the end, you are alone.
objects.title: Lonely

objects.text:
Choose any character, it could be one of your companions, a canon character from the world you are heading to, your significant other, or even someone random. You both now suffer from extreme separation anxiety. Being in different rooms will already feel deeply uncomfortable, but when you are separated for more than a few hours, the anxiety and depression will be so overwhelming that you will not be able to function unless with the purpose of reuniting with each other.

It is up to you how exactly you first meet this character; either you already have history with them, or you are going to meet them soon, but it cannot take more than a few days for the drawback to take effect.
objects.title: Separation Anxiety

objects.text: "You two were already inseparable. But it wasn't enough was it? Now not even death can separate you." You are now officially bonded with the character you have chosen. Hooray! Unfortunately you get the negative side of it. All damage done to you and your partner will be dealt equally to both of you, whether it be conceptual erasure, magical fire that burns the soul, or plain old bullets, you will take the exact damage. This is not damage transfer or damage sharing, meaning you will take the full blunt of the damage they took and vice versa. Additionally, you will also feel the exhaustion, hunger and even boredom of your partner, but to a way lesser degree to help you differentiate between what you are feeling, and what they are feeling. However there is one exception to this. The damage and recoil from your powers are not shared, for example whatever dark magic you are using will not corrupt your partner thanks to this drawback.
objects.title: Life Linked

objects.text: For each selection, you gain one stalker. These people suffer from the Obsession insanity drawback, directed towards yourself, and they will go to great lengths to get your attention and affection. You may choose which character this will apply to or let it be someone random. If you have Persistent Suitor, you can choose how many also fall under this drawback. While not necessarily stronger than you, they nevertheless possess abilities which allow them to act on their obsession and make dealing with them really difficult. They may have a natural talent for stealth and espionage or have a power like invisibility or teleporting.
objects.title: Stalker

objects.text:
Your stalker not only wants your attention and affection, they wish to spend the rest of their life as your spouse. Whether or not you're interested does not really factor into the equation.

At first, your suitor will open with mundane methods to get your attention, love letters, serenades under your window, marriage proposals in public, and so on. If you rebuke them enough times, they will start to take a more forceful approach, starting with legal but ethically dubious means like an arranged marriage and escalating up to abduction.

If they resort to kidnapping, your stalker will have means to keep you contained. This could range from simple handcuffs to tinker-tech or powers that can counter your own abilities. The harder you try to escape, the shorter your leash will be. 

Thankfully for you, this stalker is quite gentle and caring; even if you get kidnapped and trapped they will treat you with love and respect and won't attempt to force themselves on you.
objects.title: Persistent Suitor

objects.text: You attract unstable people of the gender you are attracted to. It's very easy for you to become a target of a yandere, be invited to a party of a goth girl only to realize she plans to sacrifice you to the dark powers, or get hit on by a best guy you ever met, but then get acquainted with his other 9 personalities.
objects.title: I Will Fix Her

addons.text:
You don't just fall for red flags—you nurture them, feeding into their instability with care and devotion until they blossom into full-blown disasters. What might have been minor flaws in someone else slowly grow into consuming storms whilst in your orbit, magnifying their worst impulses. The more you give of yourself, the more they unravel, becoming clingier, crueler, and more erratic in the process, until they finally collapse.

And the deeper they spiral, the tighter you hold on. Every outburst, every breakdown feels like proof they need you more, dragging you from affection into obsession. At some point, you stop loving them despite the damage—you start loving them because of it.
addons.title: They Can Ruin Me

objects.text:
You find yourself involuntarily, inexplicably, and irreversibly drawn to red flags, as if the warning signs of these toxic traits and unstable behavior in those you're attracted to only seem to embolden your desire to pursue them.

The more broken, volatile, or dangerous they are, the harder you fall for them, no matter how problematic it'd be to do so, instinctively rationalizing their actions and convincing yourself they're not as bad as they seem. Just try not to lose yourself entirely chasing after those who might break you far more than they ever love you.
objects.title: Red Flag Lover

objects.text: You are much more likely to encounter villains in your new life, either as a victim or as a target of recruitment.
objects.title: Villain Target

objects.text: Three other people arrive on Earth Bet with a build of their choice, except that they arrive at a time before you, coming at different points of time, and have a build of similar strength compared to you.
objects.title: Late to The Party

objects.text: Three other people arrive on Earth Bet with a build of their choice at the same time as you and have a build of similar strength to you.
objects.title: Party's Just Getting Started

objects.text: Three other people arrive on Earth Bet with a build of their choice, except that they arrive at a time after you, don't arrive at the same time as each other, and have a build of similar strength to you.
objects.title: This Party's About to Get Crazy

objects.text: For each selection, one more individual is added to the roster of <u>Late to the Party</u>, <u>Party's Just Getting Started</u>, or <u>This Party's About to get Crazy</u>. You can freely choose how the number of individuals is split between the choices but they otherwise follow the rules of their respective choices.
objects.title: This Party is Super Crowded!

objects.text:
Your fellow inserts into Earth Bet do not know Worm, the story of Taylor Hebert. No, they know Worm, the story of you self-inserting into this fictional world. It's a very popular series with a lot of fanfiction and a very large number of haters to rival the amount of fans it has.

Because of this, all other inserts know about you. They know about your powers, your personality, your abilities, and what you would have done once you got inserted—to varying degrees. Some only know sparse bits or a lot of fanon, while others have actually read the original and know everything. Their disposition towards you varies between disliking you as a character, wanting to "save" or "help" you, or fangirling over you and going out of their way to make sure they're with you as much as possible to live out their dream fantasy.

If you do not go to Earth Bet, then the story will change to whatever world you go to instead.
objects.title: I'M YOUR BIGGEST FAN

objects.text: Instead of there only being one you to worry about, there’s a few. For every purchase of this drawback, 3-5 clones of you will be made either at the same time as your entry or shortly afterwards, being at most a year after your arrival. Of these clones, at least 1/3 are guaranteed to be hostile and inimical to you, with the rest falling anywhere along the spectrum of their opinion. Their aims are not certain to be contradictory to yours, but they will definitely have aims and goals of their own. Most notably, these clones will have variants of your Perks and powers, these can be as small as cosmetic differences and as great as completely different expressions of the same underlying power. For instance, if you have Blank all of the clones would have Blank, but if you had a Breaker power, they might instead have a Changer or Striker variant of the power. If you have a shard, as your clones possess the same DNA as you, you’ll experience greater power drain, as it has to share energy between each of the clones’ abilities. If you’re Shardless this is far more variable, but they will always be equivalent to you in strength and utility. These clones are full people with a full internal experience, and can be reasoned with, though it’s likely to be difficult depending on your circumstances. In addition the circumstances of their creation are variable, they could all be batch made clones, parallel versions of you, or yet more stranger methods of creating duplicates, but they will always be at the very least reflections of you.
objects.title: Clone Conspiracy

objects.text: Instead of arriving discreetly in your new world, or assuming an extant identity, you are intentionally summoned in a magical (or technological) ritual. Your summoner doesn't actually have a way to control you with the ritual, but they will know that you're an outsider. For Drop-Ins this is straightforward, but for Reincarnations or Character Inserts, the ritual puts you in the person's body.
objects.title: The Summoning

objects.text: Your summoning is not some simple action, no mere chalk pentagram scribbled on the floor or flick of a switch on a simple machine. Instead it is a gruesome ceremony involving a human sacrifice, whether it requires runes drawn in heartblood or a person being locked in a molecular disassembler to provide the raw material to construct the summon's form. How do you know this? Because you initially awaken not as the summoned being, but the sacrifice, forced to endure the ritual but helpless to prevent anything, before reawakening inside the result of the summoning. You're starting your adventure with the traumatic experience of having undergone a ritual murder, so have fun with that. It will only be after the summoning that you gain your Skills, Powers, and Objects of Power, so they cannot help you. If you have selected Eventful Day, Bad Day, or Worst Day, the ritual becomes more elaborate, taking longer and becoming more gruesome. Optionally, you may choose to awaken before you are tied to the altar, metaphorically or literally, and can launch a desperate if ultimately futile attempt to escape your fate to mitigate the ritual's severity. If you have selected Extremely Obvious Summoning, expect most people to treat you with horror and disgust, as they know how you came to be.
objects.title: Sacrificial Summoning

objects.text: Instead of being summoned by a person messing around with incantations, by accident, or by a small secret select few, you are instead summoned by a person that is livestreaming (or some other suitably public event, like inside a sold-out colosseum), and your summoning will be very public, with almost everyone knowing you are not from Earth Bet, or any other currently known Earth!
objects.title: Extremely Obvious Summoning

objects.text: With this, the ritual used to summon you will also compel you to obey your summoner for a year and a day, or until you have completed a task they defined when you were summoned. You can only resist commands that are deeply heinous to you, and the summoner will have commands for you before letting you leave the circle.
objects.title: The Binding

addons.text:
Right, it looks like your big entrance is no longer a one-and-done thing, as now, when you overindulge in your vices of drugs and/or alcohol, you have a chance to blackout and wake up later from a wild bender with no recollection of your recent misadventures. While these may not be as big as your debut, they will have an impact on your life and those around you, these events will be a mixed bag at best, with the fallout being a source of stress that will push you to use your addictions to cope, thus perpetuating the cycle. Naturally, Lightweight makes this exponentially worse.

Your debut will not reveal your addiction(s) to others, but these later blackouts can, along with giving them more information they can use regarding yourself and those around you.

Note: We are not responsible for your actions; don't cry foul because you married an Endbringer in a reverse shotgun wedding during a bender.
addons.title: Hangover Sequel. Not Again!

objects.text:
Welp; you've barely even started, and you're already the talk of the town. This goes beyond people merely knowing you're not from Earth Bet, as they have seen what you can do, whether it's due to some memory loss, being inebriated, or some form of sleepwalking, the people of the world have seen what you are capable of and have taken note. Whether it's due to heroically fighting a multiversal threat or showing off for the fun of it is up to you.

While this does not mean they have full depth and knowledge of your powers, they do have some idea of scale and basic information about what you can do, giving other parties some clue on how to act and move around you. But this goes a bit further; as the reach of said knowledge scales with your power (SP) in such a way, it's possible for the entire multiverse to become aware of you, pushing others to change plans, form new alliances, and perhaps reshape whole cultures on a foundational level.

It is also possible for other Powers, Perks, and Drawbacks to have interactions with this drawback, such as "A Pencil. A Fucking Pencil!" amplifying the reactions others will have, and Spiral Power seeding countless worlds with life as it aids in the development of other species.
objects.title: Why am I in the News?!

addons.text:
For Shardless powers, this drawback manifests in the form of an Awakening. Unlike a Trigger Event, an Awakening does not necessarily require a traumatic event. They can happen in moments of great need or in situations that would fit the mythos of an origin story.

(Note: You cannot force an awakening by manufacturing those situations but being genre savvy and taking advantage of situations is allowed.)
addons.title: Awakening (Shardless)

addons.text:
For Patron powers this drawback manifests slightly differently. You do not need a traumatic event as with a Shard or something fitting an origin story as with Shardless. You need only be desperate <small>(or stupid)</small> enough to take the first hand that reaches out without reading the fine print. 

(Note: You cannot force a pact by manufacturing those situations but being genre savvy and taking advantage of situations is allowed.)
addons.title: A Pact Formed

objects.text:
You have yet to trigger with your powers. To trigger you will need to get deeply traumatized. There is a possibility you will trigger from finding out you fell through a portal in your sleep into Earth Bet and that if you don't fix things, the whole multiverse, including your own Earth, will be destroyed, or at least heavily damaged. If you chose Shardless then you can Trigger with a Warrior Shard, but it'll be a random power, likely weaker than most of those listed, and you're guaranteed some Shard Influence.
If you chose Character-Insert, you still keep whatever power they already had before you remembered your current life. Your Trigger Event for your chosen powers won't Second Trigger your Character-Insert power unless it is similar to the original Trigger Event of the person you were reborn as.
objects.title: Corona Pollentia

objects.text:
Only part of your powers are available when you gain them. At first, you will only have at most 50% of your total SP worth of powers available.

Once you undergo a traumatizing event, either the first time or as a true second trigger, the remainder of your powers will unlock.
objects.title: Second Trigger

objects.text:
For your trigger event(s), you no longer need just a generic traumatic event; you need a traumatizing event with some relation to your powers.

What this means exactly can vary. It can be simple and obvious, like needing to nearly drown to unlock many water abilities. Or it can be more like traditional shard triggers, with more physical traumas granting Brute, Striker, or Blaster powers, or more psychological and abstract ones giving things like Thinker, Tinker, or Master powers.

Additionally, the wider the array of powers to be unlocked, the less direct the connection between the trauma and the powers will be. To trigger healing powers, you might just need to have someone you care deeply about be gravely injured. To trigger a wide selection that includes abilities similar to those of many famous heroes, it might be a painful realization about your worthiness among such heroes.
objects.title: Specific Trigger

addons.text:
Now, each needed trigger event is specific to each power. This even includes package selections like Glory Girl as multiple separate powers. This is waived if the seeming outward facing abilities are all resultant of one cohesive power, like in the case of Alexandria’s stasis.

Furthermore, upgrades would need to meet the standard requirements for a second trigger, needing to be similar to the event that triggered the original power. For an upgrade to something like Skitter, you would need to experience a further traumatic event where you feel trapped and/or unclean.

Fusions are even more difficult, requiring combinations of events. If the trigger event for one power was fire, and the trigger for another was being assaulted, the trigger for the fusion might require you to be violently shoved into a furnace.
addons.title: Individualized Triggers

objects.text: Now, instead of triggering a collection of powers with one or two traumatic events, you must unlock each of your powers, upgrades and fusions individually. Thankfully for your sanity, the threshold of trauma needed for a trigger event is slightly reduced, being somewhere between a typical trigger and that experienced by a second generation cape. If you have Awakening (Shardless) then each Awakening Event after the first wouldn’t have to be comparable to an origin story, instead would be a “defining character moment” like the loss of a mentor figure, or facing a nemesis for the first time. If you have A Pact Formed it would instead be slowly making more and more deals with your patron, increasing your debt.
objects.title: Trigger Happy

objects.text: Any of your powers that are not regularly used will degrade over time. If you do not use the active component(s) (ex: flying, shooting lasers, casting spells, building tinker-tech, etc.) of a power for more than 3 day, its strength will degrade at a rate of 10% until it reaches 30% of its original strength after 7 days (same rules as Acclimation); for powers that allow you to permanently hold other powers, such as Manager or Prototype, the sub-powers degrade individually instead of the parent. Powers that have no active component are not affected. This weakening can be reversed through active use of the power. The time it takes to revert to full strength depends on the state of degradation and how strong the power was at its prime, a weak power worth 3 SP at 90% strength would only take a few minutes to recover, while one worth 120 SP at 30% strength would take upwards of days.
objects.title: Dirty Kitchen Sink

objects.text: Your powers start 50% weaker and grow over time to 200% of their base power. Normally they will grow to 100% in 6 months and 200% in 12 months. The more you use your powers creatively the faster they will grow. In the context of powers with multiple numerical values (i.e. number of charges and strength of charges), the product of all the values doubles. This means either one parameter doubles, two parameters increase by 1.4, three by 1.25, etc. (the n-th root of 2 for n parameters). For frequencies, they are multiplied by the inverse. (2x becomes 1/2, and so on). You can choose which parameters are affected. This drawback progresses in "real" time, this means time as experienced in the same reference frame as everyone else in the solar system. Anomalies like localized temporal distortions, pocket dimensions, and the likes do not affect the growth in either direction. In summary: this drawback cannot be cheesed with time travel of any kind. Temporal rewind effects like (Thinker) Time Loop and Return by Death from Re:Zero reset your growth to where it was at the last checkpoint. True time travel, where you physically move from one point in space-time to another, does not change your progress.
objects.title: Acclimation

objects.text: The time necessary for Acclimation to grow from 50% to 100% increases to 12 months and the time from 100% to 200% to 24 months. The more you use your powers creatively the faster they will grow.
objects.title: Jet Lag

objects.text: The time necessary for Acclimation to grow from 50% to 100% increases to 4 years (48 months) and the time from 100% to 200% to 8 years (96 months). The more you use your powers creatively the faster they will grow but each stage will last at least 12 months.
objects.title: Snail's Pace

objects.text: The time necessary for Acclimation to grow from 50% to 100% increases to 8 years and the time from 100% to 200% to 16 years. The more you use your powers creatively the faster they will grow but each stage will last at least 2 years
objects.title: Snails Are Quicker Than You

addons.text:
Your acclimation growth is no longer almost entirely passive. Without training, your powers will only grow to around 75% of their potential upon entering puberty. Further reaching up to 125% at full physical maturity without training or use. With training, they can be brought up to the normal values. This also makes outside effects on your physical age less effective.

On the plus side, being de-aged will no longer remove any benefits of your training. Likewise, having your age accelerated will not give you the benefits of actually training your powers.
addons.title: Buried Potential

objects.text:
Instead of time, Acclimation is now linked with your physical maturity, and training is less effective at growing it. You'll reach 100% at the beginning of puberty- around 12-15 years old give or take a couple years for a baseline human- and reach 200% at full physical maturity. Around 22-25 years old for a baseline human. 

If you're a race that grows slower or faster, the time it'll take you to acclimate will change, staying linked with your physical maturity. If, for whatever reason, you are physically de-aged or have your aging accelerated, your acclimation percentage will change with your body. If you are de-aged into a newborn, your percentage will be as low as it can get.
objects.title: Growing Up

objects.text: Acclimation is modified to make your powers start at 25% instead of 50%. This does not affect the time necessary to grow.
objects.title: Quarter Pounder

objects.text: Acclimation is modified to make your powers start at 0% instead of 50%. This does not affect the time necessary to grow.
objects.title: Starting From Nothing

objects.text: Acclimation no longer grows past 100% strength.
objects.title: No more, No less

objects.text: Acclimation cannot be made quicker through training.
objects.title: Not faster, Not slower

objects.text: Your powers no longer grow passively over time, the only way for you to regain the rest of your power is through training, creative power usage and live combat. If you took choices such as Jet Lag, Snail's Pace, or Snails Are Quicker Than You, then the effectiveness of your training drops, requiring more effort and time to reach 100% or 200%. In the case of Snail's Pace and Snails Are Quicker Than You, your rate of growth is also unable to exceed their minimum time. If you took Start From Nothing, then you start with the barest minimum instead of 0%, just so that you can start training.
objects.title: Train As Hard As You Can

objects.text: Instead of all your powers being reduced to 50%, you can choose the level at which each of your powers is affected (in increments of 5%) as long as the final value averages to 50% or lower. Powers cannot be increased above 95% or reduced below 5% and they keep their relative strength until they reach the maximum of 200%. In this context, all the members of an upgrade chain, or a cluster created by Power Tweak or Arbitrary Limitations can be treated as one singular power. (If you have Quarter Pounder or No More, No Less, the values adjust accordingly.)
objects.title: Mixer (Acclimation)

objects.text: You can exclude one power per purchase from the effects of Acclimation. In this context, all the members of an upgrade chain, or a cluster created by Power Tweak or Arbitrary Limitations can be treated as one singular power. You can't exclude all of your powers from Acclimation unless the total cost of this choice is equal or greater to the gain from Acclimation and all of its upgrades, even if you have fewer powers.
objects.title: Exclusion (Acclimation)

objects.text:
Your powers need some time to fully manifest and reach the Acclimation floor. This can take between a few hours if you have a few weak powers to a few days if you have several strong powers. Powers manifest in order of usefulness and stressful or dangerous situation can increase the rate at which they appear.

(Powers with multiple sub-powers, like Dynamist, manifest progressively.)
objects.title: Hard Reboot

objects.text:
Not all your powers will just start unlocking automatically. Some of them will instead now only unlock once you've met a specific condition to unlock it, at which point it will start progressing through its own growth-period lasting the regular Acclimation's 18 months, or however long it would normally take if you've taken time-extending drawbacks. Any power not Quest-Locked will develop normally.

The unlock-condition will fit the respective power, for example solving a mystery or logic-puzzle to unlock a Thinker-Power, building something by yourself to unlock a Tinker-Power, or fighting a specific enemy. More expensive powers will have either harder or multiple Unlock-Conditions. You will always know exactly how to unlock each power.

If chosen once, Powers worth 10% of the total points spent on Powers will be Quest-Locked, you can choose which. Select it twice and it will be 20%, three times for 30% etc. If taken ten times all your powers will start of Quest-Locked.
objects.title: Quest-Lock

objects.text:
Now your powers grow and develop one at a time over your Acclimation period, proportional to their SP cost to how much you've totally spent on all your powers. If you bought 100SP worth of powers, then a 10SP power would take one-tenth the acclimation period to develop.

You are now forced to take the entire length of your acclimation to grow into your abilities and in the same order as their requirements; no level of creativity will shorten the duration. Multitasking abilities can't allow you to train more than one purchased power at a time but may be used to work on abilities contained within a power.
objects.title: Can't You Walk and Talk at the Same Time?

objects.text:
Now, like powers, your OoPs also suffer and benefit from Acclimation and its crawl from 50% to 200% of their base power. Notably, the benefit gained by training with your powers also applies to quickening the development of OoPs unless you have Not faster, Not slower.

Any modifiers to Acclimation such as Snails Pace, Quest-Lock, or Train As Hard As You Can also affect your OoPs.
objects.title: Acclimated

objects.text:
Instead of growing over the course of a year, your powers will instead remain at a base of 50%. Whenever you use your powers they will begin to grow in strength, with every minute of continuous use being equal to a month of standard growth with Acclimation. If you stop using a power, it will begin to return back to 50%, at a rate of a month of growth per ten seconds. This does not effect passive powers, which instead follow Acclimation's normal growth pattern.

Acclimation's normal boosts associated with training are instead used to increase the rate at which this growth applies, with 6 months worth of hard training being enough to increase the speed of growth by 100% linearly.

If you choose any of Acclimation's upgrades they will effect this drawckback, such as Jet Lag increasing the time it takes for your powers to reach their peak, or No More, No Less preventing you from going beyond 100% power.
objects.title: Slow Start

objects.text: Your powers are not just diminished, they’re partially bound as well. Until these bindings are removed you cannot begin to grow your powers in strength, keeping them locked at the level Acclimation previously placed them at. The bindings can take any kind of form, whether it be multi-layered arcane seals or quantum-locked power-interfering tinkertech shackles, but regardless of what form they physically take they are currently beyond your ability to remove. Make no mistake, it is possible to remove these bindings however doing so will be a task of immense effort and time. If you are subject to arcane seals perhaps you’ll need to decipher the eldritch workings of each seal and undo them one-by-one, or if they take the form of literal power-suppressing shackles quantum-locked to you then they might be subject to a form of All-or-Nothing stasis, rendering them completely unbreakable and only able to be released by high-level space-time manipulation and careful precision. And you can’t cheese this either, as the specifics and difficulty of the task needed to remove the seal corresponds to your own powers and what you have available. If you are a genius at magic and have magical seals, expect them to be so complex and alien that even you with all your potential and understanding are unable to solve them without immense trouble.
objects.title: Shackled

objects.text:
You or your Shard have placed limitations on all of your powers. When restrictions are imposed on some aspects, others can be improved to compensate. These changes either apply to individual powers, or merge multiple powers to work together as a single whole, or a combination of both. The restrictions can be extended to some or all of your perks and objects of power.

For example, your powers can only be used through minions, only one set can be used at a time (powers are grouped thematically), you have to build Tinker devices to produce those powers (if you have a Tinker power for example), etc.

If the restrictions for a group of powers are centered around one power, like a minion Master power or Tinker ability, this ability gets a major boost.
objects.title: Arbitrary Limitations (All Powers)

objects.text:
You or your Shard have placed limitations on one of your powers, perks, or objects. When restrictions are imposed on some aspects, others can be improved to compensate. This drawback affects one power per selection, up to 10.

For example, the power can only be used under certain circumstances but the effect is increased, the range is reduced in exchange for potency, the number of choices is limited but they can be improved over time, etc.
objects.title: Arbitrary Limitations (One Power)

objects.text: Powers that would give starting items and/or companions no longer do so. For example; Witchcraft & Wizardry (Harry Potter) will no longer include a wand, and House of the Dragon (ASOIAF) will no longer provide a weapon and dragon. You may choose to exclude certain powers from this so long as the total cost of affected powers is equal to the number of points gained from this drawback.
objects.title: Starterless

objects.text: Powers that give knowledge and experience no longer do so. Instead, knowledge and experience is replaced with a knack and instinct for said subjects. For example; Witchcraft & Wizardry (Harry Potter) will no longer provide Hogwarts graduate knowledge, instead making one a decent savant at the covered subjects, and Caveman Wisdom will give an instinctive talent for creating primitive tools and shelters instead of knowledge on how to do so. You may choose to exclude certain powers from this so long as the total cost of affected powers is equal to the number of points gained from this drawback.
objects.title: Knowledgeless

objects.text:
The overall power of all of your abilities is capped at a certain level, dependent on the strength of the most powerful individuals based in the area you operate in, excluding any outliers.

If you limit yourself to only a certain region or country, your power will scale with the strongest person in the area, while if you expand your area of operations to an entire planet or solar system or more (provided you are actually capable of doing so), then the power-scaling's range will increase accordingly. 

This scaling has a lower bound as well, so you will not become entirely powerless if you spend time in a small village. At minimum, this drawback covers an area that includes at least one major population center. What this means depends on the setting; on Earth Bet, for example, it would be a city with at least 100'000 inhabitants, while in Skyrim it would be one of the hold capitals, like Whiterun or Solitude. It takes a few days to weeks for the scaling to update.

Outliers are individuals that are very far ahead of the rest of the pack in terms of strength; on Earth Bet, for example, Scion would be considered an outlier if you were to operate at the planetary level. This group would generally include gods and celestial beings.
objects.title: Power Cap

objects.text:
Now, the overall power for all of your abilities depends on the strength of your current enemies: for example, if your opponent only has city-destroying levels of power at most, then you will be limited to city-destroying levels as well, regardless of how strong you actually are. Outliers are included for the purpose of this scaling.

It is only when you are fighting an enemy with equal or greater levels of power that you can unleash your full strength. When out of combat, you will default to the scaling of <u>Power Cap</u>.
objects.title: Adaptive Difficulty

objects.text:
With this, you can now prolong the duration of any time-limited drawback or applicable effect of your choice, extending them by an additional five years.

If desired, you may continue to stack this extension on the same drawback each time you take this or apply it to a different eligible drawback instead.
objects.title: Prolong the Pain

objects.text:
One of your powers can never be deactivated, neither by the power's in-built mechanisms nor by outside sources or your other abilities. If you have laser eyes, they will be constantly active. If you have an invisibility power, you will forever remain unseen.

While the power can never be fully deactivated, you can still control the intensity if you were able to in the first place. Instead of laser eyes constantly disintegrating everything in your field of vision, they may now be merely a harmless source of light. This, however, does not affect all-or-nothing aspects of the power.
objects.title: Constant Activation

objects.text:
One of your powers or OoPs has a required maintenance and upkeep to remain functional. 

This does also mean that the specific maintenance will change in order to fit the power it’s applied to. An implant that generates chi for instance would likely need to be maintained by mechanical means while a purely mental ability could make do with meditation. Whatever the cause, you’re at the whim of this maintenance to make proper use of this ability.

Should you fail to perform this maintenance you will lose access to the power, and depending on the power itself it may even become a hindrance, such as a robotic leg breaking down. It will require extensive maintenance to bring it back into proper operation again. For instance, what would usually be a ten minute meditation would require an hour long ritual to return should it break down.
objects.title: Maintenance (One Power)

objects.text:
Your powers or OoPs have a required maintenance and upkeep to remain functional. 

This does also mean that the specific maintenance will change in order to fit the power it’s applied to. An implant that generates chi for instance would likely need to be maintained by mechanical means while a purely mental ability could make do with meditation. Whatever the cause, you’re at the whim of this maintenance to make proper use of this ability.

Should you fail to perform this maintenance you will lose access to the power, and depending on the power itself it may even become a hindrance, such as a robotic leg breaking down. It will require extensive maintenance to bring it back into proper operation again. For instance, what would usually be a ten minute meditation would require an hour long ritual to return should it break down.

Each of your powers can require different maintenance if they come from a different source.
objects.title: Maintenance (All Powers)

objects.text:
Using one of your powers or OoPs is addictive, necessitating its constant or repeated use. The effects of this addiction can vary, whether it’s esoteric in nature or simply an endorphin rush. 

When going for moderate to long periods without using an addictive power you begin to suffer withdrawals, which can range from typical drug-like withdrawal symptoms to more esoteric consequences depending on the nature of the power.

If multiple of your powers are addictive, you may choose whether they are both individually addictive to use or whether they both contribute to the same addiction. However, the more powers contribute to a single addiction the more they will have to be used to compensate.
objects.title: Addictive Power (One Power)

objects.text:
Using your powers or OoPs is addictive, necessitating their constant or repeated use. The effects of this addiction can vary, whether it’s esoteric in nature or simply an endorphin rush. 

When going for moderate to long periods without using your powers you begin to suffer withdrawals, which can range from typical drug-like withdrawal symptoms to more esoteric consequences depending on the nature of the power.

You may choose whether your powers or OoPs are individually addictive to use or whether they both contribute to the same addiction. However, the more powers contribute to a single addiction the more they will have to be used to compensate.
objects.title: Addictive Power (All Powers)

objects.text: Maybe they were just having a bad day and you were a convenient target for their frustrations, or maybe you accidentally spoiled the ending of a TV series for them. Whatever the case, sometime after your insertion, a usually kind-natured, skilled, and powerful hero will become incredibly pissed off at you and do their best to beat you to a pulp. This doesn’t permanently affect their mood; if you manage to escape and lay low for a few months, they should return to a normal emotional state and not want to beat you into hamburger. If you are a villain or just have a poor relationship with the law, they just might hate you forever.
objects.title: Get back here Shocker! SHOCKER!!! You can’t escape me! I’ll chase you to the ends of the EARTH!!!

objects.text: Events will conspire to ensure that every embarrassing moment you ever have in public will be remembered in some fashion. The more embarrassing it is to you, the better recorded it will be. Stutter when talking to someone you like? That stutter will always be what the people involved will remember first about you; get hit in the face by a flying stop sign during a cape fight? The GIF of that will become an instant meme, guaranteed.
objects.title: Memetic

addons.text: Good News! You finally had music that fit the situation! What a time to be alive! Bad News…The music fits a little too well, and TL;DR, you have long term trauma… What a time to be alive… While your survival is guaranteed, you will also be bound to unintentionally encounter the object of your fear once, no matter how improbable it may be, within a year. This will come at a time when you will be the least prepared. Already, that’s pretty bad, but your Drawback will play a piece of music that not only perfectly fits the situation, but will additionally amplify the terror of the encounter twofold. You will figuratively (and maybe literally) walk out of this encounter with this music playing in your nightmares. A small silver lining to this is that you no longer fear the thing you originally were afraid of, and you are perfectly fine being around it. But now, you fear the music more than you ever feared the object. You will have small flashbacks to that dreadful encounter whenever you hear the music or have panic attacks. To supplement this, you will hear at least an obvious leitmotif or the music outright once every 1-2 months.
addons.title: Post Boss-Music Stress Disorder

objects.text: Good News! You now have a soundtrack for whenever you enter combat of any kind! Bad News… the music will rarely fit the situation the ‘combat’ revolves around. A small debate that you and those hearing it will forget within the day could have this Drawback to making an epic orchestral piece that sounds like the argument decides the fate of the world. A genuine battle to the death could have a lullaby that threatens to take you out of the mood even to continue fighting.
