Furthermore, whatever music is being played will attempt to get on your nerves with varying degrees of success, from a couple of moments of losing focus throughout the battle, all the way to figuratively driving you mad mid-fight.
objects.title: Why Do I (Not) Hear Boss Music?

objects.text:
When taken you will suffer Gordon Ramsay’s worst nightmare. With this drawback, the flavors of food and drinks randomly change to something you dislike, regardless of how they are prepared or appear. 

For instance, a bite of chocolate ice cream might suddenly taste like a mint strawberry swirl or a juicy steak might have the flavor of cricket meat. Even a simple glass of water could unexpectedly taste like cough syrup. These flavor changes are completely random and occur at any time, but are always palatable enough to ensure you won't starve. However, they will consistently be flavors that you find unpleasant. 

The changes are random but you are guaranteed to suffer at least one fiasco a day at least. This doesn’t make any changes to the food and will not affect the food in any way besides how it tastes.
objects.title: Flavor Fiasco

objects.text: Beware, for the IRS is on your tail! They will ruthlessly attempt to audit you and your funds. And remember, this is the organization that brought down Al Capone, and which even the Joker would dare not cross. If you fail to be 100% squeaky clean for the 3 years the IRS will continually test and try you for, you will be thrown in jail and be unable to get out of jail regardless of powers. This isn’t saying your powers are gone, they just can’t be used to escape the property line of the prison.
objects.title: The IRS

objects.text:
Your arrival into the world is heralded by a strange omen, something unnatural. It may take the form of a total eclipse that lasts far too long or appeared with no warning, an eerie blood rain that falls for mere minutes and then vanishes without a trace, or perhaps an ocean momentarily turning black under the noonday sun. Whatever the phenomenon, it defies all natural laws and occurs with such dramatic effect that it becomes an instant, undeniable part of public consciousness.

Initially, the omen is seen as an unexplained mystery. Only a few fringe voices suspect any connection to you. But as time passes, more people begin to draw the link, eventually believing that you are the cause. Given the ominous nature of the event, this association often stirs fear and suspicion in those who believe it. Depending on the state of the world you are in, getting attacked by a mob is possible.

As the connection strengthens in the public mind, many begin to see you as a harbinger of evil. Individuals and organizations may rise against you, seeking to destroy what they believe to be a great threat. These enemies are not inherently malicious, they are sincere in their belief that they are protecting the world from a force of darkness.

Additionally, forces of true evil may see you as either a useful pawn or a threat to their power. Some will attempt to manipulate or exploit you for their own ends, while others may frame you as a scapegoat to divert attention from themselves. If they view you as too dangerous to control, they will not hesitate to send agents to eliminate you.
objects.title: Great Omen

objects.text:
The strongest, the one with the skills and abilities to consistently surpass their contemporaries, the one burdened with starting and ending the biggest of fights, the overwhelming might that leaves behind a legacy that is revered, envied, or feared. This is a legacy you will never possess, for you will never be the strongest.

Whether through a stroke of fate or divine intervention, in whichever universe you find yourself, there will always be someone stronger than you, surpassing you in every capacity. Worse yet, surpassing this individual will be impossible for you; every improvement you make, they will improve twofold. Even if you were to conquer this mountain, another individual would quickly rise to take the mantle of the strongest, forever preventing you from being the strongest. This also affects public perception, as others will always know that there is someone stronger than you, making propaganda or manipulation futile.

This individual will not have a predetermined disposition towards you unless you initiate it. Their disposition will also be random—they could be a hero, an antihero, a villain, or anything in between.
objects.title: The Strongest

addons.text:
If you have Countdown Malefices will no longer override your choices. Your mental list now also details each Malefice you will get in the future and keeps a record of the ones you have overcomed.

If you have Unspent then half of the points—rounded down—a Malefice would've given you will count for it.
addons.title: Small Mercies

addons.text:
You now have the power to confront your Drawbacks and eliminate them forever. With enough effort, patience, and determination, even the most deeply ingrained drawbacks can be overcome. While minor drawbacks might take months to resolve, the most powerful ones could require years—or even decades—but the reward is undeniably worth the struggle.

To accelerate your progress, you must actively work against the nature of your drawbacks. Keeping a detailed record of your thoughts, emotions, memories and experiences will help you better understand and mitigate mental drawbacks. Practicing self-awareness and learning to control impulsive actions will help you overcome emotional drawbacks. Immersing yourself in meaningful experiences that challenge your drawbacks can also drastically hasten it's elemination.

This journey will not be easy. It will test your resilience, determination, and patience. But through the ocean of pain and suffering, you will eventually reach your dawn—a moment of true freedom and peace. In this light, you will find loving and accepting parents who were always waiting for your return, ready to welcome you into their hugs with warmth and unwavering support. This is the ultimate reward for your courage to face and conquer your Drawbacks.
addons.title: Pushing Through The Pain

objects.text: "Are you sure whatever you are doing is worth it?" They say time heal all wounds, but it seems like time will just hurt you. Over the course of 25 years you will slowly gain all Drawbacks in the form of Malefices, with the exception of those that alter the world in any way and those you already have. Malefices are weakened variations of a drawback, not only that but Malefices aren't absolute and can be overcome—so drawbacks that erase memories would for example only seal them away temporarily, and allow you to recover them through means similar to a fictional amnesia. If you overcome a Malefice you will have a small reprieve before needing to deal with it again. The worse a Malefice is the further you must be in your journey to start getting it. If any Malefices you receive are incompatible with a choice you took the Malefice will still apply—how this happens changes from choice to choice, Orphaned for example might affect your first parental figures if you are a Drop-in or Orphan. Your perks are the exception, incompatible ones will just override the Malefice. Multiselect Drawbacks and Drawbacks that offer some sort of choice like Unconscious Geas or Arbitrary Limitations will have their effects decided randomly every time you gain their Malefice. You also gain a mental list detailing the names of each Malefice you acquired and their effects—Malefices might or might not share a name with their Drawback counterpart, depends on their new effect.
objects.title: Safety Can't Last Forever

addons.text:
Whether or not this build is made for Taylor Hebert or someone character-inserting as her, to be Taylor Hebert truly means to suffer.  
  
Originally, Malefices couldn't override incompatible Perks; that is still true, but it no longer matters because over time your Perks will weaken in strength and potency, eventually disappearing entirely and then getting replaced by a brand new malefice. But it doesn't stop there; you receive Malefices at a faster pace, they grow at a faster rate, and the side harms themselves will also grow in potency until they make side harms of their own. Like Dynamist Jr. but for Malefices!
addons.title: Being Taylor Hebert is Suffering

objects.text:
You just can't stop can you? Is your own suffering everything you strive for?  
  
After you reach 25 you will start getting new Malefices that aren't tied to existing drawbacks, essentially ensuring your problems will forever increase. Malefices also now grow in strength for every Malefice you have and passively get worse. If the effects of the Malefice are already the strongest it can be it will instead develop new effects, essentialy side harms.
objects.title: Personal Hell

objects.text:
Well, looks like you have lost your Objects of Power upon arriving at your destination! 

You will have a vague sense of the direction of where your OOPs are, with each of them located within a dangerous dungeon full of traps and monsters based on the Object of Power. The level of these dungeons’ danger and difficulty is scaled based on the Object of Power’s cost. You will always have a non-zero chance of finishing the dungeons with your current abilities. Should you die in the dungeon, you will respawn out the dungeon’s entrance and be locked out from entering it again for a week. Other people are unable to see or enter these dungeons.
objects.title: Lost Relics

objects.text:
The danger has risen, the stakes are higher, and death is now a very real consequence within these dungeons. Mistakes will cost you far more than just time. And should you die, your soul will remain trapped within the dungeon—forever bound to wander its depths with nowhere else to go.

In time, once your body has decayed beyond any hope of repair, you'll become a vengeful ghost, cut off from the afterlife entirely.

That said, due to their unique conditions, if your corpse is healed quickly enough and isn't missing too much mass, your soul can simply re-enter it and reanimate you. More extreme cases, though, will require resurrection magic, alongside some method to call back your soul.
objects.title: Darkest in Dungeons™

objects.text: Whelp, you have done it now. The dungeons are now seen and accessed by others. Should they somehow complete them, they will claim the Object of Power within. In order to regain your Object(s) of Power, you must defeat them in combat. You do not have to kill them, just defeat them. Should an Object of Power normally be bound to its user, you can still reclaim it. Regarding consumable Objects of Power, the Object(s) in question will reappear in its original form in a container by which you can then consume normally.
objects.title: Artifact Chaos

objects.text: Now, instead of having retroactively crafted all of your Objects of Power before arriving in your new world, you will arrive with the knowledge of how to make them, but if you want them, you will have to do so with your own two hands. Acquire the materials, the power, the methods, everything you need, and from there you'll be able to start.
objects.title: Gotta Make It

objects.text:
You've been separated from your chosen Companions, the bonds that should exist left unformed. You will have a vague sense of the direction of where they are, though nothing precise enough to be able to pinpoint them on a map.

Should a Companion be native to the world you enter, when you encounter them in a relaxed setting (aka walking past them on the street in civies, not when in combat or a chase), both of you will be sucked into a Dungeon full of traps and monsters based on the abilities and personality of your Companion that you must escape together. The level of these dungeons’ danger and difficulty is scaled based on the Companion’s cost, though you will always have a non-zero chance of finishing the dungeons with your current abilities. Should you or your Companion die in the dungeon, you will respawn at the point where you got sucked in. Success will lead you both leaving with the relationship you chose at purchase, should you fail to complete the Dungeon together your Companion will lose all memories of the dungeon and you must wait a week before you can try again. Regardless of success, no time will have passed between the moment you enter the dungeon and the moment you leave it.

Should you have chosen a non-native Companion, then instead of triggering when you meet, the dungeon's entrance will instead be at a fixed location and you must instead conquer the its dangers alone, finding the Companion in question sealed at its very end. The dungeon's traps, monsters, overall design, and difficulty are still determined by the powers, personality, and cost in the same way as previously described. Should you die in the dungeon you'll respawn at its entrance, being unable to access it again for a week. If you succeed, the Companion in question will be freed, joining you with the relationship you decided at purchase.
objects.title: Scattered Companions

addons.text: Instead of receiving your objects ready-made, you will instead receive the materials necessary to make them, and will enter a one time tinker fugue in order to do so at the first opportunity that will not endanger you.
addons.title: Delayed Fugue

objects.text:
There have been some delays with Items you've purchased. Instead of right away appearing in your possession, or in your Hammerspace/Inventory, Home/Lair or similar, you will receive them in a natural way after three months. How exactly will depend on the nature of the Item, whether it will be an inheritance you receive, a lottery win, or you literally stumbling across it.

You can choose this Drawback up to five times to increase the delay until you get your items by an additional 3 months for the first four selections. By selecting it a fifth time you can increase the time until you receive your Items by an arbitrary amount of your choosing.
objects.title: Delayed Shipment

objects.text: Unless gained through this CYOA, you have no access to the power systems of any world you’re sent to. I’d recommend getting used to items and indirect applications. For instance, in Worm you would lack a Corona Pollentia if you didn’t select Shard, while in Avatar: The last Airbender you would have no chance of being a bender, if a world has multiple power systems you gain access to none of them. If one of your powers would otherwise allow you to learn one of these ‘Meta/Universal’ power systems, you would merely learn it at 20% of the average rate of development. This only affects supernatural and preternatural abilities, mundane martial arts and skills can still be learned as normal. Similarly you can still use objects created or maintained by these abilities such as tinkertech and enchanted objects.
objects.title: Deadened

objects.text:
Any powers you gain through this CYOA can no longer grow beyond their initial level, regardless of the method used. You won’t be able to enhance your psychic powers, you will never be able to create new spells, and your martial arts will plateau forever. 

While the way the Dead End manifests may vary depending on the nature of the power, the core effect remains the same: you can no longer grow any of your CYOA-acquired powers beyond their initial level—whether through practice, blessings, or items.

This does not prevent you from becoming more familiar with your powers or discovering creative applications—such as using basic telekinesis to trick an opponent. However, you will never be able to increase the strength or depth of that telekinesis.

Any effects that specifically grow other powers or yourself, like Dynamist Jr, Gamer, or Breaker of Chains, can still function. But Dead End slows their growth rate by an equivalent 25× times.

Powers that have built-in growth, such as power copying, power theft, or power manifestation, still function as well—but they will suffer a 50× slower growth rate. For example, the Celestial Forge will have their point gain and roll rate severely reduced.

This drawback only applies to powers gained through this CYOA. Powers acquired through other means, unrelated to your purchased powers, will not suffer from Dead End. Acclimation can still double your initial powers, and Countdown can remove this drawback entirely. No other effect can help you move past Dead End.
objects.title: Dead End

objects.text:
One of your drawbacks becomes worse. You can choose how this manifests; perhaps Childlike no longer wears off on its own, your Stalker knows exactly where you are at all times or your heat vision can't be dialed down with Constant Activation.

The changes to the drawback must result in it being notably more severe than before, whether by intensifying its effects, widening its scope or introducing more serious consequences. 

For example, Enmity would escalate to the point of causing people under its effect to potentially attack you rather than just dislike you. In contrast, only having your powers constantly fixed at 5% output with Constant Activation would not be considered sufficiently severe.
objects.title: Twist the Knife (One Drawback)

objects.text:
All of your drawbacks becomes worse. You can choose how this manifests; perhaps Childlike no longer wears off on its own, your Stalker knows exactly where you are at all times or your heat vision can't be dialed down with Constant Activation.

The changes to the drawbacks must result in it being notably more severe than before, whether by intensifying its effects, widening its scope or introducing more serious consequences. 

For example, Enmity would escalate to the point of causing people under its effect to potentially attack you rather than just dislike you. In contrast, only having your powers constantly fixed at 5% output with Constant Activation would not be considered sufficiently severe.
objects.title: Twist the Knife (All Drawbacks)

addons.text: Your injury on entry will be the result of one of your early attacks, cementing how dangerous these can really be when unexpected.
addons.title: Reasonable Cause

addons.text: Your spasms now decrease in frequency twice as fast, halving in frequency every 3 months. They remain at the same severity, however.
addons.title: Relief

objects.text:
Your molecules aren’t fully adjusted to your new universe, as a result, you will unpredictably experience incredibly painful spasms, leaving you wracked with pain. These ‘attacks’ will decrease in frequency over time but not in severity. 

During your first day after gaining this drawback, you will experience spasms at least every hour, then multiple times per day, until settling at a few times per week. After this, every six months these attacks will halve in frequency. (ie, a few attacks every two weeks, every month, every two months, every four etc).
objects.title: Buggin’ Out

objects.text:
You will be betrayed. This could be by a companion, ally, friend, lover, mentor or a more abstract entity, but they will be someone you trust or, at the very least, never expected to stab you in the back.

The exact form or nature of this betrayal may vary, but it will always be significant and meaningfully harmful to you and/or your goals. Perhaps an ally is bribed to abandon you at a crucial moment, or a partner believes you have wronged them and seeks to strip you of your power and progress.

You do not know who the betrayer is or when the double-cross will occur, but it is inevitable. It may not even be fully intentional, as they could be acting under duress, mind control, a misunderstanding or with the sincere belief that they have your best interests at heart.

While you cannot avoid this betrayal, you can feasibly uncover and counter it before any plans can be executed, or reduce its potential repercussions. To achieve this, however, you will need to maintain constant vigilance as you never know who might turn on you and when.

You may take this drawback multiple times to have numerous separate betrayals forced upon you.
objects.title: Backstabbed

objects.text: Through whatever mystical, technological or esoteric process, your face has permanently changed shape and you hate it. No illusion can indefinitely hide it. When applying makeup to your face, your contours still scream out at you; only by placing physical barriers can you truly hide its appearance. Trying to change it back to how it used to be is of no help either, for your biology would reform to that awful shape the moment the surgery was complete. You could have the most beautiful face in the universe, and the only emotion it would evoke in you is disgust.
objects.title: Not My Face

objects.text:
Instead of just your face, your entire body has changed into something unrecognizable, and you hate it. Whatever strange force caused this transformation, it has remade every inch of you into a form that feels alien and wrong. No illusion or disguise can last forever, and though clothing and armor can hide what you’ve become, you can feel the wrongness of your shape in every movement, every breath. You can’t return to how you once were; any surgery, spell, or ritual only makes your body twist itself back into that unbearable configuration the moment it’s done.

You could have the most flawless, powerful, or beautiful body in all creation, but the sight and feel of it fill you only with revulsion. Every step reminds you that you are trapped within something that is not truly you, and no amount of praise or reassurance can ever make you believe otherwise.
objects.title: Not Me

addons.text:
Your transformation is no longer limited to the face; your entire form has become that of someone else. Every feature, every scar, every contour of your body now perfectly matches the figure. You are not merely similar, you are indistinguishable. No magic, no science, no testimony can convince the world that you are not who they think you are. To all who meet you, you are that person reborn, and you will be treated according to the weight of their reputation.

Yet the resemblance is only skin-deep. You have none of their strength, skills, memories, or personality, only their appearance. To the world, however, that difference means nothing. Wherever you go, people react to them, not to you. You are forced to live the consequences of a life that isn’t yours, blamed for their sins, burdened by their legend, and forever seen as someone you will never be.
addons.title: Body of Another

objects.text: Instead of a random or unrecognizable visage, your new face is that of someone else, someone known. Through whatever strange twist of fate or cruel design, you now bear the unmistakable likeness of a famous figure: a hunted hero, a reviled tyrant, a long-dead legend, or a living icon whose name stirs emotion in every heart. No disguise, illusion, or explanation can truly convince others otherwise; to all who see you the first time, you are that person. Even those who know the truth find it hard to look at your face without the weight of history clouding their eyes.
objects.title: Face Of Another

objects.text:
"Good Morning, Campers!"

You are stuck in a one day long time loop. This time loop will repeat infinitely until you have a "perfect day", whatever that means from your point of view. This depends on what is actually possible for you to do solely on that day, so you don't have to worry about your "perfect day" being a day spent drinking on the beach, and therefore impossible to complete inside The Birdcage, or something like that.

No powers or perks will help you brute force your way out of the time loop, but you can obviously use them to contribute to your "perfect day."
objects.title: Groundhog Day

objects.text: You are stuck in a time loop, it could be from the moment you arrive or after some time — weeks or months, at most. The length of the loop can vary from days to months and is usually anchored to a climactic event at the end; for example: the ABB bombing campaign in Brockton Bay, the events of Infinity War in the Marvel Universe, the Reaper invasion in Mass Effect, or maybe just the 4th of July fireworks. The only way to break the loop is to discover the win condition. This does not necessarily mean an overt victory, it can also involve finding the source of the time loop, the people pulling the strings behind the scenes, or any number of difficult challenges. The loop will reset when you die or if you reach the end point alive (midnight of the last day or 24h minimum). It will always be possible to break the loop with your chosen powers but it will never be easy by any means, even with Path to Victory or Omniscient; this is meant to be a challenge after all. When the loop resets, only your mind and soul are sent back to the beginning, while your body is reset to its initial state; meaning some progress can carry between loops, depending on the source and powers. Shard, Patron, and Artifact powers never carry over, since their source is external, while some Shardless power can (ex: magic, psychic) and others won't (ex: physical), depending on their mechanics. You can freely time travel within the loop itself but no powers or perks can help you brute force your way out of the time loop.
objects.title: Groundhog… Week?

objects.text: Someone else is also part of the loop and their goal opposes yours. They might be behind the events of the loop or just taking advantage of them for their own ends, the result is the same: they are determined to win and will remember every trick you pulled on them during previous loops. This opponent isn't necessarily as strong as you (or stronger) but they will always have plenty of tricks up their sleeves. They could be your Nemesis, Stalker, Clustermate, an existing character, or an original character.
objects.title: Adversarial Time-Loop

objects.text: For each purchase, another person is pulled into the loop; they could be one of your Nemesis, Stalker, Clustermate, or another enemy of yours. Depending on their goals, they will not necessarily cooperate with each-other.
objects.title: This TARDIS is Getting Crowded

objects.text: For each purchase, one of your companions, allies, or other person is pulled into the loop with you.
objects.title: This TARDIS is Getting Stacked

objects.text:
Whether it was a blinding light-show, a deafening explosion, or the very sky cracking to spit you out, your arrival to your chosen world (or empowerment, if you chose No Transfer) was not a quiet one. Interested or concerned parties will quickly come to investigate the aftershocks of your appearance or empowerment. If you don’t move quickly, there is a good chance of this event being linked to you.

The exact method and effect of this drawback is up to you, so long as it fits your location and draws sufficient attention.
objects.title: Crash In

objects.text:
Congratulations, you are now a parent. By taking this drawback, you gain one newborn child per purchase of this drawback. Each time you take it, a new child is added to your responsibility list.

These children can be biologically yours, adopted, a sibling, or a relative. For each child, you may decide whether they appear with you at the start of your journey or are discovered within the first few days. You may also decide each child's gender or leave it up to chance.

You are fully responsible for each child's well-being. You must feed them, raise them, protect them, and care for them until they reach 18 years of age. Neglecting or abandoning any child will cause you to experience increasing amounts of pain proportional to how badly that child suffers. This penalty stacks for every neglected child. If one or more of your children die, you will suffer constant pain for each child until the day that child would have turned 18 years old.

If you take this drawback multiple times, the children may be twins, triplets, or born years apart, at your discretion. Their personalities, needs, and development are all separate, and complications such as illness, conflict between siblings, or external threats may arise naturally.

If you are a Drop-In and a child is biologically yours, then each such child was created in an incubation chamber using your DNA and another person's DNA, unless you prefer to have carried the child yourself. If you possess the Perk Altered History, or choose Reincarnation or Character-Insert, you may decide how each child came to be and who the other parent is for every instance of this drawback.
objects.title: You are the Father

objects.text:
You have had all internal sense of social norms, decency, and behavioral rules removed from your head and instincts.

Ideas like personal space, turn-taking in conversation, laughing at weak jokes or even bodily shame, none of these exist for you. All the invisible, untaught programming that makes human interaction flow smoothly has been erased, leaving you unable to read or produce the tiny courtesies that keep society from rubbing raw.

While you can relearn it, you will struggle with learning it all from scratch again, and can even find them unnecessary or unnatural.
objects.title: Tarzan

objects.text:
Something about your very existence, be it your body or soul, acts as an irresistible beacon to evil spirits of the dead. It draws them to you with a maddening, obsessive compulsion akin to a druggie seeking their fix. You are the most cursed person in the world, beloved and followed by an unseen legion of horrors.

When you linger in a place, the boundary between the living and the dead thins, allowing evil spirits to manifest with a level of power and physical presence they could never achieve on their own. It also accelerates the birth of new malevolent entities, causing the spiritual residue in your location to congeal into full-fledged evil spirits in days instead of years. This doesn’t create spirits out of nothing, only working when there is already existing grudges and residue.

Every spirit drawn to you has a compulsion that ensures they will never want to end your life. This creates a localized truce-state within your sphere of influence that allows all manner of rival and hostile entities to at minimum tolerate one another's presence. But do not mistake this for mercy. They will never kill you, but they have no compulsion to leave you in peace. Only spirits created or attracted by this drawback are affected by this compulsion. Unrelated spirits can still harm and kill you before your presence influences them.
objects.title: Lighthouse of the Damned

objects.text:
Instead of being reborn or dropped in as a human or even an animal, you unfortunately end up as an inanimate object. It could be almost anything from a tool, a weapon, a doll, etc. So long as it can reasonably be owned by somebody in your setting.

Character shall be applied to your first owner. Perks and Drawbacks may transfer between owners as well, and would only be of those that can reasonably be given to humans (such as Kill Order or Wealthy). This won't apply if they don't care about you.

You are also, unfortunately, unable to move unless you have any power mitigating that. This means you can't communicate with your owner unless again, you have a power to do so. This also means that even if say, you're a car, you can't just begin driving on your own unless you pick something that allows you to do so.

Overall, you're stuck lying there for a bit. But maybe it's not that bad, depending on how you make it work for you and whoever owns you?
objects.title: Inanimate Reincarnate

objects.text:
You are painfully, almost cripplingly shy. Social interaction becomes difficult even when people are being kind to you, and attention feels like a spotlight burning into your skin. Speaking up in groups, asking for help, introducing yourself, accepting praise, arguing your point, or showing genuine emotion in front of others all become far harder than they should be.

You instinctively avoid being noticed and often struggle even with simple interactions. You may freeze, stammer, mumble, blush, avoid eye contact, hide behind others, or retreat entirely when pressured. Compliments can leave you flustered and unsure how to respond, confrontation makes you shrink back, and unfamiliar people feel exhausting or intimidating to deal with. Even when you know exactly what you want to say, actually saying it can feel like forcing yourself through a wall while everyone is watching.
objects.title: Painfully Shy

objects.text: You will be unconscious for the first 12 hours after entering your new world. While this is unlikely to cause issues if you arrived somewhere abandoned, it could be rather worse if you were in a restricted area, battlefield or 40,000ft in the air.
objects.title: Unconsciousness

objects.text:
After an unknown period of time, you will be sealed, imprisoned, or incapacitated in some way, either by magical, technological, esoteric, or other method. If your chosen setting lacks the means to do so, it will quickly be discovered by rapid advancements, otherworldly artifacts, ancient legacies, or individuals with suitable abilities. 

There is no way to avoid or predict this. You will be incapable of freeing yourself on your own and will need an outside help to escape your predicament. Fortunately, there is a silver lining: your seal can easily be broken from the outside. This could be done by opening a cursed book, destroying a delicate piece of technology, or disrupting a sensitive ritual. However, it does not guarantee that your prison won't still be guarded.

Another ray of hope is that you can exert some influence through prison, albeit limited. Perhaps you have telepathic abilities that can create a mental allure to draw someone in. As a powerful summoner, with great effort and strain, you could call a small creature outside to send a message. If you are a probability manipulator, perhaps you can pull the strings of fate enough to be discovered after being long forgotten. Your influence is weak and fragile, and the result is uncertain so be prepared and better seek some allies. 

Due to the unpredictability of the length of your imprisonment, you should probably have some form of immortality and strong enough will to endure loneliness and boredom for a such long time.
objects.title: Seal Designate
Pre-Sealed
objects.text:
Rather than being sealed away at an indeterminate point in the future, you will find yourself already imprisoned upon Insertion. If you are a Drop-In, your prison suddenly manifests with you already inside, while for Reincarnation or Character Insert you were sealed away some time ago, which depending on your build could have been anywhere from five minutes to literal centuries ago. Either way, you are already trapped, and thus have no chance to influence the plot directly other than via the limited influence you have on the outside world.

Any effects that are supposed to trigger upon or shortly after your insertion such Worst Day Ever, Great Omen, or meeting your Significant Other or Companions will happen after you are released, unless they are worldwide such as Second Wave Parahumans or End of the Kaiju, in which case you can choose to have them still happen as normal while you're trapped.

objects.title: Early Parole
objects.text: You are now guaranteed to be unsealed within a reasonable amount of time. At most, you will be released after five years even if you do nothing, but if you are smart about how you employ your ability to influence the outside world, you could be free in as little as one year. No matter what, you cannot free yourself any faster than that, but now you are certain to not be forced to outlive everyone you know while stuck in a cage.

Whenever you take a drawback that gives you a designated enemy such as Fairy Goddess or Endbringer Target, these enemies are now cosmically linked to you and will follow you to any and all worlds you travel to. They will either travel there under their own power or be transported to your new dimension by cosmic happenstance. The only way to stop them from continuing to follow you is by rendering them permanently incapable of doing so, either by death or cosmic guaranteed imprisonment.
objects.title: A Wild Scion Appeared!

objects.text:
When you insert into the world, a complete dossier on your powers, abilities, and skills is released to several major players, including higher-ups in intelligence/military institutions and heads of major crime organizations. These documents are extremely thorough, going into minute detail on how your powers work, and exactly what their limits and capabilities are. There's a section describing the effects of any other drawbacks you've taken, and even a psychological profile, with a thorough run-down of your habits, weaknesses, and beliefs.

These documents include a few identifying details, but not enough to out your civilian identity (if that's something you maintain). Once you start showcasing your abilities, however, it'll be nearly impossible to stop people from putting the pieces together, connecting the documents to you through the capabilities you exhibit.

If you've taken any drawbacks that put you in opposition to a particular adversary, they're guaranteed to receive one of the copies.
objects.title: Known Quantity

objects.text:
You gain a Nemesis who has an ideological position incompatible with yours that cannot be reconciled. This person will have a build of similar strength to you. Your nemesis does not necessarily want to kill you their goals will just be diametrically opposed to yours, they will be the Villain to your Hero, rival business partner, or competing shadowy organization.

Your Nemeses will respect the Truce as long as you do as well if they’re a person who values their privacy or has something to lose otherwise.

If you picked <u>Late to the Party</u>, your Nemesis will be part of them.

(You can pick your Nemesis alignments in the section below).
objects.title: Nemesis

objects.text:
Your powers have been split from you, your strength evenly distributed with another.

(You can pick the number of people in your cluster and it's specific mechanics in the section below)
objects.title: Cluster

objects.text:
You gain a form of insanity. They can range from various forms of mental disorders to hallucinations.

(You can pick your insanity in the section below)
objects.title: Insane

objects.text: Your first day on Earth Bet (or wherever you arrive) will suck.
objects.title: Worst Day Ever

objects.text: Did you slight a Fae? Or try to trick a Devil? No matter what you have been cursed. This curse may take many forms. (Choose one from the section below.)
objects.title: Cursed

addons.text: Earth is still developing its identity. Your eventful life, as well as the lives of the people on the planet, will determine how it shapes, but it is still forming. Its destiny is bright, but it'll get far more chaotic before it reaches a stable aspect.
addons.title: Developing

addons.text: Your world, although still forming, is one of the early cruxes of your universe, making it a prime target for cosmic threats. It's one of the linchpins of your universe, requiring defending before it’s completely undone by either entities or other threats. Protecting the world will take a great deal of time and energy. No matter the threat, it will always be possible to defeat them.
addons.title: Linchpin

objects.text:
Throughout the universe, there are Crux worlds. Worlds that embody aspects of reality. Technology, magic, heroism, Horror, Entropy and more. 

Unfortunately, your world is on the irreversible track to becoming one of these crux worlds, forming the identity that will shape its place in the universe. As a Crux World, it is being slowly shaped based on what’s happening in the world. 

The concept it’s aspected from will also begin to shape the populous and contents. A Crux world of horror for instance would produce monsters and tragedies with great frequency, warping fate and probabilities around it to ensure such events happen. 

Similarly as an important part of the universe, should the world undergo some kind of catastrophic disaster, or god forbid it be destroyed, it could have disastrous effects on the universe as a whole, destabilising it as its concept is spread across the universe and fluctuates before ultimately ending the concept entirely.

For this reason, Crux worlds are magnets for chaos and conflict, both as places of upheaval and development on the small scale and as cosmic targets on the large scale.
objects.title: Crux World

objects.text: All the Endbingers have been charged, what this effectively means is that they are no longer holding back, and you can never be sure which Endbringer is going to attack as they no longer hold any specific order in which they attack or how long they stay dormant in between attacks, as well as being around twice as strong as they were before they got the power-up.
objects.title: Reign of the Kaiju

objects.text: Every time this drawback is taken, 3 more dormant Endbringers becomes active. When taken 5 times, you will have to contend with 18 active Endbringers. This does not speed up the rate of attacks.
objects.title: Even More Active Endbringers

objects.text: Every time this drawback is taken, 20 more Endbringers are created. When taken 5 times, there will be 120 dormant Endbringers ready to take the place of their fallen brethren.
objects.title: Even More Dormant Endbringers

objects.text: Reduces the time between Endbringers attacks by one month for the first 2 times this drawback is taken, one week for the next 3, and one day for the next 5. When taken 10 times, an attack will occur every other day.
objects.title: Even More Endbringer Attacks

objects.text:
At the moment of your arrival, the Endbringer attack cycle will be modified so that an Endbringer will be awakened every time an Endbringer attacks until all of them have awoken.

After all 20 are awoken, they’ll revert to their previous attack cycle.
objects.title: Waking Titans

objects.text:
All Entities have been greatly altered. They will have all the powers of their Shard regardless if they have been deployed or not and are now much stronger than before. With full control over kinetics, energy, and matter they are immune to any conventional form of attack. They are completely secured within hidden pocket dimensions that are defended to the brim with Sting-like weaponry. They even have various redundancies that prevent them from having a specific weak spot to attack. Entities will even be capable of properly interacting with out-of-context things.

Though Eden would still be dead if you did not take Not So Dead After All.
objects.title: Reign of The Entities

objects.text:
Zion is no longer suicidal and never will be. No amount of reminders regarding Eden's death, the pointlessness of the Cycle, or anything else will make him stop trying to survive with all his faculties. Hope those points were worth it because you'll have to go all out to win.

He is still depressed and apathetic, as long as nothing sets him off he continues his current behavior for at least a century. Unless a major event happens to his core Shards, he will not notice any missing or subverted Shards.

After 250 to 300 years, he will proceed with the end of the Cycle, collect all of his and Eden's surviving Shards and depart from the planet, destroying all parallel versions of it in the process.
objects.title: Desire For Survival

objects.text: Contessa did not kill Eden, she only damaged the Entity's core Shards and they have been stuck in a loop ever since. In the background, automatic repair protocols were working tirelessly to bring back functionality and restore it. A few years after your arrival (from 2-4 years) the process finally completes and Eden will wake from her slumber. Cauldron will be cut from the dimensions containing Eden's corpse as the dimensional interdiction Shards activate. It will take the Entity at least six months to sort out the complete mess Cauldron has made of it, the shadowy organization did a number on the dormant Entity's network. During this time, Eden's Shards will receive several update packets and update their configurations. The ones attached to hosts will properly connect, and Case 53s will have their powers correct themselves to function as intended. Once the process is complete, Eden will appear and reconnect with Scion. The Cycle will continue.
objects.title: Not So Dead After All

objects.text:
Whispers on the Shard Network are that someone has the [ANSWER]. Thankfully, you or your Shard is smart enough to not advertise that fact. As you meet more Parahumans and fight with or against them, the Network will slowly be able to discover your identity. Some Shards are smarter than others and will catch on faster, once they do they will push their host to enter into conflict with yours to acquire that sweet sweet [DATA]. Shards with a higher rank than yours will attempt to bully yours into handing over the [ANSWER]. If things go on for long enough, Scion will finally check his inbox, from this point on the golden man himself will be on your tails.

Fear not, however, it is still possible for you to survive the encounter depending on your relationship with your Shard. One option is to willfully become Scion's new partner, your Shard will be elevated to the rank of HUB and will be the start of a new Entity with your consciousness at the helm. There are other options as well, killing Scion will quiet things down significantly.
objects.title: The Answer to Life, the Universe, and Everything

addons.text: The Entities receive a massive boost in critical thinking, being capable of rapid innovation and figuring out new and dangerous ways to challenge you. They also receive a full understanding of your build, from Drawbacks to Powers, and Skills. After 10 years, you may now travel around the limited Worm Multiverse freely. This is not a reward, however, because the Entities will have finally cracked the secret of risk-free negentropy from their constant observation of you. Instead of a defensive war in which you can never truly strike back, you must now attempt to hunt down every last Entity before they multiply and consume all of reality.
addons.title: Intelligent Warfare

objects.text: Your summoning was undeniable, maybe a bit too noticeable. Regardless of your circumstances, you will find that every Entity in the Universe has seen you. And they will inform every Entity that hasn’t, you have a way to survive past heat death, the answer they’ve long searched for. Also, don’t even think of trying to run away, you’ve been dimensionally anchored into the Universe you started in, and not even killing the Warrior with the Countdown Perk will let you escape from this universe. And don’t bother with trying to hide, your aura of oddness is so strong it will give away your location no matter what. Good luck, you’ll need it.
objects.title: An [ANSWER] Is Seen And A Trillion Crystal Eyes Look Upon a Blue And Green Dot

objects.text: At some point within a few years after your arrival (ranging from 5-10 years), a second pair of Entities will arrive and begin a new Cycle. If the Warrior and/or Thinker are still alive, they might clash or join forces. If you have already defeated the Warrior and Thinker, they will try to take over the Shard networks for their purposes. Take a lot of points because you'll need all the help you can get.
objects.title: The Cycle Begins Anew

objects.text: Apollyon is heading to Earth: a hypothesized third Entity 3x stronger than Zion and Eden combined, as well as having twice the number of Shards. He is coming to take over the Cycle that Eden and Zion have failed to finish. Apollyon is different from Zion and doesn't intend to preserve the current cycle, instead, will carry out his original plan for Earth and initiate anew from the previous Cycle’s ashes. This new cycle will see thousands of Shards dispersed onto Earth, plunging the world into chaos. If you have selected The Ancient, then instead of Apollyon, a new rival predator will be the one coming to usurp the cycle. They will NOT get along.
objects.title: Apollyon: the Destroyer

addons.text: Moving between worlds makes quite a few ripples through possibility. Unfortunately, adding so many variables ensures Snakes will start to notice eventually, putting every universe you visit at risk.
addons.title: Thrill of the Hunt

objects.text:
To a human, the Entities are overwhelmingly powerful, terror-inducing creatures that stand to destroy everything and everyone that they have ever known. While this is not an inaccurate statement, there’s always a bigger fish. Quite naturally, the universe, being a rather large place, has quite a few species fulfilling the niche of entity-killers. But when you think you’re at the top...

A great ‘Snake’ has begun coiling through your multiversal cluster, feeding on universes it comes across. These ‘Snakes’ feed on Quantum possibilities. They are lifeforms composed of networks of these possibilities. Of never-weres and could-have-been living in impossible flux. As they eat, they replace the fluctuations that have stabilized, discarding them as they go. These stabilized points soon grow into universes of their own, and the cycle continues.

The more variables existing in a universe, the more nutritious the meal. The ‘Snake’ latches onto the Universe and slowly drains it dry until there isn’t a single possibility or uncertainty remaining. Thankfully for it, yours has quite a few variables on the cosmic scale, enough to draw it to your cluster, and enough energy to sate it for some time.

You have a decade before its arrival and a year of it draining your universe before all is lost. Driving it away or, god forbid, killing it will be orders of magnitude more difficult than even the most warlike entity’s dream scenario.

Or, of course, you could flee. But your Multiversal Cluster has already showcased its nutritional value to the Snake, and where there’s one...
objects.title: Jormungand

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, the rate of triggers around your chosen world will increase by 0.1% per day until it reaches the new rate. The triggers have a lower activation threshold than standard triggers, closer to that of second-generation triggers. These parahumans can second trigger if they encounter a situation sufficiently similar situation to their first trigger. 

There is a 5% chance of a Parahuman also becoming a Noctis Cape, a 2% chance they'll be enhanced to peak human, a 2% chance they'll become a minor thinker blindspot and a 1% chance they'll gain a resistance to master powers. A Parahuman with resistance to master powers will have a 50% chance of also becoming a thinker blindspot. There is a 0.001% chance that Parahumans will gain resistance to Trump powers.
objects.title: Second Wave Parahumans

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, people will also begin awakening Shardless powers at a base rate of 1 in 500'000 people, separate from shard-based triggers, and increasing by a multiplicative 20% for each rank after the first. The rate of awakenings starts at the base rate and increases by 0.1% per day until it reaches the same rate as whichever rank you chose below. The awakenings have a similar activation threshold to standard triggers but can happen through more than just traumatic events, such as moments of great need or situations that would fit the mythos of an origin story. All of these parahumans' powers, by nature, are considered Negentropic and can improve with training and/or time.

All the powers listed in the Shardless power sections will get triggered, save for Ascensions and Paragons and any powers that can't be afforded. Since not all powers are completely unique, some of them will trigger with the powers you chose if you have access to them, potentially being highly different from your versions due to the versatility of some powers.
objects.title: Mass Awakening

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, the native people of whichever non-Worm setting(s) you're traveling to will begin to awaken potential abilities - as described in the Origin of Powers and Super Abilities sections of each Alternate Earth - at an accelerated pace, gaining a multiplicative +20% increase per Rank taken to whatever amount/population of powered individuals exists in those settings. For Low-Tier, these newly-Awakened individuals only have the bare minimum potential on average, or close to it, but for Mid- and High-Tier, this instead results in increasing chances of people developing powers on the higher ends of those settings's scales.

For most settings, this behaves as you would expect, with a sudden uptick of people developing Metahuman abilities/high Chakra/magic potential/Etc. For more "grounded" or "realistic" settings that mostly rely on super-geniuses and advanced technology, this drawback will instead cause an uptick in said hyperintelligent individuals in order to propagate more supertech. In settings where powers instead originate from an outside source, such as anomalous materials that grant abilities, this drawback will instead cause a sudden resurgence of said resource(s) proportionate to Ranks taken.
objects.title: Native Awakening

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, people will begin gaining Objects of Power at a base rate of 1 in 500’000 people, separate from shard-based powers, or shardless awakenings, and increasing by a multiplicative 20% for each rank after the first. The rate of arming starts at the base rate, and increases by 0.1% per day until it reaches the same rate as whichever rank you chose below. 

Enough copies and variations of all the Objects listed in the Objects of Power section will be distributed, save for any that cannot be afforded. This will include Objects of Power you have selected.
objects.title: Mass Arming

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, those who Trigger as Parahumans potentially undergo a "Broken" Trigger, unnoticed by the Entities. These Broken Triggers can jump from person to person, affecting multiple people. Those affected by Broken Triggers can certainly die as a result of their powers or the Trigger Event. If the Parahuman survives, they have a small chance of having a second Broken Trigger, merging with their shard into a "Titan."

These "Titans" have full access to all the powers of the host's Shard, including those it could have given out but didn't. These "Titans" appear to experience a significant loss in their original personality, attacking seemingly indiscriminately and slaughtering anything they can reach, often heading towards populated areas, causing widespread destruction, Titans are relatively equal to Endbringers in terms of durability and destructive potential and on rare occasion may be able to overpower them.

Titans activated by this Drawback, will draw an Entity's attention sooner or later, and be dealt with, though the Entities will do nothing to prevent further such Titans from being created.

This Drawback has a variable expiration date, After 10 years at the Common Titans rate, 15 Years at the Normal Titans rate, and 20 at the Rare Titans rate.
objects.title: Titanomachy

objects.text:
Upon taking this Drawback, people will start to be visited by Patrons offering them covenants. In exchange for agreeing to represent their Patrons interest in the mortal plane they shall be granted Powers to use as they see fit, so long as they abide by their contract.

People will begin to gain these Powers at a base-rate of 1 in 500’000, separate from powers gained through other Power origins such as shard-based powers, shardless awakenings or being empowered through an artefact, and increasing by a  multiplicative 20% for each rank after the first. 
The rate of contracting starts at the base-rate, and increases by 0.1% per day until it reaches the same rate as whichever rank you chose below. 

The Patrons can assign any combination of powers available to them to their Contractors, including powers you have chosen, so long as your chosen Rank can support those Powers.
Patrons will grant powers that align with their goals, philosophy and Demesne/Portfolio.
objects.title: Constellation Chatroom

rows.title: Drawbacks
rows.titleText: Drawbacks are side-effects that harm or hinder you.

objects.text: The Snakes have never been erudite. In fact, they’re little more than animals in cognitive power, existing only to search for food and move on. This makes them easier to combat on a tactical level when compared with the sapient, if alien, mindset of the average Snake.
objects.title: Feral

objects.text: The ‘Snake’ at the very least, is sapient… for a certain meaning of the phrase. It’s capable of reason, and complex thinking, and can even communicate with a creature such as you. Naturally, its opinion of you is quite low, its mindset quite alien, and its values near-diametrically opposed to your own. But it can think. And if it can think, it can be reasoned with. Allegedly.
objects.title: Small Mercies

objects.text:
The Snake that has come to devour your universe has quite the issue. A beast that is, by its nature entropic, reducing possibilities down to their simplest nothings in its stomach, it has gorged itself too long on many succulent universes. 

Now, it has developed a kind of stomach ulcer. With its incredible size, and with the ulcer sapping its meals, it has to eat more and more universes to keep itself from eating itself from within. Eventually, much like a lobster, it will become too big to fulfill its appetite, starving to death. 

Upon its starvation, it will collapse, as every possibility contained within its ‘ulcer’ spills forth in a massive explosion. Echoes of this explosion will create universes of their own, all continuing within its great corpse, forming the walls of a new multiversal cluster. Of course, the Ulcer itself will remain at the center of this cluster. A roiling Nuclear Chaos from which a new young brood of Snakes will be born to suckle on the energy of an infinitely expanding cluster of infinite multiverses.

Naturally, Its condition has made it a desperate creature, and with its death new worlds will spill forth, repeating the cycle once again.
objects.title: A Lobster's Death

objects.text: In an infinite omniverse, filled with infinite multiverses, filled with universes of their own, there are many bounties for Snakes to find. Unfortunately, your neck of the woods is quite rife with energy, and the Snakes travel in packs. Thankfully, they don’t tend to intrude on each other’s kills, but after dealing with one… well.
objects.title: Pack-Hunting

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses is currently your rival. A friendly rival that competes with you for whatever goal.
objects.title: Rival

addons.text:
You may optionally have The Loved Nemesis already a member of your group. While you still have no control over the specifics of their builds, you’d be delighted to have them on your side, and luckily for you they already are. They’ll be incredibly if not perfectly suited for you and you for them, both in character and build. This applies to all nemeses who fall under The Loved option. 

Whether they’re dropping in at the same time/location as you, whether they reincarnated and were life long friends of your new life alongside you, or perhaps they suddenly drop in while you awaken your memories in your reincarnated life and you two hit it off immediately, whatever the scenario they will be an immediate member of your network. This also ensures that all your nemeses under the The Loved option will arrive no later than your own awakening/drop in point.

There isn’t anything that can break the bond between you and them, they’d be happy to lend you all their strength and more with no strings or caveats attached and will follow and support any endeavors you have. 

Regardless of whatever powers, perks, and other options that they may have chosen and strength they have, they've already willingly joined your network, granting you the totality of their abilities, and subject to any of the other effects of being in your network would entail.
addons.title: Dynamic Duo

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses are the kind of people you absolutely get along with. They no longer wish to defeat you or have ideological differences. It's likely that they will assist you with whatever goal you have.
objects.title: The Loved

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses are the kind of people you absolutely despise. Their personality, actions, and behaviors are exactly the kind of things you hate. If there's something that annoys you, it's likely they're doing it.
objects.title: The Hated

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses wants you. They will do anything to get your love and attention. They want nothing more than to kidnap you and shove you into their basement for all of eternity. They are twice as strong than you. Unless they have Weaker than You.
objects.title: Yandere

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses are half as strong as you. You cannot stack these onto a single Nemesis.
objects.title: Weaker than You

objects.text: One or more of your Nemeses are twice as strong as you. You cannot stack these onto a single Nemesis.
objects.title: Better than You

objects.text: After some time, a powerful being will introduce itself. This being is directly opposed to both you and your nemeses. The True Antagonist is the collective strength of every Nemesis and you combined. It will require you to get along with and work together with your nemeses in order to defeat The True Antagonist.
objects.title: True Antagonist

rows.title: Nemesis Choice
rows.titleText: Choose the alignment of your Nemeses

objects.text: You gain a member of the cluster. You’ll need at least one of these for anything in this section to mean anything.
objects.title: Clustermates

objects.text:
There exists a dark ritual that can let one drain their clustermates of their powers. If you were to utilise this ritual to drain all of your clustermates, your secondary powers would be boosted back to the strength they originally were.

By taking this, you will get some initial clues towards how to discover and perform this ritual.

Whatever it is, the ritual is guaranteed to be lengthy and costly in some fashion.

While you could hypothetically discover this ritual or an alternative without taking this, it would be significantly more difficult.
objects.title: Power Drain

objects.text:
One of your clustermates will receive clues towards the ritual from Power Drain, and will attempt to discover it and use it to drain you & the rest of your clustermates. (They will still attempt to drain you even if you made them Kiss for you)

Additional purchases have another one of your clustermates affected by this drawback. You cannot select this drawback more times than you have clustermates.
objects.title: Power Thief

objects.text:
For each selection, one of your clustermates will feel an intense attraction (platonic, romantic or otherwise) towards you.

You can only select this as many times as clustermates as you have.

Note that this relationship is one way and you would need to select the Kiss/Kill option adjacent to this to have the compulsion to love them back.
objects.title: Kiss

objects.text:
Frequently, members of clusters find themselves having unnaturally strong feelings for each other as a result of the bond of their powers, which is referred to as the Kiss/Kill effect.

This drawback will give you a kiss/kill response to one of your clustermates for each time you’ve selected it: you will feel either an intense attraction (platonic, romantic or otherwise) towards a clustermate (Kiss) or an intense hatred for a clustermate (Kill).

You can select this up to twice for each clustermate, once for the Kiss and once for the Kill.

Note that this relationship is one way and you will need to select the individual Kiss or Kill options adjacent to this to make them hate or love you back.
objects.title: Kiss/Kill

objects.text:
For each selection, one of your clustermates will feel an intense hatred for you.

You can only select this as many times as clustermates as you have.

Note that this relationship is one way and you would need to select the Kiss/Kill option adjacent to this to have the compulsion to hate them back.
objects.title: Kill

objects.text: Now the membership of your cluster is more… fluid. If another person experiences a significantly traumatic event (such as a trigger or second trigger) in your presence, they will be automatically added to your cluster.
objects.title: Open Relationship

objects.text: You are now capable of choosing whether a person can join the cluster or not.
objects.title: Closed Invitation

addons.text:
Now, whenever a person is to be added to the cluster, time will pause and everyone in the cluster will be mentally transported to a meeting place. In this meeting place, your cluster will be required to democratically vote on whether this new person gets to join the cluster, requiring a majority of ‘yes’ for the vote to succeed. 

If a person attempts to delay the ending of this meeting by deliberately not voting for too long, they will automatically count as having voted neutrally.

As soon as everyone in the cluster has voted, they will all be transported back to their bodies and time will resume once again, with the whole process appearing to have occurred instantaneously to onlookers.
addons.title: Democratic

objects.text: This effect now extends to all of your clustermates as well: if anybody experiences a significantly traumatising event in the presence of your clustermates, they will automatically be added to the cluster.
objects.title: Exponential Spread

objects.text: Here you can select additional rules that your cluster can follow.
objects.title: Cluster Mechanics

objects.text:
Your cluster is governed by a cycle that takes place over a span of days equal to the number of people in your cluster. Over this cycle, each member of the cluster will get a power boost for a day, with the rest of the cluster instead getting their powers weakened for that day. 

The order in which cluster members are empowered is random, although over the cycle each member will get empowered once.

After each cycle has been completed (every member has been empowered once), there will be a day of lull in which everybody will have their normal power strength before the next cycle starts.
objects.title: Power Cycle

objects.text:
At fixed intervals, you and all your clustermates will begin to feel a steadily increasing sense of drowsiness. You can choose to resist this drowsiness for a bit, but no matter how strong your resistance, after 10 minutes have passed you will be guaranteed to pass out. After everybody in the cluster has become unconscious, you will all be mentally transported to a dream room, unable to be woken for the next hour at least.

While in the dream room, nobody can harm, target or otherwise affect each other outside mundane communication, making it a safe space to talk among each other.
objects.title: Dream Room

objects.text:
The call of the dream room is no longer unavoidable. A person is capable of resisting the scheduled drowsiness that pulls one into the dream room completely, although it will be harder to resist the longer it has been since they've last entered. As well as this, everybody is capable of doing the opposite: intentionally pulling themselves into the dream room with normal rest outside the scheduled time, although mechanics in the dream that rely on others in the room will still require their presence to work.

Either way, after entering the dream room, a person will only be unwakeable for 10 minutes, being able to leave the dream room from anything that would normally disturb their sleep after that.
objects.title: Could Be An Email

objects.text: When asleep you’ll occasionally see a glimpse of the life of your clustermates, which one’s changes each time. This vision can either be something they’re currently doing or a memory triggered by a recent event. Each clustermate will get these Interludes, although they’re often only a few minutes long, with the longer ones only being a few dozen minutes in length. You can try going for a more specific memory or moment at the expense of opening yourself up for the same treatment from the others.
objects.title: Dream Interlude

addons.text: The time at which you get your tokens and the time at which you fall asleep will be one and the same, allowing you to negotiate and barter with your clustermates in a safe space.
addons.title: Dream Poll

objects.text:
At fixed intervals, you and all of your clustermates will get a semi-random (You are more likely to get more of your own tokens) set of “tokens” representing each clustermates' primary powers. You are all capable of sending these tokens to each other to give a power boost to the recipient's equivalent of the tokens represented powers. 

Unused tokens are lost when you gain the new set of tokens.
objects.title: Playing Favourites

objects.text:
As well as your primary and secondary powers, you now have a third category some of your powers fit into. Shared powers to which no member has a claim. These powers get a moderate nerf; greater than the nerf to your primary powers but less than the nerf to your secondary powers.

Unlike your other powers, these manifest in the exact same way for everybody, only differing in how exactly they interact with the other powers in each person's set.

If you’ve used perks/drawbacks to modify these shared powers, the rest of your cluster gets the same modifications, except for those that don't make sense with them (e.g. if you make changes that rely on the specifics of your primary power).
objects.title: Shared Power

objects.text: Instead of having primary or secondary powers, it appears everybody in the cluster has the exact same powerset. There are no more primary or secondary powers, all your powers are now shared powers, with all that that entails.
objects.title: Standardised Format

addons.text: A portion of the power boost gained from draining a clustermate will be you gaining the strongest possible version of the boost you would have gotten from defeating the victim.
addons.title: The Loser's Standing Small

objects.text:
Whenever one person in your cluster defeats another, the winner will get a temporary boost to all of their powers. Meanwhile, the loser will find their powers weakened for the same amount of time. 

In terms of the boost to the winners' powers, the winner will get it in the form of extra elements to their powers either relating to the theme of the losers or, if not possible, at least buffs to where their powers overlap.

For example, in a cluster of two tinkers, the winner would get partial access to the specialisations of the loser, improving the blueprints where those specialisations overlap with their own.

Another example would be if Foil beat March with this cluster mechanic, she’d get the ability to empower her projectiles to explode (mundane explosion) after a set time; the ability to predict the timings of things over a longer term than usual and for her to be able to take half a second to further empower objects imbued with sting to maintain their effect even when broken apart (such as by exploding).

The power boost will only occur from a proper contest in which stakes are involved, with the strength of the boost (and the losers weakening) based upon the severity of the stakes for the winner.

For example, beating a clustermate in a game of chess with nothing on the line would result in a pitiful boost that would only be noticeable if one were paying attention.

If a clustermate dies, part of the power boost everyone would get will be permanently having a weak version of the boost they would have gotten by beating the dead cape.
objects.title: Winner Takes It All

objects.text:
All powers you have that store some form of non-unique (so no power copies, created powers, etc) internal points/resources/energy can now draw from a pool of the same points shared by the whole cluster. Your clustermates will also be able to draw freely from this pool for their own powers however.

Whatever method you use to restore or gain these points (Over time, absorbing sunlight, taking drugs, etc), now has half of its gains instead redirected to this shared pool, with the same going for all of your clustermates as well.

If whatever points your power uses has a maximum capacity/size/amount that you can have at any time, your maximum capacity is halved, with that sacrificed capacity added to the maximum size of the shared pool. Combined with the max capacity sacrificed by all of your clustermates as well, this shared pool will add up to be larger than the capacity you sacrificed. If a member of the cluster dies, the pool shrinks accordingly.

This mechanic can only be taken if at least one of your powers utilises some form of non-unique points (mana, ki, electricity, etc) to begin with. Taking this will ensure that your clustermates’ variants of those powers will also manifest in such a way that they use, store and can collect those points.
objects.title: Pooled Resources

objects.text:
All powers in the cluster that internally create/absorb and store unique resources (such as power copies, created powers, skills, etc) can now access the resources of their clustermates on top of their own stored ones.

However if a resource is drawn from a clustermate using this mechanic, it will be weaker compared to having the resource itself.

If the power relies on slots this will not give you “extra slots”, you will simply be capable of filling those slots with your clustermates resources instead of filling them in the normal manner.

Whatever resource is drawn will automatically get converted to work with the copiers version of the power, allowing them to utilise aspects of the resource the original holder could not.

For example, if you had the power Tinker of Chance, you would be capable of filling one of your tinkering specialisation slots with a lesser version of a “specialisation” one of your clustermates holds in their own slots instead of randomly rolling for a new one (this works even if your clustermates version of that power doesn't manifest as a tinker power: the copy will be converted into something applicable for your power).

This mechanic can only be taken if at least one of your powers utilises some form of unique resources to begin with. Taking this ensures that your clustermates' variants of those powers will also manifest in such a way that they use, store and can collect some version of those resources.
objects.title: Communal Rolodex

objects.text: Your connected shards ensure a form of loyalty towards you from one of your cluster members. Master powers owned by you will permanently bind to selected members of the cluster (unless you possess Cluster Revolution), enhancing their loyalty. Optionally, you may decide for certain powers not to influence them.
objects.title: Authoritarian Cluster

objects.text: Every purchace increases the amount of people under the effect of your master power by one.
objects.title: Additional Authoritarian Effect

objects.text: It is, in some manner, possible to break free from the control shard imposed control.
objects.title: Cluster Revolution

objects.text: Your connected shards ensure a form of loyalty towards another member of your cluster, effecting a select amount of your cluster memebers. You are also under the effect of their master power.
objects.title: Authoritarian Cluster (Other)

objects.text: It is, in some manner, possible to break free from this control. You do not know how, but should be capable of figuring out how.
objects.title: Cluster Revolution (Other)

objects.text: Everyone in your cluster is affected by the perks and drawbacks you have chosen.
objects.title: In It Together

objects.text: Skills possessed by clustermates will mix, granting each member some of the abilities of each other member.
objects.title: Anything You Can Do

objects.text: The closer each member is to each other the stronger their powers are.
objects.title: Buddy System

objects.text: Other people all recognize each member of the cluster as the same person. You can identify yourself through codes and other such systems but your appearance and voice will never be enough.
objects.title: Identical Triplets

objects.text: The strength of each members powers shift across the course of the day. Everyday you will experience a full range from 0% to 200% strength.
objects.title: Early Bird Gets The Worm

objects.text: Cluster members that die appear as ghosts invisible to anyone but the cluster members. The same is true for sound.
objects.title: Haunted

objects.text: Portions of each member's personalities will be swapped randomly to the other members.
objects.title: Made For Each Other

objects.text: Your powers are such that they are far less effective on their own, but far more effective in tandem. If a member of the cluster dies your powers shift to not need them.
objects.title: C-C-C-Combo

objects.text: Each day each member of the cluster will teleport to the location of the clustermate next in the cycle.
objects.title: Get Out Of My Room

objects.text: You can't read each other's minds, but each member of your cluster understands how the others will react to different situations, and gets a gut feeling about secrets the others are keeping.
objects.title: We Finish Each Others...

objects.text: The powers of the cluster will all be from the same random power classification. i.e. all breakers.
objects.title: Team Theme

objects.text: You may choose the powers of each of your cluster members. You must abide by any other gimmicks you chose that regulate what powers they receive.
objects.title: Duck Duck

objects.text:
The powers in your cluster will tend to be stronger so long as the other members of the cluster are involved, “stretching” towards and intensifying around them. Striker powers will soften the requirements for their application, applying through clothes or even becoming short ranged instead of touch temporarily so long as it is to reach towards a clustermate, as well as having a stronger impact on whatever it hits; Shaker powers will have their ranges stretch and morph in the direction of them and their effects will be amplified in their immediate vicinity; Thinker powers will give headaches slower and grant greater detail about them & to a lesser extent anything around and/or connected them; in general powered effects will be stronger so long as a clustermate is the (or one of the primary) intended target(s), including partially bypassing their resistances/immunities (such as your perks).

Self-targeting powers aren't affected by this mechanic; the powers have to be targeted at another member of the cluster to get the boost.
objects.title: Arms Outstretched

objects.text:
You and your clustermates now gain an additional effect when near and far from each other, depending on your kiss/kill dynamic. 

If you or your clustermate have a kiss reaction to another clustermate, then being near them will make you and/or your clustermate feel comfortable and safe, while being far will make you and/or your clustermate feel anxious and uncomfortable.

If you or your clustermate have a kill reaction to another clustermate, then being near them will make you and/or your clustermate feel anxious and uncomfortable, while being far will make you and/or your clustermate feel comfortable and safe.
objects.title: Social Distancing

objects.text:
