With a single application, you can render metal immune to rust, make asphalt and concrete crackproof for centuries, and turn wood, plastic, or glass into weatherproof, shatter-resistant composites; you can also make advanced composite materials, such as variable-resistance semiconductors, near-perfect insulators of all types, pressure-sensitive foams, and custom lenses for a variety of purposes.

Furthermore, your ability dramatically improves the efficiency of mechanical systems by reducing friction and wear in moving parts, gears, and engines, enabling machinery to operate with near-frictionless precision and minimal maintenance.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, but especially well with (Tinker) Chemistry.
objects.title: (Tinker) Ruggedization

objects.text: You specialize in making equipment that works with/enhances a user’s usual capabilities. This ranges from making a taser gun powered by the user's electricity to respiratory augmentations that significantly improve the user's ability to hold their breath. This synergizes with the powers you have, making them better and easier to control with your Tinkertech. A user will be able to maintain and use Tinkertech built for them with proper training or manuals.
objects.title: (Tinker) Ergonomics

objects.text:
You specialize in pushing technology beyond its breaking point. Normally, your inventions appear modest or even underwhelming, but under high-pressure conditions or intense need, you can rapidly amplify their capabilities to extraordinary and destructive levels. Components hum, glow, and vibrate on the brink of self-destruction as your inventions deliver overwhelming performance—turning ordinary tools into engines of chaos.

While overclocking grants immense power, your equipment deteriorates as quickly as it gains strength, risking catastrophic meltdown and leaving behind molten wreckage and scorched battlefields.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, but especially well with (Tinker) Repair, (Tinker) Salvage and (Tinker) Ruggedization.
objects.title: (Tinker) Overclock

objects.text:
You specialize in Tinker technology centered around corpses and dead biological matter, enabling you to work with any suitably "dead" carbon-based organism, whether animal, plant or... human.

This specialisation allows you to reanimate corpses through various techniques. You can create puppet-like skeletons reinforced with mechanical frameworks, inject chemical agents to reactivate a corpse's biosystems or repair and replicate dead cells via specialised nanites.

You can produce a variety of "undead", from stereotypical zombies and skeletons to Frankensteinian monstrosities and vampire-like beings. You can build numerous enhancements into these corpses, making them far more powerful in death than in life, and combine bodies to form horrifying hybrids.

Your expertise extends beyond reanimation, covering post-mortem brain data extraction, grafting dead limbs to the living and numerous other corpse-based technologies. However, you’re limited by material condition: the more decomposed the tissue is, the less viable it becomes, with excessive decay rendering it useless. Any parahumans you reanimate retain their powers if their Corona Pollentia remains intact.
objects.title: (Tinker) Necromancer

objects.text:
You specialize in producing limited proof-of-concepts for more ambitious tinker projects, for a fraction of the time and materials. This smooths out Tinker cycles by letting you play with gimped versions of major megaprojects while the full versions are still out of reach. Data from these prototypes is incredibly useful for improving the eventual replacements, especially if tested in varied or extreme conditions, such as combat; and if the device is reasonably intact, it can be cannibalized for parts and labor when it's time to upgrade, all but eliminating the opportunity cost of the detour.

From ray-guns that can't reload to teleporters with long charge-ups and limited range, you decide which corners to cut and by how much, though you need a solid idea of what you're working toward (which must be within your capacity to build eventually).

This provides a wide-but-shallow repository of generic supertech, but shines alongside other tinker specialties. This is less useful if you can devote all week to perfecting your megaproject, but if not, it gives you something functional to use without delaying your long-term ambitions. It's especially useful with specialties that trade high time or resource costs for greater effectiveness, like (Tinker) Electromagnetism, giving you something functional during their long ramp-up periods.
objects.title: (Tinker) Rapid Prototyping

addons.title: Inception
addons.text: You can build devices that let you (and other users) enter dreams, at least virtually. This lets you probe and manipulate unconscious minds in particularly fine-tuned ways, such as implanting complex behaviors and triggers or inducing deep personality changes in only a single night. Basic applications can function across long distances, though the most insidious manipulations require you have physical access to the body of the individual whose mind you're invading. Be warned: although this can produce faster, subtler, and more complete effects than Dreamlife can on its own, the trade-off is that you're also subjecting yourself more completely to another's mind. This can be psychologically/neurologically hazardous, and can lead to unintended effects on the target, all depending on how deep an understanding you have (and how adept you are at navigating) your target's psyche.

objects.text: You specialize in sleep, dreams, and related mental states. Induce a dreaming coma where years feel like centuries, or impair the formation of long-term memories over a large area. Transmit thoughts and images to sleeping minds, or spy on the dreams of those you subject to your technology. Includes a minor Thinker power related to depth psychology and the interpretation of dreams.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Dreamlife

addons.title: Perfect Chimeras
addons.text: The divides between parts of your chimeras will slowly blur, positive traits from all pieces bleeding into each other. This ends with the chimera becoming an optimized hybrid of their component lifeforms. During this melding process, their body will easily adapt to your other Assimilation Tinkertech.

addons.title: Half Dead Chimeras
addons.text: Your ability to prevent transplant rejection in your creations has been adapted to your use of dead biological matter, freely integrating living and dead materials together without the worry of necrosis and other maladies.

objects.text:
You're a Tinker that can make chimeras, hybrids created from the parts of different creatures.

Your power makes you supernaturally skilled at transplanting organs. The properties of body parts you're connecting together are altered by your power, turning them into a form of biological Tinkertech that prevents transplant rejection.

The closer body parts are genetically, the less your power alters the organs, to the point where parts from the same species don't get altered at all. This means that, counterintuitively, transplant rejection is actually more likely to occur in more mundane transplants.
objects.title: (Tinker) Chimeric

objects.text: You can create sci-fi swords, halberds, spears, and other melee weapons. A sword made by you might be able to truly damage an Endbringer. If used by a Brute, it might even kill one... with a lucky hit.
objects.title: (Tinker) Swords

addons.text: Before, your ability to tinker was limited to just trees and their produce. Now your tinker specialisation has expanded to enable you to work similarly with any and all plant life along with their produce. You can make superconductive plant roots to channel electricity, bamboo and plant fibres tougher than steel, self-healing smart natural rubber, berries filled with meals worth of nutrients, toxin-filtering respirators using moss and so much more.
addons.title: Tinker of Nature

objects.text: You are a tinker that specializes in trees and their produce, you can make faster-growing acres, fire-proof paper armor, explosive charcoals, healing maple-syrup, wood shields harder than iron and many more!
objects.title: (Tinker) Lorax

objects.text: You can enhance others, granting them weaker versions of your tinker powers. While they cannot design anything by themselves, they can recreate and maintain anything you made. You can take away this boost at any time.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Assistant

objects.text: You specialize in tech involving speed and mobility. You can create jetpacks, suits that give the wearer super speed, and are generally capable of making things move faster.
objects.title: (Tinker) Speed

objects.text: You possess a Tinker specialty that creates and incorporates tinkertech into various forms of silk or silk-like materials. You can create anything related to clothing, such as color-changing cloaks, self-regenerating weaves, sticky webs, and so on. This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, as you can convert and compress them into clothing.
objects.title: (Tinker) Weaving

objects.text: Your Tinker power enables you to manipulate and fabricate memories. You can create devices that alter or implant memories in individuals, allowing for memory modification, erasure, or fabrication. These inventions can have profound implications in fields such as therapy, intelligence gathering, or even manipulation of adversaries.
objects.title: (Tinker) Memory Fabrication

objects.text: You have the ability to create shields, whether they are mobile, fixed, or personal. These shields can vary from those inspired by ancient civilizations (Romans, Greeks, etc.) to advanced forcefields or skintight variants. When connected to a potent energy source, they might even have the potential to withstand an attack from an Endbringer.
objects.title: (Tinker) Shields

objects.text: Your tinker-tech specializes in the phenomena of acoustics and vibrations, capable of constructing sonar radars able to picture cities, and acoustic cannons with both concussive and disorienting effects. Anything relating to sound and vibrational frequencies can be replicated through this.
objects.title: (Tinker) Sound/Vibration

objects.text: Your tinker specialty lies in the realm of virtual reality. Your tinker specialty lies in both the hardware and the software components of VR and AR, allowing you to create seamless virtual worlds that feel no different from reality. You will be able to create lifelike AI to populate your virtual creations; however, true AI will be out of your reach for a long time.
objects.title: (Tinker) Virtual Reality

objects.text:
Your Tinker specialization lies in Synchronicity: technology that works best when used/activated in concert with the occurrence of a predefined event. i.e. a shield that blocks attacks better if you’ve just provoked your attacker to speak; a set of mortars that work best when fired in sync or canon with each other to increase the spread of the destruction or maximize damage to the bombarded area; a crossbow that pierces through solid slabs of concrete when it's knocked and fired to an inbuilt beat, but is little better than a BB gun if operated too far off beat.

The efficacy of the tinkertech inversely scales to the controllability and commonality of the event it's synchronised to; becoming better the harder it is to time the use of the tinkertech to the event it's built for.

On its own, this Tinker specialization doesn't work well with electricity, instead being clockwork themed.
objects.title: (Tinker) Clockwork Precision

objects.text:
You specialize in precision, ensuring every gadget you build operates with absolute accuracy, stability, and reliability. Tolerances and margins of error are for others; you aim for perfection—down to the finest detail. Every gear meshes flawlessly, every circuit is calibrated to perfection, and every tool is built to perform at its peak, every time, with zero tolerance for errors.

Your creations accomplish feats of engineering accuracy that defy reason: your automated turrets hit bullseyes through dozens of ricochets, your chemical stations synthesize compounds or solutions exact down to the molecule, and your mechanical limbs are steady enough to paint the Mona Lisa on an electron cloud. However, this comes at a cost—your Tinkertech requires more time, resources and maintenance compared to most other Tinkers.

Your devices might lack raw firepower, but their efficiency, precision, and consistency make them the best choice for any situation that requires discretion.

This pairs exceedingly well with most other Tinker powers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Precision

objects.text:
You can manufacture circular filtering portals that separate things from other things and redirect them away. The portals themselves have no true physical existence, as they are simple two-dimensional spatial anomalies. Each portal is surrounded by a ring of machinery that is responsible for the creation and stability of the spatial portal. The portals can be any size, as long as they are completely contained within stabilizing machinery. For the same reason, moving a portal's location can be an ordeal.

The filtering for these portals can work with selectable specificity, meaning you can remove above or under a limit, singular types or a spectrum, matter and energies both. Metals from ore, UV-rays from sunlight, pollution from water, all can be removed, redirected and contained. Only the smaller portion can be transported away to a specific receptacle attached to the portal.

The portals work in two directions, removing things while the flow through them is one way, and adding things back from the input/output receptacle when the flow moves to the other direction. Either way, the flow becomes homogenous, as the portals equalize any incoming variance in their output.

Warning: as living beings normally can not survive being homogenized, travel through the portal is not recommended.
objects.title: (Tinker) Filter

addons.title: They're a Feature
addons.text: You specialty in Electromagnetism synergizes well with your Bugs, allowing you to easily work their properties into your Tinkertech. From devices powered by Bugs, to those controllable by a single Bug, and even ones that can supercharge your Bugs.

objects.text:
You specialize in the manipulation of electromagnetic fields, waves and currents. Your specialization is incredibly broad, allowing you to construct railguns, arc throwers, personal magnetic forcefields, mag-lev flight systems, electromagnetic lockpicks, and multispectral visors that allow you to see through walls via radio frequencies.

However, your creations are power hungry, and your specialization does not exactly include convenient ways of generating power, forcing you to siphon power off of the existing power grid via induction, or to carry oversized chemical batteries with you. Furthermore, your technology also has high material standards - a gadget made with high purity metals will both be much more powerful and last significantly longer than one made with scavenged copper or impure alloys.

All of this makes you a "Win-More" tinker: nearly unstoppable given a secure, well-funded workshop and access to the power grid, but forced into desperate, self-destructive tactics when cut off from civilization.
objects.title: (Tinker) Electromagnetism

objects.text:
This power grants a Tinker specialty revolving around resource gathering. Which might sound a bit boring but in practice means that once you have a half way decent setup you’ll never have to worry about resource shortages other Tinkers might suffer, at least when it comes to resources that can be found in regions you can harvest resources from.

The technology offered by this power offers a versatile array of options towards harvesting resources in various environments. But the focus for that harvesting is through the use of personal equipment, the kind a miner might use in a sci-fi setting.

So you can make things like handheld mining lasers that separate desired materials from what they’re pointed at and teleport them up to thousands of meters away into a connected container, or a water filtration system able to ensure pure drinking water from even the most polluted sources.

Another example could be making power armor, with advanced sensors capable of locating desired materials through hundreds of meters of earth and moving hundreds of tons of useless rock out of the way.

Of course like other Tinkers you can experiment to make technology that diverges from your specialty especially for combat such as the construction of weapons and armor. 

However, given that this power touches little on combat, the idiosyncrasies of its specialty will be apparent in such Tinkertech, for good and ill. 

An example of this could be that power armor you could build being able to easily support and move hundreds of tons making carrying heavy weaponry or feats of raw brute strength easy, but be relatively frail compared to the power armor of a combat focused Tinker who has a similar level of resources and development to you.

A second example could be those laser tools you make could be designed to ignore organic matter, making them perfect for disabling the equipment of any opponent, but as it was based off a mining tool it is relatively short range with a massive drop off in effectiveness beyond a few feet.
objects.title: (Tinker) Resource Exploitation

addons.text: You can create vehicles that contain entire civic and commercial services. This can include ambulances that contain high-tech clinics, school buses that hold several spacious classrooms, taco trucks that expand into entire food courts, and news copters with full studios and broadcast stations. Mega big rigs can carry municipal infrastructure such as power, garbage collection, factories and trade docks, as well as public spaces like parks, apartment blocks and malls. Entire fleets of vehicles you create can function together as an urban whole whether parked or on the move. They can be equipped with guidance systems that allow them to move, dock, and split off together without crashing into or running over eachother. Special rovers and connectors allow utility service to be distributed across a fleet without slowing down, while ramps, walkways and carts can be deployed to easily traverse across several moving vehicles in a fleet. With Red Line you can coordinate an entire moving nation of mobile cities. Infrastructure like highways, pipelines, bastions and power stations can be made to sprout wheels or rotors to follow the cities they connect, while entire croplands, mines, seaports and natural landmarks can be dug up to be put on rolling platforms. You can also plan routes and networks that allow mobile cities and infrastructure to move freely without crushing everything else that isn’t on wheels.
addons.title: Nomadic City

objects.text:
You specialize in mobile homes and RVs, the chosen vehicle of people who can’t afford an actual home (you) and the rich. Trailers and caravans that can be pulled by nearly any vehicle and placed just about anywhere, motorhomes for that genuine home-on-the-road feel, campers for those who want to sleep under the stars for a week but just can’t leave home behind, the whole shebang is yours to design and create.

You have a knack for interior design when it comes to homes in general, but especially those built into vehicles. You can create incredible motorhomes with all the amenities a person would need: living areas, bathrooms, kitchens, bedrooms, and more. The interiors you design can be highly unique, but they must always be livable, a person has to be able to live in them comfortably for extended periods of time.

You are not limited to simple four-wheeled or land-based vehicles. As long as the interior is livable, comfortable, and capable of movement, you can design it. A submarine that lets its occupants safely explore the depths while living inside, possible. An airship spacious enough for a family of eight to live in comfortably, doable. Even a vessel capable of traveling through space, protecting its inhabitants from the horrors of the void while they sleep under the stars, closer than most people ever will. Unfortunately, FTL is not included. You’ll need another Tinker power for that.

You can also redesign existing vehicles to make them far more comfortable for everyone inside, turning even long, miserable trips into something manageable, maybe even pleasant.

Ride on and relax. It’s a breeze from here.
objects.title: (Tinker) Home on the Road

objects.text:
While awake you only have normal access to your Tinker powers. But if you happen to sleep in your lab or even just around adequate supplies, you will dream. 

Except for the fact you will be guaranteed to have them in those scenarios these will be regular dreams. The catch however is that during those dreams your body will begin to sleepwalk and build a random piece of Tinker-tech based around the dreams you were having. This Tinker-tech will be far more advanced and powerful compared to your waking efforts.

As an example, if you have Tinker powers centered on enhancing the physical capabilities of living beings but normally your best work can only compare to the average Brute, then a dream about eating food can lead your sleeping self to make a candy that when eaten temporarily grants a Brute rating of 10. Which for context is comparable to Behemoth.

You are perfectly capable of maintaining, repairing, and even modifying technology you built while asleep so long as it isn’t destroyed beyond repair. However the more you modify that technology away from the design you made while asleep the simpler and weaker it will become until it’s just like the tinkertech you can make while awake.
objects.title: (Tinker) Dream Craft

objects.text:
You specialize in watercraft of various kinds. This includes canoes, caravels, submarines, hydrofoils, and so on.

A dreadnought built by you could sail through Leviathan’s storm on his home turf without sinking.
objects.title: (Tinker) I’m On a Boat

addons.text:
Your Tinker speciality no longer draws solely from mundane human martial arts. The kinetic blueprints generated by (Thinker/Striker) Martial Arts is now integrated into your Tinker library as valid source material. This means the physics-cheating combat instructions your Shard installs into your muscle memory can also be reverse engineered, iterated upon, and embedded into technology.

The training robots you build now execute shard generated kinetic sequences, their limbs generating impossible force and their joints ignoring leverage constraints. Skill chips can establish a temporary uplink that lets the recipient gain the  shard assisted combat instructions, allowing them to perform the unlearnable katas they could never replicate through practice. Your cybernetics and bio mods serve as bridge components, limbs reinforced to survive the recoil of technique generated overforce, or supplementary nervous systems that interpret kinetic blueprint data without requiring the user to enter a true fugue state. Your Tinker power can also refine the styles, using your hyper accelerated design cognition to evolve a techniques into a more advanced variant, then feed it back into your own combat library for personal use.
addons.title: Martial Arts Sensei

objects.text:
You are a Tinker whose specialty revolves around martial arts, giving you a preternatural skill in the creation and application of martial arts. Essentially a minute of contemplation on ways to develop martial arts from you is equivalent to years of hard work from a normal black belt or equivalent expert. 

But you also have a decent amount of versatility in the technology you can create as a Tinker, all themed around either teaching martial arts, or facilitating the use of martial arts. A few examples could be putting together training programs designed to teach combat in various environments, making robots that act as training partners, skill chips to implant skills into a recipient's brain, medicine to ease recovery from injury, supplements to aid training, light cybernetics and bio mods that barely brush past peak human capabilities.

Synergy with other Tinker powers is possible, but mostly revolving around integrating the technology you can make into martial arts.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Martial Arts

addons.title: Build to Last
addons.text:
Your creations are built to outlast you. Reinforced materials, fault tolerance, and designs meant for other hands come together into a single philosophy: technology that never quits, and no longer needs your personal attention to keep working.

Your tech is more reliable than ever. Fault tolerance is no longer a feature layered on top but part of how every piece is designed. Failures don't cascade, damaged systems reroute around the loss, and a device that should be scrap degrades gracefully instead of dying outright. Left alone, it simply endures. Seal a machine in a bunker, sink it in a swamp, or abandon it in a field for three hundred years, and it will power on when someone finally finds it, its seals intact, its lubricants unspoiled, its circuits free of corrosion.

Most importantly, your tech no longer needs a Tinker to keep running. Components are standardized, interchangeable, clearly laid out, and nearly impossible to fit together wrong. Anyone with basic mechanical sense and ordinary tools can assemble your devices from a kit, learn to operate them in minutes, and keep them running indefinitely.

Finally, while fabricating true Tinkertech spare parts from scratch remains beyond mundane science, your technology is exceptionally forgiving: if a part is lost or damaged, any conventional, non-Tinker equivalent can be fitted in as a substitute at only a marginal cost to overall performance. A village mechanic can keep your water purifier running for generations on junkyard plumbing and car batteries, and a soldier can patch your rifle with hardware-store springs.

objects.text:
You specialize in creating fault-tolerant Tinkertech devices that can withstand extensive damage or component loss. An opponent can blast a hole clean through the chassis, rip out the wiring, and detonate the power cell, and yet the device will keep working on whatever residual charge remains in its surviving circuitry.

Your tech is also built to withstand environmental dangers such as EMPs, deep submersion, and extreme radiation, remaining functional until literally ground down into individual screws. So long as a recognizable fragment remains, it is safe to assume that it's operational.
objects.title: (Tinker) Redundancy

objects.text: You have a Tinker specialization focused on traps, with the ability to create complex and destructive devices with anomalous effects, such as landmines that erase everything within its radius, or simple objects made to surprise people. You also have a minor specialization in hiding your creations in plain sight and a minor Thinker power focused on strategic positioning. These powers enable you to strategically place your traps, keeping adversaries off balance and increasing your chances of success in battles.
objects.title: (Tinker) Traps

objects.text:
You have the power to improve one aspect of tinkertech, whether it be the durability, functionality, or utility, to an incredible degree, but this will come at a price, with every other aspect of the piece degrading to almost unusable levels. With this power, you can create hyper-specialized technology, able to do one thing to a level of mastery, but falling short when trying to perform any other function.

Whether it's building a machine that can lift a hundred tons but breaks at a gust of wind, or building a computer that can process a million times more data per second than the current supercomputers but has no memory to store the data, you have the ability to create machines that can exceed anything ever created before, with one caveat: they have to excel at only one thing at the cost of failing at everything else.
objects.title: (Tinker) Hyperspecialized

addons.title: Hotswap
addons.text:
The slots and hardpoints on your chassis become even more modular. You can create smaller slots around your hardpoints that dedicated submodules can be inserted into to further enhance their transformations. The transformation process also becomes faster and smoother so that you can switch out inserted tech on the fly.

You can create cartridges that other tinkers and tinker powers can work technology into, that do not do anything on their own but will fit into slots to create much smoother and more powerful specialized modes than if it were randomly acquired tinkertech.
You also gain the ability to bodge slots directly onto objects and tinkertech that you did not make, though the transformations will be cruder and jankier than if it were a dedicated chassis.

objects.text:
You can create many types of basic devices, such as vehicles, robots, or weapons. These devices are somewhat larger than usual, while having very unremarkable capabilities for tinkertech. However, they have slots that other tinkertech can be inserted, after which they will reconfigure and transform to gain capabilities based on the inserted tinkertech.

For example, a plasma rifle made by you can take an electro-tinker’s tesla coil and gain the ability to shoot a 500 Gigawatt beam. You could put a tinkertech diving suit into a truck to cause it to transform into an amphibious submersible. Placing a biotinker’s med-scanner into a supercomputer would install programs that could track health and sickness in an entire city.

By default, this does not allow you to create tinkertech that can be slotted in, unless you have other Tinker specializations, especially broad modular ones like (Tinker) Add-On Augmentation and (Tinker) Basic Tinker
objects.title: (Tinker) Chassis

objects.text: You create technology that interacts with emotions. This can manifest in two different ways. The first is technology that detects and manipulates emotions. The second is technology that is powered by emotions. For the latter, the type of emotions used to power the device can affect its effectiveness. An offensive weapon may be better powered by negative emotions, while a healing device may be better powered by positive emotions. Artificial emotions gained from direct power use or tinkertech have reduced or zero effects when powering your devices. Indirect methods, such as illusions, don't have such restrictions.
objects.title: (Tinker) Emotions

objects.text: Your expertise lies in the realm of software and programming. You possess unparalleled skills in designing and developing complex software systems, hacking tools, and programs. With the right materials, you can create powerful software applications that can analyze vast amounts of data, infiltrate secure networks, or control robotic systems. Your creations can range from sophisticated cybersecurity algorithms, artificial data generation, and advanced virtual reality simulations. This power synergizes well with other Tinker abilities, allowing you to integrate software seamlessly into Tinkertech.
objects.title: (Tinker) Software

objects.text: You specialize in quantum computers and other forms of highly advanced calculations. You can create Tinkertech that can simulate the past and future, and connect the dots to create detailed, informative guesses. The better and more accurate information you feed into them, the better you can simulate various kinds of things. This pairs especially well with (Tinker) Software and (Tinker) Code.
objects.title: (Tinker) Quantum Computing

addons.text:
When you speak, you can choose to disguise your speech under layers of coded words and ciphers that you have created, while letting the people you address your speech towards be able to understand and replicate this speech. For example, when you say 'Let's flank them', while your allies will understand you, anybody listening in might hear the complete opposite, in reverse, and in Morse code within the same timespan as you speaking.

You and the people who learn your codes will not suffer any disorientation when speaking in code, and will find encrypting messages into this code as instinctive as speaking their native language. However, the people you share your code with cannot do the same towards others, meaning that if they're with strangers, they'll just be speaking without anybody understanding.
addons.title: 3|\|6|_|5|-| Motherfucker, Do You Speak It!?

objects.text: With this power, you possess the remarkable ability to safeguard information, unravel ciphers, and more, while also granting you the capacity to black box any device, rendering it impervious to reverse engineering and preserving its inner workings as an impenetrable enigma to others.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Encryption

objects.text: You specialize in Illusion-based technology, where you excel at utilizing holograms, sound systems, and even manipulating the senses to create a vast array of illusions. Your abilities allow you to craft incredibly convincing and immersive displays that can have a profound impact on your audience. Whether through sound, visuals, or a combination of both, your illusions are sure to leave a lasting impression on those who witness them.
objects.title: (Tinker) Illusion

objects.text: You can disguise your tinkertech in a wide variety of ways that obscure it from various forms of detection. It can pretend to be something harmless when it's actually something dangerous. Even when disassembled, it can not only still work, but it can also fool other Tinkers and Thinkers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Camouflage

addons.text: You don’t just counter enemy tinkertech – you corrupt it from within. Your expertise in neutralizing technology now extends to subverting it entirely. By creating specialized add-ons, you build mechanical parasites that infiltrate enemy tech, latching onto critical components and making themselves nearly impossible to remove. These enhancements disguise themselves as harmless optimizations while subtly sabotaging functions, overriding safeguards, and even rewriting operational parameters. Given time and several add-ons, you could turn an enemy’s greatest creation into your own weapon.
addons.title: Malicious Augmentation

objects.text: You are a Tinker who specializes in countering other tinkers. You can create devices that locate and modify tinkertech, disguise it as other tinkertech, and even bypass tinkertech safeguards. You also gain a minor specialization, which changes to be the optimal counter to any tinker specialization of your choosing. It takes an hour to change your minor specialization.
objects.title: (Tinker) Counter-Tech

objects.text: Your Tinker power allows you to create specialized add-ons and enhancements for existing Tinkertech devices, seamlessly integrating them to optimize functionality, push the boundaries of technology, and become a valuable asset in any tinker collaboration by expanding the group's technological arsenal.
objects.title: (Tinker) Add-On Augmentation

objects.text:
You are a wizard in the lab. You have the skills to create new materials, from super-alloys to acids to explosives to superconductors and beyond.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Chemistry

objects.text: You can create tinkertech that has Manton Limits, preventing powers from directly influencing your tinkertech. With greater research into your specialty, you can even create things that block out powerful technopathy, anti-machine powers or devices.
objects.title: (Tinker) Manton Limits

addons.title: Runes
addons.text:
You can design hyper-efficient microcircuitry that produces esoteric effects merely by being powered or interacted with. Things like a thin layer of microcapacitors that absorb kinetic energy when struck, or dense designs that counteract gravity when powered at particular frequencies. In addition to being useful on their own, these circuits pack tremendous power and versatility in paper-thin layers, making fantastic internal components.

This synergizes well with "Turing-Machine" and Tinker powers that let you power devices with energies other than electricity, since more esoteric energies can produce more diverse effects.

objects.text:
A techie's best friend, your skills with electronics are unparalleled. With the right materials, you could make a supercomputer the size of a smartphone.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers, especially (Tinker) Mechanics.
objects.title: (Tinker) Electronics

objects.text:
You are a tinker specialized in detainment, compliance, and, most of all, punishment. Capable of creating “housing” structures that caged any type of prisoner, elaborate tailor-made cells for a particular type of parahuman or paranatural entity, you also fashion any paraphernalia or bondage to keep anyone compliant or simply docile enough to obey orders or assignments. Suppose this compliance isn’t sufficient for the poor schmuck. In that case, you can build any device, contingency, or feature in your project to dish out a penalty or punishment against disobedience or rebellion.

Amidst all the unpleasant implications, it mostly depends on how you apply this specialty, for all that it entails.
objects.title: (Tinker) Imprisonment

objects.text:
This specialty involves the understanding, replication, and manipulation of human genetics and physiology. To this end, various types of technology revolving around cloning, genetic engineering, surgery, and medicine are available to you, all of which are specialized for use on humans and human genetics.

A few examples of things you could do include turning animals and plants into human hybrids, integrate animal and plant DNA into a human’s genetic structure, make artificial organs for a human, cure any mundane ailment a human can suffer, and enhance a human to be comparable to a low grade Brute, Mover, and Thinker through pure physical ability.
objects.title: (Tinker) Oh, the Humanity

objects.text:
Your tinker speciality is a grim and purposeful art: the creation of killing machines. 

You construct overly complex and overbuilt killing machines using primitive, outdated technology and the poorest quality materials available. Each device is a single-purpose instrument, engineered not just to kill, but to kill in a specific, often theatrical, manner. Instead of guns, you build guillotines. Instead of traps, you build iron maidens and pendulum blades.

Your focus is on categorizing and inflicting distinct forms of death. One device may be designed solely for precise beheading, another for systematic exsanguination, and another for slow compression or piercing. Your technology favors direct, physical intervention over energy weapons or subtlety, relying on gears, counterweights, rusty iron, and sharpened steel. As long as it was made to kill in particular gruesome ways and doesn’t used overly advanced technology, anything can be build, from automatons to vehicles.

Despite its crude and brutalist construction, the sheer mechanical redundancy and over-engineering render your devices unnaturally robust and potent, allowing a massive spring-powered spear launcher to match the range and piercing power of a fellow Tinker's railgun, or a clockwork automaton to grapple with a powered armor suit. However, this comes at the cost of any practicality; your creations are labyrinthine tangles of levers, exposed mechanisms, and idiosyncratic controls, making them hopelessly unwieldy and dangerously unpredictable for anyone but you to operate. 

The archaic technology and shoddy materials demand constant, grueling maintenance, more so than other tinkertech. Due to its overbuilt design, such maintenance is near impossible as well. Luckily, through function, your tinkertech can maintain and even make lesser repairs itself. A blade being used to behead will not dull, a gear train that drives a crushing press will not wear, and rust will not spread so long as the device is periodically used to fulfill its lethal purpose, no matter if it’s not cleaned. The act of killing cleanses, sharpens, and repairs your tinkertech. This doesn’t improve your tech in any way, merely fulfils the act of maintenance.
objects.title: (Tinker) Murder

objects.text:
Your tinker specialization is, in a somewhat broad sense: technology able to increase a person's capabilities. This technology, on a more mundane level, can indeed include gym equipment, weights, etc. In fact, you can go to your local gym and augment any equipment yourself.

But on the higher end, you could have weighted clothing that weighs upward of a few hundred kilos, exercise equipment that detect the users bio-signs and adapt to make the workout harder, and even certain drugs that can temporarily stop your physical growth in exchange for an even greater strength boost once its effects "wear off." Your average joe could go from being able to bench press 200 pounds, to being confused for a lower end Brute and Mover even if they don't have superpowers.

However, when it comes to powers, it isn't nearly as fast as (Tinker) Amplifiers and Dampeners, since this focuses more on the physical.

This works very well with other Tinker specialties, like (Tinker) Density, (Tinker) Amplifiers and Dampeners, and (Tinker) Refinement.
objects.title: (Tinker) Workout

objects.text:
You're a Tinker specialized in working and living underground.

You can create both personal mining equipment and larger boring machines. From lightweight exoskeletons equipped with rock splitters, to massive drilling rigs, you can produce machines which dig through the earth with ease.

Digging randomly underground is dangerous. Luckily, you can make devices that scan and map the depths. This includes ground-penetrating radar systems and advanced surveying equipment, revealing objects, materials, and structures hidden beneath the surface.

To facilitate long-term subterranean survival, you're able to construct some buildings. For instance, you could build compact hydroponic or mushroom farms, oxygen scrubbers and support structures.
objects.title: (Tinker) Subterranean

addons.text:
Your bodies can now contain powers through technology or biological modification that acts as a pseudo-Corona Pollentia, where previously they only housed your consciousness.

This would imply a wide range of uses you can give to your customized bodies in addition to the capabilities you have granted them with your Tinker specialty. Furthermore, they will be able to create their own network through which they can share the same source of their powers.

You still retain the limitation of controlling only one body at a time. However, if you alter your own brain/mind or that of others through the Neurology specialty, you could acquire what is necessary to function as a hive mind.

Lastly, the variety of bodies you can inhabit has expanded thanks to the Neurology specialty allowing you to adapt your consciousness into non-humanoid bodies, such as extra limbs, quadrupedal bodies, alien bodies, or even stranger forms that stray far from any human notion.
addons.title: Power Transfer

objects.text:
You specialize in the creation of bodies that you can remotely control, transfer consciousness into either permanently or temporarily, or introduce a copy of the original consciousness into. Such bodies can be made from virtually anything.

They can be perfect clones of yourself or any individual and controlled accordingly. Or you can create an android built in such a way that it is difficult to distinguish from a human being. You could even interact with a virtual/cybernetic worlds if they exist, creating a virtual body capable of navigating and interacting with them. It can be any body you wish to inhabit.

Your specialty comes with a broad range of highly generalized technological trees, enough to allow you to make any type of modification you desire to the bodies you create, both in appearance and in the capabilities you can grant them. However, you will never surpass highly specialized fields such as (Tinker) Communication or any specialty you attempt to compete with directly.

Keep in mind that you are only capable of controlling one body at a time, and the same applies to anyone who wishes to transfer themselves into another body. Unless you possess multitasking capabilities or some special condition that allows you to generate a hive mind. A good measure to overcome this limitation would be to grant them AI, though whether they are loyal or not would depend on their programming.

You cannot apply this specialty to yourself or others only to the bodies you create. If you chose Shardless, your bodies will be able to house your powers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Avatar

objects.text: You can create advanced guns, though nothing that can't be transported by a non-Brute person. If you gave a Sniper Rifle you've made enough time to charge—say about 10 minutes—you could probably damage an Endbringer's core. Unfortunately, that means you'd have to charge your Sniper Rifle before the Endbringer battle, and you'd only have one shot. You'd also have to know where the core was, and the Endbringer might be able to dodge it even if you aimed correctly.
objects.title: (Tinker) Guns

objects.text:
You have the skills of a master mechanic. You can design and effectively make any mechanical device—from precision timepieces to clockwork soldiers to pneumatic rifles to hydraulic battering rams. Anything that relies on purely mechanical power, you can build.

This power works best when paired with other Tinker powers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Mechanics

objects.text: You specialize in tech involving various forms of gravity and weight. You can create devices that are heavier or lighter than they should be, beams that change the gravity of whoever is hit, and fly.
objects.title: (Tinker) Gravity

objects.text: You have a Tinker specialty working with water. You can create all kinds of hydrokinetic machines and devices powered by water, or even anti-water machines. This can range from containers that store more liquids than they normally can to devices that repel all water in a large radius. This can even trump Leviathan's control over water.
objects.title: (Tinker) Nautical

objects.text: You possess a Tinker specialty working with various kinds of gases and air. You can create air cannons, air-based jetpacks, windmills, and other things that utilize air. This includes gas-based chemical weapons and other things that spread through the air.
objects.title: (Tinker) Aero

objects.text: You possess a Tinker specialty that works with and controls thermal energy. You can create devices that can flash freeze entire areas, flamethrowers that set even concrete on fire, and jetpacks. Essentially, you can create anything that involves the increase or decrease of various temperatures or anything that involves generating heat or cold.
objects.title: (Tinker) Thermal

objects.text:
You possess a specialty in terrestrial, seismic, and volcanic phenomena. You can create a worldwide seismic wave emitter inducing localized quakes and faults, as well as a seismic wave dampener to promptly mitigate them. You can fashion the manufacturing, elaboration, and utilization of minerals and metals capable of different properties, the advantage of using volcanic material or any substance within the Earth’s substructure as a form of energy fuel to power your creations, and think of projects capable of subverting the Earth’s tectonic fields.

Essentially, you can create anything involving the Earth’s structure and all that is tangentially related to a lesser degree. This can trump Behemoth’s volcanic eruptions.
objects.title: (Tinker) Terra

objects.text: You can create advanced armor of various kinds. A set of power armor made by you might be able to shrug off a hit from an Endbringer.
objects.title: (Tinker) Armor

objects.text:
When it comes to Tinkering, it’s not all about functionality—aesthetics can play a critical role in the effectiveness of your devices. With your power, you can improve the performance of your tinkertech by making it more visually appealing.

Additionally, you have an innate sense of style and design, allowing you to instinctively craft technology that is stylish. This makes it so that everything you create is exclusively good-looking, making even the most utilitarian gadgets visually striking.

This pairs well with other Tinker powers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Style

addons.text:
You can breathe life into any toy you make. This has two modes—passive and active.

Passive mode simply makes them animated and grants them intelligence. This drains a set amount of stamina the first time it is activated. The amount of stamina is dependent on the complexity and size of the toy. An electronic toy will cost more stamina in comparison to a doll-like toy.

Active mode drains your stamina at a constant rate when active. The amount of stamina is similarly dependent on the complexity and size of the toy. In active mode, your toys grow and gain additional abilities based on their build, type of toy, and base materials. Any ability it already has is boosted in this mode. For example, a Mr Potato Head can freely detach, create and control limbs at will.

You will have a passive awareness of all toys you are connected to, allowing you to have any toy enter active mode regardless of how far away it is from you.
addons.title: Toys Story

objects.text:
You specialize in the creation of tinkertech centered around the concept of 'toys'. You can construct a wide range of tinkertech oriented around this theme; miniature action figures that can move and fight, weaponised bladed yo-yos, huge toy robots able to fight Brutes, toy guns with lethal effects, explosive marble grenades, remote-controlled toy drones, decryption devices in the style of a Rubik's Cube and more.

From implementing existing technology into toys to improving toy designs to be unbelievably efficient and effective, there are few limits to what you can build under this theme. This pairs very well with (Tinker) Electronics and (Tinker) Mechanics.
objects.title: (Tinker) Toyman

objects.text:
You have a tinker specialization in the creation and manipulation of “technological seeds”. These seeds do nothing initially, but they will mutate over time to become various pieces of technology, gaining random modifiers to their existing functions or even entirely new features (their very first mutation will always be gaining some kind of feature, which will influence the chances of all future mutations).

Your tinker specialization gives you the tools to manipulate the growth of your seeds, including speeding up the rate of mutation; encouraging and discouraging them to/from certain types of mutations; and pruning away any unwanted mutations that have occurred (although you cannot choose to keep only part of a mutation, so if a mutation manifested as a positive & a negative, you would be removing the positive alongside the negative if you chose to remove it).

With sufficient time, resources, and the right string of mutations, you could hypothetically grow tinkertech from any tinkers tech tree as effectively as the tinkers themselves.

This synergizes well with other Tinker powers, as they will give you the ability to heavily influence the mutations in the direction of your other specializations, allowing you to produce tech for those trees cheaper than building them directly, although at the cost of potentially having to spend a long time pruning mutations to get the fine details you may desire.
objects.title: (Tinker) Bonsai

objects.text:
You know that sci-fi trope of describing something as energy-infused to say it’s stronger and more capable than it normally would be? Yeah, this Tinker specialty revolves around that concept.

You can create items—handheld consumables—that infuse strange types of energy into whatever you desire.

These energy infusions are usually temporary buffs that can do things like increase structural integrity and defense, impart heat, kinetic energy, electricity, repair damage, etc. The sky’s the limit as all sorts of useful buffs are at your disposal.

For a few examples, the average energy infusion will last around a minute while being capable of increasing the defensive capabilities of a modern tank tenfold, or being capable of enhancing an iron sword to cut through bank vaults like warm butter, and that’s before you consider any strange or esoteric capabilities you added to the energy infusion.

But you aren’t limited to just temporary enhancements; you can create generators that can be integrated into items and will continuously release a desired type of energy into them so long as it has power.

Finally, this specialty grants a minor focus of its techbase on metallurgy and general engineering, so you can create personal equipment such as weapons and armor to infuse.
objects.title: (Tinker) Infusionist

objects.text:
You are a wide-reaching tinker whose specialization revolves entirely around backpacks. Anything you create or design must be capable of fitting inside a backpack and supporting its weight in such a way that the user can carry and operate it without issue. This restriction applies across all types and sizes of backpacks.

This can range from a functional, controllable jetpack that allows you to fly, to a backpack from which multiple tentacles emerge, ending in human-like hands or equipped tools designed for multitasking.
objects.title: (Tinker) Backpack

objects.text:
You build compact, palm-sized spawner devices that are easy to fuel using ambient energy sources like solar, thermal, or kinetic input, making them highly energy-efficient during operation. They require regular hands-on maintenance to prevent drift and component degradation, as with any tinkertech, but their low power draw means a single device can run for weeks between refuels under normal conditions.

When activated, a spawner saturates a designated area with a non-reactive energy that poses no danger to ambient matter or people, and its range scales upward based on how much fuel you supply. This energy within that saturated area automatically coalesces and stabilises into solid entities without further input from you. You can choose to concentrate the energy into fewer, stronger entities or spread it thinly for larger numbers of weaker ones, at your discretion.

The resulting entities follow a detailed but script-like behavioral program that can be mistaken for animal intelligence, lacking true adaptability or learning, though the script can be extensive enough to mimic basic threat assessment and patrolling. When an entity dies inside its spawn area, its form disperses safely and returns to the ambient energy field, reforming after a cooldown of at least one hour that increases with the entity's strength, with no maximum upper limit. Death outside the spawn area causes permanent destruction with no respawn, taking longer to replace.

Before spawning, you set each entity's form, abilities, and behaviors via the device's controls, but you have no influence over them after they spawn unless you specifically built a loyalty protocol into that preset script. You can place multiple spawners in the same area to produce different creature types simultaneously.
objects.title: (Tinker/Master) Spawners

objects.text:
You build devices that emit a directed, short-range radiation harmless to ordinary humans but debilitating to certain parahumans, with each device calibrated during construction to exploit specific vulnerabilities in how a target's power operates at a fundamental physics level.

When building a device, you select three targeting parameters: function (the underlying mechanism, like dimensional folding or quantum locking), appearance (the observable expression, such as Alexandria packages or pyrokinesis), and match purity (how exclusively the target's power aligns with your first two choices; a pure match suffers full drain, while additional unrelated abilities reduce effectiveness). For example, you build a device set to the function to gravity manipulation and its appearance to Alexandria package. A target whose power is purely an Alexandria package driven by gravity manipulation suffers full drain. However, a cape who also flies via gravity manipulation but additionally has laser eyes (different appearance) automatically matches less on purity, so the radiation weakens. Similarly, a cape who flies via telekinesis (different function) despite looking like an Alexandria package also cases the radiation to weaken.

The radiation manifests as a colored glow unique to the target type, and within its limited range it saps strength, coordination, and power reliability, but disperses harmlessly beyond that range.

Improving your power expands the device's effective radius and allows broader targeting parameters. For example, a wide targeting like “all Brutes” requires a larger, hungrier device and delivers weaker radiation than a narrow “gravity-manipulating Strikers with no flight.”
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Kryptonite

objects.text: You are a Tinker specializing in robotics. Unless you put in a significant amount of work, your robots won't have more than a simple AI (relative to something like Dragon), but they're perfectly capable in the role they were designed for. You are capable of programming your robots to function autonomously for some time.
objects.title: (Tinker) Robots

objects.text:
You are a Tinker specializing in altering the composition and properties of blood, allowing it to exhibit a range of anomalous effects. You can make blood that enhances physical abilities when consumed, accelerates healing when injected, or even grants temporary powers through direct absorption. Additionally, you can enhance mundane objects using blood as a primary material, either by infusing them with specialised properties through prolonged contact or repurposing blood as a form of ammunition.

Your expertise extends into biotinkering, granting you the ability to modify or engineer living organisms to naturally produce your altered blood. This allows you to create custom-built creatures, symbiotic organisms, or even modified humans capable of sustaining and distributing your specialised blood. 

Be ready to smell like you just committed a bloody massacre.
objects.title: (Tinker) Bloody Tinker

objects.text:
You don't create cars that drive on wheels or float, or even drive at all. Your cars are able to spin their way to any destination, at blazing speeds.

What about a gun? Well, this gun doesn't even shoot. Instead, it calls upon a strike of lightning! Regardless, your 'specialization' is utterly absurd. Your inventions do completely ridiculous things instead of what they're meant to do.

A tank that uses its barrel to fly into the air? Why not. A sword that can spin, the rotational force causing it to fire 9mm parabellum? Sure. How about a generator that reduces power instead? Okay. It's all there.
objects.title: (Tinker) Absurdity

objects.text: You specialize in creating tinkertech that transforms Energy into Mass and vice versa. You can create highly condensed energy batteries that can construct and deconstruct blueprints on the fly. This Tinker specialty is heavily Energy-dependent, but so long as it has Energy, it can constantly repair and reconstruct itself. This Tinker specialty pairs well with other Tinker powers, but especially (Tinker) Energy.
objects.title: (Tinker) E=MC²

objects.text: You are a Tinker specializing in all things crystals. A few examples of what you can accomplish are things like crystal super computer cores, and crystal lenses that make making laser weapons easy. Beyond the various kinds of technology you can make are also crystals that have special properties, like elemental crystals that can be used to manipulate classical fantasy elements with the proper setup.
objects.title: (Tinker) Crystals!

objects.text: You can build intricate machines that emulate the features of living beings. They are just as effective, if not more so, than their biological counterparts and can be programmed with semi-advanced AI to perform tasks with precision and accuracy. For instance, you can construct a device that camouflages the wearer, mimicking the properties of a chameleon, allowing them to disappear from sight.
objects.title: (Tinker) Bio-Mimicry

objects.text: You can create complex, biological machines that can be programmed using custom-designed chemical compounds. These creatures can perform a wide range of tasks and can be programmed with intricate logic, making them just as advanced as any mechanical contraption. An example of this technology could be a firearm made from flesh and bone that fires pressurized jets of blood.
objects.title: (Tinker) Living Machine

objects.text: You specialize in the creation of preservation-based technology. With this technology, you can preserve objects and life forms, allowing them to ignore the effects of time. Using it on food stuff would make it so that the food will never expire. On living creatures, it can keep them alive. On objects, it can keep them from breaking down. With time, a recreation of Alexandria’s stasis effect is possible. In a crueler method, it is possible to keep people alive in a similar state to Mannequin.
objects.title: (Tinker) Preservation

objects.text: You specialize in creating non-intelligent biological creatures that specialize in augmenting other biological creatures. These symbiotic relationships can be mutualistic, parasitic or commensalistic in nature. Examples include a living mech suit that acts as power armor, a leech-like parasite that warps its host’s mind or a virus that grants those it infects boosted physical capabilities.
objects.title: (Tinker) Symbiote

addons.text:
Your machines no longer just shift between different modes, nor are they simply modular in isolation. Now, every device you create has its own unique mode, but all of them are inherently compatible with each other, allowing them to connect, fuse, and integrate to form new hybrid devices.

Each piece of technology you build follows the same core principles as before—every device has a specific mode it can shift into, like a gun that transforms into a scythe or a shield that expands into a giant fan. However, now these devices can merge while in their active modes, creating entirely new constructs with combined capabilities. The outcome of each fusion depends on the modes involved at the time of merging. A gun in sniper mode, combined with a fan in wind-generator mode, might result in a railgun that fires air-compressed projectiles at extreme speeds, while that same gun in shotgun mode merging with the fan would instead create a scattergun that launches razor-sharp wind slashes.

These fused devices remain stable as long as needed but can also separate, shift into different modes, and recombine into new forms. A weapon that started as a wind-powered scythe could detach from its fan component, switch to its rifle mode, and then fuse back with the fan to create something entirely new.

While every device is fundamentally compatible, some combinations work better than others. Certain fusions produce highly optimised results, while others may be clunky or inefficient, requiring careful planning and experimentation. The more complex a fusion becomes, the harder it is to maintain, and stacking too many layers of integration leads to diminishing returns.
addons.title: Modular Fusion

addons.text:
Your multimodal tech can now access advanced stages of operation, layering functions instead of just switching between them. As you overclock your devices, you can force them to activate multiple modes at once, combining capabilities into a single, devastating form. For example, a sniper rifle in a Stage 2 can simultaneously function as a scythe. Similarly, a scout drone in a Stage 3 can deploy its stealth field while firing all of its weapons and performing high-fidelity scans. All combined systems also benefit from the enhanced performance of Overclock.

This is not sustainable. Forcing otherwise incompatible systems to operate in parallel generates immense, exponential heat, which is contained by your Overheat systems. Your device can only maintain this combined form for as long as its heat batteries hold out. Reverting to a Stage 1 allows the device to cool down before it self-destructs into a molten wreck.
addons.title: Cumulative Modes

objects.text: You specialize in creating machines with various modes. These machines are capable of changing modes on the fly. You could create a car that turns into a robot, or a sniper that turns into a scythe.
objects.title: (Tinker) Modes

objects.text: You possess a specialty that works with and controls kinetic energy. You can create devices that absorb kinetic attacks to machines that output more kinetic force than something of its size could reasonably do.
objects.title: (Tinker) Kinetics

objects.text: You can create cybernetic augmentations, such as a prosthetic arm that gives super strength, or eyes that have heat vision. You don't necessarily need to replace your body parts to use your creations.
objects.title: (Tinker) Cybernetics

objects.text: You possess a Tinker specialty that allows you to improve existing Tinkertech. This can improve the foundation and material of something without replacing the device in question, allowing it to inherit any unique properties, such as Enhancement charges. You can greatly improve the power and flexibility of Tinker devices.
objects.title: (Tinker) Refinement

objects.text: You can alter the genome of living beings to add or remove traits. Building upon genes to give alterations to the body for various abilities, this can range from poisonous blood to night vision. You can work with the DNA of other species to add to a different one.
objects.title: (Tinker) Geneticist

addons.title: Potential Wells
addons.text: Your tech can exhibit particularly fine control over the pathways by which energy moves, transforms, and is expressed, especially on thermodynamic scales. From disintegration fields that lower molecular binding energies, to artificial maxima of gravitational potential that exert powerful repulsion, this is a versatile set of tools that synergizes with almost every other Tinker specialization in one way or another. You can use it to build an even better battery, yes, but also to project forcefields, synthesize super-materials, deflect harmful energies, and exploit physical law in a myriad of subtle and delicate ways.

objects.text:
The most necessary ingredient of any technology. With this specialty, you could make a battery that would last for years or a power source that could run a spaceship.

Be warned, as such inventions will draw heavy attention.
objects.title: (Tinker) Energy

objects.text: You can create magical-themed personal gear, including clothing, concealed weapons, armour, and accessories. You also possess a minor ability to mark equipment and items with a symbol that allows you to keep track of them no matter the distance between you and the marked item, and finally, you possess the ability to gain greater insight into arguments and plans, allowing you to figure out weaknesses in arguments and plans.
objects.title: (Tinker/Striker) Taking The Stage

objects.text:
You specialize in memetic hazards. Creating anything that can transfer data through a medium that can influence minds. Ranging from paintings that harm the minds of whoever you look at to objects that can pretend to be what it is not. You can rewire an entire human mind to do your bidding. However, you are not capable of creating memetic constructs that can spread across a large distance. Information Hazard is much stronger with (Tinker) Meme.

You can create devices that can block and protect the mind from outside influences and even reverse Simurgh Bombs.
objects.title: (Tinker) Information Hazard

objects.text:
You gain a newfound specialty to create incredibly delicious food from ordinary ingredients, and your culinary prowess reaches extraordinary heights. Through your mastery of flavors and techniques, you can transform mundane materials into delectable dishes that tantalize the taste buds.

Every meal you prepare becomes a sensory delight, enchanting those who partake in your creations. But your talent extends beyond just exquisite flavors, enough to even make anyone fall into bliss—by incorporating exotic ingredients, you have the power to craft food that bestows temporary effects upon those who consume it.

From heightened senses to enhanced abilities, your culinary creations offer more than just a feast for the palate. With each dish you prepare, you bring a taste of enchantment and wonder to the table, leaving a lasting impression on all who indulge in your culinary artistry.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Gourmet

addons.text:
Your mastery over hard-light technology has reached an unprecedented level, allowing you to replicate the function of any machine with absolute precision. Your constructs do not merely resemble the devices they mimic—they become indistinguishable from the original, functioning at an imperceptible level of accuracy. Even an outdated emitter can flawlessly emulate the workings of its latest iteration without stress, effectively bypassing the Tinker cycle and eliminating the need for materials other than energy.

This ability extends beyond mechanical replication. You can simulate biological structures to such perfection that even living organisms cannot discern the difference, creating synthetic tissues and organs that are fully functional and seamlessly integrated. However, your greatest achievement is the ability to digitize physical matter, storing it as raw data before reconstructing it flawlessly when needed. This provides an almost infinite storage capacity, limited only by the available drive space, allowing for the perfect preservation and restoration of objects, machines, and even living beings.
addons.title: Virtual Digitization

objects.text: You can create devices that generate and control hard light constructs. These solid and durable projections can be shaped into various forms and structures, including barriers, weapons, and armor. Your inventions have versatile applications in defense and offense.
objects.title: (Tinker) Hard Light Manipulation

addons.text:
Not only do the past accolades of the object matter, but what people say about it as well. The more famous an object is for its achievements, the more powerful the resulting Tinkertech will be, with the legends about it being able to influence the item's end capabilities.

You could even use objects that have purely fabricated back stories, although your best works will always be made of that which has lived up to their expectations.

In addition, your Thinker power expands to also tell you the stories told about this item, allowing you to more effectively appraise its usefulness.
addons.title: Legendary

objects.text:
You have the touch-based ability to learn the lore of objects, giving you an understanding of the age and various things achieved using them. This includes snippets of information about their previous users where the object in question is concerned.

You are a Tinker, specialized in using "artifacts" to produce thematically related devices. You are capable of breaking down existing objects into Tinkertech with functionality based on their past uses. The effects produced are influenced by the purposes the item was used for and the philosophy of its past wielders (e.g., you produce dramatically different things using the weapon of a pacifist compared to the weapon of a bloodthirsty warmonger).

The more significant and grander the accomplishments of the item, the more powerful the ensuing Tinkertech will be. A freshly made knife wouldn't be usable at all, but a knife used by an effectively powerless mortal to slay a god-like being against all odds could be easily and cheaply turned into an S-class superweapon.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Legacy

objects.text:
This power grants access to an expansive, if somewhat generalized and basic, tinkertech base to build with. In other words, you can build any sci-fi technological or biological phenomena you can think of, as long as they are on the low end of sci-fi strength.

So while versatile, you’re never going to be able to overcome the average Tinker in their own specialty. You can, however, match the average Tinker’s casual efforts in their specialty.

To put this into perspective, a power armor Tinker might be able to build power armor that can withstand blows from an Endbringer, while you’ll struggle just to make power armor that has defensive capabilities similar to a modern tank. Another example could be a laser Tinker being able to build a handheld laser weapon that can pierce through over a dozen meters of steel, while your handheld laser weapons might take a few shots to destroy a tank.

It’s not all bad, though; you can stack multiple different types of technology in your favor to compensate for their individual weaknesses. Using a combination of power armor, forcefields, cybernetics, and bio-enhancements to provide you with a respectable level of defense, for example.
objects.title: (Tinker) Basic Tinker

addons.title: Lucky Slots
addons.text: When Tinkering with Russian Roulette and Tinker of Chance, the success rate of your tech goes up for each current Tinker of Chance specialty that is used. While this won't guarantee that your Russian Roulette Tinkertech will work, it can weigh the odds heavily in your favor.

objects.text:
You are a Free Tinker, able to build practically any tinkertech permitted within an Entities' cycle that you can think of. However, you are restricted in that all of your tinkertech is reliant on the luck of the draw to work.

When you trigger your tinkertech, the dice are rolled on whether it works or fails. The more versatile and powerful the tinkertech is, the greater the chance of failure and the slimmer the chance of success. Depending on the tinkertech and how it functions, this gamble may only apply for its initial activation or each individual use, with the odds adjusted accordingly.

A second handicap is that the more potent the tinkertech you create, the greater the danger and odds of it backfiring if it fails. Consequences can range from simply not working or safely shutting down to catastrophic disasters, such as the parahuman clone you just made trying to kill you. You can adjust these odds, building safer tinkertech at the cost of it having a far lower chance to activate successfully or vice versa.

For example, a ray gun with a 1-in-6 chance of successfully shooting on each trigger pull could take down a mid-level Brute. In contrast, an orbital cannon with a 1-in-100 chance of firing (and a notable chance of catastrophic failure) could kill an Endbringer. You have an innate awareness of the chances and risks involved with your tech.
objects.title: (Tinker) Russian Roulette

objects.text:
You are capable of building advanced technology that manipulates density to compress materials into hyperdense states. Unlike other examples of density manipulation you might know about, this technology operates by reducing the space between different atoms and the arrangement of subatomic particles. As an example, you could fit a hundred tons of steel into a one-inch cube using a special industrial process.

Hyperdense materials are useful for more than an ease of storage as they tend to be exceptionally durable, and if the matter is arranged correctly, it can start displaying various useful properties—like say, a sphere of hyperdense iron being the perfect centerpiece for an electromagnetic shield generator or hyperdense silver being critical to the development of a handheld railgun.

You can’t make something so dense that it becomes a black hole. You can, however, make various types of neutronium with various applications once you’ve fully built up this tech tree.

It is probably possible to apply this technology to organic life without destroying that life, such as with a decent bit of tech development or synergy with other Tinker powers. But by itself, the goal of this power in particular is to fit hundreds of tons of material into personal equipment you can hit people with, shoot people with, or defend yourself with.

As an example—power armor that has simple or even basic functions as far as other Tinkers are concerned, but has more mass than most buildings, providing the wearer immense durability and strength.
objects.title: (Tinker) Material Density

objects.text:
You are technically a Tinker with a decently versatile knowledge base, but the way your power is formatted you'll struggle to create anything yourself. This is because the knowledge you possess hardly contains any schematics or the instincts to create completely new technology.

One of the only things this power provides you the schematics and instincts to create is 3D printers with integrated AI.

The AI iterates on all technological knowledge it is programmed with. You can give it a prompt for a piece of Tinkertech, and it will do its best to create it in the 3D printer.

The designs for this Tinkertech can either be randomly generated by the AI or a recreation of an already known design, such as a design the AI previously generated.

Technology created through random generation will often need to be modified to get rid of bugs or faults in the design. For example, you might get power armor with only four fingers on a hand, or a cure for the common cold that makes your skin blue.

Your techbase and the quality of Tinkertech your AI powered 3d printers can put together is generally comparable to (Tinker) Basic Tinker.
objects.title: (Tinker) AI Generated

objects.text:
You possess a specialty in freezing objects in both space and time. Your technology generally revolves around one scientific mechanism that allows you to freeze objects relative to the nearest major gravity well, which will typically be Earth. Frozen objects are invulnerable and stationary, able to take arbitrary amounts of force without deforming or moving.

You can create guns that can shoot blasts that freeze objects, for between 15 seconds to 5 minutes, though with work and good materials you could compress or shift this range. You can create bombs, generators, or boxes that temporarily or permanently freeze all space within a radius or area.

This power also gives you a relatively simple way to freeze small objects permanently. This allows a variety of different feats of construction, from space elevators to indestructible bunkers to floating skybases. The energy cost of freezing an object this way rises more than linearly with its volume, so applying the method to brick sized objects and building with those tends to be the best option.

What you can freeze, you can also figure out how to unfreeze, though it is a bit harder. Your knowledge in this regard may be applicable to other powers; you could likely figure out how to pop Grayboy bubbles, though doing so safely would be tricky (there's a reason those haven't been popped yet).
