At the highest end of your tech tree, with a lot of effort and perhaps investigating other space related tinkertech/powers, you might even be able to change the reference frame of the objects you freeze, allowing you to shoot unstoppable projectiles.
objects.title: (Tinker) Stasis

objects.text:
Throughout the breadth of human imaginings about the fantastical, there are few as diverse as the concept of dragons.

And now, your mind holds the key to creating ANYThing even remotely related to what can be defined as a dragon.

That includes any type from Wyverns & Drakes to Quetzals & Lindwyrms.

Everything from mechanical or biologically functional dragons, to dragon blades or themed martial arts, to transformative serums & paintings & even teas that let you breathe fire.

Sadly, you are limited in the expression of power.

For example, short of your own Magnum Opus (like Bonesaw's Slaughterhouse 9000), you can never approach the sheer devastating scale of something like Lung, let alone an Endbringer.

This specialization synergizes very well with (Tinker) I Wanna Be The Very Best or (Tinker) Absurdity.
objects.title: (Tinker) But Where's The- DRAGON!!!

addons.text: Your specialty expands to include armored walkers, or "mechs." These machines range from 4 to 15 meters in height, are incredibly strong and durable, and feature integrated weapon systems. A mech built by you could wrestle an Endbringer for a short while.
addons.title: Mechs

objects.text:
You specialize in armored fighting vehicles of various kinds. This includes tanks, self-propelled artillery, and so on.

A hovertank built by you could meaningfully damage an Endbringer, while also being able to take a hit from one.
objects.title: (Tinker) Armored Warfare

objects.text: You are a Tinker specializing in poison. You also gain a specialty in applying said poison. Poison from you might be able to kill Alexandria.
objects.title: (Tinker) Poison

objects.text: You are a Tinker specializing in medicine. You also gain a specialty in applying said medicine. From antibiotics to synthesized molecules that mitigate the most chronic illnesses and parasites, your medicine could improve the health and strength of people for a short time afterward. Medicine from you might be able to cure Case 53s.
objects.title: (Tinker) Medicine

objects.text: You gain a Tinker specialization in Missiles and Rockets of any kind. This ranges from self-tracking missiles, EMP blast rockets, missiles, to rockets with anomalous effects, such as a missile that explodes, freezing everything within its radius. You also gain a minor specialization in launchers and can outfit a launcher onto anything.
objects.title: (Tinker) Rocketman

objects.text:
You are Tinker with a specialty that constantly changes.

You start with 100% of one specialty, every 6 hours 1% will shift to a different specialty. These specialties are random, with a new one being chosen each time you reach 100% in a specialty. At 100% your ability to Tinker in a specialty, will be equivalent to that of a Tinker that actually has that specialty.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Fluctuation

objects.text:
You specialize in aircraft of various kinds. This includes gliders, rotorcraft, VTOLs, zeppelins, and so on.

A jet built by you could outfly and outmaneuver even upper-tier Movers.
objects.title: (Tinker) Ace Combat

addons.text:
You can build incredibly luxurious and comfortable buildings and spaces. Small shacks and packed apartments can have dozens of spacious rooms, every hallway opens up into a courtyard or lobby, while windows can be space-shifted to give every room the best view in the building. Nanites keep the floors clean and pest free and rooms can reconfigure and redecorate themselves. Yards and gardens can be geoformed into any landscape, while greenhouse gardens can be built in any room.

Cities become beautiful public spaces. You can construct climate-controlled domes and sustainable arcologies over entire districts. Parks and green spaces contain miniature nature reserves and theme-park playgrounds. Transit becomes seamlessly self-guided and smooth with plush cabins in cars, busses and subways. You can build gigamalls with artisan fabrication boutiques, five start gourmet fast food drive-thrus, and psionic projection cinemas and VR arcades.

Your designs are also inherently aesthetically pleasing in any style you like, such as traditional, baroque, googie, or minimalist modern.
addons.title: Lap of Luxury

addons.text: You can turn cities into completely impenetrable fortresses that keep their inhabitants safe from any attack. Districts break apart to lift massive bastions, barracks and bombards. Streets begin sprouting blockades while turrets sprout from statues and mailboxes. The city systems track the position of every invader before deploying defensive drones from underground bays. Buildings cover their entrances in layered shutters and recede into bunkers and project force fields over themselves. Inside, the corridors rearrange themselves to redirect and confuse intruders. Inside, transit tunnels empty into bunkers and shelters and closets open into hidden panic rooms or escape tunnels, fully stocked with rations and decentralized power to last for decades and CBRN sealed even from esoteric hazards. With Lap of Luxury citizens can stay in these bunkers for years before siege conditions bring a noticeable drop in quality of life.
addons.title: Locked Down

addons.text: Your cities can fully run and expand themselves. Drones and automation can now handle all services and utilities and maintain themselves. Buildings can be made to build new floors, wings and basements and rearrange rooms. You can create programs that automatically plan districts and roadways before deploying automatic cranes, bulldozers and steamrollers to construct them while construction foundations sprout around completed or partially complete buildings.
addons.title: The City Must Grow

objects.text:
You are a Tinker focused on architecture and urbanism. You can construct buildings and cities, small or massive, though this specialization is very hungry for space, materials and labor.

You can design and build buildings of any scale, from shacks, villas, bunkers, skyscrapers, to megabuildings. You gain a variety of tech for use specifically in architecture, such as load-bearing antigrav generating girders, self-healing walls and inner structure, reconfigurable modular prefab rooms, digitized space that can make the inner floor plan up to twice as large.

Beyond individual buildings, you also gain specialization in the civic infrastructure to run entire communities, from small communes, villages, suburbs, major towns to megacities. This includes decentralized automated utility and service stations, webs of subterranean logistics and hyperspeed transit railways, spatially optimized roads and walking paths that perfect the flow of traffic, and municipal AI that can adapt to any emergency or shift in needs.

This pairs well with (Tinker) Construction and (Tinker) Materials, and could put you just short of creating a plan to turn Earth into an ecumenopolis, though it won’t help you get over all of the many non-material obstacles to that.
objects.title: (Tinker) Metropolis

objects.text:
You are a Tinker with a very focused and narrow function: to contain, isolate, and maintain any entity, phenomenon, or anomaly for study. You can design facilities where each block and every cell is a containment zone, capable of stopping or at least slowing down what is inside. Naturally, the entire facility itself acts as a containment zone as well.

You can design esoteric methods of containment, such as time-stopped cells, multi-dimensional closed spaces, and the use of non-euclidean matter-energy. You also ensure that these containment methods keep occupants functional, alive, and isolated from the environment, while still allowing them to be studied by others.

You have an innate understanding of potential escape methods, allowing you to create custom-designed cells that are escape-proof for their intended occupants. However, these cells are less efficient if used to contain anything other than what they were specifically designed for.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Suppress, Conjecture, Predict

addons.text:
Your mastery of Synchronicity and Chain Reactions has allowed you to create seamless, closed-system interactions within your inventions. The restriction of needing distance between devices in your Rube Goldberg Machines has been eliminated, allowing complex, multi-step reactions to occur within a single, compact device. Instead of relying on space and external triggers, your mechanisms now function as self-contained systems, where every part moves in perfect harmony—like a grand mechanical symphony.

Now, the chain reactions are directly tied to the synchronicity of your technology’s internal mechanisms. Each precisely timed movement within a device contributes to the chain, ensuring that every tick, rotation, or shift fuels the next stage of the reaction. A kinetic watch, for example, could use every tick of its internal mechanism to channel force, storing and releasing energy in controlled bursts. A clockwork automaton’s every movement would be the result of countless small, synchronized mechanical motions—gears turning, pistons firing, joints locking and unlocking in a precise sequence—allowing it to walk, strike, and react with perfect efficiency, while having strength great enough to out-punch low to mid-end Brutes.

The tradeoff remains: your creations still require precise timing and coordination to function at their best. However, they no longer need physical space to facilitate their chain reactions. Instead, their internal mechanisms now form the chain, allowing for incredibly intricate, split-second sequences to be executed within a single, self-contained mechanical masterpiece.
addons.title: Perpetual Motion Ballet

objects.text:
You are a Tinker capable of touching most specialties and tech trees to one degree or another, specializing in the construction of Rube Goldberg Machines, or rather, chain reactions designed to perform tasks in an indirect and overly complicated way. On average, this often manifests as making dozens of small-scale devices that individually have limited capabilities but interact and activate in a chain reaction to perform tasks of significance.

The longer a chain, the more potent the result, as the devices amplify and modify the chain reaction. For example, an air gun part of a dozen-device-long chain could send a grown Lung flying miles. Chain reactions can be interrupted, which produces less impressive but chaotic and unpredictable results, depending on how far along the chain reaction is.

It usually helps performance if there is distance between all devices when they activate.

After a few dozen devices are added to a chain you start getting diminishing returns on the amplification of the chain reaction, and by a hundred the only thing further devices add is a method of transporting the result of the chain reaction, though you could probably blow a hole through an Endbringer if you land a solid hit with such a chain.

This power perfectly synergizes with any other Tinker power so long as its theme is followed.
objects.title: (Tinker) Rube Goldberg Machines

objects.text: You can detect, identify, counter and destroy memetic and antimemetic beings, creatures, objects and phenomena. You can also create memetic constructs that exist in the form of aggressive ideas. They spread rapidly and cannot easily be contained. These ideas may be able to actively seek out and destroy/overtake certain other ideas and replacing them in entirety.
objects.title: (Tinker) Meme

objects.text:
You specialize in education, teaching, and imparting knowledge to others. The tech you create has the capabilities of even elevating a Neanderthal into a 21st-century genius.

You can design neuralware that aids neuroplasticity, even brain implants to aid in memory, a dream-learning inducer to reinforce what you learned throughout the day, and a VI teacher programmed to educate someone at any age through college-level subjects. If needed, it will adapt to the student to help them learn better.

You can even design brain-to-machine devices that can implant skills onto people or copy skills from VR simulations to train soldiers for war, making them veterans before they even step onto the battlefield.

You can also enhance classroom experiences by creating augmented reality tech to develop unique learning environments.

Beyond technology, you are also a great teacher with an inner archive of knowledge containing numerous teaching techniques. You can teach nearly anyone, provided you have expertise in the subject.

You could go into an underperforming school, identify all its flaws—from how it functions to how the teachers teach—and fix every potential problem. You could even train people to become better teachers, creating a virtuous cycle.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Class In Session

objects.text:
You can create technology that can keep people safe from all sorts of harm. Your inventions are able to provide a variety of defense mechanisms, including force fields, bunkers, and more. This not only allows you to protect people from physical threats but also to keep them safe from the dangers of the environment.

Moreover, you have the potential to enhance tinkertech, making it safer to use. You can create devices that are less prone to malfunctions. Additionally, you can also scale down certain technology to keep it from causing damage to its user.

As you explore different areas, you gain the ability to sense the safety of your surroundings. You can immediately detect any potential hazards and identify how safe or dangerous an area is. This comes with a wealth of knowledge of various safety techniques, allowing you to recognize common safety hazards and how to avoid them. For example, you can spot a defective power plug and know how to safely deactivate it to prevent electrocution. Similarly, if you come across a construction site, you can quickly identify any violations of safety regulations and advise the workers to fix any issues before continuing.
objects.title: (Tinker/Thinker) Safety

addons.text:
Your workshops and facilities are now the epitome of industrial innovation, capable of supporting any Tinker specialization. You can design automated mining bunkers, underwater biological cultivation centers, or entire manufacturing compounds. These self-sufficient facilities include automated defenses such as turrets, energy shields, lockdown protocols, and self-destruct systems for enhanced security. Centralized focal points like reactors or server farms generate non-detectable fields that improve efficiency, maintenance, and repair across the facility, ensuring peak performance under any conditions.

This mastery extends to production capabilities, allowing you to construct facilities like factories and fabricators that can mass-produce items. While producing Tinkertech still requires blueprints or collaboration, your creations can handle all intermediary steps, from raw material refinement to final assembly. Additionally, your ability to enhance and ruggedize structures ensures they are fortified against environmental extremes and hostile attacks, making them ideal for even the most challenging environments.
addons.title: Passive Production

objects.text:
You specialize in construction, toolkits, workshops, and building in general. Your expertise lies in creating machines designed to manufacture other machines and components. From 2D printing devices to 3D printers capable of producing objects and structures with a precision surpassing what could be achieved by hand or mundane equipment.

You can also craft a specialized toolkit that, in the hands of those with the necessary knowledge, outperforms ordinary tools. With a keen eye for design and structural analysis, you can assess the quality of objects at a glance.

Additionally, you excel at constructing workshops tailored to the specific needs of other Tinkers, whether they require bio labs for wet tinkering or high-end computer labs with powerful servers for programming, elevating their capabilities from mediocrity to a level that gives villains second thoughts about confronting them. The only limit is your Tinker ingenuity.
objects.title: (Tinker) Construction

objects.text: You specialize in the creation of various forms of matter. They can have a wide variety of effects and abilities, even creating forms of matter that defy the laws of physics. From heavy metals that can float, synthetic plasteel, elaborating polymers, and metamaterials or minerals capable of physical forces to a lightweight unknown material that can absorb and negate flames.
objects.title: (Tinker) Material

addons.text:
The technology from Techie that composes your body acts as a focus and extension to your non-Tinker powers. Letting you use them with increased effectiveness and efficiency, this allows you to accomplish tasks involving them with half the effort that would be required otherwise.

Modifying this technology acts as a way to modify and train the associated power.
addons.title: Sci-Fi Enhanced

objects.text: You have the ability to build tinkertech that imitate your non-tinker powers. Additionally, you are able to study and analyze the abilities of others to create items that replicate their abilities to some degree, though it is impossible to fully recreate them perfectly.
objects.title: (Tinker) Techie

objects.text:
You are a Tinker specializing in remote-controlled technology such as drones. The average Drone built with average resources when starting is initially very limited, maybe comparable to rats, but can swarm in numbers limited only by computer management and communication technology.

Drones can be improved with research and development. They can be given specialized roles and technologies for different purposes, but that is initially limited to things like a taser drone or a flame lighter drone. Other facets of this specialty besides drones and the associated support technology are various bits and pieces that allow advanced communication between technology, advanced computers, advanced programming (not capable of making advanced AI by itself without years of development), and computer-brain interface technology.
objects.title: (Tinker) Remote Control

objects.text:
You have an interesting Tinker specialty, as it gives you three focuses. First, special inks are made with various materials. Second, symbols are made to be written or drawn with the earlier ink. Lastly, papers are made to have the earlier symbols drawn on them. All together, they form Seals.

The inks, depending on what material is used to make them, will have different properties, from fire-like properties or gravity-based properties. The symbols are used to channel the properties, specifying what they are to do. The paper is its output; the better the paper, the stronger and/or more stable the effect. To put it in perspective, the ink is the type of programming language, the symbols are the code itself, and the paper is the hardware.

When you activate the Seal, the paper will stick to whatever it was placed on, applying its effect to it. A minor effect you also gain is an increased skill in handwriting and brushwork.
objects.title: (Tinker/Striker) Fuinjutsu

addons.text: The line between reality and the dimensions you craft has blurred. You can now design your pocket dimensions to be capable of overlapping or intersecting with the real world at will, imposing your custom physics upon the world directly.
addons.title: Extraterritorial Enforcement

objects.text:
You are a Tinker specialized in the creation of custom pocket dimensions of varying properties. The more the physics of a pocket dimension differs from the real world, the more expensive it is to create and maintain the pocket dimension.

An ever-shifting escherian labyrinth within which to trap your enemies; a subspace through which you can thread the bulk of your other technology to make it impossibly small; or even an arena with physics favorable to your powers that you can temporarily kidnap people into—all are within the realm of possibility for you.
objects.title: (Tinker) Domain

addons.text:
While others might joke about compensation, you understand the engineering required to make war machines truly function. Most devices operate optimally within a narrow size range: too large, and they become unwieldy; too small, and they lack sufficient power for the task, with efficiency plummeting sharply at either extreme. But not for you.

You can scale your technology up or down without sacrificing function or reliability. This applies to virtually any technological concept you conceive. Your creations, even when appearing to be of regular size, perform wonders far beyond their apparent capabilities, being both miniaturized and magnified. You can seamlessly upscale or miniaturize your technology to perfectly fit any situation or blueprint, ensuring peak performance regardless of the dimensions required.
addons.title: Matter of Scale

objects.text:
This Tinker specialty could be considered a conceptual mirror of Colin Wallis’s power. Instead of technology focused on efficiency and miniaturization, this power focuses its techbase on increasing the size and effective capabilities of its technology. To put it simply, you specialize in Effectiveness and Magnification.

Essentially, the bigger you design a piece of technology, the more ideas you get for increasing the effectiveness and power of its functions. You’ll also have an easier time designing things to be durable and survive various environments the bigger you make them.

So this specialty truly shines in the construction of large structures such as building-sized robots, fortresses, battleships, or even outrageously huge energy cannons. Say you build a mecha as large as an Endbringer; with sufficient skill and a bit of luck, you just might be able to singlehandedly drive off an Endbringer just as a hypothetical alternate universe Colin could with his armor, prediction system, and nanothorn.

Just like Colin, you have a versatile and wide-ranging techbase covering most forms of Tinkertech.
objects.title: (Tinker) Huge Scale

objects.text:
You specialise in the design, construction, launch and operation of artificial satellites and similar orbital spacecraft.

Your satellites can serve an enormous variety of purposes, whether intended for communication, surveillance, navigation, defence, habitation or other applications. They may be deployed across a wide range of trajectories and altitudes, from a low earth orbit of 500 km up to a geostationary orbit of over 35,000 km away.

You could build a world-wide broadcasting network, telescopes that can map countries and monitor individuals from space, weather forecasting systems accurate weeks in advance, habitable spacecraft or platforms equipped with powerful laser weaponry. For example, you might deploy observation satellites to track parahuman activity or, with sufficient effort, create a planetary orbital defense array.

This pairs well with numerous other Tinker specialities; for example, if combined with Lookout, you could build the perfect spy satellites, or, with Mannequin, an expansive, self-sustaining space station.
objects.title: (Tinker) Satellites

addons.text: Your understanding of artillery has grown with your ambition. Your weapons are no longer installations—they are juggernauts. Mobile fortresses, crawling artillery cities, continent-cracking siege engines. Each machine is a self-sufficient behemoth, bristling with guns, reactors, repair bays, and command centers. They flatten city blocks just by arriving. Endbringers are no longer the most terrifying force on the battlefield—your creations are. Although building one is easier said than done.
addons.title: Siege-Ready

objects.text: Your specialty is the making of anything that cannot be easily moved. If you had a couple of good shots, you could probably kill an Endbringer with one of your guns.
objects.title: (Tinker) Fortifications and Artillery

objects.text:
Your Tinker specialty is creating tinkertech that enhances itself through combat. By engaging in combat, your tech will start to ‘mature’, gaining features that make it stronger, better, and more versatile as time passes. By default, the maturing process takes 30 minutes; however, this scales in proportion to the scale and danger of the combat. Should you leave combat or combat end before the current maturing process is done, the tech will slowly start to revert to its original state. The process can be rekindled should combat start again.

When the maturing process finishes, another will start up soon after if the user is still in combat. Additions to your tech that have finished maturing can be added onto other tech like normal tinkertech.
objects.title: (Tinker) Escalation

objects.text: You specialize in creating adaptive Tinkertech that can reconfigure itself based on threats it comes across. The better the information that's fed and analyzed, the better the adaptations it creates. It can grow adaptations during combat and outside of it, although it is much faster while in conflict. Your Tinkertech is high-cost and material-intensive, and if it runs out of fed materials, it will stop adapting.
objects.title: (Tinker) Reconfiguration

objects.text: You can make anything you build self-replicating. This ranges from giving bio-tinkered creations the ability to reproduce to making machines able to create copies of themselves. The only limitation is that your technology cannot self-replicate if it lacks the needed materials. This can be worked around by having the replicated version be inferior to the original. If it can already self-replicate, then you can make it even more efficient, such as allowing people to undergo mitosis instead of requiring pregnancy.
objects.title: (Tinker) Self Replicating

objects.text: Your Tinker specialty is based on your public perception. It can be whatever people think your Tinker specialty is, and the more famous you are, the better those specialties you may obtain. You gain special Tinker specialties based on powerful threats you overcame—those threats are decided by how infamous or famous the threat you defeated was.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Glory

objects.text:
You can create technology that accesses other dimensions and parallel universes.

You could make bullets that go through obstacles by sinking into another dimension, or goggles that let you see every dimension.
objects.title: (Tinker) Interdimensional

objects.text:
You specialize in the creation of long-term, wide-area, indiscriminate effects. Your tech tree starts at effects covering a block and grows in range from there.

Examples of things you could build are: a static generator that emits intense apathy upon everybody in a multi-block radius; a thick fog that forces immense downward gravitational pull upon every airborne object inside; you could even create direct weather events, forcing a city to endure a constant barrage of powerful lightning strikes from a permanent thunderstorm or survive an eternal sub-zero blizzard.
objects.title: (Tinker) Weatherman

objects.text:
You are a minor Free Tinker whose specialty revolves around the concept of Assimilation. Essentially, you can create various types of basic tinkertech from most tech trees available.

However, this technology will, by default, always include some way to meld with other objects to increase its capabilities as part of its design. Fighting this aspect and excluding those elements from a design will drastically lower your technology's capabilities, if it even functions at all.

Examples of how your technology melds with other objects could include a nanite swarm, adaptive mutagenic retroviruses, or even a specialized computer virus. It all depends on what it’s trying to meld with and how you designed it to meld in the first place, as a computer program probably isn’t going to be able to meld with anything physically unless it also contains some sort of physical element to it.

You can put in parameters for how and what your technology can meld with when you design it. Particularly strong immune systems and other defenses can prevent your technology from melding with other objects, especially if the example of your tech in question isn’t particularly advanced, powerful, or is damaged in some capacity.

This specialty includes ways to modify your technology after it melds with new objects to make sure it develops along paths you desire. You can also design your technology with certain capabilities that only activate once it acquires enough mass from melding, such as mitosis-style replication or self-repair.
objects.title: (Tinker) Assimilation

addons.text:
You no longer need the entire intact gadget to reverse engineer it. You can puzzle out its original function and underlying design principles by studying its fractured remains. With time and effort, you can reconstruct “close-enough” knockoffs that perform similarly to the original device, though they may be prone to quirks or slight inefficiencies.

In case of having both (Tinker) Repair and (Tinker) Salvage, you can faithfully reproduce any Tinkertech device, regardless of how incomplete or degraded the available pieces are. Even a handful of warped components or residual energy signatures is enough for you to rebuild the technology to its intended specifications.
addons.title: Scavenger

objects.text: You can reproduce the technology of any other Tinker. You can only reproduce technology you've analyzed. Any Tinkertech you've analyzed will be easier to convert to real tech, but only mildly so.
objects.title: (Tinker) Reproduction

objects.text:
You are a biotinker/prosthetist hybrid who is focused on self-improvement. It is similar to Bonesaw's power, as the both of you will be able to learn a lot from each other, finding it easier to understand what each other's powers did and how they did them.

This could be easily combined with most Tinker powers, with a few such as Bakuda being an exception.
objects.title: (Tinker) Self-Alteration

objects.text:
You specialize in constructing technology that manipulates probability fields, subtly stacking the deck in your favor. Your devices don't create impossibilities; they stack the odds until the improbable becomes nearly inevitable, though absolute certainty is always out of reach. No matter how much energy or processing power you commit, you cannot force an outcome to 100% or reduce another to 0%. The more you push an event closer to certainty, the more energy and computational power it consumes, making total guarantees impossible.

The complexity of the task is your primary constraint. Influencing a simple event, like a coin toss, is trivial. However, complex chains of events, such as causing a sniper's bullet to ricochet off three surfaces to hit a target, require immense processing power and energy. After enacting such a change, your equipment must recalibrate, as the "butterfly effect" of your action throws all previously calculated variables into chaos, effectively putting the device on a cooldown.

Your influence is limited by time and range. The power works best on a scale of minutes and is ineffective beyond a day. Handheld devices operate within fifty feet, while larger emplacements with dedicated power sources can influence probabilities across the city. Pushing an event farther from its natural probability costs exponentially more energy and processing power, as well as increasing the risk of unintended consequences.

This specialization pairs especially well with (Tinker) Detection and Analysis, (Tinker) Kinesis, and (Tinker) Quantum Computing.
objects.title: (Tinker) Probability Manipulation

objects.text:
You can create robots as well as a headset to mentally control them. Your robots can make robots as well. There is no maximum or minimum size for your robots... well, they can't go far from subatomic, but that's the only real limit.

You cannot program these robots without (Tinker) Code, and if you have (Tinker) Code, you can overwrite the AI with your headset. You have unlimited multitasking.
objects.title: (Tinker/Master) Nanobots

objects.text:
You can transform into and manifest materials to create machines you understand or tinkertech specialties that you have out of your own body. While this harms you, you also have a minor regeneration power to keep you alive.

You will have a link that enables you to control any machine that is made from you within 1 km, although you can make relays to extend this range as well as fuse with them as long as they are in touching range. This doesn’t come with multitasking abilities.

This synergizes well with other tinker powers. Note that without some kind of regeneration power, this can be extremely risky.

Examples of uses for this power are making metal spikes extrude from your skin for combat or vomiting molten metal to forge. More advanced uses include creating entire machines, such as robots (either from understanding their materials, systems, and mechanics or from a tinker specialty), directly rather than just creating the materials, but doing this is harder, riskier, and even more painful.
objects.title: (Tinker/Master) Machine World

objects.text:
This power grants you a Tinker specialty revolving around nanotechnology. Nano-scale technology has a variety of purposes, but to list a few examples, you could make nanites for construction, spying, and even flying destructive swarms.

But you aren’t limited to just swarms of nanites; you may also construct larger pieces of generic Tinkertech out of nanites, such as armor, weaponry, and cybernetics. The nanites coming together to take the shape and functions of various electronic and mechanical components.

Though versatile, the larger pieces of Tinkertech you can construct out of nanites can only be considered average compared to the casual work of a dedicated specialty.

By necessity, given the limited space within a nanite for technological functions, different types of nanites will possess and specialize in different functions. A few examples could be one type of nanite focusing on delivering energy to other nanites, another might focus on serving as a signal relay, and a third type might focus on serving as the structure of any larger pieces of Tinkertech you might construct out of nanites.

Your nanites can be programmed to take on different shapes in different situations or in response to different signals. Like a suit of nanite power armor that can take the shape of clothing when in a casual setting, just by taking advantage of the fact that nanites are objects measured in nanometers, allowing vast quantities of nanites to fit in small configurations for easy storage when not in use. 

Though when taking on smaller configurations, your nanites will not possess the capabilities of any larger pieces of technology they can form. So that aforementioned suit of nanite power armor, when in the form of clothing, they won’t have the protective qualities, strength augmenting servos, and other technological functions of power armor.

One final thing to note is that, despite specializing in nanotechnology, this power does not include any designs or instincts for creating a grey goo nanite apocalypse. Though synergy with other powers could let you bypass this limitation.
objects.title: (Tinker) Nanites

objects.text: You specialize in the manipulation of nuclear physics. The obvious use is to create nuclear reactors and bombs, but you can do much more than that. You can create machines that transmute elements, advanced diagnostic imaging machines such as X-ray or MRI machines, and much more.
objects.title: (Tinker) Nuclear

objects.text: Your Tinker power specializes in the manipulation of space, creating things such as teleportation pads or a small device that allows small-scale teleportation would be child's play to you. But you can do so much more than that, like bending space much like Vista with specialized devices—notably without the Manton Limits of regular powers, so do be careful. You could create things that are bigger or smaller on the inside. Your imagination is the limit when it comes to creating technology that has to do with space.
objects.title: (Tinker) Space

objects.text: You specialize in destruction. Your Tinkertech is made to be as dangerous as possible. You can create bullets that delete matter on contact, bombs that consume concrete like the plague, napalm that can last thousands of years, and so on. You can destroy and defeat Endbringers as well, but the price for it is what most would consider not worth it.
objects.title: (Tinker) Destruction

objects.text:
This power is to Legend’s Shard what Hero’s is to Stilling. You have the capacity to make devices that produce lasers with various effects, limited by your creativity and the research you do.

Examples include lasers that can turn corners, fork into multiple lasers, pass through walls, freeze, ignite targets, cut, disintegrate, impact, heat, focus, staccato bursts, fat lasers, and invisible lasers. These are just examples, though you could develop lasers with capabilities other than those examples and combine effects. Your power also isn't limited to just these forms of esoteric energy manipulation and support technology; the true purpose for this power is space travel, so beyond dealing with harmful space energies, a form of FTL technology might not be out of reach, especially if this power is whiteboxed.
objects.title: (Tinker) Lasers!

objects.text:
You can create machines capable of manipulating raw information. In its most basic state, you can create Stranger effects, such as making specific information impossible to process, causing it to slip from memory. You can also create machines meant to analyze others to gain information. In its more advanced stages, you could transform the state of information, converting virtual data into physical form and vice versa. The only flaw is that your technology has a limited range, incapable of affecting those far away.

This pairs extremely well with (Tinker) Meme and (Tinker) Informational Hazard.
objects.title: (Tinker) Information

addons.text: Your infectious enhancements can now be designed to far more rapidly enhance anyone they infect. With your average work able to modify every cell in a human body within hours and less complicated work could happen in minutes.
addons.title: Sped Up Enhancement

objects.text:
You specialize in the construction of all manner of cybernetic and biological modifications. Though versatile such enhancements are, at their best, only mildly above average compared to the casual work of a dedicated Tinker specialty. But that’s only when you compare the aspects this power shares with other enhancement focused Tinker specialties. 

The unique area where this power shines is that you can design every enhancement you make to be infectious.

For example, say you enhanced someone with wolf based cybernetics and bio modifications, that person could bite other people injecting them with a mix of nanites and mutagen which would slowly but surely modify their body to possess similar enhancements.

These infections take resources from the host body to build the desired cybernetics or biological modifications. 

It takes on average a month for someone infected by your Tinkertech to be fully enhanced by an average example of your work. Though that timescale can be sped up or lengthened depending on the complexity of the enhancements in question and how completely they alter the host body. Though obviously that only applies to people being infected by sources of your Tinkertech instead of someone you directly modify.

Depending on the enhancements being made, an infected individual might experience an increased appetite. That hunger comes from their infection driving them to gather the materials it needs to make its enhancements. The things they can be driven to be hungry for can include inorganic material such gold, uranium, or platinum depending on the enhancements being made. Not consuming such materials can slow or even halt the infection progress depending on why that material was needed in the first place.

Your Tinkertech enhancements can be designed to be capable of self repair, drawing resources from the host body to repair damage and preform maintenance at a rate similar to a normal human's healing factor.

You can design your Tinkertech enhancements to possess multiple strains of enhancements they can infect people with. As an example, say you enhance someone with cybernetics and bio modifications based on vampire characteristics. This artificial vampire could produce two strains; the first is obviously more vampires, while the second could be a ghoul strain that has most of the same capabilities as the vampire strain just weakened and innately loyal to vampires. 

As for what determines what strain manifests it could be as simple as the person doing the infection choosing or a response to different conditions you programmed it to respond to.

Unless they are specifically made to be compatible or don’t interfere with each other people can’t be infected by multiple strains of your enhancements. They can however be infected with new strains that’ll replace their previous enhancements. This requires either a successful handshake protocol between strains or for the new strain to be able to ignore the defenses of the previous strain.

Your infections aren’t absolute, things like sufficiently enhanced immune systems, specific forms of Parahuman healing, and the work of other Tinkers can prevent or cure an infection.
objects.title: (Tinker) Infectious Enhancements

objects.text:
Have you ever heard of “Soulslike”? It’s a particularly difficult genre of action RPG. Why is that relevant? Well, the technology this power provides you seems particularly focused on replicating a similar style of combat and risk in you with a sci-fi twist.

First and foremost, you can create a network of machines that have many different functions that will be touched upon throughout the rest of this power’s description. These machines are also individually rather small, about the size of the average bonfire. So, for the sake of simplicity, these machines will be called bonfires throughout the rest of this power’s description.

Several basic applications for these bonfires include: reviving you in the event of your death, teleportation between different bonfires, healing you, and providing maintenance for your other pieces of Tinkertech equipment.

Your bonfires can also shift out of phase with normal reality, becoming intangible and invisible to avoid danger, an effect they can extend to when you’re making use of a bonfire. Though you won’t be able to affect the outside universe until the effect ends.

When you first start with this power, you’ll also be able to build basic Tinkertech cybernetics, bio augmentations, weapons, and armor. Along with a basic Tinkertech pocket dimensions to store and retrieve materials and equipment from.

Know that in the event of your death that when a bonfire revives you, you’ll revive with all of the equipment you had on your person before death, including any cybernetics and bioaugmentations you added to your body.

The way your bonfires revive you and repair your other Tinkertech is rather unique, in that it involves space-time manipulation to retrieve your body and equipment while making all repairs necessary to make it as if you never died and your Tinkertech was never damaged.

Unless you set it up to work otherwise, in the event of your death, you’ll revive at the last bonfire you interacted with.

Another function of this power is the ability to gather data from combat, using Tinkertech cameras and sensors that can be made into cybernetics.

You can use that data to slowly but surely improve the designs for your non-bonfire Tinkertech until you reach the pinnacle of Parahuman power.

It should be noted that different combat encounters give different quality data; so, a hundred combat encounters with mundane crooks might give you the data needed to improve a particular type of basic Tinkertech you used by a few percent; meanwhile, a prolonged combat encounter against a Parahuman could give you the data needed to improve your equipment by dozens of percentages.

Data you gather from combating Parahumans and other foes beyond the mundane can also be used to make equipment that can partially replicate their capabilities in some capacity. Say a battle with Lung might give you the data needed to make a greatsword that can light itself on fire, and can tune the energy it gives off to slowly get better at burning a target the longer it's used in combat against them.

One final thing to note is that you can use your bonfires as a basic general-purpose Tinker workshop, allowing you to make basic modifications to your Tinkertech while out on the field away from more substantial workshops.
objects.title: (Tinker) Souls Tech

addons.title: “No Capes!”
addons.text: Thanks to your capacity for sheer Style, you are no longer limited to needing to mimick capes’ costumes. After all, you can do a much better job than those hacks! So long as you draw inspiration and design a costume around a specific parahuman while tinkering, you can create an entirely original outfit that still bestows their powers. Furthermore, you can amplify the powers granted beyond the original individual's capabilities. The more visually striking, iconic and higher quality the costume, the greater the boost, potentially giving powers up to 3× stronger than the actual parahuman. Keep in mind that these magnificent creations will demand ample time, dedication as well as only the finest materials to be completed.

objects.text:
You specialise in creating replicas of parahumans’ costumes; these may grant whoever is wearing them a copy of the actual cape’s powerset.

These powersets can range in strength, from a tiny fraction up to a 1:1 copy of the original parahuman, depending on two main factors. Firstly, the closer a replica matches the original in appearance and the better its condition, the more potent it is. Poorly made or damaged costumes provide weaker powers or, if too tattered, don't work at all.

Secondly, parahumans with stronger and more versatile abilities require proportionally more time, effort and higher-quality materials to replicate at equivalent potency. For example, a week's hard work might yield a 1:1 copy of Skitter's powerset while the same investment into a Legend costume could only achieve a tenth of his strength.

You can also work directly with an existing cape’s costume to grant their powers to its wearer. These outfits are easier to fully copy their powers with but extensive, bespoke tinkering is still needed to empower them. Like other tinker tech, the costumes you make require maintenance to stay functional.

This obviously synergises extremely well with (Tinker/Thinker) Garment.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Cape Cosplay

objects.text:
You are a genius when it comes to Code. You could make AI that would revolutionize the world... if they didn't destroy it. Be careful with this power... if only there were a benevolent AI that could help...

Warning: The Dragonslayers WILL try to kill you out of fear of AI.
objects.title: (Tinker) Code

objects.text:
You are a tinker specializing in environmental technology with dual approaches to that specialty. One approach focuses on surviving hostile environments in various ways, from specialized genemods, cybernetics, armor/clothing, vehicles, or shelters. The other focuses on changing the environment to suit your needs, like purifying water on a large scale, changing the composition of the gases in the air, manipulating the materials composing the ground, dealing with radiation, dealing with heat or a lack of heat, and changing the weather.

These approaches are not incompatible; if you work at it, you might be able to make cybernetics or armor that can shoot bolts of electricity or manipulate the environment in various ways.

While this specialty is very versatile, it does not surpass specialties like (Tinker) Thermal or (Tinker) Cybernetics in their field, as it merely offers a specialized approach. It has great synergy with specialties related to either of its approaches.
objects.title: (Tinker) Terraforming

objects.text:
You can create pieces of technology that can either amplify or dampen parahuman powers. The limits on how much you can diminish/boost powers depend on the tinkertech’s size and your experience in your power’s usage and practice; the smaller your tech is, the smaller the range, to the point where rings or necklace-sized pieces of technology require physical contact to work, but in exchange for this limitation, the smaller the piece of technology, the more powerful the amplification/dampening is, with the boosting/dampening’s maximum limit being 1000% of the original power. At first, you will barely be able to create pieces of tinkertech that can boost or dampen parahuman powers by 10% and are roughly the same size as a portable gas generator.

And if you have Negentropy, then your technology becomes geared to recharge and supercharge Shards. Along with this, the boost your technology gives can reach over 1000%.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Amplifiers and Dampeners

objects.text: You are a biotinker similar to Blasto, where you can make hybridized creatures; however, instead of being limited to plants, they can be a plethora of elements. From shadow humanoid tigers, crystal-organic reptilian birds, to even flame-breathing dragons.
objects.title: (Tinker) I Wanna Be The Very Best!

addons.title: The Garden of Forking Paths
addons.text:
Informed by your interdimensional tech, your time specialization expands to include splitting, merging, and traversing parallel timelines. This remains local in scope (don't expect to split off or merge entire alternate earths), but is otherwise a particularly versatile form of time manipulation.

You might build a device that facilitates Coil-esque timeline splitting. Or a chamber that shunts its occupants into disposable timelines, harmlessly containing any hazard they might pose (while giving you a window to study what those hazards are). Or material duplicators that selectively branch and remerge reality, with just enough of a phase shift to double select objects or resources.

Note that in the absence of other powers none of this tech will be Negentropic, and may consume large amounts of energy to fully utilize.

addons.title: Operation of Parallel Worlds
addons.text:
Combined with your probability manipulation, the reach of your timeline manipulation technology expands to include possible, yet ultimately unrealized divergent timelines.

This allows you to build things such as a retroactive safety anchor that triggers upon taking a fatal blow, merging your timeline with one where the attack narrowly missed, undoing damage without needing to split the timeline in advance. Or superposition weapons that force multiple unchosen combat actions into a single physical space, causing a single shot or blade swing to manifest along dozens of alternative trajectories simultaneously. You could even upgrade the material duplicator to manifest items you've never had in the first place by pulling them from an alternate timeline where you did have them.

Naturally, both the energy costs and the risks of side effects scale exponentially the more divergent the desired timeline is from the existing one. A handheld device might consume marginally more power to interact with a timeline that diverged a few minutes ago at most, whereas summoning a parahuman ally from a theoretical timeline where you've earned their loyalty is nothing short of a megaproject. Even then, there's always a chance of it backfiring - after all, their loyalty ultimately belongs to your alternate self, not you.

objects.text: Your Tinker power allows you to manipulate time on a localized scale. You can create devices that alter the flow of time, either speeding it up or slowing it down within a specific area or for specific objects. This power can be utilized for a variety of purposes, including time-based weaponry, time-limited force fields, or time-accelerated manufacturing processes. However, manipulating time comes with its own risks and challenges, as it requires precise control and understanding of temporal mechanics.
objects.title: (Tinker) Time Dilation

addons.text:
Your ability to second trigger has extended to (Tinker/Trump) Variable Tinker, enabling you to second trigger your current Tinker specialization for up to 1 week at a time. This second trigger will work to best suit your current problem and immediate circumstances, although you can't precisely determine how it will impact your specialization.

This can range from either focusing or widening your Tinker specialization to granting you minor additional non-Tinker powers to support your specialty. This second trigger manifestation can be reverted to allow you to go back to your original Tinker specialisation at any time, but after the second triggering, there is a minimum of a week-long cooldown before you can second trigger again.
addons.title: High-Grade Tinkering

addons.text:
This power has now evolved into being something similar to a second power 'slot' for Paramount, albeit focused solely on Tinker powers. You can choose to either get a single, somewhat random, Tinker specialization centered around solving a problem of your choice as normal or give yourself any one of the Tier 1 Tinker powers in this CYOA. The time limits for how long a Tinker specialization can be kept have been removed.

Note that Paramount can still acquire Tinker powers, allowing you to potentially have two Tinker powers at once. Variable Tinker can now also be improved through Negentropy, similar to Paramount, such as allowing you to directly summon any Tinker power you can think of that is equal to a Tier 1 power.
addons.title: Paramount Tinker

objects.text:
When you trigger this power, you get a single, somewhat random, Tinker specialization centred around solving a problem of your choice. This Tinker specialization can only be on par with a Tier 1 Tinker power at most, but it's generally oriented around helping you with whatever problem you present to it.

This specialization can stay for either a maximum of 1 month or as long as the problem persists, whichever is shorter. You can freely drop your Tinker specialization and acquire a new one at any time. You have an instinctive understanding of what your Tinker specialization is and have full access to the Tinker technology tree encompassed by it, akin to a normal Tinker.

You can operate and maintain any tinkertech you've previously built, regardless of your current specialization, but you cannot build it from scratch again. You may also integrate and mix tinkertech from your current specialization into previously constructed tinkertech, but you're unable to do the reverse.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Variable Tinker

objects.text:
You are a Tinker who specializes in the construction of living metals, a multitude of different metallic substances that possess DNA and various other organic properties.

These organic properties include but are not limited to: living metal being able to passively self-repair and maintain itself if it has adequate access to energy and resources while not damaged beyond repair. You’ll also find that, similar to different organic organisms, different types of living metal excel in different environments like the desert, rainforest, Mars, Antarctica, or even the deep sea.

You will find it easy to recycle or modify Tinkertech made out of living metal, using forms of genetic manipulation technology provided by this power that specializes in the manipulation of living metal DNA.

Another big benefit to living metal is the way it communicates with itself, saving space in the Tinkertech you construct. Essentially, technology made of living metal has little need for cables and other such methods to transmit instructions to its various components.

This is because living metal, in addition to its other capabilities, can be used as a medium to transmit information and instruments to other pieces of living metal and technology if it is physically connected to either, all while being used to form the frame, armor, or even the entirety of a piece of Tinkertech.

This specialty is capable of touching most forms of Tinkertech constructed out of inorganic materials to one degree or another, such as melee weapons, guns, armor, computers, circuitry, cybernetics, or robots—just to name a few examples.

While this specialty is versatile, it does not surpass specialties like (Tinker) Robots or (Tinker) Cybernetics in their field, as it merely offers a specialized approach. It has great synergy with specialties that focus on the construction of tinkertech out of inorganic materials, especially metals.
objects.title: (Tinker) Living Metallurgist

objects.text:
You are a Tinker with a dual specialty: one aspect of this power focusing on light manipulation, the other on darkness manipulation.

Your first specialty is capable of any and all conceivable technological light-based shenanigans to one degree or another.  This includes, but is not limited to, hardlight, photon beam weaponry, solar reactors, and even limited temporal manipulation.

Your second specialty is a bit more esoteric and hard to understand from a purely human perspective. After all, darkness is just the absence of light.

Yet this technology is somehow still able to interact with darkness and use it to affect the world in ways equal to your light manipulation specialty.

To list a few examples, your darkness manipulation technology is capable of feats such as making solid shadows, enveloping an environment in shadow even in the middle of the day, reducing energy and matter in an environment, and even some limited spatial manipulation.
objects.title: (Tinker) Twilight Tinker

objects.text: Your specialty is creating evil opposites of parahumans. You can clone people, build robot duplicates, or create power-granting serums that only work for candidates who are opposites of the original in some way. The powers you give are based on the powers of the original, but work in different ways; for example, an opposite of Skitter could have powerful telekinesis that only works on bugs, rather than control over insect nervous systems. These powers are usually moderately stronger than the original, and tend to be more overtly destructive and forceful. You have a secondary Thinker ability to identify core core components of a person's identity and what the inverse of those would be, and a minor additional specialty in evil versions of cape costumes.
objects.title: (Tinker/Trump) Antagonist Builder

addons.title: Juryrigger
addons.text: The ceiling on what you can throw together on the spot is raised dramatically, at the expense of durability, repairability, and interoperability. With this, it's no longer fair to call your tech "low-end"; you would be considered a solidly mid-tier Tinker based only on what you could cobble together in a few minutes time. Just don't expect tech you assemble under those conditions to last very long. You can choose not to make this tradeoff when you need to build something more robust, but if you're willing to make the sacrifice you can always be expected to have a varied assortment of impressive but disposable tinkertech at hand, even if that means building an arsenal mid-combat. This is particularly useful for single-use gadgets and weapons, which don't suffer as much for the lost durability. However, short of Frankentech-tier resourcefulness, don't expect devices you put together under these conditions to be worth iterating on or salvaging once they've been used up.

objects.text:
You have access to an extremely basic, low-end database of generic tinkertech. To say you got the short end of the stick, to have 'lost’ the Tinker lottery is… a lie. Because you have something all those other Tinkers don't have enough of: Time. Not in the sense that you can give yourself more of it, or something to that effect. But rather, you have more time in the sense that you tinker so impossibly fast that you make use of the time you have far better than any other Tinker ever could.

You tinker approximately 25x faster compared to the average Tinker, without sacrificing even a shred of quality from your creations. The sponge that takes much of a Tinker’s time, that of maintaining all of their creations, becomes a mere fraction of your day rather than a fair chunk of it. This allows you to maintain even more pieces of tinkertech than a Tinker reasonably could.

Furthermore, this allows you the option to adopt a reckless 'playstyle’ that would normally be dashed away as inefficient by the rest of the world: Tinkering in the middle of combat, and in environments that are not prepared by the Tinker in advance. Having a small army of expendable drones hold off your enemy as you use the surrounding materials to give yourself additional means of fighting your opponents is now a viable strategy for you to perform.

You still require materials like any other Tinker, and this doesn't negate the weakness of time entirely, merely allowing you to do far more with what time you have.
objects.title: (Tinker) Fastest Tinker Alive

objects.text:
You are a tinker specialized in energetic exothermic reactions. This includes everything from the humble campfire to the propellants of rocket ships and missiles, to nuclear bombs, and all the chemistry in between. 

Plus, you can put those tiny to large explosions to use. If it requires some form of exothermic release to power, or needs to resist the energies of such, you can build and make it. From guns to flamethrowers to cookware to blast furnaces to, at the highest end, nuclear engines, to the blast and heat and chemical resistant materials needed for all of it.
objects.title: (Tinker) The Dao of EXPLOSIONS!

objects.text: Anyone you hit with this power experiences migraines and sees flashing colors. This blast smacks with the force of a strong punch, traveling at twenty miles per hour (20mph). It can be utilized on a Thinker to stop their power from working for about 10 seconds, tops.
objects.title: (Blaster) Epilepsy

objects.text: You can fire off large, seemingly ominous beams of energy blasting a thundering noise once it strikes something. Said beams, when colliding with a living being cause them to be mildly ticklish.
objects.title: (Blaster) Super Murder Death Beams

objects.text: When you throw an item, it’ll come back to your hands if you so choose. Thrown items will slowly and continuously accelerate when flying back. Once closer, it’ll be easily caught at all times with no harm. It will continue to fly back and forth if you don’t catch it, though.
objects.title: (Blaster) Boomerang

objects.text: You can summon an icicle anywhere within your sight. You do not have control over it once summoned, and it causes physical strain in proportion to mass.
objects.title: (Blaster) Icicle

objects.text: As long as you have at least one projectile left, you will never run out. You can create phantasmal copies of your ammo that work just as well as the original, though they do dissipate 10 seconds after impact.
objects.title: (Blaster) Unlimited Ammo Works

objects.text: You can modify any projectile to whatever form you want. You can change the projectile’s appearance, shape, size, and weight. At most, its size and weight can be off by a single order of magnitude.  Modifying the projectiles’ surrounding properties isn’t out of your reach, altering their visibility, loudness, or air resistance, sacrificing other properties. While you can change various properties in tandem, one altered property will stand out at their expense.
objects.title: (Blaster) Custom Projectile

addons.text: You can now use your phantom limbs for purposes beyond violence. With your newfound dexterity, you may use these phantom limbs better than you could your own body. They are limited by LOS, and may be selectively tangible. You may treat these phantoms limbs as an extension of your own body, allowing them to be an origin for your powers. While the strength of a phantom limb is originally a mirror to its physical counterpart, it does not have a limit on how much it may grow from extensive usage. The maximum amount of phantom limbs that may be present at once is proportional to your ability to concentrate on them.
addons.title: Mage Hand

objects.text: Punching and kicking empty air creates phantom limbs in the distance which will copy your movements. You can choose where they appear.
objects.title: (Blaster) Phantom Punches

objects.text: You can point at any small object and teleport it directly into your hand. If something is too big, it will feel a strong tug in your direction and fail to teleport.
objects.title: (Blaster) Mine Now!

objects.text:
By slapping your hand against the hollow end of a tube-shaped object, your power rips through it and hits whatever it's pointed towards. At impact, it detonates, causing a shockwave strong enough to lift a person off the ground.

You can adjust the specifics of this shockwave by using different tubes, longer ones increasing range, narrow ones increasing throwback and larger ones broadening the affected area in exchange for shorter range.
objects.title: (Blaster) Tubeshock

addons.text: Through your ability to speak by not speaking at all, you do not need to audibly say "Gandr" to summon this projectile anymore and can instead just point while silently speaking to yourself. This also applies to any of Gandr's upgrades.
addons.title: Chantless

objects.text:
You gain the ability to shoot a red ball-like projectile by pointing your index finger and saying "Gandr". This projectile has no real effect on objects but has an aura that decreases the physical health of people near it. This aura only extends about 2 meters, and the farther someone is from the projectile, the less effective it is, with it being most effective when the projectile directly hits someone. This effect translates into making them slightly more tired, slightly weaker, and healing marginally slower, but the effects stack with each shot.

Note: This aura does not affect you
objects.title: (Blaster/Shaker) Gandr

objects.text:
You can summon classic cartoon hazards directly above a target in your line of sight, namely anvils, pianos, or boxes of lit dynamite. The objects appear suspended for a brief moment before dropping rapidly under normal gravity.

The summoned objects are real and permanent, capable of causing damage and disruption, though they follow exaggerated “cartoon logic” more than realistic physics. Dynamite explodes on impact, while anvils and pianos deliver crushing force capable of flattening, pinning, or heavily injuring targets. These exaggerated capabilities disappear shortly after impact turning into mundane items.

Accuracy decreases with distance and movement, making stationary or distracted targets much easier to hit.
objects.title: (Blaster/Shaker) ACME

objects.text:
Not only do your blasts hit with a good amount of force, just as the strongest kick you can muster, but they also get ideas or thoughts stuck in the target’s head. If you prefer, another blast to their face is enough to remove these earworms.

These blasts resemble Gallant’s in appearance and similarity.
objects.title: (Blaster/Master) Earworm

objects.text: You can shoot a blast of energy that, if it hits an opponent, forces them toward you at about 5 miles per hour.
objects.title: (Blaster) Hookshot

objects.text: You can modify your projectiles to apply a debuff, such as burn, stun, caustic, poisonous, disease, hypnotic, sensory deprivation, or fatigue.
objects.title: (Blaster) Debuff

objects.text:
The microsecond you launch a projectile, whether via a weapon, your hands or any other means, you can instantaneously accelerate it up to the muzzle velocity of a standard M16 rifle round, approximately 960 m/s. 

For example, a thrown penny would carry similar kinetic energy to that of a handgun’s bullet whereas a brick could strike with force equivalent to an autocannon shell. You can set the exact speed of your projectiles, which follow normal aerodynamics after acceleration.
objects.title: (Blaster) David’s Sling

objects.text: You can shoot blasts out from your hands that hit with the force of a sledgehammer, and move at roughly 100km/h. These blasts can be modified, such as increasing the blast angle in exchange for effective range, thinning them to increase their piercing power, lowering their force to increase their speed, or lowering their overall power for sustained fire. You cannot have more than one modification happening at a time.
objects.title: (Blaster) Handcannon

objects.text: You’re capable of shooting endless sprays of needles at the firing rate of a machine gun. These needles can punch through concrete, are about 30cm long and are made of steel. Due to being needles they'll also fly a lot farther than machine gun bullets generally would.
objects.title: (Blaster) Needle Gunner

objects.text: You can release bullets from your hand, at about the fire rate of an M16. These bullets are homing, going after who or whatever you choose as the target. The longer they home the slower the bullets go.
objects.title: (Blaster) Blaster

objects.text: Unseen attacks from you deal twice the damage they normally would. This can apply to any form of attack so long as they are not aware of its existence.
objects.title: (Blaster/Striker) Sneak Attack

objects.text: You can create beams of energy that can connect and interact with the real world instead of destroying it. You can control these beams freely, allowing you to make them wrap around objects, latch onto buildings, use them as a grappling hook, intercept attacks, and so on. You can control how thin these get and how large they get. While there is no range, you cannot sense through them.
objects.title: (Blaster) Hand Lights

addons.text:
Your coins can now be set on ghost trajectories themselves, on a much finer scale. You can ‘deposit’ your coins as you throw them, making them disappear into thin air. All that remains of them is their ghost trajectory locked in stasis relative to yourself, from which you can ‘withdraw’ them anytime back into existence at any point within their ghost trajectory, from the apex of their arc to the moment they land at your feet. So long as they remain in the air, you can deposit them back into the nothing. 

Any ranged attack that comes into contact with these coins is imbued with Stop-Hit’s effect in an instant, redirecting to wherever you please the moment it makes contact with a coin. Punching a coin also imbues it with Stop-Hit. Lastly, ricochets between coins become instant, allowing for immediate build-up of force.
addons.title: Breaking the Bank

addons.text:
Your power now refines your understanding of trajectories and instant impacts by merging your spatial intuition with the spatial warping provided by Stop-Hit. Your ghost trajectories become physical impossibilities, as the nature of your power changes.

You gain a passive Thinker sense that constantly maps out all potential ghost trajectories in your line of sight, taking and factoring in any geometry and dynamic environments involved. The power runs a predictive algorithm that updates in real time, highlighting when and how a shot will connect even in evolving combat situations. A bullet can now hit someone behind a wall if there exists any line—straight or snaking, bouncing or burrowing—that lets it.

Lastly, you can now choose for the ghost trajectory to dynamically ignore or acknowledge certain environmental physics at different points along itself. This allows for insane amounts of precision and accuracy: a projectile dropping then going steady, the wind curving it then going straight, ricocheting against what it should have pierced and piercing through what it should have ricocheted against.
addons.title: Down Sights

addons.text:
When anything enters your line of sight that you deem a target, they are instantly marked by a ghost trajectory from somewhere out of your sight, unable to be seen no matter how you turn your head - as if you’d launched an attack yourself but without an actual projectile, from the perfect vantage point at the time. You can choose to invoke the usage of this trajectory at will by assigning a projectile to follow along that path, which will act as if it had hit the moment your target was first marked by a ghost trajectory. No matter how many defenses they put up, no matter what powers they might call upon - when you saw them, they had already been shot. You just make them realize that in the now.

You can choose to reset the ghost trajectory at any time in case you first saw your target with all defenses up or in a place without any too good vantage points, allowing you to ‘shoot’ them while they are/were more vulnerable or open. You can use your set ghost trajectories over and over even past the expiry of your targets, hitting the same spot every time.
addons.title: A Full Stop to Life

objects.text:
Any projectile utilized by you - thrown, fired, etcetera - immediately reaches the endpoint of its trajectory, connecting in an instant. Stones flung from slings disappear into thin air, reappearing right in front of an enemy’s head. Bullets exit the barrel and simply pop back into reality a millimeter away from contact. Your power takes the beginning and end of the trajectory, and cuts out the time between the two.

The ‘ghost trajectory’ of your projectiles, by default, ignores nearly every environmental factor present that could affect its direction. Like an FPS character, anywhere you point a gun is where the bullet will land. No wind affecting where it goes, no gravity dragging it downwards. However, its effective range remains the same - neither friction nor air resistance can be ignored, as do other such relevant forces, unless they’re actively shortening the projectile’s natural effective range. Alternatively, you could choose to let select factors affect the ghost trajectory individually, allowing you to plan your shots much more effectively. If bullet drop can help you land a good shot, you can let gravity affect the trajectory.

This means you can teleport anything you throw for as far as you can throw it, as well. To assist your control over this power, you gain an understanding of your ghost trajectory as it moves according to the objects you plan to throw, and as it shifts depending on what environmental factors you choose to exclude from it.
objects.title: (Blaster/Thinker) Stop-Hit

addons.text:
Incandescent intensifies your beams of light, enhancing the beam’s potency to burn through steel and concrete, range to a 900ft radius, and versatility to modify your beams to a burst of light containing concussive force and heat or a volley of beams of light.

This union loosens the power’s limitations concerning celestial bodies to a limited degree, as you can use limited beams of light coming from the sun or moon for a finisher within a 50ft radius of your choosing that leaves a 50-meter deep crater, offset by a window of recharge of 2 minutes.
addons.title: Missing Star

objects.text: You can amplify the luminous intensity/power of any light source, such as lamps, street lights, or candles, within your vicinity to a blinding and concussive force, emitting rays of light out of them. This, obviously, makes you immune to blindness or ocular damage you may suffer from this and require external sources of light to function, excluding celestial bodies.
objects.title: (Blaster) Incandescent

objects.text:
You can absorb the practical expertise of anyone you focus on.

The skills you can absorb can be increased by things such as eye contact or physical contact, with each connection made increasing the breadth and depth of what you are able to steal, whether a specific skill or a target's general skill set.

Unless you completely steal a target's skill, they will regain the skill over time.

You permanently retain any stolen skills and can improve them by re-stealing partially stolen skills or stealing similar skills.
objects.title: (Blaster/Master) Skill Thief

objects.text: You can erase matter using your blood as a medium. Anything your blood touches can be atomized. An example is splattering your blood on their opponents, which disintegrates your targets. Blood loss is still a fatal concern, as you’re still a normal human without Brute or Breaker powers.
objects.title: (Blaster) Bloody Hell

objects.text: You can now shoot whatever type of weaponry with the correct gestures and sounds e.g. copying a pistol or revolver with a ‘Bang!’ and a finger gun or a ray gun with ‘pew-pew!’.
objects.title: (Blaster) Pew Pew!

objects.text: You can grow large feathers along your skin that are hard enough to act as light armor and can fire these feathers as accurate projectiles.
objects.title: (Blaster/Changer) Birdie!

objects.text: You can imbue projectiles with your powers. Powers like Mover and Brute powers would affect the projectile itself, while powers like Striker powers would affect those the projectile touches.
objects.title: (Blaster/Trump) Imbue Projectile

addons.text: Your ability to inflict damage with insults has synergized with and grown in combination with your nature as a savant of insulting others. Not only do your insults inflict physical damage, but also mental damage and, should you have Shardless or Esoteric Knowledge, even spiritual damage. A well placed insult can not only eviscerate someone’s body but also flay their psyche. You can selectively choose what is damaged by your insults, such as shredding someone’s mind without physically harming them. The damage your insults inflict is still dependent on how hurtful the insult is.
addons.title: Words Hurt

objects.text: When insulting someone or a group of people, you can cause actual physical damage. The more hurtful the insult, the stronger the damage. The damage ignores conventional physical defence.
objects.title: (Blaster/Shaker) Vicious Mockery

objects.text: You gain a short-ranged Blaster power, taking the form of writhing, near-invisible "whips" of energy. These whips are Manton limited, allowing them to pass through inorganic matter only. The whips work by inducing debilitating, permanent physical mutations on those struck. Examples include: having the targets legs fused into a single mangled, paralysed limb or having heavy tangle of bone snakes grow between the targets ribcage making every breath a struggle.
objects.title: (Blaster) Mutation

objects.text:
You can conjure and launch tangled orbs of forcefield bindings. These orbs will uncurl and tangle around whatever it hits, binding the object in the most immobilizing way possible.

If an orb strikes an already entangled object, its energy will be absorbed into the existing bindings, making them stronger, tighter and thinner, digging into and slicing the object.

The entanglements will dissipate if it takes significant damage, or if the object its surrounding is destroyed.
objects.title: (Blaster) Shibari

objects.text:
