Note: If you choose to give one of your Characters the RESET button your ownership of the AU will allow you to remember across Resets and your own Resets can overrule theirs.

objects.text:
Connected to your soul is your very own world. This world exists within its own pocket dimension but can also be brought into any universe you're currently in. Be careful not to accidentally crash it into another planet.

Its size, shape, and composition are perfectly tailored to your needs, whether it's a normal Earth-sized world, a ring world, or an Alderson Disk. You have a sun of appropriate size and distance to make the world habitable, along with at least one moon of any color or design. Once chosen it's shape is not stagnant. It will continue to change to match your preference such is becoming bigger, smaller, changing the color of the atmosphere, changing what animal life is around.

Any powers you possess can potentially alter the environment, flora, fauna, or even the atmosphere to suit your needs. Your abilities can shape the planet into an ideal habitat for your growth. For example, if you have mana, your world might develop leylines that saturate the environment with magical energy, transforming the wildlife into magical creatures. A crafting ability could modify the metals on your world, creating esoteric materials necessary for your craft.

If your world is ever severely damaged or destroyed, you can return it to its pocket dimension, where it will be almost instantly repaired. Be careful not to accidentally leave yourself stranded in space! As this is your personal world it cannot be stolen from you, you can teleport to it and from it, make portals to allow access, summon it with a thought, or even move it as a vehicle for travel. Your world will continuously grow and improve as you grow stronger and observe unique traits of other worlds.
objects.title: Personal World

addons.text: Summoners deal, it’s just what they do. Your patronage has given you an incredible insight into certain External entities. So much is this the case, that you can retain your ability to Summon while bonded to them. This onl;y applies to your own patron, and you still must make your own deal with them, but this will massively increase the potency of your relevant abilities from them.
addons.title: Born Diplomat

objects.text: Your body has been changed, edited, warped, into something truly magnificent. Running through your veins is the legacy of one of the great concepts, great external beings from outside the multiversal clusters they orbit. In the space between these worlds they sit and influence, rarely placing their fingers into clusters, but allowing echoes of their great might to fundamentally alter these clusters as they develop. You are a Heir of one of these great beings. As a Heir, the fundamental nature, your body… isn’t. Your mind is held outside of existence while your body is a shell, a kind of avatar that has the meat of a man stretched upon it. Beneath the meat stands the force of your parentage, waiting to break free from its meaty shackles. As such, you possess a kind of resurrection, in that if the echo your patron Concept can be found where you are, you’ll be restored when finally rendered ‘dead’. Each Heir presents in a manner fitting of their personality and tendencies filtered through their patron in this way. The remaining nature of your abilities is determined by your Patron. Though there are many minor concepts permeating countless Multiversal Clusters such as Light and Hope, below are common examples with their echoes virtually omnipresent throughout many clusters. Gravity, The force that moves all things. As the force that defines attraction, Heirs of Gravity gain more than the obvious domain over the ambient force, but can express it through social means, pushing and pulling people together as they see fit. As one of the most constant constants of all, Gravity can be found in almost every multiversal cluster comprehensible to the human mind, and as such they are exceptionally difficult to dispatch without an understanding of their nature. Time, the force of consistency. As the force of sequence and all that moves, Time also represents a kind of balance. Time necessitates cost, it represents both a relentless decay that ever moves forwards and the growth that proceeds and follows it. Time necessitates cost in all it touches, Magic, Gravity and Life bend to its necessity on cause and effect. Heirs of Time, therefore find themselves emphasising these costs, both metaphorically, manipulating the expenditures of energy and effort, and literally, finding wealth within their purview as a corollary. Matter, the force of the real. Matter is foundationally a consistent reality, an underlying set of rules that allows existence to function under them. Mater is not strictly objects, but Energy and Emotion as well, it constructs that which constructs rules as much as it is them itself, social as well as physical. Heirs of Matter tend to take this to the extreme, finding purchase in both the obvious and vulgar manipulations of energy and matter, but also in the construction of rituals, rules, and social contracts that though ethereal are impossibly strong. Life, the force of creation and finality. Life is near omnipresent within observed multiversal clusters. It’s overruling principles of adaptation and persistence affecting more than even magic. But Life is not just beings that live, it is the force of all things animate. Death is an aspect of life also. Heirs of Life often find themselves at the crossroads of an apparent dichotomy. Emphasis on the dead and the living go hand in hand, finding bridges and crossing over often. The summoning and creation of creatures is as much a piece of life as actively denying its effects to another. A Heir that focuses on adaptation to the ends of nothing else may well find themselves incomprehensible if they were to consider ‘life’ as only living. Luck, the force of possibility. Having the dubious honour of being the only External that’s capable of being accurately called ‘mercurial’, Luck is the essence of choice. Every possible path exists within its purview. Every vector and mathematical improbability. Heirs also follow this trend. Unknown and unpredictable, Its Heirs tend to act similarly, agents of alteration and opposition for its own sake. Predicting the path of history, or changing it to their designs. They hold both vulgar denials of likelihood and subtle knives in the dark. Fate, the force of resolution. All things come to an end, such is the way of things that they end. Even Death must die eventually, and this is as Fate is. Fate represents certainty, and clarity, a denial of the subjective to produce the factual in totality. It is in this manner it represents thought and logic in addition to the final end. Fate is progressive, and its end everchanging, but the end will come, it is a certainty. Heirs of Fate find this certainty and ending as their primary expressions. Stillness and certainty are their weapons, as devastating and relentless as their patron. Magic, The force of all that is nonsense. Magic is everything which Is Not. Everything that is unreal and does not exist within a cluster it surrounds. Its echoes deny its kin, break rules and possibilities, and present themselves a kind of ordered chaos both beautiful and terrible to behold. Heirs of Magic are unpredictable completely and utterly. They define their ‘domains’ because there are no rules to their patron. Where one defines a touch that chills as elemental, another sees it as necromantic, to say nothing of the source of their energies, constantly changing from universe to universe even within their clusters. These are only the most homogenised accounts of Externals and their heirs, as mentioned earlier. Heirs can work to grow their abilities, each beginning with only passing and minor influence over their patron’s aspects. Similarly, they are only able to focus on one aspect of growth at a time.
objects.title: Heir of an Echo

addons.text:
Your ability to manifest and command opposing extremes has prompted your Domains to mutate. Aside from the knack of letting you swap Domains between hands semi-freely, this can manifest in one of two ways, depending on your choice of pairing:

If you chose to have synergistic Domains, you may apply the effects of Dual Embodiment to them like any other power, though with only a fraction of the energy expended; evolving a pair of Fire and Lightning into also being Ice and Water would only be a slight drain rather than fairly exhausting, and further developments where possible would be similarly faster and cleaner.

If you chose to have opposing Domains, however, you could instead ‘bootstrap’ Dual Embodiment to link both Domains into parts of a greater whole; both domains would share a much greater upper limit and rate of growth, due to the combined well of ‘power’ for them to draw from. Furthermore, DE could also be used to stretch and broaden the variety of what your dual-Domain can accomplish, at least to a decent upper limit.
addons.title: Two Sides of One

addons.text: ...Hold on, what? You know what, no, just roll with it. It seems that, rather than being able to pick more freeform Domains by taking this addon - if you opt in to it - you now have access to not only a PAIR of Aspects rather than singular, but also a pair of Classes as well: You must pick either your Aspects or Classes to be bound to your Twin Hands, but the other pair can be used and exchanged freely between both. For the purposes of related/opposite pairings concerning Aspects and Classes: Related pairs must be "adjacent" to each other on the proverbial wheel (e.g. Light & Life/Time, Witch & Heir/Knight/Thief), and opposites must be paired with their counterpart twins (e.g. Light & Void, Prince/Bard & Maid/Seer). With the newfound power granted by the Twin Hands, you can now access a lesser imitation of true God-Tier abilities; nowhere near the forces of nature a fully realized Classpect can achieve, but still a force to be reckoned with - and one that can grow over time, potentially up to such heights with extreme training. If you somehow achieve a more natural God-Tiering as well, then the power from that will compound with whatever strength you've bled for on your own as well. If taken with Master Classes, Lord and Muse must be taken either with each other or a same/opposite-polarity Class, based on which pair-type was chosen.
addons.title: Twin Roles

addons.text:
Faced with similarities like this, it should be obvious, shouldn't it? The power of your Domains has now also bled into the thousand other hands at your disposal, allowing them to draw on your Twin Hands' powers as well.

While this comes at the small cost of being forced to choose between their normal strength and drawing on your Domains when in use, the benefits are immediately obvious: As your more spectral limbs are already formidable on their own, each one can harness the same level of initial power as you yourself, with you being able to exploit their sheer quantity and capacity for merging and compounding strength to reach especially monstrous levels of power.

Bear in mind, however, that they are still subject to your own strain proportionate to the amount you use. If you tax your additional hands beyond their own proportionate limit, they will still suffer temporary weakening or crippling from the backlash, as if they were struck by psychic damage.

At-will as a bonus, you may opt to give the Unseen Hands a more spectral and ethereal appearance rather than invisibility, for when you want them to be overt and/or just to show off.
addons.title: Spectral Dominion

objects.text: You now possess a two-sided ability; in each arm you have a Domain, an aspect or element that you can use to channel powers of various kinds - with a catch. While you can pick any two concepts to be your Domains, from classical elements like Fire or Metal to the more abstract like Creation or Evolution, the two aspects must be tangentially linked in one of two ways: Either A) your Domains must be sufficiently close, like pairing Fire with Lightning, or they must oppose each other, like pairing Healing and Poison. Your Twin Hands' powers can be used in a variety of ways: If one Domain was Creation, you'd be able to create handheld mundane items easily, or make entire rooms' worth of more temporary, ethereal constructs that'd last up to hours if not maintained; If you chose Healing, you'd be able to cure most-anything short of lost parts or death by touch - yourself included - or exude a house-sized aura that more slowly regenerates. Overuse of your abilities beyond what's listed above will result in increasing physical and mental strain; aches, soreness, headaches and fatigue, possibly scaling up to unconsciousness and long-term injury. Training and routine usage can acclimate you more and more, gradually increasing your soft and maximum "thresholds" for exerting your powers. If you instead have limbs like wings, pincers or tentacles in place of more humanoid arms, you can still channel your Domains through them. Should you completely lack anything that could be called "arms", however, as a failsafe your power will let you conjure a pair of phantom limbs that function like your own flesh and blood.
objects.title: Twin Hands of Power

objects.text: You have been gifted a most wondrous blessing, one that can give others something out of their wildest dreams. Of course, we mean the privilege of going to another world with their memories intact. How? The good old fashioned way, that’s how! The ‘Truck-Kun Classic’! Congratulations, you are now a Truck-Kun Foundation Verified Isekai’r! As a signing-on bonus, you will be given a mundane vehicle of choice on the house. The only condition is that it must be a land-based vehicle. This vehicle will be given endless fuel, enhanced to endure what it normally couldn’t, and is given a little more ‘oomph’ for anyone you may find on the road! If you have an Object(s) of Power that fits the criteria, you may use them as well for the purposes of this Power. Using your chosen vehicle(s), you can designate any person you take the life of as your ’Victim’. By doing this, you legally usurp jurisdiction over their soul and send them to a random world. This could be one you know, maybe one you don’t, who knows! Upon their arrival, they will be given a mental list of objectives or ‘Quests’ of varying difficulties. By completing Quests, they will not only be rewarded for their efforts, but it’ll also fill out a bar meant to record their progress in completing Quests. If they completely fill the Progress Bar and finalize it, they are given the choice of either going back to their world with everything they earned in the other world, or stay in the world they were Isekai’d to. Regardless of their choice, this will be counted as a ‘Successful Isekai’ to you. If the Victim dies before they can fill the bar and/or somehow is in a position where they can’t continue completing Quests (i.e. being sealed away forever), then it will be marked as a ‘Failed Isekai’. To you, achieving a Successful Isekai gives you a well of Energy that you can use to permanently upgrade or otherwise improve this Power, with the amount depending on how many Quests they completed. A Victim who fills the bare minimum would give a fair amount, but someone who took their time to complete every single Quest on the list would give a *humongous amount!* A Failed Isekai does not take Energy away, but it gives nothing in return. Using Energy, you can either enhance your vehicle, making it able to give more powerful people a chance of a lifetime, or you can gain more control over the Isekai process. From retroactively establishing identities for your Victims, having a moment to explain their situation personally, giving them new bodies to inhabit, or even giving them a Cheat Ability or Skill! All you need is the Energy to afford it. With a drive to improve and a wheel to get behind, you’ll be ready for anything! So go ahead and get driving! Starting out, you can only have 3 Active Victims (Victims who are still alive, completing Quests) at any given time. Inactive Victims (Victims who have Succeeded or Failed in their Isekai, either or) do not take up those slots. Using Energy, you can increase the maximum number of Active Victims you can have, and much more. The Truck-Kun Foundation is not liable or held responsible for any rogue elements or heinous actions your Victims perform or become involved with. Designation as a Victim does not bind them to the Isekai’r in any way, shape, or form, beyond having the final say on where their soul goes to when they die, bar intervention from a higher-up from the Truck-Kun Foundation. Choose your Victims wisely.
objects.title: Me and My Truck(-Kun)

objects.text:
You can take an idea for a thing and turn it into actual, solid matter. Metal, stone, glass, plastic, ceramics, exotic alloys, strange crystals—anything that counts as non-living substance is fair game. You can form it in any state you like: solid blocks, flowing liquids in containers, gases held in tanks, even glowing, superheated material, as long as it’s not part of a living system. This power simply refuses to produce flesh, organs, blood, plants, food, or anything that qualifies as “alive” or directly sustains life.

What you get out matches what you understand. Simple shapes and tools are effortless: beams, plates, wires, chains, pipes, basic weapons, armor, mechanical parts you know well. For complicated objects, your knowledge sets the limit. If you know how a gun, engine, or computer actually goes together—the parts, their layout, the connections—you can produce a working version. If you only know the outside shape, you get a convincing shell and dead guts inside. No “fake it ’til you make it” shortcuts.

Every piece you make can be either permanent or temporary. When you create it, you decide whether it behaves like ordinary matter from then on, or whether it’s tied to your will. Temporary items stay solid and functional until you dismiss them or set a time for them to break down, at which point they vanish cleanly or crumble into harmless dust, your choice. Permanent items behave as if they were always part of the world and stay that way unless someone breaks them by normal means.

You have edit rights over your own work. Anything you’ve created can be reshaped, resized, reforged, or broken down and re-made into something else, as long as you’re in range and paying attention. A wall can become a staircase, a sword can become a chain, a solid block can hollow out into a vault. You can also “patch” or repair your own creations instantly, filling cracks, replacing lost pieces, or upgrading them with new details as your understanding improves.

The strange part is what you can do with materials themselves. You’re not limited to the periodic table as it exists. If you can clearly describe what you want a substance to do and how it behaves—unbreakable under normal forces, impossibly dense yet stable, perfectly blocking all radiation, no friction on one side but high friction on the other—you can bring that material into being and build with it. It doesn’t have to obey real-world engineering, only the rules you lay down for it.

That said, you don’t get free omniscience. If you try to specify contradictory properties (“weightless, infinitely dense, melts at room temperature, never melts at all”) the power forces a compromise or simply fails to produce anything until you settle on a coherent set of traits. The clearer your concept, the more reliable and usable the end result. Over time, as you experiment and learn, your library of custom materials and working designs naturally grows.

You can’t fix or rewrite matter made by other people with this ability—only what you’ve created yourself. But within that domain, you own every bolt, slab, and impossible alloy, from ordinary steel beams to exotic, physics-breaking components that simply shouldn’t exist and yet do.
objects.title: Unreal Foundry

objects.text: There is always a bigger fish. You have a rare talent for fixing big problems by calling a bigger problem. When you use this power, it will summon a random creature that is approximately 50% stronger than the target you select. The creature will always be selected from creatures capable of killing your target that have a reason to kill your target. The multiverse is quite large after all. All other factors are disregarded. You are treated as if you have Beneath Notice protecting you from whatever you summon regardless of their power relative to you. This doesn’t prevent it from killing you by accident, only from doing so intentionally, so watch out for splash damage. After being summoned, it will then proceed to go on a rampage, killing whatever you summoned it to fight, most likely causing immense collateral damage in the process before disappearing back to wherever it came from shortly after the target has been dealt with. This power has no cooldown and activates instantly. However, you can only have one creature summoned at once per target.
objects.title: Caller of Disaster

objects.text:
You gain the ability to selectively change the effective weight of yourself or anything you touch. For example you can simultaneously make a sword weigh next to nothing for you, but weigh a ton for anyone else, resulting in a nigh immovable block. 

One effect is when things fall beneath a certain weight they gain a slight buoyancy similar to a feather. This can allow you to jump incredibly high, then float slowly down and land. You could make yourself an immovable object, assuming your natural durability could keep up, or make yourself weigh next to nothing in the air.

The weight range is from 5 ounces to 10 tons. This power does not effect the actual weight of the target, only the weight they are treated as having when interacted with. The effect persists even when you let go, and you need to touch the target again if you want to re-alter their weight.
objects.title: Light as Air, Heavy as Stone

objects.text:
You have inherited the unique protection of the prototypical damsel. That may seem bad but it comes with its perks. Your enemies won’t try to kill you they will instead capture you. They will do their best to avoid hurting you as well. 

For some reason you will always have nice accommodations. This power always activates without fail. 

This doesn’t limit your powers in any way and you can still try to escape if you wish. If you get caught they will just put you back in your “accommodations” without seriously trying to prevent another escape attempt. 

This is accomplished through a combination of mental filters and specialized fate manipulation.
objects.title: Damsel Syndrome

objects.text: You have a unique connection to dragons. This connection manifests as an absurd talent and empathic instinct for interacting with dragons as well as luck in general when it comes to them. This is to the extent that you could stumble upon a young wild dragon and within a matter of days have it fly you around as your loyal mount, or accidentally trespass into the lair of an ancient dragon and walk away not only unscathed, but with a piece of treasure freely given from their horde if you had no malicious intentions. Dragons in general instinctively feel that you are trustworthy, noteworthy, and your mere presence is soothing to them in such a way that a rampaging dragon can be brought back to their senses and cease their violence just from hearing you sing a lullaby. This can quickly develop into genuine love, compassion, and respect towards you if you choose to develop a relationship with them. Even an evil dragon would hesitate to harm you unless you give them a genuinely good reason to, such as you attacking them first, and you could theoretically help them commit to a heel face turn with enough time and effort (though expect members of innately malevolent subspecies to take at least a decade of work on your part). Note that if you actively antagonize them, these effects won’t work as well, though they at least keep the possibility of eventually reconciling with them and earning back their trust and friendship where for others they would swear an unending bloodfeud. Your luck is similarly affected, such that if there is a one in a million chance of anyone even seeing a dragon on a given day, for you it’s more like one in ten. Whether it is a small batlike lizard that shoots sparks or a mighty reality warping Dragon God, it is always possible, and even somewhat likely for you to run into them. If you actively try to find them, you are pretty much guaranteed to unless they are actively trying to avoid you or anyone in general. Not only that, but the random meetings are almost always somehow favorable to you in some way, whether that is you ending up with a minor piece of treasure, a hint towards completing a quest, a threat to scare off some bandits chasing you, or the dragon itself being willing to fly you to the grocery store. This partially extends to beings related or connected to dragons, though the more tenuous the connection the weaker the effects are. A being made in the image of a dragon like a mechanical dragon or an insect dragon would be nearly as affected by this as a true dragon, while a half-dragon would be much friendlier to you than the average person. A human with a dragon core or aspect would have an easier time getting along with you especially if this aspect was strengthened in some way, while a mere dragonfly would be nearly completely unaffected due to how tenuous their connection to dragons is. Note: If you have a dragon aspect yourself it is somewhat enhanced, mostly by being easier to use, though if interacting with dragons can in any way strengthen it, it is practically guaranteed to happen unless you don’t want it for some reason (such as if the method is ‘squicky’ like a blood sacrifice or if it causes mental / spiritual degradation). If you are part or fully dragon, expect to get lots of offers to be adopted into other dragons families or clans if that’s a thing and for them to try ‘showing you the ropes’ when it comes to being a dragon.
objects.title: Dragon Tamer

addons.text:
Eldritch Bloom transforms the Fog into a medium shaped by your alien nature, a mist that carries the quiet wrongness of something born outside the boundaries of ordered reality. Half-Eldritch Child gives the Fog its living core — an echo of your true form, the deep instinct and impossible geometry that your mortal shell can only partially contain. Eldritch Magic expands that core into the surrounding air, letting the Fog express the strangeness you normally keep restrained. The result is an atmosphere where the world bends in small, steady ways that erode sanity long before any physical harm occurs.

Inside the Fog, angles drift away from Euclidean truth. Lines that should run straight deviate by imperceptible degrees, creating impossible shapes that seem to rearrange themselves when not directly observed. Colors warp into dull, unnatural hues. Surfaces ripple as though made of thin liquid. Sounds behave inconsistently — too loud, too soft, or coming from directions that cannot exist. Even light seems confused, producing shadows with edges that twitch as though breathing.

The effect is not random. It reflects you. The Fog becomes a quiet extension of your eldritch self, mirroring your emotions, thoughts, and attention. Calm produces gentle distortions, subtle and dreamlike. Anger sharpens the geometry until every shape becomes jagged and hostile. Focus causes the environment to crystallize into impossible clarity, making even reality-aware beings recoil as they recognize patterns not meant for mortal minds.

Those inside the Fog begin to feel observed. Not hunted — observed, as if consciousness within the mist is brushing against their thoughts, curious and unblinking. This low, constant pressure erodes mental stability with soft persistence. A person might feel their memories drifting out of sequence or experience a sudden sense of déjà vu that lasts minutes rather than seconds. Some find their emotions muffled, while others feel them distort into something foreign. Identity becomes slippery. The longer they stay, the more their inner sense of self begins to drift away from what it once was.

Distance becomes unreliable. A step toward a door might stretch into three, or collapse into half a stride. Opponents misjudge spacing, overshoot attacks, or swing at echoes that seem real until the moment of impact. Even experienced spatial manipulators struggle, as the Fog quietly rewrites the rules they rely on.

The Fog does not harm you. It harmonizes with you. You feel every distortion as naturally as breathing, moving through warped geometry as easily as through normal space. Distances remain consistent for you alone, and the shifting landscape becomes a map only you can read. The eldritch pressure that weighs on other minds invigorates yours, sharpening insight and granting fleeting alignment with the deeper laws your blood remembers.

If you wish, you can amplify the Fog’s influence until madness becomes inevitable. Minds begin to unravel, thoughts loop, senses desynchronize, and the boundary between dream and waking dissolves. At its peak, the Fog becomes a domain where reality bends toward your will and everything else is forced to endure the strain of existing in a world that was never meant to support them.

Eldritch Bloom does not merely warp the battlefield — it reveals the truth beneath ordered nature. A truth that only you were meant to survive.
addons.title: Eldritch Bloom

addons.text:
Umbral Fog reshapes the world inside its radius into a quiet, oppressive reflection of itself—an atmosphere drained of life, stripped of warmth, and smothered beneath a weight of stillness that feels older than the ground it rests upon. Eldritch Magic gives the Fog its subtle distortion, a sense that the world’s texture is thinning at the seams. Void Energy hollows out everything it touches, erasing motion, sound, and vitality. Silent Hill’s Call anchors the transformation to the psyche, letting the Fog draw out the emotional residue buried in the environment and twist the space into an echo of the fears and guilt carried by those who enter. The result is not a separate dimension, but an overwritten version of reality, imposed wherever the Fog spreads.

Inside the Umbral Fog, familiar places become unsettlingly quiet. Streets stretch a little too long. Rooms feel colder than they should. Colors leach into muted grey. Shadows linger as though reluctant to move. The world feels uncannily abandoned, as if something essential has been removed and everything left behind is merely pretending to be real. Sound becomes scarce. Footsteps echo with a dull hollowness. Voices die inches from the throat. Even the wind seems unsure of itself. The silence is not peaceful—it is dense and watchful, a silence that implies something is listening even if nothing is there.

Surfaces begin to decay in subtle ways. Wood splinters without cause. Paint curls and peels. Metal tarnishes into orange-brown corrosion. Light flickers with no source of interruption. The environment behaves like a memory beginning to rot, collapsing into symbols shaped not by cosmic truth but by human emotion. A corridor might narrow without explanation, mirroring a victim’s sense of confinement. A neglected room might fill with faint, indistinct stains, echoing guilt they never voiced aloud. Windows cloud. Mirrors blur. Doors that should lead nowhere open into places that feel intimately wrong.

The Fog does not invent horrors—it draws on those already present in the mind. People stepping inside find the world bending toward their own unresolved fears. Someone who hides from truth might see silhouettes shifting at the edge of vision. Someone carrying regret might hear faint sobs echoing from empty spaces. Someone gripped by anger may find walls marked by deep scratches that were never there. These manifestations remain vague unless you choose to sharpen them. You can coax the Fog to amplify certain impressions, letting the environment itself confront its occupants with reflections of their emotional wounds.

Movement becomes heavy, as though the air has thickened. Heat leaks from the body faster than it can be replaced. The longer someone remains inside, the more they feel a subtle dissociation creeping in—objects look just slightly unfamiliar, memories blur at the edges, and time grows irregular in small, disquieting ways. Nothing is overt. Nothing is dramatic. But the pressure builds steadily until they begin to doubt their senses and their own recollection of the world.

The Fog recognizes you as its origin and anchor. You walk through the Umbral world unhindered. Sound follows your steps. Color bends around your presence. The decay never touches you unless you wish it to. You can direct how deeply the environment shifts and decide which emotional impressions solidify into experience. With focus, you can intensify the atmosphere until the Otherworld fully asserts itself—peeling back the remaining layers of normalcy and revealing a rusted, skeletal version of the space shaped by the collective residue of suffering within the Fog’s boundaries. This deeper layer is harsher, heavier, and more symbolic, but remains entirely under your authority.

When the Fog withdraws, the world returns to normal as though nothing happened. But those who walked through it rarely leave unchanged. The silence lingers in their thoughts. The decay clings to their memories. The emotional wounds the Fog revealed do not vanish simply because the environment has. The Umbral world leaves scars that feel like truth glimpsed too clearly, and the mind struggles to forget.

Umbral Fog does not rely on spectacle or overt violence. Its strength lies in the quiet collapse of familiarity, the suffocation of normalcy, and the way it turns the world into a dim reflection of what people fear most. Inside its boundaries, reality feels drained, brittle, and haunted—not by monsters, but by the weight of everything unspoken.
addons.title: Umbral Fog

addons.text:
Eldritch Umbral Domain is the perfected state of your Fog, a fusion of Silent Hill’s psychological overwriting and the cosmic distortion inherent to your eldritch lineage. When invoked, the Fog no longer creates an environment shaped solely by fear, guilt, or emotional residue, nor does it limit itself to the wrong angles and reality fractures characteristic of pure eldritch intrusion. Instead, it blends both forces into a single domain where every distortion, symbol, and atmospheric shift reflects the victim’s subconscious while bending toward the alien truths that reside within your blood.

Inside the Fog’s boundaries, the world collapses into an uncanny version of itself. The silence that fills the Umbral layer becomes heavier, acquiring a depth that feels almost sentient. Shadows stretch and coil, moving with slow intelligence rather than simple absence of light. Surfaces degrade into rusted, peeling textures, yet the decay never settles into something purely physical; it feels conceptual, as though the world is decomposing along emotional and metaphysical lines at once. Familiar rooms narrow or widen without consistency, following the logic of memory rather than physics. Hallways bend in ways that mimic forgotten guilt. Doorways elongate into proportions that obey neither geometry nor common sense.

The psychological imprint of Umbral Fog molds the foundational layer of the domain. The world responds to the internal wounds, unresolved conflicts, and buried fears of anyone trapped inside, resurfacing fragments of their mind as environmental details. But Eldritch Bloom pushes these reflections beyond simple symbolism. The subconscious no longer manifests as metaphors alone; it is twisted through the lens of an alien understanding. A childhood memory might appear as a hallway that loops into itself. Regret may take the shape of a blurred silhouette caught between too many angles. Personal shame might appear as a flickering distortion, its features eroding whenever one tries to look directly at it. Every fear becomes filtered through a logic that does not belong to humanity.

Time inside the domain behaves strangely. Minutes stretch or collapse without warning. A person may walk down a corridor and find themselves returned to the point they started from, only to discover that the lighting, color, or texture has shifted subtly in their absence. The world feels aware of them, not in an overtly hostile way, but with an indifference so vast it becomes terrifying. The domain adapts continuously, never settling into a stable form. It seeks out what the mind resists acknowledging and reveals it through a geometry that should not exist.

You move through this domain effortlessly. Every distortion, every spatial fold, every psychological apparition recognizes you as its source and center. The domain bends around your presence, clearing paths where you walk and thickening the atmosphere where you direct your attention. If you choose, you can sharpen the environment’s focus on a single individual, letting the domain peel back layers of their psyche until their deepest truths and fears bleed visibly into the world around them. The experience is overwhelming, forcing them to confront parts of themselves they have avoided for years.

The domain can deepen beyond its initial layer. With intent, you can collapse the remaining fragments of normalcy and allow the eldritch structure underneath to fully emerge. Walls unravel into fractal folds. Ceilings rise into impossible height. The ground ripples as though breathing. Symbols carved from no known language pulse faintly along surfaces. The psychological aspects do not vanish—they fuse more tightly with the cosmic ones. A victim’s guilt might manifest as a corridor of repeating doors, but each door opens onto a variation of the same memory refracted through alien proportions. Their fear takes form as a figure whose shape changes with each attempt to understand it. Their anger becomes a vibration in the walls that resonates with inhuman rhythm.

Leaving the domain does not undo its impact. Even after the Fog withdraws, survivors struggle to recall what was real. Memories feel disjointed, as though borrowed from someone else. The psychological confrontations echo faintly in their thoughts, and the eldritch impressions remain as lingering afterimages they cannot fully shake. The experience does not break them outright, but it leaves a subtle fracture—an awareness that reality is thinner, and their own mind is more vulnerable, than they once believed.

Eldritch Umbral Domain is not a battlefield, nor a torture chamber, nor a dreamscape. It is the point where personal truth and cosmic wrongness meet, a layered reality that reveals the self through alien eyes. Within its boundaries, the world becomes a mirror made from fear and impossible geometry, and no one who enters can rely on their senses, their memories, or their understanding of what it means to be real.
addons.title: Eldritch Umbral Domain

addons.text:
Killing Sea Fog turns the Fog into a battlefield predator—an environment saturated with malice so concentrated it becomes a tangible force. The Fog no longer merely obscures or slows; it becomes the medium through which your Killing Intent circulates and evolves, carried on every drifting strand like a silent tide. The air grows heavy, and even the bravest instinctively stiffen as something primal whispers that they have stepped into the territory of a hunter.

Sea of Blood gives your intention weight, enough to warp perception and induce visceral fear. Killing Sea Fog expands that influence into a full sensory world. Within the Fog, every target feels watched, pursued, and pressured. Their heartbeat grows louder in their ears. Muscles tighten. Thoughts fragment. They sense presences moving behind them, breath at their necks, phantom footsteps following their own. These illusions aren’t visual projections but emotional imprints lodged directly into the mind, shaped from the echoes of death that trail behind your aura.

The Fog amplifies these impressions with unsettling detail. A person might swear they hear someone drowning in the distance or feel the cold of deep water around their ankles. A heartbeat might echo from below the ground. Shapes might flicker in their peripheral vision, always gone when they turn to look. Taken together, these phenomena break rhythm, interrupt focus, and wear down resolve. The Fog becomes a psychological weapon that strikes without ever revealing a blade.

This pressure scales with your strength. Against the weak, it induces paralysis, panic, or collapse. Against the strong, it forces hesitation, disrupts spellcasting, derails coordinated movement, and corrodes their mental clarity. Even those who resist fear begin to struggle against the constant sense of being hunted. Painful memories surface. Paranoia blooms. Small mistakes begin to pile up.

The Fog also reacts to killing. Each death inside it strengthens the field, quickening the spread of its emotional density. The clammy heaviness grows thicker. Shadows move with more weight. Whispers sharpen. The more consciousness the Fog devours, the deeper its psychological imprint becomes. In prolonged engagements, this creates a runaway escalation where every casualty empowers the Fog, making escape or recovery harder with each passing moment.

Killing Sea Fog doesn’t physically restrain or harm—its violence is subtle, lived in the mind and the nerves. It shreds confidence, disrupts discipline, and forces even seasoned fighters to confront their own mortality. The battlefield becomes a place where no one can hide from their fears, where every step feels watched, and every second stretches under the suspicion that something unseen is moving closer.

For you, the Fog remains a sanctuary. It carries your awareness, heightens your senses, and lets you taste the emotional state of every foe caught in its reach. You know exactly who is panicking, who is suppressing terror, who is faltering, and who is close to breaking. The Fog becomes an extension of your instincts, turning every shift in fear into an opportunity.

Killing Sea Fog transforms the battlefield into a psychological death march. It is not loud, not showy, and not explosive. It is pressure—inescapable, suffocating, and patient—until the moment those trapped within finally break.
addons.title: Killing Sea Fog

addons.text:
Null Fog changes the Fog from an atmospheric hazard into an active undoing force, a quiet field where the supernatural begins to unravel at the seams. It doesn’t lash out or explode with violent negation. Instead, it weakens the structures that hold magical, enchanted, or metaphysical systems together, forcing everything inside to operate on less stability than it was built for. The effect feels subtle at first, but the longer a supernatural phenomenon remains in the Fog, the more its integrity begins to leak away.

White of Mars gives the Fog the ability to interfere directly with magical construction, erasing key threads of power and collapsing the control loops that sustain spells, barriers, enchantments, and spiritual techniques. Void Energy adds a deeper decay, pulling at the foundations of metaphysical forces until their coherence falters. Together, they turn the Fog into an environment where all supernatural actions cost more strength, force more strain, and yield less predictable results.

A spell cast inside the Fog might fizzle or fracture, split into incomplete fragments, or behave as though its parameters were being rewritten mid-activation. A barrier that should withstand immense force starts trembling at its edges, its shape warping under the strain of holding itself together. Enchanted weapons lose sharpness or fail to manifest their hidden effects. Summoned creatures flicker or glitch, their forms caught between stability and collapse. Long-duration blessings begin to fray, losing potency with every passing breath.

This erosion isn’t immediate. It’s pressure without spectacle. Supernatural abilities continue to function, but each moment inside the Fog drains a little more resilience from them. A combatant might not notice the decay until a spell they’ve cast a hundred times suddenly misfires or a defensive technique fails to fire at full strength. Complex abilities break down first, while simpler effects last a while longer, but nothing retains its full power for long unless it comes from a source vastly stronger than the Fog itself.

Null Fog does not discriminate. It weakens hostile magic, ambient enchantments, and even environmental supernatural fields. The Fog becomes a soft countermeasure against everything that relies on perfect metaphysical engineering. That includes ritual circles, spiritual wards, divine blessings, aura-based techniques, and constructs made of pure energy. Anything born from magic or bound to the supernatural finds its footing eroding the moment the Fog touches it.

For you, the effect is transparent. Your own abilities remain stable unless you deliberately let the Fog influence them. The Fog recognizes you as its anchor, not its target. If you wish, you can direct the effect toward specific enemies or constructions while allowing allied techniques to remain untouched. You can even shape pockets of “stable air” where supernatural activity functions normally, surrounded by zones where Null Bloom is working at full strength.

Null Fog doesn’t destroy magic outright. It weakens it, undermines it, and forces every supernatural system to fight the environment as much as the battle itself. Under its influence, even powerful enemies find their techniques faltering, while you move through a battlefield where the rules bend in your favor.
addons.title: Null Fog

objects.text:
The Fog is a supernatural atmosphere that answers only to you. It manifests the moment you will it, rolling through any chosen area and saturating every space without resistance or delay. No wall, barrier, seal, or force can halt it; the Fog simply flows through and around everything, settling into a dense, unnatural stillness that reshapes the environment the moment it appears.

For anyone caught inside, the world stops behaving correctly. Visibility becomes unreliable—depth, distance, and motion blur together, and even familiar shapes feel distorted at the edges. Light scatters unpredictably, sometimes snuffing out entirely, while shadows move as if they’re detached from their sources. Sound fares no better. The Fog doesn’t merely muffle it; it swallows noise whole. Footsteps cut off mid-echo, voices flatten, and mechanical noise fades into a hollow, airless quiet that feels wrong on a physical level.

Movement inside the Fog becomes sluggish and imprecise. Enemies feel a drag on their limbs, as if the air has thickened around them. Balance suffers, coordination slips, and every action demands more effort. Precision attacks—whether bullets, spells, beams, or thrown weapons—lose stability the moment they enter the Fog, veering off-course or unraveling before reaching their mark. Even basic tasks become clumsier as time inside the Fog wears on.

The Fog weighs on the mind as much as the body. Thoughts turn unfocused, reaction times slow, and moments of clarity come with effort rather than instinct. It doesn’t cause fear or madness; instead it layers a quiet static over a person’s awareness, obscuring concentration and eroding confidence in their own senses.

The presence of the Fog feels strangely alive. Its mass shifts with faint, rhythmic pulses, like slow breaths moving through the air. The pressure of the room subtly changes with each pulse, nudging perception just enough to throw off timing and orientation. The Fog moves in patterns that defy airflow, coiling and hesitating as if paying attention to the world around it without understanding it. Nothing about it behaves like weather.

You are the exception. Inside your Fog, your senses remain completely clear. Your sight cuts through every distortion, your hearing is untouched, and your movement is smooth and silent. The Fog treats you as its center of gravity, parting around you without resistance. Through subtle changes in pressure and temperature, you can feel disturbances anywhere within the Fog’s reach—a natural, instinctive awareness rather than a supernatural detection. It provides constant spatial intuition that enemies cannot hide from so long as they remain inside.

The Fog leaves its mark even after someone escapes it. For a short time, their balance remains uncertain, their vision lags behind their movements, and their sense of distance continues to slip. The world outside the Fog feels slightly misaligned, as if their senses haven’t fully adjusted back to reality.

The Fog is an overwhelming field of atmospheric and sensory distortion that turns any location into your terrain. Inside it, your enemies can’t trust what they see, hear, or feel, while you retain perfect clarity and control.

Note: You can create as much fog as you want and even leave it in an area, and then create Fog in another area, you are still able to edit and affect any fog you have created. Meaning you can create as many Fog zones as you wish, and apply different effects and powers to them if you desire.
objects.title: The Fog

addons.text:
You have gained an extra ring of light in addition to the first one, which functions as surveillance. It constantly analyzes all your surroundings and utilizes any power-granted senses you possess.

With Model Creator, Threads of Clarity can create precise models of the future and hypothetical scenarios you wish to delve into, and through Automatic Defense, flawlessly guide your body in performing them.

Note that Threads of Clarity isn't perfect, and its Path Tracing function can still be fooled upon encountering information it hasn't analyzed, though it will quickly recalibrate to take it into account. The further you try to simulate the future, the less accurate it becomes.
addons.title: Path Tracer

addons.text:
Through the phenomenon of Quantum Entanglement, Threads of Clarity are able to transform bits of information into qubits and thus synchronize with the Halo of the far superior version of yourself, incorporating its qualities. You gain an additional ring of light.

Due to this superposition, Threads of Clarity can bypass the time requirement through information exchange, allowing it to view a huge number of possibilities at once and explore many solutions simultaneously.

Your Threads of Clarity is able to compute and answer any questions you may pose it in whatever manner you wish, be it a vision, a percentage, or a straight explanation.

If you possess Path Tracer, the models created by The Threads of Clarity lose their blind spots and permit you to gaze into the past, the present, and thus the future. This grants you a wealth of information, from analyzing multiple ways to reach an outcome, to estimating the reactions or thoughts of others, and theorizing new avenues to use your abilities.
addons.title: Intuitive Answer

objects.text:
Spinning silently behind your head floats an intangible golden ring of light called Threads of Clarity. It is capable of vastly improving the efficiency of all your energy reserves by increasing their energy density and preventing waste when channeling them.

It can also interface with any of your powers, allowing it to control them in your stead. For example, if you can cast magic, Threads of Clarity can use it without the need for chanting or hand movements. If your reserves are low, it can convert any of your energies as fuel on a 1:1 ratio or take the backlash if this proves ineffective, though this will momentarily deactivate it.

You can change its color and make it invisible whenever you wish, but it will reappear if you are in a high-stress situation.
objects.title: Threads of Clarity

objects.text:
You have been imbued with the power of Entropy, allowing you to control the pace at which creation marches toward eternal equilibrium.

You can control the measurement between disorder and order in a system. This can apply to physical phenomena, such as inducing radioactive decay, dispersing the heat and motion of particles, or complete destruction by creating a bubble of False Vacuum Decay.

You can also apply the opposing effect and revert Entropy itself, bringing order to chaos. You may reverse the destruction of objects, restore lost cities to their former glory, and prevent the decay of biological organisms, yourself included.

There are many possibilities and physical phenomena your entropic control can influence, as entropy is an inherent concept of thermodynamics, leaving it to you to learn how to control and apply it.
objects.title: Entropy

objects.text:
An interface has been grafted onto your soul. Through it, you become a living debugger, a sculptor of variables, able to perceive and manipulate the fundamental properties that define all matter and energy.

You gain a UI overlay known as the Administrative View, a minimalist, holographic interface. Focusing on any object allows you to mentally open a Property Panel. This panel displays a staggering, often overwhelming, stream of data quantifying the object’s existence. Initially, this data is filtered to a macroscopic level: tensile strength, thermal conductivity, density, elasticity, luminance, and aerodynamic drag. From there, you can edit these variables. You can select a property, such as a blade’s sharpness, and increase its value. 

However, the Engine cannot create from nothing. To increase one property, an equal value must be drained from one or more other properties within the same object. A sword made sharper must lose durability, mass, or structural cohesion. This is the primary, conscious trade-off.

The process, however, is far from clean. A macro-level property like "sharpness" is ultimately built upon countless micro-level properties: atomic bond angles, electron shell stability, quantum wave function alignments. When you, as a novice, increase sharpness, the Engine automatically tries to make this change physically possible, adjusting the underlying quantum and atomic variables. It takes the path of least resistance to instantiate the change, but this is a blunt, inelegant process. These automatic adjustments often conflict, creating deep systemic imbalances. The newly ultra-sharp blade might find its atomic nuclei rendered slightly unstable, or its electron clouds forced into a state that makes it intensely radioactive or ferociously reactive with oxygen.

At the start, you need physical contact with the target object. You will also be limited to several dozen macro physical properties. You can only increase or decrease properties that are already visible on the panel; you cannot add entirely new properties an object lacks. Lastly, your creations are more than likely unstable. A hyper-aerodynamic arrow might fly straight through a hurricane but dissolve into powder upon impact. A wall made harder than diamond might also become a perfect thermal conductor, leeching all heat from the surrounding area in a deadly frost.

As you repeatedly practice, the Engine’s safeties gradually disengage and you begin to see past the macro-properties to the molecular and atomic variables, and eventually, quantum states. By perceiving these micro-properties, you can start to manipulate them directly. Instead of just commanding "more sharpness" and letting the Engine auto-adjust atomic bonds poorly, you can manually strengthen specific molecular bonds along the edge while deliberately weakening van der Waals forces in the core to pay the cost, creating a stable, lasting alteration. Additionally, your range extends to line-of-sight as you learn to focus the administrative "cursor" across space.

By this point, once you understand a property well enough, you can add them to objects. This allows you to make fundamentally impossible objects: water that is also a rigid solid, a cloth with the friction coefficient of ice. At your peak, by understanding the lack of the distinction between "object" and "environment,” you can define an area and edit its local properties: increasing the friction coefficient of the floor, draining the kinetic energy transfer property of the air to create silence and absorb impacts, or tweaking the refractive index of light in a corridor to create perfect invisibility.
objects.title: The Administrative Engine

objects.text:
You can create breaches in reality that can lead to any point in existence. As if breaking through a glass window, reality debris flies outward at the exit point; it can even be used as a method of attack, as this debris shreds through anything in its path.

At first, you start only being able to skilfully open miniscule breaches to another point somewhere in the world, enough to let you through and close right afterwards. But, with training, there is nowhere you will not be able to reach, even across time, other universes, or metaphysical spaces like dreams, and much more. The fractures produced heal over time, although how much it takes depends on your skill and how far away you are breaching.

Should you lack the skill, however, you can substitute it with raw power. If you possess magical, spiritual, or other types of supernatural energy, you can use it to fuel the breaching, brute-forcing your way through reality. The more energy you dedicate to the task, the more violent the breach, and with more force the dimensional debris is scattered, leaving fractures that take a much longer time to heal. If you dedicate enough power, you can create breaches that will last for decades or even become permanent.

The expelled reality debris rapidly decays, leaving no traces of its existence after a few seconds at most. If you are skilled enough, you can open breaches in such a way that debris evaporates nearly instantly.
objects.title: Reality Breach

addons.text: A peculiar interaction has emerged from the fusion of your physiology as a Star Spirit and your nature as a Bad Star. Your Astral Body and your true form have fused, allowing you maintain both your perception as a celestial entity and your heightened power over your celestial body. Your Star Body, on the other hand, has swelled massively in size, becoming a star in the truest sense. With your false form having fused with your Star Body, it has also become far more malleable, able to be freely reshaped from anything between celestial bodies to monumental creatures. By shedding the barest shred of mass you can form other, smaller Bad Stars, and send them out into the vast universe to eat for you. These Bad Stars are still connected to you, and any gains they make will reflect upon your true form. A final facet of this fusion is that the range in which your true body can influence has become larger still, able to effect anything within about a dozen light minutes of it. This also allows you to disconnect your true form from your false one, allowing you to wander away from it should you wish to explore beyond it. In this state your ability to influence reality is again reduced in size, though you can still effect the area around your false form all the same.
addons.title: The Star of Evil

objects.text: In a distant universe, there existed a small civilization on the only planet orbiting a lonely star. Unlike traditional primitive societies that grow to worship their stars, this one grew to fear it. After all, who wouldn't be afraid after watching a star eat? Stella Malum, otherwise known as “Bad Stars,” are parasitic higher-reality entities that fuse with small planets or asteroids, subsuming their mass and using them as both a lure for prey and a disguise to hide from the rare few larger predators. Their true forms exist as myriacosms stored in unseen folds of reality, working to reshape and rewrite the edges of reality that their false bodies inhabit. Bad Stars consume pieces of real-space to turn it into pure energy, which then acts to fuel their own growth. Due to their nature as higher-reality entities, they have a great influence over the lower layers, though it requires close distance to their false bodies to exert any real influence. Within their bodies, they are able to completely control reality as a whole, from simply controlling matter to altering fundamental laws and constants of the universe. They exert a similar, albeit lesser, level of control over their false forms as well. By using this they can freely move through space, and avoid falling into orbit of larger objects. When the time comes to eat, a Bad Star will unfold it's false body before contacting its prey and absorbing it into its true form for consumption. Bad Stars take time to consume anything that cannot fit within their true form, taking it in pieces to slowly build up to the final bite. In areas with dangerous flavors of physics, such as a black hole, consuming such prey requires a Bad Star to be exponentially larger than the stellar body that formed it. By eating interesting types of stellar objects with unique energy or physics, a Bad Star will be able to replicate them in their entirety, passively and actively warping reality to mimic them. It requires an increasing amount of energy to increase the size of their true form, and by compressing their false form, Bad Stars can increase the strength of their influence to fight off their kin. In times of desperation, they can shed their false form, becoming what is best described as an “Eldritch Horror,” resembling warps and cracks in reality itself, from which parts of their true form leak out. They don't typically do this, not because it is stressful or harmful, but because they are naturally lazy and prefer prey to come near them by orbit instead of hunting it down. You begin as a hatchling and are only able to subsume matter about the size of a large building. Within about a century of active hunting, you would be able to consume a planet, and within a century more, a star. As you were once human, you also have the ability to make your false form resemble one and are capable of using your true form as a pocket dimension in which you can alter reality. The range of your influence over real-space as a hatchling is middling, only about half as large as your true form, while your ability to alter your false body is near absolute, barring size restraints. If your false body is damaged, it may take a few moments to regenerate, during which time parts of your true form may be exposed. As Bad Stars have little desire beyond getting larger, they only use the matter they consume for their own growth, not requiring it for their continued survival. As you were once human, however, you may find use in the matter you eat beyond consumption, such as transmuting it into more useful types or using the raw energy as an offensive maneuver. What you can turn it into within your true form is limitless, but once this energy or matter re-enters real-space it will collapse back into the closest equivalent that is able to actually exist within local physics. If you are unaware of how something works, or it can't exist under local physics, it will leave twisted voids in your creations where they were once supported solely by your reality alteration.
objects.title: Stella Malum

objects.text:
You have awakened to a primordial force of the universe, imagination, a hidden webway connecting every universe. Most humans go, unaware and sleeping, ignorant of the true potential that lies within themselves. Imagination is what powers reality, the unconscious minds of trillions imposing upon the laws that govern reality. You are no longer dormant to the true nature of reality.

Through this realisation, you have the power to draw forth characters from fiction by holding a representation of the media they belong to, calling forth those created by the dormant imagination of those who are still asleep to the true nature of reality. You could summon forth both heroes and villains from comic books or from literature, creating living beings that house all the powers that the character would possess. Despite what they would ordinarily be like, those you summon will be extraordinarily loyal to you, regardless of your nature or their original personality.

To start, you won't be able to summon vastly stronger characters than yourself; however, even the average person would at the very least be able to summon someone like Spiderman or Bullseye. With time, you would become able to summon characters that are vastly stronger than yourself through practice and experimentation with your power. As with any resource, the more beings you summon from fiction, the more exhausted you become with those that are stronger, taking more of your energy to summon; however, any summon is permanent until they are killed, in which case you can summon them again from whence they came.
objects.title: Avid Reader

objects.text:
You are an architect of flesh, a sculptor whose medium is the very essence of life that flows through your veins. Your blood is primordial clay, a thick, warm, and malleable substance that holds the latent potential for any living form you can conceive. You can manually design and sculpt living creatures using your own blood as a physical medium. Your blood exits your body with a thick, mud-like consistency, with it taking the shape of your creation. The creature's final size and mass are directly proportional to the volume of blood you sacrifice.

The addition of biological traits increases the cost. Common, biologically plausible traits such as standard animal intelligence, dense fur, or sharp claws are relatively inexpensive. More complex or efficient biological structures like an exoskeleton of exceptional durability, enhanced sensory organs, or venom glands are more costly. Traits that defy known biological principles such as active flight on an unsuitably large frame, hyper-regeneration, internal energy production, or heightened intelligence has an exorbitant multiplicative cost, making them vastly more expensive than the creature's base mass alone would suggest.

For any aspect of the design you do not explicitly specify, the power automatically completes it. It selects the simplest, most biologically plausible, and least costly option that fulfills your stated intent for the creature. This ensures basic viability but prioritizes mundane biological solutions.

Your body can store a vast reserve of blood far beyond natural human limits, enough to have more blood than 4 dozen humans combined. Your body produces new blood at a drastically accelerated rate, over 10 times faster than an ordinary human. This accelerated production requires no additional nutritional intake beyond that of a normal human; the power covers the vast majority of the metabolic cost.

Your creations are independent, biologically real organisms. They require sustenance, are subject to disease and injury, and possess survival instincts. While you can design a foundational loyalty, it is not absolute mind control; their core drives can conflict with your commands. You share a faint empathic link with your creations, sensing their general condition and location, and experience a sharp psychic recoil upon their death. The creation process itself is mentally and physically draining, with complexity leading to fatigue, headaches, and fugue states. Finally, the biological nature of your creations means they are permanently part of the ecosystem, leaving evidence and requiring ongoing care and management.
objects.title: Bloodworms

objects.text: You possess the Creative Vision, granting you the ability to edit how you perceive reality itself. You may remove sound and replace it with floating dialogue boxes, captions, or stylized sound effects. You can simplify visuals into outlines, highlight threats in bold lines, blur irrelevant details, or render the world like a storyboard, script, or comic panel. But this is only the surface. You perceive reality not as a single continuous world, but as a layered creative construct made of countless levels of abstraction. The most recognizable layers resemble stages of creation, though in truth there are infinite subtle levels between each one. At the deepest known layer, existence appears as raw text. Every object, person, law of physics, and event is reduced to narrative lines and rules. From here, reality can be directly edited by rewriting, removing, or adding words, altering outcomes, forms, and even concepts. Above this lies the animation keyframe layer, where reality exists as a sequence of crucial moments rather than continuous motion. You may shift which keyframe occurs, rewrite a pose, or reposition yourself within a frame. You can even adjust your personal frame rate. By inserting additional frames, you move far faster than the world around you. By lowering it, attacks that occur between frames can pass harmlessly through the gaps of existence. Between frames, entire moments simply do not exist. Next is the onion-skin layer, where past and future moments overlap the present like translucent echoes. You can subtly tug on these overlapping timelines, adjusting timing, trajectories, and momentum. An incoming strike can be shifted to where it was or where it is about to be, missing you entirely. Above this is the sketch layer, where reality appears unfinished and malleable, like pencil lines on a living page. Here, you may make small edits: altering posture, shifting position, adjusting angles, or warping shapes. Dodging an attack can be as simple as moving the outline of your body a few inches. Between every major layer exist infinite intermediary levels, each offering increasingly fine or increasingly absolute control. The deeper you descend, the more fundamental your influence becomes. However, the deeper you go, the more your sense of self unravels. At higher layers, you remain mostly human in perception. As you descend, you begin experiencing yourself as part of the construct. Your thoughts appear as text. Your body becomes lines, frames, or poses. Emotions flatten into simple descriptors. Prolonged exposure leads to numbness, dissociation, and identity drift. At the deepest levels, you may forget you were ever a person at all, seeing yourself only as editable data within reality’s structure. Power grows with depth. So does the danger of becoming just another line in the script.
objects.title: Creative Vision

objects.text:
You are able to alter reality through the power of getting scammed… but not really.

You have an internal pool of Charges (you can perceive them as a base-ten, ten-point counter if you want) that fuels this power. You start with a pool of 10 Charges. At noon and midnight, your pool recharges by five Charges until you hit the cap. If you already have your full Charges when noon or midnight hits, your maximum Charges increase by one–at least in the beginning. As your body grows stronger and you evolve your power further, you will both recharge more Charges and have your maximum pool increase by more Charges.

By spending Charges, you may “accept” a scam (digital or otherwise) and alter reality to comply with the promise as if it had been real all along (even if the other side doesn’t realize this). This includes scam emails, pop-ups, DMs, phone calls, shady contracts, street cons, miracle supplements, “limited-time offers,” and other frauds like these. The scam must be a recognizable attempt to deceive someone into believing a false offer. The power is in the lie.

Charge cost scales with how extreme the scam is. Small, mundane manifestations (a suitcase of money, an exclusive membership, a plausible document, martial arts course videos for fantasy arts) are cheap. Something that changes reality on a greater scale–such as changes to biology, metaphysics, or causality (instant mastery, super serums, bloodlines, pocket dimensions, god-killing weapons)–costs exponentially more: anywhere from thousands to millions of Charges. You can always “see” the price before committing.

Scams are only the training wheels for what you can truly do. Right now, the easiest way for your ability to “get traction” is by anchoring an effect to an existing deception–an email, a con, a too-good-to-be-true offer–because the lie provides a ready-made shape for reality to snap into. Over long periods of use, strain, and acclimatization, you will gradually learn to cut out the middleman and “scam” reality itself, forcing the world to accept outcomes that were never offered by anyone but you. This is not a quick process, and it’s not free, either. Even once you master the power, you will still have to pay using your pool of Charges, but you will no longer be as limited as you are now.

Activation is as simple as choosing to accept the scam (clicking the link/button, signing, verbally agreeing, or mentally consenting if no medium of interfacing exists). On use, you suffer a wave of mental and physical strain proportional to the amount of Charges spent–anything from mild dizziness to debilitating exhaustion. You also cannot activate scams that you have already accepted in the past since gaining this power (this will only apply until you have mastered your power and no longer need a medium).

If you try to spend Charges you do not have, you immediately fall unconscious. If you attempt to force this while empty, you may die. Your power will not stop you from making such mistakes. As a bonus, however, external factors cannot prevent you from activating your power, nor can they force you to activate it.

Finally, under rare circumstances, you may absorb and convert certain high-quality external energies into Charges, recharging or increasing your pool. This only works on specific potent energies (divine power, equivalent cosmic forces, a uniquely refined magical source, etc.). Ordinary electricity, ambient mana, or other such sources will not work.
objects.title: Scamming Reality

addons.text: Your ability to pull phenomena and elements of other worlds into your own has also expanded to your Personal World. Your World Index now has a separate ‘tab’ from which you can apply your modifiers to your personal world. While this acts in much the same way as World Index would usually, any changes made to your personal world only affect the world itself, anyone within it, or anyone connected to it like yourself. Additionally, as it is fundamentally your world you can modify and alter the specifics of any system you drag into your personal world with far more finesse than your greater setting. For instance, you could drag fates as a concept into the world and then modify the way in which it acts, whether it would be specific destinies for each person or a loose set of targets to be met. You can still dismiss anything you bring to your world at any time.
addons.title: Time :: Fate :: Karma :: God

objects.text:
You gain access to the World Index, granting you dominion over worlds across the omniverse. Beyond merely allowing travel between worlds, this power enables you to summon entire universes from other multiversal clusters and blend aspects of different settings into any world you choose, creating countless crossovers. For example, you may integrate power systems such as genetic mutations, chakra, ki, cultivation, magic, or psionics into a single world. You may also import elements from other realities, including alien species, the Warp from Warhammer 40k, countless afterlives, toon force from cartoons, or dungeons from fantasy worlds.
﻿
The World Index manifests within your mind as a search interface, allowing you to locate specific types of worlds with ease. When viewing a world within the catalogue, you receive detailed information about its nature, inhabitants, power systems, governing laws, and overall danger level. When summoning a world wholesale or importing elements from it, you may choose whether its inhabitants are included or excluded entirely. The interface also tracks how many elements you add, with each addition taking a charge to implement, of which you get five per day (that are not banked over time). It takes no charges however to remove anything added.
﻿
You may designate up to five worlds as favorites, ensuring they are always readily accessible. While you control how imported elements function in the abstract, the implementation is completely indiscriminate, allowing anything brought through to be used by everyone, not just yourself. Additionally this does not grant you authority over the inhabitants themselves if brought over; any beings brought along retain their free will and are not guaranteed to be loyal to you. At any time, you may dismiss summoned worlds or imported elements, fully undoing any changes their integration caused. While initially this only affects the planet you're on, it can grow to affect your entire universe.
objects.title: World Index

objects.text:
You can register any modification/component integrated/equipped with you (body/mind/soul) — tattoos, implants, prosthetics, wearable, enchantments, equipment etc.—as part of your natural state. Once registered, modifications are treated as natural for any effect referencing your natural state, persist through effects that remove or suppress enhancements, and are recognized by perks/powers/effects that scale from a natural state.

You have a mental record of all registered states. You can instantly switch between registered states. Switching will not restore/repair the components if damaged but can summon it back if lost.
objects.title: All Natural

objects.text: “I was there when the first bricks of Rome were placed, when they dropped two suns upon Japan and when man first stepped upon the dirt of Pluto. Make no mistake, I am the architect and guiding hand of the very civilisation you’ve given your allegiance to, you ignorant child!” You’ve studied it all. The lows of the Dark Ages to the heights of the Age of Enlightenment and now the Ages of Civilisation are now yours to command. You may slow down, accelerate and halt the passing of the ages; a distinct period of history. Also, when a previous Era comes to a close, you may define what the next Age entails. This does not manipulate time, for that moves ever forward, but influences societal development to better suit your goals. Bring forth the advancement of the Nuclear Age, the explorative nature of the Space Age or lay low mankind by bringing them back to the hunter-gatherer period. To facilitate these natural events, you may decide a broad scope of what you wish to happen. For example, the demise of the fossil fuel period due to lack of resources may give rise to the era of solar powered electronics but specific events are uncontrollable to you, at least at the start. These transformations happen on the scale of years, decades or centuries depending on the extent of the changes you wish to enact and as such you’ve been given a limited form of immortality. Whilst you can still be struck down by blade or fist, no sickness nor age will cause your death. Humanity's future is yours to sway.
objects.title: Future Maker

objects.text:
<small>“Batman Neg Diff with Prep Time.”
“WHAT ARE THESE WORDS!?!?”</small>

Whenever you face an opponent or an immediate threat, you retroactively become prepared for them.
