The records that detail and lay the foundation of your Evolution have themselves evolved due to the supplementary information of the entire existence of Humanity and any other species you possess; this means that all your evolutions are supercharged, with any weaknesses that could come from them removed, as you gain access to greater power, with each evolution becoming the idealized version of itself, which then becomes the perfect foundation for your next leap.

However, while the evolutions are empowered, you still need to work towards them and meet any special requirements, such as needing to understand several True Magics to become an Age of Will human from the Nasuverse.
addons.title: Echoes of Newmanity

addons.text:
Your ability to evolve into a greater version of yourself has merged with your ability to create new linear and branching forms, the three powers feeding into one another to make them greater.

At the bare minimum, the increase you gain from all evolutions becomes x10, liken to you assimilating your x10 transformation into your base form, before other factors come in to push it even further.

Your various forms gain a piece of Evolution's power, allowing the different forms to grow stronger passively through use. This is especially evident with your alternate/slide forms as they become more than specialized forms based on your current evolution, and instead become branches of your evolution tree you can draw upon, providing stronger abilities and specialities. You can stack these different forms on top of one another for more creative and strange forms.
addons.title: Over Evolution!!

addons.text: Your ability to evolve has seeped into the Omnitrix to create a new function allowing for each DNA sample to undergo gradual evolution; however, unlike the Ultimate Evolution function, these evolutions will be more well-rounded and are stored in the Omnitrix as separate DNA samples as you alien transforms evolve, unlocking things like divergent and convergent evolutions. Note: Should you have the Echoes of Newmanity and Over Evolution addons, then they will apply to the alien transformations as well.
addons.title: Advancing Specimen

objects.text:
Every action performed by you is meticulously recorded, and each action generates a specific amount of energy based on its nature, significance, and impact. This energy accumulates over time, steadily building within you. Once the accumulated energy reaches a critical threshold, you will undergoes an evolution.

The nature of this evolution is influenced by three core factors: your inherent powers, your racial or biological traits, and the precise combination of actions recorded before the evolution. The powers and traits of the wielder act as a foundation, setting the boundaries and potential paths for the transformation. Meanwhile, the recorded actions shape the specific direction of the evolution, ensuring that the transformation reflects your experiences, choices, and growth.

Each evolution represents a leap in your capabilities, reshaping your physical form, mental acuity, or abilities in ways that align with their developmental journey. They boost your existing powers, enhancing their strength and effectiveness, while also unlocking new variant powers or subpowers. These variants can complement your core abilities or introduce entirely new ways to use your skills, expanding your versatility and adapting to your needs. In most cases, your evolution also refines your physical form or mental capabilities, aligning them more closely with your enhanced powers. 

The rate at which you evolve depends on the quality and significance of your actions. Challenging, impactful, or meaningful deeds generate more energy, allowing you to evolve more quickly, while mundane or repetitive actions contribute less to your growth.
objects.title: Evolution

objects.text:
To get more for less. This is your philosophy and now it has become your very nature.

Whatever you lose, give away or use up, you ‘lose’ 10% less than what the original amount would be. Similarly, whatever you gain, develop or produce, you ‘gain’ 10% more than you would otherwise, so long as it makes feasible sense.

Reality itself adjusts to accommodate these bonuses. For example, if physically fighting an enemy, you would expend 10% less energy and effort while delivering 10% more force and damage with every strike. When shopping, you can buy at a 10% discount and get 10% more of whatever you purchase, with the same effect applied when selling.

This power applies on a conceptual level to nearly everything concerning yourself, as long as it is a ‘loss’ or ‘gain’. This power would not affect your blood pumping around your body, for instance, but it would apply if you were bleeding out. Whether it concerns your body, mind, powers, social relationships, the technology you operate, your assets or anything else, you will always retain and acquire more than expected.

These discounts and surcharges are always beneficial and you can freely control when this power is active. You can also choose whether the power's effects are noticeable, preventing others from perceiving them if you prefer. This power does not affect itself, nor does it repeatedly affect growth or limit-breaking abilities; applying only once in such cases.
objects.title: More for Less

addons.text: A line of wriggling maggots line your arm, surrounding art of exposed muscle The Brand & Bond has allowed you to store your parasites for future use, transforming them into lines on your body. At a moment’s notice you can expel them from your body to use as minions, though you still have to produce them the first time.
addons.title: Scarified

addons.text: Your symbionts can now act as focus points for your parasites, letting you absorb up to seventy-five percent of someone’s abilities instead, storing them inside symbiont ‘batteries’.
addons.title: Manifestation

objects.text:
You have become able to produce parasitic organisms. Specifically, they steal people’s abilities, powers, skills and potential the longer they are attached. The longer your parasites remain in skin contact with people, the more of the subject’s power you can steal. This is permanent unless you specifically choose to relinquish them.

You produce parasites from your body, each sloughing off in piles of quickly regenerating but necrosed flesh they then eat their way out of. They then continue to eat this flesh until they are fully grown, ranging in sizes from a few centimeters to the size of a large dog. You can produce one of these parasites every week, though this can be decreased to every three days at the cost of excruciating pain when the flesh comes off of your body.

Contact for roughly one minute equates to ten percent of their abilities, though unfortunately the maximum amount you can steal from any one individual is only half of their total strength and potential. That said, if two people have powers from an identical source the amount you drain from another does increase your existing strength.
objects.title: Parasitism

addons.text:
Your archive’s internal world has become a personalised realm shaped by your creativity and focus. Whether it takes the form of a sprawling library, a high-tech laboratory, or a mystical forge, it adapts to your needs, offering the perfect environment to explore your powers, theories, and inventions.

Within this internal world, you can create fully interactive simulations, testing abilities, designs, or ideas without risk to the outside world. You also possess the ability to pause moments in your experiments, entering a slowed-down mental state where every detail can be analysed with perfect clarity. Failures and successes alike resonate through the archive, sparking moments of revelation and evolving the space itself. Each experiment you conduct feeds the archive, unlocking new tools, environments, and insights tailored to your unique journey.

In this internal world you can manifest multiple versions of yourself within it to debate, brainstorm, and collaborate on complex problems. They can offer real-time insights, alternative strategies, and even unexpected combinations of your abilities. Each duplicate works independently, allowing for unparalleled multitasking, but the mental burden is shared equally among them. Two of you mean twice the mental strain and overdoing it with too many duplicates can lead to headaches, fatigue, or other symptoms. After all, not suffering from burnout is different from literally splitting your mind.
addons.title: Archive of Research

addons.text:
You possess an instinctive understanding of where to direct your efforts in research and study, building a strong foundation that accelerates your progress and makes it easier to expand upon your initial discoveries. Each step strengthens your grasp of the subject, helping you identify promising paths for deeper exploration while avoiding unproductive avenues.

This strong foundation sharpens your ability to discern which methods, topics, or strategies will yield valuable insights and which will lead to dead ends. Over time, this instinct doesn’t just help you master subjects—it allows you to innovate, create unique approaches, and achieve breakthroughs that others might overlook.
addons.title: The Scholar of the Grind

addons.text:
Through Carnwennan you have achieved a far less patient way to pursue knowledge. By sacrificing harvested souls, you can forcibly accelerate the results of research, experimentation, and training. 

Instead of spending months or years refining an ability through practice and trial, you can burn the innate potential contained within a soul to push that development forward instantly. The more complex or revolutionary the improvement would normally be, the more souls must be sacrificed to force the breakthrough.

This greatly enhances your research capabilities in a more indirect way. Your natural experimentation still works as it should and allows you to advance, but when progress slows or a discovery proves difficult, you can simply brute force the solution. 

Skills can be refined beyond their original limits into transcendental forms, inefficient abilities can be optimized to the point of costing essentially nothing, and even simple techniques can be evolved into far greater forms befitting that of legends. 

The souls of strong and unique beings can have additional benefits depending on their nature and what they’re being used for. The soul of a Dragon could grant a defensive barrier technique the properties of dragon scales, and the soul of a powerful fire mage would be especially suited to enhancing a fire spell.
addons.title: Brute Force Development

objects.text: You can choose any power in the world, and you chose to study? Well, I’ll be damned. You can study any power you have and can naturally learn, though this doesn’t mean you get information handed to you for free. Through study, experimentation, and practice, you increase the potency and variability of your abilities. Time is on your side—your powers can always be improved. Even if you lack powers entirely, you are able to study mundane principles, pushing them to new heights. Physics, engineering, chemistry, or even simple crafts become your playground, letting you pioneer advancements that no one else can imagine. What sets you apart is that you can’t suffer from burnout. In fact, it’s the opposite—studying energises you. The deeper you dive into understanding your abilities, the more focused and alive you feel. Experimentation becomes your playground. Each failure is a chance to refine, and every small success unlocks new layers of potential. Failure is never the end for you; it’s a stepping stone. Every time you fail, it’s as if the pieces of the puzzle rearrange themselves, revealing a new insight. Each failure sparks a revelation, an exponential boost to your understanding. Instead of frustration, failure feels like uncovering the next secret layer of your abilities. As you study, you don’t just become stronger—you become adaptable. You learn to layer your powers, combining them in ways that multiply their effectiveness. You create variants, tweaking the nature of your abilities like a craftsman refining their tools. Over time, you gain a perfect understanding of your powers’ essence, breaking them down to their core. This lets you reassemble them with precision, changing how they work, expanding their use, and sometimes creating something entirely new. This isn’t limited to your powers but to anything you can study, from technology you make to mundane subjects.
objects.title: Researcher's Madness

objects.text: Time is an enigma, it never quite acts how you expect. Time doesn’t truly work around you as it should. Your natural state of existence is at a dead stop, able to perceive things around you in frozen time. Thankfully, with a bit of effort you should be able to right yourself into moving at regular speeds. This isn’t all however, as by focusing your will, and undergoing a not insignificant amount of training, you can change the flow of time around you. This means you could create time-locked zones where not even oxygen can move, slow bullets, reverse local time, bring things back from future timelines and the past, and more. It is worth noting: going forwards is always easier than back, speeding time up, advancing age, all of these things take about half of the effort and energy it takes to do the inverse. Traveling back in time any substantial distance is a monumental feat of will and skill, for instance. Learn enough about how Temporal Meta-Chrono-Physics works and one day you might truly be a time-warping monster to behold, but until then I’m afraid we’ll just have to call you Temporally Challenged.
objects.title: Temporally Challenged

addons.text:
Congratulation! Your guarantee to become a God, your ability to dictate laws in your owned lands, and the newfound sapience of your units have resulted in the Base Building Game power being boosted! Now, instead of only building a town that you rule, you can build a whole civilization. This civilization will always worship you, resulting in Path to Divinity’s growth being boosted enough that you get a Divine Domain right at the start! However, this domain will be restricted to Street-Tier level like if gotten with Fragmented Divinity (In fact, just use the rules of how that works to choose your domain.).

You can also bestow permanent blessings on a certain amount of individuals, starting at 5 individuals. To be able to bless more individuals, you will have to make the next jump for your civilization, aka: Tribe to Small Town, Small Town to Town, Town to Large Town, Large Town to Small City, etc. Each stage will grant you 5 more “Blessing Slots”. Keep in mind however that those blessed individuals can only have up to 3 different blessings each.

Sovereign Domain is also boosted, resulting in the amount of time needed to claim a territory being reduced to a week as long as you are the one that holds the majority of the territory.

There are a few more buildings you can build now, those are:

Church: This building boosts the Faith you gain from your worshiper that goes there.

Graveyard: This building lets those who died still contribute a small amount to your Faith need as long as those individuals are buried there.

Holy Order: This Building lets you recruit a Paladin or Priest; Paladins are guards or combatants that can use a portion of your domain for combat while Priests are the same except for more support/healing needs.
addons.title: Faithful Civilization

objects.text:
You have been granted a base-building system to establish your dominion. You begin with a castle and two workers. The castle serves as your primary base and can be customized in both style and decoration to match your preferences. Your workers are Golems, capable of constructing various mundane and supernatural buildings, crafting magical equipment and consumables, or gathering resources.

At the start, you can construct the following buildings:

Resource Center – Produces common resources such as different types of stone, wood, minerals, and metals.

Farm – Generates crops and animal products.

Recruitment Center – Allows you to summon or induct others as units under your control. Those under your rule gain a weaker version of the Gamer System.

Training Center – Enables your units to train, acquire new skills, and enhance their abilities at an accelerated rate.

Research Center – Facilitates the discovery of new technologies and magic, as well as the ability to transfer your knowledge directly to chosen individuals.

Exploration Portal – Grants access to resource-rich but dangerous locations where rare materials can be obtained.

Mission Hall – Provides missions for your units to complete, yielding various rewards.

Production Center – Supports raw material processing, equipment creation and repair, and the production of additional workers.

Guard Tower – A defensive structure that fires projectiles at hostile enemies.

Wall – Supernaturally reinforced barriers designed to keep out invaders.

Each building enhances the efficiency of its respective activities tenfold. For example, a farm will produce ten times the output of a normal farm of the same size in just one-tenth of the time, while training and research centers dramatically accelerate their respective processes.

As you gather resources, you can upgrade your castle, unlocking additional building types as well as allowing existing buildings to be upgraded to a higher level. 

Upgraded buildings besides further improvement of their efficiency boost can also unlock new functions. For example, advanced farms and resource centers can produce rare or exotic materials. However, the level of your castle determines the maximum level your buildings can reach. Higher-level structures require more resources, including rare and exotic materials, for both construction and upgrades.

Like your units, you also have access to a weaker version of the Gamer System. However, if you possess the full Gamer System ability or any similar RPG-based power, such as Falna, you can bestow that system upon your units instead.
objects.title: Base Building Game

addons.text:
Your Tales and Crystallised Legends are no longer separate—they are two sides of the same myth, bound together in an eternal cycle. When you immortalize an event into a Tale, it takes shape as a Crystallised Legend, a living embodiment of the story’s essence. Likewise, any Crystallised Legend you summon imprints its Tale upon reality, allowing its story to be recorded and invoked. Neither exists without the other, and as one grows in strength and significance, so too does its counterpart.

The power of a Crystallised Legend is directly tied to the magnitude of its Tale, and as a Tale deepens—whether through retelling, understanding, or the unfolding of history—its Legend becomes stronger, more refined, and more enduring. In turn, the presence of a summoned Crystallised Legend reinforces and enriches its Tale, shaping the abilities drawn from it. The two influence each other; the Crystallised Legend may be able to use the Tale’s invocation, while the abilities granted by the Tale may have the appearance similar to that of the Crystallised Legend.

Anyone who holds a Tale may summon its Crystallised Legend, manifesting the idealized hero, monster, or moment contained within. However, just as only the worthy can bear the weight of a Tale, only those strong enough can command its legend. If the story is too great, it may consume them, fracturing their mind, soul, or body under its burden.

Your connection to great events deepens—your instinctual pull toward moments of significance now resonates with both your waking and dreaming self. Whether wandering the world or adrift in the currents of fate, you are ever drawn to the heart of history as it unfolds.
addons.title: The Bardic Scribe

addons.text: You are no longer a bound as a simple observer. You can freely interfere with events without comprising their authenticity, with Tales that you find yourself as a character in being a noticeable deal heavier than average. The threshold for what qualifies as a Tale has also been lowered: so long as you are able to add enough weight behind it, even something such as witnessing the coming of spring or the warmth of a home's embrace will be able to be used as a minor Tale.
addons.title: Autobiography

objects.text: You are the Watcher, the one who records all that unfolds. You are the living archive, the keeper of a limitless library of stories. You are capable recording and transforming significant events into immortalised Tales, which are not mere stories but powerful fragments of reality. Each Tale carries a distinct power, and by invoking it, you can directly access the abilities or strength tied to the event you have recorded. The greater the event—the more it alters the flow of the world and defies the mundane—the stronger and heavier the Tale becomes. You must witness an event firsthand for it to be transformed into a Tale, as only through your eyes does it become immortalised.  As a storyteller, you are able to share these Tales with others. When you recount a Tale, you imprint its essence onto the listener, granting them access to its abilities. However, only those who are strong or insightful enough can bear the weight of a great story. If the Tale is too overwhelming, it can shatter the mind, corrupt the soul, or even destroy the body of the unworthy. Due to unique nature as the Scribe, you are exempted from this toll unless you invoke its power while unworthy. You are guided by a deep, almost instinctual pull toward moments of great significance. This intuition leads you to the epicenters of change—places of triumph, tragedy, and transformation. However, this compulsion often places you in danger, as the events you are drawn to are frequently chaotic and perilous. Despite your power, you are bound by your role as an observer. You must carefully decide whether to remain impartial or to intervene, as influencing events may compromise the authenticity of the story.
objects.title: The Scribe

objects.text:
The older you become, be it mentally, physically, or, with the right abilities, spiritually, the stronger you grow. 

Your physical strength increases beyond natural limits, muscles becoming denser, reflexes quicker, and endurance lasting longer. Injuries heal faster, fatigue becomes a less prominent, and your body adapts to new challenges with greater efficiency.

Your mind follows the same path, expanding in intelligence, clarity, and resilience. Memory becomes clearer, thoughts process at greater speed, and your understanding of the world deepens with each experience. Emotional control strengthens, wisdom accumulates, and your strategic thinking sharpens until you can predict outcomes with near-perfect accuracy.

Your powers and abilities also grow alongside you. With time, they refine, strengthen, and become more efficient, reaching levels that were once impossible. Control becomes effortless, limitations fade, and what once required focus or effort eventually becomes second nature.

If you possess spiritual or supernatural abilities, they too evolve alongside you, growing in power and mastery. Every year, at minimum, you will have grown by 10% with this growth being additive rather than compounding. If the age between your mind, body or soul is different, this will use the oldest one.

On its own, it gives a form of longevity, but not immortality as the issues of age will eventually catch up.
objects.title: Get Off My Lawn!

addons.text:
Your ability to alter your potential selves has allowed you to reallocate spent pieces of your pool.

Unfortunately, for all intents and purposes this is more akin to a ‘reset’ of your form whenever you actively use ‘Across the You-Niverse’, separating your different past forms into ‘past potential selves’ that you’ve since shifted out from.
addons.title: Reshaping

addons.text:
Thanks to your developmental power, your ‘pool’ from which you built and adapt your form from is ever growing, giving you more SP to spend. 

The rate of this growth depends on the specific nature of your ‘development’, with more focused or powerful tools providing faster growth.
addons.title: The Only Thing Constant

objects.text: You have a formless energy around you allowing you to take many forms. Unfortunately, this energy doesn’t like to play nice with linear time, meaning that you’ve only ever had the one form, no matter how many times you change it. You have a pool of 10sp you can use to, at any point, make changes to a form, giving it limbs, tough hides, even more esoteric powers, but beware, once it’s made an effect on reality, it can never be changed to make that affect impossible. Eventually, this will result in a completely solidified alternate form depending on your history and its previous uses. For instance, if you were to make it bulletproof, and be shot, it would always have to be bulletproof, or possess some kind of ability that would make it impervious to that specific damage, rendering it more or less permanent. The form must always conform to its history. If it’s picked something up, it must always be capable of picking something up, be that through hands, tentacles or telekinesis, etc. Though your form takes many shapes to you, to others it will always have been the latest result, once all its energy is spent. After all, it never stopped being bulletproof, or at least internally consistent to their perceptions. This also appears on cameras, recording devices, and other means of taking evidence, being truly retroactive, if obscenely limited in application. This retroactivity does not so much have ‘butterfly effects’, as anything that would cause a meaningful change in the timeline would be something solidified into it.
objects.title: Retrofitting

objects.text:
You can now view potential quests or tasks from people around you. When a quest is detected, a board will appear displaying an entry with a brief description of the task, the predicted reward, and what might happen if you fail. You can choose how this information appears—either as a invisible window or as knowledge flowing directly into your mind.

At present, the Questboard can detect opportunities within your line of sight. You can filter the types of quests you're looking for—whether it's monster hunting, magical research, or just a simple fetch quest. Once a quest has been seen, it will remain on your Questboard as long as it’s still available.

However, the more complex the task—or the more powerful the individual offering it—the less information the Questboard will provide about the quest, its rewards, or its potential consequences.

As you complete more quests, the Questboard will evolve. Its scanning range will extend beyond your line of sight, eventually allowing it to detect quests from across the universe. Descriptions will grow more detailed, reward predictions more accurate, and entirely new features will unlock—such as unique chain quests that uncover conspiracies, or limited-time event quests offering rare and valuable opportunities.
objects.title: Questboard

objects.text:
As a Roguelite Survivor, failure is never the end—it’s just another step in your endless journey of growth. This ability works in two folds, firstly anytime you defeat or kill an enemy, it grants you exp that fills up a bar that when full grants you a choice of three semi random upgrades, abilities, gear or weapons based on an aesthetic of your choice (fantasy, sci-fi, modern miliary hardware/ordinance or even choices based on other universes like Warframe, bloodborne etc), regardless of what aesthetic you picked the choices you get would have ‘gamelike’ attributes to them like crit chances and elemental effects for example 

Which means that even if you pick medieval as your aesthetic, you can in time have chain mail that negates 80% of any type of damage, crossbows that shoot seeming normal bolts that can wipe out armies due to crit chance and explosive type damage etc, The possibilities are endless and what's more is that you can change the aesthetic anytime you want. 

The gear, items or weapons you get are kept in a practically limitless storage space that you can easily access by willing it to get them and what's more, the passive abilities the items give you will still be active even if the item in particular is in your storage space so you don't have to worry about lumbering with hundreds things on your person.

The second aspect of this power is that every time you are killed, you disintegrate and come back to life in a safe spot, But lose almost all your accumulated skills and abilities gained by this ability but do not fret too much, like any other roguelite, you have a second upgrade path that allows you to upgrade yourself with choices that carry over between ‘runs’. 

Note: the resurrection aspect of this power is not absolute, a sufficiently powerful wizard, reality warper etc can erase you from existence, and you have no protections against retroactive attacks with this alone
objects.title: Roguelite Survivor

addons.text: Your control over your clones development allows you to rapidly speed up the development of any skills or abilities given to your ‘selves’, Essentially allowing you to farm your growth and increase your rate of growth dramatically, especially with attributes with varying paths of development.
addons.title: Blood Ties

objects.text:
You have become a Hive Mind… of one. Within your hive mind, all minds within begin to melt at the edges, sharing experiences, attributes and powers between each other. As the administrator of this Hive Mind, you are the sum total of all of these dispersed among your bodies. 

Unfortunately, you only have one body. This said, there are… circumstances to be noted. Every clone, doppelganger, paradox duplicate, alternate reality visitor or otherwise slightly altered ‘you’ that exists enters a kind of ‘Hive Mind’ with you. This includes any clones you may have gained from another power or source. 

Additionally, you can divide and combine any of ‘you’ into new selves depending on the parts. Dividing a ‘you’ results in a new body being formed. You decide the attributes, skills, personality fragments and powers that create these divided selves, but any pieces placed into a new ‘you’ are absent from any other ‘you’ in direct proportion to how much was given to the new self. 

When a ‘you’ dies their personality, skills, memories, powers and any other qualities they may have gained outside of the hive are redistributed evenly across the ‘you’ network. If there are no more of ‘you’ left to distribute these into, and the last body is destroyed, you will die. 

Fate will transpire to create various ‘selves’ at an inconsistent rate, but they will be relatively random and vary depending on your world and it’s tendencies. Ie a magical world probably won't dispense a vat grown clone of you. Eventually this will give your network access to an eclectic collection of attributes.
objects.title: A Singular Vision

objects.text:
Powerful tools are often double-edged. While they can elevate your performance in battle, they frequently come at a hidden cost: the dulling of personal progress. Most who rely heavily on enchanted weapons, rare artifacts, or potent spells find that their own development slows, as their tools begin to shoulder the effort that would otherwise lead to growth. Their skills plateau, their instincts dull, and their experience accrues at a crawl—because it’s the weapon doing the work, not them.

But you are no longer bound by this limitation.

Now, your progression remains steady as long as you are actively involved in the action. If you defeat enemies using high-tier equipment, magical items, or other external advantages, you will still gain the same amount of experience and skill development as if you had done so through your own unaided effort—provided the experience is relevant to your actions. Swing Excalibur in combat, and your swordsmanship continues to grow regardless of how much it amplifies your power or lightens the load. But direct a Flying Sword to strike from afar while you stand idle, and your blade skills remain untouched. The growth reflects what you do, not merely what your tools accomplish.

In essence, your learning curve remains sharp. Your tools enhance your capabilities without diminishing your personal evolution. Whether you slice through a monster horde with a cursed blade or dispatch them with raw strength, your growth is no longer tied to how hard the fight is—only to the fact that you engaged meaningfully in it.
objects.title: Growth Tool

objects.text:
You’ve gained the ability to steal anything, not just physically but conceptually. What this means is that you can take anything from anyone or anything, whether it's tangible, intangible, or entirely abstract.

Steal someone’s strength and they’ll grow weak as you gain what they lost. Steal their immortality, their ability to lie, their confidence, their fire resistance, their voice, their divinity, their potential, or even their friendships. You can even steal their powers, leaving them helpless while you wield their abilities as your own. You can steal their fate, twist the future meant for them, or take their memories and leave nothing behind. If it exists in any form, you can take it.

Theft applies to more than just people. You can steal a building’s structural integrity, a forest’s dryness, a concept’s relevance, or a technique’s uniqueness. You could take the sharpness out of every blade in an army, the originality out of an artist’s work, or the light of day from the sky itself.

The things you steal become yours to keep, to use, or to return. This can be permanent, temporary, or conditional. You can steal from groups, objects, locations, phenomena, or even from entire systems or ideas. Steal the need for fuel from a machine, the definition of law from a courtroom, or the effect of gravity from a falling object.

At first, your theft is simple and grounded. Small physical objects come easiest, and things like tools, weapons, or basic traits offer little resistance. More abstract or conceptual targets, such as powers, fate, or identity, can be taken, but doing so is difficult and draining, sometimes nearly impossible. The deeper or more essential something is, the more effort it takes to steal and hold. The more you try to carry at once, the more the strain builds as pressure weighs on you. If you push yourself too far, you may begin to lose your grip, allowing some things to slip away as you're forced to let them go.

While you begin with only smaller-scale thefts coming easily to you, such as minor traits, basic abilities, surface-level emotions, or single moments of luck, your power can grow with use, sharpening your grip and expanding your reach. These things may stay with you for a time, but without rest or experience, you’ll struggle to maintain your hold. With continued use, your power grows rapidly, and what once took effort to keep can be held with ease as your limitations begin to loosen. In time, even the most complex things on the greatest scales can be stolen so completely and deeply that they remain permanently yours as if they always were. There is no real limit to how far your theft can eventually go.

You can choose how thoroughly to steal. You might take just a portion of someone’s charisma, or all of it. You can steal something and make it so no one notices it’s missing, or make it glaringly obvious to all.

You can also freely choose what to steal and from whom, allowing you to take only what you want without affecting related elements. You’ll intuitively steal only what you intend to steal, never causing unintended loss unless doing so intentionally.
objects.title: Theft

addons.text: Interesting thing isn’t it, ownership? Not only does the Inventory give you access to potentially infinite novel items, your Hoard now encompasses anything kept in its ‘pocket dimension’. But furthermore this link goes both ways, allowing you to store anything you have in your hoard in your pocket as if you’d summoned it. Additionally, you can now get a ‘return on investment’ from your hoard, essentially being able to sacrifice parts of it to receive charge in your pool that can be spent like any other you’ve naturally developed. That said, the value extracted from this never exceeds 5sp worth of charge at a time, and has diminishing returns the more items of similar type are used. Ie; coins, weapons, etc. Meaning you’ll have to keep a diverse (or overwhelmingly huge)hoard to maintain any steady flow out of this conversion.
addons.title: Krepel

objects.text: The manifestation of greed and desire. You possess an ability conceived as one of the potential explanations for why dragons hoard; that they draw power from their hoard, and now so do you as well. Every single object you possess ownership of, regardless of how it was acquired, provides a boost in power. The boost your hoard gives you is more than a simple increase in power, it bolsters and enhances all factors of your very existence, loosening restrictions and potentially even evolving you into a higher life form with new abilities once your hoard grows big enough. The boost gained from an object scales with its value, both intrinsic and perceived, but suffers diminishing returns as you gain more of it. In an average world gold may provide some boost at first, but acquire enough eventually it’ll take literal tons to make even the smallest of gains. On the other hand, In a world where gold is scarce, non-existent, or has a higher perceived value than it will provide greater gains, although it will still be subject to diminishing returns. The only things exempt from diminishing returns are one of a kind objects such as powerful magical artifacts or mastercrafted pieces of art. If you lose ownership of an object, i.e. it is no longer conceptually yours, then you lose the boost you gained from said object. There are certain exceptions, like if your hoard became large enough that you evolved. Losing your hoard won't make you suddenly unevolve, although you'll still lose the extra boost to your power.
objects.title: Dragon’s Hoard

addons.text:
Your Ancient name has been recognized as your main title standing above all others you will gain. It now has received a permanent 50% buff in whatever it provided for you and if you have more than 1 ancient name they all receive the same buff and you can choose any one or all of them to be public as your Main title always being the first thing people think of when they see you.

Your Ancient name can now also grow stronger by absorbing related titles with similar domains to it to grant it new effects or increase the base strength of the title. Your main title is counted as separate and doesn’t affect your 3 public slots.
addons.title: Grand Epithet

objects.text: You now have the power to gain epithets or titles when you accomplish something noteworthy or if enough people attribute something to you. There are titles for everything, and each one grants you some kind of positive effect — whether that be an affinity for something, a physical buff, or anything else, as long as it stems from you. These titles can be turned off or on, but can never be lost, and there is no limit to how many you can have active at once. The title of “Vampire Slayer”, for example, would give you an advantage against vampires of all kinds, with your attacks hitting harder against them and making it easier to pick up on their weaknesses. The more specific the title, the greater the buff. A title like “Element Master” would give you a 20% boost in using and controlling all elements, but one such as “Master of Fire” could make you immune to all natural fire, give you an easier time learning anything related to fire, and reduce the energy cost of any fire magic by half. You are able to set up to 3 titles as public. This makes it so that anyone who sees or knows about you instantly knows the names of those titles, which may bring people trying to challenge you or believing you unworthy of being called that title — but in exchange, those titles get up to a 50% boost in all categories. At the beginning, you are able to select either 1 title that can give you a 100% collective boost in something, or 3 separate titles that each give a maximum boost of 30% in separate fields. Titles can only improve so much, and if a title is too strong for your body to handle, it will be downgraded until it can fit you — for instance, changing “God of Fire” into "Flameborne" or “One Loved by Fire”.
objects.title: Epithet Collector

objects.text: Your are not prideful because you are strong, You are strong because you are prideful. Your claims are true. Your claims are adamant. Your might, unbound. Your will, unbreakable. Your ego unshatterable, for you are pride, and pride is for those at the top. You draw power from the sin of Pride—not the shallow arrogance of the boastful, but a deeper, honed pride rooted in your actions, your identity, and your unwavering belief in your worth. This path allows you to grow stronger not by denying your ego, but by mastering it—fueling your evolution through confidence, self-respect, and the will to rise above mediocrity. There are two forms of pride that shape your power. The first is hollow pride: the pride of appearances, of empty boasts and fleeting praise. In moments of vanity, when you are blinded by unearned glory or a need to be seen as superior, your power will spike dramatically. This kind of pride grants you sudden, potent surges—a blow that strikes harder than it should, an overwhelming presence that demands attention. But it is as unstable as it is intoxicating. When that illusion falters—when doubt, humiliation, or self-loathing sets in—the power vanishes as fast as it appears. It is a brilliant flare in the dark, but it leaves you emptier than before. The second is rightful pride: earned, honest, and rooted in both action and self-awareness. This is pride in what you’ve done—from facing trials, overcoming adversity, and staying true to your principles—but also in who you are. When you stand tall not because others told you to, but because you know your value, your power begins to evolve. When you take pride in your hard-earned victories, your loyalty, your growth, or even your flaws overcome, it rewards you with steady, compounding strength. The longer you walk this path with true pride, the faster you grow. And this applies not just to your victories, but to your very sense of self. When you take pride in your personality—your resilience, your compassion, your discipline, your ambition—your power deepens. You become difficult to sway, harder to break, and far more than the sum of your skills. This pride is not arrogance—it is a kind of armor, forged from truth, self-knowledge, and persistence. A mage who embraces the years spent mastering their craft, who knows their mind is sharp and their vision clear, will find their spells not just stronger, but more refined, faster, and harder to counter. A warrior who fights not for glory but because they know their strength protects others will grow with every battle, each strike carrying the weight of conviction. The more pride you take in your every step, the more every step transforms you. In time, the pride you carry will not merely empower you—it will define you.
objects.title: Greatest of Sins, Pride

objects.text:
You generate an energy when you consciously avoid an important task you know you should do. The energy's magnitude scales with the how important the task is and the duration of the delay, such as a major work project versus a minor chore. 

When you finally take action, for example opening that report minutes before the meeting, this stored energy is instantly spent. It warps probability around that single effort, condensing the time, effort, and quality of results that would normally require a prolonged, focused period into that one burst of activity. A higher energy reserve creates a more dramatically favorable and improbable outcome, smoothing over errors and generating exceptional results from minimal actual work, like producing a flawless, insightful document in a frantic, last-minute scramble.

The energy generated is task-specific. Procrastinating on your taxes builds a pool separate from avoiding a difficult conversation. However, if you delay to the point of absolute failure, like missing a flight or a final submission deadline, that specific energy does not vanish but distributes evenly, adding a boost to all other existing procrastination energy pools you hold, such as for the gym or a home repair.

However, this comes with a curse. The act of procrastination is intensely pleasurable. This bliss only activates when you are actively choosing to shirk a known responsibility. Sleeping in, playing a video game, watching a show or using your powers for convenience and pleasure become profoundly satisfying and effortless only when you are using them to escape that duty, like studying for an exam. If you play the same game on a free Saturday with no duties, it provides only normal enjoyment. This pleasure is proportional to the importance of what you're avoiding; neglecting a life-changing opportunity provides a deeper euphoria than skipping a daily chore. 

Once you begin the procrastinated task, the bliss vanishes, replaced by a grating inertia that makes starting the work feel physically and mentally uncomfortable. This discomfort is proportional to the amount of procrastination energy being spent, so a last-minute miracle on a major project feels like tearing yourself out of a warm bed and into a cold, grinding gear. It causes no injuries, and only lasts until you have fully started working. However, it’s impossible for you to get used to it.
objects.title: Allure of Sloth’s Embrace

objects.text:
You are a master at identity theft. You must first study a living human and mimic their appearance, voice, mannerisms, and personality as closely as possible. As your performance becomes convincing, the world begins to assist you by generating coincidences that hide minor flaws in your act. This includes lost documents, faulty memories in others, or technical glitches that cover your mistakes.

The more believable you are, the more the world starts to retroactively alter small details of the past to support your new identity. Photographs may subtly shift, or people’s recollections may blur to include you in the target’s history. With each of these historical edits, you gain fragments of the target’s skills, knowledge, and memories. Simultaneously, the target loses those same fragments, becoming progressively more confused and less capable. 

If the target dies at any point before the process is complete, the assimilation halts immediately. The subtle retroactive changes the power has woven begin to unravel over several days. You retain only a small fraction, typically less than ten percent, of any stolen skills or memories.

Upon completion, you gain all the target’s body, powers, skills and memories while they are left in a vegetative state. At this point you can switch between your original form and the stolen identity at will. However, in this state, your hold on the stolen identity sustained primarily by the ongoing belief of others. If enough people who matter, such as family, close friends, or key institutions, become convinced you are not the person you are mimicking, the stolen identity can unravel. The retroactive changes supporting it may begin to reverse, the skills may fade, and the target may even begin to recover.

The alternative is to choose a full replacement. This triggers a complete, permanent rewriting of reality where you become the target in all respects while your previous identity is erased from history and memory. You retain all its skills, but they are integrated into your new life’s story. The target’s becomes an anonymous invalid. This choice is final and makes the stolen identity absolute and unassailable.

There is no limit to how many times you can do this. However, the greater the difference in power between you and your target, the harder it becomes. The process stretches exponentially longer the more skilled or powerful the target is compared to you.
objects.title: Behold the Face of Envy

objects.text: People? I don't see people. I see assets. Assets to be used. Used, and hoarded. You are able to grow in power through two mechanisms derived from the people who work under you, treating your subordinates not as allies but as resources to be exploited for your own advancement. The first is a static buff to your strength calculated from your strongest asset. The greater the gap between your strength and that of your most powerful follower, the higher the percentage of your base power you gain as a bonus, stacking linearly with no maximum ceiling. If your strongest asset is roughly equal to you in power, you gain one hundred percent of your base power, to ensure you remain above them. If they are notably stronger than you, you gain two hundred and fifty percent. If they are vastly stronger than you, you gain five hundred percent, and this scaling continues indefinitely the more powerful the individual you manage to bring under your authority. The second is a growth multiplier that accelerates how quickly you can increase your base power through training and effort. The more total assets you have, the greater this multiplier becomes, increasing in a linear fashion based on sheer numbers. With ten people under you, your training efficiency increases by fifty percent. With one thousand, it increases fifty-onefold, ensuring that your personal growth accelerates alongside the size of your following. Anyone who has formally sworn loyalty to you, whether through employment, oath, contract, or coercion, and who recognizes your authority over them counts as a subordinate. This extends hierarchically, meaning the subordinates of your subordinates are also counted as your assets, even if they have never met you or do not know you exist. You are always aware of who is and is not counted among your assets, allowing you to instantly identify spies or moles who have not genuinely sworn themselves to you.
objects.title: Greed of Authority

objects.text:
Whenever you let overwhelming emotion fuel you, acting impulsively without any plans or knowledge, you gain permanent, exponential growth in whatever abilities or skills the situation demands. The growth scales in proportion to the recklessness of the act, as well as how unprepared you are.

For example, by throwing yourself into a street fight when outnumbered and outmatched, with no strategy or knowledge of your opponents, you will find yourself dodging and striking with skills you never practiced. Your body moves before you think, anticipating attacks you could not have predicted, and within seconds you are fighting with the instincts of a lifelong brawler despite never having thrown a real punch before. In that moment, you are flooded with an all-consuming fury that pushes you to press every advantage far past wisdom, disregarding any strategy, consequences, and self-preservation. The faster you grow, the more reckless you are, the stronger the flood becomes in the moment. 

The growth is purely practical, granting no theoretical understanding or conceptual knowledge. You cannot teach what you did or explain the skills you gained. You simply did it. This growth works best with purely practical, physical skills. The more a skill depends on muscle memory, reflexes, and physical intuition, the more dramatically your recklessness enhances it. Skills that require theoretical knowledge, diagnosis, or careful understanding receive a far cruder and weaker version of this growth.

Furthermore, the growth is never guaranteed to be sufficient. The power activates instantly, but the growth itself unfolds in real time, meaning you can still lose in the seconds it takes for your skill to rise to meet the threat.
objects.title: The Impatience of Wrath

objects.text:
Whenever you consume something excessively, you automatically generate a charge. Overspending money, oversleeping through an important meeting, overplaying games instead of working, or overindulging in any resource generates this charge. The quality of the waste matters exponentially more than the quantity. Wasting a single dollar that was your grandmother's last gift to you generates a charge many times greater than wasting one thousand dollars on a meaningless luxury. The power rewards the worth of what was squandered, not merely the amount.

After the act of waste, the charge slowly spends itself to twist fate to return more than what you originally spent. Waste a fortune on nothing, and over the following weeks, opportunities will present themselves that allow you to regain that fortune dozens of times over. Waste time that should have been spent on obligation, and you will find yourself with unexpected stretches of free time to use as you wish. Waste your physical energy in a frenzy of pointless activity, and your body will gradually grow healthier and more energetic than before, repaying your squandered vigor with interest. The return is guaranteed, but it operates on its own timetable, taking days or even months to fully manifest.

If you waste something of low worth, you generate a weaker charge, which may repay you less than what you spent, leaving you at a net loss. Wasting ten dollars on candy generates a return of five dollars found in a coat pocket. Wasting a priceless family heirloom on a momentary whim generates a return that could change your life entirely. 

The power demands that you become a connoisseur of waste, because only the finest remains turns into the finest rewards.
objects.title: The Remains of Gluttonous Waste

objects.text:
You can, at will, designate anything to be improved. This may be a skill, an item, a person, or any other discrete thing you can interact with and alter. Upon doing so, you gain an immediate and intuitive sense of how to perfect this designated thing. This guiding knowledge extends far beyond simple improvement to show you the full path toward transforming it into its ideal state. The closer it already is to perfection, the more fleshed out and clearer your vision becomes of how it would look if it were truly and utterly perfect. You may freely remove this designation at any time and replace it with another as you wish.

For example, should you designate a martial art, you will see how to refine its techniques and to strip away every inefficiency or flaw it has. You will sculpt it into a form that flows with absolute and unbroken grace, such that each movement becomes a pure expression of intent. Should you designate a weapon, you will understand precisely what materials, what craftsmanship, and what minute adjustments to balance and weight will render it an extension of your own will that is flawless in its function. Should you designate another person, you will perceive the exact words, actions, and influences required to reshape them into your perfect mental image. Their mind, body, and spirit will be molded to match the ideal you hold.

You gain the skills, instructions, insights, and knowledge needed to elevate your designated thing, and the progress of your improvements are also accelerated so that moving from zero to fifty percent of your ideal takes only a tenth of the normal time before the speed tapers off. It also ensures you have the luck to find the opportunities and means required for improvement. The further the thing is from perfection, the more potent these gifts become, while the closer it draws, the more you must rely on your own abilities, though you will never be completely without help. In every case, the perfect state you work toward is defined not by any objective standard but solely by what you personally see as perfection.

The closer you bring something to that ideal, the more intense the enjoyment and pleasure you derive from the process. Each step rewards you with a deep and resonant satisfaction. Yet you will also know with absolute certainty that true perfection will forever elude you. As you near it, you will see ever more clearly the smallest remaining flaws. You will understand that reality itself cannot bridge the final gap to make an imperfect thing truly perfect. You are left to savor the endless pursuit while knowing the final consummation, where you behold a masterpiece utterly flawless and shaped entirely by your will, is a pleasure forever forbidden to you.
objects.title: Imperfections of Perfect Lust

objects.text:
Most warriors plateau when no longer challenged. A seasoned swordsman can only sharpen their blade so much against a novice; without a worthy rival, progress stagnates. Growth demands friction—conflict against those who match or surpass you, a mirror that forces evolution.

You felt it was a pain to leave the tutorial zone.

Now, even foes beneath your level become stepping stones, their cumulative resistance shaping you. It’s arithmetic in motion: if your opponent possesses only half your strength, then facing two of them will yield the same growth as one battle with your equal. Ten weak foes, ten fragments of strength—they add up. Fight enough, and even the meek can forge the mighty.

This applies to all parts of combat: physical effort, reaction speed, movement control, and decision-making. Even if the fights are easier, repeating them still builds physical conditioning and sharpens awareness. Over time, you will gain the same amount of experience and instinctual growth you would gain from fighting stronger opponents.
objects.title: One Thousand Cuts

addons.text:
Your Oneness with a concept has permanently altered not just your essence but how you interact with it as well, which has in turn impacted your ability to enforce your actions. 

You experience rapidly accelerated development of conceptual weight and greater returns when enforcing your actions when said act falls under the umbrella of your enlightenment. For example an enlightenment relating to oneness with nature would make actions relating to nature benefit more from your conceptual enforcement. The benefits are greater and more efficient the closer the act committed aligns with your enlightenment.
addons.title: Enlightened Enforcement

addons.text:
Your soul is simply worth more than others, its presence fundamentally greater than that of others. And with this your metaphysical importance has soared, your every action carrying orders of magnitude more conceptual weight. 

Even from the beginning you have enough force to make your actions minorly warp reality to align with their purpose and intent. Hiding causes your presence to fade, spear thrusts unerringly seek weak points, dodges warp space to turn sure hits into near misses, etc.
addons.title: Spiritual Decree

addons.text:
As the embodiment of a concept tethered to the fear of an entire species, you naturally exert more influence upon the world, especially when it comes to what concept you represent.

As the manifestation of the fear of a concept, you are naturally conceptual important, possessing greater metaphysical weight which only grows greater the more your concept is feared.

But this is only the tip of the iceberg, the real benefit lies in your ability to derive extra conceptual force from the fear of what you represent. You can use it as an extra source of weight, albeit one which can only be used to enforce acts related to your nature and powers as a devil.
addons.title: Devilish Authority

objects.text:
You have learned how to actualize and enforce the intent behind your actions, using your metaphysical weight to enhance their effects. This begins rather weakly—merely making actions slightly more successful than they should be: a dodge carrying you farther and being more effective, an attempt at hiding leaving fewer traces, and so on. However, as the conceptual weight behind your actions grows stronger, so too do the effects of your enforcement—eventually bestowing supernatural traits and culminating in truly conceptual acts at higher levels.

While low-level enforcement of a sword swing might merely cause the blade to cut slightly better than it should, medium-level enforcement could allow you to block or cut things you normally couldn’t—such as a simple steel sword slicing through metal like butter or even blocking a lightsaber. At the highest levels, you achieve truly conceptual feats: an attempt at hiding could become so effective that reality itself forgets your existence, allowing you to do things like achieve agelessness by hiding from the very flow of time.

There are two ways to increase the conceptual weight you can bestow upon your actions. The first is by enriching your own existence—enhancing your metaphysical weight through some means. Whether through time and experience, sheer power, or something more exotic, the greater the meaning and significance behind your existence, the more force your actions will carry.

The second method is more specialized: by repeatedly practicing an action, you increase the weight behind that specific act. Your mastery bestows further force. The speed of this development depends on how specific the action is. Mastering the entirety of swordsmanship to a conceptual level might take several lifetimes, while mastering a single sword stroke could be achievable within an average human lifespan.

This effect is incredibly pervasive, capable of being applied to any act—both mundane tasks and the use of powers. For example, enforcing fire magic might initially make your flames burn hotter and spread faster than they should. But with enough metaphysical weight, your flames could eventually burn through space, time, fate, and other conceptual entities.
objects.title: Conceptual Enforcement

objects.text:
You and your powers are empowered in direct proportion to the adversity you face. The more severe your situation—the greater the number of enemies, the stronger they are, the more injured you or your allies become, the fewer allies remain, and the closer you are to failing your objective—the more your power increases. This scaling is responsive to the real-time conditions of the battle or scenario, adapting to both physical and strategic pressures.

If you succeed in completing your objective while under this heightened stress—regardless of whether success means defeating your enemies, surviving a set period, rescuing a target, or any other defined victory condition—you retain a portion of the enhanced power permanently.

If you exceed the required conditions—for instance, defeating or disabling your enemies when you only needed to delay them, or completing your mission with zero casualties when only one life needed saving—the retained boost increases exponentially. A flawless or overwhelming success can result in the full temporary power becoming a permanent enhancement to your base state.
objects.title: Against the Tides

addons.text:
You have gained a special locale for your Personas, a ‘Cortex Compound’. This ‘compound’ is composed of three main locations, the ‘Garden’ the ‘Compound propper’ and the ‘Observation deck’, not to mention the network of tunnels and pathways between each and around your mind.

The Garden is where the majority of your Personas will tend to migrate, a relatively peaceful area to congregate with each other and make themselves very easily found.

The Compound propper contains multiple cells for the more problematic members of your mind. These cells, while not completely foolproof, allow you to siphon their powers without letting them near you or facing them directly. 

The Observation Deck is a place for your ‘command team’, any trusted personas, interesting perspectives, or convenient powers you need full and easy access to at a moment's notice.
addons.title: Cortex Compound

addons.text: Unfortunately, your Personas no longer fade away, becoming consistent and persistent fixtures of your internal landscape.
addons.title: Sanctity of Life In a Profoundly Strange Way

addons.text:
Your separation has merged with your means of power generation. Rather than your separated selves being essentially random in attributes, you can instead manifest your personas into reality. 

Similarly, when manifesting these Personas, you are not limited to five selves, instead being able to produce as many bodies as you have Personas to imbue them with. Additionally, you only need five of them to combine to enable ‘you’ to manifest fully. 

Naturally, this also means should there be multiple groups of Personas merging, you can have multiple instances of yourself manifest at a time, or should a single group be made of more than five, the corresponding manifestation would be proportionally stronger. (for example, a group of ten would be twice as powerful as normal).
addons.title: So Five Wasn’t Enough?

objects.text:
You are a power manifester of great speed and potency, able to create specific, esoteric powers worth 15sp in seconds. Unfortunately, it has a severe side effect: every time you manifest a new power, it comes with a personality of its own. These ‘Persona’ run the gamut from vague caricatures to fully formed individuals with bespoke backstories.

When using a power created in this way, you can use the Persona’s power, in which case you’ll have to either force an agreement from them or forcibly mentally dominate them, or you can give the Persona full control of your body, in which case they will be able to use the power generated at full potency and with a natural skill that would put you to shame.

After a Persona has been created, they will persist, slowly losing focus and ‘strength’ as the power they’re attached to is not used, until they eventually reintegrate with your mind. Until they do so, they are capable of talking and acting internally, and in extremis can take over your body, though retaining control of it requires great will from them. Similarly, multiple Personas are not guaranteed to be amicable—not just toward you, but also toward each other. When a Persona is reintegrated with you, the power they’re connected to is similarly lost and must be constructed again. Using the power also helps maintain their consciousness.

It’s probably best you don’t create too many at once lest they become a true cacophony. Thankfully, they may not choose to remain in your ‘conscious’ mind at all times, giving you both a much needed break, though this is still at their discretion.
objects.title: For We Are Many

objects.text:
When killing a creature with a soul, your soul automatically claims it, storing and metabolising it. This absorbed soul is broken down and used to expand and strengthen your own. As your soul grows, it subtly alters your capabilities. There is a minor, risk-free bleed through in skills, though this is rarely direct. Most of the bleed through manifests in the form of talents, instincts, and experience.

As your soul expands, its presence begins to exert pressure on the world around you. This pressure is spiritual in nature. Creatures with smaller, weaker souls feel it as a growing weight in your presence. The effect causes unease, tension, or hesitation that deepens in proportion to the gap between souls.

Your growth does not stop at the soul. Due to nature’s innate tendency toward balance, a soul that far outpaces the body places it under increasing strain. In response, your body begins to adapt. It grows stronger and more resilient to keep pace, changing to match the scale of the soul within. This change focuses on density over volume, with a ratio of roughly 4:1. The transformation extends beyond raw strength and speed—it enhances vitality, sharpens the mind, and deepens your resilience to age and harm. 

At a certain point, the separation between soul and body begins to blur. Your soul, too dense to remain passive, starts pressing outward into the physical. The result is subtle at first: a step that lands too heavy for your weight, a glance that causes glass to tremble, a word that echoes louder than it should. These are manifestations of pure intent bleeding through your form. As this fusion deepens, your very presence gains weight—your movements carry not just mass, but meaning. Strikes hit harder not just because of strength, but because your soul demands impact.

However, growth is not infinite. As your soul expands, it eventually reaches thresholds—bottlenecks where its scale begins to outpace its coherence. At these points, continued absorption yields diminishing returns; lesser souls offer only fragments, barely enough to stir movement. 

To progress further, you must either consume vast quantities of minor souls over time, each one a drop in an ocean, or claim a singular, powerful soul—one vast enough to shake the foundations of your own. Breaking through these bottlenecks does not increase the size of your soul, but its quality—its density, clarity, and depth. 

The result is a soul that weighs heavier on the world, its pressure more refined, more absolute. With each breakthrough, your body suffers renewed strain, forced once more to adapt. The soul’s advance scours the form it inhabits, expelling weakness, refining structure, and burning away the subtle impurities of flesh. 

Additionally, if you have any absorption based or absorption-adjacent powers, the souls you automatically claim are counted as absorbed by them.
objects.title: Soul Giant

objects.text:
This ability lets you wager your own growth on a roll of the dice. You hold a strange pair of six-sided dice that governs your potential. When activated, you roll the dice three times: once for how long the effect will last, once for how strong the effect will be, and once to decide whether it helps or hurts you.

The first roll determines duration. Each point equals one day, with a maximum of twelve. Until those days pass, you cannot use this power again and will be stuck with its effect. The second roll sets the rate of change, with each point representing a 10% modifier. At best, you could gain a 120% boost or penalty.

The final roll is a contest of chance. You roll for a high number against the power itself. If your result is higher, the growth is positive. Your efforts accelerate, learning improves, and abilities progress faster according to the rate. If the power wins, the growth is negative. Progress slows down, and even existing skills or abilities will begin to decay, all based on the rolled rate.

These dice are completely and utterly random. No force, magical, technological, or divine, can predict or alter the outcome. If rolled regularly over the course of a month, a new additional die will form, giving you better potential rewards or worse penalties.
objects.title: Roll for the Future

objects.text:
There comes a point when a warrior no longer relies on their weapon because they have surpassed it. Over time, you grow past any weapon, growing until steel is frail compared to your skin and arrows seem sluggish next to your stride. 

When you use a weapon in its intended manner, you begin absorbing its defining strength. This process does not damage or drain the weapon; instead, you gradually adapt and outgrow it. The weapon’s primary physical trait, whether sharpness, durability, reach, speed, or precision, becomes a quality your own body begins to emulate and eventually surpass. For instance, wielding a finely tempered sword will eventually grant your strikes the same cutting potential. Using a reinforced shield long enough will result in your skin and bones developing greater resilience than its surface.

The rate of absorption is governed by two key factors. The first is the relative strength gap between you and the weapon. The greater the weapon's advantage over you, the faster your growth toward it. The second is your familiarity, both with that type of weapon in general and the specific weapon you are wielding. Familiar tools accelerate the transformation. This is a gradual process, not instant empowerment. Meaningful progression requires actual combat use and time. Sparring, training, and life-or-death situations all contribute to integration.

This does not trigger if the weapon in question has no trait that currently surpasses your own capabilities. Additionally, while you cannot absorb magical effects and gain completely unrelated abilities, you will still grow beyond a weapon that possesses such qualities by outclassing it through its physical nature alone. Once your body exceeds the weapon’s purpose, it is considered obsolete to you and will no longer grant further progression.
objects.title: Greater Than Arms

addons.text: You gain the ability to convert any rewards you would gain from quests given by Questboard into progress towards one of your quests from Covenant. The amount of progress you get is based on the difficulty of the quest from the Questboard. Do note that this addon has a soft cap, where at most it can fulfil 50% of the completion requirement for a quest generated by Covenant. Should you push this addon further, there are further diminishing returns capped at 75%. In simple terms, this addon cannot fully complete Covenant quests on its own, and you will still need to put in some amount of work, just less than normal.
addons.title: Progress Rewards

objects.text:
You can declare a desired reward, anything from the very specific—such as a weapon that ignores all defenses, or the power to become a dragon—to something vague like “I want to be stronger.

Rewards can be concrete (a weapon, wealth, abilities), abstract (love, influence, knowledge, safety), or even a mixture of unrelated things. You may ask for one prize or several at the same time.

Requests do not have to be precise. A vague wish is enough, and the power will always determine the perfect and most fitting form of the reward, even if you aren’t fully sure what you want. A vague request will be interpreted into an ideal result.

Sometimes, even when a request is made very specifically, the result may be adjusted and refined into something better than the user thought to ask for. In this way, every reward feels like the “true” version of what was wanted, whether clearly named or only half-formed in intent.

You may also choose how the reward comes to you. It can be produced directly by the power at the end, or it can be gained naturally along the course of the quest itself. Smaller, related rewards may also appear as milestones while progressing. Rewards do not necessarily need to be aligned with the quest you take, although if you want to acquire it naturally along the questline, it will naturally accommodate that.

When a request is made, a quest forms. You’ll immediately know its name, its themes, and a general sense of what lies ahead. You gain an instinctive feel for the difficulty involved and a constant awareness of your progress as you advance. The quest keeps you updated, lets you track your current status, and shows you the next few objectives and steps, though never the entire quest.

When the quest first forms, you have the ability to accept it as is or renegotiate it. You can raise the difficulty for greater or more numerous rewards, or lower it for smaller, safer rewards. You can also alter time-based components as well, expanding or crunching them for similar effects.

You may also nudge the quest towards a certain style, whether combat-focused, investigative, social, or endurance-based. The final form, however, is always set by the power itself. Once accepted, the quest is fixed, and the only way out is to abandon it, forfeiting the prize. You can abandon a quest at any time; it will not prevent you from trying to get the same reward at a later time.

You may have as many active quests as you want, although some may merge into one larger one where appropriate. Every quest is tailored to the user, taking the user’s requested rewards and their own capabilities into mind. The same request may demand little from someone strong but impose a great trial on someone weaker. This means that as you get more powerful, the difficulty scales in your favor.
objects.title: Covenant

objects.text: This power grants you three Prototype Slots, each of which can be devoted to an object, device, or consumable of your choice. Every slot generates one Engineering Point (EP) per day, a resource that fuels the gradual advancement of that prototype. The conversion rate is steady: each EP is worth roughly half a SP in long-term value, and a prototype begins at the equivalent of about 1 SP, comparable to a minor Out-of-Profile item. Left to develop on its own, a slot naturally adds the equivalent of one SP every two days, steadily strengthening the design over time. Unlike powers, which are immediate and flexible, prototypes are slow, permanent investments. Once an item is developed, its progress is never lost, even if set aside to free the slot for a different project. Prototyping does not follow a single path. A design may advance through Blueprinted Engineering, which favors precision and predictability at the cost of speed and flexibility, or through Parametric Evolution, where adaptive growth pushes results faster but risks quirks or unpredictable changes. A more balanced method is Reservoir Prototyping, which allows EP to be stored and spent deliberately, offering control at the cost of risk—if the prototype is destroyed before investment is applied, the stored EP vanishes with it. Slots can also be locked, binding them permanently to one prototype in exchange for accelerated growth. A single locked slot doubles its output to two EP per day, while committing all three raises their production to two and a half EP daily each, for a total of 7.5 EP. Consumables interact with the system differently, with 2 modes. Instead of upgrading individual items, EP strengthens their recipe, ensuring that every future batch reflects the improvements. A healing potion worth 3 SP, for instance, could be refined into a 10 SP version in just two weeks of investment, after which every potion brewed from that template would carry the improved potency. Consumables retain their single-use nature unless reinforced through prolonged and specialized development, at which point they may become semi-permanent effects or even renewable constructs. And spwaning, where you use EP to "create" the item with the price being more costly the higher it's SP rating being, with batches having a discount on proportion with the price. The efficiency of prototyping depends heavily on synergy. Enhancements that complement one another—such as durability paired with self-repair—progress more cheaply and cleanly, while contradictory traits, like fire and ice in the same system, cause development to stall until the conflict is resolved or the design rebalanced, and the deeper the conceptual coherence of the design, the faster and more reliable its growth. In practice, a prototype can transform dramatically with steady attention. A minor 3 SP tool might reach 10 SP in roughly two weeks, climb to 20 SP within the next three, and, with sustained focus, evolve into a 40 SP marvel within two months. Though this pace is slow compared to direct powers, the results are enduring and accumulate without regression. Growth is deliberate, sometimes unpredictable, but always permanent.
objects.title: Prototype Engineering

objects.text:
