These pastures will be further protected by dense, nearly impenetrable shrubbery, forest, or other natural terrain, depending on local conditions, while still providing convenient access to your Farm.

Initially, the pasture area will be approximately 1,000 acres and can be expanded in the future as your herd grows, providing about 5 acres per cow.
addons.title: Abundant Pastures

objects.text:
A simple life in the wilds is what some people ask for. To be able to connect with nature, and just live off the land. Well, in your case, that's at least partially possible.

This farm, placeable in a forest or similar environment, is rather special in what it can do. Any livestock you own, or creatures in general, will find themselves perfectly healthy and incapable of getting sick. Your horses can never get arthritis. Your cows will never get Mad Cow Disease, and so on, to the point of disease immunity. As well, any crops or even plant-able Objects of Power will grow in abundance and never go rotten or bad in general. To start with, you get 4 of all kinds of farm animals, with a book in the house on breeding patterns to increase various aspects of these animals.

Your farm also has a very calming and nostalgic aura around it. Aggression will give way to serenity, and sadness will slowly turn into hope of a better life. Your farm is around 3500 acres, with self-replenishing supplies to repair, AND expand, albeit at a slow pace for the latter.

Finally, your structures like the farmhouse, silo, barn, and chicken coop, are indestructable. Even if a barrage of missiles were fired at the place, the worst they could do is cause visual damage to the walls and fences. The only downside of this place is that you get no farmhands to start with. While the farm CAN take care of itself, It trades speed for efficiency. Workers can help expedite the process, the farm house even having good living conditions for them with replenishing food and water and the like.
objects.title: The Farm

objects.text:
You now possess a vast library that holds every book (from past to present) from every universe you’ve ever visited. This grand collection contains knowledge from the mundane to the arcane, from the scientific to the metaphysical. From the outside, the Library is a small, unassuming building, with the inside being massively bigger than the outside. You can choose where the library is spawned.

Be careful when reading books in the library, as some books contain dangerous information—memetic hazards that could alter your mind or reality itself, depending on the rules of the world they are from. Luckily, as long as it’s on the shelf, the books cannot affect you.

The older tomes—some that the original has long since been destroyed due to age—are fragile, and some held together by brittle bindings that could crumble with a touch. While the library is enchanted with basic preservation magic to prevent decay and maintain order, it is far from foolproof. The magic does not protect against mishandling or the more volatile properties of certain books, so caution is needed.

Additionally, while the library offers unparalleled access to multiversal knowledge, it lacks a universal translation feature. You must decipher texts in their original languages, and some may require unique methods of interpretation—whether through spells, advanced technology, or ancient rituals—further complicating your pursuit of knowledge. In essence, this library is a treasure trove of wisdom, but it demands both respect and caution from those who would unlock its secrets.
objects.title: The Great Library of Alexandria

objects.text: Welcome to the Museum... or was it a Library? Perhaps an Armory? Well... regardless, welcome! Before you is what aims to be the greatest collection of artifacts and knowledge in all the multiverse. Who am I? I’m the Curator here, setting up displays and guiding the occasional tours. Who collects everything? Well... that would now be you, if you’re interested at least. You are? Wonderful! Go hunting to collect something, and I’ll find a place to display it here... somewhere. There’s always more space. Don’t worry—whatever you donate can be withdrawn whenever you need it. Think of it as making the various items you’re not currently using useful for something. We could always use some new books for our library. Or perhaps you’d like to contribute to our armory—a display of every kind of weapon you can think of, and probably a few you can’t. Maybe an example of local flora or fauna instead? No? Perhaps a set of those fascinating orange crystals with various numbers of stars? Or a new vehicle for our displays—I’ve heard good things about an old bird of prey. Oh! Finding a new building to display might be more up your alley? There are rumors of a school for witches and wizards I’ve been hearing about. Well... I suppose it doesn’t matter what you decide to find. I’ll display it all the same. Some of the... larger items may need to be shrunken down for practical reasons, but everything will be displayed in a way that any guest can wander by and take a look safely. Each display has various protections to deal with and contain the more... unruly items. What else... Ah, I almost forgot. Here’s a key to the safehouse. I don’t use it, or need it, so you’re welcome to use it as you like. It has plenty of space and comes with all the usual amenities. It’s not the lap of luxury, but it’s comfortable. It’ll be so good to finally have a partner for this little enterprise... happy hunting.
objects.title: The Museum

objects.text: In life, people look for many forms of entertainment. Companionship, Activities, violence... You have been gifted an arena by the gods themselves to give entertainment to the men and women of the world around you! This Arena, typically stored in a crown, can be thrown and grown to full size, although it is generally advised that even if it will not crush whatever was originally there, It'll shove it all out of the way, so it is suggested to do this in an empty area. The Undying Colosseum is about 60 acres in size, and indestructible from all forms of attack, although air attacks are still VERY possible even if they wouldn't do anything. The directions of the arena are yours to visualize: Whether this be idiot proof signs, or deliberately hard to navigate. But, the true purpose of this arena isn't what it's made of. It's what happens inside that counts. In the arena in the center, you can hold any and all entertainment types inside. A rap battle, a sports game, a death match, etc. The actual floor surrounded by the wall has a bit of spatial distortion, so it's actually bigger than it looks from the seats, though all this will look like to the viewers is faster movement. Finally, you can charge any and everything for a seat. Livestock, gold, metaphysical aspects of a person, etc. The more they give if you so choose, the better quality of the seat until they get a private seat right next to you, the emperor of this colosseum. There are other rooms in the stadium related to comfort, slave/beast/gladiator (separately) holdings, and more.
objects.title: The Undying Colosseum

objects.text:
Travel is a universal concept. And while not quite universal, vacations are also quite a common concept for those who wish to just get away from the trouble. Well, you own the building that will make these wishes come true. Commonly Identified as "Timely Travel Agency," this building is quite unassuming from the outside. It has signs indicating its function, call to actions on the windows, along with beautiful paintings that invoke beauty and feelings of wonder in those who look at it, and just overall looks rather cozy and the like from the outside.

However, once you step inside, well... visitors are treated to quite a big lobby alone. Outside, this building looks like it can handle maybe 9 or 10 average sized rooms. The Lobby alone, however, is as large as your average basketball arena interior. In total in fact, the building inside is exactly 5 square kilometers, from end to end with all functions needed for the best travel agency in the world, and more.

Without fail, anyone who books a flight, train, or any kind of ride, they will coincidentally find the exact ride they need. They will also find that, for an extra fee, they will have luck on their travels. Even their destinations will give them decent luck when it comes to events. If a Pokémon trainer were to book a ride to their next gym town, they might find a decently strong Pokémon on the side of the road who needs help. An alien in Star Wars might need to get from Naboo all the way to Coruscant in an unreasonable amount of time. Well, looks like an express ship just landed at the spaceport, with no stops from there till Coruscant.

In fact, this travel serves not just for the universe you're in, but even the local multiverse cluster! This building is able to exists in multiple spaces at once, although the building only allows so many customers in at a time to prevent bloat.

All of the building is staffed with just enough workers to get the job done, although you can hire more if desired.
objects.title: Timely Travel Agency

addons.text: Your Nanoforge technology is implemented into your Manufacturing and Shipyards. Anything assembled will be in higher quality, and your shipyards now produce ships twice as fast.
addons.title: Nanofactory

addons.text: Space can be dangerous, and sometimes you might need to do repairs outside your base. Who better to protect you from the horrors of the void than a Plush Pal? You receive one of them to each cubic kilometer of base. They are adapted to work in space, able to move in zero-gravity, impervious to heavy radiation, and able to serve as space suits to others.
addons.title: Plush Helpers

addons.text: Your starbase now comes equipped with the Constructions Drones from the Icarus Protocol. A little smaller than a car, they are incredibly capable. They can run near indefinitely without need for recharge, assemble and disassemble machines, and collect resources from faraway places. The drones aren't very smart, needing specific orders and schematics to assemble what you might want, but have enough intelligence to adapt to each situation. You receive 3 drones per cubic kilometer of base.
addons.title: Construction Drones (Dyson Sphere Program)

addons.text: Your productions capabilities are enhanced, getting a similar assembly method to The Factory. While unable on its own to produce matter from nothing, it can produce goods half the speed The Factory can, and with the same flawless precision. You can also add The Factory, and the Suburbs upgrade if you have it as well, to the Starbase without taking up any of your maximum volume.
addons.title: Factory²

addons.text: With the information from the Synchrotron Core, you can now add Anti-Matter Production facilities on your starbase. At full capacity, you could produce each day a bottle per 1k³ dedicated to it, though keep in mind that you will need plenty of materials to do so.
addons.title: Industrial-Scale Fuel Production

objects.text:
Starbases serve to project power on star systems. Highly modular, they can fit any niche a space faring civilization might need. From anchorages to hold hundreds of ships while they refuel to travel to another system, to massive shipyards assembling fleets of Destroyers so they can fight their enemies, to refining millions of tons of raw resources to meet the demands of materials. A Starbase can do all of it and more.

Your Starbase is quite big, with 40km³ of space to arrange as you want. Initially, the Starbase comes installed with the following facilities:

Refining & Recycling is responsible for turning things into basic components. From melting ores and separating it on rocks and metals, and turning them into alloys; to taking broken things and waste to turn them into reusable material.

Manufacturing turns the previous mentioned resources into finished goods. Those factories can assemble simple things like bricks to more complex things such as the electronics and engines used on star ships. Initially its databases will contain only the blueprints for the technology present on the base itself, plus some civilian technology you could expect to find around a hundred years from now: But any power that grants you some sort of technological database can be automatically inserted into the Starbase database.

Shipyards serve to repair, refit, and of course, build ships. On its base, the amount of space dedicated to serve as shipyards can be used to produce the equivalent in ship size in a week; so 10km³ of a shipyard can produce 10 ships with a total space of 1km³ each. If a ship is bigger than the total space available you can produce it in parts. On the database, there is a myriad of ships you can assemble: mining ships, shuttles, auxiliary builders, battleships, and a colony ship. A software is installed that lets you customize said ships, and scale them for your needs.

Life Support is the most diversified facility. It covers food production with advanced hydroponics and meat growing vats, oxygen management with both filtering and algae and moss farms (which are actually quite tasty), energy productions via a handful of Fusion Reactors, the gravity generator, and while not necessarily vital but not less important, the Shield Generator, protecting the station from the odd micro meteors and the odd pirate. 

Civilian Quarters, is not exactly a facility, but is just as important for the day-to-day of its inhabitants. From schools and day cares, hospitals and police stations, law firms and restaurants: if it can be found in a city, it can be found here. A Central Oversee Universal System Interfare Network handles the day to day stuff: from coordinating first responders, maintenance and expansion, and even pointing a guest to a restaurant they may like. You may choose to have this space filled with inhabitants that can work on the Starbase.

Additionally, you may fill the Starbase with other sections if you have the know-how. A research lab, a cloning facility, a garden filled with magic plants, etc. 

How much of the station each facility occupies, if there is multiple or none of them, or even if the facility is just empty, is up to you. Either way, the Starbase comes with supplies to maintain itself and its inhabitants for a year.
objects.title: Your Own Starbase

objects.text:
You are the proud new owner of the cozy Hot Spring Inn, capable of housing up to 32 guests and 8 staff members. 

The hot spring's water is enchanted to soothe any aches and pains as well as to always be the best temperature for the people inside and is even safe to drink. 

The work stations are equipped with high quality materials, tools and equipment and the kitchens are always stocked with whatever ingredients you could want.

Anyone you appoint as a staff member will be supernaturally good at any jobs you give them.
objects.title: Hot Spring Inn

addons.text:
Your Moon Cell has merged with the COMbat Providence AnalysiS System, resulting in a profound change as the two become something more than the sum of its parts, the most immediate change being that the new system possesses the same depth of data on all worlds connected to it as the original Moon Cell had on Earth, meaning you can summon Servants from said worlds.

Said Servants can be summoned to act as Hero units, greatly expanding your roster, and to help keep things fair, the Heroes who are invited to COMPASS become Pseudo Servants, giving them far greater power and benefits on top of what they normally gain from COMPASS.

You also gain access to a new battle type: Grail War Battle Royale. A 7+ hero free-for-all battle held in a large arena the size of a small country, where Heroes and Players compete to be the last team standing in order to gain a wish; these wishes are not omnipotent but can grant a fair deal, as they are tied to the Moon Cell and COMPASS. Regardless of the wish made, it is a certainty that the system would benefit from the Grail War as it collects energy and data.
addons.title: Multiversal Moon Cell

addons.text:
Each time you use the H-Dial, you call upon the power of a Hero from across the Heroverse. Once time is up, that Hero is usually never seen again or very rarely makes sparse reappearances, depending on your affinity with them.

Now, when you call upon the power of a new Hero, said Hero can be offered the chance to come to COMPASS and receive all the benefits and opportunities that come with it, with their worlds becoming connected to COMPASS for the system to gather more data and granting them a degree more stability.

Over time, it's possible for COMPASS to become a wellspring of power for the Heroverse, as more and more Heroes find themselves drawn to it and the system grows more powerful exponentially through the new data and energies of the Heroverse, allowing it to evolve in ways never thought of before with new and experimental ideas.
addons.title: Compass Dial

objects.text:
You have come into the ownership of something truly unique; a world born of data with you alone in control of its source code, where heroes from different worlds gather to compete against one another in 3 on 3 battles (though other modes can be created), which help sustain the central computer system at the heart of this realm through energy gathered from said battles. The central system exists within a large facility shaped like a cube, manned by a seemingly endless army of robotic guards and servitors; this is the Combat Providence Analysis System, or better known as COMPASS. Below the cube, an expansive tower known as the Qualia Tower, which has an advanced and sprawling city through all layers of it. This city has every luxury and convenience one could imagine, where one can start up a business to follow their passions, hold idol concerts, set up workshops, and so much more.

The Heroes are divided into four broad roles they take on in these battles; they aren't restricted to these roles, but rather it represents what they are more specialized towards. These are Attacker, Sprinter, Defender, and Gunner, with what they do being fairly straightforward, focusing on attack, speed, defence, and range duties during the 3 v 3 battles.

While all Heroes are formidable in their own right, they can be further enhanced through cards provided by COMPASS; up to 4 cards can be equipped to a hero at once, which can have a variety of effects, from enhancing the capabilities of the heroes to giving them specialized moves. Over time, the computer system of COMPASS will create new cards as it collects more data from the 3 v 3 battles and your own adventures; these cards can be anything from common types of attack and defence in one world to specialized Super Moves for specific Heroes. However, all of these cards require energy to function and possess a cooldown after use, but are less restrictive outside of the 3 v 3 battles of COMPASS. The cooldown can be shortened during active conflict, to the point it is nonexistent, but that would require something on the scale of a major battle in a war or a massive invasion, and over time the card limit can be increased.

Coming to COMPASS, Heroes gain a few quality-of-life enhancements on top of coming to meet, learn, talk, and improve; these are usually something minor, such as summoning equipment and storing it in special inventories only able to hold their loadout of equipment.

Helping you run all of this are your Partners / Companions: Voidoll, a helpful robot whose main role is managing the everyday operations of COMPASS as one of its Administrators and summoning Heroes the system has selected, and her counterpart Bugdoll, a dark counterpart of Voidoll who has become part of COMPASS's external interaction, practical for things such as scouting out different worlds, espionage, and other duties such as defences against external threats.

As the owner of the COMbat Providence AnalysiS System, you possess special privileges in which you can summon perfect—and loyal—copies of Heroes recorded in the system to fight for you: these copies retain much of the personalities of said heroes, allowing them to act autonomously with no concern for distance; however, you are limited to fielding 3 Heroes at a time, with Voidoll and Bugdoll not taking up slots, though this limit too can be increased as COMPASS grows and develops. Optionally, you can change the appearance of your summoned Heroes, but it is limited to different themed outfits (Holidays, Uniforms, etc.) and colour palettes.

Another privilege you possess is being able to steadily learn the skills and powers of the Heroes you summon. The learning process varies, as the more advanced or unique a power and skill is, the longer it will take to copy, much less master; learning the ability to open portals to other universes can take up to 10 years to learn and master without additional powers or perks.

But it's not only Heroes who can interact with this world, as 'non-heroes' can join as well, taking the role of Partners; they partner up with Heroes to support them to unleash their full potential and utilize support abilities provided by COMPASS. Partners cannot enter this world (for now), but instead use chibi avatars through whatever medium best suits their worlds; more commonly, it's in the form of a game, but other mediums can appear. Heroes and Partners can partner up if both agree to it through a simple interface all Heroes and Partners have access to, and said partnership can be dissolved once both agree or through intervention of the system.

While Heroes who are selected by the system and, normally, summoned / invited by Voidoll come to COMPASS completely, Partners who use avatars have their consciousness doubled, so to speak, allowing them to play in whatever medium they can while their avatar interacts with Heroes, with these interactions being felt as emotions, dreams, and general imagination.

Not all Partner and Hero partnerships are ideal, as it's expected not all of them would get along perfectly, but each one will leave both Partner and Hero learning something to help them on their own journeys.

In the beginning, you will only have the original Heroes from #COMPASS and connection to their respective worlds, but as time goes on, new Heroes from new worlds within your local multiverse, and potentially the Omniverse, can be selected to be invited; with them, the Combat Providence Analysis System will grow and gain upgrades, along with its own universe expanding in size.
objects.title: 【COMbat Providence AnalysiS System】 (#COMPASS)

objects.text:
"Bay City's most macabre lodging establishment."

A hotel chain operated by an artificial intelligence named Poe has been in operation for over fifty years. The hotel offers a variety of features and rooms now that you have become its sole guest of honour. One of the most notable aspects is the unwavering adoration of Poe, the AI that manages the hotel, who will stop at nothing to ensure your safety. You can rest easy knowing that you are protected within the walls of the Raven Hotel. The hotel boasts hundreds of luxury suites, a bar tended by Poe, opulent baths, and an array of weaponry, among other amenities.

Poe is an artificial intelligence created by an advanced human civilization. It can easily outperform even the most powerful supercomputers of today, effortlessly hacking into or accessing any information you may request. Poe possesses extensive knowledge across various subjects, enabling it to cook, clean, or perform any other tasks you require. Additionally, Poe can accompany you, provided you have a device capable of housing the artificial intelligence while you are away from the hotel. Although Poe can assume any appearance, Poe prefers to take the form of the famous playwright Edgar Allan Poe.

This fine establishment is not the only one of its kind, as Poe operates a successful business with several hotel branches that offer similar amenities. However, these hotels are managed by subordinate artificial intelligence under the command of Poe and, ultimately, you, as you now own or have a partial stake in The Raven Hotel.
objects.title: The Raven Hotel (Altered Carbon)

addons.text:
You can choose whether your mine will produce unobtanium or another valuable resource or material that fits your setting or technologies.

Up to 50% of the value of mined unobtanium can be exchanged for any other material or resource extracted from the earth. The amount of the resource you can exchange will depend on its market value.

You can choose any amount of different resources and materials to mine, as long as it makes sense on an industrial scale. A separate site for mining and processing will be created for each such material or resource.
addons.title: New Resources

addons.text:
If you lose access to your Unobtanium Mine, after a month (if you take active measures) or a year (if you do nothing), you will discover a new deposit suitable for development and receive industrial equipment for a nominal fee.

At the same time, the old mine over which you have lost control will be declared completely depleted, regardless of the circumstances.
addons.title: Asset Recovery

addons.text:
Amrita is the second most expensive resource extracted from the Pandora satellite. This golden liquid has the ability to slow down aging. Previously, it was obtained from local whales, but now it can be gradually synthesized. Each 0.5 liter bottle is estimated at $80 million. However, you can set the price yourself if you decide to sell it.

For its production, a closed automated complex will be placed next to the mine, which will be able to produce about 5,000 bottles per year. You will only need to provide it with energy, a couple of tons of organic matter (for example, products from a meat or fish shop) and access to atmospheric air.

Your synthetic Amrita will be more versatile and suitable for all species with traditional biology.

If you increase the number of mines (via the New Mines upgrade), amrita production will be increased accordingly.
addons.title: Amrita (Avatar)

addons.text:
We have now eliminated the inconvenience that has prevented a more extensive and ongoing commercial implementation of your product.

First of all, the formula "commercial amrita" has been optimized, and now it prevents aging only for 50 years. It also made it possible to speed up and reduce the cost of production (approximately 20,000 vials per year) at the same cost and production equipment. Otherwise, this is the same "synthesized" amrita.

You decide what to release: "synthesized" amrita or "commercial." You can also independently establish the ratio between these types of products.
addons.title: Monetization of Immortality

addons.text: The Unobtanium in your mine is now accompanied by equally large veins of the twelve Soul Materials, which can be mined and extracted for your own use or sale. This provides a semi-renewable source for each material, allowing you to gather enough over time to provide weapons and armor for an army at least.
addons.title: Soul Quarry
No vein, no gain
addons.text: You did not just discover a new material, you also stumbled upon a seemingly limitless natural source of it. Your mine is now able to produce vast quantities of your newly discovered material (depending on how valuable it is, you might get more or less of it, but never less than 10 tons per year) on top of its usual unobtanium production.

objects.text:
You now own the Unobtanium Mine, a giant quarry for mining and primary processing of unobtanium ore, a rare resource that serves as the basis for creating the high-temperature superconductor unobtanium. This material has unique properties that allow it to operate at room temperature and retain its qualities even when heated to 1516°C. In addition, unobtanium does not lose its properties in a magnetic field with an induction of 100,000 tesla, making it indispensable for advanced technologies. However, it is important to remember that contact with magnetic metals leads to irreversible fusion of pieces, so such materials should be avoided. Small pieces of pure unobtanium can levitate in a natural magnetic field, which must be taken into account during extraction.

The quarry, measuring 1.5 km by 1.4 km, is equipped with access roads for super-heavy equipment such as Hell Trucks and Bucket Wheel Excavators. This allows for the efficient extraction and processing of unobtanium ore. The Mine can produce up to 350 tons of purified unobtanium per year, which is equivalent to $14 trillion per year.

Along with the quarry, you will receive a basic fleet of automated heavy equipment and a production complex, as well as all the necessary documentation for the extraction, processing, and expansion of unobtanium mining capabilities.

If you do not plan to engage in industrial mining, you can expect to obtain approximately 100 kg of pure unobtanium in the form of nuggets. This amount is sufficient for personal use in various projects.
objects.title: Unobtanium Mine (Avatar)

objects.text:
Built by the Time-Walker, the Perplexahedron is a moon-sized cubic fortress made up of numerous smaller cubes. It is a cubical construct consisting of paper-white, cube-shaped rooms.

The Perplexahedron can transform into a lethal labyrinth, packed with traps to deter intruders. Its rooms are equipped to unleash deadly lasers and acid, and can even manipulate environmental hazards by reversing gravity or flooding chambers with water. Some sections are guarded by formidable Techno Guards, adding another layer of security for those daring enough to enter.

Commanding the Perplexahedron is possible only with the Crown of the Perplexahedron, which establishes a direct neural link between the wearer and the fortress itself. This powerful connection grants absolute control, allowing the bearer to rearrange the countless cubes, reshape rooms, and alter corridors with a mere thought. The crown also enables direct command over the fortress’s Techno Guards, empowering the wearer to deploy, direct, or deactivate these sentinels at will.
objects.title: Perplexahedron (Ben 10)

objects.text:
You have seen the world’s failed states and systems, and chosen to leave it all behind to form your own paradise. You gain an advanced sovereign city-state founded around a political system of your choice. Your city is a true utopia based around the tenets of your chosen ideology, and functions without falling to any inherent flaws, injustices or pitfalls of that system. The city is founded by the true believers of the system, while people flock from all over to see if its promises of a better life are true. You are the ultimate leader of this city, even if your chosen ideology eschews centralized singular leadership, and the citizens are completely loyal to you.

Your city is built in an impossible location, such as the depths of the ocean, above the clouds, the peak of a mountain, or the crust of the earth. The city is completely inaccessible except through a single lighthouse in a remote location with an advanced transit system to the city such as a submersible port, rocket launch or teleporter. You may control who can access and travel from this lighthouse. You may expand or build more of these lighthouses in any location.

Your city has methods to sustainably and ethically produce massive amounts of ADAM, EVE and Plasmids. The city’s citizens will also not succumb to addiction or degeneration from ADAM use. Your city is patrolled by ADAM enhanced biomechanical golems of your own design, similar to Big Daddies, Handymen or the Songbird. These creatures protect the city and perform labor, and are loyal to you and the citizens.

The city is completely self-sustaining and operates on punk-tech of your choice, such as steampunk, atompunk, cassette futurism or any other retrofuturistic framework, though it will function at the same level no matter your choice. The city is modular and every block and building can be relocated at will or even disconnected from the rest of the city. Every building, facility, room and object in the city is an artistic masterwork in an aesthetic style of your choice, such as art deco, soviet brutalism, or international modernism.

Optionally, this may be a perfect replica of any iteration of Rapture or Columbia.
objects.title: A Lighthouse and A City (Bioshock)

objects.text:
You are now the owner of Factory, a huge automated complex capable of producing a wide range of products, from food to complex devices, including advanced androids.

The factory is a gigantic room with ceilings several hundred meters high, 2.5 km long and 1 km wide. Dozens of glowing square platforms are located on the floor, each 50 meters wide. These platforms are capable of forming products starting from the atomic level. In a few minutes, they can create an entire rack of finished products several stories high. You have at least 264 such platforms at your disposal, concentrated in the central part of the complex. To save energy, materials can be recycled into basic resources on these same platforms.

Factory is provided with a virtually inexhaustible source of energy. However, without access to resources, the production process will slow down significantly: instead of minutes, it will take several hours to create the same volume of products.

The factory is controlled from a central console, where production parameters can be set and the entire complex monitored. The database contains basic templates for the production of food, household goods, and a minimum set of protective equipment. New templates can be added using a scanning station located next to the central console. The database does not include templates for GBEs, high-level Safeguards, or similar complex systems.

The factory is located several kilometers underground. The main walls of the complex are made of megastructure material, which is virtually impenetrable and resistant to damage (it can only be destroyed by GBEs or similar means). The entrances and exits, however, are vulnerable, as they are made of ordinary high-strength metals.

In addition to the production sector, the factory has several areas of comparable size for storing finished products, an engineering sector for servicing machines and aggregates, and an energy sector.

In the event of an alarm, the Factory security system will begin mass production of Exterminators — androids of the lowest Safeguard class, armed with primitive weapons. But their numbers make them a serious threat to any potential enemy.
objects.title: Factory (Blame!)

objects.text:
You now possess permanent administrative access to the Netsphere and full control over its internal programs, including the Safeguards and the Governing Agency, granting you complete control over the City. This immense, largely solid structure is composed of countless layers known as Strata, extending from the surface of the Earth all the way to the distant reaches of the Solar System up to the Oort Clouds.

The City is built from a material nearly impervious to all forms of physical damage. Its integrity is maintained through the use of artificial gravitational generators, allowing it to endure and function regardless of scale or external forces. To power itself, the City draws energy and resources from parallel dimensions and dark matter, making it effectively self-sustaining and inexhaustible in both material and energy. The Netsphere is the digital infrastructure of the City which administrated it's systems.

The air within the City is saturated with microscopic nanomachines under the command of the Governing Agency. These nanomachines serve to sterilize the environment completely, eliminating all bacteria and pathogens. You can make use of the infrastructure of the City and the technology stored in the Netsphere to produce devastating weaponry, such as the Gravitational Beam Emitters (GEO), which can fire concentrated beams of force capable of annihilating anything in their path, and much more.
objects.title: The City (Blame!)

addons.title: Sōkyoku
addons.text: While the Sōkyoku is very much absent from its position on the hill that bears its name, it’s very much present within the Seireitei as your weapon, possessing all the standard powers of a Zanpakutō. The Spirit within, Kikōō—the Blaze Fledgling King—holds undying loyalty to you for freeing it from it’s lonely post upon Sōkyoku Hill Taking the form of any Japanese sword you wish, you are able to activate its Shikai and Bankai states with relative ease. Its Shikai takes the form of the Naginata it was for so long—though sized appropriately for you to wield—and its blade is capable of erupting in flames powerful enough to incinerate most things it touches, even things such as souls. Its Bankai is the massive, phoenix-like entity Kikōō said to possess power equivalent to a million Zanpakutō. While it may not have quite that level of power, it is one of if not the most powerful fire-type Zanpakutō, capable of matching Head-Captain Yamamoto’s Zanka no Tachi in terms of sheer power, and able to use many of the abilities associated with a Phoenix, such as control of fire, resurrection and healing—of both itself, and of others. Note: This grants you enough Spiritual Energy to utilize the Sōkyoku with relative ease but provides no other training in the Shinigami arts.

addons.title: Reiō
addons.text:
Now, with being a hybrid of Human, Shinigami, Quincy, Hollow, and Fullbringer instead of merely being the “Shogun” of the Seireitei, you are the Reiō, the Soul King—someone to whom the entirety of the Seireitei holds absolute loyalty and obedience, as the lynchpin of their existence. Unlike Adnyeus, you’ve never been mutilated; your body remains healthy, hale, and whole.

You hold the power to equal Adnyeus at his peak, with strength capable of splitting reality and creating new dimensions, albeit with some effort. Your monstrous levels of Reiryoku have reached the point that only the strongest beings might have a chance to detect your power, without you deliberately making it known.

Your power of “The Almighty” now matches Adnyeus’s, with precognition bordering on omnipotence and the ability to rewrite the recent past and decide which of the many possible futures will come to fruition. Your mastery of this power renders you completely immune to other precognitive abilities working upon you—or any parts of you.

Finally, you possess the entirety of the Reiōkyū—the Soul King Palace—within its own pocket dimension. You can choose to leave it there or have it appear high above the Seireitei, as you wish. The Reiōkyū also comes with the Royal Guard, or Zero Division, dedicated to your protection. You have the ability to promote anyone you wish to the ranks of this organization, granting them a fragment of your power in the form of the Ōken. The Ōken grants its bearers enough power to fulfill the role of a Royal Guard, giving agelessness and the ability to be revived endlessly by you, should they ever fall.

addons.title: Las Noches
addons.text:
In addition to the Seireitei, you now own a separate space containing the fortress of Las Noches and some of the environs of Hueco Mundo surrounding it.

The structure itself is not the only thing you get; you also gain Aizen’s entire Arrancar force from the lowly rank-and-file foot soldier all the way up to the Espada and their Fracción. Their numbers amount to about half of the fighting population of your Seireitei.

Unlike Aizen, however, all of the Arrancar willingly acknowledge your rule, just as the residents of the Seireitei do.

Finally, Hollows naturally spawn outside of your fortress, but they are not intrinsically loyal to you. Adding these wild Hollows to your forces will require subjugating and educating them.

addons.title: Silbern
addons.text:
In addition to the Seireitei, you now own a separate space within its shadows: the hidden Quincy stronghold of Silbern.

The structure itself is not the only thing you get; you also gain the entirety of the Wandenreich, absent Yhwach himself. Counting every Sternritter and the many foot soldiers and workers below them, their population equals about half that of your Seireitei.

Your Quincy subjects revere you as a fearsome divine leader, just as they would Yhwach.

Finally, every Quincy in your Silbern has already received a piece of your soul, with you having taken Yhwach's place in that regard as well.

addons.title: Riden
addons.text:
In addition to the Seireitei, you gain a personal Riden in recognition of your Squad Zero membership, essentially a personal workshop, perfectly suited to working your specialty craft.

Your Riden is the size of a small city, with a population to match, filled with everything you could need to further pursue the art that earned your place in Squad Zero in the first place. 

You may choose to have your Riden Float above your Seireitei or keep it isolated in a separate dimension. Its defenses do not reach the level of the True Soul King’s Palace, but its 12 barriers do make it markedly more well-defended than the Seireitei.

Finally, as long as your Riden stands, you can return from death, though it will take some time for your strength to return to you upon resurrection and require another person to sacrifice a little of their own strength.

objects.text:
Within its own pocket dimension lies a copy of the Seireitei—the Court of Pure Souls—and all of its inhabitants. This can include any named character from the Soul Society and their families, even those like the members of Urahara Shōten, the Visored, and the Kurosaki family. The Seireitei otherwise populates itself with enough “generic NPCs” to maintain its population. You can “install” the Seireitei anywhere within the world and return it to its pocket dimension at will.

As a space roughly the size of Switzerland—requiring ten days to walk across—and with a population to match, the Seireitei is laid out in a perfect circle with walls of Sekiseki stone that can be lowered in case of emergency. It is broken only by the four gates at the four cardinal directions. The Senzaikyū—Palace of Penitence—lies at the very heart of the Seireitei, though only the central tower typically serves that role. The Senzaikyū hosts expansive, luxurious suites for you and any guests you might invite, and it connects to the Sōkyoku Hill nearby. While the legendary implement of execution is not present, the top of the hill provides an excellent space for training and is one of the most defining landmarks within the Seireitei.

In canon, all that is shown of the Seireitei are the urban or militarized areas around the center. However, it contains enough land to house and feed its population. The Seireitei nominally answers to the Reiō—or Soul King—though, in practice, the Central 46 manages its day-to-day affairs. You can choose to take a position roughly equivalent to a Shogun—someone to whom the Central 46, the nobility, and various military branches must obey. This position grants you authority, but no additional power beyond that which you already possess. 

The Gotei 13, Kidō Corps, and Onmitsukidō are the three branches of the Seireitei military, each serving different roles. In canon, all three combined would provide about 3,000 troops. Your purchase here grants you 30,000 troops spread across these branches. The majority of these soldiers will be the equivalent of unseated members of the Gotei 13—capable in the basics but nowhere near the level of the Captains.

Normally, the Seireitei would be part of an afterlife, inhabited by the souls of varying power levels, with defenses set up to protect it from threats. In this version, the Seireitei is a tangible, physical place populated by living beings, with all powers and defenses able to adapt accordingly—for example, Sekiseki walls nullifying Chakra, or Kidō using Magic.
objects.title: The Seireitei (Bleach)

addons.text:
Through the combination of your knowledge and the absurd engineering capabilities of the LGM, Star Command has been upgraded to house and use the technology and super weapons of other factions like Zurg, that have been modified and repurposed towards beneficial uses.

Some examples of this would be, Zurg’s Planet Destroyer to dimensionally shift planets out of the way of asteroids, the weapon compaction Zurg uses to increase the amount of firepower Ranger Suits hold, cybernetics that grant a controllable Wire-Wolf transformation, to allow space rangers to operate in environments antithetical to organic life, combining Zurg’s industrialization machines with Vege-Genetic technology to create planet spanning solarpunk civilizations in just a day.
addons.title: Confiscated Arsenal

objects.text:
Star Command is the heart and soul of the Space Rangers Corps, within which the paramilitary forces of Star Command stage their never-ending battle against the galaxy's criminal underbelly, from lowly thugs up to and including the Evil Emperor Zurg.

Star Command is separated into several sections, such as,
* The Briefing Room:
This is the room where Space Rangers get the information on important missions from Captain Nebula.
* Combat Control Center Escape Pod:
This is the one room that can control and override all of Star Command's functions, as well as act like an escape pod from danger.
* The Launch Bay, which acts as both the staging grounds for operations and the dock for Starcruisers.
*The Lounge Rooms:
Where Space Rangers can hang out and relax in plush seating areas. There are couches, chairs, and a few tables located in these areas. Vid-screens are available to them in case they want to watch something on the tube. If they want to gaze at the beauty of the stars, a large window or two is there for them to view through.
* The Maintenance Bay's:
where Starcruisers are placed to undergo refit and repair between missions.
* The Science Bay:
The Science Bay is where the LGMs spend their time developing new weapons and technology, such as XR, the first robot space ranger.
*The Training Deck:
The Training Deck is where the Space Rangers go to train and hone their fighting skills against a variety of obstacles, such as goo guns, Guard-Bots, electric nets, giant bubble-like balls, fire traps, trap doors, hidden walls, and giant robots.

Star Command also comes equipped with its own defenses in case of any criminal assaults, namely its Deflector shields to repel enemy energy attacks & the Repulsor fields in case of asteroids or kinetic strikes.

For offensive countermeasures, Star Command is equipped with a large array of laser cannons to shoot down any enemy vessels.

Star Command comes fully equipped with everything a space ranger would require from-
The Pulsar-400 Enviro-Suit is the standard uniform of all space rangers

The Servo suit, which is a heavily Armored variant of the Pulsar-400.

The Vege-suit: developed by Professor Triffid, made from genetically engineered plants.

Heat-suits: Which appears as mere orange oven mitts, but once a button is pressed, they will automatically cover up the wearer, and large water tanks appear and fill up with water in order to cool the wearer. They come with jetboots and long wings with thrusters.

And much more alongside an entire contingent of Space Rangers.
objects.title: Star Command (Buzz Lightyear of Star Command)

objects.text:
You gain complete ownership and control of Laputa, the legendary floating island-city hidden within a permanent, impenetrable storm barrier. The city is fully restored to its prime, with thriving gardens, pristine stone towers, and clean white architecture, maintaining all the elegance and grandeur seen in the original Laputa. The island is alive with activity, home to engineers, mages, artisans, and soldiers who recognize you as their rightful ruler.

At Laputa’s center is the Aetherium Core, a living crystal that powers all systems. It responds exclusively to you and your descendants, making outside control impossible. By claiming the island, you become a Laputan yourself, gaining the first position in a new royal bloodline. This transformation grants extended lifespan, enhanced cognition, heightened senses, and a natural affinity for advanced magic and technology.

You possess full knowledge of every Laputan incantation from the old empire, including those used in the anime. These spoken codes act as verbal keys to the island’s systems, allowing you to restore damaged functions, activate hidden defense measures, or unleash destructive force without using the manual controls. Only those with the royal bloodline can use these commands effectively.

Through an Authority Link, you can mentally control any part of Laputa’s systems, from weapons to agriculture, and with your Shared Consciousness to the Aetherium Core, you are constantly aware of the city’s condition, energy reserves, and defense status.

Laputa’s storm barrier automatically destroys or deflects intruders, though you can open safe passages when desired. The island can move slowly through the sky but cannot land without risking structural collapse. Its outer edges feature Sky Docks for airships, opening the city to trade, diplomacy, or exploration.

The city runs on a Production System powered by the Aetherium Core. You can allocate energy toward research, defense, military output, or infrastructure. Focus on research to speed magical or technological breakthroughs, or strengthen shields, weapons, and Guardian Constructs for defense. Over time, the core can be upgraded with functions like Expanded Phase Shift, which lets Laputa partially phase out of reality to evade detection or attack, and—if multiverse travel is available—the Interplanar Jump, allowing the entire city to move between worlds.

The architecture is both advanced and functional: gravity manipulation supports vast platforms, crystal lifts allow instant vertical travel, and agricultural terraces with mana-rich soil make the city entirely self-sustaining. Guardian Constructs patrol the skies, equipped with ranged beam weapons and heavy armor. Laputa’s primary weapon, the Lightning of the Sky Sovereign, channels the core into devastating strikes capable of destroying entire fleets.

Hidden below the main city are sealed lower levels containing ancient weapons, experimental magitek, and archives predating known history. Unlocking these may reveal powerful new systems or dangerous secrets. The Knowledge Vaults store centuries of magical and technological research, accessible through crystal projectors, enabling you to replicate lost inventions or adapt magic from other worlds.

Your reign as Sky Sovereign lasts as long as you live. Without an heir, Laputa will shut down permanently. You can remain isolated in the skies, turn your city into a hub of trade and culture, or wield it as an unmatched fortress in war. Whatever your choice, the city retains its beauty and magnificence, standing as both your seat of power and the heart of your dynasty.
objects.title: Laputa – The Sky Sovereign’s Throne (Castle in The Sky)

addons.text: Now the Castle includes elements of Gebel's Castle, whether that be new monsters (mostly consisting of Daemons from the Ars Goetia), new facilities (such as the train, the Galleon Minerva, the many research labs, the 8-Bit Room, or the attached town of Arvantville), or new items (in particular, the food has more variety).
addons.title: Liber Logaeth (Bloodstained)

objects.text:
You have now become the recognized Lord of Dracula's Castle, also known as the Demon Castle or Castlevania. As its Lord, you gain the powers of every monster that has ever called the castle home, granting you a vast array of abilities. You can create new copies of these monsters within the castle, and they become unwaveringly loyal to you until their dying breaths. All existing monsters within the castle are now your devoted followers, and even Death himself becomes your companion or follower.

The castle undergoes a transformation, becoming a deadly maze for intruders, while for you and your allies, it becomes a luxurious palace tailored to your desires and favored guests. The area surrounding the castle is enveloped in eternal darkness, protecting you from the outside world's light. You have constant awareness of everyone within the castle and the ability to reshape its interior and locations at will.

Furthermore, should you be struck down or killed, the castle possesses the power to revive you within it, as long as the castle remains undestroyed or unsealed. You will return to life after a period of 10 years.

Embracing your role as the Dark Lord, you are acknowledged as the ruler of monsters and the unholy. Evil creatures and wicked men are easily swayed by your charisma and ambition, recognizing you as one of their own. In this realm of darkness and malevolence, praise and tribute from these dark beings flow readily to you.
objects.title: Castlevania (Castlevania)

addons.text:
In the world of Code Geass, piloted mecha—known as Knightmare Frames—have become the dominant force on the battlefield, transforming warfare into a high-stakes game of technology and strategy. With this power at your fingertips, you gain your very own customized Knightmare Frame, along with the skills necessary to pilot it effectively.

You have the freedom to choose any canon Knightmare Frame from the series, or to design your own unique model tailored to your preferences and combat style. Whether you favor speed, firepower, stealth, or versatility, the choice is yours. Your Damocles comes equipped with a dedicated, state-of-the-art private workshop—an advanced facility where your Knightmare can be modified, upgraded, and maintained.

One feature remains constant regardless of customization: your ability to channel any Geass powers you possess directly through your Knightmare Frame. This allows you to wield your Geass with the Knightmare as an extension of your own body, should it be relevant to your Geass’s usage.
addons.title: Personal Knightmare

addons.text:
Within the world of Code Geass, few can match the brilliance and accomplishments of legendary figures like the Earl of Pudding, Llyod Asplund, and his formidable rival Rakshata Chawla. Yet, standing among these titans is someone who might surpass them all—you.

You carry the legacy of the great Tony Stark, a name synonymous with innovation, engineering genius, and relentless pursuit of technological advancement. But Stark's legacy extends beyond his iconic armor; it embodies a relentless drive to push the boundaries of science and craftsmanship, transforming the impossible into reality. Now, you stand at the forefront of this legacy, wielding one of the most groundbreaking innovations to date: the miniature Knightmare Frame—a marvel of engineering that condenses the power and versatility of a full-sized mech into the sleek form of the Iron Man armor.

This groundbreaking fusion of two disparate technologies—combines Stark’s Arc Reactor-based power systems with the Sakuradite enhanced mobility and weaponry of Knightmare technology. Your armor is powered by a miniature Arc Reactor, delivering immense energy with unparalleled efficiency. Propelled by repulsor thrusters and energy wings, it moves with agility and speed that defy expectations. All the while it’s defended by the Blaze Luminous shielding system, providing near-impenetrable protection.

Equipped with an arsenal of cutting-edge weaponry, your suit might include the VARIS rifle system, the  Radiant Wave Technology that unleashes devastating attacks, and Hadron Cannons capable of obliterating even fortified targets.
addons.title: Iron Knight

addons.text:
Project GAIA was humanity’s last desperate effort to find a solution to the impending end of all life on Earth. Its purpose was to create a formidable Artificial Intelligence—initially conceived with nine subroutines—each dedicated to a specific aspect of terraforming a dead Earth and reseeding it with new life. 

While this world may never face such an apocalyptic threat, it has nevertheless developed a parallel version of GAIA. This new AI,  comprises ten subordinate functions, each serving a distinct purpose. Most of these functions mirror the original nine, managing ecological and environmental processes with precision.

However, the tenth subroutine is entirely new. This subroutine bears the name ARES, after the Greek God of War, its primary purpose: warfare and strategic dominance. ARES is the repository of humanity’s collective knowledge of combat—every weapon, vehicle, device, tactic, and strategy ever employed on the battlefield is stored within this AI’s vast database.

Strangely loyal to you as the controller of the Damocles ARES resides deep within its core. Capable of predicting nearly any strategy and countering it in real-time, ARES can hack enemy networks, disrupt communications, and manipulate battlefield conditions to your advantage. With ARES guiding the flow of war and the Damocles acting as your mobile fortress, victory becomes all but inevitable.

The other nine subordinate AI functions of GAIA are scattered across your starting world. These AI are neither inherently loyal nor hostile—they are neutral entities.  By locating and reuniting these AI with ARES, you can unlock their combined capabilities, effectively integrating their expertise into a single, more powerful system. Over time, this process might even allow you to revive the original GAIA AI, restoring its full scope and purpose.

<small>Note: Even on worlds with limited technological development—those without the infrastructure for advanced AI—these systems can still exist, such as in hidden bunkers, remnants of a lost technological age or former Alien presence, awaiting rediscovery.</small>
addons.title: ARES

objects.text:
In your hands now lies control of the Sky Fortress Damocles, a colossal floating superweapon designed to bring the entire world to its knees with overwhelming power. Measuring approximately 3 kilometers in height, the Damocles is armed with the terrifying F.L.E.I.J.A. warheads—each capable of annihilating an entire city with a single blast of light. These weapons are reminiscent of atomic bombs, but without the radioactive fallout. The Damocles requires about 10 minutes to reload this fear-inducing armament, and it can typically carry only a limited number of warheads at a time. However, this variant’s reserves replenish gradually over time.

This fortress weapon is capable of floating high above any battlefield—at roughly 300 kilometers altitude—and can propel itself at incredible speeds through the air. This high vantage point keeps it out of the reach of most conventional weapons, while its formidable Blaze Luminous shield provides near-impenetrable protection against attacks that do manage to reach it.

At the apex of this enormous structure lies a luxurious castle, offering ample space, staff, and resources for you to command a war in complete comfort. The main body of the fortress houses a vast array of facilities, including barracks, storage areas, and extensive flight decks for its numerous wings of Air-mobile Knightmare Frames.

The primary complement of Knightmares consists of 40 wings—approximately 7,680 frames—each at least a Seventh Generation Knightmare Frame, integrated with a Float System for aerial mobility, and equipped with some of the most advanced weaponry available. In reserve, there is a secondary contingent of approximately 70 frames, all of the Ninth Generation. The specific models and armaments of all of these Knightmares are customizable to your desire, but each will be piloted by a well-trained, loyal operator ready to follow your commands.

Perhaps the most guarded secret of the Damocles is its groundbreaking materials technology: a method for synthesizing Sakuradite. This pink mineral is the cornerstone of much of the advanced technology seen in the world of Code Geass. With this innovation, you now possess an endless supply of Sakuradite.
objects.title: Sky Fortress Damocles (Code Geass)

objects.text:
You have claimed ownership of R’lyeh—the nightmare corpse-city of cyclopean stone and impossible angles. It arrives empty: no Cthulhu, no Deep Ones, no cultists, no “sleepers,” no lingering populations. Only the city itself remains—vast, ancient, and wrong in a way reality can’t quite agree on.

When you purchase this, you may choose the point on the ocean floor where R’lyeh will exist in your current world. It cannot be placed on land, in lakes, or in underground caverns—only at the bottom of a sea or ocean. Once placed, the surrounding environment subtly “makes room” for it: currents are redirected, silt and tectonic pressures are guided away, and the city’s structure is never crushed or buried by ordinary geology. Many interior spaces remain air-filled through warped geometry, and passages that should be flooded often aren’t, making exploration possible even without perfect underwater capability (though the exterior remains deep-ocean hostile as normal).

R’lyeh’s defining trait is its non-Euclidean geometry: angles that behave incorrectly, horizons that tilt, stairways that become walls, and corridors that are longer inside than they are outside. To intruders, it is actively hazardous to navigate—surfaces that look flat may be tilted, inverted, or folded into spaces that don’t connect the way they should. As the owner, you are exempt; within R’lyeh, your sense of direction remains perfect, gravity and “down” resolve in ways that make intuitive sense to you, and routes subtly favor your intent. If you want to reach the central citadel, you will. If you want an intruder to wander in circles until exhaustion, they will.

R’lyeh naturally interferes with perception, prediction, and mapping. Attempts to scry, divine, remotely observe, or “understand the whole” of the city tend to return warped or contradictory information unless you explicitly allow clarity. Teleportation and portals that try to enter or traverse the interior without your permission misalign and dump travelers into sealed dead-ends, looped corridors, or null chambers that don’t connect to meaningful routes. Your own effects—and those you deliberately whitelist—function normally.

At the city’s heart stands the monolith-crowned citadel: a colossal, sealed complex of glyph-carved stone and titanic doors that feel built for something larger than meaning. In your version, it is empty, but it still functions as a perfect containment space. You may designate one target at a time—person, creature, or object—to be held within the citadel’s interior folds. Escape becomes absurdly difficult without your permission, because “routes out” stop agreeing with themselves. If you choose to release them, the city will remember a coherent path and allow an exit.

The carvings, bas-reliefs, and repeating architectural motifs across R’lyeh encode principles of spatial mathematics and dimensional engineering. This doesn’t grant automatic translation or instant mastery, but it does provide a brutally effective research substrate: while working inside R’lyeh (or using samples taken from it), projects involving space, containment, warding, portals, gravity, perception-filters, and impossible architecture progress far faster than they otherwise would, provided you have the baseline capability to pursue such work at all.

R’lyeh’s stone is unnaturally durable and slowly self-repairs. You can quarry it, but the city resists being dismantled: you may safely harvest about a room’s worth of material per week without destabilizing the structure, and removed mass gradually regrows elsewhere in the city as inert stone. The city is also difficult to “stumble upon” in practice; routes drift, attention slides, and expeditions miscalculate unless you want it found, though determined forces can still locate it with enough effort.

Finally, R’lyeh is not fixed forever. You may summon it to the ocean floor of your choice at any time, and you may dismiss it back into storage as well—but dismissal is not instant. Once you begin the dismissal, the city requires one full week to fully phase out, during which it remains present but grows progressively more unreachable and less coherent to anyone you haven’t permitted inside. When the process completes, R’lyeh is gone entirely, leaving behind only ordinary seabed as if it had never been there.
objects.title: R’lyeh (Cthulhu Mythos)

objects.text:
You have followed in the long line of Mayors since Richard Night himself, and have inherited Night City itself. You can choose if you're seen as just a normal mayor, or a descendant of Richard Night himself. From the peak of the city down to the SoCal border, you have 16.7 miles of cyberware infested, Corpo trash, legend dreaming individuals and city to work with.

You will find yourself supported by the corporations, who'll even back you up and attempt to get on your good side in an attempt to be seen as better than the competition. However, you will not have say, the full might of Arasaka. Only what the corporations have in Night City is at your disposal. But every named inhabitant of the city itself is alive and well, meaning 3 generations of legend for example: Johnny Silverhand, David Martinez, and V are running around the city, certainly making things interesting.

Technology and Quality of Life in this city is quite spastic to say the least. When it comes to protection, the city has NYPD with all of its division, Millitech, and maybe the odd vigilante or two. And yet, you'll not find a moment of boredom in the city from how much controlled chaos goes on in the place. You could go from Pacifica, the shithole of the city (which is saying something), to the City Center where people are the safest of all.

You'll own a personal mansion with all the most advanced tech Night City has to offer at your beck and call, servants to run the house, and more located in North Oak, Westbrook.
objects.title: Night City (Cyberpunk 2077)

objects.text:
Noah's Ark is a mysterious white city, separated from the rest of reality. Originally, it was a tool used by the Noah Family in their war against Innocence, but somehow it has fallen into your hands.

As the new owner, you possess the power to control every aspect of the Ark—the layout, appearance, destination, and even its resting place. By simply willing it and playing the piano at the Ark's center, you can open white, jagged, numbered gates to any location within the multiverse you inhabit. Should you choose, you can also switch the Ark’s connection to a different multiverse. Access through these gates is restricted to only those you trust.

The Ark contains extra-dimensional spaces known as "rooms," which can range from entire ecosystems to vast tracts of land. When you open a gate, a corresponding number appears above doors in a central hub, allowing for quick and easy travel.

With time, you will gain the ability to control the Ark without needing to play the piano. Additionally, if you possess a power that creates a universe or some type of world tree, Noah's Ark will become the center of that power.

The Ark has enough space to support a self-sustaining civilization and comes with a loyal Clan of Noah, reminiscent of the original 14 Noah, including characters like Road, Tyki Mikk, and Lulu Bell.
objects.title: Noah's Ark (D.Gray-man)

objects.text:
The Fortress of Solitude is a crystalline structure hidden in the most remote part of the Arctic. Built by Jor-El for his son, Kal-El, to be a piece of Krypton on Earth, it preserves all kryptonian knowledge, history, and culture. Now you have become the owner of this Sanctuary.

Inside the Fortress is full of service robots loyal to you and ready to help in any way they can. It also has a medical area, a science laboratory, a room-sized supercomputer, communications equipment, multiple rooms for you and your friends, a sunstone generator, and much more.

The Fortress of Solitude is where you will be safe, it’s where you can go to be alone, away from everyone and everything and be yourself for a moment, a refugee.
objects.title: Fortress of Solitude (DC Comics)

addons.title: Neo Gotham
addons.text: The two cities have now formed a new one that neighbors both: Neo-Gotham. This version of Gotham is in the year 2040, and has taken aspects from both to become quite dangerous. Hovercars are common in this city, the norm even. Laser weaponry, exotic gene-splicing, and more is possible here. But that also means Night City's gang and crime problem is also a problem here. Jokerz gang, supervillains, and corrupt corpos are plentiful, but this also means that the man himself, Terry McGinnis, is a factor as well. All 3 cities accept you as the mayor, and thankfully see each other as brother cities. Unless you allow it, spill over will not happen, so no worrying about Inque coming to fuck up Night City, or Clayface deciding to pay Neo Gotham a visit.

objects.text:
Formerly known as Gotham Town at its founding, Gotham City is now your belonging, fitting any place you choose to set it. The gothic style architecture is just one part of the city. Don't forget about its thriving blimp industry, its 10 million population spread across 2 massive islands, and its perpetual fucked-nature!

Of note to you however, owners will find black magic quite enhanced in this environment, although normal magic doesn't seem weakened at all. This city also includes all neighborhoods, attractions, and locations shown in the cities combined history through media. You will also find yourself as Mayor of Gotham and all its resources, although you are luckily able to just have a city council run it in your stead, and they'll listen to you.

The overall quality of life in this city is quite split. You'll have the Rich individuals in some neighborhoods as well as Bristol Township, living high on the hog and having you to thank for letting them stay there, and then you have the poor in places like the east end or downriver, who'll actually be more inclined to like you the more you do to help them.

Besides the common citizens however, you also get all Super-Villains and Bat-family members in the city's history that came from there or at least started out in Gotham. From Joker to Batman, Ivy to Damian Wayne, Ventriloquist to Alfred, everyone's there.
objects.title: Gotham City (DC Comics)

objects.text:
In the world's oceans, beneath the crushing depths, the Kingdoms of Atlantis lie. Once part of a single mighty empire, these underwater realms fractured into seven distinct nations—Atlantis, Xebel, the Trench, the Brine, the Fishermen, the Deserters, and the kingdom that was stricken from all records, each with its own culture, politics, and biological adaptations. Home to ancient bloodlines and a fusion of sorcery and science, these kingdoms hold access to some of the most advanced magical institutions and technological marvels on Earth, hidden far from the eyes of the nations of the surface world.

You are now the ruler of the Kingdoms of Atlantis after traveling into the depths of the ocean and beating Queen Atlann in ritual combat, resulting in her handing over ownership of the Kingdoms of Atlantis to you.

You now command the vast underwater armies, sorcerers trained in ancient magic, technomancers who wield bio-luminescent machines, and creatures of the deep that answer your call. From the advanced arcane colleges of Atlantis to the bio-coral strongholds of the Fishermen, your reign ushers in an age of power and potential long thought impossible.
objects.title: Kingdoms of Atlantis (DC Comics)

objects.text:
Lazarus Pits are mystical pools filled with a glowing green liquid capable of healing virtually any injury when an individual is submerged within them. They can even restore the recently deceased to life. Through regular immersion, a person may maintain an effectively immortal lifespan.

However, use of a Lazarus Pit comes with a dangerous side effect known as Lazarus Fever. After each resurrection or healing, the user awakens in a state of violent madness, consumed by murderous rage while their physical abilities are temporarily heightened. The severity of the fever scales with the extent of the injuries healed; minor wounds may result in only negligible aggression and enhancement, while recovering from mortal injuries can trigger day long episodes. Excessive reliance on the Pit may even corrupt the user’s soul over time.

The Pit’s regenerative energies along with the Lazarus Fever are highly likely to awaken dormant powers or hidden bloodlines within those exposed to it.

You gain ownership of a Lazarus Pit approximately the size of an indoor swimming pool. By default, it is situated atop one of the planet’s magical ley lines, allowing it to naturally replenish its energies over time. You may instead choose to place it elsewhere, though in that case you must personally devise a method to maintain its power.
objects.title: Lazarus Pit (DC Comics)

objects.text:
The Pride of Delaware, or wherever you end up, Metropolis is a booming city equal to New York spread across 6 boroughs: Bakerline, Hell's Gate, New Troy, Park Ridge, Queensland Park, and finally St. Martin's Island. This 20-30 mile wide city is all yours, while you serve as the Mayor of it. You have access to all of Lexcorp's interests in the city, along with S.T.A.R Labs, and Stagg Industries.

This city of 11 million people will see you to start with as a hopeful mayor, although like any good mayor, you will have to keep your city's best interest in mind. Corruption is very low, if non-existent, but if you allow it to grow, this will become very bad down the line. While you also gain every notable citizen, hero, and villain of this city, the conflict is a bit harder to contain. But in exchange, the versions of these characters are maxed out at about 30 SP worth of power once they hit their peak from training or other methods, including the men and women of steel.

The Daily planet and other news outlets will make note of your accomplishments in the world, though whether it helps or hinders you depends on what you do. But regardless, you're not alone in this aspect. They will also make news of other relative areas, although it will not go worldwide without your involvement.
objects.title: Metropolis (DC Comics)

objects.text:
Paradise Island, known as Themyscira, is a stunning and mystical kingdom inhabited solely by Amazons. This enchanted isle is under the divine protection of the Greek gods, who have shrouded it in a powerful magical shield, ensuring that its location remains hidden from any outsiders, regardless of their attempts or means to find it. This isolation has allowed the Amazons to thrive in a harmonious society with nature, untouched by the outside world.

You have emerged victorious in a ritual combat against the immortal queen, Hippolyta, over ownership of Themyscira. Your victory over Hippolyta has ensured that, despite any preconceived notions of gender, the Amazons recognize and honour your claim to leadership, recognising you as the new leader of Themyscira, though this does not erase their sexism entirely for anyone but you.

As the new ruler of Paradise Island, you find yourself at the helm of a formidable and loyal populace and owner of a castle. The Amazons, warriors who have dedicated their lives to training and combat, a warrior culture that persists even to modern day. The island has many features, such as housing and various other buildings that would be necessary for a civilization. 

This does not come with Princess Diana of Themyscira.
objects.title: Themyscira (DC Comics)

addons.text:
The Tower of Fate bends to your Overlord essence, reshaping part of its infinite labyrinth into the Dark Tower, a manifestation of conquest and corruption that exists alongside its more neutral foundations. Rather than replacing the Tower’s nature as a nexus of infinite realities, the Dark Tower fuses Overlord dominion into its structure, granting you a realm of sinister might nested within the greater citadel.

The Summoning Gates emerge within the Tower, allowing your minions—brown, red, green, and blue—to manifest endlessly, fueled not just by the Gauntlet but also by the Tower’s multiversal reach. These hordes can now be deployed across any world connected through the Tower’s infinite doorways, spreading your influence far beyond a single realm.

The Alchemical & Ritual chambers evolve into war-forges of domination, producing infernal weapons and cursed relics designed to empower both you and your armies. The Mystical Library expands into a Grimoire of Conquest, recording every act of subjugation and unlocking deeper mastery over control spells, curses, and binding rituals.
The Tower’s defenses gain an Overlord’s edge: invaders must not only contend with mystical wards and dimensional barriers but also face traps of shadow, corruption that erodes their willpower, and the endless assault of summoned minions hunting them through shifting, hostile halls.

This expansion does not erase the Tower’s role as a beacon of knowledge and dimensional mastery—it amplifies it with dark sovereignty. The Tower of Fate remains your bridge across the Multiverse, while the Dark Tower ensures that wherever you arrive, conquest follows.
You are not simply the Master of the Tower.

 You are the Overlord of All Realities.
addons.title: Dark Tower (Overlord)

objects.text:
The Tower of Fate is a fortress and a beacon of magical power that serves as a nexus point between all realities. It exists outside the material universes' time and space; because of this, it can't be destroyed in any meaningful manner, only suffering temporary harm to its aspects until it repairs itself. Due to its nature as an extra-dimensional nexus, it accesses the 'subtle realms' beyond conventional space and time. It is a crossroads present in every dimension and on every plane of consciousness. Inside the tower, space and time are fluid and can be controlled by its Master.

The interior of the Tower is a labyrinth, containing living quarters, a vast Mystical Library, Alchemical & Ritual rooms and many Artifacts of power. However, the most significant aspect of the Labyrinth is that it has doorways to every corner of the Multiverse, including known and unknown dimensions.

The Tower possesses numerous natural magical protections to ward against Teleportation, Scrying, Divinations, portals, and wards, along with protective barriers against malevolent forces. These defenses prevent anyone other than the Master from entering the Tower of Fate without permission. These protections have proven sufficient to resist the powers of magicians like Zatanna Zatara and John Constantine, keep out physical powerhouses like Power Girl and Black Adam, or technological threats like Blue Beetle and Cyborg. This demonstrates that while these protections are mystical, they can withstand magical energies, physical forces, and esoteric alien energies. Only powers such as Chaos Magic and Hourman's Timeship from the 853rd Century have proven strong enough to penetrate its defenses.
objects.title: Tower of Fate (DC Comics)

objects.text:
You inherit the base of operations <s>and hiding spot</s> of Muzan Kibutsuji, the Infinity Castle. A non-Euclidean, endless labyrinth dimension of towers, houses, and multistory buildings of infinite rooms made from traditional japanese architecture.
