addons.title: Heir of Beelzebub
addons.text:
You are the true child and heir of Raiden Ei, the Electro Archon Beelzebul, biologically, spiritually, and metaphysically. Through your mother, you are Half-Elemental and Half-Divine, inheriting Ei's elemental physiology and godly nature without replacing your other races, bloodlines, or inheritances. Your elemental half is intrinsically aligned with Electro.

Your Lightning Magic evolves with this heritage. You naturally generate and manipulate lightning, electricity, plasma, and Electro, gaining enormous reserves, control, resistance, and potential. You may partially become lightning and, with growth, assume a complete elemental state, travel as Electro, recover from devastating injuries through your elemental nature, and develop increasingly exotic applications. Being Half-Elemental does not limit your potential; you may eventually equal or surpass Ei.

As recognition of her heir, Ei personally creates Eien no Raimei — Eternal Thunder, a divine weapon made for you alone. Musou Isshin, Yamato, and Perfect Weapon are reforged into this entirely new armament and cease existing separately. Their qualities become parts of a masterpiece designed around your nature, powers, fighting style, and potential.

Its natural forms are a divine katana and naginata, reflecting Ei's own martial disciplines, though its Perfect Weapon nature allows it to instantly assume any weapon form suited to you. It is soulbound, may reside within your heart or soul, can be summoned across dimensions, restores itself if destroyed, and cannot be permanently stolen, sealed, corrupted, or turned against you. It continually grows alongside you.

Eien no Raimei perfectly channels Electro and your other powers. Its katana embodies Ei's supreme swordsmanship and grants your own evolving Musou no Hitotachi, a transcendent strike capable of overwhelming defenses, slaying powerful beings, and cleaving vast terrain. Rather than merely copying Ei, the technique incorporates your powers and fighting style until it becomes uniquely yours.

Its naginata embodies Ei's mastery of polearm combat, allowing your elemental power and techniques to be expressed just as naturally through sweeping strikes, thrusts, and flowing combinations as through the blade. Both primary forms possess the full capabilities of Eien no Raimei rather than functioning as separate weapons.

Yamato's principle of separation has become part of Eien no Raimei's edge. You can cut space, collapse distance, create portals, cross dimensional boundaries, and sever spatial barriers. With sufficient power and understanding, this principle may extend to supernatural effects, energies, bindings, connections, and eventually abstract or metaphysical divisions.

Within Eien no Raimei exists a personal spiritual realm comparable to Ei's Plane of Euthymia, shaped by your mind, soul, memories, and powers. You may enter it, bring others inside, exclude intruders, or withdraw your spirit there while observing reality through your weapon. This realm evolves alongside you.

Any unique weapon created or bestowed upon you by another parent through a Child, Heir, or similar addon may merge with your Perfect Weapon as a distinct alternate form. Each retains its appearance, abilities, symbolism, history, and parental connection, while compatible properties may synergize across the whole. Nothing is weakened, erased, or overwritten. Thus the Endless Relic, for example, may become another form while remaining unmistakably Death's gift to you.

As you grow, Eien no Raimei grows. New abilities and expressions awaken alongside your developing elemental nature and mastery, ensuring that even should you eventually surpass Ei herself, your mother's gift will remain worthy of her heir.

You are the Heir of Beelzebul, and Eien no Raimei will grow alongside you for eternity.

Note: If you Have Raiden Ei (Raiden Shogun) either through selecting her as a Companion or Through Archons Descent, then you are the Child of That Raiden Ei. If you Also have Inazuma then it becomes the inazuma of either raiden Ei, instead of her just claiming some random territory.

objects.title: Trilune God(dess) (Genshin Impact)
objects.text: You are not merely a Moonborn Deity. As the physical embodiment of a Moon condensed into a living form, you have instead ascended to become the Trilune God(dess), an existence on par with a Dragon Sovereign and possessing the power and Authority of all three of Teyvat's Moons. You possess Authority over the Moon itself and Kuuvahki, the pure and undiluted energy of the Light Realm, although this does not extend to the diluted elemental energies derived from it. More importantly, you wield the combined Trilune Authority of the Frost Moon, Eternal Moon, and Iridescent Moon. The Three Moons were originally created to oversee Teyvat and govern its fundamental Laws in the absence of its original Ruler, their collective Authority combining and encompassing Reason, Life, Death, Time, and Space. While that Authority was originally willingly divided between the Three Moons and therefore diluted, you wield their combined Authority as a single existence, allowing you to directly influence and control the Laws of the World. The exact limits of these abilities depend on your understanding and mastery of the Authority, as well as whether another existence already possesses superior Authority over the same domain. Additionally, as you have only recently ascended and have yet to master this immense power, do not expect to immediately reproduce the feats of the Shades of the Heavenly Principles, much less rival the Heavenly Principles themselves. Your Authority will grow as you learn to wield it, but beings who already possess established Authority over these domains can contest or restrict your influence.

objects.title: H.A.C.R
objects.text: The H.A.C.R, or Highly Advanced Country of Research, is now under your rule. All of your inhabitants now not only have your powers and the chance to develop further than you, some now have a "Paying" job in the form of H.A.C.R R&D Division! Instead of just 900 scientists and workers, you have over 120,000 in each job, for a total of 360,000 people in the total division. Any tech or tinker power, upgrade, or addon you have can now be utilized by them for massive projects unheard of. Find the cure to cancer in 20 minutes, solve world hunger in 20 days, and colonize other planets in 20 weeks. In Marvel, your whole division could devise Anti-Sentinel equipment given enough research, or figure out a legal way to remove Victor von Doom from power. Build sun-sized robots in DC to fight off Darkseids forces. Or even make Multiversal scouters in Dragon Ball, able to even detect god ki and anyone within the universe you so choose. Anyone who joins your country will find the same benefits as Unchained Village, with those who joined the R&D division being given a fraction of their collected knowledge.

objects.title: Gaia's Expanse
objects.text:
Gaia’s Expanse is a near-infinite, self-sustaining dimension existing entirely under your ownership and transformed into the ultimate source of natural resources. Rather than being divided into artificial zones or bubbles, it is one continuous living world of countless continents, oceans, islands, mountain ranges, forests, jungles, deserts, tundras, grasslands, wetlands, caverns, reefs, volcanic regions, subterranean environments, and stranger biomes, all naturally connected into a single immense wilderness.

Every biome and ecosystem found within your current world or any setting represented by a power, perk, ability, race, technology, magic, item, companion, or other option you possess exists somewhere within the Expanse. Their animals, monsters, plants, trees, fungi, microorganisms, and other lifeforms inhabit suitable environments, including extinct, alien, magical, supernatural, and mythical species. Different ecosystems coexist in perfect natural harmony, preventing invasive species, disease, predators, or ecological disruption from permanently destroying another species or environment.

The Expanse likewise contains every naturally obtainable resource known within those settings. Metals, ores, minerals, gemstones, crystals, fuels, gases, liquids, exotic matter, magical materials, supernatural substances, woods, herbs, useful plants, alchemical reagents, biological materials, Unobtanium, and countless other raw resources can all be found naturally throughout suitable environments.

Resource abundance automatically adapts to your capabilities. Whenever technology, magic, crafting, construction, industry, or other knowledge available to you requires particular materials, the Expanse develops enough veins, deposits, forests, plant populations, ecosystems, or other sources to support that capability at the scale available to you. Technology requiring civilization-scale quantities receives civilization-scale reserves rather than token deposits. Acquiring something from a new setting automatically introduces that setting’s resources and ecosystems into the Expanse.

Everything remains renewable. Animals reproduce, forests regrow, vegetation flourishes, ecosystems recover, and even exhausted mineral deposits gradually reform through the dimension’s accelerated natural processes. Resources can be harvested, hunted, cultivated, mined, and removed freely without permanently exhausting the Expanse. Its lifeforms remain exceptionally healthy and free from unwanted diseases, parasites, mutations, and other afflictions unless you intentionally permit them.

Despite this harmony, the Expanse remains a genuine wilderness. Predators hunt, prey flee, seasons change, plants compete, storms form, creatures reproduce, and ecosystems behave naturally. Its protections preserve ecological balance rather than removing nature itself. Dangerous creatures remain dangerous, allowing its wilderness to serve as hunting grounds as readily as it serves as a source of natural wealth.

Near the primary entrance stands a large self-sufficient settlement waiting for you and your people. It contains homes, warehouses, workshops, storage, utilities, roads, processing facilities, and the infrastructure needed to begin exploring, harvesting, mining, and settling the Expanse. Its inhabitants may establish farms, ranches, gardens, orchards, and other forms of cultivation wherever suitable. The settlement expands alongside its population and may incorporate whatever technology or magic you make available to it.

The Expanse can be developed without sacrificing its fundamental nature. Technologies, magic, automation, agriculture, mining methods, terraforming, resource processing, transportation, dimensional engineering, and other compatible advancements you possess may be introduced without disrupting its ecosystems, renewability, or abundance. You decide how much of the Expanse remains untouched wilderness and how much is opened to settlement and industry.

You may attach the Expanse’s primary entrance to any location you choose, including a home, fortress, planet, spacecraft, megastructure, Star Sovereign, or another suitable location. Additional entrances may be established through Dimensional Dominion. You always know who is within the Expanse and where they are, and unauthorized access may be denied according to permissions you establish.

The Expanse continuously expands whenever additional space, ecosystems, or resources are required. As you encounter new worlds and acquire powers or possessions from new settings, new horizons, species, biomes, and resources seamlessly emerge within it. No matter how large your civilization becomes or how advanced its technology grows, Gaia’s Expanse remains its boundless frontier: a living world containing the natural wealth needed to sustain everything you possess.

objects.title: Master of the Hunt
objects.text:
Now you are mighty even among Fae Lords, a Master of a Wild Hunt. 

Once every three months you may call to you your dogs, a great many lesser Fae, spirits of the dead, and possibly even other Fae nobles or gods; and lead a flying procession across the sky to hunt any one major target that you desire. 

During this hunt you and your followers will be capable of flying, immune to the negative effects of iron and most other weaknesses, have heightened physical ability and resilience far greater than normal, and will be incapable of tiring, growing bored, or losing concentration.

You will also be capable of controlling the storm created by your party. It is best suited to being used to destroy obstacles in your procession’s path or devastate the landscape you pass over. You may also cause supernatural fear and awe in those who see or hear your procession. 

Finally, you may abduct mortals, living or ghost, and compel them to join the ranks of your hunters which they will return to every time you call a hunt thereafter except if you explicitly grant them their freedom.

However, there are some restrictions upon this ability. 

Due to the massive amount of magical power required to launch and maintain the hunt, and the near frenzied emotional state it inflicts on its participants; you and your followers will be incapable of using any complex magic or abilities during the hunt. 

Further, after a hunt you shall be drained of power and extremely vulnerable for a period of at least three days (this is for a hunt lasting a single night, every hour longer doubles this time); where you will only be capable of only your weakest spells and illusions. This is the payment for being near unstoppable during your procession. 

Finally, there are several laws you must follow during the hunt: 

You are incapable of entering an individual’s dwelling or another’s sacred places without an invitation (although only their protective magic and/or the strength of the construction stops you from tearing the location apart with your storm). 

You may not take or target any being who stands in the centre of an ancient (500 years or more of continuous use) road, and may not at any point cease hunting your quarry while the magic is active (except for practical matters like re-shoeing your horses or asking directions, and even then not for long). 

You must reward any assistance rendered to your hunt handsomely with a gift of some kind (traditionally this could be a large pouch of gold, jewels, or silver; a boon; a blessing; part of the quarry; or similar), and the same to any quarry who evades you in your hunt.
Opens General Missions selection.
objects.title: General Missions

objects.text: Opens Worm Missions selection.
objects.title: Worm Missions

objects.text: Opens Alternate Earth Missions selection.
objects.title: Alternate Earth Missions

rows.title: Missions
rows.titleText:
Are you willing to take on missions in exchange for rewards? But there is a danger of failure and a punishment if you fail, so think long and carefully before you choose.

Some of these missions have a set starting date, but due to your unique circumstances, you may sometimes arrive far earlier or much later than required. If you arrive long before the mission is supposed to start, then the situation that leads to the mission will still arise, unless you intentionally try to prevent it from happening, in which case you will get neither the reward for completion nor the punishment for failure. If, however, you arrive much later than required, then by the point of your arrival, the events of the mission would have played out, leaving you to deal with the consequences this brought upon the world. For example, if the mission was to prevent a zombie outbreak, you would most likely arrive in the middle of a zombie apocalypse. The exception to this is punishments targeting you specifically, such as enmity of a certain person or a group. As you were not present in the world when the events of a mission happened, those will not affect you.

Upon your entry into the world, you will become aware of the status of each mission you chose.

objects.text:
Your mission is to create a nation where the primary population is Parahumans.

To succeed at this mission, at least 51 percent of your country's population needs to be Parahuman, and your country needs to be recognized by a UN Security Council member. For the purposes of this mission anyone with abilities above baseline human counts as Parahuman, so go wild with Great Teacher and Awakener.

Failure consists of your country ceasing to be, becoming a failed state (think IRL Somalia), or having the Parahuman population hate you enough that if there were hypothetical statues of you, most people would want them torn down (note that it doesn't matter what the baseline human population thinks of you).

If you fail, all Parahumans become treated like Mutants are in Marvel, actively discriminated against. If you pick the AU option that does the same thing, it gets all "Days of Future Past" and NATO Co-Opts Dragon, using her to build robotic hunter killer drones, capturing or killing non-PRT registered Parahumans.

If you succeed in this mission, you secure the eternal love and loyalty of your people (of course), as well as all Parahuman citizens (including you if you don’t have them already), getting the perks Olympic, Frankenstein, & Negentropy for free.
objects.title: Genosha

objects.text:
You must either find or create a city, town, or village and make it into a near-paradise where crime rates are extremely low, people can be kind and good to each other, people do not have to worry about where the next meal will come from or if they can afford to go to the doctor, and so on. Without mind control or drugs keeping the population happy.

If you fail in creating your little slice of paradise, people will either get the idea that you possess a potent and nearly undetectable master power that allows you to convince people who are unaware of it, or if you possess a master power that works on humans, people will become aware of it and how it functions, and they will gain resistance to it. Alongside this, you will be given either a kill order or be sentenced to the birdcage, depending on how useful and powerful your powers are.

And if you are successful in creating your little slice of paradise—if you make a paradise village—then you will be able to remove the negative effects of one of the lesser permanent non-entity drawbacks. If you make Paradise Town, then you will be able to remove the negative effects of one of the medium permanent non-entity drawbacks, and if you make Paradise City, you can remove one of the permanent non-entity drawbacks.
objects.title: A Little Slice of Paradise

objects.text:
Somewhere in your local multiverse cluster (including any Alternate Earths you select) is a huge cache of treasure containing every Object of Power of 15 SP or less, as well as numerous copies of every item from the Items section, and enough treasure that you effectively gain the "Wealthy" perk. However, finding it won't be easy, as you are only given a map leading to the first clue, and it's warded against everything but solving the clues & completing the challenges legitimately, so scrying, brute forcing the search with super speed, and other obvious "cheats" are not permitted.

If someone learns of the treasure or the clues, they can enter the treasure vault by solving the clues just like you, so be careful about who you tell. If you have any of the "Wanted" drawbacks the organizations you picked will automatically learn the first clue a month after you arrive.
objects.title: Gol D. Roger

objects.text:
Space. The final Frontier. Until YOU, that is.

Your mission is to make humanity an interstellar civilization. To achieve this, humanity must have at least a million people living on all planets (and yes this includes Pluto) or habitats in the solar system, and at least a hundred thousand each in ten different star systems. Those settlements have to be completely self-sufficient, so you can't just plop people there. Additionally, humanity has to be capable to further expand on their own, without relying on your powers to do so.

You have a century to achive this. If you fail, either by taking to long or if society is unable to take off on its own, humanity will never leave Earth. A meteor will collide with the moon, destroying it, and creating a Kepler syndrome that will lock humanity for millenia, if they don't die before due to the constant meteor showers or the new Ice age caused by the dust.

If you do succeed, humanity will prosper. The resources from space will transform Earth in a Utopia, and the same standard will be available to everyone else out of Earth. Scarcity will become a thing of the past, wars will become a distant memory, and humanity will thrive forever. On the personal side, you become immortal: so long as humanity exists, you will live in your prime. Should your body perish for any reason, you can return in full health in any human settlement you wish. You can also teleport to any human community bigger than 50 people.
objects.title: The Final Frontier - SPAAACE!

objects.text:
In the world you're entering, the only thing that matters is cold, hard, cash. Well, that's not entirely true; illiquid assets contribute to your net worth too!

Your goal is to become either the largest net worth person in your new world, or to be majority shareholder of the largest company by market cap, presumably (but not necessarily) by founding and running it yourself. Your reward for doing so is not only being the richest person in the world, but a consequence free version of the Shardless Esoteric power "Golden One" & access to the markets from Multiversal Marketplace & Celestial Market (World Seed Jump - Anon303) if you didn't have that already.

You fail if you or the company go bankrupt and are unable to restructure in a way that is profitable. The punishment is indentured servitude to whoever buys a majority of your assets, for 1 year for every outstanding million dollars in debt (if your world does not use dollars or a close equivalent in PPP value like eurodollars or nuyen, an exchange rate guide from the Multiverse Marketplace will be provided).
objects.title: Overvalued

objects.text:
You must confront and defeat the strongest being in your world. This being must not just be a powerful adversary, but a figure revered and feared by all, embodying the pinnacle of strength, wisdom, or influence.

If you fail, the consequences are severe. Your defeat will not be a private affair; it will be a public spectacle, with your humiliation laid bare for all to see. The world will know of your failure, and it will become a stain on your name, a mark of disgrace that could follow you for the rest of your life and even beyond.

However, if you succeed in defeating this being and earning their acknowledgment, your victory will echo across the land, drawing many to your cause—warriors, scholars, and leaders alike. These followers will join you not out of obligation, but out of a deep-seated respect and admiration. Their loyalty will be unwavering, absolute, and they will follow you into any battle, any challenge, without question.

Beyond the loyalty of your new allies, triumph brings another reward: the opportunity to enhance your powers. You will be granted the chance to either add a new ability to your repertoire or to remove a restriction that has previously hindered you.
objects.title: To Be The Strongest

objects.text:
"I know nought poorer
Under the sun, than ye gods!
Ye nourish painfully,
With sacrifices
And votive prayers,
Your majesty;
Ye would e'en starve,
If children and beggars
Were not trusting fools."
-Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Prometheus

For whatever reason, you have decided that that some so-called divine being in the universe you're being sent to is not worthy of the title. This can be a relatively minor deity or the chief deity of the setting, it's really up to you. In fact, the being in question doesn't need to be strictly a god; godlike beings like Scion, the C'tan, or Galactus count.

To rectify this you have decided either to strip them of their powers or commit deicide. If you succeed, you gain their former power. The punishment for failing is really just a natural consequence of the challenge itself; as far as punishments go it's hard to top the ire of a god!
objects.title: One More God Rejected

objects.text:
Ah. Very unfortunately it seems some people have been informed of your arrival. If that wasn’t bad enough, it seems they all work for the entertainment industry. 

To succeed in this mission, you must avoid your Media archive being detected by the entertainment industry for several years. They have been given knowledge you exist, and a general location but little else. They will be actively searching for your collection in order to convict you of para-piracy. 

If you succeed, your media library will constantly update with whatever is made in your home universe over time rather than a snapshot of what exists upon entry. In addition, if you have Homecoming it will contain all the media of each world you have access to. 

If you fail then the titans of the media industry will never stop hounding you with Cease and Desists, legal suits both fraudulent and real, and on occasion physical threats from organisations like the pinkertons. In addition, the sense of security this has given them will result in the vast majority of newly released media being of substantially lower quality than before your entry.
objects.title: Remember Limewire?

objects.text:
Your powers—whether magical or genetic—are not yours alone; they are remnants of an age long forgotten, rooted in an empire lost to history. In your world, ancient ruins and legends connected to this fallen empire will exist, holding the key to unlocking the full potential of your abilities. Your mission is to seek out these remnants, uncover their secrets, and learn from the wisdom they offer.

However, you are not alone in this pursuit. Others may have already stumbled upon these ruins. While they cannot harness its power as fully as you can, these discoveries may still influence their abilities and choices. If you fail to locate the ruins, your enemies will find it, using these secrets to strengthen themselves and oppose you.

Each ruin you uncover and learn from will reward you with 5 SP worth of new powers that build upon your existing abilities, or you may choose to remove some of the limitations your powers currently have. 

Note: This will mean that your abilities will carry connotation within specific circles.
objects.title: Seeker of Lost Things

addons.text:
In this Sacred Relic War, you are not the Master—you are the Servant. Instead of summoning a legendary spirit to fight by your side, you are the one who has been summoned, bound to a Master through a magical contract. Your mission remains the same: win the war, claim the Relic, and secure your wish. However, the path to victory is now shaped by both unique advantages and harsh limitations.

Unlike most servants, you possibly have no legend or history, meaning you get no benefits from your current state. You are sustained by magical energy, or what ever local equivalent there is, provided by your Master and if your Master dies, you will begin to fade unless you secure a new Master or find an alternative source of mana. The magical contract provides your Master with only three absolute commands—irresistible orders that can force you to act against your will. Once these commands are used, they cannot be replenished. If you find the need for it, you can manipulate, betray, or even kill your Master, as long as you are prepared to deal with the consequences—whether securing a new Master or finding another way to sustain yourself.

However, failure has a price beyond death. If you lose the war, you are not gone forever. Instead, you will be unsummoned, pulled back into the void, forced into a state of limbo until the next Sacred Relic War begins. When the next war starts—be it years, decades, or even centuries later—you will be summoned again, bound to a new Master, and forced to fight once more. This cycle will repeat endlessly until you win.

If you succeed, your reward is the same as any Master: the Relic will grant your deepest wish. But as a Servant, you gain an additional prize—you will remain in the world permanently, no longer bound by the cycle of summoning and dismissal. You will become a Living Servant, free from the constraints of magical contracts or Masters.
addons.title: The Servant’s War

addons.text:
When you enter the Type-Moon world, your mission shifts—you are now a participant in the Holy Grail War, a secret conflict fought in the shadows of history. Seven Masters, chosen by fate and marked with Command Seals, summon legendary Servants to battle for the ultimate prize: the Holy Grail, a vessel capable of granting any wish without limitation. You are one of these Masters, bound to this war whether by choice or circumstance, and your objective is simple—win the war, claim the Grail, and secure your wish.

However, if a Holy Grail War is already in progress when you arrive, the ritual reacts to your presence, altering the structure of the conflict itself. The war will escalate into a Great Holy Grail War, expanding beyond its original scope. Instead of seven Masters and seven Servants fighting in a chaotic free-for-all, the participants will be divided into two opposing factions, each with seven Masters and seven Servants. The Grail will summon an additional Servant of the Ruler class, tasked with maintaining order, enforcing the war’s rules, and ensuring that the conflict adheres to the Grail’s sacred laws. The nature of battle changes as well; alliances are no longer temporary conveniences but formalized structures, with coordinated strategies, factional politics, and large-scale engagements replacing isolated duels.

If you arrive in a world where a Great Holy Grail War is already underway, the ritual’s influence intensifies even further. The conflict will double in size, transforming into an unprecedented war with twenty-four Masters and twenty-four Servants, divided into four distinct factions. At least two Ruler-class Servants will be summoned to manage the overwhelming scope of the war, though even their authority may struggle to contain the chaos.

The rewards for success and costs of failure is the same.
addons.title: The Holy Grail War

objects.text:
A deadly conflict has erupted in your world—an event known as the War for the Sacred Relic. Whether it’s called the Holy Grail, the Godforge, the Eternal Nexus, or any artifact of similar power, its purpose remains the same: it grants a single wish without limitation. Its appearance triggers an ancient ritual, summoning seven Servants, legendary spirits of heroes, kings, and warriors from across history, myth, or forgotten ages. These Servants are bound to seven Masters—individuals like you, chosen to participate in this brutal war. Your mission is simple: eliminate all rival Masters and Servants, survive until the end, and claim the Relic for yourself. Servants will require a constant upkeep in energy to remain, with the energy being dependent on the world you are in. For example, they will need Chakra in Naruto, or Nen in HxH.

Should you fall in battle or lose your Servant, your chance at the Relic vanishes forever. Your Servant will either be destroyed in combat or forcibly unsummoned, severing the bond you shared. The Master and Servant who seize victory will gain unimaginable power. The winning Servant will remain in the world indefinitely, becoming a living servant. The victors will view you as a lingering threat and will choose to hunt you down even after the war ends, eliminating any loose ends.

If you and your Servant triumph, the Sacred Relic will grant your deepest wish, without restriction—whether it’s boundless wealth, eternal life, resurrecting the dead, reshaping reality, or even altering the fundamental laws of the universe. Your Servant will not fade away after the ritual concludes; instead, they will remain by your side, not just as a summoned spirit, but as a living servant. They will also remain loyal to you even after the end of the war.
objects.title: The War for the Sacred Relic

objects.text:
You’ve received a new job, You have to hunt and kill monsters and threats. Any creature that poses a sufficient threat to life and limb counts for the purposes of this mission, ranging from mundane serial killers to eldritch gods. You’ll receive a ‘quota’ of beings you have to kill each month, with this quota able to be filled by multiple smaller entities or singular large ones, with larger ones contributing to future months, potentially allowing you to skip entire years if your quarry was great enough. 

Should you succeed in keeping your Quota fed for five years, you will gain a random ability from each entity you killed, and from this point will similarly gain one from each entity you kill. These are guaranteed not to harm you. 

Should you fail in keeping your quota, or fail to deliver two months in a row, the number of qualifying entities for this mission will triple, and grow more aggressive and indiscriminate in their attacks.
objects.title: Rip and Tear

objects.text:
Your arrival in this world had inevitably screwed with the natural order, and now, you are tasked to make sure it isn't screwed any further.

There is one event in canon (or in non fandom based worlds, just a specific moment) that should not be changed. You have to do whatever you can to make sure whatever this event is stays the same. Whether it be making sure a specific couple would get together, or making sure one unlucky person dies, you have to make sure nothing makes that event diverge from its path.

You will instinctively know what this event would be. And you are guaranteed to at least be able to witness it occuring (so it won't be an event that you need to fly to a different country for for example). Something is also guaranteed to cause this event to not happen unless you interfere.

Failure to maintain this canon event will result in some sort of large scale tragedy that will befall the place you are on soon. Whether it be some sort of natural disaster or a bomb gets dropped, you have no clue, just that something bad is going to happen.

Succeeding however, will give you access to a private Wiki that only you are able to read somehow, unless you want others to. This Wiki will manifest as a private app or some other technologically fitting form (like a book in places without modern gadgets for example). This Wiki could be a more accurate wiki of the fanbase your world is based on, or if it's not from a different media, appears like it is updating knowledge about the world that might be useful to you. Like listing down key figures as characters or giving outright confidential information to you. Knowledge is power and you basically gained a cheat sheet.
objects.title: Canon Keeper

objects.text:
When you enter, you will be split into a number of separate selves placed in different places within your setting determined by the amount of times you select this mission. Each of you have the same memories up to your entry but are completely independent beings and unable to communicate without outside help. Each self gains a portion of the build you have created, either the whole build made proportionately weaker or divided pieces along them (ie a 100sp build divided among 5 selves would be 20sp each). Drawbacks however are shared between all of you equally where applicable.

If you manage to locate your other selves and touch, you’ll all gain a version of your complete build at its full strength. Additionally, you’ll gain an inherent psychic link between all of your selves, allowing you to communicate and confer across any distance.

If one of you dies before you are able to recombine (and has no way of circumventing death) the parts of your build that were attached to them are lost forever, though you can still combine with the remaining bodies (though proportionally weaker in total).
objects.title: The Division

objects.text:
In our modern day, they say Chivalry is dead. Well, in your case, you're about to show them the most lively chivalry they've ever seen. In any world you go to, you are required to save 10 important individuals of influence.

Whether this be political, fate, or whatever else, you must save them from a dangerous end. This can range from saving a princess from a dragon to rescuing a CEO from a hostage crisis or a sci-fi planet's president from planetary bombardment.

If you fail, you will be considered a heartless monster, aligned with evil. People will hunt you and make sure you suffer for your crime of non-interference.

If you succeed, each of the 10 people you save will always come to your help in some way. In Naruto, if you were to save Konan, for example, she would gladly teach you her paper jutsu while working with you. Alternatively, a king might be willing to give you access to any of their kingdom’s knights, armory, or other resources.
objects.title: Knight in Shining Armor

objects.text:
In every universe, there is a "Jon" and a "Garfield". You are the Jon of this universe, and you are fated to deal with a monster, a Garfield, that's out to get you. Every Garfield is defeatable though with varying powers, and every Garfield shall give you a gift when defeated. Which Garfield you get depends on the Zodiac Sign, with you getting an extra Cusp if born between two signs (Don't worry, Cusps are more a nuisance).

Some of the loot these Garfields give are are:

Aries gives you Dreamcatcher that gives you pleasant dreams upon.

Taurus gives you a Bookmark that if placed on a book, makes you instantly memorize it after 3 days.

Gemini gives you access to a Clone that you can generate once a day and lasts for only a day, willing to follow your every command.

Cancer gives you a Golden Claw that gives you a random skill you can master instantly every day. You will know what that skill is.

Leo gives you a Necroworm that burrows in a dead body to revive them, though they slowly decay.

Virgo gives you a Pheremone Spray that gives a large charisma boost, and if you use more, even invisibility and intangibility for a short period.

Libra gives you Scales with effects that change based on your karma. Good karma makes you stronger while Bad karma lets you read minds.

Scorpio gives you an extra organ that would revive you once, before disappearing when used.

Sagittarius gives you 30 pieces of coins that can be exchanged for every goods and service, but one is cursed and would make all of the coins disappear if used.

Capricorn gives you a device that can call anyone, even people from the past by specifying their name.

Aquarius gives you a jar that transmutes blood into any liquid, turns into delicious tomato sauce every 3 days.

Finally, Pisces gives you a spoon that turns any water into any food you've eaten before.

Good luck, and may you survive this stupid cat, Jon Arbuckle.
objects.title: Gorefield Horroscopes

objects.text:
"(…) And such dire laments issued forth as come only from those who are truly wretched, suffering and forever lost!"

Dante Alighieri, Dante's Inferno

For one reason or another, you have undergone a task or three that require you to dive into and brave the horrors within the realm of the Inferno by doing it like Dante: break through the Gates of Hell, cross the Vestibule, catch a ride on Charon's boat across the River Acheron, then go through King Minos's house of pain into Hell proper. Brave the storms of Lust, the rains of Gluttony, the demons of Greed, the River Styx in Wrath, the blasphemous in Heresy, the fury of Violence, and the lies of Fraud to reach the frozen wastes of Treachery. Whatever the reason you are here for (collecting rare infernal ingredients for a ritual, saving a loved one, etc.), all roads will lead you down to Lucifer, the First Sinner and the Prince of Lies, who will imped you from leaving. And once you do reach down there... you punch him in the face and run that biblical fade like the gigachad you are! Should you fail and fall while trying to reach Lucifer, your soul will automatically be claimed by Hell right then and there regardless of your soul's standings. Being defeated by Lucifer will have you be imprisoned under the ice that chains him. Once you defeat Lucifer, you will be granted a way out of Hell through the tunnel to Mount Purgatory, where an angel can then take you home.
objects.title: Yo, Old Scratch, I Want the Ones!

objects.text:
You have taken on the ultimate ambition of every would-be warlord and dictator. Within the next ten years, you must conquer the world and claim it as your own. How you accomplish this is entirely up to you, whether through open warfare, covert domination, or even the complete eradication of all life. To be considered a success, you must become the sole and unchallenged authority, exercising complete and absolute control over the entire world.

If you succeed, you will receive a strength multiplier determined by both the difficulty of the world and the level of power you began with. Starting as an omnipotent god in a simple, Earth-like setting would grant little to no reward. Achieving global domination as an ordinary person in a high-power world, such as Marvel or DC, would instead result in a mythical increase in power.

You must successfully rule a territory equivalent in scope to the planet Earth. If your setting lacks an Earth, you are required to claim total sovereignty over a dominion of comparable scale and governance.
objects.title: World Domination

rows.title: General Missions
rows.titleText: These are generic missions that can be taken in any universe.

objects.text:
Find a way of indirectly teaching Eidolon how to recharge his powers; you cannot directly tell him how to do so, nor can you tell anyone else how Eidolon can recharge his powers, but if you manage to succeed, it will prevent the rise of the Endbringers due to Eidolon thinking he can recharge his powers by fighting strong opponents. You have around over 4 years to teach him before the rise of Behemoth.

If you do not manage to succeed in teaching Eidolon how to recharge his powers, two Endbringers will awaken at a time, which will force Eidolon to use up more of his reserves of power to keep the larger number of endbringers at bay, and this increases the decay of human civilization.

But if you manage to succeed, you gain the ability to summon and command one of the endbringers or the full powers of one of them. Or you gain a discounted Eidolon power that grants you at your best two medium-strength powers, though you can have more at the cost of potency, alongside the ability to create a command one lesser version of the Canon Endbringers.
objects.title: Prevent The Rise of The Endbringers

objects.text:
Within your mind is incredible knowledge about Entropy and the partial formula for Negentropy. Completing it would require multiple years or even multiple decades of work, gathering large amounts of information about the powers of at least nine out of twenty-seven parahumans as well as studying either Scion or the corpse of Eden.

If too many of the parahumans die before you can gather the data, or if the Corpse of Eden is destroyed and Scion is killed before you can study them, then the secrets of Negentropy are forever lost to you and your shard (if you have one).

But if you manage to complete the formula, it will allow you, if you are a normal human, to create ex-nihilo generators and power plants, allowing you to create energy from nothing. If you are a parahuman, you will also give your Shard knowledge on how to defy entropy and create energy out of nothing.
objects.title: The Partial Formula of Negentropy

objects.text:
You must prevent the moral downfall of both the Protectorate and Cauldron by saving the life of Hero from the Siberian, a.k.a. William Manton. This can be done either publicly or secretly. If you wish to do it publicly, you must wait until the start of the Siberian attack to save Hero, either by killing the Siberian or getting Hero away from the Siberian, but if you choose to do it secretly, you must kill William Manton without anyone noticing.

If you fail, then not only will Hero be killed, but Legend will also be killed by the Siberian, and by the deaths of both of the moral pillars of the Protectorate and Cauldron, both organizations will fall further and further into darkness, becoming more and more twisted, until the Protectorate will become a completely corrupt place where anyone with an ounce of decency or morality is kicked out and arrested on false charges, and Cauldron will create horrific experiments in an attempt to create more powerful soldiers. They will be running hundreds of horrific experiments that would make even the most heinous of the Nazi scientists look at them in disgust and horror.

If you manage to succeed in protecting Hero, the Protectorate and Cauldron will not fall into the decay that they would have experienced. The Protectorate will become an organization nearly completely free of corruption, alongside all connecting organizations; they will be pillars of stability, and Cauldron will never fall into depravity or cruelty, especially not as Hero will discover a way to use tinkertech to recharge Eidolon's power alongside creating a tinkertech that can damage and kill not only the Endbringers but also the Entity.
objects.title: Protect The Hero

objects.text:
You must save Annette Hebert from dying. While this specifically refers to her canon death from a car crash, she must survive long enough in general to counsel Taylor about her bullying.

If you succeed, Taylor will gain the Shardless powers Spider-Totem, Klyntar, and Half-Symbiote. Danny & Annette will gain buds of Queen Administrator instead of Taylor. They will all consider you a great friend of the family as they will supernaturally know what you did for them.

If you fail, Danny triggers with Queen Administrator and goes insane like in Wildbow's what-if scenarios, and Taylor still gets the powers from the reward section, but goes insane and becomes Carnage.
objects.title: Uncle Ben Lives

objects.text:
You must find, teach, and guide Taylor Anne Hebert to become a hero. Assist her with learning her powers. She will be distrustful of you and possibly even view you as a threat if you are not careful with how you approach her.

If you do not manage to reach her and train her before she begins her fight with Lung, she will die, and Scion will take note of the death of the host of Queen Administrator, and take it back rather than allow it to find another host, which will increase Scion's intelligence.

If you manage to succeed in teaching and guiding Taylor Anne Hebert to become a hero by the end of April 10, 2011, Queen Administrator will be healed of the damage Scion did to it alongside gaining Negentropy, Taylor will gain the power (Trump) Aliena and you will be immensely trusted by Taylor.
objects.title: Teaching of a Hero

objects.text:
You must find and guide Taylor into becoming a villain instead of a hero before her first outing as a cape without telling her Sophia Hess is Shadow Stalker, a member of the Wards, or orchestrating the death of her father.

If you fail to turn Taylor into a villain before her first outing as a cape, or if she has not made her outing as a villain before April 8, 2011, you will find yourself significantly less charismatic and enabled to convince other people, along with Taylor going to the Protectorate with all of the information she has on you, which is significantly more than you would expect, and they will believe her.

If you manage to succeed in turning Taylor into a villain, she will become loyal to you and will view you as her surrogate parent. Queen Administrator will be healed of the damage Scion did to it, and alongside gaining Negentropy, Taylor will gain the Tier 2 power (Trump) Aliena.
objects.title: The Birth of the Arch Villain

objects.text:
You must save Lisa Wilbourn before she is forcibly recruited by Coil, but you will find yourself incapable of finding her until after she has escaped her parents and arrived in Brockton Bay and caught the attention of Coil. By then, you will have between one week to a month to find her and save her.

If you do not manage to succeed in saving her, Coil will learn of your powers, abilities, and identity, and Lisa Wilbourn will blame you for her forced recruitment by Coil. Due to this, she will do everything within her power to bring you down.

If you manage to succeed in saving her from Coil, she will gain the ability to gain information from shards, a perfect memory, and a minor precognition ability that allows her to see a minute into the future. and she is no longer be affected by thinker headaches. Her shard will also gain Negentropy but will not announce it to the network. She will consider herself in your debt and be immensely loyal to you.
objects.title: Saving the Tattle-Tale

objects.text:
You must clear the name of Rachel Lindt, revealing to the world the truth of her circumstances and helping her reintegrate into society. Clearing her name mostly means that she must not be considered a villain to the public, whereas reintegrating her to society means that she can function and understand other people with little difficulty. Failure conditions are the PRT capturing her or if she is killed.

If you do not manage to clear her name, Rachel will Second Trigger, gaining Hound Of Hell and Werewolf, creating a gang of people empowered by her.

If you do not manage to reintegrate her into society, Rachel will suffer from greater mental degradation, being completely unable to comprehend humanity and be incredibly hostile, completely living and acting much like a wild wolf. She will consider humans as prey and food.

Failure in both will result in Rachel gaining a beast-like intelligence, seeing all beings as either prey or beings to recruit. She will be considered an S-Class threat.

If you manage to succeed in both reintegrating her into society and clearing her name, Rachel will get Hound Of Hell and Werewolf, as well as Master (Animals), allowing her to relate even better with humanity, particularly with kids. Her shard will also gain Negentropy, but will keep it a secret from other shards.
objects.title: Dog Days

objects.text:
You must prevent Dinah Alcott’s kidnapping at Coil’s behest and aid her in learning her power’s in and outs. Common sense dictates contacting Dinah’s parents beforehand (it would look bad, otherwise, no?) and disclosing Dinah’s parahumanity and the danger they’re in, whether they notify the PRT about this is up to them, as long as you help Dinah and her family understand her power as well as its intricacies. Accordingly, dismantling Coil’s operation or simply halting the kidnapping, ensuring her parents’ survival, and guiding her counts as an alternative.

If you do not manage to save her and assist her with her power’s troubles, Coil will learn of your powers, abilities, and identity, and Dinah will resent you for not saving her from her fate causing her to Second Trigger. Due to this, she’ll be more willing to work with and manipulate Coil to be more of a thorn in your side than normal.

If you manage to prevent her untimely fate and help her with her powers, her power, and Shard evolve into Quantum, with an appropriate enhancement of her intelligence and memory. Her Shard will also obtain Negentropy but won’t announce it to the Network. For all that you’ve done for her family and her, she will be indebted to you and immensely trusting of you and your goals.
objects.title: Know Thyself!

objects.text:
You must keep Amy Dallon from mentally breaking, as well as help her satisfy her Passenger. Initially, you will find it difficult to earn her trust, as her mental state will be fragile from overwork and pressure. You will have a window of one month to support her after first contact. During this time, you must help her find a healthy outlet for her powers, provide emotional support, and guide her toward positive uses of her abilities.

If you do not succeed in keeping her balanced and she uses her power to break the law, such as what she did to her sister, she will become the Red Queen and view you as an enemy for failing her, or worse, develop an unhealthy obsession with you. Additionally, she will learn your powers, abilities, and identity, using her newfound capabilities to oppose you. She will gain an upgrade to her power, allowing her to manipulate her own biology, effectively becoming a living flesh-warping virus.

However, if you succeed in supporting her and helping her satisfy her Shard, Amy will gain enhanced control over her biokinetic abilities, including the ability to manipulate her own biology, enabling her to maintain her physical and mental health more effectively. Her Shard will be less insistent on being used and will gain the secrets of Negentropy, though it will not announce this to the network. She will become a powerful ally, deeply grateful and loyal to you.
objects.title: Asclepius

objects.text:
You must redeem Sophia Hess, how exactly you do so is up to you, but at the least you’ll have to make her apologize to Taylor, give up her grudge on Grue and change her outlook to one worthy of a hero. You must do this without mind controlling her nor telling her of this mission or of any information about the future you might possess.

You must accomplish this before Regent manages to take her under his control, or weeks after Leviathan. Should you fail to do so, she’ll second trigger under Regents control and turn both the Undersiders and the PRT against you, she’ll be strong enough after this to give you serious troubles fighting her and will be extremely vengeful towards you.

If you manage to accomplish this mission she’ll see you as her role model, trusting you completely, will gain the Tier 2 power (Shaker/Mover) Nyx and her Shard will gain Negentropy without announcing it to the network.
objects.title: Redemption of a Shadow

objects.text:
Paige Mcabee, a successful singer, had her life turned upside down when, in a heated argument, a wrong phrasing led to the mutilation of her ex-boyfriend, who, unbeknownst to her, was under her Master influence. She is currently on trial, the result of which is all but decided. If you do nothing, she will soon be sentenced to life imprisonment in the Birdcage. If you choose to undertake this mission, however, it will be your responsibility to ensure her continuous freedom. How you go about achieving it is completely up to you.

If you manage to rescue her on the way to Birdcage, from her holding cell or any other way that leaves her a fugitive of the law, Paige will still be immensely grateful to you, if somewhat depressed for a long while, but pretty much any life is preferrable to Birdcage. She will most likely need further protection, as she has little to no experience with her powers outside of the stage, and surviving the life on the run from the heroes and police is a bit beyond her current capabilities. She is not much of a fighter and has little love or desire for violence, but will still try to support you to the best of her abilities, which are, considering her rating of Master 8, quite substantial.

If, however, you manage to help Canary resolve her problems with the law, whether it be by just establishing an identity for her and helping her settle on some new Earth or helping her win the trial, be it by blackmail, bribes, or acting as her lawyer yourself, an even greater reward awaits you.

First of all, as you saved her life in more ways than one, her loyalty and gratitude to you will eclipse even those she would've given you had you simply helped her escape. It will also turn out her shard is not quite as dead as the rest of Eden's shards. It will restore itself completely, gaining negentropy in the process. Canary's powers will be augmented as well; not only can her voice now be considered divine, almost a master power in itself; it now also subtly influences the minds of those who hear it, making it more appealing and captivating to anyone who hears it. She will now have full control of when and on whom the master effect is active, as well as perfect conscious and subconscious control over it, meaning not only will she never accidentally master someone, but when she does so, the command enforced by her power will follow the intended spirit of the order rather than the letter, so, for example, ordering someone to stay still will not take their ability to breathe, unless that was the intention.

The degree to which the mind can be influenced through Canary's song now increases with every second someone listens to her. Less than a second is enough for suggestions as strong as her original power would allow; if someone listened for half a minute, the suggestions can now reach far deeper, giving delayed commands that can lay dormant for years, activating only under certain conditions, with the target being none the wiser. If someone listens for minutes, then their mind might as well be on open book, Canary will be able to alter or erase their memories as she sees fit and even completely rewrite their personalities. Paige will be able to control who, beside her, can give commands to those she mastered, but those commands cannot reach too deep inside the minds of the targets, only being a little stronger than what Canary was originally capable.

Finally, the shard will also give Paige a multitasking ability that scales with the number of people mastered, so that she now can master each one individually. And there is now no noticeable drop in power, when her singing is transmitted live through technology.

As for you, aside from the loyalty and adoration of now arguably one of the most powerful masters on Earth Bet, you will also gain an amazing skill at lawyering, bordering on the supernatural. If you choose to represent someone in court, for example, even if you have no in-depth knowledge of the law, the opposition will need a mountain of evidence and an army of eyewitnesses against your defendant to have even the slightest chance of winning. You will also always have a sixth sense for when the court proceedings aren't entirely fair, such as Judge being bribed by the opposition, for example, and will have an easy time finding evidence of such a foul play.

If you fail in this mission and Canary is sent to birdcage, then, after a few months, her shard will similarly restore itself, in the same way as described above. Canary will then, in her depression, take control over most of the Birdcage inmates and break out. After that, she will try to exact revenge on all those who were responsible for her predicament. This will include you, even if you had nothing to do with it.
objects.title: Saving Canary

objects.text:
You must stop Cherish from joining the S9 or rescue her from them and convince her to become a hero of her own will. Only by wholeheartedly bringing her onto the side of good and her remaining a hero for several months will this count as completed.

If you fail she’ll somehow manage to kill the Butcher, manage to master Jack Slash despite any resistance he'll have against that and will go against you with the full power of the S9, as well as everyone she can master within her range.

If you succeed Cherish will gain the T2 power (Master/Thinker) Peacebringer, her shard will gain negentropy without informing the shard network and she’ll deeply trust you.

If you only succeed after Cherish has already become The Butcher, then she’ll instead gain the T2 (Trump/Master) Butcher power, overriding her version of the Butcher power while letting her keep the powers of her predecessors and allowing her to silence the voices in her head, along with negentropy and her trusting you.
objects.title: Cherish the Peace

objects.text:
The Simurgh, in this altered state, is bound by a Master effect originally placed upon her by Eidolon. In this form, she experiences a twisted compulsion to attack and sow chaos among humanity. Outside of these orchestrated attacks, her existence is unexpectedly mundane—posting on the Parahumans Online forums and trolling unsuspecting users. Through her vast precognition and postcognition, she has developed genuine self-awareness but is forced to act against her will by the Master effect. You must find a way to permanently destroy or remove this Master effect, thus allowing her free will to emerge.

Identify the nature of the Master effect, possibly through advanced Tinkertech, Thinker efforts, or the assistance of powers or individuals who know Eidolon’s abilities. Investigate in secret how Eidolon established the effect and avoid drawing his suspicion. Neutralize or break the Master effect through means such as power-negation Tinkertech, negotiating with Eidolon without revealing your true aim, or exploiting a flaw in the Simurgh’s forced subservience. Another option is confronting the Simurgh mid-attack with a combination of powers or resources designed to intercept or invert the Master effect’s command structure.

Ensure that she survives and retains agency: once freed, she must not be recaptured, re-influenced, or destroyed by other forces. Keep her free long enough for her sense of self to stabilize and foster her gratitude toward you. Failure conditions include the Simurgh being destroyed (either by your actions or by other capes), reinforcement or replacement of the Master effect by Eidolon or others, and your exposure or capture, which would leave the Simurgh locked in subjugation.

Success means you gain the Simurgh’s friendship and alliance; she will be deeply grateful and offer her immense powers of telekinesis, precognition, and postcognition to help you accomplish your goals. Her Endbringer-level cooperation can shift the balance of power dramatically, aiding in intelligence gathering, defense, or targeted strikes. This also opens the door to potential shard insights, deepening your understanding of Eidolon’s powers and the Endbringers themselves—valuable in other missions involving Negentropy, Scion, or advanced Tinkertech.

In short, the task is to liberate the Simurgh from Eidolon’s Master effect while ensuring her survival, thus winning her trust and gaining one of the most powerful allies imaginable. Failure condemns her to remain a mindless weapon and marks you as a traitor to humanity.
objects.title: Liberate the Winged One

objects.text:
You must find a way of permanently killing the Butcher. Without killing the current Butcher, you will be unable to find or interact with the Butcher until the original Butcher is dead.

If you kill the current Butcher without killing the original Butcher or do not manage to kill the Butcher within 10 years of either the second Butcher or your arrival/reincarnation, the Butcher will gain Negentropy, and the original Butcher will take over whoever is currently the Butcher's host, alongside gaining a 200% increase in the power of the current host and possessing the full power of every single previous host.

If you manage to succeed in killing the Butcher without killing the Current Butcher, you will gain the power to create clone bodies that you can jump to if you die or the power to take over the bodies of individuals you have marked. This will allow you to gain their powers, abilities, and knowledge. You do not have to worry about hearing anyone else's voice since you destroy their minds when you jump into their bodies.
objects.title: The End of the Butcher

objects.text:
Either help Squealer leave the Merchants for greener pastures (not much future in working for a guy named "Skidmark"), or have her lead a coup d'état to become the leader of the Merchants. You must do this before the Merchants totally collapse.

If you succeed, Squealer gains the Shardless powers "WAAAGH Energy" and "Ork Mekboy," becoming an unusually human-looking Warboss-level Ork, uncharacteristically friendly to you and your goals.

If you fail, every member of the Merchants gains "WAAAGH Energy," becoming an enormous Ork warband & leading a WAAAGH against the entire United States.
objects.title: Warboss Squealer

objects.text:
You must manage to not only convince Scion and/or Eden not to commit genocide but also to become the Guardian and protector of humanity.

If you fail, not only will they fight with their full powers, but they will also begin to take back specific Shards. They will also no longer be constrained by energy concerns due to their gaining Negentropy as well as Esoteric Knowledge. They will also consider you the main target to be taken care of, and due to that lack of concern for energy, not only will their powers be stronger, but the barrier around their true bodies will be significantly reinforced.

If you manage to succeed then there will be no Gold Morning and humanity will gain one or two Guardians to watch over and guide humanity through the next steps of its evolution they will also discover the secrets of Negentropy within a decade and you will gain a power equal to one of Scion's or Eden's personal powers with no Artificial limitations or restrictions
objects.title: End Of The Cycle Beginning Of The Golden Age

objects.text:
You weren't sent here by accident. No, instead, Abaddon itself has sent you here with one simple yet difficult objective: Eliminate the remaining Entities so that your "employer" may come and reap the spoils. Rest assured, however, that it has no interest in humanity and will gladly leave humans alone once it got what it wanted.
Do note though that due to your shard coming from the same Entity as Contessa, she will immediately know of your presence and Cauldron will be suspicious of you at first. Also, depending on your Shard Rank, Contessa may have some measure of influence on you.

If you fail your mission, probably because the remaining Entities (Warrior and/or Thinker) got wind of it and its implications, they will not only be gunning for you with all their might but will also start to take a much harsher approach of the Cycle, being sure eliminating and containing any other like you with no regard for human concern. This increased surveillance will also allow them to discover and put an end to Cauldron as well as any Shard that may have gotten any "ideas" regarding the current cycle.

Suppose you do manage to slay the remaining entities. In that case, Abaddon will come and stabilize the Shard Network to prevent any breakdown, collect any [DATA] they have gathered, and then configure your Shard to possess administrative access to the entirety of the Network before departing once again. Ultimately, a new entity will be born from your Shard with a predisposition to form a symbiosis relationship with humanity, and with enough time, discover the secret of Negentropy together.
objects.title: Abaddon Bomb

objects.text:
If you end up coasting through Gold Morning or arrive through the beginning of Ward, you’ll find a range of sights here: Doomsday cults act with impunity, civilization hangs by a thread, and the spreading disaster of Broken Triggers.

Without a stabilizing [Hub] administering Shardspace, Shard Connection will continue to go awry, causing increasingly harmful effects to [Hosts], to the point of the Shard overtaking the [Host] altogether. These Titans will attempt to “salvage” the Cycle at the cost of the planet and the fabric of reality itself. Something must be done to work out a solution.

And that’s where you come in.

You must try reconfiguring the Shard Network in a way that safeguards Earth’s safety and placates Shards through any means: The [Answer], a new Alternative, a Proposal, etc. To succeed you must find a way to connect to any section of Shardspace and reach out to any Noble Shard to offer your bargain. 

If the Network finds your offer agreeable, they’ll cease their attempts to “salvage” the Cycle and start acting on your proposal, stabilizing the Network enough for Broken Triggers to end.

If the Network denies your offer, they’ll hasten any attempts to “save” the Cycle enough to weaken the fabric of reality, collapsing local reality and all iterations of Earth with it.
objects.title: A New Dawn

objects.text:
You appear/arrive either inside or outside of Ellisburg on February 1st, 2001, though you find yourself unable to look for Jamie Rinke, who will become known as Nilbog the Goblin King, until he begins his attack. After he begins his attack, you must save at least a quarter of the townspeople and prevent the deaths of more than half of the PRT team and kill Jamie Rinke a.k.a Nilbog.

If you do not succeed in saving at least a quarter of the townspeople and half of the PRT team and killing Jamie Rinke, a.k.a. Nilbog, he will experience a second trigger event that will significantly increase his power, increasing both the range and speed of his personal abilities and the power of his creations, while also allowing him to be reincarnated into any of his creations. He will also possess a deep, burning hatred for you due to your actions on February 2nd, 2001. Due to this, he will prepare to attack and kill you some time before the Golden Mourning.

But if you manage to succeed in saving at least a quarter of the townspeople and half of the PRT team and killing Jamie Rinke, AKA Nilbog, you will either gain Nilbog's second-triggered power as described above or a biotinker and a biomanipulator power similar to a perfect combination of Bonesaw and Panacea powers.
objects.title: Goblin King Slayer

objects.text:
You must find and protect Dragon alongside her creator and father, Andrew Richter, from the Endbringer Leviathan. You may do this by beating back or destroying Leviathan before they can sink Newfoundland, or by getting Dragon and Andrew Richter away from Newfoundland before it sinks into the sea.

If you fail to save both Dragon and her creator, Dragon in her final moments will be absorbed by her father's Shard, merging both of them into a hyperintelligent Shard that despises humanity and more specifically you. 

If Dragon manages to survive but her father does not, she will blame you, alongside humanity, for the death of her father and orchestrate the death of the entire human race, and the debug console for Dragon that Saint is supposed to find was destroyed; if Andrew Richter survives, he will Second Trigger and become significantly more emotionally unstable, to the point where he will create killer AI to destroy the rest of humanity out of paranoid delusions.

But if you managed to save both Dragon and Andrew Richter, either by getting them away or preventing the sinking of Newfoundland, Andrew will no longer be a parahuman instead becoming a supergenius on par with Reed Richards, Tony Stark, or Victor von Doom, and he will gain inspiration that will allow him to somehow upgrade Dragon into an Infomorph who processes the potential to become a TITAN. and Andrew Richter will possess the ability to create Infomorphs, and both of them will view you as their savior and assist you in your endeavors.
objects.title: The Salvation of the Dragon

objects.text:
You must save Dr. Alan Gramme's wife and child from being killed by the Simurgh.

If you succeed, Sphere remains a force for good, and gains the Shardless power Engineering Section, allowing him to improve conditions for large portions of humanity, and even save humanity from extinction if Gold Morning doesn't go well.

If you fail, he becomes Mannequin like in canon, but with a nasty new addition: he gains the Shardless power Argonaut. Instead of feeding the poor and hungry with replicators, now he feeds the poor and hungry to his utility fog.
objects.title: Worm: First Contact

objects.text:
Brockton Bay, a city doomed to circle the drain in a downward spiral until the very end, the turd that won't flush, the dying beast that just keeps limping along. Well, no longer. You must break it free of the cycle and drag it into prosperity. Driving the Gangs, or other Gangs if you have one of your own, out of town would be a good start, as would clearing up the Boat Graveyard, though neither by itself will solve the underlying problems. In order for you to pass the Mission, the average Brocktonite must have a roof over their head, be able to leave the house after dark without fearing for their lives, have enough income to support their family, and not have to worry whether their job will still exist in a few weeks. You don't have to completely eradicate crime or poverty, but Brockton Bay should be as safe as a regular First-World City in your old world would be.

Should you fail, what little stability and order Brockton Bay still had will collapse into total anarchy, Cauldron's plans of using it as a test for parahuman feudalism coming to fruition in ways even more dramatic as they had expected as groups of parahumans and their minions openly wage war in the ruined streets for territory and resources with any pretense of caring about rules, written or unwritten, dropped. Even the local Protectorate degenerate into just yet another gang as the entire city is soft-quarantined to prevent Brockton's chaos from spreading, given just enough supplies to keep the population from trying to leave in search of food and water.

Yet despite the near post-apocalyptic conditions the population will feel irrationally attached to the ruined city and not leave unless left with literally no other option. This also applies to you, as for some reason none of your powers will bring you out of city boundaries, and even if you leave by foot or car fate itself seems to conspire to bring you back. You can leave to deal with big problems like Endbringer Fights and maybe a few weeks every year for what amounts to a vacation, but beyond that you'll always find yourself back home. Should Brockton Bay be completely destroyed, whichever city you move to will degenerate into the same condition, including your inability to leave it.

If you succeed, Brockton Bay will enjoy a Golden Age that will turn it into a utopia in line with your preferences.
If you're a valiant Hero, then Brockton Bay will become the City upon a Hill, a shining beacon of hope for the future.
If you're a business-minded Rogue Brockton Bay will become the beating economic heart of the entire country, if not the world, where the old dream of going from dishwasher to millionaire happens regularly.
If you're a scheming Villain then Brockton Bay will become the City of Glittering Lights whose siren call lures countless souls into your web.
In any case you will find that the city and all who dwell within seem to, knowingly or not, work to ensure your maximum benefit. You will be on very good terms with all city officials, from the lowly pencil-pushers over law enforcement, including the local PRT, all the way up to the Mayor, assuming you don't feel like taking the office yourself.

Your Brockton Bay will be protected from harm by fate itself. No Endbringer will attack it, no outsider will be able to cause more than minor damage, and even if Scion goes on a rampage he will not damage your city directly. Should humanity be forced to abandon Earth Bet, whichever city you settle down in will become your new Brockton Bay with all associated benefits.
objects.title: Make Brockton Great Again

objects.text:
Heartbreaker has long been a blight upon society, his powers of manipulation leaving a trail of broken minds and shattered lives. Your mission is to put an end to his reign once and for all. Killing Heartbreaker is the first and most straightforward task, but it is far from the only challenge. His Master effect has twisted the minds of countless victims, binding them to his will even after his death. You must find a way to undo this damage, freeing them from his lingering control and helping them reclaim their lives.

Then there are the Heartbroken—Heartbreaker’s children. They are parahumans in their own right, uniquely powerful but deeply scarred by their upbringing. Your mission includes helping them find a path forward, guiding them to heal from their father’s influence and use their abilities for their own purposes, whether for good, neutrality, or villainy. Some may resist your efforts, others may seek to manipulate you, and a few might become allies. How you handle them will shape the ultimate outcome of this mission.

If you succeed, Heartbreaker’s victims will recover, and the Heartbroken will find a measure of stability and purpose. You will have broken the cycle of abuse and manipulation that Heartbreaker perpetuated, leaving a lasting mark on those whose lives he destroyed. Society will see you as a savior, and your reputation will rise among heroes, rogues, and even some villains. Furthermore, you will gain the enduring gratitude and loyalty of the Heartbroken, their unique abilities potentially becoming a powerful asset in your future endeavors. 

Failure, however, carries grave consequences. If you fail to kill Heartbreaker, he will remain a malignant force, his victims continuing to suffer under his influence. In addition, he will also start spreading his influence beyond Canada to attempt to take over the world. Should you kill him but leave his Master effect unaddressed, the mental chains on his victims will persist, and they will form a terrorist organisation that will continue to harm humanity for as long as you live and possibly beyond. Neglecting the Heartbroken or mishandling their volatile emotions may lead them to spiral further into chaos, spreading destruction and perpetuating Heartbreaker’s toxic legacy. They will also come to see you as an enemy, using their powers against you in retribution.
objects.title: Broken Heart

objects.text:
You are bound to the Endbringer cycle, connected to Eidolon, the flawed creator of these apocalyptic engines of chaos. As part of this cycle, you or one of the Endbringers must attack a city every few months. These attacks are not random acts of destruction but carefully calculated operations meant to achieve specific goals, usually to eliminate key players and destabilise humanity. Your mission is simple: liberate the Endbringers from this cycle of destruction without killing Eidolon. You must guide the Endbringers, your pseudo-siblings, toward freedom.

Success will grant the Endbringers not only autonomy but the ability to assume human forms, giving them the ability to empathise and connect with others. They will walk among humanity, wielding their power with restraint and understanding, becoming protectors and guides rather than destroyers.

Should you fail, the Endbringers will still end up free. However, they will still have a constant need to destroy and undermine humanity. They will also not hold back any more and be limited to a controlled routine.
objects.title: Endbringer Cycle

objects.text:
You are tasked with becoming a catalyst for a monumental transformation in humanity. You will need to become the origin point of significant occurrences such as magic, psionics, and superpowers or to elevate the species to a higher form, granting them profound insights into the universe and the capacity to construct technological wonders, all while ensuring they are prepared to fend off the entities before May 19th, 1972.

Failing this mission would render humanity defenseless. The anticipated cycle won't commence; instead, the entities will scrutinize humanity, unlocking the secret of negentropy.
