objects.text: Rather than the Alternate Earths you selected all being merged into one world, this modifier instead makes them separate universes within a singular multiverse. You may choose to exclude certain settings from this, having them be merged into one as normal. You can decide the exact 'shape' or 'structure' of the multiverse assuming that a canonical one doesn't exist, or mix and match them if there are multiple. You may also decide if there is any form of preexisting link connecting these universes and what it is, such as perhaps Cauldron being aware of the existence of specific Alternate Earths, or maybe a handful of portals (naturally occurring or not) connecting various Alternate Earths together. You may choose for this to also apply to non-multiserval power systems, allowing things like cursed energy or aura to have a presence on multiple worlds just like Parahuman powers or Linker Cores do. Same for modifiers like Surprisingly Short Apocalypse or Guardians of Gaia. Note: If you have other modifiers that alter how Alternate Earth Crossovers work, such as Not just Earth or Layers, Jerry. Layers, you may mix and match them at your discretion.
objects.title: Shared Multiverse

objects.text: The buildup of energy gained due to connecting to so many dimensions has caused a breakdown in the local fabric of space. Slowly at first, but with increasing frequency, portals to alternate dimensions you have chosen in the Alternate Earth and Original Settings menus will begin to open in your immediate area. At first, they will be small, and unassuming which will prevent large factions from taking notice, and close fairly quickly. However as resonance builds up these portals will become larger, last longer, and even form in areas farther away from you. If nothing is done to solve this, over time these connections may become permanent and alter the fabric of your local multiverse.
objects.title: The Brockton Incident

objects.text: What will it take for you to just. STAY. DEAD!? You know that really annoying trope? Where a character- probably a big baddy- gets offed pretty thoroughly, only to show up later as if nothing happened? Nope. Done. No more. Dead is dead. Meet oblivion. Good. Bye. Direct revival is now impossible in whatever setting you chose- unless Afterlife is selected, in which case the consequences are amplified- and indirect revival is extremely difficult and carries its own costs and penalties. Even spiritual succession gets murky, with reincarnations and clones becoming distinct individuals with no chance of being possessed by their past lives. Cheating death via backups is non functional. Any made will deviate, break down and fail. On top of that, any memories and personality will fail to transfer clearly. Clones, as a consequence, quickly deviate as well. Rapidly, if not immediately, turning into their own individuals with their own interpretations and views on the memories they have, with distinct personalities. Unfortunately, this only applies to beings who actually die, and not those who fall into some semi-living wraith or soul-based state. As long as continuity of existence is maintained, and they do not actually die, they can recover. Whether that be by finding or making a new body, or something else. As a plus, it becomes alot harder to cheese certain death. No more sudden, barely-if-you-squint 'explicable' powerups or mutations on the brink of death. Bit of a double edged sword, but worth it to stop that one bastard from popping back up for the Eighth damn time—!
objects.title: People Die When They Are Killed

objects.text:
After death, a person's soul is transferred to a mystical realm referred to as the afterlife. In this dream-like world, their spirit lingers on, their consciousness suspended in perpetuity. It is widely believed that this afterlife serves as a final destination for souls, where they can find everlasting peace and rest.

However, the existence of this realm has been discovered by some, allowing them to retrieve the essence of the deceased from the afterlife and bring them back to life. Although resurrecting someone from the afterlife may seem like a miracle, there are significant consequences to consider. Those who return from the afterlife often return with their minds in a state of confusion, their memories and thoughts blurred. The transition back into the living world can be disorienting, leaving them feeling lost and unsure of their surroundings. Additionally, the trauma of their death can haunt them, leaving them with emotional scars that may take years to heal.
objects.title: Afterlife

objects.text:
”Hero died? I just saw him this morning, really, what do you mean?“

Heroes and Villains now have a habit of coming back from the dead after a few months, especially when their presence is sorely needed. Hero returned just in time Leviathan attacked Seattle, Richter returned from death to assist in resolving the Boston Games, and heroes previously dead have come back to fight against threats that their powers are especially effective against. However, heroes aren't the only ones with comeback stories. King returned after his death at the hands of Jack Slash and is now forming a new villain team, Gray Boy somehow unshaded himself and is now on a never-ending time bubble spree, and numerous villains that bitten the bullet for their recklessness and seemingly unremarkability have become cautious and serious threats.
objects.title: Death’s like Breadsticks for these People!

addons.text: Congratulations, in your attempt to make sure people would still trigger from death, you made things worse for everyone. No therapy sessions allowed. Do you think we can afford free therapy? What do you mean money isn't a thing in the netherworld? Of course it is. Anyways, from now on we'll be sending the folks that died right back to the respawn point with no breaks. As a result, dying is very traumatic and has a significantly higher chance of causing a trigger or a second trigger. You can still choose to opt out and move on to your prescribed afterlife if you wish..
addons.title: You Thought Death Doesn't Have Consequences?

objects.text:
Congratulations, death is now hilariously cheap. Whenever someone dies from anything other than old age, they are revived in perfect health at the nearest respawn point as if they were never hurt to begin with. Additionally, touching the respawn point fully heals the user of any ailment they are suffering from. 

Every town has at least one respawn point, and cities have multiple. The larger the settlement, the more respawn points there are. If a respawn point is damaged, it takes up to 24 hours to repair itself depending on the level of damage. It will still restore itself if it is completely destroyed, and if its initial location becomes unavailable or it is inaccessible, it moves elsewhere. 

Areas within 300 meters of respawn points are considered no-combat zones, and people are incapable of violence within the zone. There is also a barrier around it to prevent attacks from outside the zone from reaching in.

Death comes with a free therapy session with the entity in charge of the respawn points. Not to be confused with the type of entity Scion is, we promise they are different. No time passes in death space, so you can spend as much time as you need to fix all that death-related trauma before you go back to the material world. What, you thought you could opt out? When we said it was free, we meant mandatory. Don't worry, we'll let you out once you're healthy.

You can stay in the netherworld for as long as you wish, and no time will have passed on the outside. If you wish to die permanently—a valid choice for somewhere like Earth Bet—you can simply go on to your prescribed afterlife, though you cannot return if you choose to do so.
objects.title: Death is a Vacation

objects.text:
Congratulations! You have solved the number one (technically only) cause of death. 

Respawn points can now be used to alter the user's age. Aging is part of life, after all. This allows people to alter their age as if they have the "Who Wants to Live Forever?" perk. That person who looks like they're in their late 20s could be pushing 400, and you have no way of knowing. 

No, you still shouldn't ask a woman her age; that's rude. As for the overpopulation problem, it would most definitely happen if we stopped here; we solved that, too. 

Now when someone chooses to pass on permanently it opens a slot. Unless there is a free slot conception is impossible. Additional slots are added whenever a new settlement is formed. 

See, we really thought of everything. What? Mortals won't like that? Again, you should have thought of that before you created a possible overpopulation problem that we at Life Cycle Incorporated LLC had to fix.
objects.title: Overpopulation, What's That?

objects.text: Okay the repawn points seemed like a good idea at first. Just save a bit of paperwork by making mortals die less often. But now i have to do even more paperwork for different reasons dammit! Okay, breathe. Since this is your fault and not mine I've decided to take my frustration out on all mortals who use my system. Constant unavoidable death and rebirth for all! Every 3 days people die an unavoidable death and are forced through the respawn process. What do you mean these amount of deaths is starting to look comical? What do you mean how people are dying is so stupid it's making the Darwin Awards look like a checklist? Nuh-uh! You will take your mandatory therapy and you will like it. Then you will be sent out to do it all over again. No you cannot pass on permanently anymore. Tantrum?! You're throwing a tantrum!
objects.title: Damn Paperwork!

objects.text: Welp. With people making Death like something you bounce back from, no wonder trauma has caused them to trigger beyond the grave. Ordinary people will now have the chance of coming back to life as Parahumans for the fact their deaths are life-shattering enough to cause them to trigger, and groups of people dying in mass casualty events will also have the chance to cluster Death Triggers. Parahumans also apply, with the chance of undergoing a Second Trigger.
objects.title: Death Triggers

objects.text: In this world, an individual's character shapes their outward appearance. A cruel and heartless person would be unattractive, while a kind person would possess a radiant beauty. A cunning person will have a sharp look, marked by a sharp gaze that reflects their astuteness and quick-witted nature, whereas someone slow may have a more rugged appearance, akin to that of a brute, often characterized by a lack of finesse or refinement in their demeanor and expression.
objects.title: Judge A Book By Its Cover

objects.text:
Everyone speaks the universal language, English. From the Americans, Chinese, to the space Australians, they all speak English. English isn't the only language, just the language everyone can speak.

Or if you're boring, you can choose another language.
objects.title: The Universal Language

objects.text:
Everyone, everywhere, uses the same currency. Whether you’re buying coffee on Mars, renting a car in Tokyo, or tipping an eldritch god at the edge of the universe, the currency is always accepted, always understood, and always works. No more exchange rates, confusing coins, or awkward bartering. Just a smooth, seamless economy that keeps the galaxy spinning. Sure, some places might still collect weird local tokens for fun or tradition—but when it’s time to pay, everyone knows what matters.

Credits, dollars, gold, or galactic units—call it what you want. It all spends the same.
objects.title: The Universal Currency

objects.text:
The world is noticeably better, not because major problems like wars and poverty have disappeared, but because the quality of everyday life has improved. Food tastes better and is healthier, technology is more efficient, and people are generally more polite. The economy runs smoothly, and things are simply more refined. There aren’t futuristic inventions like flying cars, but fuel-efficient and electric vehicles are now the norm.

This improvement is subtle but widespread. Healthcare is faster and more accurate, homes are better built, and schools are more effective at teaching. Even in casual conversations, people communicate more clearly, and disagreements are resolved more smoothly. 

It’s not a perfect world, but it feels like everything is a more polished version of what came before. Problems still exist, but people handle them with greater ease and efficiency.
objects.title: Just Better

addons.text:
Despite being in a different time period, your world’s technology is still equivalent to the high end of your original world’s 2011. However, the infrastructure and principles it is built on are rather retro and possibly wackier, being based on the aesthetics of ‘-punk’ styles associated with different eras.

Based on which era you are in, you could have VR sims on cassette tapes, bullet-steam-locomotives, passenger line gliders, or social media posts transmitted to your iStone through hiveminded insects apps.

If there are multiple retrofuturistic styles associated with an era, such as atompunk, cassettepunk, or cyberpunk for Cold War, or there are subgenres of a punk style, such as decopunk and trenchpunk for deiselpunk then you may choose which one applies.

Alternate History allows you to apply any punk style you like to the modern era, combining them, or creating your own, as well as fine tuning and making minor changes to which paths of technological development were followed.
addons.title: Punk’d
Mustache Science
addons.text: The new exotic materials lead to major technological development across all fields. On the more mundane side of things this means hologram computers, robotic helpers, new medicines and all-round better quality of life. On the other side it also leads to more wonderous things, like flying cars, teleporters, cloaking devices or even super serums.

objects.text:
Technology is remarkably advanced, far beyond what the current time period would suggest. In 2011, society has access to innovations and devices that feel like they belong in 2111. Everyday life is infused with futuristic technology that seamlessly integrates into people's routines. Homes are equipped with smart systems that anticipate needs, energy is harnessed from renewable sources with incredible efficiency, and communication tools are faster and more intuitive than anything expected for the era.

Transportation has evolved too. While traditional cars still exist, most people rely on electric and autonomous vehicles with advanced navigation systems. Public transit is similarly upgraded, with high-speed trains and eco-friendly options becoming the standard. The healthcare system benefits enormously from advanced medical technologies, offering treatments and diagnostic tools that are far ahead of their time. Diseases that were once feared are now easily treatable, and healthcare is more personalized and accessible.

Even entertainment has been transformed—immersive virtual reality, holographic displays, and interactive media are widespread. Education, too, has changed, with learning being more personalized, adaptive, and engaging, making it possible to master complex subjects in record time. People now have access to information and tools that allow them to innovate and create at unprecedented levels, accelerating progress in every field.

While the world still operates under the norms and culture of 2011, the technology is far more advanced than they normally would have been.
objects.title: Improved Technology

objects.text:
Your chosen setting now functions on the opposite of the phrase “World of Cardboard”. The setting is now much more durable than normal to such a degree that powered individuals will find it extremely hard to do any large-scale lasting damage to the world around them. To put this better into perspective only the strongest individuals and effects may cause a threat to the world and even then the world will quickly recover. This also affects other living beings and requires great effort and power in order to cause permanent harm or death.

The world will be able to function as normal with the world still able to be harvested for materials both nonliving and living.

Accidentally destroying planets and entire galaxies or universes is now a near impossibility. So have fun going all out in your powers.
objects.title: World of Iron

objects.text:
Various phenomena centered around a single element will appear all across the world, be it something like gravity, magic, water, electricity or time. 
Here some examples with time:
Time-loops, time-travel, areas with faster/slower time, precog/postcog devices, people with time-based powers and many other time-based anomalies all across the world, though their effects won’t all be far-reaching, if there’s for example a time loop it will either be relatively short if it affects a lot of people, or longer if it affects only a single person. However time loops could also be scenario dependent, like only stopping if an accident is prevented. Time-travel on the other hand will only ever change minor things retroactively, like making it so that a few people stay alive instead of dying, someone becoming rich instead of remaining poor or stuff being differently named, though that doesn’t stop people in the present from taking advantage of future knowledge.

Each time you select this you can choose another Element which will have about the same level of influence, fire could cause volcanoes to burst or grant fire powers, something like ‘moon’ could affect the tides or make some of the moon-based stories more grounded in reality. 
If taken ten times then all elements will be affected by this.
objects.title: Element-based Anomalies

objects.text:
The true nature of the multiverse remains unknown. No one understands why it exists in its current form—or how—but the research of Professor Haywire, a renowned Dimensional Tinker, has revealed that within its infinite, or near-infinite expanse, the impossible becomes possible.

Contrary to the classical image of a universe—a star surrounded by a ring of planets, all orbiting massive black holes that in turn orbit even greater ones—Haywire introduced his findings on some other parallel earths. He described vast, potentially infinite flat expanses he called Planes. These planes extend in all directions, challenging the very definition of a universe.

All of those "planes" have been studied where first the portal's have been open, experiments by Tinkers attempted to test the "ceiling" of these Planes where conducted. One notable launch sent a small missile equipped with gravity sensors and cameras to detect curvature or diminishing gravitational pull. Instead of thinning out, the gravity remained roughly 1G up to 100 kilometers, where the missile collided with a flying landmass larger than the United States.

This led to a radical theory: rather than the universe spreading outward after its birth, it may have condensed downward. In this model, matter and space collapse into dense, layered strata, giving rise to Earth-like realms containing rivers the size of nations and oceans with surface areas surpassing that of Earth itself.
 
Despite the absurdity of such environments, Tinkers and Thinkers alike—para-human and otherwise—found no deviation from fundamental physical laws. Even in a world where logic seems to fold, gravity, thermodynamics, and light all behave consistently—at least to observers. Curiously, the "sun" and "moon" in the sky remain unchanged in size or brightness, no matter how far one travels vertically.

Some speculate these Planes are artificial constructs—perhaps colossal megastructures like a Birch World or Alderson Disk. Others propose spatial manipulation on a scale akin to the combined powers of Dodge and Vista: a continuous warping of reality, stitched into a coherent illusion of space.

Some theorize Planes are layered constructs, each stratum hosting ecosystems separated by gravitational eddies. Others suggest they are fragments of a bulk dimension, where our 3D reality is a shadow on higher-dimensional geometry. Haywire’s final notes speculate Planes are "failed universes"—aborted expansions that collapsed into flat, recursive manifolds, their latent energy birthing impossible geographies.
objects.title: Of Planes and Universes.

objects.text:
The world is dulled, its people blunted in wit and perception. Everyone seems noticeably less intelligent, as if their awareness and reasoning are trapped within narrow rails. They are not mindless, nor are they incapable of thought, but their understanding of the world is strangely limited, as though their responses were drawn from a shallow, prewritten list of possibilities. Conversations tend to loop, assumptions go unchallenged, and obvious flaws in logic pass by unnoticed unless they are explicitly pointed out.

People are unusually easy to deceive, distract, or mislead. A tossed coin, a sudden noise, or a half-hearted explanation can readily divert suspicion. Even those meant to be trained in vigilance or investigation fall prey to glaring blind spots, repeatedly convincing themselves of simple answers that gloss over the obvious. Someone could vanish in plain sight, and those nearby would more likely assume it was their imagination than question the reality before them. Loud noises, missing items, open doors, and other clear signs of disturbance are almost universally dismissed with vague reasoning like “it must have been the wind” or “I probably just misplaced it,” without deeper consideration.

Even when presented with mounting evidence, people struggle to connect dots outside their narrow understanding. Crimes can go unsolved for years under their noses, hidden passages remain undiscovered despite regular use, and strangers in obvious disguises can walk freely with little resistance.

Yet despite this broad dulling of personal perception, the overall growth of society, science, and progress is not significantly affected. The world still moves forward. Innovations are made, discoveries occur, and civilizations develop at a normal pace. The people’s practical intelligence remains intact when it comes to structured learning, engineering, medicine, and the construction of society.
objects.title: Must Have Been The Wind

objects.text:
Life force, anima, aura, vibe, chi- whatever you want to call it, all living things have a meta-energy that affects how hale and hearty they are. Larger, more complex, and more aware organisms tend to have far, far more life-force than smaller, simpler ones. The more Life force something has compared to its size and species, the healthier, stronger, and more robust that being becomes.

When living things die, or are in the process of dying, they leak and disperse their life-force into their surroundings. This can then be picked up and absorbed by other living organisms through a form of pseudo-osmosis. This process gets less efficient the higher the receiver's life-force compared to the energy released. The benefits of having more life force than average also eventually fall off, requiring more and more life force for an equivalent percentage of enhancement. 

Those who handle the slaughter or injuries of other living things naturally pick up more life force over time, and thus are stronger than others of the same species. Farmers, Fishers, Surgeons, Nurses, Torturers, and other similar professions become physically healthier and hardier over time. Serial killers, gladiators, soldiers, and hunters- especially those who do not use ranged weapons or traps- even more so.

Every purchase of this modifier increases the amount of life force an individual can have before they start experiencing negligible gains. With one purchase, people with high life-force live longer, are a bit stronger and healthier, and are more resistant to diseases. 
At two purchases, people and animals can acquire enough life-force to become distinctly superhuman. With the high end of humanity able to reach low super-soldier (Captain America) levels of enhancement.
At three purchases, becoming highly resistant to small arms fire is rare but not comepletely unheard of. With people at the high end of life-force enhancement scale able to lift and throw objects weighing several tons, face tank grenades, and live for a few hundred extra years.

If magic, or other supernatural energies and beings, exist in your world you should expect the maximum enhancement able to be reached via life force to be far higher.
objects.title: Quasi-Realistic Leveling

objects.text:
No one is quite sure of their origin. Some think it was alien visitors, others believe it was fallen Atlantis, or perhaps even a gift from god. All the same, humanity is host to powerful nanomachines so advanced they might as well be magic and have been for as long as man can remember. These machines enter the host during fetal development, interweaving into every cell of their being almost like artificial organelles, and grow and change with the host as they age.

The benefits of these nanomachines are manifold. First, they accelerate healing, rapidly repairing their hosts to the ‘standard body template’ such that physical birth defects and permanent injury are mere myth for humans, though not so fast that, say, a limb can be regrown in less than a year. They also improve the immune system such that only the strongest plagues have any hope of infecting someone and developing cancer is nearly impossible unless something has gone horribly wrong. This regeneration as a consequence allows for rapid gains from training and exercise, such that most career athletes reach modern olympic standards, and olympic athletes edge just slightly into superhuman territory (no more than a PRT Rating of 1-2 just from this).

Second, they form a powerful quantum network with each other, essentially creating a collective unconscious through which all skills and professions are contained, as well as interfacing with the brain to ensure that such data can passively be absorbed if desired. This means that, even without a teacher, any human can learn potentially any skill that someone, somewhere has created with enough effort and time, though having a teacher drastically accelerates the process, and talent still applies. Theoretically, a non-talented person can self-study to become a neurosurgeon in less than 20 years, 4 years with an experienced teacher or any natural talent, and 2 years with both. Also as a consequence, neuroplasticity drops off at a far slower pace than before, and degenerative neural diseases like Alzheimer's and Dementia are very rare.

Third, via the combination of inducing the continual creation of reserves of pluripotent stem cells, a comprehensive internal genetic database with the capacity to simulate any number of possible mutations, as well as the ability to edit DNA directly the nanomachines are capable of modifying their hosts in any number of ways, effectively allowing for elective personal evolution. From developing basic Traits such as night vision, cellulolysis, or denser bone tissue, to more dramatic Traits like cat ears, true homosexual or even asexual reproduction, ultradense muscles for effective superstrength, or the ability to change your own sex, to exotic Traits like novel organs in the hands that allow the host to shoot small lightning bolts, internal glands in the mouth for breathing napalm, secondary brains that act as backups in the event of brain damage and / or act as devoted internal computers, or even the ability to interface with the nanomachine network itself as a sort of debugger or admin. Traits gained from this ability can potentially reach a PRT Rating of 4 with enough time and effort (around 20 years of devoted growth).

Fourth, the previously listed abilities are all grouped together into a Class-Based System. Every human starts with a basic class selected upon turning 5 years old, such as Learner or Sketcher, which improves their talent for Skills and increases the rate at which they can adapt Traits related to that Class. Over time, these Classes can be upgraded, and new ones can be gained, streamlining the process of growth, with most adults having a minimum of 4 Classes, and at most 10 Classes. This System allows for the possibility of anyone potentially becoming a true omnidisciplinary scientist, a one man army soldier capable of fighting in literally any environment, a world leader without peer, or anything else they desire with enough effort with a maximum PRT Rating of 6 at 10 fully developed Classes, though most people peak at 5 Classes and settle long before reaching those heights.

The main drawback for this system is that in order to incentivize humanity to seek growth, the nanomachines will, upon a sufficient density of humans being present, seep out of their hosts and slowly congregate nearby to begin construction of Nests, enclosed areas that passively generate bioengineered monsters. These monsters naturally try to attack nearby human settlements upon reaching a certain concentration, though rarely in enough numbers to threaten to wipe them out completely if they are prepared. Upon death, they are rapidly deconstructed, with a portion of their mass converted into Loot such as rare minerals, special foods that can be eaten to accelerate Trait acquisition, consumable disks that act as instant downloads of certain rare skills, or even exotic metamaterials such as metals stronger and lighter than steel, high temperature superconductors, or liquids that rapidly speed up healing to an insane degree, with better Loot dropped by more dangerous monsters found in larger Nests.

You can decide how exactly this affects history and culture, whether the world is nearly the same on the surface somehow or some crazy alt history is up to you. Note that no matter how insane the abilities of these machines are, they are based purely on advanced technology. If any sort of supernatural system is already active then the nanomachines will interface with it and develop more esoteric abilities. For example, having Quasi-Realistic Leveling could lead to the possibility of developing Traits that streamline Life force absorption or allow the host to use it to power exotic powers like Ki attacks or healing others; or they could develop Traits that modify their Corona Gemma in such a way as to alter their power expression, eventually allowing someone like Clockblocker to freeze things within arms reach even if he’s not touching them; or they could add an internal interface allowing gods to more easily communicate with their followers and assign tasks to them while improving their ability to channel foreign energies to let magicians recover faster. How this all works is up to you.
objects.title: Quasi-Realistic Class-Based RPG System

objects.text:
A colossal island, long concealed from satellite scans and global awareness, has emerged in your world—an ancient land untouched by time, where evolution followed a forgotten path. Here, prehistoric life still thrives in full, roaring splendor. Towering sauropods trudge through lush valleys, massive theropods rule over dense jungles, and swarms of primeval insects cloud the skies like smoke. In colder regions, Pleistocene giants such as mammoths and sabertooths roam the tundra.

The local plant life is no less extraordinary. Towering ferns, oversized fungi, and alien flora from ancient epochs dominate the landscape, many bearing unusual chemical or energetic properties that defy modern understanding. Some are toxic, others medicinal—some seem almost... aware.

This island is a naturally occurring anomaly, a pocket of prehistory displaced in time and space. The size is comparable to a sprawling Jurassic archipelago, complete with varied biomes, from volcanic highlands and deep primeval swamps to vast open plains and monsoon-fed rainforests.

The creatures that dwell here are a striking blend of scientific realism and cinematic spectacle—evolutionarily plausible, yet awe-inspiring in their scale, color, and aggression. Their instincts are sharpened by eons of uninterrupted survival, making the ecosystem as deadly as it is majestic.
objects.title: The Lost Island

objects.text:
No matter how powerful your time-traveling abilities are—no matter how many timelines you access, how far back or forward you jump, how deeply you peer into the folds of existence—there is one universal constant: the timeline cannot be changed.

The multiverse plays fair, but fate does not.

When you attempt to alter significant historical, personal, or causality-defining events, reality corrects itself. If you kill a dictator before they rise to power, someone else takes their place and enacts the same atrocities. If you save a loved one from a tragic accident, they succumb to illness, violence, or coincidence shortly thereafter. You are not just resisted by causality. You are bound by it.

Your time travel still functions perfectly, but history always finds a way to assert itself.

You can learn from the past. You can even watch it. But you cannot change what it already decided.
objects.title: Threads of Inevitability

objects.text:
Something has damaged the fabric of reality, tearing holes in the dimensional walls which separate reality from the chaos which surrounds all worlds. This has led to the manifestation of Gates, portals formed by those holes connecting to loose “debris” in the multiverse, usually the remains of dead or decaying worlds which have since collapsed and left their contents to drift aimlessly. While most of these debris come from nameless worlds you’ve likely never heard of, some can be from worlds you do know, whether it be a dead copy of the world you’re in or even a world you’ve seen in fiction before.

The connection somewhat stabilizes these remnants, forming a pocket realm akin to a dungeon or demiplane. This realm’s makeup and contents are derived from the remnants, for example the remains of a dead RWBY timeline could contain Dust and Creatures of Grimm, or maybe some Faunus or Huntsman, driven mad and mutated by exposure to the void between worlds. Rarely you can even find survivors or even small civilizations who are still somewhat sane, having retained their minds either through sheer luck, power, strength of will, or somehow adapting to the exposure to the void.

However, the stability of Gates and their Dungeons is temporary, as the holes in reality are naturally prone to shifting. Once a Gate inevitably destabilizes, the pocket realm collapses, spitting out its contents into reality in an event known as a “Dungeon Break.” Alternatively, if the inhabitants of a Gate are cleared, either through being killed or somehow let out of the Gate, the lack of beings inside it removes the metaphysical weight holding the Dungeon in place, causing it to harmlessly disperse once no one is inside. This necessitates the clearing of Gates as soon as possible, entering them to slay the usually hostile inhabitants and close the Gate before it can spill its contents into the world.
objects.title: Dungeon Gates

objects.text:
Through intense training and mastery of martial arts, people—capes or otherwise—can learn techniques that allow for superhuman capabilities. These techniques, along with their associated martial arts, may also optionally originate from other settings.

For example: Total Concentration Breathing from Demon Slayer, or the Niko Style and its secret technique, Possessing Spirit from Kengan Ashura/Omega.

If the world does not possess supernatural powers, then the supernatural components of these techniques—such as techniques like Transparent World or the use of Ki (or any equivalent)—either do not exist, or are instead the result of heightened awareness and physical ability during near-death experiences, combined with hallucinations and synesthesia.
objects.title: Superhuman Martial Arts

objects.text:
Existence is no longer arranged as universes and omniverses stacked endlessly above one another. Every reality instead belongs to the Meta Manifold, a boundless framework containing every world, timeline, dimension, mythology, and possibility. Separate settings are not merged unless you want them to be merged. Each remains a distinct World with its own history, inhabitants, metaphysics, and laws.

The medium connecting them is the Sea Between, the extradimensional expanse through which inter-world travel and influence pass. Stable currents form routes between compatible or nearby Worlds, while distant shores may lie beyond storms, dead zones, and lightless abysses. Broken timelines, ruined realities, abandoned realms, and creatures able to survive outside conventional existence drift within its depths.

“World” is an umbrella term, not a measure of size. A Pocket Realm is a small, dependent reality attached to a creator, artifact, or larger World. A Realm-class World is limited in scope but independent. A Universe-class World contains a universe with its connected timelines, heavens, hells, underworlds, spiritual planes, and subordinate dimensions. A Multiverse-class World contains numerous universes and parallel histories governed by a shared origin or higher structure. A Cosmos-class World may contain multiple multiverses, conceptual domains, higher planes, or realities beyond ordinary space and time, yet remains one coherent patch rather than another Meta Manifold.

Worlds may also have structural relationships or traits. An Anchor World supports attached Satellite Realms, while a World Cluster consists of independent Worlds joined by unusually strong currents. Parallel Worlds arise from divergent histories and may remain clustered or drift apart. A Nexus World, such as Little Garden, stands where innumerable currents converge and serves as a crossroads between distant realities. Worlds may also be Sealed, Wandering, Artificial, Parasitic, Predatory, Dead, Shattered, or Nascent. These describe condition or behavior, not size, and several may apply at once.

All dimensional and inter-world travel is retroactively adapted to this cosmology. Portals, teleportation, summoning, divine paths, technological gates, reality breaches, and similar effects navigate the Sea Between rather than tearing through stacked dimensional walls. Their appearance, speed, range, functions, and protections remain intact. Reliable powers follow stable currents and may cross almost instantaneously, while uncontrolled or deliberately uncharted travel risks becoming lost, reaching the wrong shore, or encountering the Sea’s hazards.

Your possessions, pocket dimensions, divine territories, artifacts, and gateways adapt as well. Pocket realms retain their functions but gain stable moorings; breaches become routes across the Sea; creating or expanding a reality establishes or enlarges territory within the manifold. Nothing is weakened merely because its method changes.

For you, this structure is an advantage. You instinctively distinguish an internal realm from another World, recognize familiar currents, and understand how your abilities interact with the Sea. Established routes cost less energy and make travel smoother, safer, and more accurate. With experience, you may chart currents, establish passages, anchor or relocate pocket realms, locate hidden Worlds, conceal your course, and guide others. Greater mastery lets you leave known routes and survive crossings that would strand lesser travelers, but grants no authority over other Worlds or their inhabitants.
objects.title: Meta Manifold Reality

objects.text:
At the center of the Meta Manifold, where every current of the Sea Between converges, stands the **Eldritch Court**. Azathoth is revealed as creator or ruler of the entire Manifold: an awakened sovereign who shaped its Worlds, laws, possibilities, and Sea from boundless chaos. No local Root, divine order, or system native to one World stands above the Court.

Beside Azathoth stands Yog-Sothoth, companion and confidant, the Gate and the Key. Yog-Sothoth touches every boundary, current, entrance, timeline, and connection. Azathoth defines the highest order while Yog-Sothoth preserves continuity. Local cosmologies govern themselves, but the Court may overrule anything threatening the Manifold or defying its fundamental laws.

The Court has changed the Outer Gods, Great Old Ones, and lesser eldritch races. No longer compelled toward senseless destruction, they can experience curiosity, restraint, loyalty, affection, and love. They may teach, protect civilizations, form families, or wear survivable avatars. Alien grandeur is no longer inseparable from cruelty.

They have not become human, harmless, or reliably benevolent. An eldritch god may love a city yet preserve it outside time, transform its people into a collective, or annihilate anything deemed a threat. Blessings may mutate, knowledge erode identity, and comfort drown a region in shared dreams. Even kindness passes through minds that may not understand autonomy, freedom, or mortal proportion.

The Court enforces limited peace. Its subjects cannot destroy the Meta Manifold, consume the Sea Between, or exterminate creation. Beneath that threshold, they retain their hungers, rivalries, cults, experiments, and purposes. They may wage conflicts through civilizations, reshape Worlds to prove a principle, claim species as children, or punish insults across generations. The Court prevents cosmic collapse, not mortals becoming pieces in divine games. Nyarlathotep and similarly malicious beings remain cruel and exploit every freedom permitted.

Earth gains the **Nexus** trait regardless of its World class. Countless currents now connect it to eldritch Worlds, sealed realms, and the Court. Dreams, artifacts, cults, summons, and incursions become commonplace. Some bring allies; others unleash predators, revelations, warped environments, or divine battles.

You bear the Court’s resonance. Eldritch beings notice your dreams, creations, companions, and travel. Favor brings obligations, jealousy, and enemies. Rejecting a gift may offend; accepting one may create an unintended bond. Entities may compete to guide, adopt, study, marry, transform, protect, or possess you. You gain no authority over them, and affection need not respect your wishes.

If you possess **The Creator**, that deity becomes steward of your World and its representative before the Court, not creator of the Manifold. A **Half-Eldritch Child’s** progenitor gains familial love but remains alien, independent, and potentially possessive or they can change to be more human. Eldritch companions replace their alternatives and retain their loyalty; other beings do not become allies or convenient duplicates.

The Manifold is more orderly, not safer. Predators hunt its currents, shattered Worlds leak impossible laws, hostile gods test the Court’s limits, and good intentions can cause catastrophe. Mortals may find wonder, kinship, or love before the incomprehensible, but any encounter may still end in transformation, madness, or servitude.

Court decrees reach all Worlds. Local powers may exploit their wording or test limits, but cannot nullify them.

You may choose eldritch forms, presentations, and genders, but not non-companions’ loyalty or disposition. Most can be neutral or kind; none are guaranteed to practice either safely. You can also choose to change the eldritch beings to be more human if you wish, but they are Eldritch so they can only change so much. Keep in mind yes, the Eldritch can be kinder, safer, and more human, but they are still eldritch, and there are still Eldritch Gods and Beings that are not changed.
objects.title: Eldritch Court Manifold

objects.text: A confluence means a merging or meeting of multiple flows. At the center of the Manifold, where every current of the Sea Between meets, resides the greatest Confluence of all: the Divine Confluence. The Divine Confluence serves as a neutral meeting ground for the Gods of the Manifold, functioning as a cosmic agora, divine council chamber, or crossroads between pantheons. Gods who would otherwise belong to completely incompatible cosmologies can meet, converse, form alliances, exchange knowledge, settle disputes, or simply observe one another. Most of the Supreme Godheads spend the majority of their time here, as it is the only "place"—however loosely that term applies—that can both contain them and allow them to interact with their peers. However, the Lesser and Greater Godheads are not excluded. A Godhead does not need to abandon its native World to reach the Confluence. Instead, its divine presence extends into the Sea Between, allowing it to manifest there while its true existence remains anchored to its own World. It is up to your discretion whether there is a Supreme Authority presiding over the Confluence. If a Supreme Authority is included, they will be the ruler and potentially even the creator of the Manifold itself, with their word becoming the law that all others must follow. Whether you elevate an existing pantheon to this position or make it a custom entity or group is left to your preferences. Elevating an existing pantheon may cause it to be changed in a manner similar to what happens in the Eldritch Court Manifold modifier. Speaking of which, if said modifier is selected, Azathoth will automatically become the Supreme Authority of the Confluence, and the Confluence itself will be merged into the "Eldritch Court."
objects.title: The Divine Confluence

objects.text: Your World becomes an Imaginary World, governed by the Imaginary Tree and Sea of Quanta. Its contents determine whether it is Universe-, Multiverse-, or Cosmos-class, but it remains a single World within the Meta Manifold. Other Worlds and the Sea Between remain unchanged. The Tree determines which realities possess enough coherence to endure. Stable universes and timelines grow as leaves, while damaged, contradictory, defeated, or pruned realities fall into the Sea of Quanta as bubble worlds and broken possibilities. This local Sea lies beneath your Tree, while the Sea Between separates your World from independent Worlds. Every universe, timeline, afterlife, dimension, and attached realm enters this system. Leaves may remain separate or merge where their laws permit. Routes allow inhabitants, factions, gods, technologies, and supernatural forces to cross between them. These routes can be guarded or obstructed, but cannot be permanently abolished while both leaves survive. If you choose The Tree and the Sea, things are relatively straightforward. However, if you possess any of the Hoyoverse settings, they are incorporated as their actual worlds and histories, not copies, simulations, or recreations. Their genuine inhabitants, factions, powers, relationships, conflicts, and consequences remain authentic and independent. You may influence the Tree's initial arrangement and decide whether compatible realities begin separate or fused, but you cannot selectively remove inconvenient elements. With Honkai: Star Rail, Aeons, Paths, Stellarons, Imaginary–Quantum phenomena, and conflicts over destiny spread throughout the Tree. With Honkai Impact 3rd, Honkai becomes a World-wide pressure; Herrschers, Stigmata, collapse events, and evolutionary trials may emerge on suitable leaves. Multiple owned settings combine rather than replace one another. Aeons may interact with Herrschers, Paths may influence Stigmata, and fallen leaves may carry Stellarons or Honkai corruption. Possessing both incorporates the wider Hoyoverse as a World Cluster containing its main universes, variants, side worlds, and lesser realities. After establishment, the Tree and Sea operate autonomously. You cannot simply declare a threatened leaf stable, restore a fallen reality, deactivate an unwanted system, or deny discovered routes to enemies. Internal travel follows the Tree and Sea of Quanta, while reaching independent Worlds requires crossing the Sea Between. Existing travel powers retain their functions and protections. If you possess The Creator, they establish and steward the Tree. Whether they rule absolutely or only in part is left to your preferences. In the latter case, they may cultivate branches, stabilize leaves, alter routes, and guide development, but must expend power and overcome resistance. Instability can produce anomalies or failing laws, giving you time to save a leaf; restoring one that has already fallen requires extraordinary effort. You may also fuse any other settings you possess into this World. They will merge naturally into the cosmology in the most appropriate way, while retaining their relevant elements and characteristics.
objects.title: Imaginary World

addons.title: The Akashic Tree
addons.text: Akasha becomes the foundation of the Imaginary Tree, uniting your Nasuverse with the genuine Hoyoverse (presuming you didn't only pick The Tree and the Sea) within one World. The Root originates and records all phenomena, while the Tree structures its possibilities and determines which realities can endure. Universes, timelines, Textures, afterlives, Parallel Worlds, and attached realms grow as leaves and branches. Defeated, pruned, contradictory, or unstable histories descend into the Sea of Quanta as bubble worlds and fragments while remaining recorded within Akasha. The Sea of Quanta lies beneath the Tree and receives your World’s fallen realities. It remains distinct from the Sea Between, which surrounds your World and separates it from the independent Worlds of the Meta Manifold. Falling into the former remains within your cosmology; crossing the latter leaves it. If you've obtained the Hoyoverse, it will be its genuine version that occupies the Tree, with its inhabitants, histories, factions, powers, conflicts, and consequences remaining authentic and independent. Aeons and Paths cross branches, Stellarons infect leaves, Honkai pressures civilizations, Herrschers rise, Stigmata awaken, and bubble worlds drift through the Sea of Quanta. Nothing becomes a copy or obedient recreation. The Nasuverse exists in the form established through Akasha. Only the settings, routes, people, events, threats, and systems accepted into the Foundation belong here; excluded material never existed. Everything retained is genuine and independent. Gaia, Alaya, the Counter Force, Textures, the Reverse Side, Inner Sea, Throne of Heroes, Quantum Time Locks, Singularities, and Lostbelts retain their functions. The systems interact naturally. Servants may cross leaves, Paths influence Heroic Spirits, Honkai tests planetary Textures, and the Counter Force may oppose a Stellaron or Herrscher threatening Human Order. Singularities can become diseased branches, Lostbelts isolated leaves, and pruned histories bubble worlds still recorded within the Root. Second Magic, Rayshifting, Imaginary–Quantum travel, and compatible methods gain routes through this structure. Travel within a leaf follows native laws. Passage between leaves may use the Tree, Sea of Quanta, or equivalent abilities; reaching an independent World still requires crossing the Sea Between. Existing travel powers retain their functions and protections. Other realities joined to your World settle naturally into the Tree as leaves, Textures, Parallel Worlds, attached realms, or independent branches. Their inhabitants, histories, and metaphysics remain intact, while contradictions reconcile beneficially without erasing essential identities. Alternate selves may remain separate or merge into a united history when you deliberately choose. Note: Unrelated settings may be merged into one main World if you wish.

objects.text: Your World is rebuilt around an Akashic Foundation, a local expression of the Root from which every phenomenon in your selected Nasuverse continuity originates and ultimately returns. It governs only your World, not the Meta Manifold or Sea Between, and grants no automatic access to the true Akasha, which resides in a different World. The Foundation creates whatever retained material requires: Gaia, Alaya, the Counter Force, planetary Textures, the Reverse Side, the Inner Sea, the Throne of Heroes, Parallel Worlds, Quantum Time Locks, and more. Existing afterlives, pantheons, planetary wills, and cosmologies may coexist with this framework as initially decided. How much of the Nasuverse is incorperated in your Foundation is up to your discretion. You curate its initial scope: the entire Nasuverse, most of it, or selected settings, routes, timelines, people, events, threats, and systems. Disliked material may be omitted, favored continuities may form a single history or remain Parallel Worlds, and excluded material simply never belonged to your version. Everything retained is real, independent, and fully integrated. Once finalized, you cannot erase people, civilizations, or enemies simply because they inconvenience you. Later additions bring their authentic histories, consequences, and threats; removing them afterward requires sufficient reality-altering power. Curation may reconcile contradictions, but cannot reduce retained people to idealized or automatically loyal versions of themselves. Fate/Grand Order may add Chaldea, Singularities, Lostbelts, Servants, Beasts, the Alien God, CHALDEAS, ORT, and selected crises. You may replace Ritsuka or exist as another Master when appropriate. Fate/stay night adds its Holy Grail Wars, Servants, magi, the Church, Dead Apostles, and selected routes, which may remain Parallel Worlds or merge where compatible. Tsukihime allows you to choose its Original, Remake, or Melty Blood continuity and retain its people, factions, mysteries, and struggle for Primacy as desired. You may also incorporate Kara no Kyoukai, Mahoutsukai no Yoru, Fate/Extra, Fate/Apocrypha, Fate/strange Fake, Fate/Prototype, Notes, and other works. Settings reconcile through Parallel Worlds, timelines, and Textures. Shared characters may remain alternate selves or become a single person with merged histories, memories, relationships, and abilities. The Foundation governs divergence, pruning, Singularities, summoning, and internal travel. Gaia, Alaya, and the Counter Force remain independent, while retained factions continue pursuing their own goals. The Second Magic(the local version, which is based on the Foundation), Rayshifting, and equivalent systems operate internally; reaching an independent World requires crossing the Sea Between. The Root remains inaccessible unless another choice provides a means of reaching it. If you possess The Creator, they establish and steward the Foundation. They may arrange Textures, mediate between Gaia and Alaya, and repair instability, but cannot become the Root or gain absolute control over every inhabitant. Note that you can fuse any other settings you possess into this World, and they will merge naturally and in the most appropriate way.
objects.title: Akashic Foundation

objects.text:
Somehow, everyone are ponies. Cartoon ponies. How does that even work? Hell if I know. 

The world does seem a little more peaceful, however, as if you had the Cops and Robber and Benign choices from this section.
objects.title: My Little Parahuman, Conflict is Magic!

addons.text:
The destructive nature of magical girls is tempered. While magical girls still have great power, nothing too bad ever lasts. There's always the right power to undo the destruction of a city, heal a terrible wound or save innocents caught in the crossfire. Drama happens, tears are shed, but at the end of the day there will be a happy ending. Even when someone does die, it's in a way that means something, such as a great heroic sacrifice. 

Heroes are in a far better place, as the bonds they create with their friends help them overcome their trauma. Elite parahuman academies such as Arcadia High are particularly favored by shards, who nudge their hosts to form strong bonds there. This likewise influences their shards, which reduces any negative influences from their shard and increases compatibility with their power. Shards grow fond of their hosts and treasure them, and will even expend a great amount of energy to save a host from death. Villains can be turned into heroes through friendship, and those that do stay villains are more likely than not to find redemption eventually. Not even the Endbringers or Scion can overcome this, and may possibly be changed like any other villain.

As a side effect of this, powers that can heal are much more common. It's now possible but uncommon to trigger with a power solely dedicated to healing.
addons.title: Shoujo World

objects.text:
This world is... strange. 

Most of the world's Parahuman population are women, and less than 1% of Triggers are men. Most of the canon characters have mysteriously changed to match. Parahuman crime is prevalent but somehow softer (as if you had the Cops and Robber and Benign choices from this section).

When a Parahuman Triggers, their appearance changes to make them more attractive. This manifests by smoothing out imperfections and changing the body towards a more ideal state. Nearly all Parahumans look like actors or models after a round with Photoshop (you are affected by this as well). Due to this, a large amount of Parahumans have paper-thin secret identities. Case 53s are all unusually attractive as well despite their monstrous appearance.

Dotted all over the world are Elite Parahuman Academies, of which Arcadia High in Brockton Bay is part of, which provides young Parahumans with a number of hero courses in addition to the normal ones offered in most schools. These academies all have a large number of clubs, the Hero club being the most popular, as well as a strangely powerful student council. The uniform is also mandatory and has uncomfortable short skirts even in the dead of winter. It is rumored that Villains have a secret academy as well.

While the Endbringers still exist they are less of an existential threat to civilization, still as hard to kill, however. Scion will go nuts at some point but his defeat (one way or another) is more or less assured. 

(This alternate world runs on Anime logic, prepare for a lot of shenanigans)
objects.title: High School Worm x Worm

objects.text:
This world operates on Anime Logic. 

Individuals often find themselves shouting and expending great effort to activate and power up their abilities, reminiscent of shonen heroes from popular anime. 

Likewise, time may run abnormally, as a fight that should last only five minutes can feel like multiple episodes of an anime to the participants. Adults in this world often appear younger than their actual age, another common anime trope. 

Furthermore, people may have unusual and vibrant hair colors, and individuals display amazing feats of strength, such as a normal girl being able to slam a person through a wall while in a state of embarrassment. This doesn’t affect the world much, since darker tropes are also brought in to balance it out.
objects.title: Anime Logic

addons.text:
The world now carries the quiet weight of a storybook—a place where happy endings are not just possible, but gently expected. Life unfolds with the rhythm of fairy tales, where sincere dreams, honest efforts, and heartfelt love have a real chance of shaping destiny. Struggles still exist, but the world leans toward resolution, healing, and joy. It feels as though life itself favors those who pursue kindness, hope, and connection, gently guiding them toward moments of beauty and fulfillment.

Villains and monsters remain, but they are no longer inevitable tragedies. They are storybook threats—still dangerous, but capable of being overcome through courage, cleverness, and sometimes, redemption. Even the most broken can be reached by honest compassion. Death and loss are not erased, but they are extraordinarily rare, and when they come, the world tends to offer second chances, unexpected survivals, or paths to peace. Conflict resolves like a well-told tale, where endings may be hard-won but are almost always worth the journey.

The world itself seems quietly enchanted. Fortunate coincidences, meaningful encounters, and poetic justice happen more often, though never in a way that feels forced. Wishes made with true belief can matter, and even the grandest threats can sometimes be softened, not by overwhelming force, but by the strength of human hearts. This is still a world of struggle, but now it feels like a story where, more often than not, the good can win and happiness is something real people can reach.
addons.title: Fairytale

addons.text: The subtle improvements from Just Better no longer stop at everyday conveniences. The quiet refinements that made life smoother now extend to the world’s larger, more daunting problems. Wars, poverty, disease, environmental decline—these major issues still exist, but they have been significantly scaled down in scope, intensity, and frequency. They are no longer overwhelming, ever-present forces but challenges that can now be managed, mitigated, and meaningfully addressed by those willing to try. Conflicts still occur, but diplomacy and peaceful resolutions have become far more common and successful. Global health crises are swiftly handled with improved medical systems and better cooperation between nations. Poverty, while not eradicated, is drastically reduced, with more stable economies, accessible education, and wider social support preventing many from falling through the cracks. Even environmental problems, while still a concern, are met with smarter technologies, more responsible leadership, and societies that actively work toward sustainable solutions. The world feels like it is not just improving—it is actively healing. Solutions are within reach, and people have the will, resources, and coordination to pursue them. Problems are no longer insurmountable obstacles; they are challenges that can be worked through, step by step. The tone remains hopeful, the pace steady, and the progress visible. The world is not perfect, but now, it is not just better—it is even greater, and its people truly have the chance to build something lasting.
addons.title: Even Greater

objects.text:
The world is a happier place.

Parahumans still experience traumatic events that trigger their powers, but they don’t let them define or destroy them. They heal from their wounds and learn from their mistakes. They use their abilities for good and join the ranks of heroes more often than villains. Crime is less violent and more playful, like a game of cops and robbers. Even the most hardened criminals can be swayed by a heartfelt speech or a sincere apology. Death is rare even when facing the monstrous Endbringers that threaten the world. And even in the case of death, there might be people who somehow survive to come back.

Even the Entities can be persuaded to change their ways. By coming across the Humans of Earth, they feel curiosity, wonder, admiration, and even affection for these creatures that display such diversity and creativity. It realizes that there is more to life than just survival and optimization. While they have yet to fully abandon the Cycle, they will not destroy Earth when they finish and instead just leave. Even if you do not convince them, another great hero may convince Scion.

By being convinced to stay, the Entities learn to feel emotions from the Parahumans, and in doing so, discover a new meaning for their existence. The Entities help Parahumans overcome their challenges and achieve their dreams. They share their joy and sorrow with them, and in turn, receive their gratitude and love. And maybe, they could learn the secrets of negentropy together.

(Taking A Brighter World is as if you had the Cops and Robber, Benign, and Soft Trigger choices from this section).
objects.title: A Brighter World

objects.text:
Humanity is much more scientifically advanced in Earth Bet, to the point where they have a galactically spanning civilization. There are many non-human intelligent species, many of which you'll recognize from fiction, but others you will not. None of these aliens will have inherent superpowers that make them stronger than a below-average Parahuman, but they will be able to trigger. Humans trigger more commonly than any other species.
The ratio of Parahumans to humans and aliens is the same as it was on Earth Bet.
All 20 Endbringers are active and instead of raving cities, they ravage whole planets.
objects.title: Galactic

objects.text:
Civilization has grown to a multiversal level, with aliens from different worlds possessing innate superpowers. These powers are equal or weaker than below-average Parahuman powers. These aliens can also trigger, gaining superhuman abilities similar to those on Earth Bet. The ratio of Parahumans to humans and aliens is similar to that on Earth Bet. All Parahumans also have the Pocket Shard perk.

However, all the Endbringers are also active and have the ability to ravage entire solar systems instead of just cities. Unlike on Earth Bet, these Endbringers have the ability to disappear into a pocket dimension to recuperate. They can create various minions that resembles them to attack first. After a while, the Endbringer will appear, coming out of their personal dimension. Even after the Endbringer leaves, the minions will remain to continue their assault.
objects.title: Multiversal

objects.text:
Your Earth is connected to Earth Bet in the same way that Earth Aleph is connected to it. Due to this, people from your world can be experimented on by Cauldron or even drawn into Earth Bet through other means, according to the plot of Worm. This also means that should the Entity destroy the local multiverse, your earth will also be destroyed. Furthermore, all knowledge about Worm will be replaced by a similar novel with similar popularity in your world.

(Taking this allows you to return to your earth without Homecoming)
objects.title: Connected

objects.text:
Earth Bet doesn't seem different on the surface, but in the right place, at the right time, you'll learn that what one would consider part of classic horror exists on Earth Bet, such as Vampires in Transylvania, a deadly shapeshifter in Antarctica, a strange but dangerous blob in Pennsylvania, Vengeful Ghosts, rare zombie outbreaks, mad scientists, and the occasional Slasher. 

However, things aren't necessarily as bad as they seem. Not only do these creatures all have weaknesses, but the supernatural exists outside of simple monsters, such as fortunetellers, psychics, and voodoo practitioners giving warning and aid against even the likes of the Endbringers and Entities.
objects.title: Horror Bet

objects.text:
While still rare, there now exists a wide variety of supernatural beings throughout your starting world, including:

Ghosts, Poltergeists, Demons that possess humans or inanimate objects such as dolls, Vengeful spirits, Werewolves, Vampires, Wendigos, Tulpas, Golems, The Boogeyman, Yōkai, Banshees, Pagan monsters, Fay, Changelings, Skinwalkers, Ghouls and much much more.

As well as practitioners of many different forms of magic—such as Voodoo, Paganism, Witchcraft, Romanian, Kabbalah, Asceticism, Satanism. Cults that worship Demons or Pagan gods.

There are also anomalous or cursed items, such as keys that, when inserted into any door with a keyhole, can become a portal to any other door in the world, or summon an “echo” of a deceased person. Other objects include a comb capable of stopping time, or a pen that can microwave people, among many others.

In addition, there are legendary artefacts such as Excalibur, Gram, the Eye of Ra, the Holy Grail, the Ark of the Covenant, the Shroud of Turin and many more.

While this makes the world significantly more dangerous, the general threat rating of these beings or items does not usually exceed a PRT threat rating of 1–5, with only rare cases reaching a maximum of 6-7. Most of these entities are hidden to the wider world and prefer to avoid attracting too much attention.

In response, there are individuals and organisations dedicated to dealing with supernatural threats, including ghost hunters, exorcists, monster hunters, specialised government divisions that seek to capture or eliminate them and more.
objects.title: Supernatural Files

addons.text:
The pantheons' emergence and their overarching mythologies elevated the creation of new fields of study for the Arcane, Mages enriching themselves from the resurgence of the world's mysteries and the soaring wellspring of magical energy at their return, and, most importantly, the revival of Applied Theology, a venerable yet forsaken field of magic, most commonly known as Divine Magic. Partakers like Paladins, Priests, and Clerics regain their standing, empowered by Gods of their choosing they never required the same rigorous academic training and research normal mages usually lived through (although, it did help immensely) so long as their faith stood strong, and remained on their gods' favor.

High Priests, once and forever, are recognized as Divine Magic's strongest users whose power is in the same class as most Sages, with the chance of potentially, and temporarily, becoming leagues above them if their Patron answers a prayer for aid
addons.title: Applied Theology

objects.text: The land of myth and legend is now a reality in this world. From the powerful and noble Thor to the wise and cunning Zeus, the ancient gods of yore have returned, walking openly among humanity for the first time since their supposed passing. Along with these legendary figures, other fantastical beings such as monsters like Fafnir and Typhon have also emerged from the shadows, roaming freely in the world in all their terrible splendor. This comes with various dimensions such as heaven, hell, Tartarus, and more. While this new reality has left many in awe, it has also introduced a host of challenges and dangers to this world, as these beings have the power and capacity to disrupt the world's delicate balance, and it will take all the strength and cunning mankind can muster to survive this new age of myth and magic.
objects.title: Mythology

objects.text:
The supernatural world and the mortal realm co-exist in separate dimensions. Despite this separation, the supernatural has found ways to touch the mortal world, often through reincarnation. Reincarnation is a process whereby a supernatural entity leaves a small part of its essence within a human or animal body, which slowly awakens the powers and abilities they left behind. This process can take years, or even decades, but as the individual's powers awakened, they will slowly remember their past life, not entirely, but enough to affect their personallity and know who they are the reincarnation of.

The reincarnated are known as the Awakened, and they are often viewed with fear and suspicion, as their powers can be difficult to control, and their memories of past lives can sometimes cause them to act unpredictably. Most Awakened are far stonger than ordinary Parahumans, simply due to the fact that most of their abilities are conceptual in nature.

The Awakened animals are primarily reincarnated from mythical monsters such as the Chimera, the Fenrir, or even Fafnir. The reincarnated animals often inherit the traits and abilities of their previous mythological forms, and some even retain parts of their memories, giving them a unique perspective on the mortal and supernatural worlds. Some will help protect humanity, but many will also seek to destroy it.

Note that it is possible for multiple reincarnations of the same being to exist at once, although that would mean they will embody different parts of their core aspects, for example; having 12 different Hercules for each of his labors.
objects.title: Reincarnation

objects.text:
The Age of Gods has long passed, and most of the supernatural world is gone. Only a few gods remain, weakened and hunted. The Entities see them as both a Threat and a subject of study. 

The gods remain in hiding, and even their strongest can only match an Endbringer.

Magic based powers will be weaker in this world, and shards will have a natural resistance to them.
objects.title: Dying Gods

objects.text:
The End is nigh.

Seeing the Entities, the Gods decided that the world was to be pruned.

The Norse will begin Ragnarok, the Christians will begin Judgement Day, etc… 

At the beginning, the gods will only send their armies, as it will be tiring to manifest in the mortal world. 

Each Chief of the Pantheon will be as strong as Scion (the avatar) when manifesting.
objects.title: Ragnarok

objects.text:
The world has begun to stir with faint traces of the supernatural. Magic exists, but it lingers just beneath the surface—subtle, quiet, and often unnoticed by the masses. Low-level spells, mystical races, and supernatural creatures have started to appear, their presence woven carefully into the fabric of everyday life.

If magic or the supernatural already had a place in the world, this shift amplifies it. Their influence grows, and weaker, more common variants begin to emerge. However, this expansion only adds to the world’s arcane depth—it does not diminish the power or rarity of the original forces.

Depending on the setting’s foundation, this evolution may gradually shift the tone toward Urban Fantasy, where the mystical blends with the modern to preserve narrative cohesion.
objects.title: Low Fantasy

addons.text:
With the arrival of the Demon Lord Scion, even if the world does not know of his true nature, a prophecy was born. A Hero, blessed with a holy blade will one day be born, having the strength necessary to slay him. This prophecy spread like wildfire across the lands, whispered in the taverns of bustling cities and sung by the bards in quiet villages.

Scion is too apathetic to look for this Hero, however, he will fight with all he has should the Hero face him. Cauldron actively seeks the Hero, to both protect and nurture them.
addons.title: The Grand Quest

objects.text: Humanity has reached an understanding of the world. They have learned to interact with this mysterious energy known as Mana and know how to weave it into spells of power. Schools like Arcadia are schools made to teach and cultivate skilled Mages. Parahumans are considered weird Mages who have abnormal innate spells, and everyone can cast spells. Magic is a common tool, and technology has advanced with a fusion of magic and science. Esoteric capabilities are common in higher levels of magic. The strongest of the Mages are known as Sages, each being extremely powerful and equal to S-Class threats simply due to their sheer power, understanding of magic, and experience. Most Sages can be considered ancient, using magic to either extend their lives or transform themselves into something more than humans.
objects.title: High Fantasy

addons.text:
One day, a natural prodigious Esper will be born. They will reach LEVEL 5, what many consider the peak of what humanity can naturally gain, with the only supposed exception being Scion. This prodigy will then Trigger, pushing past humanity's limitations and becoming the LEVEL 6. They will pave the way to further growth, helping others follow in their footsteps. This prodigy will be instrumental in the survival of humanity should Scion begin his rampage on Earth.

For years, Cauldron prepared for the arrival of this Esper, aware of their existence thanks to a precognitive Esper that foretold their importance.
addons.title: Mythical LEVEL 6

objects.text: Humanity has reached an understanding of the mind. They have learned to interact with this mysterious energy known as Psionics and know how to wield them to cast supernatural effects. Schools like Arcadia are schools made to teach and cultivate skilled espers, improving their psionic energy. Parahumans are considered weird Espers who have abnormal psionics and everyone can wield psionics. The strength of espers are measured by LEVELs, the more psionic energy one has the greater their LEVEL. Due to the nature of psionic energy, people with higher psionic energy also have heightened mental capabilities. Due to this, science and society itself has improved. The highest LEVEL an Esper has ever reached is LEVEL 5, and at that strength it is not wrong to think of them as S-Class threats, both due to their sheer power and their intelligence.
objects.title: Esper Earth

objects.text:
Humanity has reached an understanding of Heaven. They have learned to interact with this mysterious energy known as Qi and know how to cultivate it for greater powers.

Schools like Arcadia are known as lesser or subordinate Sects to bigger ones like PRT. Parahumans are considered weird Cultivators who have abnormal bloodline abilities and everyone can cultivate. While Scion and the Endbringers still exist, it is more of a question of how long they will live than any real threat.
objects.title: The Path to Heavens

addons.text: Arcadia is now one of the few prestigious schools in the USA that teaches cultivation both aiding Parahumans along their path and helping normal mortals learn the basics.
addons.title: Cultivator High

addons.text:
The Entities are a race of extremely powerful cultivators that have monopolized the resources of the realm directly above humanity, send Shards of themselves to gather spiritual information from lower beings, and plan to combine together into a single Entity at the end of the multiverse in order to maximize their power as they ascend to the next realm. Fortunately spiritual practices have been practiced before the Entities got to where they are and as such there are those who have ascended to higher realms before the Entities like the Buddha and Sun Wukong. 

While this does mean that there are benevolent higher beings hostile towards the Entities, resulting in circumstances like what happened with Eden and Khepri, the sheer number of Entities and the comparative size between Entities and those beings makes their trying to interact with them comparable to a normal human trying to interact with individual germs without causing undue harm, and what is worse is that some of those higher beings can be considered malicious towards lower beings, albeit the difference between malice and lack of care can be hard to tell on this scale.
addons.title: Always a Higher Realm

addons.text: The difference between a galaxy and a planet is meaningless to these entities so in order to reap the most reward from this cycle the entities upgraded the spirituality of every planet within the Milky Way across the local multiverse. (With the Milky Way for some reason having previously generated nearly zero excess qi that could be used for cultivation across the multiverse.)
addons.title: Galactic Cultivation

addons.text:
The knowledge of cultivation is also in the hands of the animal kingdom. They have used the power of qi to strike back at humanity and claim swaths of land and formed their own dynasties and continue to wage war against mankind.

Thankfully for humanity, they have also begun to fight amongst themselves in their pursuit of more power. This is about the same amount of conflict as there is between human nations, meaning they may even be willing to team up with humans if they believe one of their rivals to be enough of a threat. This is rather rare however, as their own cultivation has turned them into an excellent resource for humanity and vice versa. It is however more common in animals that humanity has treated as companions throughout history such as cats and dogs.
