Interestingly, due to the knowledge of cultivation coming from humanity, beast cultivators end up becoming more humanlike the higher their realm, with some even becoming indistinguishable from a regular human at first glance. This does not fundamentally remove their animalistic mindset, but they can easily learn about human’s way of thinking, some even using it for espionage. They don’t lose their animal origins however, and instead learn to either become a full beast again or a hybrid between the two depending on their needs.
addons.title: Beast Cultivators

objects.text:
While superficially similar to canon worm, for example, possessing the same people on a modern earth, during the same time period, along with the appearance of heroes and villains, there are a number of differences. For example, instead of “just” being based on advanced physics and alien physiology, entities and shards in general are also cultivators who gather, generate, and manipulate qi to fuel and accomplish their abilities.

Qi is also not restricted to just entities and their shards; instead, it is a universal phenomenon, with humanity having the misfortune of evolving on a planet with too little spirituality to generate much excess qi for cultivators to develop. In order to rectify this, the entities have sacrificed a large number of resources to upgrade the earth’s spirituality across the local multiverse. Increasing the excess qi the environment generates to levels cultivators can thrive and develop in, even separate from a shard, while developing spiritual beasts and rare cultivation resources.

Learning from what they could study from parahumans and environmental qi, humanity has achieved a basic understanding of qi cultivation that is taught to normal mortals in several different schools worldwide in various different ways.

This qi-based education being available for regular humans to learn and become cultivators in their own right and potentially, with decades or centuries of development, be able to match parahumans in strength has led to a great number of societal differences from canon Worm, some subtle and some very obvious. For example, graduates of a cultivation school often find work in their government’s military if they aren’t press-ganged into it. For example, the PRT has tens of thousands of normal human cultivators in its ranks spread across America, serving the various roles the organization needs from them.

Though not all governments force cultivators to work for them, when governments try, they aren’t always successful. For example, in America, a country that grants non-criminal cultivators much freedom, it isn’t uncommon for the average city to have a couple of “loose” cultivators who find work by providing services only a cultivator can provide, like slaying a nearby dangerous spirit beast, selling spiritual herbs they found or grew themselves, and even things like breaking apart qi-infused materials that are too tough for normal humans to do anything about that get in the way of city development.

Parahumans work by having their shards feed them knowledge, instincts, and a steady stream of the right type of qi in order to use their shards abilities that they can then cultivate to further develop their abilities in new and unique ways while also growing stronger in general, though entities are stronger to compensate.

The cycle is extended to be a hundred times longer than canon. This includes the time until the remaining entity goes on a rampage, not taking into account your actions or the effects of any other options.

If your power source is shard-based, then your powers also operate under these principles, while if they are shardless, you can choose whether your abilities are at least partially qi-based.
objects.title: Immortal Journey of the Earth

objects.text:
What... is a Star?

In the past Stars were said to be something that littered the pitch-dark sky in beautiful patterns. But scientists believe they were making it up. As Stars or even other planets don't even exist. Just the Sun, Moon, and Earth.

Humanity is alone in this empty Universe. And while they might not know why, you think you know why.
objects.title: The Last Civilization in The Universe

objects.text: Once, long ago, the universe was full of stars and Entities. Now, there is only one star, and only a pair of Entities, one of which is dead. This is not a coincidence, something caused this. Something erased every last star, planet, moon, everything from beyond the edge of the solar system. The Entities tried to fight it, run from it, hide from it, but in the end only this tiny little pocket containing the Last Light remains. No one knows why, only that even the Last Light will not last forever. The Cycle has changed. Now that there is nowhere else to go, nowhere else to run, the surviving Entity has shifted the cycle to instead prepare humanity for what is coming. Much like before, humanity will be encouraged to spread across the entire solar system, with powers adapted to make that possible, and like before they created Endbringer-like creatures to patrol the outer edges, only instead of being meant to keep humanity inside, they are meant to keep something out. The Entity hopes that, through empowering humanity as much as possible, eventually they might become strong enough to fight off whatever destroyed everything else. If taken with Modifiers that introduce other Entities, then the Thinker and the Warrior were not alone in making it to the temporary safety of the Last Light. Perhaps the Wanderer managed to convince them to let it follow them for better safety in numbers when they met, maybe Apollyon arrived after expending a great deal of power to avoid its gaze and now wishes to take over the Last Cycle for itself, or the other Entities from Worm Notes possibly saw something was going to happen and set up a [DATA] rich defensible position to try fighting it off. You may decide what exactly that something is that erased everything. Perhaps it is a species in the same family as the Jormungandr that more directly feeds on universes? Maybe the ENDBRINGER successfully manifested its full form into reality, and its Heralds of the Apocalypse are already here, luring it ever closer to the Last Light? Maybe it's a hivemind of Berserker Probes that consumed everything? Maybe it's a Divine Machine meant to bring the Last Mercy to a dying universe before the Entities could turn it into their homeworld writ large. Whatever it is, it's much more dangerous than any Entity.
objects.title: The Last Light in a Dying Universe

addons.text:
At the core of each Singularity lies an irregularity, something out of place for its era. Perhaps a caveman stumbled upon a modern firearm, granting them technological knowledge centuries ahead of their time. Or a doctor appeared during a medieval plague, curing patients with remedies far beyond the understanding of that era. 

These anomalies, once rare occurrences, are now becoming increasingly frequent, disrupting the natural flow of history. With altered pasts bleeding into the present, the stability of reality deteriorates even further. The consequences of these disruptions are vast and unpredictable, threatening to reshape the course of civilization.
addons.title: Heroes of a Lost Age

addons.text:
The impact of these singularities has taken on a troubling new aspect—they now affect events retroactively. Few, if any, notice the changes they bring. Entire cities could be replaced with alternate versions without anyone realizing, as if it had always been that way.

As time and parallel universes collide, reality becomes increasingly unstable. Certainty gives way to uncertainty, and the very foundations of existence tremble. With each collision, the fabric of reality is threatened, risking widespread upheaval. As these disruptions continue unchecked, the very laws governing the universe will come under threat, their once-ironclad principles beginning to fray at the edges.

The stability of reality is in jeopardy as the lines between time and space blur. Urgent action is needed to address this growing instability before it spirals out of control, potentially leading to chaos on a cosmic scale.
addons.title: Information Alteration

objects.text:
Perhaps reality is in a flux, or the Thinker had an ongoing experiment before her untimely demise but people from the modern world are falling through time, appearing in the past. Lung, who ruled as the revered First Emperor of China, shaping dynasties and destinies. Miss Militia, celebrated for her bravery on the battlefields of World War II, inspiring generations with her courage.

In the realm of myth and legend, there's Clockblocker, said to possess mastery over time itself, earning him the title of the Greek God of Time, the father of the Olympians. The ominous figure of the Red Queen, whispered to be the dark force behind the Black Plague, a symbol of human frailty and fear. Khepri, revered as the first woman, embodying both innocence and sin.

This also means that when a parahuman appears in the past, they will bring their shard with them.

As more people continue to appear in the past, the present becomes increasingly unstable. Paradoxes caused by these time-traveling encounters put pressure on the fabric of reality, leading to disruptions in space-time. These disruptions create anomalies, areas where the normal rules of physics no longer apply.

The effects of these paradoxes extend throughout the universe, causing disturbances and unsettling the balance of cosmic forces. As these disruptions worsen, the stability of the present becomes precarious, risking a collapse of reality itself.
objects.title: Lost in Time

addons.text: In this world, the fantastical beings that emerge are not merely from other worlds, but entities from different timelines. Certain Singularities will grow massively, able to erase and replace entire countries. Not only that, some singularities will have smaller singularities within them, causing even more problems to deal with.
addons.title: Lostbelt

addons.text: Singularities are now not limited to only alternate timelines, but now can even be entire fictional worlds. Characters and locations from fictional settings can now appear and erase whatever is in their relative location in space.
addons.title: Bringer Of Fantasy

addons.text: Singularities can affect higher dimensions such as heaven, hell, Tartarus, and more. This can replace entire mythos with alternate version of themselves. Singularities can also be much more smaller now, replacing only a single person instead of an entire area.
addons.title: Alien Gods

objects.text: The timeline is broken. In many areas, particularly areas with rich history, singularities form. Singularities are spaces that are not part of the regular temporal axis. In these separate timelines certain individuals within a key historical time period will awaken powers, disrupting the proper flow of time, thus creating a singularity and appearing in the modern time. Singularities form at random, and with it brings many historical characters with various changes and powers. When they appear, they tend to erase whatever was in their relative location in space, replacing it with themselves.
objects.title: Broken Timeline

addons.text: The effects of incursions can now spread, as the destruction of universes cause’s universes nearby to become unstable, and begin breaking down.
addons.title: The Broken

objects.text: Singularities are the only remains of their world after a catastrophic event. Entire universes are collapsing into each other, crashing and merging with your own reality. The singularities will cause even more destruction when appearing, and some of their inhabitants may not react well to witnessing their own world being destroyed. The effects of singularities are far more random, as alternate version of beings may now coexist at the same time.
objects.title: Incursions

objects.text:
The end of the world is nigh, whether it is through a rogue tinker's device malfunctioning, the sun just not cutting it anymore, maybe the moon was damaged slightly not enough for chunks to threaten the planet but enough to block out the rays of the sun, or simply its just that time again, the Earth is set to freeze. 

Starting after a week of your arrival and over the course of a month the world will slowly succumb to ice and snow. Temperatures dropping so low in the negatives not even Russians would be willing to go out. Artic Gales, dozens of feet of snow, and said snow freezing over the course of days if not hours.
objects.title: New Ice Age

objects.text:
The end of the world is Nigh!

Whether it be through the Earth becoming tidally locked, malfunctioning tinkertech, a doomsday device, evil magicks, a curse, or all of the above, the world is destined to become almost completely uninhabitable.

One week after your arrival, the global temperature on one half of the world will slowly increase to a blazing heat, and the temperature of the other half will similarly decrease to a freezing cold.

Once the global temperatures stabilize the only survivable place on earth will be the land and sea in between these two extremes, (about 10% of the earth's surface.) these lands will be plagued with constant hyper-storms from the massive temperature difference.
objects.title: Frostfire Planet

objects.text:
The end of the world is nigh. Whether it's due to climate change, a rogue tinker's malfunctioning device, an ancient curse, or divine judgment, Earth is destined to become a desert planet.

Beginning one week after your arrival, the global temperature will start to rise. Over the following months, it will steadily increase until it stabilizes at an average of 45°C (113°F) in what were once the world’s colder regions—significantly higher elsewhere. This transformation will be accompanied by the rapid expansion of desert biomes and a dramatic worldwide decline in sea levels.
objects.title: Desert World

objects.text:
When the Entities arrived, their momentum pushed Earth off course, first slowly, but by 2011 Earth had entirely left the solar system and is now considered a rogue planet.
﻿
Thanks to Tinkers, and Zion putting a hand on the scales, the vast majority of Earths are just fine, but it does close off several avenues of development for Earth, such as solar, and removes most incentives for space travel.

The Earth is alone, only orbited by what it ejects, and might chance upon over time.
objects.title: Rogue Planet

objects.text:
In the Entities’ native solar system, a tear in reality is what allowed their Shards to jump to homeworld’s alternate versions, eventually evolving the ability to cross dimensions on their own.

Such a phenomenon, while incredibly rare, is also somewhat common throughout the multiverse. 

Tears in space that one could travel through, sections of space that overlap between dimensions, which could result in a person entering a location such as a cave through one entrance in one dimension and exiting in another through a different entrance.

There are even locations that have these phenomena happen at intervals, sometimes regular and easily accessible, and other times the intervals are incredibly spaced out, chaotic, and difficult to predict, often opening up to new locations rather than previous ones.

On Earth, there exists what is colloquially known as the Ferrymen. A mysterious organization that maps and facilitates travel between these worlds. 

Made up of various species, groups, and individuals throughout the multiverse, no one knows how large or old the organization truly is, not even the Ferrymen themselves.

The organization in truth exists as a set of loose connections between those aware of the various entrances and worlds, usually self-expanding systems until they encounter one another, driven by different goals and purposes, they help one another map all manner of planes and help Travelers get to their destinations or set up the transits between locations and worlds.

Unfortunately, these connections can also disappear, especially when one side is dependent solely on an individual's knowledge or if the tears become unpredictable, isolating branches of the Ferrymen from one another for incredibly long stretches, sometimes rediscovering one another millennia after as “new” branches, previous histories forgotten to the erosion of time.

Earth Bet has various instances in history where the tears have emerged, Earth Bet society is unaware of their true nature as it’s typically written into history as myth or a result of people suddenly going missing.

The lost city of Atlantis, the lost city of Roanoke, the lost planes in the Bermuda Triangle, the stories of ships gone missing in mysterious fogs never to be found again, whether alive or as wreckage. 

Earth Bet in particular has three major points, The Bermuda Triangle in the Atlantic, The Dragon’s Triangle, and the Mediterranean Sea.

The Bermuda Triangle is the most chaotic, often tears opening up to various dimensions and commonly resulting in strange storms. It’s also the most predictable, frequently opening up to the same dimensions many a time at regular but changing intervals. The tears typically lead to different periods in time for these worlds, meaning traveling through a tear once it reopens to get back may shoot the traveler years in the future or past. 

The Dragon’s Triangle in the Pacific is almost always active, although hidden in small pockets of the world, they can occasionally go dormant for periods, and will now and again massively expand, often resulting in large areas covered in fog. These locations seem to cycle between dimensions, usually settling on a new dimension every couple of millennia. 

The Mediterranean Sea is the most ephemeral, resulting in small pockets that typically result in powerful but otherwise typical storms. This generally manifests as a mysterious fog or a large tear will open up under the sea itself and end up in large whirlpools opening up.

The major cave systems of the Americas seem to contain a mineral that exists in multiple dimensions at the same time, on occasion having certain pockets that will overlap with other dimensions on regular but greatly spaced out intervals allowing one to travel between them, although yet to be mapped this is the reason for the vast number of missing cases reports noted in modern history, and why search parties also tend to go missing when looking for them despite going in large groups. 

There are multiple locations apart from these, The Great Glen in Scotland, The Michigan Triangle, and more. 

Stonehenge in particular was an open and stable rift for millennia, leading to another world that ancient humans would often travel to and from, and from where ancient myths of faeries, trolls, and other fantastical creatures come from, the tear having suddenly disappeared long before and the few inhabitants surviving on Earth Bet long enough to make it into the history as myths, perhaps they’re still around hidden somewhere, but it’s unlikely. 

The various stories of strange monsters and beasts of myth are often creatures that have crossed over from other dimensions into our own, whether by accident or not.
objects.title: Ferrymen

objects.text:
The combination of naturally occurring portals and the integration of Shardmatter into almost all life on Earth has led to the Shardmatter retaining far more of its cross-dimensional properties.

Various species, including humans, can open portals to alternate worlds; so long as they put in the effort and are at the right place at the right time.

Throughout history, humanity's travel across alternate earths has been commonplace, mirroring how we trekked across our world's seas and rivers.

So much so that mapping and forecasting a safe point in space-time to open a portal is as necessary as it was mapping oceanic currents. The control of a nexus where portals can be reliably and predictably opened to known alternate earths at almost any time (Stonehenge or specific cave systems, to name a few) is considered as economically and militarily crucial as the historically significant control of the Mississippi, the Nile Rivers, or the Suez or Panama Canals. Wars have been fought over, and entire civilizations have risen around these Nexus points, implicitly drawing lines in the sand that strife usually does.

Due to easier access to resources, this version of humanity is far more numerous with the estimated human population of all "civilized earths" at 80 billion.

Ready access to portals to alternate Earths and the ability to study Shardmatter extracted from various animals has allowed interdimensional physics to become as mature and well-developed as nuclear physics. The first method of creating artificial portals that did not require a Nexus point was tested on July 14, 1945, as part of the Pantheon test, the combination of the Chicago project. This changed the course of this timeline's version of the Second World War as much as nuclear weapons did. While Nexus points are still more important than ever for trade as transport through them consumes orders of magnitude less energy, by the 80s most passenger transport between alternate Earths occurred through artificial portals outside Nexus points. Being as common as any other amenity in civilization, the cost of a portal generator is comparable to that of a jet airliner.

The phrase "civilised earths", while generally referring to the Bet Cluster, is increasingly in disuse after the Aleph cluster’s discovery.

80 billion is only the population of the cluster of Earths immediately surrounding the Proto-Entities’ crash site (referred to as the Bet cluster). There are other Earth Clusters, portals that periodically connect to this central cluster, and while these portals are stable and stay open for decades, they only open roughly every 25,000 years. Plenty of lost tribes and colonies got stranded by this recurring event, which then colonise and settled on other clusters throughout approximately million years since the Proto-Entity’s crash landing. 

The oldest and most populous of which is the Aleph cluster, which was breached into by this timeline equivalent of Professor Haywire and which in terms of population and technological development is roughly equivalent to the Bet cluster.

Note: Trade between the two Clusters is far more common than trade between Earths Aleph and Bet in Canon, but is far more limited than trade within Clusters as Tinkertech is a costly requirement to travel between them economically; mundane technological means to travel to other clusters exist but the price per tone is comparable to putting a satellite into orbit.
objects.title: 5D Earth

objects.text:
Hollow Earth theory was actually true. 

Across the globe are systems of caves, caverns, and breaches that allow one to travel from the surface world into Earth’s inner world, the Hollow Earth. Most had remained undistributed for centuries until recently.

Within the Hollow Earth life has evolved to be much stronger and more dangerous having far longer to adapt and evolve without the issue of extinction events. Many of the lifeforms that call it home have evolved from prehistoric life and can even fit into new niches. There are galloping crocodilians, elephant-sized carnivorous plants, dog-sized insects, and even bullet-proof theropods.

Above all the other life that calls the Hollow Earth home is a sapient race. A form of lizard-people that supposedly share relations to ancient humanity. 

The lizard-people are physically superior to humans comparable to brutes, but are less advanced currently at the Bronze-Age of development, having even domesticated several of the other inhabitants of Hollow Earth. Their society is based upon the concept of strength and battle. As the strongest is naturally the leader, and the winner in a duel is in the right.

The confirmation of the existence of the Hollow Earth came from the return of a mocked expedition, who had proof of what they had endured. Since then many more expeditions have been attempted, with many bringing back strange rumors. 

Rumors that scattered throughout the wilderness of the Hollow Earth ancient ruins can be found that show signs that a civilization more advanced than the lizard-people had once ruled. Rumors that there had been other ancient civilizations that were just as advanced had ruled upon the Surface. There were even rumors that there had been less savory sorts that had made the Hollow Earth their home. Yet they are still just rumors for now.
objects.title: Hollow Earth

objects.text: The Earth is flat with an ice wall at the edge of it and all other planets and the sun revolve around Earth. Due to the false assumption that Earth is a sphere, humanity developed incorrect equations and calculations. As a result, many of the fundamental principles of physics in this world are inaccurate, leading to widespread misunderstanding and confusion about how the universe operates.
objects.title: Earth Conspiracy

addons.text:
The returning aliens have encountered their mythological counterparts—the divine figures that humanity once envisioned them as. They’ve achieved a fusion with these gods, merging their advanced alien biology and technology with the supernatural traits humans attributed to them over millennia. Now, each alien embodies both their original extraterrestrial power and the mythological characteristics of a god, blending science beyond human understanding with supernatural abilities beyond belief.

The mythological domains once belonging to the gods have been reactivated and claimed by these alien hybrids as fortified bases of operations. Olympus, Tartarus, Asgard, and other legendary realms have returned as real, tangible places on Earth, but they have now been overtaken and reshaped by alien technology. These sites serve as strategic footholds, giving the alien deities direct influence over key regions on Earth, enabling them to manipulate human affairs and gather resources for their plans with ease.

Now, the once-hallowed lands of ancient myth are twisted blends of divine splendor and alien advancement. Olympus has become a towering citadel where Zeus, the alien king, wields cosmic energy through both godly and extraterrestrial means, his lightning storms intensified by alien weaponry. In the caverns of Tartarus, alien technology amplifies the fearsome punishments and protections, creating an impenetrable fortress that holds rebellious humans and even other alien factions captive. Asgard’s gates are fortified by technology far beyond human comprehension, its defenders blending Norse fury with extraterrestrial power.
addons.title: An Alien Mythology

addons.text:
The aliens and the gods have achieved a complete fusion. The aliens have not only absorbed the powers and traits of the gods but resonated with the lingering godly instincts within them has created a singular, unified will—a drive not only to conquer Earth but to eradicate humanity entirely.

This new “Alien Pantheon” now holds a profound, almost fanatical hatred for humans. This hatred is not born of mere strategy or necessity; it is fueled by a strange merging of ancient grudges and alien motives. The gods’ desire for the world to be pruned, combined with the aliens’ disdain for “inferior” beings, has become a united impulse to cleanse the Earth of all human life. Their desire to rule Earth has now transformed into a dark ambition to create a purified world free from humanity’s influence, an Earth molded solely to their will and vision.

Fortunately for humanity, the Alien Pantheon sees the planet itself as a valuable resource. This means they will not resort to wholesale planetary destruction or cataclysmic weapons; instead, they aim to exterminate humankind with surgical precision. Their attacks are relentless but controlled, targeting population centers, governments, and resistance forces with terrifying efficiency while leaving Earth’s natural systems intact. These deities use their godly powers and alien technology in terrifying harmony: earthquakes are selectively unleashed to devastate cities, storms obliterate resistance strongholds, and plagues of alien origin sweep through human populations, sparing the environment while reducing humanity’s numbers.
addons.title: The End

addons.text:
The aliens that arrived on Earth bear a history steeped in violence and survival; they are remnants of civilizations that managed to survive past Entity cycles, barely escaping total annihilation. Now, having fused with the weakened but still potent remnants of the gods, they find renewed strength and purpose. They are done running, done hiding; they will take the fight to the Entities themselves.

By wielding a terrifying mix of advanced alien technology and divine abilities, they overcome even the Shards’ natural resistance to magic. No longer simply alien, they now bring the wrath of fallen gods to their conquests, each one a formidable force that blends ancient divinity with technology from beyond the stars. In their onslaught, Parahumans get hunted, their powers challenged, as the Alien-God hybrids kill and plunder with cold efficiency, harvesting Shard data to enhance themselves further.

Sensing the threat, the Shards begin to adapt in response. They begin to intensify their hold on their hosts, amplifying their conflict drive specifically toward these Alien-God hybrids. Hosts are rewarded with surges of power whenever they engage with or kill one of these new enemies, and their abilities begin evolving to counter the hybrids’ unique combination of godly might and alien technology. The Shards know that these hybrids are more than a mere obstacle; they are a danger to the cycle itself, and they cannot be allowed to persist.

As the war unfolds, Parahumans are caught in the crossfire of an escalating arms race. Empowered by their Shards, they become deadlier than ever, driven by the pull of conflict and the promise of newfound strength with every victory. Yet, for every surge in Parahuman power, the Alien-God hybrids evolve in turn, making their attacks more ruthless and their defenses harder to penetrate.
addons.title: Arms Race

objects.text:
In ancient times, humanity’s religions and mythologies were not simply the products of imagination—they were inspired by interactions with advanced extraterrestrial beings who visited Earth. These alien civilizations seeded religions, influenced cultures, and used their technology to shape human beliefs and societies. Each pantheon or figure we revere as divine was, in fact, a highly evolved alien with motives beyond our comprehension.

Satan, the bringer of forbidden knowledge, was an alien rebel who sought to uplift humanity. By giving humans access to advanced knowledge, he broke the chains that held early humans as bioengineered workers, freeing them from servitude to their alien creators. Meanwhile, the Olympians, like Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades, were stranded extraterrestrials. They used their technology to not only survive but to enhance their lives and elevate themselves as gods in the eyes of early civilizations. Over millennia, the teachings, stories, and interactions between these alien beings and early humans were distilled into mythologies, philosophies, and religions that continue to shape humanity. As humanity uncover the truths about their past, the fingerprints of these extraterrestrial influences can be seen everywhere—from the tales of Prometheus to the Biblical accounts of angels and demons—all leading back to the distant stars.

In the modern era, the original architects of these myths, the aliens themselves, have returned, seeking to reclaim Earth and assert control over humanity. However, they are not a unified force. Multiple alien factions, each with their own agenda, have arrived, and ancient rivalries flare up as they vie for dominance over the planet. As they unleash their advanced technology and strategies to gain the upper hand, humanity is caught in the middle, witnessing clashes reminiscent of mythical wars of old.
objects.title: Alien Myths

objects.text:
It is a grim fate indeed that an ancient evil, existing beyond the boundaries of reality, has set its sights on your universe as the next target for its malevolent ambitions.

Regardless of its exact nature or ultimate goal, the consequences of its arrival would be catastrophic: the total subjugation of all life or the outright annihilation of the universe itself.

This ancient evil wields unimaginable power, surpassing even the mightiest of entities, capable of eradicating them en masse with ease. Fortunately, due to its otherworldly nature, it cannot fully manifest or enter reality without great effort and meticulous preparation. To do so, it must select a specific world (yours) and begin its invasion there.

In the initial stages of its incursion, the ancient evil can only project a fragment of its malignant energy into the world. This energy corrupts living beings, transforming them into unwilling thralls. If left unchecked, these corrupted individuals will spread their taint to the environment, transforming it into a hostile alien landscape. Such changes would allow the ancient evil to channel even more of its power into reality. 

Those with power of any kind or are strong of will are more resistant to the corrupting influence of the ancient evil’s energy—unless they willingly submit to it. Those who willingly submit can be granted immense power, their strength increasing in proportion to their loyalty and service to the ancient evil.

Shardless power with certain properties, such as magic, can cleanse corrupted creatures and environments and reverse the ancient evil's progress.

Once the corruption reaches a critical threshold, a permanent gateway to the ancient evil’s realm could form, enabling it to unleash powerful minions and, eventually, lesser manifestations of itself into the world. The strongest of these minions could battle multiple Endbringers simultaneously and emerge victorious, while even a lesser manifestation could challenge Scion himself.

If the corruption consumes the entire world, a final ritual could summon the ancient evil’s true form into reality. At that point, all hope would be lost, as the universe itself would be devoured and absorbed into the ancient evil realm.

Let us hope that you possess the strength and vigilance to resist this darkness. It is coming, and it will not stop until all is under its dominion.
objects.title: Dimensional Breached

objects.text:
Due to the impossibly large number of alternate Earths, the Entities group near-identical Earths together for their cycle. A single inhabited "representative" Earth is selected from each group by a shard to be used, while the remaining Earths are sealed off from dimensional travel.

The shard then exploits these sealed off Earths to power itself, similar to batteries. Naturally, this leads to the complete destruction of the partitioned earths as they're converted into fuel. Instead of being on the "primary" Earth you selected, you are now on one of these locked-off alternate versions of that Earth, destined to be consumed by a shard.

The Earth you are in is identical to the one you initially selected through your choices in this CYOA and it is guaranteed to not be drained by the shard within the first 6 months of your arrival. Once started, the obliteration of the Earth will take only a week at most as the shard rapidly consumes vast quantities of material and energy.

Certain shard powers and dimension-traversing shardless abilities can bypass the shard's dimensional barriers but it is harder than before and less accurate, potentially causing you to initially go to a different universe than the one you want. Stopping the shard linked to this Earth will prevent the world’s destruction.
objects.title: Earth for Harvest

objects.text:
Earth was, by all accounts, a disastrously designed game. From the start, it was plagued with blatant pay-to-win mechanics—those born into wealth or privilege had a massive advantage over everyone else, and there was no real system in place to level the playing field. The developers, if they even exist in any tangible way, remained entirely silent, pushing no updates, offering no roadmaps, and refusing to respond to even the most desperate requests for balance patches. Spectator mode was a mystery—some claimed to have unlocked it, while others insisted it didn’t exist at all. There was zero interactivity with the mod team, assuming there ever was one, and community enforcement was left to a shaky, often toxic mix of honor codes, social norms, and vague philosophical rules.

The storyline was chaotic at best—no clear protagonist, an ever-expanding cast of unpredictable NPCs, and major plot threads introduced only to be abandoned without resolution. It felt as though the writers were making it up in real time, relying on improvisation rather than structure. Despite centuries of player feedback, nothing changed. The world trudged on, buggy and unbalanced.

But now—finally—it’s been properly optimized. 

The patch notes, though unofficial as always, are impossible to ignore. For the first time in what feels like forever, the game’s core systems actually work. Wealth and privilege, once the cheat codes to success, have been rebalanced—progression now scales more with effort, collaboration, and ingenuity than with arbitrary starting stats. The economy, once a glitched mess of inflation, exploitation, and hoarded resources, has been revamped to reward sustainability and creative trade. Resource drops are more fairly distributed, and grinding is no longer a soul-crushing necessity but a meaningful path to mastery.

Latency between action and consequence has been drastically reduced. Players can now actually see the impact of their choices in real time, encouraging thoughtful strategy instead of mindless farming. Communication systems have been upgraded too—language barriers are easier to overcome, and the global chat is no longer a cacophony of misinformation and trolling, but a space where cooperation and shared goals can actually emerge.

Combat? Smoothed out. No more sudden permadeath with no warning, no more random encounters with overpowered enemies from half a world away. The mechanics of conflict have been fine-tuned to emphasize skill, diplomacy, and timing, not brute force or luck of the spawn point. PvP is still chaotic, but now there’s a sense of fairness in it—victories feel earned, not scripted. 

Most importantly, for the first time in the game’s messy history, there’s actual moderation. Real oversight. Griefers, once able to ruin entire servers with no consequences, now face swift and meaningful repercussions. Hate speech, exploits, and toxic behavior are no longer shrugged off as part of the “meta”—they’re being actively addressed. Mods may still be unseen, but their presence is unmistakable. Infractions are met with action, not indifference, and players are finally protected by more than just the vague hope of mutual decency.

Even the storyline seems to have found its footing. After millennia of directionless lore, scattered side quests, and contradictory worldbuilding, there’s finally a sense of cohesion. Themes are echoing across continents, characters are connecting in surprising ways, and player choices are starting to shape a narrative that feels alive. It’s not all predictable or safe—but that’s part of the appeal. The improvisation is still there, but it’s sharper now, more like jazz than noise.

And maybe best of all: it feels like the devs are listening. Not speaking directly—of course not, that would ruin the mystery—but watching. Tweaking. Responding in subtle, elegant ways that suggest someone—or something—is finally paying attention.

The game still has its rough edges, sure. But now, for the first time in recorded play, it feels like it was actually meant to be played.

(This choice doesn’t make Earth a game—it simply makes it feel like one that’s finally been well-designed and responsibly managed.)
objects.title: World’s Best Game

objects.text: No one truly knows whether the world, the universe, or even the multiverse was created by someone—or something. Some realities emerged from nothingness, while others were shaped from scratch by beings such as The Presence, Veldanava, Akatosh, or even The One Above All. Some worlds simply began with a bang. In most cases, the process of creation remains a mystery, unless the creator reveals themselves and remains involved. As for your world—whether it exists as a standalone reality, a fusion of many, or part of a vast multiverse—it was created. That creator could be an unknown force, an outerversal entity, or a being so alien they defy understanding. The identity of the creator is yours to choose—or leave to chance. Perhaps Veldanava formed your world, or maybe it was The Presence, Akatosh, or The One Above All. Regardless of who it was, your world’s connection to others remains partial—its roots tied to its creator's origin but not wholly intertwined. If Veldanava is the source, then your world is loosely connected to the Cardinal World. The Voice of the World may not echo here, but travelers may still cross over, and vice versa. The same applies to worlds made by other beings. With every choice comes both consequences and possibilities. New cosmic forces may now be able to contact, influence, or even enter your world depending on who the creator is. The degree of connection to other realities can be expanded, allowing individuals with ties to other worlds created by the same being to freely travel between them. They may bring with them the energy systems and powers of those realms. Eventually, something like The Voice of The World may fully echo to your world. Some people may be summoned, reincarnated, or find themselves in alternate versions of your world. The possibilities are limitless—but so are the risks. Threats equal to entities like Ivaragé or Darkseid may exist within reach. If you've chosen other modifiers that introduce new cosmic forces—such as The Endless—those forces will fall under the authority of your world's creator, second only to them in power. The same rule applies to any beings borrowed from existing worlds like High School DxD, whether integrated into a fusion world or newly created by your chosen deity.
objects.title: The Creator

objects.text: The impossible has occurred. The Creator is dead. Maybe they gave their life fighting off a universe eating abomination, perhaps were backstabbed by one of their greatest creations in a moment of weakness, it could have been that they merely had an immense yet still finite lifespan rather than immortality and died of old age, or some other reason. In the end the outcome is all the same, the architect behind the entire universe and all its dimensions and timelines has fallen. The good news is that the universe has enough ontological inertia such that it didn't poof out of existence the instant the Creator died, and it will continue to exist for a time. The bad news is that certain aspects of reality and various systems which maintained it still required the Creator to personally oversee them in order to properly function. And now that they are dead, that isn't happening, and while perhaps they planned to eventually 'update' the universe such that they were unnecessary or uplift someone into being their 'heir' to take over their duties, they died before any of that could actually happen. Over time, various 'glitches' will happen. At first they will be relatively rare and minor; time will randomly jump a few seconds forwards or backwards, dimensions will begin to brush against each other swapping people and things between 'nearby' alternate dimensions, gravity may fluctuate for a split second, reality will 'hiccup' and suddenly someone has a different hair color, things like that. Somewhat disruptive, and people will absolutely be left confused and worried by some of the more obvious glitches, but overall not that dangerous. However, as time passes and errors begin to pile up, these glitches slowly stop being 'rare' and 'minor'. Suddenly, everyone is freaking out as time jumps forward hours or even days at a time. Dimensions begin to slam into one another instead of lightly brushing, causing spatial tears leading to parallel dimensions, or worse as places literally fuse together into a broken mishmash of overlapping matter. Gravity warps violently for minutes at a time causing vortexes that rip apart anything caught inside or will randomly intensify or reverse causing towns to be crushed or flung into space. Reality distorts severely, causing unlucky people to randomly have their age, sex, appearance, or even their memories shift out of nowhere. Eventually, the errors become too much and the universe 'crashes'. Systems built into the foundations of reality will activate as failsafes force reboot the universe, but without the Creator to 'debug' the 'code' of reality some data will be corrupted, resulting in a host of new issues in and of itself. This combined with glitches being left unresolved means that the next crash isn't that far off, and the next one after that happens even faster, and so on until reality enters a truly broken state where only a handful of beings can function while everyone and everything is left frozen in time and space, glitched to the point of being unrecognizable, until even that breaks down as the universe completely self destructs leaving nothing of your starting Setting behind. By default, you have a month before glitches start noticeably happening, roughly one minor glitch every week and one major glitch every other month to start before accelerating. After 5 years, you can expect a minor glitch or two every day and one major glitch every week. The first crash will occur after 10 years, then the next 9 years after that, then 8, and so on. After 100 years the universe will break down completely, though human civilization is very unlikely to last even half of that before glitches and crashes render it unrecognizable. The only way to stop this is for someone to somehow usurp the empty throne the Creator left behind, which is not an easy feat as it requires becoming as powerful as them, learning how to interface with the systems governing reality, somehow obtaining the necessary permissions to use said systems, and then figuring out how to use them to restore reality to its correct state. This means that even if you are strong enough to do it yourself it would still be a difficult challenge to gain the throne, especially as automated defense programs and cosmic beings loyal to the deceased creator are liable to fight back against your attempts unless and until you somehow prove yourself 'worthy' of the throne. Alternatively you could resurrect the Creator, but good luck, as it's far more complicated than just casting True Resurrection using D&D magic, and even the Dragon Balls or an Aladdin Genie would be unable to directly wish them back, though using them to skip certain steps in the resurrection process is possible. Note: Depending on what Creator you chose, any supernatural systems linked to them may also glitch. For example, if you chose Arceus it would result in the Unown randomly going berserk and things such as Type matchups breaking down to where you might see a Dragon Type Pokemon being immune to Fairy Type instead of weak to it. Meanwhile, YHVH could result in Demons and Personas spontaneously changing form or attributes, or the Metaverse randomly merging with reality in various locations.
objects.title: Mors Creatoris

objects.text:
Rupturing onto the surface, countless entrances appear to the strange, warping structures and tunnels of the Labyrinthos. 

Sprawling underneath and between worlds and filled with monsters, horrors, traps, treasures, and wonders. A dimension onto itself, the boundary line, the rubicon. Tunnels and paths that cross the gulf between dimensions. Natural, and artificial. A wondrous construct, filled with alien landscapes and bizzare, beautiful geometries. Sometimes mimicking the very structures humans have built or imagined, even if always slightly off.

Space and distance inside are warped. Certain paths- if one can find them- can save one days of travel. Taking just a few hours to walk across and emerge from an entrance on the other side of the world... or, if one went deep enough, into a different world entirely. But the Labyrinthos is not static, and will move when not watched. Paths traveled one way may not take you back to where you came from in the other, or be the same on a different day. The halls and corridors shifting to an alien whim. Worse, one is never far from danger.

The creatures that inhabit The Labyrinthos hold only hate for all from outside its depths. Living bundles of malice and curses, a mockery of physical form. From warped, distorted animals. To machines. To Nightmares. To beasts and beings of myth and fairy tale. All growing more and more dangerous the deeper into the Labyrinth one descends. Spawning from the walls, floors, ceilings, nooks and crannies. Ever hungering hate, despising all travelers. Sometimes growing to such an extent that they surge- monsters rapidly forming and flooding out of an entrance, attacking everything that lives.
Thankfully, it is not just monsters that can be found in these depths. Strange materials, gems, and metals can be found growing in the walls or harvested from the corpses of the beasts within. Useful for tinkers and craftsmen, or to empower an individual's abilities when properly processed. From the more dangerous tool-using creatures and beings one can even loot tools, armor, weapons, and other trinkets with esoteric effects. Though, often such loot is cursed with the monsters' dying breaths.
objects.title: The Labyrinthos

objects.text: The malice within the Labyrinthos grows. Now, not only does it produce monsters hostile to outside life, but the very atmosphere within has become deleterious to foreign intrusions. Materials from without rust and decay. Machines breakdown. Living beings weaken and wither. Staying within the Labyrinthos has now become a race against the clock. Stronger beings and objects can fend off its toxic encroachment for longer, but even they will eventually succumb. Due to this, culling monster populations is even more difficult, thus increasing the likelihood of monster waves breaking out onto the surface.
objects.title: Toxic Labyrinth

objects.text: There are no oceans. At least, none made of water. Instead, there are huge, sprawling, dark woods taking their place. I suggest brushing up on your geobiology. Also called the Bramble, the Deep Wood, the Great Wood, and The Dark Forest, the Wyrd is, for all intents and purposes, hundreds of forests and jungles stacked up on top of each other like strata. Light vanishes just a few layers deep. Filled with caverns and tunnels made of bush, wood, fungus, and even more bizarre plants and creatures. Things only becoming stranger the deeper one goes. The Wyrd takes the place of and fills the empty space all the world's oceans would've normally taken, the 'canopy'- an ocean of leaves- being firmly at sea level. There is no sailing the Wyrd. There is no making permanent roads either; as the Wyrd has a tendency to consume permanent structures. Even stone, treated steel, and other non-perishable materials decay, rust and rot far faster than they normally would. Even plastics tend to vanish and decay within the overwhelming abundance of life. Even wild fires at its driest- but still moist- locations are smothered almost unnaturally quickly. Even using the materials harvested within from beasts and plants to construct with fails; the floor itself shifting and moving slowly over time, but enough to swallow a single story house in under a week, pulling it down deeper into the Wyrd and below the Canopy. Despite all that, the Wyrd is navigable. Sunlight pierces the canopy just fine, and even the ground at that level is almost like that of a normal- if ancient and hole filled- forest floor. As long as one is careful of the megafauna, watches their step, is properly equipped, and plans their trips appropriately, it is more than possible to safely cross; even just on foot. There is bountiful food and fresh water if one knows where to look and how to hunt, after all. But deeper, below the canopy, it becomes far more difficult to survive and navigate. Sunlight quickly vanishes. Only the dim bioluminescence of critters, plants, and fungi lighting the wooden caverns and tunnels. It gets harder to breathe. Harder to move. Tools become less effective. The air wet, hot, and humid, even in the Artics. A few layers deep and it becomes impossible for most 'surface' creatures to breathe without assistance. Never mind the spores, pollen, and other things that can fill the air- sweeping through like storms without warning. Geysers and steam erupt from vents in the wood, scalding and melting flesh, only growing more common and dangerous as one descends. The creatures as well, growing stranger and more deadly. The weight of the world above pressing down on one's shoulders, and the growing, ever present, faint feeling of being watched by something other. If one is able to brave these depths, the strange esoteric resources below can become available to them. Ore veins, growing from the wood like sap, plants that are far tougher and lighter than metal, creatures with hides and bones stronger than stone, fungi with almost miraculous medicinal use, and much, much more. Never mind the treasures that can be found in the different 'zones' of the Wyrd- like the arctics with their frost resistant- sometimes ice making- plants. The Wyrd, much like the oceans, shaped how the world and all its societies developed. Including the climate and storms. Plants, animals, and fungi are common even in desserts and the artics. More species having adapted due to the Wyrd's strange properties. 'Sailing' is limited to lakes, rivers, and land-locked seas. Salt water is almost unheard of. Ships are small things, mostly to travel rivers, and no carrier ships would ever be invented. Flight may very well have come about far earlier in civilization's development as a way to cross the Wyrd in a far more reasonable time; whether through blimps or planes. Entire nomadic societies with no permanent structures can likely be found living within, ever wandering and hunting through the Wyrd.
objects.title: The Wyrd

objects.text:
Long ago, the world was shattered into countless fragments floating above an endless sea of clouds. No one who has tried to cross the great cloud barrier has ever returned, and the skyfolk have long since stopped trying. 

The Islands form clusters, with islands in the same cluster being close and the clusters themselves being some distance apart. Each cluster is around the size of a large city. Airships are a common mode of transit between clusters and can carry you swiftly to your destination. In addition to that, every major city has a teleportation gate, which comes with a heavy fee.

Everyone is capable of some level of flight, the level being determined by the user's general fitness. As a general rule, you can fly as fast as you can sprint, and it takes the same amount of stamina as a light jog. Flying near clouds drastically boosts flight speed and grants infinite stamina for flying. This quirk takes effect regardless of the method of flight. 

If you did not take a power that allows flight, you gain the standard flight method for this setting modifier. If you are already capable of flight, it is considered "native" and will be made compatible with anything that interacts with the native flight method. If you leave the setting, you can choose whether or not to keep the alterations to your flight power. Additionally, if your flight power is weaker than the native method, it is buffed to be of equal power.

The clouds are not really clouds; they just appear as such. Functionally, they are an ever-expanding barrier, keeping the void out and everything else in. The speed boost and stamina buff are defensive functions to prevent people from crossing them. The islands stick to the inside of the hollow sphere, and the clouds themselves allow some level of gravity to exist.

Finally, the islands appear to be ever-increasing in number at a rate slightly exceeding humanity's ability to expand. Where the matter comes from is a hotly debated topic, but the most common belief is that the matter is shunted from other dimensions. This is supported by the fact that fresh islands tend to have exotic materials and creatures.
objects.title: The Shattering

objects.text:
Defying entropy isn’t just possible—it’s practically routine. For advanced civilizations, discovering negentropic processes is as foundational as electricity was to the Industrial Age. However, while reversing entropy is now a known science, the trade-off is steep: generating large amounts of usable energy remains extraordinarily difficult.

Negentropic systems are marvels of stability and order, capable of maintaining perfect equilibrium and near-zero degradation. But their energy output is minuscule. Constructing a power source equivalent to a common AA or C battery demands an installation the size of a small building. Scaling beyond that leads to extreme instability—devices the size of continents are required to approach modern industrial power levels, and anything larger becomes exponentially more prone to catastrophic failure. This hard ceiling has caused stagnation in energy production, with even advanced science facing diminishing—and ultimately terminal—returns.

As a result, even super-advanced alien civilizations, Entities, and Shards rely on negentropic tech only for low-power or long-duration applications. Internal chronometers, passive sensors, archival memory cores, and similar non-volatile systems are typical uses. These systems aren’t meant to produce energy—they're prized for reliability, precision, and endurance in environments where traditional power generation is unreliable or impossible.
Attempts to chain multiple negentropic generators together—whether by stacking interdimensional energy taps, exploiting differential potentials across layered realities, or invoking hyperfolded multidimensional geometries—have consistently failed. These generators interfere with one another unpredictably. At best, they suffer a massive efficiency loss. At worst, they cancel each other out, go inert, or even begin consuming energy rather than generating it—functioning as near-perfect energy sinks. Ironically, this makes them highly effective for containment systems and fail-safe dead circuits, but not for scalable energy output.

This isn’t a case of early-stage technology. Negentropic generation has been exhaustively researched across eons and civilizations. The field is mature—and closed. No further breakthroughs are expected within the known lifespan of the multiverse. In this world, entropy is no longer the enemy. Energy scarcity is.
objects.title: Negentropy is Common

objects.text: Somewhere in the world you chose, a Dungeon was created, whether it be a tower piercing the heavens or a large hole seemingly leading into an infinite void, it is up to you. Rumors about a great treasure of sorts are what lead people into delving in, dying, or disappearing into the dungeon's depths. You are potentially one of these people. The Dungeon is divided into several floors, each with separate Trials that one must overcome to progress. Some floors even have Floormasters who serve as strong bosses that are tricky to defeat. Heck, some floors are so vast that they almost feel like their own mini worlds, with their own cultures and ecosystems, vastly making trials more complicated in their solutions. And of course, something is horrifying you must face once you reach the end. Whether it be a powerful character like Scion in the Parahumans world, or some sort of bloodthirsty boss monster, you must defeat this thing to finish this mission. Conquering the Dungeon turns you into its Dungeon Master, with full control over the dungeon's properties as well as the ability to slowly spread its influence across your world. You can even make use of the people tempted to conquer it themselves. Losing within the Dungeon, however, is terrifying, as you are turned into one of its denizens, bound to be trapped within as a servant to your Floormaster and Dungeon Master above you. Depending on who that is, that might be a fate worse than death. So, weary adventurer, are you brave enough to venture these halls?
objects.title: Dungeon of God

addons.text:
Parahumans are not the only beings with superpowers in this world. A vast array of mutations has radically altered the planet’s flora and fauna, imbuing them with extraordinary abilities that defy natural biology. Nowhere is this transformation more dramatic than in the world's oceans. Once relatively barren at great depths, these waters have become unimaginably vast and vibrant—thanks in part to the post-Scion shift in global ecology.

The deep sea, previously a cold and lifeless abyss, now teems with mutant lifeforms that glow, hunt, and evolve with uncanny intelligence. Massive sea creatures with super-dense armor or sonic weapons cruise the Abyss, while smaller fish swarm in coordinated patterns akin to living storms. Some aquatic species possess psychic abilities or emit disruptive EMP-like pulses, effectively disabling nearby ships and submarines. Coral reefs, once fragile ecosystems, have become sentient bio-structures that can manipulate currents or shield entire regions from detection—almost like natural fortresses.

These changes aren't isolated to the oceans. On land, weather-altering trees whip up endless cyclones, and predatory beasts now sprint faster than cars or fly on wings of plasma. The natural world has become wild, volatile, and deeply alien.

Together, these mutations have reshaped Earth’s ecosystems into something almost post-apocalyptic—more fitting for a planet at war with gods than the quiet cradle of human civilization. Exploration, colonization, and survival now depend not just on technology, but on powers capable of matching nature’s new, terrifying scale.
addons.title: Unfathomable Depths

addons.text:
Following the world's transformation, the oceans have become realms of pure dread. No longer mere expanses of blue, they are vast, unknowable catacombs of pressure, darkness, and hunger. The depths are not just populated by enormous mutant sea life, but things that should not exist—things that predate humanity, or perhaps were born from Scion’s coming. Sentient shipwrecks that whisper in Morse code, impossible sea creatures with maddening psychic auras, entire sunken cities populated by the drowned and the damned.

These aren't just giant sharks or glowing squids—some deep-sea beings twist the line between biological mutation and occult horror. Leviathans that seem to "remember" the humans who trespass. Ghost ships piloted by the corpses of their former crews. Abyssal zones where time moves incorrectly, or where diving teams come back... changed.

Even the surface isn't safe. During red tides, seafoam carries whispers. Lighthouses glow with lights that shouldn't be possible. Occasionally, something vast brushes against oil rigs or cargo ships, unseen, unidentifiable.

Yet Earth Bet is not entirely helpless. While monsters and madness walk the Earth—and now swim its oceans—so do those with knowledge and power. Mediums, occultists, psychics, and miracle-workers hold ancient rites and rituals passed down in secret, able to protect or empower those who fight the darkness. Even some parahumans exhibit abilities disturbingly similar to necromancy, prophecy, or possession, bridging the gap between science and the supernatural.

So while things have grown darker, stranger, and more terrifying—there is still resistance. But in the deepest parts of Earth Bet, in waters never meant to be disturbed... something stirs. And it's waiting.
addons.title: Horror Bet: Thalassophobia Edition

addons.text:
Humanity is not the sole apex species of this world. Beneath the waves lies a rival civilization—ancient, enigmatic, and terrifyingly powerful. Unlike in our history, where the oceans were gradually explored, mapped, and commercialized, this world tells a different story. The ocean-dwellers never relinquished their dominion. They remained—and they defended their realm with ruthless precision.

As a result, humanity's expansion was forced inland. While the continents flourished with sprawling cities and vast empires, the oceans remained off-limits—an untouchable domain ruled by beings whose motives and minds are utterly alien. Maritime trade is nearly non-existent. The few vessels that do brave the waves are crude, short-range, and heavily reinforced—remnants of a failed dream to master the seas. Most are destroyed or turned back before ever reaching deep waters, driven away by swift and deadly retaliation from beneath.

In response to this impassable barrier, human innovation turned skyward. Denied the oceans, humanity leapt into the air. Dirigibles, advanced airplanes, hybrid rotorcraft, and vertical lifters became the backbone of global infrastructure. Massive skyports replaced what in another world would have been coastal harbors. Entire nations depend on fleets of aircraft to transport goods, people, and ideas—creating a society more reliant on air travel than any we have known.

Efforts to communicate or negotiate with the oceanic civilization have ended in frustration. Their biology, culture, and language seem fundamentally incompatible with human understanding. They do not respond to diplomacy in any recognizable way. Some scholars argue they operate on timescales or principles too alien for us to grasp. Others claim they simply view humanity as a pest to be contained—not a peer to be engaged.

Over time, resentment has grown. The loss of trade, the stunted maritime industries, the ruined coastal settlements—all of it festers. Propaganda paints the sea-dwellers as tyrants hoarding untold wealth and technology. The idea of reclaiming the oceans by force gains traction. Military factions call for retribution. Adventurers and mercenaries vanish into the deep, seeking vengeance—or treasure.

War has not yet come. But tensions rise with each passing year. The skies are full of promise, but humanity still hungers for the blue horizon. And sooner or later, someone will strike the first blow.
addons.title: Ancient Dominion

objects.text:
The oceans of this world have undergone a dramatic transformation. No longer the familiar blue expanses of the past, they have become realms of both breathtaking wonder and unimaginable terror.

One of the most profound changes is the dramatic increase in ocean depth. In most regions, the average depth has doubled or even tripled compared to the original seas. Vast chasms and trenches, once rare geological features, are now commonplace. Many of these rifts rival—and even surpass—the legendary Mariana Trench, plunging into darkness well beyond the known limits of the Challenger Deep.

Yet, it is not only the geography that has changed. Life now thrives in places that were once desolate. Traditionally, the abundance of marine life diminished with depth, tapering off beyond the sunlit surface. But no longer. From the dimly lit Twilight Zone to the pitch-black depths of the Abyss, vibrant ecosystems have taken root. Bioluminescent creatures, vast schools of strange deep-sea fish, and alien-like invertebrates flourish in every shadowed crevice. The deep ocean is now teeming with life—strange, luminous, and often unfathomable.

This biological explosion has had a profound effect on global industries, particularly maritime trade and fishing. Overfishing, once a dire environmental concern, has become virtually impossible due to the overwhelming abundance of marine life. Modern ships are larger, faster, and more technologically advanced than ever before, designed not only to navigate these deeper waters but to harvest the wealth hidden within them. The ocean has become humanity’s greatest resource—but also its greatest frontier.

However, with such richness comes peril. The deep's abundance has given rise to predators of extraordinary size and power. Colossal sea creatures, reminiscent of the legendary Giant Octopus or the long-extinct Megalodon, are no longer myths—they are reality. These massive beasts roam the mid and lower ocean zones with unsettling regularity. While they typically avoid the shallow coastal waters and the upper Daylight Zone, their presence adds a constant layer of danger to life at sea.

Fortunately, for now, most of these leviathans steer clear of human activity. But with oceans deeper, darker, and more alive than ever before, the line between awe and fear grows thinner each day.

(You can optionally choose for the oceans to cover a larger portion of the planet's surface.)
objects.title: Transformed Oceans

addons.text: These strange oceans are now larger, much more all encompassing to the point even stranger creatures now lurk within. From collosal lava leviathans, to literal cookie based cookie sharks. These oceans are now as vast as they are terrifying. But what great creatures exist within the depths, and what dangers could they pose to this world's humanity?
addons.title: Leagues Under the Sea

addons.text:
The civilations whom call the oceans home have adapted to the strange oceanic environments they now find themselves in. As such, different subspecies and races of this aquatic civilization have developed depending on the oceans they are native to. A milk based deep resident would be inherently different to one who lives in a liquid metal ocean, and so on.

Thus, whenever there are conflicts between them us, we must learn their biology and culture further, lest we become victims of their unfathomable ambitions. But could humanity even deal with the masters of the strangest seven seas?
addons.title: Alternate Aquamen

addons.text:
Aquatic based cities have always been common within a world believing in Municipal Darwinism. With this change however, Amphibious Urbivores have been upgraded to adapt in these new oceans. From a heavily cybernetic based one which can traverse through liquid metal, to heat resistant homes able to power through the immense heat of lava oceans and their boiling neighbors. 

The cities live on, no matter what.
addons.title: Hungry Hungry Ferries

addons.text:
Unfortunately, due to the extra wack flora and fauna that already exists, this had major consequences to the environment. Pick one or two large areas of soil, and it too had changed to a specific solid material. The plants and animals have adapted to this change. Here, fishes from the body of water it is connected to had rose up and became amphibious. Thus, evolution finds a way, and now you see more bizzare land dwellers as well as consequences to environment fuckery.

I hope you enjoy walking oreo fishes and cybernetic frog people.
addons.title: Welp, There Goes the Land Too

objects.text:
One or more of this world's oceans or an equivalent large body of water is now no longer made of water, but instead, an alternative liquid substance. There are creatures living within them, having adapted to the change in their environment. Like a lava ocean with creatures who quite literally breathe fire, or an ocean made of fruit juice with equally fruity fishes somehow. Whatever it is, this obviously has immense effect on this world's environment as well as, of course, society at large. As sailing becomes a much trickier endeavor.

Are you down to sail through the wacky wacky seas?
objects.title: Water? What Water?

objects.text:
With this, the world becomes made of Lego, or any brick based building block. And thus, people can just disassemble and rebuild things into new forms with enough knowledge and creativity of the material. Everyone has the potential to be a master builder! This is both a good thing and a bad thing because it wouldn't be fun seeing your house just randomly broken and rebuilt by somebody who wants a particular block.

Unless you don't want to, choosing this may also turn everyone into Lego (or other play block) looking versions of themselves. If not, this will only affect solid material that the world is made out of, nothing else.
objects.title: Legoland

addons.text:
While Pyrobloin does enter the atmosphere through volcanic eruptions, the lion's share of it actually comes from the World Tree, whose massive roots dig deep into the earth, absorbing it and transporting it up its massive trunk and into its canopy many miles above, where the leaves on lower branches shed it to bind clouds as sources of moisture, leaving much of the lower canopy shrouded in white as if wrapped in cotton candy. Yet even solidified, clouds are still clouds, and the wind constantly pulls tufts away, with the occasional storms tearing free larger portions.

This is also how the Sky People came to be, when ages ago a tribe of people climbed the World Tree to live in its canopy, only to be scattered and spread when the Island Clouds they had settled on were ripped free to float through the skies.
addons.title: Ladder To Heaven

objects.text:
Your world's atmosphere has transformed into a vast, living tapestry of diverse sky biomes, each brimming with strange beauty and vibrant life.

This remarkable evolution stems from the sudden proliferation of floating landmasses—great chunks of terrain now drifting leisurely through the upper atmosphere. These airborne realms, ranging in size from modest platforms no larger than cottages to colossal islands the size of small nations, are sustained aloft by two newly discovered cloud types: Sea Clouds and Island Clouds.

The origin of these buoyant cloud types lies in a rare and volatile new element: Pyrobloin. Formed deep within the earth and expelled during volcanic eruptions, Pyrobloin reacts with water vapor in the atmosphere. The density of the surrounding vapor determines which of the two unique cloud types emerges from this reaction:

Sea Clouds: These clouds behave more like a dense, suspended liquid than a vapor. They possess a fluid, almost oceanic consistency, allowing those who reach them to swim, float, or even dive—though denser beings may gradually sink if they’re not careful. Their surreal, undulating surfaces are home to entire ecosystems of aerial marine life.

Creatures dwelling in Sea Clouds have undergone bizarre and beautiful adaptations to survive in this semi-liquid environment. Many have evolved reduced densities—flattened bodies, gas-filled bladders, or balloon-like anatomies—to remain buoyant within the vaporous sea. The result is a floating menagerie of glowing jellyfish, translucent sky-eels, and ribbon-like serpents that ripple through the clouds like waves.

Island Clouds: In contrast, these are semi-solid and malleable—similar in texture to firm yet pliable clay or dense foam. They serve as structural foundations, capable of supporting vast amounts of weight. Entire ecosystems and civilizations now rest atop these clouds, their solidity allowing for the creation of roads, buildings, gardens, and even forests in the sky.

While still light enough to float, Island Clouds are remarkably stable, making them ideal for supporting Sky Islands—the aerial landmasses that have reshaped the geography and politics of your world.

The rise of sky biomes has given birth to a new branch of humanity: the Sky People. These civilizations have taken root on floating islands, constructing cities suspended above the clouds. With access to abundant, untapped resources and unique aerial wildlife, these cultures have diverged dramatically from their land-bound counterparts.

The need for connection, trade, and defense has led to rapid innovations in aeroengineering. Advanced airships, gliders, and aerial rail systems now crisscross the skies, linking the scattered archipelagos of the air with the continents below.

These skybound realms are more than just scenic wonders—they are political powers, cultural hotspots, and scientific frontiers. From drifting monasteries of wind-priests to cloud-harvesting factories extracting rare vapors, the Sky Biomes represent a new age of discovery and dominion over the heavens.
objects.title: Sky Biomes

objects.text:
The moon has... changed. Once a desolate sphere of cold, dead rock, it now hangs in the sky as a vibrant, living world—an alien twin to Earth.

This remarkable transformation stems from a divergence in cosmic history. In this alternate timeline, the moon was not born from the colossal impact between Earth and the protoplanet Theia. Instead, it was a wandering dwarf planet, one with its own rich geology and a nascent atmosphere, that was eventually captured by Earth's gravity. By sheer cosmic coincidence, it settled into a stable orbit within the Goldilocks Zone.

Already bearing the essential conditions for life—liquid water, a breathable atmosphere, and Earth-like temperatures—the moon followed a developmental path eerily similar to Earth’s. Over billions of years, life emerged. But unlike Earth’s familiar biosphere, lunar life evolved under very different pressures: lower gravity, a unique rotational cycle, and a slightly altered atmospheric composition. The result is a world filled with strange, otherworldly organisms that are as beautiful as they are bizarre.

The presence of this living moon—clearly visible from Earth, glowing with alien vitality—has had a profound psychological and cultural impact on humanity. Inspired by the promise of a second home in the heavens, space exploration accelerated dramatically. Investment in rocketry, lunar colonization, and orbital infrastructure surged decades ahead of schedule.

Today, humanity has established multiple permanent settlements across the lunar surface. Regular travel between Earth and the Moon, while still costly, is no longer the exclusive domain of the ultra-wealthy. With determination and some financial planning, even middle-class families can afford passage to the lunar frontier. A new era of interplanetary civilization has begun—with the moon not as a cold relic of the past, but as a thriving partner in Earth’s cosmic journey.
objects.title: Vibrant Moon

objects.text:
Mars has changed. During the formation of the planet, it collided with and ultimately merged with a protoplanet similar to the way Earth did, resulting in a size similar to Venus, just barely smaller than Earth.

Mars is not the same cold, dry, desert world it once was; it now has a breathable atmosphere, a strong magnetosphere, an Earth-like climate, and vast oceans covering most of the planet's northern hemisphere. 

As Mars is much larger, it has fallen into a more stable orbit, preventing large temperature fluctuations caused by its varying distance from the sun. It has a similar level of gravity to that on Earth. 

With the presence of all the essential conditions for life, liquid water, a breathable atmosphere, and Earth-like temperatures, Mars has developed an abundant biosphere. The differing environments have led plants to primarily use carotenoids and anthocyanins for photosynthesis rather than chlorophyll, leaving most plants with orange, red, or purple colors.
