While convergent evolution ensures that things like trees, crabs, and sharks exist in recognizable forms to their Earthborn counterparts, many other species of both plants and animals are entirely alien to Earth's ecosystem.
objects.title: Vibrant Mars

addons.text:
There are two properties counteracting one another in this world. Half of the planet is completely made out of machine, metal, and chrome. While the other half is organic, carbon, and ever evolving. These two sides are often not good at getting along, this cyborg world now having to deal with two halves that find each other strange or stinky depending on each other's moods.

That doesn't mean there's no cooperation though. There are times when a symbiotic relationship is formed between flesh creature and metal. The two working in tandem, as the more logical metallic guides the ever changing organic. The two covering for each other's weakness. Sometimes, hybrids even happen, somehow.

If you end up here, you get to choose between either being born organic, metallic, or a naturally born cyborg version of the two. Either way, this world would be rather interesting...
addons.title: Machine Meets Flesh

addons.text: With the change, Gaia and Alaya have evolved as well. Gaia in particular now works less like a defense mechanism but as a legitimate AI of sorts within the planet. It's like an anti-virus, sending its machine agents to protect itself from anything disrupting its natural order. This makes Gaia stricter, but oddly, would have it get along more with Alaya as humanity no longer finds the need to strip Gaia of her resources as they are both machines.
addons.title: gAIa

addons.text:
Instead of being two completely separate sides of the planet, everyone is now a perfect synergy of synthetic and flesh. Born hybrids of machine and organics, these naturally occuring cyborgs live in this strange landscape, where everything is also partially flesh and not. This has caused a massive advancement to Biotech technology, which is now basically the default study of Biology in this world. So Doctors are now doubling as Technicians.

You too are born this way,  a perfect cyborg. Enjoy this new body, iron man.
addons.title: Iron Men Lives Again

objects.text:
One day, all life on Earth from Fauna to Flora turned mechanical. Babies crying became vocoded, flowers turned to steel rather than organic matter. This could’ve happened at any point in the past of your choosing, whether that be yesterday or a million years ago. This transformation happened with no explanation though if it occurred within living memory people will generally not assume this to be natural and have all sorts of theories regarding it whether that be alien lifeforms doing a cruel experiment on humanity, or an act of god. Whatever the case, all life has become advanced Robots.

Compared to Tinkertech, almost all life, even infants and plants, could have any possible innate technological capabilities that falls in a 3-4 range on the PRT rating scale. These capabilities are somewhat personalized, influenced by that lifeform’s environmental needs and desires as they developed to maturity so a little girl could be a literal bouncing ball of joy through shock absorbers and kinetic redirectors, or a young man could be able to reconfigure his body into a vehicular form to be on time, or a dog could have a tongue full of nanomachines that can be directed to clean anything from rust to silica, and so on.

Depending on the setting in question, these capabilities could merge with powers in interesting ways. For example in Worm, Shards could have components that physically connect to their Hosts physiology, with Triggers becoming trauma-less with some file restructuring. My Hero Academia might see the biological drawbacks some Quirks impose either be lessened or non-existent due to the new biology.

Even on an emotional level, logic is at least a little more prevalent. This could lead to a decrease in crime, beings that were originally AI are now viewed equally as people, maybe even natural advancements in technology. But regardless, this change is something that will impact that world heavily.
objects.title: Terra Machina

addons.text:
It seems that the all encompassing anime logic had also affected the Toons as well. Some Toons are instead born as stereotypical Anime Girls (and other gender), exhibiting exaggerated traits their tropes represent.

You can have people asking for reddit advice on how to work out their problems with their Tsundere girlfriends, cat girls who speak in UwU speech and always ends their sentences with a "nya", haughty rich elves who have the signature "OHOHOHO!" laugh being CEOs of large companies, etc.

They're still Toons. Just with a more... Anime flavor to them.
addons.title: Attack of the Anime Girls (and Boys, and Others)

objects.text:
Want to divide the world even further?

In this world, people are separated into two categories, Realsies and Toons. 

Realsies are the normal, realistic looking people. They make up the majority of the world and are basically what your world constitutes as "normal". 

While Toons make up a minority, and are characterized by their strange appearances and high durability, even moreso than Realsies. They seem to also have an effect where if there's enough toons in an area, the world could shift into THEIR logic, which could prove problematic to Realsies.

This is a major source of conflict within this world. Realsies tend to have more freedoms than Toons who are seen as potential danger to the public. There are however, Toons who fight back against that, and tend to be treated worse as a result. Especially since they may be durable... But they ain't immortal.

You can choose to be a Realsie or a Toon. As a Realsie, you still keep whatever power or other modifications you made to you and the humans around you. As a Toon, you get to choose your aesthetic (2D, 3D, Pixel, etc) which may have some mild effects on your abilities based on what you look like. Remember though, again, you may be durable but there are ways to kill Toons. For example, an Ooze that supposedly could easily melt your kind like quick acting acid.

Question is, do Toon Realsie Hybrids exist..?

I'll leave that up to you to decide.
objects.title: Art Fight!

objects.text:
Congrats! You can now have one wish be granted!

...as well as every other person in this world.

Once everyone reaches adulthood (so 18 in human years, other ages for sapient non humans) they are given a Genie. Said Genie is able to grant one wish per person, and only one (so no wishing for more). Despite that however, these wishes are near limitless! With the only caveat being wishes that cancel each other out is nulled (like a person wishing for world peace vs a person wishing for world war will have both their wishes not work and be wasted).

This did not stop people from making very precise, very stupid wishes however. The world has been intensely changed due to this. Lands turned into candy, people who wished to be superheroes flying around, a shitton of kaiju, it was a mess. And it was when this phenomena first occured.

It's been years now however and things have settled down. Most people have stuck to personal wishes so it doesn't get cancelled out. While you, upon entering this world, get your own genie. You may use this wish however you please while keeping in mind what was said above.

In a world where almost all wishes had come true, ravaged by human desires, you too get one powerful wish. Use it wisely.
objects.title: Maybe King Magnifico is Right?

addons.text: Worlds, as you know them, are no longer inorganic. Instead, they are supermassive organisms of unbelievable size and vast psychic potential that have been evolving and growing since the dawn of the universe. There are a multitude of different species, like those that live on their surfaces, with the rare predator included. All planets are capable of natural FTL travel, and tend to find stars to feed on (though not strictly on light, solar wind, or gravity itself), settling into 'orbits' and remaining sedantry for the vast majority of their lives. Different species even tend to settle into different, preferred orbital zones. Dwarf planets and moons are instead baby planets. Often hanging around their parents as they grow. Gas giants tend to be elder planets, that have lived long enough for their 'bones' to condense inwards, shrinking, yet with growing, obfuscating, atmospheres. Their psychic potential is far, far greater in their older age. Lesser organisms can be easily driven insane with too close a glimpse. With various 'stages' in between. Asteroids, on the other hand, tend to either be large clumps of organic material, pieces of dead- torn apart- planets, or smaller- but still massive- organisms. Potentially even parasites capable of FTL, or defunct, 'living' ships. The galactic society that has grown around a universe full of these organisms tends to lean far more into biotech on average as a matter or course. But other than that, they can be incredibly diverse. From cultures that attempt to, usually unsuccessfully, 'enslave' planets, to ones that attempt to kill and harvest them, to others that developed on a predatory planet that they help hunt and pillage other planets, to survivors of said predatory planets, and everything in between. As above, so below.
addons.title: The Biology of Planets

addons.text: The psychic capability of planets is even greater than first imagined. Not only are they capable of natural FTL movement through space, they are capable of directly creating wormholes to parallel universes. Though such an action tends to be rare, as it is highly exhausting and energy intensive. Still, this has allowed civilization to learn about and expand into alternate universes, and has created a long, long history of dimensional mixing. But that is not the only consequence of such potent psychic and anomalous abilities. Stars are now another faze of the planetary life cycle. Born- or evolved- rarely from an ancient elder planet (at death or not is unknown), stars are living as well. Great, psychic infernos whose atmospheres are near pure plasma, generated from their sheer power. Yet, these great infernos are mere shells- like eggs- for the bizarre, anomalous evolution taking place over millions, to billions of years within, and in the process feeding planets with their cast off energy. What hatches, eventually, are either failures, or organisms that defy all conventional understanding or description. 'Black Holes'- named such for the lack of information and understanding able to be gleaned from such things. For to even come close in astronomical terms is to be subject to forces not even normal planets can withstand. Practically tears in reality itself, that exist in multiple dimensions at the same time. The Failures, despite being called that, are still wonders of sheer might, power, and defiant physics. Biology ascended past any known material, weight beyond any reasonable grasp. 'Neutron stars'. Abominations. Often smaller than planets, barring newborns, but far, far more dangerous and powerful than any elder planet. It is debated whether they could be considered a form of zombie. Not alive. Not quite dead. But it is unknown. The multiverse is a strange place. Filled with life from top to bottom. As below, so above
addons.title: The Sleeping Stars

objects.text: What is "stone"? The planet and world you find yourself on has no 'naturally' occurring pure inorganic materials. Instead, it is entirely biological. Organic. Fleshy. With strata of breathing bones, nerves, veins, and rivers and oceans of blood and lymph, with even more esoteric- alien- biological processes indescribable. Flesh and more, all the way down to the planet's literal beating heart(s). With this gross biological abundance, life is far more advanced and evolved on average. A 'human' evolved on this planet into a similar form as on normal Earth would have a vastly improved immune system, at minimum, and would be carrying enough potent plagues to wipe out human life on that mundane Earth. Many organisms have become mutualistic or parasitic with the planet itself. More have evolved to absolutely enormous sizes, taking advantage of the sheer breadth of resources available to them. Meanwhile, the actual world has some degree of sentience and awareness, and even psychic abilities and anomalous properties. Its mind is utterly alien in comparison to the tiny specs living on the outermost layer of its skin. It takes a lot to attract its notice (like a nuke at minimum), and its notice may not be entirely survivable for the weak minds atop it.
objects.title: World of Flesh

objects.text:
The geography of your world has been retroactively and radically reshaped. Mountains, once relatively rare features, are now nearly ubiquitous. No matter where you go, peaks dominate the horizon.

Most new ranges are comparable in scale to the Alps, with a few rivaling the Himalayas. Existing ranges, however, have been dramatically expanded—longer, taller, and far more imposing. The tallest peaks now challenge Olympus Mons on Mars, soaring more than 20 km into the sky.

This transformation has profoundly altered the course of history. Humanity in this world is far less advanced and far less widespread than in the original timeline. Travel across vast distances is a monumental challenge, and while clever solutions for traversing mountains exist, the absence of railroads, airports, and other modern infrastructure means the Industrial Revolution never reached full momentum. As a result, much of the population remains in a medieval state of development.
objects.title: Mountain World

addons.text:
How the heck did this happen? Your world's geological past is a bit of a confounding mystery, but whatever caused it doesn't change the results. The world is now retroactively covered in large plateaus seperated by inhospitable mountains, cliffs, canyons, pillars of stone, and sharp peaks, as well as oceans and other bodies of water far below. There is a surprising lack of tectonic activity, despite all these raised geological features, and the weather tends to be windy but not extreme atop the ubiquitous plateaus that cover the world.

While there is still a lack of forests, and wood and water is semi-limited atop the plateaus, other natural resources are plentiful; especially food, stone and metal. Technology is still lower than 'modern' day, but varies between plateaus. Some have even experienced or are experiencing a slower form of industrial revolution, making use of alternative biofuels such as from bred animals due to the lack of natural coal. However, due to the great difficulty of travel between plateaus such advancements have not spread quickly or ubiquitously. Flight is the only realistic—if only semi-reliable—method of travel between plateaus, but is currently incapable of shipping vast amounts of resources. 

War is less common, even unheard of outside of a civil sense, due to people historically being limited to the plateaus they were born upon. Honor duels, duels to the death and other such traditions to settle conflict are common across cultures.
addons.title: Plateau World

objects.text: The world is flat! Well, flatter. It's still a sphere (unless you're heading somewhere strange), but now the terrain is retroactively covered in large, sweeping plains and rolling hills. With no mountains, cliffs, or other extreme terrain. Even the oceans are slightly smaller. Plus, nearly every biome of the surface of the world is a variant of grassland with the occasional small swamp. Due to the lack of mountains and tectonic activity, earthquakes and volcanoes (only dome and supers) are rare, but extreme weather is common. Tornadoes, hurricanes, high-speed winds and heavy storms are more frequent, last longer, and are more devastating. Floods are especially common due to the flatness of the terrain, and tsunamis are even more destructive. Due to the above, as well as the relative rarity of wood, infrastructure is minimal and the average technological level is far lower, with no industrial revolution even on the horizon. Most tools are made of rope, leather and bone. People themselves are mostly nomadic. With the lack of stable infrastructure, farming never developed properly; though herding developed to a far greater extent, alongside animal husbandry and wild medicine. Even chemistry, based on natural and easily acquired resources, is decently advanced. Predicting the weather is an extremely important skill in this world, giving people time to prepare for or escape storms. Weaving and tying knots is also considered a universal necessity by nearly every culture on the planet, and instead of paper and books, words are often made from weaves and knots, able to be 'written' into cord and spooled. There are abundant natural food sources, so even those with minimal knowledge of what is edible can keep themselves from starving.
objects.title: Grass World

objects.text:
The world you are going to is 97% covered in ocean. The remaining 3% land is concentrated in a handful of large islands scattered across the world. Thankfully, a good portion of the ocean is shallows less than fifty meters deep, mostly around said islands. The world was not always like this; humans and mammals managed to evolve before it became a water world. But it has been covered in water for at least the past two hundred thousand years. 

The human population, consequently, is much smaller and at a lower technological level due to limited natural resources. There is limited space to expand to and exploit, and not enough resources to create ships capable of traveling to distant islands from what is readily available. The ocean, outside of the shallows, is also more dangerous and chaotic due to extreme weather, and tsunamis can be an existential threat.
objects.title: Ocean World

objects.text: The world you are going to has no oceans of water—instead, they are all molten rock. The coasts experience constant tectonic rumbles and earthquakes, with the boiling magma often geysering into the air. Thankfully, this does not produce (many) poisonous and toxic fumes, and the atmosphere (barring the temperature) is still mostly breathable. On top of that, the constant volcanic activity and weather—Including tides, tsunamis, and hurricanes of lava—has built up impressive boundary cliffs, acting to mitigate some of the effects of the oceans on the continents. Though any islands are out of luck. This comes paired with an exceptionally active—if bizarre—magnetosphere. Especially over and through the magmatic oceans. Auroras are prevalent at all times of the year, nearly everywhere on the planet and especially near and above the oceans. Lightning is also near constant over said oceans, even on a clear day. The average temperature across the world is high. But only the oceans themselves are hot enough to melt rock. At its coolest, far from the actively boiling oceanic coasts, the temperature can drop under 100º Fahrenheit—38º Celsius. At the south pole, deep in the Antarctic, there may even be fleeting snow in the winter during particularly cold years. Despite the oceans, the planet is not without water. In fact, dry locales are practically unheard of. On a good day, the sky will be filled with bloated clouds, with intermittent but frequent rain showers. On a bad one, monsoons look tame and the sunlight will be completely choked out. Near the coasts, the rain can be boiling hot when it does occur, and the air will generally be filled with a fog of scalding steam. Regardless, the planet is (technically) still habitable, and life has evolved to survive. Any low and flat areas of land tend to be shallow jungle-swamps, similar to mangrove forests, with hardy trees, chaotic branches, and tangles of thick roots forming the 'ground' of the ecosystem for many species. Crocodiles—or species like them—are disturbingly abundant. Elsewhere, grass and bush evolved to withstand the heavy rains atop mountains and on slopes, vines being particularly common, alongside different forms of trees that have grown resistant to the weather. Humans, likewise, have developed adaptations to live in this world. Their ancestors did not evolve in a grassland, instead evolving in one of the many great jungle-forest swamps across the world. For this reason, they've kept a prehensile tail and gained enhanced balance even as they evolved partial bipedalism, pursuit predation, and the ability to throw things with high accuracy. Technologically speaking, they've developed sideways. Fire became much harder to reliably use due to the everpresent wetness, and getting close to the 'oceans' was fatal due to the heat. However, using the abundant and diverse natural resources around them, chemistry has advanced regardless, allowing the use of herbs and processed natural materials to cook foods, process materials, and create tools. As such, the average society on the planet can be considered around the level of the early iron / late bronze age.
objects.title: Almost-Hell World

objects.text: There's no one here but bones, haunted thoughts, and eldritch corpses that won't stop moving... Something went wrong long ago in whatever world you've tried to get to. Now, there's naught left but ash, corpses, and memories—of both people and places that once were—made manifest but twisted by rot, decay, and time. No one is here. Nothing is alive. No matter how convincing the guise of some of the memories may become, everything is dead. And if anything living does arrive, it won't be living for long. Nothing and nowhere here is suitable for the living. Even the rocks and ash are metaphysically rotten and sickly. The ground is stiff with rigor mortis. The air is stale, laden with dying breaths. What little water there is is bloated with choked whispers and glutted with disease and fetid blood. Even sound is dead and quiet, yet haunted by things that are not. Not even the remains of the locals can offer succor. They, what few remain, have been warped by this place. Bodies—corpses—twisted with decay and eldritch illusions. Haunted by a never ending hunger that transcends flesh and spirit; a hunger for what they once were. A hunger to be whole. They are maddened and hostile. The kindest of them are mere shades; memories and spirits gouged and abused, barely clinging to the phantoms of what once was and reliving nightmarish renditions of their lives over and over... but they are also hungry. And not necessarily sane. However it came to be, this world is a mockery of the living. Flesh abandoned, soul usurped by decay. To live here, is to either be dead and tormented, or hunted and hated by all that no longer is.
objects.title: Dead World

objects.text:
Space around and in the world is stranger than it would first appear. Numerous areas across and within it naturally have larger internal dimensions than their entrances and exteriors would suggest; whether those entrances be an arbitrary border, a forest, the base of a mountain, a hole into a cave, or a natural arch formed between two trees. 

These 'Pocket' spaces can be highly divergent from the places they are found within. Up to and including having skewed physical laws. As such, creatures, energies and materials that develop within can sometimes be alien and foreign compared to the immediate surroundings they form within. 

You are free to go as wild as you want with these pocket dimensions and warped spaces. Or, you can keep it rather simple and just make them bigger than they should be. How this integrates into the world's history is also up to you.
objects.title: Thanks! It has Pockets!

objects.text:
Physics is just broken in this universe apparently, as somehow, your world isn't a globe! How the heck that works is up to you, or not, and maybe it just happens to work like that.

Despite all this, the planter's gravity is still somehow livable. You can walk between "sides" or "corners" of whatever shape you chose to turn the world into, and gravity will adjust accordingly. This obviously changes both the landscape and the culture of your realm. How much so? You'll see. Lastly, you can have this affect either only your planet, or other planets as well, you decide.

The world is wide and round ,or maybe a square, or even an elephant. How wonderful.
objects.title: Flat Earth? Please, Get On My Level

objects.text:
This planet only has one continent. Whether it started out like this or a massive shift happened over the years or some fairy dust fell and everything is Pangea now, you decide. Regardless, one continent has a potential to be very problematic, with old borders being made near obsolete and old conflicts being sparked with this change. But then again, maybe this could also be a good thing? After all, travel should be a little simpler when everyone is connected like so.

The world is one, whether that is a good or a bad thing, you shall see.
objects.title: The Reunion Nobody Asked For

addons.text: You now have free rein to design the civilizations, cultures and histories of your world to your heart’s content. You can have wars between jazz age tribal confederations and gothic workers’ kingdoms, a grand impressionist culture shaped by ancient clans of chefs, or any other world you could desire. There will still be equivalents of all plot-relevant figures, factions, and conflicts in some form, however.
addons.title: Worldbuilding

addons.text: You have free rein to design what kind of landscapes and wildlife exist in this world. You can have things like lava honeycombs, mountain-sized fossils, islands that travel on storms or anything else you want. Likewise, you can make lifeforms like trees that mimic cities, semi-intelligent kangaroo tribes, crops that grow ores, microbes that form illusions and anything else you wish. Heck, do both and have living continents. Everyone loves those. Be aware that this cannot significantly change or mitigate any threats inherent to the setting, however.
addons.title: Landscaping

objects.text:
Looking at maps in your new world is going to be confusing, kinda. All of Earth’s continents and countries are replaced with a completely new set with different geography and names. You can design the shapes and borders of this new earth and give them new names as you wish, though history will remain generally the same.

You can also choose what kind of environments are on this map, as long as they are conceivable by known ecology, so no floating isles or bioluminescent grottoes (unless those kinds of things can happen in your world). You can also create any new wildlife that could have possibly evolved in these environments, but you cannot create any lifeforms significantly more dangerous, more useful, more intelligent, or weirder than similar earth wildlife. You can create new variants of strange creatures that already exist in the world, however. This will also not significantly change the world’s cultures. A civilization that developed in a forest that is now a tundra will only change as much as it needs to: No more, no less. They might use environmentally appropriate materials for food, clothing, and dwellings, but it will not change their styles or values. Despite having different names and places, these countries will have the same culture, language and history, give or take.

Likewise, historical figures will have different names and faces, but you will be able to clearly place who they are. For example, instead of General George Washington founding the United States of America after rebelling against the British Empire, Sir Roland Litwiller founded the Republic of Camberia after rebelling against the Tarvean Crown. All the general leading factors, details and consequences of this event will still happen as they did in your history, even if you’re going to have to re-learn all the new names, places and minor details for history class.
objects.title: Fantasy Map

objects.text:
Your chosen setting now has its very own World Tree. Similar to mythic trees like Yggdrasil or Irminsul, it is a colossal structure that rivals—or may even surpass—the highest mountains in your world.

The tree itself is composed of magical, fire-resistant wood of incredible toughness and serves as the heart of an entire enchanted ecosystem. From fairies to nymphs, centaurs, and glowing magical mushrooms and fungi, countless creatures make their home within its vast branches and roots. Any magical elements already present in your world are amplified the closer one gets to the tree.

Naturally, the Tree’s presence has had a profound impact on the culture and history of the world. As the focal point of countless religions and the foremost source of magical power, it is revered both as an irreplaceable cultural treasure and as a vital strategic resource. Countless alchemists seek to study it and harness its magical materials to further their research.

Yet, while it has been a boon to scholars and practitioners of magic alike, it has also been the cause of much bloodshed. Entire wars have been fought for control over its power.

You may decide on which continent the Tree takes root.
objects.title: World Tree

objects.text:
It seems that, lately, the world has started to look out for the little guy. There’s a quiet shift in the balance of fortune, not enough to make headlines or fill research papers, but enough to be felt in small, personal ways. People have begun to talk about a new kind of luck, not beginner’s luck, but “Poor Man’s Luck.”

It’s the kind of luck that makes the bus arrive just when you’re about to give up waiting, or lets you find a forgotten twenty in an old jacket pocket when your wallet’s thin. It’s the right person overhearing your struggle and offering help, the rain holding off just long enough for you to get home dry, or a small opportunity arriving at exactly the moment you need it most.

Those stuck at the bottom of the proverbial ladder are finding that, somehow, life has started to tilt ever so slightly in their favor. Minimum wage workers catching unexpected breaks, single parents finding small but meaningful moments of relief, students barely getting by discovering just enough luck to keep them moving forward. Not dramatically, not enough to change the system or erase hardship, but enough to ease the edges of it. Over time, these tiny strokes of fortune begin to stack up, like a chance meeting leading to a better job, a small favor turning into a lasting friendship, or a series of lucky breaks finally landing someone the promotion they’ve worked years for.
objects.title: Look Out For The Little Guy

objects.text:
Through some quirk of this world, some items, animals, or even concepts end up manifesting as anthropomorphized people. These gijinkas tend to have personality traits and abilities stereotypical of what they were based on, like a horse-human having the instinctual love of running and being very fast, or a human based on the country of the USA being rebellious and can summon eagles that they can command, and so on.

This has some great effects on this world's society. Maybe humans manifested from weapons tend to become elite soldiers in their respective countries, or those manifested from negative concepts, such as Violence, could have immense hatred for humanity and are thus feared? There are a lot of possibilities, especially in worlds with Parahumans and other powered individuals, these gijinkas gaining additional powers based on what they are based on.

It'll be beneficial to befriend one of these creatures; maybe there's even a small chance that you can manifest as one? Either way, the specifics depend on you.
objects.title: Gijinka Everything!

objects.text: As the name implies, Space isn't a vacuum, instead, it is filled with substances of your choosing. Maybe the planets are floating in an endless ocean? Maybe space is filled with oxygen so we can all breathe while flying there? Maybe space is actually filled with immense magical energies that make exploring them incredibly worthwhile for magic users? Either way, this changes space travel as you know it. Rocket science has to be relearned in this brand new frontier beyond the stars.
objects.title: Space Is Not A Vacuum

objects.text: You know those special places? The locations where the plot takes place? Always slightly different, more dangerous, more active than the rest of the world? Well, no more! Now, whatever special activity or heightened danger level that exists in the main area of the setting affects everywhere possible. In Worm? Every city becomes like Brockton Bay in terms of parahumans. Bleach? The soul-energy levels of Kankura town are now global (or galactic, multiversal, etc). If you're in a setting with mundane plot locations, they'll instead take on stranger properties that exist elsewhere- or even elsewhen- in the setting. And if no such strange locations exist, that won't be the case for long...
objects.title: Sharing is Caring

addons.text: Each dimension that your world has been split into follows a specific main theme or set of themes. However, there are still different zones with their own secondary themes. For example, a train-themed dimension will have an electric train zone, a steam train zone, a candy train zone, and a dragon train zone.
addons.title: Variations Within a Theme

objects.text:
This world is now separated into several different zones that are based on various themes. These themes can be anything from natural things like fruits and bones, to artificial constructs like planes or offices, or ideas like coolness or culture. You can decide whether zones will have a single theme or a mix of similar or idiosyncratic themes. Both the natural world and the civilizations of these zones will be based around these themes, as will the powers or magic used in them. Tests will grow on the trees of a school-themed zone, in a car-themed zone, every building will be a garage, and in a mobster-themed zone, capes will cast their powers through Tommy Guns. This may make it seem that everything about these zones can be stereotyped, though one can still find the diversity and nuance of an actual culture or ecosystem within them.

The seeming wackiness of different zones will not change the rules or tone of a world. Even though the power expressions are based around a theme, they still follow all the rules of a power system. This also goes for the laws of nature; a tree that is also a smokestack or a living gust of wind will still somehow follow all the natural or supernatural rules of biology of the original world. How the people of these zones dress and talk will be influenced by the zones they were raised in, but their actual culture and values will not be changed from how they would normally be in this world.

The size of these zones will depend on the scale of the setting. They can be the size of villages or city districts, countries or islands, or even entire planets or dimensions. The boundaries between themed zones will be clearly defined, shifting from one to another at the borders. These zones will also have their own climates that are not affected by neighboring zones. A scorching desert can border frozen sugarscapes, tropical beaches, and rocky jungles without a gradual transition between them.
objects.title: Themed Zones

objects.text:
It seems that your passing into this world has accidentally left the door open, so to say, to a lower dimensional qliphothic shell universe. Or in lay man terms a "Hell". Now the contents of this Hell can differ quite a lot, its severity depending largely upon how many times this drawback was taken. Either way the demons and or devils inhabiting this dimension can now travel into your chosen setting with relative ease, only needing to be willingly summoned or otherwise have enough power to cross over themselves. Though paradoxically the more power an infernal has the harder it is for them to be summoned, and a higher power from the hells forcing themselves into your world is severely weakened for quite some time.

This “Hell” need not be the traditional Christian underworld, and can instead be any kind of “bad” afterlife you can think of. It has no need to be connected to any real or fake religion either. Though the one constant is that the denizens are, generally speaking, bad news.

This comes in 3 tiers. The first being that the inhabitants, while indeed somewhat “sinful” and presupposed to what would be considered antisocial behaviour amongst humans aren't actually irredeemable or in any way pure evil, though some select members might be, it is not entirely by nature. Think along the lines of DxD devils or Hazbin Hotel sinners. Them being unleashed upon the world is still bad news, but they aren't complete monsters.

The second tier is an underworld of genuine pure evil, these are motivated by little other than malice and the desire to corrupt and destroy, forget antisocial behavior, these demons would treat the geneva convention like a to do list for little other reason than just to do it. It would take a genuine miracle of willpower and introspection for them to even seek redemption, much less actually get there. Think the Abyss from Pathfinder or Hell from DOOM.

The Third and final tier signifies a Hell of lovecraftian proportions, indescribable beings of pure torment to which even just looking at would be utter torture for the mind. Things which know only malice and corruption of good. The only “goal”, if you could call it that, is the complete and abject torment of every soul in existence in perpetuity, including themselves. These are powers of literally unimaginable evil. Should they get their hands on someone, said person is likely to experience a tailor made hell created specifically to corrupt, and abuse them into the worst possible version of themselves, in perpetual torment, for however long it takes for that to be permanent. Think the worst Nephandi and Demons from the World of Darkness, or the Warp as it exists in Warhammer 40K.
objects.title: Hellish invitation

objects.text:
The world has become more dangerous and strange. Although there are no supernatural creatures unless they already existed or were introduced through other Modifiers, there are now individuals with supernatural and sci-fi abilities in your starting world, though these people are rare.

There are now different ninja clans whose training makes them low-level superhumans and gives them ability to use different Ninjutsu like Shapeshifiting, Elemental manipulation, Shadow teleportation, Animal control, Dōjutsu, Genjutsu and much more.

There are Samurai and Martial artists who can withstand low caliber bullets and defeat whole squads with nothing but their Martial arts. There are also people who possess psychic powers like Telekinesis, Telepathy, Clairvoyance, Pyrokinesis, Cryokinesis, Teleportation and more.

Diviners who can see the past and future, assassins who can bend the trajectory of bullets they fire, super geniuses who can create advanced tech, strange viruses and more, secret government and corporate supersoldier or bionic programs, genetically engineered animals, and much more.

Most of these powered people are hidden to the wider world and prefer to avoid attracting too much attention. There still will be different individuals or organisations who will know about them. The general threat rating of these beings does not usually exceed a PRT threat rating of 1–5, with only rare cases reaching a maximum of 6-7.
objects.title: The Strange World

addons.text:
Rather than allow themselves to be disrupted, many states and corporations will begin moving to monopolize these new resources for themselves. They will mainly accomplish this through endless war.

Major powers will begin drumming up support among their allies and citizens to “liberate” places that just so happen to have major deposits. New weapons will be developed using human experimentation and tested on civilian populations.

New resources will become proprietary to the biggest corporations as they are discovered and entire economies, industries and livelihoods become reliant on their supply. Irresponsible use of these resources by corporations might also cause new types of health conditions, pollution and disasters.
addons.title: Dick Cheney’s Paradise
Mutagenic Materials
addons.text: The new exotic materials that cover the world are mutagenic in nature, this mean that only creatures near these material veins will undergo mutation. While this does make the world somewhat safer, it also makes the new wonder materials harder to access, as the area nearby will be infested with mutated creatures.

addons.title: Alpha Mutants
addons.text: In addition to the hordes of mutated creatures surrounding them, each pocket of exotic material will be protected by an extremely mutated animal. These animals may even be able to tap into the properties of their material, thus granting them special abilities.

objects.text:
Massive deposits of several strange new types of ores, minerals, crystals, fluids and gases that don’t appear on the known periodic table begin growing deep inside the earth of your World.

These resources are easy to work with known industrial methods, can have very high energy density and efficiency, can be refined into new supermaterials and fuels at a mass scale, and, if used consciously, are clean and sustainable. This will even extend to medicine and agriculture. This will create a new boom in industry, science and technology that the world has never seen.

These materials begin resonating in strange ways when exposed to powers, magic, psionics, qi, ect. Through experimentation, different alloys and compounds can be made to perform controlled effects such as hardening, levitating, difracting light, contracting and expanding, or conducting or blocking the flow of esoteric energies through this resonance. This makes them excellent for support gear, tinkertech, containment devices, magical foci and enchanted artifacts. When combined with existing esoteric materials, these elements can increase their energy output and other aspects, as well as stabilize dangerous byproducts and volatile reactions.

Many existing industries and economies will be upended by the discovery of these resources as new innovations and opportunities arise. There’s alot of money and inventions to be made here for those who are quick, smart and lucky.
objects.title: Unobtanium Rush

objects.text: Your Soulmate(s) now have their fates tied with you since lives past. As such, you share abilities from your past life that can be triggered so long as you're in close proximity as one another. This is a relationship that transcends time; whether it be romantic, familial, hatred, or even platonic. Your fates are bound in this life then the next.
objects.title: Across Time and Space

objects.text:
Exactly one year after your arrival in the chosen world, broadcast panels begin appearing across the planet. These panels belong to the List, a powerful neutral entity. The List observes, analyzes, and ranks the world and its inhabitants, forming global rankings and granting rewards to those who reach the top.

The evaluation is divided into several ranking categories. The primary and most important is Power Level, which measures overall combat and supernatural strength. The second major category is Local Power System Development, reflecting how advanced and refined people's in the world’s primary system is (such as Devil Fruits, Nen, Chakra, or similar systems). A third and subsequent rankings are based on what is most widespread or culturally significant in that world, such as mastery of specific skills, accumulated wealth, political or social influence, ownership of powerful artifacts, territorial control, and similar factors.

The scope of each ranking varies. Some lists may include the top 1,000 individuals, others the top 100, top 10, or any number in between. Entering a ranking grants rewards, with their scale directly tied to one’s position. These rewards can include direct increases in power, the granting of artifacts, expansion or refinement of existing abilities, removal of weaknesses, complete recovery, and in rare cases, resurrection.

The List may grant a synergistic secondary ability or a weaker power with high growth potential, but it will never bestow a power equal to or greater than the one that qualified the individual for the ranking in the first place. The List follows a strict principle of balance and analytical evaluation: those near the bottom receive modest but useful rewards, while those at the very top gain powerful enhancements suited to their current strength, desires, and needs. All rewards are always tailored to the context of the world being evaluated.

Whenever someone enters a ranking, the List provides a detailed explanation of why that individual occupies their position. These explanations may be delivered through written analysis, visual breakdowns, or full broadcast-style presentations.

Once all rankings for that cycle are completed, the List disappears. It will reappear only after a long interval, such as 10, 100, or even 1,000 years.

If you are sufficiently powerfull, you also can enter the rankings and receive rewards. If you possess the ability to world traveling and remain in a world long enough, the List may follow you to evaluate that new world. In such cases, you will not be immediately included in the main Power Level ranking, as you were already evaluated in previous cycles. However, you may still appear in other rankings, and after a long enough period, the List may once again include you in the primary ranking.
objects.title: World's Ranking

objects.text:
Everyone sentient is now a Muppet. This causes them to become more family-friendly in their actions, and the world's logic seems to follow Muppet logic as well (villains still commit crimes, but more classic supervillain stuff). Strangely enough, while everyone tends to be 3 to 4 feet tall now, everything remains made for human size in mind. 

Also, there is a single person who remains normal, but no one seems to find it odd. It is whoever would be funniest in this scenario.
objects.title: FELT

addons.text: The inhabitants of the New World are the sole survivors of the Multiverse. There are no other dimensions left aside from those that make up the New World. Perhaps other multiverses might exist, but if they do no one can reach them without running face first into something that will erase them for trying. The New World, the Last Light, and everything in this star system was created by a coalition of powerful beings from your purchased Alternate Earths with the mutual goal of not dying. As such, even if it consists of beings with as varied motives as the Warrior Entity, an Aeon, YHWH, Lucifer, a Q, and SCP-████, they would all still work together (even if begrudgingly) because there is something out there that scares them too much not too. On the one hand, with such a powerful group actively working together to try to empower humanity and whatever other species were brought here, the situation is technically more stable. On top of that, the various power systems and tech trees being available means that they’ll be better prepared to handle whatever is coming. On the other hand, something that both terrifies such a group of beings so much as to use a hail mary like this, and is able to destroy the rest of the multiverse is so dangerous that it might not be enough without help from some Outside Context Problem. Note: If you have Homecoming or some other ability that lets you traverse the Omniverse, expect to catch a lot of attention.
addons.title: The Last Hope in a Decimated Multiverse

addons.text: It seems that not everyone has crossed over yet. Now even after your insertion, more people, places, and subdimensions will continue to be added to it. Strangely the world doesn’t seem to ever run out of room, instead it constantly expands with each addition while never changing its gravity, atmospheric pressure, day-night cycle length, year length, or any other effect this would logically have. At least once a year, a new set of major ISOTs will happen, ranging from just a single new nation to one that rivals the size of the first one, with many, many smaller ISOTs affecting singular individuals or small villages happening every few weeks. At first, there will be more people and places from your purchased worlds, but over time it will expand to cover more realities until your world is a complete Sci-Fi / Fantasy Kitchen Sink. If you have The Last Hope in a Decimated Multiverse, these additional ISOTs will be other survivors of the multiverse who through one method or another managed to hang on to existence after the Decimation just long enough to reach the Last Light. Perhaps they hid in mobile pocket dimensions, or they temporarily exited the timeline just to be yanked towards the only piece of time to still exist when they reentered it? The methods are as variable as those ISOTed are, and the creators of the Last Light will have their hands full integrating these survivors into the solar system, leading to a greater potential for undesired events like wars to happen.
addons.title: Endless Mode

addons.text: It seems as though the New World was created using the remains of the worlds destroyed in the Incursions. As more Incursions happen, more people will be brought here as each Singularity is subsumed into it. Though whether the creator of this world has good intentions or not, who can say? Either way, the ISOTs are much more chaotic, and people are left horrified as many now know why they were brought here. If you have The Last Hope in a Decimated Multiverse, then the Last Light was created to survive the Incursions. The multiverse still exists, but is dying, and when the last Incursion happens, something which was responsible for the Incursions will finally notice and begin to track those surviving fragments to the New World. Since the Incursions are a rather chaotic affair, it is far harder for the creators of the Last Light to plan for the Singularities inclusion, many of them being haphazardly thrown into the star system even as the next one arrives, resulting in far more chaos.
addons.title: Battleworld

addons.text:
Along with peoples and elements from different worlds being brought here, Amalgams of characters from different worlds will begin to appear, with their histories and abilities being merged like with the baseline Amalgam, and while some can seemingly be random on the surface, they will have some thread to connect them, either through similar experience or themes, and will add an extra dose of chaos to this world.

These Crossover Amalgams can be especially powerful due to the combination of different experiences, abilities, and knowledge base from their composite existence; should a Crossover Amalgam meet one of the people who make them up, both would feel a connection as a subconscious acknowledgement that they share a connection, but nothing more beyond that. This also extends to Amalgams made up from people from the same world; as an example, along with Spider-Man and Moon Knight, there will be an Arachknight present.

If you have The Last Hope in a Decimated Multiverse, then these Amalgams are not an accident but something planned, either being the results of previous attempts to create surviving worlds that failed or used as a means to create an individual or a group with the ability to prevent the destruction of the Last Light and perhaps restore the Multiverse. Whether this “throwing everything at the wall to see what sticks” attempt will work or not remains to be seen.
addons.title: Crossover Amalgams

addons.text:
Where once there was one new actor in play who was a fan of the source material, there are now several, with each being a fan of one of the other worlds whose elements have been brought onto this new world.

This, in turn, leads these people to being Wildcards and, depending on circumstances, force multipliers depending on their powers and knowledge regarding other settings. They are likely to team up with people and characters they're familiar with or actively recruit them to their factions if possible, being everything from a foot soldier to an advisor and more to whomever they side with, sharing what meta-knowledge they possess to tip the scales. However, unlike their powers, their knowledge regarding settings outside their favourite is less reliable, dooming their allies because they fail to understand the strength of another power system just as easily as conquering their foes.

Should you have Endless Mode, then just like the yearly addition of new ISOTs, there will be more Wildcards appearing, with them either being only one person or the same number there were originally. Due to this, the level of chaos from new ISOTs arriving will increase and, as time goes on, people will realize new Wildcards will appear each year; this will lead individuals and groups to go after these Wildcards for their own reasons, from recruitment to hunting them and more. As more arrive, the more likely Wildcards will band together or come into conflict with one another due to distress; wars breaking out because of Wildcards will become increasingly more likely as time goes on.

Should you have Crossover Amalgams, then it becomes possible for them to have two sets of power or skill rather than one: a Kryptonian who is a Jujutsu Sorcerer, the combined tech bases of Gerald Robotnik and Dr. Light, etc. However, good synergy between these powers and/or skills is not guaranteed, with the pairing being more burden than boon being possible.
addons.title: Info Powerhouses

objects.text: Rather than having your Crossovered Alternate Earths retroactively be considered one and the same, they are all different worlds existing in different dimensions. Or they used to be anyway. It seems someone or something took various individuals, towns, cities, countries, continents, and / or supernatural subdimensions from these Alternate Earths and dumped them all at once onto a virgin planet. Whether this planet is a version of Earth without humans or a truly new world where the only landmasses are those dumped here is up to you, although either way any natural resources will be at Virgin Earth levels. You may decide exactly what parts of each setting were transported here, from specific individuals to entire nations or parts of them, with as few or as much ISOTed from any given world as you want. Maybe Brockton Bay is in this new world, but instead of Worm's USA they are now in the northeast territory of the USA from Metal Gear Solid, which only had its eastern half transported here while everything West of Missouri is home to Code Geass' Brittania, except for a small city on the West Coast called Angel Grove home to the Power Rangers, and somewhere in this territory one can find a very confused Cain, the only 1st Generation Vampire from the World of Darkness, and the only one of his kind in this New World. In addition, you may decide where they are placed, whether they are logically spread around the closest equivalent location in the New World, or somewhere else. Thus, the Teen Titans could find their version of California landlocked as it is plopped in the middle of the North Chinese Plains, while elsewhere the Eldians find themselves freezing in the south pole, and Digimon such as the Royal Knights find their home suddenly in the ‘real’ world. All worlds affected can optionally bring their various supernatural subdimensions along for the ride, though you once again can decide if any inhabitants or civilizations that lived in said subdimensions are brought too or if this New World just spontaneously developed an empty version of it. Optionally, you can choose to merge compatible dimensions, with the resulting dimension taking after its component parts, though you can choose for it to take after one over the other such that the new psychic plane is more like that of D&D than the Warp. This can cause some friction if, for example, you bring more than one version of the Greek Pantheon into the same realm. If you choose not to bring any of a specific world's subdimensions that its power systems rely on, then either one of the other subdimensions can take over that role, such as the Reverse Side of the World being the source of a Ferelden mage’s power instead of the Fade, or a freshly made 'generic' version of it will manifest to fill the role, allowing Psykers to draw power from the new psychic plane rather than the Warp. All supernatural power systems from the component worlds will immediately permeate across this new world, with anyone able to learn any system they aren’t incompatible with, and any children born afterwards able to manifest inborn powers like Quirks or Innate Cursed Techniques. In addition, all technologies possible in the component world's tech trees will be possible in this new one, even technologies impossible in one of the component settings, and all unique resources found in the transported lands like Sakuradite, Unobtainium, Dust, and more will have deposits formed across the planet where they would sensibly be found, with about as much rarity as their homeworlds. If one or more of the component Settings is Interplanetary in scale, you can optionally have entire planets ISOTed to the New System. The same if they’re Galactic in scale, bringing entire interstellar civilizations or at least parts of them to the New Galaxy. The same can be done if you take a modifier that expands the base setting, like Celestial Cycle or Galactic. Overall, this New World is looking forward to years of chaos as people rapidly scramble to find their place, wars are sparked between nations looking for resources, land, or to spread and / or suppress ideologies, supernatural forces clash for dominance, new powers and technologies upend the balance of power, and more. You will arrive at the same time as everyone else in this new world. Good luck. Note: You can decide what happened to the original worlds. Maybe they still exist with their inhabitants freaking out at the disappearance of entire nations and the resulting political and ecological mayhem that ensues. Maybe they still exist along with the nations in question, the ISOT’ed world actually possessing perfect copies of the original nations and their peoples. Maybe they exist in completely different multiverses with no realistic way for anyone who could to travel back to their home universes even if they could. Or maybe their homeworlds were completely destroyed in some multidimensional calamity, this new world an Arc hastily put together by various Gods and other Powers That Be who snatched everyone up seconds before they died. If the latter, you can decide which if any ISOTed beings of sufficient power were involved in its creation, up to and including beings like the Warrior Entity, the Q Collective, or the Aeons, with everyone being forced to ‘play nice’ whether by tense negotiations or simply the threat of M.A.D.
objects.title: ISOT Map Game

addons.title: Degradation Zombies
addons.text: Rather than an infectious plague of zombies, the world must deal with Degradation Zombies. The good news is that this variant of zombie is not infectious, as instead they are the soulless corpses of heavily Degraded people that have yet to be fully erased from existence, meaning they can't turn others into their kind. The bad news is that they retain the powers they held in life. Worse news is that there are potentially entire civilizations worth of Degraded people that could come back as Zombies, all ready and willing to kill everything in sight in an omnicidal tide as what little of their minds cry out for everything to just End. These Degradation Zombies have an origin point, some location where the Degraded bits of the universe gathers together that they make their way out of. Normally there would be some guardian or system in place that prevents them from leaving, but for whatever reason that isn't the case anymore, allowing them to escape. Through a variety of means whether walking, flying, or teleporting they will spread all over the world seeking to kill everyone they find. Degradation Zombies are also walking cognitohazards, as the mind instinctively rejects the existence of that which was rejected by the turning of the Spiral, causing anyone without unique defenses to be weakened in their presence, with the effect growing the more powerful and the more numerous they are. While a normal human might be able to fight a Shade, the most ephemeral of the Zombies who barely have any undegraded concepts they are connected to, the strongest of them can kill even the likes of Alexandria if they come in numbers. The worst are those who still have semi-intact souls, as they can plan and reason making them more effective. Negotiation is possible with them, but unlikely to work as their minds suffer even more than normal due to being just as affected by their cognitohazard, in addition to the horrible condition Degradation has left them in, many being partially melted or fused together with other Degraded souls who share similar concepts, some being entire families of people fused together. Fortunately they tend to come in 'waves' that are somewhat easier to prepare for in exchange for being much harder to fight off, and the location they come from may eventually be sealed off again if you can find a new person with a suitable power to act as their Warden or develop a new system to contain them. But it will be immensely difficult, and time confusing to do. Even if you succeed, you will know that this is the eventual fate of everyone should Degradation not be stopped. Note: The size of the ‘waves’ depends on Z-Day. If you don’t have its Addons, then they are large but somewhat manageable, at least enough for civilization to still exist (though at most it’d be 1/10 the size it could be with Z-Day alone). If you also have The Tide, then they are massive enough that only a few select holdouts containing the strongest defenders have any chance of surviving them. If you have The Devouring End then there are no waves at all, as instead every fallen civilization has escaped at once intent on destroying everything in the hopes that their suffering might end.

objects.text: You know all those things which only show up a few times before never appearing again, stuff that was retconned, plot threads or hooks that were never expanded on? Now there’s an explanation as to why, and it's not pretty. The firmament upon which the universe was built is fundamentally broken, forcing a downward spiral upon existence itself. Every few centuries, the universe just breaks and some things are simply lost. Of course it reforms almost instantly, but the result is unequivocally less than what came before. Degradation is indiscriminate about what it wipes away, a single Collapse might erase an empire from the pages of history while also altering someone’s hair color. Additionally, Degradation isn’t an all-or-nothing state, something can be only partially Degraded, usually from losing something related to it to Degradation. Even if something is completely Degraded, there are still a few bits of it left in the form of connections it had with other things, condemning anything that suffers it to a torturous existence as a few ragged shreds of conscious thought and connection held in perpetual suffering. This segues into how Degradation impacts those not directly removed by a Collapse. If someone knew or was connected to something which has since Degraded, then their memories/connection is also somewhat degraded. If a major event took place only to be subsequently lost, people who met each other during that event might be rendered unable to remember how they met, or may even no longer recognize each other at all aside from a vague sense of familiarity. In the case of particularly important and intense connections this can cause issues. For example, a student losing their teacher and parental figure; they unequivocally know that this person existed yet are unable to remember more than a few scrap details about them, causing much mental distress. The metaphysical process of Degradation may interact oddly with certain aspects of reality if they exist, for instance if there is an afterlife then there may be a lesser known - or even entirely unknown - deeper layer where the resulting detritus of Degradation naturally gathers, a junkyard of broken memories and eroded dreams. While the average person may not know about Degradation, if there is anything remotely abnormal about the world then the "higher-ups" in the world, be they powerful gods, wise sorcerers, or eccentric geniuses, will likely have some way of knowing about it, and there may even be a few initiatives or plans in the works to try and counteract it, not that anyone has succeeded yet. If there are Gods in the universe you are going to, they are either unable or unwilling to prevent Degradation as a whole, although they may have ways to protect themselves and their chosen few.
objects.title: Universal Degradation

objects.text:
While theoretically endless and capable of supporting infinite growth, the universe and its many worldlines despise imbalance. Every so often the universe performs a sort of automatic error checking on all the worldlines to determine if they’re healthy, and indeed most worldlines are. 

However, sometimes a worldline fails the check; maybe an entity is corrupting reality or maybe there’s a bunch of time travel twisting the local timeline into a gordian knot. Whatever the case, when a worldline fails the check the universe attempts to “correct” the situation. The only problem is that the universe’s methods of error handling start at apocalyptic natural disasters designed to wipe worlds clean and escalate all the way to erasing the entire worldline if all else fails to solve the problem.

Unfortunately for you, the worldline you’ve arrived in is one that is incredibly likely to fail the upcoming error check. The exact reason may vary, but the end result remains unchanged; your worldline is currently on course to be “corrected.” Your only options are to either solve the problem before the universe decides to do so for you, or to find some way to escape the worldline entirely.
objects.title: Worldline Error Correction

objects.text:
In your world, there exists a society of martial artists known as the Murim. Depending on your starting world, these forces may either be hidden from the public, or operate openly.

These martial artists strengthen themselves by accumulating and refining Ki through meditation and specialised breathing techniques. There are many different martial arts techniques, and mastery of these arts grants superhuman abilities such as enhanced strength, speed, durability, and the power to perform different techniques depending on which martial arts they learn.

The Murim is typically, divided into many different sects, clans, and factions, who mainly, though not always fall in one of these alignments:

Orthodox Sects, which uphold traditional virtues and pursue justice.

Unorthodox Groups, which operate outside conventional norms and are sometimes associated with bandits or criminal organisations.

The Demonic Cult, a powerful and often antagonistic faction that practices forbidden or “evil” martial arts.
objects.title: The World of Murim

objects.text: You know how there are fears of humanity eventually running out of non-renewable resources, such as fossil fuels, oil, minerals, and other such? Well no worry, because now they've all been restored to peak levels! Every oil well, every mine, and every other source of non-renewable resources has been completely refilled as if humans had never touched them. This even extends to certain renewable resources, such as rainforests being restored, meaning that potentially centuries of ecological damage has been undone on top of humanity gaining centuries of potential resources to use. Truly this must be a good thing, right? Wait, what do you mean a bunch of people who worked in mines died when the tunnels they dug suddenly became filled in and the equipment they had inside was destroyed, causing countless millions of dollars in damages? Or that thousands of people lost their homes and primary source of income when their farmland got replaced with pristine rainforest? Hold on, how many towns got damaged or even destroyed when large areas got turned to pre-developed land? What do you mean militaries all around the world are gearing up to invade other nations!? They want to steal each other's resources now that they are back!? Why!? Maybe this wasn't the best idea after all...
objects.title: Resource Shortage Averted

objects.text: This world, this universe, is not like the one you were born in. Instead of countless stars, planets, moons, and such floating in a vast vacuum, the universe is a continuous volume of matter, with large caves or other cavities, some of which can be as large as entire worlds from a more conventional universe, acting as the equivalent of planets. There are vast regions where the matter is completely solid, smaller regions where the matter is nearly entirely liquid, and some few spaces where it is gaseous to the point one can convince themselves that they are merely in a dense nebula found in a more conventional reality, not to mention those regions made of various types of exotic matter. Needless to say, the laws of physics are much more fluid here than it is in your universe, especially gravity which depending on location can be either non-existent or pointing in an entirely arbitrary direction. In fact, physics is so fluid that it can be entirely different depending on where you are. For instance, the local version of earth has physical laws almost identical to a normal earth, such that somehow it has evolved life and civilizations matching it, however the atmosphere doesn't end at the edge of space but instead it is cut off by the outer edge of the continent sized caverns humanity lives inside of. The 'Earth' is divided into a handful of continent sized caverns, with roughly 30% of the caverns having land while the other 70% are entirely oceans. The 'surface' is roughly spherical, centered around a point that the local gravity arbitrarily points 'down' towards. The ceiling that the sky ends at is held 'up' by miles thick columns of nearly inviolate exotic matter simply called Firmament for its role in keeping the 'heavens' held aloft. At the edges of the continents lie massive walls of Firmament somewhere between 10 and 100 miles thick separating them, with various tunnels ranging from a dozen feet to several miles wide one can travel through to reach the other continents, some being land based that you can walk through while others are covered in or even entirely filled with water that require boats or submarines to travel through, and others still being so hard to traverse by foot or ground vehicle that flight is the only realistic means of traversing. Most connecting tunnels are at or near 'ground' level but a handful go through the 'earth', requiring specialized environmentally sealed vehicles to traverse through the extremely hot tunnels, some of which cut through inhospitable caverns filled either with volcanic magma regions, unbreathable toxic atmospheres, or both, before reaching the middle of another 'continent'. In the sky, one can find large masses of pseudocrystalline exotic material embedded in the ceiling that consistently go through phases of high and low energy states every 24 hours. In their higher energy state, they release enough light and heat to illuminate the entire cavern, while in their lower energy state they dim until they become small pinpricks of light akin to a starry sky, thus simulating a day and night cycle, timezones being the result of each 'continent's day-night-cycle not being synchronized with one another. In addition, there is a singular mass of material above each 'continent' that is less bright and operates on a 28 day cycle that is the equivalent of the moon. Needless to say, the rest of the solar system, if it even exists, is found in caverns so distant that they are completely unknown to man. Somehow, humanity and human civilization both exist and have a 90+% identical history and culture to the Canon universe of your Setting. Though differences do exist (which you can decide what they are if you want), for the most part Canon still happened and will happen in some form. You can also decide how this affects any space faring civilizations found in Canon, perhaps they came from distant caverns and emerged from the sky via the very rare sky tunnels that the local version of the space program explores? As for other dimensions, who knows, maybe they are all like this, or maybe this one is an anomaly, again it's your choice. Note: If you decide this is the norm and choose to go to Worm, then the Entities primarily travel to new 'worlds' through rare 'void' dimensions that are similar to more conventional universes except for being so empty that there is only a single star system's worth of matter for every galaxy that exists in our universe, but they are otherwise largely identical to Canon.
objects.title: Space? Never Heard of It.

addons.text:
With the addition of both the Hollow Earth and Cloud Sea, Earth can now be roughly divided into three layers, the Lower, Middle, and Upper Stratum. Furthermore, with the extra evolutionary pressure and variables from the Hollow Earth and Sky Biomes, the makeup of the planet is practically optimized for the development of exotic life.

The Upper Stratum consists of the atmosphere as well as the sky island and cloud seas, being home mostly to life of aerial persuasion, although some islands may have purely terrestrial lifeforms which were trapped there and evolved separate from the surface.

The Middle Stratum encompasses the surface as well as a few miles underground, covering forests, plains, mountains, and shallow caves and other such biomes. This almost resembles the world of a normal Earth, save for the many fantastical creatures which call these biomes home. 

The Lower Stratum consists of the Hollow Earth as well as any other deep cave systems. Its inhabitants are primarily those of the Hollow Earth, however there are other cave systems which have developed some truly alien life, secluded from the surface in nothing but the dark for millennia.

As for the sea, it's a bit of a mix. While the upper layers can be seen as part of the Middle Stratum, the abyssal depths solidly cross over into the Lower Stratum, with many a passageway existing connecting the depths of the ocean to the Hollow Earth.
addons.title: Planets Are Like Onions

addons.text: With the Moon being just as vibrant and filled with life as Earth, it is no longer spared from the same unique development as Earth, its ecology and lifeforms just as bizarre and exotic as those on the Earth.
addons.title: Exotic Moon

addons.text: The death of the Proto-Entity who crashed into the Earth was no accident or fluke, rather they were slain in a brutal fight which left all the Proto-Entities who partook dead, their bodies drifting and crashing to the various planets, leaving the entire Solar System a graveyard ripe for the development of exotic life. This has had consequences, as now the effects of Exotic World have extended to every other planet in the Solar System, drastically amplifying their already existing ecosystems and life as life develops powers in adaptation to their surroundings. It should be noted that due to each planet getting remnants from different Entities, the subsequent life that develops on each planet will draw from differently specialized Shards. This means that while there is bound to be plenty of overlap, in time each planet will develop different trends and themes in powers. If taken with Exotic Moon then its effects spread to every moon in the Solar System as well, with varying levels of consequences. Jupiter for instance, with its 95 moons, is the Solar System equivalent of Australia, a veritable melting pot of dangerous life that seems to be trying to kill everything else around. Same for Exotic Leveling spreading the life force leveling system to other planets as well.
addons.title: Did I Say World? I Meant Worlds

addons.text:
The meta-energy all life forms possess is, at least in part, the result of the Proto-Entity who died here, with the remnants of its Shards which integrated into all life forms facilitating the flow of energy. This increases the efficiency of both transferring and benefiting from this life energy, making the effects more noticeable and the maximum able to be reached drastically higher.

But that isn’t all, as due to their shared source this life energy can now augment and amplify the natural Shard powers the many species of this world have evolved. While it may take plenty of time and effort, it is entirely possible to raise a natural power to match or even surpass the greatest of Parahuman powers.

This isn’t all good news though, as all life forms can benefit from this and indeed they have. There now exist Titans in the world, animals which have survived and killed enough to accumulate such vast reserves of life energy that they are incredibly long-lived and powerful, being the origin for many myths.
addons.title: Exotic Leveling

objects.text: The mutations to flora and fauna brought about by Bizarre Ecology are nothing new, in fact they’ve always been here, after all the influence of Shards has been felt for hundreds of millions of years ever since a Proto-Entity died here long ago. And with millions of years worth of evolution, helped along by the fragmented remains of the deceased Entity’s shards, there is the potential for some truly incredible lifeforms to emerge. From serpentine dragons soaring the upper atmosphere and coasting on electromagnetic waves to great krakens lurking in the abyssal depths which wield the tides themselves as hunting tools, all sorts of unique and exotic life has developed, some still resembling the lifeforms of a normal Earth, others completely alien to what you once knew. And humanity hasn’t escaped unchanged either, after all they still evolved on this fantastical world and it shows. While the modern human would doubtlessly be rendered extinct, the many subspecies of humanity have adapted and evolved just as all other life has. While their shared roots are still evident, the various biological and even powered adaptations possessed by the subspecies of humanity are much more prevalent than they were before. Additionally, Bizarre Ecology’s effects have loosened the limitations on what natural powers can be developed, their maximum potential increasing in both scope and versatility even if the average being remains similar.
objects.title: Exotic World

objects.text:
No one in the world benefits from plot armour anymore. While this does not mean that seemingly miraculous coincidences could not happen at all, they will remain incredibly rare occurrences.

This won’t make anyone smarter or prevent occasional mistakes from happening, but it does mean that enemies won’t forget to fire on escaping heroes or inexplicably lose any semblance of skill in firearms, nor will enemy commanders suddenly lose all tactical and strategic acumen.
