Similarly, the hero will not be able to miraculously survive injuries which, by all rights, should have had him dead; the consequences of any injury will be as severe as they should be, potentially leaving people crippled for life; and any actions taken will not be brushed under the rug, resulting in much-deserved consequences.

This works both ways. As such, just as the protagonists won't benefit from any plot armour, neither will the antagonists.
objects.title: No Plot Armour

objects.text:
There are many names for them. Heroes. Champions. Geniuses. Chosen Ones. Favored Children of Heaven. Protagonists. Regardless of their designation, what these individuals have in common is headstrong personalities, near unshakable will to achieve their goals, extraordinary talent, and uncanny luck that safely gets them out of situations that should have killed them ten times over, while constantly guiding them to opportunities to grow stronger or gain comrades and equipment that greatly improve their power and situation.

And now, thousands of these individuals, at minimum, are scattered all over your world, their backgrounds ranging from gutter-rats clawing their ways to the top to those born with silver spoons in their mouths, wanting for nothing. And while that may sound good, and there are many of them who do at least try to do good, all of them are extremely headstrong people who follow the beat of their own drum, regardless what any official authority might say. They're also do not tend to spend too much thought on the aftermath of any of their actions, either because they're confident it'll all just work out or because they're really only passing through and the question of what comes next never really occurred to them, which means that they generally tend to be a destabilizing factor in any situation they find themselves in, even if they themselves tend to come out ahead.

Their incredible luck not only allows them to gain benefits even when everything around them falls apart, but also ensures it's practically impossible to really hold any of them responsible for their actions in any meaningful ways. Perhaps some can temporarily be locked up, assuming they comply with legal authority or are caught by someone far more powerful they can't escape, but inevitably they'll get away, whether it is because some procedural error ruins the case against them, critical evidence vanishing or getting destroyed, or some form of jailbreak happens and they get out with the intended targets.

There are however limits to how far their luck can carry them. Facing a threat on the level of an Endbringer-fight they have good odds of making it out alive, but even that is not guaranteed if they attract too much of the Endbringer's attention, and may not necessarily contribute more or even as much as other volunteers. And against something as powerful as Scion, whatever fortune protects them will be completely depleted in seconds, leaving them as doomed as everyone else.
objects.title: Heaven's Favored

objects.text:
The world has changed further. It is now not just that plot armour does not exist in this world, but also that neither does any sort of contrivance tangentially related to the concept. 

Chosen Ones? Heaven Blessed Talents? Prophesized Demon Lords? No such thing has ever existed outside of fairy tales. There are no divine grandpas waiting in easily found artifacts to bless anyone's journeys, there is no prophecy protecting anyone's path, there is no sword in the stone waiting for a true king or army of darkness waiting patiently for an almost arbitrary set of circumstances to manifest to give them another warlord. 

Talent and privilege reflect the distributions you'd find in the real world, down to how extreme the outliers can be, how rare they are, and how  much any one person can truly affect the world. The Alexander the Greats, Charlemagne's, Julius Caesar or Genghis Khans of the world and history still exist, but they are appropriately rare and grounded in their backgrounds.

The scales of history are now ruled by the collective of sapient beings, unweighed by the artificially inflated mass of "protagonists" or "antagonists".

This applies to you as well, in as much as such things could have taken place within the constraints of *A Slice In Life* to begin with.
objects.title: Thumbless Scales

objects.text:
The world is extremely odd in that it is entirely covered in water, barring man-made structures. However, the water is covered by an indestructible membrane. The membrane makes the water act as if it's as deep as a puddle to unpowered individuals.

Powered individuals can phase through the membrane at will. They are called divers and all possess a few core powers to allow for this. Powers always work underwater even if they seemingly shouldn't, like pyrokinesis.

- Dive: The power that allows them to phase through the membrane. They can choose when to activate this to avoid accidents.
- Waterbreathing: Divers can breathe underwater indefinitely.
- Master Swimmer: Divers start at peak human when swimming, regardless of their overall fitness, and have no growth limit in that regard.
- Barrier: Divers are completely unaffected by water pressure and can extend this protection to anything within a sphere that is roughly an arm's length in radius. As a result, they can eat food underwater without it getting cold or wet.

Countless treasures and horrors exist beneath the sea. The deeper you travel, the greater the danger and reward. Even the most basic of items is valuable enough that you can earn a week's salary at a moderate wage by successfully bringing one back. If you find the truly rare and valuable, you may be set for life.

The materials used in man-made structures and objects like stone, metals, and wood can all be found beneath the surface.

So dive, find treasure, fight battles, and win glory.
objects.title: Aquarium

objects.text:
The majority of organisations and factions within the world will possess roughly equal raw technological progress regardless of their individual specialisations. No single power holds a decisive tech advantage over others, and the general level of innovation remains consistent across the board during the same time period. Even if different groups focus on different technological paths, the overall level of general technology will be the same.

You can choose whether this equalisation sets the entire world to the lowest tech level present among the affected groups, which is the minimum possible setting. Alternatively, you may set it to the average or median level of all those affected, which is the highest possible setting. 

If the world contains alien civilisations, this applies to them as well.
objects.title: Equalised Technology

objects.text:
Your planet has long since shattered into shards, a debris field that is still, somehow, supportive of life. 

This field is slightly larger than earth, with shards from the size of towns to continents all floating in the same vicinity. If your world is larger these can be even larger, potentially becoming a small asteroid field surrounding your star under the same macro-atmosphere. 

Crossing the gaps between these shards can be quite difficult, but paths can range from constructed bridges and tunnels to charted skyship routes depending on the world and technology available. A world without suitable technology to traverse different shards can produce shockingly isolated communities.
objects.title: Debris Field

objects.text:
Somehow, whether it be through mystical, technological or esoteric means, the entire planet has been reset to prehistoric times, apart from human themselves. All evidence of human civilisation have been swept away and modern mankind has been left to fend for itself against nature once again. 

This has also reverts all natural resources, environment, flora and fauna giving man a second chance to either exploit or harmonise with nature. 

Any Human that would be placed in a precarious position (i.e. flying in a plane) will be put in the nearest safe place. Also, everyone keeps their clothes on their back and anything held in their hands.
objects.title: Return To Monke

objects.text: Sol, the star that grants warmth and light to Earth is dying. No one currently knows what is causing this phenomenon, just that it is happening. Whatever the case, if nothing is done, the sun will cool over the next hundred years before dying, with the Earth freezing in the first fifty.
objects.title: Dying Sun

addons.title: Splitwarp World
addons.text:
Your world just got a bit more chaotic. Everyone in your world experiences both a split and merge, and is affected in at least one of two if not both ways: Either they have been split and then the splits merged with others, or they have been merged with someone(s) else and then split into different, new individuals. 

Good luck figuring out the exact 'original' versions of everyone.

objects.text:
Everyone within your chosen setting is fused with another random character, resulting in a new life that is an amalgamate of their powers and the most important of their experiences. 

The results from this can be quite unpredictable, for instance; Taylor Wallis might well be the leader of the protectorate ENE, a tinker specialising in small yet efficient drones (leading many to speculate her specialty may be ‘surveillance’, or the mystical reincarnating Doctor Hawk, who channels his previous lives through a mystical ‘Helmet of Fate’, or ‘Professor S’, a Psychic Vampire Were-Dinosaur leading his X-Men.

These new people and personalities may be quite unpredictable, and the ‘power’ of the mixed form will not be as strong as both combined, but the average of them.

You may choose whether this amalgamation also applies to you, and whether with merge it applies to you, and your merge partner/s independently.
objects.title: Warpworld

objects.text: Everyone within your chosen setting has been split into two independent characters. These people may only take certain parts of their combined history or be disconnected. For instance, one pair may be a parent and child where the background is the parents but the powers and future events are the child’s, while another may be a duo that’s had their histories split between them. The results of this can be relatively unpredictable. For instance, Vilgax I, former space pirate turned ruler of ‘Vilgaxia’ and his heir ‘Vilgax II’ avenging his father might be separated from one continuous backstory. Alternatively, Sophia Hess might be significantly better adjusted while her brother Howie pushes her into more and more flight-or-die situations to fulfil his own strong vs weak philosophy. These new people and personalities may be quite unpredictable, and the ‘powers’ of the split duo will be split so that the full power is equal to the original combined duo. Whether this is 100% to one, a 50/50 split or something less equal is up to chance. You may choose whether this split also applies to you. If you have Merge you may decide whether you are fused with one of these halves or the original.
objects.title: Splitworld

objects.text:
"(…) Before me there were no created things, Only eterne, and I eternal last. All hope abandon, ye who enter in!"

Dante Alighieri, The Inferno, Canto III

Turns out The Divine Comedy is no mere story, it was Dante's autobiography. Hell, Mount Purgatory, Paradise, it’s all real and interconnected. While the exact number of Circles of Hell and Spheres of Heaven may fluctuate depending on how much you personally believe there should be, the path Dante walked from Limbo down into the frozen reaches of Treachery is considered the fastest on foot path down, making an absolute minimum of 9 Circles & Spheres. Be warned, would-be travelers, if you do try to follow in the Supreme Poet’s footsteps into the Inferno, know that the path for you is far more dangerous than it had been for Dante, both to dissuade mortal people from treating the Three Kingdoms of the Afterlife as Mount Everest 3.0 and due to the fact Dante had divine protection ensuring he was safe from danger.
objects.title: Dante the Supreme Traveler

objects.text:
Wormholes aren’t theoretical anymore! In fact, they are quite common. Thought usually so small that they wouldn’t be visible to the naked eye, the world is filled with them, with a handful of the bigger ones being as tall as mountains!

Luckily, for whatever reason, natural made wormholes seem to be paired to similar locations, so don’t worry about Earth being scorched by a hole opening inside the sun. Natural wormholes seem to last longer the bigger they are, and slowly closing as time passes. 

What this imply for society is up to you. Maybe people rush to the other side and strip it of resources before the hole closes. Maybe people migrate to the other side and humanity is spread across the cosmos. Maybe someone figure out how to extend the holes life and even create more artificially. Whatever the case is, be ready for space to resemble a Swiss cheese.
objects.title: Where did all those WORMs holes come from?!

objects.text:
Not only is your setting connected to an alternate plane of existence that almost seems to be an in between of worlds, very similar to the concept of the Backrooms, but it also seems like you're not the first to have stumbled upon this.

With this choice, the existence of these liminal dimensions is no longer a question. Through some strange means, many folks and items get lost in the in between, and are rarely able to come back. This has resulted in several settlements being established, formed from survivors of many alternate worlds whom were lost in this one. And you have the potential to access this shared space.

These settlements vary depending on the worlds you've chosen to be involved in this one. This in between morphs and expands based on the memories of those it had taken. And thus, obvious conflicts are easy to brew, as people from way too different walks of life are forced to coincide while trapped here in this nightmare. So be sure to keep that in mind should you find a two way entrance to this mysterious world and your normal setting.

What was lost shall never be forgotten. The void swallows without remorse. Shall you be one of the many trapped in this new reality?
objects.title: Liminal Settlements

objects.text:
One day, one of what could be presumed as unthinkable occurred in your world. Without a bang or a whisper, the sun simply vanished.

Somehow, the temperature of your world did not changed too much, maintaining a good enough degree that doesn't outright kill everybody in one fell swoop. What ended up screwing the most folks over however is the death if several plants and other organisms that need sunlight to survive. Besides a few that were saved by humanity's best efforts, a lot of people died with the subsequent ecological collapse. This world of darkness truly did became a sudden apocalypse nobody could prepare for. How or why this happened is unknown, but all everybody could do now is to make do in a world untouched by light, drenched in a sea of seemingly eternal shadows.

What happens afterwards depends on you. Maybe at some point, after several decades until this had became a new normal, the sun suddenly came back bringing forth new issues to the people who are now too used to the once darkened world. Maybe the sun even comes back wrong? Changed in some way that either makes it only somewhat similar to our old sun or utterly bizzare, to the point of being legitimately dangerous to you and your setting's inhabitants. Or maybe the sun simply remains gone, leaving the world in the perpetual night it had since adapted to.

When the world suddenly goes black, what is there left for those still living?
objects.title: The Sun Vanished

objects.text:
Death isn't permanent in this world. Similar to a lot of other modifiers in which revival is a thing, the dead has the habit of coming back, at least so long as the body remains in tact. As such, people tend to go into great lengths to preserve their loved ones, awaiting their near inevitable return. Of course, unless the body is too mangled or is buried underground where there is nothing left to get back to, one can expect a reunion at some point.

It is what happens to people's souls before their return that is the real focus of this choice however.

Within the afterlife, a person is given the choice of either moving on and not being revived, or the choice to embark on a dangerous journey for the chance to return. Should they choose the latter, they are placed in a labyrinth which they must traverse to find an exit. A dangerous maze filled with traps and monsters wanting to tear at their soul's flesh, one they must evade if they want any chance at a revival. Good news is that "death" within the labyrinth isn't permanent, and you merely respawn at the start every time you get killed. Bad news is that the labyrinth has a way to prevent a lot of powers from being useful in traversing it, from it being too tight to fly to having near indestructible walls. Unless you have a specific ability that grants you actual advantage, you may have to traverse this the old fashioned way.

The labyrinth rarely stays the same, so repeated deaths doesn't mean you may fully memorize your route. Even then, it is rare for folks to even remember there was a labyrinth in the afterlife post revival, the brain seemingly blocking out most memories of that ordeal besides passing deja vu. Finally, one last thing to keep in mind is how long you are at the labyrinth corresponds to how long your body remains dead, so do try not to take too long or else there's nothing left to inhabit.
objects.title: Labyrinth of the Dead

objects.text:
Turns out, another conspiracy theory is just plain old reality in your Earth. There is an eight continent that exists which serves as almost a bridge between America and Asia, right in the middle of the Pacific Ocean. The structure of this land's biomes as well as the creatures and locals who inhabit this area is completely up to you. What this does however is cause a domino effect in regards to trade and people's mobility. The age of exploration becomes even more hectic, as the European powers now have a rather convenient stepping stone between their old home and the brave new world they are seeking.

As of the modern era, once more, what this eighth continent is like and what countries or people exist within it is largely determined by you. Just remember that they had always existed and aren't some lost ancient civilization with vast technology going above the rest of the world like how people see Atlantis for example. They're regular people by the standards of your setting. It just so happens that their existence just ended up both unifying and dividing the world further. Would you be interested to see the consequences of this choice?
objects.title: The Eighth Continent

objects.text:
Within your setting, the term "collective unconscious" which was supposedly shared by all of humanity is actually way more literal than what was expected. Instead of a genetic blueprint of sorts, the collective unconscious is instead a whole other plane of existence. A hidden world which was formed by the overall collective psyche of us all, morphed and changed not unlike how Warhammer's Warp or a literal Mind Palace functions. For awhile, this plane of existence remained untouched, simply existing alongside the progress of humanity. The nature and look of this world is determined by you, for example, it could be an infinite library or an abstract void. Either way, it isn't some place one can get to. That is, until now...

Through some means determined by you, maybe through some fancy new technology or some sort of magical technique, for the first time ever it was discovered that not only a collective unconscious world exists, but there are means to access it. This revelation has a lot of consequences, namely, the fact that many are now seeking to enter this realm with the want to influence it. As it is believed that external changes in this world might have a large effect on people's minds, a tempting thing to have for people who want to spread their power. Thus, depending on your setting, how accessible or even well known the existence of this realm to the public is determined. For example, Cauldron might have the only access to this world in a Parahumans setting, or it could be a place only the elites could get to in the Cyberpunk 2099 setting, etc.

Selecting this won't guarantee you have access to this world yourself, though you always have the potential to later acquire the means to do so. Just keep this in mind as you may not know immediately what those who can enter this world is doing to everyone's heads. Now isn't that a harrowing thought?
objects.title: Collective Consciousness

objects.text:
Instead of falling down towards the ground, gravity is a little screwed in your world. Ok, maybe a lot more screwed. Either in some areas of your world or encompassing the entirety of your setting as determined by you, gravity is instead reversed. People fall not downwards but instead upwards into the sky, the vast blue void swallowing up people until they either leave orbit or just keep falling forever in settings where there is no outer space.

This does make living here trickier to folks much more used to conventional gravity such as ourselves. That being said, society had adapted as it tends to do. Structures are put in place for people to live comfortably and not find themselves falling upwards into the aether. Flight had became even more valuable than it was in our reality. And there's even some subtle changes in human evolution which makes us more used to climbing and keeping a hold of nearly flat surfaces.

Overall, while there are some changes, this world is hardly a dystopia. People simply live on, except in a stranger environment.
objects.title: Gravity Swap

objects.text:
Weirdly enough, the movies are right!

In this world, either folks are just completely color blind or the world is just quite literally just like this. Everything everyone could see just so happens to be completely monochrome, going from black, white, and several shades of gray. It's almost as if you live in an old timey movie, drenching the world in a noir-ish filter. For the longest time, the concept of color is simply foreign in this reality.

Now, there's two ways this choice could lead. Either the world remains like this, making this a mostly aesthetic change as there's little difference this does to reality. Or... Color would suddenly be introduced into this setting in some way. If you choose the latter, people will be hit with a sudden onslaught to their senses, as the monochrome world bursts with new beauty. This will be a brief source of panic, and then fascination for the residents who don't understand what is going on. Why this occured is unknown, but there may be some consequences to suddenly shifting the world into seeing things in a new light, literally.

But you won't find out what these consequences would be unless you select this now, wouldn't you?
objects.title: A World Without Color

objects.text:
Reality was never a singular entity.

Multiple systems of existence occupy the same world, layered over one another without fully merging. These may include differing physical laws, magical frameworks, metaphysical rules, or entirely separate interpretations of how reality should function. With none of them fully overwriting the others.

Most of the time, the world appears stable. Everyday interactions behave as expected, and each system functions normally within its own context. However, when different systems intersect, their rules do not resolve cleanly.

In some cases, effects reinforce each other, producing results far beyond what either system could achieve alone. In others, they interfere, weakening or distorting one another. Occasionally, interactions produce entirely new outcomes—temporary rules that belong to neither system, but arise from their overlap.

These interactions are consistent enough to be studied, but never fully predictable. Individuals who operate across multiple systems may learn to exploit these overlaps, while others find their abilities behaving inconsistently outside their native framework.

Certain locations may naturally favor one set of rules over others, forming areas where specific systems become more dominant. These zones can shift over time or form around significant events, individuals, or concentrations of power.

When overlaps intensify, the results can escalate beyond simple interaction.

Conflicting rules may fail to reconcile entirely, causing local breakdowns where cause and effect lose coherence, actions fail to produce results, or multiple outcomes attempt to occur at once. In these moments, reality enters a state of instability until one system asserts itself or the interaction collapses.

Conversely, when systems align too well, they can produce runaway reinforcement. Effects may scale uncontrollably, sustaining themselves or escalating far beyond their intended limits, creating phenomena that persist longer, grow stronger, or spread beyond their original scope.

In rare cases, prolonged overlap can give rise to stable anomalies—areas, objects, or entities defined by their mixed rules. These do not revert once formed, instead existing as permanent expressions of incompatible systems forced into equilibrium.
objects.title: Overlapping Realities

addons.text:
The game that is your world is corrupted.

And that is terrifying.

Something is spreading in this world and in other worlds connected to it, an infection resembling glitches that is twisting and turning the people into horrifying versions of themselves. This corruption not only affects the people anymore, but reality itself. A glitch in the matrix that only spreads, unless you and the Players do something about it.

And even then, could this world really be saved?
addons.title: Corrupted Cartridge

addons.text: The liminal space that exists in Liminal Settlements is now part of this game world, becoming the out of bound realms similar to the popular "multiple leveled" interpretation of the backrooms. Each "floor" of this supposed backrooms has its own sets of rules and dangers, which is a challenge to every denizen who ended up trapped here. Thankfully though, being stuck here isn't a permanent endeavor, as there had been discovered many ways to escape, and to also go back. It had come to a point where there is a growing trend of liminal delvers now braving deeper and deeper floors of this esoteric maze, seeking potential riches from its confusing caverns.
addons.title: Backrooms Levels

addons.text: There are no longer many Players, but instead, only Seven of them. They also don't manifest directly into your world, instead bonding with a specific NPC who becomes the chosen of this world in their stead. It is a Player and PC relationship, where the Players don't fully control you, but instead, encourage your actions in a way that aligns with their character and their mission. Think something similar to the Soul and Kris' bond in Deltarune, but less restrictive. Overall, this means mere NPCs such as you may suddenly be chosen to bear immense power a Player would typically yield, at the cost of having a nagging voice in your head. Who the chosen are, you don't know, maybe one of them could even be you? So, shall you go forth and become the hero you may end up chosen to be?
addons.title: The Chosen Players

objects.text:
This selection turns your world into a video game, except, unlike other modifiers, this choice makes it so that almost everybody is an NPC. And this includes you.

As an NPC, you and everyone around you are pretty much immortal. This is because everyone is unknowingly following a script since their conception. This script does not outright forces an NPC to follow their given roles, but makes them feel fulfilled whenever they do so, even manipulating their memories to reach a given conclusion. And unless your script says you have to die, you shall simply keep respawning. Which is useful considering how common death tends to be whenever Players are around.

Players exists alongside you NPCs. They tend to possess incredible powers beyond what NPCs like you are normally capable of, and they are also immortal. Players are not as common as NPCs as they tend to suddenly disappear off to who knows where whenever they aren't either causing chaos or actually helping people. The coming of these Players have long since become the norm in your world, with folks only being confused by the shennanigans these weirdos tend to do. That doesn't mean there isn't any suffering though, as it is common for a player to treat you NPCs with callousness, as if you aren't people. And the repeated random slaughterings does take its toll. Overall, Players are powerful, but they could be jerks. But what can mere NPCs such as you do?

For a while, this hierchy remains, Players are on top while NPCs just have to live these Players' actions. But now, things are about to change. You and a couple of other NPCs are starting to become... Self Aware. This system is rigged and soon the script is becoming more loose. It doesn't help that there are now rumors of some Players no longer being able to "log out", or NPCs who supposedly managed to gain Player tier abilities.

What are you to do in this restrictive world?
objects.title: You're Just an NPC

objects.text:
It all happened without warning.

From many other realities, certain individuals have returned, and whatever they have experienced in these other worlds have changed them, warped them into something that no longer resembles "human". Whatever it may be, these folks later came to be known as Returnees, and soon, the people shall fear these invaders. Or should we call this a homecoming?

While not every one of them is outright evil or even actively malicious, the one thing they each have in common is immense overpoweredness. These were isekaid "heroes" at their peak, it should not be a surprise that some of them would choose to abuse this power after years living a power fantasy. Soon, one particularly bad egg ended up choosing to bring the world under their heel, and when others followed suit, thus starts the proper invasion.

Returnees from all around the globe now wage war amongst each other, each possessing such overwhelming strength that they turned the entire world into a battlefield, civilians be damned. This world shall end up split into several factions of Returnees and their followers, all vying for total control and rival annihilation. Even in powered settings, the magnitude of these gods seem to overwhelm even the typical mightiest non-returnee of your realm. You are one of these unfortunate masses who can only watch on, as these otherworldly monsters paint the skies with blackened smoke.

Unless you do something about it?

Not everyone wants to go down without a fight. Pockets of resistance starts forming against these double isekaid despots, people begin researching for ways to take them down, and counterattacks may start happening soon. Who knows, maybe your influence will be enough to turn the tide in this senseless conflict? After all, these creatures were all human once.

We'll see if they can still bleed.
objects.title: Returnee Invasion

objects.text:
The seasons pass rather differently in your setting compared to our world. Instead of it being a natural cycle that occurs with the climate, every country instead has an organization that handles the seasons. The specifics on how this is done is up to you, but regardless, this means the power of the climates is in human hands.

This is both a good and a bad thing.

On the one hand, this is a huge natural phenomena that humanity now has control over. The world is now less chaotic, at least, so it seems. This however means that something as vital as the seasons is in the hands of a select few individuals with their own agendas. It isn't uncommon for the cycle to be disrupted when conflict arises amongst these organizations. Sometimes, even disasters occur as the power of the seasons are weaponized. Is humanity truly to be trusted with such responsibility?
objects.title: Manual Seasons

objects.text: "I dreamt I was a butterfly, fluttering hither and thither, to all intents and purposes a butterfly. I was conscious only of my happiness as a butterfly, unaware that I was myself." This world does not exist. Or does it? With this modifier, the world instead exists within the mind of a dreamer. Who this dreamer is, you don't know. But what is important is that if something were to happen to this dreamer, like say, if they were to be suddenly awoken, the world will end. Take note that killing the dreamer in the dream won't actually wake them up, as there will simply be a new identity they will unknowingly take. No, waking this dreamer up would take more effort than that. Maybe that will give some reassurance? There may be some hints as to who the dreamer is. The dreamer tends to have immense power over this world, even moreso if they are aware they are dreaming. There's even a possibility that you yourself are the dreamer, but what the real waking world is, you have no idea. This dream is your reality, whether you like it or not. Though, maybe there is a way to escape before the waking could truly happen? To dream a dream, what else is there? Is this reality truly fleeting? Or is there meaning in this supposedly meaningless world?
objects.title: It's All Just A Dream

objects.text:
Your world is infected.

While you may at first expect a typical zombie apocalypse, the way this infection works and manifests is more esoteric than that. The specifics are up to you, but the disease spreads less from bites or from a physical virus, but instead, through something more abstract like spiritual corruption or through a cursed sound for some quick examples. As such, vaccines and genetic immunity don't exactly exist here, though people could gain immunity through different means. The infection also spreads much more faster due to its non physical nature, warping its victims into more uncanny and twisted horrors instead of just rotten corpses.

The virus had long since spread even before you entered your setting. Familiar characters around you have either become hardened survivors or twisted infected. Beware powered settings in particular, as the infection does really well with super powered individuals, creating monsters with their same abilities, and thus further spreading the disease.

In this world ravaged by a corruption barely anybody can understand, what is there left to hold on to? Will you fight, or will you succumb?
objects.title: Infection AU

objects.text:
When a kid lets their imagination run wild, they emerge.

Imaginary friends are not only real, but everyone knows they exist. This means that it is common for creatures of many shapes and sizes to exist alongside us humans in this reality, and that may cause a lot of issues. With how strange and out there child logic could be, these imaginary friends could range from mostly normal humans to outright horrific and violent monsters, with the only thing similar amongst all of them being their intense loyalty to their assigned kid. This is both a good thing and a bad thing, as these creatures may not be an outright harm to the kid that created them, but they could definitely cause damage based on their kid's whims, like inflicting harm on bullies or causing massive collateral damage while roughhousing.

It becomes even more of an issue once the kid grows and loses connection with their imaginary creations. These creatures just loses their purpose, becoming their own entities, which is terrifying when it comes to the more boogeyman esque variations of them. Freed Imaginary Friends are now forced to live in a world where they are abandoned, doomed to exist for themselves, which isn't something a lot of them are able to cope with.

As a response to this, there is definitely a ton more restrictions when it comes to childlike creativity. Some people are scared of these creatures, others are accepting of them. Some seek to weaponize their children, while others seek to discourage children from even making them. There are even organizations specifically made to deal with these denizens, either to treat them as people or as monsters that need to be put down. This is a surprisingly grounded world still, even despite the realization of our children's creations.
objects.title: Living Imagination

objects.text:
Similar to the modifier called Manual Seasons, this world has organizations handling something that typically just comes and goes in our reality, but this time, it's something less "natural".

Holidays are now ran by a group of magical individuals who make it their job to spread cheer across your world. This might mean that Santa is real and is not just a capitalist mascot, and he is legitimately able to give presents to the entire world in one night, Krampus may or may not be included. Or maybe there's a town specifically focused in spreading Halloween fear across the world, inhabited by the ghosts and ghouls of the night. Heck, maybe there's a bunch of leprechauns just sitting on couldrons of gold, awaiting weary travelers under the rainbow. How does this even work in places where Christmas isn't a thing? You decide. There could also be a possibility that fictional holidays from different worlds have their very own version of these holiday themed organizations. Who knows?

Otherwise, the knowledge of these orgs are left up to you too. Maybe people know that the Easter Bunny is real, or maybe they all agree that a giant rabbit that hides eggs for kids to find is a rather silly fairy tale. Again, it is up to you.

Finally, which holidays get affected by this is all up to you as well. So spirits might indeed be passing by in Dia De Los Muertos, but a giant turkey spreading Thanksgiving "joy" might be too far fetched. Just keep in mind, some of these people might take their holidays really seriously, so I hope you'd be ready once the agents of Christmas end up clashing with Halloween every November. Things just weren't the same since All I Want For Christmas took over.

For intents and purposes, the last part is a joke. Or is it? Again, the choice is yours.
objects.title: Holiday Worlds

objects.text:
This is a utopia, or so it would seem.

The world is mostly the same, though things are just a little bit... Better. Problems aren't completely gone, but there is now a sense of fairness in all things. People are treated equally and comfortably, with a lot of respect for everyone's rights and needs. It is a rather miraculous pipe dream that was somehow achieved, and you get to enjoy this supposed paradise.

Happiness is at a cost however.

Every few years, a ritual is done. A single child is chosen at random to be a world's representative. Afterwards, they are sent away in a remote location, where everyone gets to watch them brutally fight against other children from other worlds. The losers die, and their worlds are left in squalor, whatever blessing that is being given to them suddenly getting cut off until the next ritual, which tends to result in a lot of turmoil and violence. The winner however gets to have their world enjoy more years of peace and prosperity, and even then, this child doesn't get to experience that for themselves. As the winner is then sacrificed and executed, with the popular excuse being that it is to ensure they don't live with the trauma, as well as making sure they don't get to compete once again in the next ritual.

It is a clearly barbaric practice, the origins of which you do not understand.

But can you stomach living in a paradise such as this?

Whatever your answer is, you may not be the only one protesting. There have been instances where certain groups rebelled against this brutal competition. Unfortunately, these folks are fighting a battle against the majority, a lot of people being content living the luxury while only one in their world gets to suffer.

So now what? Are you to join these resistances? Walk away from all this? Or simply accept this as a worthy sacrifice? The final choice is up to you.
objects.title: One Soul for Many

addons.title: Infinity Train
addons.text: Whatever your choice of transportation may be, it had became rather... Strange. How exactly is unknown, but your civilization ended up becoming a bridge between our world and the void in between. Lost in a strange landscape, escape may or may not be possible. How long you and your people may last here, currently nobody knows.

addons.title: Transforming Urbivore
addons.text: Mobility is now of far more importance in Urbivore life. It isn't uncommon for urbivores to shift fully into a full on vehicle when it's out hunting for resources. Imagine living in a country sized Transformer essentially.

addons.title: Feed the Machine
addons.text: On the one hand, the world is just... Better, in some way. Maybe the government is less corrupt? Maybe the world is just a little more fair? Regardless, whatever it may be, the world is just more Utopic... Except for the fact that it requires the sacrifice of at least one soul within a certain length of time. A coal train cannot keep chugging without coal. In this case, the life of an individual. But maybe that's worth it?

objects.text:
Maybe it was because of some sort of disaster, maybe it was done out of convenience, or maybe people simply just really like trains, regardless of the reason, what is left of civilization had decided to live inside some sort of large vehicle of your choosing. It could be a train, a cruise, an aircraft, etc. Whatever your choice may be, society as you know it has changed to fit within the limits of being mostly stuck in a moving vehicle. A train civilization could have hierchies based on which cart you are in ala Snowpiercer, or maybe a society within an aircraft carrier would put an emphasis on sending out planes for exploration, there possibilities are nearly endless.

As for what's outside, as hinted at prior, this would also depend on you. The world could be a post apocalyptic wasteland or is just hostile enough that loving outside isn't feasible. The world could also be perfectly fine, barring what might be other setting modifiers you have selected. Whatever the case, here we are now.

Humanity shall ride on onto the great beyond, and we won't stop, we can't stop.
objects.title: The World Rides On

objects.text:
The world is alive, literally. We are living in an organism that may or may not be aware of us. We have a specific role within this setting, mostly in regards of keeping our world alive in a more literal sense. Think Cells at Work and how we have White Blood Cells beating back invaders, or Red Blood Cells delivering nutrients as they do so in real life. However this may work in your setting, everyone now has a specific part to play in keeping it alive.

This does not fully change the setting, what it does is it adds another layer to it that keeps it functioning. It could be something like the Endbringers being viruses while heroes are Earth's antibodies keeping them from fully killing it, or a certain type of unobtanium is actually an important source of nutrition that needs to keep flowing within your world. However it may be, the tricky part is keeping going whatever cycle is being held up, all the while whatever troubles is going on in your chosen setting. Choose wisely if you ever pick this, you may need it.
objects.title: Us At Work

objects.text:
The world has undergone a colossal geographical reversal. Earth is now composed of approximately 71% land and 29% water, creating a world dominated by an enormous Single Continent with vast stretches of wilderness. The familiar oceans, seas, lakes, islands, and continents have effectively switched places. Areas that were once oceans are now part of one immense landmass, while former continents and islands have become bodies of water. The result is a planet covered by a gigantic interconnected supercontinent, broken only by comparatively smaller seas, lakes, and oceans.

This reversal has also affects elevation, with the world’s original elevations have been inverted, meaning that the mountains and trenches have traded places. The Himalayan Mountains would know be considered one of the deepest regions of one of the world’s oceans, while the Mariana Trench would know be consider the tallest point on Earth, rising into an enormous mountain range. Other mountains, valleys, plateaus, and ocean trenches have undergo the same reversal. The geography of the world therefore looks radically different from modern Earth, with colossal mountain ranges occupying areas that were once deep ocean trenches and enormous basins replacing former mountain systems.

Human history has consequently developed along a radically different path. Civilizations, kingdoms, and empires have formed around entirely different geographical features, with access to water, fertile land, mountains, and natural resources determining the rise and fall of civilizations. The British Empire, for example, would never have been an island-based naval power because Britain is no longer an island. Instead, Britain would have developed around a powerful land-based military and become a major continental empire. Likewise, countless historical wars, migrations, borders, trade routes, and civilizations would be completely different from those of our Earth.

Humanity also has vastly more land available for expansion. Populations can spread across enormous regions that were previously beneath the oceans, resulting in countless new cultures, nations, languages, and civilizations developing in isolation. However, this expansion comes with a major problem: water is much harder to access in many regions. Rivers are rarer, and many of the world’s former major waterways are now land. Some regions may instead rely upon enormous underground reservoirs, natural springs, seasonal waterways, or dramatically increased rainfall. Trade is also more difficult, as merchants must cross enormous stretches of land rather than relying upon relatively easy oceanic transportation, resulting in powerful overland trade networks and isolated civilizations.

The environment has changed just as dramatically. With far more land exposed to sunlight, enormous regions can absorb and retain vast quantities of heat, creating unusual climates that would be impossible on modern Earth. Vast swamp-jungles, enormous tropical forests, sprawling grasslands, and other strange ecosystems can develop across the new continent. The greatly reduced oceans also mean that hurricanes become far less common and generally weaker, while tornadoes and other land-based storms become much greater threats. Weather patterns, rainfall, deserts, temperature zones, and ecosystems are all substantially different from those of modern Earth.

Ultimately, this is no longer the Earth you know. The continents, oceans, mountains, rivers, climates, ecosystems, and even the course of human history have been reshaped into something entirely new. The reference image provides an approximation of the world’s general appearance, with an immense interconnected landmass replacing much of Earth’s modern oceans. Super Mega Ultra Continent transforms Earth into a world where exploration, migration, warfare, trade, and civilization itself must adapt to a planet ruled by land rather than sea.
objects.title: Super Mega Ultra Continent

objects.text: There is a cultural change in your world as you know it, and that is how certain nations and other places seem to be more visible fusions of mostly unrelated nations from our Earth. It could be something like San Fransokyo from Big Hero 6's very Japan looking USA, or Egypt for some reason having elements of Viking based architecture and customs, the combinations could be almost anything. How deeply this combo is ingrained into your given setting and how this even came about is up to you. Either way, you might end up with a rather colorful world, with combinations one might not immediately expect. Have fun mixing and matching, the world is indeed a melting pot, even moreso with this choice.
objects.title: Cultural Fusion

objects.text:
For one reason or another, all technological methods of FTL travel native to the universe have stopped working, such as hyperspace in Star Wars or warp drives in Star Trek, or any kind of wormhole or portal networks.

If there was an interstellar society, it would have to rapidly adapt to the breakdown of the majority of interplanetary travel.

Any methods not native to the universe, such as an FTL-capable OOP or a portal device, will continue to work as intended.
objects.title: Einstein had Enough

objects.text:
Existence is a Cycle.

By picking this modifier, your setting is now subject to cosmic cycles called "Kalpas." A Kalpa, as described in Buddhist cosmology, is a cosmic age of incomprehensible length that is divided into four subsections.

The first is Vivarta (Formation). This is the period in which the cosmos comes into existence. The cosmos in question can be a single universe, a multiverse, or even a larger cosmological structure.

Then comes Vivarta-siddha (Continuation). During this period, the cosmos has been fully established, and sentient beings begin to inhabit it.

This is followed by Saṃvarta (Destruction). The entire cosmic system undergoes destruction until nothing remains.

The final period is Saṃvarta-siddha (Empty Period). This is the post-world nothingness that exists before a new Formation begins, starting the cycle all over again.

But the new cosmos won't be a carbon copy of the old one. While the setting will still be recognizable as itself, its specifics can change drastically, ranging from changes as minor as Clark Kent having a different last name to ones as major as Mew replacing Arceus as the Supreme Deity of a Kalpa.

Due to the sheer length of a Kalpa, these changes are only really relevant to immortal and near-immortal beings, who may either accept their end or try to save themselves. They may succeed, as it is possible for beings from a previous Kalpa to survive into the next one, provided they possess the necessary means. They may even transcend the cosmic cycle entirely if they become a Buddha-like entity.

You decide the cause and nature behind the cycle. Be it Karma like in Buddhism, cosmic evolution like in Marvel or even a cosmic restart like in the Elder Scrolls.

It is also up to your discretion whether you live in the first Kalpa or whether your setting has already gone through countless cycles of rebirth before your arrival.
objects.title: Kalpas

objects.text:
With each purchase of this option, an Object of Power you have NOT purchased and is native to your chosen setting(s) may be altered such that it is affected by any of its upgrades and add-ons on the CYOA (your choice how many and which). You may also choose to “naturalize” any unpurchased Object of Power that is not native to your chosen setting(s) and apply this option to that object instead. If you purchase this option 10 times, you may choose for this to happen to any and however many Objects of Power in the CYOA you have NOT purchased. 

Importantly, because you have not purchased them, these artifacts are naturally inserted into their reality and will have a background, reputation and in all probability, previous and/or current wielders/owners. Both surviving what that does to the setting and possibly acquiring these enhanced artifacts for yourself falls entirely on your shoulders.

Any add-on that explicitly relies upon a specific power being possessed by the wielder will not be accessible to a wielder who doesn’t possess that power. This applies to anyone in the setting, yourself included.
objects.title: Artifact Contamination

objects.text:
Your chosen world now possesses an equal and opposite force to any faction, universal law or location. If your world has monsters, they will now have heroes too, and vice versa.

This will be applied to any forces in the world, and you can direct how exactly this will be implemented, but it will affect mainly the major ones, such as eldritch gods now having an equal and opposite faction consisting of your world's regular mythology gods. In short, any good will have an equal evil, and any evil will have an equal good.

Should the forces in your world be morally ambiguous, then their opposites will also be morally ambiguous, but with opposing goals. Additionally, should your chosen world already have opposing forces, selecting this option will add an extra faction that opposes the existing ones.
objects.title: Opposite Force

objects.text: The nature of divinity across the Omniverse has fundamentally changed. All gods and sufficiently god-like beings, such as high-tier angels, demons, fae, etc., now have the potential to develop an "Oversoul." An Oversoul is a deity's higher conceptual self that exists beyond the boundaries of a single universe, or even a multiverse in more notable cases. When a god's existence grows beyond what a single universe can contain, and the right conditions are met, they can ascend into a Tier 1 Oversoul, also called a lesser "Godhead." A Godhead is unique on a multiversal scale, with all versions of that being encountered across different universes being merely Avatars of the Godhead. Harming or killing an Avatar will not affect the Oversoul, while harm done to the Oversoul extends to all its Avatars. True Form Darkseid from DC Comics is an example of a Tier 1 Oversoul. Raw power is not the only factor in developing an Oversoul. Power, age, mental strength, will, desires, domains, and many other factors contribute, but the most important is "story." A god's triumphs, failures, struggles, myths, and legends combine to form their "Divine Narrative." Their conceptual self defines what they are, while their story defines who they are. Both are equally important to an Oversoul. The more widely a god's narrative spreads, the more weight their existence gains, granting them greater influence and authority. Since stories can spread regardless of distance or physical barriers, a deity can theoretically grow without limit. A story merely needs to be told for the deity to gain some awareness of and influence within a new reality; belief is not required, though it certainly helps. This influence is normally minor unless the deity's story becomes relevant to the setting's "plot." At that point, they may form Avatars and potentially even develop a new Godhead within that multiverse. However, these manifestations will be heavily shaped by that reality's history, laws, and context. This is why DC!Zeus and Disney!Zeus can be radically different despite ultimately being aspects of the same greater entity. Once an Oversoul grows beyond a single multiverse, it becomes a Tier 2 Oversoul, or Greater Godhead. They generally use their lesser Godheads as middle management, allowing them to influence the realities under their purview. However, while they may have transcended the boundaries of a single multiverse, they may still be confined by the cosmological constraints of a single setting. Beings like the Presence and the One Above All belong to this category. Finally, at the top, we have Tier 3 Oversouls, or Supreme Godheads: beings who have transcended the constraints of cosmology altogether. No ontological system, regardless of size or complexity, can contain them. As such, they exclusively exist in the void beyond reality, or the Sea Between if you have selected the Meta Manifold Reality modifier. This is the category for beings like YHWH, the Buddha, Greek Chaos, and similar entities in their truest forms, without the recontextualization and constraints imposed on their lesser and greater Godheads by different settings. For most people, this change has little practical effect. For Dimensional Travelers, however, it is highly relevant. The interconnected nature of divinity allows for omniversal divine gossip networks, and your actions in one setting can influence how gods in others perceive you. How much awareness Avatars and Godheads have of their counterparts' actions varies, but there is generally some degree of awareness. For example, befriending Marvel!Thor and leaving a strong positive impression on him means that the Thor of DxD is almost guaranteed to be favorably disposed toward you. Conversely, killing the Godhead of Zeus in DC would make you persona non grata in settings with strong Greek influences, such as Percy Jackson or Saint Seiya. Not every god possesses an Oversoul, but you can expect every "relevant" deity to have one and should act accordingly. This modifier is retroactive and affects the entirety of the Omniverse. You may choose whether the gods of your native setting have developed Oversouls, unless they already canonically possess one.
objects.title: Divine Oversoul
The Road
objects.text: Interconnected with reality lies a peculiar subdimension; one with many names, dependent upon how one interacts with it. The trail, if one walks. The path, if one rides. The current, if one sails. The sky, if one flies. If one drives, it is most oft called The Road. This is a realm of travel, and it has its own rules. Speed limits are not one of them. It can be accessed by anyone seeking to use it given that they are currently traveling under their own power and direction, and know of its existence. Above a certain distance in real space it drastically cuts down the time needed to move from point A to B, and can allow one to cross normally insurmountable obstacles to a given form of locomotion—such as the ocean while walking, or space in a normal, grounded car. There are a few important bits to note. First, if one enters this dimension with a given form of locomotion, they must continue to use that form of locomotion for as long as they remain within. This means no flipping a switch while you're on The Road and having your car take to the Skies—grounded vehicles remain grounded. Flying vehicles remain flying. People walking remain walking. Etc. Failure to comply will see the dimension retaliate, and the most common fate of violators is becoming Lost. Second: One must remain moving. There are rest areas that act as exceptions to this—pit stops on the Road, air stations in the Sky, campsites on the Trail and Path—but otherwise, to stop moving is to become Lost. Becoming Lost causes one's intended destination and exit point to become completely random. You will know—down to your soul—if this occurs to yourself. One becomes automatically Lost if their method of locomotion breaks down or is destroyed. Thankfully, one can always 'fall' to the other variants—such as the Trail for walking—or they can find, salvage, purchase at rest areas, or repair other methods of locomotion such as from 'junkyards', so they are not technically trapped in this dimension. However, with exits that can be almost anywhere—including other realities, on the surface of stars, underwater and more—simply exiting while Lost can be—and often is—a quick death sentence. Third and finally: protect yourself. This dimension is not without dangers—it even encourages them. Ignoring the 'scripted' encounters, races, and conflicts; Lost trapped here can steal another's journey to guarantee a decently safe exit, but dooming their victims to the fate of becoming Lost in turn if not simply murdered. Weapons and methods of defense are a must. The only guarantee is that anything you face is something you can—with a clear head, strategy, and awareness—handle due to the dimension's manipulations. The Road awaits. "Life is a highway~♪ I want to drive it all night long~♪"

objects.title: Deep Whispers
objects.text: There are rare oddities in your world. Often unnoticed, unexplained, and rarely remarked. Singular fragments of old carvings that seem to look back. Letters with no known pronunciation, but that feel unsettling—unsteady. Glitches. Hiccups. Places where, despite all measurements and confidence, the geometry just doesn't feel right. Your world is influenced by the Eldritch. These are signs. Thankfully, this influence is very light. This world is in the eldritch equivalent of a wasteland. There's no outer beings here right now or in the foreseeable future. No matter how many sacrifices cultists make, nothing is around to notice the pleas or the screams. There are no gods close enough to hear any prayers. Nothing to borrow or bargain authority off of. That does not mean one cannot learn to do some strange things to reality with the right perspective, talent and twisted knowledge. But doing such is vanishingly difficult and rare. Nevermind the likelihood of offing oneself without guidance—or possibly worse. In most cases, this will take the form of exceedingly rare but powerful 'talents'—people who may as well be giants. Cats that teleport when unobserved. These effects become more and more apparent, but never common, the more supernatural the setting. This does add Eldritch gods to the setting. Just not ones that are omniscient or nearby. Unless this setting already has such gods present, in which case... well. Good luck.

objects.title: The Second Great Flood
objects.text:
The world faces a second Great Flood, a mass extinction event that will reshape the planet and eradicate much of its existing life. Every civilization will be submerged beneath a vast ocean, leaving only scattered islands and the remnants of humanity clinging to whatever land remains.

Unlike the first Flood, there is no promise that the waters will recede. This is the new world, and humanity must learn to survive within it.

As terrestrial ecosystems collapse, the oceans become the last refuge for countless species. The depths conceal the ruins of the old world, and those brave enough to venture beneath the waves will earn the name 'Divers'. Essential to humanity's survival, they recover resources and materials buried beneath the sea.

With fertile land scarce and civilization scattered across the rising tides, humanity must adapt. New societies will emerge aboard ships and floating settlements, while others seek refuge in submarines. Whether this second Flood is divine punishment, a chance for renewal, or something beyond human understanding remains unknown.

You may choose to have the flood already happened retroactively or to have it begin during its earliest stages.

objects.title: Irradiated Earth
objects.text:
Welp, it's over. Sorry to say, but this Earth's future is going to be wiped away by atomic fire. Somehow, someway, this world is condemned to experience Nuclear Armageddon. How it happens is up to you, or you can simply leave it to fate. Maybe, as societies across the world deteriorate, their leaders become desperate or unstable and eventually trigger MAD against their rivals. One country launches a nuclear weapon, and everyone else responds by launching their own. Maybe someone creates a hidden cache of Tinker-modified nuclear weapons that goes unnoticed by Scion and Ziz before being accidentally activated. Maybe it's all the result of a technical glitch, or perhaps a series of nuclear weapons from another world somehow ends up being shunted into the world you just happen to live in. Or, if this is Worm, maybe Scion simply decides to say screw it, destroys the world in radioactive waves and blasts, and leaves because he's finished with this broken Cycle.

However it happens, when it does, life on the planet will never be the same. Fire will scorch the Earth for miles upon miles, vaporizing everything within the initial impact zones. Those who aren't killed by the blast, shockwave, or flames will still have to contend with the enormous amounts of soot and debris produced by the explosions. When a nuclear weapon detonates, this material is pulled high into the atmosphere, forming enormous pyro-cumulonimbus clouds. With enough detonations occurring across the planet, these clouds and the debris they carry can spread far beyond the stratosphere, blocking sunlight and triggering a nuclear winter. Normal rain clouds won't be high enough to clear the atmosphere, leaving the planet cold and dark for years.

Plants and animals will die from the cold, lack of sunlight, radiation, and destruction of their habitats. The winter may only last around a decade, hopefully, but the damage to the biosphere will last much longer. Food chains will collapse as plants disappear, herbivores starve, and predators lose their prey. Entire ecosystems will be thrown out of balance, with some species going extinct while others may become strangely dominant in the environments left behind. Rivers, forests, farmland, and coastal ecosystems will all be affected, leaving surviving wildlife struggling to adapt to a world that has been violently altered. Electronics and modern technology will be flash fried due to numerous EMPs that will come from the blasts, throwing the technical world make centuries.

And as the ecosystems collapse, so does human civilization. People will starve, and when people are starving, or know they soon will be, they become desperate and violent. Expect looting, people prepared and willing to kill for food and supplies, militaries that begin acting more like armed factions than protectors of their nations, and entirely new gangs forming from the survivors. Most importantly, expect radiation. Radioactive fallout will scatter across continents, seeping into the soil and water tables. Radiation will linger in the air, cling to ash, settle onto buildings, contaminate food, and eventually cling to you. It will become the silent killer and a part of everyday life.

The world shall burn, but hey, get the right things together and maybe you can survive in a well built bunker. Grow fungus for food, purify your own water, stockpile supplies, and perhaps establish your own settlement. Maybe you'll become the leader of a small community, a warlord, or even the new ruler of your own little kingdom. Who knows? What is known is that the old world has been burned away, now there is only ash and the world that will keep turning whether you like it or not.

objects.title: A Scavenger's Paradise
objects.text:
Somehow scavenging the ruins of previous civilizations is now a viable method of living as loot becomes self replenishing. Properly sealed food somehow is almost always edible regardless of expiration dates, old tech somehow still functions despite not receiving maintenance even if in a reduced or damaged state, ancient artifacts of some power can rarely be found to work as advertised, and somehow the supply seems to slowly restock over time as if by magic. Why and how? ...That is a good question.

If the world is post-apocalyptic, this is a wonderful asset for any survivors. If not, this is an archaeologist's dream come true. If the setting has any long existing supernatural power systems, whether native or introduced through other modifiers, this may lead to an archaeological / scavenger arms race as nations fight over ancient weapons and tools, though the stronger they are the rarer they are, but overall this is a net positive since even then civilian applications for artifacts are aplenty.

rows.title: World & Reality Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the physical planet, and/or reality in various ways

objects.text:
Humans do not exist in this multiverse, maybe a different species evolved to sapience on Earth, or maybe the plans The Entities have for this cycle don’t need a viable host species.

If you chose for another sapient species to have evolved you are free to choose what they are, and their general characteristics so long as they are roughly equal to humanity. Any modifiers geared towards affecting humanity will instead affect this new species. You may also choose if this species has variants of canon characters.

You can choose to be a member of that species or the sole human in this multiverse.
objects.title: What is a Human?

objects.text:
The World you've ended up in has another sapient race living on it. This can range from just any type of sapient life. 

The limits are that it must fit with the setting so no Elves on Earth bet unless you either make it a crossover or alternate Earth setting that has magic in it.

And to keep it fair the sapient species must not be overwhelmingly more powerful compared to humanity. They can have a certain number advantages though like how Elves in LOTR possess superior craftsmen, Warrior, artists, etc.... 

But Humanity must be able to have at the very least be able to have a fighting chance should for some reason they be at war.

Should you choose a setting like Star Wars or another space setting that encompasses more than one planet in its narrative you can decide to add in a sapient species that is not already been depicted in the setting and the above rules apply all the same.

Note: Any species you purchase in the CYOA can be a native species in the setting of your choice.
objects.title: Native Species

objects.text: One or more of the species powers you have selected are added to the world retroactively as a new species. For example you could have elves added to Earth Bet if you picked Elf. Unlike Native Species there are no limitations as to what can be added where.
objects.title: Propagation

addons.text:
When we said every animal became more dangerous, we meant every animal. Even the most dominant species on the planet—humans.

With the world teeming with fanged squirrels, venomous cats, and raptor pigeons, humanity didn’t just survive—it adapted, again. The same evolutionary pressure that turned rabbits into walking nightmares pushed humans even further into the role of apex predator. Those already shaped by strength, aggression, and survival instinct were forced to sharpen every edge they had.

Now, modern humans aren’t just stronger and more primal. They’re hunters among hunters. The brain may still take a backseat to instinct, but instinct itself has evolved—quicker threat recognition, pattern-seeking, tracking ability on par with the best bloodhounds. Eyes adapted to spot movement faster. Ears tuned to the subtlest of footfalls. Smell and taste sharpened to identify toxins or fear. Some humans even developed subtle biological shifts: scent glands for territory, muscle fiber variants adapted for quick bursts or long endurance hunts, and pupils that slit like a beast’s in bright light. Due to these new adaptations, they have also become increasingly more aggressive, violent and conflict-driven.
addons.title: Red in Tooth and Claw

objects.text:
The entire world has become as perilous as the Australian outback, with every animal and piece of wildlife now just as deadly as Australia’s infamous creatures. No matter where you go—lush forests, frigid tundras, vast oceans, or even suburban parks—you’ll find nature ready to kill you in new and horrifying ways.

But it’s not just their danger levels that have changed. Many animals have also undergone disturbing physical transformations to match their newfound lethality. Harmless-looking bunnies now sport venomous fangs, their fur masking potent neurotoxins. Housecats have gained the venom of stonefish, turning their scratches into agonizing, flesh-rotting wounds. Elk and moose have developed an eerie, reptilian cunning, their antlers now barbed like a cassowary’s talons. Even pigeons, once the world’s most annoying but harmless birds, now resemble harpy eagles, their talons capable of snatching up small animals—or unsuspecting humans.

And then there are the spiders. Some have grown to the size of small puppies, their fangs dripping with venom potent enough to kill in seconds. Others have developed trapdoor-like hunting techniques, ambushing unsuspecting prey from underground burrows or the corners of homes.

As for the Land Down Under itself? It’s practically a breeding pit of hell’s favourite pets. Somehow people still survive there however.
objects.title: Aussie

objects.text:
The collective intelligence of the world has experienced a quiet revolution. Average IQ and EQ levels have both risen considerably, resulting in a more thoughtful, emotionally aware, and intellectually capable population. More than just raw cognitive ability, people now exhibit a natural curiosity and an intrinsic openness to new ideas, theories, and perspectives. 

Gone are the days of widespread ignorance, willful or otherwise. People are no longer baffled by basic facts, indifferent to nuance, or easily led by shallow arguments. Everyday conversations are marked by a clearer understanding of context and consequence. Civic awareness is no longer niche; media literacy is second nature. The average person might not know everything, but they know how to know, and more importantly, they care to.
objects.title: Little Einsteins

objects.text:
Immortality, it seems, is not as rare or mythical as it should be. In this world, history never truly ends because some of its most ancient figures never quite died. While the supernatural may not be openly present (especially if magic doesn’t exist in your setting), there are countless workarounds, loopholes, and borderline-miraculous technologies that have allowed certain individuals to defy time itself.

These ancients still walk the world, though few would recognize them. Their methods of survival are as varied as the cultures they once ruled. Some remain through long-forgotten rituals combining esoteric science with metaphysical theory, ancient pharaohs entombed not in gold, but in alchemical suspension, their minds preserved in embalmed gray matter, their bodies stitched back together with careful precision, reinforced by forgotten biotech and sacred geometry.

Others are remnants of early transhumanist ambition, their flesh long since discarded in favor of gleaming brass and tarnished copper. Steam hisses from their joints, and their artificial eyes glow dimly behind cracked lenses. These bronze-and-bone hybrids still function, still think, still remember, though what they’ve become might be more machine than man.

Some are spectral only in appearance, holograms projected by ancient devices, mistaken for ghosts. Others may live inside armored suits or prosthetic vessels, their true bodies reduced to skeletal fragments or mummified remains hidden deep within.

Their continued existence isn’t always obvious. Many hide in plain sight, wearing synthetic skin or projecting illusions, while others slumber in tombs and sealed vaults, waiting for the right trigger, be it prophecy, disaster, or a forgotten activation code.
objects.title: Ancient Bag of Bones

objects.text:
Just as many animal species are divided into distinct subspecies, humanity too possess its own subspecies. These are not entirely separate species, but distinct human populations that have, over time, developed divergent physical or cognitive traits.

These human subspecies may differ in appearance, physiology, or innate capabilities, but they are all still fundamentally human. Interbreeding is possible, and there is a shared ancestral lineage, but millennia of isolation, mutation, and adaptation have shaped them into something more or at least, something other.

Some subspecies have developed biological advantages perfectly suited to their environments. In regions of eternal night or deep subterranean tunnels, humans may be born with large, reflective eyes, slit like those of a cat, to allow for precise vision in near-total darkness. In high-altitude or toxic regions, certain groups may have evolved larger lungs or secondary respiratory structures to process thinner air or filter out contaminants. Skin tones might shift far beyond the usual human range, deep obsidian, muted gray, or even bluish hues adapted for extreme sun exposure, underwater living, or cultural distinction.

Some subspecies display far more exotic traits: small, vestigial horns curling back from the forehead. Others might have elongated limbs, or shortened, stockier builds for heat retention or mobility in tight spaces. Certain forest-dwelling populations may have prehensile toes, granting them greater agility among the trees, while others, adapted to aquatic life, might possess slightly webbed fingers and toes, with pale, almost translucent skin and eyes that can adjust focus underwater.
objects.title: Human Subspecies

objects.text: ...-and there's something wrong with the bees! Maybe it's something in the water. Maybe it's a form of radiation. Or maybe a tinker screwed something up. Whatever it is, it's not safe. It isn't healthy. And it's growing worse. All over the world random small animals- at most a thirtieth of any population, and of non-microscopic species smaller than an adult human's palm- begin to change. Growing. A bug smaller than a grain of rice will begin to grow to the length of a pinky, then a hand, then a forearm. With larger species increasing proportionally. Becoming hyperaggressive, almost rabid, but with no fear of anything. Extra limbs may sprout, along with new sensory organs. Bodies warp, mutating new weapons, and losing access to reproduction. Remade into indiscriminate biological weapons with no care for their own lives. Only barely being held back from attacking others like them through some deeply ingrained instinct in their new forms. Instead attacking everything else around them These mutated pests become an endemic problem in the world, causing untold chaos and destruction of the environment and infrastructure. Thankfully, the more common a species the less frequent the mutated members, and the 'pests' do not stay small and hidden, and don't necessarily have mercy for their own species. Unless the world has supernatural effects, these mutants won't grow too deadly, though they will become highly resistant- if not outright immune- to small arms fire when fully 'grown'.
objects.title: Mutating Pests

objects.text:
Instead of being limited to small organisms no larger than a human palm, the mutations now slowly start to spread to larger species, and grow more and more dangerous.

As time passes the species affected grow more numerous, and the mutations more potent. Though never taking up more than a tenth total of a species' population. From bugs, growing over months to affect housecats, and in years even affecting humans, before growing even further. In decades the largest animals on the planet- including whales- can find themselves mutated, with even more extreme mutations. Growing further and further away from their original species, with ever more destructive weapons and capabilities appearing over time.

This is made worse if the world you are heading to has any supernatural phenomenon- though the base strength of a species will delay the time until mutations can effect them- with superpowers, magic, and other supernatural capabilities becoming common among the mutated beasts. Even in non-supernatural settings, fully grown mutants can become almost immune to higher-caliber weapons and toxins.
objects.title: The Mutation Grows

objects.text: When Scion appeared, something strange happened to the animals. They suddenly became much smarter, able to understand language, read, and even use tools. From the smallest ants to the biggest whales, all of them can understand and communicate with one another. However, they found humanity to be disgusting and began to plot against them, acting normally around humans while concealing their true intelligence. An organization formed, with the goal of achieving world domination.
