With their intellect, they pose a major challenge to the Parahumans, and must be dealt with quickly before they become too powerful.
objects.title: Animal Conspiracy

objects.text: All animals can now awaken parahuman abilities of their own, with a thinker power that enhanced their mental abilities so that they can use their powers effectively and a secondary ability that was tailored to their specific need.
objects.title: Animal Power

addons.text: The moment the Age of Beasts arrived long ago, animals and para-animals noticed how endangered they’d be if their lack of action against the Beasts amongst them were left unopposed for all animals. Their attempts at communication or rapport with what they regarded as fellow animals ended up disastrously once they realized the Beasts’ hatred and inhumanity (ha!) ran deep. They wouldn’t stop till their prey lay bleeding at their feet. Thus a call to arms against the Beasts emerged around all para-animals, which continues to this day; para-animals will build organizations and societies around defending their brethren, taking the role of defenders and hunters of Beasts. This stance allows institutions owing their existential threat. The Beasts, for all that, adapt. With societies and formidable abilities on their own, their loathing and brutality ramp up to cover entire communities, with all their militant actions, natural and paranatural weaponry mutating to be effective against para-animal powers, their tactics barbarous once in active combat.
addons.title: Beastly War

addons.text: In order to maintain peace between Carnivores, Herbivores, and Omnivores, there is a single amazing person that's elected to be a "Beastar", someone between a celebrity and a politician whom deals with the social issues between all three forms of humankind. They were first selected by their academy as a Young Beastar, who shall be trained in their would be role, before potentially being selected as the Sublime Beastar, the one above them all. Their roles range from being able to influence politics of their given countries for everyone's betterment, to even going around dealing with criminals of their homeland. The balance of this world rests on their shoulders, who knows, maybe you can be chosen as the one?
addons.title: Beastars

objects.text: In this world, all animals have evolved to a level where they can walk on two legs and possess vastly increased intelligence. The herbivores are generally more intelligent than the carnivores, focusing on problem-solving and strategy, while the carnivores tend to be more physically capable, with high strength and agility. This dichotomy has led to a society where the herbivores rely on their intelligence to defend themselves, while the carnivores use their physical prowess to hunt and seek out resources. This alternate world has developed in a completely different way, with animals taking the place of humans and creating their own civilizations and societies.
objects.title: Zootopia

addons.text:
Around 10-15 percent of the monstrous population is part of subspecies with a mutation that gives them an appearance and intelligence resembling humans, while retaining distinctly monstrous traits, such as horns, claws, tails or other features. These monsterfolk will not be genetically related to humans, despite appearances. 

While having similar intellect and sociability to humans, including the ability to speak. Monsterfolk will still have strong monstrous natural instincts and habits. How these monsterfolk live will depend on their natural monster instincts. Monsterfolk will have a natural affinity with their feral cousins. For example, the undead may mingle in the hordes of their mindless fellows, while fairies coul call on strange things in the wilds. Some will live in packs and family structures, while others will be solitary. Some will form their own tribes, nations and empires. Eagle harpies will probably live in small tribes over the wild, while pidgeon harpies will roost in urban apartments. Monsterfolk species will have their own distinct cultures that reflect their origins. Seraphim might be deeply religious, while unicorn-taurs will appreciate fairy-tail princess styles.

Certain species might even integrate into human societies, like dog kobolds and satyrs. Stronger monsters like dragonfolk and archdemons might gather or conquer their own subjects of both humans and weaker monsters. Discrimination and wars between humans and Monsterfolk will be likely in some cases, while in others they may live as allies and equals.

These Monsterfolk will retain the strength and abilities of their monster ancestors, making them much more powerful than humans. In addition to these natural strengths, Monsterfolk with powers or magic will tend use abilities that reflect their heritage. Orcs may tend to have Brute powers, lamiae might have venom-based Striker powers, while wraiths could be Strangers. Monsterfolk may use their special abilities to profit in human society. For example, arachne will sell silks while molemen will work construction. Some humans will develop specialized services and technologies for the needs and wants of monster neighbors, such as pool hoses for mermaids and trimming for treants.

Between one in ten to twenty canon characters will become monsterfolk based on their themes and backgrounds. The Laborns could be shades, Lung could be an actual ryu, and Glaistig Ulaine could be a descendant of the mythical Titania. If you have Case 53, you may choose to become a monsterfolk though you will have to buy your natural abilities as powers.
addons.title: Everyday Life With Monsterfolk

objects.text:
Humanity is far from the dominant species in this world. Various fantastical creatures, some vaguely resembling different animal species, have long since existed in the world and are in an eternal struggle with humanity for resources. These creatures have all been lumped together into one category by humans -- Monsters.

Monsters are spread out across the planet and vie for supremacy in the skies, lands, and seas. They have evolved to be physically stronger, more durable, and faster than humans. Fortunately, they are also often less intelligent than humans. Furthermore, depending on species they can have unique biological abilities such as spitting massive torrents of acid, multi-layered scale armor, or cave-spanning web networks. These abilities are unique to each species, though they often mutate into different variations, giving rise to various subspecies of monsters.

Some rare monsters even develop the capability to use innate special abilities (magic, if it exists), though they are too stupid to develop anything advanced and often rely on the same few basic techniques which they utilize through instinct. Some examples include fire breathing wolves, trees with soul-devouring addictive fruits, laser-blasting crystal crabs, etc.

As a monster grows older, its innate biological and unique traits are strengthened, generally along with an increase in size. Older monsters can command lesser members of their species, though the exact number depends greatly on age and strength. The strongest monsters have lived for millenia and can rally the equivalent of a small army under their banner, as well as having the personal power to raze cities. Only around a dozen monsters have reached this level.

The existence of monsters has greatly impacted the development of civilization. Cities are often walled off to prevent attacks, and even small towns have basic ramparts for protection. Venturing away from established and patrolled road networks is often an easy route to a quick death, and even the well-policed roads are susceptible to the occasional raid or two. Merchant caravans and those seeking to travel usually hire armed escort to guide them. Large parts of the world remains unexplored and undeveloped, and it is unsafe to go alone into woods and caves without weaponry. 

Of course, monsters have provided various boons as well. Their corpses can be harvested for valuable materials and body parts, making up a significant portion of the economy. Furthermore, various monsters have been tamed and bred to become docile, and are used for various functions such as transport, food and dairy production, and labor. Exotic monster parts/corpses are particularly valuable to study their innate traits or to create magical objects.

Like humanity, monsters are far from united. They often fight with each other for mates, territory, or for no reason whatsoever. Only members of the same species can occasionally work together in small groups, and any cooperation is dependent on a powerful leader uniting them. There are some exceptions, such as wolves naturally working in packs and eusocial telepathic spider hiveminds. 

There are countless different monster species and variations, many of which are undocumented. However, most of the common monsters have extensive records on their traits, weakpoints, and potential loot.
objects.title: A World of Monsters

objects.text: Parahumans are not the only beings with superpowers in this world, a plethora of mutations has transformed the plants and animals as well. These changes have imbued them with unusual capabilities, creating a stark contrast from the world before Scion's arrival. For instance, some plants have developed the ability to manipulate the weather, causing constant storms and hurricanes in their area. Some animals may have developed superhuman speed or the ability to fly, making them much more formidable predators. These mutated creatures have reshaped the environment, creating new ecosystems and habitats, including some that are almost entirely alien to human experience.
objects.title: Bizarre Ecology

addons.text:
As nature changed, humanity was pushed back further and further. First out of the wild into the settlements, then out of smaller settlements into large cities, and then even those cities had to fortify themselves with massive walls in order to survive. Yet it seemed nature was not willing to leave man even that, with walled cities becoming stationary targets more than anything else. Left in a situation where man saw they would not be able to hold the walls, yet also unable to survive without them, that left only the option of taking the walls with them as they fled, and so cities became mobile, Bastion became Urbivore, constantly on the move to harvest resources while fleeing the worst of nature's fury.

And while larger cities still regularly devour smaller ones, often this process is desired by the smaller metropolis if they are in too dire a pickle to continue onward alone. For these smaller Urbivores are built and sent out by the larger ones, both as scouts and as hopes that they prosper and grow to match their parent, so that man may spread across the globe once more. Though equally often it is the unending appetite for resources that pushes a large Urbivore to gobble up its kin, a seed for the future ripped from the soil to feed the hunger of the present.
addons.title: Mobile Bastions

objects.text: Nature has been enormously influenced by the appearance of powers; so much that it has started taking over many of the world's settlements, and travelling it is dangerous even for strong parahumans. As such, there is only a few hundred major cities left as bastions across the planet. Communication and travel between them are rough, though still possible thanks to volunteer parahumans. Starvation and homelessness are common, exiting the cities requires permits and many younger people aren't even old enough to remember a time where going out to nature wasn't seen as a suicidal endeavor.
objects.title: The Last Bastions

addons.text:
Looks like the boogiemen didn’t STAY boogiemen. Some Numans, whether from desperation, curiosity, or just plain loneliness, decided to reveal themselves and join the Animal Kingdom. Not only that, but it turns out that after so much mutation, they became cross compatible. The result is a surprising number of Beastmen running around.

This happened long ago enough to the point that these Numen have almost completely died out and been replaced with their hybrid children. That isn’t to say there isn’t still Numen running around. Not everyone liked this decision. The Humans, Numans, and Animals, and Beastmen themselves are divide in their opinions.

While many Humans find Beastmen disturbing, as they consider them progeny of bestiality, others are perfectly fine with them considering they look human enough. Numans also consider Beastmen bizarre but less so. They are fully aware that they were born from sapient beings, so they don’t look down on them too much. Racism surprisingly still exists despite humanity’s near extinction.

The Animals mostly consider them just another subspecies, like how lions and tigers are still both felines. Racism still exists here, its just lumped in with the “normal” racism, meaning a Beastman is as likely to be called out for the human part as they are the animal part depending on their community.

The Beastmen are rather torn when it comes to their identity. Some chose to fully integrate into the animal kingdom, some decide to go join the Numan hideouts, and others still feel like they don’t belong wherever they go.
addons.title: Life, uh, Finds a Way

addons.text:
Turns out, years away from each other have resulted in different factions amongst humanity. Not to mention, the Animal Kingdom isn’t as united as one might think. Who would have guessed? 

First, for humanity, we have the Vault Dwellers. They are from the underground bunkers and have a more “idealist” view of the world, thinking that they can just come up topside and live normal lives again. Reality is a harsh mistress to the ones who discovered just how much they CAN’T.

Next, we have the Sea Divers. They come from the deep-sea stations and have spent most of their time planning on how to terra-form the planet back into a more habitable space. The fact that life can now be supported means that that technology will probably be redirected into using it to conquer the world anew.

Then, we have the Spacers. They are from space colonies made by the rich and powerful, along with their “help”, to escape Earth in comfort and style. They don’t actually care about recolonizing; they only want resources to fuel their lavish lifestyles.

Finally, we have the Mountain Men. Their mountain fortresses were relatively topside and as a result, they actually have relations to both the Numans and Animals. If Beastmen exist, most can probably be found in nearby cities.

We technically have the Numan communities as well, but they are too scattered and small to genuinely be considered factions in and of themselves.

In the Animal Kingdom, we have the Peaceful and the Predatory. The Peaceful want to advance as a society. They are all about technology, innovation, and modernization. They rapidly welcome the returning humans, seeing them as beacons of industry and keys to advancement. Most of them consider Numans nothing but barbarians.

The Predatory believes that this goes against the laws of nature. They are about strength, instinct, and tradition. They consider the returning humans an evil from a bygone age, one that should have been erased with the changing world. In contrast, they are perfectly fine with the Numans, seeing them as fellow equals in this strange and savage world.

Having Fractured will get you the human factions. Having Divided will get you the animal factions. If you have BOTH, prepare for the inevitable war.
addons.title: New Nations

addons.text:
Uh Oh, it turns out that some of humanities’ avenues of retreat were occupied. 

Maybe those who went underground found the lizard people. Perhaps the ones who went underwater discovered the deep ones. Those in the mountains might have been hunted by the beast alongside the animals. Who knows if those who fled to space ended up making a rather violent first contact with aliens. Humanity seems to have fled the aftermath of one war and dived headfirst into the next.

Thankfully for them, as the history of Earth’s surface has proven, humanity is more than capable of destructive warfare. The results of these different wars have lasting impacts on the world at large. Depending on your choices various survivors of the opposite side of the conflicts will be scattered across the world. Some might just want to give up and live in peace, but most are simply licking their wounds and waiting to strike. Not to mention that each different colony of humanity got more robust and fit after their war. Not to the same standard as the Numans, but certainly to our current standard of peak human.

The effects that these wars have on the planet depends on if the options The Alien Invaders, Monstrous Awakening, In The Deep, and Hollow Earth were all selected or not. If you selected one or two, the world won’t change too much considering that it was already changing. If you chose ALL of them, however, the changes to this world are such that humanity and the animals will have to band together if they want to survive.
addons.title: Sure, More Apocalypse, WHY NOT!?

objects.text:
The world was changing, becoming more and more dangerous. This world was being shaped by human war and alien mutation into something that was simply too dangerous for mankind. Action was taken and most of humanity fled. They fled into underground bunkers, deep sea stations, hidden mountain forts, and somehow even into the dark of space. They waited until the time was right, when they could go back and reclaim what was lost. When the time came, what they found was something they never expected.

The world didn’t wait for them to come back. The constant mutation and destruction had an unexpected side effect. While animals’ bodies changed, so too did their minds. They learned to use tools and build. They made culture and civilization. They had advanced like mankind and had become the new owners of this world.

Opinions were mixed. Some wanted to achieve peaceful coexistence, some wanted to conquer them, some wanted to exterminate them, and others thought they could just continue living in their bunkers and just ignore it entirely. The animals’ opinion was just as varied, but with a twist.

See, not every human retreated when disaster struck. Either purposefully or accidentally, some humans stayed behind and changed with everything else. They became stronger, smarter, and overall better than humanity was before. These “Numan” became boogie men to the animal kingdom, akin to legend of bigfoot. As a result, they are more than a bit distrustful of humanity. Not to mention that the Numans have their OWN culture that is distrustful of BOTH sides. Put all this together and you have a recipe for disaster.
objects.title: Planet of the Apes

addons.text:
All the new monstrous animals have not only grown larger but have also become significantly more intelligent.

In fact, they have established their own sovereign kingdoms, each governed by a ruling monarchy. These monarchies preside over well-organized societies, complete with intricate laws and customs. Their armies are formidable, consisting of thousands of loyal compatriots who are trained and ready to defend their territories with fierce determination and advanced strategies. The creatures' ingenuity extends to their technology and infrastructure, making their kingdoms thriving and formidable realms. 

These kingdoms, however, have formed with a singular purpose: to kill and replace humans. United by this common goal, they relentlessly strategize and mobilize their resources to overthrow human dominance, seeking to establish a world where they reign supreme.
addons.title: Beast King

addons.text:
As the monstrous animals continue to mature, they have developed new abilities that defy comprehension. These newfound powers vary widely, showcasing their incredible adaptability and versatility. Some can emit powerful laser beams from their eyes, capable of slicing through the toughest materials with ease. Some possess telepathic skills, enabling them to communicate instantly and coordinate complex strategies over vast distances. Others can manipulate the elements, summoning storms at will, conjuring devastating lightning strikes, unleashing torrents of water to drown their enemies, igniting infernos with a mere flick of their fingertips, or freezing objects solid with a single touch.

Together, this vast array of skills makes the monstrous animals not only a formidable force but also highly adaptive and capable of overcoming any challenge they encounter. Their continuous evolution and the sheer diversity of their powers render them an existential threat to humanity, poised to reshape the world in their image.
addons.title: Demon Beast

objects.text:
Over the course of the past millennia, man has evolved to cover the majority of the Earth. Becoming the top predator on the planet through our unique minds and capability to adapt to challenges presented to us.

Unfortunately, this age of man shall be tested by the coming age of the beast. 

Over time, animal groups from across the globe will slowly but surely evolve into new and strange forms, creating new sub-categories. Birds that were once small, herbivorous, and simple minded grow to become as large as bears, carnivorous, and with traces of subtle intellect. Canines, our best friends, abandon us, they become hateful and can become as large as houses. Strong enough to tear through neighborhoods easily, while shrugging off bullets like gnats. Even sea animals aren't safe, some groups of fish grow capable to breath on land and are able to move just as easily on land as they could in the ocean.

There will even be entirely new species as well, each stranger than the last, draconic like beast that can spew fire or even acid, large avian creatures that should seem to large to fly, and even some terrestrial beast that can produce electric like eels but so much worse. Some traits seem supernatural, all of the abilities of these creatures are strictly biological, simply far more advanced than what can found on Earth

As different species generate new subgroups one thing becomes obvious to all; their heightened aggression and hatred towards humans. These creatures are normally territorial to the mundane animals but when it comes to humans all hell will break loose. They will attack to kill people on sight, using their new capabilities and in some cases pack tactics. 

They also reproduce differently then normal animals, they create hive-like areas where they can multiple vastly. And sizable groups can wipe out towns and do great damage to cities.

The Age of Beast comes, are you ready?
objects.title: Monstrous Awakening

addons.text:
Scion's arrival was a monumental event across the world, which was noticed by he who waits behind the wall. 

The emergence of heroes and villains changed the world, which was noticed by he who waits to end it all. 

Then he noticed some of his horrors coming out into the open, so decided to let the rest of his horrors start to openly play their Great Game.

Don't say his name or else he comes.
addons.title: He Noticed

objects.text:
This is a world of old, eldritch monsters, some of which may appear familiar to you from horror stories on the internet, perhaps from shared fears within cultural similarities, your own fears serving as the catalyst for new manifestations of them, or even those monsters existing in your world in the same way they exist here. Expect impossible things like widespread invisible creatures that feed on fear, haunted electronics, email-based cognitohazards, strange extradimensional spaces, and godlike entities. 

There are three things that make it so that this isn't too overwhelmingly bad, though. Firstly, society as a whole hasn't been disrupted, which in part is thanks to the subtlety of these horrors. Secondly, there are relatively benign horrors that can be taken advantage of to incredible benefit, albeit such comes with incredible risk as well. Thirdly, any threats to the world from this are long-term threats that can be prevented or stopped.
objects.title: What Hides in Shadows

objects.text:
Hundreds of millions of years ago one of the first Proto-Entities crashed into Earth in a violent explosion that destroyed it. It was not however completely destroyed, pieces of it’s Shards survived on Earth Bet which was ground zero for the crash, and on several nearby dimensions bonding with Earth’s life being integrated, and replicated into DNA over time.

Obviously this change to evolutionary history has dramatically affected modern life on earth, with most species having a minor natural shard power or two useful for survival that average 5 SP, plants might be better at gathering resources, and surviving in various environments, animals could have improved physical capabilities or thinker abilities that help them survive, maybe certain species could have a type of elemental manipulation. 

While there are variations, and outliers, the abilities a species possess are almost always universal to all members of that species, except for humans who instead have nearly unlimited diversity in the powers they can develop.

While there is plenty of wiggle room in this process for people to have more, or less power than their fellow humans, most people only have one or two minor abilities averaging 5 SP in strength each. With no one ever having had more than ten powers, or a power stronger than 10 SP. 

Most people acquire the majority of their abilities during puberty, and finish developing them by adulthood. What powers they develop is decided by a combination of genetics, and environmental pressures encountered as they grow up. 

These powers can be nearly anything with some caveats: first beyond the limitations of strength there are no natural tinker powers, while comparable to the complexity and versatility of modern shards these powers are hyper specialized to Earth life, and environments over the millions of years, and finally natural Trump powers have little to no effect on parahuman abilities as a consequence of the differences in mechanics, and from safeguards the Shards have.

Natural powers all have the equivalent of Uninhibited; they can, and will adapt to how they are used, their owners' knowledge, and to changing circumstances in their owner’s life. Though these changes will be focused on versatility instead of raw power.

Some countries have recently managed to make very basic cross-dimensional travel technology just from the advantages that having an evolutionary history being part Shard gives. This tech is capable of the equivalent of putting a man on the moon for the first time, and cannot locate, or breach Shard nesting dimensions.

Seeing as these powers have been a natural part of human biology for all of history they have affected human culture massively. For some, having a power only means having a power; for others the wrong kind of power is something to discriminate against.

As part of your arrival you can choose to be a Shard hybrid like the humans of this earth, and can choose up to 10 SP worth of the powers you’ve already purchased to be natural abilities that you possess separate from a Shard connection. Though use your best judgment and the rules stated earlier as guidelines for which powers you pick.

These Shard hybrid humans can trigger, and are being studied by the recently arrived Shards. Though their natural powers do not react to a Shard connection because of Shard safeguards, their natural powers can however adapt to synergize with Shard given powers. The Cycle is also studying regular humans who aren’t hybrids in distant dimensions.
objects.title: Alien Earth

addons.text:
Due to the transformation of animals into monstrous forms, a dark shadow has been cast over the lives of the beastmen, imbuing them with a harrowing existence fraught with prejudice and ostracization. Their very semblance, bearing an uncanny resemblance to the savage creatures that haunt the nightmares of mankind, serves as a constant reminder of their cursed lineage. 

Compounding their plight is the relentless cycle of their berserk state, an affliction that grips them with primal ferocity, stripping away the thin veneer of humanity to reveal the untamed beast within. During these tumultuous episodes, they are consumed by an insatiable frenzy, their actions driven by primal instincts and feral urges that transcend rational thought. 

Older beastmen tend to achieve mastery over their berserk state, transcending its chaotic grip to wield it as a formidable tool at their command. Through arduous discipline and unwavering determination, they harness the primal energies coursing through their veins, bending the savage fury to their will, allowing them to use its power at any time. 

However, even amidst this mastery, they will still feel the effects of the berserk state's cycle, where a tempest of emotions remains a turbulent force within them. Though they may guide the raging storm with a steady hand, their inner turmoil still rages, fueling their actions with a volatile intensity that threatens to overwhelm even the most seasoned of warriors.
addons.title: Werebeast

objects.text:
A unique evolution appeared during Earth Bet's history, resulting in approximately 30 to 50 percent of Earth Bet's population having physical traits resembling those of various animals. 

These individuals' personalities often match the traits associated with their respective animal counterparts. For instance, those bearing traits reminiscent of typical farm animals tend to exhibit industriousness and perseverance, evoking the symbolic image of a workhorse diligently fulfilling its tasks.

What distinguishes these individuals extends beyond their psychological dispositions; they frequently manifest physical attributes that surpass those of ordinary humans. Their heightened strength, agility, and perhaps other latent abilities render them formidable counterparts, imbuing them with a distinct advantage over their unaltered peers.

Racial discrimination exists, be it between the beastmen and humans or between the different types of beastmen.

Certain canon and historical characters will have animal traits.
objects.title: Beastmen

objects.text:
With this modifier, you can completely change human physiology, with biologically conceivable traits for modern Earth. Do you want humans to have gills, wings to glide, or just be more muscular on average? You can do all that and more with this modifier. This can optionally affect both you and the entire human population of the local Multiverse.

You can have certain percentages of the population possess different physiologies from other percentages, so normal humans could exist alongside humans with cat ears.

You can choose why this is the case within reason, maybe evolution happened a bit differently here, or maybe a biotinker released a dimension-traveling, gene-editing virus shortly before or just after your arrival which will slowly spread.
objects.title: DNA Redux

addons.text:
Within the heart of this civilization, something sleeps. Something even more eldritch than these creatures. A god-like being lies in a dormant state, its very existence warping reality around it. The name of this civilization is now known to you: R'lyeh. As it slowly awakens, its influence seeps into the minds of the beings within R'lyeh, causing subtle shifts in their behavior and an increase in their already unfathomable powers.

The sleeping god, an ancient entity of immense power and malevolence, is said to be the source of R'lyeh's advanced technologies and arcane knowledge. Its dreams ripple through the depths, manifesting as strange phenomena both above and below the water. As it stirs, forgotten secrets and forbidden knowledge begin to surface, spreading whispers of madness among those who dare to delve too deep.

With the awakening of this god-like being, more eyes have taken notice of your blue planet. Eldritch entities from the furthest reaches of the cosmos, drawn by the stirrings of their ancient kin, turn their gaze toward Earth. These otherworldly beings, each with their own inscrutable agendas, bring with them the potential for both great peril and unimaginable change.
addons.title: Priest of the Great Old Ones

objects.text:
An ancient civilization in the deepest parts of the ocean has awakened. Technologically equal to humans but physically greater due to adapting to deep sea pressure, this civilization has developed advanced biotechnology and underwater engineering that surpasses human understanding. Their bodies are adapted to the crushing depths, with bioluminescent skin, multiple limbs, and a heightened resistance to extreme conditions.

Their manner of thinking is entirely alien to humans, shaped by eons of isolation and the vast, dark expanse of the deep ocean. They communicate through a complex combination of bioluminescent patterns, ultrasonic waves, and chemical signals, which convey intricate concepts and emotions incomprehensible to the human mind. Their society is structured around an enigmatic hierarchy, with leaders who possess unique abilities derived from the deep sea environment, such as controlling ocean currents and commanding marine life.

Their civilization operates on principles that defy human logic, valuing concepts like temporal fluidity, where past, present, and future are perceived as intertwined, and symbiotic existence with the ocean's ecosystems. They have a profound understanding of marine biology and ecology, enabling them to harness the power of sea creatures and manipulate underwater habitats.

As they emerge from the depths, they seek to reclaim their ancient dominion over the ocean and potentially expand their influence to the surface world. Their goals and motivations remain inscrutable, driven by purposes beyond human comprehension.
objects.title: In The Deep

objects.text:
In this world, human evolution didn’t favour the clever or the crafty. The thinkers, the tool makers, the fire starters—they were outpaced, outmuscled, and outbred. Instead, it was the strong who survived. The aggressive, territorial, and physically dominant early humans became the foundation of the species, and over time, humanity evolved into something far more primal.

Modern humans are built like predators: broad shoulders, thick muscle, dense bones, and lightning-fast reflexes. They walk with power, move with purpose, and carry the weight of a thousand generations of violence in their stride. Their bones are thicker, their muscles denser, and their hearts stronger—pumping more blood, more oxygen, more fury through a body built to fight and endure. Pain is dulled. Recovery is rapid. Even a broken bone can knit in days with the right rest and meat.

The hormonal structure shifted too—higher baseline testosterone and growth hormone levels in both sexes, leading to naturally larger, more aggressive individuals. Puberty strikes early and hard, triggering not just physical growth but an instinctual sharpening of dominance behavior. Children grow fast, fight early, and mature into adults with predator eyes and combat instincts. Aging is slower too. Muscle and bone stay strong for decades, and a forty-year-old still has the physique of a prime warrior.

Even the brain changed. The limbic system—the part tied to emotion, fear, and aggression—is more dominant, giving these humans faster threat responses and stronger territorial instincts. The prefrontal cortex, responsible for long-term planning and abstract reasoning, still exists but plays a smaller role. Logic serves instinct. Strategy serves survival. Emotions are simple, powerful, and direct—rage, loyalty, fear, lust, hunger. Everything else is unnecessary.

And the body adapted in more primal ways. Teeth are slightly elongated—especially the canines—designed to tear meat and intimidate. The jaw is stronger, the bite more dangerous. Fingernails thicken into keratin-rich claws—nothing dramatic, but enough to slash skin or dig into prey. Skin is tougher too, with a subtle leathery resilience against cuts and scrapes. Scars are worn like medals, and most adults carry at least a few.

And when creatures like this built a world, they built it in their image.

Civilization came, but not the way we knew it. There were no quiet farmers shaping the land. The first “cities” were war camps. The first tools were weapons. Fire was for cooking meat and burning enemies. Writing developed not to record trade, but to mark bloodlines and victories. Culture grew around strength, not stories. Oral traditions were chants of conquest, not myths or morality tales.

Tribes became clans. Clans became warbands. Warbands became empires. But diplomacy never drove these powers—force did. Power passed by ritual combat, challenge, or sheer intimidation. Leadership was never inherited, only earned through strength. Bloodlines were respected, but only if their heirs could fight as fiercely as their ancestors.

Religion, where it existed, revolved around war gods, beast spirits, and primal forces. Temples were arenas. Sacrifices were battles. The divine was found in domination, not mercy. Those who could not fight were either protected as rare assets—healers, thinkers, breeders—or cast out.

Technology rose slower, but when it did, it was brutal and efficient. The wheel was for chariots before carts. Metallurgy began with swords and armor. Engineering served siege and fortress before comfort and shelter. Medicine? It began as battlefield triage. Science only gained ground when it could sharpen blades or build bigger engines of war.

Even in the modern age, the world reflects this origin. Cities are shaped like strongholds. Architecture is solid, angular, imposing. Nations are led by war councils, not politicians. Schools train mind and body equally—but always with the body first. Children spar as part of their basic education. Weakness is a flaw to be corrected, not accommodated.

Technology exists—vehicles, weapons, even computers—but it’s wrapped in a culture of dominance. Smart people thrive, but only under the shadow of the strong. Ideas are tools. Innovation is tolerated so long as it doesn’t challenge the hierarchy. Everything, from economics to art, exists in service to survival, glory, or control.

Peace is rare, and never trusted.

You are not the human we know. You are the human shaped by a million years of claw, fang, fire, and war. You are the apex predator who learned to speak.
objects.title: Human Orcs

addons.text: Pick a sport, any sport, and humanity had grown so obsessed with it that we've basically evolved to better win in said sport. Whether it be immunity to death by car crashes for racers, or longer limbs and bodies for basketball. We are the ultimate sports creatures, the best of the best, the greatest of all time.
addons.title: Put the Ball in Biology

addons.text: With how war hungry the world has gone, people have evolved in the intense evolutionary pressures this has caused. People are now more stronger, more agile, built for prolonged conflict even further than we already are now. It doesn't help that the powers above have taken to weaponizing this, experimenting on their soldiers to further force the most lethal of adaptations to manifest in them. War never changes, and now, it's the next step to our evolution.
addons.title: The Warrior Race

addons.text: The non speculative biological species counterpart of your many races also pop up from time to time via getting isekai'd. This has strange ramifications as the isekai'd creatures act like a sort of invasive species, putting more adaptational pressures on your ecosystem that they are not used to due to being from a different universe altogether. Whether this means the isekai'd folks slowly adapt to be like their main counterparts here or if it's the other way around, only time will tell.
addons.title: Invasive Isekai'd Species

objects.text: The mechanisms and appearance of different beings has been dramatically changed. Rather than power justifying a human appearance, biology takes a more ‘speculative’ route. Aliens will look more explicitly alien. Human subspecies will be clearly divergent, and esoteric effects will have major practical changes on the subject’s bodies. This, however, does not change the function of powers, merely their internal biology and, in extremis, the ‘justification’ of their workings to bring it more in line with conventional evolutionary understanding. For Instance, a Kryptonian may be a form of plant, capable of transforming solar energy to bio-electricity. A Cybertronian is a colony organism akin to a siphonophore whose transformation is fueled by its constituent 'pieces', specialised for their roles. Atlanteans adapted to deep sea life with increased blubber to compensate for the pressure, etcetera.
objects.title: Speculative Biology

objects.text:
Alongside humans, other humanoids of sorts exist. There are species similar to the typical Tolkien classic fantasy races such as Elves, Dwarves, Orcs, etc, all of whom lived alongside us throughout history. Humanity isn't aware of this for the longest time however, dismissing them as merely myth. Until recently, that masquerade had broken, and now somehow, the Fantasy Races have returned.

While moreso similar to humans to the point half-humans had existed among them, they have some key differences that makes them stand out. Some few examples are:

Elves are pointy eared folk with inherent connection to magic, to the point that they can easily sense whatever magic system this world has as if merely breathing air. 

Dwarves are stout but hardy folk, capable of surviving underground where they are adapted to.

Orcs are big burly humanoids with non naturally human skin tone, and tend to be stereotyped as all brawn no brain by non Orcs.

Halflings are tiny mostly pastoral folk with unnatural luck which explained their supposed typical innocent nature.

Gnomes are yet another little person race who seemed to be incredibly capable at tinkering technology, sometimes called Goblins due to some folks seeing them as troublesome.

And many more. Not even counting subspecies dependent on where they are from.

This turn for the fantastical had affected the world in many ways. From having Elves run for office, to Giants being used for war, the rights of these races are tension filled. Should you take this, you are free to edit the specifics of their traits. There's even the chance to be one of them. Some Canon characters in certain settings might even be these species. In powered settings, they should be able to also have abilities like any other human.

How we treat these new neighbors are how we humans treat ourselves. Who knows how this will affect society at large?
objects.title: Tolkienism

objects.text:
Emotions and desires are powerful things in this world. Whether it be positive or negative, a person's desires could push them not just to extremes, but also transform them literally. A man obsessed with painting could slowly transform into a paintbrush looking creature. While a girl who wishes to protect the people around her could turn into a literal birdcage, and so on.

Thus, these emotions can push people to greater heights but also lowest of lows, especially when they become obsession. This tendency for people to transform into things they are passionate about of course has a profound effect on the world. With some cultures encouraging restraint and letting go of your desires, while others embrace it, seeing it as the next evolution of humanity.

If you land in this world, you have the chance to slowly mutate into something you are particularly obsessed in. Unless you're careful, it might consume you. That is unless... You do want to be consumed? The transformation could turn you into something much greater, much more powerful after all.

What you become depends on what you feel strongly towards. Would you risk it and embrace the change? Or would you pace yourself and cling on to your "humanity?" You decide.
objects.title: Emotion Evolution

objects.text:
All humans have an internal biological radar that makes them aware of other humans who they share different interests with, within a mile radius. While also knowing which specific interests they share.

You can choose whether this is a new ability or if it’s something humanity has always possessed. Either way society will adapt.
objects.title: Gaydar

objects.text:
Your world is now insinuated with (normally) small spirits that pop into existence one way or another. Maybe they just manifest out of the aether, are constructed from nanomachines, or are born from ambient emotions or something else as long as it matches, roughly, with the way your world works. If your world is completely mundane with no advanced technology to explain their appearance, the world becomes slightly supernatural in some way in order for the spirits to exist. Or maybe the spirits just exist regardless. Either way, they're here to stay.

These spirits can vary wildly in shape, ability, and personality, from mischievous to malicious to benevolent. Their abilities, natures, and appearances heavily depend on the actual nature of your world. In worlds with magic, they'll be obviously magical. In worlds with ghosts, they can be be little cast-offs of other ghosts that collect and manifest. In a grimdark world... well. They'll probably lean more towards malevolent than good. 

One purchase keeps the spirits small—the bigger ones being the size of a large housecat—limited in abilities, and relatively simple and unintelligent. More like jellyfish that only passively react to outside stimuli. Two purchases causes some spirits to spawn with the same physical and mental capabilities as animals—on top of whatever supernatural ones they already had. Three purchases lets huge spirits spawn; beings that can be up to the size of two story houses, as intelligent as humans, and far stronger than normal physics would allow. At four purchases, kaiju and god-like spirits (Limited, with ranges at most affecting a city, barring other factors) can appear. Each purchase also makes the previous sizes of spirits more common. At just three purchases, it would be hard to go through a day without seeing a handful of the smallest spirits, even if huge spirits would still be rare. 

The more powerful, magical, or advanced your world is, the stronger and more common spirits can get. Both in simple strength, and esoteric capabilities. For example; In galactic-scale settings god-like spirits could affect huge swathes of a solar system at once, and small spirits could form massive interplanetary clouds.
objects.title: Little Spirits!

objects.text:
You can freely decide the gender distribution of the world. From one gender simply outnumbering another to erasing one gender entirely.

You can decide if this happens upon your arrival or is retroactive. In the case of the latter, the society has adapted to function perfectly even in these unusual circumstances, whether by means of biology, technology, magic, or any other.
objects.title: Gender Ratio Change

objects.text:
Each purchase lets you add one biological trait to humanity as a whole. This can be anything from low-light vision, to venomous fangs, to extra limbs or organs, to anything else you can think of. These traits can even be fully novel traits that don't exist anywhere in nature so long as they are at least somewhat biologically plausible. No matter what, these traits will not be supernatural in nature, although native supernatural powers may adapt to interact with them in unique ways.

If the setting has other sapient species, you may add additional traits to them too per purchase, and they need not be the same as other races. Either way, you may choose to be affected by this if you are a member of one of these species, or you may choose to be exempted from receiving certain traits. You may also choose if these traits manifest across the targeted species upon arrival or have retroactively always existed.
objects.title: Additional Universal Traits

objects.text:
Humanity multiplies in a way that's different in how we typically do in real life. Either through cloning, growing new babies from fruits, literal storks, mitosis, holding hands, or some other new method, the way new humans are created had changed drastically from what we are used to. This has obvious large effects on society and gender roles at large. Not to mention how it affects population growth, as depending on how easy it is for more babies to be birthed, humans could either be overpopulated or in the midst of our extinction.

This is an interesting choice, do be careful with the possible domino effects this entails. Especially since it's all about human reproduction.
objects.title: They Come From Storks, Son

objects.text:
The world is divided more than ever, and now, it's not something one can easily find common ground in.

In this world, humans (or whatever is the most common species that exists in your world) are separated based on their diets. The very common Herbivores, the slightly more uncommon Carnivores, and the rare Omnivores. 

Herbivores tend to be the majority, and thus have the most social and political standing in this world. They however, have high instinctual anxiety, almost akin to a danger sense as an evolutionary adaptation. They also tend to have less strength than their Omnivorous and Carnivorous counterparts. As their name implies, they cannot digest anything but plant and fungi.

Carnivores are the second most common, and also the most feared. They tend to be more physically stronger than the other 2 types of folks, but are also plagued with cannibalistic urges that they need to learn to keep down, whether through discipline or drugs in worse cases. As such, they tend to be treated worse by the others, and seen like ticking timebombs. Once again, as their name implies, they can't digest anything except meat.

Finally, Omnivores are the rarest, almost deemed like a myth to the other types. They tend to only spawn as rare hybrids between Carnivores and Omnivores, gaining both their danger sense and their strength. They however, also tend to have dietary issues such as needing more calories or not having a sense of taste. Due to their rarity, they tend to be treated as freaks in this culture, as such, it is common for Omnivores to try to pretend to be any of the other 2 in order to fit in. As stated prior, they're the only ones who are able to digest meat and plants.

You can pick to be any of these 3, though keep in mind you will have both their pros and cons both socially and physically. Can you survive in this heavily divided world where it's eat or be eaten?
objects.title: Predator and Prey

objects.text: All fauna on Earth no longer dies of old age, instead they will continue to grow bigger. Creatures will continue to grow until they hit a point where their bodies give out from the process, this may be from health issues caused by being so big, or ones related to the growth process itself, like being unable to shed properly.
objects.title: Like Lobsters

objects.text:
Colorful hair and eye colors have become completely natural and can be any color on the visible light spectrum.

The hair and eye colors made accessible through this modifier are as inheritable as regular hair and eye colors.
objects.title: Colorful People

objects.text:
In comparison to the ecosystems of other worlds, just about any organism on Earth could be considered a delicacy. This does not actually change the biology of Earth, but instead changes the biology of every other planet.

Plants on other worlds only very rarely evolve strategies such as edible fruit, with the vast majority of them being as inedible as they can possibly be. Even something like oak leaves could fetch a fairly high price at an alien restaraunt.

Just about every other world had a much more prominent evolutionary arms-race of prey making themselves less tasty. What aliens would consider the best cuts of meat of their favorite livestock would be borderline inedible gristle to any human, while even the poorest cuts of a cow would be the equivalent of a five-star meal to an alien.

This leaves Earth a very valuable resource, which could be their downfall or road to greatness depending on the setting.
objects.title: Tasty Planet
Friendly Neighborhood Monsters
objects.text:
It seems that where you're going, there are a multitude of supernatural beings, monsters, cryptids, spirits, and such. Normally vampires, werewolves, ghosts, bigfoot, and other things existing would be a bad thing, but surprisingly they are rather friendly. Your neighbor may be a blood sucking vampire born in the thirteenth century, but he's well known for his famous sculptures, gets his blood from cows, and is the leader of the neighborhood watch. Bigfoot communities are well known as some of the best tour guides on hikes through old growth forests, haunted houses are some of the best attractions especially on halloween when the ghosts throw huge parties, and werewolves are outright amazing at search and rescue.

By taking this modifier, you can choose which mythological, folklore, creepy pasta, and other supernatural beings are real, what version of them they are, and how they integrate into society. What their specific powers are and the strength thereof is dependent on the setting, on a mundane earth vampires might be at most a couple times peak human strength and have very limited blood-based telekinesis, while in Worm they might have a set of generic vampire powers that average around a 4-5 on the PRT Rating Scale with some going up to 7, and in Digimon or other very high power settings they could be on the level of high-end Dead Apostles or low-generation World of Darkness vampires.

This isn't all sunshine and rainbows of course, criminals and villains still exist among their kind, but overall this is an improvement. You can decide exactly how society has changed from these beings existing, and optionally even how long they've existed from a minimum of 20 years to as long as humans have as a species. If there are already such beings in the world you are going to, then this modifier makes coexistence more common, and even possible if it wasn't before.

For example, in Blade it could make it such that clans of 'vegetarian' vampires who subsist off of animal blood exist who act as benevolent guardians of humanity from the predations of the canonical 'carnivorous' clans, or in Tokyo Ghoul a drug was discovered that allows ghouls to subsist off of meat in general instead of human flesh specifically, and now there is a movement among them that advocates for peace between humans and ghouls with some actual success.

rows.title: Biology & Species Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the species and/or biology of the setting

objects.text:
While this world is for the most part completely identical to the fictional world you know (barring the effects of other modifiers) certain people you know from that fictional world, have at some point in the past had their lives diverge from the “canon” you know, which led them to have completely different lives and being much happier in the present day. Though before that point of divergence, their personal history was the same as what you know from that fictional world.

You can choose who has had their lives changed, when their lives changed, and how their lives have changed. Though only within reason as the changes must make sense, and be plausible for the world. The people you’ve selected must be “canon” characters of the fictional world you remember. How their lives have changed cannot involve killing or otherwise eliminating “Antagonists” or threats this world faces. If you’ve selected an Antagonist as someone whose life has improved in such a way they are no longer a threat, then a new Antagonist will rise to fill a similar role as the person you’ve selected, this antagonist will either be a canon character you haven’t selected or someone unknown to you, whichever makes the most sense for this world.
objects.title: A Brighter Yesterday

objects.text: While this world is for the most part completely identical to the fictional world you know. (barring the effects of other modifiers), one or more characters of your choice that you can genuinely say you like will have led a sadder much more tragic life here without affecting the overall state of the world before your arrival.
objects.title: A Darker Yesterday

objects.text:
Since the dawn of parahuman existence, visitors from other dimensions have found their way to Earth Bet. Whether their history as a visitor is known to the public or remains a secret is determined by their own personal history. Some have arrived by choice, while others were forced here. Some see their stay as temporary, while others have made this world their new permanent home.

With this upgrade, you can rewrite the history of any canon parahuman, making their origins interdimensional. This includes the ability to replace any of their shard-derived powers with a shardless equivalent, maintaining the same effective abilities while altering their source.
objects.title: Otherworldly Visitors

objects.text: This world's history has not gone the way it normally has, instead going down an alternate path. Anything ranging from the Mongols conquering the world, the Holy Roman Empire surviving till the modern day, Mao Zedong becoming the Emperor of China, or something as simple as a town receiving a different name or the border of a nation being changed a few feet this way or that. You may choose what is different, going anywhere from extremely specific to very general, either way history will keep to the changes you've made, even when continuing the timeline past the divergence point. In short: this is the alternate history option.
objects.title: Alternate History

objects.text: The Bubonic Plague... the Black Death... the Great Pestilence. Epithets to the bacterial infection preceding its pandemic in mid-14th Century Europe. Spreading through rats using fleas as the true vector, the Yersinia Pestis, caused the worst pandemic on Earth as we know it. 50 million people that befell these afflictions are merely remembered as casualties of this disease; swollen lymph nodes the size of eggs, fever, chills, even vomiting blood, and that's not to say how their bodies rotted from the insides as gangrene took over. Concepts such as hygiene and self-care weren't something people bothered or saw of much importance, thus droves perished, in turn, it is theorized this event cut almost half of Europe's population. And with those deaths, came change unwarranted, stretching from cultural and economic repercussions. And it's such a terrible event, let's hope nothing of the such occurs once again, yes? Can you imagine the ramifications of such a horrid tragedy in the Modern Age 😊? It begins in Europe, a strange illness causing people severe fatigue, drowsiness, and lethargy. It makes it so people can barely move and do anything so much so that they are bedridden for weeks. Russia is next, a virus spreads causing people extreme Irritable Bowel Syndrome so unbearable that people alternate between severe week-long constipation and diarrhea so bad folks stay in the bathroom all day. Mexico fares the same, a bacterial infection that spreads through bodily fluids causes skin to calcify, and joints to lock up, creepingly absorbing muscle into bone tissues, slowly but surely. And Africa, at last, coming to grips with a fungal infection that wreaks havoc on the nervous system, said infection causing neural decay at a slow pace. These afflictions spread through the liquids, the air, and other people, even animals. New diseases appear quickly and they either vanish after killing the available victims only to pop up somewhere else after mutating into something else, leaving scientists sputtering in trying to quarantine and study them enough to make vaccines for them. Over time these diseases get more complex and odd, Bonesaw would have her hands full trying to understand them and a Tier 2 Biotinker is going to have problems as well. Welp, I hope you're an introvert who likes locking themselves in their house for months on end, cause going outside becomes a rarity, except for the occasional supply run. Pack your gas mask, zip up your hazmat suits, and clean everything a dozen times over cause you’ll need to be very careful. And be careful of your fellow man too, they are a disease on to themselves. Oh! And under no circumstance, do not go to Australia. Something is happening over and no one knows what.
objects.title: The Omega Variants

objects.text:
The Earth Bet medical authorities have noticed a new mental disorder, and after years of study, it has been given a name: Yandere Syndrome.

It is a chronic syndrome that usually is present from birth but only shows symptoms later in life, usually in the late teens, but some sufferers have been known to only start showing symptoms in their 30s and 40s.

The symptoms themselve of Yandere Syndrome include increased muscle density, enough to allow an ordinary-looking girl to be on par in strength with professional athletes such as Mike Tyson. This changed physiology will also greatly synchronize with a large variety of Brute powers. Beyond the physical symptoms, there are behavioral symptoms as well, such as possessiveness, obsessiveness, and over-protectiveness of a single target of their affection, as well as paranoia and delusions of infidelity from their target.

Yanderes make up 5%-20% of Earth Bet’s population. You may choose the gender demographics of the sufferers of Yandere Syndrome, anywhere from all male to all female and everywhere in between. You may also be able to decide if a Yandere’s obsession and affection for their target is solely romantic in nature or extends to familial love, friendly love, or any other kind of love.
objects.title: Yandere Syndrome

objects.text: Something has gone wrong. Yandere Syndrome was a genetic disease. Just a quirk of genetics. Now it's more, it's contagious. Now the majority of the population are susceptible to being yanderes, and only a small percentage of the population are naturally immune. There is no rhyme or reason to who is immune, no link to exploit and make a cure or at least a vaccine. You may choose how much of the population is yandere, ranging from 50% to 90%, with the remainder being the immune. Be warned that the higher the percentage of people are yanderes the more likely violence will break out between them.
objects.title: Yandere Plague

objects.text:
In 1947, Albert Einstein convinced President Harry Truman to found a town that would be a scientific haven where the brightest minds could do their research in absolute secrecy. Formed originally as Camp Eureka, for decades Eureka was the foremost location in the world for cutting edge scientific research. 

But with the discovery of a Golden Man floating above the Atlantic Ocean, and the advent of parahumanity change was inevitable. Revealed to the world by the intrusive meddling of various Tinkers and Thinkers, Eureka rapidly evolved itself to adjust to it’s new place in the spotlight becoming the center of research for Parahuman Science.

Eureka is a specialized location within the United States for the testing of ‘Super Powers’ of all forms, while many regions have their own localized form of power testing, it’s here in Eureka that the top most level of powers are tested, analyzed, and rated. From artillery ranges capable of testing high-tier blasters, advanced laboratories filled with materials for Tinkers, if a power needs tested Eureka has a place and way to test it.

But Eureka hasn’t forgotten it’s roots as the world’s top scientific research facility, many of humanities brightest minds reside within this isolated small town. Each brilliant in their own ways or fields, one of the crowning achievements of Eureka has been it’s success in reverse-engineering Tinker-technology. While not always successful, the Eureka scientists have made great strides in recreating many Tinker creations, including the nearly ubiquitous PRT Containment Foam as perhaps it’s greatest success.

Oddly while this quiet little town has it’s share of disasters due to the sheer concentration of Tinkers and other geniuses, the big one’s the Endbringers, and the Slaughterhouse 9 among others seem to pass it by. Whatever the reason may be with Eureka’s inclusion in the Parahuman landscape, greater understanding of Parahuman powers and abilities, and greater advancement of technology are the result.

<small>Note: In worlds without Parahumans, this town and it’s genius population will either study the equivalent powers, or simply push the boundaries of science once more.</small>
objects.title: A Town Called Eureka

objects.text: Gary, Indiana - Q1; Freedom, California - Q2; Eagleton, Tennessee - Q3; Elisburg, New York - Q4; Flint, Michigan - Q5; Gallup, New Mexico - Q6; Madison, Wisconsin - Q7—these seven towns or cities were the original quarantine zones maintained by the United States at the start of Worm. Now, Brockton Bay has the unfortunate honor of becoming the eighth. Whether through an Endbringer attack, escalating Parahuman violence, a natural catastrophe, or something else entirely, Brockton Bay has fallen into chaos—The government has officially announced their inability to control the situation, and thus declared Brockton a new Quarantine site, Q8 a lawless zone where the U.S. government has all but abandoned control, leaving behind a land of warlords and anarchy. Various Parahuman organizations stake claim to this shattered territory, while its citizens—either too poor or too stubborn to flee—are caught in the crossfire. The PRT and Protectorate have withdrawn, to now man the various checkpoints and defences, albeit with some elements going rogue in a desperate attempt to save the people of the Bay. You arrive at the dawn of this chaos, when social order is unraveling. In this brutal landscape, chaos can be a ladder—for those with the skill, luck, and ruthlessness to climb it. The question is: can you rise fast enough to survive? Note: If you start somewhere that’s not Brockton Bay, you can choose to have this apply there instead if you wish.
objects.title: No Man's Land: Brockton Bay

objects.text:
Humanity, no, everything living has simply just vanished. Perhaps it was due to their unique biology, but Shards and Entities didn't disappear. But every other living creature from Humans to Bacteria simply disappeared.

If Eden is still dead, then it's because she was a distracted driver and crashed horribly in some freak accident.
objects.title: All Living Beings Just Vanished One Day

addons.text:
An unknown catastrophe, born in your world, has spread across the entire local multiverse, erasing not only all living beings but also the very concepts of time and space. Time no longer moves, and motion itself has become impossible. Everything, from the tiniest particles to the largest galaxies, is frozen in absolute stillness. Light has ceased to travel, stars remain suspended mid-collapse, and even entropy no longer moves.

And yet, for some inexplicable reason, you remain untouched by this disaster. You are the only one capable of moving through this frozen world, seeing what no longer emits photons, touching objects with which you can no longer truly interact. Everything that once was is now nothing more than an immutable monument to the past—a lingering echo of infinite possibilities that will never come to be.

You are alone in this endless, unchanging void of reality. And all that remains is the realization that the end has already come.
addons.title: Dead Reality

addons.text:
Few in this dead world still "live," if they can even call it that. At the moment of their death, they fell through time—only to land in a world where time no longer moves. Their bodies are trapped in the moment of their death—wounds never close, lungs never fill, pain never fades. A drowned man will always choke on phantom water, a burned woman will forever feel the fire’s touch. Time should have taken them, but instead, it left them stranded in endless suffering.  

Their own existence fights against the frozen world. Their hearts beat erratically, their senses blur and distort, and their bodies refuse to change. Hunger gnaws at them but never kills, exhaustion crushes them but never grants rest. Their nerves misfire, making them feel injuries long after they happen, a cruel echo of pain that never stops repeating.  

And yet, they still move. A walking corpse that cannot heal. A dying soul that cannot rest. They roam through empty streets and silent ruins, carrying their agony with them—remnants of a time long gone, trapped in a world that has already ended.
addons.title: The Perpetual Dying

addons.text:
Time has collapsed, and with it, history has shattered into fragments, scattered across the world like broken glass. In certain places—where the weight of the past was heaviest—singularities form, pulling moments from history into the present. Streets shift without warning, revealing cobbled roads that lead into ancient markets where ghostly merchants haggle over wares that no longer exist. A stretch of desert becomes a battlefield, where spectral soldiers clash with weapons that leave no wounds, forever trapped in the final moments of their forgotten war.

Yet, nothing here is truly alive. The figures that emerge from the past are not people, but echoes, reflections of those who once were, acting out their lives without ever realizing that time has abandoned them. They speak, they move, they go through their motions as if nothing has changed—but if you reach out, your hand passes through them like mist. A queen might sit upon her throne, staring into eternity with unseeing eyes. A scholar might endlessly rewrite the same passage, unaware that the ink never dries.

These places are static dioramas of history, where moments replay but never progress. A knight eternally raises his sword to strike, but the blow never lands. A scientist holds a discovery in trembling hands, but the words never leave his lips. Some of these echoes seem aware, their eyes flickering with something like recognition, but they can never break free from the loops they are caught in.
addons.title: The Museum of Echoes

objects.text:
An unknown catastrophe that erase out all living beings, and with them, also erase the very flow of time. Despite its name, the end of time doesn’t mean everything has stopped completely. Time still moves, but it no longer progresses, the world is stuck in a strange stasis where things happen, but nothing really changes.

Day turns to night, rain falls and stops, but the seasons never shift. Snow might fall, but it will never melt. Flowers might bloom, but they will never wither. Rivers still flow, but their banks never erode. Metal doesn’t rust, and buildings stand untouched forever, because the force that once pushed everything forward is gone.

In this world, food never spoils, clothes never wear out, wood never rots, electricity never runs out, and ashes never scatter in the wind. Everything stays frozen in place, stuck in a moment that leads neither to the future nor the past.

And in this world, where life has long since vanished, only the memory of time remains—time that no longer moves forward.

This catastrophe didn’t just affect your planet, it's wiped out time across the entire your universe.
objects.title: End of The Time

addons.text:
The world shattered into islands when Scion arrived, forcing humanity to adapt to a sea-dominated existence. The upheaval also awakened an ancient deep-sea civilization, physically superior and armed with advanced biotechnology. Their alien way of thinking defies human understanding, and their emergence is marked by hostility. They seek to reclaim the oceans, viewing humanity as intruders or irrelevant.

The seas are chaotic and dangerous. Rising water levels, aggressive marine life controlled by the underwater civilization, and unpredictable currents threaten survival. Pirates exploit the turmoil, while island settlements face attacks from both raiders and the hostile forces from the deep.
addons.title: Shattered Depths

addons.text: The drastic shifts in climate coupled with the world's landmasses breaking up into countless islands has led to odd results in some islands. While the majority islands will eventually stabilize in accord with humanity's scientific understanding, some islands will end up with anomalous climates, locked in a single season and with ecosystems not in line with their latitudes, such as tropical jungles or even Sahara-esque desert islands locked in eternal summer in the arctic circle, or ice-covered winter islands on the equator. The sea is not spared either, with powerful storms and even hurricanes raging across the oceans far more frequently, though most never make landfall.
addons.title: Island Climate

addons.text: With the global upheavals of heaven and earth the mutating effects have spread beyond flora and fauna, with the weather itself defying scientific understanding on certain islands, resulting in phenomena such as lightning falling like rain or wind solid enough to run on. The oceans too experiences inexplicable phenomena, such as reverse waterfalls leading to pockets of reverted gravity where ships sail upside down, or currents that lift themselves above the waves like giant serpents of water. These phenomena are not permanent and while making sea-travel more difficult and dangerous, are not enough to prevent sea culture from growing dominant across the world.
addons.title: Bizarre Climate

objects.text: When Scion arrived, the world experienced incredible upheaval. Enormous chunks of land broke off, creating islands all over the world. After a year, the world had stabilized, with sea culture becoming a more significant aspect to the world. Pirates and other maritime groups thrived in this new world, even with the threat of Leviathan nearby.
objects.title: Island Earth

objects.text:
When Scion's arrival illuminated the world with a golden light, all technology instantly became obsolete. Despite efforts to restore or replicate mundane devices, the process only yielded errors and malfunctions. The only functioning technology in this world is Tinkertech.

(Any technology that isn't tinkertech and beyond Cold weapons will not be able to function. This will not effect any Shardless technology)
objects.title: Stone Age

objects.text: The most shocking event in human history would be the birth of Parahumans, but the second would definitely be the abrupt alien invaders that began terrorizing the planet. They are extremely advanced and hellbent on something that Humanity has barely been able to translate called "Purge" whatever that meant. They seemed to hate Parahumans, the only protectors of Humanity, the most for unknown reasons. But they are an extremely hostile alien species that are only barely stopped by super-powered Heroes and Villains.
objects.title: The Alien Invaders

objects.text: A Zombie Apocalypse has started. The world is coming to an end as zombie Parahumans and humans gain a ravenous appetite for human flesh. Zombie Parahumans seem to also be able to use their Shard powers as well.
objects.title: Zombie Plague

addons.text: The Altered are the very prelude for the Destroyer’s coming and subverting and plundering Shards within the Network to subvert the Cycle as another method of its predation wholly.
addons.title: Annihilation

objects.text: The Zombies aren’t your usual zombies but are a prelude to something worse. What could be termed as an infectious invasion, the Altered appearance in Parahumans grows within them a higher propensity for violence and psychotic tendencies, once a group of Altered Trigger/Second Trigger in a Cluster sets off the full brunt of the pandemic. Altereds appear veined and off-putting, bodily proportions seeming wrong to the common view, infecting physically and electronically, being a horrific blend of Necromorphs, Crossed, and the Rage Infection. The Altered communicate and link up with a form of Network, seamlessly sharing information and power expressions to scheme and put people and capes off guard with psychological warfare.
objects.title: The Altered

addons.text: Forget anything about civilization being guaranteed to survive. Those who have powers now not only possess no innate resistance to infection, but they both are guaranteed to keep their powers and are able to use them somewhat effectively. Where before it would always be possible for someone to carve some kind of society out of the chaos, now nowhere is safe. Even in worlds without powers, Super Zombies will show up, giving the Hordes the edge needed to break even the strongest bastions. If you want to make a safe haven for yourself and your people, you must fight with everything you have, because The Tide certainly will. Without your intervention, global civilization will fully collapse within a year at most, and it will never recover, with the survivors being reduced to small groups hiding in temporary shelters at best.
addons.title: The Tide

addons.text: There is no hope. All Zombies are linked in a hive mind, capable of seamless coordination across the entire world. Even the weakest shambler is capable of strategizing, potentially acting as bait for wannabe Zombie hunters before they get ambushed by hidden runners, while the now fully sapient Super Zombies may pretend to be normal humans to sneak into supposed safe havens in order to contaminate their food and drink and will assassinate anyone that the combined Thinker powers of The Tide says may pose a threat to their expansion or are somehow immune to infection. Eventually, no one will be left uninfected, and when the last survivor falls, The Tide will turn its hungry gaze to the stars. Soon, all will be fed to the HuNgeR.
addons.title: The Devouring End

objects.text: No one is quite sure what caused it, whether it was a viral or fungal infection, badly programmed nanomachines, a necromantic curse, a runaway power effect, some exotic radiation, or something stranger. No one is quite sure who did it, whether insane terrorists or villains, a government or corporate conspiracy, alien or interdimensional invaders, an Endbringer or other monster, a cruel god or demon, or just random chance. All the same, the freshly dead have risen as Zombies to consume the living, with anyone bitten by a Zombie turning into one unless the bitten area is immediately amputated or their brain destroyed. Zombies may vary from slow shamblers that vaguely wander without direction to fast runners that actively hunt for prey to even stranger varieties, but all the same they wish for nothing more than to eat human (and other sapient) flesh and add to the Horde. How strong they are beyond that depends on the world they are in, the stronger and better prepared the world in general is, the stronger the infected are to maintain their status as a threat. In a medieval, low- to no-fantasy world most could be shamblers with only the rare runner. In base Worm, there could be Hordes entirely composed of runners, with more special infected with low-tier power-like abilities mixed in as well as the extremely rare Super Zombie with mid- to high-tier powers acting as pseudo-commanders for the Hordes.
