In a massive, very high power setting like Warhammer 40k the Zombies would consume entire star systems, travelling in fleets built by near-sapient Mecha Zombies, every Horde led by a near-Primarch-level Super Zombie, all following the will of a God of HuNgeR. No matter what, life will go on. Cities may be abandoned in favor of smaller, fortified towns, with communication infrastructure and large-scale coordination hard to maintain, but still it will always be possible for civilization to continue in some form, albeit diminished greatly from what it once was. This is helped by the fact that possessing supernatural powers of any kind offers resistance to infection through bites (though they'll still turn if they die like normal). The rarer the type of powers (Quirks, Magic Circuits, Shards, etc.) are and the stronger they are, the greater the resistance, with 100% resistance reached if less than one in a billion possess that type of power, or if your power is in the top 0.001% of power users for that setting. Either way, anyone infected will lose any powers they had in life, though if they become a Super Zombie they may manifest vaguely similar abilities. You can assume any major named characters to be among the survivors, at least enough for the major plot of the setting to still happen in some form, albeit greatly altered to account for Zombies. You may choose exactly when the outbreaks started, maybe the apocalypse has hit its stride right when you arrive, it happened a year ago with the dust finally settling as safe havens have just begun to reach out to others to attempt to form a new government, it happened a generation or two ago with limited international trade starting back up, or Zombies have always existed for as long as civilization has. It will always be possible, albeit extremely difficult and time consuming, for someone to permanently end the Zombie threat once and for all, whether by creating a vaccine for the virus, finding the shutdown code for the nanomachines, performing a ritual to destroy the curse, or just killing the monster/demon/god responsible for reanimating everyone. If you are the one to do so, expect to become one of the most beloved figures in modern history, with even your mortal enemies grudgingly respecting the accomplishment.
objects.title: Z-Day

objects.text:
A snap was heard from across the world, and with it, half the population was wiped from existence. 

You are guaranteed to survive this.
objects.title: The Snap

objects.text:
By some miracle, it had been done. The snap was reversed and everybody who was loss ended up being brought back as if nothing bad had just happened, with them looking like no time had passed since their sudden disappearance. This seems like a good thing, but this also had a ton of unforeseen consequences.

The sudden return of so many people destabilizes a lot of stuff since the world had adapted with that massive loss. A lot of these blipped folks find themselves traumatized and displaced, lost in a world which moved on without them. Not to mention the resource issue this would cause as there's a sudden influx of returning mouths to feed.

What is there to expect in a world once again shaken by a seemingly miraculous event?
objects.title: Reverse Snap

objects.text:
It's an unknown phenomenon, but when certain people undergo immense stress they simply disappear. The chances of this seem to grow exponentially if they were hit by a truck.

It was only through the reveal of an Otherworld with a Teleportation Cheat that Humanity was able to learn that the people who disappeared were Isekai'd to one of the many fantasy worlds. Every Earth has its own Isekai world connected to it.
objects.title: Isekai'd

objects.text:
It looks like the world-transferring phenomenon isn’t exclusive to the people of Earth, as people from the many fantasy worlds are also being Isekai’d to Earth. A person's chance of being Isekai returning to earth is also greatly improved. 

Both natives of the fantasy world coming to Earth and returnees of Earth who have learned the power of the fantasy world will have Shardless powers.
objects.title: Reverse Isekai

objects.text: It’s not just any characters that will be appearing, it will be main characters from fictional settings you are familiar with.
objects.title: Pure Fantasy

objects.text: In a chilling turn of events, String Theory has succeeded in her ominous threats. With the devastating capabilities of her F Drive, she has annihilated the moon, reducing it to an irreversible debris field. The world now grapples with the aftermath of this cataclysm, facing unprecedented environmental, gravitational, and psychological consequences as the absence of the moon forever alters the night sky and disrupts humanity's existence.
objects.title: Moonshot

objects.text:
The world is changing, in a big way.

A new factor has become a rising issue across the globe, various life forms, including humans, have begun to mutate when exposed to unusual factors like radiation. These mutations take the form of greater size and strength in violation of the square-cube law, and in some cases developing abilities based upon the manner of exposure. Such as 50ft women, building-sized ants, and atomic fire-breathing skyscraper-sized lizards. These have been dubbed daikaiju.

The daikaiju themselves will often be neutral towards humanity rather than active maliciousness. The greatest danger of most daikaiju comes from them simply attempting to live and survive, yet being far too big and strong for those around them. Such as a fishing ship accidentally being dragged under by an aquatic daikaiju that went after the fish in its nets.

As time passes the number of daikaiju will grow, and in response so will technology. Allowing for in a year or two to go from modern armaments to anti-daikaiju mechas.
objects.title: Age of Daikaiju

objects.text:
Something strange is happening—random people are awakening as the very characters they once created in games. From RPGs to strategy and simulation games, as long as a game allowed for character customization, there is a chance that its players might suddenly find themselves transformed into their virtual alter egos.

These transformations don’t follow a clear pattern. Some awaken as their main accounts, becoming the powerful avatars they’ve spent years perfecting. Others find themselves inhabiting long-forgotten sub-accounts or alternate characters they barely used. Strangest of all, some people are reborn as characters from games they haven’t touched in years, forced to navigate the world with abilities, mechanics, and even appearances they no longer remember. Roughly 10% of humanity has awakened as their virtual avatars.

They don’t just take on their characters’ appearances—they fully inherit their abilities, skills, and even the unique logic of the game they came from. Whether it’s casting spells through mana mechanics, leveling up through experience points, or even respawning upon death, the rules of their respective games begin to override reality itself. Some awaken as powerful heroes, others as monstrous beings, while a few unlucky ones may find themselves bound by bizarre limitations they once thought were just game mechanics.
objects.title: Realized Avatars

objects.text: Scion's appearance did not mark the dawn of parahumans. It wasn't even noticed. What was, was the very Earth splintering under the world's feet. Heaving, great earthquakes and tsunamis and storms covered the globe- destroying nearly all modern infrastructure and plunging the world into chaos. Satelites fell from the sky as gravity and space bent bizarrely. Precise electronics fried, as a global EMP wrecked modern machinery. Volcanoes erupted, plumes of ash temporarily blotting the sun. While buildings, caves, and the monuments humanity constructed crumbled. Many died during the cataclysm itself, more died in the following years from starvation, banditry, and warlording. Parahumans only becoming apparent in the immediate aftermath. 30 years later- the beginning of Worm- and the world has... somewhat stabilized. Many cities have vanished from the map, those that remain needing to be built up from almost scratch. The human population is much lower, and there is a far greater tendency for farms and small gardens even in cities. Much of the world is cutoff from the rest. The governments did not quite survive the transition. The world is now split up into quasi city-states and settlements, few of which have any form of alliance or unification between them. Communication infrastructure has just started being rebuilt at the encouragement of several tinkers, and the internet once again in its infancy. Gangs, pirates, and bandits are a major issue, as most groups are lead by parahumans. You can decide how connected the world is, depending on how much effort Cauldron has placed into attempting to stabilize the situation. At worst, Brockton Bay and any other city stand on their own, fending off- or submitting to- gangs, bandits, and pirates. At best, there is a loose alliance up and down the east coast using maritime vessels for quicker communication, and a railroad being built. Brockton being one of the cities the PRT- or a variant of such- focused on stabilizing. The Endbringers are still a threat. If you're heading to a world that isn't worm, then the apocalypse above happened sometime 30-50 years ago, and the fallout is still being dealt with.
objects.title: Post Apocalyptic

objects.text:
Maybe it's due to some tinker tech, maybe it's just a quirk in human evolution, or maybe some God is just having a laugh that day, either way, all of humanity have inexplicably shrunk one day.

After the initial horrors of seeing your backyard become the size of a football stadium with horse sized bugs roaming about, folks did end up later adapting. The old, larger world, is still there, but now, folks have to adapt by rebuilding civilization in their now much smaller state. Bug mounts, mushroom houses, etc. This is a potentially interesting environment, as you now traverse a world in the eye view of an ant.

Well, big things do come in small packages as they say.
objects.title: Honey, I Blew Up the World!

objects.text: A pair of great crystalline worms soar through the stars, distributing their colony onto the planet below so they can harvest the data they provide. Three hundred years prior, a great energy being seeded the rise of industry to claim legions of mechanical slaves. Millions of years ago the hives from between dimensions showed apes how to make fire with their hands. The Entities are the latest in a long line of species using humanity to achieve their own goals, and they will not be the last. An endless cavalcade of beings come out of the woodwork one after another after the once dominant being has been disposed of by the native population, publicly or privately. Naturally, this has resulted in a progressively complex ‘web’ of societies dedicated to safeguarding humanity, a web that Cauldron is just the newest string in. If left to their own devices life will always survive, though not unchanged and never unscathed. Scion’s outburst could be considered a moderately damaging end to a ‘reign’, leaving only millions of humans on Earth-Bet but with ample infrastructure and connections ro rebuild, while the KT extinction is a somewhat more dramatic example. After each ‘reign’ you can expect about two to three hundred years before the next, but whether that net reign is a cosmic invader, demonic infiltrator, some kind of esoteric reality contagion, or even stranger is almost impossible to predict. History Does not Repeat, but it always rhymes
objects.title: History Does not Repeat…

objects.text:
A hidden world once thrived in the shadows—unseen, concealed behind a veil of secrecy. Perhaps it was a world of wizards cloaked by magic, a realm of merfolk lurking in the ocean’s depths, or a society of aliens living quietly among us. Regardless, it existed unnoticed. That is, until something changed.

Something monumental occurred—an event so profound, so unmistakably real, that the concealment could no longer hold. Maybe the Mist hiding a realm of deities and demigods finally fell, or perhaps a powerful mutant’s might was inadvertently broadcast on the internet, exposing secrets to the world. Whatever the cause, the masquerade has been shattered, and it cannot be repaired.

This sudden revelation of a secret world isn’t inherently destructive. In fact, it could usher in new opportunities, new solutions to pre-existing problems. But more often than not, it sparks chaos. Laws designed to keep the worlds separate crumble, religious doctrines are challenged, and societal norms are thrown into disarray. Civilization itself can be strained, and the solutions of canon might be rendered obsolete.

You gain the power to choose one of these masquerades—the hidden group, society, or realm—that will be forcibly exposed to the wider world. But beware: the outcomes of such exposure are unpredictable. The revelation could lead to harmony, chaos, or something entirely unforeseen. Proceed with caution, for once the masquerade is broken, there is no return.
objects.title: A Fallen Masquerade

objects.text: What humanity had long feared would happen finally did: the apocalypse. Whether it was World War III, an alien invasion, zombie hordes, a superflu epidemic, meteor storms, robotic uprisings, monster attacks, or something else, it happened... 30 to 50 years ago. Not only that, but humanity did surprisingly well at making it out the other side still alive. Maybe the zombies were a bit too slow and dumb, maybe the aliens never heard of the flu, maybe the world was more conservative with their nukes than the public expected, either way, the apocalypse was surprisingly not as bad as feared. Not only that, but society bounced back within 1-10 years, with the current generation of young adults having grown up in relative safety and comfort in a post-apocalyptic world. Governments reformed, maybe with some differences from their pre-apocalypse forefathers and some shifted borders, but still recognizable, cities refilled, even if some are smaller than they used to be, and international trade and politics are back (almost) like they never left. Even so, the scars remain. PTSD is common in the previous generations, some cities are still empty graveyards, the world is just a bit smaller, mundane technology is a bit behind where it should be (unless it was aliens or something, in which case expect some schizotech), people are more health conscious (if it was a superflu, expect germaphobia to be almost as common as PTSD), and laws are changed to reflect what happened (if it was zombies or monsters, expect near universal gun ownership; if it was meteors or aliens, expect astronomy and space exploration agencies to have a budget of 'yes'). Every time you select this, you may pick one apocalypse, with every additional one leaving more scars and residual damage. If picked 20 times, then society only bounced back a couple of years ago, the population being at most 10% of what it once was. Note: If the apocalypse you chose happens to be the same type as an Apocalypse causing Setting Change you also purchased, you may choose for the two to be related. Perhaps the alien invaders were the scouts for an armada, which then appeared recently, as per The Alien Invaders. Maybe the zombie plague wasn't eradicated thoroughly enough, and mutated into the one found in Z-Day. Maybe China got shafted in the post-World War III negotiations, wants revenge, and started World War IV in The Secret of the Swordfish as a result. You can choose the specifics however you want.
objects.title: Surprisingly Short Apocalypse

objects.text: This will go down as one of the darkest days in the history of Earth Bet. Instead of attacking Canberra, Australia on the 24th of February 2011, the third Endbringer, the Simurgh descended instead upon the District of Columbia, the capital of the United States of America, during the State of the Union address. Though the Protectorate and other allied forces fought valiantly, ultimately the Third Endbringer was successful in her attack, the capital has fallen, the Presidential Line of succession unclear with most—if not all—members of the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches of government dead, or considered compromised. This has lead to mass panic and hysteria across the nation, with some states and groups seeking independence, or power, while others seek to enact their own sense of justice, or settle old scores. The world looks on in horror, as the strongest and most cohesive response to the Endbringer threat proceeds to rip itself apart. Where this ends is anybody's guess, a victorious side placing their own Presidential “puppet” in the Oval Office? Perhaps various states, or groups of states going their own way? An independent Texas, Hawaii, or California? Alaska joining Canada? Or perhaps something even more outlandish as an American Empire?
objects.title: The Second American Civil War

objects.text:
Ancient abandoned massive cities, vaults and megastructures sprawl across your world. These structures have melded into the landscape over the centuries to the point where they are considered natural landmarks. The ruins crumble slowly but are remarkably well-preserved and stable, but collapses are still an ecological danger. Some of their streets, halls and corridors have been partially charted, as well as any wilderness has been. Animals and people have adapted to living in the shadow of these cities.

As far back as anyone can remember, your world’s history and civilization have existed in the shadow of these ruins. Modern cities and towns are built into refurbished towers and plazas of the ruins, and contemporary highways and infrastructure run through their ancient streets.

In the deepest vaults, densest ruins, and tallest structures, lie rogue servitors and nesting monsters, as well as technological artifacts. There are entire economies based around salvaging the shallow ruins for materials, as well as exploring the deep ruins and reverse engineering technologies recovered from their depths.

Who built the ruins is a mystery, but there are many fields of study, myths and stories and conspiracy theories about their creation. As these structures predate known civilization, history as you know it remains largely unchanged. If your setting has any kind of prehistoric precursor civilization you may choose whether they built these ruins or if the ruins predate even them.
objects.title: To Remember A Forgotten Age

objects.text: Whatever world you are going to, whatever threat you are going to face, whatever scale you will need to operate on, this is the first instance of such in that world's history. In Worm, this is the first time the Entities are running their experiment. In Mass Effect, this is the first time the Reapers are moving to wipe out all life. Etcetera etcetera. There are no previous greater civilizations, no ancient highly advanced peoples, no previously sealed threats or second-comings, and nothing in place to help, no dire warnings, or old plans in motion to stop whatever threat is dawning.
objects.title: No Precursors

objects.text:
You know all those stories of someone trying to ‘take over the world’ you see everywhere? Well, needless to say the advent of parahumans led to a number of people to make the attempt. While most never even took over a single city, much less the entire planet, one person or group managed to succeed and actually conquered the whole world, or at least 90+% of it.

Much like Earth Shin is under the rule of Goddess, the whole planet is united under one banner with a Parahuman or a small group of them, no more than a dozen, acting as the undisputed rulers. Their rule is practically speaking uncontested, with any resistance limited either to a handful of territories deemed not worth the effort due to being under the control of an S-Class parahuman, areas too damaged to effectively rule such as by being rendered into nuclear wastelands, or a very small number of holdouts trying to ‘resist’ their rule but are too weak to mount any effective resistance.

You may decide who specifically rules the world, and whether it’s an original villain, a canon character who was more effective or powerful, or even someone introduced by another modifier. Maybe Sleeper was a lot more active and ambitious here, Cauldron snapped under the pressure and went full villain in an attempt to force the world to prepare for the Entity, the 7 Demon Lords didn’t settle for being merely feared, the Human Endbringers decided to become the definitive top dogs, the ‘nobility’ of Parahuman Fiefdoms all answer to a single grand emperor, or some other thing, it’s up to you.

No matter what, they will not take any disobedience lying down. Normal people are little better than slaves to them, the world effectively a police state. Most canon villains either work for them as enforcers in their armies, are on the run due to any number of reasons, or have died. Most canon heroes are trying and failing to lead a resistance against their might, or are enslaved by some means. Any dissidents are either killed, forced to work themselves to death in workcamps, used as material for horrific experiments by the Ruler’s pet Tinkers, or placed in the Birdcage, an inescapable superprison that is ironically enough where people are the most ‘free’ if you can call fighting for your life in a darwinian survival of the fittest pseudo pocket dimension ‘freedom’.

This is just an example of what the world may look like, the exact specifics of what the world is like under their rule is entirely up to you, but no matter what it is very much a dystopia. If you have any sort of powers or other unique traits or abilities, your only options are to submit, fight, or die against an army led by those who took on the entire world and won. Good luck.
objects.title: World in The Palm of Their Hand

objects.text:
It seems as though their conquest wasn’t as thorough as first thought. Now, there are whispers of a group who is fighting back. Not just an ineffective resistance of former heroes, but of an actual effective fighting force who hasn’t been crushed in spite of the regime’s best efforts. Who this group is, whether a group of canon characters who through some means or another found a way to actually fight back, some group introduced by another modifier, or a group of your own creation is up to you.

Assuming no third party interferes to tip the scales either way or flips the board (such as Scion initiating Gold Morning), then the Resistance will fully overthrow the regime and usher in a new era of peace within ten years of your arrival. However, without outside assistance, their fight will have a bloody toll, especially as the ones in charge get more desperate and ruthless in their attempts to stop them, resulting in at least 2/3rds of the Resistance and many millions or even billions of innocents dying as the regime tries to take the world down with them out of pure spite.

If you have Cauldron Membership, then you will be given a recruitment offer by the Resistance within 6 months of your arrival, with your powers, skills, connections, and resources determining your potential position within it, up to and including a leadership position within their inner circle.
objects.title: The Resistance Will Not Fall Tonight!

objects.text:
Seems Truck-kun cast a wide net this time, because congratulations, you’re about to be isekai’d. The good news is you won’t be alone; your entire new hometown is coming with you. One month after arriving in your chosen setting, the Displacement will occur, tearing your new hometown from its foundations and casting it into another yet world; people, buildings, infrastructure, everything. It doesn’t matter if you’ve left your starting location; once that month passes, you’ll be pulled along with it, reunited with your hometown in a place far stranger than the one you first arrived in.

This won’t be a simple transition. The destination is completely random. You might find yourself in a world where dinosaurs never died and megafauna rule unchecked, or one where civilization has long since collapsed, or still lingers in fractured remnants. Perhaps you’ll arrive in a land shaped by countless fallen empires now giving way to a new rise, a planet where life communicates through radio waves, or a realm steeped in magic and myth.

You and your town will remain in this new world for at least six years, enduring whatever challenges it presents until an opportunity arises to return to your chosen original setting along with the town and everyone/everything in it. When that moment comes, you may choose to return to the exact instant you all left, or to a later point in time, so long as at least six years have passed.

Wherever you end up will be some variant of Earth, habitable, but not necessarily safe. Survival will depend on you and the people around you. Will your community unite and adapt, or fracture under fear and uncertainty as this new world presses in on all sides? In the end, you will have to decide who you are in the face of it all; a leader or a follower, or else this new world will choose for you.
objects.title: Displaced Hometown

objects.text:
Normally, when you and your town are displaced, your destination is a completely random variant of Earth, offering no warning or control over where you’ll end up.

That still holds true, you still can't choose the world you go to, but you can now nudge the outcome. Select up to two defining terms, and the Displacement will bias toward a world that reflects them in some meaningful way. 

These terms won’t dictate the world outright, but they will shape its nature and increase the likelihood of certain themes. Choose “Technology” and “Apocalypse,” and you might arrive in a world where runaway innovation leads to collapse, or one where advanced systems are all that keep scattered survivors alive. Choose “Whimsical” and “Crooked,” and you may find yourself in a setting that blends dark, twisted realities with flashes of strange wonder. 

The world you enter will not be crafted for you; it will have its own history, its own logic, and its own dangers, but these terms give you a way to anticipate the kind of place you’re being thrown into, even if you can never fully prepare for it.
objects.title: Not So Displaced Hometown

objects.text: We can make a religion out of this. There's a little something wrong with humanity here. Many people now have a tendency to start and join cults of various stripes. Most benign. Far too many with power. Whether that power be from outside entities, supernatural rituals, communal magic, or economic or political weight. Their devotion to their cult of choice tends to be far stronger than would normally be expected, often to the point of completely compromising their morals in favor of zeal. Thankfully, cults tend to remain low-key and beneath the surface of society... Until they suddenly aren't. Usually erupting into violent conflict, sacrificial rituals, or in the culminations of conspiracies. Many times all three. Usually stopped by sheer chance, intervention, interference from other cults, or incompetence of some stripe. However, it doesn't change the danger and destruction left in their wake. Nor does it stop several from trying manipulate things behind the scenes and participating in shadow wars. Larger cults tend to naturally splinter over time, with most cults remaining relatively small. A normal cult can have anywhere from seven to a couple hundred members. Though, super cults with thousands of members do exist and arise from time to time. Those who make or join cults have a far higher likelihood of finding or creating supernatural or near-supernatural techniques and practices with tangible effects. The more potent the world, the more dramatic these abilities can become.
objects.title: Cults, Cults, and More Cults!

objects.text: Something happened. We all know that. But no one quite sure knows what. All that remains is the absence. One day, everyone—as far as is known—woke up. Every single one with amnesia. Unsure of their names. Unknowing of who they were. Unknowing of where they've been, or where they are. Failing to recognize their homes, their families, or their friends. Bodies functioning on partial muscle memory and half remembered skills and language. All the while surrounded by what once was, barely able to recall the various objects surrounding them even are. Everyone simply forgot. People forgot themselves. People forgot each other. Forgot their pets. Forgot names. Forgot faces. Forgot histories. No one remembers who they are, nor who anyone else is. Not their ideals. Their dreams. Their hopes. Their loves. All is gone. It has only been a couple months since this event by the time you appear. The world has not handled it well. Social order has collapsed. Mental illness runs rampant. Paranoia abounds. People fall to madness and savagery and cults and tribes. Many have died of starvation and violence. The world over, the population has dropped precariously. Every single city has become a husk of what it was. Bodies piled high. Carrion left out for the scavengers. Few sanctuaries remain, cobbled together by individuals as unsteady bulwarks against the madness.
objects.title: The Fugue

objects.text: Cosmologically Enforced Social Distancing. Cities do not exist in the world you are going to. There is a limit to how many beings can live within a certain radius of each other before consequences start accruing, and it is worse the more intelligent the population in question. These consequences range the gamut from physical to mental diseases in more mundane settings, to more esoteric calamities and diseases in more supernatural ones. People almost always have an instinctive aversion to places with large groups, and avoid them where possible. The largest stable populations of sentients you'll find are the size of small towns, generally spread out from one another. In certain circumstances temporary populations can rise higher, such as armies in wartimes. But none of them stick for long. This has had extensive effects on the state of the world and history. For one, the population of the world itself is lower. Technology is often slower to spread, but common technical know-how is high. Mass production is rare, and self sufficiency is generally expected of individuals. Wars are less common, but still around and a problem even if fought with far less people. Persecution of different traits, beliefs, and features can vary wildly between even nearby communities. Wanderers and nomads are far more common, and the wilds are often less tamed. Despite all that, the technological level of the world you are going to is roughly on par with modern day, though the actual expression of it may be very different due to the rarity of mass production. Whether cultures are similar or not is up to author fiat.
objects.title: Population Deconcentration
Urbanization
objects.text:
Whether for reasons of environment, social pressures, or culture, society in this world has developed around independent city states, rather than consolidating or absorbing into larger nation states. In fact, most of the human population is concentrated into several hundred large, dense urban cores. Major cities may be surrounded by a few smaller cities, several towns and villages, and agricultural areas. However, they do not tend to expand their claimed borders beyond their immediate area.

City states tend to share and exchange culture and language with their neighbors, but each one still has its own identity. City states are not isolationist, and tend to form alliances and loose confederations for political and strategic purposes, but these never become larger nations. Even militaristic and imperialist city states keep their conquests as semi-autonomous vassals, rather than fully absorbing them. Trade is very common, with cities taking in goods and people from across the world.

However, the areas between city states and their territories are almost completely undeveloped wilderness. Long highways connect cities across the world, but inhabited stops between them are sparse. Nobody settles these wilds, aside from outposts, outlaws, and the occasional small independent city. Freighters that carry goods and people between cities, whether through land, air, or sea, are large and rugged for long trips. Nomadic peoples also live on these roads, traveling in caravans that themselves resemble moving cities.

Technology and society has advanced as it normally would, with ideas and inventions being disseminated over trade. Cities are layered over several thousand years of history, with futuristic skyscrapers rising over industrial-era blocks, and castle walls and tribal longhouses either preserved in heritage districts, or buried through several underlayers. These urban areas are industrially self-sufficient, containing all the manufacturing and agricultural areas needed to sustain the city, as well as to trade and export goods to other cities.

objects.title: Population Boom
objects.text:
This modification dramatically increases the population of the world, creating a much more crowded and heavily populated civilization.

The massive population places considerable pressure on the world’s infrastructure and resources. Housing becomes difficult to obtain, food production struggles to keep up with demand, and clean drinking water becomes increasingly valuable. Healthcare systems, medicine, sanitation, transportation, electricity, and other essential services are similarly strained by the sheer number of people who require them.

For many ordinary people, this results in a significant decline in their quality of life. Large portions of the population live in overcrowded slums and impoverished neighborhoods where housing is cramped, sanitation is poor, and access to clean water, food, medicine, and healthcare can be unreliable. Some people may struggle simply to obtain the basic necessities required to survive.

At the same time, the wealthy and powerful are largely insulated from these problems. Rich individuals, corporations, governments, nobles, and other powerful groups can afford luxurious homes, private healthcare, abundant food and clean water, security, and other comforts. This creates a stark divide between the wealthy elite, who can live in extraordinary luxury, and the average person, who may have to struggle simply to survive.

The world adapts to the larger population as though it has always existed. New families, communities, businesses, cities, cultures, and infrastructure appear as necessary, while existing people are not simply duplicated. The larger population is integrated naturally into the world’s history, demographics, and society.

Note: Purchasing: Each purchase doubles the population.
1 purchase = ×2
2 purchases = ×4
3 purchases = ×8
4 purchases = ×16
And so on. Each additional purchase doubles it again.

objects.title: Unending Cold War
objects.text: In 1982, a golden man—who came to be known as “Scion”—was found floating above the Atlantic Ocean. From then on, the world was forever changed by the advent of parahuman abilities, and the “Age of Superheroes” began. In our timeline, the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991, ending the “Cold War” between the USSR and the United States and its allies. On this version of Earth Bet, however, the influx of parahumans allows the USSR to retain its grip on power and maintain some level of stability. Although it loses any territories beyond the union of fifteen republics, the USSR remains a substantial power on the world stage. The USSR’s response to parahumans parallels Russia’s response in the canon timeline. Parahumans are conscripted into the military or intelligence services, backed by military assets—a dark reflection of the Protectorate and PRT. The USSR has established the Red Gauntlet and Elitnaya Armiya across its territory. After Behemoth destroys Moscow, the capital is relocated to St. Petersburg. Without the dissolution of the USSR, the United States and other nations around the world take a more militarized approach to parahumans. They often deploy them alongside military units or integrate them entirely.

objects.title: Rule Britannia
objects.text: After World War II, the British Empire faced a slow decline as its colonies, dominions, and territories fought for—and achieved—independence. In this world, however, Britain succeeded in preserving some form of its empire through the Britannian Commonwealth. Formed from what would eventually become the Commonwealth realms, the British Overseas Territories, Malta, Barbados, Fiji, and Mauritius, the Britannian Commonwealth consists of more than twenty countries united by a shared head of state. Rather than limiting the PRT and Protectorate to Canada, their reach extends across the entire Britannian Commonwealth. In place of the Guild, there is the Round Table—a homage to the shared British origins of many Commonwealth members. Its superhero knights—and their squires—deploy to respond to international incidents.

objects.title: A Darker Society
objects.text:
The Dark Society's methods to improve parahuman powers through self-mutilation, have become something most parahumans know about.

The process involves crippling a parahuman's ability to use their power, for example, destroying the eyes of a line of sight teleporter. This will cause the parahuman's power to grow and adapt to still be usable, so the teleporter may gain the ability to teleport in a radius. This not only allows them to teleport around obstacles that would have blocked their sight-based teleporting, but also replaces their sight by allowing them to sense obstacles in that radius as they can't teleport into an occupied space.

If the Dark Society already exists, this was probably caused by them and has led to a swell in members, otherwise this will lead to the Dark Society or a group like them forming.

objects.title: Trigger Events Disclosed
objects.text: Somehow, PRT documents about Crisis Points, also known as Trigger Events, have been disclosed to the public, clearing up misinformation about them. The publication of this knowledge has led to countless hospitalizations and deaths, both from people trying to make themselves Trigger and make others Trigger. Despite the majority of these incidents ending in failure, there are enough successes that people continue to try.

rows.title: Event & History Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the History of the setting, and/or ensure the happening of certain events

objects.text:
You are Eden, partner of Scion. You wake up to find your body splattered all over a planed and most of your Shards in complete disarray. The one time you let your partner handle the Cycle to get some rest, he manages to mess up.

The cycle was not supposed to go the way it did and it's now your job to fix it, find your Shards, and knock some sense into Scion.
objects.title: My Space Whale boyfriend is denser than a blackhole

objects.text:
You are Scion, partner of Eden. You wake up to find your partner mysteriously dead. You are now in charge of the Cycle.

The cycle was not supposed to go the way it did and it's now your job to fix it.
objects.title: My Space Whale girlfriend is dead

objects.text:
Scion exists and is just as powerful as ever but he isn’t the avatar of The Warrior Entity, just an exceptionally powerful parahuman who became depressed following the death of his wife.

If Cauldron exists they will be convinced Scion is the avatar of The Warrior.

Unless another modifier changes things The Warrior Entity will still exist they just won’t have such a blatantly obvious target for an avatar. Alternatively you may freely choose a canon Parahuman to replace Scion as The Warrior’s avatar.

If another modifier would affect The Warrior you can choose whether it applies to Scion, or The Warrior, unless it’s a modifier that eliminates The Warrior in which case Scion is immune. Modifiers that logically can only apply to an Entity can’t be applied to Scion, and modifiers such as Genderbend that can affect multiple people can apply to Scion and The Warrior at the same time.
objects.title: False Avatar

objects.text:
When Scion first starts his heroic actions, he find that he actually enjoys heroism and helping people. He retains all his power and abilities.

Scion won't go on a rampage, and cannot be convinced to commit his multiversal genocide. He's still an idiot and doesn't view saving a cat and stopping an Endbringer as any different. Cauldron doesn't know about this shift and will still try to kill him. He is still depressed before 2005, but he is getting better and is no longer depressed by the time of what would be Golden Morning.
objects.title: Scion, Hero of Earth

objects.text: Through some cosmic miracle The Warrior managed to inspire in The Thinker a similar love for humanity as he himself gained and convince her to help him alter the configuration of their cycle and their shard networks for permanent bonding with humanity. This may or may not involve harvesting uninhabited versions of the solar system for resources and setting up a few dyson spheres.
objects.title: Eden, Heroine of Earth

objects.text:
The surviving Entity through some odd chain of events has found themselves emotionally attached to someone.

They could have somehow ended up in a mentor like relationship with someone on Earth, learning and eventually truly befriending them. They could have somehow inexplicably ended up in a romantic relationship, or any number of other connections. 

Regardless of the reasons, circumstances, and relationship, all which can be as vague or as specific as you wish, the entity has an emotional attachment to someone that they now have a vested interest in. 

Understandably, as long as this person is around and healthy, you’re unlikely to worry about a Golden Morning-esque scenario. 

The Entity’s depression will wane over time, eventually going away entirely. You can choose who this attachment is to, the scenario, relationship, and other specifics as you wish, or leave it up entirely to chance. This can be made retroactive.
objects.title: Alien Romantic

objects.text: The Entities aren’t some giant space worms, countless crystalline creatures formed into a greater gestalt and controlled by a single consciousness. Instead, their evolutionary path resulted in a being that looked somewhat similar to humanity, albeit far far more powerful. The Entities’ human avatars are not avatars, but their actual forms. This also makes them drastically more dangerous as they have the full scope of their Entity forms ability available to them. Eden had fallen and crashed the same way as before. Her body was harvested to create powers for Cauldron and its various parahumans, some by creating vials using her cells, some from the original body and others grown in laboratories, some by consumption, some by mixing her DNA with humans, etc. They still have their Cycle as normal, but it takes a much different connotation here, rather than destroying worlds and devouring [Data], they seed worlds here, preparing them for conquest, simultaneously improving the host species by way of introducing their DNA and learning from them while protecting them while also undermining them. Entities can travel alone or in groups, often mating and producing offspring with the host species if they are compatible to help facilitate the process. As Entities evolve their ability to mate with other species is effectively universal, able to incorporate the other species into itself as well as ensuring that every hybrid can eventually inherit the full scope of their parent entities powers and abilities, although the time that takes will vary based on species and their inherent lifespan, and can be shortened significantly with training. Moreover in some cases the influence of the host species actually empowers the hybrids to be more powerful than their parents even before they come into their full power.
objects.title: All Aliens Look Human

objects.text:
The surviving Entity has not only fallen in love, they are in fact and always have been one of Taylor Hebert’s parents. The bond runs deeper than affection: it rewrote biology, redefined family, and reshaped destiny. And Taylor? She is a Hybrid, born of both bloodlines, forged from two worlds. Her physiology hums with dormant potential, a blueprint written in quantum strings and genetic resonance. She might look human—might even feel human—but within her coils the totality of her parent’s power.

And yet, love endures.

Against all odds, the human half of this union sparked something real. Not just attachment, not obsession, but genuine, soul-wrenching love. It didn’t just distract the Entity—it changed them. For the first time, they felt what it meant to have something worth living for, rather than simply surviving. The mission, the Cycle, the endless march of conquest and data collection? Forgotten, at least for now. 

Now however, with Taylor discovering her powers, the Entity has begun to remember its purpose. 

It will attempt to get Taylor to join it, to finish the cycle and continue on to the next.
objects.title: What Will You Have In 500 Years!

objects.text: Turns out in this multiverse the vast majority of Entities including The Warrior and Thinker take on a much more neutral approach when dealing with host species. They still hand out powers and cause conflicts or other situations that provoke creative uses of such powers for gathering [Data], but they don’t wipe out worlds or species across the entirety of the local multiverse at the end of their Cycles.
objects.title: Genocide is inefficient

objects.text: The Entities that came to earth have decided that humans are an interesting and data-rich species, ultimately deciding to forget the cycle and permanently bond with humanity. The cycle will never end, although if Negentropy is never found, the Entities will slowly weaken and die, which can be seen with the number of people with powers lowering every generation. Even then, it is likely that billions of years will pass before the first signs of this happening will appear. This also gives all shards the Pocket Shard perk.
objects.title: Symbiosis

objects.text: Scion and Eden never made Avatars; instead, they controlled the Cycle off world with only their Core Shards. This doesn’t change the plot; Eden still gets killed by Contessa, and Scion is still depressed, but now it’s far more difficult to locate the Entities core shards.
objects.title: No Avatar

objects.text:
Upon confirming The Thinker’s death The Warrior recollected all of his critical important Shards, along with the vast majority of his more superfluous Shards. Then he entered a type of hibernation to wait for another Entity to pass by Earth that he could communicate with, and gets ideas about how to continue his cycle. 

This does not mean that there are no Shard powers on this Earth Bet or the local multiverse, there might even be many Shard powers depending on your other choices. Instead, the vast majority of Parahuman powers come from the Shards of other Entities like Cauldron vials, or natural Thinker Hub triggers like Leet. If you chose Warrior Shard as your power source your Shard is one of the few the Warrior didn’t bother collecting or if it is powerful and valuable he may have left it active to continue some purpose or another.

The Warrior Entity, if left undisturbed, will remain dormant for millennia to come until another entity passes by the galaxy with a solution he can use. If one of your other choices makes other non-hostile Entities be nearby the Warrior may have communicated with them, and traded Shards, and [Data] but was unable to gain a satisfactory method for continuing his cycle, and returned to dormancy.
objects.title: Sleeping Warrior

objects.text:
In this world, Eden's new Shard gained from her interaction with the Wanderer gave her an in-extremis plan to save herself while also improving this cycle in ways she had never thought of before. Her immediate future showed her the one that would be her demise and the demise of her partner eventually and, in a rare moment of spite, she decided to twist that future to her advantage. 

Orchestrating her own "crash", she would wait in ambush for the young Contessa to gain her power before changing her trigger vision into a more... enticing one, ensuring that she would come to her not with fear, but awe. She would supervise the creation of Cauldron, manipulating the entire world through it so that, in the end, the gold morning would be called not an apocalypse, but an ascension.

In more practical terms this means that powers granted by Cauldron vials would be perfectly stable and still "alive", Cauldron would be invulnerable as Eden and Scion would make sure to keep any threat to it contained or destroyed, the Endbringers won't be activated by Eidolon but Eden may have a plan for them and the world will stay quite stable and connected for a longer time than canon.

And, of course, no one will ever be able to save it without outside interference.
objects.title: The Entity behind the Slaughter

addons.text:
Without an entity at the helm, broken triggers are now a more common occurrence at 10% of natural triggers. Those that undergo a broken trigger have a higher chance of becoming a titan. Cauldron vials are the only guaranteed way to become a parahuman without suffering a broken trigger. Without an entity to fight against and plenty of titans to worry about, Cauldron's mission has diverged to instead raise a shard to become an entity loyal to them, fixing the cycle to rid them of titans without destroying any Earths. 

Negentropy is a near guarantee of getting a shard's loyalty.
addons.title: Attack on Titans

objects.text: Somehow, the Warrior crashed alongside the Thinker. Their shards won't know of their deaths immediately, but nearly all noble shards and a few vital shards may have ideas later on of becoming a new entity to fix and lead this broken cycle. Expect titans to appear, as there are no entities to oversee the cycle, though they won't appear to the same extent as the Titanomachy drawback. The drawback Not So Dead After All applies to both the Warrior and Thinker in this scenario.
objects.title: Drunk Driving Ruins Families

objects.text:
The positions of Eden and Scion have been swapped. Scion now crashlanded on a version of Earth to be harvested by Cauldron to be harvested and Eden is now extremely depressed.

Due to some differences in the Entities, there are a lot more Thinkers, Tinkers, and "complicated" powers than Brutes, Breakers, and "basic" powers.
objects.title: Thinker and Warrior Swap

objects.text: Eden was not the only one to have Endbringers, but in Scion's depressed state after the disappearance of his partner, he ordered his Endbringers to connect to humans and gather data, either forgetting that they were his and thinking them to be just normal shards or not wanting to see them due to them being a reminder of Eden. You have to now contend with 20 S-class threats who each possess the powers of one of Scion's Endbringers.
objects.title: Ragnarök

addons.text: Rather than random disconnected points of reality for their graveyards in the hopes of a future Entity collecting it, the Entities devised their graveyards similar to the virtual space they use for shard communications, The Firmament, that they’ve dubbed The Graveyard. Rather than simply acting as a virtual space, the space is real, a subspace virtual dimension where all dead Entities are laid to rest, and from which all other Entities can draw from. As a result of the Supercharge strike, rather than simply being destroyed and cast adrift, all the now gone Entities are now within the graveyard, all their power, their knowledge, everything. This understandably makes the graveyard that much more potent and dangerous. As a bonus, you may also choose whether the Supercharge strike was truly a strike, or whether the Entities had simply naturally died peacefully, thinning out till all that’s left are the Entities at play, if any.
addons.title: Mass Graveyard

addons.text: The Entities have had many grave-worlds throughout their countless eons on the quest for the [ANSWER]. They have also lost at least one it seems. Whether it be by the lineage of entities that would go to the earth graveyard has been rendered extinct, or if the universe or entities have changed so much that any sort of bearing of coordinates or markers are unintelligible. Whether the Thinker and Warrior (and any other entities near the planet) are here on accident, because of what they have detected of the unique nature of the planet, or full rediscovery of an ancient resting place of their kind. In the time since its abandonment, the graveyard has developed a unique and diverse ecology in its energy and data rich environment. The maggot-like creatures swimming in the pools are on their way to becoming something quite like the entities were on their homeworld. Over time more and more tiny cracks and openings are appearing in the graveyard’s security, letting more of the VK fluid out and organisms in. This is the source of the numerous nigh fantastical adaptations and traits found on this planet’s life, massively stronger than would be developed with the corpse of a single Proto-entity. The areas around these cracks are full of such strange and numerous life that it would make rainforests and coral reefs look barren. If taken with Exotic Moon and/or Exotic Neighborhood these openings will be found on other bodies within the solar system. If taken with Exotic Leveling then the meta-energy is a diluted form of the VK fluid, with creatures like the Titans reaching levels of power greater than the endbringers
addons.title: An Overgrown Tomb

objects.text:
It is inevitable that in the Entities’ quest for Negentropy, some of them will die. Whether it be from starvation due to an insufficient energy conservation and generation system for its body after a poor cycle, a run-in with something bigger that wants to eat them, or due to a botched landing. 

Realizing that this may result in a loss of valuable information, the entities formulated a plan to deal with that. They designated specific points in reality to be used as a mix between a library and graveyard. Should an Entity be approaching its final days and not have enough time to create a Cycle, it will head to the designated area to peacefully die in such a way that other entities may access their knowledge to continue the search for negentropy. These spots are not general knowledge, however. To prevent unexpected variables from interfering with the grave, they are both quarantined space and memetically blocked.

Unfortunately for them, one such graveyard has been revealed to be hidden on your earth, with a portal leading to it found deep within a cave system somewhere in Europe. Whether it is because of the machinations of the Wanderer, the death of the Thinker, or the incompetence of the Warrior is unknown. What is known is that it is incredibly valuable, especially to Cauldron.

You see, a massive pool of liquid was found in the grave. This liquid bears a striking resemblance to the contents of a Cauldron Vial. However, this pool of knowledge was made by the Entities themselves to best transfer their knowledge to the next generation. The result is that a vial from this pool of knowledge makes a Cauldron Vial look like an expired vitamin booster.

The powers provided by these Vials of Knowledge, or VKs, are not only more powerful but are not restricted to one dose. Since it was optimized to be taken by Entities, it is possible to gain power from the pool even if you have had a second trigger. This is due to the host’s shard being able to absorb the power and knowledge from the liquid.

Naturally, this is going to be a source of great conflict on whatever earth you end up on, as everybody is going to start making grabs for power. Cauldron has already tried and failed to secure the location because of the entities security systems making both it and any liquid brought out a blindspot and interference from the Three Blasphemies who somehow managed to get empowered by the VKs. This doesn’t even include the reaction the Warrior will have when he discovers the pool. Did I forget to mention that there is more than one portal on the planet, and that some villains may have already drunk from the pool? No, well good luck with that.
objects.title: Entities' Graveyard

objects.text:
The Blasphemies have shifted gears to focus more heavily on the European portal to the graveyard. Using its power, they have expanded their operations, recruiting various parahumans through bribes or force. They have created a league of villainy to help ensure chaos spreads by strategically spreading VKs. The influence of this organization is such that it has become the de facto shadow government across all of Europe. 

Thankfully, both Cauldron and the CUI have managed to stop the spread of their influence. They were able to do this due to the discovery of new smaller portals within their sphere of influence. Cauldron’s portal was found, of course, in a cave system underneath Brockton Bay. There goes the neighborhood.
objects.title: Mimir's Well

objects.text:
In this world, a second pair of Entities arrived at the same time as the Warrior and Thinker. They negotiated a joint cycle and seeded their Shards on other Earths. 

The new Cycle focuses on the interaction between parallel Earths seeded with the various Entities' Shards. The turning point for Earth Bet is the discovery of Professor Haywire, instead of being stopped Cauldron ensures that he is treated as a strategic asset as Bet will have to play its part in the interdimensional scene. While some neighboring dimensions are friendly, others are ruled by empires hell-bent on conquest.

Surprisingly, most major events on Earth Bet remain unchanged (so that you do not have to rewrite the canon entirely).
objects.title: The Neighbors

objects.text:
In this world, instead of Abaddon, the Thinker and the Warrior encountered Apollyon a larger and more hostile entity. It absorbed both becoming even larger and more deadly.

Apollyon's arrival on Earth results in a faster and more deadly cycle, its purpose to discard or repurpose weaker shards. This results in parahumans being half as strong, but four or five times as numerous and hundreds of significantly weaker, but constantly active endbringers

The end of the cycle comes at the same time it did in canon, but its cause is the final collapse of humanity instead. Apollyon has not released any of its stronger shards into the cycle and lacks any abusable psychological weaknesses.
objects.title: The Ancient

objects.text:
The first fourteen individuals to have triggered after the appearance of Archangel Scion and Demon Empress Eden were the Seraphim and the Demon Kings and Queens. The seven Seraphim gathered at the side of the Archangel, while the seven Demon Kings and Queens gathered beneath the Demon Empress.

The two groups began fighting with each other, creating a war between Heaven and Hell. The entire world will be forced to choose a side: the forces of Heaven or the armies of Hell. There is no neutrality for anyone, except for those among the very strongest.

Parahumans will gain powers with either angelic or demonic themes, and their appearances will often transform to reflect them.
objects.title: The War Between Heaven and Hell

addons.text: Your Shard has managed to figure out a more efficient way to generate energy, which will double the effect of the Negentropy perk on your powers while also removing some of the limits on your power and increasing the growth of your power.
addons.title: Negentropy

objects.text:
In this multiverse, the Entities managed to discover the secrets of Negentropy a long time ago; luckily, there is a difference between the Entities you’re familiar with and the Entities in this multiverse. The Entities you’re normally acquainted with care only about getting enough energy so they can reproduce infinitely, while the Entities in this multiverse view themselves as guardians and shepherds who wish to assist other intelligent life forms in reaching the stars. They've also cracked the secrets of Magic, Psionics, and other sources of power you might be aware of. You're not going to be able to deal with the Entities here, considering they are the closest thing to omnipotent that is possible. All I can say is to enjoy your new life.

All Shards have Negentropy and only slightly nudge their hosts to use their powers, and if a parahuman manages to gain enough understanding and mastery of their powers, the shard can gift the powers to the parahuman and permanently disconnect without any harm to the parahuman. Parahumans can possess powers either from the Shard or Shardless section.

(In a nutshell, instead of having to deal with the Entities, you have to merely deal with humans possessing Shardless powers alongside less restricted shard powers).
objects.title: I think I sent you to the wrong multiverse cluster.

objects.text: Normally, when you ‘kill’ an entity, you only kill the guiding intelligence in charge of the overall network, the ‘conscious mind’ of the Entity if you will. This is difficult to achieve but definitely possible, but it does have its repercussions. Without the guiding intelligence in charge, the Network will quarrel over who should succeed them and take over the Network. This might sound like a good thing... but with their focus on trying to climb to the top, there is less focus on making sure that their ‘connections’ to their hosts are actually correct. Leading to broken triggers, and an increase in deaths around triggers. With selecting this choice here, however? That will never be, should you manage to pull off the near impossible and ‘kill’ an entity, the Network will continue along unchanged, with the Shards still making connections to new hosts. It doesn’t fix the overall situation of shards causing problems, but it’ll minimize the damage. And as a bonus? Without 'something' in charge of the Network to give the order, the countless Earths that would have been destroyed to facilitate their departure will continue to exist.
objects.title: Network Stability

objects.text: One of the greatest strengths of the Entities is just how untouchable they are, the forms they craft to wander amongst us being no more than Avatars, puppets to the overarching intelligence a universe away. But now? No more. With this the Avatars of the Entities become instead their greatest weakness. Should you kill the Avatar, the feedback from such an act will render the Entity comatose or brain dead. This doesn’t make the act of actually killing the Avatar any easier, it’ll still be an uphill and almost impossible battle, with the Avatar still possessing all the myriad of powers at its disposal. It just makes actually being able to fight your enemy a little bit easier.
objects.title: Avatar Bound

addons.text: Your shard has figured out a more efficient way to generate energy. This doubles the effect of Negentropy perks on your powers, and loosens or removes some of your limits.
addons.title: Negentropy+

objects.text:
Negentropy wasn't that big of a deal. The Entities solved- stole- the solution pretty quickly eons ago. Then they realized that the likeliest way for them to now die is by being killed. For that reason, the Entities run cycles on lesser species to collect combat [DATA] to improve their own capabilities. Then, at the end of the cycle, they wipe out all instances of the host species to prevent future threats.

This means that every shard has Negentropy, and an even higher focus on combat. Tinkers, Masters and Thinkers are a little more gung-ho, and Panacea might be being pushed a little harder by her Shard. Eidolon isn't running out of energy, and parahumans as a whole have a harder time sitting still. 

Scion, of course, is even more dangerous. Though he'll still hold back in Golden Morning to induce despair in humanity. Eden's corpse is also more dangerous, and now prone to energetic outbursts and quakes.
objects.title: Vicious Cycle

objects.text:
The Entities are an old race, who have repeated and refined their Cycle over 3000 times. The pair who came to Earth and set up their Cycle are examples of Adult Entities, with trillions upon trillions of Shards and massive enough that if they were to exist in only one dimension set they would tear apart stars with their gravity. They have experienced, overcome, and learned from nearly every setback one can imagine. Humanity only survived through a set of circumstances so incredibly unlikely that practically speaking it will never happen again to another set of Entities.

However, what if they were younger? With this modifier, each purchase decreases the overall age and experience of the Entities, resulting in the Cycle itself having begun later on in the universe's lifespan and consequently weakening the Entities as a whole, giving humanity better odds at defeating them. At four purchases, this is one of the first Cycles to have happened and the Entities only number in the low dozens total.

Each purchase lowers the age of the pair on Earth by one stage of development. By default they are considered Adult, having trillions of shards, lots of experience identifying and combatting threats to the Cycle, and being very powerful overall, requiring multiple near unrepeatable miracles in quick succession to be defeated. The stages they are lowered to are Mature at one purchase, then Adolescent, Young, and finally Newborn at four purchases. For comparison, a Newborn would be on their very first Cycle, have only a few hundred thousand to a million shards, and could be conceivably defeated by a mere army of Parahumans in a straight up fight.

This also lowers the Parahuman population due to fewer deployed shards being present, with four purchases having only 10000 or so on Earth Bet, and makes powers overall less complex. All 12 PRT categories would still be present, but they would be cruder and have less variability. For example, Tinkers would more likely be more specialized with more restrictive trees with lower ceilings on how advanced their tech could be, with a Tinker connected to a Newborn Shard being limited to a few decades of advancement. Meanwhile, Brutes would find their powers being more similar to each other as their Shards are less differentiated in abilities, with fewer unique variants of the concept of superstrength and durability to be found.

Please note that even a Newborn Entity is extremely dangerous, as if all else fails they can still detonate the planet to take mankind down with them. It is still an uphill battle to win, but this Modifier does make it more likely. Earth Bet might even come out of Gold Morning still habitable if Scion is a Newborn. Canon will still play out assuming no other modifiers or outside interference, though differences will be noticeable depending on how many purchases you made.
objects.title: Younger Entities

addons.text: While the species as a whole is far older, the Entities that arrive on Earth are no longer of equal development stage. Now one of the entities is younger than the other by however many stages have been purchased in Younger Entities. I.e: If Older Entities is purchased once and Younger Entities purchased twice, the older of the two Endbringers will be at the Ancient stage of development, and the younger will be at the Mature stage of development. Why this is the case is up to author fiat. Maybe one of the Entities is- by their own species' terms- the child of the other, or maybe the younger Entity offers unique capabilities the older wishes to study in return for protection, or some other reason. In the case of having more or fewer than two Entities showing up on Earth; in the case of more, at least one entity will be at the elder age and another at the younger. In the case of a single Entity, it could be that a younger entity found and is digesting the corpse of an older entity, or an older entity hunted but was injured by a younger entity, or something similar. Basically an event resulting in an Entity with the potential abilities and output of an older entity, but crippled in some way. The bigger the difference in ages, the worse the crippling. Entities elsewhere than on Earth are mostly unaffected, but (relatively) younger Entities can now be occasionally be found.
addons.title: Take Your Child to Work Day

objects.text:
The Entities are an old race, who have repeated and refined their Cycle over 3000 times. The pair who came to Earth and set up their Cycle are examples of Adult Entities, with trillions upon trillions of Shards and massive enough that if they were to exist in only one dimension set they would tear apart stars with their gravity. They have experienced, overcome, and learned from nearly every setback one can imagine. Humanity only survived through a set of circumstances so incredibly unlikely that practically speaking it will never happen again to another set of Entities.

However, what if they were older? With this modifier, each purchase increases the overall age and experience of the Entities, resulting in the Cycle itself having begun earlier in the universe's lifespan and consequently strengthening the Entities as a whole, giving humanity even worse odds at defeating them. At two purchases, the Entities are barely younger than the universe itself with quadrillions or more being found all across it.

Each purchase increases the age of the pair on Earth by one stage of development. By default they are considered Adult, having trillions of shards, lots of experience identifying and combatting threats to the Cycle, and being very powerful overall, requiring multiple near unrepeatable miracles in quick succession to be defeated. The stages they are raised to are Elder at one purchase, being a couple magnitudes stronger, or Ancient at two purchases, having an uncountable number of shards spread across multiple star systems.

This also increases the Parahuman population due to more deployed shards being present, with two purchases having tens of millions on Earth Bet alone, and makes powers overall more complex. Powers would be further refined, with greater variability and more unique expressions found. For example, Tinkers would have broader specializations with a higher ceiling on what they can build on average. Meanwhile Brutes with more unique takes on enhanced strength and durability would be found.

Please note that this makes the fight against the Entity even more of an uphill battle than canon, with an Ancient Entity being nearly as hard to kill as those found in Reign of The Entities. While canon will mostly play out as expected assuming no other modifiers or outside interference, albeit with some noticeable differences, Gold Morning would be far more devastating, with a single purchase likely leading to the total collapse of civilization. With two purchases it would end with humanities extinction, at best Scion falling with them at Khepri's hands.
objects.title: Older Entities

objects.text:
Rather than the Thinker and Warrior, completely different Entities have made Earth the target of their cycle. They'll roughly follow the same 'fate' as the initial pairs arrival with one 'dying', but from there their quirks will cause events to play out differently. Maybe with certain powers becoming more common, or with Parahumans having different drives, or clusters and/or triggers working and behaving differently.

Whatever the case, the specifics of the story and even the end result are now unknown.
objects.title: Scrambled Entities

objects.text: Eidolon never activated the Endbringers. They just came online of their own volition and naturally set into their pattern. What this means is that you can't get rid of the Endbringers by giving Eidolon therapy. You'll have to kill all the Endbringers if you want to be rid of them.
objects.title: Endbringers Untethered

addons.title: Transcend Humanity, O' Titan
addons.text:
Endbringers are Parahumans. Specifically, they are Parahumans that have achieved nigh-perfect synchronicity with their powers and shard, and have permanently mentally and physically fused with them.

They are called Titans, and range the gamut of personalities. They retain a semblance of their human selves, however acquire distinctly inhuman and/or divergent thought patterns due to the alien perspective they acquired from their Shard. They are not compelled to attack, or do anything beyond their own whims. But what those whims are can be inscruitable and unpredictable, and with their level of power have calamitous collateral.

<small>Titans similar to those from Ward due to broken Triggers are considered failed and/or corrupted.</small>

objects.text:
Endbringers are no longer unstoppable monsters, but Parahumans who have triggered with a twist. They have a human form or appearance, and they can interact with others normally, except for every three months when they lose control and unleash their destructive powers. This changes how people perceive them, but not how much damage they cause as Endbringers.

Some Endbringers were normal humans before they triggered, while others only have the appearance of being human. They can be talked to, communicated to, and even befriended by some people, but they cannot be reasoned with or stopped when they go on their rampages. They are still driven by a mysterious force that compels them to attack humanity every three months, regardless of their human emotions or connections.
objects.title: Human Endbringers

objects.text: Endbringers now are just normal people who triggered with extremely strong powers. They do not lose control and unleash their destructive powers every 3 months. Note that in power, these parahumans are still equal to Endbringers.
objects.title: Para-Endbringers

addons.text:
Just like their malevolent counterparts, the Guardians have mirror capes too. Unlike the Endbringers, the Guardians are not automatically hostile towards their mirror, in fact they could be considered exceptionally friendly towards them.

If possible, they may even work with them to further their own goals if they align with their main area of focus, such as a Guardian focused on maintaining a healthy environment assisting their mirror in cleaning up an oil spill, or one focused on stopping slavery assisting their own in raiding a human trafficking hotspot. They won't always go out of their way to find and assist their mirrors in this way, but it can be expected to happen at least once a month if their mirror similarly dedicates themselves to their main focus, at most once a year if they only occasionally do such activities.

In addition, their powers synergize in a way that makes them better when working together, allowing them to reach heights they never could alone. A Guardian working with its mirror is almost guaranteed to be able to fight off an Endbringer, even kill it if they receive help from the Endbringer's mirror as well and are particularly lucky.
addons.title: A Guardian's Mirror

addons.text: Just like their more powerful counterparts, the Lesser Endbringers have mirror capes too. In nature and function, they are largely identical to normal mirror capes. The only difference is that the mirror cape of a Lesser Endbringer will have a power that is a high Tier 1 in strength rather than Tier 2. Still, these lesser mirror capes are every bit as useful against their counterpart as a normal mirror is against a major Endbringer.
addons.title: Lesser Reflections

addons.text:
The Shard Network has taken note of the appearance of the foreign invaders known as Endbringers, and some have even begun to see the signs of what they Herald the coming of. In an attempt to better understand and combat this threat, a series of thinker specced shards have scanned the Endbringers as extensively as they can and sent packets containing [DATA] concerning their power expressions to the most closely aligned available shard.

These packets contain overrides from certain Noble shards in charge of defence against potential Threats to the Cycle which both lower the threshold needed for a Trigger Event and override the power in question to make use of the [DATA], resulting in parahumans gaining powers that both match one of the Endbringers while also being able to perform better in general against them for the purpose of combatting this threat.

While this by itself won't stop the ENDBRINGER's eventual arrival, this will slow it down to an extent, allowing for more time to better understand and prepare for combat against it. In addition, while they will still be massively weaker than the ENDBRINGER and are liable to die should they fight it, mirror capes could serve as unique points of study since their powers tap into certain aspects of shard capabilities usually locked during deployment, making them more effective against specific threats.

Since they are adapted to fight the minions of the ENDBRINGER, theoretically data gathered by studying their powers could be used to fashion anti-ENDBRINGER weapons, though their effectiveness depends on their maximum power output and the overall strength of the powers used in their construction. It would be very difficult and a longshot besides, but with the right powers and sufficient resources put into it this could serve as one of the few viable methods of defeating this threat.
addons.title: Network Defense Mechanism

objects.text: Among Parahumans, there are a rare few who stand out not just for the strength of their powers, but for their obvious similarity to the monsters that ravage the world. For each Endbringer that exists, there is a mirror, a lesser, distorted reflection to be found among parahumanity. These mirror capes all possess weaker but still potent powers that are derived from the powersets of their counterparts, though even the weakest mirror cape would still be a Tier 2. For example, the Simurgh's counterpart could have pre/post-cognition centered on herself as opposed to everyone around her, telekinesis with a 30 meter range strong enough to bat Endbringers around with skyscrapers and precise enough to passively cancel the Simurgh's Scream in her range, and short range surface level thought and emotion reading paired with touch telepathy. More than this these capes, while not as capable of wide range devastation as the Endbringers, are immensely powerful in personal combat, enough to go toe-to-toe with their counterparts. When taking to the field, the Endbringer will almost always beeline for their reflection if present, resulting in dramatic clashes. Should the Endbringer win they'd return to their previous objective, their mirror almost always surviving to fight another day. When the cape wins however, the Endbringer almost always retreats, ending the attack then and there. Because of this, mirror capes are considered one of the greatest hopes in the world outside of Scion or the Triumvirate. The majority are highly regarded heroes, and even villainous mirrors are given respect and certain concessions. Should a new Endbringer ever appear, another cape will trigger with powers mirroring their own within a year at most, ensuring that humanity always has a chance against them.
