This modifier by itself adds between ten to twenty years to the estimated lifespan of global civilization. Note: Should you possess Bringer of the End or The End-Becomer, you may choose to have a mirror cape trigger somewhere in the world whose powerset is derived from your personal Endbringer or Endbringer form's powerset. If you have both or possess multiple Endbringers, you can have one cape for each appear.
objects.title: Mirror Capes

addons.text:
The Harbingers will also change into smaller forms when not being made to rampage. 

You may choose whether the forms they take are pets or children (Children are between the ages of eight and fourteen. The fewer there are, the older they appear).

You may choose whether or not the Harbingers are aware of the rampages or if they have blank spots in their memories in place of the rampages.
addons.title: Pint-Sized Annihilators

addons.text:
All of the Simurgh's Harbingers are cats when not rampaging. They all are also just as trolly as she is. They still have scaled-down versions of their powers.

She has twelve of them.

If she is your planned Significant Other, just remember that you wanted this.
addons.title: Cat Lady of the End

addons.text: Just like the Endbringers themselves, their Harbingers also have a propensity for random assaults. The more Harbingers an Endbringer has, the more often one will assault somewhere, with three Harbingers leading to a monthly assault while twelve means weekly. This means that if all three canon Endbringers have twelve Harbingers each, you can expect an assault every other day. Generally only one Harbinger will assault a location at a time, and unlike with an Endbringer they can indeed be fought off without risking an attack. However, if they die during the assault, the next attack will be much worse, with the Endbringer holding back less in proportion to how many Harbingers have died since their last attack. If every Harbinger an Endbringer has is killed during their assaults, then the next attack will at minimum be as devastating as the Sinking of Kyushu.
addons.title: Harbingers Assault

objects.text:
Purchasing this grants each Endbringer between three and twelve minions called "Harbingers". These Harbingers each resemble their Endbringer's theme/appearance and are about a quarter to one-half the size of their Endbringer. They each have the power (Brute) Typhon, as well as weaker versions of their Endbringer's powers, equivalent in strength to the "Lite" powers found in this CYOA, scaled as described below.

The fewer Harbingers an Endbringer has, the stronger each individual Harbinger is. Their individual powers will never fall below a high T1, and will never exceed a high T2, in strength.

During fights, they will always aim to help their Endbringer reach its target. Whether that's accomplished by spreading destruction over a wide area—causing defenders to be spread thin—or by targeting specific parahumans who are particularly problematic, they will always aim to help their Endbringer reach its goal.

Between Endbringer attacks, the Harbingers will recover or be reformed so long as their Endbringer lives. Any given Endbringer will always attack with the same number of Harbingers that they brought during their first attack.

As a result of this, Endbringer attacks have much higher casualty rates, and the targeted locations are far more devastated. However, this also means that Endbringer attacks result in far more triggers than they typically would. Efforts to combat and recover from Endbringer attacks are also elevated.

Should you take "The End-Becomer" or other powers which grant you control of, or allow you to turn into, an Endbringer, you will also gain a number of Harbingers of your choosing.
objects.title: Harbingers of the End

addons.text:
In addition to the normal Guardians, there now exist an equal number of Lesser Guardians. These function much the same as their Lesser Endbringer counterparts, being an order of magnitude weaker than the normal version while having the benefit of being more easily replaced compared to the much more finite regular Guardians, but like Guardians have more heroic prime directives.

Much like Lesser Endbringers, Lesser Guardians lack a core and when they are killed, are replaced with another of their kind. Additionally, the surviving Guardians, both lesser and greater, will adapt in some manner to whatever killed them. However, due to having a different source and subnetwork than the Endbringers, the adaptations do not carry over between the two groups. If someone kills a Lesser Endbringer via dropping a blackhole on them, the Guardians won't be any less vulnerable to spaghettification than normal until one of their own is killed via the same method.

In addition, due to the nature of the Guardians as being more finite than Endbringers, at best having half as many exist as the minimum number of canon Endbringers, Lesser Guardians are replaced at a vastly slower rate, taking over a year for another to appear if one is killed.

Just like normal Guardians, Lesser Guardians will attack Endbringers if they are in the area. Against Lesser Endbringers, they fight the same way their stronger cousins do, but against greater Endbringers they will be much more defensive and evasive, well aware of the power disparity between them. Acting in more of a support role when assisting defenders or focusing on search and rescue and evacuation if their powers are a particularly bad matchup.

However, when a greater Guardian encounters a Lesser Endbringer they don't hold back in fighting them off. The only reason Guardians aren't responsible for half of all Lesser Endbringer deaths being that they are aware it would only make it harder to fight them off in the future.

This counteracts the damage Lesser Endbringers inflict such that civilization will last longer, though not as long as Guardians of Gaia would without them existing. At worst, civilization gets an additional 25 years rather than 50 assuming no other modifiers.
addons.title: Lesser Guardians

objects.text: Now in addition to the regular Endbringers, there now exist a number of Lesser Endbringers at least equal to the number of active Endbringers, with a new one appearing if a new full Endbringer activates or another Lesser Endbringer is terminated. Whenever there is an Endbringer-attack, there is now a 40% chance that a Lesser Endbringer attacks instead of a regular Endbringer. Lesser Endbringers are mostly similar to regular Endbringers, possessing great strength, durability, and a unique power of their own, but do sport a few key differences. One, they are an order of magnitude weaker, and, while still possessing the typical layered body, lack a core, making them easier to drive off and vulnerable to destruction via accumulated damage as opposed to having a singular weakspot. Due to this, though still stronger than any parahuman, a Lesser Endbringer is within the realms of what large groups parahumans working together can destroy. And while most have powers that will make doing so the best option, depending on what power the Lesser Endbringer has it may in some cases be tactically smarter not to do so in order to have a manageable threat fill a slot in the Endbringer-rotation. Overly simplified it can be said that power-wise Lesser Endbringers sit roughly at the halfway-point between regular Endbringers and that of the Harbingers granted by that Modifier. However, while Lesser Endbringers seem like a perfect testbed for anti-Endbringer-tactics, the opposite is very much true as well. Because whenever a Lesser Endbringer is destroyed, all Endbringers and Lesser Endbringers develop a resistance against that method of destruction, anything that's not either simple brute force or an All-or-Nothing-effect like Sting or Scion's Stilling becoming effectively useless after two or three destroyed Lesser Endbringers at most. And while it would take longer, even All-or-Nothing-attacks become less effective with every Lesser Endbringer destroyed by them. In this way, Lesser Endbringers could be described as a by itself rather destructive immunization-system designed to coax out and ultimately nullify maneuvers that may otherwise pose an actual threat to the actual Endbringers, rendering them even more insurmountable.
objects.title: Lesser Endbringers

addons.text:
The Legions now have their commanders... and their Originators. 

Legions do not replace the Endbringers. Rather, they act in their stead. Endbringers themselves rarely attack, instead creating more and more Legionnaires to send out, similar to eusocial insects like ants and bees. Likewise, they no longer randomly wander the world. Instead, they create nest-like areas of alien design, defended by the rest of their Legions with them as the center. 

The Harbingers, in turn, are now Elite units of the Legions, and guards for the Endbringer's nests. More powerful than normal Legionnaires, and far more difficult to combat. On top of such, while each Legion only brings between three to twelve Harbingers on an attack, far more can exist surrounding the Endbringers themselves, making it even more difficult to attack the root of the armies and bring a 'stop' to them. 

Unfortunately for the world, Nukes are not enough to rid them of these nests. They tried.
addons.title: Broodmothers of the Apocalypse

addons.text: We never expected aliens to invade. We also didn't expect them to get along with each other about as well as we did with ourselves. That is; not at all. The Legions of the End of different Endbringers now come into conflict for resources, territory, and occasionally for what seems to be no good reason (Patriotic pride, maybe?). These conflicts can last multiple days, becoming warfronts that more and more members of the Legions arrive to reinforce before breaking off via some alien logic not well understood. While this may seem good for humanity at first, these conflicts have devastating consequences. Twisting and warping local biospheres and terrains into inhospitable locations, wracked by what seems to be lingering traces of each Legion's powers. The Behemoth Legion leaving irradiated hell scapes, the Leviathan Legion leaving storms that never seem to fade, and the Simurgh Legion leaving zones they, despite appearing torn up, look otherwise normal at first, until one realizes that random telekinetic 'shears' hang invisible throughout, and those who stay too long within start getting driven mad by whispers. More and more of the Earth is slowly being consumed by these conflicts, and humanity is now on a timer until the entire world becomes consumed unless they can stop it.
addons.title: Clash of the Endings

addons.text: Just like the Endbringers, the Guardians have been replaced by small armies of empowered beings who share the same fundamental goals. These Brigades function much like the Guardians did, travelling the world performing actions in accordance to their main focus whatever it may be, trading immense power in exchange for being able to act in multiple areas at a time. Generally speaking, these Guardian Brigades will be much more active than their counterparts in the Legions of the End, with a member of a given Brigade always active somewhere in the world, at the cost of being far more spread out. This means that at least one is likely to be present for any given attack by a Legion, with reinforcements quickly summoned, but rarely will any significant numbers be able to manifest before the attack ends. In the rare instances a Brigade manages to fully muster for battle, the tide generally turns in their favor as they do their best to coordinate with local defenders. Overall, these Brigades are humanity's closest ally in the War Against the End, especially as they are far more able to cooperate with other Brigades than Legions are with each other. Should you have Broodmothers of the Apocalypse, the Guardians also exist alongside their Brigades. They will generally stay in their Nests producing more Brigadiers, leaving their task to be completed by them. Their Harbingers are more active, used to address more difficult tasks, such as cleaning major oil spills if their Guardian's focus is environmental health, or deployed as Elite strike forces against enemy Legions. Surprisingly enough, the immediate area around Guardian Nests are a popular place to live for their near guaranteed safety from Legion attacks, and hikes through the Nests are popular, though the Brigades do not let people build homes inside the Nest itself. Should you have Clash of the Endings, then the Guardians are in a near constant state of warfare against the Legions, with multiple fronts across the globe. Unlike inter-Legion conflict, these wars are practically never ending, as the Guardians and the Endbringers refuse to coexist with one another. The main upside is that the Guardian Nests are clearly allied with humanity and thus its best and closest ally against the Legions. Their territory is generally a safe place to live, especially around the Nests themselves, which now host rapid deployment military bases whose sole job is to follow large deployments of Brigades since they almost always are going out to fight Legions. In addition, Brigades frequently reinforce one another or come to the rescue of humans much faster due to their constant state of combat readiness, with some even appearing after battles to 'clean up' power traces. The main downside is that this never ending battle has left several regions near-permanently uninhabitable, with many caught in the crossfire from their war. In addition, Brigades don't work together perfectly due to sharing different hiveminds with different directives; though they do try to communicate with and will assist one another, coordination is imperfect and accidental friendly fire is not uncommon. Occasionally they may even have battles between Brigades, though the low casualties paired with minimum collateral damage and lack of constant warfare has led Thinkers to conclude them as merely mock battles used as training exercises. Overall the war is now far bigger, but at least humanity has a clear and present ally to fight it with.
addons.title: The Guardian Brigade

objects.text: Endbringers are no longer kaiju- single, nigh unstoppable beings of mass destruction- instead, they are Legions. Small armies of individually weaker beings that all share similar powers and aesthetic, with variations between armies, like the Simurgh Legion having the smallest and weakest but most numerous and cooperative monsters, or the Behemoth Legion having the largest, strongest, and most independent monsters, but also the least numerous. While weaker than an actual Endbringer, each 'individual' within a given Legion is within striking range of the most powerful parahumans at a minimum. However, not only are they hive-minded to their fellow Legionnaires, due to such they are capable of working and coordinating with other members of their own Legions nigh seamlessly. They are also capable of combining their powers together for amplified abilities. With an entire Legion's maximum output their powers can exceed the capabilities of an actual Endbringer, at least temporarily. Their durability is not as high as a full Endbringer, and such cooperation can be disrupted. Legions themselves retreat after their objective has been fulfilled, made impossible, or a certain number of their own have been felled. Any felled members shall be replenished by the next strike- though notably, the numbers and individuals within a particular Legion are not consistent. While Legions are overall more dangerous and destructive compared to normal Endbringers, the relative 'weakness' of their individual members has led several to being killed and subsequently studied, providing the world hope and information- even if the former may be poisoned. After all, just like the normal Endbringers, the Legions of the End have been holding back...
objects.title: Legions of the End

objects.text: Instead of Leviathan, Behemoth, and Simurgh there are three other Endbringers instead, with different powers and abilities.
objects.title: Endbringers Scrambled

objects.text:
All the Endbringers awakened alongside Behemoth. While only three are currently present on your starting world, the others now roam the multiverse, leaving devastation in their wake. Each Endbringer has established a "homeworld," focusing their attacks on it and the surrounding worlds. Rarely, they relocate to a new homeworld. Notably, on the dates when Leviathan and Simurgh canonically appeared on Earth Bet, they instead shift their homeworlds to that universe.

The Endbringers have also gained the ability to teleport between universes, making them even more dangerous. They are hyper-aware of interdimensional teleportation near their homeworlds and will hunt down anyone responsible. If you teleport into a universe near an Endbringer's homeworld, you risk drawing their wrath—not only on yourself but also on the city where you arrive.

The only truly safe way to traverse the multiverse now is to travel shortly after an Endbringer has attacked or to avoid their homeworlds and the surrounding regions entirely. Every jump between universes has become a high-stakes gamble, with the looming threat of an Endbringer’s destruction always hanging over you.
objects.title: Interdimensional Endbringers

addons.text:
The Endbringers’ failsafes have transformed. Upon their destruction, they no longer unleash simple energy explosions. Instead, their deaths trigger catastrophic wide ranging Death Curses. These Curses are just as destructive as the explosions they replace, but far more unpredictable and dangerous.

Each Endbringer’s Death Curse reshapes entire regions or worlds in ways that reflect its core identity. Behemoth’s death might cause the ground to split open, unleashing permanent volcanic eruptions and choking the atmosphere with ash, plunging the world into a volcanic winter. Leviathan’s death could drown continents in unending floods, transforming the land into endless oceans battered by eternal storms. Simurgh’s death might leave behind a telepathic field that drives instantly survivors to madness, twisting entire societies into roving bands of murderers.

Unlike the simple energy blasts these Death Curses have replaced they often cannot be contained or mitigated. Killing an Endbringer has become a gamble that risks dooming not just a city or nation, but entire worlds.
addons.title: Endbringer Death Curse

addons.text:
The death of an Endbringer now extends beyond the physical realm, corrupting the fabric of the afterlife. When an Endbringer dies, the death curse ripple outward, destabilizing not just the mortal world but the spiritual and divine realms tied to it. Each death carries the potential to upend the balance of entire realities. 

Behemoth’s destruction might ignite Ragnarok, spelling the end of a pantheon and plunging its worshippers into despair as their gods perish. Leviathan’s demise could to the end of the river styx, drowning the souls of the dead in an eternal, unending tide. Simurgh’s death might unravel the threads of prophecy across multiple realities, leaving a void of uncertainty where fate once guided civilizations.

The danger grows exponentially if Endbringers are killed too close to one another, either spatially or temporally. The cumulative effects of multiple deaths could destabilize the underlying mythological order of the local multiverse, severing the connection between realms of the living and the dead, erasing divine influence, or collapsing entire cosmic orders that holds the multiverse together. Even the gods may intervene, or flee, in the face of such catastrophic consequences.
addons.title: Mythical Collapse

objects.text:
The Endbringers are now equipped with devastating failsafes triggered upon their destruction. If an Endbringer’s Core sustains too much damage—resulting in its death—a failsafe activates, releasing the entirety of the Endbringer’s energy capability into real space in a single, catastrophic explosion. The resulting blast is powerful enough to obliterate entire continents and plunge the planet into a global nuclear winter.

However, these explosions are purely energy-based explosions, free of esoteric effects. This means that, in theory, they can be contained, redirected, or countered—provided you possess the power to rival or surpass that of the Endbringer itself.
objects.title: Endbringer Failsafes

objects.text:
Normally the Endbringers attack in a predictable order, taking turns and waiting for the others to have attacked once before they do so again. This regularity, while dreadful, does allow a measure of preparation, of narrowing down targets and readying specialized countermeasures against the next enemy.

Now however, that regularity is no more. Instead of following a predictable cycle, now every time an Endbringer attacks all active Endbringers have an equal chance of being the one chosen to engage a target. If Behemoth, Leviathan and the Simurgh are the only currently active Endbringers then each will have a 1 in 3 chance of attacking. If Khonsu, Tohu and Bohu are activated without Behemoth or another Endbringer being destroyed they will each have a 1 in 5 chance of being the attacker as Bohu and Tohu will still attack together as a unit.

This has no impact on the frequency of the attacks, one happening every three months unless another Modifier is chosen, only on who carries out the attack when the time comes.

Since now the attacking Endbringer is a matter of pure chance this can lead to outcomes like a particular Endbringer attacking three times in a row and then not attacking at all the next eight cycles, robbing the defenders of any chance of predicting what will hit them next time.

Each attack is now a roll of the dice, and the odds are not in mankind's favor.
objects.title: Randomized Attack Cycle

objects.text:
The Conflict Engines have deviated from their canon schedule. Instead of striking every three months, Endbringers now attack at least once per month.

This relentless onslaught has pushed humanity to its absolute limits. With little time to recover between assaults, nations and organizations are in a constant state of crisis. Infrastructure is destroyed faster than it can be rebuilt, economies teeter on the edge of collapse, and relief efforts are virtually nonexistent in the face of the unending destruction. Governments, heroes, and even villains are forced to operate under extreme pressure, their resources stretched thinner with each passing battle.

Even the shards have adapted, reinforcing the stability and durability of Tinker-tech to ensure both their hosts and their influence remain relevant in an era of constant warfare. Once-fragile prototypes now endure repeated use, allowing advanced technology to remain widespread and effective despite the relentless attrition.

The only silver lining is the rapid acceleration of innovation and militarization. Tinker-tech advancements, military recruitment, and international cooperation have all surged as humanity struggles to keep up. Continuous combat experience has forged defenders into hardened veterans, their skills honed through necessity rather than choice. There is no room for complacency—every nation, every hero, and every scientist knows the next attack is always just around the corner.

Yet, for all their resilience, the toll is undeniable. Burnout among heroes and military forces is rampant, while vital resources dwindle at an unsustainable rate. The world has no choice but to fight, but with each passing year, one question looms ever larger: How much longer can humanity endure?
objects.title: Monthly Endbringer

objects.text:
The Conflict Engines have deviated from their canon schedule. Instead of striking every three months, Endbringers now attack only once per year, with just one appearing each year. Behemoth begins the cycle in 1992, followed by Leviathan in 1996, Simurgh in 2003, Khonsu makes his debut in 2012, with the Twins following in 2013.

This shift to a single annual attack has drastically reshaped the way humanity faces these overwhelming threats. The additional time between appearances has given nations and organizations a much-needed reprieve. With fewer attacks to endure, relief efforts are better coordinated, economies face less strain, and infrastructure has more time to recover. This extra breathing room offers hope to a world that has long been battered by relentless devastation.

The predictable yearly schedule allows humanity to focus on preparation and innovation. Strategists, thinkers, and tinkerers have more time to analyze past battles, develop countermeasures, and strengthen defenses. Military forces and hero organizations can allocate resources more efficiently, conduct longer training cycles, and foster deeper international cooperation. The reduced frequency of destruction ensures that critical resources are not stretched too thin, giving humanity a stronger footing in its ongoing fight for survival.

However, the reduced frequency does not diminish the severity of the threat. Each Endbringer strike remains an unparalleled catastrophe. While the reprieve has provided significant advantages, it has also led to complacency in some areas. The singular, annual attack remains a stark reminder of the power of the Endbringers, ensuring that the world cannot afford to let its guard down entirely.
objects.title: Yearly Endbringer

objects.text:
Rather than attacking at set times on specific targets, the Endbringers once created and announcing themselves proceed to wander the world. Occasionally setting up temporary domains or 'nests' for themselves. Acting almost like wild animals. They still attack, destroy, and ruin anyone who approaches too closely to them or their territories, including cities if they wander across them, but they no longer have actual targets. Instead they act with a degree of freedom. 

They also still hold back somewhat in fights, scaling to the threat they are represented with. This lets them become 'challenges' for the world to test and prove themselves against. Giant monsters wandering the world like living, natural disasters.
objects.title: Wild Endbringers

addons.text: Where before Endbringers would mostly ignore or avoid each other in their wanderings, now they can come into conflict and compete over territory. These clashes are likewise devastating to the surroundings wherever they happen, and the world has a strong inclination to prevent such instances from occurring, lest everyone be caught in the crossfire.
addons.title: Territorial Infringement

objects.text: Individual Endbringers are no longer synced. Instead, each Endbringer has its own cycle time determining when it will attack, ranging and varying anywhere from 5 to 9 months. The upside to this is that the Endbringers do not seem to coordinate their attacks with each other. The downside is it is now possible for multiple Endbringers to attack at once, though generally in separate locations. But it is possible for multiple Endbringers to attack the same target, during which they may or may not coordinate with each other, to the detriment of all the defenders.
objects.title: Independent Attack Cycles

addons.text: The third Endbringer, known as the Simurgh has become intensely Yandere for you. In between her assaults on humanity she cyber stalks you online, particularly on PHO, and offline will go out of her way to use her powers of Telekinesis and Precognition to destroy anyone else she considers you to be “being attacked by” or “betraying her” with. This obsession on the part of the Simurgh will ruin the lives of your friends, family, and many other acquaintances, but gain you the ‘protection’ of a fanatically obsessed Endbringer. I hope you can survive it.
addons.title: Yandere Simmy

objects.text:
The Simurgh transforms into her fandom version, becoming a victim of a master effect created by Eidolon. This effect forces her to attack humanity against her will. In the time between attacks, she spends her days trolling and posting on PHO.
Through her precognition and postcognition, the Simurgh gains sentience, allowing her to develop a sense of self and awareness beyond her programmed purpose.

Alternatively: if you selected Endbringers Untethered then the Simurgh is instead only just gaining sapience and starting to chip her inherent programming. Maybe this is due to a lack of direct oversight from the Entities, or maybe something fundamental is finally breaking down in her core, or something about simulating the human psyche for purposes of terror is causing errors. In any case, she will slowly become somewhat similar to her popular Fanon version overtime.
objects.title: Winged One
Unwilling Endbringers
objects.text:
It turns out that the Simurgh isn’t the only unwilling Endbringer to be forced into destroying humanity.

Behemoth, Leviathan, Tohu and Bohu, Khonsu, and any other Endbringers there might be are all being forced by the directives of Eidolon’s Shard into committing atrocities against mankind. They could all have their own wants and desires, like the Simurgh’s love for PHO, or they could just want to mind their own business and wander about like aimless animals.

Other Endbringer Modifiers could influence how this is expressed, like Alien Endbringers being forced by their own creators into attacking humanity to weaken it for their eventual arrival.

Khonsu, Tohu, and Bohu have been charged. Not only that, but they have been activating since the Simurgh first appeared, with Khonsu debuting in 2006, terrorizing the world since then, and The Twins set to arrive in 2011. You can't stop The Twins from showing up, even if you arrive before them. The Endbringers are also on their Pre-Gold Morning schedule of attacking every two months.
objects.title: The Second Set

objects.text:
Another Endbringer’s been charged, terrorizing Earth Bet alongside his siblings with a necromantic spin. The name handed out to him reflected his methods: Anubis.

Anubis is an emaciated-looking humanoid, his skin marred pitch-black as if being burned to a crisp, adding an air of famine and deathly desolation around him. He stands at 18 meters, and while having a human resemblance or form, just like the Simurgh, he shares little to no similarities with us. Anubis’ resting place resides in the African continent, wandering around the continent’s deserts when standing by.

Anubis possesses the standard layered durability and strength shared by his siblings, along with his unique powers of reanimating the corpses of deceased parahumans he’d killed in current and previous fights. This allows him to control his revenants and their power accordingly to gain relevant information through and from them, such as his revenant’s location, and, potentially, the enemy. Revenants, while slowed by Anubis’ meddling, are still decaying, becoming unusable to the Endbringer at their third attack after collecting their corpses. These revenants, or “Parazombies” as other capes like to call the revenants, join Anubis on his wanderings during his stand-by.

Anubis journeys to his scheduled attack through his revenant’s powers, one or multiple depending on the number of corpses he has at his disposal, meaning the time of his arrival may vary from instant travel to taking hours to reach his destination. Anubis’ battles are divided into two stages: 1. An Anubis without revenant support strikes the parahuman’s main contingent in charge of stopping him while directing his “parazombies” to seek out and cause as many human casualties as possible. 2. After Anubis has taken out enough parahumans to replenish his ranks of lost revenants (the agreed standard being 30, losing around 10 due to decomposition by his upcoming fight), he’ll seek out and assault normal humans while his revenants continue fighting against parahuman forces combating Anubis.

What drives Anubis, that is, his Endbringer directive, is to cause demoralization by inflicting the most loss of life in the place he attacks, favoring cities with higher population density as a consequence. He retreats once he suffers noticeable damage, or more often than not, loses a large number of his “parazombies” in his second stage leaving the city’s dwindling population in shambles.

Anubis not sandbagging has him place his strongest parazombies into a form of stasis not too dissimilar to that of Alexandria’s in the fact that it stops the aging of the corpses so that they don't become unusable by his power.
objects.title: Anubis has been Charged

objects.text:
Another Endbringer has been charged, recently terrorizing Earth Bet along with her siblings. The name given, Deceit Killer, Tithonus.

Tithonus has an insectoid frame resembling an amalgamation of several insect species; its main body matches a furless honey bee with beetle chitin-like armor coating, with large pincers and furled butterfly wings, juxtaposed by its meager size of less than a meter in length and not even a foot in height. When standing by, Tithonus remains inactive in her sprawling hive beneath unknown regions of the Amazonia. When found and interfered with, instead of swiftly dealing with the interference, she’ll quickly relocate with her Hive in tow, leaving the area eroded after interlopers leave, causing untold ecological damage.

Despite her tiny size, she keeps the classic Endbringer durability, strength, and speed her brethren are famed for, yet her power specialty makes her especially dangerous for Parahuman grounds. Her primary ability allows her to duplicate or spawn mini-versions of herself by consuming surrounding materials, while retaining their layered physiology and core, composed of the consumed materials. These miniatures—commonly known as drones—are nearly identical to her Queen, with the sole exception of being 3’’ in length, taking after the materials they’re made from and consume, helping them to heal and reproduce for more drones, as well as adapt against powers if they consume power effects or Parahumans to grow more resilient to similar effects progressively.

When on schedule, while making her way to her target location, Tithonus will soar out from her Hive and burrow into a structure or the underground terrain, beginning the reproduction of her local brooding swarm. Generally, it’s noted that she starts with a hardy swarm of 500 drones and targets opponents who will be most affected by her words. During the fight, she’ll be “protected” by at least 100 of her drones as she wanders through the battlefield, and in the latter stages, her swarm will start spewing “truth bombs” to Parahumans in the battle. After her swarm is destroyed or the chance that Tithonus is currently engaged with a meaningful group of enemy capes, she’ll immediately flee from the battlefield—abandoning the remaining swarm—and return to the main Hive.

Tithonus’ prime directive isn’t physical destruction, but the erosion of Parahuman trust between Hosts, as she will actively search out Parahumans that, when they come to know a truth, will potentially cause a schism in either a team or community effort, driving a wedge between them. This draws Tithonus not to target particular places but particular people surrounded by lies.

When not sandbagging, Tithonus begins to cannibalize herself–or even another Endbringer if one is nearby–to create drones made out of Endbringer flesh. As well as beginning to explain fundamental truths of the wider world or bringing in the truth about something related to her opponents, anything that will cause the most mental strife or even inspire conflict between comrades in the moment. She will even if pushed fall back on her reputation of only ever speaking truths to present blatant lies as irrefutable facts.
objects.title: Tithonus has been Charged

objects.text:
Another Endbringer’s been charged, terrorizing Earth Bet alongside her siblings. This Endbringer is known as Nemesis, and she is the Powerkiller.

Nemesis is a vaguely feminine humanoid figure with a single pair of ‘wings’ protruding from her back, possessing copper brown ‘skin’ with an appearance similar to tarnished marble, and a face that lacks eyes while her lips extend past her jawline and end halfway down her throat, razor sharp teeth lining the entire passage. She stands at 8 meters tall with a wingspan of twice that, and fingers that reach the ground with claws making up half their length. When in stand-by mode, she wanders the mountains along the border of Europe and Asia, avoiding people but killing anyone who tries to interfere with her.

Nemesis, other than the standard Endbringer physiology, possesses powers that make her the ultimate Anti-Parahuman weapon. First, are her physical stats. While she is not as strong as Behemoth, as fast as Leviathan, or as nimble as the Simurgh, she can be called second to each of them in those stats, making her the ideal melee fighter. Second, she has the power to generate spores from her wings. These spores, upon landing on a solid surface, begin to spawn nodes of exotic matter not found anywhere else. Each and every material generated has some kind deleterious effect on Parahuman powers and / or their users. From crystals that emit a unique form of radiation that forces Breakers exposed to it to painfully assume their true form, to metals that constantly hum which give any Thinker who hears it massive Thinker headaches, to pools of liquid that Shaker effects can’t cross, and more, stranger substances.

Third and perhaps the most dangerous is her ability to control spores that are within a foot of her. If she is fighting a Brute, she’ll have her spores coat her claws in a substance that tears away at flesh, the tougher the flesh the faster it decays. If she is fighting a Tinker, she’ll begin emitting a unique form of radiation that accelerates the wear and tear of their technology up to a day of intense use per minute. If she is fighting a minion Master, she’ll coat her throat with a layer of metal and scream in a pitch that causes their control to waver and their minions to go berserk. This power even reacts defensively such that attacks by Parahumans result in the spontaneous generation of substances meant to counter their powers, though this has a limit in that it can only counter one or two broad categories at a time.

Nemesis arrives at her target location via flight, ascending into low orbit before crashing into her targets at several times the speed of sound, creating an explosion that spreads her spores across a massive area all at once in the process. Her attacks are brutal and animalistic, flying around at high speeds ripping apart anyone she ‘sees’. Generally, her targets will possess a dense population of Capes, with her focusing on killing as many Parahumans as possible while spreading her spores as far and wide as possible. If she successfully kills all the native Parahumans, she will try to kill any non-native Parahumans, only ending her attack when she has killed double the number of Parahumans native to the city or if she takes sufficient damage.

Generally when fighting her, the go to strategy is to constantly switch up attacks against her to try to outpace her ability to adapt to specific targets. Unique to her attacks are teams of Parahumans whose sole job is to try destroying as many of her spores and the deposits they create as possible, as if they spread enough the deposits will grow to massive sizes and begin regenerating over time. Fights against her are on a timer, as if not defeated in time, the city will be condemned as normal life becomes impossible.

What drives Nemesis, her prime directive, is to create conflict by both attacking large groups of Parahumans who bring stability to an area, such as a city where the Heroes have successfully defeated all local villains, and also by spreading as much anti-Parahuman material as possible. with her secondary targeting parameter being cities that are either on the border of one or more powerful nations, prone to attacks by a stronger neighbor, or in areas prone to large scale internal conflict, all with the goal of causing an arms race to either acquire these materials for anti-Parahuman operations, or to destroy the materials to prevent them being used against Parahuman factions, thus sparking wars.

Nemesis not sandbagging has her physical parameters exceed Alexandria by a wide margin, with her spores actively generating counters to any number of powers based on proximity rather than in response to an attack, and her spore creation ramping up to the point that she can create pseudo-sandstorms from them.
objects.title: Nemesis Has Been Charged

objects.text:
Another Endbringer has been created, terrorizing Earth Bet alongside its siblings. While others cause death and destruction with their own powers, this one brings it through technology. The name given to it by the public is Vulcan.

Vulcan is a massive, heavily-built Jaguar-like construct standing at approximately 10.67 meters tall, its body resembling layered plates of obsidian black metal veined with glowing orange light like molten steel beneath a cracked surface. Its limbs are thick and segmented, resembling both armor and machinery, while its back constantly vents heat and particulate ash through chimney-like protrusions. Its “face” is featureless save for a single horizontal slit of white-hot light, while its tail seems to almost be made of electricity with how bright it shines. When inactive, Vulcan resides deep beneath tectonically active regions—volcanoes, fault lines, and geothermal hotspots—where it slowly reshapes its surroundings into sprawling subterranean foundries.

Vulcan possesses the standard layered durability and overwhelming strength of an Endbringer, but its true power lies in its ability to transmute and construct. Through a process analogous to alchemy, Vulcan can convert any available matter—stone, metal, water, debris, even organic material—into complex machinery almost instantaneously. This is not traditional Tinker-tech; rather, it is the direct conversion of matter into fully realized, fully functional constructs without the need for intermediate fabrication steps.

What drives Vulcan, its' Endbringer directive, is escalation through production. It targets areas of high infrastructure value—industrial centers, technological hubs, and major cities—seeking to destroy the human's capacity to create.

Its attacks are designed to trigger destabilizing global balance through lack of equipment. Vulcan retreats once it sustains sufficient core damage or when it destroys all factories, labs, or means of science and engineering in a city.

Vulcan not sandbagging results in a dramatic increase in its processing and production capabilities. Its counter-unit generation becomes predictive rather than reactive, producing effective counters before Parahumans fully engage. Its constructs gain limited autonomy and coordination independent of Vulcan’s direct control, allowing simultaneous multi-front engagements. In extreme cases, Vulcan can begin constructing macro-scale war machines; city-sized artillery, self-repairing fortresses, or autonomous production lines—turning entire regions into self-sustaining warzones. And even on a smaller level, It can still produce devices that allow it to hit people on the inside, whether freezing their skull solid with a freeze ray, melting their bones with a fire ray, Robots to act as extra defense, and more.
objects.title: Vulcan Has Been Charged!

objects.text:
Another Endbringer has been charged, terrorizing Earth Bet alongside their siblings. Their name is Acedia, and they are the Standard Killer.

Unlike their siblings, Acedia is different in many ways, the most blatant of which is their form. They appear to be made up of a mass of ink or oil roughly making up a humanoid figure with glowing spots typically where eyes would be, though that roughness fades away during battles. The oil isn’t like typical Enbdringer flesh but that doesn’t make it any less difficult to pierce through, as it acts like an extreme version of non-Newtonian fluid, which makes it capable of protecting its core.

Besides a variation of the standard Endbringer durability, Acedia’s abilities during combat include the ability to ‘conjure’ copies of itself who are always physically weaker than itself. These copies have the ability to mimic the appearance of nearby capes as well as outright copy their powers, creating scenarios where Parahumans are often literally fighting themselves during the Endbringer battle. Acedia themselves also possesses this mimicry ability, but doesn’t often go into direct combat themselves, preferring to hide amongst the crowd of copies.

Acedia’s Endbringer directive is to force Parahumans who have grown stagnant or haven’t made any significant progress with their powers to grow. By literally forcing Parahumans to fight themselves and copies of other Parahumans, Acedia makes Shard Hosts generate more [DATA] than they otherwise would have. Acedia also acts in a sadistic manner during combat in order to psychologically stress Parahumans for the purpose of making them prone to violently acting out after the battle, thereby generating even more [DATA].

Acedia’s target locations include cities where the local Parahuman population has stopped developing, as well as cities which have not developed industrially, economically, politically or socially to any degree.

When in standby mode, Acedia reabsorbs previously made copies that haven’t been destroyed, somehow not increasing in size. They then typically wander isolated areas such as plains or valleys while constantly shifting their form from their standard body, previously copied Parahumans, a simple blob of their oil, or even nearby animals.

When Acedia stops sandbagging, they take to the field themselves, generating vast amounts of their oil to increase their size by several meters. They then take characteristics from any Parahumans or other life forms on the battlefield in order to copy their powers, often resulting in them looking like a massive eldritch abomination. Their copies also do this transformation to a lesser extent.
objects.title: Acedia has Been Charged

addons.text:
With Eidolon’s control, the Conflict Engines’ purpose and utility take a more constructive approach: The Simurgh can work as the world’s lighthouse and soothsayer in the situation of mankind succeeding on their aspirations of going to the stars and the world at large, Leviathan can assure the ocean’s health, and Behemoth ensures the use of accessible nuclear energy for the whole world, are among the examples. 

They, hence, act as monuments… to be toppled in the eyes of villainy, which see the Engines’ fall as an approach to be the pinnacle of their goals: some as a way to be remembered in the annals of history, others as a statement of intent from their cause, or simply as means to an unforeseeable goal. This shapes them to be more crafty and ambitious in how they carry themselves, for a large portion of villains. This might push them to organize into a coalition or a League. This makes them more dangerous in the long run, as there’s nothing more formidable than men with vision.
addons.title: Terraforming Engines

objects.text: All 20 Endbringers have been released. Randomly around the world, the world will have to face 20 Endbringers.
objects.title: 20 Endbringers in 1 World

objects.text: Originally, the Endbringers may have served the role of unstoppable city destroying monsters, but they were pretty small, weren't they? Even the first version of Godzilla was tall enough that Behemoth, the largest of the original three Endbringers, wouldn't come up to his waist. Well, not anymore. Now, the Endbringers truly deserve the title of Kaiju, with all that it entails. The Endbringers are now absolutely massive, being at minimum 50 meters tall. They are also much more beastlike. Behemoth is now a massive walking mountain of spikes and magma, Leviathan is far more serpentine, being a massive eel-like monster capable of eating small ships, and the Simurgh's wings span from city block to city block with more feathers than body. They are also comparatively more destructive, with them merely moving through a city leveling buildings and killing thousands. Additionally, if not driven off in time, Endbringers typically move to target nearby cities, possibly destroying 3 or 4 if not stopped. Endbringer battles now frequently involve military intervention, with tanks, planes, and ships firing on them constantly. Anyone who isn't strong enough to survive being around such firepower is now relegated to search and rescue or other non-combat roles, with Brutes who can't stand a punch from Alexandria not even being allowed near the Endbringer. With such massive targets, killing them is much more difficult, with the few who possibly could having a much harder time getting to the core, much less finding it in all that bulk. Expect the world to be in a much worse state, with more cities ruined, a refuge crisis unlike any seen before, and even nations like America on the brink of collapse if no other modifiers have improved the situation. Also expect most government Tinkers to have superweapons in development, more combat training being standardized, and other knock-on effects.
objects.title: True Kaiju

addons.text: Congratulations, you being an Endbringer Target has synergized with Endbringer Assault to make you the Endbringer's personal punching bag. The level of the Drawback you have determines how bad this is. With Endbringer Target, Leviathan may attack a ship carrying materials and goods you imported, making it never arrive, or the Simurgh may break a satellite right when the show you were watching was getting good, disrupting the broadcast, just a general inconvenience to your life. With Hostile Endbringers, sometimes they'll assault you directly, holding back to their usual assault level while still trying to kill you, allowing you the chance to run away only to assault you again a month later. With Singular Target, they will use their full power against you and only you during their assaults, chasing you for hours and killing anyone who tries to help you, ensuring that most people will run away or even pre-emptively chase you out of town, leaving you to face the Endbringer alone. Good luck.
addons.title: Favorite Punching Bag

addons.text: Good news! The Para-Endbringers don't lose control and unleash their destructive powers! Bad news! They still unleash their destructive powers of their own accord because they are all villains! While they don't destroy entire cities out of hand, they still frequently attack people and places whether at their whims or to ensure no one encroaches on their territory. At best they are gang leaders who rule over the crime of their homes, at worst they are full blown warlords. All the same, they are violent individuals with a love of bullying others. If you somehow befriend them, which is an uphill battle no matter what, they will become violently overprotective of you, treating your enemies as their enemies, i.e. destroying them utterly without regard for collateral damage. If you intend to 'redeem' them into upstanding members of society... good luck. Unless you have Favorite Punching Bag, in which case, if that was ever possible, it certainly isn't for you. If you have Harbingers Assault, then whether they are pets or children the Harbingers are every bit as mean as their 'parents'.
addons.title: Para-Endbringer Assault

objects.text: You know that one Fanon where Leviathan occasionally attacks boats and that's why the shipping industry died instead of the Canonical reason that destroyed ports lead to a poor shipping economy, or that the Simurgh attacked any given space launch when that wasn't the case? Yeah, while that might not be a thing in canon, it sure is a thing where you're going. Now, even outside of their attack cycle, the Endbringers will occasionary do small attacks in random places: Behemoth will sometimes collapse a mine or make a volcanic eruption worse, Leviathan will occasionally appear out of nowhere to sink a boat or slaughter a small coastal village, the Simurgh might strafe a satellite or attack an airplane, etc. Basically, they will just make things a little bit worse for everybody, albeit they will typically hold back most of their powers. So no nuclear armageddon, massive tidal waves, or city wide screams, just pure carnage, like a bully kicking over a sandcastle just because they can. Even worse, if they face sufficient resistance during their attacks, they may decide to go ahead and do a full blown attack early (i.e. the Triumvirate tries to save a fishing hamlet Leviathan is assaulting, resulting in him summoning tidal waves as he beelines for the nearest city to make his displeasure known). This means that most of the time, nothing can really be done to save their victims lest millions of lives be put in unnecessary danger. And yes, this does lead to some attacks having a delayed response from defenders due to being falsely labeled a mere assault. Again, this just makes them all around worse than Canon. Note: If taken with another Modifier that gives the Endbringers human-like personalities, they will enjoy bullying others and just being all around assholes, at best being very, very Tsundere to people they actually like.
objects.title: Endbringer Assault

addons.text:
The species the ENDBRINGER belongs too, much like the Entities, have destroyed innumerable worlds. Their kind is full of monsters who think nothing of wiping out countless civilizations simply so they can feed and grow in power. However, no species is without its outliers, and among this one a rare few can be found who have turned their back on these ways. The GUARDIANS have instead dedicated themselves to helping the very worlds their brethren would consume, and one has dedicated themself to at least trying to save humanity.

This GUARDIAN has deployed its Heralds to earth with the intent to fight off the incursion by the ENDBRINGER. It focuses on assisting the native species in a variety of ways, such as maintaining a healthy environment to live in, curtailing the worst excesses and crimes such as slavery or genocide, or inspiring people to help one another as heroes, all while doing its best to prevent its counterpart's Haralds from killing cities.

In the meantime, additional Guardians roam the alternate earths searching for and fighting their counterparts. Thanks to this, the time it takes for all 20 Endbringers to reach Earth Bet and initiate their fusion into an avatar extends from 20 years at base to 50 years. When this occurs, the Guardians will initiate their own merger for one last attempt at saving the world.

However, by itself it stands no chance at winning. Due to focusing on ethical but far less efficient means of feeding and power growth, the GUARDIAN is much weaker than the ENDBRINGER, being at best half as strong compared to it as the Wanderer is compared to the Warrior and Thinker combined. Still, even if it is an uphill battle with low odds of success, the GUARDIAN might be the single best ally humanity has against the predations of the ENDBRINGER, and should they win, against the Entity as well.
addons.title: A GUARDIAN Against the Apocalypse

objects.text: The Endbringers are giant monsters that attack a major city every three to four months. They terrorize the world, striking fear into the hearts of everyone who hears of them. They are practically unstoppable monsters, living siege engines seemingly designed to slowly wear down civilization. Overall, they seem to operate exactly as per canon. But that can't be right. Where are their Harbingers? Why are they still so small? What is going on? Then, you begin to notice something. Whenever they attack, you feel like you are being watched. People feel like they are being crushed by their mere presence, like a predator is seeing them through eyes that seem bigger than they are. That's when you put it together: these are the Harbingers, and you feel like you're being watched because something is looking. The Endbringers of canon never existed. These monsters were never a creation of the Entities. They are merely the Heralds of monsters on the level of the Entities themselves. Devourer of Worlds, eldritch beings from beyond the material universe. When one is killed, it is merely replaced with another of its kind, the damage mounting as slowly, from the outer edges of the known earth's, worlds begin to go silent. Groups like Cauldron, the Haywire Collective, and other multidimensional organizations will be the first to notice as one by one entire earth's begin to simply vanish from their sight. One of the Interdimensional Endbringers appears in a world, it vanishes, and it reappears in another. When it runs out of worlds in its 'territory' it invades Earth Bet and joins the attack cycle. Over time, the rate ramps up. More Endbringers appear. As they do, they slowly get bigger. They get stronger. They start to spawn their own Harbingers. This continues, until they are stronger than the base True Kaiju, and their Harbingers are more numerous, and just as strong as the Canon Endbringers. When finally Aleph itself falls, which will take approximately 20 years if you don't interfere, all 20 Endbringers will be on Earth Bet. That is when The End begins. The Endbringers will tear a portal into Earth Eden itself, and consume the Thinker Entity. Using its corpse as fuel, they will merge together to become an avatar for the ENDBRINGER, a monster fit to match an Entity. And then they will return to Bet to battle The Warrior. No matter who wins, humanity will lose barring outside interference. Should you have other Modifiers that empower the Endbringers, they will stack exponentially onto the ENDBRINGER, empowering it further. Waking Titans accelerates the rate at which Earth's are consumed, while 20 Endbringers in 1 World means that you are a year away from the ENDBRINGER's arrival. Even More Dormant Endbringers increases the number of Endbringers and therefore the total strength of the ENDBRINGER. Reign of the Kaiju boosts its power to match a full power Entity rather than one that is mid-Cycle. Ragnarök means another ENDBRINGER will arrive and battle its counterpart for the right to Devour the World. Should you have all of the above, then it would take a pair of full power Entities empowered by Reign of the Entities to defeat them. Note: If you are an Endbringer or control them, you are / control canon versions of the Endbringers, not the ENDBRINGER.
objects.title: Heralds of the Apocalypse

addons.text: It wasn't just a lucky break or miraculous event that resulted in an Endbringer falling. Now, all of the Endbringers were felled before your arrival. You can decide how exactly this happened. Perhaps it was a series of operations carried out by the world's Thinkers in order to give Flechette the opportunity to slay each Endbringer in turn. Maybe Leet made an anti-Endbringer weapon and it lasted just long enough to kill them all before breaking. Or Eidolon, Glaistig Uaine, or some other Trump discovered the exact power combination needed to kill one and proceeded to hunt them down one by one. Either way, the Endbringers have been dead for some time now, and the world is now much more likely to survive Gold Morning without them constantly killing humanity's best and brightest. You can also decide how this affected the dormant Endbringers. Perhaps Eidolon became content and stopped activating them, or he was informed of his part in their existence and burned out years worth of power in order to destroy the Endbringer creation Shard. Or Eidolon had nothing to do with it and killing all of the Active Endbringers caused the Endbringer creation Shard to glitch out and go dormant again. Or maybe they did activate, but the world still managed to slay them one by one. Or they just all had their cores destroyed on your arrival as per End of the Kaiju.
addons.title: The Endslayer

objects.text: Endbringers are the Kaiju-like monsters that have been laying siege to Earth Bet since Behemoth's first attack in 1992. In that time, with their ever-increasing numbers, and tempo, they have laid waste to countless cities and caused devastation affecting entire countries and continents. They have always been a threat that must be fought, but after so long enduring their attacks there is little hope of success. At least there was no hope, until now. During one of the many unrelenting attacks by an Endbringer, the stars aligned, and the unthinkable happened, an Endbringer fell in battle. Which one, and how they were defeated though? That is up to you. It could have been a lucky strike by an all-or-nothing effect managing to reveal the greatest weakness of the Endbringers by shattering their core. Maybe a Bakuda bomb or one of Greyboy's bubbles managed to lock one away frozen in time. Or perhaps it was something else entirely? Regardless of exactly how the Endbringer was defeated, the result is undeniable, there is real belief that these terrible monsters can finally be defeated. There is hope once more. Note: Fallen in this context can cover any situation that ends the Endbringers' ability to return to the cycle of attacks.
objects.title: A Fallen Beast

objects.text:
Behemoth has sensed a future in which it dies. Refusing to allow such an outcome to come to pass, the Endbringer has chosen deception over simple confrontation.

Using its absolute control over energy and electromagnetic fields, Behemoth can now generate vast numbers of autonomous energy constructs. These projections range from simple holographic illusions to semi-solid hard-light constructs and even fully condensed energy avatars capable of independent combat. 

At their weakest, these constructs are little more than insect-sized scouts, false heat signatures, phantom movements, and sensor ghosts designed to mislead defenders and draw attacks away from the true Behemoth.

At their strongest, they can temporarily rival the true Endbringer they imitate. By compressing enormous quantities of energy into a construct, Behemoth can create mobile combat avatars capable of operating far beyond its normal control radius. These avatars can be programmed and given enough energy to fight independently for hours, unleashing radiation, lightning, heat, and kinetic force, and even creating lesser projections of their own before eventually collapsing as their stored energy is exhausted. 

Worse still, each avatar can perfectly reproduce the detectable signatures of the real Behemoth, including effects associated with all four fundamental forces. Radar, infrared sensors, satellite imaging, gravimetric detection, and most parahuman senses identify the constructs as genuine. Even specialized observations normally capable of distinguishing Behemoth from ordinary battlefield interference can be deliberately reproduced.

To anyone relying solely on human technology or solely on shard-derived abilities, every sufficiently advanced duplicate appears to be the real Behemoth, and only by combining human and shard ingenuity can the real Behemoth be found. The war against Behemoth therefore becomes a hunt for the one signal that even the greatest shards in the network cannot convincingly fake.

The result is a battlefield where no one can be certain which Behemoth is real. Cities may celebrate the Endbringer’s apparent destruction, only for another Behemoth to rise from the earth months later.
objects.title: Behemoth’s False Army

objects.text:
Leviathan has sensed a future in which it dies. Refusing to allow that outcome to come to pass, the Endbringer has chosen distance over direct confrontation.

Using its planetary-scale hydrokinesis, Leviathan can now manipulate major ocean currents, atmospheric moisture, and the global water cycle with terrifying precision. The fragile equilibrium governing Earth’s climate collapses under its influence. Hurricanes form without warning. Typhoons appear in the wrong oceans. Storm systems change direction without explanation. Regions that have never experienced tropical weather are suddenly struck by superstorms.

But the storms are only the most obvious barrage.

By coordinating the oceans and atmosphere across enormous distances, Leviathan can turn the planet’s water systems into precisely aimed artillery, allowing the Endbringer to trigger carefully engineered disasters anywhere on Earth. A specific dam collapses under sudden hydraulic pressure spikes. Coordinated lightning strikes cascade through power grids across entire regions. Storm systems stall above cities far from any ocean until streets become rivers and foundations begin to fail.

Each is deliberately timed and positioned to create cascading failures: destroying infrastructure, severing transportation networks, disrupting food and fuel shipments, isolating population centers, and overwhelming emergency response systems with simultaneous crises.

All while Leviathan itself remains hidden in the deepest trenches and farthest caves of the world’s oceans. Leviathan no longer needs to assault cities directly, instead choosing to hunt the entire world from the abyss. Humanity must find Leviathan before the entire planet becomes nothing more than an uninhabitable weapon in the Endbringer’s hands.
objects.title: Leviathan’s Storm Artillery

objects.text:
The Simurgh has sensed something in the future that would end with its death. Refusing to allow such a outcome to come to pass, the Simurgh has decided to take immediate action to preserve it life.

Using its vast knowledge of tinker-tech, the Simurgh has created backup copies of its own mind and hidden them across the multiverse inside autonomous cloning facilities. Each installation contains the data and resources necessary to reconstruct the Endbringer from scratch.

When a Simurgh body is destroyed, one of these facilities activates creating a new Simurgh body with each new body as capable as the original and fully aware of how the past iteration died. Now every destroyed Simurgh returns smarter than the last with every death now simply being a lesson for it to learn from.

The only way to permanently end the Simurgh threat is to locate and destroy every hidden cloning facility before they can rebuild the Endbringer or the Endbringer can construct new cloning facilities. Taking this modifier once spawns a single cloning facility and each selection after that double the number of cloning facilities from the previous selection. 

May whatever gods exist have mercy on your soul. You’ll need it.
objects.title: Simurgh’s Backup Cores

objects.text:
Khonsu has sensed a future in which it dies. Refusing to allow that outcome to come to pass, the Endbringer has chosen speed over prolonged confrontation.

Using its mastery of time and spatial displacement, Khonsu can now conduct devastating attacks across multiple locations simultaneously. In addition to teleporting across vast distances, the Endbringer can displace itself through a limited span of its own timeline, temporarily bringing multiple moments of its existence into the present at once.
These are not true duplicates.

Every temporal instance is the same Khonsu, drawn from a different point along a single continuous timeline. They cannot create paradoxes, directly touch one another, or overlap their temporal fields, but they can otherwise move, attack, and coordinate independently. Damage inflicted upon Khonsu remains part of that shared timeline, and destroying the Endbringer even once ends every temporal instance with it.

Reaching that point is the problem.

Khonsu can deploy its temporal selves as a concentrated assault, surrounding a single city with multiple versions of itself and collapsing every temporal field inward at once. Alternatively, it can scatter them across the planet, striking several population centers within the same few minutes before defenders can even determine where the battle is taking place.

An Endbringer attack that once lasted hours may now last mere minutes. Now, before any meaningful counterattack can be organized, Khonsu retreats beyond the reach of conventional pursuit, allowing its timeline to stabilize, its body to regenerate, and its energy reserves to replenish before traveling forward through time to launch another impossibly short offensive months later.

There is simply no longer enough time to evacuate a city, assemble hundreds of parahumans, establish command structures, and gradually wear the Endbringer down. By the time humanity understands the shape of the attack, Khonsu may already have accomplished its objective and escaped into the flow of time.

Entire populations can vanish before reinforcements arrive. Several cities can be struck before the first emergency response finishes mobilizing. Even when defenders manage to engage one temporal instance, the others continue their attacks elsewhere.

Yet Khonsu's greatest strength is also its vulnerability.

There may be many Khonsus on the battlefield, but only one Khonsu truly exists. Humanity does not need to defeat an army; it needs to kill a single Endbringer once.

The challenge is forcing Khonsu to remain in the present long enough to do it.
objects.title: Khonsu’s Relentless Offensive

objects.text:
The Twin Endbringers have sensed a future in which they die. Refusing to allow that outcome to come to pass, the Endbringers have chosen unity over separate confrontation.

The connection between Tohu and Bohu has deepened until the distinction between their powers has disappeared. Each Endbringer can now access the abilities of the other, allowing either twin to wield their entire combined arsenal independently.

Tohu can reshape cities, distort terrain, and transform the battlefield with Bohu's abilities while simultaneously wielding the powers it has copied from parahumans. Bohu, in turn, can manifest and wield copied powers while its environmental transformations continue around it. Separating the twins no longer divides their capabilities; wherever either Endbringer appears, defenders must prepare to face the might of both.

This bond now extends even to their Endbringer cores. So long as one twin survives, its core can reconstruct the other, gradually rebuilding its destroyed counterpart and restoring the pair. Killing either one while the other survives merely begins a resurrection. Only the destruction of both cores can permanently kill them.

Worse still, when greater force is required, Tohu and Bohu can take their unity even further.
The twins can physically merge into a single composite Endbringer, fusing both their bodies and cores into one. In this state, their powers reinforce one another, dramatically increasing their range, precision, output, and versatility. Entire cities can be transformed while copied abilities are unleashed throughout the altered battlefield, with each power supporting the others as though wielded by a single intelligence. The weaknesses of one are countered by the strengths of the other, creating something far more dangerous than either twin alone or even the pair fighting side by side.

Normally, confronting such a nightmare would be insanity, yet their fusion also creates humanity's greatest opportunity.

By merging their two cores into a single unified core, Tohu and Bohu place both halves of their existence within reach at once. If defenders can breach the fused body and destroy that core before the twins can separate, Tohu and Bohu die together. If they fail, the twins can divide once more, and destroying only one will merely allow the survivor to resurrect its counterpart.

Humanity can no longer defeat the Twin Endbringers one at a time. They must kill both before either has the chance to make them two again.
objects.title: Twin’s Unity Protocol

addons.text: While the Shard Network may be more subtle in saving other versions of the planet, on Earth Bet at least the Guardians are the main tool by which the planet is prevented from dying. Instead of the ozone layer mysteriously being restored, perhaps a Guardian used aerokinesis or Tinkertech to fix it. Instead of the Great Pacific Garbage Patch vanishing, a Guardian spent a week cleaning it up. Instead of the fallout from nuclear accidents or weapons testing mysteriously going inert, a Guardian could have absorbed the radiation and nullified it. If you have certain Modifiers or Crossovers that add more unique methods by which the world may die, the Guardians will adapt to fix those issues too, or attempt to work towards it if it’s too big for even a dedicated Construct to fix. If the cycle of reincarnation is broken so that new life can’t be born, one Guardian might create bypasses to allow new souls to reenter the world. If Shinra is draining Gaia’s Lifestream dry, a Guardian could reach across the multiverse to pull slivers of energy from countless other versions of Gaia to restore this one. If Universal Degradation threatens the world, there will be a Guardian who specializes in researching it and while they (very probably) will not succeed in stopping it, they will at least try. This extremely blatant and continual saving of the world will massively boost the reputation and goodwill the Guardians have. If other forces are also actively saving the world, the Guardians will attempt to assist their efforts, though again, communication issues remain and may result in their assistance being indirect or limited unless a means of proper communication is found, such as someone with a variation of (Thinker/Trump) [Query] [Response] existing.
addons.title: What, You Thought The Title Was Metaphorical?

addons.text: The Guardians have noticed your strange nature and due to a misunderstanding will now view you as a major threat, though they will not actively seek you out if you aren’t actively working against their primary focus. However, if you are near one of them, they will attack you, though they will seek to avoid collateral damage or harming anyone else, even avoiding attacking people who try to defend you, retreating if needed to avoid harming them. It would take an immense amount of effort to convince the Guardians that they are mistaken in their assumptions, especially if you lack powers that could overcome the communication barrier, and if you are actively working against their goals or worse, manage to kill one of them, they will escalate in response up to and including forcefully dragging you to the middle of nowhere so they can safely unleash their full power against you. People will take note of this, and many will assume that you must be a threat as well. No matter what, the fact that both the Endbringers and the Guardians are trying to eliminate you will isolate you as no one wishes to fight both forces at once, and some may try to kill you to appease either group.
addons.title: Dangerous Anomaly

addons.text: With the Endbringers slain, the Guardians now stand uncontested as the world's protectors. Without them constantly undoing their efforts to help people, the Guardians existence has pushed the estimated lifespan of civilization towards the End of the Cycle at minimum as they'll work continuously to ensure humanity survives. With their help, the chances of mankind surviving a Gold Morning scenario is now much greater, and humanity's ability to recover in the aftermath is vastly improved as well. Or you could instead have them killed like their malicious brethren. Though this would, at least according to the average person, be considered a bad thing. It is highly recommended that you don't do that.
addons.title: Unchallenged Guardians

objects.text: Upon purchasing this Modifier, three more Endbringers are created. However, unlike their counterparts, these are benevolent Guardians rather than destroyers. You can decide the specifics of how and why they exist, maybe the Thinker wanted to create pseudo gods for people to worship, maybe they are meant to extend civilization’s lifespan to collect more data, maybe someone got a backup Construct Shard and it responded to their desire for the world to be saved. Perhaps something stranger like the earth being sentient and hijacking some dormant Endbringers for its own purposes, or maybe they are divine creations designed to mimic the Endbringers. Either way, they exist now. These Guardians are every bit as strong as the Endbringers, but focus purely on more heroic actions. One might work on cleaning up pollution and preventing natural disasters, another might help shepherd refugees to safety and free slaves, and a third might focus on toppling malevolent warlords or perhaps encouraging others to become heroes. You can decide what each Guardian's primary focus is. While they rarely interact, when they are in the same place at the same time, the Endbringers and Guardians will fight each other as they have mutually incompatible prime directives. However, the Guardian will go out of its way to avoid collateral damage and protect any humans caught in the crossfire, and will work with human defenders if they are present, albeit to a limited extent due to communication issues. You can decide exactly what their appearance and powers are so long as they are no stronger than a normal Endbringer, or leave it to chance. You may also decide if other Endbringer Modifiers affect them too, such as Harbingers of the End or Human Endbringers. No matter what, they will always be benevolent and heroic in nature, and there will always be three of them. This Modifier extends the time until civilization collapses by at least fifty years. Note: These Guardians are quite literally the same type of being as the Endbringers (or a good enough emulation to fool the Shard Network), simply with more benevolent objectives. This may lead to a divide on public opinion on them, and could possibly lead to conspiracy theories like them being aliens undergoing a civil war or something, or even Counter Cults who believe them to be angels or something with the Endbringers being their Fallen counterparts. The specifics of the social and political impact of their existence can optionally be decided by you.
objects.title: Guardians of Gaia

objects.text: Each Purchase adds one more Guardian as per Guardians of Gaia up to ten Guardians in total. If all ten are purchased, assuming no other modifiers, the End of the Cycle will be delayed to 300 years from now, and civilization is guaranteed to survive long enough to reach it.
objects.title: Additional Guardians

objects.text: Earth Bet is no longer alone in having Endbringers. Now, every earth that has one million or more humans on it has at least one Endbringer. Depending on the population and technological advancement of the earth in question, it may have more than one Endbringer present. Any earth with less than a billion people and / or is pre-industrial simply has one Endbringer, while modern earths like Aleph have at least two Endbringers. Larger worlds like Chet that has over 12 billion people or more advanced / powerful worlds like Bet that has a massive parahuman presence will have at least three Endbringers, at least one of which will focus on preventing them from becoming spacefaring. Any earths that successfully become spacefaring anyway or manage to kill an Endbringer will have four or more Endbringers active.
