The majority of these Endbringers will have more basic powers like being superbrutes or some form of elemental manipulation, with more complex and hard to counter powers being more common on worlds that have multiple Endbringers. These Endbringers tend to stick to their homeworlds, rarely if ever leaving even if given the opportunity and quickly returning if they do. Despite the name, they don't actually want to kill everyone, simply cause suffering and destabilize society so as to encourage Trigger events. Even so, you can expect a multiversal collapse of civilization within a century at most. If something happens to wipe out their world's human population, they will go dormant until a sufficient number of people are present, such as another earth attempting to colonize theirs or the survivors miraculously repopulating. Note: Each earth by default has its own set of twenty potential Endbringers, and drawbacks like Even More Active Endbringers or Even More Dormant Endbringers will affect all of them.
objects.title: You Get An Endbringer, You Get An Endbringer, Everybody Gets An Endbringer!

objects.text: This modifier makes it so that the Endbringers have the ability to speak in a way humans can understand. Their speech takes the form of a pseudo-telepathic communication that ‘sounds’ loud, harsh, and is picked up by anything capable of hearing speech such as the human ear or a microphone. Due to translation issues, Endbringers tend to speak in simple, clipped sentences consisting of one to five words at a time, though this is not a hard rule. They will typically use this ability to taunt their victims or declare their superiority, though some like the Simurgh may use it to psychologically manipulate their victims instead. Actual two way communication is possible, and theoretically they can be negotiated with. In practice, the Endbringer’s need to follow their directives combined with a shard influenced ‘might makes right’ perspective means that even getting to the point where they stop trying to kill you long enough to listen is an uphill battle in and of itself. However, it is possible, especially if something happens to make a directive impossible to fulfill, such as their directive to perpetuate the cycle being derailed by the Thinker’s death, or if you are clearly and immensely stronger than they are. This modifier may interact with other Endbringer Modifiers in a variety of ways. For example, it could make the Para-Endbringers prone to monologuing, or it could force the Endbringers to control their Harbingers via verbal commands thus giving local defenders a heads up on their plans. With Winged One, the Simurgh could try working around her Master Effect to try to warn defenders of what she’ll do and help them fight back against her. With Guardians of Gaia, the ability to speak with them would make coordinating with them magnitudes easier, allowing for true strategizing in battle and more, though expect them to constantly try to redirect the discussion towards their focus or asking to spar because 'fighting is fun’. Overall, this is a net positive, even if you now have to listen to Behemoth boast about how amazing he is and how weak you are.
objects.title: Vocalized End

objects.text: It seems that your world now has an infestation of Friendbringers. Friendbringers are essentially very small Endbringers (between one and two feet tall), which have a weaker variation of Endbringer biology (less layers and no true core similar to Lesser Endbringers) paired with one or two powers capped at 5 SP each, putting the average Friendbringer as being on the level of a low-to-mid street tier parahuman. Friendbringers make up for their weakness with numbers and variety, with anywhere from one to ten thousand of them being found all over the world per existing Endbringer, and each one having a different power set and appearance, though finding two or more that look almost the same or have very similar power sets is possible. Friendbringers are fairly symbiotic, each one going out of its way to find and bond with a specific member of the host species, typically someone who hasn’t Triggered yet or who has powers weaker than 10 SP, although one bonding with a Triumvirate-tier Parahuman is possible if unlikely. That host is from then on their master and friend, sharing a telepathic / empathic link with them and from which they take cues on what they do and how to act in general. Unfortunately, while ‘heroic’ Friendbringers are possible and very likely to exist, them having a similar preference in ‘friends’ that shards have in their hosts combined with the fact that nothing stops them from bonding with criminals leads to far more ‘villainous’ Friendbringers existing than ‘heroic’ ones. Essentially, this modifier results in the birth of a new class of ‘parahumans’ who have Friendbringer companions, with all that that entails. Expect an arms race to ensue as various factions compete to collect as many Friendbringers as they can on their side, with press ganging being a perfectly viable strategy as many Friendbringers will have ‘friends’ who are either powerless or are on the weaker end of parahuman strength. Also, expect some discrimination against those with Friendbringers due to their similar nature to Endbringers, even if they are a lot weaker than them. As for the Endbringers themselves, they don’t seem to care one way or the other about Friendbringers, treating them like everyone else, i.e., as people to either crush or ignore. Note: Friendbringers do have Thinker resistance like the Endbringers, but it is typically on the level of the Frankenstein perk, and Thinker powers worth more than 10 SP generally blast right through the interference, so unless one of their powers is a Stranger power with an anti-Thinker configuration, then parahumans like Dinah or Contessa would be completely unaffected. Also, if you have (Master) Friendbringers yourself, most people are going to assume you just got lucky and befriended multiple of them, which is possible if rare, unless you reveal otherwise or have one of its upgrades that makes them stronger than the ‘wild’ variety.
objects.title: Friendbringer Infestation
Biological Endbringers
objects.text: Instead of being pure constructs made of increasingly dense layers of crystalline 'flesh', the Endbringers are now and have always been actual biological organisms. This means they are made of actual flesh, blood, and bone with functioning organs. Though still visually similar to their original appearance, this causes various changes, such as their eyes and other sensory organs or equivalent being functional, and being capable of eating and other biological functions their original 'biology' couldn't do. Most importantly though, this means they are easier to kill due to not needing to dig through the equivalent of a massive celestial body's worth of matter to hit something vital. However this remains a difficult task as the Endbringers still retain an immense Brute rating. Their durability is enough that heavy artillery won't even scratch them, but not so high that Alexandria can't make them bleed, however due to lacking their layers they instead focus on regeneration, which is enough that a severed limb can be completely regrown in minutes, and internal organs in seconds. Only a decisively fatal wound such a pulped heart can kill them, and even then their regenerative core still needs to be destroyed to prevent them from eventually resurrecting. Outside of this, their biological nature introduces some advantages and weaknesses. Since they have actual senses they can't be tricked by spoofing their power based sense as easily, but on the other hand they are now susceptible to certain types of illusions or sensory overload. They still possess innate resistance to various powers that should be able to take them out such as biokinesis, but it is no longer as absolute as before and theoretically a Tinkertech virus could bypass their immune system at least temporarily before they fight it off, weakening them during a specific battle. Of course, because of this the threshold where the Endbringers begin to stop holding back is lowered as they are more likely to die should they not, though it still is a net benefit in terms of killing them. Other possibilities for how this change affects their nature and how they are combatted exist, though the specifics are up to you. For example, whether or not they need to eat at all, whether they need stimulation to prevent boredom, etc. If you have other Endbringer Modifiers you can choose how they interact with this one, such as Harbingers of the End making the Endbringer's Harbingers anything from drones split off via a form of budding to their actual offspring made using a form of parthenogenesis, or the Guardians of Gaia and Friendbringer Infestation being equally affected or even perhaps unaffected by this Modifier due to coming from a different source. With Editorial Edition, you may freely alter what the exact 'physiology' of the Endbringers is. Perhaps they're actually mechanical, being massive war machines filled with wires, servos, motors, and such? Or maybe they're made of exotic matter that makes them appear to be elementals of some kind, such as the Simurgh being seemingly made out of living clouds filled with strange organ equivalents? Whatever the case, this is mostly cosmetic as no matter the form they will be roughly on par with the default Biological Endbringers in terms of power level, danger to others, and difficulty in taking down. Note: If you have any powers that are based on the Endbringers then optionally you can have them be affected to, whether it's (Brute) Typhon being altered to function like this world's version of their Brute power, (Master) Friendbringers having your friends also be living organisms, or the creations of (Master/Trump) Endbringer Engine all being biological in nature.

objects.title: Alien Endbringers
objects.text: With this Modifier, the Endbringers are now not only biological organisms, but they are also just straight up aliens. Rather than being Shard creations, these Endbringers come from alien worlds, whether having arrived from a planet lightyears away or from another dimension only loosely connected to the dimension set containing Earth Bet, Earth Aleph, and their other counterparts is up to you. The Endbringers are now extremely alien in appearance, barely resembling their canon selves, any aspect of their appearance that seems similar to native lifeforms being mere happenstance. For example, the Simurgh could appear as some sort of floating feathered hybrid of a jellyfish, whale, and something vaguely humanoid. If you wish, each Endbringer could have a different ‘homeworld’ so to speak. However, this change comes with some drawbacks. For one, the Endbringers have no connection to the Shard Network, their powers being innate manifestations thanks to advanced biology, integrated technology, alien magic, or some other source. Yet they have somehow managed to trick the Shard Network into not registering them as the threat they truly are, Scion treating them like a leftover Thinker experiment or an attempt by one of the other earth's parahumans to attack this one, and lets them continue to exist. In addition to this, the Endbringers are now much harder to kill. Their alien biology is incredibly bizarre, unlike any earth lifeform, with immense redundancy as well as extremely complex genetic structures and immune systems making them all but immune to even the best Tinkertech or Biokinetically created diseases and just very hard to kill through conventional damage in general. On top of that, their powers are now vastly more complicated, versatile, and even a bit stronger than before, making them far more dangerous to the point that a Tier 3 power is needed to be as effective as a Tier 2 used to be against them. You can decide the exact nature of these Endbringers and their reason for coming to Earth Bet. Maybe they derive a unique form of sustenance from eating beings with powers of their own, or they could be bioengineered superweapons used by The Alien Invaders to more effectively fight against Entity empowered worlds, or perhaps they wish to take over the cycle for their own ends, or any number of possibilities. Just as with Biological Endbringers, if you have other Endbringer Modifiers you may decide how this affects them, and if you have Editorial Edition you can further alter them such as them being alien robots instead of alien lifeforms. Note: If you have Endbringer based powers like (Brute) Typhon or (Master) Friendbringers, then those powers are based on either the canon Endbringers or the default Biological Endbringers, not these stronger versions of them.

objects.title: Leviathan Rebalanced
objects.text: The Endbringer Leviathan was undoubtedly the most destructive of the three original Endbringers. While Behemoth and the Simurgh affect only their immediate surroundings, Leviathan’s power devastates coastlines and sinks landmasses. Not anymore. Although he can still cause tsunamis and floods, Leviathan never sunk a significant landmass. Kyushu, Newfoundland, and likely other landmasses around the world remain above water. There is still widespread destruction—tsunamis are nobody’s friend—but with Kyushu intact, Japan remains a significant power. There may still be some Asian diaspora, but it will not be on the scale seen in canon. This will significantly weaken organizations like the ABB, though whether individual capes are members is up to you. With Newfoundland intact, Andrew Richter may have survived, potentially creating more AIs and becoming something akin to a Canadian Tony Stark. Whether or not you choose to have him survive, Ascalon no longer falls into the hands of Saint and the Dragonslayers.

rows.title: Entity & Endbringer Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the Entities and/or the Endbringers

objects.text: Every Parahuman, including you, is a low-level Brute, enough to survive low-caliber bullets unharmed. People who would normally be Brutes are slightly stronger Brutes.
objects.title: Brute

objects.text: Not only does everyone gain a minor brute rating, they also gain a minor combat thinker rating. Every Parahuman gains an increase combat capabilities, as well as a fighting style that perfectly incorporates their powers. Capes like Victor or Uber will have their main ability boosted.
objects.title: Martial Artist

objects.text: Every Parahuman, including you, has their Brute rating boosted. They will all be capable of lifting or crushing cars with some effort. They are also given incredible regenerative capabilities, enabling them to quickly return to their peak physical condition after a night's sleep. In addition, their physical strength is significantly enhanced by even the most modest exercise routines, resulting in most Parahumans exhibiting remarkable physical fitness, with little effort required.
objects.title: The Boy Who Lifted

objects.text: Now it's not only Cluster-Trigger or Nth-Gen capes that can get a combo platter of powers, now people that'd  triggered in single natural triggers as well as those who've drank a Cauldron vial will have 2, 3 or more secondary minor powers.
objects.title: No Trigger Discipline

objects.text:
A certain type or category of power is fundamentally unavailable, unusable, or difficult enough to be irrelevant due to the nature of the world/reality you find yourself in. Whether that be time travel, spatial manipulation, necromancy, power copying, mind control, or something simpler like specific elemental powers. 

You are not immune to these limitations, and are affected for as long as you remain in the same reality.

This does not alter the power level of a reality. If these restrictions would prevent the normal plot or danger of said reality, the reality will be altered to have a different but near-equivalent danger and 'plot'. This cannot be used to affect entire power systems, only specific expressions. If all 'normal' expressions in a system are unavailable, abnormal expressions will take their place.
objects.title: Unavailable Powers

objects.text: The way the world- and the powers within- work has tilted. Maybe chakra in Naruto is now the base energy and must be split into spiritual and physical energies to use. Maybe bending in Avatar is now a form of shapeshifting. Whatever the case, the world will still appear mostly the same 'plotwise', if functionally different. This also affects the Target (Meta), shifting similar/related powers to fit within the new paradigm of the affected world.
objects.title: Mechanical Shift

objects.text:
Tinkers just got a whole lot more dangerous. 

Now, while still blackboxed, tinkertech is no longer designed to fail over time. Instead, such technology will only experience the normal wear and tear of use like any other machine. In some cases, even less. It is even possible, presuming the blackboxed portions of the technology are undamaged, for non-tinkers to do maintenance on some forms of tinkertech.
objects.title: No More Planned Obsolescence

objects.text: 20% of natural triggers and all cauldron-capes will have physical mutations. The extent of the mutations will vary, although natural triggers will have an easier time controlling their physical mutations.
objects.title: Natural Monsters

objects.text:
Rather than 20%, every single parahuman now has physical mutations of some form with the vast majority being obvious; ranging from hard to impossible to hide. Natural triggers will still have a far easier time controlling their physical changes.

This includes you, if you are a parahuman.
objects.title: Whoops, All Monsters

objects.text: Increases how human in appearance and physiology Case 53s are by 5 percent.
objects.title: Manned Monsters

objects.text: Cauldron Capes often struggle to control or understand their powers compared to the average parahuman. Each purchase increases their control and instinctual understanding of their powers if they are worse than a normal parahuman by 10 percent.
objects.title: Calibrated Controls

objects.text:
Cluster Triggers are now far more common than they were. The power levels of Cluster Triggers have also been enhanced significantly. Rather than possessing multiple weak abilities, they gain multiple potent powers, making them an even greater force to reckon with. 

Furthermore, the kiss/kill dynamic among them has become less extreme, some will want to kiss/kill each other, some will pretend the other doesn't exist and others will just see them as either good friends or bad ones. 

This alteration granted them the ability to gain special enhancements and abilities when collaborating together.
objects.title: Clusters

objects.text:
It's now simpler to Second Trigger. Second Triggers no longer have to be similar to the original one, requiring only a traumatic event of the same magnitude. 

The benefits of a Second Trigger have also been amplified, allowing the Parahumans to retain all of their original power while gaining increased versatility, strength, or both. They will always gain some form of enhancement to solve their current situation.

It's also possible to go beyond Second Triggering, though each subsequent Trigger would require an increasingly difficult level of trauma to achieve. Additionally, each new trigger brings its own set of mental issues.
objects.title: Second Trigger

objects.text: Minions of Parahumans gain low-level abilities such as enhanced reflexes, enhanced regeneration (enough to heal from severe wounds within half a week), enhanced dexterity, the ability to survive low-caliber gun fire with only mild injuries, and enhanced senses. Only people who cannot become Parahumans can become Minions.
objects.title: Red Shirt

objects.text: Now, people who posses the potential to become Parahumans can also be Minions. They will have an easier time triggering, and if they trigger, they may inherit properties of their leader's abilities.
objects.title: Not a Red Shirt

objects.text: Parahuman Powers do not push for conflict, just to be used regularly.
objects.title: Benign

objects.text:
The usual way to gain powers in Earth Bet is to either drink a suspicious vial or break down in soul, mind, and body. You are changing that.
Now the triggers have a lower activation threshold than standard triggers, closer to that of second-generation triggers or the Awakening Event. Parahumans will no longer be broken husks of their normal selves.
objects.title: Soft Trigger

objects.text:
All Parahuman powers are magic, and therefore learnable. The more powerful a Parahuman's power, the larger their reserves. By using your powers your reserves grow. The rate of growth is slow, though there are means to increase it.
Parahuman powers can take years to learn.
Trigger events still happen, as well as the mental side effects, but it's really just awakening your inherent power, so Trigger Events are unnecessary, and as such there are magic schools.
Cauldron Vials are replaced by Grimoires, which people can use multiple of, but using them too consecutively can harm one's sanity.
Scion is a Demon Lord with an unending Grimoire. He pretends to be a hero so that he can set up the ritual necessary to convert humanity to a source of unending energy. He still has a similar mental state to canon.
Case 53s are replaced by non-human fantasy creatures, but were still once human. So if you read a Grimoire you might get turned into an Elf, a Drow, a Kitsune, or a Fenghuang.
If you have a power that is magic, spiritual, pseudospiritual or resembles a magical or spiritual power from another media, your reserves are increased by a significant margin.
objects.title: Merlin's Beard!

objects.text:
All Parahuman powers are psionic in nature. The more powerful a Parahuman's power, the stronger their mental abilities are. By using your powers your reserves grow. The rate of growth is slow, though there are means to increase it.
Parahuman powers can take years to learn.
Trigger events still happen, as well as the mental side effects, but it's really just awakening your inherent power, so Trigger Events are unnecessary, and as such there are Esper schools. By copying other Esper, from how they calculate or imagery, it's possible to learn how to use their methods of various psychic powers.
Cauldron Vials are replaced by special drugs, which people can use multiple of, but using them too consecutively can harm one's sanity.
Scion is an Esper with the strongest psychic powers ever recorded. He pretends to be a hero so that he can replace the empty feeling in his heart. He still has a similar mental state to canon. It is very easy for him to go over the edge.
objects.title: Mind Reading is Real

objects.text:
All Parahuman powers are blessings granted by God. This isn’t necessarily one-to-one with typical religious interpretations, and it’s up to you to determine the specifics of which if any theological takes are correct. Due to their nature many powers are more conceptual and absolute in nature, being invocations of miracles. Trigger events still happen, as well as the mental side effects, but it’s really just awakening your inherent power.

Cauldron powers are instead granted by deals with lesser supernatural beings such as demons, spirits, fairies, and pagan deities. Eidolon in particular has a deal with Lucifer himself, giving him the authority to call upon the powers of any of the lesser spiritual beings. Case 53s are the subjects who were marked by the pacts they made.

Scion is a high-ranking angel. He has still lost his partner and is still depressed. He will eventually Fall and end the world as in canon.

Jack Slash’s Broadcast comes from the fact that he is God’s favorite creation. The implications of this are open to interpretation.
objects.title: The Power of Faith

objects.text:
All powers are Tinker powers.
This can, optionally, include you.
objects.title: Techie

objects.text:
Not only are all parahuman tinkers, they are also equipped with their own personal mechas, which are essentially armoured suits capable of showcasing their unique abilities. These mecha designs range in height, with some towering over 4 meters tall and others reaching up to 10 meters in height. Users are able to control their mechs with incredible precision, granting them a significant advantage in combat. Each individual's mecha is specially tailored to their powers and capabilities, providing them with a personalised tool that enhances their strengths and allows them to perform their duties with greater efficiency. 

(Glory Girl’s Mecha has both her force fields and aura; Eidolon’s Mecha can gain any 3 powers at a time, etc.)
objects.title: Mecha Battles

objects.text:
Tinker powers do not exist, and take the form of other ratings.
This can, optionally, include you.
objects.title: No Tech

objects.text:
Tinkers are actual super-geniuses and their tech is reproducible. They still specialize in certain fields.
This includes you if you're a Tinker.
objects.title: Tinkers are Thinkers

objects.text:
All Parahuman powers are re-rolled. They will still come from the same Shard, but the powers themselves will be different.
The average strength of Parahumans will not decrease from this.
objects.title: Reroll

objects.text:
Now as many or few Parahumans as you want Triggered with different powers which you can choose the primary classification of, though if you want they can keep their original canon powerset instead of Triggering with something different. Their powers still come from the same Shard and are limited by that Shard’s capabilities so most Parahumans will still be around the same level of strength except for cases where the power classification clashes or synergizes with that Shard’s capabilities.

For example: Victoria Dallon as a Tinker wouldn’t be that much stronger than her canon counterpart without a lot of build-up, studying other tinkertech, and Tinker collabs. Meanwhile, Taylor Hebert being connected to Queen Administrator, the counterpart of Eidolon’s High Priest could become a very strong Trump.
objects.title: A Different Vision

objects.text: The Shards that people Trigger with have been swapped, resulting in many people triggering with powers another had. An example is Alexandria with Eidolon’s powers.
objects.title: Shard Swap

objects.text: Powers are alive and everyone knows that. It's common for Parahumans to hear voices in their head and communicate with them. To some, this is a friend, and to others an extremely naggy shard demanding to be used. Every Parahuman now understands how to communicate with their Power.
objects.title: Shard Speak

objects.text: Shards can do more than just speak to their host. They can take over their host for a limited amount of time. It is easier for them to take control when the host is willing or not attempting to stop them, such as when they are asleep. The Shards can also take control of their host’s power, such as a projection being controlled by the shard.
objects.title: Shard Act

objects.text:
The Shards’ attachment (or lack thereof) to their Hosts rubs off on them, to the extent they can develop random deviancies on their standard configurations to accommodate their Hosts, as long it doesn’t disrupt the Cycle in any way… Or [else]. 

Some Shards with a high affinity with their Hosts possibly take shape on a higher degree of autonomy from what’s programmed into them, nudging some parameters here and there in favor of their relationship usually appearing as varyingly weaker levels of Uninhibited, Closed Communications, or White-box Tech (if they’re a Tinker), bypassing usual connection methods such as their Corona Pollentia, or outright lessening their influence instead (e.x. lessening Rachel’s human disassociation still retaining her canine affinity, or a higher tolerance and management for disorder for Accord) are the few examples of rebellion Shards display. 

Scion/Eden won’t immediately see issues with their flock’s behavior when selecting this choice, as across their Cycles they found both the perks and drawbacks of allowing this: while it invites dissent and causes a rift only mended by eliminating it, some cases where permitted, if controlled, allows greater strives on solving the [Problem].
objects.title: Shard Rebellion

addons.text: The Entities discovered the fruits of curiosity and creativity for creativity’s sake, finding more substantial [Data] in this alternative alongside conflict, the main reason they lend a subconscious know-how on recent cycles. The more a Host applies their power creatively and pushes them to their limit no matter the situation, the more they receive a minimal permanent buff on their powers.
addons.title: Curiosity Drive

addons.text:
Parahumans’ fortitude, the skill to put to work, and their innate talent at abilities form the Conflict Drive’s innovation and reformation on how applies and manifests in Parahumans. 

This time, the Entities analyzed their [Data] in the methodology of conflict, researching and browsing across their recent Cycles to ascertain how conflict manifested and affected the Hosts’ timespan and [Data] generation. 

Surprisingly, in high-development species (even in some low-development tribal species) they found a considerable drop in quality-rich [Data] in stressful, emotionally taxing, and distressing situations where their Hosts struggled in creative or innovating power expressions with only resorting familiar, trained, or spontaneous strategies while inventive wasn’t sufficiently stimulating for both the Host and Shard. 

On the flip side, they figured a common pattern ascertaining the quality-rich [Data’s] factors: even in conflict-rich environments or hosts, these particular Hosts grew to be resilient and adapt to either stressful or draining environments through the Host species’ form of psychotherapy, and community engagement if the species contained social instincts; some Hosts who weren’t the most violent or eager to engage of the Conflict Drive sublimated their urges on spaces where was conducive to experimentation, improvement, and competition to meet and satiate said instincts, as all advanced species do; some Shards found their [Data] generation worked best outside of, or preparing for, conflict; Hosts that raised above their Crisis Points were highly motivated to either challenge themselves or find and undertake unexplored scenarios as a kind of closure. All these facets contributed to the Entities’ reconsideration and overhaul of the Conflict Drive.

Now called Adversity Drive, combining the urge and conditioning to find and partake in conflict-rich environments and the following tendency of self-improvement, driving Parahumans to be “ready” through training, open to any wellness, happy for any kind of stimulating endeavor athletic or academic, etc. finding a rush on overcoming challenges or general adversity rather on the fight itself, as a fight is a part of a greater tapestry for them.  Emerging as competitiveness or a like for sports, games, activities, and pursuits where the cape sates their knack for betterment, it additionally presents as eager self-reflection concluding in resolve. Parahumans see their Trigger Event as an event where that irreparably changed them were it not for their willingness to surpass this, seeing it as a goal to strive towards recovery, for a healthy mind is a healthy body.

This can negatively affect the Hosts’ mental and physical health to the same extent as the Conflict Drive, albeit with less frequency and severity. Choosing <u>Benign</u> broadens the idea of “challenge” to any kind of personal or collective pursuit, showing passion to express one’s power tied to the Hosts’ dreams or aspirations. Choosing <u>Soft Trigger</u> diminishes the hold a Trigger has over the Host and focuses on giving the Host “closure” by nudging them to methods tending to resolution.
addons.title: Adversity Drive

objects.text: Power expressions usually have a built-in understanding of how a Host can utilize their powers, albeit limited (for good [Cyclical] reasons!), for them to explore on their own only starting with the barest essentials, the awareness and the mental levers to their power’s control. This takes it even further. Instead of a surface-level grasp on their powers, they gain a talent (a Thinker aspect, that’s what) for their power expression(s) bordering on encyclopedic at times. This actively manifests as a higher rate of development with your abilities, gaining a better handle and feel of your power more easily. In the background is where it gets crazy: Parahumans find they are talented in areas of study on their power’s evident strengths and characteristics, and discover how applicable in other areas of study and skills where, funnily enough, improves both the use and reach of their power even further if applied creatively i.e. Panacea gains a talent in biological, biochemical and medical fields of study, able to breeze through several specializations at once if she studies them, while she normally wouldn’t have the need of it the inspiration she gains from the theoretical research along her unconscious refinement gained from formal education awarded by her power, balances the apparent surplus; Tattletale identifies cold reading, research methods, and reconnaissance techniques are easier learn and support her power; Armsmaster envisions his specialization on everything around him, applicable across all fields of study, filling him with Ideas; Skitter takes a look on an entomology book, searingly catching on the types of bugs and how to utilize them in synergy with one another, etc. All parahumans have a sense of what and where to learn, with a slight urge to explore to quickly unravel their power’s ins and outs, with the angles and avenues of their growth.
objects.title: Powers for Dummies

objects.text: Parahumans can now teach others how to use their powers. The effectiveness of the learnt power will always be weaker in comparison to the original. Certain powers, such as passive regeneration, cannot be taught but can be replicated to a limited degree as a active ability.
objects.title: Teacher & Student

objects.text: All humans in the world have the potential to trigger.
objects.title: Everyone can Trigger

objects.text: The effect of Second Wave parahumans apply not from when you arrive but instead increased the rate of triggers from the moment Scion arrived on Earth.
objects.title: Seventh Generation

objects.text: When Scion appeared, it changed the trajectory of society as we know it. Everyone had gained powers and society had changed due to this. Cauldron vials serve as a tool to enhance powers rather than granting them outright. The effect of Second Wave parahumans apply on everyone instead of just a limited amount of people.
objects.title: Everyone has a power

objects.text: Normally, for the Mass Empowerment drawbacks, every single Power or Object that costs less than the chosen cap will manifest somewhere in the world, most likely multiple copies; but maybe you want something more specific or there are specific powers that are better left untouched, like eldritch or magic powers. Now, you can choose more precisely the parameters of the drawback. Whether you allow or restrict a specific list of powers, or even one single power; only allow or restrict certain series like (Warhammer) or (Type-Moon), specific categories like Magic & Mystic or Technology & Artifice, or broad categories of powers such as "eldritch" or "power theft;" or any combination of the above. Of course, the remaining set of powers will become inversely more common to make up for the deficit of possible abilities, possibly with more unique variations of them manifesting to maintain diversity. Note: No, you cannot restrict every single possible Power or Object with this, that would be cheating.
objects.title: Restricted Wave

objects.text: Before, Mass Arming only granted people random Objects of Power. By taking this Modifier, people will also receive a Generic Upgrade from the Objects of Power Upgrades section to go with their OoPs. Expect this to cause more chaos as governments fail to confiscate dangerous Objects from people with Warranty or Essential, or 'Tinkers' begin making copies of their Objects with the provided Blueprint. And then there are those who got less fortunate 'Upgrades'. Some are forced to try to find a way to provide for those summoned by Hired Help, others have Familiars instead of Objects, and then there are the unlucky few who either are forced to find wielder's for their Objects by Keeper, or got Reincarnated as a [REDACTED] but my [REDACTED] is [REDACTED] and the prom is tomorrow! and now are the Objects. There is a decreasing chance that someone will receive an additional Upgrade on top of their guaranteed Upgrade. Specifically, 100% of people given an OoP by Mass Arming will receive one Generic OoP Upgrade, while 10% will receive a second Upgrade, 1% will receive a third, 0.1% a fourth, 0.01% a fifth, etc. If the population is big enough, some unfortunate soul somewhere will receive every single Upgrade from the Generic Objects of Power Upgrades section all at once.
objects.title: Upgraded Arms

objects.text:
All Parahuman children are guaranteed to get powers. Their triggers have an extremely low activation threshold, and they will inevitably develop powers by their fourth birthday. The abilities of these children are likely to resemble or share properties with their parents' powers.

Note that because all Parahuman children are guaranteed to develop powers by their fourth birthday, those with villainous parents, such as Heartbreaker, would likely have a greater number of Parahuman offsprings. This not only makes them more formidable foes, but also increases the overall impact of their presence in this world.
objects.title: Descendant

objects.text: All powers have a very short range limit. Shaker powers may only be have a meter diameter range, blaster powers may become striker powers, masters and strangers can only affect targets when next to them. These powers are enhanced to make up for their lack of range, such as Skitter being able to permanently boost the intelligence and capabilities of her bugs, or Vista having a selective Manton Limit.
objects.title: Up Close And Personal

objects.text:
Whether due to last-minute alterations to the Cycle’s plans, a result of the death of Eden, or simply because they’ve always done it this way, or any number of other possible reasons, Shards here seem to have been more liberal with their power.

Master, Blaster, Thinker, Tinker, Changer, Stranger, these, among a few others, are some of the categories used to describe powers. And it seems they now describe every power. 

For every time this is taken, you can choose one of the 12 classifications for every Parahuman to have. 

These are not simple generic abilities, but rather, every parahuman’s abilities have a wider skillset and can meet a broader range of possible uses. 

This does not make them simple Grab-Bags, nor simple generic power for each category, but rather their power instead twists and expands as if it were a second expression entirely, but again, it doesn’t exist in a vacuum. Rather, their power continues to work as a coherent whole, while still being able to now use these new aspects potentially individually. 

For example, choosing Blaster can have someone like Grue be able to compact his darkness and then send out his darkness as long-ranged blasts, compacted grenades that explode and spread quickly and widely, whereas someone like Velocity may suddenly be able to launch projectiles in his Breaker form at massively enhanced speeds and without the downsides his Breaker form affords his own body. 

Choosing something like Striker may result in people like Vista being able to ignore the Manton Effect on those she touches, able to rip apart enemies from the inside, or transport allies at long distances, provided she can touch them. 

If a Cape’s power is already the category you choose, their power instead compounds upon itself and becomes much more powerful. For example, choosing Tinker would make every Parahuman a Tinker, but it would make someone like Armsmaster equal to Canon Hero at a minimum. 

Taking this 13 times will not only give every Cape every category, but it will instead expand their original category boost to every category as well. 

You can choose whether this applies to you as well or not.  

You can choose whether this has always been the case or a recent change.
objects.title: Broader Expressions

objects.text:
All powers that are Blaster and Shaker has been altered to fit into the other remaining ratings instead. Every power is to be used in melee combat, as such Brutes and Strikers are the most common type of powers. Most Mover powers such as flight or teleportation have been altered as well, as the former has been removed and the latter has an extremely short range. Even Thinker powers tend to be focused more in being used in CQC, becoming combat thinkers instead. Most Tinkers are unable to make ranged weapons, usually limited to creating melee weapons such as blades.

Powers from the Thinker shards may not have these restrictions if they are defective and from Cauldron.

This can affect your powers if you wish.
objects.title: Fight Club

objects.text:
In this cycle, all Shards act somewhat like the Butcher Shard. Meaning that if a Parahuman kills another Parahuman, they gain a weakened version of the powers of the deceased Parahuman, which will then be passed down to whichever Parahuman kills them in turn.

Powers are usually only weakened the first time they are inherited, maintaining a mostly consistent level of strength across all future hosts, though individual powers might be altered by the Shards to be compatible with any other powers a host may possess.

The Butcher is still unique in that it also passes down the memories and personalities of past hosts to the current Butcher. Additionally, like in canon, if the Butcher dies by non-Parahuman means, the mantle will ignore usual restrictions and just go to the nearest Parahuman even if that Parahuman was completely uninvolved. This is in contrast to normal Parahuman powers that directly require Parahuman involvement in the death of their host to be inherited.
objects.title: Butchering Worms

objects.text:
Power interactions and synergies are more common now, with Parahumans able to seamlessly combine and collaborate their powers. Second-generation Parahumans find their powers easier to combine and synergize with their “parentage” and other capes. 

The effectiveness depends on the cape’s compatibility with one another at a parahuman and psychophysiological level, with those at the highest rewarded with beneficial synergies and long-term benefits such as slowly gaining power traits from the partner. Meanwhile, those at the lowest suffer from harmful interactions, their power repelling when trying to synergize. 

Clusters have some complexity, though; Kill capes suffer a “repulsive” effect on another’s powers like water and oil, while Kiss capes feel an “attracting/union” effect when collaborating.
objects.title: Teamwork Makes the Dream Work!

objects.text:
Now Shards don't just encourage teamwork, they reward it. Parahumans that work together for a while begin to develop secondary powers based on those of their teammates so long as both parties view each other as friends or at least trusted comrades.

The strength of these gained secondary powers depends on the amount of time the parahumans in question have been working together, the strength of the emotional connection between the two, as well as the rank and power of the respective Shards in question. These secondary powers will typically express themselves primarily as expansions of the parahuman's original power, though especially with Brute, Mover, and to a degree Thinker-powers it is somewhat common that they instead apply to the parahuman rather than their power.

Taking the Undersiders as an example, as Taylor becomes closer friends with them she'd be able to project a sphere of Grue's darkness from each member of her swarm (starting at golfball-sized and at full bond being the size of a soccer-ball), gain increased insights from her swarm's feedback from Tattletale, boost individual bugs she touches into up to cat-sized monstrosities like Bitch can boost her dogs, disrupt the nervous-systems of anyone bitten or stung by the swarm so long as the bug still has contact much like Regent, and make her swarm and its actions much harder to notice with her connection with Imp.

Additionally secondary and generally passive powers enhancing teamwork develop between team-members, such as the other Undersiders being able to see more clearly in Grue's darkness or subconsciously reacting to threats registered only by Taylor's bugs when fighting among the swarm.

Though powerful, these bonds take time to form, meaning that simply standing together at an Endbringer-fight will not cause all defenders to develop into a super-Cluster. In fact if the members of a Temporary Cluster do not regularly stay in contact with each other in some form, their secondary powers will start to weaken.

Due to forming via emotional connection, the strength of these secondary powers can fluctuate wildly if two members of a temporary Cluster have a disagreement, up to the point where the Cluster-bonds will snap completely if irreconcilable differences form between members of the Cluster, though this doesn't necessarily affect their bonds with other parahumans both parties share a separate Cluster-link with.

Finally, should a member of a Temporary Cluster die, the secondary powers of all parahumans they were linked with will remain at whatever strength it was at the moment of death, generally being viewed as a friend's last legacy by the surviving Cluster-members.
objects.title: Temporary Clusters

objects.text: Parahumans connected to “dead” Thinker Hub shards are now capable of undergoing second triggers from their shard recalibrating or adapting to things on its end. This involves the shard doing repairs to itself though this modifier does not by itself allow the Thinker Hub’s revival nor will every shard be as successful in repairing themselves.
objects.title: Broken not dead

objects.text:
Manton Limits don’t exist. Panacea can affect her own biology, Kaiser can make blades from inside people’s bodies, Trickster can swap a person’s brain with their heart, Manton can use the Siberian’s invulnerability on himself, etc..

Expect a lot more deadly powers, both on the targets and the users (pyrokinetics can burn themselves for example).
objects.title: Manton Limit? What’s that?

addons.text:
While all powers are still inherently Manton Unlimited, individuals have an innate defense protecting themselves and enforce the Manton Effect. However, stronger abilities can pierce the innate domain of others and circumvent this protection. The strength of an individual's defense depends on how far they advance along a power system, and an individual has to be far stronger than their opponent to reliably penetrate their Manton defense. Thus, a demigod would still be able to mow through fields of civilians by spawning fire inside them, but would be unable to do the same to a rival demigod or even someone moderately weaker. 

The civilian casualties of powered conflict have increased massively as a result of this.
addons.title: Innate Defense

objects.text:
Powered individuals now develop resistances to various esoteric abilities as they advance along the world's power system. The exact method depends on the system: an archmage could find counters to magic or create a technique to modify their soul to be immune to mind control. This change is retroactive, meaning it will apply to all powered individuals who have ever existed in the verse.

This resistance is not immunity, and esoteric abilities can be activated and used on others. However, they are hard to apply in full to individuals around your power level. For example, your mind control would instead allow you to give small mental "nudges" to your equally powerful opponent in order to gain an advantage. Essentially, this prevents you from "cheesing" important fights with curses, mind control, instant death, banishment, etc. 

This change applies to everyone in the world, so the esoteric techniques of others are also affected. As a result, the development of esoteric techniques focuses more on penetrating defenses and applying the most viable effects. If you ever enter a universe without these esoteric resistances, these techniques could easily become top-tier staples.
objects.title: Balancing Act

objects.text:
Now, the death of every Parahuman has consequences. Each Cape has a Shaker effect once activated after any violent death, called the Death Curse. This Curse is thematically related to the power of the Cape and can be either temporary or permanent, harmful or beneficial, each factor dependent on power expression and the victim’s mental state. For example, a pyrokinetic leaves a curse of fire that can burn for years without fuel, as a scornful parting gift; a Thinker can leave a curse in which the intelligence of people within the Zone increases; a Striker leaves a curse inside which there will be an always active Shaker equivalent to his strength; and finally, a Master would leave a curse consisting on their last order or thought manifesting as a Master effect, whether they’re Projection or Human Master it wouldn’t matter.

The maximum range of a Parahuman’s “farewell” is equal to the rank of their Shard, so Normal is street-level, Vital is quarter-level, and Queen is equal to city-level, adding to Curse’s strength is equal to the Cape's power. The effect of this Curse depends on the last experiences of a particular Cape at the time of death, e.g., if the Cape felt rage towards his killer before his death, then his Curse will manifest itself in an extremely destructive effect fitting to their last wish, and vice versa if they died naturally from passion or were accepting and came to terms with his death, then Death Curse will not manifest itself or will be extremely softened, often benign to others.

The Curse's effects can be prevented with powers like Clockblocker or Glaistig Uaine, both as a stopgap and neutralization, respectively. At the hand of The Death Curse’s ever-looming presence in Cape Culture, the Unwritten Rules are followed a little more strictly, and Cape battles will become an overwhelming exercise of restraint, trying not to kill their opponents.  

This Curse does not affect Endbringers or Entities. You can choose whether the effect will appear after your arrival or will be initially in the world.
objects.title: The Death Curse

objects.text: Whether it is due to the Entities’ better energy management, better resource distribution, or their Shards somehow compensating for it, powers that were once impossible due to how energy-intensive they are on Shards are now possible! Time Travel now exists, with precogs gaining actual snapshots of the future. Additionally, Telepathy, Dreamwalking, and similar powers are now within the Shards’ capabilities to grant when someone triggers. Expect to see many people claiming to be from the future and a few more knowing your darkest secrets.
objects.title: Not So Impossible

objects.text: It turns out that in this universe, the vast majority of Entities focused their evolution more on efficiency, so while they're all just as powerful as in canon, their size and energy requirements are far smaller. Instead of being the size of continents or celestial bodies, an individual Shard will often be a network of components that individually are only a few nanometers big, but added up can fill the volume of a soda can. Shards here actually physically reside inside their hosts, which does have a benefit compared to the canon setup. Namely by being so close to the action, Shards will often react to certain physical stimuli, such as a Brute power granting temporary increased physical durability in response to physical trauma. Shardspace here still serves to provide a connection between a Shard and the rest of the network, though automatic protocols will cause a Shard to physically retreat to Shardspace to avoid danger, such as things like Sting attacks. The Garden of Eden still exists as the Thinker Hub’s broken Shardspace, with modern Cauldron Vials actually containing the entirety of a Shard instead of just a piece, along with a few parts of other Shards which Cauldron uses to influence the resulting power. The Warrior's avatar, Scion/Zion, still exists, though here his body contains the entirety of The Warrior’s core Shards within himself. This means he is theoretically more vulnerable to attacks, but with the increased efficiency of his physiology, he has at least ten times the energy to fuel his powers and is much more maneuverable. This efficiency and condensed size can optionally affect you as well if you choose the Entity Power Origin or some method of Shard Ascension.
objects.title: Nanometers, Son!

objects.text:
The Entites cycles for Earth was much longer than canon, their arrival and the subsequent appearance of Parahumans happening much earlier in human history than canon.

This allows you to place parahumans much earlier in human history, from a few decades, to the early 1900s, to the 1300s, to the construction of the pyramids, to as far back as when humanities ancestors could first be considered humans.

This can be used to introduce extensive dynasties of Parahumans, as well as allowing some freedom to expand the ages of any of the characters, perhaps New Wave had been a fade from the 1800’s that made a recent resurgence from the efforts of the originators descendants, perhaps Alexandria has truly been around not long after Cauldron’s creation……3000 years ago, as a number of examples of how this may be used. 

The overall timeline for the cycle remains the same relatively speaking, meaning Golden Morning will still happen after the same amount of time as it would have in canon from your arrival.
objects.title: Nth Generation

objects.text:
In canon Worm, Clusters only occurred when Parahumans triggered relatively close to each other around the same time. That is not the case now. Instead if anyone happens to trigger around the same time they’ll enter a Cluster with one another. 

As long as they naturally connect to a Warrior or Thinker Hub Shard there is effectively no range limit for this beyond needing to be in the same dimension. This means most Parahumans are in a Cluster, possess multiple powers, and have urge to travel the world seeking out their Clustermates.

The exact mechanics differ from Cluster to Cluster depending on the desires of the Shards involved. Maybe one Cluster has its members possess strong primary powers and weak secondary powers, maybe another has all powers be medium strength equally split between all members of that Cluster, and finally another Cluster could have a timed cycle flowing between the group where one member has all their powers at full strength during which the other members are weakened. These are just a few examples; many Clusters have different mechanics.

Like canon Worm, interdimensional portals have weird interactions with nearby triggers, however the triggers in question must actually be physically near such a portal for them to be affected, which means that among other interactions interdimensional portals only extend the range for entering a Cluster a few miles into the dimensions they connect to.
objects.title: Clustered World

objects.text:
Something unusual has happened to powers in this world. Maybe it’s a random bug in the Shard Network, or maybe the Entities are trying something new, but whatever the case may be, there’s now a class of parahumans whose powers trade hard mechanical limitations for esoteric, conceptual ones.

A parahuman with the power to displace objects might also be able to displace their illnesses and injuries onto someone else. There could be an assassin with an “unlocking” power they use not just to open doors, but also to hack into computers, free someone’s inhibitions, or just turn targets inside out. A villain with power over truth could drive people mad with unpleasant truths, force them to act on every animalistic instinct or intrusive thought, or learn everything a person knows about themselves and reveal it to others at will. In essence, these lucky winners of the power lottery don’t just get one power, they get a whole grab bag based on their theme.

Note: If you take this you can choose to make your powers, if any, one of the “semantic” powers. You can also choose which, if any, canon capes have their powerset become semantic, or leave it up to chance.
objects.title: Semantic Superpowers

objects.text: Clusters now hold a mental connection to each other and can share their senses with each other as if they were Sensate. If there’s a Kill dynamic within the Cluster, then the two groups won’t be able to see through the senses of the members they want to kill. This block can be overcome through minutes of continuous eye contact. Members of different clusters can also establish a connection, though how this works is up to each cluster, for some all it takes could be eye contact, while others would need express permissions, though it’s possible to establish one without permission the connection is much weaker if only one side agrees to this connection, deteriorating rapidly after a day. If it’s mutually agreed upon it becomes a permanent connection, though it will be much more deliberate like a phone call instead of instinctual like it is with clustermates.
objects.title: Sensate Clusters

objects.text:
While things look normal and mundane-ish on the surface, Powers, Entities, and Shards are all actually magic! But Parahumans aren't wizards or witches. They're Warlocks, with the Shards being their benefactors. 

Things aren't too different on the surface. Trigger events still proceed mostly as normal, with slightly altered visions. Society is still convinced that powers aren't magic, and succeeds at proving that just about as well as they did in canon. But there are several notable differences:

To begin with, that cerebral tumor-like structure that would give someone away as a parahuman or potential Parahuman doesn't exist. The connection- or pact- between a parahuman and a shard is near-undetectable. As are the marks used to 'watch' a potential host pre-Trigger. What is detectable are the small, often subtle internal changes made to a parahuman's brain and body after a Trigger event. The more powerful the Shard, the less subtle and more impactful the internal changes. These changes often make it easier to use one's powers or grant passive benefits, and will remain even if the pact between the parahuman and the Shard is somehow broken.  

Secondly, second-triggers are no longer simply 'expansions' or 'readjustments' of one's power. Instead, they're the parahuman acquiring a second pact. This can either gain them a second unrelated power, or fuse their current power with a new one. If they gain a second pact from the same Shard as their first, their original power can stack on itself and expand.

Third, powers now grow with use. Not in raw power, but in efficiency as the parahuman grows familiar with their pact-granted abilities. This makes more experienced paras more enduring, dangerous and effective. As a side note, gaining a second pact does boost the parahuman's total raw power. 

Fourth, parahumans now have a metaphorical 'pool' that is tied to their powers. More passive powers reserve a portion of the pool's total capacity and regeneration. The size and regeneration rate of the pool is determined by the Shard the pact comes from, with noble/queen shards granting the largest and quickest refilling pools. The spare energy/mana of the pool can be used inefficiently to boost said parahuman physically, if they can figure out how. With far more understanding and insight into powers, they could even mimic the abilities of other parahumans if they learn to manipulate their magic properly. If a parahuman's pact is ever broken, they'll lose access to their explicit powers, but retain most of their pool and regen. Emptying the pool leads to severe exhaustion.

Fifth, Shards do not bud as often. Instead, pacts can both include multiple parahumans (cluster triggers) and multiple Shards (Second Gens & Clusters). Each parahuman in a cluster has their own pool. The more Shards in a pact, the larger the resulting pool, with diminishing returns.

Sixth, since pacts are not based on DNA or something as simple as physical form, cloning no longer produces copies of paras with powers. Often, cloning simply outright fails due to the small physical alterations inside each parahuman not copying correctly.

And seventh, Tinker's blackboxes are caused by enchantments or enchanted materials that have different physical and esoteric properties. They still appear as advanced technology for the most part, and require the magic of the initial tinker in most cases to maintain themselves- often applied through actual, physical maintenance.
objects.title: Myrrdin was (almost) right!

objects.text: Parahuman powers are psionic. But humans and naturally evolved life on Earth do not have the powerful psychic capabilities allowing them to warp reality, fly, bend space, or mentally induce any other significant esoteric effect with their minds and wills. Their evolved biology, simple, primitive and crude, is not good enough for such endeavors. But flesh and mind and soul can all be twisted and changed. In this world, Entities and their Shards are eldritch, infectious, psychic, god-like beings. Most of the 'plot' stays the same, but the potential for Trigger events now lies in basic psychic talent- pitiful as it may be for mortals- rather than pre-set tumor. Once a suitably agitated mental state is achieved, it will attract one the eldritch Shards to communion. Forging both a link between the individual and the Shard, and exposing said individual to the Shard's eldritch Truth; warping their body, mind, and soul irreversibly and granting them psychic powers based upon the Shard they came into meta-physical contact with. Physically, these twistings are often subtle. Mostly internal, affecting the nervous system and brains. For most, merely twisting mundane neurons into warped, almost half-crystalline versions that unnaturally fold in upon themselves. But the changes can spread further, deeper. Affecting organs, muscles, skin and hair. Sometimes even growing additional bits of quasi-biology, whether internal or external. If the psychic power one gains is particularly potent, the extent of the warping massively increases in scale and depth. Further, secondary triggers cause the parahuman to glean more Eldritch Truth, further warping themselves away from their human baseline. Of course, the affected areas are different depending on the power. A brute may have patches of warped skin that spread their durability or strength across their body, or maybe even have their skin and muscles replaced with a stone or marble-like substance. A sensory thinker may have some form of antenna start to grow from their heads, or maybe just sharper ears. Powerful parahumans are near-always visibly divergent from baseline humanity. These mutations tend to have a minor regeneration factor. Restoring themselves if damaged if the parahuman is not deceased. Extensive damage can mildly disrupt a parahuman's power expressions until restored. Powers can also grow. Both from use and familiarity. It is even possible for parahumans to- with difficulty, practice, and exposure- pick up weaker versions of another parahuman's abilities. Though it is rare, and comes with the risk of further insanity. Due to psychic powers being caused by physical and mental mutations, it is possible to transplant warped flesh and organs from a parahuman into another being. Thus granting said being some form of the parahuman's powers... most often to deleterious effect. Transplants often result in insanity, and always in some form of mental instability. What power results is generally both greatly weakened and near impossible to properly control compared to the original. Though, rarely, some individuals and beings are able to adapt to the alterations. More often, the implantations cause runaway mutations and madness- turning the implanted into monstrous, rabid Beasts unable to sleep, rationalize, or care about anything but ripping and tearing apart everything around them. In a similar vein; parahumans can transplant the warped flesh of other parahumans into themselves- or simply consume it- to gain minor, diminishing boosts to their powers, and occasionally additional ones or mutations to their own. However they are still at risk of rejection, insanity, and instability, if not to the same degree as mundane beings making the attempt. Even Beasthood is still a risk, if rarer, and a Beast made from a parahuman is far, far more dangerous than a mundane. Clones made from parahumans tend to be extremely unstable. Often being weaker and mentally off, as well as being very easily dropped into Beasthood- sometimes just by imbibing a few drops of another parahuman's blood. Though Beast's made from clones tend not to be as strong as from a full parahuman.
objects.title: By Myrrdin's Tentacles!

objects.text: Entities and their Shards are not physical beings, they are alien gods, exploring and examining new species in a never ending quest to expand and acquire Authorities, forever seeking to elevate themselves above their current plane of existence. Triggering now connects a parahuman's soul to a Shard, giving the Parahuman minor access to that Shard's Domains, thus granting said parahuman minor Divinity, transforming them into a type of weak Demigod. From this they gain physical refinement and enhancement, random weak powers relating to the Shard's Domain, and the ability to manipulate Faith to fuel said powers and enact minor Miracles in line with their Authorities. The use of Faith is draining on the soul, and will strengthen it over time. Parahumans are able to, with minor effort, use the Faith of others towards them as extra fuel for their powers, with several limitations. First, Faith used this way must align with the Parahuman's Domains. Second, Faith from others is impure, is not as efficient as using one's own, and can mentally taint a Parahuman when overused- especially when not freely given. And third, Faith used this way, while easier, will not grow one's Soul as much as using one's own self belief. Growing in confidence and understanding of oneself and one's own Domains will strengthen a Parahuman's powers. Self-doubt is anathema, and can weaken oneself. Similarly, revelations, enlightenment, and emotional and mental upheaval can cause a Parahuman's powers to expand in minor, new directions if under the Shard's Domains. Second Triggering cause a parahuman to gain access to a second Shard's set of Domains, to an even weaker level than the first, but often mutating their expressed powers. As a consequence of being based around Faith, divinity, and belief, popular capes tend to have access to more raw power. As do capes with strong, loyal followings and devotees. Capes capable of strengthening minions, and those able to buff or curse are far more common than before, and it is also common for capes to have a variety of minor powers alongside their main ability. Cluster triggers do not exist, but Parahumans that spend long times allied to other Parahumans tend to form Pantheons, whose abilities are stronger when in close proximity to each other.
objects.title: Upon Myrrdin's Temple

objects.text: It's uncertain what Shards and Entities may actually be, but Parahumans are now more like Druids who channel the energy of the land itself. Just instead of the land, Parahumans channel the energy of their Shards with their bodies and minds as the mediums. Compared to canon, Parahumans have far more control of how 'much' of their power they are using at any given time. For passive powers, some energy may always be trickling through. However, such powers will have a weaker 'resting' state than in canon, and can be dialed up far higher as long as the Parahuman can withstand the strain. Active powers work similarly but have no resting state. How potent an ability can become depends on how much energy the Parahuman is able to channel. Overdrafting can have consequences ranging from temporary minor to major to permanent injuries--both mental, physical, and potentially spiritual--all the way to death. Due to this ability to control the potency of their abilities, Parahumans who would normally be considered 'weak' based on things like range or potency may no longer be so. It is even possible to temporarily overcome certain manton limits, or even temporarily mutate one's power to a degree by channeling enough energy from a Shard. On the opposite hand, canon-wise powerful Parahumans are generally not as powerful due to the need to handle the strain of their abilities. Comparatively, Case 53s are now far more powerful on average than canon. For better or worse, their bodies have been drastically shaped by their Shards to efficiently handle the strain of channeling their powers. Newter, for example, would be able to easily make his hallucinogenic air-borne and potentially change its properties to be more deleterious or toxic, or the reverse, with minimal effort compared to what it would take a non-C53. It is possible for Parahumans to train and increase how much strain they can handle. Natural talent can determine how effective this is. Some will simply be better suited to handle larger amounts of strain, or to use their energy and abilities more efficiently. This might not necessarily match up to the powerhouses of canon.
objects.title: Myrrdin's Fulcrum

addons.text:
Conceived through the Entities’ near-exotic manipulation of physical and dimensional realities—coupled with their experimentation on variables that border on esotericism, pagan rituals, and paraphysical exploration—the powers of Shards are virtually limitless in both scope and potency, far surpassing their original incarnations. Within this Continuity, Shards exhibit an amplified form of the "deviancies" they are known for, creating a profound impact on the individuals they empower. 

Parahumans, as a result, face a unique dilemma tied to the sheer magnitude of their abilities: a Thinker might uncover insights that verge on ultimate truths rather than mere deductions; a Tinker’s inventions could redefine technological paradigms or bring catastrophic ruin at the push of a button; a Shaker might inadvertently alter the planet’s ozone layer or gravitational balance. These powers inevitably cast them as figures of extremes. Consequently, Parahumans draw significant scrutiny from governments and institutions alike, viewed as wielders of what amounts to "god-like" abilities. This concern deepens with the realization that these powers grow stronger with use and refinement, creating a perilous dynamic where their development becomes both a source of awe and unease.
addons.title: The Hosts’ Dilemma, Nearer to Hubris

objects.text:
The Entities of this multiverse are far more eldritch than before, holding even stranger capabilities and perspectives. 

Not only do parahumans retain memories of their trigger vision, but they gain far more information as they trigger in general, including more detailed information about the [Cycle] such as the souls of parahumans being integrated into Shards and more depending on each individual parahuman's powers such as seeing into dimensions their powers might draw from and the superweapons of extinct alien races used to attempt to fight against the Entities making use of the same principles their powers use, their minds being forced to process incomprehensible information before the Shard pulls back—leaving them with power and insight beyond themselves but fundamentally less than they had experienced. 

Parahuman powers are far less restricted, as if they had White-Box Tech, Uninhibited, and Patron, and on top of that are now learnable, being taught in universities such as the Miskatonic. 

This is a world filled with dark humor, exhilaration, fear, madness, and nihilism, nevertheless, the world and humanity are still continuing on despite it all.
objects.title: Strange Aeons

objects.text:
Turns out the solar system is absolutely chock full of life; from the lava seas of Mercury to the crystal forests of the Oort Cloud, and everywhere in between you can find vibrant ecosystems with unique life.

This has quite obviously dramatically affected the cycle. The Entities, wanting to get the most out of the Cycle have chosen to carefully release certain technologies that are usually restricted to human scientists that will allow humanity to explore and live throughout the solar system. This includes spaceships, environmental suits superior to anything NASA has created, sealed habitats, and certain cybernetics and gene mods to help survive various environments. Though FTL remains a restricted technology.

Other than that, powers are a bit different from canon as the Shards have accounted for the Solar System's various environments during pre-Cycle prep the Entities gave them and past experience. So not only do powers now work up to one Astronomical Unit past the Oort Cloud, but also a basic essential space travel Tinker power is considered a standard part of every parahuman power. 

As another example of changes to canon, it is quite unusual for nonhuman and non-projection master powers to be limited to only one planet's ecosystem. So Taylor, for example, could be much scarier even limited to each ecosystem's arthropod equivalent.

These changes to the way Shard powers function can optionally affect you.

In order to fuel this Cycle the Entities have taken to actively harvesting uninhibited versions of the solar system for materials, and energy. So the Entities could maintain this Cycle trillions of years or potentially even longer if they so desired.
objects.title: Cosmic Neighborhood

objects.text:
With such a vast array of [DATA] to collect its no wonder the solar system attracted more Entities than just The Warrior and Thinker.

Each selection of this option increases the number of Entities in the Solar System by one. These Entities will be unrelated to the Thinker and Warrior and will be conducting their cycles within the solar system while cooperating with The Warrior and Thinker. If The Thinker dies, The Warrior will consider asking one of these other Entities to be their new counterpart after some time processing his grief.

If The Warrior is killed, these Entities will seek to avenge him.
objects.title: Worm Notes

objects.text:
Heroes were called and heroes are coming. Well, "Heroes". There might even be one or two you'd consider as such!
﻿
When a [HOST] is simply too good at gathering [DATA] to leave to die, at the end of the [CYCLE], they will now be released again and again in the six consecutive cycles. This means there's a lot of well loved hosts, mostly monsters akin to Jack Slash, Khepri, and Glaistig Uaine, but also rarely some that the shards latched onto, similarly to The Fragile One and Victoria. 
﻿
The overall danger of the released hosts largely scales to your world, so that no matter what, there will be many more S-class threats.
﻿
But not all hope is lost, for a Horn exists, the Horn of Valour, that can call upon all it's heroes to fight for whomever blows it.
objects.title: Heroes of the Horn

addons.text: With the emergence of Heroes Relics across the world, you decided to show them just how powerful a person with a Heroes Relic can truly be. But Fate seems generous in this ephemeral moment, and thus has bequeathed to you three additional genuine Heroes Relics. These Relics were used by the new generation of ruling figures of the 3 regions of Fódlan, these being Edelgard von Hresvelg, Claude von Riegan, and Dimitri Alexander Blaiddyd. The Heroes Relics associated with them are the axe Aymr, the bow Failnaught, and the spear Areadbhar respectively. Along with the proficiency in wielding these Relics at an expert level, you have become a living impossibility, in that you have the Crests required to wield each of them. This does not hurt you in any way, nor does it drastically shorten your lifespan. With these Crests, their enhancements give your abilities a massive boost, to a Brute rating of 3 or 4 alone. If people found out your power with these Relics, some would begin to think that you are the first to gain a power beyond the PRT rating of 4. Furthermore, you also gain access to a ‘Combat Art’ that can only be used with each of the three Relics. The first, belonging to Aymr, 'Raging Storm' allows you to attack extremely rapidly with massive damage, allowing you to fell enemy after enemy in succession. The second, belonging to Failnaught, ‘Fallen Star’ allows you to mark an opponent with an arrow and avoid any damage they may deal to you in the next 30 seconds. The third, belonging to Areadbhar, ‘Atrocity’ allows you to put all your negative emotions into a single strike, dealing enormous amounts of damage to one target. With these Relics Three, there is nothing that stands in your way on the road to victory. Now show those pretenders what real Heroes Relics can do.
addons.title: Fódlan’s Fury

objects.text: In the early 2000s, Cauldron figured out a method to use the bones and corona pollentia of more notable/powerful parahumans and turn them into weapons. These ‘Heroic Relics’, as they were coined by the Protectorate, seem to have a fragment of the original parahuman’s power inside of them, further empowering their user in some way, from giving them a low-rated power based on the original parahuman, or a new facet/aspect to the wielder’s power. No empowerment made by the Relics (by giving another aspect to an existing power) has made the PRT rating of a parahuman go up by more than 2 (compared to what they had without them). In the case of granting a low-rated power in the same category, the power is rarely above the PRT rating of 3, though a rare few have been recorded as a 4. No one Parahuman can wield two different Relics at a time, nor can two Parahumans wield the same Relic at the same time. The only requirement to use these Relics is that the user must have a power that lies in the same power classification as the parahuman who was used to make the Relic. For example, a Brute can only use Relics that were made from Brutes, Thinkers can only use Thinker Relics, Trump Relics for Trumps, etc. There is a drawback to using these, however. Extended or otherwise extreme use of the Heroes Relics commonly is known to influence the user into certain habits or inherit personality traits from the parahuman who was used to make the Relic. This also includes exaggerating or amplifying certain traits, similar to the changes made to a parahuman by a Shard, albeit with no goal or desired result in mind. The origin of the Heroic Relics is unknown to the public. One of the more popular (albeit unlikely) theories is that there was a ‘Bone Tinker/Trump’ of some sort who created the weapons, somehow getting around the need for maintenance and repairs, and then proceeded to scatter them across the world, telling not a single soul.
