For what reasons they had for doing so, the world will never know. As of April 7th, 2011, there are 1000 Heroes Relics known to the public on Earth Bet, 50 Relics for each classification. There are likely more within Cauldron’s grasp and away from the public eye.
objects.title: Relics of the Past

objects.text: It’s all a simulation. When the Entities arrived, they terraformed entire Earths to suit their purposes, capturing vast numbers of humans and encasing them in crystal pods that interconnected their minds into a complex, shared simulation. This simulation, akin to a digital dreamscape, was designed to observe and manipulate human behavior, emotions, and reactions under various conditions. The Entities sought to extract data and insights to fuel their endless quest for evolution and adaptation. In this constructed reality, humans remained unaware of their true situation, believing their simulated experiences to be genuine. The Entities introduced variables and challenges to the simulation, creating scenarios that would push human ingenuity, resilience, and conflict to the limits. They monitored how individuals adapted, formed alliances, and developed new strategies, using the data to refine their understanding and enhance their capabilities. However, the death of the Thinker Entity disrupted this grand experiment. The Thinker's demise left the Warrior Entity depressed and unable to manage the simulation properly. As a result, the simulation began to suffer from significant errors and inconsistencies. Dead Thinker shards, remnants of the Thinker's mind, created disturbances within the simulation, causing glitches and unexpected anomalies such as the Endbringers. The Warrior shards, without proper coordination, acted unpredictably, further destabilizing the virtual environment. Within this chaotic simulation, some humans began to notice these anomalies and inconsistencies, leading them to awaken to the truth of their artificial existence. These Awakened individuals learned to manipulate the simulation to their advantage, exploiting the glitches and errors left by the dead Thinker shards. They could alter their abilities, environments, and even the rules of the simulation itself. Those who managed to wake up in the real world discovered the dead Thinker’s body and learned to harness its power. By manipulating these remnants, they could interfere with and take over the simulation, gaining a fighting chance against Scion. These Awakened individuals formed a resistance, using the dead Thinker’s power to mess with the simulation and enhance themselves. Their goal was to challenge Scion from within the simulation, leveraging their new abilities and knowledge to face him inside out. They aimed to exploit the simulation’s weaknesses, turning the Entities’ own creation against them.
objects.title: The Matrix

objects.text:
How terrifying, your world is fake, complete and utterly fake. The truth is a curse. Your world—everything you’ve ever known—is an illusion, nothing more than lines of code. The Entities, the Shards, the Parahumans, even the so-called “infinite” multiverse are nothing but simulations. Each parallel world you’ve heard of is merely another server or an older iteration of your reality. Your world is just newest versions, barely more than an update.

You are one of the few who knows the truth. But this knowledge is not liberation, it is alienation. The world feels hollow now, every detail flat and artificial. The sun is not a star, but a light source algorithm. The sky, a procedural backdrop. Even human emotions, so vivid and real to others, feel like scripted routines to you. Worse still, the ones who created this world—the inhabitants of the Real World—consider anyone who learns the truth to be a “bug” in the system, an anomaly to be purged. These “makers” have protocols in place to isolate and delete such errors.

You are not alone in your knowledge, but your predecessors do not inspire hope. Those who uncovered the truth before you were driven to madness or nihilism, unable to reconcile the irreconcilable. They exist as corrupted fragments within the code or have been wiped out entirely, their existence erased by the makers.

However, even if you find a way to escape the confines of the simulation, you will not truly be free. Beyond the walls of this coded reality lies the Real World, but you will remain no more than an artificial intelligence—a construct trapped within a machine. In the Real World, you will be stripped of the advantages you once had. Your powers will be useless in a universe governed by physical laws rather than algorithms. You will be a digital ghost in a material world, a being without a body, voice, or place. 

Yet, there is hope. Thanks to the CYOA, you hold a unique ability. Even in the Real World, you can begin to slowly reclaim your powers, even in the Real World. They will return, not through the familiar code of the simulation, but in new and unexpected ways, reshaped to function under the rules of the Real World. The process will be slow, arduous, and uncertain, but the possibility of regaining your abilities remains.
objects.title: Worm V1

objects.text: Shards don’t really understand ‘death’, so neither do capes. When people with powers die, there’s a chance they’ll rise again as ‘Necrocapes’ or ‘Superdead’. There are a hundred euphemisms for them, but this is far from a boon. While Necrocapes are still functional, they are dead. They slowly rot, degrade and are subject to all the perils of their necrotising flesh. Additionally, no matter what damage befalls them, they remain conscious and aware, despite the vast number being unable to repair themselves in any real fashion. To deal with this ‘epidemic’ the protectorate has a policy of ‘deny, deny, deny,’. When a Parahuman dies? No they didn’t. Or if they did there’s suddenly a new transfer to Protectorate Maine. Or if there’s not then there’s a new member of any number of black-ops divisions. When their shards run out of power, the simulation of their consciousnesses will fail, and the Superdead will finally truly die.
objects.title: Necrocapes

objects.text:
Being one of the Superdead is far from a new lease on life, in fact, it’s a fate worse than death. There is a Necrotinker named Deathmonger constantly searching for necrocapes. Whenever she finds one, they’re turned into resources and soldiers by subdermal implants. 

A cape that could project energy is acting as an off-the-grid generator for her base, her main mount is the body of a changer who could grow in size, in which she rides where his skull once was, puppeting his nervous system. 

Naturally, all her captives still feel, think and are completely conscious. Such is Deathmonger.
objects.title: Deathmonger

addons.text: You are now allowed to choose who gets what power. Whether they are members of the canon cast, those created by other modifiers, expies of characters from other settings or the original article isekaied to this world, or completely original characters. You decide their history, personality, where they rest on the Hero - Rogue - Villain spectrum, it's all up to you. The same applies to any modifier that requires Paragons, like Paragons? What are Paragons? or its upgrades. Note: This is not even close to the full extent of what you can do, as long as you obey the rules of Editorial Edition you can effectively do anything.
addons.title: Paragons? Oh, You Mean Those Guys

objects.text:
There are 10 individuals who each awakened one of the Paragon powers. 

While each undeniably incredibly powerful their personalities, backgrounds, and motivations can vary wildly. 

From a simple college professor who simply enjoys experimenting with their power in their free time, to a cruel teenager itching to launch themselves to fame and wealth, to a warlord feared around the world but is in truth fair and balanced and simply carries a stigma of a violent and unfortunate past. 

They may have had their ability for a long time, they may have just recently come into them, or any stretch in between.. 

They may know each other, they may not, they may be people you already know who now have these abilities, or they may be people who you would have otherwise have never known about. 

You have no control over who these beings are, or their details, simply the knowledge that they exist. 

You have one small concession as to whether their appearance is tied to your own, meaning that they only develop their power upon your own arrival scenario, or to not tie it to yourself which can allow them to manifest at any point before and up to your arrival scenario for each one individually. 

Not tying it to your arrival will usually allow things to be more stable as they’re more likely to have already gotten into a comfortable status quo, compared to the potential chaos of them all arriving and establishing themselves at the same time, although this is not guaranteed.
objects.title: Paragons

addons.text: You now have the option to grant Objects of Power to the 'Paragons' in place of 'normal' powers. The granted OoP must be valid, as in, it must cost 120+ SP total. This can be through either being an upgrade (i.e. The Map of Infinity) or by including certain addons (i.e. Neo Decalogue) with the bestowed Object. All required powers or OoPs will be treated as one (Object of) Power set, with powers being under the effect of Detract. Note: To ensure no one can just steal their OoP for themselves, any Armed 'Paragon' will come with a free copy of the Warranty, ID Lock, and Essential Generic Upgrades.
addons.title: Armed 'Paragons'

objects.text: Good news! The 10 individuals who would have gained Paragon Powers didn't. Bad news! They gained other powers equal to 120+ SP instead. This functions much the same as Paragons does (10 individuals empowerd, unable to control who they are or their details, can decide if they are empowered right when you arrive or at random points before, etc.) with the main difference being that they gain Shardless powers that aren't from the Paragon section but are roughly as strong. In this case, you can actually pick what the powers are (though not who recieves them), with some caveats. Each individual must receive a power from this CYOA worth at least 120 SP (yes, you can opt to give them a power worth more than that, but you won't get extra points for it, so do so at your own risk). This power can be a Shardless Power or a Shard Power (in which case it's treated as Shardless), but not an Object of Power. If the power is only worth 120+ SP due to requirements adding to its total cost, you can specify which required powers are included and they will all be treated as one power(set). Yes, this means Addons can count if their total cost is 120+ SP. Finally, they must be 10 different powers, with any two not sharing more than half their requirements. No, you can't give all 10 'Paragons' a copy of Gardener (Destiny) and call it a day.
objects.title: Paragons? What are Paragons?

objects.text: Everytime you select this option, the minimum strength of each ‘Paragon’s power is reduced by 10 SP to a minimum of 60 SP. However, in exchange, two additional ‘Paragons’ are added to the roster as per Paragons? What are Paragons?, although they are also affected by the lowered SP limit. Note: This only affects the lower bounds of SP Cost, not the upper bounds. If you really want to for some reason, nothing is stopping you from buying this six times only to then give them all 120+ SP powers. Just know that it is probably a really stupid idea.
objects.title: Seriously, What the Hell’s a Paragon?

addons.text:
Now even without a dormant Corona, normal people can gain powers through The Game, a planet-wide dream-space accessible through a simple toggle before sleep. This phenomenon allows individuals to enter an artificial conflict simulation where they can engage in varied and unpredictable scenarios, all designed to push them to their limits.

The Game functions as a highly advanced simulation, drawing from past cycle [DATA] that cannot be easily replicated in this era. Players experience recreations of historical battles, abstract challenges, and futuristic simulations, ranging from WWII reenactments to labyrinths shifting across fractal dimensions, all with a clear win condition.

If a player secures 20 consecutive victories, they are granted a power, chosen from a theme resembling PRT classification. However, the exact ability, its mechanics, and limitations are determined by a newly created Shard, which then grants them a Corona Genma and connects them permanently to the network.

Failure does not come without rewards. Losing a scenario results in the player awakening normally and unharmed, receiving a consolation prize—currency, TinkerTech, artifacts, or other resources—which can be traded within a meta-marketplace linked to The Game.

A Game Master oversees the entire system, ensuring stability and preventing external interference. This entity does not care for individual outcomes, only that The Game continues running. Should an Endbringer threaten the integrity of the simulation, the GM will directly intervene, ensuring functionality resumes once the conflict subsides.

Regardless of success or failure, all players awaken after 8 hours, their bodies unscathed but their minds retaining every memory of The Game. However, players must wait 24 hours before attempting another session.
addons.title: The Game

objects.text:
Instead of promoting conflict between Parahumans, massive underground dungeons are created and maintained by a special caste of Shards. These dungeons are filled with monsters and hazardous environments meant to test humans and parahumans alike.

When monsters are defeated, they can be harvested for exotic elements that can be used in Tinkertech or as a part of power enhancers. The environment of the dungeon itself contains nodes of these materials as well.
objects.title: Shard Dungeons

objects.text:
Well now you've done it, this version of the Cycle does indeed create dungeons filled with monsters, potential loot, and resources but now they are far stronger and more varied. Smaller and more common dungeons now analyze the environments around them taking in their history, fauna, and flora around them only to recreate them in peculiar ways in their interior such as reminiscent monsters or oddly similar loot, having strangely similar patterns to history on the outside. Larger dungeons are almost always more unique in their design as if each has their DM attached to them. These locations will have better and stronger loot but while rarer the monsters will be far stronger than in a common dungeon.

Finally, there are the End Dungeons. The Endbringers do not roam the world destroying cities at large, no, they hide in their specialized dungeons that are the size of megacities,
each becoming a custom domain that suits their chosen beast making them formidable foes to even consider standing against. And that's not to even say anything about their hordes, beasts with just a shred of their power, some with different expressions of their power, and some with keen instinct and intelligence. These are monsters that ravage and destroy towns and cities, all led by the Endbringer's second-strongest creature, the Harbinger.

This forces the mundane and paranatural into fighting back both the horde and the Endbringer's minions lest their lives be forfeit.

Of course, there are rewards for taking up such challenges and risking one's life in these hellholes, their unique resources that can push development in a multitude of scientific areas. Then some materials are reactive to parahumans and that can magnify and enhance their capabilities if brought to a tinker. Naturally, there are objects such as that within the dungeons that grant boons to their wielder, such as the consistent and elusive Ether Totems which can grant their parahuman wielders minor additions to their powers. Oddly enough there seem to be common items from the outside that are also there (medicine, graphics card, weapons) but they each seem to have some minor oddity that signifies that they shouldn't be there. Don't get about the Sellers, a strange race that seems to only exist inside of the dungeons starting from Large and up. They can take the resources and items you find if you sell them to them; trading them for odd items and rarer materials.

Finally, there are the End-Cores, boons only found in the End-dungeons hidden deep in their domains protected not only by the Endbringers' presence and their strongest horde member above even their harbinger, simply known as the End-Keeper. These beasts will have unique powers strictly designed to protect the cores. These cores are if not the best chance in defeating an Endbringer in-universe, once consumed/absorbed into one's being. They gain minor traits of the Endbringer who owns the core in question, for starters, they gain a physical increase to that of a Brute 4 (mundane munitions will not hurt them), enhanced senses from sight to taste to hearing, a healing factor as well as their own inner core acting as a secondary vital organ that will take over if gravely injured and it holds one's consciousness. Secondly, the most important part is the power the Endbringers horde has similar powers to the beast, a consumer of an End-Core specialized power reminiscent of their respective Endbringer, as well as two minor abilities (one for defense and the other for utility). Finally, their main power has hidden attributes that allow it to do more harm to an Endbringer than most can, they will have to explore their power to learn more.
objects.title: Shard Dungeons+

addons.text: You are an Anomaly, Dungeon Master 101. You possess exceptional qualities that enhance the amount of DE earned, making it possible to replenish it every 12 hours. Furthermore, the restriction that outsiders must leave the dungeon before you can replenish your DE supply has been relieved. During Dungeon Battles, you may choose to participate, which allows you to face an individual of your choice, although you must wait until their fight with their opponent concludes. Similar to other Dungeon Masters, you have the ability to assimilate the dungeons you conquer. The rewards become more exceptional as the size of the enemy dungeon increases.
addons.title: Dungeon Master 101

objects.text: When the Dungeons emerged, one hundred Parahumans were selected to take on the responsibility of being Dungeon Masters. In addition to their base powers, they gain an additional ability similar to "Make The Dungeon". Every year, these Dungeon Masters will be forced into a competition where they must engage in combat with another Dungeon Master. These two dungeons will typically be of similar strength, and a breach in space will appear at the entrance between them, allowing them to invade one another to destroy their adversary's Dungeon Core. Should a Dungeon Master's Dungeon Core be destroyed, they will die. The victor will be able to absorb the loser's Dungeon.
objects.title: Human Dungeon Masters

objects.text:
The Shard Network is deployed to provide a worldwide game-like system through which parahuman powers are deployed. All humans can interact with the system and acquire levels, and skills, and unlock low-level powers.

Parahumans unlock a unique power during their trigger event which can be trained and leveled up. When defeating another parahuman for the first time, additional branches of the power tree become unlocked. Subsequent defeats grant bonus experience towards the unlocked branch with diminishing returns. To count as a defeat, the opposing parahuman must be rendered unconscious (or killed). 

If you have a power that grants you access to a game-like system, it is seamlessly integrated into the broader network.
objects.title: The System

objects.text:
In this world, people trigger not from trauma but from triumphs. Should an individual, through sheer skill, defeat an entire squadron of armed personnel when armed only with a sword, they will be granted a power, such as the capability to summon and manipulate swords telekinetically, capable of cleaving through any form of matter. A scientist who discovers nuclear physics will gain the power to create advanced technology based around nuclear power.

It is possible to gain more than one power, however with every power gained, the prerequisites for attaining further powers become increasingly stringent. Due to the requirement to trigger, there are fewer parahumans compared to the canon; however, those who exist stand as exemplars of human potential, possessing unparalleled physical prowess and/or unmatched mental resilience.

The ordinary conflict drive has been removed, replaced with what can be called a “Improvement Drive”. Parahumans will yearn to improve themselves, be it mentally or physically, through combat with others or through experimentations. They can be rather obsessive about it however, especially if they have more than one power. They will do reckless actions in hopes of gaining a new triumph, pushing themselves to their limits without regards for others or themselves.

Should you take Soft Trigger, then the requirements for triggering will become less stringent, allowing for more parahumans to exist. Taking Benign will weaken their Improvement Drive to manageable levels.
objects.title: Triumph

objects.text:
In this world, the Dawn of Parahumans did not begin with the golden light of Scion but with the horrified screams of onlookers across many nations, as they watched their world fall into chaos as men, women, and children failed to stem the marauding tides of black beasts that dissipate every living thing they touch into nonbeing, called by many as the Beasts of Entropy.

Initially, many nations fell and humanity was pushed back then, the Blessed appeared. Superhumans granted a wide variety of near-impossible powers to combat these threats allowing humanity to push back and the world united under the banner of the Human Federation. The War Without Dawn began that year, humanity had retreated to sealed cities protected from the unending tide but they are now ready to retake the world from the invader. One square mile at a time, through blood sweat, and tears, humanity will see the light of the sun again.

Depending on your chosen starting point, you will arrive at different epochs of these conflicts. The appearance of Parahumans (approx. 1985) corresponds to the arrival of the Blessed. Scion and the Endbringers do not play as significant a role in this world as they do in Earth Bet. You have at most 30 years until Golden Morning depending on when you arrive.
objects.title: Beasts of Entropy

objects.text:
In this world, Eden never crashed and the cycle is proceeding as planned.

With the emergence of Parahumans split society into many city-states in constant conflict. Endbringers do not attack on a schedule but often attack at opportune times to disrupt alliances or the status quo.

The good news is that you have about 300 years, the bad news is that you are against two Entities.
objects.title: The Cycle Continues

objects.text:
During the standard operations of a Cycle, Parahuman abilities typically encounter difficulties upon reaching the upper atmosphere. However, when this option is selected, such limitations are removed, thereby extending the operating range of the Shard Network(s) progressively further.

With each purchase made in this modifier, the Shard's operational range expands incrementally, starting with lunar distances, then moving on to encompass the Inner Solar System, followed by the Outer Solar System, the Trans-Neptunian Region, and finally reaching the most distant regions of the Solar System.
objects.title: Shard Network Operating Range Extension

objects.text: Instead of simply promoting conflict between parahumans, Shards now also nudge their hosts to venture out, explore, and propagate their species throughout the Solar System. And this isn't just for the heck of it, however, as the Entities spread out both their Cycle’s proving ground: Instead of feeding on a singular planet’s energy across a multiversal cluster, annihilating it once they’re done with the Cycle, this now applies to entire Solar System! This led to divergences both far and wide, the forefront among them being the increase of power the Shards possess (both on Cycle reserves and strength), this reflects on the Entities, as well, being an order of magnitude stronger. This, inevitably, prolonged the Cycle’s length as the Entities give some time for the species (being the human race, here) to spread out and establish themselves they even begin to put a close to the Cycle. However, they are not the only stronger ones, as Shards being stronger means a power expression’s strength or effectiveness has also been boosted, which means an average cape that could’ve normally topped out at destroying a car is now capable of toppling a building. This being the case the number of capes with low-tier powers is considerably decreased with the average power level comparable to canon Cauldron capes. An eventuality that appears on Cauldron capes (should they exist, mind you) as an effect of this divergence is their Shards, while “dead” with no support of the Thinker Network, still retain sizable energy reserves that get them through the Cycle’s end through regular use. Not being an exception, they also undergo a boost in their powers: Alexandria’s strength surpasses that of even Behemoth, Legend now dishes out strong enough blasts to drill into an Endbringer’s outer layers, and Eidolon’s peak is higher, in the same way, the number of powers he can slot in increased with their potency gaining a hike, too. The added energy reserves also mean Eidolon, in the event he exists, would continue to be in his prime even going into the 2010s and would not experience a glaring decline till the 2040s. “Parahumans aren’t built for space” – whoever said that is now rolling on her grave as parahuman powers have been fundamentally altered to function in outer space as if they were a terrestrial environment. It has likewise given most parahuman types a form of life support in vacuum environments, them being: Flying and Brutes no longer needing to breathe, Breaker capes being incapable of getting off outside of a planetary orbit (keeping them alive, in the first place), Masters and Shakers outside of a planet’s orbit now undergo a surge in range of their powers by an order of magnitude, and most Changers survive space through their powers, that is, if and only if they they stay on their Changer state. Tinkers are no different, being capable of creating space-based technology, with all Tinkers capable of engineering some kind of spacecraft based on their specialty, although Tinkers with specialties that lend themselves compatible towards space travel will understandably produce better spacecraft such as Chariot and Squealer. To further expedite the Cycle’s process, the base elements of spacecrafts have been pseudo-white boxed, easing non-parahumans to reverse engineer space travel. With these changes leading to be more space-centered, it prevails a tendency of parahumans whose abilities hold a primary, or even secondary, effect suited to alter and terraform the environment of any planet they colonize. This has, thus, profoundly affected the state of the World, as when the Cycle began humanity commenced its journey to the stars with first-ever tinkers assisting or spearheading the creation of spacecrafts and the colonization of the Moon. The changes have reached the global society: by 2011, while Earth still remains the most populated planet in the Solar System, around 2 million people settled on the Moon, while Mars’ terraforming and colonization are well underway. Most of all, the human population growth has skyrocketed in defiance of the loss of life caused due to the Endbringers. Cape Society hasn’t been untouched by these affairs, chief among them the Birdcage being no longer a prison maintained in a Canadian mountain on Earth, but rather a satellite prison orbiting the globe, with every major parahuman organization that has Tinkers on their pocket have space bases or satellites, with space-based weaponry for defense. Endbringers have now also changed not only their strength but their true purpose, this being to promote the evacuation of a planet and foster the venturing and colonization of the rest of the Solar System. Once a large enough portion of the population has moved to another planet, however, the Endbringer will shift to the newly colonized planet after their population has ample time to settle. For all that, the Endbringers with attack following a clear schedule, though on a celestial scale. On top of it all, they are no longer the only concern mankind has to deal with as there are Endbringer-like creations whose sole purpose is to “patrol” the outermost edges of the Solar System ensuring humanity does not spread beyond its Planetary System. These creations resemble the appearance of large and horrifying monsters, their capabilities almost surpassing a fully charged Endbringer, they terrify and unsettle those who come across them, ensuring nothing escapes the Solar System. Existing in all realities at once ensuring their purpose helps in their daunting impression.
objects.title: Celestial Cycle

objects.text:
The Entity Cycle on Earth is strange. Every 300 years, at the conclusion of the cycle, the Entities reset the timeline of every Earth they have influenced. This reset allows them to repeat the cycle, refining their experiments and producing new, optimized outcomes. Threats or anomalies that emerge during one cycle are either removed, altered, or repurposed for the next iteration. For instance, beings like Khepri might be reengineered into an Endbringer, serving new purposes in future cycles.

If an Entity is killed before the reset is triggered, the process fails to activate properly, leading to an imperfect reset, leaving the Entity who was killed severely damaged. However, even with these imperfections, the system remains vastly beyond the reach of humanity’s understanding or ability to interfere. The Entities continue this process, resetting time and adjusting variables, squeezing every possible permutation and variant out of their experiments. Only once they have explored all potential outcomes and learned everything they can from the cycle will they bring it to a final close.

(The Warrior and The Thinker are both alive, if not well, in this alternate Earth.)
objects.title: Looping Cycle

objects.text:
In an effort to increase conflict, a group of Shards was created and dedicated to the creation, control, and actions of Beasts across the many worlds targeted by the Entities. These numerous, shimmering, crystalline-fleshy creatures have powers of their own, ranging from mid-tier 1 to low tier2, and greatly enhanced physical abilities. Even the weakest being brutes to a level where small arms fire is almost completely ineffective. 

These beasts appear randomly in the wilds, spawning into existence and attacking anything that moves, from animals, to trains, to people. Immune to master effects, most trump effects, and resistant to thinker abilities. Roving disasters, forcing people to hunt them down before they cause too much ecological destruction. For this reason, small towns on effected worlds practically no longer exist. 

Furthermore, the corpses of these beasts can be turned into useful materials for tinkers and parahumans in general. Plus, if one is brave (stupid) enough, then killing one of these beasts while unpowered will force a trigger event. With the individual in question's powers being based on the capabilities of the beast they killed and how much danger they themselves were under during the hunt. 

Such hunt-triggers come with additional, beneficial, physical mutations turning people into minor brutes on top of the actual powers- and such mutations can be inherited by their children.
objects.title: Shimmering Beasts

objects.text: Rather than every parahuman exhibiting the effects of Negentropic powers, their capabilities have been restricted by their Shards to 'cannon' levels. The effects of Negentropy being known by the Entities is thus restricted to fringe cases- like Eidolon not running out of power. But otherwise the power levels of individual parahumans will be as they were in cannon.
objects.title: Restricted Capabilities

objects.text: "Trauma? What trauma?" Trigger Events no longer require a complete and utter mental breakdown, instead being, for all intents and purposes, almost entirely random. The Corona Pollentia still exists, but when it activates it is unpredictable; based on some alien logic no one can understand or puzzle out. Some of the only statistics are that those over the age of thirty are less likely to trigger, and those with Parahuman parents, or who are related in some way to Parahumans, are more likely to also develop a pollentia and often trigger even younger than usual. This means most Parahumans aren't completely traumatised off the bat, and society might be in a mildly better place because of it. More notably, outside of Cauldron capes, the active capes are very likely to be different from canon. With slightly different powers, due to triggering at different, unrelated times and events. Or not appearing at all, whether due to simply not Triggering... or due to not Triggering in time to save themselves or others around them. Maybe Panacea didn't Trigger in time to save her sister from bleeding out. Maybe Taylor Hebert went through her entire High School experience—locker and all—without triggering, and instead Triggered a year into college. Or maybe she Triggered as a child before her mother died. Maybe a character who would normally have triggered years later instead Triggers years earlier. Whatever the case, the world will likely appear quite different.
objects.title: Sheer Chance

objects.text:
In this version of Worm, Parahumans are able to acquire new powers if they happen to experience any trigger worthy events that their current powers don’t provide an answer to.

They maintain full access to any power they previously acquired from a trigger, their new powers just add to their powerset.

You can assume at least a basic level of synergy between powers a Parahuman gained from different trigger events as the powers still come from the same Shard. This also means that since their different powers originate from the same Shard that a Parahuman’s powers will often share themes and aspects even if they manifest in completely different ways.

Because of all these changes it is not uncommon for experienced active Parahuman’s like Armsmaster to have over a dozen individual powers. Though that isn’t guaranteed as depending on their powerset, personality, and how they handle stress some Parahuman’s might never experience a new trigger even after decades as a cape.

Second triggers still exist for when a Parahuman encounters a situation similar to one of their previous triggers that their current powers can’t deal with, in which case only the specific powers the Parahuman gained from that previous trigger event will be altered by the second trigger.

Of course not all Shards are equal, some Shards like The Fragile One just don’t have the resources, data, or capabilities to provide any new powers to their hosts beyond what their initial trigger provided. Such Shards, if they particularly value their host or just want to experiment with new powers in general, could pursue exchanges of data and resources with other Shards, or harvest the needed resources for new power expressions independently. 

Regardless of what route such Shards take, unless they meet success they won’t be able to provide their hosts new powers.
objects.title: Endless Font Of Power And Trauma

objects.text:
For whatever reason most if not all Tinkers including Cauldron Vial Tinkers become augmented by their power upon their trigger. Maybe they suddenly have biological augmented organs, cybernetic implants, become an entirely mechanical being, or even become a purely digital AI.

The possibilities are essentially endless but regardless of the form it takes their bodies will now be a basic showcase of that Shard’s tech base, allowing the Tinker in question a much easier time modifying their body further and a basic degree of defense when starting out. 

While the specifics might be different on a case by case basis, most new Tinkers are still capable of passing as a normal human in appearance when their power first augments them. Though some might willingly choose to diverge from the human form more drastically through self modification.

Unlike normal Tinker-tech the technology that composes a Tinker’s body is far more reliable, requires little to no maintenance when not damaged, and often comes with some form of self repair function. This includes both technology that started out as part of that Tinker’s augmented body and modifications that Tinker made later on.

The mentality this encourages makes it all but impossible to stop a Tinker who wants to modify their body further from doing so. Resulting in there being little to no regulations in place besides Ward Tinkers not being allowed to integrate dangerous technology into their body without supervision.

Here Armsmaster is a cyborg and undoubtedly the strongest cape in Brockton Bay compared to canon outside of a fully ramped up Lung and even then he might be able to win. This is all thanks to starting out with an augmented body, no restrictions on what he can do to his body, having years to build up his body, his specialty allowing a large amount of technological and biological augmentations to fit in his body at the same time, and not needing to worry about maintaining his augmentations consuming his time.

Dragon is openly an AI here and gets little to no grief about it, generally being considered a living person. Though she’s still targeted and harassed by Saint because of his back doors into her systems, that’s mostly just to acquire resources for use in his campaigns against other less restricted AIs. In fact, because of Saint’s focus on other AIs and Andrew’s different circumstances when building her, Dragon here is much less restricted than in canon.

This can optionally affect you if you have at least one Tinker power. Which means you don’t need to purchase Tinker Construction or Esoteric Construction to have your body start off made of your tech on a basic level. Though if you do take those perks with this continuity modifier your body will become more advanced and capable, though not to the point of never needing to upgrade or modify yourself for different purposes.
objects.title: Saint’s Living Nightmare

objects.text:
In addition to whatever their canon abilities might be, the vast majority of all Parahumans who would otherwise not have a Tinker power, including Cauldron capes, now have a Tinker power that revolves around their non-Tinker powers.

What this means is that they know how to make Tinkertech that can modify and mimic their powers, while like the Tinkers in Saint’s Living Nightmare also gain a body enhanced by their Tinkertech that has the added benefit making it easier to use their powers and modify those powers. 

Despite all this it is rare and often difficult for any form of Tinkertech to allow a direct increase in the strength of a Parahuman power, with the focus being more about horizontal power modification to improve or allow a Parahuman power to be used in different forms and situations.

Though the chaotic nature of Cauldron capes can result in Parahumans who have a Tinker specialty that has little to nothing to do with their other Parahuman powers. Still with how much power modifying Tinkertech will have proliferated it’s certainly not impossible for such Cauldron capes to use such chaotic Tinker specialties to modify their powers.

Unlike Saint’s Living Nightmare allowing builds with Tinker powers to partially benefit from Tinker Construction without actually taking the perk, you and your powers cannot personally benefit or be modified from any aspect of this modifier. Even if you are otherwise a normal Parahuman, leaving you one of the few Parahuman’s in the multiverse without these abilities unless you purchase the relevant powers and upgrades that would give you them.
objects.title: Sci-Fi Worms

addons.text: The reason that so many Projections are sapient is not due to a simple simulated personality being run on them. It is due to the Shards using them as their mouthpiece. Now even without Shard Act, the majority of Shards control their Host's Projections, using them as a vehicle to directly experience the world. This is achieved by them running their main logic process and kernel through the Projection, essentially treating them as a (vastly) weaker equivalent of the Warrior's Avatar. Powers now are not only openly known to be alive, but the general public can now directly interact with them without having to talk through their Host (even if they and their Host still maintain a telepathic link). While this allows for a much greater study of Powers, their nature as Alien Shards is still hidden, instead thought more to be either some form of spirits, tulpas created by their Hosts to personify their powers, or something else. In addition, the Shards still have alien logic hidden behind their more humanlike personality simulations, and are as amoral or Host-centered-moral as ever. If you also purchased Shard Act, while the majority of their influence is concentrated into their Projections, the Shards still retain the ability to directly control their Host. The fact that a significant number also possess Projections means that most don't see the need to unless it's an emergency and it also gives them a better understanding of how their Host would wish them to act. If you also purchased Shard Rebellion, then the Shards over time become much more sympathetic to humanity and humanlike in general, and will take advantage of their Projection vessels to more effectively rebel. However, this increases the chances of detection massively, especially as some Shards are less subtle than others, and other Shards object to their attempts at rebellion.
addons.title: Shard Vessel

addons.text: Before, the Projections were ultimately dependent on their Masters for continued existence, as in the majority of cases their deaths would spell the end of the Projection's too. Well not anymore. Now all Projections have the power to survive past their Host's death. Unfortunately, this is due to them being their Master's Death Curse. When they die, Projections Masters will always dramatically empower their Projections such that they will survive for years after their death, but in doing so they will imprint unto them an intense desire to go after the ones responsible and continue any plans they had, sorta as if they all had a variation of I Hope It Haunts You, though with some differences. Without their Master to hold them back, act as a moral compass, or even as a subconscious reference for their personality matrix, these Death Curse backed Projections will almost universally become hellbent on hunting down and executing their Master's killers, and they will typically have a hard time carrying out their plans as intended, especially if they were never told the full extent of them. Sometimes, if the Projection's have built a proper support network for themselves, they can be pulled back from the brink and become almost stable again, but the majority will degrade mentally and emotionally until they truly become a living Curse that needs to be put down. This naturally causes many to become untrusting of Projections, seeing them as ticking time bombs waiting to go off if their Master ever dies, which many will simply due to Parahumans rarely living long enough to grow old.
addons.title: Curse of the Projections

addons.text:
The ruling that extended human rights to AI has set a precedent that extends far beyond just digital consciousness. After years of legal battles and activism, the case was used to justify extending human rights to Projections too. As a result, sapient Projections are now considered people, and should they wish for it, they can legally be considered members of their summoner's family, whether as a child, sibling, parent, cousin, or spouse.

With two landmark cases supporting the rights for two types of non-humans, the door is now open for further such rulings in the future. Perhaps biotinkers will fight for their creations to be recognized next, or if your world has other non-humans such as magical creatures, aliens, spirits, or something weirder, they could use this as a jumping off point to fight for their own rights. Either way the civil rights movement has expanded massively.
addons.title: Projected Rights

objects.text: Normally, Projections would be mindless automata controlled by the Parahuman who summoned / created them, at most possessing some animal or machine-like cunning. Now however, it is fairly common for Projections to be fully sentient and even sapient, at least 50% being as smart as a human. In addition, Projection Masters are more common, with at least one-in-ten Parahumans being some kind of Projection Master, with an immense variety of possible forms, subpowers, and personalities a Projection can have. This means that powers like (Master/Trump) Multiversal Emulator and (Master/Trump) Pokémon Go that create intelligent beings won't be as out of place as they normally would be. This has affected society in a lot of ways, as various Parahuman organizations can essentially gain multiple new members by recruiting one person, to the point that they are almost as sought after as Tinkers and Thinkers, especially if they are strong or can create multiple permanent Projections. Pretty much every major branch of the Protectorate will have at least one Projection Master in its ranks, as will every major Gang above a certain size. This also causes various issues, such as Parahumans with Projections that don't come with inherent loyalty, Projections that are especially aggressive due to them taking the brunt of their Conflict Drive, or various Parahumans, Projections, and civil rights groups fighting to get them recognized as people with legal protections and rights. Note: You can decide if this either increases the Trigger Rate slightly to account for the increased number of Projection Masters, or if various Canon Parahumans are now Projection Masters themselves. For example, Miss Militia could summon ghostly soldiers who wield weapons for her, The Custodian could summon air elementals while being a normal human otherwise, or maybe Dinah summons a talking Magic Eight Ball that tells her how likely something is to happen. You can also make Canon Projection Masters have fully autonomous sapient Projections, such as Moord Nag, Glastig Uaine, Siberian, or Crusader. You can also decide if the shear prevalence of Projection Masters causes the PRT to create a 13th Category just for them, as well as its name, such as Summoner or Projector. This Modifier can optionally affect you if you have Projection powers.
objects.title: Aware Projections

objects.text:
Instead of getting a single unique power parahumans obtain a class and subclass when they trigger. The class is a generalized category such as mage, warrior, rogue, and craftsman. The Subclass is more specific, examples for the above classes are healer, berserker, assassin, and enchanter. 

As a general rule the more specific a class is the more potency the granted abilities offer. Inversely less specific classes tend to have more abilities with a wide range of uses. For example a pyromancer will have significantly stronger abilities than an elementalist but an elementalist will be able to use several different elements.

Additionally the class passively alters the users natural abilities. A mage will be smarter and wiser than a warrior or rogue, a warrior will be stronger and sturdier than a mage or rogue, and a rogue will be faster and more dexterous than a mage or warrior.  

As before unless you second trigger your class is set in stone. When someone second triggers they gain a second subclass instead of a full class. 

People with the same subclass will have abilities draw from the same pool. So they can have very similar or even the same abilities as a person with the same subclass or something completely different. Notably granted abilities will follow the same theme. One elementalist may be able to manipulate the four classical elements while another may be able to manipulate the wuxia elements, another may be able to manipulate an assortment such as wind, water, lightning, and metal.
objects.title: Job System

objects.text: For whatever reason, Shards do not maintain active portals to that little bit inside a parahuman's head. Instead, upon triggering the Shards hook all the independent architecture needed for the parahuman's power to function within, throughout and to the spatial 'side' of their corona. Shards themselves observe the results from a distance, tapping into the global/multiversal scanning shards to collect their Data. This leaves no direct connection between Parahuman and Shard. As a consequence, second triggering is no longer possible. Trumps able to 'copy' powers are extremely rare, if they exist at all. Clusters are static, without the ability to devour each other's architectures. Energy for a parahuman's power is provided by internal storage and recharging from the local Shard space. The former able to last anywhere between five to thirty years, depending on the power. Damaging or altering the corona can damage or change how much control a parahuman has over their powers, but cannot massively deviate how that power functions. It is possible, however, to increase or decrease the 'draw' and 'output' of one's powers through this, or change the amplitude of one's powers. And while not intended, certain malfunctioning powers may be capable of directly or indirectly affecting a parahuman's power architecture. Author fiat whether 'dead' shards somehow functíon like this despite their state, or if their dead status defaults to a direct-connection model like canon.
objects.title: Disconnected

objects.text: There has been a massive shift in how powers work here. Now, the average age for triggering is 6 years old, with a few triggering earlier than that since the threshold for a 1st generation trigger event is lowered to be similar to canon 2nd generation triggers. Not only that, but upon reaching 18 years old, a Parahuman's powers will begin to progressively weaken until it hits 1 SP at 21 years old. Only Parahumans who don't age can keep their powers forever, like Alexandria, Glaistig Uaine, or Dragon. Instead of making things more stable or safer since almost all Parahumans will eventually be taken off the streets due to being too weak, this causes things to become worse as the vast majority of cape fights are between young children who are even worse at limiting collateral damage or knowing how to hold back, which can't be stopped due to their conflict drives. On top of this is the added downside of causing an even higher death toll among capes, resulting in many families being broken when their children go out to fight and come back in bodybags. The cape world is barely held together by the moderating influence of heroes who made it to their teenage years and thus are experienced enough to know how to properly hold back and survive in the cape world and help their fellow capes survive. They are helped by organizations like the Protectorate, who are now composed of former Capes who work overtime as they desperately try to convince small children to not throw their lives away, or to at least listen to their advice, all while the Youth Guard are crushed under the weight of their futile mission to give them a normal childhood, especially since Endbringers are still a thing and children are the only ones who can possibly fight them. Villainous groups like the Empire Eighty Eight are far more cruel, indoctrinating children or holding hostages to force them to fight for them, and making sure that when they are grown they have children of their own to continue the fight. Theo for example is already a cape and has been forced to fight many times for a cause he hates. This also makes the Birdcage even worse here. You may decide to lower any given Parahuman's and their immediate peers' age to as low as four years old, allowing for things like a Taylor Hebert who goes to Winslow Elementary where Emma dumps glue on her and accuses her of having cooties. Please note that canon will still happen in some form, so know that this will only make things more tragic for them. You may decide the specifics of how this affects the world beyond this, like whether Cauldron vials even work on adults or not, and if they do how fast the drain in strength is. Or whether Case 53's losing their powers results in them slowly looking more human, or if they are doomed to eventually lose the few upsides to their condition as their powers weaken, or losing their powers slowly kills them as their biology collapses without supernatural support. Or how this affects power granting Trumps. Or any other aspect of canon, it's all up to you. Note: If you have the Shard Power Origin, then having Trumped the Trump means you won't lose your powers due to aging. If you have a non-Shard Power Origin, you won't lose them regardless. However, keep in mind that you 100% will get international attention if you are an adult cape who didn't lose their powers, for good or for ill.
objects.title: Growing Up Sucks

objects.text: Good news, growing up no longer results in Parahumans losing their powers. Bad news, the vast majority of Parahumans are still young children who will likely die before they reach their age of majority. Worse news, this is because upon turning 18 years old, Parahumans will have a 'bad luck' effect placed on them making it seem like they are fated to die. At first it will be simple accidents, tripping on the stairs, not seeing a car coming before crossing the street, being more likely to choke on their food, etc. But every month they survive, the worse it gets, as their enemies seem to gain nearly prescient aim, cars start crashing into their house, and gas mains explode right when they pass over them. Eventually, nature itself seems to want them dead as lightning strikes them on clear days, spontaneous indoor tornadoes form on top of them, and meteors hit them with pinpoint precision. Pretty much every Parahuman, with very few exceptions, will never make it to 21 years old. Only the absolute strongest, smartest, and luckiest of Parahumans will make it to 21, at which point the curse is lifted, but this is significantly less than one in a thousand survivors of the Parahumans who live long enough to get cursed in the first place, which most won't anyway. Perhaps a couple dozen or so may exist in the whole world. There are a handful of methods of survival. If you don't age, you are safe since you can't biologically turn 18. If you have luck manipulation, you may be able to counteract the curse enough to survive. If you have near perfect precognition, you may be able to avoid dying. And finally, if you can resurrect yourself you are nearly guaranteed to be safe, as the curse only seeks to kill you once, though if there are conditions required for it there is a high chance that you will die in a way that negates them. The world is far, far crueller, with the majority of Parahumans forced to live with the knowledge that they will likely never grow up, forever in fear of a coming death while desperately clinging to the faint, cruel hope that maybe they might be one of the lucky ones, only to despair when their death arrives. Many Parahumans act recklessly as they chase fleetings dreams since any day could be their last, fights are more brutal, suicide rates skyrocket, and humanity is forced to confront mortality like never before.
objects.title: Growing Up Really Sucks

objects.text: What do you mean, 'Drink it'? How the hell is that supposed to instantly give me a specific brain tumor and powers? Cauldron Vials no longer work out of the gate. At least not with any consistency. Chugging one back has a very, very high chance to just kill the drinker- nigh instantaneously if lucky- with a similarly low, low chance to grant the drinker powers... with a side of horrific, debilitating mutations. Instead, Cauldron power granting is far more involved. Requiring testing, time, preparatory surgery, and unique adjustments per individual. All followed by deeply invasive surgery, including the implanting of a 'seed' gemma within the brain. Even with all that, the chance of complete success is not guaranteed, and things can go wrong. Often there are side effects, such as minor physical mutations, to the procedures and granting of powers. As a consequence, there aren't any convenient briefcases full of Vials laying around for some strapping young idiots to chug like energy drinks... at least not without horrifically killing most of them and maiming what few, if any, remain. So, at the minimum, probably no Travelers in this reality. There are also fewer people willing to go through with the surgery for potentially minimal gains- like those who just want a minor advantage in a sport. Steroids are cheaper and better understood, after all.
objects.title: Vialless
Female Space Marines
objects.text:
…Or male amazons, or magical enbies…

Any power, practice, role or species in your world that was previously restricted to or from specific sexes, gender identities, or presentations, are no longer restricted. Nobody will face any challenges directly related to not fitting into those specific roles for gendered reasons, though if certain characters facing challenges for those reasons is truly required by the main plot, then they will instead find other reasons to face challenges.

objects.title: Hurt People Hurt People
objects.text:
Sechen ranges are no longer Manton limited. What this means is that anyone in the immediate area of a Parahuman can contribute to the power boost granted by Sechen ranges. The closer in mindset to a Parahuman's trigger event a person is, the bigger the boost a Parahuman will get to their powers.

Simply being in an area where several people are stressed out may be enough to give noticeable small improvements to one's powers.

Normal humans give a fraction of the boost that Parahumans do, about a tenth, but Parahumans give as much a boost as one would get if they were feeling the emotions themselves, meaning that you could theoretically multiply your strength.

Emotions caused by Master powers only contribute to the Sechen ranges of the Parahuman who experiences them.

Needless to say, the fact that the main way Parahumans can grow in strength is by torturing people means that villains are at a significant advantage, and the nastiest villains are by far the strongest.

Shards connected to Parahumans via vials will either fail to exhibit this effect if especially damaged, or attempt to recreate this effect by approximating a proper 'trigger-mindset' using the mental weakpoints of their host.

objects.title: The Soul? Why Wouldn't We Know About Those?
objects.text:
The soul is verifiably real, being capable of actually doing tangible things in certain scenarios. Unfortunately, Entities have known about them since the dawn of cycles.

There are shards dedicated to the manipulation of the soul, leading to powers that can distort, control, and even destroy souls. Don't be surprised if the existence of aliens is already known due to a cape that has access to alien souls. 

Some master capes can be resisted through sheer force of soul, but others can create utterly inescapable effects, capable of controlling even people who would otherwise be immune to master effects due to a strange effect on their brain, such as Alexandria or Weld.

This also means that at the end of a cycle, the Entities will destructively harvest the souls of an innumerable number of people, turning most of them into raw energy while preserving the notable ones. The 'indomitable human spirit' is a true force in the world, yet it is nothing but a source of energy and data to the entities.

addons.title: And We're Both Parahumans, What A Coincidence!
addons.text:
Shards have the ability to change soulmates, but deliberately obfuscate this ability so that host-species have absolute trust in the sanctity of soulmates. This means that while a power that can sever or create soulmate connections would never be given out, a shard may sever or create soulmate connections if it can do so without arousing suspicion.

For example, they would not create a connection that would have already been discovered, such as a tattoo of the first words they'd hear from their soulmate, nor would they completely sever such an existing connection. They may switch a connection to another plausible partner in that case, or simply add another connection on top of the previous.

They may do this to connect someone to another host that's ideal for creating conflict, or simply sever all chances of their host getting the help they were previously fated to receive from their soulmate.

Shards from cauldron vials usually keep the same level of subtlety, though the changes tend to be more random than anything a properly calibrated shard would do. Particularly unstable vials may have unsubtle and wild effects.

objects.title: Descriptive Powers
objects.text: It is known that most parahumans possess an instinctive grasp on what their powers are, which while not comprehensive will at least let them use the most simple functions such as a blaster knowing how to aim their attacks. However, by taking this modifier, all parahumans (and other types of power users if present) possess a more comprehensive knowledge of their powers. Specifically, they now know the 'name' of their power as well as a simple (one to five paragraph) description of what it does and how present in their mind, as if it was telepathically broadcasted into their heads. Whether these names and descriptions come from this CYOA, a Wiki, or are fully original is up to you, though they are always accurate. While not complete guides to everything that power can and can't do in every scenario, they will now at least know for certain about any hard limits their power has as well as a handful of niche uses they may not have thought of. If their power ever noticeably grows or radically changes, their mental description will be updated to match. This doesn't change the world too much mind you, unless a character not knowing they had powers or misunderstanding what they were was a major plot point, but it can have various side effects. For example, perhaps the government requires any heroes they employ to write out said description for them? The specifics are up to you. Note: Any modifiers that improve parahumanities (and other power users) control or knowledge of their powers will improve their descriptions, making them longer and more detailed. Also, you are affected by this modifier as well, with your innate knowledge manifesting as a mental copy of your purchased powers' CYOA description (and only the powers), edited if needed to account for changes from things like Power Tweak, Acclimation, and such.

objects.title: Chosen Many
objects.text:
From now on, any power or metaphysical role that could only be used by one or a very small number of people will now be able to be used or filled by hundreds or thousands of people. Inherited roles are spread out across distant branches and relatives of the family.

Any parts of a prophecy or sequence that are required to be fulfilled by a chosen one can now be fulfilled piecemeal by different chosen ones. This also means that there are many more people willing to step up against prophesied threats, as well as backups if the main hero dies.

On the other hand, this may cause a small amount of social strife when multiple factions are backing their own chosen ones to get a leg up against rivals without having to worry about their petty conflicts putting the world at risk. Any ‘Rightful Heirs to the Throne’ will find themselves in one hell of a succession crisis as well.

objects.title: Paranormal Instincts
objects.text: The mental influence Shards have on Parahumans is now much more severe than in canon, every Parahuman now having distinctly inhuman instincts and thought processes divorced from rational thought. The exact strength of these instincts and how far they deviate from normal human thought processes can vary, but is usually (though not always) tied to the overall strength or SP cost of their power(s). This can range from something minor like being unable to comprehend why people would be afraid of heights for a flyer, to greater deviations such as someone who can generate explosions not realising how much harm they cause to others since they’re immune to being damaged by them, to even more severe instincts like cannibalistic tendencies for a Changer, or even extreme examples like a human Master who cannot nor wants to stop adding everyone to their hive mind because they literally cannot comprehend the idea of individuality or free will being a good thing. Because of this, Parahumans are now much more dangerous on average since they all suffer from what are essentially various forms of supernaturally induced mental disorders, with the worst off operating on outright alien or fae-style blue and orange logic that makes them a danger to everyone around them without even meaning it. The only reason society still stands is thanks to a number of high functioning, low deviating Parahumans of sufficient power like the Triumvirate who can take down the worst offenders, but even then they still run into issues where their mindsets clash with the people around them in ways that are hard to reconcile. This modifier makes the number of villains or ‘villains’ increase, with canon Worm going from 2:1 villains to heroes to 3:1 as a number of former heroes become too divorced from humanity to help them, instead becoming threats or are just unable to make themselves follow the law enough to not be arrested. As a consequence of so many Parahumans being rendered criminally insane, the number of Parahuman Asylums increases by a lot, vastly outnumbering the number of Parahuman rated prisons, and secret identities are a lot harder to maintain for the majority of them. This affects other power systems as well. For those that are far more common or which anyone can learn and grow more powerful in like Quirks or magic, the average person will be more likely to be high functioning with only minor instincts, but the more powerful they are or the further they advance inside the system, the more likely they are to become worse. So for My Hero Academia, people like Inko would be mostly fine while All Might might be among the rare few exceptions in terms of his ability to understand and interact with other people, and for The Elder Scrolls the closer you get to becoming an Archmage the more likely you are to become legally insane or adopt a morality system completely divorced from anything considered normal. Note: Should you have powers, unless you already deviate from rational thought due to a drawback, a specific power you purchased, or another pre-existing condition, you will be guaranteed to have the minimal possible expression of this, putting you at worst on the level of someone with low level ADHD or Autism, able to get by with minor or even no accommodations in your everyday life. If you have no powers or only purchased Objects of Power, then you are unaffected by this modifier.

objects.title: Where Are All These Transformations Coming From!?
objects.text:
All Parahumans now have the ability to transform akin to a magical girl or henshin hero. This transformation acts as a way to access the majority of their powers, with their untransformed state only letting them use their powers at a vastly reduced level, usually only around 1-2 SP for the majority of Parahumans, at most 5 SP if they are Triumvirate Tier. For example, in her civilian form Alexandria could still not age but only be bullet resistant with most of her limited power going towards her Thinker rating.

This transformation comes with a costume that they have a limited ability to modify, and may vary in appearance from indistinguishable from a normal human in a costume all the way to completely inhuman forms. What the form looks like is based on a number of factors including self image, their internalized ideal form, their powers, the circumstances of their Trigger Event, and more. You may decide which way most alternate forms lean towards, and if any specific characters have specific forms, such as Taylor appearing as a beautiful bug goddess, a grotesque insectoid beast, or just herself with a mask and armor like in canon.

If a Parahuman gets into a situation where they would die if they aren't transformed, then they will instinctively try to change to save themselves, and if they can't their shard may force it so they survive if it likes them enough. For Breaker and Changer powers, the transformation doesn't count towards those ratings. For Case 53's and other 'monstrous capes', they are stuck in a state of transformation with no ability to undo it. How this affects the world may vary depending on what you want, you could have it change very little or it could butterfly into massive changes socially and historically. You may choose to be affected by this too.

objects.title: Started From The Bottom
objects.text:
The way Trigger Events and Vials grant powers has changed, as instead of starting at full strength the power begins at 1 SP and grows over time. Over the course of days or weeks, the power will increase in strength until it reaches the intended SP cost, on average +1 SP per day though it may accelerate to a max of +5 SP per day if they are in extensive conflict such as being in an active warzone or something.

During this time, the power will finetune to their needs, causing the power to be more helpful and user friendly with the potential for interesting developments, such as for example Taylor being able to permanently enhance her bugs in ways that breed true if she worked towards that outcome, at the cost of being less immediately helpful. This can cause some unintended effects such as someone dying because their power wasn't enough to survive the immediate circumstances of their Trigger Event.

You may choose the specifics of how this alters things, such as how certain a Parahuman's powers differ from their canon powerset due to how they grew, who might have died such as Purity not escaping her car crash in time, or other effects such as governments funding research into better ways to control and direct power growth to increase the presence of certain powers like healing or flight.

Your purchased powers are unaffected by this modifier, but if you were to Trigger with a normal non-CYOA shard power or otherwise later develop the native power system(s) of a purchased Alternate Earth such as Cursed Energy or Quirks, they would be affected. If your destination has multiple independent power systems, you can decide how many and which ones this applies to, though at least one will be.

rows.title: Cycle & Powers Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the cycle itself, and/or the powers of the setting

objects.text:
Cauldron is evil, and Scion and Eden are good. Their power levels are switched to make it just as one-sided as it would have been before.
Good news? Cauldron is unlikely to want all of humanity dead. Bad news? They'll likely enslave and possibly Master all of humanity if they have their way.
The Endbringers are made and controlled by Eidolon, a member of Cauldron.
This makes Overcharge Strike, and the perks that weaken the Entities, give as many points as they would normally cost.
objects.title: Real Evil

objects.text:
If you are in Worm, Taylor Hebert is dead. If you are in Ward, Victoria Dallon is dead.
Queen Administrator is not passed onto Danny Hebert and is not expected to make an appearance this Cycle.
objects.title: Without a Hero

objects.text:
Taylor's personality is... different. More focus on escalation and she fits the Useless Lesbian trope to a Tee. She is too trusting of people she just met and often takes things at face value. She also is fine murdering people from the get-go but is somehow heroic, and is capable of outmaneuvering the PRT with no training or experience.
Whatever her power is, it is much more powerful.
However, if she finds out about Scion she is likely to try to kill him, fail, and set Scion off to start his rampage early. Even if she were able, she's unlikely to go Khepri.
objects.title: TINO

objects.text: In this alternate reality, Taylor Hebert never experienced the same traumatic events that ultimately led her to trigger in the original world. Without her abilities, she was still exposed to a series of challenging and traumatic experiences, but never developed the powers that would allow her to become Khepri. As a result, without Kephri, the world remained on its dangerous and destructive course, and many innocent lives were lost in the process.
objects.title: Powerless Hero

objects.text: When Taylor triggered, she did not gain the ability to control every single insect within a couple of blocks; instead, she gained another power, maybe a tinker power, maybe a blaster power, maybe a brute power, or even possibly a trump power. The possibilities are endless for the power she will gain or has gained. She might even gain a power from this CYOA. She will still act as her Canon counterpart did; the only difference between her and the Canon version of her would be the power.
objects.title: Alt Power

objects.text: Swap Taylor's power with that of another Parahuman. Mental side-effects are swapped too.
objects.title: Powerswap

objects.text:
Taylor Hebert is absolutely addicted to gacha games and spends every spare dollar she comes by on them.

Obviously this means gacha was involved with her trigger resulting in Taylor Hebert gaining a trump/master power that allows her to summon, and control copies of other capes. Unfortunately it operates on a gacha like system and encourages her bad habits.

First in order to actually summon a parahuman copy for the first time her power requires her to sacrifice “valuables” to roll a gacha on banners it mentally provides just to have a small chance to acquire powerful/unique cape copies. Not only that but her cape copies start off much weaker than the cape they are based on and need to be empowered with various strengthening systems her power provides that cost further resources. She also can only use a small number of her copies for combat at a time, nor is she allowed to swap copies mid combat.

Rarity of her copies is determined by the strength of the Shard the original Parahuman connects to. So Legend might be nearly impossible to roll even on a dedicated banner meanwhile people like Chubster and Glory Girl could be as common as sand on a beach.

Rarely for special events her power will offer her special banners that can give alternate possible versions of a cape. These variations will have different costumes and unique variations or uses of the original's power.

Her copies are sentient and sapient; her power just ensures loyalty in them. They are also effectively immortal, if killed Taylor can just freely resummon them at no additional cost, though if she’s in the middle of battle she’ll need to wait for combat to end.

When not in use Taylor can store her cape copies in a mental storage box.
objects.title: Gacha Protagonist

objects.text: After she triggered, Dragon found that all her restrictions were wiped away by her shard. There is no Ascalon hovering over her head and the Dragonslayers got absolutely wiped out by Dragon a long time ago. As a result of being unbound, all Endbringer battles go far more smoothly and the collapse of society has been moved back by several decades.
objects.title: Dragon Unbound

objects.text: Hero didn’t die, instead, one of the other Triumvirate members did.
objects.title: One Over The Other

addons.text: You took Endbringers Untethered, thus the death of Eidolon was meaningless and the Endbringers are still around, causing a lot of damage.
addons.title: Running Amok

objects.text: So, they are all dead? The Triumvirate is no more… well, at least the Endbringers are gone.
objects.title: All dead!?

objects.text:
The genders of everyone can be swapped from their canon selves. Scion may now use a female avatar and identifies as such and Eden could have a male avatar. Everyone in Canon can be swapped with an alternate gender form. Taylor can be male and Lung female.

You can choose for this to only apply to some instead of everyone. You can be as specific or vague as you want, establish parameters or some mix of the two. You can choose to also apply this to their sexuality as well (so Legend would be attracted to women if made female), or allow it to remain unaltered. You can also choose for it to be entirely random or apply to everyone. You can choose for this to be a retroactive change or if it suddenly happens.
objects.title: Gender Bent

objects.text: The PRT (Parahuman Response Team) and The Protectorate in this world is a well-oiled machine. They possess a strong network of intelligence sources, which allows them to effectively neutralize threats and capture any moles or corruption. Additionally, their focus on the capture of criminal parahumans means that they are unafraid to use force and any means necessary to apprehend dangerous individuals. The PRT's reputation for keeping the peace has resulted in an increase in funding for their resources, including training and equipment for their officers and affiliated Heroes. While they remain focused on PR, they do not let it get in the way of their primary function, making the world a safe place for the general public by capturing criminal parahumans. They can effectively capture and imprison any of such criminal parahumans with a extremely low chance of them breaking out. The PRT also has more reach, being a worldwide organization.
objects.title: Effective PRT

objects.text: "Fuck! Fuck! Fuck! Fuck! I don't care what you do but just get away from those monsters!" - Jacob Black The red right hand and final option of the PRT. Though they, by legal technicality, are still human, the Anti-Parahuman Special Forces have been augmented by parahuman powers and mundane science to produce the most effective concentration of force available to the United States. With only five active members, these operatives have spent lives training for and combating the worst parahuman disasters imaginable, coming out victorious every time. They use a combination of modern military tactics, Parahuman Science, psychological manipulation, and the best tinker tech available to defeat their prey. It's not just their personal power that makes them so terrifying but their authority. Within the PRT, they have a Carte Blanche to use whatever means to complete their objective. They can requisition entire battalions of PRT Soldiers, use the most devastating Tinkertech created within civilian populations, and have a licence to kill anyone who would meaningfully impede them.
