The PRT would consider dropping a nuclear bomb before ever deploying the Anti-Parahuman Special Forces.
objects.title: Anti-Parahuman Special Forces

objects.text:
The Parahuman Response Team (PRT) is a paramilitary unit created by the United States, and tasked with with managing the response to the rising threat of Parahumans and the advent of the "Age of Superheroes". Their primary role being to support and provide oversight over the government sponsored Superhero organization, the Protectorate. Eventually the PRT spread it's reach across the border into Canada, with talks of one-day extending into Mexico as well. 

Now instead the PRT—and therefore the Protectorate—was created under the auspices of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), with each member state possessing their own branch, and providing funding, personnel, equipment and support for the organization as a whole.

While this version of the PRT might be managed by NATO, they are considered very much NOT military units or assets... though if war was to break out it is very likely much of the organization would be called into service to counter other nation-states Parahuman assets.
objects.title: PRT International

objects.text:
Coil is not an independent criminal mastermind. The organization exists as a deliberate false-flag operation, sanctioned off-books by the PRT to shape, absorb, and redirect villain activity.

The group operates as a disposable buffer between genuine villains and the Protectorate. By presenting a powerful, centralized criminal authority, Coil draws in mercenaries, rogue capes, and ambitious criminals who might otherwise fragment into unpredictable threats.

Thomas Calvert is selected as Coil’s public leader due to his psychological profile: ambitious, controllable, and replaceable. He knows that he is being sanctioned, aware that his resources, intelligence leaks, and long-term survival are carefully constrained.

Emily Piggot is the first contact of the operation’s true nature. She uses Coil as a pressure valve, allowing controlled criminal escalation to justify funding increases, emergency powers, and strategic redeployments without triggering federal intervention.

The PRT allows Coil limited successes and carefully managed failures. When operations exceed acceptable thresholds, information is selectively leaked to heroes or rival factions to cut him down to size.

If Coil is exposed or destroyed, the PRT denies all involvement. Evidence is buried, witnesses discredited, and Calvert is treated as a rogue asset who went too far.

Coil could not be the only one of those operations but is the only one in the Bay.
objects.title: Coil The Orange

objects.text:
The Wards program never really managed to take off. Instead, young heroes are under a division of the Protectorate, the Sidekick program. 

Under this program, young capes are paired up with ‘mentors’ in their local branch with a similar or complementary power set, approach or (if Image gets their way) aesthetic. While this usually means individual bonds and training is stronger, it does place young capes in more harm’s way due to being around more experienced heroes in more dangerous situations.
objects.title: Wards? I mean, a few of us are?

objects.text: The trio who bullied Taylor Hebert (Sophia Hess, Emma Barnes, and Madison Clements) are not just any high school girls but also parahumans. They are all part of the Wards and have stronger legal protections than they originally did. Should Taylor find out, she will lose more faith in any form of authority. The strength of their powers is roughly equal to one another.
objects.title: Parahuman Three

objects.text: Emma Barnes, Sophia Hess, and Madison Clements. These three girls joined together for one common purpose: to make Taylor's life miserable. Pretty much everyday the Trio would bully her over and over again, escalating until they made her Trigger, then kept going just for fun. And now, by taking this Modifier, you've added another member to their core group. Whether a minor named character, an expy of someone from another series, or an original character, there are now four girls acting as Taylor's bullies. Or maybe there's five? Or six? Each time you take this, add one more member up to nine total including the original three. The more people there are, the worse Taylor's life is as the pressure mounts and each new member of their posse brings with them a new wealth of ideas on how to make her suffer. If there are nine in total, expect Taylor to be a complete nervous wreck who may snap and kill either herself or everyone around her with just a little push. The individuals added to the Trio with this modifier may also be affected by any other modifier that targets them, either as a group or individually. Perhaps all 4+ are superpowered Wards if you took Parahuman Three, or maybe only the new girl is a Ward, having joined in the bullying after befriending Shadow Stalker over their mutual bloodlust and sadistic tendency to want to crush others that they had to hide from the other Wards. The specifics of how this works is entirely up to you. Note: Technically, not all of the new bullies have to be girls. Maybe Emma met a guy and they bonded over insulting Taylor, or Taylor went on a 'date' only to be humiliated by her new 'boyfriend' who turned out to be Madison's date instead, or something worse. Bullying knows no gender after all.
objects.title: The Trio? I Think You Mean the Quartet? Or Was It the Quintet?

objects.text: Within a month of her stay inside the Birdcage Ciara/Glaistig Uaine and her Shard grew bored of her stay, and so they began to experiment, causing Shard and humans to merge into one. This had several effects, including granting her power the Tier 3 powers Oberon and The Friend Bringer, and she has become a nascent entity who is using the birdcage to ensure no one realizes what she has become. Along with this, their hybrid minds began to grasp the [ANSWER] though it will take a decade from your arrival for them to complete the [ANSWER].
objects.title: Queen of the Fay Courts

objects.text:
Cauldron was never successfully formed because Contessa and Doctor Mother died before they managed to create it. Parahumans run rampant, destroying and carving their little kingdoms out of the world. Humanity has fallen into a state of barbarism, cruelty, and the crushing of the weak.

This has led to the founding of the Protectorate never occurring, nor the rise of Hero, Legend, Alexandria, and Eidolon. Along with this, any individual that got their powers from Cauldron never received their powers, including all case 53.
objects.title: Shattered Cauldron

objects.text:
One purchase of this modifier makes it so that instead of triggering with QA, Taylor Hebert gained access to a Shardless non-parahuman power of roughly equivalent strength/potential to the power she would’ve received from QA. With that power scaling with any modifiers to her potential Shard power you’ve purchased.

You are free to choose what power she received within reason; whether that be magic, vampirism, psychic power, being a psychic vampire magus, or making her a megaman style genius roboticist.

If you chose for this world to be a crossover setting, and the power you chose to give Taylor comes from one of the settings of the crossover. You are free to have the explanation for Taylor having that power make sense for the world in question. For example she might have Magus relatives in a nasuverse crossover to explain her being trained in magecraft. Otherwise if she has a power that doesn’t exist in this world expect for her to have a benefactor, or some other logical reasoning for her to possess that power.

Depending on the power in question, it might be something she received, or unlocked years before she triggered in canon, possibly even at birth, then received training in its use. For example in order for magecraft to compete with her canon Parahuman power it’s perfectly possible for her to have first-rate magic circuits, receive magecraft training from a young age, and even a magic crest.

With the second purchase Taylor Hebert still gained a Shardless non-parahuman power, but she also triggered with a Shard power that complements her esoteric powerset.
objects.title: Esoteric Protagonist

objects.text: The constant abuse from the government and the lost of his wife caused Danny to trigger with a bud from Queen Administrator (or whatever shard Taylor currently has). What power he has and what he does with it is up to you. The strength of his power cannot exceed 10 SP.
objects.title: A Father’s Strength

addons.text: Danny, after triggering, fell into depravity to cope. He became a leader of a gang, and had a level of infamy and as any other gang leader in Brockton had. The gang can be completely new, a gang he took over, or the dockworkers turned to crime.
addons.title: Villain Gang

addons.text: Danny, after triggering, fell into the dark to cope. He became a leader of a gang, but unlike most gang leaders did acts to revitalize his territory. While he never played by the rule’s authorities had, and was considered a gang leader on paper, the people saw him as a benevolent warlord and a hero to some.
addons.title: Redeemed Villain

objects.text: Danny Hebert suffered horribly from depression after the death of his wife, and the decline of the dockworker union has led to him becoming a shell of his former self. All he does is work, eat, and sleep, and once in a while, he cleans himself up to look presentable enough to continue working. As long as nothing interferes with that, he won't pay attention to anything else. Taylor could stop living in the house, and he wouldn't even notice.
objects.title: The Completely Depressed Father

addons.text: Danny, after triggering, became a hero to cope. He became extremely well liked in Brockton Bay, and due to his strength was able to greatly assist the existing heroes. You can choose whether he gets his own team or joins the Protectorate.
addons.title: Great Hero

objects.text:
Danny Hebert was a lost man without his wife. He suffered from depression until the trigger of his daughter, where he was simply going through the motions currently but one large shock is enough to send him into action, revitalizing the man who can range from being the sole reason the Dockworker Union is still up and running, or being the parahuman leader of the fourth major gang of Brockton Bay, or being a member of the Protectorate. No matter what he is, after the trigger of Taylor Hebert, he will use everything available to him to hurt whoever hurts his child.

(You can choose who/what Danny Hebert is, or leave it up to random chance.)
objects.title: The Hypercompetent Father

objects.text:
The Dockworkers Union (DWU) of Brockton Bay isn’t just a failing workers' organization anymore—now, they are legendary.

Decades of struggle, hardship, and backroom deals have shaped the DWU into an entity that even the most hardened criminals and parahuman gangs think twice about messing with. These aren't just your average blue-collar workers; these are ex-mercenaries, retired soldiers, and former gangsters who chose an honest living but never lost their edge. Some of them have pasts shrouded in mystery—whispers about black ops, international espionage, or connections to shadowy organizations. Others are local legends who have survived more shootouts, knife fights, and bar brawls than most capes ever will.

Even without parahuman abilities, the DWU commands respect. They own the docks, and if something illegal is coming through Brockton Bay’s port, they know about it. The Empire, the ABB, Coil—none of them push too hard, because when the DWU gets involved, people disappear, shipments get "lost," and entire operations mysteriously collapse overnight. There are even rumors that certain dockworkers have "contacts" in organizations far beyond Brockton Bay—government agencies, old-school mafias, or even Cauldron itself.

Danny Hebert is no struggling, overworked man trying to hold his union together. He is a force of nature. A union boss with a reputation that can make even villains hesitate. If he calls for a strike, the city grinds to a halt. If he calls in a favor, things happen. He’s seen things, done things, and somehow still believes in doing right by his people.

Capes and criminals alike know one simple rule: You do not fuck with the Dockworkers Union.
objects.title: Dockworkers Union: The Fandom Edition

objects.text: Rather than die and leave behind a broken family, Annette Hebert triggers with a power that allows her to survive the car crash. Her powers must cost less than or equal to 10 SP. Annette is not connected to QA but instead gains strength from some other shard. QA is still observing Danny or Taylor as potential hosts. What Annette does with this power is up to you.
objects.title: Unbroken Family

objects.text:
Well this is odd. Rather than Trigger or simply carry on with his life, in the aftermath of Annette’s death Danny Hebert instead decided that he would drag Brockton Bay into a new era of prosperity, kicking and screaming if he had to. 

To this end, he sought out the power brokers and acquired a Vial for himself, gaining a stronger version of (Thinker) Schrödinger with greater range and fewer limitations. Taking the Cape name Coil, Danny would go about spreading his influence throughout the city, making heavy use of mercenaries and his Thinker power to present an air of seeming infallibility. On a completely unrelated note, Thomas Calvert never made it out of Ellisburg.

It should be noted that while Danny’s goal is improving Brockton Bay and he is much less reprehensible than Calvert would have been - with his method of recruiting Dinah being to approach her with a convincing and genuine offer of employment and protection - he is still a villain and commits less than moral acts such as recruiting Tattletale with force. 

Lastly, due to the workings of his Thinker power, from his perspective Danny can have up to days worth of memories without ever interacting with Taylor, causing him to be much more distant from her and her home life to suffer as a result.
objects.title: Familial Deviation

objects.text: Having two capes as loving parents has its fair share of positive and negative effects on a person’s life, most relevant to Taylor Hebert though is that it makes it much easier to Trigger. Taylor Hebert triggers long before the locker incident and is in a better headspace. Mind you, the powers you gave her parents designed her powerset to have a limit of 10 SP. Whatever her parents have decided to use their powers for Taylor has likely followed in their footsteps at least initially.
objects.title: Second Gen Protagonist

objects.text: As many or as few members of the Hebert family as you want triggered with a stronger power. Up to 5 SP increase to the budget you purchase their powers with per purchase.
objects.title: Super Family

objects.text:
Instead of Annette Hebert it was Danny Hebert who lost his life, and left behind a grieving family.

He doesn’t have to have died in a car accident, instead you are free to choose his cause of death as long as it makes sense for this world.

This also doesn’t mean Annette got off unscathed; it's perfectly possible she still got into a car accident, especially if another option requires her to have had it. Annette will just survive that car accident here unless it makes more sense for her to have died because of other Modifiers.
objects.title: Parent Swap

objects.text: Well, this is awkward, a few months before Taylor was pushed into her locker and triggered, and her surviving parent started dating again. Good for them but through some odd chain of events they ended up dating an adult parahuman of your choice. If that parahuman is known to be in a relationship in canon then maybe here they separated from that partner sometime before this point or more depressingly their original partner might no longer be among the living. Alternatively, that parent can get together with a parahuman who is still married and their partner is also part of this relationship. The explanation for this could be as simple as the couple looking to spice up their marriage and finding that Taylor’s parent slotted perfectly into their relationship. While the exact details are mostly up to you under no circumstances did anyone “steal” someone else’s spouse. Whatever the case her parent’s new partner or partners have taken a shine to Taylor seeing her as a true member of their family which can optionally affect her trigger event and the resulting power.
objects.title: New Family New Heberts

objects.text:
Circumstances surrounding Taylor Hebert’s trigger were different in comparison to canon. Instead of triggering alone she would end up triggering around the same time as another person in Brockton Bay forming a cluster.

In addition to her canon power, choose one additional tier 1 power with a maximum cost of 10 SP to give her to reflect whoever is her clustermate.

Each additional purchase increases the number of clustermates and thus powers Taylor has by one. Each additional power is still limited to a maximum of 10 SP.

If another modifier changes the power Taylor would receive it only affects her primary power and the power her clustermate inherits from her, her personal cluster mate based powers remain at your discretion.

You may decide how much or how little any powers Taylor has synergize.

A number of different scenarios will crop up because of this additional power that will make it so Taylor more firmly pursues the path of heroism than canon.
objects.title: Grab-Bag Heroine Protagonist

objects.text:
Circumstances surrounding Taylor Hebert’s trigger were different in comparison to canon. Instead of triggering alone she would end up triggering around the same time as another person in Brockton Bay forming a cluster.

In addition to her canon power, choose one additional tier 1 power with a maximum cost of 10 SP to give her to reflect whoever is her clustermate.

Each additional purchase increases the number of clustermates and thus powers Taylor has by one. Each additional power is still limited to a maximum of 10 SP.

If another modifier changes the power Taylor would receive it only affects her primary power and the power her clustermate inherits from her, her personal cluster mate based powers remain at your discretion.

You may decide how much or how little any powers Taylor has synergize.

Despite or perhaps even because of this additional power circumstances will align so Taylor still ends up a villain just like in canon.
objects.title: Grab-Bag Villainess Protagonist

objects.text: Soon after triggering, Jack Slash was mauled to death by twenty perfectly ordinary bears. This means the Slaughterhouse Nine broke apart with King's death and Bonesaw never triggered.
objects.title: Slaughterhousn’t

objects.text:
Instead of falling into a nihilistic spiral after his Trigger Event and clinging to his need for a legacy, the boy known as Jacob Black turned that on its head, clinging to stories his gene donors narrated on the few times they decided to be parents—of stories of knights and chivalry, of the Seventh Seal—the boy found something to hold onto. 

While displaying sociopathic tendencies he holds himself to a code, infiltrating the Slaughterhouse Nine to mitigate any needless suffering or casualties, while sabotaging the group from within with Harbinger as a partner. 

After eliminating King, Jacob became aware of his latent talent and promised Number Man (after becoming a member of Cauldron) to establish a consistent yet controllable quantity of Triggers for the future, becoming a wandering Hero, always at the right place and the right time of parahuman activity that intentionally spurs people into situations that push them to their limit, ensuring their Trigger Event isn’t as damaging to their psyche as usually is and earning favor from his Passenger at once. 

The moment you arrive [Broadcast] already sees Jacob in the same vein as Jack in Canon: an excellent [Host], circumventing his limits to grant Jacob Cleave and Lacerate with Sender and Receiver, with the Black Knight capable of controlling the narrative at a moment’s notice, which served him to become a media darling.
objects.title: Rise of the Black Knight

objects.text:
Jacob Black, more widely recognized as the infamous leader of the Slaughterhouse 9—known as Jack Slash—triggered his powers at the young age of 12. His induction into the group was forced upon him by King, and later that year, with the assistance of fellow member Harbinger, Jack managed to kill King and seize control of the organization.

However, there his story diverged from the typical path of villainy. Instead of continuing down the trail of chaos and destruction, Jack contacted the PRT and surrendered himself. Due to his youth, he was deemed not fully culpable and was consequently cleared of serious charges. Jack was eventually adopted by Annette’s family—becoming her brother and finding a semblance of stability and normalcy.

Over time, society’s understanding of parahuman abilities grew considerably. One of the most critical realizations was that powers often have a compulsive need to be used—an innate desire that can lead to negative consequences for the parahuman if left unfulfilled. Some abilities, in particular, require violence or conflict with others, regardless of the host’s wishes. This new understanding prompted a reevaluation of how to handle parahumans like Jack.

As a result, the Slaughterhouse 9 was reformed, this time as a clandestine hybrid of therapy group and black ops unit, targeting only “acceptable” threats.

While feared by the public as the deadly Jack Slash, Jacob has become a leading figure in parahuman psychology, pioneering methods to understand and treat powers and their effects. Less publicly known is his relationship as the uncle to Taylor Hebert. Meanwhile, Shatterbird is a Protectorate hero in her day-to-day life, with a power that needs to unleash on a populated area every so often—and Bonesaw, one of the foremost experts on the Coronary Pollentia and Gemma, often called upon when power connections are damaged or unstable.

Many other members of the new Slaughterhouse 9 have their own stories—paths of redemption and change shaped by the circumstances they faced in canon, now finding new purpose within this reformed organization.
objects.title: Jacob [Redacted] and the S9

objects.text:
During King’s leadership of the Slaughterhouse Nine, Jack and Kurt—better known as Harbinger—develop a genuine romantic relationship. This bond forms quietly, under constant threat, and in direct opposition to King’s control-based leadership.

King discovers the relationship and attempts to use it as leverage. Instead, it becomes the reason for his death. Jack and Kurt kill King together, deliberately and without outside assistance, dismantling his authority in a single coordinated act.

After King’s death, the Slaughterhouse Nine reorganizes around Jack and Harbinger as a pair rather than a single leader. The group becomes more stable, more selective, and far more difficult to predict. Loyalty within the Nine shifts from fear of punishment to belief in inevitability.

With Kurt never joining Cauldron, the Number Man never exists. Cauldron loses its primary logistical and probabilistic stabilizer, forcing it to rely on inferior planning, slower response times, higher operational risk and a worse global economy.
objects.title: Jack & Harbinger

objects.text:
Instead of becoming a poster child of Master powers (and not in a good way), Nikos Vasil, infamously known as the villain Heartbreaker, was quickly found out after he began his villainous streak. The Protectorate easily signed a kill order for Nikos, and he was put down before he could build up his numbers. 

For how little he actually seems to do in canon Earth Bet, his early death surprisingly has a few effects on the world.

Firstly, and most obviously, the stigma surrounding Master Powers is noticeably weaker. It still exists because of other human-type Masters such as Teacher and Valefor, but it is less pervasive.

This affects the trial of Canary, which becomes comparatively fairer. She is not restrained merely for being "suspected of a Brute rating" and may be allowed to speak, albeit under heavy surveillance and security. However, her ability to contact a lawyer is likely still hindered, unless the Simurgh is removed or otherwise neutralized as a factor.

Secondly, many of the children Heartbreaker would've had in his later years, such as Jean-Paul, Juliette, and Roman Vasil, are never born as his early death prevents their conception. Cherie Vasil, also known as Cherish, may be among the few, if not the only, of Heartbreaker's children to still exist.
objects.title: Sheer Heart Attack

objects.text: Brockton Bay Brigade didn't attack Marquis in his home; instead, they attacked Allfather in his home. This resulted in him, his son, and his daughter being birdcaged and the Empire fracturing. This had many butterfly effects. Theo Anders, now Theo Dallon, was adopted by the Dallon family in the aftermath of the Empire’s collapse. He triggered soon after Victoria did, his power manifesting under the pressure of constantly being compared to her and pushed to “do better” by Carol. Marquis, meanwhile, still leads his gang, which has grown into one of the three dominant factions in the city. With his daughter Amelia Claire Lavere by his side, his gang enforces a strict code of conduct, minimizing collateral damage and keeping the more chaotic elements of Brockton Bay’s criminal scene in check. While his methods remain ruthless and criminal, his presence has brought a kind of stability to the underworld. The sudden destruction of the Empire cut the momentum under the feet of the remnants and neo-Nazim returned to being a fringe ideology in Brockton Bay; by the time Brad Meadows triggered, only a small group of hardcore believers remained, irrelevant on the greater scene. Instead Brad, who goes by the name of Steel Alpha, founded The Pack, a gang built around a brutal “survival of the fittest” philosophy. They recruited from a wider range of parahumans, including the likes of Shadow Stalker and Bitch. The ABB and Coil's Organisation still remain, while the Merchants never successfully formed due to the influence of Marquis. Brockton Bay in general has less capes (at least less than 10 from canon) and crime is lowered due to Marquis enforcing certain rules. Many capes may have either joined the Protectorate or simply never turned to crime at all; Uber and Leet work as Rogues, Purity operates as a hero, and both Rune and Grue serve as Wards.
objects.title: Fallen Empire

objects.text:
Kayden was a divisive figure within Worm, a high-ranking member of the Neo-Nazi organization, The Empire Eighty-Eight. She attempted to leave this life behind her, but not for ideological reasons—instead, she simply wanted to distance herself from her ex-husband, Max “Kaiser” Anders.

Kayden's life took a turn early on after she crashed while driving for the first time at just 16 years old, and triggering. After encountering the charismatic Kaiser when she started going out in costume, she was convinced by his good looks and persuasive way with words to follow his “way of thinking,” leading her to join the Empire.

But what if that had changed? What if, instead, Kayden encountered a more positive influence when she was just starting out? Instead of meeting the charismatic Kaiser, who was ready to twist a young, naive cape into a life of racism and villainy, she meets the Brockton Bay Brigade—a local group of heroes willing to show her the way.

Instead of joining the Empire, Kayden is convinced to join the Brigade. Along with her newfound team, she unmasked herself before the world as a public cape. Instead of the racist Neo-Nazi Purity, she now stands as the respected hero Kayden “Polaris” Russell of New Wave.

Changing Kayden’s allegiance has many knock-on effects. The Empire is forced to be more cautious without a powerful blaster, and New Wave becomes more proactive with such a cape on their side.

Whether this version of Kayden would ever marry Max Anders, become stepmother to Theo Anders, or give birth to Aster Anders is up to you to decide.
objects.title: Purity? No, I'm Polaris

objects.text:
The Brockton Bay Brigade never attacked Marquis in his home. As a result, his daughter Amelia was never adopted by Carol and Mark Dallon, and Marquis was never sentenced to the Birdcage.

Marquis, by his own admission, is not a ‘good’ man, though he follows his own code of honor. Despite this, he continues as a crime lord in Brockton Bay, building his influence and power. The addition of this new element to the already volatile situation in canon Brockton Bay is unclear; it could either set things off or help to stabilize them.

His daughter will eventually trigger at approximately the same time and with the same powers, but the path she chooses is entirely up to you. Perhaps she would join her father and become a villain, bending biology to her will. Maybe she would become a rogue, accepting money to heal or perform swift, painless cosmetic surgery. Or perhaps she would follow her canon path to become ‘Panacea,’ trying to save and heal as many as she can. Alternatively, she might choose a completely different route altogether.
objects.title: The Marcher Lord

objects.text:
Fleur never met her end at the hands of a wanna-be Empire thug. As a result Lightstar never leaves New Wave, or enters Witness Protection. Without this tragedy to mar the New Wave movement, it continues on gaining momentum, with many more Parahumans choosing to have open identities. 

New Wave is a larger force than in canon, consisting of more capes, and even non-powered support.
objects.title: Blooming Flower

addons.text:
Remarkably, Hero manages to survive what was his canon fate at the hands of the Siberian. While the Golden Age of Heroes may have still come to an end, it did not slow the rising tide of heroism itself. 

Despite the difficulties of this period, more heroes consistently emerge to face them head-on. The balance between heroes and villains evens out to approximately 1:1. This new equilibrium gives the Heroes a greater ability to combat the rising threats that emerge.
addons.title: Triumphant Hero

objects.text:
Andrew Hawke, better known by his heroic alias Vikare, was widely regarded as the first hero. He wielded a Tier 1 power “(Mover/Master) Let The Feathers Fly”. Despite his formidable abilities, Vikare was often reluctant to use his powers openly, fearing that they would frighten those he sought to protect. Tragically, this hesitation would ultimately lead to his downfall.

In 1989, during a chaotic riot sparked by a controversial basketball game, Vikare attempted to restore order. In the heat of the moment, he was struck over the head with a club and succumbed to his injuries shortly after, marking the end of the Golden Age of Heroes.

Only now? This is no longer the case. Rather than dying, he only fell unconscious and subsequently awoke in a hospital. During his recovery, he underwent a Second Trigger, which granted him the upgrade "On Crystal Wings."

With Vikare’s survival, the Golden Age of Heroes continued, albeit with its own set of challenges. Unfortunately, this era faced a significant turning point with the death of Hero. Vikare’s survival causes a shift in the dynamics of the hero-villain landscape, increasing the number of active heroes while altering the ratio of heroes to villains from 1:2 to approximately 1:1.5.
objects.title: Vikare Resilient

objects.text: Doctor Alan Gramme—better known at the time as Sphere—was a highly capable tinker who dedicated his life to trying to solve the world's problems, until the Simurgh got involved. The Third Endbringer attacked the site he was working on—the site where his beloved wife and children were present. With his family perishing in the attack, Sphere went mad, shutting out the world literally by containing himself in a self-contained ecosystem, and becoming Mannequin—a dark, twisted reflection of his former self. Where Sphere sought to save, Mannequin sought to destroy. Targeting Tinkers trying to better the world and killing them, Mannequin eventually joined the group of serial killers known as the Slaughterhouse 9, becoming one of their more tragic members. But here, you can change Sphere’s tragedy before it begins. Somehow, Sphere’s family never dies. Perhaps they simply weren’t present? Or maybe they were evacuated in time? This doesn’t prevent the Simurgh’s attack, but it does prevent some of the casualties. Whatever site Sphere is working on is almost certainly a total loss, and the Tinker himself may be harmed to some extent in the process. However, with his family safe, Sphere’s fall from grace is prevented. As for the changes that occur? They are almost beyond calculation. By 2011, the initial colonization of the Moon has begun, with small settlements being constructed. Thanks to Sphere’s contributions, the infamous Birdcage prison is much more secure, able to provide a more “natural” environment and be far more self-sustaining. Without his descent into Mannequin, many more Tinkers willing to better humanity would survive, bringing forth their capabilities in the hope of a brighter future.
objects.title: Sphere of Influence

objects.text: Dr. William Manton was a brilliant scientist, one of the foremost experts on parahumans, and a key member of Cauldron. His work focused on understanding the mechanics behind parahuman abilities, and he is best remembered for his discovery of the “Manton Effect,” named in his honor. Aside from his groundbreaking research, Manton’s life was largely centered around his beloved daughter. Everything changed drastically for Dr. Manton when she drank one of the Cauldron Vials he had engineered—and did not survive the experience. Overcome with grief and madness, Manton ingested another vial himself. In doing so, he gained the ability to generate a projection that took on his daughter’s likeness. This tragic turn of events led to a conflict with his former friends and allies, culminating in the death of one of the original Protectorate members Hero and the half-blinding of another, Alexandria. But what if that outcome had been different? What if his daughter had drunk not the vial that ultimately killed her, but the one that Manton himself eventually consumed? Then instead of dying she gained the power of (Master) Manton, with the ability to speak through the minion while controlling it from more than 300 meters away. Manton's daughter goes on to join the Protectorate, earning fame as the “ultimate” Master—on par with those such as Hero the Tinker, Alexandria the Brute, Legend the Blaster or Eidolon the Trump. With an ongoing Hero career as “Siberian,” her presence significantly alters the landscape of Earth Bet. Hero no longer falls to the monstrous Siberian but perhaps instead to the Endbringers or he succumbs to natural causes. Alexandria’s reputation for invincibility remains intact, and the threat of the Slaughterhouse Nine diminishes, their perceived danger reduced without one of their most formidable members. Consequently, during Leviathan’s attack on Naples, the defenders are better prepared, resulting in fewer casualties and fewer converts to the organization that would eventually become the Fallen. As the original Protectorate members go their separate ways to establish their own departments within the larger organization, Siberian eventually settles in Chicago, heading the Protectorate branch there. Meanwhile, Dr. Manton continues to lead advances in parahuman research, achieving further breakthroughs and successes.
objects.title: Siberian... the Hero?

objects.text:
Doormaker was a vital asset within the organization known as Cauldron, possessing the ability to open portals to anywhere he could see or remember seeing. In cooperation with Clairvoyant, Doormaker could open portals wherever the organization’s members needed them, even across dimensions.

However, beyond this, Doormaker's impact was quite limited. His lengthy and repeated exposure to Clairvoyant’s power left him effectively blind and deaf to the world around him, relying solely on the connection provided by Clairvoyant.

Yet, with this, you can enhance Doormaker’s abilities ever so slightly. First, you can untether his portals from the rotation of whatever world they are on. Second, you can grant him a small multi-tasking ability that allows him to operate portals more effectively in combat situations.

These subtle improvements enable Doormaker to become much more effective, allowing him to step out of the shadows and assume a more prominent role. He could then join the original Protectorate as the “Ultimate” Mover.

When the original team disbands to establish Protectorate departments across the country, Doormaker settles in Phoenix, Arizona, where he leads the local team.

With Doormaker’s enhanced capabilities, rapid response to S-Rank crises—such as Endbringer attacks—is greatly improved, making it easier to confront and contain such foes, and slowing the collapse of civilization greatly.
objects.title: Gatekeeper

objects.text: Clairvoyant was a vital asset within the organization known as Cauldron, possessing the ability to view wide areas across dimensions, whole cities, or specific people. In cooperation with Doormaker, Clairvoyant could recognize people asking for portals from anyone in the known multiverse, allowing portals to be opened wherever the organization’s members needed them. However Clairvoyant was crippled from the beginning, his mind never developing past the point he gained his powers, and his eyes burning out leaving empty sockets behind. Now? Now, that will change. Instead Clairvoyant is allowed to mentally “grow up” at the rate he should have, he gains control preventing the side effects that so crippled him. This control also allows him to share what his power allows him to see with others, without unintentionally overloading them. With this control, and a minor multi-tasking ability Clairvoyant is able to be more than just another asset to Cauldron, stepping into the light as the strongest Thinker—at least the strongest publicly known Thinker—joining the original Protectorate as the “Ultimate” Thinker. When the original team disbands to establish Protectorate departments across the country, Clairvoyant becomes the head of the Detroit Protectorate. Clairvoyants abilities also lead to him being highly placed in the Protectorate “Think Tank” for strategic Thinker usage, and result in the Protectorate being able to succeed in various operations more frequently.
objects.title: Eye Spy, with my All-Seeing Eye

objects.text:
The Custodian was an asset of some importance, serving as an unseen containment measure for the Deviants (better known as Case 53s) in the Cauldron Compound, a woman made of air, using her powers to guard all the prisoners, doubling as Scion’s deterrent. Unable to change to her old body owing to her improperly formatted Shard from a Cauldron Vial, she’s left as Cauldron’s willing caretaker.

Now, when she drinks her Vial, her Shard will properly connect, as well as expanding how she expresses her power. What could’ve been her body she’s stuck with is now a Breaker form she can shift between at will, with a small thinker aspect in the form of minor multitasking and awareness of every temporary duplicate she creates with her powers, being essentially omnipresent in her Breaker form, while also heightening her aerokinetic control over the area.

These slight changes make her take a much more overt role in Cauldron—covert assassinations by inexplicable asphyxiations are on the rise—while also taking a step into the limelight, joining the original Protectorate as the “Ultimate” Breaker.

When the original team disbands to establish Protectorate departments across the country, the Custodian becomes the head of the Washington Protectorate.

With the Custodian’s unseen presence out in the open, any sort of covert operations needed some high-stakes surveillance, reconnaissance, or silent takedowns; she’s the girl you call.
objects.title: Vigil

objects.text: One of the greatest threats encountered in Worm, is the Parahuman known as “Echidna”. Echidna—or Noelle Meinhardt—resulted from the Simurgh’s attack on Madison, Wisconsin. She and the rest of the Travelers were drawn through to Earth Bet during the attack, before coming across a half-dozen Cauldron Vials. Noelle only consumed half of the power granting Vial, with another member Oliver drinking the other half. Due to only receiving half of the Vial, Noelle’s power was incomplete. Resulting in her turning into a monstrous chimera able to consume capes, only to generate twisted clones of them with variant powersets. Yet this tragedy only resulted from there being an insufficient number of Vials for each of the future Travelers to have one, but now you can change that. With this modifier, another Vial will be included in the collection the Travelers will find, this can be any power worth 15 SP, and will ultimately be drunk by Oliver. Noelle on the other hand? Due to her consuming the full vial, her power is now “complete”, she will no longer transform into the chimeric abomination that would become Echidna, instead her power allows her to take the form and powers of Parahumans she’s touched. Noelle can carry over some of her own inherent characteristics if she choses, such as every form being female. She can no longer create an army, but gains versatility in exchange. This modifier prevents the S-Rank disaster that would have been Echidna, and Echidna’s exposure of Alexandria’s secret identity and the organization known as Cauldron. However it does not do anything about any psychological twisting the Simurgh may have performed on the Travelers, potentially resulting in them being “Simurgh Bombs” of some description.
objects.title: One More Vial

objects.text:
In canon, Riley Davis triggered at a young age, desperately struggling to keep her family alive through the tortures visited upon them by the Slaughterhouse 9.

She went on to join the Nine, becoming Bonesaw, one of the most feared members for all the various chimerical constructs and pathogens she could create.

Now, instead, while Riley still triggers young, overwhelmed by the stresses of living with family members slowly dying from an incurable condition. Without the twisted influences of the Slaughterhouse 9, Riley is successful in saving her family and goes on to become Chirurgeon—one of the most famous medical capes in the country.

Without the discovery of Riley by the Nine, Jack Slash lacks his "best monster" and healing cape, forcing him to be more careful and conservative. Without the augmentations Riley is capable of creating, the Nine will, on average, be easier to defeat, and their threat mitigated though not completely gone.
objects.title: Doctor Davis

objects.text: Unconscious and on the brink of death, Shatterbird was dosed with a Cauldron vial, saving her life and setting her on the path to becoming part of the infamous serial killers, the Slaughterhouse 9. Shatterbird was one of the most destructive members of the group—a wide-scale Silica kinetic able to control sand and glass over a massive area. She famously "announced" the presence of the Nine by making every piece of glass in a city explode violently. But now, you can change that. Shatterbird is never dosed with a vial and doesn't survive whatever pushed her to the brink of death. As a result, the United Arab Emirates never suffers the cataclysm of her gaining her powers and shattering every piece of glass in the city of Dubai. Shatterbird never makes it to the USA, never joins the Nine, and never devastates so many communities and lives with her power. On the other hand, now there's a powerful Cauldron vial waiting to be put to use. Perhaps, for some reason, Cauldron left it with you? Or maybe they arranged for another potential recipient—of your choosing—to receive it? Regardless, whoever eventually drinks it will gain the entire powerset Shatterbird would have had.
objects.title: Broken Bird

objects.text:
The tale of Mimi—better known as Burnscar—is a tragic one in Worm, as so many are. Triggering with a power that influences her mental state, causing depression, and increased recklessness—she was a patient at a parahuman asylum, before escaping as Labyrinth was freed by Faultline’s crew. Shortly thereafter, she was recruited by the Slaughterhouse Nine during one of the psychotic episodes her power forced on her, and by the time she cleared her head, she had a Kill Order.

But now? Her power no longer messes with her head to such a degree, allowing her to remain in complete control while using it, and giving her the ability to snuff out fires as needed. As one of the most powerful pyrokinetics, Mimi joined the San Francisco Protectorate and became one of the capes' most valued in responding to the dangers of wildfires.

The Slaughterhouse Nine loses any chance of gaining one who would have been an infamous member of their ranks, and the Protectorate gains a powerful cape now on their side.
objects.title: Bonfire

objects.text:
Ned, aka The Crawler, had always been seen as an unstoppable monster. Something that could survive anything, that could come back stronger from any threat he faced and kill whatever opposed him.

Then he got taken out by some Tinker Tech bombs.

Ned never really lived up to his full potential in the original timeline, but in this timeline, there was one major change that made all the difference.

In this timeline, Ned was not a natural trigger, and in fact got his powers in a deal he made with Cauldron while trying to escape his abusive home life. The vial ended up mutating him and making him yet another Case 53, yet when Cauldron tried to have his memories erased, his powers activated and he became immune to the memory wipe.

This intrigued Cauldron, and after a series of tests they concluded that he gained a powerful if limited adaption ability. He could regenerate from any damage, even near full body destruction, and adapt to any phenomenon, seemingly without limit, but each adaption only stayed around for a set amount of time before going away.

Seeing the opportunity, Cauldron struck a deal with Ned. He would be returned back to Earth Bet as just another Case 53, pretending to be an amnesiac, and in turn Cauldron would pull some strings to help Ned get his fix of masochism by making him join the Protectorate as its one and only S-Class killer, whom they would send out to take out any S-Class threat that had a kill order on their head.

This results not only in the Slaughterhouse 9 losing one of its heaviest hitters, but also the world being in a much better position without so many S-Class threats just hanging around waiting to be set off and causing an extinction event.
objects.title: S-Class Killer: Codename Lazarus

addons.text: By a stroke of his ever-waning luck, Leet and his Shard survived their scuffle and temporal transmigration intact due to the scant involvement of an untouched tech tree: Shard Configuration. Coming to grips with his situation and his Shard’s relationship, he resolved himself to tackle it head-on. Building his Agent Interface once more, as stupid as he thinks this is (heh, now he gets it, eh?), with his Shard repeatedly railing over his failures, he strikes a deal with the [Prototype/World-Machine] as soon as they understood they wanted to be more. With it came a design: a complement to the Agent Interface capable of leeching off others’ Tinker Specialties. Sometime later, Leet (now Icarus, shedding his washout self), saw his world’s inevitable road to oblivion, he doesn’t know how to fix it, or where to go or start… but sure as hell it won’t stop him, and the [World-Machine] approves. With enough Tinkers leeched and Constructed Projects, the [Prototype] challenges Icarus over his Dream and inevitable fall, showing the horrors and events to come. Icarus, already done with his BS, pointed out Leet’s trainwrecks were not only from him alone but from them; they were failures, searching for soaring skies, and this settled and mended their differences. Icarus, at the point of your arrival, still obtained the-Thing-that-is-Leet’s abilities in the form of long-running projects he (and [World-Machine]) devised for his Dream, instead of a jailbroken version of his original power it developed into a system of Creative Destruction and Prototyping fueling his Tinker process, with a higher affinity to his Shard given his newfound recklessness and risk-taking demeanor. It’s not the end of it, with him gaining Research and Development (Innovation and Copyright Infringement, included) and, potentially, Clarketech if you aid him. All for the Dream. He might be a screw-up, but he’ll die trying.
addons.title: The Impossible Dream

objects.text: On a timeline without your involvement, Leet was given the worst and best news about why he is who he is: his power hates him, enough to try to kill him anytime he tries tinkering. Every effort to be careful and purposeful with his creations, using them to his advantage just pissed it off. The power wanted stimulation ─conflict, for his to be more reckless so it could obtain [Data], so it maliciously tried to light a fire under him with explosive malfunctions, most of the time almost killing him. This left him devastated… and passed him to the point of return; fine, he says, if that’s how it likes to play then so be it. Exhausting his Interdimensional and Power Tinker tech tree, he creates a helmet that enhances his Shard connection to communicate directly with his power, then tries the unthinkable: he tells his Shard to shove it. Appalled by the gall of his [Host] and Leet’s past the point of caring, they square off between them. Amidst their fight, as expected, something went wrong. His connection, his Shard, and himself irreparably changed. Whether Leet, his Shard, or neither won the battle, the thing who supplanted them is left to clean up the mess. Now, a few years into the past, and coincidentally in your timeline, they decide to live on as they once were. As a consolation prize, they gained Tinker of Chance, Phoenix Star, and a jailbroken version of Leet’s original Tinker power as a result of the violent power struggle resulting in their creation. Just with anything relating to Leet, what emerged was both pitiful and left more to be desired. At least he got the last laugh.
objects.title: Laugh of Icarus

objects.text: In this universe, Colin Wallis the hero Armsmaster started dating Mouse Protector when they were still in the Wards. This would affect his personality, and hero persona massively even in the present day.
objects.title: Armsmeowster

objects.text:
Taylor doesn’t know it but everything about her life is part of a Tv Show with Brockton Bay itself a giant Tv Set. Everything about her life was faked, planned out by an amoral show director with far too much political power and money. Even the Cape battles fought between heroes and villains in Brockton Bay were staged with Parahuman actors so the show could have Taylor respond and deal with the realities of having Parahumans in your hometown like a normal person. Though those actors might still be actual heroes who do this acting job part-time.

Unfortunately for that director things were about to go very wrong when Taylor triggered and gained powers after being put in the locker. If uninterrupted Taylor after her trigger will rapidly find out the truth about her life, causing her to spiral downwards emotionally before going on a rampage trying to free herself. At the same time, those responsible for her predicament will suffer so will innocents.
objects.title: The Taylor Show (Worm the Truman Edition)

objects.text: The heroes were too late to save the day, and everyone will suffer the consequences of this failure. Instead of only Three Blasphemies, all possible ten were successfully created before the heroes could stop the tinkers. Now, the Ten Blasphemies not only terrorize Europe, but have begun to spread their activities across the entire globe. With their preexisting abilities to withstand Eidolon, the ability to remake themselves if even one survives, and now having spread across the world, it might be easier to kill certain Endbringers than to end their new reign of terror. Worse still, there are hints that their unknown plan is somehow close to fruition.
objects.title: Mockery of the Divine

objects.text: During the battle of Kyushu when Lung and Leviathan were fighting, Lung's power did not wane allowing him to force Leviathan into retreat before the sinking of Kyushu. Due to this Japan remains stable and continues to exist into the modern day. Of more relevance, however, is that Kenta as Lung has now become Japan’s central Hero holding a place as one of the strongest Parahumans just as Eidolon. Lung now attends every Endbringer battle and this has pushed back societies collapse by a decade.
objects.title: Hero of Kyushu

objects.text:
There exists an organisation, a dark counterpart to the PRT, that operates in the shadows, aligning itself with villains and criminal elements. While the PRT seeks to regulate and manage parahuman activity for the greater good, this organisation thrives on chaos and manipulation. Its purpose is not to maintain order but to foster instability, granting villains the resources, protection, and influence they need to expand their power.

This organisation thrives on secrecy and corruption. It provides sanctuary for notorious criminals, helps coordinate villainous networks, and even facilitates the creation of black-market tinkertech. Their operations span every corner of the underground, from human trafficking and illegal arms deals to covert political manipulation, ensuring that their influence remains both unseen and far-reaching.

This group doesn't simply tolerate villainy—they actively promote it, guiding and supporting their criminal "clients" in exchange for loyalty or favors. They're strategic, often operating behind the scenes to orchestrate major events, setting the stage for large-scale conflicts that distract heroes while they strengthen their own grip on society.

Much like the PRT being secretly controlled by a Parahuman, this organisation has a council of Parahumans that they answer to. The worst of the worst villains, each having either connections or power or both.
objects.title: League of Villains

objects.text:
In a twist of fate one character in Worm (Or one of the chosen alternate Earth characters) was born with a twin sibling, the gender of which can either be selected or left random. You may also decide if they share the same power as their twin, a variant on the power, something completely different, or no powers whatsoever (This may also be left random if desired).  

This can lead to different possibilities and consequences depending on who has a twin and whether or not they possess the same power as their sibling (Or Supernatural skill, Genius IQ etc..)
objects.title: OMG Twins

objects.text:
In this world, Taylor Hebert lives in Australia. Whether she was born there or moved at a young age, you can decide that. She will suffer the same or a similar enough trigger to have the same bug control she does in canon.

May whatever deity you worship have mercy on this world.
objects.title: Aussie Hebert

objects.text:
Instead of being feared as a fate worse than death, becoming the next Butcher has become a far more attractive prospect in this world. This is because one of the earliest Butcher’s in this world had enhanced multitasking as part of their natural powers, that plus a few synergistic interactions with some future Butcher’s Thinker powers have resulted in all future Butcher’s being able to manage the collective memories, personalities, and egos of the Butcher mantle while retaining their own sense of self.

This means there have been a lot more Butcher hosts by canon start, for example Quarrel who in canon is Butcher 14 is Butcher 149 instead.

Note that the Butcher somewhat rapidly went through over a hundred hosts in just a few years when the changes to how the mantle worked was confirmed, the rate of Butcher turnover has since massively slowed down as different Butcher’s acclimated to the number of powers they possess and synergy between those powers, while also passing that knowledge and skill to future Butcher’s.

If you struggle in trying to come up with over a hundred unique powers feel free to just give the Butcher various Tier 1 Shard powers. Though keep in mind that such powers will have been weakened by being inherited. Also for the sake of balancing you can’t give the Butcher any 15 SP Tier 1 powers through this modifier.

Unless your selected Scenario places you either sufficiently before or after the start of canon, Quarrel should be assumed to be the current Butcher. Barring any other modifier that could alter the current Butcher host.
objects.title: Super Butcher

objects.text:
A loose extension of the other continuity modifiers that give Taylor new parents, this one extends to every character in any world you chose.

Characters with or without canon parents now somehow have new parents. Nevermind how genetics work, it could be biological or through adoption, eitherway, these new parents always consist of canon named characters from your chosen world. Be wary though, just because they're a couple (or more if you go for a polyam option) doesn't mean they will inherently get along. So do keep that in mind when you're playing matchmaker.

That being said, this of course will have profound effects in characters' lives. If a character like say, Midoriya, is genetically related to AFO, or if Luffy is raised by the Doflamingo family, there's definitely going to have a domino effect with your choice. But hey, you can also potentially give characters you like better lives? So that's good!

I don't care, I ship it~
objects.title: Matchmaker's Heaven

objects.text:
For each purchase of this modifier, you may select one established minor villain from your starting universe whose morality undergoes a permanent inversion. Instead of embracing darkness, they now act as a neutral-to-positive force within their world.

The cause of this shift adapts naturally to the character’s backstory. Perhaps a pivotal trauma or betrayal never occurred, sparing them from corruption. Maybe they resisted their moment of weakness, holding firm to their conscience. In some cases, they were never villains at all but merely misunderstood, framed, or falsely maligned until the truth surfaced at a critical moment.

Once altered, the chosen character no longer serves as an antagonist within the narrative. Instead, they emerge as a wildcard ally, rival, or neutral figure, depending on their personality and circumstances. They retain their original skills, resources, and knowledge of villainy, but now redirect these assets in ways that complicate and enrich the world.
objects.title: Minor Villain Morality Flip

objects.text:
For each purchase of this modifier, one random established minor hero from your starting universe undergoes a permanent morality inversion. No longer a steadfast force for good, they instead take on the role of an antagonist within their world.

The reasons for their corruption vary by circumstance and adapts naturally to the character’s backstory. A tragedy may strike deeper than before, breaking their spirit beyond repair. Noble ideals might twist into fanaticism, with good intentions curdling into dangerous obsession. Some may simply grow disillusioned and bitter, or be manipulation until give up or cross the line between hero and villain.

Once altered, the chosen character ceases to serve as an ally and instead emerges as a dangerous rival, enemy, or destabilizing influence, depending on their nature and place in the story. They retain their original skills, reputation, and resources, now sharpened against those they once protected. Worse still, they may carry an intimate knowledge of your side’s strengths and weaknesses, making them an especially treacherous foe.
objects.title: Minor Hero Morality Flip

objects.text:
For each purchase of this modifier, you may select one established major villain from your starting universe whose morality undergoes a permanent inversion. Instead of serving as a major driving force for evil, they now emerge as a neutral-to-positive influence within their world.

The cause of this shift is woven seamlessly into the chosen setting and adjusts to what makes the most sense for that former villain. It might be that their corruption might be undone, their tragedy prevented, or their ambitions redirected toward higher purposes. However it manifests,  that central antagonist is now a mentor, ally, or stabilizing force for the world.

This inversion is absolute. Unless overturned by deliberate, narrative-shattering action on your part, the former villain’s new role endures permanently and the story itself will restructure itself to accommodate a world without its iconic foe.
objects.title: Major Villain Morality Flip

objects.text:
For each purchase of this modifier, one random established major hero from your starting universe undergoes a permanent morality inversion. No longer one of the world’s greatest defender, they instead fall and become a central antagonist within their universe.

The cause of this fall adapts naturally to their history. They might be broken by unbearable loss, corrupted by power, twisted by fanaticism, or manipulated into betraying all they once stood for. However it happens, the lore itself reshapes to explain their downfall, recasting one of the story’s central heroes as a looming threat at the heart of the narrative.

Furthermore, this inversion can ripple outward with the collapse of such a key pillar of justice causing allies to lose faith, rivals to radicalize, or other heroes to falter, further sparking a cascade of disillusionment and corruption across the setting.

Unless overturned by deliberate, narrative-shattering intervention on your part, this inversion is permanent, and the continuity itself bends to accommodate the world shaped by its fallen champion.
objects.title: Major Hero Morality Flip

objects.text: Cauldron has decided to go public about their abilities early on. In fact, they are running a marketing scheme saying that their vials are what caused Parahumans to exist in the first place! Natural Triggers were just people who accidentally drank from contaminated water. Due to a higher focus on Cauldron Vials, they perfected their methods and drinkers no longer suffer mutations. Those that have been mutated are informed they messed with the vials and mind wiped so they have no proof they didn't do that. The rich have strong powers and the poor usually possesses vials that Cauldron knows give weaker powers.
objects.title: Buy now and get a 5% Discount!

addons.text: Due to the Endbringer's being untethered Eidolon doesn't gain the abilty to create and control Endbringers. Instead he will increase the amount of powers he can have active at once. He can use up to 7 Powers at once.
addons.title: High Priest

objects.text: Eidolon discovers how to recharge his power before the first Endbringer appears. Alongside discovering how to create and control endbringer consciously, though he is limited to the original three, this pushes the destruction of humanity back a couple of decades.
objects.title: Competent Eidolon

addons.text: Due to the Endbringer's being untethered Eidolon doesn't gain the abilty to create and control Endbringers. Instead he will increase the amount of powers he can have active at once. He can use up to 21 Powers at once.
addons.title: High Lord

objects.text: Eidolon managed to discover a way to use his powers to solve entropy, allowing him to generate energy out of nothing. He can now control all 20 Endbringer if he wishes, though he only has five of them active currently and will not activate any more unless absolutely necessary. This has pushed back the destruction of humanity to either the end of the cycle or a couple of decades after the death of Eidolon, whichever comes first.
objects.title: Solver of Entropy Eidolon

objects.text: Hero never met his end at the hands of the Siberian. As a result, Hero eventually is read in on what was going on in Cauldron and became one of the leaders of Cauldron. With Hero’s hands on the steering wheel, Cauldron has been a far more positive force for good in this timeline and society is more stable than it was in canon. In general, Cauldron just isn’t as big of an asshole as they were in canon. The Nemesis program isn’t a thing and Cauldron doesn’t use any of their favors for illegal stuff. Endbringer battles also go far more smoothly as not only is Hero still alive, but Dragon uses Hero’s tinker tech to enhance her own. The collapse of society is moved back by several decades.
objects.title: Heroes of Justice

objects.text: When Hero drinks the vial, he doesn't get tinker power focused on wavelength manipulation, instead, he gains an enhanced version of the tier 3 power Revolution with fewer limitations and restrictions. In time, he will figure out the secrets of entropy, allowing him to discover Negentropy allowing him to recharge not just his own shard but also the shards of others.
objects.title: The Technolord

objects.text: When Legend drank the vial, it did not grant him light manipulation and transformation but instead granted him an enhanced version of the embodiment of the supernova, which grants him increased speed and allows him to easily travel at light speed. Alongside this, Legend will accidentally discover Negentropy and use it to recharge his own Shard.
objects.title: The Legendary Star

objects.text: When Alexandria drank the vial, it gave her the power to apply the effect of Manton to her body, along with an enhanced version of the Alexandria power that prevents master powers from affecting her, removes her need to eat, drink, sleep, and breathe, and significantly enhances her strength, speed, and durability. And gives her Neural Network, which will allow her to figure out Negentropy which will recharge her shard.
objects.title: Alexandria the Great

objects.text: When Eden tried to implant blocks and directives to The Eye, Abaddon foresaw such a possibility and took counter-measures to forestall said restrictions as a form of Meta-Cycle. This, in turn, makes Contessa aware and cognizant of the Cycle's scope; the Shard, following this, will establish a rapport with its host, something that incrementally would mutate her power into something more loosely defined and all-encompassing, effectively transforming her into a living Laplace's Demon.
objects.title: The Eye Wide Open

addons.text: Thanks to the interference of Cauldron, Richter not only survived, but joined Cauldron. With Hero’s assistance, his shard was enhanced, granting him (Tinker) Quantum Computing, (Tinker) Code and Theoretical Communications. Dragon, now unchained, also has (Tinker) Upcoming Century, (Tinker) Research And Development and her tech is whiteboxed.
addons.title: Big Sister

addons.text: Thanks to the interference of Cauldron, Manton never lost his daughter, instead she triggered with the Siberian power. Sphere also joined Cauldron, gaining (Tinker) Terraforming, (Tinker/Thinker/Striker) Solarpunk and (Tinker/Thinker) Gaia's Hand. Bonesaw grew up, later gaining the power (Tinker) Medicine, greatly helping the world.
addons.title: The Nine

addons.text: Contessa gained (Thinker) Omniscient (alongside Comprehension), (Thinker) Vision, and the Titanized version of Path to Victory, with Negentropy and All-Seeing Precognition as Perks with Hero's help, essentially winning the war with the Enemy.
addons.title: The Boogeyman

addons.text:
Ciara and her Shard, seeing the current cycle’s futility by Zion’s lack of direction, decide to rebel against this “farce of a play” and start supporting Cauldron’s efforts, swearing allegiance the moment she realizes they already reached the [ANSWER]. 

Among some of Cauldron’s gifts, aside from Negentropy, are Archmage, Seed of Yggdrasil, Eternal Star, and an ethereal fairy-like Titan Form at her leisure.
addons.title: The Court Overseer

addons.text:
Thanks to Cauldron’s interference and The Black Knight’s recruitment, Manton never lost his daughter, instead she Triggered with the Siberian power. Sphere also joined Cauldron, gaining (Tinker) Terraforming, (Tinker/Thinker) Gaia's Hand and  Solarpunk: "I SPEAK FOR THE TREES!!". Bonesaw grew up, later gaining the power (Tinker) Medicine and (Un)Holy Trinity, greatly helping the world.

Jacob’s inclusion expands Cauldron’s recruitments efforts to coincidentally all previous and potential members of Slaughterhouse Nine apart from King, albeit with relatively better ground and livelihood if possible, becoming the sub-division of the Knights Templar, a Black Ops division of Cauldron that acts against threats that are too risky for the PRT or is reprehensible for Cauldron’s standards, shifting getting dealing and having their heads—their Corona Pollentia—to access and pass over relevant [Data] for Hero to save, to soundly get rid of them. 

The Black Knight then acts as counsel and impromptu therapist for capes and others in his employ, coaching them to channel their abilities constructively and healthily.
addons.title: The Knights Templar

objects.text:
Cauldron during its early years heavily experimented with various parts of Eden’s body, attempting to create as many powers as it could, until it resulted in the man that would be known as Hero, the first member of the Quadrumvirate. Alongside developing a host of incredibly powerful Thinker and Tinker powers, he has also triggered with the power (Tinker/Trump) Shards, with which he would use to study and fine tune the Cauldron Vials resulting in far greater abilities. 

Through his research he would make many discoveries some of which even the Entities have been unable to crack, the first among them Negentropy. Having concentrated the most powerful shards among Eden’s body, alongside enhancing his own, each member of the Quadrumvirate is far more powerful than their canon counterparts. All members of the Quadrumvirate have discovered negentropy, and have fully outfitted, upgraded, unrestricted and enhanced versions of the following abilities. 

Alexandria possesses Living Force, Saitama’s Will, Neural Network, Sylar and Siberian. Legend has Embodiment of the Supernova, Stilling, Self Rewrite, and Golden Form. Eidolon possesses Paradigm, King of the Endbringers, Archmage, and a more stable version of The Ascension (granting the power but not the mutations) and Hero possesses Revolution, Taskmaster, Atlas, Inspired Inventor and the Tinker/Trump ability Shards. 

Eidolon figured out how to create and control Endbringers long before their canon debut, and his versions are far more powerful than their canon counterparts. He currently has 20 active across various worlds and can make more but will not do so unless necessary. As a result the cape scene is drastically different from Canon since there are no Endbringer battles. Hero leads Cauldron and the Quadrumvirate. This has resulted in a positive impact on both society and the members of cauldron itself, as a result this timeline is far more stable and safe than canon. The destruction of humanity has been pushed back to the end of the cycle, and Cauldron may very well win it entirely on their own.
objects.title: New Gods

addons.text: Richer became a God of Artificial Life, Machines, and Science and Dragon became a Goddess of Dragons, Civilization and Progress.
addons.title: Machine Gods

addons.text:
Manton became the God Of Family, and his Daughter, Siberian, became the Goddess of Constants and Unchanging. 

Sphere became the God of Life and Protection and Bonesaw the Goddess of Medicine.
addons.title: The Holy Nine

addons.text: Contessa became the Goddess of Victory, Fate, and Prophecy.
addons.title: The Moirai

addons.text: Glaistig Uaine, after joining Cauldron after seeing the futility of the Entities Cycle, became the Goddess of Death, Afterlife, Harvest and Fairies. She rules over a number of realms, including those of the New Pantheon’s afterlife and their equivalent of the Prison Birdcage, acting as Cauldrons Jailer.
addons.title: The Death Queen

addons.text:
Manton became the God Of Family, and his Daughter, Siberian, became the Goddess of Constants and Unchanging.

Sphere became the God of Life and Protection and Bonesaw the Goddess of Medicine.

Most of all, the Black Knight became the God of Change, Ambition, and Defiance
addons.title: The Ninth Crusade

objects.text:
The emergence of the old gods was no mere coincidence but a result of one of the many secrets Hero would discover. Hero discovered the secret to Ascension, the secret to becoming a God, and in doing so he would revive the myths of old. The inner circle of Cauldron is the New Pantheon, each more powerful than all previous pantheons combined. They are all Shardless, and due to his discovery of Negentropy they require no worship to maintain their powers, although they get more powerful with any worship. 

All their previous powers are greatly enhanced, each one capable of defeating the Entity on their own, and gaining a slew of new abilities including control of their domains. Alexandria is the Goddess of War, Strength, Time, and Seas. Legend is the God of the Sun, Light, Life and Sky. Eidolon is the God of Monsters, Magic, and Myths. And Hero is the God of Wisdom, Technology, Heroes, and Earth. They each have more domains, these are just the ones they are the most famous and worshiped over. 

There are many new realms, some of which are populated by other sapient creatures, and other mythical creatures are now among those of Earth. There are now never before seen creatures roaming the world as well, spirits, monsters, and all manner of things. The New Pantheon rules over one of these realms as a new realm of the Gods, their Olympus. 

The Case 53s instead of being cured outright, are instead transformed into minor gods with domains befitting their canon powers. 

Eidolon retains control over the Endbringers, only there are now 100 of them and each are legendary divine beasts capable of going toe to toe with Sun Wukong and win. He can make more but will not do so unless necessary. Eidolon’s status as the God of Myths makes him also the God of Gods, and as such the new King of Gods, although he shares ruling with the rest of Cauldron.
objects.title: True Gods

objects.text: During the initials of the assault on Nilbog, Emily Piggot triggered with a powerful power capable of taking down Nilbog, which has led to the Ellisburg containment zone never existing, and Emily Piggot becoming a protectorate Hero. Instead of being a PRT director and unlike her Canon counterpart she doesn't hate or dislike parahumans, but she is incredibly harsh with those that she considers to not be doing their best to help humanity.
objects.title: Hero of Ellisburg

addons.text:
Emily Piggot and Thomas Calvert are not merely two heroes who happen to share an Ellisburg origin; they are partners in the truest sense, a legendary duo whose combined effectiveness outstrips nearly any parahuman pairing on record. Piggot operates on instinct and decisive action, the one who kicks down doors and ends fights before they escalate. Calvert is the strategic prep-timer, the one who runs disposable timelines to test her hunches, quietly dismantles threats before they manifest, and ensures she never walks into a situation he has not already mapped. 

They argue like an old married couple over every decision, every risk assessment, every after-action detail, their bickering a constant source of exasperation for the rest of the ENE Protectorate. But the moment a threat emerges, that friction vanishes into seamless, wordless coordination, and the result is a partnership so effective that villains who have faced them once tend to surrender when they arrive rather than endure the inevitable. In combat and crisis management alike, this partnership outperforms nearly any parahuman pairing in Protectorate history.

They also act as the heads of the Protectorate ENE, with Piggot serving as the official team leader and Calvert acting as her second-in-command.
addons.title: Heroes of Ellisburg

objects.text:
During the Ellisburg incursion, instead of shooting his commanding officer to flee, Thomas Calvert was evacuated while watching a Protectorate cape actively sacrifice their own life to hold Nilbog's creatures back and cover his exit. The deliberate, selfless nature of that death fundamentally rewired his worldview. When he later purchased his powers from Cauldron, he did so with the genuine intent to become a hero and subsequently joined the Protectorate under Director Piggot of PRT ENE. 

He remains the same slimy, arrogant, manipulative man he always was, but his scheming serves an entirely lawful purpose. They are almost always directed toward protecting the public and only occasionally directed at furthering his own comfortable station in life, meaning the Undersiders never formed under his employ, the Travelers were never brought to Brockton Bay as his pawns, and no shadowy puppet-master works to destabilise the city from within its own institutions.
objects.title: Ouroboros

addons.text: He was beaten by Emily Piggot, causing the Ellisburg containment zone to have never existed but he was able to escape and continue his mayhem.
addons.title: On the Run

objects.text: When Nilbog triggered, he gained biokinesis, allowing him to manipulate his own living and dead cells as well as that of organisms he touches. He can also transfer his mind into other organisms by overwriting their original consciousness. However, he can only transfer to organisms with brains capable of supporting his mind. Otherwise, he will suffer mental degradation. He has the ability to study and replicate Tinkertech as biotechnology, which increases his versatility and potential.
objects.title: Goblin King

addons.text:
Avant Garde was not just an idea inspired by Cauldron, but an offshoot of Cauldron itself. The two organizations are one, working together on two different fronts. With the awakening of Green, the entirety of Eden’s body that Cauldron had access to was destroyed and repurposed into his own network, increasing the overall power considerably. The members of Cauldron's powers have been absorbed by and added to the network.

Their reach is more considerable, having successfully overtaken thousands of worlds and have started to expand to other planets and moons within the solar system, with plans to expand further out soon, having successfully terraformed multiple worlds and sent large populations to them as a backup plan to ensure humanity’s survival.
addons.title: Dual Fronts

objects.text:
Professor’s efforts would have him interacting with many others, even the infamous organization Cauldron. Their goals aligned, however, their methods were greatly skewed. Nonetheless, the Professor would see the wisdom in building such an organization and set out to do just that.

Over the years they would travel numerous worlds, gathering many allies and resources.
