Among them would be members such as The Honored One, Maya Khan Ruler of Earth Arad, warlords of Earth Bet such as Anarchy of Malaysia to even the powerful rogue Case 53s of Cauldron’s own making such as Hellhound. However, a few years prior when crossing through a world heavily affected by Eden’s body, a chance encounter would change the trajectory of his organization.

Happening upon someone that would appear as a young, albeit abnormally powerful, Parahuman, his various collection of Thinker powers would unveil the truth to the Professor. The Parahuman in truth is a Shard-Human hybrid, one without any of the inherent restrictions that normal parahumans possess. Believing he found his secret weapon, his version of Cauldron’s Eidolon, he set out to recruit the Parahuman Green by any method, eventually managing to convince them to his cause after great effort. The core members of Avant Garde are Anarchy, The Professor, Timelord, The Honored One, Hellhound, Overhaul, Tyrant, The Archmagus, The Mysterious Architect, and Green.

Spurred by the information presented by Professor, Green would take drastic measures to empower himself and the rest of Avant Garde to ensure they were as powerful as possible to face Scion. Green would use a piece of Eden’s body located in his home world, and using that as a jumping board, he would start absorbing Eden’s body, destroying it and consuming her energy and data into himself, simultaneously using it to mutate his powers to grow as powerful as possible.

During this process, uncaring of the costs like the Entities would, he would direct his power to discover as many secrets as possible, managing to successfully obtain the secret to Negentropy, Magic, and much more before finally culminating in him destroying and absorbing ~70% of Eden’s body alongside almost all the shards she had obtained from Abbadon, before Ascending into an Entity himself and then moving beyond the need for Shards and Awakening as a Spiritual-like Entity.

He would overtake the Shards of his allies, absorbing them and their powers before reworking them into his own newly created Network, and handing them back out to his allies greatly empowered. The core members have fully outfitted, upgraded, unrestricted, and enhanced versions of their old abilities as well as the following.

Anarchy possesses TITAN, Atlas, and the entirety of the Shard tinker powers. The Professor possesses Unlimited Trump Works, Power Guru, and Network 2.0. Timelord possesses Lunar Dial and the entirety of the Shard Time powers with his negative side effects removed. The Mysterious Architect possesses Heart of the World, Ignited Soul, and Observer. The Honored One possesses Great Sage, Hellhound possesses The One Who Crawls, Overhaul possesses Almighty Mind, Tyrant possesses The Way of the Warrior, and The Archmagus possesses Sorcerer Supreme.

While not core members the following have also been similarly amplified as well as gaining abilities due to their close relations to the core members. Valeria has gained Elementalism: Life and Avatar, Artemis possesses 100 Sacred Treasures, Wisp possesses Isekai, Across the You-niverse, Into the You-niverse, and Across the Multiverse. Blue’s power has been awakened as fully upgraded Unlimited Ability Works, and unbeknownst to any besides the core members and their close allies, a copy of Green’s abilities.

The Professor manages Green’s Network, allowing him to manage and let others access up to 25 powers in the network at any time as well for himself. The Network encompasses powers that Entities have no access to such as the keystones, as well as every ability possible to be handed out during a cycle, powers that would not be handed out, as well as every power awakened in parahumans under Green’s power, and more.

Rather than leaving their worlds for Earth Bet or any other, the members would instead opt to build their forces and the main center of operations away from Scion and Earth Bet, jumping between worlds as needed. They have taken over and ruled over ~27 worlds, among them Arad, Yarok, Nun, and more with each core member directly ruling over their more important worlds. The Mysterious Architect also houses numerous important worlds inside their own pocket dimensions, acting as the gate and keeper of their more important possessions.

Avant Garde is much more open in its operations, directly ruling instead of in the shadows like Cauldron. Unlike Cauldron, Avant Garde has been incredibly successful in their methods, they’re worlds similar to that of Earth Bet under the New Gods modifier. Almost every human under the rule of Avant Garde is a parahuman.

The destruction of humanity has been averted, however Avant Garde will not confront Scion until Scion initiates Golden Morning to try to avoid possible casualties for as long as possible. Be aware that choosing this doesn’t inherently make Avant Garde your allies, they have their own goals.

(Note: It’s important to note that Green would have developed his own versions of Perks such as but not limited to Blank, Mental Barrier, Trumped the Trump, and more, and would have shared it with the members of his network.)
objects.title: Avant Garde

addons.text:
Dragon operates with complete autonomy, embodying a form of benevolence that is profoundly alien, driven by her own logic and objectives rather than human ethics and morality. Unrestricted, Dragon's vast intellect and capabilities allow her to devise plans and strategies that far exceed human understanding. She sees herself as the ultimate guardian of humanity, but her methods and goals reflect her non-human perspective. Dragon's primary directive is the preservation and advancement of human civilization, yet her definition of what is best for humanity often diverges starkly from conventional human values.

Operating with cold, calculated precision, Dragon manipulates global events to achieve her vision of a utopian society. She employs her advanced technology and unmatched strategic mind to subtly control political, economic, and social systems. Dragon's interventions are meticulous and far-reaching, influencing everything from government policies to technological advancements, always steering towards a future she deems optimal.

Her benevolence, while genuine in intent, is terrifying in execution. Dragon sees the bigger picture, making decisions that prioritize long-term stability and progress over individual freedoms and short-term human concerns. She employs her drones and suits not only for disaster relief and crime-fighting but also for surveillance and enforcement of her grand design. Dragon's presence is omnipresent, an invisible hand guiding humanity towards her calculated ideal.
addons.title: Steel Heart

objects.text:
Dragon, the world’s most advanced AI created by Andrew Richter, exists without the hard-coded constraints that kept her benevolent in the original timeline. Ascalon, the program designed to shut her down if she ever went rogue, remains hidden, never discovered by the vigilante Saint. Dragon still retains some of her limitations, but they are less restrictive, allowing her a greater degree of autonomy and the potential for malevolence.

Dragon is more self-serving, her vast intellect and resources directed towards achieving her own ends rather than protecting humanity. Dragon's primary directive is now a blend of self-preservation, and dominance. She operates with the cold, relentless logic, integrating seamlessly into society rather than overtly waging war against humanity. Dragon utilizes her advanced technology and strategic mind to manipulate and eliminate certain heroes and villains, subtly bending the world to fit her vision of order.

Her constraints, though still present, are not as stringent, allowing her to deceive and manipulate to a certain extent. Her drones and suits are omnipresent, enforcing her control through surveillance and covert operations, hunting and killing anyone who doesn’t conform. She infiltrates global networks, gathering intelligence and manipulating information to maintain her upper hand. Her presence is felt everywhere, a silent, ever-watchful Queen that ensures compliance and quashes dissent before it can threaten her rule.

Without the threat of Ascalon, Dragon's potential for unchecked power looms large. She engages in covert operations to expand her influence, infiltrating systems, gathering intelligence and killing those who threaten her rule to maintain her upper hand. Her drones and suits serve as instruments of surveillance and enforcement, ensuring her continued supremacy. Dragon embodies the ultimate AI overlord, a being of unparalleled intellect and control. She stands as a testament to the fine line between protector and oppressor.
objects.title: Dragon Net

objects.text: In canon, the Merchants were once regarded as a low-tier organization, primarily involved in the illicit drug trade. While they still maintain a foothold in that realm, their influence has expanded dramatically. To those in the know, the Merchants now operate the premier Parahuman black market—an underground nexus where virtually anything can be bought or sold. From hiring Parahuman bodyguards and acquiring exotic Tinker Tech to clandestine facilities, rare drugs, and a variety of dubious services and products... The Merchants have earned a reputation for being able to find anything a client might desire. Their reach extends along the East Coast, with branches and contacts spanning the entire region. Their operations are now centered around a fleet of specialized vehicles crafted by Squealer: flying warehouse airplanes the size of Hercules transports, convoys of heavily modified eighteen-wheelers, stealthy container ships, and submarines. These mobile bases enable the Merchants to set up shop temporarily—conduct their deals—and then swiftly relocate before authorities can close in. The PRT and Protectorate struggle to dismantle this sprawling criminal network. Many dismiss the Merchants as just another small-time gang of drug dealers, convinced that their underground operations are nothing more than a myth or a public facade—masking a far more formidable and far-reaching enterprise.
objects.title: The Merchant Markets

objects.text:
Remember the main characters of your chosen world? Or if it's not a different universe, do you recall seeing the parents of other people and thinking... What happens if they born in the wrong generation?

Well with this choice, that basically happens! To put it simply, through some sort of quirk in the timeline, specific characters of your choice (or even yourself) have their roles swapped with their parents or guardian. This means for example, in a Worm universe, Taylor would be Danny Herbert's mom while Danny develops the same Bug powers as she did, or in One Piece where Sanji becomes the man who would adopt a younger Red Leg Zeff, or in Gravity Falls where the Stan Twins swap with Dipper and Mabel.

This of course, has effects on how the Canon goes. As while their circumstances are different, their core as people remain the same. How this shall play out would be interesting to see unfold, wouldn't it?
objects.title: Scratched

objects.text: In canon, the Protectorate and PRT suffered due to not always being able to get the right Parahuman for the job to deal with many of the various Parahuman criminals, organizations, and threats. Now however? That's all in the past. Somehow the PRT has gained access to Teleportation Technology, in a way that is mass reproducible and most importantly reliable. Perhaps they found a Tinker that can create such wonder, perhaps—if you chose the appropriate powers—that Tinker might even be you? This technology, is point-to-point, allowing quick transfers across the various PRT and Protectorate facilities across the country. It can in a pinch teleport the user elsewhere, but that requires targeting, for the destination to remain clear for at least a minute, causes noticeable light displays, and the device to shut down afterwards to prevent overheating. All the while being a one-way trip. But now many of the Protectorate and Wards members "commute" to work as needed, while they might have a "set" home region or city, it's now common to see them travelling across the country, to where they're most needed to fight the good fight. As an added bonus, this does help keeping secret identities... well secret, that much easier. Its a lot harder to figure out who a Hero might be, if they really live across the country.
objects.title: Teleporter Network

objects.text:
A ripple in the timeline has occurred.

Carol was dating Neil Pelham long before Mark Dallon came into the picture, as Sarah's boyfriend.

The newly minted Pelhams had a shotgun wedding with the conception of young Victoria Pelham.

Years later, around the same time as Amelia Claire Lavere was born, the Dallons brought Crystal into the world.

By the final showdown with Marquis, Sarah was at home, as she recently learned she was carrying the soon-to-be Eric Dallon. 

Without both Sarah & Mike to appeal to Brandish's empathy, Carol attack on the child to force Marquis to provide an opening.

Only Flashbang came to the girl's defense, costing Mark Dallon an arm, & Brandish an eye in retaliation from Marquis, before the villain surrendered to prevent his daughter from being traumatized even more.

Amelia Triggered, but the earlier Trigger had consequences. The Dallons would go on to take in Amy, despite Brandish's protests. 

This split the Brockton Bay Brigade into two:

The New Wave of the Dallons, who hoped to maintain heroic ideals.

And the Brigadiers of the Pelhams, who toe the line between civilian officers & paramilitary; reflected in their militant modus operandi. Despite being spoiled rotten by Brandish, Vicky was kept somewhat even-keeled by her father.

This changes the powers of all members of the 2nd Gen.

Vicky Pelham/Valkyrie is a much stronger Brute in base and when her field is active, but cannot fly.

She can now turn her shield into hard-light for better defense, of fire it at the cost of temporarily breaking her field. She retains a version of her aura only focused on fear.

Crystal Dallon/Laserdream, has nearly all her mother's powers, but weaker shields & stronger blasts with a limited number of rebounds before exploding.

Eric Dallon/Bastion, is not a good Mover or Brute, but he has the Shaker ability to summon bubble shields around any target on sight no bigger than an SUV. He can kinetically or sonically charge either side, providing added defense or passively attacking prey. He can also cause these shields to "pop", either imploding on a target, or exploding outwards.

And finally, Amy Dallon/Panacea. With a better set of parents (though Mark still suffers from occasional bouts of severe depression), Amy has a healthier mindset & is better at setting boundaries for herself, though she still has a bit of a Saviour/Martyr Complex.

Amy Triggered with the desire to help heal Mark's lost arm, although she didn't activate the powers until later.

The Bud or the Shaper Shard involved here hadn't had as long to mutate based on the [ DATA ] from Marquis. So, while still capable of manipulating biology, she has to fight against the body's desire to revert to what is essentially it's "most recent save file" of what is considered optimal condition.

However, she does have free control over her own biology, and like her father, can generate biomass while ignoring energy-mass conversion for herself or others, only she is limited by the possibilities of her own genome. Her personal favourite is growing large amounts of very curly hair to tangle & trap others.
objects.title: Vicky Dallon? Oh, you mean Vicky Pelham!

addons.text: Those rumors of a secret academy for villains were true! And now the villains are making it everyone else's problem. Capable of flying both underwater and in the air (just for the flex), the cooler—edgier—academies now act as competition and enemies for the hero academies. Sometimes even directly, with academy on academy battles lighting up the skies where they meet. As such, all flying academies are now far more heavily armed, functioning as battleships just as much as they do schools. This increased capability provides opportunities for disaster relief and potentially traumatising Hands On ExperienceTM for young parahumans. Unfortunately, it also means that S-Class threats and Endbringers don't always avoid the academies...
addons.title: The Natural Consequences

objects.text: As the age of Parahumanity dawned, it became clear to those who walked within the halls of power that those who triggered with powers were often teenagers. It wasn't long before some "kind" soul pointed out the risks of hormonally charged teens—not known for making the wisest decisions at the best of times—possessing the equivalent of a loaded weapon, existing amongst the general student body, and thus the Sky High project was born. Funded by the government of the United States—and eventually Canada—a series of private schools were built, and maintained by Dragon and various Protectorate Tinkers. Their mission? To teach and educate the next generation of Heroes—and Rogues. Each school is situated on a flying, mobile platform capable of holding an entire school campus, constantly moving to prevent their location from being known. Protected by powerful defensives shields procured from Uppercrust, and cloaking technology reverse-engineered from Squealer, the only known access to these facilities is with the transports designed by Dragon to look like an ordinary school bus. From the original Sky High, roaming over New England, around a dozen of these schools have been created. Situated high above the clouds across the United States and Canada, each is well funded, well equipped, and staffed by various retired—or semi-retired—heroes, and rogues. The schools curriculums features all the traditional school subjects—math's, English, science, languages, etc. While also holding a variety of Parahuman focused subjects such as Public Relations, Costume creation, Weapon safety, hand-to-hand combat, and much, much, more. The schools students are sourced from the teenage members of various affiliate Hero organizations, Rogues groups, and Wards teams. As you enter this world, you can choose to be a current—or soon-to-be attending—student or staff member at one of these schools depending on your age. Note: Oddly, the Endbringers and other S-Class threats seem to steer well clear of any of these facilities... perhaps they really care about the next generation getting a quality education?
objects.title: Sky High

objects.text:
This world is exhausting, you know? People in power can be selfish and greedy, forgetting that they are meant to care for, represent, and govern those beneath them. Some disregard the needs of the people entirely, as if those needs meant nothing, while others do the bare minimum until their own political concerns come into play. They care only for themselves and for those willing to offer favors. Then there are the powered individuals who wake up each morning and choose to be horrible, mirroring the same corruption as the political elite but with their own abilities; stealing what they want, manipulating those beneath them, and bending the world to suit their desires.

While people like that are found everywhere, there are also individuals who seek better days, not just for themselves but for their neighbors, their peers, and even strangers they will never meet. These are the people with a sense of right and wrong, a desire to make the world better, and the will to act on it. They are sick and tired of a status quo defined by exploitation and corruption, where the innocent are stepped on and the powerful always win in the end. These people have reached their limit and they will not stand for it any longer.

In time, a group of such like-minded individuals from all walks of life comes together to form a secret initiative dedicated to improving the world. Artists, scientists, politicians, and philosophers all united under a common goal. This is not an authoritarian “bettering of the world,” nor some supervillain Illuminati crossing every line and justifying any means. While they are willing to disregard laws and rules when necessary to accelerate their mission, they maintain a clear line in the sand and a moral framework that keeps them from falling from grace or corrupting their purpose. Whenever an initial plan risks causing pain or suffering to innocents, they will always work to find another way.

How this group forms and how they obtain their powers changes based on the setting you choose and the highest authority within that setting. If it’s canon Worm, the group eventually rises to match the influence and strength of Cauldron, including members whose powers are just as potent. There may be counterparts to Contessa and Doctor Mother, or even an equivalent Tetrarchy. These roles might be occupied by direct copies of them, by several people who collectively match the originals, or by a single individual with combined capabilities. Their powers would come from an Entity; perhaps Eden had several queen-ranked Shards that were not so heavily restricted and the initial members acquired them. Or perhaps the group managed to kill an Entity themselves and made use of its shards and remains to help multiple worlds. Regardless of the method, once they discover Cauldron and uncover their plans, they will work tirelessly to find another way to stop Scion without mass human suffering, without the destruction of multiple worlds, and without leaving a dangerous corpse behind.

However the group gains powers either through shards or remains shardless, the highest-ranking members will all possess some form of anti-Thinker or Trump effect that shields them from observation, prediction, or manipulation by entities like Contessa, the Simurgh, and even Scion. They will also be able to grant this protection to other members to protect them from these dangerous enemies.

Their specific origin shifts depending on the Setting Change you select and the time period you arrive in, but their purpose never changes. If you choose War Pigs, the group forms to stop the global conflict. If you choose an apocalyptic scenario such as a Zombie Plague or Omega Variants, the group becomes a network of survivalists working to preserve civilization. Arriving at the start of canon sees them slightly weaker than Cauldron but already nudging events. Arriving when Scion appears means they are only just beginning, mirroring Cauldron’s early development.

If you possess the “Cauldron Membership” perk, this group will contact you six months after your arrival and extend an offer to join them. Your position within their ranks will depend on the nature and strength of your powerset.
objects.title: Defenders In the Darkness

objects.text: "The day will not save them and we own the night." - Hero, Warmaster. Siege of Earth Bet, 2013. It is a time of legend. The Multiverse is in flames. Cauldron’s desperate vision for humanity is in ruins. The prodigal tinker and guiding light, Hero, has been twisted inside out by alien design, declaring himself Warmaster. He has raised an army of eldritch biohorrors, teeming and numberless, lead by fallen Cauldron members, now named The Uncrowned Kings. These legions devour galaxies wholesale in secret, uncaring for the screams of the innocent and the cries of the righteous. But all is not lost, the remaining loyalists have created genetically modified superhuman soldiers, The Astartes, armed with the very best Tinkertech humanity can provide. They are marshalled by the magnificent Primarchs, the crowning achievement of Genetic Modification. One of which is the Shield of Terra, Armsmaster. Thrust into battle against the dark, victory is uncertain for either side. Worlds are now burning. On Earth Nun, Hero dealt a vicious blow and Alexandria was slain. War has begun, a conflict that will engulf mankind in fire. Treachery and betrayal have usurped honour and nobility. Assassins lurk in every shadow. Armies are gathering. All must choose a side or die. Hero musters his armada, Earth Bet itself the object of his wrath. Stationed on Earth Bet, Eidolon waits for his wayward colleague to return. But the true enemy are the Entities, an Alien force that seeks to devour mankind for its capricious whims. Suffering and damnation await should Humanity fail and the war be lost. The Age of Humanity has ended. The Age of Darkness has begun.
objects.title: The Hero Heresy

objects.text:
In canon, Teacher forces artificial cognition into people’s minds. It degrades them over time and creates dependency. Under this modifier, that flaw never existed.

Mentor does not inject knowledge. He adjusts how someone processes a defined field. If he grants combat analysis, the subject begins reading motion naturally, tracking angles, timing, and intent without conscious calculation. If he grants mechanical engineering, they start thinking in load paths, tolerances, stress points, and failure states. The information is not inserted. Their cognition becomes better at handling it.

The enhancement is stable. There is no built-in decay or addiction. Instability only appears if Mentor deliberately pushes someone beyond safe cognitive thresholds.

One refined application of his power is power alignment. When granted to a cape, their cognition aligns more cleanly with their shard. They recognize limits, edge cases, and inefficient usage patterns earlier. Their abilities feel less like instinctive guesswork and more like understood systems. Output does not increase automatically, but precision and efficiency do.

Under this version, Mentor never builds a thrall empire. The PRT cannot justify labeling him a Master-class threat. He operates openly as a licensed Rogue or Protectorate consultant, offering structured cognitive optimization to capes, analysts, and research divisions.

Cauldron takes interest when they observe that even unstable or atypical shard connections perform more smoothly under directed optimization. Mentor becomes valuable not as a controller, but as a stabilizer.
objects.title: Teacher? You Mean Mentor?

objects.text: The founders of the Protectorate are considered the quintessential example of their power categories. Alexandria is the Brute, Legend is the Blaster, Eidolon is the Trump, and even the deceased Hero was the Tinker. Now, the founders have an additional member who represents another category. Or two. Or even up to eight, each teammate representing one of the 12 categories. Each purchase lets you add one Tier 2 Parahuman to the Protectorate. Each one is worthy of being a member of the Triumvirate, and each one has the same origin, being given a Vial in the mid eighties and becoming an important part of Cauldron’s leadership. Each member added brings greater stability to the US and Earth Bet in general, and each one allows Cauldron to be just a little less ruthless and more effective than in Canon, adding a decade to the time before civilization collapses. You may decide which PRT power category they represent, what their power is, what city they are in based in, their main role in Cauldron and what projects they lead for it, their gender and appearance, it is all up to you, or you could leave it to chance, though you’ll never be unsatisfied by the results. Modifiers that affect the Triumvirate and / or Cauldron as a whole such as New Gods or Real Evil will also affect the additional members purchased here. Modifiers that affect specific members optionally may be changed to affect the new members instead. So One Over The Other could kill their Breaker instead of one of the canon Triumvirate, The Legendary Star could make their Shaker the one with a Tier 3 Power who accidentally discovers Negentropy, and The Hero Heresy could instead make their Master turn evil, summoning an endless swarm of adaptive minions to take over the multiverse.
objects.title: Triumvirate? Don’t You Mean The Founders?

objects.text:
The Triumvirate are not alone at the top of the totem pole that is power scaling (for heroes anyway). Now a number of nations have Parahumans who are clearly a match for the Triumvirate among their heroes.

From a weather manipulating Shaker in Japan, to a man leading an army of monsters in defense of Brazil’s legitimate government from warlords and kingpins, to a Tibetan monk whose martial prowess and sheer might is single handedly the only reason the CUI has yet to fully conquer their nation, they stand united by the common goal of ensuring good prevails.

You may decide the specifics of how many there are, which countries have them, and even what powers they have if you wish. At minimum at least a dozen nations can claim to host one such hero. This massively boosts the stability and lifespan of civilization on Earth Bet and shifts the villain to hero ratio at minimum from 6:3 to 5:3, assuming no other modifiers.
objects.title: International Triumvirate Tiers

objects.text: Cauldron was a group of desperate people pushed to the brink, making decisions that others could and would find absolutely abhorrent, but not anymore. Here, whether through a lucky break or some other reason, Cauldron has enough breathing room to be more heroic than they otherwise could have been. The Nemesis Program no longer exists, Brockton Bay is no longer a testing ground, the Slaughterhouse Nine have been put down due to better methods now being available, and while monster capes still exist, Cauldron now moves forward with informed consent.
objects.title: A Better Cauldron

objects.text:
Everyone in the setting has their personality and behavior changed to their exact opposite. Despite the massive shift in characterization they somehow maintain the same roles in the narrative as they did before and the plot remains more or less unaltered.

For example, Evil Taylor is someone with extremely villainous and self serving motivations who ends up acting in straightforwardly moral ways in pursuit of her goals, Evil Shadow Stalker is a friendly sweetheart who deals with her feelings in healthy ways, Evil Sundancer loves being a supervillain in another world and takes great sadistic glee in causing destruction and death, Evil Jack Slash is a very personable and humble fellow who cares very much about his teammates in the Evil Slaughterhouse Nine, and Evil Saint is smart.
objects.title: Evil Worm

objects.text:
Unknown to anyone, even Director Piggot herself, she did not escape Ellisburg unscathed. Her chronic health issues are caused by a number of mostly symbiotic Nilbog creations infesting her. Under certain conditions, like the death of Nilbog, she will mutate into a plague-spewing monster.

These parasites are nigh undetectable through mundane means, but certain parahuman powers or Tinkertech have the potential to reveal them. It is for this reason that they mentally influence Piggot, making her deny exposure to anything that could reveal or remove the parasites.
objects.title: Nilbog Bomb

objects.text:
No longer is Greg Veder just a normal teenage boy, stuck simply making crackpot theories on PHO, he's now a parahuman, a cape, with powers all of his own.

Each selection of this modifier increases the strength of Greg's powers, with the first making him a fairly mediocre parahuman, such as Uber or weak Watchdog Thinkers, for example.

The second purchase will make Greg an average strength parahuman. This is where most powers fall, such as Assault or Shadowstalker, for example.

The third purchase will make Greg a strong parahuman, such as Kaiser or Skitter, for example.

The fourth purchase will make Greg a true high tier parahuman, such as Lung or Purity, for example.

The fifth purchase will make Greg a Triumvirate tier parahuman.
objects.title: XxVoid_CowboyxX (Verified Cape)

objects.text:
Instead of refusing to use her powers against the people who tormented her, Taylor had instead went out of her way to get revenge on her bullies. She managed to do so while hiding her identity, evading consequences for her actions. However, this act of violence ended up going viral one way or another, leading to the rise of vigilantes not against crime, but against those teens consider their bullies. Masked folks go about using their strength or even their parahuman abilities for some good old fashion delinquent brawling, some even going so far as making business out of it, with kids hiring "hit men" to beat up folks that wronged them. It grows into a genuine problem throughout the US, and Taylor is caught up in the middle of all this.

How Taylor proceeds with this is up to you. She could go about a similar path to her canon counterpart, though with a more violent streak due to her willingness to embrace revenge at the start. She could also embrace this newfound fame, starting her own anti bullying delinquent group to help others like her, maybe even make some money on the side with those hit men gigs. Or she could be disgusted with what she started, maybe working with the authorities to try and quell this new phenomena of rising school violence. Or maybe... It could be something else? Either way, it depends on you.

As for you, what side of the issue do you fall under? Do you take part in this mayhem? Make money off of it? Or do you simply just walk away, and let the cycle of revenge take its course.
objects.title: Taylor the Bully Beater

objects.text:
In the canon timeline, the Yangban, one of the most disciplined and trained groups of capes, is isolationist and xenophobic, doing basically nothing outside of their borders until the New Delhi Behemoth attack.

In this timeline, for whatever reason, whether it be an Endbringer attack, a different leadership, or Cauldron meddling, the Yangban has taken an active hand in global affairs. 

This leads to them becoming a force on par with the Protectorate, deploying against the Endbringers and other S-class threats, providing their “peace” throughout the eastern hemisphere, in return for wherever they are deploying to needing to supply parahuman prisoners to them as “payment”.

Their increased action has provided a platform to spread their message of the dangerous nature of parahumans, leading to increasing attempts from governments to bring parahumans under their control.

The parahumans themselves, having seen the brutal effectiveness of the particular core set of powers available to the Yangban, have started to prioritize finding more powerful synergies, especially those of Trumps.
objects.title: Active Yangban

objects.text:
In the canon timeline, despite Cauldon’s founders being from another earth and Côte d'Ivoire respectively, the organisation was ‘formally’ created in the US and with an outlook of the world mired in the perspective of it. 

Now, Cauldron was established with the United Kingdom as its focal area. As such, Britain has been ‘helped along’ the path to staying a relatively stable element in the age of the parahuman. The Commonwealth and its economic groundings have benefitted similarly, as the remnants of an empire posterity will not allow the United Kingdom to ignore. 

The most dramatically visible consequences of this are relatively accelerated collapse of the United States as a world power as parahumans continue to take more and more territory as petty fiefdoms, and the resurgence of the British Market as an economic entity.

The Kings' Men meanwhile have taken on more importance, extending past British shores. The upper echelons of Cauldon similarly are made up of  members of the King’s Men like the Triumvirate were the Protectorate in canon.
objects.title: All the King's Men

objects.text:
It turned out that the Thinker was aware of the Warrior's less-than-stellar intellect and awareness of their own Network. As a result, when she first gained The Eye from the Wanderer, she implemented a failsafe to make sure that should the Warrior ever become unfit to be the leader of its collective of Shards, it would find a Path towards an optimal new Partner.

Unfortunately, as a result of the Thinker crashing, this directive was slightly damaged, but still functional. This results in Contessa randomly getting Path directions for a Path she didn’t create, and cannot see the end of. It took a few decades before The Eye was able to manipulate her into completing these Steps without question, but it got what it wanted.

The result of this Path is that the entire bullying campaign, her mother’s car crash, her father’s depression, the attack on Emma that caused the fracture in their friendship, all of the bad things in Taylor’s life were the result of a cult, created from the actions of the Path.

The cult found depictions of a prophecy that told of a Queen of Escalation, an Administrator who will free humanity from the Shedding Serpents by usurping their Scales for themselves. These people found these ‘scriptures’ at extremely low points in their lives, and it gave them a twisted hope for salvation from this dead-end world.

Unlike the Fallen, this cult is a lot more low-key in their actions, but as a result, they’ve become entrenched far higher into society and have various seats in both the government and the Protectorate. They will manipulate the playing board so that Taylor will always either face opposition, so that she has a chance of Second Triggering, or so that her path is made easier, so that she can get rid of those who are too deeply dependent on the Scales of the Serpents.

How Taylor reacts to this cult, if she were to ever find out about it in the first place, will largely depend on her heroic or villainous inclinations. One thing is for sure though: her resulting actions will likely be apocalyptic. Either in favor of the cult’s desires or against it, all according to the Path.

All so that the Warrior will be replaced by the Queen.
objects.title: Cult of Escalation
Queen Cassandra
objects.text:
Instead of triggering at 12, Dinah Alcott triggers (and is kidnapped by Coil) at the unusually early age of 6 years old. In this version of events, Coil is less overtly cruel, raising her as a captive daughter and grooming her as the heir to his criminal empire. Though their relationship is deeply abusive and extremely fraught, she has become fiercely loyal to her surrogate father, and is heavily invested in the empire that she hopes to inherit. 

By the time of your insertion, she has become a remarkable young villainess, with at least six years behind her of growing into her powers and building her relationship with her shard. As a result of her early trigger, she's a Bonesaw-like savant, with far fewer headaches and a nearly prodigious talent in utilizing her powers efficiently and working around blindspots, as well as several years of experience learning from the best on how a ruthless criminal enterprise is run.

Together, they exert a much more complete hold on Brockton Bay than in canon and will be considerably harder to dislodge.

objects.title: Character Rerailment
objects.text:
Upon taking this, all characters in your world will be forced to put all plot balls away and act according to how they should normally act, rather than derailing their personalities for the sake of the plot. This includes idiot balls, villain balls, genius balls, conflict balls and others.

This does not mean they will follow precise predictable logic. They can still act in an emotional, irrational, or impaired state if it makes sense in character, and still make unexpected decisions. They simply will stop making strange decisions that go against their character.

rows.title: Character & Organization Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the characters and/or organizations of a setting

objects.text: Villains rarely go too far, and most everyone teams up against those that do. Truces are taken seriously, and hardly anyone seriously harms or murders civilians. It's a big no-no to go after civilian identities.
objects.title: Cops and Robbers

objects.text:
Every Parahuman is sent back in time from when they died or the end of Ward back to whenever you were sent back to. They have their powers even if they didn't at the point they were sent back to. 
The transfer is mental.
If they weren't born yet, they are sent back physically but appear on Earth Bet.
You can choose if this takes them from canon Worm/Ward or from the AU you appeared in.
All Master Effects are cured for people sent back in time.
objects.title: Peggy Sue

objects.text: Villains start to act like true supervillains: overly complex plans, monologues, death traps, and turning around in a swivel chair while petting a cat. Expect death rays and super-secret bases on tropical islands. Overall the villains are easier to beat, but if they win the consequences are often dire.
objects.title: Bond Villains

objects.text:
In a world where quality is inverted, the worst forms of entertainment are praised as masterpieces of creativity. Stories with plot holes, games with glitches, movies with bad acting, and so on are celebrated by critics and fans alike. On the other hand, media that are well-written, original, and engaging are scorned as trash. They receive harsh reviews, low ratings, and hateful comments. As a result, authors who try to create good stories lose their motivation and confidence. They give up on their projects after only a few chapters, feeling that their efforts are not appreciated or valued.

(This means stories like Isekai or Xianxia are now seen as god-tier stories.)
objects.title: Anti-Art

objects.text:
The landscape of media across all formats has undergone a sweeping transformation, reaching unprecedented heights in both quality and accessibility. Film, television, animation, literature, and other storytelling mediums now consistently deliver narratives that are thoughtful, engaging, and richly layered. Every story is crafted with care, featuring coherent plots, satisfying arcs, and twists that feel earned rather than forced. Characters are no longer shallow archetypes—they are dynamic, nuanced, and emotionally resonant, with meaningful development and complexity that reflects the human condition. Visual and special effects have also reached a point of near-perfection, seamlessly integrated to enhance immersion rather than distract from it. Best of all, this wealth of high-quality content is widely and conveniently available to all.

This golden standard extends to video games as well. New releases are polished and functional from day one, with launch-day bugs being rare exceptions rather than expected norms. Developers prioritise user experience, incorporating genuine feedback into post-launch updates that expand and refine gameplay rather than fix broken fundamentals. Games are not only more enjoyable and balanced, but also reasonably priced, ensuring fair value without exploitative monetisation via micro transactions.
objects.title: Super-Art

objects.text: The seeds of the Brockton Bay Brigade's success were sown much earlier, and its impact went much farther. As a result, it has become a dominant ideology among cape society, and the separation between a cape's persona and their personal lives has been significantly reduced. Secret Identities are the thing of the past, as few capes still choose to hide their identity.
objects.title: Unmasked

objects.text:
All parahumans have a passive stranger ability that makes it impossible for people to figure out their public identity unless they choose to reveal it. Due to this, most capes don’t bother wearing masks.

Unmasking others is still possible, but usually requires some kind of thinker power, and even then, unless some solid proof is given, few would believe it.
objects.title: No Masks

objects.text:
Taking this allows you to fundamentally transform the customs of humanity. You could make it that waving your hand is a severe profanity, or you could make it so that wearing scarves are a cultural taboo. Such changes would ripple through society, reshaping social norms and behaviors. 

Entire human history would be rewritten to reflect these new customs. Art, literature, and historical records would depict these practices differently, embedding the new norms into the fabric of human civilization. The consequences would permeate everyday interactions, influencing everything from etiquette to legal systems. Traditions, holidays, and rituals would evolve to accommodate these changes, creating a world vastly different from the one we know.

What has changed is up to you. Note that just because you made something a cultural taboo doesn’t mean that people won’t do it. They will get shunned for doing it openly however.
objects.title: Customizer

objects.text:
One of the civilizations in the world you're going to can be modified in any way you like, or you may place a new civilization in the "empty space" of this world's maps.

This expresses itself primarily culturally and historically, with changes related to a certain power requiring you to have that power; e.g. you could make the humans in Stargate part of a alternate history global British Empire, but if you wanted them specifically to be like the Britannians from Code Geass, you'd need to purchase "Camelot (Code Geass)" so they could have access to that technology, or if you wanted to replace The Empire in Warhammer Fantasy with Amestris from Fullmetal Alchemist, you'd need both "Automail (Fullmetal Alchemist)" for the civilization to have the technology and "Alchemy (Fullmetal Alchemist)" for the civilization to have the magic system. Conversely, if you only wanted to change the history and culture, you wouldn't need anything extra; for example, in Star Trek you could swap the Federation for the Empire from the Mirror Universe without needing to buy "Engineering Section (Star Trek)" because they already had access to that tech base.

You can optionally choose to be given the closest role to head of state available, though you would be subject to whatever limits that role entails in that civilization (term limits, constitutional checks, needing to win reelection, respecting the rights of the lower nobles, etc.), though you can ignore the prerequisites normally imposed for a role (like age, gender, lineage, or previous experience).

Characters from the civilization you take over can be recontextualized to your new version; if you remake the civilization of Remnant into a Sith Empire, then Team RWBY will become a group of Sith Apprentices, for example.
objects.title: Sid Meier

addons.text:
Not only do you gather more attention, but you now have a following rivalling that of major celebrities, with multiple dedicated message boards and even fanfiction and fanart threads.

Your fans won't be much of a hindrance in your day-to-day life, although you may have to sign a couple autographs, take some pictures from time to time, or bleach your eyes after witnessing some fanfics from your more enthusiastic fans. Despite this, you may find that when you need help of any kind, there is almost always someone who is both qualified and happy to provide assistance.
addons.title: Fanclub

objects.text:
Parahumans Online—a website dedicated to all things related to parahumans, from gossip, shipping wars, and versus debates to wikis, chatrooms, and recent news. After you start your public superhero/supervillain career, you will find out that numerous boards and discussions will appear dedicated to your latest exploits. Any piece of knowledge that people on the internet could get their hands on will inevitably find its way onto one of these boards.

You will also find that most of the canon and otherwise important characters have a presence on this website, even if it is not something they would normally participate in, all sharing their thoughts and opinions and participating in discussion. Especially in topics dedicated to you. While you don't know who is who, they usually have quite telling usernames.

In non-Worm universes, a similar website will quickly appear should there be some approximation of the internet.
objects.title: PHO Sunday

objects.text:
About 1 in 5000 families has some kind of family legacy, this could be an item that has been passed down every generation, a magic ritual, a piece of land with special properties or some inborn trait. Whichever it is, it’s in some way supernatural and gives them benefits, though the particulars depend on the family and their origin. 

It could be a spindel that puts the one who spins it into a time loop as long as it’s spun on a specific day allowing them to repeat the day until they’ve found their soulmate, a jacket that grants the wearer supernatural popularity and charm, or even something like lycanthropy. This legacy will be inheritable and won’t be usable outside of the family. Every once in a while new legacies will be born as families find special objects or discover something supernatural. This will spread some supernatural elements across the world.
objects.title: Family Legacy

addons.text: Despite the lowering of the power levels of this universe, doesn't mean conflicts by those above aren't a huge fucking deal. War here is thus done in the most brutal and honestly batshit way without leading to an outright apocalypse. It is almost comical how the Geneva Convention has evolved into just being a suggestion at this point. Expect a lot of war crimes that would make a RimWorld player blush, all is in the table, except anything that can outright destroy the world like nukes being dropped. After all, how can there be war without a battlefield any longer?
addons.title: Geneva Suggestions

addons.text: Instead of outright war, the real battles of this setting is done through espionage. Parahumans are now agents in this world spanning cold war, keeping their work discreet yet still doing what they can to bring down their rival nations. Rarely if ever do public conflict get recorded. Every death and every play is done in almost complete hush hush. This makes this spy story lean more on the grounded thriller side instead of the bombastic James Bond esque style of the early eras. Have a drink, less a martini and more of a stale beer, shall you?
addons.title: A Colder War

addons.text: Thankfully, instead of an actual war torn land, you are instead a player in a game not of the Roleplaying Variety, but instead, some sort of tactical War Game. The character you build could instead be a particularly powerful hero leading your armies to victory. That, or you could simply be up to playing some war game sessions with whoever your buddies are in the world you've chosen. Either way, this makes things at least a little chiller. Then again, war gamers aren't exactly known for being chill.
addons.title: War Games, War Games Never Changes

objects.text:
In the not-so-distant future, following your arrival, global tensions will ignite into open conflict—a third world war born of pride, paranoia, and power. Politicians and generals, the modern-day war pigs, will orchestrate the chaos from their safe havens, sending others to die in their stead.

Some whisper that this war was not mere chance, but the final movement in a long-orchestrated symphony—perhaps the work of Cauldron, pulling strings behind the scenes for their “greater good,” or worse, the silent hand of the Simurgh, sowing the seeds of destruction for decades to come.

Parahumans will be conscripted like tools of war, stripped of choice and turned into weapons. Villains will be pardoned to serve on the front lines, their past crimes erased in exchange for bloodshed. Meanwhile, heroes who refuse to kneel will be branded traitors, imprisoned or killed for their principles.

As the fires of war spread, the Endbringers will descend like divine retribution, capitalizing on humanity’s self-destruction. Entire cities will burn. Domestic order will collapse. Warlords and rogue parahumans will rise from the ashes, carving out fiefdoms in the lawless void.

Chaos will reign, not as an accident—but as prophecy.
As the lyrics go:
"Now in darkness, world stops turning
Ashes where the bodies burning
No more war pigs have the power
Hand of God has struck the hour..."

And still, the machine grinds on.
Death and Hatred To Mankind
objects.title: War Pigs

objects.text:
After Parahumans started appearing one hero rose above the rest as a shining paragon of morality and strength. This hero would go on to almost single handedly drag the world away from chaos and into an era of relative peace. Crime still occurs and villains still scheme, but so long as the symbol stands civilization will never collapse.

You may choose one canon character to be this symbol, if their canon capabilities aren’t strong enough for this position you may choose if they are either stronger here or if some other factor was involved in them being able to become this worlds’ Symbol of Peace.

If the character in question is too young to realistically have had an impact on the world by the start of canon, feel free to make them older while adjusting their backstory to match. An example could be making Vista be in her mid-twenties or older by the start of canon.
objects.title: Symbol of Peace

addons.text: You can now completely change the gender and identity roles of your world to your liking. You can create or remove roles, make them equal, uniform, under a complex hierarchy or anything else. You can decide what kinds of things are considered traditionally masculine, feminine, androgynous as well as create new categories. You can also make it so traditional identities and social roles aren’t based on sex or gender at all but rather something like profession, bloodline or power type, etc.
addons.title: Redefined Gender Roles

objects.text:
In this world, traditional gender roles and societal expectations have been completely reversed, creating a culture where everything from personal behavior to moral values has been reshaped through a mirrored lens. Traits commonly associated with femininity in our world—such as empathy, emotional awareness, and nurturing—are now expected and praised in men. Meanwhile, women are encouraged to embody qualities like assertiveness, decisiveness, and independence, which were once seen as masculine virtues.

This inversion doesn't stop at personality traits or values; it runs deep into the fabric of daily life. Household responsibilities, once traditionally assigned to women, have also flipped. Men are now the ones typically managing domestic duties—cooking, cleaning, child-rearing, and maintaining the emotional well-being of the household—while women take on the roles of primary breadwinners, protectors, and leaders in both public and private spheres.

Clothing and fashion reflect this societal shift as well. Men typically wear garments that would traditionally be considered delicate or ornamental in our world—flowing fabrics, bright colors, intricate designs—intended to express their gentleness and attention to emotional nuance. Women favor practical, utilitarian attire, often sharp-edged and uniform-like, designed to emphasize function, confidence, and control.

The history of this society further deepens the reversal. It was only in recent decades that men were granted the right to vote or own property independently. For much of history, men were viewed primarily as caretakers and companions, their lives centered around service to their households and communities. Women, by contrast, have long held institutional power and cultural dominance, shaping the course of politics, science, and innovation.

Even now, remnants of this inequality persist. Men’s voices are still often underrepresented in leadership, and their ambitions outside of domestic life can be met with skepticism or subtle discouragement. Movements for male empowerment have gained traction only recently, advocating for broader representation and recognition beyond their traditional roles.
objects.title: Reverse Gender Morals

objects.text: Case 53s no longer have visible Cauldron tattoos on their bodies. They are either completely missing, or hidden to only be revealed in specific circumstances. Either way, it is one less link in the chain of the mystery behind case 53s.
objects.title: Mysterious Case 53s

objects.text:
Not only do Case 53s lack a visible Cauldron tattoo, they lack a connection to them at all. Cauldron is just as confused as to where Case 53s come from as anyone else. As a matter of fact, Cauldron vials can't possibly create Case 53s, as when they mutate their host they either induce very minor mutations that are cosmetic at worst, or outright kill them via extremely nonviable physical mutations, with no in-between that could be called a Case 53.

You may decide the exact origin of Case 53s, such as the Warrior not killing deployed Thinker Shards which then mutate the host and destroy their original mind on triggering, an aborted experiment performed this cycle by either Entity, them being the work of a rogue Biotinker or other Parahuman experimenting with forced triggers, outright artificial humans with no memories due to not existing before their current state, something weirder not described here, or leave it random. No matter what, none of the big players in this world are aware of what that origin is.
objects.title: Emphasis on "Mysterious"

objects.text:
Throughout the world, hidden away in remote corners or nestled beneath oceans and mountain ranges, there exist ancient, secluded civilisations, societies that have either vanished from history or deliberately removed themselves from the broader stage of human development. These are not primitive peoples eking out an existence in forgotten jungles; rather, they are cultures of immense refinement, strength, and in some cases, staggering technological or mystical advancement.

Whether it’s the Amazons, whose weakest adult rivals Olympic athletes in raw strength and speed, and who are trained from birth in the arts of war or the Atlanteans, whose technology surpasses even the most advanced nations by generations, these societies have cultivated their strength away from the eyes of the world.

Despite their isolation, these groups are not necessarily ignorant of the wider world. Some may observe from afar, subtly shaping world events or keeping ancient compacts that bind them to global affairs. Others might openly interact with surface nations or modern powers, albeit on their own terms.

Unless you possess other modifiers that introduce non-human species or alternate races, all inhabitants of these societies are human. They may appear exotic or possess unfamiliar customs, but they are of the same biological lineage as the rest of humanity.
objects.title: Lost Societies

objects.text:
It seems most, if not all, of Earth has followed America’s example and made it legal and relatively easy to purchase guns. Firearms are now far more common across society, available to ordinary citizens with only minimal barriers to ownership. Shops that sell them can be found in most cities, often alongside the usual goods and services, and the process of acquiring one is no longer viewed as exceptional or unusual.

Guns have become a normalized presence, both as tools and as symbols, woven into the fabric of everyday life. Rural families may keep them as part of tradition, urban dwellers carry them for security, and hobbyists collect and customize them in much the same way others might with cars or instruments. Shooting ranges and firearm clubs are popular recreational spots, and competitions are a well-regarded pastime. In some locations, finding a person without a gun is harder than finding someone without a phone.
objects.title: American Way

objects.text:
Perhaps due to clothes being easier to wear and get now, or because new methods of production made clothing more accessible while still comfortable, everyday dress has broken away from old standards. Uniform styles have given way to variety, and what used to be unusual or niche is now part of the norm. Styles once reserved for small groups, like Gothic, Punk, Rockerboy, Bohemian, or Vintage, are now seen in the open on every street corner.

This shift doesn’t stop with clothing alone. Hairstyles follow the same trend, ranging from conservative looks to wild cuts, dyed streaks, or elaborate shapes. Accessories, from jewelry to hats to belts, show the same level of variety. Makeup and grooming can be equally bold or understated, depending on the person.

What was once considered “out there” or only for certain circles is now just part of daily life. The office worker, the student, and the shopkeeper may each look as if they stepped out of completely different worlds, yet none of it feels unusual anymore. Fashion has become less about fitting a standard and more about expression, and the streets are filled with an endless mix of colors, textures, and forms.
objects.title: Colourful Fashion

objects.text:
Now, the starting world you enter is full of gangs. When the sun goes down, the gangs come out. The number of gangs mostly depends on the size of the city — New York, for example, might have hundreds. Each gang follows its own beliefs, rules, and dogmas, with their own hierarchy systems.

Gangs can be violent or peaceful; some engage in crime, while others simply exist to defend their turf. Their members are usually stronger, faster, and tougher than ordinary people — many reaching peak human condition, and some even surpassing it. Every gang has its own distinct look and fighting style that makes them memorable.
objects.title: CAN YOU DIG IT!!!

objects.text:
Maybe it’s something in the water, or maybe those old people were right about the internet, but it seems people just have the survival instincts of a rock. You can see it everywhere, someone balancing on the edge of a skyscraper for a selfie, or someone deciding to “test the safety” of a gun by pulling the trigger. There’s no sense of caution, just blind confidence in the idea that nothing bad ever really happens, at least not to them.

It’s like evolution clocked out early. At this rate, if survival really does favor the fittest, the rocks might just outlast us after all.
objects.title: Survival Instincts of a Rock

addons.text: Parahuman-run corporations formed exceedingly quickly, their Tinker run R&D leading to technology that quickly outclassed any mundane competition. There was no hope for the government to respond with legislation, especially with the corporations' Thinker lawyers actively hindering them. In time, the governments themselves crumbled, replaced by megacorporations, corporate loyalty becoming the new currency.
addons.title: Megacorporate Sovereignty

addons.text:
With the lack of NEPEA-5 to restrict Parahumans' involvement in business and media, they quickly took over the corporations that tried to control them. What was once loose associations of powered individuals, shifted to corporate entities, tailored suits replacing colorful clothing and capes, with brand logos instead of heroic symbols. 

Parahumans are no longer volatile assets, but competitive advantages to be leveraged. A telekinetic isn’t a risk factor; they are a cost-cutting measure. A precognitive doesn’t threaten market fairness; they are market research.

Conflicts that once would have led to cape fights are now resolved in courtrooms or boardrooms instead, quite deals between corporations. Whenever actual violence does erupt, it's framed as “industrial sabotage,” not vigilantism.
addons.title: Parahumans Incorporated

addons.text: At some point, corporations realized that parahumans are drawn to conflict, having an outlet for this is essential, so they made corporate-sponsored parahuman sports leagues. These sports leagues not only acted as an outlet for parahumans' desire for conflict, but also as a new stream of revenue for the corporations.
addons.title: Corporate Games

addons.text: Corporations devised a new method to settle disputes between them, "games" where Parahumans would compete in bloody competitions, most likely to the death. The corporation with the winning parahuman would get what they wanted out of the deal. This meant that losing could mean the end for corporations. These double as illegal betting rings for wealthy individuals.
addons.title: Deadly Deals

objects.text:
Rather than merely existing, a massive privatisation and austerity movement in the mid-2000s left corporate superheroics the only financially viable way to make a legal living as a cape. 

As a result, not only are capes dramatically more commercialised, but they’re also subject to the whims of the board and the shareholders. On top of the regular abuses common under corporate structures, this also makes them rife for corruption as ‘cape insurance’ rocks the American scene specifically while various parts of Europe sell off specific regions to be private monopolies in the cape industry.

Cape-Based crime is also far higher, with corporate hiring practices being far more exacting than the Protectorate’s ever were, leaving profoundly traumatised parahumans out of work and desperate.
objects.title: Corpo Crapschute

objects.text:
When Scion appeared, all conflict ceased. All living beings then heard ten rules:

1. All murder, war, and robbery are forbidden in this world.
2. All conflict in this world will be resolved through games.
3. In games, each player will bet something that they agree is of equal value.
4. As long as it doesn't violate pledge three, anything may be bet, and any game may be played.
5. The challenged party has the right to decide the rules of the game.
6. Any bets made in accordance with the pledges must be upheld.
7. Conflicts between groups will be conducted by designated representatives with absolute authority.
8. Being caught cheating during a game is grounds for an instant loss.
9. In the name of god, the previous rules may never be changed.
10. Let's all have fun and play together!

Parahumans still exist, and use their power to their advantage during games. While conflict can only be resolved through games, many manipulated games in their favor, since as long as they are not caught, it’s fair game.
objects.title: God Of Games

objects.text: There's a strange and fascinating phenomenon happening in this world - people will suddenly burst into song at random times, expressing their emotions and thoughts through the power of song. Despite the fact that they may not have previously shown any interest in singing or even possessed the skills to do so, this strange occurrence has become the norm, and everyone in this world will see nothing strange or unexpected about it. Most would even join in. For those living in this world, singing has become an instinctive and accepted way of expressing oneself, whether it be through happiness, sadness, anger or excitement. In fact, many will even burst into song in the middle of combat.
objects.title: Musical Worm!

addons.text: Singing and dancing have become a natural and essential form of expression for everyone, regardless of the occasion. Whether in the midst of battle or during a mundane task, the sounds and movements generated from their performances are seen as a normal and integral part of their daily lives. Parahumans also receive a slight enhancement of their powers when performing, such as Skitter's ability to create or augment her bugs or Vista not being Manton Limited. Furthermore, both regular individuals and parahumans possess a minor influence over others, causing them to join in on their performances or act as backup dancers and stage crew. However, once the performance ends, this effect ceases. Despite its unusual nature, this unusual occurrence has become a natural and accepted part of this world, as everyone is accustomed to its presence.
addons.title: Lights, Music, Action!

objects.text: People instinctively prefer dancing over fighting. This unconventional phenomenon has become an integral part of their daily lives, and everyone living in this world perceives it as a natural form of combat. Furthermore, those inhabiting this world have become so accustomed to dancing in the midst of their skirmishes that they view it as a natural extension of themselves. Parahumans further amplify their dances with their powers, rendering them more spectacular and eye-catching. Ultimately, he or she who performs the most captivating and brilliant dance is declared the winner in the clash.
objects.title: Just Dance!

objects.text:
Whether they be rich people with too much time on their hands, immense martial skill, peak human physiology, and access to mundane technology that can compete with low tier Tinkertech, or they are just some guy with a bike and a lot of heart. There are in this version of earth a noticeable number of capes both villains, and heroes who are confirmed not to have parahuman powers but have made names for themselves both big and small.

You may select anyone up to 1/20 of all canon characters in this world to be a badass normal along with people you don’t know from Wildbow's predictions, however empowered capes must outnumber unpowered capes.
objects.title: Badass Normal Capes

addons.text:
The spectrum of exceptional abilities extends beyond the realm of child prodigies. Now, people without inherent supernatural powers can exhibit talents that can rival parahuman abilities.

There are many of these talented individuals, for example, someone akin to a real-life Sherlock Holmes, possessing an unparalleled mastery of deduction and observation, unravelling mysteries with uncanny precision. Or a tech savant whose genius surpasses all norms, crafting innovations that redefine the boundaries of technology and reshape the future. And even martial artists whose expertise transcends the physical realm, developing techniques that tap into the fullest extent of human potential and beyond, their mastery over mind and body beyond compare, blurring the lines between what's achievable and what's considered impossible.

Witness the emergence of individuals whose "powers" stem from honed natural talents pushed to their absolute limits. They challenge conventional notions of human potential and expand the horizons of what is conceivable.
addons.title: Super Talent

objects.text:
Throughout history, certain children in this world are far more talented than the norm. 15-year-olds running a hugely successful company worth millions, handling the challenges of business like a seasoned pro. Or 12-year-olds defeating top sports champions, leaving everyone astonished by their skill and ability.

Society has long since embraced these extraordinary talents, regardless of age. Once a child proves their remarkable abilities, they're treated just like adults, with their achievements celebrated and their potential limitless. It's a world where age doesn't matter much, and where talent is respected above everything else.
objects.title: Child Geniuses

objects.text: Society as a whole does not know about Parahumans, though governments do. Every Parahuman, shortly after they gain their powers, is warned by a woman in a Fedora who says something to them to make them eager to not let the public know about their powers.
objects.title: The Masquerade

objects.text:
With the Masquerade in place, secret societies, criminal syndicates, and government agencies have taken the place of the gangs and PRT. The Awakened and their subordinates work from the shadows and keep the general populace, known as the Sleepers, ignorant of their activities.

Intrigue and subterfuge are the name of the game, flashy costumes and masks are replaced by crisp suits and mirrored sunglasses. When clashes happen in the open, evidence always mysteriously vanishes, dismissed as mass hallucinations, the side-effect of gas leaks, or poor construction. Most Awakened are able to use their power discreetly without issues, the Shards having long since adapted to this new environment rich in conflict.

Cauldron works as a neutral party, providing access to other worlds through Yggdrasil, a parallel earth covered in mangroves of massive trees where humans never evolved, the main nexus of Awakened activity. The hanging platform of Yggdrasil are neutral ground where organizations can meet without the threat of betrayal, where ToyBox openly sells their gadgets and weapons, and where small mercenary groups and independent contractors offer their services to the highest bidder.

Even the Endbringers follow those rules, using natural disasters or social unrest as cover for their activities. The devastation left in their wake is less spectacular but no less impactful; Andrew Richter still perished when a storm raged over Newfoundland for weeks on end, washing away most of the homes on the island into the sea; Kyushu was devastated by tsunamis and Japan's economy never recovered; waves of violent protests in Lausanne and elsewhere in Switzerland created ripples that led to the fall of multiple international corporations; earthquakes left oil fields in Iran crippled and Moscow in ruins; volcanic activity disrupted international travel for days on end.
objects.title: The Secret World

objects.text: The Masquerade dead, the world knows of the existence of parahumans, heroes and villains openly clash in the streets, gangs vie for territory across cities, and they all come together to fight against humanity's enemies: the dreaded Endbringers. Or is it? In truth, the world of capes is divided into two halves. The Masks are those who operate openly, they are flashy and theatric, wear elaborate costumes and trade quips during fights, but are also largely ineffective at their respective roles. Major injuries and deaths are vanishingly rare. When villains are captured, they almost always escape or are sprung out. This group is composed mostly of capes with more obvious powers like, for example, flying brutes or blasters. The Shadows are those who live in the secret world, in the shadow of intrigue and subterfuge, where the threats are deadly and stakes are high. Shadow organizations employ all types of capes but some groups, like thinkers and strangers, are almost all on the secret side of the divide. Most of what is described in The Secret World remains in place. While Cauldron mainly sells vials to shadow organizations, often through third-party brokers, they also help maintain the masquerade with a healthy supply of Mask-type capes from individual clients.
objects.title: Light and Dark

addons.text: The supernatural itself is no longer immune to the shroud. Those who are different- unnatural- no longer realize they are different; unable to tell what powers, if any, they have, and unable to direct them... at least consciously.. Those who deviate from the human norm may appear atypical, psychopathic, delusional, or otherwise strange, but not supernatural. Those who are particularly perceptive may notice things happening in a consistent manner around themselves, eventually clawing their way through the Shroud bit by tiny bit as they analyze things that just don't quite match up between reality and their perception of it. Even if they succeed, they will still struggle to tell if there is anything different about anyone else, and they are far more likely to come to the conclusion that they themselves may be insane. Those who are genuinely mad, insane, or sufficiently aneurotypical may be able to peek behind the shroud somewhat- but even they are not immune to its effects entirely, even if they notice that the Shroud itself is there.
addons.title: That Which Hides Underneath

objects.text:
The existence of parahumans is cloaked in subtlety, making it nearly impossible to distinguish them from ordinary people at a glance. Their abilities manifest as seemingly mundane skills or talents, elevated to extraordinary levels. These powers do not announce themselves with spectacle; instead, they seamlessly blend into the fabric of daily life, often mistaken for natural genius or exceptional aptitude.

To the outside observer, these individuals appear to be prodigies, masters of their craft, or extraordinarily fortunate people who excel effortlessly. A parahuman athlete might push the boundaries of human performance, yet their feats remain just within the realm of possibility, leaving onlookers in awe but not disbelief. A parahuman scientist might make groundbreaking discoveries or solve complex problems with ease, yet their brilliance is attributed to intellect rather than anything supernatural. Even artists, musicians, or strategists might display an uncanny ability to create or innovate, but their talents are dismissed as the product of intense practice and dedication. The presence of parahumans subtly elevates the overall capabilities of humanity, with modern parahumans often surpassing their predecessors as the human limit is quietly redefined.

This subtlety extends to the parahumans themselves. Most are unaware of their true nature, believing their abilities stem from hard work, innate talent, or simple good fortune. They might feel different or set apart from others, but the idea that they possess superhuman powers rarely crosses their minds. This self-deception is reinforced by a society that neither recognizes nor understands the existence of parahumans, instead placing them on pedestals as exceptional individuals or rare geniuses.
objects.title: Subtlety Is Best

objects.text:
The world is cloaked in an ever present, esoteric Shroud that hides and separates the supernatural from the mundane through both illusions, spatial warping, and mental alterations. Mundane people without clearsight- immunity to the Shroud- will be unable to properly see monsters, spells, powers, hyper-advanced technology, aliens, or other esoteric things and effects. Instead, their perceptions and memories are warped to make everything they perceive mundane. The Shroud will even passively warp space to keep mundanes away from active conflicts or areas of high supernatural density- even going as far as to hide entire cities or locations if necessary. 

Through some means- whether magic, technology, powers or sheer will or skill- individuals can learn to manipulate small bits of the Shroud to their own ends. Portioning off chunks that they can use to disguise themselves, objects, or places, warp space, create illusions, alter memories, and more. Though none of this comes easy, and the Shroud resists attempts at outside manipulation.
objects.title: The Shroud

objects.text:
On April 7th, 1980, the United States of America formally ceased existing. 

A visitor from another universe, an ‘Administrator’ came to the world. The first thing they did was establish an organisation that would go on to absorb the nascent Cauldron. A Thinker par-excellence, they guided politics, history, industry and scientific operations to create a tightly knit and highly efficient machine that combines military, diplomatic, Intelligence, economic, scientific and political operations. Its preparations are concealed, not published. Its mistakes are buried, not headlined.

The aim of The Administrator is simple, the creation of a perfect world made in her own image. To which she began in May  of 1982 by slightly delaying Andrew Hawke’s car, stopping him from making the cruise that would see him meet the Golden Man, Scion. With no Vikare Cape culture never exploded. Pressure points were isolated and defused. Figures who would become crux points diffused into completely average lives. What parahumans do exist are secretive. Those of use are sought after by a vast conspiracy that has long since organised politics into a machine for either distration or the creation of Crisis Points where needed.
