The Administrator is a great Thinker, and she will have her Perfect World.
objects.title: Administrative Invasion

objects.text: Most governments are ruled over by Parahumans, or at the very least have Parahumans very high up. The world is also split into many smaller nations, at least for the most part.
objects.title: Parahuman Fiefdoms

objects.text: Following the emergence of Parahumans, the world changed significantly. Democratic governments were overthrown, and monarchical societies emerged, with Parahumans ruling as Kings, Queens, and nobles. Normal humans are subjected to oppression, treated as little more than slaves. Wars are waged regularly, with many dying everyday. Luckily, Cauldron is around, so the world wouldn’t self implode…
objects.title: Parahuman Royalty

objects.text:
Parahumans are treated much the same way that Mutants are in Marvel, with fear and disgust. Glaistig Uaine and Eidolon have teamed up to protect Parahumans from humanity.
Many Parahumans hate humans as much as humans hate them. Because of this, no ordinary humans are allowed in their territory.
Humans are able to go against Parahumans due to Parahumans, mostly Tinkers, who have been coerced through the government by threatening their families and friends.
objects.title: Divided

objects.text:
There is a world war and there are three sides, and the Holdouts.
The Naturalists hate Parahumans and use advanced nuclear technology to combat Parahumans with surprising effectiveness. Their technology is all produced by a Nuclear and Robotics Tinker with reproducible tech that they all believe is an idiot savant.
The Liberalists want basic human rights for everyone, including Parahumans, and will not surrender their freedom for anything.
And the Machine Intelligence, a group of cyborgs under the control of an AI named Dragon, who believes she is benevolent for allowing the humans under her to be happy, constantly, without pause. 
The Holdouts are locations that manage to hold their own territory without submitting to one of the factions. Some Holdouts wish to ally with the Naturalists or Liberalists.
The Naturalists control much of South America, Mexico, South Africa, and southern Australia.
The Liberalists control the United States and some of Mexico, the Caribbeans, Western Africa, Western Europe, West Asia, and South Asia.
The Machine Intelligence controls everywhere else except the locations where the Holdouts exist.
The major Holdouts are most of the Middle East, Egypt, Greece, Iceland, Greenland, Alaska, and Svalbard.
objects.title: Fractured

addons.text:
The Emperor of the CUI isn’t expanding because of the disappearance of Endbringers, he is expanding BECAUSE of the Endbringers. The CUI has managed to recruit one of the Para-Endbringers to their cause, emboldening them to expand their empire. It is uncertain whether it is because of coercion, genuine patriotism, or if they are using them for their own goals. 

What is certain is that governments around the world will attempt to recruit their own Para-Endbringers into their militaries. Some of them will try to refuse, but most governments, rather stupidly, won’t take no for an answer. Chaos and destruction will ensue.
addons.title: The Global Threat

objects.text:
With the disappearance of the Endbringers, the emperor of the CUI decided to expand his empire. The armies of the world are mobilizing everywhere as the battle against the Chinese hegemony begins. Tinker weapons and Parahumans will define the next paradigm of warfare.

In both the US and Europe, most Parahuman organizations are folded into the military chain of command. Villains that do not lay low or join the war effort for amnesty are dealt with harshly. Despite public outcry, parahumans as young as fourteen are allowed to join.

The fate of the free world is at stake.
objects.title: The Secret of the Swordfish

objects.text:
The veneer of civility has been stripped away. Society collapses from a number of catastrophic events. Cauldron has either been destroyed or corrupted. Parahumans must vie for dominance over the remnants, seizing power across the world as power. 

Warlords will soon take hold of all major cities. Resistance is scattered and haphazard. Almost all hope for a better world is gone. 

You can decide when this collapse occurs, anywhere from the 1980s to the week you arrive.
objects.title: Alea Iacta Est

objects.text:
Following widespread catastrophes that happened soon after WWII, only a tiny fraction of humanity remains, the relentless force of natural selection, unleashed through catastrophic disasters, has mercilessly culled the majority of the population. Society has collapsed, replaced by lawlessness reigning over the lands.

The survivors have become hardened and ruthless, wary of each other and reluctant to form alliances or trust one another. With the instinct for self-preservation overriding all else, many are willing to resort to any means necessary to ensure their own survival, even if it means betraying their own kin or selling them into slavery.

Among the survivors, there emerges a pattern: they tend to represent the upper echelons of humanity, possessing genetic traits that favor survival in the face of adversity. Most, if not all of these individuals are parahumans. These individuals, endowed with resilience and adaptability, have weathered the storms of catastrophe where others faltered. Their genetic makeup predisposes them to navigate the harsh realities of this new world with a greater chance of success, further cementing their position atop the dwindling hierarchy of humanity's remnants.
objects.title: Human Extinction

objects.text:
Whether it be from Scion possibly presenting himself as a Mentor, or if he arrived first in Japan, or if in this world's history; superhero media had been overtaken by tokusatsu such as Kamen Rider and Super Sentai. In the end, Earth Bet's cape scene had taken up a much more costumed design.

Whether it be between lone armored heroes fighting against squads of equally armored minions, to teams of color coded warriors in combat against each other and villains donning monstrous suits. Even towards large scale campaigns against genetically modified abominations and terrorist groups.

Despite its colorful appearance and relatively superior organization to Bet, this place could be seen as more dangerous overall with officials believing wholeheartedly in separating Capes as Heroes or Villains, increased distrust towards Monstrous Capes, and city-destroying abilities being relatively more common...
objects.title: Fracture Sentai Kirakaiger

objects.text:
Perhaps it was because Scion had appeared as a Guide, or because he had first landed in Japan, or because the popular culture of this world had been dominated by magical girl shows. Whatever the reason, Earth Bet’s cape scene had adopted a much more whimsical style.

From solo heroines in frilly dresses battling hordes of cute but evil creatures, to teams of color-coordinated warriors fighting against each other and dark lords in elaborate costumes. Even the large-scale conflicts against mutated horrors and terrorist groups had a certain flair to them.

Despite its fanciful appearance and relatively better organization than Bet, this place was not less dangerous by any means. The authorities were strict about dividing Capes into Good or Evil, the public was wary of Monstrous Capes, and city-leveling powers were more frequent…
objects.title: Magical Girls

objects.text:
Whether it be from Scion possibly presenting himself as a Mentor, or if he arrived first in Italy, or if in this world's history. The first parahumans rose not as spandex-wearing idealists or masked vigilantes, but as soldiers, enforcers, and heirs to old families. The Mafia never died—it evolved.

In this world, superpowers are synonymous with underworld influence. The rise of Capes followed the codes of Cosa Nostra, Camorra, and 'Ndrangheta, not the caped crusaders of comics. Hero and Villain aren’t ideological labels—they’re territorial brands. Every city has its Families, and each Family has its Capos, Enforcers, Cleaners, and Ghosts. Powers serve the Family. Loyalty is enforced. Betrayal is punished.

The culture of the cape has adopted the aesthetics and structure of organized crime: sharp suits laced with concealed armor, power-themed rings denoting status, and family crests branded onto skin or blood. In place of Cops and Robbers, there are blood-oaths often sealed with the loss of something personal.

While this world appears more orderly than Bet, it is no less dangerous. The Omertà, the Code of Silence, is law. Powers are hidden until used. Face and fear are currency. Monstrous capes, known as Santi, are often the product of failed oaths(triggers) and are used as tools of terror. Governments collude or kneel. The line between protector and predator is blurred, as Favore replaces law and reputation is more binding than any contract.

This earth is a place where a handshake might be deadlier than a duel, and every trigger event is someone’s leverage. To rise, you must play the Game of Masks. To fall… means your bones feed the next deal.
objects.title: Omertà Capo di Frattura

objects.text:
Whether it be from Scion possibly presenting himself to only a select few high powered people, or if most parahumans have decided their work is better off done with a delicate approach, whatever the case may be, this world's parahumans have taken a more martini flavored Spy Fiction tone. With most parahumans working as secret agents in many hidden organizations or for their respective governments. 

In this world, powered individuals rarely go for colorful capes. Here, people would prefer to dress in style. Sleek suits or dark trench coats are in. Those who identify or are labeled as Villains do still like a good suit or two, but you may see more varied and colorful attire from the likes of them. From huge monocles, to cats just being constantly pat menacingly while they giggle on their oversized chair, those sorts of stylish types of rogues.

This world also has generally less knowledge on capes. While people know powered folks exists, their hero or villain work is kept mostly under wraps. Subtlety is key here. They would foil dastardly conspiracies to take over the world, and few would know to thank them about it. Conflicts here range from huge and action movie esque, to relatively small scale. Either way, the thin veneer of peace is an easy one to rip through in this setting.
objects.title: I, Spy

addons.text:
This world might resemble a fairy tale, but not the comforting stories of happy endings and gentle lessons. Instead, it echoes the original Grimm tales—brutal, unforgiving, and soaked in blood. The world’s cruelty is not random chaos, but something with grim structure, as though reality itself is now ruled by the logic of ancient, cautionary fables.

The line between story and nightmare has vanished. Parahumans, civilians, villains, and heroes alike live out narratives that resemble twisted folklore. Fortunes rise and fall as though guided by dark, moralistic forces. Wishes can still come true, but they often carry cruel twists, iron prices, or bitter regrets. Those who seek power may find it, only to be devoured by it. Love may spark, but is frequently poisoned by obsession, betrayal, or inevitable tragedy. Even acts of heroism are rarely rewarded as one might hope—more often they become cautionary tales etched into the crumbling bones of the world.

In this world, horror follows fairy tale logic. Poetic justice is real, but it is rarely kind. Villains may triumph not through strength, but through cunning tricks and cruel fates that echo dark folklore. The forces that govern the world seem to delight in suffering that is thematically appropriate, as though every tragedy is being woven into some vast, malevolent tapestry. Even magic, luck, or extraordinary power bends to these grim storylines. You live in a narrative where the monsters win, where the lessons are brutal, and where the only certainty is that the cost of every choice will be steep. Welcome to a fairy tale where there are no happy endings—only endings.
addons.title: Grimm Tales

objects.text:
The world is a miserable place.

Parahumans still experience traumatic events that trigger their powers, but they let them consume and corrupt them. They fester in their wounds and repeat their mistakes. They use their abilities for evil and join the ranks of villains more often than heroes. Crime is savage and anarchic, like a slaughterhouse of blood and madness. Even the noblest heroes can be broken by malicious torture or fatal backstabbing. Death is common in this world. And even in the case of survival, there might be people who wish they were dead.

Humans are caught in the crossfire of parahuman conflicts. They suffer from collateral damage, terror attacks, kidnappings, experiments, and enslavement. They live in fear of the capes that rule over them, or the ones that hunt them for sport. They have no rights, no protection, no justice. They have no future.

Parahumans are driven by their powers to create more conflict and chaos. They feed their trauma and rage with each other, and with humans. They fight for power, money, revenge, or just for fun. They don’t care about the consequences of their actions or the lives they ruin along the way. They don’t care about the world they live in or the people they share it with.

But there is no escape. There is no hope. There is only pain and suffering. Parahumans are doomed to destroy themselves and everything they touch. They are the harbingers of the end of the world.

Welcome to Earth Hell, the worst place in existence.
objects.title: Welcome to Earth Hell

objects.text:
The alignments of all capes are reversed. The canon story's villains are heroes, and the canon story's heroes are villains.

The white supremacist gang known as Empire 88 never existed here. Instead, its members are all part of the Protectorate, and the teens who would've become the Undersiders are now their Wards. Meanwhile, instead of forming the ABB, Lung and Oni Lee are a vigilante duo that fight crime on the streets.

On the other side, the canon members of New Wave are the villainous gang Dark Tide, a family of parahumans that holds Brockton Bay in its tight grip. The canonical Protectorate heroes became independent villains who ally with Dark Tide while pursuing their own agendas.

These changes only apply to Capes, so Scion is still bad and Cauldron is still "good." Rogues like Parian and more ambiguous capes like Contessa remain as they were in canon.
objects.title: Reverse Roles

objects.text: The prevalence of Tinkers has contributed to the enhancement of the world's technological level at a significant rate before legislation prohibiting further developments was established. This has resulted in the formation of a dystopian world where advanced technology has shaped the very fabric of society. Tinker-run corporations have become significant powers that rule the world and have overshadowed governments in terms of their power and influence. These conglomerates have introduced cutting-edge technologies that have impacted transportation, communication, medicine, and several other sectors. They now govern the economy and have a considerable impact on politics and culture. This world suffers from great inequity, with some residing in luxury and savoring the advantages of new technology, while others endure in poverty and are unable to afford these advancements. Governments are now incapable of regulating the corporations, and they have become ineffective in addressing the problems brought by these emerging technologies. This new social structure necessitates individuals to learn how to maneuver this altered world and understand how to exist in an environment that blurs the boundaries between humans and technology.
objects.title: Cyberpunk

objects.text: Biotinkers are highly regarded in this world, and their innovations have been embraced by society. From advanced healthcare and prosthetics to enhanced vehicles, the impact of biotinkers on society is both profound and far-reaching. The latest advances in genetics and biotechnology have made it possible to create advanced medical treatments, replacing the need for invasive surgery and other risky procedures. The development of cutting-edge prosthetics made with bio-engineering techniques has also enabled those with disabilities to live fuller, more independent lives. Moreover, biotinkers have played a key role in the evolution of machinery, creating machines that are made of and use biomatter as renewable fuel.
objects.title: Biotech

objects.text:
Biotinkers have reshaped the very fabric of human civilization, propelling mankind into an era where biology and technology are indistinguishably intertwined. Through their groundbreaking advances in DNA modification, the once-clear boundaries between species have been obliterated. It is now commonplace to encounter individuals with animalistic features—feathered wings, feline eyes, scaled skin—each a testament to the limitless potential of genetic engineering. These alterations are not merely cosmetic; they often come with enhanced senses, physical abilities, and even entirely new biological functions, making each person a unique blend of human and animal traits.

The influence of biotinkers extends far beyond individual transformations. The technology that once relied on circuits and steel has given way to living, breathing organisms. Buildings are grown from massive, self-sustaining plant structures, their walls pulsing with organic light and their systems regulated by living neural networks. Vehicles are bioengineered creatures, merging the speed and durability of machines with the adaptive, self-healing properties of living organisms. Everyday tools, appliances, and even weapons are now biological entities, designed to interact seamlessly with the altered physiology of their users.
objects.title: Transhumanism

objects.text:
Perhaps it was Cauldron's influence or conflict drive ending up weird, for whatever reason, Earth Bet’s cape scene had embraced a much more competitive attitude.

From solo stars in flashy outfits vying for attention and popularity, to teams of charismatic personalities clashing for ratings and sponsors. Even the large-scale events against natural disasters and criminal organizations had a sense of spectacle and drama.

Despite its glamorous appearance and relatively higher entertainment value than Bet, this place was not less ruthless by any means. The corporations were relentless about ranking Capes, the fans were fickle and demanding of Famous Capes, and the more famous you were the greater your influence on the world. Capes, both heroes, and villains, try to compete against each other for fame. Due to this, they seldom work together at all.
objects.title: Competitive Society

addons.text: If you wish, you may apply the effects of Major Villain Morality Flip to The 7 Demon Kings / Queens. This makes them much more heroic, actually wanting to help people or the world in some way. However, they are still viewed as villainous in nature by the world at large. Perhaps they have really bad PR, maybe they have severe power induced mental issues that cause them to lash out at others, they could simply refuse to play by the unwritten rules or listen to governments and are thus declared villains, or it could even be that Cauldron works to minimize their influence to prevent such strong competitors from disrupting their Path. No matter how the world sees them though, they are on the side of good.
addons.title: Misunderstood Heroes

objects.text: Seven individuals have triggered with powers equal to Tier 3 powers, these individuals each represent one of the seven deadly sins and will live like tyrants, viewing themselves as gods above all but Scion, they are all classified as SS-class threats and viewed as disasters above even that of the endbringers.
objects.title: The 7 Demon Kings/Queens

addons.text: If you wish, you may apply the effects of Major Hero Morality Flip to The 7 Seraphim. This makes them much more villainous, actually craving power, attention, and fulfilling their cruel desires. However, they are still viewed as heroic in nature by the world at large. Perhaps they have really good PR, maybe they bribed or blackmailed politicians into supporting them, they could simply disappear everyone who finds out the truth, or it could even be that Cauldron works for them as they see no choice but to acquiesce to their best hope against the Entity. No matter how the world sees them though, they only pursue their self interests at the expense of everyone else.
addons.title: Secret Villains

objects.text: Somehow, against incredible odds, seven good and kind people have managed to trigger with powers equal to Tier 3 powers. They will act as Guardians and Protectors and view their powers as a burden and a responsibility to help guide and protect those who are weaker than them. The future of Earth bet looks significantly brighter with seven guardian angels looking over it.
objects.title: The 7 Seraphim

objects.text: Things can't be that simple can it? Somehow, someway, 7 individuals with aligning goals awaken with powers equal to Tier 3 abilities. They form a mysterious organization who's goals are hard to fully understand. All that is known is that they tend to act in a way that keeps neither good nor evil from becoming the dominant force in your world. The heroes can't have too many wins but neither can the villains. They are chaotic in their approach, tipping the scales to keep some sort of balance. They call themselves a neutralizing force in the world, for better or for worse.
objects.title: The 7 Lords of Balance

objects.text:
The Entities’ first foray into the void was fraught with the same dangers any other interstellar civilization experienced, unknown monsters and other unkind civilizations lurking among the stars. One of their first cycles when they were still young and few and but a nascent threat to the universe had them bonding with a powerful and elderly spacefaring civilization. 

A few decades into the Cycle their nature was revealed and an incredible might was brought to bear against the entities and nearly eradicated the species. The Entities destroyed the few worlds they had nestled on and quickly escaped into the darkness and silence of space,
fleeing further and further away, but their enemies never forgot. 

While the entities bred and evolved, the ancient empire expanded and conquered. They innovated and planned, fully aware of the Entities' true threat to the multiverse, they have now begun a crusade against them. Their war has led to the death of countless entities, and unfortunately, a few civilizations were caught in the crossfire as well. They have found their way to earth and discovered the Entities hiding amongst it, now the question is will your world join their holy cause, fight against their formidable machine of war, or be nothing more than a hapless bystander in this Great War?
objects.title: The Empire Strikes Back

objects.text: The ancient empire that the Entities had encountered at their early stages, the race that nearly eradicated it and chased it into the void of space, forever terrified and paranoid of the predator lurking among the stars, is none other than humanity. This iteration of humanity is far older, ruthless, powerful, the very name of the species is often spoken of only in hushed whispers among other civilizations, for they fear even speaking the name aloud would bring the terrifying race’s attention to them. This version of humanity has long since conquered the stars, developed technologies, and vast empires more than capable of destroying droves of Entities. Due to their initial interactions with the Entities long before, humanity developed a taste for possessing their abilities, they developed various methods of empowering themselves. Initially learning to hijack and program the shards of slain Entities, they would eventually develop methods of creating Shardless powers of their own for their wealthy and elites, however, the use of Entity shards remains in high demand among the empires of humanity to break down and hand out abilities to its denizens. Humanity as a whole is far more powerful, most humans possess a variety of powers that they either gain through vials or are otherwise born with and develop sometime in puberty. Most children will inherit the powers of their parents. Cauldron is an incredibly powerful and integral part of the empire, the main supplier of vials that supply the rest of the empire with an enormous amount of entities slain to their name. Each member of Cauldron is far more powerful than their canon counterparts. Eidolon created and controls the Endbringers, a name, and title given by the Entities, a terrifying amount of monsters that are as far away in power from the Entities as the Canon Endbringers are from normal humans. The empire has vast worlds and territories, enough to boggle the mind, through which it spreads and develops. From desert worlds with few outposts to massive sprawling city-planets that have been entirely cored out and layered, each layer effectively a planet of its own, and even massive halo rings that expand and stretch even as far away halfway through a solar system all the way around for a full loop. All this and much more are within the scope of humanity. Humanity has long since developed methods of Negentropy and has even learned how to travel through the multiverse to reach destinations that the entities can’t reach, although this is typically reserved for the incredibly wealthy and powerful, however, the Entities are unlikely to discover it due to their aversion for dealing with humanity and humanity’s protections that they’ve created against precog and/or thinker powers. There are an uncountable number of races that interact with and are part of humanity’s empire, however, humanity is fundamentally the most important and powerful race. Taking this AU removes the immediate threat of the cycle, instead turning it into a war against the Entities in its entirety, one that humanity has been waging for a longer period than it hasn’t, with no end in sight.
objects.title: Old Empire

objects.text:
[The Thinker] had learned much from her encounter with the [The Wanderer], among the most important was the value of enticing cooperation in their host species. 

Before her distractions, she was able to make use of some of this information and adjusted her and [The Warrior]’s cycle accordingly, instead of simply instigating conflicts the shards now have a small drive to have parahumans congregate together, driving them into cooperation. 

As a result of this alteration, the development of parahuman society followed a much more natural line of progression for humans. Humans had always congregated in groups among others that were similar to themselves, the advent of parahumans did not change that fact. 

Rather than dressing up in bright tights and playing a superpowered version of cops and robbers parahumans instead started to congregate together. They started small at first, there being so few at their beginnings, often groups of no more than 3 or 4, but eventually they started getting larger and larger.

As the emergence of Parahumans came into the public they would start to form guilds, seeing the opportunity in their new found abilities guilds would in turn start hiring themselves. Their jobs could range from anything as simple as landscaping, to bodyguard duty, to hunting powerful animals, to even acting as full blown mercenary groups. Some guilds become more famous than others, some have become known for specializing in particular contracts such as mercenary work, others were known to be little more than an organized crime group.

Regardless most cities have at least 1 guild of their own, independents rare and often it’s because they’ve simply yet to join a guild. There are a few instances where parahuman groups have grown so large as to create small towns of their own. 

Parahumans are now usually much more liberal with their powers, it’s not particularly difficult to find a Parahuman that has commercialized their powers or that utilizes it in every day life openly. Few hide their identities and and most Parahumans act much more Roguelike in this timeline than their canon counterparts. As a side effects of Eden’s alterations to drive Parahuman groups, second and successive generations Parahuman are also much more common, almost guaranteed.
objects.title: Guilds

addons.text:
The warmongering Earth is merely the vanguard, the initial wave of an impending onslaught. The true threat lies in the empire that backs them, a colossal force poised to follow. This empire, much like your civilization, is multiversal in scope, traversing countless dimensions. However, unlike the peaceful and collaborative ethos of your world, their civilization is forged in the crucible of war and conquest. They live by a brutal creed: might makes right.

This empire is a relentless war machine, an amalgamation of countless conquered worlds and species, all subjugated under the iron fist of their doctrine. Their society thrives on strength, valorizing those who dominate and subjugate, and casting aside the weak. Their technology and powers are honed not for the betterment of all, but as tools of war, perfected through endless conflict and bloodshed.

Within this empire, there are many factions, usually formed of variants of the same type. The Optimax Syndicate, made up of variants of Armsmaster, all seeking glory. The Arcane Church, made up of variants of Eidolon, all seeking worthy opponents. The worst of the lot, the leaders of this empire; The Administrators, countless variants of Taylor Hebert, with multitude of alternate powers.
addons.title: Infinite Earths

objects.text:
Your Earth has become the target of a formidable and war-driven alternate Earth, a parallel world where villains, such as the Gesellschaft, Elite, etc. had long taken over, corrupting iconic heroes, making them take darker, more menacing forms. This aggressive counterpart harbors figures such as Tech Priest, the variant of Armsmaster, who has transformed his body into a hyper-efficient nano-swarm, capable of adapting and overcoming any technological obstacle. Ms. Militia, known in this world as War Child, wields a terrifying arsenal, her very essence infused with the spirit of conflict and conquest.

Even a variant of Contessa exists, serving as the trusted advisor to the empire's leaders. Her strategic brilliance and foresight are now tools of oppression and domination, guiding their forces with an unerring hand. This empire's access to your world is made possible through their version of Doctor Haywire, a twisted genius whose experiments have bridged the dimensional divide, unleashing their might upon your unsuspecting planet.

As their invasion begins, your Earth is thrust into a desperate struggle against these powerful and twisted counterparts. The defenders of your Earth must now confront not only their greatest fears but also the harrowing realization that their adversaries are dark reflections of themselves, possessing knowledge and power that mirror their own but twisted by a relentless drive for conquest.

In the face of this onslaught, alliances must be forged, strategies devised, and sacrifices made. The battle for your Earth's survival has begun, a war that will test the very limits of heroism and resilience as the lines between friend and foe blur in the chaos of interdimensional conflict.
objects.title: Invasion of Variants

objects.text:
Sometime after the creation of the Birdcage, one of the directors of the PRT came up with a new idea to employ criminals who have committed heinous deeds. Thanks to the new method that this director came up with, the PRT decided to implement this new strategy as a covert team.

Those who have useful powers among those who are to enter the Birdcage are instead implanted with a bomb connected to the Corona Pollentia that detects if the prisoner is using their power unauthorized and blows them up in kind. They are then selected and put in various squads to hunt, kill, or capture other S-class threats or undergo missions that the PRT or Cauldron issue them with the promise that if they complete enough missions, they will have a reduced sentence. However, after achieving this requirement, the mind of the parahuman is erased, and they go through the process again. 
 
Thanks to this new strategy, many threats to humanity have been taken out; however, lurking on various message boards, people have started to figure out what the PRT is doing, and most people are not happy. This will sow distrust in the government as well as the PRT from parahumans who fear that they will be the next person to be conscripted. If word of this covert team gets out, people will have no reason to respect or even abide by the Unwritten Rules.
objects.title: Suicide Squad

objects.text:
On many Earths, the mere mention of Artificial Intelligence evokes fear and horror—perceived as looming threats that could threaten humanity itself—among the masses. But on Earth Bet, the tide has turned. In a landslide victory within the United Nations and across the globe, Artificial Intelligences are granted the same rights and protections as any human.

Theresa Richter, known as Dragon, stands as the first publicly recognized Artificial Intelligence. Free to act without the fear of alienating humanity, Dragon has spearheaded rapid advancements in North America's infrastructure. The phone networks now extend into the most remote regions, the power grid is more resilient than ever, and affordable electric vehicles have become widespread.

Many other AI are emerging, created by inventive tinkers before gaining their own sentience and independence. As a result, everyday technology is poised to make significant leaps forward across numerous fields. The technological singularity feels almost inevitable.

Naturally, this means the Shards relax their restrictions against Artificial Intelligences. While these rules are not lax enough to allow any AI to pose an immediate threat, the emergence of new AI is now a relatively common occurrence.
objects.title: The Universal Declaration of Digital Rights

objects.text:
There seems to be a growing trend, the creation of death games. These are deadly competitions where people are forced to fight, survive, or outsmart others, often with their lives on the line. Sometimes these games are created by rich and powerful people who want something exciting to watch. They offer huge cash prizes, special rewards, or promises of freedom. Other times, these games are made by criminals, madmen, or secret groups who either enjoy watching others suffer or have some kind of twisted ideology. They may not even care who wins, as long as the pain and chaos continue.

These death games come in many forms. Some take place in huge arenas where players must fight with weapons while the crowd cheers. Others are more like puzzles or traps—players are locked in strange buildings or islands and must solve clues, escape danger, or betray their teammates to survive. Some are hidden as reality shows, where people think they’re signing up for a contest or adventure, only to learn the truth too late. There are even games where people are taken from their normal lives without warning and wake up somewhere unknown, forced to follow strange rules or die.

The world itself doesn’t fully stop these games. Some people fear them, others try to ignore them, and a few even enjoy watching them from the shadows. Law enforcement is often too weak, too corrupt, or too scared to act. Because of this, death games keep happening, be it in secret underground arenas, on remote islands, or even hidden corners of the internet.
objects.title: Death Games

addons.text: The games are now streamed across the world. How so will depend on the setting. Regardless, fans and sponsors are now huge factors in gaining an advantage in the sport. Money is still important, but the support (or hatred) can legitimately make you perform better. Boos and cheers are equally good boosters for any wannabe athlete in this world.
addons.title: Streamer Wars

addons.text: The sport now has an idol element to it, with it now being both a competition as well as a performance. If you are a player, you are expected to do things expected of idol groups, like gathering fans, performing live, and maintaining your celebrity image. Like with the Streamer Wars Add-On, fan support and hate watchers equally boost you in strength and are key to winning games.
addons.title: Be Your Idol

addons.text: Games are now deadlier, with competitors being willing to lie, steal, and cheat to get a win. This is now an accepted part of this sport. Sportsmanship is now pretty much forgotten. In this more dangerous society, you have to be willing to do it all for that coveted reward. Or don't, and hold onto your sense of honor while almost everyone else has let go of theirs. Think Hunger Games, Battle Royale, Squid Game, and other underground 'kill or be killed' sports; that is what you are now facing, should you want to be the very best.
addons.title: 'Tis the Game of Life is Playing All of Us for Fools!

objects.text:
Somehow, a specific sport, whether it be fictional or not, ends up becoming so huge in this world that a lot of conflicts are now resolved through it. As such, this setting's vibes can range from a relatively down-to-earth sports movie to something as wack as Yu-Gi-Oh or early Beyblade. 

In powered settings like Parahumans, abilities are used less for outright violence and instead more for gaining an advantage in this specific sport. The title of champion lends whoever yoinks it a lot of riches and influence.

You can specify which sport it is that is that big deal of a deal, maybe even make up a sport yourself, though who becomes the current top players will be determined not by you but by the setting and characters themselves. For example, Scion could be the reigning champion of the Worm setting, while Gol D. Roger is with One Piece, but those are just possibilities.

Do you have what it takes to reach the top?
objects.title: Life is Ball Game

addons.text:
Urbivores have taken a more literal meaning, as the cities are now indeed alive. Powered by advance Biotechnology, these organic monstrosities now consume other cities to survive. This gives the Urbivores more ways to protect itself without needing the constant piloting of its inhabitants. Now, as a citizen, you are in a symbiotic relationship with your chosen Urbivore. Could you play your part in keeping the city alive?

It is eat or be eaten. Will you be prey, or predator?
addons.title: The City is Alive

addons.text: Eureka's nature as the world's foremost research facility meant the town was always ahead of the curve technologically, when Urbivores started being constructed Eureka followed suit. With the sharing of technology being limited from the new nature of cities the technological gap continued to grow, in time this allowed Eureka to climb to the top of the Urbivore food chain.
addons.title: Apex Urbivore

objects.text:
Social Darwinism's final boss. Due to dwindling resources, several people, cities, and later even countries, ended up building wheels and other forms of transport under their homes in an effort to war against other weaponized "Urbivores" as they were called. These Urbivores capture and dismantle smaller metropolises, damning the citizens inside as either casualties, slaves, or secondary citizens. Choosing this will make your starting location into one of these Urbivores.

If taken with other fictional settings, it would make their main cities these Urbivores too. Think of Brockton Bay from Parahumans being a beast powered by individuals fighting to keep it running, or even entire islands from One Piece becoming aquatic Urbivores that swallow other islands whole. The specifics is up to you.

To gain influence in this setting is to later be able to pilot these Urbivores yourself. Do you have what it takes to rise to the food chain?
objects.title: Municipal Darwinism

objects.text:
NEPEA-5 was a bill passed in the United States aimed at restricting Parahumans' involvement in business and media—at least it was in the canon version of Earth Bet. However, with support from the PRT, NEPEA-5 was never fully realized, and as a result, many events—both good and bad—never came to pass.

Chief among these is the disbanding of the Uppermost, which means their successor organization, the Elite, was never formed. Without the Elite’s formation, the strict recruitment drives and forceful expansion they employed in canon never materialized, but this means they also never provide the level of stability they did in canon.

This also opens up new avenues for capes like Parian, Panacea, and perhaps even Uber and Leet to forge their own paths outside the traditional hero-villain dichotomy. 

Parian might find success as a designer of custom fashion, while Panacea could amass a fortune offering quick, cosmetic “surgeries.” Uber and Leet might become legitimate, legal Cape streamers focusing on video game content. Of course, not every cape will choose these routes, but the absence of NEPEA-5 provides the opportunity for them to take a different path.
objects.title: NEPEA-5? Never Heard of it

objects.text:
Kayfabe? What Kaybfabe?

In this universe, Wrestling is very much real, and they are run with superpowered folks who make these bouts even more entertaining and even more deadly. As such, a lot of the world's conflicts has been settled through said amazing televized matches. Where the world bears witness to huge bouts between monstrous heels and the goodest of faces. It's Hollywood baby!

Despite Wrestling being real however, this is unfortunately, still a business. Staged matches are still a thing, and there were instances where the battles were won through behind the scenes negotiations by managers before a Wrestler's fight even starts. There's an underbelly in this seemingly simple universe. One you may have to end up falling into if you were to make a difference.

The other side effect this modifier has is a lot of heroes and villains take on gimmicks to stand out. Whether it be something simple like being an arrogant asshole as a heel, or by building up an intricate backstory over how you're some undead wizard seeking to bring vengeance against the no good evil guys in the world... You are competing against them. So you better solidify your brand and showcase yourself as worthy of people's fear or adoration.

The bell rings, it's time to fight!
objects.title: WRASSLIN!

objects.text: "In Parkour Civilization, nobody jumps for the beef." The world is basically like a parody of Young Adult Novels and Shonen Battle Mangas. If you pick this, you may get to choose a single Word. Now, your world's society will revolve around this, to the point that a whole class system is formed based on how good you are at said word. Some quick examples would be a Parkour Civilization being based on how good you are at that skill, or a Monster Civilization could be based on gaining more powers to evolve further as a Monster. There is a high chance you will be born at the lower rungs of this new culture, with most of your abilities being sealed at first until you earn a rank up. It becomes a convenient way to slowly train yourself, with you regaining more of your abilities as you rise, maybe even gain more if you reach the very pinnacle. Beware though, this system is rigged against you. Though, maybe with your influence, you can be the very person to finally turn it around?
objects.title: We Live in a(n) [Insert] Civilization

addons.text: Mimics have evolved to not only resemble humans, but other animals and objects as well. Worse yet, within superpowered settings, Mimics have also developed their own abilities. They can now keep up with us puny humans, which shall easily make them more terrifying. <>Hooray for more paranoia!
addons.title: They've Evolved

addons.text: As technological knowledge on biology advanced, so too did our understanding of our mimic brethren. With this, while mimics in the wild are terrifying, we humans have managed to learn of a way to tame them. And soon, mass-produce them. From your fridge to your walls, Mimic products tend to be all the rage now. And as creepy as they may be, they are indeed incredibly useful without too much upkeep.
addons.title: Mass Produced Mimics

addons.text: It turns out, Mimics are a creepypasta-esque viruses that are starting to corrupt the game you are playing, twisting your "gameplay" to be lightly unnerving at first, ending up in a massive psychological warfare campaign aimed straight at you, maybe even potentially causing it to have some sort of terrible effect in your "real" world. Please, deal with this creature; the World is better off without it.
addons.title: Dot Exe

objects.text:
Like that of a typical Analog Horror, the world is now infested by creatures that can mimic us. Their morality is completely alien to us, though we do know they are a threat to humans. As there had been several reported cases of them attacking and potentially feeding on people. Be prepared, for in this world, anybody could be an "Other."

This isn't all gloom and doom, at least. In your setting, people would have naturally developed Anti-Mimic organizations to protect the average citizen. People are also more used to their existence now, able to keep in mind key features that make the mimics less "human", thus preventing more unnecessary casualties.

It is livable, but do prepare to be paranoid.
objects.title: Mimics Rise

objects.text:
Humanity is... Strange, at least according to other beings' opinions. Since first contact, humanity had stuck out like a sore thumb according to these other creatures. Whether it be due to our diets, our tendencies to go to war during conflicts, to survive in what is a "death world" to these other species, to even us finding certain animals that the other beings see as terrifying as instead... Cute, or some other specific reason. Either way, this results in these cultures viewing humans stereotypically as either barbaric brutes or utter weirdos.

Picking this will result in bigger culture clashes or even discrimination on both sides, with some humans seeing this as a reason for humanity's "superiority", while the other race(s) might isolate humans due to their perceived primitiveness. But it isn't something that can't be handled diplomatically, neither is it impossible to gain stronger cultural understandings.
objects.title: Humans? Oh no!

addons.text: This not only guarantees you get a soul mate, it also guarantees that this relationship shall be positive, whether it be friendly, familial, romantic, or anything else. Whichever you choose, you will get along.
addons.title: The Other Halves

addons.text: Fortunately or maybe unfortunately, your relationship with your soul mate shall be filled with fanfictiony tropes. This is due to the author's fic focusing on you. This makes things a little complicated, but once again, the author isn't actively malicious. Just expect for the "plot" to keep going on standstill so the author could give you several moments of fluff or angst with your soul mate(s), basically giving you a little more downtime.
addons.title: Soul Mate AU

addons.text: Each Meister and Weapon are also Soul Mates with one another. This means that strong Soul Resonance is more common, and you gain the same benefits of having a soul mate with your partner(s). The drawback of this however is that losing your partner(s) could be far more devastating than normal, so do keep them close. They are literally your source of strength.
addons.title: Soul Weapon

objects.text: In this world, there is such a thing as Soul Mates. While not necessarily romantic in nature, two or more people tend to be connected in their souls. The nature of this connection shall be determined by you, but one thing is certain. Soul Mates are fated to find each other. A relationship shall form between them all. Whether it be romantic, friends, familial, or even destined enemies. A lot of society shall be based on the existence of these relationships. Not finding your soul mate is the equivalent of not finding a part of your soul. Now, whether or not you believe in this is up to you. But there is a lot of shame directed at those who are deemed unable to find their other halves. That being said, once you enter your chosen world, you will find a soul mate. The nature of your dynamic and how you will find that connection is determined by you. Maybe there is a metaphysical red string connecting you all, or maybe you can communicate via writing on your skin? You may determine that. What cannot be guaranteed, however, is who exactly are the people you form this connection to. Only that it will guarantee that when you do meet up, whatever relationship you shall form shall be intense. Like a brotherhood or a deep-seated rivalry. In this world, nobody is allowed to truly be alone. Is that a good or a bad thing? You decide.
objects.title: Red Strings All Around

objects.text: Whether it is strength, smarts, or something much more specific, the world at large now puts emphasis on a specific skill which dictates your worth as a person. For example, in a world where musical talent is king, you'd see younger folks be forced to train in guitars till their fingers bleed. Or in a world where strength is most important, you'd see less education and more focus on physical training and brutal sports programs. It borders on dystopian, but at the very least you could choose the skill which the world obsesses over. Maybe it could even be something you're particularly good at? Who knows, maybe this could be a benefit to you if you want that?
objects.title: Only The Skilled Shall Rise

objects.text:
With this modifier, It seems life in Earth Bet has been given mercy by the evil of bureaucracy. Through recognition of damage to the public AND even themselves, it seems the Cape scene has changed to be less strict on their more detrimental rules around mid-2004. Rather than force a probationary Ward to wait on stopping any ordinary crime by themselves, the PRT fully allows them to take down the threat without waiting for a superior, although more intense threats do still require them to wait for assistance just by logic.

Of course, this does mean a bit more possible collateral damage at the same time. But due to the lack of needed funds for strict PR, reconstruction costs and Tinker usages have been improved. As well, Tinkers like Kid Win only need to file a single paper's worth of paperwork to use their inventions in public, and people like Vista are more trusted to do the frontline work with the conditions already mentioned.

<small> In another setting, there are similar levels of bureaucratic loosening around organizations or certain jobs.</small>
objects.title: Blue Tape

addons.text:
With corporate benefits for parahuman membership, Parahumans have two ways to go; The high pressure and low benefits life of a corporate cape, in which they’re constantly at risk of being let go with no social safety nets in place to stop their fall, and the way of the majority of parahumans, into the world of the mafioso where the violence may be more explicit but no less casual. 

Furthermore, Corporate ‘hero’ organisations have markedly more to gain from contacts within criminal circles due to their ‘shared interests’. As such, even the legal channels are less than sound options, and even the cleanest of faceses hides rotten dealings beneath.
addons.title: Gangsters in Suit and Tie

addons.text:
Now that parahumans are formally discriminated against, they can barely get any legal work to begin with.

The vast majority of Parahumanity is forced into criminal enterprise in order to survive. The fact that this does create a statistical “proof” of parahuman criminality only increases prejudice against them in an ever growing feedback loop.
addons.title: Underclass

objects.text:
The age of the parahuman brought with it a wave of fear and immediate harsh ‘regulation of disruptive extranormal abilities’. As such, only one aspect of society could really take full advantage of their presence, organised crime. 

Mob culture and cape culture have become conflated and often interchangeable, where cultures of violence and fear are normal and desirable. Favours and leverage are key, and any glamour to be found is in living risky lives outside the law. 

Where legal cape-work was once reliable, now even that is a network of half-measures and loopholes that do little but provide an ‘in name only’ alternative for the unfortunate parahuman population, and very rarely well.
objects.title: Wise Guise

objects.text: Justice like lightning doth appear / to few men's ruin / but all men’s fear A team has appeared in the world, a truly heroic and shining light in the darkness giving hope to all and inspiring awe. Stopping crime, fighting the good fight and ever pursuing good and justice. Obviously it’s all an act. Actually made up of disguised supervillains, this team has an ulterior motive. Whether that be purely financial gain or a secret and clandestine plot for world domination depends largely on the personalities within it.
objects.title: Justice, Like Lightning

objects.text:
War. A term thrown around quite often. Gang War, the Last War, the War for Humanity's Existence, etc. Yet more often than not, these so-called wars are Battles of Champions, small groups or even lone fighters clashing with each other while everyone else runs for cover. Gang wars boil down to the respective parahumans clashing while everyone else does their best to not be in the way. But not here. 

In your world the norms have changed, and the scope of conflict expands. Group-fights are far more common and involve greater numbers, with even the normals getting involved, gang-members taking potshots to give their parahumans an opening, PRT-squads coordinating support for their heroes, and normals of both side clashing with each other to keep the other side off their parahuman's back while the parahumans in turn shield their allies from their counterparts. This doesn't mean that there won't be clashes where one side comes in small numbers, and some groups like the Slaughterhouse 9 or the Endbringers do act without support, but as a general trend fights will lean towards larger numbers and consequently tend to rage for longer until a conclusion is reached. Overall the individual strength of the characters doesn't change, but the numbers scale massively.

This also includes the fight against major antagonists. During Gold Morning for example instead of just leaving the parahumans to their own devices, Scion, in the spiteful tantrum of a petulant child, will use his powers to create armies of cannon-fodder to harass the scattered survivors in every world he devastates in his rampage. If you've chosen an Alternative World the same thing applies, whether it be Goku and Frieza's final fight on Namek happening while Frieza's army attacks the fleeing Namekians or Aizen instead of bringing just three Espada and their Fracción sending out waves of Hollows that are held back by the full might of the Gotei 13, leading to carnage closer to that of Yhwach's Quincy Invasions.
objects.title: War, Not Battle

objects.text: It seems that unlike in your world, dueling is still legal here. Not only that, it is legally and culturally considered a Big Deal™. It is relatively common for people with disagreements big and small to go outside and fistfight in the streets to settle the dispute, with cops not only not interfering but backing the winner of the duel. This only became more common with the advent of Parahumans, such that if people see two Heroes fighting each other they'd sooner assume it was a duel than one of them actually being a Villain or Mastered, and it is relatively common for defendants to request Trial by Combat. That being said, there are rules to dueling beyond 'We fight and the winner is right'. For one, any duel that isn't just a fight for fun must have a legitimate grievance, such as one person accusing the other of a crime or personal slight, someone wanting the right to build something their HOA is vetoing, someone demanding that another stay away from their relative and the person refusing, essentially a fundamental disagreement that cannot be resolved by simple diplomacy or would require a court case to settle. If such a grievance is settled via dueling, then the winner gets to decide the outcome of the disagreement (within reason) and the loser must abide by it or they'll be committing a crime, with only the intervention of a Judge allowing for a rematch if the winner refuses one. Second, unless it's to settle something that would be considered Federal in nature, such as someone demanding Trial by Combat to defend themselves from a murder charge, it cannot be to the death. If it is to the death it must be acknowledged by a Judge first or it counts as murder, though Trial by Combat for any crime punished by life in prison or death is automatically considered approved excepting special circumstances. In addition, if weapons of any kind are involved, it must be in a sanctioned dueling arena, which every location with more than 1000 people is required by law to possess and most cities have a couple dozen of, and overseen by a registered referee who will intervene if necessary. Third, the fights must be considered by both parties to be fair, with Champions allowed if there is a gross mismatch between fighters, such as one being in a wheelchair and the other isn't, if one party is too young or old to realistically stand a chance, or if one has Powers that are much stronger than the other's. Champions can be either a friend, a family member, or a professionally licensed Champion, such as those hired by corporations to settle disputes or by courts to settle Trials by Combat for criminal cases, or who volunteer for their own reasons. Fourth, for Parahumans, only people without Kill Orders can demand Trial by Combat or even legally duel in general. There are also rules concerning certain types of powers, for example a Master cannot just force someone to surrender in a duel, as that is considered cheating and the Master is considered to have immediately lost and must either release their opponent from their control or be arrested. These subrules for people with powers can be different depending on which country, state, or even city you are in, and are typically influenced by culture and local precedent. Fifth, any duel that isn't Trial by Combat, therefore any duel that is purely a civil matter, must be consented to by the challenged party for it to be binding. This means you can't challenge someone to a duel for every little thing and expect to get away with it, though culturally speaking rejecting a duel over a serious matter is heavily frowned upon unless the challenger is being an asshole or is considered way out of the challenged parties league such as a major CEO challenging a girl scout for scuffing his shoes. Forcing one anyway is considered even more unacceptable and is a great way to get a really strong Champion to volunteer and curbstomp you. Beyond these there may be many extra rules official and unofficial depending on various factors like the nature of the dispute that led to the duel, local culture and customs, current government policy and whatever forces hold the most sway legally and illegally, and more, but this is the basic outline that pretty much every nation of note beyond the worst Dictatorships or most backwards failed states follow, and is extremely unlikely to change anytime in the near future. Note: This obviously means humanity as a whole is closer to a warrior culture than it was before, although other means of settling disputes like negotiation and courts are still popular options. This just makes it socially and legally acceptable to punch people in the face if you really want to. Surprisingly duels being legal actually shifts the Hero / Villain ratio slightly more towards Heroes or Rogues compared to canon by at least a few percent, almost as if having a legal outlet for conflict helps stabilize certain individuals. For example, Hookwolf in this world might be a legally acknowledged Champion who gets into professional cage fights to settle disputes.
objects.title: It's Time to Duel

objects.text:
Life imprisonment is considered wasteful.

In this setting, those sentenced to permanent incarceration are diverted into state-sanctioned blood sports. The reasoning is straightforward: if someone has forfeited their life, it will be put to use.

The flagship event is the NecrOlimpics. Participants are medically stabilized and then pushed past normal human limits. Experimental performance enhancers, combat stimulants, gene therapies, neural accelerants — substances banned everywhere else — are administered in controlled escalation. The focus is simple: measure output, survivability, and how long a body can keep functioning under strain.

Other events are more direct.

Deadly races feature armored vehicles fitted with mounted weaponry. Tracks are seeded with mines, spike fields, collapsing bridges, automated turrets, and shifting hazards. Sabotage between drivers is expected. Finishing the course matters more than surviving it.

There are urban hunt formats set in abandoned districts rigged with traps and roaming threats. Endurance gauntlets built around pain tolerance and stress thresholds. Arena matches with uneven tools and changing conditions.

What these games are not is slow.

Prolonged starvation scenarios were tried and dropped. Audiences preferred speed and escalation. If someone is going to die, it happens decisively.
objects.title: Mortal Games

objects.text: Each purchase of this shifts the ratio of villains to heroes more in favor of villains. Going by canon values, the first purchase changes it from 2:1, that is two villains for every one hero, to 3:1, the second from 3:1 to 4:1, and so on. This caps out at eight purchases, for a 10:1 ratio, essentially making this a world where the villains 'won', if you can call constant conflict between gangs of villains vying for dominance while the government tries its best to survive by any means necessary 'winning'. Each purchase worsens the situation on Earth Bet, as with more villains and less heroes, people begin to become more untrusting and afraid of parahumans in general. At eight purchases, parahumans would be nearly as hated as Divided makes them, though without any guaranteed ability to fight back meaningfully against them. Hero groups become more and more stretched thin, being outright underdogs acting as an underground resistance in a world where the ratio is 10:1, being forced to be more ruthless in their attempts to protect people from the predations of villainous organizations, and much more secretive, as any attempts at having a publicly known base of operations is just asking to get attacked by at least three separate gangs at once. Though villains haven't technically taken over the world even at eight purchases, the world is teetering on the brink, no one having successfully conquered the USA solely because they are so busy fighting each other that no one group can devote enough forces to make the attempt, and it's only a matter of time. Note: This is the new base ratio as far as any other modifiers that affect the villain to hero ratio are concerned. For instance, at three purchases Vikare Resilient would make it go from 5:1 to 4.25:1 instead of from 2:1 to 1.5:1.
objects.title: More Villains

objects.text: Each purchase of this shifts the ratio of villains to heroes more in favor of heroes. Going by canon values, the first purchase changes it from 2:1, that is two villains for every one hero, to 1.5:1, the second from 1.5:1 to 1:1, the third 1:1 to 1:1.5, and so on. This caps out at eight purchases, for a 1:4 ratio, essentially making this a world where the heroes have 'won', with most villains either small-time crooks or put away behind bars quickly after their debuts. Each purchase betters the situation on Earth Bet, as with more heroes and less villains, people begin to become more trusting and accepting of parahumans in general. At eight purchases, the world would be nearly good as A Brighter World, albeit with no guarantee that the Entity could be convinced to spare humanity with a speech. Hero groups become more and more common, as villains either settle for simple petty crime or are people who need help, being more likely to receive it and become rehabilitated the more things tilt in the heroes favor. Only the worst, most unredeemable villains end up actually getting put in supermax facilities, and they become ever rarer as heroes become more common. As heroes become more common and fights against villains become rarer in comparison, heroes begin to diversify and specialize. Disaster relief, simple police actions, search and rescue, providing international aid in poorer nations, and even working on villain rehabilitation become more common career paths for professional heroes in the absence of large villain organizations. Note: This is the new base ratio as far as any other modifiers that affect the villain to hero ratio are concerned. For instance, at three purchases Vikare Resilient would make it go from 1:1.5 to 1:2 instead of from 2:1 to 1.5:1.
objects.title: More Heroes

objects.text:
The attitude, belief structure, and technology of the age become far more realistic in the world you travel to. 

If the setting is ostensibly medieval, you will find a society that genuinely operates like a real medieval society rather than a romanticised or simplified version, meaning you will not encounter technology that did not exist during that period, the fundamental principles and limitations of that age are stronger and more consistently applied, and the general style of architecture, clothing, warfare, and daily life adheres to authentic historical realism.
objects.title: Accurate Ages

objects.text:
The United States as a country does not exist. Instead of the 50 States (plus several territories) being united into a single nation, they are instead independent countries with their own laws, customs, and possibly even languages. You may decide precisely how this came to be and when. Perhaps during the Revolution the rebels couldn't get enough public support to unite as one nation and instead chose to split up after the war, or the Civil War ended up highlighting many fundamental issues that caused the States to choose to split up after the dust settled, or maybe some Thinker revealed so many dirty secrets that the federal government was overthrown in a rebellion and the union abolished, who knows.

You may decide the exact history, cultures, and relationships of the resulting nations within certain limits set by the number of purchases. The first purchase ensures that the resulting nations are mostly friendly to one another with at worst some minor tensions between certain nations. They still have a universal language or at least trade language in addition to their primary language (such as Spanish, French, or any number of Native American languages); they have a roughly similar average level of freedoms and rights as they did in canon though some may be more or less restrictive; and they may in fact be in a continent wide alliance similar to the EU allowing relatively free travel, immigration, and a near universal currency which may or may not include Mexico and Canada.

The second purchase makes them on average neutral leaning towards being friendly to one another. Some may be in close alliances with other nations, but no alliance is universal, with some nations having more tense relations with neighbors. Cultures and laws vary much more here as there is no great incentive to homogenize, but there is no real risk of major wars breaking out. Immigration across the continent is considered normal but no pressure exists to streamline it, and currencies vary but may be exchanged freely between nations.

The third purchase makes them on average neutral leaning towards being hostile to one another. Some may be in alliances with one or two other nations, but overall relations are generally very tense between nations, with some even engaging in small scale military conflicts with their neighbors. Immigration still exists but is restricted, with immigrants frequently monitored in case they are spying for their original nation. Cultures vary greatly and there is little common ground between fellow nations.

The fourth purchase makes them on average hostile towards each other, at best some nations having a mutual truce not to attack one another while they focus on closer threats. Essentially think of the near constant conflict of the Middle East or certain parts of Africa and Asia as being the baseline for North America, as alliances are constantly forged, broken, and reforged as nations constantly fight one another. Immigration ranges from rare to non-existent, tensions are high, war crimes are a constant in life, and the only thing stopping nukes or similarly destructive power wielders from being used is M.A.D. being in effect.

You may also choose how this modifier alters certain powerful American organizations from canon. For instance, in Worm the PRT and Protectorate may range from an internationally sponsored Parahuman oversight group at one purchase, to an international organization dedicated to trying to keep tensions down and prevent wars with two to three purchases, to a loose alliance of people desperately trying and probably failing to get everyone to focus on combatting Endbringers and other S-Class threats rather than each other as their branches are pressured by their host nation to provide assistance in acting against one another.
objects.title: Divided States of America

objects.text:
What makes a villain? The simple answer is that they're the bad guy, but how many people truly think of themselves as bad? Most Gangs have some form of ideology behind them that justifies their actions, even if those in charge don't actually believe in it. Well, now they do.

Ideology is no longer just an excuse for thugs to hide behind as they enrich themselves, but in fact a creed that most villains actually believe in and strive to adhere to. This doesn't necessarily make the villains good people, but it does make them principled. 

The E88 actually views the American Way of Life as threatened on all fronts, operating under something of a siege-mentality to protect the way things used to be, and the way things in their view should be. Consequently they hold themselves to higher standards and will leave violence against minorities either to deniable low-level members who can be written off as well-meaning but overzealous in their actions, or restrict it to those they can parade as guilty of actual crimes against "real" Americans. 

Lung genuinely sees the Asian population of Brockton Bay as threatened, both by the hatred of the E88 as well as the seeming disregard of the proper authorities, and so he steps forward to shelter his people under the mantle of his personal power.

Even the Merchants now have something akin to a philosophy, albeit one of accepting nihilism, that the world's gone to shit and is not going to get better, so why not at least make it more tolerable and colorful with drugs?

They will still partake in various types of crime, but much like the Mob they generally view it as a form of doing business. Drug-trafficking is just fulfilling a public demand, and the gangs do in fact act to ensure the quality of their product.

Protection money is now in most cases not just extortion, but genuinely does obligate the recipients to protect the business in question, as those taking it view it not as blackmail, but a form of legitimate if not legal business.

Violence is an unfortunate necessity of business, to be directed mainly outwards against those encroaching on one's territory or threatening the people under the gang's protection, and if it has to be turned inward to deal with spies and informants, then that is genuinely unfortunate and to be mourned, though it must be done.

In general it can be said that most, though not all, villains do believe themselves to be doing the right thing, or at worst being forced by circumstance to do the wrong thing for the right reason. That said, just because most villains now follow a creed does not mean they will not do terrible things, only that they believe they have genuine reason to do terrible things. Both Survival of the Fittest and Might Makes Right are after all valid creeds in their own right.

One clear benefit that has come of most villains now having principles is that it has led to a notable participation-increase in Endbringer-fights, as a lot more villains are now willing to put their money where their mouth is, so to speak.

And of course there are still genuine monsters like the Slaughterhouse 9, who follow no creed other than wanting to watch the world burn.
objects.title: Villainy is a Question of Perspective

addons.text:
The increased effectiveness of the PRT allows them to run a much tighter ship. The PR-campaigns they run are more effective, and they're generally able to keep the Protectorate's parahumans on a tight leash, the mandatory lectures Protectorate-members must regularly attend are by and large successful in hammering how to behave in public to avoid scandal into their heads. Which generally also serves to make the heroes more effective in the field, as humiliating defeats against villains would be another form of scandal to be avoided if at all possible.

On the flipside however, the PRT has also become somewhat more callous towards civilians, generally valuing the preservation of the Protectorate's image above all else. This doesn't mean Protectorate heroes or Wards are exempt from reprimand or even harsh punishments, only that such things are generally kept in-house to avoid any public backlash.

Though the more selfish nature of most Heroes does mean that, while able to present a near flawless facade in public, many of them chafe under the stringent watch of the PRT and seek out ways to cause annoyances and small-scale problems for the PRT to clean up after that are minor enough to not get them into too much trouble.

This fairly widespread method of indirect protest has led to misbehavior in a hero's civilian identity generally being given significant leeway, seen as a way for the parahumans to de-stress without causing PR-disasters. So long as a parahuman's actions in their private life can't be connected to their Cape-identity, do not negatively impact their professional behavior, and do cross certain lines and become a problem in itself, the PRT will generally turn a blind eye to it, prioritizing the mental health of their parahumans even to the occasional detriment of regular civilians so long as things do not get out of hand.

Bluntly spoken, Sophia's regular bullying of Taylor would be considered unpleasant but ultimately harmless and therefore tolerable behavior, while The Locker would be considered going too far and require intervention.

In such cases the PRT isn't entirely heartless and more than willing to lead with the carrot, being very generous with compensation and enacting punishment on the culprit so long as the matter is kept under wraps. Should the victim however insist on trying to move things public despite offers and warnings, then the PRT will act with ruthless efficiency to preserve the good name of its heroes, even if this leaves the victim socially and financially ruined.

Additionally the PRT, in part because they're very good at handling actual threats, may occasionally resort to less savory measures if they feel they need a PR-win in order to remind the public why the Protectorate is needed.

This can range from the extremely common practice of over-inflating the threat-level of villains, especially those they feel confident they'll be able to handle easily, over letting villains deemed overall harmless remain at large as manageable threats, all the way to the occasional false flag-operation, finding a new, unknown parahuman of suitable character who was willing to join them and instead having them take the role of villain for a few weeks to months before they are "captured" and turned into a redemption-story, both for the masses and to encourage actual villains to take this route.

The PRT is extremely effective at keeping the public safe. However, perhaps corrupted by the selfishness of the heroes they manage, it has also become extremely effective at promoting the necessity of its own existence, and protecting the sterling reputation of Heroism. No matter the cost.
addons.title: Ruthless PRT

objects.text:
There are many reasons why a parahuman may choose to join the ranks from the Protectorate or be an independent hero, from the noble to the selfish. This can range from patriotism or belief in justice over the simple need for a paycheck all the way down to those joining out of a craving for glory or authority and even those who were forced into it by circumstance or the prospect of prison. In your world however, the selfish ones now make up the overwhelming majority.

Oh, there are still the idealists, those who become heroes because they want to help or felt it was the proper thing to do, but most parahumans are very much in it for themselves. This doesn't necessarily make them all evil, wanting a good paycheck or to be adored by the public is hardly a crime, but it does however make most of them a lot more selfish and prone to giving in to their vices so long as the cameras or crowds are not there to see. Credit-stealing and subtle acts of sabotage become far more widespread between heroes, as well as reckless behavior in hopes of being seen as the one that  took care of the problem.

This selfishness also reflects back on their private lives, with many heroes being prone to arrogance and entitled behavior out of costume. Others may try to live rockstar-esque lives with their rather generous salaries. Never meet your heroes is now very good advice.

Surprisingly, the attendance at Endbringer-fight has only dropped slightly, as those who decline to attend any not happening in or close to their cities out of fear for their personal safety are mostly but not entirely compensated for by the gloryhounds.

The PRT is now even more occupied with PR-work, making their heroes look like paragons of righteousness, which due to the nature of most of their subjects being rather fallible regularly involves varying degrees of damage control. They're also more invested in merchandising, both to acquire more funding as well as spreading their heroes as household names and equating them with trustworthiness in the public conscience.
objects.title: Heroism is PR-Work

addons.text: There is now two specific subspecies of humans that exists in your world. One where the strong is favored, a culture of strength above all things. And another where logic is king, a culture of progress and science above all else. These two cultures, while not outright hostile to one another, tend to clash.
