Their ideologies hugely different from one another to the point that fighting isn't something too uncommon for these two types of humans. You can pick whether you fall into the strong or the smarts, or neither if you aren't human or if you're one of the more vanilla esque humans of our universe.
addons.title: Brute and Brains

objects.text:
Fortune favors the rational.

There is a subtle shift in human culture which lead to the favoring of logic above all else. Education became more of a genuine focus among all nations, scientific advancements reached an all time high, and it almost seemed like we're in a new age of enlightenment. As the unnecessary things such as emotions and irrationality is stamped out, things have only seemed to be more peaceful, fostering an era of cooperation and friendly competition, raising humanity in our next step of evolution.

Or so that would seem.

See, emotions aren't just lost, they were stamped out, repressed due to how it supposedly go against the doctrine that logic is superior. People are raised to act more like unfeeling machines for the greater good of all. This is, of course, a bad thing considering how incredibly unhealthy it is. This complete focus on rationality also might seem hypocritical as we are still human overall, and one cannot fully lose the irrational sides that we have which is always a part of us. For all the glitz and glamour this supposed utopia had raised, lies an underbelly of abuse which forced this world into the path it is now taking. Not to mention the unhealthy emphasis on IQ over EQ leading to discrimination on folks unable to keep up.

Maybe you will thrive in this world? Maybe you will not? In terms of Worm, Thinkers and Tinkers are especially beloved in this universe, so maybe that can be incentive to try this out?
objects.title: Rational Earth

objects.text: In every society, there are a set of rules, social customs, and battle etiquette that people are expected to follow if for no other reason than that not doing so leads to endless escalation, loss of life, and eventual anarchy. Whether it is something mundane like a code of chivalry, anti-corruption laws, or the Geneva Convention, or perhaps something that applies to empowered individuals like the Unwritten Rules of Worm, these rules are meant to keep conflicts constrained and prevent certain abuses of power from being done by everybody, whether formally written into law or not. However, such rules only function as well as they are enforced by others. If the person breaking them is strong enough, rich enough, has enough political or monetary influence, or if enough people have simply stopped caring, then even the most flagrant and despicable breaches of these rules can go unpunished. At least, that would be the case if not for the existence of someone strong enough to force everybody to follow them. And now that person exists. In your chosen setting there now exists an Enforcer who sits head and shoulders above everybody else. If you are in a setting where the strongest person is street tier, then they would be country tier. If you have individuals capable of cracking planets running around, then they can shatter galaxies. Whatever the case, they are undoubtedly the strongest person in the setting, with at best plot device or cosmic level beings such as Entities or Paragons sitting a single step below them. However, rather than act out to warp the setting in any number of ways whether to initiate world peace, conquer the planet, or destroy everything, the only thing they care about is enforcing a set of rules meant to keep things ‘tame’. What these rules are precisely is up to you, though they must have some basis to go off of, such as a variation of the Unwritten Rules or something like that, and they can’t favor you in any specific way (so no, ‘this guy is the ruler of the world now’ isn’t a viable rule), but otherwise can be as simple and straightforward or as complex and multilayered as you wish. Common rules include limiting the scale of fights to prevent collateral damage, preventing specific heinous crimes like rape or blatant corruption, forcing people to respect civilian identities, and more things along those lines. Everyone in the setting will know what these rules are, whether having discovered them through trial and error, having had a telepathic broadcast lay them out to the world, or through a website created by the Enforcer that details them. Anyone who breaks the rules and isn’t punished for it by others will be punished by this Enforcer relative to how badly they were breached, whether it was intentional or not, and the consequences of said breach. To use an example, if one rule is that ‘civilian identities must be respected’, then accidentally saying a parahuman’s real name out in the open but no one makes the connection could result in a headache and a sense of ‘being on thin ice’. Meanwhile, if a gang broke into a parahuman’s house while they slept, kidnapped them, publicly revealed their identity, then killed them before placing a bounty on their next of kin, then the next day the entire gang could find itself dead along with its backers, everyone who was working for them, and even any and every paid off police officer or government official no matter how strong they were. Certain beings may have different levels of enforcement or rules attached to them though, so a street tier parahuman might have different rules to follow than an Endbringer would, and an Entity could have a third set of rules, set by their power levels, roles in cape society, and more. This might mean that your average parahuman can’t kill a city, but an Endbringer would be allowed to once per year for example. Certain particularly powerful beings like an Entity could get away with a blatant rule break for a time before being sufficiently punished, so Scion could set off Gold Morning, and while he would eventually be stopped dozens of worlds would still die. You may choose the exact nature of this Enforcer and their powers, such as a reality warping superhuman, an infinite power copier, a god of order, an alien lifeform that wants the world to continue existing no matter what, a divine computer buried in the planet’s core, or something stanger. Whatever the case, outside of this duty, the Enforcer is rather hands off in influencing the world, allowing people to do their own thing and self govern as they please as long as no rules are broken, for better and for worse. If certain particularly powerful beings even by cosmic standards exist such as a universe creating deity as per The Creator, then the Enforcer may or may not be aware of and have at least a tacit understanding or arrangement with said being(s). Whether they are their equal, lesser, or superior is a different story. Note: Yes, you are also bound by these rules too, and you will be weaker than the Enforcer no matter your powers. So if you’re dead set on doing something specific, don’t make one of the rules ban that activity unless you want to get sent to the pain dimension or something.
objects.title: Unwritten Rules, More Like Unbreakable Laws

objects.text:
With this modifier there will be an increase in people's desire to be or do more, which will lead some of them to begin acting as Superheroes or Supervillains; those who do follow these paths do gain a notable increase in their luck and abilities. For example, a teenager could go on to bring down an established crime family that rules New York's underworld, while another could kidnap a mayor for ransom and get away with it.

This scales differently with each world, as different sources of power and circumstances can determine the kind of heroes and villains that will appear, but whatever the scale, they will have an impact on the world.
objects.title: Desire for the Mask

objects.text:
In this world, instead of having the Protectorate focus on PR and ‘playing ball’ with villains, Cauldron has chosen to take a more hands on and ruthless approach to parahumans. Cauldron is now integrated into the Protectorate as a black ops program with the full support of the US government. The inner circle each have official governmental positions, such as Doctor Mother (now with actual PhDs) as head of research, and one of their number whether old or new is President (for life) of the United States.

Whenever someone triggers in the USA, which between Contessa, Number Man, Clairvoyant, and the Think Tank, the Protectorate almost always know when one happens and where within a matter of days, they are given one of three options: a) join the Protectorate or Wards, b) don’t use their powers, or c) get kidnapped, dragged to a black site, and have their personality rewritten by The Slug so they are a loyal American citizen willing to do anything for their country. The Case 53 and Nemesis programs were similarly scrapped in favor of turning any viable deviants into loyal soldiers.

Across the country, Thinker created propaganda is used to mould the masses in ways beneficial to Cauldron’s goals. Tinkers are used as strategic assets to outfit special forces, create high-tech facilities, and more. Other parahumans are given official ranks in the military as the Protectorate itself is militarized, with ‘home teams’ that protect against domestic threats and ‘away teams’ deployed internationally. Some people are recruited for ‘classified power development programs’, whether exemplary members of the armed forces given reliable vials, or desperate people under threat by crippling debt, terminal illness, or prison used to continue testing of new strains, before being recruited into the Protectorate.

As for international relations, the USA now has a very strong ‘with us or against us’ policy. They proclaim themselves the only ones who can save the world from the threat of rogue villains and S-Class Threats, and will fight anyone who refuses to bow to them. Mexico and Canada have been integrated into the US as new States, whether by negotiation, invasion, or strategic bribery, blackmail, and straight up Mastering. Other nations are being outright invaded for the purpose of integration, since Cauldron has decided that a world ruled by one nation under their control is best able to fight off an Entity, and the other nations will either get with the program or become strong enough opponents to be useful against it when the day comes.

Not all is going to plan though. Various groups resist their control one way or another, such as the Elite who on the surface are simply a group of lobbyists and business savvy Thinkers and Tinkers who toe the line in public but in private have used blackmail and threats of M.A.D. to get Cauldron to let them be, or various members of the Protectorate and Wards who hate the direction the country is going and wish to resist the increasingly militant and fascist takeover. Others outright fight back, from various resistance groups who through one way or another have survived Cauldron’s ire, with some more radical than others, to terrorist groups like Teacher’s Pets or the Slaughterhouse who either want to rule the nation themselves or wish to burn everything down.

Essentially, Cauldron has turned America into the CUI with them as the Yangban, but likely much worse in a number of ways, with all the problems that entails. If you have powers, your only options are to toe the line or fight with everything you have, because Cauldron refuses to take no for an answer. Good luck.
objects.title: The Eye of Providence

objects.text:
They say your online following is your life, but here, it is taken to the extreme. In this dystopia, your life is tied to a specific social media of your choice's follower count, literally. Not only is there insane hyper competition for the spotlight, but also, the quality of your life dramatically raises the more internet famous you are. Successful influencers are actually given more rights, such as higher income and better necessities compared to the nobodies beneath them. People with low follower counts are left in squalor, treated as subhuman trash, which isn't even the worse part. The worse part is what happens after the follower count hits zero.

When that happens, the person who lost their followers will immediately die. How they die tends to be random but instantaneous. This is at least normally prevented through maintaining a followerbase of your closest friends and family, but this tends to not last as followings from deceased people's accounts do not count. So if all your followers are dead... Then you're effectively doomed.

This world is messed up, but how it came to be like this as well as the specific mechanics is determined by you. Is the world doomed, or is there anything that can be done to this wretched place?
objects.title: The Social Reckoning

objects.text:
In this world, a specific career has taken over as the most sought after, even more than any other career. Think of how Pro Hero Work is in My Hero Academia, or Racing for Umas in Uma Musume. For some reason, there was just so much high prestige for this particular career to the point that those few who do make it become celebrities in their own right, comparable even to movie stars and viral sensations. Not to mention the fame and riches, making competition fiercer than ever, ESPECIALLY in powered settings (Doubly so in the Parahumans setting, where NEPEA-5 might've been slightly modified or even entirely non-existent, and parahumans are more encouraged to take on less cape activity. Instead, pursuing jobs related to the career path you've picked).

The why in regards to the origin of this societal shift, as well as the how in regards to how this affects society at large is of course, up to you. There could be stuff like the appearance of many specialized schools for this particular career, worldwide events and competitions pertaining to whatever this career is, or even certain jobs becoming obsolete due to being overshadowed by this specific profession that almost everyone seems to be obsessed with. This modifier could definitely cause a massive shift in your world's culture, or barely a change at all, besides the fact that more people may end up knowing the names of famous janitors than there are celebrity chefs for example. That is up to you.
objects.title: Careerland

addons.title: Fandoms
addons.text: "Madness, Jerry. It's all madness." Cults now only rarely form around ideals, movements, or distant gods. No, their gods are now more... real. Closer. And it has driven the cults to greater heights and strengths. There is a new name for these cultists: Fans. Cults, or Fandoms, are now more unhinged. Gaining further power and supernatural abilities in the worship of their idols- often mimicking the abilities and appearances of said idols- and waging wars against other Fandoms and in the name of their gods and beloved ships. There is minimal to no subtlety here. The few who do not dedicate themselves to a fandom live in constant fear of forced recruitment, brainwashing or targetting. Forever watching their words lest a random comment or opinion set off a mob that'll tear them limb from limb. Meanwhile, the governments keep a careful balance of managing such idols from the shadows, all so as to not usher in chaos that would tear the world asunder. As a side effect, totalitarian dictators are now idols of significant power. Whether this changes their aesthetics or not is up to author fiat.

objects.text:
Whether it be from Scion possibly presenting himself as some sort of manager, or maybe he landed on either Japan or South Korea or any other Asian country with a thriving pop idol industry, whatever the case may be, this world's capes have taken on a more entertainment focused style.  One that is more glittery, more appealing, and most of all, more marketable.

The capes of this setting, particularly heroes, now double as idols. One has to be able to sing, dance, and perform to a group of loyal fans if one is to make it as a successful hero. So the Wards for example would end up also as an idol training program while larger hero teams form idol groups whom stop crime just as equally as they grow a brand based on their persona. This isn't limited to heroes too, with villains being the rebellious alternatives, taking on more hardcore and heavy aesthetics that might not be considered appropriate for the squeaky clean idol scene of professional heroism.

This world might seem more light and colorful, but knowing how cruel the idol industry could be in the real world, it shouldn't be a surprise that there is a lot of darkness hidden just underneath the surface. The pressure of both the weight of your persona as well as people's legion of followers might be too much for some. Would you survive in this industry?
objects.title: Be Our Idol

objects.text: Whatever drugs were like before, they're much more extreme now. In a world with mostly mundane drugs there'll be drugs that essentially give low-level superpowers, such as super-speed, absurd hysterical strength, or incredible muscular growth, with comparably extreme side effects. In this world, cocaine is probably a prescription medication.
objects.title: Drugs Are Really Bad

objects.text:
The societal, economical and political elites are no longer the degenerate parasites who hoard wealth and power they are in the original timeline. 

They are now instead genuinely good people who are working to make life better for everyone.

While they may differ in ideology and nationality, their true goal will always be the betterment of humanity.
objects.title: Good Elites

objects.text:
People in your world fight much differently from how they usually would. Exactly how it is different is up to you. You can choose exactly which weapons, styles, tactics and strategies are used to fight in your world. This can be samurai viewing the macahuitl as the most honorable weapon, space troopers wrasslin' aliens, medieval knights moving like modern special forces operators with crossbows, or Shaolin Monks honing discipline through the art of rocket launchers.

The logic and technology of the universe will shift just enough to allow your changes to work, though this will not change why people fight or the effect it has on the world. You may also selectively choose how this affects different eras, factions and characters, though it will not change the balance of power.
objects.title: Alternate Artstyle of War

objects.text:
With the rise of parahumans and the devastation they brought, the nations of the world came together behind a single answer: containment.

Rather than allowing parahumans to integrate freely into broader society, governments and major institutions established vast quarantined metropolitan zones, commonly known as Prison Cities. 

Any person identified as a parahuman, whether through public trigger, confirmed ability manifestation, or state screening, is apprehended by the PRT and relocated to one of these enclosed urban territories.

Parahumans are considerably more common in this world than they otherwise would have been, with the Cycle producing hosts at a far greater rate across the population. In addition, every child of a parahuman is guaranteed to eventually become a parahuman themselves, often manifesting their powers at a young age.

By law most countries require testing of the Corona Pollentia every year as part of a yearly checkup, with warrants for capture and testing issued if one misses it for too long, with the PRT hunting them down. Children of known parahumans are monitored particularly closely due to the certainty that they will eventually develop powers.

These cities are not death camps, nor are they mere holding pens. They are complete societies unto themselves, containing housing, markets, schools, hospitals, factories, entertainment districts, internal governments, criminal networks, and carefully managed industries. Their populations consist almost entirely of parahumans, along with select guards, administrators, contractors, and support staff who permanently reside within the walls.

Each city is sealed, heavily monitored, and extraordinarily difficult to escape. Many are enclosed overhead, partitioned into districts and blocks, and shaped to resist breakout attempts, mass unrest, and power abuse. Travel between cities is rare and tightly regulated. Travel to the outside world is a privilege granted only to trusted assets, indispensable specialists, and state-approved operatives.

The major power behind the scenes keeping the otherwise powered population that could break out under heel being no other than Cauldron itself, carefully controlling and monitoring the Parahumans inside. 

Publicly, this system is justified as a humanitarian compromise. Parahumans are kept away from the fearful general population, while also being housed among others like themselves. In practice, it is a global caste system enforced at gunpoint.

Inside these cities, power determines comfort. Reputation determines opportunity. Compliance determines survival.

One of the most famous institutions within the Prison Cities is the Coliseum Circuit: organized combat spectacles in which parahumans volunteer or are pressured into participating for wealth, privileges, celebrity, reduced restrictions, better housing, sponsor patronage, and political favor. 

Matches range from duels, team battles, and tactical war games to staged monster hunts, live scenario puzzles, and mock invasions. Some events pit capes against engineered beasts, rogue constructs, or parahuman-made horrors. Others take the form of strategic contests such as naval warfare, territory capture, urban survival games, or coordinated defense exercises.

These broadcasts are wildly popular in the outside world. Star fighters become household names. Fans send gifts, money, luxuries, and sponsorship packages into the cities. Entire local economies rise around famous capes, teams, handlers, betting rings, and arena politics.

Millions of parahumans are spread across a relatively small number of these cities. Some become laborers, gang leaders, civil officials, contractors, entertainers, researchers, or soldiers. Others gain exceptional privileges by cooperating with the authorities, the city administrations, or Cauldron itself.

Capable Movers, Thinkers, Tinkers, healers, and rare utility capes may be granted special contracts, off-site work details, better living conditions, or semi-free status in exchange for service. 

Many heroes and villains who would once have operated conventionally instead work as arena stars, city enforcers, contractors, gang leaders, or privileged state assets.

Cauldron had a hand in designing and supporting this system from the beginning. To them, concentrating parahumans into a small number of controlled zones made observation easier, recruitment simpler, experimentation safer, and long-term preparation more efficient.

The Triumvirate serve as the public heads of the foremost Prison Cities, each ruling over one of the largest and most influential contained populations. Beneath them, each city is divided into smaller sectors, blocks, or wards with their own power structures and local authorities.

In this continuity, Eidolon is aware of and controls the Endbringers. Eidolon knowingly commands the Endbringers in this continuity, deploying them as controlled large-scale Coliseum events every three months. These battles serve publicly as terrifying spectacles and privately as training for the eventual war against Scion.

Publicly, Endbringer appearances are framed as catastrophic but managed special events: apocalyptic-scale Coliseum spectacles held once every three months. The damage is controlled, the casualty rate far lower than in canon, and the participating parahumans unknowingly serve as combat drills for the true purpose behind the system: preparing Eidolon, key assets, and humanity’s strongest capes for the eventual war against Scion.

Because the prison system aggressively identifies and contains parahumans, and because Cauldron has quietly fostered broader parahuman proliferation, there are far more capes in the world than in canon. 

The old Protectorate still exists in spirit, but its members are less traditional superheroes and more state-sanctioned elite assets, arena icons, city enforcers, and privileged trustees of the prison order.

Likewise, villains are not absent. They simply take different shapes. Gangs, warlords, black-market brokers, corrupt block bosses, contraband rings, cults, rogue breeders of parahuman beasts, and arena fixers flourish inside the walls. 

Many conflicts that would once have spilled across a city instead become internal struggles over districts, contracts, prestige, sponsorship, and controlled violence. 

Heroism still exists here.

It just exists in a cage.
objects.title: Panopticon Cities
Motorbike Jousting
objects.text: Long live chivalry. Knights are now a ubiquitous feature of this reality, no matter the setting. Stronger. Faster. Well educated, and more often noble and honorable than not. Paragons of whatever species they are a part of, dispensing justice, slaying evil, and uplifting the innocent. The reason for their existence may vary. Mayhaps in a modern setting they are the result of several noble heads who refused to lay down their arms and fade into history choosing instead to pour their wealth into advanced material and medical sciences, and the breakdown and rebuilding of armed combat from the fundamentals. Eventually, developing into Orders of supersoldier-level humans that do not fall under any particular military or government, wielding advanced exo-suits and technology with bodies exceeding the human norm and minds honed in politics, engineering, psychology and combat. Their horses now replaced by all-terrain motorbikes and arms now ranging from cannon-lances to guns to energetic melee weapons and shields. Whatever the shape they take, their presence leads to a more stable world. Knights holding up virtues and honor irrespective of government wishes, dethroning despots and slaying bandits. Their Orders will exist mostly separate from political institutions, wielding small but unignorable political power and a deep faith from the populace. These orders also stabilize revolutions, preventing them from descending into chaos when an Order puts their weight behind them. That is not to say these Knights and Orders are uncorruptable. But such corruption is rare, and almost never complete. Governments have and will try to create Knights completely loyal to them as part of their own militaries, but will always face difficulties truly matching up.

rows.title: Social, Cultural & Political Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that change the Social, Cultural, and/or Political dynamics of a setting

objects.text:
Whatever world you are heading to now has its own subspace/hyperspace acting as an extra dimension of space that follows different physical laws from the normal 4 dimensions of our reality. This can allow things that are normally impossible in regular space, for example a form of Faster-Than-Light travel using subspace/hyperspace as an extra-dimensional shortcut is one of the most obvious examples.

You could also have Subspace and Hyperspace be their own separate dimensions. Typically subspace will only allow data transmissions, but will carry them almost instantaneously. Hyperspace however will be slower, but will at least temporarily allow matter (spaceships) to travel through it. 

You can decide which version of subspace or hyperspace this manifests as or it could be your own completely original creation. Examples include, but are not limited to: Star Wars, Star Trek, Stargate, Babylon 5 and Halo just to name a few.
objects.title: Higher-Dimensional Spaces

objects.text: For each selection of this choice, you may select one Specific Companion Modifier and choose to have its effects applied to the version of the character native to this world without them becoming your companion. If they aren't native to your chosen setting, or any of its component settings if you chose Crossover, you may choose to have a version of the character exist in the world anyway as a local counterpart to the original. If you wish, a second purchase may be used on the same Modifier to make it the default for that character across the multiverse.
objects.title: Specific Character Modifiers

addons.title: Tripled Stretch
addons.text: Your Perk to double the plot’s duration has merged with Stretched Story. The story’s total length now triples, with each purchase of Stretched Story being added before the multiplication.

objects.text: Sometimes a story simply happens to quickly to make sense and events are too close to each other for you to keep up. With every purchase of this, you can stretch the overall events of the story by up to one year, with things being as similar as possible to the original story, or delay specific events and all that necessarily follow by up to one year instead.
objects.title: Stretched Story

objects.text: With this modifier, any centralized government for interstellar civilization (or the equivalent for interdimensional or other types of multiple world / system scale civilizations) has broken up into multiple smaller governments. The exact form this takes can vary, so for settings like Star Wars, this means the Galactic Republic / Empire is retroactively replaced with anywhere from a few dozen to several hundred interstellar nations, while for Nanoha the TSAB would be replaced by at least a half dozen major Dimensional Sea travelling societies and dozens of minor ones. This also applies to various civilizations that claim dominion over most if not all of a given species, whether human or alien. For Halo that means the UNSC could literally be the same as the United Nations on most baseline early 21 century Earths, that is a semifunctional regulatory body with little actual power as humanity is split into several civilizations allied with one another instead of one big one. Meanwhile in Mass Effect, this means that the Asari, Salarians, Turians, and other species are split into a multitude of nations, some being predominately one species and others being multiracial. You can decide the specifics of why this is a thing and how it happened in this timeline. It could be that one centralized interstellar nation used to be dominant but internal stress / a major disaster / logistical issues / some other thing resulted in it becoming a failed state and it balkanized into the current form. Maybe the idea of any given species' homeworld almost always forming a true planetary government before heading to the stars is laughable, with the current interstellar nations being descendants of any number of homeworld nations like the USA, China, India, etc. Or perhaps some other explanation entirely or a mix of them instead. You may also decide the specifics of the new nations. For example, perhaps the Quarian / Geth war had a different outcome than canon and now the Quarians are split between the New Rannoch government consisting of the pro-Geth survivors who live with their digital allies, the Migrant Fleet consisting of the anti-Geth survivors who are banished from central Quarian Space, and a couple minor Quarian polities in distant systems who didn't wish to deal with the Geth at all either way or answered the Geth's soul question with "Maybe? Probably? Do we? Who knows." before moving on. You can also decide other details like how progressive, free, religious, warlike, xenophilic, and other such variables any new nations are or are not as well as their international policies, primary exports or trades, and more, being as vague or as detailed as you want. If you wish, there can be some exceptions to this, such as another galaxy / dimension not central to the main plot being united, or perhaps a specific species having only one government due to consisting of too few members or being a hivemind or something. However, these are always rare exceptions rather than the rule. You can also decide how this affects the main plot if relevant, from 'barely any major differences' to 'completely derailed from the beginning, possibly with new heroes and villains entirely' to anywhere in between, as well as major interstellar organizations like big companies or the space police or other such if you wish. No matter what, the stars are far more varied than before, with all that such a thing entails. Note: If you take a modifier that makes a planet bound setting interstellar / interdimensional or something like that, such as Galactic or 5D Earth, then this applies to the new version of the setting as well.
objects.title: Balkanized Stars

objects.text:
Choose a specific fanwork based on the world you are going to; a fanfic, a webcomic, a video series, a modded or fangame, story concepts from a tumblr blog, anything goes, even just a list of tropes or what if scenarios for a custom AU that currently doesn't exist. The setting of that fanwork is now crossing over with the setting you are inserting into. For example, pick Mauling Snarks and suddenly Maul and Skitter will find themselves in the same world. If the setting you are going to is already a notable AU due to other modifiers, then you can select the canon setting with your destination being considered the fanwork, or leave canon out of it with two AUs meeting instead.

You can pick the exact nature of this crossover. Maybe portals are opening between the two, perhaps people are randomly displaced between one or the other, suddenly the two worlds are within spitting distance of one another without explanation or the expected apocalyptic gravitational effects, or only a handful of notable characters crossed over and they are working to go back. As for why, it could be that another modifier you selected happened to bring them in contact with one another, random chance, or any other reason you want. If both worlds have incompatible multiverse structures, you can decide exactly how that either resolves itself, or causes more problems.

No matter what, this will have ramifications on the world, especially if the fanwork is radically divergent such as one where one character became ludicrously overpowered or something. But even if they are nearly identical, it will still cause chaos as villains try to work with or fight their counterparts, countries try to take advantage of having another world full of resources available, people trying to return to or flee their worlds exacerbate various issues, and potentially even cosmic threats begin to take notice and act.

If you want, any and / or every Alternate Earth purchased can have a fanwork chosen, such that a version where the chosen worlds were always one comes in contact with versions where that was never the case, or anything else you can think of. Additionally, you can choose to have it such that modifiers that are similar to elements of the chosen fanwork can be caused by 'setting bleed' between the two worlds or something of that nature. Finally, you can purchase this again to pick yet another fanwork to bring into the crossover, and then yet again up to 10 purchases. If purchased 10 times, there is no limit to how many fanworks you can incorporate into this world.
objects.title: Clash of the AUs

objects.text: Superpowers, magic, psionics, cultivation, whatever the form these supernatural systems grant reality redefining power to whoever has access to them. But where do they come from? Well this modifier answers that by creating a singular, immensely powerful Source from which they originate. Not only that, but this Source is sapient, sentient, and fully capable of acting on the world in ways independent of just granting humans and other beings power. What this Source is, what they look like, why they grant powers, and their personality can all vary. Maybe they are a god made of an array of geometric shapes that grants powers to gain followers, acting as a distant watcher of mankind who does not interfere beyond granting powers. Perhaps they are an alien machine made of strange matter housed under the moon's surface, granting powers to analyze how they are used yet finding humans themselves interesting and interacting with them through fabricated online personas. Or they could be a mere human inexplicably born with powers that gave them wings and bearing a crown of spiked horns, granting powers to humanity so they can one day master them and join them in immortality, acting as a paragon who saves innocent people from disasters and villains yet their mind is warped by their power so they have a hard time understanding why anyone would hate them for what others do with their granted power. All of these you can choose the specifics of or leave to chance, but there are two constants that must be adhered to. The first is that it will be influenced by the power system itself. So while the source of Psykers and the Warp may be anything from a harried benevolent force desperately trying to purify it to a monstrous omnicidal beast even the Warp Gods are afraid of, they will nonetheless be inherently chaotic and alien by human standards both in form and personality even if only slightly. The second is that as the very origin of the power system, it is by far stronger than even the strongest power wielder, being at minimum comparable to somewhere between Endbringer and Entity strength vs normal Parahumans for that system. If multiple power systems exist or one system has multiple distict aspects (such as Aura vs Dust in RWBY), you may choose for only one Source to exist for all of them, one Source for each of them (who may or may not get along), or have the Source be the origin of one but the others come from something else that isn't aware. If there is a canon origin of powers and it's not a person or at least capable of acting intelligently, then this Source is either the creator of it, its administrator who has gained absolute control over it, or it becomes aware and able to manifest an avatar such as being the manifestation of humanities collective unconscious in Code Geass from which that Codes and Geass are born. If there is a canon origin of powers and it's already self aware, such as Scion and Eden for Parahumans in Worm or the Brother Gods for Magic in RWBY, then this modifier does nothing unless another modifier retroactively removes them or introduces another power system which it can affect. Should the Source die then the power system itself will still exist, but afterwards things will begin to start breaking down, resulting in various issues ranging from fewer power users being born, previously unbreakable rules suddenly being bendable or even outright broken, powers becoming unsafe for their users, to outright apocalyptic scenarios such as all power users slowly going insane or turning into monsters, unnatural disasters spawning as supernatural energies infuse the environment chaotically, or worse. The only way to stop them would be to either modify the system itself to function without them, best done by the Source itself ahead of time, or to somehow have someone replace the Source and become the new origin of powers. Try to avoid it if possible. Note: If beings such as monsters, cryptids, spirits, gods, and other empowered entities that aren't human / demihuman / alien or adjacent exist, you can decide if the Source(s) deliberately made them, they are an unavoidable byproduct of the power system, they are foreign beings that managed to forcibly tap into the system, or some other reason they might exist.
objects.title: The Source of Powers

objects.text:
At first glance the world of Planetos seems simple and mundane, there’s certainly some magic but it is few and far between, with politics being the primary power. But if you look closer the masquerade begins to fall. There is; credible evidence of the existence of gods, a group of semi-immortal warlocks, multiple references to the Cthulhu Mythos, and more. And with this purchase, all of that and more becomes true. 

With your arrival magic returns to the world on a level beyond even what was triggered by Daenerys hatching her dragons, and the old horrors of millennia past begin to stir once more. And that isn't even beginning to get into whatever lies in the far off continents beyond the known world.

You can expect a noticeable increase in the strength of magic, old bloodlines manifesting ancient gifts once more, all sorts of gods becoming more active and interfering with the world, and eldritch horrors beginning to wake up or break free of their seals, among other things. 

Not to mention, the current political climate was already pretty unstable and is in no way ready for the resurgence of magic, so you best bet you’ll be seeing lots of eventual political upheaval. Additionally, people have grown accustomed to the lack of magic and no longer believe in it, so don’t expect much help from the ‘civilized’ and ‘worldy’ who are in power.

This is no longer a low fantasy world, but a high fantasy one which had previously been disguising itself as low fantasy.

<sub>This doesn't have to just be canon or canon-implied stuff, feel free to invent all sorts of things. Maybe the Stormlands used to have innate weather magic, or maybe dragons used to be really powerful and magical and the current dragons are but pale shadows their former glory.</sub>
objects.title: Old Magic (A Song of Ice and Fire)

objects.text:
Somehow, a Yautja (Predator) hunting vessel has crash-landed somewhere.

The ship’s cargo hold contained multiple Xenomorph eggs (around 100 or so) stored in stasis chambers. The crash damaged the containment systems, allowing several of the eggs to hatch, releasing Facehuggers, which have escaped and infected hosts. This resulted in the birth of numerous chestbursters, which have fully matured into Xenomorphs, including at least one Queen that has already begun forming a hive.

If left unchecked, the Xenomorphs will expand aggressively, capturing or killing nearby populations. Most captured victims will be used as hosts, increasing their numbers exponentially. Entire cities or wilderness regions may be overrun if a coordinated response is not launched. 

It is not sufficient to kill only the Queen. If the Queen is destroyed while other Xenomorphs remain alive, there is a 100% chance that surviving drones will scatter and eventually evolve into new Queens, forming multiple independent hives across world. To permanently end the threat, every Xenomorph must be eliminated. There is also a chance that one or more Yautja survived the crash. These survivors may attempt to hunt the Xenomorphs, local parahumans, or both, viewing the situation as a trial of honor rather than a disaster. Their presence introduces an unpredictable wildcard to the conflict.

NOTE 1: This Alternate Earth modifier may be taken multiple times. Each additional purchase represents another Yautja ship crashing somewhere on the planet. For each additional ship: At least a dozen or so Xenomorph egg survives, and one successfully produces a Queen Xenomorph, which will result in a new hive beginning to form in a different region. If you so wish, then there can be Yautja that survived the crash; it is up to you. Though there can only be up to 10 Yautja that survived per ship. also it is possible to acquire technology from the Yautja (Predator) vessels that have crashed.
objects.title: Xenomorph Infestation (Aliens vs Predator)

objects.text:
In the world of Avatar exists people known as Benders, individuals who can bend one of the four classical elements of Water, Earth, Fire, or Air. In this world, Bending is hereditary, where if you are the descendant of a Bender you have a chance of being one of the same type, with it generally being the most recent such Bending element in your direct lineage being the one you can wield if you're lucky. Only certain situations like being born the child of two different types of Bender can lead to variability in what you can Bend, with the four Elemental Nations generally keeping to their specific type. Well no more.

With this modifier active, Bending inheritance is and has always been completely randomized. If a pair of Firebenders have children together, their children are equally likely to be able to bend Fire as they are Water, Earth, Air, or nothing at all. In addition, non-Benders who come from a long lineage of other non-Benders have a small chance to have Bending children as well, meaning even if every single Bender of a given type is killed, it will always reappear somewhere, and the world maintains balance by making sure there are always an equal number of all Elements of Bending present by shifting the ratios of those born as needed, so no Element can go extinct.

This has changed the world in a number of ways. The differences between the Elemental Nations are now more focused on their philosophical and cultural values rather than what they Bend, with each Nation focusing on different aspects of Bending. For example, in the Water Tribe Firebenders would be more likely to specialize in hunting and acting as living heaters while in the Earth Kingdom their style would focus on smithing over fighting. Meanwhile, an Air Nomad who is a Waterbender would connect to the world spiritually through meditating on flows while also doubling as the temple's algae farmer, and a Fire Nation Airbender would be one of the most dangerous foes to face on the battlefield as they rip the air from your lungs, with many more possibilities and subdisciplines to be found.

This also introduces a number of differences to the canon timeline. For example, perhaps Katara remembers how the Fire Nation Raider who took her mother bound her in a prison of stone before taking her away, crying in the arms of her 'uncle' Bato as he made tiny puppets of flame dance in an attempt to distract her from her grief. Or maybe King Bumi is the world's strongest Airbender who helped Aang develop the air scooter, or Ozai having thrown a massive celebration in honor of Azula becoming the first known Bloodbender. The possibilities are numerous, and up to you to decide or you can leave it to chance.

It should be noted the Avatar still follows the cycle of elements, with the caveat that in this world they follow both a cycle of what element they Bend as well as a secondary cycle concerning the Nation they are born in. Though whether they are fully synced is another question; perhaps once a cycle completes itself the two randomize, so one cycle it's Airbender - Air Nomad, Waterbender - Water Tribe, etc., but the next cycle it is Airbender - Water Tribe, Waterbender - Earth Kingdom, etc., or maybe it's always the same but offset so the Earthbender Avatar is always found in the Fire Nation? The specifics are up to you. No matter what though, the eventual plot of this world will be far different from canon.
objects.title: Bending Lottery (Avatar: The Last Airbender)

objects.text:
In your world, there now exists a species of transcendental lifeforms that live outside the universe, known as "Celestialsapiens." Most of the time, they will be standing motionless within their own homeworld, known as the "Forge of Creation," but that's only because their multiple personalities are constantly debating within their own minds.

Should any Celestialsapien reach an agreement during one of these debates, they will use their powers to alter reality and put their agreed-upon decision into effect, whether that means changing the world's "art style," adding a new element or concept to the world, deciding that the meteor that killed the dinosaurs should have left a few alive or never have happened, or even creating a new universe.

Despite how drastic this might seem, the Celestialsapiens will rarely reach a decision, and making major changes to the world is something they will only ever do if they believe they have a very good reason for it. However, should someone or something outside the natural order perform a similar act, such as erasing or recreating a universe, their entire species will unite and pass judgment upon that being, regardless of whether they are good or evil. Should that being pass their judgment, they will be free to continue living as they did, but if they fail, the Celestialsapiens will enact what they consider a "fair punishment" for their actions.
objects.title: Forge of Creation (Ben 10)

objects.text:
Hidden in plain sight, yet invisible to the masses, exist the personifications of humanity's collective unconscious, mythological beings known as Heretical Gods. Born from myth, folklore, and faith, these entities are divine incarnations of characters in stories whispered across generations, such as Athena or Lancelot.

Once they take form in the mortal world, Heretical Gods wreak havoc upon the earth. To ordinary humans, these events appear as natural disasters, as the gods are visible only to those possessing supernatural abilities. Those who manage to slay a Heretical God through their own strength, while remaining fully human, can undergo the Rite of Usurpation created by the Heretical God Pandora and transform into Devil Kings known as Campione.

Campione possess the divine Authorities of the Heretical Gods they slay, gaining power and influence from their deaths. They become monarchs of either the place where they are reborn as a Campione or the place they were born at. Only seven Campione may exist at any given time, though not due to impossibility. Whenever more than seven Campione are active at any given time, the King Who Manifests at the World's End awakens and slays the existing Campione, restarting the cycle. New Heretical Gods may appear depending on the legends that exist in a given setting.
objects.title: Devil Kings Awaken: Heretical Gods Invasion (Campione!)

objects.text: In the spaces in between reality the Faceless Angels wait and watch. They are things that do not exist, that have never existed and cannot exist in the future. From their vantage point outside reality they push themselves in through weak points in the fabric so they can replace the world with one where they Are. These beings range from objects never invented, to animals that never evolved, to spells never cast, and even timelines that never came to pass. As such their methods also vary greatly, from subverting organisations to overt and hyperviolent instructions. Thin places are intermittent yet ever present. Abandoned places, where physics becomes strange and weak, where magic has torn holes between worlds. All of these and more leave room for the Angels to move and intrude into reality seeking to reshape it and make themselves real. The Angels will ooze into every crevice and infect every part of your world looking for places to secrete themselves into physical form.
objects.title: Faceless Angels (Chronicles of Darkness - Mage: The Awakening)

objects.text: Three things now lurk in the dark corners of the world. Among them, sit hundreds of thousands of tattered alchemists, the ones who know they are right, in dingy rooms, abandoned houses and half-flooded basements. Each of them searches for one thing, the spark of divine fire Pyros, and god help them should they find it. The others are their creations, that wander in their throngs longing for what they cannot understand. The most benign of these new fellows to the world are Prometheans, misshapen almost-men that wander across the world in their small throngs. They are not human, but facsimiles of them. Most humans in the vicinity of a Promethean are filled with a Disquiet that only grows, disgust, hatred, and obsession follow them and fades in their absence while the earth below revolts and slowly turns to wasteland around them, necessitating that they remain constantly migratory. As they wander however, they gain experience and understanding, growing not only as a beast but a person. Refining and purifying their Pyros until at last they can perform their final magnum opus. Creating and abandoning another of their kind, and embracing their New Dawn, leaving all of their might behind and returning at last as a true and utterly mundane mortal. However, not all of these Prometheans are so successful. Some fall to monstrosity, abandoning the idea not only of humanity but of their own personhood. They become little more than monsters, reshaping themselves to fill this role. Further still, sometimes the creation of a Promethean goes wrong, imbuing their pieces with divine fire but no personhood, leaving them starving and sick Pandorans, seeking only to consume their brethren for even a scrap of their Pyros. The Alchemists themselves meanwhile are insensate and paranoid. Needing their reagents, they are willing to hunt and rip apart their errant children for parts. The most even tempered of the trade satisfy themselves with elixirs of life and turning lead into gold, but the majority detest their humanity, all too ready to throw it to the wayside. Even the most well adjusted of Alchemists are avoided by the wiser of their children, as all it takes is a single poor response to their Disquiet for them to realise what a bounty is near them.
objects.title: Divine Fire (Chronicles of Darkness - Promethean: The Created)

objects.text:
It seems the canon and official World of Darkness gameline isn’t enough to satisfy you.

Maybe you find the variety of supernatural beings still too limiting for your taste, or perhaps you feel it isn’t already complex and chaotic enough.

Now you have the option to expand your World of Darkness with fan-made supplements such as Genius: The Transgression, Princess: The Hopeful, Leviathan: The Tempest, and Dragon: The Ember, to name a few.

Even crossover splats aren’t excluded, so if you want, you can throw in Highlander: The Gathering. After all, it’s your World of Darkness.
objects.title: Fan-made Supplement (Chronicles of Darkness/World of Darkness)
Lavos (Chrono Trigger)
objects.text:
Millions of years ago, something fell from the stars...

The extraterrestrial organism known as Lavos crashed into your world, buried itself beneath the surface, and spent millions of years absorbing energy and genetic information while influencing evolution.

Lavos is something akin to the Entities, not through any connection, but through convergent evolution. It will awaken at an undisclosed point soon after your arrival with the abilities and power systems of the life it has absorbed, each refined to its theoretical peak or beyond through millions of years of optimization. Depending on your actions, it may also copy your abilities unless you have a means of preventing this.

Its strength depends on the world it has consumed. Worlds with powerful or exotic genetics and powers, such as Monster Hunter or Bleach, will produce far stronger Lavos, while completely mundane worlds will produce a weaker incarnation.

Some may even produce a Lavos capable of surpassing the Time Devourer, which threatened the universe and all of space-time.

If your world is set near the year 2000, or a similar millennial turning point, Lavos will awaken at that point potentially giving you more years to prepare.

<small>If the wait is 20 or more years till the turn of the millennia then the above is ignored and Lavos will awaken at the undisclosed point soon after you arrive.</small>

One of the most difficult and heartbreaking things someone can experience is the death of a loved one. And in your world, in this darkest moment when the grieving person stands weeping over their loss, a mysterious figure calling itself the Millennium Earl appears to them with what looks like a cross between a plastic model in a sprue and a skeleton. Inhuman in appearance yet somehow not raising alarm, he will offer the bereaved the opportunity to bring back their loved one, if only they call the deceased's name.

Should he be refused, he will vanish as suddenly as he arrived. Should his offer be accepted however, the deceased soul will be drawn into the construct in the sprue, the voice of the deceased speaking out... in horror. For now they are bound inside an Akuma as its power-source, slave to the Earl's every whim, the first of which will inevitably be to kill the one who called them forth, and take over their identity as the fresh corpse they are made to wear binds itself to the skeletal frame of the Akuma.

Akuma live the lives they took over perfectly, fooling even relatives and close friends. Yet this life is but a cover for them, for all Akuma constantly look for any opportunity to kill humans, as each kill makes them grow more powerful, while also avoiding as much attention as they can, for Akuma are far from indestructible.

While even the weaker Akuma are sturdy against conventional weapons, they are unusually vulnerable against parahuman abilities, particularly those that are light-based in nature. Should the world also contain holy or divine energies, Akuma are also vulnerable to those. However on the flipside, killing a parahuman will empower an Akuma far more than normal humans, making them seek out their natural enemies.

A trait all Akuma share is that they evolve with sufficient time and murder. They all begin as Level 0 in their skeletal frame. Once they have a human shell, they will rapidly evolve to Level 1, in which they all resemble floating orbs with giant gun-barrels sticking out of them.

It is however once they've killed enough to reach Level 2 that they begin to diverge from each other, gaining a unique appearance and power, which can be as varied as those of any parahuman.

The few Akuma that make it to Level 3 begin to look more uniform again, looking like humanoid monsters clad in in ominous plate-armor, their powers being typically less esoteric in nature in return for far greater physical aptitude.

And extremely rarely an Akuma manages become a Level 4. Appearing like a winged white marionette, a Level 4 is considered an S-Class threat, being a high-level Brute capable of wiping out entire towns within a short time, though they are no match for an Endbringer.

Overly simplified it can be said that that Level 1 Akuma are no match for the average parahuman unless they get the drop on him or attack in overwhelming numbers due to their inherent vulnerability to them. A Level 2 is an even match for the average parahuman, the outcome depending on what powers both have. A Level 3 would require a fairly powerful parahuman to overcome. And against a Level 4 only a Triumvirate-tier or above Parahuman would stand a chance.

Nobody knows why the Millennium Earl does what he does, for he never acts directly outside of the creation of Akuma. Some believe he is amassing an army while waiting for something that has yet to come to pass.
objects.title: Akuma (D.Gray-Man)

addons.text:
Due to the presence of both the Inner and Outer Planes, you now also gain access to the final piece needed to complete the Great Wheel: the Outlands.

The Outlands are the True Neutral plane that sits at the center of the Astral Plane. Unlike the other Outer Planes, they are unique in that, despite being infinite in size, they possess a definitive center.

This center is the Spire. The Spire is a tower of infinite height located at the center of the plane that constantly emits an anti-magic field. The closer one gets to the Spire, the weaker magic becomes, until it is completely nullified at its base. Even deities are not exempt from its effects.

Surrounding the Spire are the Hinterlands, an infinite neutral landscape filled with forests and towns. These towns are called Gate-Towns. Each Gate-Town contains a portal to one of the Outer Planes and reflects the alignment of that plane.

By far the most interesting location in the Outlands, however, is Sigil. Sigil, also called the City of Doors, is a ring-shaped demiplane that floats above the top of the Spire and is ruled over by an entity known as the Lady of Pain.

This city is the prime nexus: the political and cultural center of the multiverse. This status is well earned, as it not only contains portals to every other plane in the Great Wheel and numerous portals to the Prime Material Plane, but is also the only location from which gods are completely barred.

No deity, regardless of status or strength, may enter the city, as decreed by the Lady of Pain. Any deity that dares attempt it will find itself violently slaughtered with extreme prejudice.

As with the other modifiers, the Outlands will adapt to the local laws of your setting and retroactively integrate into its cosmology and history.
addons.title: The Outlands

objects.text:
Due to this modifier, your chosen setting now retroactively includes a set of Inner Planes similar to those found in the Dungeons & Dragons multiverse.

These planes exist outside the standard physical multiverse. Unlike the physical universe—often referred to as the Prime Material Plane—their environments and laws are extremely hostile to non-natives, making visits extremely dangerous if proper precautions are not taken.

This is because the Inner Planes, unlike the Outer Planes which are based on morality, represent different aspects of the physical universe, leading to the creation of extreme, hyper-specialized environments.

There are six major Inner Planes, each infinite in size. These are the four elemental Planes of Fire, Water, Earth, and Air, as well as the two Energy Planes: one of Positive Energy and one of Negative Energy. Outside of the major planes, there are also the para-elemental planes, which exist at the intersections between elemental planes, and the quasi-planes, which exist in the border regions between an elemental plane and one of the Energy Planes.

For example, there is the Para-Elemental Plane of Ice, which exists between the Planes of Water and Air, or the Quasi-Plane of Radiance, which exists between the Plane of Fire and the Positive Energy Plane.

All of these planes are inhabited by various species, the largest portion of which is made up of elementals. Their appearance, power, and behavior are strongly influenced by the plane to which they are native.

Travel between the Inner Planes is often accomplished via the Ethereal Plane, a transitory plane that exists adjacent to both the Prime Material Plane and the Inner Planes and is filled with ethereal proto-matter that gives it its name. While one is in the Ethereal Plane, one can see the plane to which one is currently adjacent, though affecting it usually requires leaving the Ethereal Plane.

The Inner Planes and their inhabitants will be adapted to the local physical and metaphysical laws of your setting, and depending on your preferences, the Inner Planes will either integrate with or replace the local cosmology.
objects.title: The Inner Planes (D&D)

addons.text:
It turns out the damage to reality was more extensive than anyone anticipated.

Dungeon Gates don't just lead to the wreckage of dead worlds — they also open into shattered fragments of the Outer Planes, drifting aimlessly through the Astral Sea.

These Astral Gates are rarer than standard Dungeon Gates, but far more dangerous. Occasionally, they bring with them mad or corrupted Outsiders, remnants of realms beyond comprehension.

Worse still, the Dungeons they lead to possess a terrifying trait: they begin to transform their surroundings, reshaping the environment around the Gate into a warped reflection of their home Plane.

Fortunately, this corruption has limits. It cannot spread far from the Gate, and will rapidly dissipate once the Dungeon is cleared.

In the case of a Dungeon Break, the corruption will gradually recede once all the Outsiders have been killed and/or relocated.
addons.title: Astral Gates

objects.text:
Due to this modifier, your chosen setting now retroactively includes an Astral Plane, similar to the one found in the Dungeons & Dragons multiverse.

The Astral Plane, also known as the Astral Sea, is a timeless, otherworldly expanse of nothingness that exists outside the standard physical multiverse. Unlike the physical universe—often referred to as the Prime Material Plane—the Astral Plane has no consistent laws of reality. Concepts like time and space exist here only in abstract forms, rather than as concrete, reliable constants.

Because the Astral Plane connects to all locations in the multiverse, it serves as a convenient highway for dimensional travelers moving between universes, realms, and planes of existence. Accessing it can be difficult, however—typical methods include astral projection or dimensional portals, especially for those wishing to enter it physically.

Within the Astral Plane exist eight major Outer Planes, each representing a philosophical alignment arranged along the cosmic axes of Good, Evil, Law, and Chaos. These include:

Lawful Good/Neutral/Evil

Neutral Good/Evil

Chaotic Good/Neutral/Evil

Like the Astral Plane, these Outer Planes are infinite in size and not bound by the conventional laws of space and time. Between them lie numerous lesser planes, which serve as transitional realms and travel routes between the major ones.

The Outer Planes also function as the afterlife for sapient mortal souls from the Material Plane, who reach them via the Astral Plane after death. A soul’s destination depends primarily on its moral alignment, which determines the Outer Plane most closely aligned with its values. If your setting already includes an afterlife, it may either be merged with or replaced by this Outer Planar system, depending on your preferences.

These realms are inhabited by powerful supernatural beings known as Outsiders. Each Outsider's nature, appearance, abilities, and power level are heavily influenced by the traits of their home plane. These beings adapt to the metaphysical laws of your setting and vary accordingly. Outsiders aligned with Good and Evil are locked in an eternal conflict—one unlikely to end, as Outsiders who die outside their home plane simply reform there over time. Only destruction on their native plane results in permanent death.

Outsiders frequently visit the Material Plane for various reasons. Some seek to guide and aid mortals, others aim to conquer or corrupt, while still others come out of curiosity or exploration. Regardless of intent, their visits—and the confirmed existence of the afterlife—have had a profound and lasting impact on society. Populations in such settings tend to be significantly more spiritually aware and martially inclined, having adapted to the twin realities of divine intervention and infernal invasion.
objects.title: The Outer Planes (D&D)

objects.text:
In your starting world, Spirits exist, and possess an innate reservoir of spiritual power that allows them to wield supernatural abilities, this reservoir also exists within humans. For spirits, this power is accessible from the moment they come into existence.

In humans, however, it lies dormant, and only a rare few ever awaken it. It`s awakening is unpredictable and varies from person to person, making those who wield spiritual power both rare and remarkable.

Spirits are deceased humans who have not crossed over into the afterlife and instead roam among the living. They cannot be seen by humans who lack spiritual awareness and are drawn to sources of strong life-force energy. Every spirit is unique and possesses its own abilities. Spirits are classified into three types:

Earthbound Spirits
Spirits unable to pass on due to a strong attachment to a specific place. It is said to be impossible for a spirit medium to exorcise an earthbound spirit while it remains within its bound territory, as its connection to that location greatly strengthens it.

Yokai (Evil Spirits)
Hostile spirits that prey upon the living. These beings have become well-known among humans and are often given aliases as warnings of their existence. Yokai possess powerful supernatural abilities—such as casting curses or manipulating bodies—and are physically stronger than humans. Their unique abilities often reflect traits they possessed in life and retained after death.

Guardian Spirits
Though little is fully understood about them, guardian spirits are believed to bind themselves to humans in order to see a final desire fulfilled before passing on to the afterlife. While bound, they may lend their spiritual power to the human they protect.

Humans with heightened spiritual awareness are more likely to be attacked by Yokai, especially if a Yokai realises the human can sense its presence. The supernatural abilities granted by spiritual power vary widely.

Spiritual power is not always permanent. Over time, it can fade in some people, and return to dormancy unless reignited by an external force. While awakening spiritual power is usually a gradual process for humans, certain factors can accelerate it—such as contact with an object imbued with a large amount of spiritual energy.

Spiritual power stems from two distinct forces: ki and auras. Humans harness ki, an internal energy that fuels supernatural abilities gained through training and the powers itself can vary, such as Enhanced physical abilities, Mediumship, creating Mystic Barrier, Power of Words, Psychokinesis and others.

Yokai, on the other hand, draw from auras—a life-force energy that sustains their existence. Without it, a spirit will crumble into nothingness and be forgotten by both the living and the dead. Humans can acquire Yokai-type spiritual power by possessing a Yokai’s aura, and a Yokai may also willingly bestow their abilities upon a chosen individual.
objects.title: Spiritual World (Dandadan)

objects.text:
In the world you are going to, there will be those who possess Ultimate Talents, individuals whose mastery over a specific skill, hobby, or field is boosted by a natural Talent able to grow further and a lifetime of dedication that pushes them into being Superhuman in their niche.

Ultimate Talents are local celebrities at the absolute minimum, with them being force multipliers when used wisely; even more so, when several Ultimate Talents work together, they can be a force unto themselves, able to affect whole regions and even the world through their Talents, becoming Symbols of Hope or Bringers of Despair.

Talents are not exclusive or locked to one person, with the titles of Ultimate being just that: titles of recognition, and people can have similar or overlapping specialties that differ only in minute details, such as someone being a better general gamer compared to someone more specialized in Rhythm games. It's also possible for a person's Talent to be mistaken for something else, intentionally or not; in theory, anyone can become an Ultimate Talent, only requiring time to find and nurture said Talent through hard work.

History will remain the same, with various notable figures merely being suspected Ultimate Talents and what their Talents would be, with Ultimate Talents being a more recently acknowledged topic. Because of this, several characters from different worlds will become Ultimate Talents, for example: Elliot Ludwig (Poppy Playtime), the Ultimate Toymaker; Tessa Elliot (Murder Drones), the Ultimate Repairer; Sidney Prescott (Scream), the Ultimate Survivor; Salem (RWBY), the Ultimate Terror; Ai Hoshino (Oshi No Ko), the Ultimate Idol; Ichigo Kurosaki (Bleach), the Ultimate Delinquent; etc., etc.

This also means you can have an Ultimate Talent too, but you will not know it, it will be completely random, and you will have to train it from the ground up.

Death games, battles of HOPE vs DESPAIR, and monochrome bears not included.
objects.title: To Attain Talent's Peak (Danganronpa)

objects.text:
The Falna, as powerful as it is, had some odd quirks. Those not part of a race with natural magic affinity have to simply hope that they manifest a spell, most of which aren't particularly powerful, and no matter how much power it gives, your god being sent back to heaven removes the benefits you're gained until another god grants you the Falna once again. In this world, neither is the case, whether because of the gods figuring out new methods or the Falna always being that way, the falna persists no matter what happens to the god who granted it, making the power it grants permanent. 

In addition, the Falna now grants people the ability to learn weak, chant-less spells, though most adventurers take days, if not weeks, to learn even a single spell, with these universal spells, called cantrips, being roughly comparable in power to Bell's firebolt when he was at level 1. Cantrips do not improve with a higher magic stat or level, so they are largely seen as utility tools. Examples of cantrips would include Light Spark, which can generate a floating ball of light as bright as a normal torch and Shock Snap, which sends a short range jolt of electricity, just strong enough to stun an enemy.
objects.title: Upgraded Falna (Danmachi)

objects.text:
When Scion first appeared, so did Lantern Rings. Scion is an Emotional Entity that creates and gifts Rings to those who meet the condition.

The Rings Scion gives out will need to be recharged by a Lantern Battery, they can be found randomly across the map. But most important places usually have a handful. All cities will have some as well.
objects.title: Scion, The Emotional Space Whale (DC Comics)

objects.text:
In any world—whether you are born into it, dropped into it, or find yourself in a fusion of realms or a singular plane—seven anthropomorphic beings known as the Endless exist. Born at the very moment of creation, whether of a world, plane, or multiverse they are the children of two cosmic forces: Time and Night. Each Endless embodies a profound universal concept, and their family includes Destiny, Death, Dream, Destruction, Desire, Despair, and Delirium. They exist in your local multiverse and every multiverse related to it. 

Each sibling rules over a personal realm where they are absolute sovereigns, embodying and enforcing their respective aspects of existence along with the counterpart to their aspect. They are among the most powerful entities in the omniverse, inherently multiversal in nature and power, yet still susceptible to forces that can modify or enhance their power, the Endless can be distant or choose to walk among humanity.

In a world like High School DxD, the Endless would surpass and command beings such as Great Red, God, Ophis, and Trihexa. Even in a fused world or across multiple universes, they remain the dominant powers, second only to the original creator of that segment of reality. Introducing the Endless into a world brings not only immense power but also the complex intrigues, dramas, and inevitable troubles that follow them. Unless you wield a power beyond a certain threshold or are related to them, you are not immune to their influence. Their very presence brings change to the world.

The Endless are true to their name: eternal, immutable, and bound to their duties until the end of all things. Should you have one as a companion, they would replace that world’s native version of them. While the Endless are capable of having offspring if they choose, strict laws forbid the spilling of family blood—though that does not prevent them from interfering with your fate. Tread carefully; the presence of the Endless marks the beginning of a far more terrifying world.
objects.title: Rise of The Endless (DC Comics)

objects.text:
In the world you arrive in, the Emotional Electromagnetic Spectrum now exists, which will be harnessed to create seven Lantern Corps.

The Guardians of the Universe will harness the green light of will to create the Green Lantern Corps as an intergalactic police force, Ganthet and Sayd will harness the blue light of hope to create the Blue Lantern Corps and help countless worlds by creating miracles, Atrocitus will harness the red light of rage to create the Red Lantern Corps to enact vengeance upon the many wrongs committed throughout the cosmos, and so forth.

Each of these Corps will have a huge impact on the cosmos of your chosen world, and some people on your planet might even be chosen to become members of a Lantern Corps. However, the relationships between these Corps also mean that while some will help each other, others will frequently come into conflict, such as the Green Lantern Corps and the Yellow Lantern Corps or the Red Lantern Corps.

However, while this will add the Lantern Corps to your world, it will not necessarily add every character from those Corps. For example, the Yellow Lantern Corps may have been created by someone other than Sinestro, or the greatest Green Lantern may be someone other than Hal Jordan or Kyle Rayner.

Lastly, even though there will initially be only seven Corps, it is possible for new Corps to be created, such as the Black Lantern Corps and the White Lantern Corps.
objects.title: Lantern Corps (DC Comics)

objects.text:
"Have you ever wanted to fight for the fate of the multiverse? No? Well, too bad!"

It seems like your multiverse has taken some inspiration from the DC Multiverse. Because from now on, it will be subjected to so-called "Crisis Events" on a semi-regular basis.

A Crisis Event isn't simply a crossover between various alternate universes. It is a massive disturbance to the fundamental structure of the Multiverse itself that can alter reality, history, continuity, and sometimes even the very nature of existence.

During a Crisis, countless universes can be destroyed, created, merged, rewritten, recreated, etc. Cosmic boundaries can change, cosmological structures can be damaged or entirely new ones created. The end of a Crisis is usually punctuated by a multiversal restructuring event and the emergence of a new status quo.

There is no single universal mechanism behind these Events. One could be the result of a cosmic entity's rampage, another of a time-travel experiment gone wrong, or even deliberate meddling by interested parties. Either way, preventing a Crisis before it happens is nearly impossible, as they carry an enormous amount of narrative weight.

Crisis Events also generate two opposing cosmic energies in vast quantities: Crisis Energy and Anti-Crisis Energy, respectively.
Crisis Energy represents separation, selfishness, and disruption. It is generated by the selfish actions of individuals during a Crisis and seeks to break the connections that bind people together. 

Anti-Crisis Energy is its opposite. It embodies connection, continuity, and harmony. Generated by selfless actions, it seeks to reinforce the bonds between people and remind them that they are all part of a greater whole.

Both of these energies are immensely powerful and can be harnessed to accomplish absurd feats. Even the creation of a new Multiverse is possible if you have enough of either one.

You can choose how frequently these Events occur, but remember: while the Multiverse is guaranteed to always survive in some capacity, the same doesn't apply to you or your universe. Even if you do survive, you might not recognize what has become of your home afterward.
objects.title: Crisis Events (DC Comics)

objects.text:
Even in death, you can't seem to get some rest.

To stay in the world of the living, ghosts need to be remembered. When you are forgotten, you would fade away. What comes after? Nobody knows. Of course, a lot fear this supposed inevitability, so there's only one way a lot of folks thought to do in order to etch their place in this world somehow.

And that is to be seen.

Ghosts are creepy, naturally horrifying even. That much is obvious. Using that, it has become an industry to provide hauntings and scares in order to stay in the hearts and minds of the living.
