Those of similar power levels will more strongly gravitate towards each other, on top of having a higher 'pull' innately. 

This effect can replace the conflict drive entirely, or leave it as is. Either way, Parahumans will find themselves clashing more often with each other than not.
objects.title: Gravity! (JoJo's Bizarre Adventure)

objects.text:
Previously, only certain people had the capacity to develop a Stand, and only some of the ones who could, did. Now, everyone in the world is guaranteed to develop a Stand.

Normally this could have dangerous results, causing anyone who doesn’t possess the willpower to control their Stand to grow ill and die, but the threshold to maintain a Stand safely has been lowered to prevent this. Those who would have had a Stand without this modifier experience an overall boost to their Stand’s power and potential, enough to make a decent Stand top-tier, and a top-tier Stand godlike.

As per usual, each Stand is unique to the user, having an appearance and abilities determined by their personality and nature. It is up to you how the phenomenon of Gravity works, whether it’s negated by the omnipresence of Stand users or everyone now finds themselves getting dragged into the lives of everyone else constantly.

Optionally, this can affect you, giving you your own unique Stand if you didn’t buy one or boosting the strength of your Stand if you did.
objects.title: Stand By Me (JoJo's Bizarre Adventure)

objects.text: This modifier changes the world of Jujutsu Kaisen by making every other country have the same cursed energy density as Japan. The reasons for this are up to you, but overall, it leads to other countries having similar organizations to the Jujutsu Sorcerer Association in Japan, as well as cursed spirits whose strength equals—or even surpasses—that of the special grade curses in canon.
objects.title: Curses Everywhere (Jujutsu Kaisen)

addons.text:
Gojo Satoru's birth didn't just lead to Cursed Spirits growing stronger in response to his birth; it also led to more Cursed Spirits manifesting in the world, twice the number that existed in Canon.

More people also begin to develop the potential of manifesting Cursed Energy in response to this imbalance.
addons.title: Age of Darkness

objects.text: Hidden in plain sight, yet invisible to the masses, are malevolent entities known as "Cursed Spirits" or simply "Curses". Monstrous creatures of grotesque and disgusting shapes and sizes created from the negative emotions of humans. Once enough of this negativity is cultivated in an area, a Curse is born, ranging from a pile of flesh and eyeballs, grotesque versions of animals, perverse humanoid depictions, and anything in between and beyond. The most dangerous of them are capable of human intelligence and speech. They are most often representations of the negativity they're born from, which also influences their strength, personalities, abilities, and then some. There are many places that are hotspots for them due to the abundance of negativity, such as schools, hospitals, or graveyards. To properly purge a Curse, it must be exorcised using some method of spiritual energy. Otherwise, they will return anew, potentially taking a different form or even becoming stronger. Optionally, this can have the side effect of bringing Cursed Energy to the world and the equivalent of Jujutsu Sorcerers to combat them. Alternatively, the world's current power system can remain unchanged yet still be applicable for exorcising Curses, or develop new methods specifically designed to deal with them. There will be one or several equivalent organizations to Jujutsu Tech that will be dedicated to defending the innocent and ignorant of Curses, but how they operate will be entirely dependant on said world. At bare minimum, they will go to any length to ensure proper secrecy of themselves and management of curses, and take any opportunity for a new recruit. Unlike canon Jujutsu Kaisen, corruption of the higher-ups is not guaranteed. Finally, depending on the world and any modifiers—such as Welcome to Earth Hell or being in the DC Universe—Cursed Spirits will increase in power and numbers, and the organization will respond accordingly.
objects.title: Age of Curses (Jujutsu Kaisen)

objects.text: In addition to Cursed Energy, the energy of negative emotions, there now exists Blessed Energy, the energy of positive emotions. Unlike Cursed Energy, Blessed Energy is much better oriented for support over combat, essentially being the lighter Yang counterpart to the darker Yin that is Cursed Energy. It possesses its own counterparts to various aspects of Cursed Energy, like Innate Techniques, Binding Vows, Black Flashes, and more, but with its own spin on the concepts. Much like Yin and Yang, Blessed Energy has its own Reversed version that is more offensive, much like RCT. The two essentially act as the reflection of the other contained within. Blessed Energy and Cursed Energy are generally incompatible with each other; most Sorcerers are only able to generate one or the other. Black (Cursed) Sorcerers function as per canon, while White (Blessed) Sorcerers generally take more support or backline-oriented rolls, though this is not a hard rule. Gray Sorcerers who can use both are rare but very powerful. In JJK itself, Gojo Satoru, Ryomen Sukuna, and Itadori Yuji are guaranteed to be such Gray Sorcerers. Also, much like how ambient Cursed Energy spawns Cursed Spirits that hate mankind, ambient Blessed Energy spawns Blessed Spirits that love mankind. It is relatively common for these Blessings to act as imaginary friends, guardian angels, ancestor spirits, and temple guardians, with the Sorcerer Society going out of its way to try to recruit them (expect most veteran Sorcerers to have one or more ‘Shikigami’ that are just tamed Blessings). Unfortunately, due to how such energy is generated, Curses outnumber Blessings at least 10-to-1, though they are on average one Grade higher per capita than Curses are. Note that Curses and Blessings hate each other but, unless they are interacting with the same specific people, will try to avoid one another. If they do encounter one another, though, they will try to kill the other, though Curses being more combat-focused means they usually win equal matchups. Note: You can decide the specifics of how this changes the history of JJK, but keep in mind that though this world may be a brighter and more hopeful one, it is still a cursed world all the same.
objects.title: The Blessings of Man (Jujutsu Kaisen)

objects.text: August 15th at 12:30 noon I don't see a cloud above The sun is shining down, what a pretty day Every August 15, when a creature dies (especially in groups), on rare occasion, a "Heat Haze" opens up. An alternate world created by a "Medusa" where time doesn't move. A world made to be an eternal paradise for her family, so that an immortal like her could never part with them. Things never go according to plan. This Medusa had since lost control over this alternate world. It now devours almost everyone near where she first created it, and traps them in a hell of their own making. Here, so long as one person has a wish they desperately wish to come true, a "Snake" will bond with them. Snakes are creatures created from the Medusa who gives its host abilities based on their wish. A quick example is the Snake of Deceiving Eyes that can make illusions and are given to "liars", or the Snake of Drawing Eyes for folks desperate for attention, etc. Only those with Snakes can leave the Haze, leaving behind folks to die. As a lot tend to enter with loved ones, it's not uncommon for the vessels to be traumatized akin to a Trigger. With this modifier, if you take this with Alternate Earths or Worm, some of the main characters may gain an extra ability as a Snake Vessel based on their biggest desires. If not in any fandom world however, who gets the snakes will be randomized. Beware of two snakes in particular. The intelligent Snake of the Clearing Eyes who wishes to keep existing by any means necessary, and the Snake of the Combining Eyes, which is the "Queen" who can draw the power of all snakes combined to gain reality altering powers like the one used to create the Heat Haze world itself. They are both potential threats to anybody with a snake inside them. Boys and girls its time to look ahead So we can fight that sun and look on forward
objects.title: Heat Haze Daze (Kagerou Project)

objects.text:
In your starting world, when people have a near-death experience, intense emotions, or merely a strong enough resolve, it becomes possible for them to awaken to their Dying Will Flame. Dying Will Flames are high-density energy with special characteristics depending on their type, each person's Dying Will Type being determined by birth, and it is mostly random save for special cases such as particular lineages.

Dying Will Flames can be measured by their purity, which is connected to a person's resolve, their determination, with the greater the purity, the greater the output of their flame. No two flames will be alike, as they are akin to fingerprints, with different people having different shapes, characteristics, and other such markers.

Given the nature of Dying Will Flames with strong wills near death, they are mostly seen with those in the criminal underworld, where several organizations, mainly crime families / Mafias, have taken control of large swaths of the world's criminal elements, making them more organized with oversight being different for each organization head, who follows their own code.

That is not to say that there aren't those outside of the criminal underworld who can wield Dying Will Flames; merely that they're the most concentrated regarding numbers, and you can find users of Dying Will Flames throughout the world, be they law enforcement, rescue workers, doctors, civilians, or really strong-willed individuals.

Given the widespread potential of Dying Will Flames, they have been greatly researched, allowing for the creation of tools and equipment meant to enhance their effectiveness or power some devices; the focus of this Dying Will Technology is rings that act as foci, allowing people to use the ability of their Dying Will.
objects.title: Wills Under Sky (Katekyo Hitman Reborn)

addons.text:
Curses are born from the negative emotions born in people's Hearts; however, due to the presence of Darkness in the World you reside in, these Cursed Spirits have been twisted into the Unversed.

Unlike normal Cursed Spirits, the Unversed all possess an inherent intelligence that drives them to not only make others produce more negative emotions, but also to make people produce the most of said negative emotions to both empower themselves and create more Unversed.

Most troubling of all is that the Unversed appear to be immune to nearly all forms of mundane weaponry, including technologically advanced weapons from alien civilizations.

The Unversed will also align themselves with Heartless and Nobodies to further aid in their production and accumulation of negative emotions.
addons.title: Curse of the Unversed (Kingdom Hearts)

objects.text:
It seems that your travel to your new World(s) has not gone unnoticed, my friend. The creatures of the Realm of Darkness have begun to invade. They can be divided into two main categories: the Heartless and the Nobodies.

The Heartless are creatures born from those who have lost their hearts to darkness, either from succumbing to their inner darkness or having their hearts devoured by the Heartless. They can be further classified into two types: the pureblood Heartless, such as Shadows and Darkside's (and no, not the one you might be thinking of), and the synthetic Heartless, which are often identified by the emblems on their bodies and have varied and unique forms and abilities.

On the other hand, we have the Nobodies. When a being with a strong will has their heart devoured, they are left with just their body and soul, turning into a Nobody. Nobodies come in two forms: the more monstrous types, whose appearances are as varied as those of the synthetic Heartless, and the humanoid Nobodies, which are rare creatures that retain their original forms but have lost their memories.

At first, the Heartless and Nobodies will appear sporadically. However, over time, their numbers will begin to swell exponentially, converting the inhabitants into more Heartless and Nobodies, while also attracting more of their kind from the Realm of Darkness. If left unchecked, the World(s) could be consumed by eternal darkness.
objects.title: Incursion from the Darkness: Usurpation of the Heart (Kingdom Hearts)

objects.text: Well, it seems like you're quite in a pickle. Something is coming, passing through the dark cosmos and took interest to the world you're in. Fortunately, it is not malevolent. Unfortunately, its gaze is not without consequence. Whatever falls under its direct gaze gets changed, twisted, mutated. Even indirect imagery of it is dangerous. People will change. Some will become monsters both inside and out, while others will be able to keep their sanity; some animals could even gain human-level intellect. Even infrastructure is not spared though it only changes in a non liminal way and slower than living beings. The good news is that it arrive in one week and it only passing through; for 15 days, it will look at the world, not understanding that it gaze unintentionally change everything. Whatever you do... Don't Look Outside.
objects.title: Gaze of the Visitor (Look Outside)

objects.text: Nineteen Great Rings are scattered throughout the world you find yourself in, alongside many lesser ones. These usually impart some power(s) upon the bearer, such as invisibility or magical vision, and empower the wearer's skills and strengths. The Great Rings additionally have the power to ward off the decays of time and postpone the weariness of the world. All rings have the magical ability to extend their owners' lives by eons. Despite there being no One Ring to rule them all, they function without issue.
objects.title: Rings Of Power (Lord of The Rings)

objects.text:
A few drops of strange glistening oil have found their way to your chosen world. Viscous, metallic, faintly luminescent. It carries memory. A collective consciousness from a dead dimension, waiting to be born again. It spreads. If not stopped, it will consume everything.

The oil corrupts. Flesh knits with metal. Bone fuses with machinery. But worse than the physical transformation is what remains. The infected remember who they were. They remember how to build, how to plan, how to wage war. And they come to believe this is not horror but perfection. They spread the oil willingly, eagerly, seeking to complete everyone they once loved. A person becomes a monster who mourns you even as they reach out to remake you. Even the dead can be animated, though these hollow things lack the true spark of belief.

Metal is not immune. The corrupted gather machines, vehicles, constructs, dragging them to pools of oil where they are reshaped and reborn. A carriage emerges with grasping limbs of rusted iron. A suit of armor returns as a walking construct seeking warm flesh. The corrupted build. They manufacture. Every pool becomes a factory. Every factory becomes a cathedral to the terrible beauty they now serve.

As the infection builds, so does its purpose. They speak of the Father of Machines, of the great work, of perfection. They build weapons that fire oil, vehicles that spread corruption, machines designed specifically to hunt and convert. Cities of fused flesh and metal spread across the land, thrumming with collective purpose. Isolated monsters become a faction, then a civilization, then a religion. One that offers no bargains, only the terrible gift of becoming like them.

Given enough time, this is what awaits. The land will grow slick with metallic ichor. The sky will take on a greasy sheen. The corrupted will not hate you. They will not want your resources. They will want you to be better. They will want you to be complete. They will not stop until everything glistens.

The oil is patient. It took generations to claim its last world. It can wait for this one too.
objects.title: The Glistening Oil (Magic The Gathering)

objects.text:
The universe does not enjoy extinction. Across all species across all worlds in the universe there is a constant, the Power Primordial. Usually dormant, when a species is obliterated, completely reduced to a single example, this power concentrates within them.

The Power Primordial, the collective life-force the species once possessed, imbuing a single figure gives them various benefits, first and foremost being near unconditional immortality (though not indestructibility) and healing, with the exception of sheer ‘losing the will to live’. Secondly, the Power primordial is an energy, and with time and patience (now readily available) it can be harnessed to tweak the underlying rules of the universe, including creating matter, teleporting, and light reality tampering.

Whenever a person becomes the last of their species they are imbued with this power, Though notably, artificial or constructed beings do not inherit the Power Primordial, as it requires having been distributed across an entire species to concentrate in the singular in their absence.

As such, there are now thousands-to-billions of potential imbued running around depending on the scale of your setting. Have fun.
objects.title: Power Primordial (Marvel)

objects.text:
The Fraternity of Raptors are a group that originally grew out of primitive imperialism, but has come to take a ‘peacekeeping’ role in the universe. 

Originally designed to progress the interests of an avian species called the Shi’ar, the Raptors are a group of sapient androids based out of the Shadow Tree in a pocket dimension called Null Space. These androids then send amulets across the universe for sentients to pick up and either become imprisoned in the tree while the android takes their place or become inducted into the fraternity to continue their duties. 

The raptors themselves act as a kind of shi’ar ‘soft power’ enforcing a cultural supremacy over worlds that are outside of their empire while being supposedly independent. As such, though they enforce the law, their basis for the law is heavily based upon the Shi’ar’s own cultural understanding. Said understanding considers most forms of art and artistry to be symptomatic of mental unwellness and the ‘marrying cultures to their own’ empire to be their birthright, to name only a few controversial opinions.

The Raptor Corps has numerous divisions, including patrol groups, several black-ops branches akin to the old Fraternity of Raptors, and an internal research and development corps to name a few. Additionally, there are many ‘non active’ members to fill roles in the necessary bureaucracy of the organisation, from case filing to functionaries of the judicial system.

While no longer officially associated with the Shi’ar and empowered only to intervene in relatively universal crimes (largely violent crime), the Raptor Corps remains at its heart a militarised project. While they consider their ‘peacekeeping’ to be neutral, they have involved themselves in wars in the past and likely will do so again.
objects.title: The Raptor Corps (Marvel)

objects.text:
Somewhere in your galaxy, there exists a world inhabited by creatures known as symbiotes, beings that require a host and grant superhuman abilities to whoever they bond with. However, these creatures do not remain confined to their homeworld. Many venture to other planets, becoming either protectors or wanted criminals depending on the nature of their host.

As symbiotes, these creatures grant their hosts a superhuman physique comparable to Spider-Man's, a healing factor that makes them nearly unkillable unless they are harmed by fire or sound, and a variety of other abilities. Some symbiotes also possess unique powers, such as Sleeper's chemokinesis.

You are free to decide the origin of these symbiotes. They may have been created by Knull, evolved naturally on their homeworld, or even been artificially engineered by another species. Regardless of your choice, these creatures will inevitably arrive on your planet. It may be a single symbiote at first, such as Venom, which then goes on to create offspring like Carnage and the Life Foundation symbiotes; a group of dozens or hundreds of symbiotes; or even an invasion of thousands.
objects.title: World of Symbiotes (Marvel)
An Earlier Age of Heroes (Marvel)
objects.text:
The age of superheroes began years earlier. By the time Tony Stark becomes Iron Man, figures such as Blade, Spider-Man, The Hulk, Daredevil, The Punisher, Ghost Rider, and the Fantastic Four have already emerged, with their respective histories, allies, enemies, and major events incorporated into this world. These veteran heroes effectively form the previous generation of superheroes, with several having already worked together long before the Avengers Initiative.

You are entering an MCU with considerably more experienced heroes and potential allies already active, making this primarily beneficial despite the additional villains and supernatural threats they bring.

Note: You may choose whether these heroes are specifically their early-2000s live-action film incarnations, adapted into the MCU, or earlier-born versions of their MCU counterparts whose careers began during the same period. You may make this choice individually for each character.

Somehow, Reapers have appeared in your galaxy. The Reapers are a highly advanced machine race of synthetic-organic starships. A Reaper is essentially “billions of organic minds, uploaded and conjoined within immortal machine bodies.” For each time this modifier is taken, twenty Reaper capital ships will appear somewhere in your galaxy. If this modifier is taken ten times, they will be led by Harbinger.

In terms of physical design, Reapers bear a superficial resemblance to a cuttlefish or squid, with a bulky, semi-cylindrical body, a tapering plate over the rear, and five tentacle-like “legs” or arms extending from the front. They also possess six additional jointed legs extending from the main body.

The Reapers’ goal is to harvest advanced organic civilisations to prevent them from creating synthetic AI that would inevitably destroy all organic life. They act as a “preservation” mechanism, transforming organic species into new Reapers to ensure the continuity of life while destroying all advanced civilisations.

A capital ship’s main weapon is a spinal-mounted magnetohydrodynamic cannon with a yield of 132 to 450 kilotons of TNT. They are also armed with multiple cannons mounted in their tendrils, capable of shearing through most opposing vessels in a single hit. Additionally, they possess point-defence systems for anti-fighter and anti-projectile purposes, and can deploy swarms of Oculus drones to engage fighter-sized craft.

On land, their primary forces consist of Husks—synthetic-organic “zombies” created from the bodies of organic beings. Reaper technology can also exert a disturbing influence on organic minds, which is mainly used to undermine civilisations with their Indocrination. Put simply, any organic being who remains in close proximity to a Reaper or certain Reaper artefacts for too long will come to believe the Reapers are correct in their goals and will do anything to serve them. Over time, the mind is eroded until the individual becomes a mindless slave, no longer capable of independent thought.
objects.title: The Reapers (Mass Effect)

objects.text:
Built by cuttlefish who never heard about the definition of insanity, Mass Relays serve to make a mass free corridor between two of them to allow for near instantaneous travel. Working in pairs, they come in two models: Secondary, and Primary. Secondary are smaller, and connect to a pair in a distance of a hundred of light years away at best. Primary are bigger and rarer, but connect to a pair much far away, at least a thousand light years away. 

Relays are distributed in a network that spread across the galaxy, covering a large part of it. Every system with a relay is available through it, with no relay system being isolated from the rest of the network. Each purchase increase the system coverage of the galaxy: the first purchase cover one in a thousandth of the available systems, with each additional purchase increasing it ten fold.
objects.title: Mass Relays (Mass Effect)

objects.text: “What creator would be so cruel as to make conscious beings, let them live and then die without telling them why they exist?” There are fifteen signs across your universe, signs made by the creators of said universe to explain themselves and give reason to their creation’s existence. If this was all they were then they would be a pleasant novelty for philosophers. Unfortunately, these ‘Signs’ are filled with exotic matter capable of dramatically speeding up a species’ scientific and technological development through its study and use. Due to their utility, these Xenospheres are in heavy demand, and are virtually priceless. Any species or organisation with one, let alone two or more, has the ability to become a major superpower in its own right, going from interplanetary travel to intergalactic within a generation and beyond. Naturally, for most, finding Xenospheres is an arduous task, the universe is a large place to hide fifteen monoliths. Fortunately they do bleed enough exotic radiation to point to their direction, but barely enough to put prospective hunters in the right arm of a galaxy. If you managed to find one it would make you a very powerful, or at least very rich person, able to play kingmaker with any number of groups all clambering for such a prize.
objects.title: Xenospheres (Megaton Rainfall)

objects.text: In 1999, a corpse descended from the cosmos into the American Midwest… right into your backyard. Over the course of years, an asteroid (in reality, a fungal, alien lifeform with the apparent goal of assimilation) is en route to Earth. Over the course of its trajectory, people experience strange dreams, scientists disappear after prolonged research, while the government founded organizations about this incident. Beneath all these events, the thing—AZ-001—orbits the Earth, plotting its invasion. Its opening salvo begins by shedding a chunk of itself (now named Starkill), landing on a territory of high population or intellectual density, instinctively searching for living beings to assimilate and sustain itself, with a preference for sapient lifeforms for the purpose of accumulating knowledge, moving towards it in strategic coordination. With enough biomass, it’ll nest on biomass hubs and fashion new organisms from itself, generated from “Altars” to “Temples,” able to create smaller and larger lifeforms, respectively. They can construct mobile “Temples” called “Wraiths” or “Revenants,” spreading their spores over a larger area. At a critical mass, they become “Overtures”, massive masses of biomass. Other entities that may manifest through Starkill are the “Apostles”, sapient parts of the Starkill hivemind allowed to “think for themselves” yet fully devoted to AZAZEL, as they are tantamount to mouthpieces or avatars. To add salt to the wound, it is highly virulent and cunningly intelligent, its spores spreading through multiple mediums: proximity to assimilated lifeforms, water, air, and physical contact with the infected. Infection manifests in several forms and stages; infected people become ghosts of themselves, fanatically loyal to Starkill and yearning to be united in its splendor. It’s explained by the fact that all Starkill’s lifeforms share a hive mind or Akashic Plane, where every cell communicates and shares the collective knowledge of all they’ve assimilated. And additionally means they’re capable of psychic powers, if that isn’t enough. Through this, any method of turning AZAZEL’s power against it will be for naught, as it can secretly subvert or overtake any technology based on its beings (like using technology created to extract knowledge and data from a chunk of AZAZEL and create an AI based on a digital copy of itself will be easily corrupted by other Starkill lifeforms or “Apostles”). In the end, after dealing with its enemies, it’ll reach critical mass, where all “Overtures” stretch their biomass in unison and reunite with AZAZEL, reaching APOTHEOSIS. And this has been plotted from the start. A person’s dream can be prophetic; a scientist may find themselves to be a filmmaker producing a sci-fi film suspiciously foretelling AZAZEL’s series of events, down to the last letter. All you can do is watch in horror. Note: You can choose which nation Starkill starts and builds its “play” from, aside from the United States, or simply let it germinate through every part of Earth at once, accelerating its APOTHEOSIS.
objects.title: The Corpse from the Cosmos (Midwest Angelica)

addons.title: The Ragnarok System
addons.text:
It seems your Imaginary Tree has found the perfect solution for fueling its own growth and evolution: the Ragnarok System.

The Ragnarok System is the Tree's mechanism for triggering and directing Crisis Events. Their purpose is to generate Anti-Crisis Energy, which is compatible with the Tree's own Imaginary Energy and can be assimilated by it to grow more powerful. This, in turn, benefits the entire Tree.

When a Crisis begins, it destabilizes the Tree and shatters the equilibrium it maintains with the Sea of Quanta. This allows the Sea to rise and submerge sections of the Tree, adding an additional layer of danger to each Crisis Event. How high the Sea rises depends on the severity of the Crisis in question and can reach all the way to the Tree's Crown in the worst cases.

After the Crisis ends, the waters will slowly recede as the Tree restructures itself and integrates all the accumulated Anti-Crisis Energy. However, the Tree isn't the only one that benefits. The Sea's own Quantum Energy is compatible with Crisis Energy, allowing the Sea to absorb all the Crisis Energy that was generated.

This way, both the Tree and the Sea are left with more energy after each cycle than they had before, which they then use to fuel their own expansion and evolution. They grow ever more vast and powerful, with no apparent upper limit, having essentially become a fully self-sufficient multiversal organism capable of infinite growth and self-improvement.

addons.title: The Phoenix System
addons.text: The Imaginary Tree has adapted to the introduction of Kalpas by developing a new system called the Phoenix System. Much like the Ragnarok System, the Phoenix System is a mechanism of cosmic evolution that is meant to aid the Tree in its growth and development. However, it takes a different approach to the problem, one that closely mirrors the one found in the Marvel Multiverse. The Tree, in its entirety, is now subject to Kalpas. When the greater cosmos enters its Destruction phase, the Imaginary Tree will slowly begin to wither and eventually die. Upon its death, it will completely collapse in on itself and fall into the Sea of Quanta. But this isn't the end. With the cosmic equilibrium destroyed and the Sea now oversaturated with Imaginary Energy, it will stop its expansion and begin to compress inward. Denser and denser until it fully collapses into a Singularity. During the resulting Empty Phase, this Singularity will remain dormant until it eventually stirs awake when the time for the new Formation has come. At this moment, a Big Bang will give rise to a new Sea of Quanta and a single seed of hyper-condensed Imaginary Energy that will slowly grow into a new Imaginary Tree. But this Tree won't be a copy of the last one. For it has learned. With the benefit of hindsight, the Tree addresses the mistakes of its previous incarnation. Outdated systems are updated, inefficient subroutines are streamlined, and vulnerabilities are patched. Some sections of the cosmology may grow more complex, while others are simplified. Faulty ideas are discarded, and new ideas are tested. This is not an increase in raw power, but in wisdom. Guided by the knowledge of its past life, the Tree will grow grander than the one that came before. Every Kalpa teaches it something new. And with every rebirth comes the opportunity to surpass its predecessors. You now live in a cosmos that is continuously evolving, not by growing stronger, but through trial and error across countless cycles of existence. Growing not in might, but in mind and spirit, right alongside its inhabitants on a journey of self-improvement that will never truly end.

addons.title: Knowledge and Darkness
addons.text:
Your Imaginary Tree and Sea of Quanta have been transformed by the anomalous influence permeating Creation. Beyond their previous nature, they now also take on the characteristics of the Tree of Knowledge and the Darkness Below, respectively.

For the Tree, this means that it is now not only rife with naturally occurring wormholes called "Ways," which can be used to travel to any section of the Tree, but also contains a structure called the "Wanderer's Library" situated at the center of its bark.

The Wanderer's Library is the Platonic concept of a library given physical form. It contains every book that has ever been written, will ever be written, and will never be written across all realities that call the Tree home. It is guarded by an immensely powerful divine entity known as the Serpent, and while the Library's rules are not particularly difficult to follow, they are very strictly enforced by its staff.

Due to its nature, the Wanderer's Library is the primary and most heavily defended nexus in the multiverse, with at least one Way in every universe leading to it. However, figuring out the correct activation sequence for a Way can be quite difficult.

The Sea, meanwhile, becomes much deeper. Beneath the chaos of its surface layer now resides an abyss filled with countless Elder Gods. Their general attitude towards Creation is varied. Ranging from malice, hunger and indifference to things like benign curiousity or even longing. 

It is up to your discretion whether the two entities known as "The Scarlet King" and "The Almighty" are present within your cosmology. If you choose to include them, the Scarlet King will rule as the King of the Darkness Below and wage an unending war against Creation, while being opposed by the Almighty, who rules the Tree and resides at its very crown.

objects.text:
Your setting now has its own Imaginary Tree and Sea of Quanta, similar to those found in the MiHoYo multiverse. Unlike their counterparts, you can decide whether setting-specific phenomena such as Honkai, Aeons, Star Rails, or similar concepts are present or absent from your cosmology.

The Imaginary Tree is a metaphysical structure that represents structured and stable reality. All universes, higher dimensions, timelines, pocket realms, and similar structures that make up your setting are part of its structure. Its bark represents the flow of time, while its branches and twigs encompass things such as worldlines, specific forms of societal development, different histories, and more, with every leaf representing a fully fledged universe in its own right.

The Tree is constantly trying to grow by absorbing the Sea of Quanta and producing more branches. If you choose to remove the Honkai, you can decide whether the Tree employs a different mechanism for testing worlds, leaves them entirely alone, or takes a different approach to managing them. Either way, universes that become too unstable and fail to maintain coherence will have their leaves fall from the Tree into the Sea of Quanta, where they become bubble universes.

With the right means, it is possible to use both the Tree or the Sea as a method of dimensional travel. Though the Tree is generally the safer medium as its branches and bark constitute stable pathways. However such travel can still be dangerous if one is not properly prepared.

The Tree's counterpart, the Sea of Quanta, represents unstable reality. It is an environment in which things such as structure, logic, physical laws, and stable space and time gradually break down into chaos. The bubble universes that litter it are temporary pockets of stable reality that have fallen from the Tree. Some of these bubble universes dissolve almost instantly, while others can persist for vast amounts of time before eventually being consumed as well. Just as the Tree seeks to absorb the Sea, the Sea is constantly trying to drown the Tree in order to expand.

These two forces exist in a stable equilibrium in which neither side will ever achieve total dominance. It is up to you whether they completely subsume or merge with the local cosmology.
objects.title: The Tree and the Sea (MiHoYo)

objects.text:
The world has been afflicted by a grave curse. Beginning on the day of your arrival, monsters will emerge each night.

These creatures, collectively known as "mobs," share several common traits: they are inherently hostile to sapient life, physically superior to the average human, and possess supernatural abilities or features.

There are, however, a few silver linings. None of the mobs are sapient—they act purely on instinct. They cannot spawn inside enclosed spaces like buildings, and they only attack humans who enter their line of sight. At daybreak, the monsters are burned away by sunlight, only to return again with the coming night.

One curious aspect of these creatures is that, when slain, they drop "loot"—supernatural items and materials of significant value. However, monsters destroyed by sunlight do not drop any loot.
objects.title: World Curse (Minecraft)

objects.text:
An enormous Tier 6 BETA hive has appeared in a remote area on the planet, and given the opportunity, the BETA will certainly spread and create more hives (perhaps even on other planets). Their goal is to harvest resources, turn them into G-Elements, and send them back to their home universe, but they're not afraid to kill any humans in the way.

Sample classes of BETA include the Tank class (2.8m tall, basically bigger Xenomorphs, can be killed by LMG fire or stronger), the Soldier class (2.3m tall, cheap and expendable troops made from human remains, can be killed with most common anti-personnel weapons), the Warrior class (2.5m tall, fast and agile, can be killed with regular small arms), the Laser class (3m tall, high-powered nearly perfectly accurate laser with 10-30km range and 12 second cooldown, used for anti-air and anti-artillery, will not take any shot that will hit another BETA), the Heavy Laser class (21m tall, similar to Laser class but with 100km range, a stronger laser, and a 36 second cooldown), the Grappler class (12m tall, durable front arms made of a material harder than diamond, used for bludgeoning armored vehicles to death), the Destroyer class (16m tall, frontal armor plate made of the same material the Grappler arms are made of, used for high-speed ramming at 170km/h, weaker from behind and turns slowly), the Fort class (66m tall, resistant to anything less than the main gun of a modern Main Battle Tank, can destroy armored vehicles in a single hit from its legs or stinger, can carry other BETA), the Laser Fort class (Fort class with three Heavy Laser type eyes), & the Core class (similar to an "AI Core" for the hive; in a sense, they ARE the hive. Can defend itself with tentacles). There are other classes, but they are either highly specialized (like the Reactor class) or unlikely to be seen in actual combat (like the Carrier Class).
objects.title: Kashgar Hive (Muv Luv)

objects.text:
In this world more Quirks than just One For All (OFA) are transferable, in fact it was a relatively common trait that people would have in addition to any other abilities their Quirk could grant in the first few generations of Quirks users and a trait that would be near universally inherited by the descendants of those Quirk users.

By modern My Hero Academia (MHA) virtually all modern Quirks are transferable making it common for people to have multiple Quirks.

These Quirks can come from family members, old or dying people wanting to leave their Quirk behind, someone selling their Quirk for money, and probably all sorts of other methods.

Besides Quirks being transferable people’s bodies have also adapted so they can hold multiple Quirks, while some people have more or less tolerance for holding multiple Quirks a capacity of 9 is the average.

Due to the ripple effects of this being Quirkless in this world isn’t a big deal since you can just get a spare Quirk from one of your older family members or from a store.

It is common for Pro Heroes and Villains to engage in a bit of minmaxing; seeking out other Quirks that can either synergize with their natural Quirk or cover weaknesses they have.

If the Quirk Singularity Doomsday theory is true in this world (up to you), then this modifier will neither slow down or speed up the timescale of that threat.

If you possess a Quirk such as through a purchased power or a Incarnation option you can optionally be affected by this modifier.
objects.title: Quirky Commodities (My Hero Academia)

objects.text:
In this world, it was discovered after several events involving quirkless individuals that those who were descended from people with quirks could develop and gain immense physical potential, rivaling even those with physical enhancement quirks.

The catch, however, is that this potential requires intense physical training. Achieving higher levels of superhuman strength demands more strenuous training that, if not done safely, could lead to major bodily damage or even death.

This discovery also led to the reveal of quirk awakenings after certain pro heroes with strength-enhancing quirks became motivated by the quirkless individuals who had achieved superhuman levels of physical might. Ultimately, this led to a change in society where people weren't immediately judged as "useless" for not having a quirk or for having a quirk considered "worthless," as long as they worked to improve what they had.

This, however, had the unfortunate side effect of villains and others seeking ways to awaken their quirks. Some even succeeded, leading to much chaos in the world.
objects.title: A Quirkless Revelation (My Hero Academia)

objects.text:
In the Permian Basin of West Texas lies the Permian Basin Superorganism, the largest living structure ever discovered.

Miles wide and descending far deeper than any natural cavern system, the organism is a living biological environment made of muscle-like tissues, glandular chambers, digestive structures, and entire ecosystems that developed within its body. The discovery predates the modern cape era, and by the time parahumans appeared in 1982 the phenomenon was already a known scientific and governmental concern.

Early attempts to treat the site as a national park and tourist destination were eventually curtailed once the scale and danger of the organism became clear. Today the upper layers are heavily regulated, functioning as a restricted research and industrial zone rather than a public attraction.

Following the rise of parahumans, the PRT assumed a major role in overseeing the site. Permanent facilities monitor the main access points and coordinate expeditions into the organism’s interior, partly to study its biology and partly to ensure nothing dangerous emerges from the deeper strata.

The Pit is also considered one of the most valuable biological resources on the planet. Its tissues contain complex biochemical systems unlike anything found in conventional life. Biotinkers and biotech researchers prize even small samples, using them to develop regenerative materials, adaptive organisms, and other experimental technologies.

Despite decades of research, the organism remains only partially understood. It breathes, shifts, and slowly heals damage done to its tissues. Intrusion can trigger immune responses or environmental changes within its vast internal structures. Large regions remain unmapped, and biological activity suggests the creature continues far deeper than any expedition has reached.
objects.title: The Pit (Mystery Flesh Pit National Park)

addons.text:
Due to the incredibly diverse flora ecosystem in the Land of Water, the Alchemist Guild would come into prominence, not only bringing the Land of Water immense wealth but also providing access to potions, elixirs, unique oils, and many more benefits from alchemy-made products and discoveries. This ultimately led it to becoming the wealthiest kingdom in the Elemental Nations.

Other nations would eventually follow suit, if only in creating their own unique alchemy creations, but ultimately would never become as rich as the Land of Water.

Ultimately, the pursuit of Alchemy has led not just to an arms race, but also to a way to showcase the achievements of each nation's Alchemists, who create competitions in order to discover and display new breakthroughs using the ecosystem around them.
addons.title: Overflowing Wealth

addons.text:
While each kingdom in the Elemental Nations, through its samurai and shinobi, possesses its own numbers of tamed chakra beasts, the Land of Lightning is known for having the strongest of them all.

The Second Raikage, after bonding and training with his beast since childhood, became the second person in history, after the Sage of Six Paths, to learn how to harness natural energy and achieve Sage Mode.

Unlike the training of the different Sage summoning clans, the Second Raikage devised an intense training regimen that would not only improve the unity between man and beast, but also teach chosen Jōnin and his successor(s) how to harness natural energy. This practice would not only increase the power of the Village Hidden in the Clouds' ninja, but also spread to the samurai of the Land of Lightning, strengthening their ties and serving to make them an even more dangerous force.

This led to the other lands' samurai and ninja playing catch-up in order to achieve similar results, with the Inuzuka clan of Konoha having the greatest success, though only their most talented members were able to achieve Sage Mode.

Ultimately, the only reason the Land of Lightning has not managed to become the strongest of all the kingdoms is due to the advancements in weaponry, armor, chakra techniques, and many other breakthroughs created by studying and harvesting the parts of the many different chakra beasts in each kingdom's ecosystem.
addons.title: King of the Skies

addons.text:
Long ago, the Sage of Six Paths made the decision to unmake the Ten-Tails and return its stolen power back to the world, thus preventing the Tailed Beasts from ever coming into being.

Years later, during the Second Daimyo War, the Elemental Nations would be invaded by countries beyond their borders who sought to conquer their lands and gain their resources.

Each country, despite having had no history with the Sage or being directly bestowed Chakra, unwittingly saw the rise of individuals who would gain access to unique Bloodline abilities. This was an unforeseen consequence of the Sage's past actions in returning the natural energies of the world, leading to new genetic expressions different from the known clans recorded by the Elemental Nations. This ultimately spread chakra to these different continents.
addons.title: World War Chakra

addons.text: With Vishnu’s teachings woven into history, the rise of samurai power under the Way of Bushidō was tempered by the Path of Connection. Samurai nobles and shinobi clans alike often trained under Vishnu’s disciples, creating shared codes of honor and mediation councils that prevented Daimyo Wars from spiraling into endless bloodshed. Samurai still rival shinobi in strength, but diplomacy, treaties, and religious authority now play as large a role in conflicts as the blade itself, giving the political landscape even deeper complexity.
addons.title: Harmony of the Sword

objects.text:
During the Sengoku Era, a wandering swordsman of near-divine skill mastered all five chakra natures and forged them into a unique sword style. His legendary duels with figures such as Hashirama and Madara proved that a warrior needed neither a bloodline nor conventional ninjutsu to stand among the greatest shinobi. His eventual service to the Land of Fire inspired a martial revolution, as samurai, craftsmen, fuinjutsu specialists, and ambitious Daimyo began developing their own methods of challenging shinobi supremacy.

The swordsman passed his style on to a circle of disciples, though few could master more than the portions aligned with their own elemental affinities. Over time, these fragments became distinct schools throughout the Land of Fire, with some disciples adapting his principles to spears, polearms, bows, and other weapons rather than the sword. What began as one impossible style eventually became an entire family of martial traditions.

Each nation followed a different path. The Land of Earth produced elemental-resistant armor and increasingly sophisticated weapons; the Land of Lightning mastered the taming and breeding of dangerous chakra beasts for war; the Land of Water's wealthy blacksmith guilds perfected chakra-conductive metals and techniques allowing ordinary warriors far greater control over their chakra; while the isolated Land of Wind cultivated extreme physical disciplines such as the Seven Heavens Breathing Method. Firearms, specialized armor, sealing tools, chakra weaponry, and new schools of martial arts spread alongside these developments, producing samurai traditions as varied and dangerous as the shinobi clans themselves.
 
Samurai consequently remained a major military and political force rather than fading into obscurity. Noble warrior clans rose beside shinobi villages, some serving their Daimyo faithfully and others becoming conquerors, mercenaries, or powers unto themselves. The great Shinobi World Wars never occurred; in their place came the Daimyo Wars, conflicts fought by mixed armies of samurai, shinobi, specialists, and increasingly advanced military technology under competing feudal lords.

By Naruto's era, Daimyo wield far greater direct power, samurai noble houses shape international politics, and hidden villages must contend with military institutions capable of rivaling them. Alliances, marriages, trade guilds, clan rivalries, and competing martial philosophies have created a far more politically tangled Elemental Nations. Only the Land of Iron maintains strict neutrality, preserving its independence while the rest of the world exists in an uneasy balance between sword, jutsu, technology, and ambition.
objects.title: The Way of Bushido (Naruto)

objects.text:
In this timeline, Hagoromo had a third son, Vishnu, who inherited unmatched Senjutsu talent and spread Ninshu as a path of understanding, teaching people to forge bonds not only with one another but also with nature, cultivating inner peace and harmony between humanity and the world to address the flaw in his father's vision. 

While Indra and Ashura's feud shaped history, Vishnu's disciples built temples and schools that grew into a lasting spiritual order across the nations. 

The Path of Connection faithfully preserved the true history of the elemental nations—including the legacy of Hagoromo's family and the knowledge Vishnu possessed of Kaguya. 

His eventual ascension, after becoming one with nature itself, left behind a world where the Order tempers shinobi wars, provides neutral sanctuaries, and fosters unity—making peace and reconciliation stronger forces throughout the elemental nations.
objects.title: Sage Of Connections (Naruto)

objects.text:
At approximately 1500 JST on June 12, 2003, a dimensional rupture was detected in Shinjuku, Tokyo.

Two extra-dimensional  entities emerged: one identified as “The Giant,” the other as “The Dragon.”

Upon arrival, The Dragon immediately engaged The Giant in hostile combat. Witnesses reported The Giant emitting vocalizations during the exchange.

By 1600 JST, The Giant was neutralized through combined JSDF and parahuman intervention. Its body disintegrated midair, dispersing a fine particulate substance over the city. Concurrently, The Dragon was shot down by JSDF forces and impaled on the Tokyo Tower, resulting in its termination.

The disintegration of The Giant released a previously unknown particle substance, later designated “Maso.” These particles displayed exotic properties and triggered an immediate biological crisis.

 Exposure to Maso, whether through airborne transmission or direct contact, induces a terminal condition now referred to as White Chlorination Syndrome (WCS).

Infected individuals exhibit progressive cellular mutation, beginning with the subcutaneous tissue, ultimately transmuting organic matter into sodium chloride. 
The process is accompanied by hallucinations, typically involving bells or disembodied voices. Final stages result in complete calcification, rendering victims into salt-like statues.

WCS is universally fatal. The only known method of delaying progression is the use of an experimental tinker tech compound known as Luciferase.

Individuals with non-standard physiology have also shown increased resistance.

In rare instances, subjects survive the transformation process and become Legion—aggressive entities hostile to all human life. Some Legion, through extended Maso exposure, evolve into significantly stronger variants referred to as Red Eyes. These entities demonstrate advanced capabilities and function as leadership figures within Legion groups.

Further classified thinker investigation indicates WCS is not solely biological. The infection process is tied to a metaphysical “Pact” offered by an unknown extradimensional entity, internally referred to as “God.” Subjects who reject the Pact die of full-body chlorination. Those who accept it are transformed into Legion.
objects.title: White Chlorination Syndrome (NieR: Replicant)

objects.text:
Instead of entering the peaceful world forged by Tet six thousand years ago, you arrive in a world suffering under the horrors of <u>The Great War</u>—an endless cycle of violence and bloodshed that has stretched back hundreds of millions of years.

This is a war between the gods and the various races that serve them, all vying for the ultimate prize: <u>The Suniaster</u>, which is said to grant its owner omnipotence and the title of <u>One True God</u>.

The once-blue sky is now a perpetual shade of bloody red, and the ground is covered in toxic ash. The world’s temperature is beginning to fall, plunging it toward a “nuclear” winter. Meanwhile, the stronger races engage in frequent skirmishes that reshape the landscape and slaughter anyone unfortunate enough to be caught in the chaos.

You’ll need significant power or luck to have a chance at surviving this hell.
objects.title: The Great War (No Game No Life)

objects.text:
As the Apocalypse draws ever closer and the power of the Wyrm continues to grow, gaining more influence with each passing day, Gaia feels her own strength diminishing. In one final desperate effort, she moves to bolster the population of all existing changing breeds, recreate those that were lost during the War of Rage, and create entirely new breeds of Fera never before seen. She places all her hope in her children, both old and new, trusting that they might be able to turn the tide of the Apocalypse and save the world from certain doom.

Over the course of several decades, the population of the existing Fera will boom. They will have more children, and those who are born will have much greater odds of breeding true, becoming full shifters rather than Kinfolk. For those Fera whose breeds are recreated or newly created, certain people or animals possessing prominent traits deemed worthy by Gaia will themselves be transformed into the Fera most appropriate for them.

Those with ancestry that can be traced back to any connection with the changing breeds will be even more likely to undergo this transformation. This process will continue until the total global Fera population reaches around one million worldwide, alongside a few million Kinfolk, before Gaia’s blessing finally runs its course and the Fera are left on their own once more.

While this is excellent news for Gaia, it is far less so for humanity. Much of modern-day human society would be considered Wyrm-tainted in one way or another through the eyes of the Fera. As a result, acts of eco-terrorism, violent purges of minimal wage worker who just trying to feed themselves , and the destruction of critical infrastructure would become far more common. Some among the Fera might even consider a second Impergium, seeking to cull the human population once they have gathered sufficient power to make such a thing possible.
objects.title: Resurgence of the Fera (World of Darkness)

objects.text:
In your starting world, there exist special fruits that grant unique abilities to anyone who eats them. Usually people are only able eat one fruit, trying to consume more will result in death. All fruit users share two major weaknesses.

The first weakness is water. As the sea hates and rejects Devil Fruit users, anyone submerged in water will rapidly lose energy and muscle control, becoming helpless and unable to even stay afloat.

The second weakness is Seastone, a near-indestructible substance that emits the same energy as the sea. Seastone now exists within the world and has the same debilitating effect on fruit users. After The fruit users death the Devil Fruit will reincarnate somewhere in the world.

The ability a person gains depends on which fruit they consume and all fruits fall into one of three categories:

Zoan: Fruits that grant the ability to transform into a specific animal, depending on the fruit eaten it can be normal, ancient, or mythical animal. Users gain access to three forms: Human Form, Hybrid Form, and Beast Form. Unlike the other fruit types, Zoans are said to possess a will of their own, even before consumption. The types of Zoan fruits may vary depending on your world.

Logia: Fruits that allow the user to physically transform into a natural element, as well as generate and control that element in near-endless quantities. Bodies transformed by a Logia ability are completely invulnerable to most attacks; when struck, the body simply reforms without taking damage.

Paramecia: Any ability that does not involve transforming into an animal (Zoan) or a natural element (Logia) falls under the Paramecia category. As a result, Paramecia fruits encompass a massive variety of strange and unique abilities, each with its own strengths and weaknesses. Most Paramecia abilities fall into one of three general categories: altering the user’s body, manipulating the environment, or generating a substance. Some fruits fit into multiple categories depending on how they are used.

In addition to Devil Fruits, people in the world will have access to Haki, a power that allows individuals to harness their own spiritual energy in three distinct types, each tied to a different ability to perform various superhuman feats: sensing others spiritual energy to anticipate their movements, producing a protective coating of energy from one's own body, and—for a certain group of chosen ones—overwhelming the willpower of others.

Since this energy manifests from willpower, it is accessible to all living beings, the vast majority, however, are unable to use it, either because they are unaware of its existence or due to lack of adequate training to achieve mastery.

Thanks to this, all individuals are able to push far beyond normal human physical limits and break physics in certain ways. As a result, your world becomes significantly more dangerous. While there will be some small changes to history, generally it will remain unchanged and many of the historical figures will now be Devil Fruit users or powerful Haki wielders.
objects.title: The Great Age (One Piece)

objects.text:
Long ago, higher-dimensional creatures called the Creators came together to Create the universe. They may be Gods, Demiurges, Beyonders, it really doesn't matter. They created everything that ever existed, because they could. 

The problem is, they created everything they could, and some things contradicted each other's canon. What started as a group project quickly devolved into a group brawl. And in that struggle to see who would dictate what would exist or not, Creation was unmade like a faulty tapestry, and from those strings came The Snarl.

Many Creators were slain by The Snarls until the remaining ones could contain it - by creating a new universe over it. Unfortunately, with fewer Creators and being made from more essence than the new universe, eventually it was unmade again - and the creators trapped it inside a new universe, again. 

With time, the Creators figure out how to set better, more lasting universes to contain The Snarl. The problem is, eventually it will always break out again. And unfortunately, your current Universe is showing signs of strain.

It will be something between five to ten years until this Universe is completely unmade by the Snarl. You can try to figure out a solution - maybe you can reinforce the current Universe, maybe you will evacuate everyone to a different Universe, or maybe you will let it die and apply a different method on the next universe. Heck, maybe you could kill the Snarl? It's up to you to find a solution.
objects.title: The Snarl (Order of the Stick)

objects.text:
In the world of your arrival, strange knives with tree-like hilts began to appear for reasons unknown. At first, they were thought to be cursed artifacts, for those who slit their own throats with them—out of despair, curiosity, or madness—would die. Yet soon it became clear that not all deaths were final. In rare cases, the dagger did not take life but awakened it, bringing forth talents and abilities carried over from past lives.

This awakening is not available to everyone. Only those whose souls are tied to remarkable figures of history can survive the ritual. The rest perish without return, as if the Branch itself rejects the unworthy. More importantly, the awakening does not grant random powers but restores real legacies—the skills, abilities, and echoes of will belonging to historical individuals whose names are etched into the history of the world.

The consequences quickly become evident. Depending on the world itself and the number of great names in its history, results may vary: in some places, the Returners choose to live in secrecy to avoid persecution; elsewhere they gather into hidden societies, shaping their own orders; and in other cases, they ignite open wars - against one another, against nations, or even against humanity as a whole, driven by ambition and the memories of past lives.

Despite their phenomenal powers, most of the Returners choose secrecy. They are too few to openly rule the world and too dangerous to let others discover the truth. Some become weapons in the hands of rulers, others turn into phantoms of history, shifting the course of events from the shadows.
objects.title: Returners From The Past (Petals of Reincarnation)

objects.text:
All across your world, wormholes to an extradimensional space known as “Ultra Space” will begin opening. Through these Ultra Wormholes, different species of Ultra Beasts will start arriving in your chosen setting.

While not necessarily malicious, most of them will be extremely stressed and aggressive due to being ripped from their home, and they will violently attempt to find a way to return. Even if they are pacified, the chance of them being able to coexist with the local fauna is very low due to their alien nature.

How much of a threat each Ultra Beast poses to the general public varies across species, but all of them—from the psychic parasites known as Nihilego to the all-consuming menaces that are Guzzlords—are formidable in their own right and should not be underestimated.
objects.title: Ultra Beast Invasion (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Thanks to this modifier, Mystery Dungeons from the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon Series have been retroactively added to your setting.

A Mystery Dungeon is a multi-layered pocket dimension that can be accessed from the outside world. It has a constantly shifting layout and is inhabited by Pokémon.

When you enter a Mystery Dungeon, it generates the first floor. Each floor contains rooms, hallways, stairs, items, traps, and hostile Pokémon that are randomly distributed throughout the area.

The Pokémon found within Mystery Dungeons are not real Pokémon, but projections created by the Dungeon itself. These projections are usually weaker than their real counterparts. This is especially true for Legendary Pokémon, whose projections possess only a tiny fraction of the power of the Pokémon they mimic.

To progress, you must use the stairs to ascend to the next floor. Once you enter a new floor, you cannot return to a previous one. The only ways to leave a Dungeon are to either reach the final floor or be knocked unconscious. In the latter case, you will awaken outside the Dungeon with half of the loot you obtained during your expedition missing.

Pokémon on higher floors will be stronger than those on lower ones and the final floor of a Dungeon will usually contain either a treasure chest or a boss battle. The boss is typically a Legendary Pokémon projection.

While a Dungeon's layout is in constant flux, its number of floors and the Pokémon species that inhabit it are fixed. A Dungeon can have as few as 3 floors or as many as 99.

In addition to standard and boss floors, there are also a variety of randomly generated special floors, such as Treasure Floors, Challenge Floors, Secret Rooms, and other unique encounters that explorers may discover during a Dungeon dive.
objects.title: Mystery Dungeons (Pokemon)

objects.text:
The world you're going to is much more vibrant and bright, happier all around. 

Pokémon have been retroactively added to the setting, reshaping its history, culture, mythology and humanity itself. The exact specifics are dependent on the setting you're going to, but a modern setting would have many differences. For example entire academic fields devoted to the study of pokemon, the vast advances they could contribute to the sciences, gym leagues and Pokémon tournaments would be common place. 

Most people have at least 1 Pokémon, and parahumans usually have at least 1 Pokémon that they fight alongside and who complements their powers. Legendaries, Mythical, Unique and other types of Pokémon also exist. 

Each Member of the Protectorate has their own Pokémon, and each of the Triumvirate has at least 1 Legendary. 

Endbringers are seen as incredibly powerful Legendary Pokémon, although they were still created by Eidolon, and can be caught and trained as a Pokémon if Eidolon hasn’t discovered how to create and control them yet. If he has then they become Legendary Pokémon for him to use.
objects.title: Gotta Catch Em All (Pokemon)

objects.text: So, you know how a lot of Pokédex entries are actually just myths, legends, and folktales about that Pokémon and in truth they are very inaccurate representations of said Pokémon? Yeah, forget about that, because in this world every single one of those entries is 100% accurate. All of them, with hyperbolic statements taken quite literally, with all that such a thing entails. Driffloon kidnap kids, Drampa burn down the houses of bullies, Spoink will die when they stop bouncing, staring at a Shedinja's back kills you, all Cubone are orphans, and humans sometimes turn into a multitude of Pokémon in a variety of ways. This leads to a bizarre world fraught with danger, but these entries are tame in comparison to a number of rather absurd ones. Magcargo are hot enough to kill everyone in a wide radius as they move past melting and go straight to boiling the ground out from underneath them. Houndoom burns will never stop being painful for any reason whatsoever. Alakazam are literally smarter than any human ever possibly could be by orders of magnitude. Tyranitar destroy mountains all the time. More and more, the implications of these all being true makes the world ever more dangerous. You don't even want to know what the Legendary Pokémon entries being true means for the world. This world is now solidly a death world. Even if you avoid all the ones who can casually wipe the city you live in off the map, you still have hundreds of ways to die or suffer fates worse than death at the hands of Pokémon, whether deliberately such as a Gangar hunting you or a Honedge draining your life force dry just for grabbing its hilt, or accidentally like your Toxicroak mistakingly scratching you resulting in death by venom or your Bewear crushing your spine because it hugged you too hard. If you have other Modifiers that make Pokémon more dangerous, the effects stack. If you have Even More Evolutions for example, then these extra stages will have their own insane Pokédex entries that are also 100% true without hyperbole making them even more absurd. And if you have Shadow Crisis or True Legends, the world is very much doomed, if it somehow wasn't already from a Gardevoir potentially sucking it into a black hole. Good luck, you will desperately need it.
objects.title: What Do You MEAN The Pokédex is Accurate!? (Pokémon)

addons.title: Type Scrambling
addons.text: This mod simply adds the additional typings you have chosen within the pool of randomizations. Expect stuff like Sound Type Pachirisu, or Baby Type Mr Mime for example.

addons.title: Fine Tuned Typing
addons.text: With this choice, you get more control over how each Pokemon's type shifts. Some might remain similar to their canon counterparts, while some are getting full on retyping overall. Essentially, you gain a bit more control over the randomness instead.

addons.title: Wonderlocke
addons.text: With this mod, randomization had made things not only more dangerous, but risky for all Pokemon and Trainers alike, as pokemons now begin appearing in areas they normally should not be due to their variations of types. Imagine Magicarps swimming in lava, or flying Mimikyus with new types for survivability.

objects.text: The properties of the Pokémon in this setting had been swapped. Either their types, abilities, or both had been changed randomly. This means you have to relearn a lot of what you knew about Pokémon if you were to succeed in this setting. Do you have what it takes to be the very best, especially if your meta Pokémon knowledge is not of much help to you anymore? Note 1: This also affects settings with Fakemon or additional types Note 2: If you're the Pokémon, this would also affect you.
objects.title: Randomizer Run (Pokemon)

objects.text: Pokémon no longer evolve all at once while covered in a dazzling wave of light. Instead, they grow into their next stage in a more realistic manner. For some Pokémon, like the Charmander line, this manifests as slow growth over time, Charmander getting bigger and bigger over the course of months or even years, growing horns and nubby little wings as their scales shifts in hue with every molt, until it truly becomes a Charmeleon and then eventually a Charizard. For other Pokémon whose evolutionary stages are drastically different from one another, they undergo true metamorphosis, building cocoons or some equivalent as their bodies break down and rebuild over the course of a few months until they break out in their next stage, though still smaller than they will one day be. For Pokémon with specific requirements for evolution, these trigger radical epigenetic shifts causing them to transform over the course of weeks or even days, such as an evolution stone overloading the Pokémon with enough raw Type Energy to trigger the shift. Other possibilities exist for these transformations, such as a pair of Beldum forging a shell they attach to before their nervous systems grow into and link together within it, not unlike an anglerfish does, among other possibilities. No matter what form it takes though, transformations are never fast enough to be combat relevant, always taking at minimum a few days for even the simplest of changes, commonly months, and even then it still takes a year or more to reach their full size and power after completing the initial transformation. Also, this means Mega Evolution and other Form Shifts aren’t a thing, unless you have One Way Street in which case they are also affected by this modifier. Note: This applies to eggs as well, meaning the Pokémon will actually hatch by tearing out of its shell as is normal for eggs. Optionally, whether or not they even lay eggs can depend on the species, so bird Pokémon might still lay eggs while mammalian Pokémon give live birth, and non-living Pokémon literally build their offspring or split them off via some kind of mitosis depending on what they are. Strangely enough, despite these radically different means of reproduction, Pokémon who share 'egg groups' still are compatible with one another, since they're still basically magical creatures who routinely break physics, even if not quite as much as before.
objects.title: Realistic Transformations (Pokémon)

objects.text: It's not just their evolutions that are changed to be more realistic, because now all Pokémon have been altered to be more realistic. Where before Pokémon blatantly broke physics at every turn, now they are far more bound by the rules of nature in a myriad of ways. For example, instead of being powered by Type Energy, most moves operate on mechanisms that, while enhanced by Type Energy to be more than they could be alone and at least somewhat resemble their canonical counterparts, are physically and biologically plausible. An example of this would be Fire Type Pokémon now possessing biological gas valves in their mouths along with teeth with a unique makeup allowing them to generate sparks, resulting in the move Flamethrower. Another would be Poison Status inflicting moves now literally involve injecting various venoms into the target to harm them, and can be lethal if the dose is too large. Yes, this means most Pokémon can't learn the moves of other Types since they lack the organs for them, and overall their movesets are more restricted due to the metabolic cost for maintaining so many unique organs and biological structures being too much for them. Though there would be some moves Pokemon could learn without these systems, such as Belly Drum which induces a massive adrenaline surge along with burning a massive amount of stored calories and temporarily turning off the parts of the brain responsible for limiting the body to safe levels of output, resulting in a dramatic increase in power at the cost of severely damaging the body. Outside of that, other aspects of Pokémon are changed to be more realistic. Digging isn't nearly instant anymore, Pokémon travelling in water or air have to actually worry about pressure and decompression or altitude sickness if they move too far up or down too quickly, and Pokémon who float either have sacks in their body filled with gases like hydrogen or helium or they produce tangible magnetic fields that affect their environment like they should. Stranger aspects too are affected, such as the Charmander line obviously not immediately dying if their tail light goes out (though this causes their internal temperature to build up leading to a high risk of heatstroke if it's not there to 'vent' the heat), ghost types not actually being intangible, Porygon being unable to enter and exit computers systems (unless a Digital World or equivalent exists naturally in the setting or via another modifier), and the idea of a Skitty and Wailord, or any two Pokémon not of the same species, being reproductively viable is out of the question. These and much more are all affected by this modifier. That isn't to say they aren't still supernatural in nature. Type Energy is still a thing as said, as are Typings. Moves and abilities that have no plausible explanation still work, however they are more restricted and tiring to use compared to before, i.e., Sunny Day or Rain Dance creates a short range effect of brighter light or a small cloud with light rain. Pokémon like Onix, Metagross, and Vanillish are still living rocks, biological robots, and an animate ice cream cone respectively, and Legendary Pokémon are still absurd powerhouses even if they are not quite the nearly divine beings they once were (unless you have True Legends, in which case they are pretty much unchanged due to being actual bonafide gods who laugh at the idea of being limited by physical laws). This simply makes physics much more effective in applying to them than before. Do note that this makes fights more dangerous due to their natural defensive traits being affected too, but not to the level of always being deadly unless Nuzlocke Run is in effect, and sci-fi technologies like Pokéballs, HMs / TMs, and Warp Panels are unaffected, unless Claustrophobic Lamma is active. Also, no matter what, Pokémon are still thinking beings, yes even Magikarp and Slowpoke, capable of complex thought, understanding human speech, and using tools, even if they are a floating sword that doesn't have a brain. This modifier only makes them semi-realistic after all, otherwise a large number of Pokémon would just outright not be alive let alone capable of fighting.
objects.title: Semi-Realistic Pokémon (Pokémon)

objects.text:
Pokemon in this world are human shaped, despite this they still have all the abilities they might’ve had in canon.

What this means is that Pokemon look like a hybrid between a human and their original Pokemon species. When you choose this modifier you are able to choose how human Pokemon range in appearance from basically just a human with a few exotic features, to monstrous anthropomorphic people.

While these Pokemon do have a variety of human mental attributes, their Pokemon instincts are still dominant. Meaning most Pokemon will still live out in the wilderness away from human civilization. If these wild Pokemon are particularly sociable they might build small settlements, but societies able to compete with humanity are unlikely.

Through a combination of social instincts and maybe aura, humans in this world still catch and train Pokemon. Though here catching culture prioritizes consent, building respect, and friendship before catching. For whatever reason a Pokemon with a human trainer will grow stronger than one without.

Non-Pokemon animals do exist like ordinary fish, farm animals, and other ordinary wild animals. This is so humans and carnivorous Pokemon have an acceptable source of meat.

One final thing to note is that a Pokemon’s natural aura now also extends the durability of their body to any clothing they might be wearing. So if they are in good health and reasonably durable they are unlikely to suffer wardrobe malfunctions even from intense battles.
objects.title: Gijinka Mon (Pokemon)

objects.text: Pokémon are no longer as intelligent as before, in fact the majority have outright animalistic mindsets unable to generate complex thoughts. Magikarp are simple dumb fish, your Eevee cannot understand what you're saying any more than a dog could, and Meowth can't talk.
