This makes them much more dangerous since you can't negotiate your way out of a confrontation with a wild Pokémon, and training them is much harder since you have to teach them like an actual animal, to the point that many regions require Trainers to be adults with licenses from specialized Trainer academies in order to catch a Pokémon to begin with due to how hard it is. If paired with Nuzlocke Run then expect this to be one of the deadliest professions in the world, with wild Pokémon nearly universally feared and domesticated Pokémon being limited to rare breeds specifically selected for docility and high obedience to humans. Only a select few Pokémon actually have human level minds, mostly those from the Human-Like Egg Group like Gardevoir or Machamp, certain mechanical or Psychic Type Pokémon like Metagross or Beheeyem, and the majority of the Legendary Pokémon. These Pokémon may in fact have special laws giving them more rights than normal Pokémon or could even be recognized as citizens depending on the Region they are in, treated not as wild animals but as another species of people depending on how xenophilic / xenophobic the culture is and where on the bright / dark scale the setting is located. No matter what this modifier massively changes the way humans interact with Pokémon, mostly negatively.
objects.title: Feral Pokémon (Pokémon)

addons.title: Apocalocke
addons.text: The apocalypse had made training pokemon much trickier than it already was prior. Not only are both Pokemon and people more desperate and dangerous, but a lot of pokemon had outright gone extinct or adapted further to barely survive in this new norm. Certain types might not even exist anymore, it is that harsh.

addons.title: Soul Link
addons.text:
Pokemon catching is no longer just folks going out and throwing pokeballs at random Caterpie. With this choice, almost every trainer has their soul tied to pokemon whom are fated to be part of their team. As such, most trainers only have a small team, with a single ace they are closest with.

The deepest of bonds forges the strongest of Trainers and Pokemon, but also the biggest risk. For a sufficiently bonded Ace and Trainer have their souls so tied that one dying might cause the death of the other. So do treat your partner well, for they are your lifeblood.

As a side effect, Battle Bonds and Mega Evolution seem to be more common.

addons.title: Hardcore Run
addons.text: As if Nuzlocke Run isn't hard enough, the world of Pokemon has now considerably tipped further into the realism scale. Forget having deadlier battles, Pokemon are now legitimate wild animals handled only by a few professionals whom know what they are doing. You are not gonna be a Trainer at 10 years old, you will need a license, degree, and sufficient funds to even have a chance at making it as a professional in this field. This is pokemon but legitimately grittier and more realistic.

objects.text: Pokemon battles are now inherently more dangerous, having grown in violence to the point that death of pokemon is common. Not only that, it is harder to catch pokemon, making it trainers a bit of a rarity nowadays in fear of losing their beloved partners. Expect a more brutal journey should you select this.
objects.title: Nuzlocke Run (Pokemon)

objects.text: The Pokémon setting might be solarpunk, but it’s capitalist solarpunk. Now, Nuzlocke Run affects the very socio-economic constraints and pressures of trainer life. Most people can’t necessarily afford to go on a journey, much less keep it going for the long time it takes to actually train your partners to be ready to take on all 8 gyms. Even then, Pokémon have to eat- and their dietary needs reflect their size. Most people can’t afford to keep fully evolved dragons, or Torterra-sized Pokémon, or Arceus forbid a full grown *Wailord*. Most forms of trying to skimp on the monetary requirements carry a significant increase in risk- if you can’t afford to feed fully evolved Pokémon, how will you survive camping in the wilderness? One night of bad luck and you’re dead, after all. The rangers aren’t omniscient, the routes are immense in the real world and repels are about as effective as a flu shot- in that they’re developed barely faster than they cease to be effective and even before then, they CAN fail. Especially if you buy the cheap, off-brand kind - the only kind most people can afford, which is also true of much of the typical hammerspace technology of the original setting. Pokémon Centers give shelter for a nominal fee, but there’s never a shortage of trainers trying to save money and to serve the most people possible, the moment you get a room you get a maximum amount of time you can be there before no amount of money will prevent the center from evicting you. How long you can stay, and how long before you’re allowed back at that center is inversely and directly proportional to how large demand is (respectively). Seeing as you’ll probably need to stay in town to train, you’d best be able to find a more permanent arrangement- which again, costs money. In short, to be a trainer there are only 3 real roads to being anything but a hobbyist who goes on vacation from their real job every five to ten years to get their next badge. The first is to be rich or close enough, such as having rich parents, being related to highly successful trainers or even Gym Leaders or having relatives working in the industry who can give you some degree of connections and support through their jobs. The second is to essentially win a scholarship by impressing the boards responsible for granting them, such as being sponsored by Professor Oak (who is a board unto himself, as his lab is immensely successful). The third is to just not lose. Fighting other trainers for money is inherently designed to funnel the funds of the hopeful many into the ruthless, lucky or talented few; if you can keep fighting and not losing, reinvesting all your winnings into your team and maintaining your momentum through setbacks and lean times, you could go the distance. But this is Capitalist Nuzlocke- frankly, just be born rich. And don’t die a fool.
objects.title: Nuzlocke Capitalism (Pokemon)

objects.text: Any Pokemon species that previously lacked an evolutionary line, or whose line contained fewer than three stages, has been granted new evolutions to reach this minimum. A Ditto for example will now be a first stage evolution, able to evolve with enough experience. Kangaskhan's joey is now its first stage, with the second stage resembling the little one's mega evolution form. This further extends to branch evolutions, for example each of Eevee’s branched evolutions now can evolve one final time into greater forms. Even legendary Pokemon with single stages now have additional forms, though whether their canonical base form is their first, second, or third stage evolution may be variable. Note: Some of these original evolutions may require triggers like evolution stones or high friendship, and some may even be branch evolutions. How common this is and what they are is optionally up to you or can be left to chance.
objects.title: Original Evolutions (Pokemon)

objects.text: In addition to the standard three stages each Pokemon has, they now also possess additional evolutionary stages, each Pokemon now having a full six stages in their evolution path(s). Considering that their original final evolution stage is as strong as ever, this means true final stage Pokemon are typically around pseudo-Legendary strength, with some being a match for the canon mid-tier Legends, while a Legendary Pokemon's true final stage is on a whole other level. Some of these additional evolutions are rather strange, and if you have Branching Evolution (Pokemon) as well, things will get even more bizarre. Pokemon Journey's are now much more dangerous due to the possibility of encountering a city killer going way up, with trainers frequently grouping up or being chaperoned for protection until they too have a strong extra stage Pokemon to defend themselves with. Tournaments now require additional safety measures for their audiences due to the frequent use of such Pokemon, and caring for such Pokemon can be a hassle since the majority are some form of giant beast. In addition, if before Legends such as Groudon and Kyogre fighting was a potential disaster, then in this world their final stage forms battling one another is a potential apocalypse.
objects.title: Even More Evolutions (Pokemon: Evolved)

objects.text: Every Pokemon in the world that is capable of evolving now possesses the potential for vastly expanded evolutionary pathways, transforming simple linear progressions into sprawling, intricate trees of possibility. Every Pokemon’s evolution can branch into multiple distinct forms based on a combination of factors including environment, held items, moves known, time of day, friendship, and even the specific composition of a trainer's party. A single species like Growlithe might evolve into a Fire/Rock variant if exposed to a sunstone near a mountain, or a Fire/Water variant if leveled up while knowing Rain Dance near a volcano. Eevee’s evolution is also no longer limited to one form per element but instead gaining access to every elemental combination imaginable, such as a Fire/Ice Eeveelution, a Grass/Poison form, or even a Dragon/Fairy variant. Beyond these standard environmental and conditional branches, hidden evolutions have surfaced, requiring special circumstances to unlock. These special evolutions are often unreplicable, making each unique to their bloodline. Shiny Pokemon now also possess their own distinct evolutionary branches entirely separate from their common counterparts. By default, this only affects Pokemon that can naturally evolve. However, if you have another modifier that adds more evolutions, such as Original Evolutions (Pokemon) which allows all Pokemon to evolve, then every Pokemon affected will possess multiple branching evolution paths. There could be multiple Ditto lines specializing in empowering certain transformations, alternate possibilities for what an Unown can become based on its shape, and even the Legendary and Mythical Pokemon each have a multitude of possible forms. The possibilities are endless.
objects.title: Branching Evolution (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Pokemon are no longer constrained by species boundaries as any two Pokemon can produce hybrid offspring that blend the traits, types, and abilities of both parents. A Charizard and a Blastoise might produce a hybrid with steam-based Water/Fire typing, shelled wings, and cannons built into its wing joints, while a Gengar and an Alakazam could create a psychic ghost that phases through walls while telekinetically hurling spoons, its transparent form revealing a floating brain. The resulting hybrids inherit a mixture of abilities from both parents and often develop unique signature moves that neither parent could learn alone.

Hybrids occur naturally in the wild wherever the territories of different species overlap and inter-species bonds form organically. Environmental factors play a significant role in natural hybridization, with certain regions acting as melting pots where diverse species coexist in close quarters. For example volcanic islands might host Fire and Ground type hybrids, while misty mountain passes see frequent cross-breeding between Flying and Ice types. These wild hybrids adapt to their ecosystems in unique ways, sometimes outcompeting purebred species in niche environments where their combined traits offer distinct advantages.

If you wish, any canon Pokemon may now be retroactively changed to be a hybrid of two or more purebred Pokemon species that have since gone extinct, their original forms lost to history while their blended descendants continue to thrive in the modern world.
objects.title: Hybrid Pokemon (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Well, now you've done it. If you thought Pokemon hybridization had made predicting the typing of a random pokemon difficult, think again, because you've made it MUCH worse.

Pokemon are no longer limited to 2 types, and in fact mono-type pokemon are practically unheard of. 3-type pokemon are extremely common, and occasionally you'll meet a 4-type pokemon. This doesn't neccessarily make them more powerful, mind, since for every new STAB they get they're also losing immunities or diluting resistances. 

The real problem is that the specific typing can change within the same pokemon lineage. Whether this is due to hybridization over time is something Pokemon researchers have been debating for a very long time, but the outcome is that every lineage has a type-pool, and any specimen can have any type within that pool. Some lineages have bigger pools, some have a greater tendency to have more types in a single specimen, and all of that can vary because someone bred that lineage with something else.

In short, the only way to know a pokemon's typing is to make some educated guesses based on their appearance and figure out how different attacks affect them. On the plus side, if you have Type Bias (Pokemon), your pool of available lineages has just become MUCH wider.
objects.title: Variant Multi-Typing (Pokémon)

addons.title: Further Human Evolution
addons.text: Due to the nature of Humans in this setting, humans are also allowed further evolutions as well. Whatever the next stage of humanity might be depends on you, whether it be us gaining more monstrous traits, more types, more abilities, etc, that is the next step to the pokemon called Humans.

addons.title: Different Types of Pokemon-Humans
addons.text: Taking both of these two Human Pokemon Modifiers makes it so that Human Type Humans and Normal Type Humans live together, with the Normal Types being far more common. Human Types are since seen as a rare Delta version of some sort, more commonly able to exist with dual typing as opposed to the Normal Type Humans. Human/Normal Humans exists too, and they were theorized to be hybrids born with enough ancestors from two sides of the human spectrum. We have since become the most dominant and adaptive Pokemon in the world because of this.

addons.title: The Pokemon Furry Scale
addons.text: Hybridization had since affected Gijinka Mons and Humans as well. A lot of the Gijinka Mon population has gained the adaptive traits of Humans, furthering their civilization's development as proper partners with the humans whom bond with them. Monstrous creatures still exists however, thought to be very distant relatives of humans, gijinka mon, and animals, with these creatures moreso resembling the pokemon we know from the games. With these modifiers, we can now trace a rough estimate of a scale between Human, Gijinka, Pokemon, and Normal Animals, all of which coming from a same ancestor that has since diverged long ago. Evolution is truly fascinating indeed.

objects.text:
Rather than sharing a distant common ancestor, humans are now understood to be a direct branch of the Pokemon family tree, making them far closer relatives to creatures like Pikachu or Machamp than to any primal ape. This reclassification places humanity within the known taxonomy of Pokemon species, fundamentally altering the scientific and cultural understanding of what it means to be human.

In practical terms, this means that every human is classified as a Normal-type Pokemon with no evolutionary stages, possessing the inherent ability to learn and use a wide variety of Pokemon moves through training and practice. Much like how Eevee possesses the genetic flexibility to evolve into numerous elemental forms, humans possess the cognitive and spiritual flexibility to master moves of any type given sufficient dedication. Furthermore, under specific and rare conditions, humans can undergo temporary Mega Evolution or similar transformative states, unlocking immense power for a limited duration.

As a consequence of this redefinition, individuals who are born with innate psychic abilities or a natural command of Aura, as opposed to those who must study and train to achieve such feats, are now officially recognized and catalogued as Shiny humans within the global Pokedex system. Pokeballs now incorporate failsafe filters calibrated to recognize human genetic markers, preventing accidental capture or targeting. These safety protocols are mandated globally and regularly audited by international regulatory bodies. However, black market technicians are able to jailbreak these safety protocols, selling modified capture devices to criminal organizations, human traffickers, and unethical collectors.
objects.title: Humans Are Pokemon (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Alpha Pokémon are a phenomenon that originally emerged in ancient Hisui during the crisis caused by the time-space rift. They are larger and stronger than other members of their species, possess glowing red eyes, and are usually highly aggressive.

But no more. Alpha Pokémon have now retroactively become a global and common phenomenon, with roughly one in every hundred Pokémon being born as an Alpha. Fortunately, without the rift their aggression is at normal levels for their respective species.

Despite this, traveling through the wilderness is now more dangerous due to the presence of potentially territorial wild Alphas, and the Gym Circuit has become more challenging as many Gym Leaders, Elite Four members, and Champions now have Alphas on their teams.

Even among Legendaries, Alphas can now occur in species with several members.
objects.title: Alphas (Pokemon)

addons.title: Divergent Evolution
addons.text:
Normal animals can now be classified as alternative evolutions or relatives of other Pokémon, albeit with fewer fantastical abilities and access to far fewer moves. There has been some debate as to whether these animals should instead be reclassified as simply Normal-type Pokémon.

Overall, the world seems to have become a little more mundane, as Pokémon are generally weaker, no longer being powerful enough to guarantee the extinction of most normal animals. The strongest Pokémon are also considerably rarer.

addons.title: One Way Gimmick Risk
addons.text: While this is not always the case, there have been several instances in which these gimmick evolutions have become permanent. This is, of course, notably dangerous and carries significant risks when using any of these power-ups. As a result, laws surrounding their use are much stricter, as there have been numerous cases of Mega Evolutions and Dynamax Pokémon being left to rampage.

addons.title: Metamorphose or No?
addons.text:
Evolution is a bit more nuanced than initially understood. Normally, Pokémon simply metamorphose into their evolved forms, physically shifting their bodies as they grow. However, sometimes mutations occur during birth, causing Pokémon to appear as smaller versions of their later forms. This is a relatively uncommon phenomenon and isn't particularly dangerous to the parent Pokémon.

These smaller, later-stage Pokémon have higher stats than their unevolved counterparts, though they typically have difficulty learning new moves as quickly as their unevolved counterparts. Finally, it is also possible for Pokémon to grow up without evolving at all.

Further research into Pokémon evolution is still needed.

objects.text:
Pokémon do not evolve from one species into another. Every Pokémon is born or hatched already in what would have been considered its final evolutionary stage, just smaller, weaker, and less developed. A baby Charizard has tiny wings, a small flame on its tail, and can only produce embers instead of flamethrowers, but it is unmistakably a Charizard, not a Charmander or Charmeleon. A baby Dragonite resembles a miniature version of the adult, not a Dratini or Dragonair. Magikarp does not exist; instead, baby Gyarados hatch directly, weak and harmless despite their fearsome adult shape. 

The only transformations that remain are temporary battle states like Mega Evolution, Gigantamax, or form changes such as Castform’s weather-based shifts, none of which are permanent or heritable.

For Pokémon that previously had multiple possible final evolutions, those forms are now considered separate species within the same biological genus, related like humans are to chimpanzees rather than like a caterpillar to a butterfly. Eevee does not exist as a base form; instead, baby Vaporeon, baby Jolteon, baby Flareon, and all other elemental Eeveelutions are distinct species that hatch directly, each with its own immature version. A baby Poliwrath and a baby Politoed are cousins, not stages of the same line. A baby Hitmonlee, baby Hitmonchan, and baby Hitmontop are separate species that share a common ancestor, not evolutions of a single Tyrogue, which never existed.

This change is retroactive; the concept of Pokémon evolution as a metamorphic process has never existed in this timeline, and all historical records, Pokédex entries, and scientific understanding have always reflected this reality.
objects.title: That’s Not How Evolution Works! (Pokémon)

objects.text:
Temporary battle transformations are no longer temporary. Mega Evolution, Gigantamax, Primal Reversion, Ultra Burst, and similar mechanics are now permanent, one-way metamorphic processes. When a Pokémon meets the conditions to transform, such as holding the correct Mega Stone with a strong Trainer bond, possessing the Gigantamax Factor in a Power Spot, etc, the change triggers and never reverses. The Pokémon's body, typing, ability, and stat distribution are permanently altered to match their transformed state. A Mega Charizard X is no longer a Charizard borrowing power; it is now simply what that Charizard has become, forever.

This is treated no differently than any other form of Pokémon evolution. Mega Stones become single-use catalysts, consumed in the process and treated with the same cultural weight as any evolution stone like a Fire Stone or Thunder Stone. 

For forms that previously had time limits or required specific battle conditions, those restrictions are gone. The transformation simply happens when conditions align, and afterward, that Pokémon lives its entire life in that state. Pokémon that previously had access to multiple mutually exclusive Mega Evolutions (like Charizard with X and Y) can only undergo one permanent change. The first catalyst used determines the irreversible path, cementing divergent evolutionary futures for the same species. This is treated identically to branch evolutions like Gloom into Vileplume or Bellossom.

This change is retroactive; the concept of a "temporary transformation" has never existed in this timeline.
objects.title: One Way Street (Pokémon)

objects.text: Life has occurred over millions of years, Pokémon and humanity living side by side. Sometimes they war, other times there are peace. But for the longest time, they were distinct in their capabilities, humans being fairly normal compared to Pokémon. But with this modifier, this has changed. Whether as a recent phenomenon or something known long ago, Humans discovered they were the most distant of cousins to Pokémon, being their own type dubbed "Human-Type." Like Pokémon, they could learn various moves, and UNLIKE Pokémon, they could learn any move that existed and create more over time. Of course, Aura Guardians and Psychics are in their own league and considered a subset of these humans, but otherwise, the sky is the limit for growth for the most part. Each human generally falls into a secondary typing. The rarest humans, pure luck being a known cause for this happening and no genetics or anything able to change that, are given a third type and can inherently learn more moves, although obviously at a reduced rate due to sheer time and effort needed. A Fire type can obviously learn Fire-type moves, Steel Steel type moves, Fairy type moves, etc. TMs can be used on them, but generally aren't suggested since it's been found that T/HM's take a lot longer to work on humans than Pokémon, up to about 8 hours while you can't interrupt the process without wasting the TM/HM. This has lead to a relative change in how Pokémon society works. While indeed, stuff like the gym challenge still exists, battles where humans participate against themselves or other Pokémon are more common, with ALL Gyms being allowed to choose whether or not the trainer and/or themselves fight as well. Other details are left up to interpretation, but the world has still changed quite a bit now that humans can also join the fray.
objects.title: Human Type (Pokémon)

objects.text: Now introducing: Mon! ... Just Mon. Due to a fundamental adjustment in the nature of the world, ways to conveniently store your friendly (or not so friendly) monsters- like pokeballs- no longer exist. Further, Pokémon can no longer be digitized or converted to conveniently storable, transferable, and/or carriable energy at will. No more shoving your hundred-pound snail made of lava into your pocket to get through the forest. Nor a way to shove them into a PC to then withdraw them later, like in the next city. Nope. Now you gotta do it the hard way. Hope you don't start a forest fire. As if giving living, breathing, super weapons to toddlers wasn't already enough of a risk... Other storage items still exist in the world. Maybe even better versions due to necessity, with all the food and other supplies one needs to carry around for their team on journeys. With no convenient little cages one can shove an annoying, lazy, smelly, thousand-pound Snorlax into, moving or capturing Pokémon that don't want to be is now a lot harder and more expensive. On the downside, this makes wild Pokémon rampages and such far harder to descalate and solve, with relocation of troublesome Mons becoming, occasionally, an impossible hassle. On the upside, Poachers are far more likely to quickly get what's coming for them. How exactly the world has adapted to these changes is up to author fiat, but good luck getting your Wailord to the tournament grounds.
objects.title: Claustrophobic Lamma (Pokemon)

objects.text: Before, Legendary (and Mythical) Pokémon were certainly powerful beings even by Pokémon standards, with many of them being practically godlike such as Palkia and Dialga with power over space and time itself. However, they were still able to be defeated by normal Pokémon and captured by trainers to use in battle. Even Arceus, the literal creator of the world, was nearly killed by a simple meteor in Pokémon: Arceus and the Jewel of Life. Well, no more. Taking this modifier makes all of the Legendary (and Mythical) Pokémon become a pantheon of actual bonafide gods. Even the weakest of Legends would require a full team of Level 100 Pokémon with a Type Advantage, maxed out EVs & IVs, and specialized Items and Abilities just to survive an actual battle against them. As for the strongest of them, they are less Pokémon and more the personification of concepts or systems of reality that need to create avatars just to interact with the world, and the mere idea of Arceus’ avatar being even so much as inconvenienced by a planet killing asteroid slamming into it is completely laughable. As for what they are like, Legendary Pokémon are living forces of nature and divine might. Most humans and Pokémon can’t stand in their presence unless they suppress their Aura, with many having true forms that merely seeing up close could result in the deaths of weaker individuals. These Legends maintain important aspects of not just nature but reality itself and will rarely acknowledge the majority of people unless they are particularly noteworthy for whatever reason, such as being powerful in their own right or being involved in major events such as a prophecy. The idea of someone catching one and using it as part of their team is completely laughable, and capturing it and harnessing its power with some machine as seen in the movies would just result in the person responsible getting wiped off the face of the Earth with an attack that could level islands. If you have Gotta Catch Em All (Pokemon), then not even the Triumvirate has any Legendary Pokémon on their team unless the True Gods modifier is in effect or something, and the Endbringers are obviously not treated as Legendary Pokémon either, with it being likely that at least one was killed because they angered a Legend due to their constant attacks, the others changing their behavior in response. If someone ever somehow did convince a Legend to join them, it’d be less they are their Pokémon now and more that the Legend acknowledges them as their Champion or their only human friend, and would likely result in that human being elevated to the equivalent of saint status in that Legend’s religion (and yes, there will be entire religions that worship some or all of the Legends since they are literal gods). Great for the trainer and their Pokémon who are liable to receive boons from the Legend, not so great for anyone who so much as scratches them since that is a great way to get smited. The only way to truly outright capture a Legend would be to be at least as strong as them, meaning being a god slayer or god in your own right, with a high-Tier 2 or low-Tier 3 power or equivalent needed to beat even a young Shaymin. Doing so would instantly make one among the most famous and / or infamous worldwide, revered and feared by literally everyone. Meanwhile, Legends like the Creation Trio would require star killing power to even have a chance against a mere avatar, and Arceus himself would require more than that, being at minimum as powerful as Scion's avatar when not holding back. The only reason humanity even exists is because of their general benevolence or at least willingness to leave mankind alone most of the time, with those who hate mankind forced to abide their existence due to being outvoted. Even still, this obviously affects the setting in a number of ways. Religion is more common, Legends are treated with far more respect and wariness, and fights between them can reshape continents if they aren’t careful. More than once human civilization has been nearly annihilated whenever Kyogre and Groudon, the Legendary Bird Trio, or any other Legends fought. Entire organizations exist whose sole job is to keep track of and appease them, and various laws and customs were created just to avoid angering them, such as environmental protection laws concerning maintaining water purity to appease Suicune for example. This is a world of living Legends and Myths, with all that such a thing entails. Good luck. Note: There may or may not be multiple instances of some Legends. If so, then they are either treated as twin (triplet, etc.) gods for the weaker Legends such as Shaymin, or they are one Legend with multiple bodies, such as a regular and shiny Rayquaza being two separate avatars controlled by the real Rayquaza who is the consciousness of Earth's stellar defense system. Also, if a Legend somehow dies, expect literal disasters to ensue due to them no longer maintaining whatever aspect of nature or existence they are responsible for and their lingering power going out of control.
objects.title: True Legends (Pokemon)

objects.text:
A new layer of divinity has been added to the pantheon: the Demi-Legends. While the True Legends themselves remain unchanged, they now each possess Demi-Legend variants that serve as the bridge between them and mortals.

In terms of power and nature, these Demi-Legends are much closer to the Legendary Pokémon of the canon setting. The relationship between Demi-Legends and True Legends is comparable to that between demigods and gods in the Percy Jackson series. Like their counterparts in that setting, Demi-Legends act as servants of their respective Prime(s). For example, Demi-Suicune would travel the world purifying rivers and lakes on behalf of the True Suicune.

The origins of these Demi-Legends vary. Some may be the offspring of a True Legend and a mortal. Others may have been created directly as servants. For the greater Legends, they may even be sapient emanations born from their Prime's overwhelming power or intentionally weakened avatars created to interact with mortals more easily.

Naturally, this means that most intelligent villains will shift their ambitions toward capturing and exploiting the Demi-Legends, as they are significantly easier to confront than their respective "parents."

Even so, this comes with a major advantage. You no longer have to choose between the awe-inspiring majesty of the True Legends and the familiar appeal of the canon Legendaries.

Now, you live in a world that embraces both.
objects.title: Demi-Legends (Pokemon)

addons.text: As if to adapt to the environmental pressures that pokemon puts them through, a lot of animals have since began to evolve further. Fiercer. Wilder. Creatures start to grow into becoming proper threats to humanity and pokemon alike, with the aggression to back it up. The line between pokemon and animal blurs further and further. This simply becomes a much more dangerous world than what we expect of Pokemon, as the missing link between the two types of species fight for survival, with us humans in between.
addons.title: Primal Evolution

addons.text: As if the conspiracy can't get anymore complicated, Pokemon seems to have their own conspiracy too. Though they are within an alliance of sorts with the animals, they aren't full on partners. They are only semi united by their shared view that humanity is the enemy. Now, this is a three-way war instead.
addons.title: Pokemon Conspiracy

addons.text: There's probably something in the water, cause now even the pokemon gets to manifest strange abilities as well, albeit in a bit rarer case compared to normal animals. Now you might have to end up dealing with superpowered spearows or even more fiercer legendaries. This world just got a bit more dangerous.
addons.title: Powered Pokemon

objects.text: Instead of supposedly replacing all animals within the world with pokemon of all types, this world mostly follows the same logic as earlier iterations of the franchise, in which animals still do exist alongside their powered counterparts, and are somehow not driven into an early extinction considering how powerful pokemon can be comparatively. Through unexplained means, normal animals still remain rather numerous despite this change in the ecosystem. Pokemon classification is thus now more in depth, analyzed like how you would any other living organism. Efforts are of course maintained by zoologists to maintain the delicate balance of this world, making sure the less common pokemon counterparts of normal animals don't immediately overrun them to extinction. This also ends up explaining the age old question of where people get meat in the pokemon world (the answer? Both animals and Pokemon). Overall, this world is just a little more grounded than the normal pokemon world. Research on the difference between normal animals and pokemon is still being studied, and there's much to learn from where evolution diverged which resulted in some rats for example gaining the ability to excrete lightning. Maybe you'd find a lot of joy in this realm as a professor?
objects.title: Animals and Pokemon (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Ever thought a Pokémon possessed or should have a certain typing but didn't? Well, with this modifier, you can now retype any species of Pokémon you wish, either by adding a subtyping to an originally Monotype Mon, changing either one of a dual-type Pokémon's types, or changing a Monotype Pokémon's typing from its original typing into another.

For example, you can have it so Regular Mewtwo is now a Psychic/Dark type, change either Regular or Mega Gyarados into a Water/Dragon type, or change Happiny, Chansey, and Blissey from Normal-types into Fairy-types.

Do note that by itself, this modifier will only use the canon 18 types.
objects.title: Retyped Pokémon (Pokemon)

objects.text:
The Professors' meddling with their Time Machine have done far more damage than anyone will ever realize. Dimensional cracks from two different paradoxical timelines have begun to form in various regions across the world. Through these dimensional rifts, different species of Paradox Pokémon will start arriving. Paradox Pokémon are Pokémon hailing from either one of two version-exclusive timelines that Professors Sada (Scarlet)/Turo (Violet) found with their Time Machine. Past Paradox Mons resemble primeval and ancient variants of familiar Pokémon, while the Future Paradox Mons resembles futuristic, robotic variants of familiar Pokémon.

While not necessarily malicious, they will be extremely stressed and aggressive due to being ripped from their home, and they will make sure you know their stress. Unlike the Ultra Beasts, while the chance of cohabitating is not impossible, the Paradox Mons will still be an invasive species of sorts, and without a known gender system, it is unknown if they are capable of reproducing outside of their home timelines.

How much of a threat each Paradox Mon poses to the general public varies across species, but all of them—from the brutish cave elephant known as Great Tusk to the cold-blooded breakers that are Iron Valiants—are formidable in their own right and should not be underestimated. Additionally, the Raidons and the Past/Future Paradox variants of the Legendary Beasts & the Swords of Justice will be among the roster of Paradox Mons appearing in your location.
objects.title: Paradoxical Invasion (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Your world now has its very own COAL-style chat system. This system connects all Legendary and Mythical Pokémon in the world through one vast Aura Network, allowing them to interact with each other on a regular basis.

In practice, the chat operates very similarly to Discord. All Legendaries are innately able to create an account for themselves. Once they have an account, they can chat with other members, read and create threads, take pictures, and even livestream music or videos. Arceus serves as the Administrator and highest authority, with several other high-ranking Legends, such as the Creation Trio and Zygarde, acting as Moderators to help manage the chat and keep things peaceful.

Beyond allowing Legends to socialize, the chat is also used to help them coordinate their duties and work together to resolve problems and deal with threats. As a result, the world has become measurably safer, and organizations and individuals who seek to exploit or harm Legendary Pokémon will have a much harder time succeeding in their goals.

If you are a Legendary Pokémon yourself, you may choose to create an account of your own.
objects.title: COAL Server (Pokemon: Chosen One's Adventures with Legendaries)

objects.text:
It seems that someone made a rather terrible mistake in the past. Whether it was Team Cipher thinking they could rule the world, some idiot fully corrupting the Rainbow Wing and then letting Marshadow touch it, an ancient flawed-prototype Legendary being accidentally released, or by some other method, whatever the case Shadow Pokemon now plague the world. Unfortunately, however, unlike in Pokemon Colosseum or XD: Gale of Darkness, there is no convenient way to purify them.

Shadow Pokemon are Pokemon corrupted by darkness or negativity, which "closes the door to their heart", giving them a boost in power while also rendering them psychotically hyper aggressive to all regular Pokemon and humans. While they can occur naturally in rare circumstances, most were corrupted using specialized machinery or direct infusions of negative energies, with certain powerful Shadow Pokemon and all Shadow Legendaries being able to also spread the corruption to surrounding Pokemon.

As a result of past events, the world has had to deal with literal millions of Shadow Pokemon for at least half a century. Entire Regions have been devastated, as without a method of purifying them (any hypothetical blueprints for a device capable of such being lost in the initial outbreak), the Shadow Pokemon ended up killing countless people and Pokemon, leading a far harsher world. Nowadays things have settled into a tense equilibrium, society functional but damaged, as between a fifth to a third of all Pokemon have been corrupted.

Most Regions require Trainers to be at least 13 minimum to go on a journey, and all must carry weapons such as guns to defend themselves if a Shadow Pokemon attacks them out of nowhere. Gym leaders now have the additional duty of dealing with Shadow Pokemon attacks, defending their territory with their lives; people like the Sensational Sisters or other such can no longer get away with slacking off or just giving away badges, which now serve the additional function of showing off how strong a Trainer is in the event a crisis requires recruiting local help to deal with.

All Pokemon must learn to fight lethally if required, with many wild Pokemon changing their behavior to adapt to the new world. For example, Snorlax might now live in groups with one awake at all times with Munchlax scouting out the area while foraging to warn of incoming Shadow Pokemon, as a sleeping Snorlax is a dead Snorlax without protection. This increased aggressiveness adds to the danger Trainers face on their journey.

Society is affected in other ways too. Air and sea travel is dangerous due to potential Shadow Pokemon attacks, such that any travel requires the vehicle to have mounted weapons and high level Pokemon escorts, effectively killing the passenger cruise and flight industries. Relations are more tense as regions are more desperate for resources, and society has partially regressed to more feudal cultural structures with nobility, warrior traditions such as knights and samurai, and walled towns with armed city guards being readopted in large parts of the world. Meanwhile, some regions are outright defunct, consisting of scattered bands of survivors fighting one another for resources while hiding from roaming hordes of Shadow Pokemon, and a few are graveyards where literally everyone was killed in the initial crisis, such as the Ranger Regions as Capture Stylers are worse than useless against Shadow Pokemon.

Worst are the Shadow Legendaries, corrupted beasts of immense power capable of single handedly threatening entire regions. Fortunately they were all sealed away thanks to the sacrifice of the Champions of old, but all it takes is one idiot with delusions of grandeur to release one for the world to be in danger once more. The only reason the world survived their first rampage being because of the intervention of the non-corrupted Legendaries, who are now much more active trying to maintain the world and slaying the occasional pseudo-Legendary or Dynamaxed Shadow Pokemon.

There is still hope though. Some people, due to specific bloodlines, unique connections to certain Legendaries or ancient artifacts, or just having the exact right power in crossover settings, can indeed purify Shadow Pokemon. They are incredibly rare though, such that in Worm for example they would be rarer and more sought after than powerful Tinkers, Thinkers and Trumps are combined. Theoretically, such abilities could be studied and the principals used to create mass-producible purification technology, but all such endeavors have failed up to now.

Outside of that, it is technically possible to capture and train a Shadow Pokemon, and in rare cases even somewhat rehabilitate them until they act like a normal if somewhat aggressive Pokemon. However, the likelihood of this working is very slim, only 0.1% of attempts succeeding. Overall, this crisis has made the world much worse off than normal, and it will take a significant amount of work to fix even if mass producible purification technology becomes available due to the sheer number of Shadow Pokemon if nothing else.
objects.title: Shadow Crisis (Pokemon: Shadow of Time)

objects.text: You know how in canon a lot of Pokémon Trainers have a bias towards one specific Type of Pokémon? Well, now instead of being a preference or a practical move to save effort on training and caring for multiple different Types with unique needs almost all Trainers have such a bias due to it being an actual phenomena. Humans must now bond with Pokémon in order to properly control them, their aura resonating with their Pokémon over time resulting in a subconscious empathic link allowing for them to actually listen to orders and making them more docile and thus safe to be around. Most Trainers will have a limit to how many Pokémon they can bond with at all, some only having one or two Pokémon they can train and use at a time, averaging at around five or six for League level trainers, with most Champions and Elite Four being at the peak of what is normally possible with as many as a dozen they can control at once. On top of that, everyone now has a Type Bias, a particular Pokémon Type their aura resonates with above all else. Attempting to bond with a Pokémon that isn’t within your Type Bias is possible but takes up multiple ‘slots’, making it not worth doing for most Trainers. Because of this, most Trainers become mono-Type specialists, at most seeking out dual-Typed Pokémon to cover any weaknesses. It is possible but extremely rare to have a dual-Type Bias, expanding the number of Pokémon they can bond with without drawbacks since they only need one Type to match one of their Trainer’s Biased Types. Attempting to go past your limits to bond with more Pokémon isn’t usually possible, resulting in an exhausted Trainer with a confused Pokémon that is likely to just wander off to find some other person to be their Trainer or return to the wild after smashing their Pokéball. Because of this, most Trainers will first be required to find out what their Type Bias is before then receiving a Starter Pokémon of that type, such as a Rattata for a Normal Type Trainer or a Caterpie for a Bug Type Trainer, with only exceptional Trainers given proper Regional Starters. Very rarely there are exceptions to this rule, individuals who can bond with any number of Pokémon of any Type. These Limitless are incredibly rare, less than a dozen being born in a given generation at most, with most people instinctively finding them disturbing, offputting, and even outright terrifying until they get to know them due to a subconscious uncanny valley effect. Protagonists like Ash Ketchum, Red, or those of other settings in a crossover are pretty much guaranteed to be such exceptions, along with (some of) their rivals like Gary Oak. You may freely choose one or two Types to be your Type Bias, or leave it to chance, in which case it will likely be influenced by whatever your strongest powers are such as a Brute having a Fighting Type Bias or a cryokinetic having an Ice Type Bias, or dependent on your personality if you choose Artifact or No Powers as your power origin.
objects.title: Type Bias (Pokémon: Eldritch)
Multiabilities (Pokémon: Elite Redux)
objects.text:
Let's make battles even more convoluted, shall we?

With this choice, every Pokémon possesses more than one Ability. These could be Abilities innate to them, such as their canonical Abilities, including Hidden Abilities. They could also be new Abilities that almost any Pokémon can learn on their own.

Either way, every Pokémon is powered up even further, as you have to keep in mind how each Ability interacts with the others, their synergies, and their counters. You also gain access to technology that allows you to mix and match the Abilities a Pokémon has, similar to how you can relearn or forget moves, and so on. Abilities are no longer something Pokemon are stuck with forever in this case.

Abilities are passive effects, after all, and a great Trainer should know how to work with them just as much as they need to fully understand their Pokémon.

Overall, this simply makes Pokémon battles a little more complex.

Instead of being already part of the natural environment from the start, Pokemon are instead digital creatures that ended up spawning into this world when the Digital World and the Real World became one at one point. This makes it so that both Digimon and Pokemon exist side by side, with the world being a perfect fusion of the two.

What once was Pokemon now can Digivolve into further forms like Digimon could, this includes special Digivolutions such as Armor Digivolution, Spirit Digivolution, Jogress, etc. Both Digimon and Pokemon now also posses Pokemon types with the same effectiveness chart as is in the normal game. People also now use Digivices to capture Monsters, though you aren't limited to only one partner. Overall, this is a whole new world, with both settings expanding cause of it.
objects.title: Digital Pokemon (Pokemon/Digimon)

objects.text:
The Dragon breeds of How To Train Your Dragon (Movies/TV/Games continuity specifically) have been retroactively inserted into the Pokémon world. They are now all Dragon-Types, many of them dual types as well, and due to their access to Type Energy, significantly more powerful and dangerous than they were in the original setting. Furthermore, these dragon breeds gain evolutionary forms, and as such the shape with which you are familiar is usually their second evolutionary form (and many have a third). However, some of them may already be the third evolution (such as in the case of Crimson Goregutter) or be the first evolution instead.

All first evolution Pokémon added by this change have as a Hidden Ability "Incorrigible", which makes them immune to Charm, Confuse or Sleep conditions. It also makes them much more difficult to train, as they many simply ignore you in any situation where your respective lives aren't on the line.

Red Death, Purple Death, Foreverwing, Shellfire, Bewilderbeast- all these are extant Pseudo-legendary lineages, with the largest and oldest of their kind being so dangerous as to survive battles with lore-accurate lower order Legendaries (as in Moltres or Entei, compared to Giratina, Palkia or Arceus). Many specimens are extremely aggressive. Due to the presence of these new and dangerous dragons, the world is significantly more dangerous now than it was before.

If you have How To Train Your Dragon, the Archipelago is a region in the Pokémon world inhabited by the cast of the HTTYD setting, focused on these Dragon-Types, where they're most common. The cast of HTTYD lives there, as can you, Berk being the starting town. The region is home to three Legendaries of its own: Jormungandr (Dragon/Water), Hraesvelgr (Dragon/Flying) and Nidhogg (Dragon/Dark).

If you have Dragon Friend, you can pick one of these breeds to be your starter, and have a natural talent for exploring the wilderness and training all Dragon-Types.
objects.title: How to Train Your Dragon-Type (Pokemon/How To Train Your Dragon)

objects.text: Pokemon are more monstrous, having traits typically seen in Monster Hunter, thus raising their danger level but also making the ability to tame them even more rewarding. Humanity has since evolved alongside their monstrous breatheren, with the attempts to tame these monsters being more involved and bloody. Monster Hunter creatures also becomes categorized as Pokemon as well. With this modifier making even pokemon battles huge spectacles with Trainers fighting alongside their monsters.
objects.title: Monstrous Pokemon (Pokemon/Monster Hunter)

objects.text:
What have you done?!

Somehow, the current amount of types isn't enough for you. With this choice, you have added more elements into pokemon. Whether it be popular ones like the long requested Sound Type, to meme ones like Too Many Type's Baby and Uno Reverse, to any other Type of your making, the world of Pokemon has just gotten even more complicated.

How this affects the environment, the new type charts, or even when these new types were discovered (if they aren't already existing even before you came in) is wholly up to you. Otherwise, this choice has an extra perk of potentially making it like how Too Many Types does it, which is having all Pokemon be Triple Types. That last bit depends on you however, as this could function as regular pokemon still, only with some Pokemon gaining or being reassigned new types (such as Chatot becoming a Sound/Flying as a quick example). Lastly, you may choose whether this is distributed randomly or if you'd rather pick every type changes.

Regardless, it is a whole new world, may Arceus bless the researchers cause they're gonna need it.
objects.title: Too Many Types (Pokemon)

objects.text: It seems like the gap between mortal and Legendary Pokémon has just become a lot narrower. From now on, all Pokémon have a spark of divinity inside them that, if properly nurtured, can allow them to achieve apotheosis and become genuine new Legendary Pokémon. But while the potential for godhood now lies dormant within all Pokémon, that doesn't mean it's easy to draw out. Quite the opposite, in fact. There are several requirements that a Pokémon must fulfill to even attempt ascension. First, they have to have reached a level of strength and mental fortitude equivalent to that of a Champion-level Pokémon, at a minimum. Next comes desire. They need to actively want to cast off the shackles of mortality and become something more. Third, and most difficult of all, they need to achieve enlightenment. Specifically, they need to achieve enlightenment about themselves: about who and what they are, and what they wish to become. Usually, this takes the form of them studying and attuning to their own Typing in a way similar to a Cultivator trying to comprehend a Dao. As their enlightenment grows, they slowly stop using their Types and instead become their Types. For example, a Raichu may stop being an Electric-type Pokémon that shoots lightning and instead gradually transform into Lightning in the shape of a Pokémon. Ascension is not a quick process like Evolution. Instead, it is a change that occurs over decades or even centuries, with the Pokémon's body slowly changing as it adapts to its new nature. For some Pokémon, the changes may be relatively small, with the end result looking similar to a permanent Mega Evolution. Other Pokémon may transform into living landmarks. It is also not required for a Pokémon to be fully evolved to attempt ascension. It is helpful, certainly, but not necessary. A Pikachu like Ash's or Red's is just as viable a candidate as Leon's Charizard or Cynthia's Garchomp. If you have taken any of the modifiers that turn humans into Pokémon, then it will now also be possible for humans to ascend as well. Upon completing their ascension, they will become ageless and be virtually indistinguishable from naturally born Legends. In terms of power, these Mortal Legends can grow all the way to the point where they can compete with canon mid-tier Legends like Ho-Oh or Lugia on mostly equal terms. If you have the True Legends modifier, however, these Mortal Legends generally cap out at the level of either low-tier Legends or powerful Demi-Legends. This modifier is retroactive, which means that there is a decently large number of these Legends already present in your world. However, their effect on history will have been rather minor, as most of them tend to either prefer seclusion from the world and/or have a habit of taking extremely long naps.
objects.title: Mortal Legends (Pokemon)

objects.text: The Legendary and Mythical Pokémon in your setting now have the ability to take on a mortal disguise, either as a human or as a regular Pokémon. These disguises allow them to hide their power and presence, allowing them to walk among mortals undetected. This could be for missions that require a more low-key approach, such as spying on groups that may seek to harm them, or simply to have fun and socialize with mortals in order to better understand and coexist with them. In turn, this helps Legends maintain a more grounded perspective and makes it easier for them to empathize with mortals. As a side effect, most Legendaries will usually be pretty up-to-date on mortal affairs and may even keep up with things like pop culture. Just imagine a Legendary using terms like "rizz" and "aura farming" and actually knowing what they mean. While this change in the relationship between the mortal and the divine is generally a good thing, as it makes Legendaries both more reasonable in general and more reluctant to unleash their true power during conflicts in order to avoid unnecessary collateral damage, it can also have downsides in certain circumstances. For example, a Legendary might make friends while in disguise and then struggle to cope with eventually losing them to old age. It is also possible for them to have children with mortals while in disguise. However, unless the Demi-Legends modifier is in effect the children will always belong to the mortal parent's species and will only receive minor benefits from their divine lineage. How much involvement a Legend has in their children's lives varies based on the duties and personality of the Legend in question, but they will always ensure that at least their partner's and offspring's physical needs are met. This modifier is retroactive, and you can choose whether any characters in your setting are now retroactively the offspring of a Legendary. For example, Ash Ketchum could be the son of Lugia, Cynthia could be Palkia's niece, or Pikachu could be the son of Arceus.
objects.title: Mortal Disguise (Pokemon)

objects.text:
Your new world is now connected to the Morphing Grid. At first, this connection may seem insignificant; however, over time, Tinkers, mad scientists, magicians, and others will discover how to tap into the Morphing Grid and gain extraordinary powers.

It’s important to note that there is nothing preventing villains from using the Grid for their own purposes, as it offers nearly limitless power. Therefore, you can expect to see giant robots and form-fitting suits appearing around the globe, but be careful not to refer to them as spandex— a certain doctor might find out.

Those who access the Morphing Grid will experience enhanced strength, speed, and durability while transformed. You may also notice certain individuals developing unique abilities from Grid energy, such as sonic screams, aura viewing, self-duplication, and the ability to phase through walls. Additionally, while transformed, the energy from the Grid acts as a protective shield around empowered individuals, though it is not infallible and can be breached with sufficient force.

Keep in mind that the Grid is a multiversal bio-energy field generated by every living being within the local multiverse. 

If someone acquires enough control over the Morphing Grid, they could traverse time and alternate dimensions; if they become powerful enough, they could potentially destroy the multiverse and reshape it according to their desires.

Stay strong in the face of this paradigm shift, and may the Power protect you.
objects.title: Grid Access (Power Rangers)

objects.text:
Oh no. It appears that the villains in your starting world have either uncovered or recreated the process that produced the original Psycho Rangers, who once faced the In Space Rangers.

At first, they will create five Psycho Rangers: Red, Black, Blue, Pink, and Yellow. These artificial Rangers are born from a perversion and corruption of the Morphin Grid’s energies. Although they can pass as human, their minds are demented and unstable, restrained only by pain-inducing implants designed to keep them under control.

Unlike traditional Ranger teams, the Psycho Rangers do not possess Zords. Instead, they can transform into monstrous forms that grow to skyscraper-sized proportions, often rivaling the scale of a Megazord.

The most terrifying part is not that the Psycho Rangers may eventually find a way to escape their creator’s control. It appears that the process is not limited to merely creating the five initial Psycho Rangers and their colors. While two Psycho Rangers cannot share the exact same color, alternate variations can exist, from Blue and Navy to Graphite and Gray.

If the process is ever replicated, the world may not face just five Psycho Rangers. It could be forced to withstand dozens of them.
objects.title: Let's Go Psycho (Power Rangers)

objects.text:
It appears that the Grid was not the only force to arrive in this new world with you; Lord Zedd and his minions have also followed. You can expect monsters, both large and small, to attack cities while battling giant robots.

On the moon, a castle has emerged from which its evil master can observe the Earth. His name is Zedd—Lord Zedd—and soon, everyone will come to fear his name.

Lord Zedd is a master of both martial and mystical arts, capable of taking on multiple Rangers at once. He can unleash powerful blasts from his visor or staff, often in the form of crimson energy. Additionally, let’s not forget Zedd’s personal Zord, Serpentera. This Zord can travel through space and has the capability to destroy an entire planet, though it cannot fight afterward.

Zedd did not come alone; he is accompanied by his wife, Rita Repulsa, her brother, Rito Revolto, Zedd’s loyal right-hand man, Goldar, and the master of monster creation, Finster. In the aftermath of this evil, your world will never be the same. 

(Note: You may replace Lord Zedd with any main villain from the Power Rangers universe, except for Dark Specter.)
objects.title: Emperor of Evil: Lord Zedd (Power Rangers)

objects.text:
It would seem Lord Zedd is the least of your worries as someone far crueler, and more cunning, has caught on to this new extension of the Morphin Grid, many know him as a tyrant and a former servant or Rita Repulsa, but the rest of the Grid knows him better as Lord Drakkon.

In an alternate timeline where Tommy Oliver was never freed from Rita’s influence Tommy would serve as her right hand man and lead not just the conquest of Earth but also the destruction of Zordon and his Power Ranger, for before Zordon could create the White Ranger, Lord Drakkon stormed the command center and turned it to rubble Claiming the incomplete White Tiger power and fusing it with his dragon coin granting him even greater power, enough to overthrow Rita and rule the Earth uncontested.

 Now he is set to claim to take the Morphin Grid Nexuses from your new World(s) and use them to expand his army of Ranger Sentries, where most villains utilize Robots, Aliens, or Supernatural entities, Lord Drakon instead uses the Morpher’s of his defeated foes to create new legions; each sentry only taps into a fraction of the full power of each Morpher and is often outfitter with more militaristic uniforms and weapons then the Ranger said Morpher corresponds to.

Lord Drakkon dimension is now parallel to you own, be careful as in spite of his world being desolate it contains untold legions of Ranger Sentries based off 4 of the 6 original power coins. Where is number 5, you ask, why it is with Kimberly now, brainwashed into Lord Drakkon’s right hand, the Ranger Slayer.

His power is ever growing and with a world with so many tapping into the Morphin Grid, so to shall he, you have been warned.
objects.title: The Black Dragon: Lord Drakkon (Power Rangers)

addons.text:
The phenomenon was left without explanation, with mankind plagued with speculation and rationalizing such an unexplainable occurrence. 

You’d have to wonder no more.

The Prehistoric Emergence is the Gods’ retaliation for Humanity’s sulling of Earth and the Entities’ invasion. The chasms are protected by divine wards, as any effort to counteract their effects on the world will be met violently by the Gods’ part. 

The mutant living fossils are then considered Champions from their respective Pantheon, exhibiting higher intelligence and overt supernatural abilities, with Titanoboa being Shiva’s, and so on.
addons.title: Gods’ Judgement

addons.text:
The living fossils that leave the chasms aren’t your normal previously extinct lifeforms now, but highly evolved descendants that have increasingly evolved into a greater size comparable to the daikaiju or monsters roaming the Earth.
 
Daikaiju seem to be either neutral or highly territorial against the living fossils, while the latter will go out of their way to fight for territory and resources with them. Not to be taken advantage of, the living fossils developed higher cognitive functions and refined biological traits such as seamless camouflage or acidic spits.
addons.title: Indomitus Genus

addons.text: Now, the living fossils surging from chasms around the world come from Hollow Earth’s system of caves. Their fauna inexplicably urged to the Surface and follow their strange yet deadly behavior, albeit deadlier, including the lizard-people with their ambition in defeating the human race in being the dominant force on Earth.
addons.title: Origin Point

objects.text:
Without explanation, chasms manifested across the caves and oceans of the world.

At first glance, it was strange. Almost off-putting in their sudden appearance. Mankind moved in all the bustling haze of the modern world… without seeing what came after. 

Animals, thought to be extinct, emerge from these chasms in droves: apex predators of the sea of old such as the Dunkleosteus, the Megalodon, the Mesasaurus, the Livyathan, and many others surged from the chasms laying waste to the ocean’s ecosystems and displaying aggressive behavior towards humans, with people frantically evacuating from any naval activity as the seas; in the ground, animals from lost eras reveal themselves, the Tyrannosaurus Rex and the Smilodon being among them, in the skies, pterosaurs like the Quetzalcoatlus pester and endanger people with their hunting for farm animals.

The range of the species’ reemergence appeared to be from the Paleozoic to the Cenozoic Era, Pliocene at most. This species exhibits ambivalent behavior regarding civilization, while adapting and blending in with man-made environments, others prefer to avoid mankind altogether. Other prehistoric species seem to have either a taste (or distaste) for people, going out of their way to attack people without provocation or wreak havoc in society, often acting unlike their hypothetical prehistoric behaviors. Although some break the mold, judging by the scant few cases, authorities search for an “talking” T. rex they call ‘the Dabbah’ or the Argentinosaurus known as ‘Behemoth’, for its greater size compared to its brethren. In general, they seem harmful to mankind in any shape or form, with no explanation as to why.

This led to a global upheaval, grappling with changes to society, a reckoning that reevaluated how humanity went on their day-to-day lives, fearing the next dinosaur attack or dire wolves in the night, which led to a more cautious populace, and organizations forming in managing and understanding this phenomenon.
objects.title: The Reemergence (Prehistoric Emergence)

objects.text:
Shortly after your arrival, the Sun will be infected with astrophage. Astrophage is an alien microbe, which acts similar to an interstellar mold or algae. It grows upon the surface of stars, decreasing the brightness and leading to a dramatic decrease in temperature of any celestial bodies in orbit of the affected star. This leads to a mass extinction on any planets with life in the affected star's system. It can travel from star to star, drawn by the light and heat of each star.

If this is not taken care of, all life on Earth will go extinct within 2 to 3 decades. Good news; there is a planet the astrophage originates from which contains microbial life that preys on astrophage. Bad news; it’s ~12 light years away. Your world will have to come together and cooperate in order to solve this problem.
objects.title: Astrophage Crisis (Project Hail Mary)

objects.text:
The world has been exposed to The 「Seed of Light」 drawn from The 「Well of Humanity」, and with it, has come the Distortion Phenomena. 

In their darkest moments, people will now hear a lulling, charming Voice speak to them. The Voice will urge them to reject the world, to ignore all things that aren't themselves and chase their desires by any means necessary. To bury themselves in self love. Should the person accept the words of the Voice, then they shall distort into a form more befitting of their inner self. A twisted mirror of their desires, traumas, and impluses. And with this transformation, the person shall gain the power needed to chase their desires. Enhancing any pre-existing abilities they may have or granting them new powers related to their desires. Most Distortions will retain the intelligence of their former selves. 

However, it is possible to reverse the distortion. Should one manage to confront their traumas which lead to their distortion and reject the words of the distorting voice, then the person shall effloresce their 「E.G.O.」. A physical manifestation of the person's mind. An「E.G.O.」 may come in many forms, though it is typically a weapon or some kind of clothing. In rare cases, it may even be a building. Once effloresced, an 「E.G.O.」 may be deployed and withdrawn at will. However, 「E.G.O.」 manifestation will typically take a mental toll or have some kind of limiter on its usage.

However, should a person lack individuality and character as an person, they fail to even distort. Such a person will become a Peccatulum, which, unlike Distortions who typically remain the ability to speak and a semblance of humanity, are completely animalistic in nature. There are seven possible Peccatula a person may become, each corresponding to a certain sin. Peccatulum Irae (Wrath), Peccatulum Luxuriae (Lust), Peccatulum Pigritiae (Sloth), Peccatulum Gulae (Gluttony), Peccatulum Morositatis (Gloom), Peccatulum Superbiae (Pride), and Peccatulum Invidiae (Envy). Unlike distorting, transforming into a Peccatulum is an irreversible process.
objects.title: The Distortion Phenomena (Project Moon)

objects.text: Far away in the depths of space, there lies an alien race known only as the Incubators. These emotionless beings of pure logic are among the most advanced civilizations in the universe. Having long since conquered death, the only thing that truly threatens them is one cold hard fact: though they may have an infinite lifespan, the universe does not. Thus they seek to fight entropy, not because of compassion for life or a fear of the end, but because it is logical for any species to seek continued existence. The best method they have found is one where they rip out the souls of young, emotional females of lesser species and turn them into gemstones, which eventually fill with corruption and turn into a Grief Seed, killing the victims as they become soul eating monsters known as Witches. These people doomed to become Witches are called Magical Girls or Puella Magi, and the only way for a Puella Magi to avoid transforming into a Witch is to kill one who already has and use their Grief Seed to drain the ‘Grief’ from their Soulgem. Using a Grief Seed too much can result in the Witch being reborn, and the only way to safely dispose of the used Grief Seed is to give it to an Incubator, which they then recycle for energy. The Incubators, in the process of creating Puella Magi, grant a Wish for them, with higher ‘Karmic Potential’ (that is, the estimated impact they would have on the world as a whole) leading to greater Wishes being able to be granted and also being stronger as a Magical Girl and eventually a Witch. Thus, they seek out young girls with great potential to fill their quota, not caring in the slightest as thousands of girls suffer due to their machinations until their Wishes turn into Curses and they become yet another monster feeding on the world, nor do they care as the Wishes they grant change the world in any number of ways. The only thing they care about is gathering energy, and shortly before your arrival, they found a world full of souls to begin harvesting from: yours. A number of girls around the world have already become Puella Magi, and then Witches before being hunted by other Puella Magi. You can expect a number of important teenage girls to already have Soulgems unless they were predisposed to being wary of ‘Wishes’ or trusting suspicious magical beings. Unless there is already a masquerade in place, you can expect the sudden presence of magical superpowers and soul eating monsters to be quickly noticed and chaos to ensue. Be wary, as the Incubators will not take any threat to their operation lightly. Though most worlds can’t do anything to stop them due to their primary terminals being infinitely respawning hivemind telepaths that can’t be seen by anyone with a lack of potential to become a Puella Magi and their true forms being a hyper advanced interstellar civilization, should anyone be able to do so anyway they will take precautions. Even a multiversal god can eventually be countered by their tech, and their ability to manipulate others and make and execute plans that require years to see to fruition cannot be underestimated. Note: If you chose to go to Puella Magi Madoka☆Magica or any of its spinoffs, then this modifier instead makes it so that the general public becomes aware of Puella Magi and Witches, which will cause panic among both civilians and governments. Expect the more violent or ambitious Magical Girls to start openly using their powers for personal gain while governments try to crack down on them in turn, as the situation spirals out of control all while the Incubators profit from so much Grief being generated.
objects.title: A World of Wishes and Witches (Puella Magi Madoka☆Magica)

objects.text:
The world you perceive is no longer reality in its unaltered form. Instead, it is the result of reality being covered by numerous metaphysical layers called "Phases."

Phases are not higher dimensions or alternate universes in the traditional sense. They are layers imposed upon the underlying world that alter how the world manifests, akin to transparent layers of paint applied to a canvas. This canvas is the Pure World, or baseline reality, while observable reality is what you get when you look through all the layers simultaneously.

These Phases are created through the religions and mythologies of the native species, with the exact Phases that exist depending on the setting you're in. A Phase can contain supernatural beings, energies, environments, phenomena, and its own distinct set of rules. For example, the "Heaven" Phase contains angels and an energy called Telesma.

However, Phases aren't isolated systems. They can overlap and collide with each other as the distances between them fluctuate. When one Phase collides with another, it creates "Sparks." These Sparks can manifest in the ordinary world as luck, misfortune, or supernatural accidents, with the practice of Magic making these collisions more frequent. This is because Magic is essentially the manipulation of Phases.

As this modifier is retroactive, this means there will be a large number of Mages in the world and, consequently, a lot more supernatural disasters. However, none of these Mages will be on the level of the Magic Gods as this modifier only adds the Phases without the inclusion of the divine order described in the Kabbalah.

Additionally, if your setting has native supernatural elements, you can choose whether they are the result of the Phases or whether they are part of the Pure World. In the latter case, these elements will continue to function even if the Phases are destroyed or if they are in an area that prevents Phase manipulation.

You can also choose whether the Phase system merges with or replaces the local cosmology.
objects.title: Phases (Raildex)

objects.text:
It seems your world has inherited more than just the Phases. Instead of being all that exists, the Phases are now a subset of a larger cosmic governing system. This system is the Tree of Sephiroth, also known as the Tree of Life.

In Kabbalah, the Tree of Sephiroth, alongside its inversion, the Tree of Qliphoth, which is now also present, governs and describes the relationship between the Creator and Creation.

The Tree is composed of 10 so-called "Sephiroth," which are divine emanations or attributes that reveal the unknowable Godhead to Creation, as well as channel the divine life force throughout all layers of existence. They continuously create and sustain both the physical world and the chain of higher metaphysical worlds that make up existence.

The Sephiroth are connected to one another through 22 pathways, which describe how these emanations relate to each other. The entire Tree was given birth by the Ein Sof Ohr, the Divine Light, which emanates from the Ein Sof, the Infinite, unmanifested state of God that existed before all division.

It is possible to use the Tree as a ladder to ascend to a higher plane of existence. Doing so allows someone to grow closer to God in both power and nature. If a mage manages to ascend to the highest Sephirah, Keter, they become a Magic God: a being of nigh-limitless power capable of creating, destroying, and recreating Phases to warp observable reality however they please.

With one important caveat: they cannot fundamentally change or affect the Pure World, only the filters that overlay it.

While the potential to ascend to Keter now exists, you can choose whether anyone has managed to reach it so far. This makes the presence of Magic Gods or similar entities, including Abyss Crossers, completely optional.

As with the previous modifier, it is up to your discretion whether the Tree(s) fully replace or merge with the native cosmology.

Additionally, if your setting already has a Creator God, you can choose whether they are an aspect of the Ein Sof or have them replace the Ein Sof entirely. In the latter case, the number and attributes of the Sephiroth and pathways may change to better reflect this entity's nature.
objects.title: Tree of Sephiroth (Raildex)

objects.text:
Somehow, the Factors of Sin have manifested within your world. There are nine in total—one for each of the traditional Seven Sins, as well as the past extra 2. Each Factor chooses a single host and binds itself to them, granting an ability equal in scale and nature to the Sin it represents.

However, this bond is never unconditional. If the chosen host is judged insufficient—if their affinity for the Sin does not meet the Factor’s minimum threshold—they undergo corruption. This corruption is shaped by the essence of the Sin, though not always in a literal or predictable way. For instance, a host selected by the Factor of Sloth will not necessarily become paralyzed by laziness; instead, they might spiral into compulsive overwork, or relentless self-punishment.

All beings who carry a Factor have their personal energies transformed into Miasma, a corrupted spiritual force. High concentrations of Miasma can induce hallucinations, madness, and emotional mania. Any individual who has suffered intense trauma at the hands of a Factor-bearer—or their cultists, manifestations, or associated creatures—develops the ability to sense Miasma through a single heightened sense, such as smell, touch, or hearing.

Crucially, no being can safely host more than one Factor of Sin. Attempting to hold multiple Factors results in catastrophic corruption as the conflicting Sins tear through the host’s mind and soul. No mortal—or immortal is capable of enduring the combined weight of multiple Sins manifested as authorities.

If you possess the power Witch Of Sin (Re:Zero) you are considered a "Sage" Candidate, allowing you to bypass the incompatability issue, as well as being able to hold as many as you wish.
