Each Factor grants extraordinary power, but only to those capable of truly harmonizing with it. All others are inevitably broken, twisted, or consumed by the burden they are unfit to bear.
objects.title: Authorities Of Sin (Re:Zero)

objects.text:
The Spirits of Od Laguna have inexplicably come into existence, without the existance of Od Laguna. They are invisible to anyone without a natural Spirit Affinity or the ability to use magic, with the rare exceptions of Full Spirits and Great Spirits, whose power makes them perceptible even to ordinary eyes. These spirits preside over the elements of Fire, Water, Earth, Wind, Yin, and Yang, each governing not only its primary element but the symbolic forces tied to it—Water also governs healing, Fire regulates temperature, Yin commands shadow and debuff magic that manipulates gravity, time, space, and the senses, while Yang governs light and buff magic that strengthens bodies, repairs objects, and generates heat or energy.

Spirits begin as Lesser Spirits, small orbs of mana with a faint sense of awareness. They cannot speak but can transmit and receive emotions through mana. Lesser Spirits possess basic elemental manipulation, intangibility, invisibility, and the ability to absorb ambient mana to sustain themselves or fuel simple spells. Their support is minor—small Fireballs, gusts of wind capable of knocking someone over, manifesting shadow or light, capable of blinding someone. As they gather mana and develop a sense of identity, they evolve into Quasi-Spirits. These beings still cannot speak but possess distinct personalities, understand tasks from a contractor, and wield enough power to boost physical abilities or cast base-level spells such as the fire spell Goa or the Yin spell Shamak.

With enough accumulated mana and self-awareness, a Quasi-Spirit becomes a Full Spirit. Full Spirits have independent minds, can communicate clearly, and can sense emotions and surface-level thoughts by reading mana. They act according to their own desires rather than human morality and can cast high-level magic such as Al Huma, a barrage of Bullet-like large ice spears. Over vast periods of time, and with immense power, a Full Spirit may ascend into a Great Spirit. Great Spirits are exceptionally rare—often only one appearing every century—and their power is vast enough to alter climates, devastate cities, and if old enough even continent's, and manipulate massive quantities of elemental energy. Their intelligence, autonomy, and telepathic ability make them formidable and unpredictable entities.

All spirits are driven by the desire to form Contracts—binding pacts viewed as sacred promises. Only beings with Spirit Affinity can form these contracts, and true Spirit Affinity is extremely rare. Being able to bond with a Full Spirit is seen as a once-in-a-generation talent, while the ability to contract with multiple spirits, or especially a Great Spirit, is considered legendary. Now that spirits exist, ambient mana has also appeared throughout your Planet, sustaining them and enabling their growth, though any your contracted with can sustain themselves on your Energies, from Spiritual, Divine, Magic, or Physical, though certain types are better and worse, such as divine being many times better, while Spiritual are more debatable.

You possess at least a Lesser Spirit Affinity, though your affinity may increase depending on the powers you hold. Any ability that grants affinity with sapient beings, or access to spirit-like entities, or even a great ability for connection, such as if you had the Skill Connection raises your affinity proportionally to its SP or CP cost. For example, possessing the Elemental Spirit Bond power (20 SP) would grant you the potential to contract with multiple Great Spirits—if you can convince the Great Spirit at least—marking you as a contractor whose talent appears only once every several millennia. this Affinity Stacks.

The First purchase causes their existence only on the Planet you Start on, the second in the Galaxy, Third the Universe, and Fourth the entire Multiverse. each purchase above the first also adds a new level of spirit above Great. keep in mind after 2 or more purchases Spirits of the Yin and yang variety will become the most common type, due to Space, and Stars, and new types of spirits may even form due to a new variety of elements.
objects.title: Elemental Spirits (Re:Zero)

objects.text:
Somehow, somewhere in the galaxy, a Chimera invasion force has suddenly appeared. This force is not a simple scouting group, but a large and dangerous alien presence made up of warships, biological transport vessels, and massive numbers of Chimera soldiers. Their purpose is simple: expand, infect, and reshape new worlds for their species.

Unlike traditional empires, the Chimera spread through infection and transformation. When they reach a suitable world, they begin establishing hive-like strongholds and conversion facilities. Captured lifeforms are often transformed into Chimera variants, swelling their numbers and allowing them to adapt to the local environment. Their technology is highly advanced and heavily integrated with their biology, making their forces both resilient and difficult to fully eradicate.

Chimera forces include a wide range of terrifying units such as infantry forms, massive war-beasts, aerial creatures, and towering biomechanical war machines. As they gain a foothold on a planet, their presence quickly escalates into a full-scale planetary infestation.

If the Chimera encounter humanity, they will immediately become extremely aggressive. Due to how Humans are considered highly compatible hosts for Chimera conversion, making them a prime target for capture and transformation. Should they locate Earth, the Chimera will attempt to invade and convert the planet into a massive hive world to further expand their species.

Each additional purchase of this modifier causes another Chimera invasion fleet to appear somewhere else in the galaxy, spreading their infection across more worlds and creating new hive-controlled territories. Over time, these infestations may link together, forming a growing alien network that threatens entire star systems.
objects.title: The Chimera Invasion (Resistance 3)

objects.text:
The Melding plague is a virus that naturally evolved from an alien species. While they created immunity to it eons ago, our machines and bodies unfortunately have not. Removing the boundary between the organic and the machine, it twists nanomachines and similar into cancerous growths. A building made of nanomachines could spread without control, with illogical corridors clearly not made for humans in mind. The nanomachines in your body might start growing new organs without need, keeping you alive as something that vaguely reassembles human life. 

The virus will be spread randomly on your setting, without warning. You can select this modifier multiple times depending on how widespread nanotechnology is in your destination: once if it is close to non-existent, two if it is moderately used, and three times if it is very widespread.
objects.title: The Melding Plague (Revelation Space)

objects.text:
A mysterious force will begin to send waves of enemies your way at regular intervals, with the number of foes and their strength gradually increasing. The enemies will be intelligent pawns that take the form of any enemies, factions or even wild animals you are familiar with.

After your first purchase, attacks will occur infrequently — roughly once every three months. Although the number of enemies and their strength will increase, this will not be catastrophic. You will always have a chance to fend them off using the available means and Powers. For example, for an ordinary person, these might be groups of marginalised bandits armed with homemade weapons.

After the second purchase, the frequency of attacks will increase to once a month. Enemies will become more numerous and powerful, making their attacks more threatening. Without proper preparation and powerful Powers, your defeat and death will become highly likely. For an ordinary person, for example, this could reach the level of attacks by army units.

After the third purchase, attacks will occur once a week. Enemies will become even more numerous and powerful, and you will have little time to prepare to repel each wave. Your life will cease to be peaceful and unhurried. For example, attacks may involve high-tech adversaries or those possessing superpowers.

You won’t receive any rewards for fending off a wave (apart from your own life), and the settlements or groups you’re taking refuge in will still be attacked. However, you’ll be awarded three modifiers, from which you can choose one to influence the next wave. Modifiers can strengthen the wave, weaken it, postpone it to a later date, or even trigger a wave immediately, but in any case you’ll gain a certain benefit. As a consolation prize, you’ll receive the enemies’ equipment and weapons, whilst the bodies of the slain pawns will quickly vanish into thin air.

Enemies will arrive from ‘beyond the horizon’, so to speak, and you’ll always have a little time to prepare. In the long run… In about 2–3 years, or after ~30-100 waves have been repelled, the entity may lose interest in you.
objects.title: Winston Waves (Rimworld Mod)

addons.text: The Grimm Pools are now producing an alarming number of Grimm each day, increasing their output capacity tenfold. Additionally, new forms are emerging, ranging from plasma-spewing bugs to liches that resurrect their victims as hordes of undead. A wide variety of fantastical creatures are now possible to encounter.
addons.title: Fantastic Grimm

addons.text: More esoteric types of Grimm can now be created, such as intellect devourers or memetic mind control parasites. Additionally, new Grimm types continue to emerge from humanity's subconscious fears. Furthermore, Grimm are developing sentience at a faster rate than before, achieving basic sentience at around C-Class instead of the previous B-Class.
addons.title: Esoteric Grimm

objects.text:
In this continuity, Salem managed to trick the God of Light and the God of Darkness into fighting each other. During the battle, the God of Darkness was killed by the God of Light. Realizing what he had done, the God of Light fled from Remnant, inadvertently destroying the moon in the process and leaving the corpse of his brother behind. The corpse of the God of Darkness has been consumed by the pools of Grimm, supercharging them and making the Grimm stronger and more numerous. They can now evolve by consuming the souls of their victims, and after absorbing a sufficient number of souls, they can achieve sentience.

Due to the god of Light fleeing, the people of Remnant still possess Magic alongside Dust and Aura. While humanity is much stronger than in Canon, so are the Grimms, with multiple classes ranging from an E-Class able to be killed by a civilian with a weapon to Apocalyptic threats capable of rendering entire cities to rubble in a day.

In a world where magic still exists, the fauna and flora are vastly different from what we would expect of Canon. Magical creatures and plants populate the wilderness, ready to be transformed into weapons and potions for the defenders of humanity.
objects.title: Lightless World (RWBY)

objects.text:
By picking this modifier, your world begins to develop strange, unexplainable phenomena. These anomalies take a multitude of forms, and the extent of what will appear in the world is determined by how many purchases of this modifier are made. The first purchase limits it to mere curiosities, simple items with minor anomalous properties that can be contained en masse in warehouses, with only a handful of Safe anomalies that require more specialized containment.

Upon your second purchase, more dangerous anomalies will begin to appear. They are still safe to contain, but now they pose a threat to individuals, such as an anomaly that upon contact raises a human's body temperature by 20 degrees instantly causing fatal heatstroke. A third purchase allows for greater anomalies, humans and locations begin developing minor anomalous properties and items that are for some reason more difficult to contain start appearing. At four purchases, these properties start to become more dangerous, with objects that threaten multiple people and people or places that are dangerous to be around manifesting. At five purchases, these become even more common, until there is at least one such person or place in every state or country, with a minimum of one Safe anomaly in every city.

At six purchases, even more dangerous anomalies begin to appear, with a number even starting to be actively malicious, such as a regenerating futuristic killer robot or a house that you can't leave even with teleportation. At seven and eight purchases these become ever more common. At nine purchases, anomalies that can affect entire towns start to appear, such as individuals who make everyone in a mile radius start forgetting their own names. At ten purchases, truly infectious anomalies such as supernatural diseases or memetic hazards start to appear, as do replicable anomalies such as ‘magic’ systems or anomalous crafting techniques that get more potentially powerful with more purchases.

At eleven purchases, anomalies that threaten entire nations begin to appear. Infections with no cure, locations that erase whoever enters them, objects that self replicate. At twelve purchases, anomalies become even more esoteric, as extraterrestrial phenomena begin to make themselves known, and anomalies that affect time or other dimensions appear. The thirteenth and fourteenth purchases make these more common.

At fifteen purchases, individual anomalies that threaten the existence of the planet and humanity as a whole appear. Beings that if awakened would remove humanity's ability to sleep, alien stars that hate mankind, extradimensional gods of hunger, mind controlling memes that turn their viewers into infection vectors, and more, with the sixteenth and seventeenth purchases making these more common.

At eighteen purchases, anomalies that threaten existence itself appear. Stickers that if removed from the inside of a doorway result in the universe rebuilding itself into a megastructure uninhabitable by humans, individuals who can rewrite entire galaxies by accident, hostile afterlife dimensions, and more besides. The nineteenth and twentieth purchases makes them even more common.

As more purchases are made, humanity finds itself in ever more danger. Organizations dedicated to containing, destroying, profiting off of, or serving anomalies begin to form, or even appear retroactively at higher purchases. As the danger mounts, a variety of end of the world scenarios become more likely to happen, and attempts to combat them are made. Eventually, some will occur and these organizations may rebuild or reset the world. By twenty purchases, the world is at the mercy of dozens upon dozens of universal threats that destroy it before some organization or Foundation resets it just for the cycle to repeat for seemingly eternity.
objects.title: Anomalous Awakening (SCP Foundation)

objects.text:
SCP-610 is a Keter-class sentient, mutagenic disease that will rapidly and aggressively expand to infect as many lifeforms as possible. SCP-610 appears to be a contagious skin disease at first, but it will quickly kill and reanimate those it infects, as well as morph the bodies of those it does in radical and unpredictable ways. Some infected by the disease will root themselves in place and spread fleshy growths across all surrounding objects and landscape, consuming them to create an environment more hospitable for infected individuals. 

The infection spreads primarily through physical contact with infected individuals—who will chase down and actively seek to infect the uninfected—though not via objects consumed by it; transmission via water or air is not usually a concern. Any organic being can be infected by the virus, such as animals. Those infected can often display strange, incomprehensible and ritualistic behaviours. A case of infection can be slowed through extreme cold, and the most reliable method of destroying the infected is through liberal application of fire.

A case of SCP-610 infection will appear in a random location in the setting you've chosen and begin expanding from there. If not discovered and contained or eradicated quickly, it has the potential to grow to consume entire ecosystems.
objects.title: SCP-610: The Flesh That Hates (SCP Foundation)

objects.text:
The world you are about to enter will become the target of a devastating calamity known as the Nightmare Creatures, also called the Corrupted or the Infected. Their minds are twisted, alien, and incomprehensible, and they possess little to no sense of self. In truth, Nightmare Creatures are beings who were once of the Flame of Desire, but whose souls have fallen into the corruption and madness of the Void.

Just as humans ascend toward divinity in the world of Shadow Slave, Nightmare Creatures descend into profanity. Their corrupted Soul Cores are divided into seven Ranks of Power, from lowest to highest: Dormant, Awakened, Fallen, Corrupted, Great, Cursed, and Unholy. Against Nightmare Creatures, modern technology proves unreliable, as those of higher Ranks are immune to conventional weapons.

For example, Fallen abominations can more or less withstand even the most devastating bombardments; Corrupted ones can survive nuclear explosions; and Great abominations can single-handedly destroy entire continents. Cursed abominations are akin to lesser deities, their mere presence exerting immense pressure upon the world, while Unholy abominations stand on par with gods.

In addition to Ranks, Nightmare Creatures also possess Classes determined by the number of Soul Cores they contain. There are seven Classes, from lowest to highest: Beast, Monster, Demon, Devil, Tyrant, Terror, and Titan.

Beasts are dangerous and powerful, but mindless. Monsters are far more destructive and possess a weak, warped form of intelligence. Demons have a clear semblance of intellect and can acquire abilities. Devils possess bizarre powers akin to the Aspect Abilities of those who walk the Path of Ascension, and they themselves are sentient, intelligent, and cunning. Tyrants can create and command armies of lesser minions. Terrors can influence their surroundings and spread their presence. Finally, Titans are colossal entities with destructive power comparable to natural disasters.

One crucial aspect of Nightmare Creatures is their capacity to evolve. Much like humans who walk the Path of Ascension, all abominations can grow stronger by following the Path of Corruption, making it possible for them to eventually reach the Unholy Rank.

At first, the Nightmare Creatures that descend upon your chosen world will consist of Dormant to Fallen Rank abominations. They will appear across the globe in the thousands, even emerging within the oceans and obstructing naval travel. As time passes, higher-Rank creatures will begin to manifest, such as Corrupted abominations, and their numbers will swell from thousands to millions. Eventually, the rate of their appearance will gradually slow, though they will never cease entirely. After decades—or even centuries—Great abominations will emerge, followed in time by the arrival of Cursed and ultimately Unholy beings.
objects.title: Nightmare Creatures (Shadow Slave)

objects.text:
Among the population of the world you are about to enter, there exists a rare group of individuals known as the “Fated.” These people, whether human or otherwise, share one defining trait: they were chosen by Fate to achieve a specific purpose or to reach a predetermined end. Though their destiny may be delayed, nothing short of the nearly impossible feat of becoming fateless or breaking Fate itself can prevent them from ultimately reaching that end.

Regardless of what their fate entails, each of them will be guided by Fate to fulfill it. In turn, they will possess the capacity to accomplish their destined outcome when the time is right—whether it be something as simple as making a groundbreaking discovery, reaching heights no one else has attained, defeating a powerful foe, or even slaying the gods themselves.
objects.title: Those Who Are Fated (Shadow Slave)

objects.text:
Every inhabitant of the world you are about to enter shares a common trait known as a Flaw—a curse unique to each individual that cannot be removed. Flaws are never random; they are deeply connected to the person who bears them and are tied to something fundamental about their nature. While Flaws can be cruel and burdensome, there are ways to work around them, even though they can never truly be overcome.

A Flaw might directly oppose the core of a person’s identity, twist something they hold dear into a grotesque reflection of itself, or have little to do with their personality and instead stem from the nature of their power or their fate. Despite their deeply personal and complex nature, a Flaw can be deduced if one understands the individual well enough.

However, it is not only people who possess Flaws. Nothing in this world is flawless—not even the world itself. Should powerful beings such as gods exist, they too would bear a Flaw. Paradoxically, it is precisely because of these Flaws that growth becomes possible. Any being burdened with a Flaw gains the capacity to grow stronger, their former limits expanding and allowing them to reach heights that would have been unattainable without one.

Note: By selecting this modifier, you will also receive a Flaw upon entering your chosen world. However, you may choose for this Flaw to be any one of your selected drawbacks. Alternatively, you may forgo having a Flaw altogether by selecting a power or perk that bypasses the Law of Imperfection, such as the Foreigner perk.
objects.title: Law of Imperfection (Shadow Slave)

objects.text:
Certain places in the world are entirely covered by a mysterious white mist, known as Death Zones. Anything beyond the veil of mist cannot be seen; however, the sight is misleading, as the mist itself is extremely dangerous. Those who enter it quickly begin to lose their sense of self and are drawn into a state of senselessness. Before long, they are erased from existence by the Nothing that the mist embodies, which is capable of annihilating anything that comes into contact with it.

The only known way to survive this mist of Nothing is to possess both a “Flame of Divinity”—or an equivalent form of divinity attainable by those who walk the Path of Ascension—and an unshakable will that affirms one’s sense of self against the overwhelming pull of nonexistence.
objects.title: The Mist of Nothing (Shadow Slave)

objects.text: In an adjacent world where which once cannot be reached... There lies a realm known only as the Crimson Realm, though not literally crimson, it is a world where powers intermingle. Harsh, where survival is nearly impossible for an ordinary being, it houses creatures known as Crimson Denizens and the far more powerful Crimson Lords who go forth and try to colonize our world for themselves, devouring people's Existences in the process. This has seemingly caused an immense rift in the power of existence which holds this and the Crimson Realm's worlds together. As Denizens and Lord's devour people to maintain their identities when traveling here, their victims fade, suddenly forgotten by everyone around them including those whom cared for them. At most, a Torch is created to be a temporary doppelganger for the victims, before they too fade away with their victim's existence. It is a harrowing loss, only prevented by other Crimson Lords who actually wished to maintain proper balance between the Crimson Realm and our world. These Crimson Lords forge contracts with exceptional humans, creating warriors called Flame Hazes. Thus is the long battle between the Flame Hazes and the Denizens, fighting a near endless war of existence. And now? Your world has been caught up in this conflict. Characters or other important people may suddenly disappear, potentially through being eaten by a Denizen they couldn't have seen, or through forging a contract to become a Flame Haze, an act that also leads to people forgetting about them. Hell, maybe you yourself would end up dragged into this war? Maybe as a person who signed a contract to be a Flame Haze, or maybe a Crimson Denizen yourself? Either way, the balance is in jeopardy, and you are awakened to this battle. Will you fade away, or will your light shine through this endless hardships?
objects.title: The Crimson Night (Shakugan No Shana)

objects.text:
Good news; a whole bunch of philosophical questions about the meaning of life and the origin of the universe have been answered! The bad news is that whatever universe you're in just became the site of a Shin Megami Tensei game. Maybe a Schwarzwelt opened as punishment for this world's sins, a Conception occurred for this world to be reborn, a War Of Bel started, the Karma Society started poking The Great Will with a stick, or maybe you got the old reliable "a cult started summoning demons". Whatever the reason, the forces of Law and Chaos have appeared to fight over this world.

The forces of Law are associated with YHVH (pronounced like a record scratch), geometric shapes & floating faces, angels like The Heralds, and Abrahamic Mythology more generally. They wish for a world of peace, order, and safety, but it comes at the expense of liberty, individuality, & choice. It is a world of benevolent tyranny, a world where everyone is nothing but a single voice in a choir. By contrast, the forces of Chaos are associated with Lucifer (frequently going by comically obvious pseudonyms like "Louis Cyphre"), devils like those found in the Ars Goetia, pagan gods, Shinto kami, & Buddhist divinities. They wish for a world of freedom, the individual will, & choosing one's own values. To get it, they're more than happy to have a "might makes right" attitude. In this world, there is no such thing as property or human rights, only the temporary facts of possession and advantage. The path of Neutrality does exist, but it is a hard road that will win you few friends.

The philosophical nature of this conflict means that the people in your world are likely to get caught up in it. Villains and heroes could easily end up working together if they have similar views on "Law vs Chaos", and friends might end up bitterly killing friends.
objects.title: War Broke Out In Heaven (Shin Megami Tensei)

objects.text:
At the pinnacle of your world of destination's metaphysics now stands the Divine Throne, occupied by a Hadou God, making the entire setting the result of this deity's emanation.

While this will not outwardly change the in-universe power systems or main plot in significant ways, now there is an intelligent presence at the top of creation, pursuing the goals only they themselves are privy to. Likewise, some inhabitants of the universe might have an inkling about the truth of the world, maybe even planning on supplanting the reigning deity and becoming the new God.

Depending on the setting's metaphysics, there might be a way to ascend to godhood, but even in this case, the divine spark that determines the right to sit atop the Throne and emanate a new world is only ever present in a select few.
objects.title: Divine Throne System (Shinza Bansho)

objects.text:
A single Borg cube has appeared in orbit above your starting world. Considering that a single Borg cube can take on a whole fleet of mid-24th century Federation ships, effortlessly seized control of 21st century Earth, has multiple redundant distributed systems so that it is fully functional even when 78 percent destroyed, regenerates, can create more of itself on-site with sufficient resources, and has a merciless army of 130,000 drones aboard, this is certainly cause for concern.

Their most terrifying ability, however, is also their primary goal: assimilation. Your biological, technological, cultural, & even supernatural distinctiveness will be added to their own, and you will adapt to service them. In other words, if an advantage your world might have in defending itself is relatively widespread (like Aura or Dust tech in RWBY), it will only take a few people with that ability to be assimilated for it to be become an advantage against you. This is not to mention that every warm body on your planet is a potential recruit, given their ability to convert other beings into drones. They can even adapt to your attacks on the fly; when the Enterprise encountered them it only took twelve or so shots on the drones for them to become impervious to phaser fire.

Your only hope of success against them is their absent-minded and task focused nature leading them to neglect strategy; if Borg drones are not actively searching for beings to assimilate or some other combative task like "guard this location", they'll ignore you, even if you're doing something with obvious long term consequences (like setting explosives around the Cube's power system).
objects.title: Resistance Is Futile (Star Trek)

objects.text:
"The knowledge and experience - of the human - Picard - is part of us now. It has prepared us for all possible courses of action. Your resistance is hopeless - Number One."
-Locutus Of Borg

The most inconvenient possible person for the Borg to assimilate, the one that represents the greatest possible increase in their capabilities, has been assimilated.

That is to say, whomever in this world besides yourself, your Companions, or anyone it would not be logically possible to assimilate (such as atomic level shapeshifters), would pose the greatest threat for the Borg to have assimilated, they have done so. Whether that's Lelouch's genius and knowledge of contemporary military tactics in Code Geass, Kal-El's advanced Kryptonian biology & technology in DC, supreme improvements in multitasking capacity from Taylor's Queen Administrator Shard in Worm, or the immortal God-Emperor on a Borg altered Golden Throne in 40k, almost no one is beyond their reach.

No matter what, this person becomes "Locutus Of Borg", a semi-independent terminal of the hivemind acting as a sort of temporary local Borg Queen, which allows for a much higher degree of strategy and coordination; the Borg Drones can now make what appear to be individual decisions related to the circumstances, meaning that their adaptability and reactiveness are comparable to that of independent humanoids.
objects.title: I Am Locutus (Star Trek)

objects.text:
Somehow, the Yuuzhan Vong have found their way into your galaxy. The Yuuzhan Vong are a theocratic society that views all technology as blasphemous. Their religion glorifies suffering; they practice ritual scarring and organ grafting to “improve” their bodies.

Their military power is built entirely on biotechnology. This ranges from organisms capable of creating “micro black holes” to swallow incoming torpedoes and laser fire, to massive, moon-sized organic vessels capable of carrying entire populations and planetary invasion forces.

You can expect about twenty to thirty worldships, each functioning as a mobile city-carrier capable of housing millions of beings. Each worldships is supported by one or two massive warships called Miid Ro'ik, comparable in size to Star Destroyers. Other vessels include Yorik-vec assault cruisers and Yorik-et high-speed organic starfighters, among others. Accompanying this fleet are millions of elite highly dedicated soldiers, as well as millions of Chazrach reptilian race used as shock troops—cannon fodder.

One of the primary means of invasion and area denial that the Vong use is terraforming—or “Vongforming”—worlds. They introduce their highly invasive ecology to a planet especially garden worlds, allowing it to alter even the planet’s atmosphere. This process is extremely difficult to reverse, and is referred as “worldshaping.”

The Vong believe they are the chosen race, and that all other life forms are inferior—meant to be enslaved or sacrificed. Because of this, they will kill or subjugate anyone in their path. Their goals are driven by a mix of desperation for survival—as their world-ships are dying—and religious fanaticism. They do not merely seek to rule the galaxy; they aim to destroy technology entirely and replace it with living systems.
objects.title: Children of Yun-Yuuzhan (Star Wars)

objects.text: During his service to the emperor, Vader finally asked who gained from his suffering. Following the destruction of the Death Star, and after a short but bloody power struggle, Darth Vader was named Emperor following Emperor Palpatine’s most unforeseen death. With his time devoted to management and not problem solving, Lord Vader has begun accounting to the issues of empire as he did with rogue agents in his last position. Swiftly and decisively. Though unable to take to the field as he once did, having a Chosen one at the head of your state does wonders for strategy, as does removing ineffective and problematic elements at the top of the imperial hierarchy, which he takes great pleasure with doing. Frequently. Notably, Vader has a distinct distaste for the doctrine of super-weapons (the Tarkin doctrine) preferring to expense vast fleets and technological superiority over larger weapons of terror, making the imperial seat of power far harder to dislodge as the force it’s credibly able to bring to bare ever increases. To continue the line of succession, it’s expected he will soon name an apprentice of his own as the emperor before once did. It’s assumed that they will be from the ranks of the Inquisitors he used to administer, but rumours say he has his eye on a more unexpected candidate… Outside of the public eye, Vader has had more time to think freely than he ever had under Darth Sidious, and more power to enact his will than ever before. It’s not unlikely that, like Revan before him, he’ll wander his way back to the light, albeit through a trail of fire and blood.
objects.title: Emperor Vader (Star Wars)

objects.text: Darth Bane was a fool and a rube, his death was deserved, quick and early with little impact on the galaxy. With Darth Bane’s rule of two dismissed, the Sith Order continued to spread across the galaxy, integrating into many areas before going underground. The new Sith Academy is a hidden sect, where they train others in the path of the dark side. As a result, a number of things have changed. First and foremost, the Jedi are far more militaristic than in the regular proceedings. Where they were once allowed to act as peacekeepers and de facto authority on The Force, the Sith provide a notable opposition that they must fervently oppose in each quarter. Similarly, with the Jedi’s influence relatively diminished, numerous cultures have become more aligned with the Sith. Mandalore’s pacifist movement for instance would still be in its earliest days by the Clone Wars with Mandalore still nominally signed to Sith ideals of struggle and righteous violence. And most strange, with centuries of knowledge in Sith Alchemy, practices, and dark-side research not destroyed by Darth Bane’s ill-conceived power-grab the galaxy at large is rife with what would be impossible without them. Living war machines, droids with Midichlorian implants, even species once rendered extinct returned through the might of the Dark.
objects.title: The Sith Academy (Star Wars)

addons.text: Instead of matching the strongest galactic powers of the Star wars universe from which era you decide to insert yourself into. The Yuuzhong Vong instead have twice the military might to be able to overwhelm the Galaxy.
addons.title: The Vong Cometh

objects.text: Instead of invading years after the defeat of the Galactic Empire, the Yuuzhong Vong, a species with a hatred of Technology and utilizing advanced Biological sciences, attack during whichever point in time you decide to enter the Star Wars Galaxy. The Vong, unlike their canon counterparts, will be a much greater threat in this AU, possessing a force strong enough to challenge and even threaten the current galactic governments like the Republic and the Sith Empire should you decide to reincarnate or drop in during the Old Republic Era.
objects.title: Yuuzhong Vong Invasion (Star Wars)
Mace Windu Lives (Star Wars)
objects.text:
Master Mace Windu was not disarmed during his confrontation with Darth Sidious. Although Anakin Skywalker still intervened on the Chancellor’s behalf, Windu retained his right hand and was instead struck by a devastating blast of Force lightning that hurled him through the shattered windows of the Chancellor’s office. The fall should have been fatal, but fate intervened when he crashed onto a passing skycar, forcing its stunned pilot to make an emergency landing and allowing the battered Jedi Master to escape with his life.

Heading for the Jedi Temple while suffering from his injuries, Mace Windu began to think about many things and was able to piece together the truth. First and foremost, was that Skywalker had willingly embraced the dark side, and the Chancellor had revealed himself as the Sith Lord the Jedi had hunted throughout the Clone Wars. Recalling the horrifying incident which had happened just a few months back in which the Clone Trooper known as Tup had suddenly murdered Jedi General Tiplar after suffering a mysterious mental break, Windu begins to suspect that event had never been an isolated malfunction.

Without wasting a moment, Mace Windu establishes contact with the head of the Jedi Temple Guard. He warned them of Skywalker’s betrayal, informing them that Chancellor Palpatine was Darth Sidious, the sith they had been searching for, and urged them to spread the word to every Jedi on Coruscant to prepare for an immediate assault. He also orders them to contact any of the Jedi off world to warn them of what is happening here on Coruscant. Mace Windu also informs the leader of the Jedi Temple Guard of his suspicions regarding the clone army, which leads him to caution them that the clones may launch an assault on the temple at any moment.

This single warning dramatically alters the opening hours of the Great Jedi Purge. The Jedi Temple Guard raise the Temple’s defenses, and evacuation plans are enacted to get as many Jedi off world as possible. This leads to countless Jedi surviving and escaping the attack on the temple that would have otherwise caught them completely unaware. Although the Republic still ends up becoming the Galactic Empire, the Jedi Order escapes total destruction.

objects.title: Fractured Orders (Star Wars)
objects.text:
When Chancellor Palpatine initiated the final stages of his plan to seize absolute control of the galaxy, fate dealt him two catastrophic blows. Upon transmitting Order 66, approximately half of all clone troopers experienced inhibitor chip malfunctions, leaving them completely unaffected by the command. Confused as their brothers suddenly turned on the Jedi, these clones retained their free will and, in countless cases, chose to defend the Jedi Generals and comrades they had fought beside throughout the Clone Wars. Moments later, when Darth Sidious transmitted the command to deactivate the Separatist Droid Army, another unforeseen failure occurred. Due to a widespread but previously undetected programming error, roughly half of all battle droids, along with many Tactical Droids, and other command units, ignored the shutdown order and remained fully operational.

The result was immediate chaos across the galaxy. Republic formations shattered into violent civil wars as loyal clones fought against brothers enslaved by their inhibitor chips, buying thousands of Jedi the precious time needed to escape. At the same time, surviving Separatist droid commanders swiftly reorganized the countless battle droids that remained under their control. Cut off from the Separatist Council, these machine leaders would take over factories, fortified strongholds, shipyards, and supply depots, each interpreting their final orders in different ways. Some continued the Clone Wars against the newly proclaimed Galactic Empire, others established independent machine-controlled territories, while a few attempted to preserve the ideals of the Confederacy without organic leadership.

The Galactic Empire is still born, but its foundation is far weaker than Palpatine intended. Rather than inheriting a galaxy stripped of its greatest military powers, the Emperor now faces three determined enemies: a surviving Jedi Order protected by loyal clone forces, large numbers of free-thinking clone troopers unwilling to accept Imperial rule, and a vast remnant of the Separatist Droid Army that continues to wage war across thousands of worlds. Instead of a swift transition into Imperial peace, the galaxy descends into a brutal and prolonged three-sided conflict that reshapes the fate of the Star Wars universe.

The very planetary cycles of this Earth are dramatically different from the one you know.

A year is exactly 112 days, there are only 4 months to a year, 28 days each, and finally each month is a different season with drastically different weather and environments even if only separated by a day.

For example there could be inches of snow on the first and last days of winter, but not a single snowflake falling from the sky a day before or after. 

Plants having evolved within these rapidly changing environments are also a bit different than the ones you know, namely it only takes most plants a few days to grow from seeds to complete physical maturity, with larger plants like trees only needing a few weeks at most.

Finally this hasn’t actually affected the lifespan of any animals one way or another, but the years being only about a third as long mean that people have a bit more than 3 times as many birthdays.
objects.title: Stardew Planetary Cycles (Stardew Valley)

objects.text:
In an uncharacteristic bout of international spirit, the Stargate wasn’t looted from Egypt halfway around the world, but instead remained in Egypt under a unified UN force. The result is a Stargate program that is highly internationalised  and under heavy civilian oversight rather than a purely militarised operation. 

As such, most discoveries made about the Stargate, physics as a whole, and the state of the galaxy are made public knowledge. Additionally, the UN’s control over the gate has led to a lot more power being placed on the organisation, now it possesses such a large bargaining chip. This also enforces its membership, as only member states have ready access to the gate’s benefits.

The program itself has become a measuring point for soft power, with major contributors to the program like the United States and China funding large swathes of it to exert their own influence. While this program may be more open than the original, the program itself is weighed down by international bureaucracy, while different nations scramble to try and figure out how to have a ‘homegrown’ Stargate organisation unbeholden to the original.
objects.title: La Porte des étoiles (Stargate)

objects.text: After insubordination, lying to superiors, and almost starting wars that EARTH cannot win, let alone the United States, the Stargate program was formally shut down. With the Stargate program formally ended in the 1990s the galaxy is still ruled by the Goa’uld, albeit bruised from their encounters, and more wary of their gates and territories. On earth meanwhile, the gap the Americans have left is being filled by various other governments. The Russian program has made the most headway, but is ultimately lacking a ‘map’ so to speak, while the largest number of American defectors are part of the British ‘Tiw’ project. Of course, as various nations are acting in their best interests a large amount of their policy is in hobbling each other and enriching their own national interests rather than for the benefit of earth, but really what’s changed other than the language?
objects.title: Consequences (Stargate)

objects.text:
The greatest American innovation, Privatisation! 

Having warehoused the Stargate since the 40s, the US government sold it off to private investors, who founded the research centre ‘Stargate’. Funded by private equity, the Stargate program is still concerned with acquiring alien technology, but more than that, the alluring fact US labour law doesn’t exist on other worlds. 

The slow corporate takeover of the stars has begun, and while the Tau’ri put the dollar back into idolatry as far as the Goa'uld are concerned, they’re most interested in finding new markets to corner, and new venues for endless expansion.
objects.title: The Stargate™©® Program (Stargate)

objects.text: Millions of years ago, all across the galaxy, an incredibly advanced precursor race known as the Ancients, Alterans, or Lanteans, seeded the galaxy with Stargates—devices roughly a few metres in diameter that connect to each other via an artificial wormhole and allow for near-instantaneous transportation from one gate to another. Naturally, what life has evolved in this galaxy built their civilisations mostly around the network those stargates provide, with your world being miraculously left out of galactic squabbles, as your gate was buried thousands of years ago, unable to be dialled. Until now. The stargate buried on Earth has been dug out by a recent archaeological expedition, and it is only a matter of time before the way to activate it is determined and the Earth has to integrate with the larger galactic community, for better or worse.
objects.title: Stargates (Stargate)

objects.text: Where Stargates were small things, barely enough to allow four people shoulder to shoulder, now they’re massive. Large enough for battalions to walk through while ships pass over their heads. While this has made them far more useful as transport, it has also made them both far more dificult to hide and far more dangerous as every activation can be seen for miles, and every traveller could be an invasion in progress.
objects.title: Mass Gate (Stargate)

addons.text: The long-dead race who designed the crystal gems, while masters of magitech, were not masters of robotics. They were masters of biotics. Rather than beings of metal, ceramic, wires, and other inorganic materials; Gemkind are designed to form and grow advanced bodies of sculpted flesh, blood and bone around their crystal cores. Advanced biological technology- from weapon systems, to processing units, to dedicated tools and supplementary senses- grown directly throughout their own bodies, all made with purposeful design to create biological super soldiers, servants, weapons, and more; supplementing the Gem's normal magical capabilities with strong, adaptable, and regenerating flesh. With training and conditioning, a Gem can grow even stronger. Not just through muscular growth, but also through incorporating or creating new magics, technology, and adaptations. As long as their cores are not damaged, such beneficial changes will not decay, either. The cores of Gems themselves run on a form of magi-tech code, but like the rest of their fleshy shells they are far more adaptable and enduring than the 'main continuity' Gems. Capable of both healing cracks to themselves over time, and adapting against external influence and corruption. Gem cores are the single most important part of a Gem; containing innate data and understanding of their caste biology and technology, any data needed for their specific caste and purpose, backup data of any beneficial mutations and changes they develop, as well as being the source of their magic, their minds, and the container of their souls. While they now have the ability to regenerate, grow, and adapt, their fleshy forms are not entirely beneficial over 'main continuity' Gems. Mostly in one, distinct category. Fusion between Gems is slower and more unstable. There is a high likelihood of minor incompatibilities between Gems during fusion causing cascading mental and physical issues, driving the Gems insane unless defused. On the flipside, successful fusions between Gems are contrarily far more stable, and will generally never defuse unless forcibly- often surgically- separated; for all intents and purposes becoming a singular, new being with the memories of its predecessors. Barring Diamonds, each type of Gem is able to (re)produce 'lesser' Gems of their own line, all the way down to the lesser shard-animals, given enough resources available to consume. Being made partially of meat has had extreme effects on Gem society compared to cannon. How this manifests is up to you, but at least the general plot of the 'main continuity' (barring other modifiers) will still take place.
addons.title: Magical Meat Machines

objects.text:
In this multiverse the artificial nature of Gems that is played with in canon is much more apparent here.

Essentially Gems are magitech robots originally made by a now dead race, that now self direct and propagate.

Gems still possess any and all abilities they possessed in canon, however their gems are usually placed within robotic bodies with the magic hardlight bodies you know from canon instead being an emergency feature that activates if their robotic body is destroyed so the Gem isn’t completely helpless.

This artificial nature extends towards the actual physical gem that forms the core of a Gem being itself a form of magitech computer, with a form of code that composes their mind.

All Gems are formed possessing the basic technological knowledge necessary to maintain or replace their robotic bodies, though some Gems through either natural capability such as Peridots or the effort to learn can possess the knowledge necessary to further modify their bodies.

These robotic bodies act as a magical focus for a Gem's natural abilities, and like most forms of technology can be modified. Though a Gem will obviously only possess abilities they modified their robotic bodies to possess when in that body.

A Gem’s robotic body is powered by their gem, which is much more efficient than forming a hardlight body which means that the power a Gem would otherwise use to form a hardlight body can further go into powering their abilities.

This also extends towards making Steven a cyborg, though just like canon he’ll need to learn what he’s capable of, as the only thing he’ll be born knowing is how to maintain and replace his cybernetics.

This artificial nature can optionally affect you if you’re a Gem, if you choose for it not to you’ll be the same mysterious type of being as a canon Gem.
objects.title: We Are The Crystal Gynoids! (Steven Universe)

objects.text:
For unknown reasons, people across the world began turning into monsters born from their own desires. Each transformation carried the imprint of who they once were: a child wishing to vanish became a slime-like creature, while a man craving power turned into a body grotesquely twisted with muscle. Yet all of them lost their reason. Their speech often collapsed into meaningless repetition of their desires, while their hearing sharpened to the extreme, making them react to the slightest sound. Most were driven by hunger—and more often than not, that hunger was directed at humans.

These monsters were terrifyingly resilient. Simple wounds could not stop them—even shattered bodies would regenerate unless the head was destroyed or the creature burned entirely. Their presence warped mobile signals: phones lost connection and instead emitted a shrill, anxious tone whenever a monster drew near.

The path to transformation began with nosebleeds, fainting spells, and intrusive voices whispering inside one’s head. That voice—the Entity behind it all—urged each victim to embrace their deepest desires and surrender. Some broke within a day, others resisted for weeks, and the strongest clung to themselves until the very end, sometimes even retaining control for brief moments during their monstrous episodes.

The minds of the transformed were trapped within the "Dream World," a realm where every desire was fulfilled. But once those desires were spent, the monster cocooned itself. In time, the cocoon opened, revealing a humanoid figure stripped of all emotion. These “evolved” beings neither aged nor died in ordinary ways—when destroyed, they returned to a cocoon, and only fire could erase them for good. They felt no hostility toward humans, yet sought to push them toward the same transformation, seeing in them kindred who had not yet “Awakened”.
objects.title: Desire Monsters (Sweet Home)

objects.text:
Four "infections" have begun to spread upon your world, warping the land and each carrying their own dangers—and, potentially, rewards.

Hailing from beyond the stars, the Astral Infection crashes down into the world in a blazing meteor. This star-borne illness is a blight upon the world, warping the natural order and twisting all it touches into vicious mockeries of their former selves. The infection’s presence is denoted by an alien, starry sky and a transformed landscape, calling back to the distant world from which it originated. Be wary—for the infection possesses a mind of its own and will preserve powerful hosts to serve as guardians, defending itself against threats. While sapient minds can muster the will to resist the infection’s siren call with effort, things without a will—such as animals, machines, and the deceased—have no such defenses.

Similarly, a formless mass of flesh has landed upon the world, half-dead yet still pulsing with ichor and driven by a primal need to survive. Make no mistake: the Crimson is still alive—at least partially—its depths still warm and throbbing with faint, scattered heartbeats. The Crimson consumes all it can, devouring to spread itself and spawn its children—twisted flora and fleshy monstrosities which wield both flesh and divine blood as their weapons. While weak now, if allowed to grow and gather strength, the beings spawned by the Crimson will begin to display overtly mystical properties, harnessing the power of the twisted ichor within.

A rogue arcano-bioweapon has been unleashed—a deadly microbe capable of corrupting seemingly anything. The spawn of twisted alchemy and foul magic, the Corruption rots land and life alike. Those touched by the Corruption exist in a perpetual state of decay, serving as vectors to spread the plague, infused with unnatural strength. At times, infected flesh may even cluster together to form mighty beasts driven by an urge to propagate the infection, or hives which exhibit rudimentary intelligence and guide the infection in its growth. Owing to its partially arcane origins, if left to grow strong enough, the Corruption will begin to manifest more potent magical properties, the foul sorcery fueling it being harnessed to spread its curse ever further.

And lastly, from within the depths of the Earth, ancient spirits of Light have been released—yet just because they are Light does not mean they are good. The Hallow is a pastel landscape of bright colors and fantastical inhabitants, but the Light does not tolerate what it sees as filth and will seek to purge all that is not Hallowed. Its creatures are infused with radiant energy, empowered by a furious desire to cleanse anything they deem corrupted. This is to say nothing of the fae-like elementals of chaotic light, or the shimmering crystal-filled depths beneath the surface.
objects.title: Twisted World (Terraria: Calamity Mod)

objects.text:
Fourty years ago, an unknown catastrophic event caused all of Humanity to lose almost all memories of his past. Much of the civilized world was reduced to deserts and ruins. Almost all records of the past and society were burned away in the calamity. Even now, those who live on and were even born after the calamity have trouble forming long-term core memories, though they are perfectly fine remembering enough to function in everyday life.

Despite this, humans are adaptable creatures, and a good chunk of technical knowledge remains. What passes as society presses on even without the hopes, ambitions, hatreds and fears that drove it before. A few cities, despite being half in ruins, continue to be lived in as people rebuilt what little they could remember about their lives and society. Despite the societal reset, those who held the technology and infrastructure that keeps the cities running have once again amassed wealth and power, while the poorest live in run-down slums and turn to crime. Cities are highly isolated, as most people would find it difficult to imagine that something else could even exist beyond the deserts that surround them. And without a past, people cannot know what their future will be, so most wander aimlessly.

Occasionally, broken data devices will be found or people will awaken with memories of the world before. These memories are highly sought after, not only for the knowledge and curiosity they provide, but the power they wield. These can be small details or conversation, or maybe a face one once knew, though those might not have even belonged to you. Fragments of culture and history are also sought after, but the most valuable and dangerous are those that allow those that hold them to reactivate or even build powerful buried technologies that may or may not be related to the world’s destruction. Most people are unaware of their past, oblivious to the secrets that may be hidden there, a few go mad chasing memories or seeking true knowledge, and there are those at the top and in the shadows who know more than they let on.
objects.title: The City of Amnesia (The Big O)

objects.text:
Within your world, it was once common to find folks called "Lost Ones." Wonderers from another world, summoned into your own to help with whatever affairs their summoners called them for, mostly for heroism or warfare. As such, they are empowered by "Pure Concepts", immense abilities that seem to be tied to fundamental aspects of reality. For a quick example, a Lost One tied to the Pure Concept of Null could destroy almost anything, sending things back into nothingness, and so on.

This is all well and good, however, there is a catch. Pure Concepts slowly corrupts their users the more they use them. The more a Lost One's ability develops, the more their Pure Concept devours their humanity, their memories, and pretty soon, their very being, twisting them to become mere vessels of their own abilities. The Pure Concept of Chaos for example, once a happy girl who loves movies, is now a creature that spreads monsters to sow chaos, their concept utilizing their love of horror for this end. These corrupted Lost Ones are called Human Errors, and they bring calamity to their worlds, as their powers go out of control, spreading violently until they are put down.

With this choice, Human Errors had already brought terror in your world in the past. It has since been made illegal to summon Lost Ones, with an organization dedicated to killing Lost Ones being formed as a result. This isn't the only way to deal with Lost Ones however, as a Lost One can be sent back to their world though at a major price, or, a Lost One could simply abstain from using their powers, making sure their Pure Concept dies with them instead.

Lost Ones are beings of immense powers. You could be facing a threat worse than Endbringers if you aren't careful. So what will you do, in this world where human weapons becomes the very thing that teethers the world into destruction?
objects.title: Lost Ones' Catastrophes (The Executioner and Her Way of Life)

objects.text: For some baffling reason, there's a single day every year in your setting where every crime is just suddenly legal. No laws, just do whatever you want, go. Now, whether that works the same way it does in the movies where several factors made it so that it was encouraged for people to outright begin killing each other, or if something more reasonable occurs such as people looting and vigilante killings being more of a thing, that highly depends on you and the setting you enforced this to. This especially becomes even more dangerous depending on your setting's power level, Gods help you if this is established in some place like The Boys or One Piece for some quick examples. Regardless, how this overall affects your setting, how widespread and accepted it is, as well as how people go about dealing with it is all up to you. Keep in mind as well that how widespread this is might also have to take on the setting as a major factor. The Imperium of Man probably won't be that willing for a full on go ahead to all heretical activity for a day, but certain planets might be. Same with Panem, but for singular districts only per year, etc. The only thing that's for sure is wherever you spawn, there will be a Purge Day. Will you take part of this madness? Or would you rather just chill on your couch somewhere and let this day pass by.
objects.title: Let Crime Be Legal (The Purge)

objects.text:
Long ago, a people called the Lokomo chained a great demon called Malladus below the earth. To ensure he would never escape, they built the Spirit Tracks to chain him. Powered by the Spirit Tower, they ensure the great demon remains jailed, unable to do harm ever again.

Whatever may be the story of your world, the Spirit Tracks exist there now. You may choose how far they cover. Maybe they cover the area of a small nation, maybe they cover a whole continent, or even the whole world. Whatever the case, this changes things. For one, the tracks can be used as regular train tracks. You could make that any culture that developed near than invented or discovered trains earlier than usual, and developed their culture around them. Is the world more united? Do they fight over stations? The tracks DO go over (and bellow) the ocean, so the world can be fully connected.

Aside from the tracks, there are the temples and the Spirit Tower. The temples are dungeons that gather the energy required by the Tower, that in turn energizes the Spirit Tracks and maintains them. While the game has only a handful of temples, the vaster the Spirit Tracks are in your world, the more temples the world will have, though only a single Spirit Tower will exist. 
Should enough temples be destroyed, the Tower will start to fail to maintain the tracks, and eventually Malladus will escape.
objects.title: Spirit Tracks (Legend of Zelda)

objects.text:
Your world is now subject to a cycle that constantly serves to end civilization, making way for something new.

Every few centuries or so, creatures known as Legendz begin appearing. They appear to be based on mythological creatures, and vary in terms of sapience. During this time, soon will emerge 4 Great Legendz, representing Wind (Shiron the Wind Dragon), Fire (Greedo the Fire Dragon), Earth (Garion the Griffin), and Water (Zuou the Bigfoot). All four will bond with chosen ones called Sagas, and thus will begin the prelude to the Legendz War.

The Sagas are bonded with their Legendz spiritually, the Legendz not only gaining some personality traits from their Saga, but are also unable to separate far from them as well, or else weaken so much that they might die. They also feel each other's pain, a Legendz' life being threatened should their Saga end up dying.

Once each Saga and Great Legendz were awakened, the Wind Dragon is fated to inevitably trigger the war. His roar shall awaken the 4 Elemental Kings, who's power shall reduce most Legendz into a feral state, kick-starting the conflict. This inevitable war shall cause the Legendz kingdom and your world to begin merging. And as the horror continue, this terror and tragedy only serves to fuel the Dark Dragon, Jabberwock, whom shall end civilization as you know it.

This war shall happen. The Sagas shall be found, and maybe one of them could even be you. You can only hope to minimize the damage this tragedy shall cause. And only then shall this round of the cycle end. With everyone forgetting the war even happened, while every Legendz disappear back into their homeworld, which begins to separate from your world, awaiting the next cycle.

Could you survive this inevitable societal collapse? Or die trying?
objects.title: Legendz War (Legendz: Tale of the Dragon Kings)

objects.text: Around the world, strange trees “grow” across the populous part of the globe. Gigantic in height and with an abnormal composition, almost pitch black in coloration, lacking leaves to speak of, and even a pointed appearance. Emitting an odd hum, almost a hymn, some might find compelling. Almost impossible to chop or damage, and for those brave enough to try, the tree will inexplicably release flashes of light and curve downwards in an arc, disappearing the ones responsible. What others weren’t aware of is that these Trees aren’t Trees, they are Special. Coming in a variety of forms, depending on where they are in the Multiverse, aside from being treelike in appearance, they even develop humanoid traits. The Special Trees live under a cooperative, interdependent relationship with their ecosystem, choosing their stationary lifestyle and communicating with their environment through their psychic hum. Each tree is connected to the others through a land beyond time and space called Wonderland, acting as wormholes if they curve in an arch, for anything struck by their lightning will allow them to travel different dimensions and universes, and cross over different planes of existence (if any). Wonderland, in turn, reflects the Trees’ true scale: a dimension robbed of color, where time and space aren’t concepts, with a surface akin to baby powder, bodies from past victims that appear stretched through the plane, and those who survive and are prolongedly exposed mutate into elongated abominations, maddened by their plight. All of this is part of the greater Entity, as the plane is a place and being both, its metastructure: The Hornet Serpent, created by its own arm, ensuring the creation with no known origin point. Its physical manifestation lies beneath the United States as its “creator”, slumbering and gorging on its populace, he is a potential True Force of Mass Destruction, as a sufficiently potent disaster or fight may wake him from his slumber, and crack the Earth whole. From the time you introduce yourself, they’ll be GOIs aware of this containing or revering him, doing all it takes to ensure their agenda comes to fruition, whether it is keeping him asleep or making the end of the world as we know it. Regardless, there’s only one truth out all of this: The Hornet Serpent Lives.
objects.title: Wonderland (THE MONUMENT MYTHOS)

objects.text: All across the world, legends of monsters and strange beings can be found. Vampires, Werewolves, Nymphs, Fairies, Kitsune, Thunderbirds, Kappa, Mothmen, Angels, Demons, Imps, Moon Rabbits, and even more myths, both old and new. Normally, they'd just be stories found in books and shows, nothing more. That was, until you selected this modifier, and suddenly they became very, very real... and also they all look like cute girls for some reason? Everywhere you look, various supernatural beings called Youkai will begin to appear, slowly at first, but eventually you won't be able to find a town, village, or forest without at least one in it. Despite the name referring to beings from Japanese folklore specifically, these beings are based on all kinds of myths and legends, not just Japan’s. Monsters, Spirits, Gods, Demons, and not just them, but even the mythological realms they inhabit, like the Dreamworld, a strangely habitable region of the moon, functional afterlives like the Netherworld, Heaven, and Hell, and more, will all begin to become real. Some may be just like the myths they represent (aside from the whole cute girl thing, don’t think about it), but others will barely resemble their legends, like Fairies who instead of being powerful, name-stealing pseudo-deities are instead child sized nature spirits who enjoy fun, pranks, and burst into ‘P-Points’ when they die only to reappear a minute later good as new. All the same, though, they are in fact affected by their myths, and at least paying lip service to them is required for a Youkai to exist lest they literally fade away. This can be somewhat concerning, especially for the Youkai based on myths of malevolent creatures who need fear to stay alive, or those who are based on maneaters who need to regularly consume human flesh and blood. Still, though, there are in fact benign and even benevolent Youkai, such as Komainu, who guard shrines or Gods who grant prayers and perform miracles for their followers. Youkai are made of magic, and so can’t be permanently harmed by mundane means, only by either attacks that contain meaning (such as a swordsman wielding an ancestral blade who sees it as an extension of themself) or by the supernatural, such as power users or magitech wielders. More than that, since they are made of magic, they possess magic powers, specifically a personal power usually related to their species’ mythos (such as a Satori’s mind reading or a Magician’s spellwork), as well as some universal powers like flight, Danmaku, and Spellcards. If a human managed to get magic, they could theoretically ascend to become a Youkai themselves by several methods. Note: While Youkai are certainly dangerous, especially since some can be extremely powerful, most will at least try to live in relative peace with humanity, and even the more actively malicious Youkai are invested in mankind's continued existence since without humans, they too would die. Even demons from hell are surprisingly chill (if arrogant and have a temper) and can even form genuine friendships with humans. Still, expect a lot of chaos, especially as some Youkai have rather inhuman perspectives and think doing something like creating a never-ending party that traps guests or stealing the concept of spring to see a demon tree bloom as nothing more than harmless fun. Also, while normally Youkai would not fare well in low-fantasy high-science worlds like a modern Earth, the Youkai who appear because of this modifier won’t have this issue and can exist just fine even in a hard sci-fi setting that actively rejects fantasy. This may have unintended consequences for worlds with preexisting magic and fantasy, especially ones where it died out, possibly causing it to return in force. This absolutely will have consequences for worlds with preexisting afterlives and gods. You have been warned.
objects.title: Youkai, Mysticism, and Gods, Oh My! (Touhou Project)

objects.text:
The World you arrived on is facing a cataclysm, for it has garnered the interest and hunger of a dark cosmic god older than the universe and known by many names: The Uncreator, The Anti-Life, The Planet Eater, The Chaos Bringer, Unicron, an Eldritch God and Multiversal Singularity who predates the known universe with only one goal: the death of the universe he has found himself in and from there, the multiverse.

Unicron will first send his Terracons, Transformers formed from his very body, based on organisms that were either devoured and remade through Unicron's own flesh or undead mechanical organisms reanimated through the power of Dark Energon, which will spread the corrupting influence of Unicron to flesh, metal, and spirit alike.

Unicron's heralds come in varying forms, though most heralds are Cybertronians corrupted by the power of Unicron and forever severed from the AllSpark and now bound to his own Anti-Spark, meaning that even if they are destroyed physically, they can remake their bodies unless they have angered their dark master.

Beware ye intrepid few, for you stand against the Chaos Bringer. Fools both Mortal and Divine alike have risen to face the Dark God, yet all, save a few, have fallen before his terrible might, consumed by destruction or twisted by corruption. Should you face him, may Primus guide your hand and guard your spark.
objects.title: The Chaos Bringer: Unicron (Transformers)

objects.text:
An impossible world that shouldn't exist. The Age of Gods had ended as it was supposed to, and yet the Age of Mystics took its place. Magecraft is exposed to the world from the start, even if its individual mysteries remain secret, and the Mage's Association and Holy Church become overt organizations.

History of all countries still largely follows the same original pattern, which is perhaps half of a reason why this world is permitted to exist. In a timeline where "mage" is a normal public profession, which shape could the Holy Grail War take?

As byproducts of this change Magecraft's existence as a whole is far more stable than in canon, while mystical phenomena in general is far more common from humans, animals, plants, phantasmals, the environment, and even the planetary consciousness itself. 

Speaking of the planetary consciousness of Earth; for whatever reason, Gaia is in no real risk of dying here like they are in some other timelines.

You may optionally extend the effects and implications of this modifier to most timelines across this multiverse, making it the norm instead of the exception.
objects.title: Lost Fantasy (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
The average quantity and quality of environmental mana, od, and magical circuits in the modern world remain just as high as they were during The Age of Gods with no signs of degrading in the future, all being considered a natural part of The World. 

This means so long as a Magus is skilled enough or utilizes the appropriate Mystery that the difference between a modern Magus and one from The Age of Gods is only the time period they lived in instead of innate quality.

This also means that a first rate Magus like Rin Tohsaka could possess personal reserves of magical energy favorably comparable to the average Phantasmal even if it’s rare for them to command a similar quality of Mystery.

Understandably this increased magical energy to play around with compared to canon has led even the most Mystery starved Magecraft to be capable of spectacular displays with even a modicum of skill or a halfway decent setup.

It should also be noted that The Human Order and Alaya specifically have also been buffed by the increased magical energy making the worldwide situation similar to canon.

This means other species are forced out of the limelight and if they try to forcibly interact with humanity in an obvious wide reaching fashion or threaten The Human Order then the strengthened Alaya fights them off. Though interacting with these species is still far easier than in canon especially if they’re sought out as many could have homes in the hidden corners of Earths surface.

One final thing to note is if you have magical circuits their quality and quantity remain unchanged by this modifier. 

This modifier can optionally be the norm for Earth throughout the multiverse instead of an oddity.
objects.title: Modern Aether (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
The old cycle was over and they needed to adapt in order to have a future.

With that in mind the remaining Entity would enter a series of negotiations with the planetary consciousness; resulting in The Warrior and the remaining living Shards, like many aliens before them, to be adopted by Gaia. 

This adoption means that all remaining living Shards from the Warrior and Thinker Hub’s become genuine children of the Earth on a conceptual level, while giving Gaia access to all their Data. Dead Shards in turn would begin rapidly breaking down into usable esoteric resources that couldn’t be easily synthesized, which Gaia would use in conjunction with their newly acquired Data to improve itself on a multiversal scale. 

Suffice to say Gaia is in no real danger of dying anytime soon even if a different modifier hadn’t already prevented such a scenario.

As proof of their adoption the Shards have been granted divinity with the surviving Entity becoming the chief deity of this new pantheon. Despite being divine, Shards and The Entity are still allowed to interact with the modern Human world and take hosts because of all they have provided Gaia.

The wealth of Data having divinity and a connection to Gaia provides will grant the surviving Shards a form of negentropy if they didn’t already possess negentropy.

Given the capabilities Shards already possess, gaining negentropy is the most notable aspect of divinity for them. Parahumans however still benefit because that divinity and connection to Gaia allows Shards to act as a Foundation for magecraft development providing Parahumans a spectacular degree of freedom in how they develop their powers, becoming natural Magi able to sense and manipulate environmental magical energy into spells based off their Shard even if they don’t possess a single magic circuit themselves.

The amount of magical energy a Parahuman can innately manipulate from their connection to a Shard scales with their Shard so the average Parahuman might only be slightly above average for a Magus. Meanwhile, someone with a high grade powerful Shard might be comparable to a Magus from The Age of Gods. 

Being a Magus or having awakened magic circuits in general does not preclude someone from triggering into a Parahuman. Nor does becoming a Parahuman stop someone with dormant magical circuits from awakening those circuits. 

Of the Thinker Shard’s that survived the Shard’s of the Triumvirate including Eidolon can be counted among that number. Meaning that Endbringers are still around and have become genuine divine beasts due to their connection to divinity. 

On the plus side Eidolon gets to enjoy negentropy so he does much better in Endbringer fights. Also due to being connected to Gaia now, Endbringer attacks are less targeted at causing destruction to civilization, and more focused on being disasters for humans to overcome.
objects.title: Adoptive Planet (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
In canon Reality Marbles are a rare phenomena on Gaia, both the type that arise naturally from the souls of creatures and those that are artificially created via a variety of methods. 

No longer; in this multiverse every single soul born of Gaia has a natural Reality Marble that reflects their soul and mentality.

Only those who can generate or otherwise utilize magical energy can truly activate and develop their Reality Marbles so the human world is mostly the same as you remember it, with the common public belief being that Reality Marbles are just instinctively created mental constructs that your mind never really forgets, Magi and those otherwise aware of the Moonlit World however do know the truth and commonly utilize their Reality Marbles for magecraft.

Given the prevalence of natural Reality Marbles making the phenomenon easier to study, artificial Reality Marbles are quite common in advanced forms of boundary fields.

Those who naturally would’ve had a Reality Marble without this modifier will find themselves with increased talent when it comes to developing their Reality Marble and its applications. On average making twice as much progress in half the time if they put in the same effort as they did in canon.

This modifier can optionally affect you, giving you potential to develop a Reality Marble if you didn’t already have one from another option you purchased, or giving similarly increased talent if you already gained a Reality Marble.
objects.title: Fate/Reality (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
