Fun fact, Shinji Matou does have working circuits. A large number of high-quality magic circuits befitting the scion of an old Magus family. The problem, however, is that the Makiri/Matou family foundation and natural mystical attributes are incredibly incompatible with the mystical environment of Japan that generations of his family living and being born in Japan made it so Shinji has a much harder time awakening those circuits.

Something along the lines of his circuits needing the magical equivalent of a nuke in order to be properly awakened from this extreme dormancy.

In this world Shinji doesn’t let these dormant circuits stop him from becoming a Magus; instead, he focuses his time, talent, dedication, and considerable desire to be a Magus towards learning Formalcraft.

Formalcraft is a method to use Magecraft through environmental mana and other external sources of magical energy. The only true requirement is knowledge and adapting the rituals and processes to be appropriate for the Magecraft being cast in question.

With Formalcraft as his means of casting, Shinji learns any and all types of Magecraft available for him to learn in the Matou library just for the fun of learning Magecraft, research, and advancing his personal goals.

With his increased worth in the eyes of Zouken, Shinji has been granted considerably more access to the Matou’s accumulated resources and contacts compared to canon. This makes it relatively easy for him to contact other Magi around the world and buy knowledge about various types of non-secret Magecraft the Matou library doesn’t cover in detail. Along with the purchase of materials he might need for his Magecraft and research.

Despite this, he desperately wants to have his natural magic circuits be awakened, correctly feeling that they would make it so much easier for him to be a Magus and advance his Magecraft research. 

Before the Fifth Grail War, his plan was to slowly gather and stockpile the needed magical energy into mystic codes he created over the course of a few decades, but winning The Fifth Grail War offers such an amazing shortcut towards that goal that you can be sure he’ll try his best to win.

With his skill in Magecraft and resources at his disposal, he’ll be sure to grant any servant at his command every advantage he can, including all the magical energy they might need to operate at full capacity with far more ease compared to canon.

His skillset by the canon start of The Fifth Grail War is very advanced and well-rounded regarding many types of Magecraft but has a focus on spiritron hacking, spiritual surgery, alchemy, modern runes, bounded fields, jewel magecraft, mystic codes, and familiars.

It’s up to you if these changes to his character have changed his personality and relationships with the people in his life for the better or worse.

When purchasing this modifier you may optionally make this the norm for Shinji throughout this multiverse instead of an exception.
objects.title: Formal Matou Heir (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
In this timeline, when Shirou first started learning magecraft, Kiritsugu ensured he properly learned the basics, including properly opening his natural magical circuits.

Unexpectedly, Kiritsugu would find that Shirou has all the makings of a first rate magus in talent and inclination, genuinely loving the process of learning and advancing his skill with magecraft.

While initially put off by his enthusiasm, Kiritsugu would do his best to foster his son’s talent while ensuring Shirou still developed proper morals.

Upon Kiritsugu’s death, Shirou would inherit a small library of books and tomes about various types of magecraft Kiritsugu had looted over the years, along with all sorts of other magecraft resources and connections Kiritsugu accrued.

By the start of the canon Fifth Grail War, Shirou will have grown into a capable Magus skilled in various forms of magecraft including figuring out his reality marble. A few specific forms of magecraft his skillset has a particular focus on includes alchemy, bounded fields, reinforcement, alteration, projection, Spiritron Hacking, temporal magecraft, spatial magecraft, and the creation of Mystic Codes that he can use as mediums to cast forms of magecraft that aren’t compatible with his sword affinity.

Shirou is still a kind person who seeks to do good, but advancing his magecraft is more important to him than vicariously living out his father’s dream.

If you want, being a more active and capable Magus could result in Shirou meeting Rin in her capacity as Second Owner of Fuyuki years before the Fifth Grail War. This meeting can go amicably, ending with both gaining a strong friendship and appreciation for each other’s presence, or negatively, with the consequences of which are yours to decide.

When purchasing this modifier you may optionally chose for this to be the norm for Shirou throughout this multiverse instead of an exception.
objects.title: First Rate Sword (Type-Moon)

objects.text: In the end, the planet simply wants to keep existing. There are two collective wills that protects the planet from events that may lead to its death. First is Gaia, which is the will of the planet itself, and from it sprung Alaya the collective unconscious of humanity. Both have a defense mechanism to protect themselves, but, due to the difference in priority, conflict tends to happen between the two. Said defence mechanism is either through subtle influence or by summoning agents loyal to either. This does help in continuing to keep the Earth alive, but, both don't exactly have a conscience. So it could stop an international war from going or it can wipe an entire city off the map. This is of course, both a good and a bad thing. In this world, your planet or whatever place you're in developed a "Gaia" and "Alaya" of their own. You may end up encountering their agents who may or may not be hostile to your arrival. You can also, potentially, make a deal with Alaya in particular to become its Counter Guardian. Giving you interesting abilities at the cost of devoting yourself as an eternal planetary janitor.
objects.title: Counter Forces (Type-Moon)

objects.text:
In your chosen world, there now exists a planet 60 times the size of Earth known as the "Land of Light," with a population of over 18 billion giants of light, each standing 40 to 50 meters tall on average.

Once similar to ordinary humans, their ancestors created an artificial sun to heat their planet after their own sun had died. This resulted in an unforeseen effect that evolved them into giants of light and granted them immense powers. Now known throughout the cosmos as "Ultras," they have dedicated themselves to becoming peacekeepers and protectors of the universe, sending members of their species across the cosmos to protect planets and battle any threats they encounter.

The Ultras of the Land of Light will consist of every single iteration of Ultraman depicted throughout the franchise, from the original Ultraman to Ultraman Zero, as well as the Father and Mother of Ultra, Ultraman Hikari, and Ultraman King. However, this will also bring any threats that originated from their world or were created by the Ultras, such as Ultraman Belial and Dark Lugiel.

In addition, the Ultras do not limit themselves to protecting a single universe. If your chosen world is a multiverse, they will send members of their species to protect other universes. There might even somehow emerge a new Ultraman in another universe who, regardless of the Land of Light's involvement, rises to protect that world. This also means Ultraman Noa will travel throughout the multiverse, dealing with whatever issues he encounters.
objects.title: Land of Light (Ultraman Series)

addons.text:
As if the strange fondness donkeys have for you wasn’t unusual enough, the world takes an even stranger turn with the existence of the Roba Musume (Donkey Girls), a rare type among the Uma who embody everything that makes donkeys unique—absurd stamina, unshakable stubbornness, and the ability to deliver incredibly powerful kicks.

Before you fully realize what’s happening, you find yourself at the center of it all as a small group of Roba Musume gathers around you as if it were the most natural thing in the world, forming a team that, although chaotic at first glance, works surprisingly well when it truly matters.

Depending on how you choose to interact with them, you can take on the role of a trainer—developing an almost instinctive talent for bringing out their best, coordinating their efforts, and refining their potential—or simply remain the one they naturally gravitate toward, letting them act on their own while you stay at the heart of their world.
addons.title: Roba Musume

addons.text: The Uma Musumes are now empowered by the three main Equestrian pony races, giving them magic rather similar to how Equestria Girls' pony related magical girl powers works. Otherwise, this provides Umas with brand new potential career paths as well, from Pegasi Umas helping maintain the weather, Earth Pony Umas using their druidic abilities to develop agriculture, to Unicorn Umas delving into the secrets of magic. Finally, some My Little Pony characters may also appear as their Uma counterparts. Overall, it is a more magical world, but the will to run and achieve racing glory is still there for all Umas.
addons.title: My Little Uma

addons.text: Uma Musumes are now blessed by the spirits of the wind, giving them more horse-like features and a deluge of trickery spells they use to mess with us puny humans. This added blessings makes Uma Musume races even more intense, with Umas taking the forms of race cars and speeding through the track like it's a formula 1 race instead. Of course, their trickster sides aren't to be scoffed at too, as some Umas have taken up the role of environmental protectors, leading selfish humans astray, away from their precious forests their people have long protected. Of course, as a fellow Tikbalang, you are one of them, whether you decide to pursue your racing goals, live with your fellow Umas as forest guardians, or something else, it is up to you.
addons.title: Trickster Umas

addons.text: Umas are no longer restricted to just being assigned female at birth. Whether this means all Umas are now Uma Musuko, meaning they're all males, or if it means both Uma Musuko and Uma Musume exists, it is up to you.
addons.title: Uma Musuko

objects.text:
The world you are going to will now have Uma Musume, Horse Girls, as part of the setting and history. These Umas have greater stamina and speed that surpasses humans, being more comparable to real-life horses, with Umas having their ears on the top of their heads and horse tails; otherwise, they are largely similar to humans. Uma Musumes can be born from normal human parents and can have children with humans without issue, the only thing being that the daughters of an Uma are highly likely to be an Uma themselves, but it's not a certainty.

Umas are a part of the world and are accepted, with them being adored by many, and more than a few accommodations being made for them, from special lanes in the road to clothes being styled a certain way. It's fairly common for Uma Musume to have two dreams: to be the best racer/runner they can be and to sing. Because of this, becoming professional runners and music stars is fairly common amongst these Horse Girls, but few reach the top, with some good at running but bad singers, and vice versa.

A few things to take note of are that there cannot be any Horse Boys, Uma Shonen; there are no normal horses in the setting anymore due to Uma Musume being here, and history largely remains the same even with the lack of real horses and the inclusion of literal Horse Girls. The Uma-to-Human ratio is about 1:1,000; for every 1 Uma, there are a thousand humans.

Oh, and you can't gamble on Uma Musume races.
objects.title: Hashire! Hashire! (UmaMusume)

objects.text:
Your world is inhabited by the Leviathan, a being representing the collective unconscious of humanity, containing all stories within it (which from some perspectives includes the ones you see as reality) in an infinite self-recursive hierarchy which loops around on itself again and again. This makes it possible to travel between stories, if you know what you’re doing and find the places where they intersect. Leviathan has a symbiotic relationship with humanity, where it is fed by the telling of stories and humans are enabled to understand the world as a result.

Leviathan also acts as an “interface” of sorts for the power of human belief, allowing ideas to become reality if enough people believe in them; even the sort of belief that comes from entertaining the idea of magic as real when reading a fantasy story can, given a proper outlet, make magic actually real, if only for the person that belief is projected onto. This has more to do with proportion of humanity than number; back at the dawn of humanity all it took was a few words to catch Leviathan’s attention and make it rewrite reality, while these days you would need to write a series of worldwide bestsellers to get the same effect.

Leviathan has a tendency to “play favorites.” Once it’s noticed an individual and taken an interest in them it never really lets go of the idea of them, which makes it impossible for them to die so long as Leviathan lives and causes the story to bend around them and the narrative role they’ve been assigned. Just being well-known isn’t enough to make this happen, the vast majority of famous figures aren’t affected by this; it really comes down to how Leviathan feels.

As powerful as it is, it is actually possible to kill Leviathan. If it can be baited into entering reality (which is technically inside itself from some perspectives, don’t think too hard about it) then it can be attacked, and with the right weapons and the right story it can actually be harmed. If Leviathan dies, or is dying, humanity as a collective will gradually lose interest in stories as they lose their ability to process them, and the fictional worlds will decay and collapse into one another.

After that things start to really go bad, as the young of Leviathan’s species start popping up to take its place. These are, to put it nicely, less discerning than Leviathan. They’ll latch on to random people and make whatever stories they tell or think of come true, whether the host wants it to happen or not. In the later stages this results in a world where the entirety of fiction has manifested into reality and the laws of physics have gone to lunch and never come back. Of course, it is possible to come to an understanding with one of the Leviathan Fries, in which case you would be protected from the chaos and potentially able to harness its power for yourself, so there are potential upsides for the ruthless.

Still, the preferable option is probably just for Leviathan to stay alive and unharmed. Luckily, it’s not like it’s that difficult to make sure it stays that way.
objects.title: The Leviathan (Unwritten)

objects.text:
In 1938, a population boom of an unknown species, assigned the Vita Carnis genus, owing to their fleshy constitution and lack of a cutaneous membrane, made only of muscle, flesh, and bone occurs. 

Their reproductive cycle comes from the near-worldwide Crawl (Scandere Carnis), changing without fully disrupting the ecosystem and sustaining itself like any plant, their fruits acting more like eggs from which all following Vita Carnis species spring, ranging from the harmless Trimmings (Ignavus Carnis), Meat Snakes (Mutuari Carnis), to the dangerous Mimics (Trucidatum Carnis), Harvesters (Congregentur Carnis), and Host of Influences (Imperium Carnis).

Nothing is as it seems, however: A cult arises worshipping the Carnis; 120-meter Monoliths (Coelum Carnis) appear around Newfoundland, guarding or protecting something... or someone; the existence of an eighth Carnis species is hidden, an idol of worship for the Cult and the aliens responsible for the Carnis’ emergences. 

For all will join together in divine purpose.
objects.title: Rise of the Living Meat (Vita Carnis)

objects.text:
A Chaos God suddenly, completely, and truly died a short period of time before your arrival. This also destroys their personal realm, along with the vast majority of their daemons and influence amongst mortals.

The realms of Chaos are temporarily in turmoil as the balance of power within suddenly and violently shifts. This will also weaken the presence of Chaos amongst mortals in general. 

So long as it doesn’t involve any other massive changes to the setting you may choose how the Chaos God died.

You may choose which Chaos God died, each additional purchase allows you to choose an additional Chaos God to die.

You can be sure any enemies of Chaos will take advantage of the situation. For example in 40k the situation might just be advantageous enough for multiple loyalist Primarchs to return and for the Emperor of Mankind to start restoring himself, especially if multiple Chaos Gods die.
objects.title: Death of Chaos (Warhammer)

objects.text:
The Gods of Chaos are formed and sustained by the emotions of mortals, especially those aligned with their domains. Yet emotions are not singular things—they possess both light and shadow, capable of being both positive or negative. More than that though, just as they draw power from the emotions of mortals, so too are they influenced by them.

Thus a hypothetical arises. If the Ruinous Powers draw their existence from emotion, both good and bad, then it follows that their existence must also be some combination of good and bad, that their existence must also possess two expressions.

With this modifier, that possibility becomes truth—one the Chaos Gods have long concealed. 

The four great powers of Chaos now possess an alternative aspect, two halves of the same divine existence. One is as they were previously, embodying the negative and destructive extremes seen throughout the galaxy, while the other reflects the constructive or virtuous forms of emotion, a positive mirror to the already existing negative.

Despite the existence of positive aspects, the negative aspects remain dominant. Millennia of endless war, despair, and cruelty have swollen them into the monstrous beings they are known as now. Their counterparts, however, exist as weakened reflections—suppressed, starved of worship, and often deliberately obscured by their darker halves, yet intrinsically linked, unable to truly destroy one another as they are but two sides of the same coin.

The domains of the positive aspects mirror the traditional Ruinous Powers, but focus on more noble expressions: Khorne embodies strength, honor, martial skill, and righteous battle. Tzeentch is wisdom, magic, discovery, and the pursuit of knowledge. Slaanesh supports love, passion, artistry, and the joy of creation. And Nurgle brings life, endurance, healing, and the acceptance that allows beings to persevere through suffering.

Of course, these positive aspects still aren’t benevolent gods in the traditional sense. They are still entities of the Warp after all, shaped by belief and emotion, but they embody the constructive side of the same primal forces that birthed the Ruinous Powers.

In a galaxy defined by misery, they remain faint lights within the Warp—forgotten possibilities of what Chaos might have been, and perhaps could still become.
objects.title: Not-So-Ruinous Powers (Warhammer)

objects.text: Now with 80% less daemonic corruption!* Whatever world you are heading to now has a psychic layer to it, acting as an interwoven dimension of subconscious thoughts, ideas, emotions, and more. Thankfully for you, this isn't necessarily the Warp from Warhammer, instead taking on attributes of whatever setting you are heading to and affected by your other modifiers. If your setting is rather grim, don't expect the manifested Warp, or the beings born inside it, to be a beneficial addition. You can nudge how this manifests in the world, but at minimum it will have a measure of chaos to it. It will also allow some people and beings to tap into psychic-magic, and cause untold effects on any environment where the boundary between the Warp and Real thins. Eldritch daemon gods not included.
objects.title: The Warp (Warhammer)

objects.text:
It would seem that Earth, and humanity as a whole, has gained both its greatest protector and its most devoted champion in the being known as the Emperor of Man—though that is not the name by which he is currently known. In this age, he bears the name Neoth.

Neoth is a Perpetual, a being whose existence transcends the normal limits of life and death. More than that, he is the most powerful Psyker in human history, and one of the most powerful ever to exist across the vast span of humanity's future. His mind and soul possess immense psychic might, placing him beyond comparison with any of his contemporaries.

Above all else, Neoth is driven by a singular dream: the ascension of humanity. He desires to see mankind rise beyond every limitation, reaching the utmost boundaries of both Reality and Unreality. Every action he takes, every sacrifice he makes, and every burden he endures is in service to that ultimate goal. His devotion is not directed toward any single nation, culture, or individual, but toward humanity as a whole.

The depth of this commitment is difficult to comprehend. Neoth's love for mankind is so absolute that he would willingly endure agony on a spiritual and existential level for more than ten millennia if doing so would secure humanity's future. No suffering, no hardship, and no sacrifice is too great a price in pursuit of mankind's continued survival and eventual transcendence.

At the same time, Neoth stands as anathema to all that is unreal, immaterial, or demonic in nature. His very existence is hostile to such forces. Creatures of the unreal, entities born from spiritual corruption, and beings that exist outside the laws of physical reality find themselves opposed by him on a fundamental level. His presence is a bane to them, and his power serves as a natural counter to their influence, weakening and repelling them simply by virtue of what he is.
objects.title: The Revelation (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Somehow, a full Imperial Battlefleet has been sent to claim your world. Consisting of between 50 and 75 voidships of varying size, the Battlefleet is made up of destroyers, frigates, cruisers, and battleships, as well as countless small vessels such as transports, shuttles, messenger craft and long-range patrol craft. In addition, there will also be numerous non-warp travel ships such as system patrol ships and defence monitors.

The armed forces of this Battlefleet include millions of Imperial Guard, supporting regiments of armoured forces and artillery, a Lesser Order Militant of the Adepta Sororitas, and the forces of the Adeptus Mechanicus. Finally, the Battlefleet is supported by a chapter of Space Marines and their Battle Barge.

Led by a particularly dogmatic Lord Admiral, heading them off diplomatically will be extremely difficult, a problem made exponentially worse if the planet you reside on is in any way non-compliant with the Imperial Creed. Your world now has to contend with orbital bombardment, kilometre-long voidcraft and a force that will willingly throw away lives for the chance of victory.
objects.title: Imperial Battlefleet (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
A single massive Space Hulk from the Warhammer 40,000 universe has appeared in your starting setting. A Space Hulk is the term used by the Imperium of Man to describe the wreckage of starships, space stations, and mangled conglomerations of various voidships and artificial debris found drifting through the vacuum of space without any apparent direction. They can be so enormous that they possess their own atmosphere and gravity. Space Hulks frequently enter and exit the Warp seemingly at random, making searching or travelling within them extremely dangerous.

While a Space Hulk can contain countless treasures, including lost technology and even an STC device, it is also filled with numerous dangers and enemies, such as Orks, Genestealers, and even Heretic Astartes. Space Hulks also emerge from the Warp in seemingly random directions and at unpredictable times, making it even more difficult to locate and explore.

The appearance of the Space Hulk will not bring any Chaos Gods or any other force into your universe.
objects.title: Wreckage (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
A Votann Prospect Fleet has marked your world for harvest, whether you like it or not. As an industrialist and mercantile race with STC-derived technology, the Squats, as they are often pejoratively called, care little for the native inhabitants of their extraction sites. They have harvested worlds to the core while paying no heed to the indigenous populations on their surfaces, or stripped their atmospheres of rare particles to doom the biospheres below. Such is the indifferent cruelty you will have to contend with if you wish to contest their claim to your world's resources.

If challenged, the Kinhosts of their fleets will descend to wreak bloody vengeance, alongside robotic Ironkin and psychic Grimnyr. Each of these warriors possesses superhuman hardiness and strength, and their cloneskins grant them a range of unique biological advantages. They will be further fortified by other Kin organizations such as the Cthonian Mining Guilds, who provide vehicular and armoured support. The fleet itself is more than capable of supporting a planetary assault: the voidships of the Leagues of Votann Fleets tend toward enormous size and redoubtable build, with even smaller vessels used for mining and other mercantile activities at least matching Imperium cruisers for armoured bulk, shielding and sheer firepower.

However, they are not mindless conquerors; this is not an invasion fleet per se. The Votann are above all practical, and profit is of utmost importance to the fleet. If the resistance proves fierce enough, their brutal calculus of war may favour retreat.
objects.title: Leagues Of Votann (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
It appears your world is facing a severe Genestealer infestation. A Patriarch has already established itself and spread its corruption across several generations. The cult it has spawned now numbers between one and two million members, organized into numerous cells across the planet, and possesses significant financial and military resources.

If left unchecked, the cult will continue its usual methods—infecting and indoctrinating more victims, expanding its ranks, and breeding additional Genestealers. Once it reaches what it deems critical mass, it will attempt a violent planetary uprising, seizing control of the entire world.

Those afflicted by the Genestealer’s kiss share a psychic link not only with the Patriarch but also with one another through the broodmind. This bond instills absolute loyalty and devotion to the cult. Without advanced medical or biotechnological intervention, curing them is nearly impossible. In the absence of such means—or another way to purge the genetic corruption—the infected must often be euthanized.

Fortunately, no Tyranid presence has been detected in the vicinity of your world. For now, you may take some comfort in knowing the cult cannot summon the Great Devourer to descend and strip your planet down to its bedrock.
objects.title: Genestealer Infestation (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Drawn by the psychic beacon of the broodmind, a Tyranid hive fleet is now on course for your world, intent on consuming every scrap of biomass upon the planet.

Sensing the approach of the hive fleet, the Genestealer cult has erupted into open rebellion, spreading unrest across the globe. Their numbers now stand in the tens of millions—perhaps even hundreds of millions.

You have roughly ten years to both crush the Genestealer uprising and prepare for the coming war of survival, when the hive fleet arrives with its endless swarm of hyper-adaptive Tyranid organisms, numbering in the trillions, to descend upon your world.
objects.title: The Great Devourer Cometh (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Bad news: the world you've gone to is in fact a 65-million-year-old Tomb World of a minor Necron Dynasty. Worse, its automated protocols have been activated, and there's no stopping them now. Legions of soulless Necron warriors sleep below, with even these base servitors armed with Gauss Weaponry that rip apart foes at the molecular level. All are immortal undead, able to revive via Reanimation Protocols that let them re-enter the battlefield after death, so long as they have a connection to the Tomb World. Additionally, Canoptek Constructs swarm in the billions, and Blackstone structures let them suppress the Warp and similar dimensions or powers. Most worringly, this particular Dynasty's Phaeron has access to C'tan shards of awesome power, though they will unleash it with due caution.

Thankfully, you still have decades before it becomes fully awakened, as its ancient systems and decrepit masters will take time to brush off the dust of ages, with its most powerful weapons coming online last. They will be at their most vulnerable during this time period, but once operating at full output, there's little that can stand in their way.
objects.title: Tomb World (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
The world you're on has a large, hidden Webway gate that make it an easily accessible raiding spot for the feared Drukhari. These Commorrites will kill, loot & enslave the local populace in swift and brutal raids, becoming an ever-present and constant threat. Worse still are the fates that await those who are captured, never to be seen again once they are dragged screaming into the depths of the Webway.

All sub-factions of the Drukhari will be involved in these raids, from skilled Kabalites and Wych Cults to Haemonculi and their depraved creations. Gangs of Scourges, Hellions, Mandrake, and Reaver Jetbikers only add to the horrific displays of violence. The only silver lining is that these raids tend to be small in size, as the gateway restricts larger forces. If this gateway is found and destroyed, or otherwise blocked from use by the Drukhari, the threat will be stopped.
objects.title: Drukhari Raiders (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text: Call them what you will — Krell, Psyrens or Enslavers. Just one witch, unsanctioned, caused the destruction of Hive Skorpios when one of those things used her brain as a gateway to this world. Within three days the entire hive’s population was reduced to drooling mindslaves. Within three weeks an entire continent was at war. And all because the governor thought his family should be exempt from the psyker cull and refused to give his daughter to the Black Ships. — Inquisitor Mallen, Ordo Xenos The Enslavers are a betentacled, spheroid xenos species hailing from outside the bounds of material reality, and are a greatly feared and insidious threat to all sapient life. Somehow, they've now arrived on your planet. These strange aliens do exactly what their names suggest, dominating the wills of all they encounter through mental control. A single Enslaver is able to dominate the minds of up to at least 10 creatures, with the victims of this mental control retaining all their abilities, knowledge and physical attributes, albeit under the command of the Enslaver. As they consume minds, they grow even more powerful; one of extraordinary power may be able to control an entire Hive of humans on its own. Thankfully, they've yet to actually arrive in person. They first require the possession of a psyker or similar being within the Materium, similar to Daemons. Over the course of a few days, this unfortunate soul will reform into a living gate into reality, allowing entry. Once on the other side, they will begin enslaving others to their will and bringing more of their kind into Realspace. On the bright side, Enslavers cannot easily possess beings trained to resist possession, including any sanctioned psykers, and can be overwhelmed if enough minds are present, as it will have too many minds to try and assimilate at once.
objects.title: Enslaver Plague (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
The world you reside on is in fact an ancient Maiden World, a planet slowly terraformed over the course of millennia by automated processes after being seeded with life thousands of years ago. While the planet itself is safe, you've attracted the attention of a minor Aeldari Craftworld, who are hellbent on removing any species that is not their own from what they consider Eldar birthright. Despite its smaller size, it still contains a force capable of bringing worlds to their knees. Depending on the Craftworld, the dominant sapient species may be given an ultimatum to leave, but if ignored, then the planet will be attacked in full force.

While they will not use bombardment that would damage the planet itself, their Aspect Warriors and Exarchs will be sent to wipe the planet clean of interlopers. The invaders will only be dissuaded if the cost of Eldar life proves to become too high, or if the Craftworld itself becomes threatened.
objects.title: Maiden World (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Somehow, somewhere in the galaxy, a large T’au fleet has mysteriously appeared. This is a full colonial armada made up of one hundred ships, thirty of which are warships, while the others include colony ships, orbital construction platforms, and support vessels carrying thousands of T’au settlers, soldiers, engineers, and diplomats. Their mission is to locate habitable worlds, establish fortified colonies, and expand their civilization in accordance with the philosophy of the Greater Good.

These fleets are not composed of the T’au alone, though. Kroot kindreds travel with them as scouts, hunters, and adaptable ground fighters, while Vespid stingwings serve as swift aerial troops and rapid assault units. Together, these allied species create a flexible military force capable of thriving on dangerous worlds.

When a suitable planet is discovered, the fleet begins rapid colonization. Orbital stations, planetary settlements, and defensive structures are constructed using advanced technology such as drones, battlesuits, and gravitic vehicles. Within a relatively short time, an undeveloped world can become a fortified colony capable of supporting both civilian populations and military forces.

If these fleets encounter humanity, however, their response will be far more aggressive than usual due to their past encounters with the Imperium of Man. thus Human civilizations know are often viewed as major threats, and if Earth or any major human powers are discovered, the fleets will likely treat them as a major threat and respond with military action rather than diplomacy.

Each fleet is typically led by its own council of Ethereals, meaning that different expansion fleets may not always cooperate with one another. Conflicting interpretations of the Greater Good, distance, and political rivalry can cause fleets to operate independently or even compete for territory and influence.

Each additional purchase of this modifier causes another T’au expansion fleet to appear somewhere else in the galaxy, slowly spreading their colonies and influence across the stars.
objects.title: Tau Expansion Fleet (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
It seems that the Greentide and its gods, Gork and Mork, have managed to find their way into your world, they have gained a foothold and are here to stay. The Orks are a violent, green-skinned menace that live only for war and will search for a fight wherever they might go. The Greenskins will inevitably become a threat to any civilization they confront as they gain strength from conflict. Orks can reproduce by releasing spores into their environment, which can develop into various types of Orkish creatures, such as grots, which are toddler-sized orks with a sadistic and cowardly personality, and squigs, which are kept as pets and emergency food rations.

As the population of Greenskins increases, mutant versions will begin to emerge, each possessing unique abilities that set them apart from the others. For example, there are the Weirdboyz, who have the ability to belch green fire, and the Painboyz, who can stitch wounds without any difficulty. These mutant versions arise from an energy field that permeates all of Greenskin kind, adapting as it recognizes when a WAAAAAAGGGHHH should diversify.

When a Greentide reaches critical mass, a WAAAAAAGGGHH will erupt, during which the largest and strongest Ork will be crowned Warboss. If that Warboss is killed, the remaining Orks will fight amongst themselves to choose a new leader. A WAAAAAAGGGHH will send the Horde into a frenzy, driving them to seek combat with even greater intensity than usual. The heightened activity of the energy field will result in more Orks appearing and converging towards the WAAAAAAGGGHHH, further increasing their numbers.
objects.title: Greentide (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
How unfortunate it is that the dark gods of Chaos have turned their gaze upon your universe as the next stage in their eternal great game.

Their objective remains unchanged: to corrupt and consume the emotions and souls of the living while breaking down the barrier between realspace and the Warp. Their ultimate goal is to drag all of reality into the Immaterium and make it part of their own twisted domain.

The Warp now overlays your universe as a parallel dimension, coexisting with whatever reality you inhabit. As a result, any soul or emotional energy not claimed by a local deity, afterlife, or similar metaphysical structure is now drawn into the Warp. Consequently, certain individuals may begin to develop nascent psychic abilities, becoming psykers. These unfortunate souls are at great risk, as their minds serve as conduits to the Warp, leaving them vulnerable to daemonic influence, madness, or worse if they lack the will or discipline to resist.

Native users of psychic abilities or magic can still wield their powers independently of the Warp, as they always have. However, they now have the option to tap into its energies to enhance their abilities, though doing so comes with the perilous risk of exposure to the Warp's corrupting influence.

Fortunately, the Chaos Gods Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Slaanesh and their most powerful lieutenants, such as Greater Daemons and Daemon Princes, cannot manifest freely in realspace. Their entry requires specific conditions: regions steeped in corruption and ritual, warp breaches, or summoning rites performed by devoted cultists. Without such circumstances, their influence is limited to dreams, whispers, mutations, and the corruption of mortals to serve their will.

Make no mistake, though: even their indirect presence is a growing infection. Where twisted belief, dark emotion, and suffering converge, the Dark Gods take root. And once established, their taint spreads like a cancer, difficult, if not impossible, to extinguish completely.
objects.title: The Ruinous Power (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Somehow, the world you head to is now the victim of a Chaos incursion. For whatever reason, the Chaos Lord of a sizable warband of Chaos Space Marines has decided on the invasion of your world. These Astartes are all nominally millennia old, with the combat experience to match, though this is complicated by fresh recruitment and how the Warp has affected their sense of the progression of time. Alongside them is a host of fanatical slaves, mutants, ancient war machines, Dreadnoughts and Terminator squads, as well as whatever voidships they've managed to acquire. Moreover, they will have the support of the Daemonic Legions and will utilize Daemon Engines of awesome power.

While often wielding outdated equipment, less supplied, less organized and more prone to infighting than their Imperial counterparts, these damned souls also have the favour of the Gods themselves. Corruption affects man and machine alike, twisting flesh and metal in ways unnatural to mortal sensibilities, and it often bestows power in exchange for the price it exacts. Powerful mutations, blessings and gifts are common among these veterans of the Long War, whether that be transhuman physiques further enhanced by the protean caress of the Warp, or a screaming Daemon Weapon that can slice apart tanks with fell ease.

Furthermore, they'll be able to access the full potential of the powers of the Warp for psychic abilities, sorcerous rituals or daemon summoning. Such usage can and will taint the area around it, spreading the corruption of Chaos far and wide. You may freely choose the makeup of the warband, that being what Chaos God(s) they worship and their Legion or Chapter of origin, which will influence its goals; they may seek to conquer and add the world to their holdings, strip it of resources and leave, or perhaps even seek to transform it into a Daemon World through planetary-scale rituals and the sacrifice of billions.
objects.title: Warband (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
Now, the Chaos Gods and the Warp entering your universe are not the 40K incarnations, but their counterparts from Warhammer Fantasy. Their purpose remains unchanged — to corrupt, consume, and ultimately dominate. Any soul or emotional energy not claimed by a local deity, afterlife, or similar metaphysical structure is now drawn into the Warp.

The Winds of Magic now permeate your starting world. These winds are raw, unfiltered currents of metaphysical Chaos, and their influence on the mortal realm is often strange, unpredictable, and dangerous. Certain individuals may awaken as wizards or sorcerers, learning to manipulate and reshape the very fabric of reality itself.

A new material called Warpstone will also start to appear in your world. The Warpstone is the ultimate physical manifestation of pure magic. Contact with the Warpstone may cause mutating influence on a person so handle it with great care.

Chaos energies bring both physical mutation and spiritual corruption to sentient beings. Mutation is the process by which a mundane creature undergoes unnatural transformation physical, mental or spiritual often caused by exposure to the raw essence of Chaos or the deliberate touch of the Dark Gods.

The Chaos Gods Khorne, Tzeentch, Nurgle, and Slaanesh along with their mightiest servants, such as Greater Daemons and Daemon Princes, cannot manifest freely in realspace. Their entry demands specific conditions: lands steeped in corruption, breaches in reality, or summoning rituals performed by devoted cults. Absent these, their presence is limited to dreams, whispers, mutations, and the subtle corruption of mortal hearts.
objects.title: The Ruinous Power (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
Now the Warpmoon, known as Morrslieb, will appear in your world. This phenomenon follows an erratic cycle, unpredictably appearing larger or smaller in the sky. In times of disaster, some claim to see a mocking, grinning, twisted face upon its surface.

Morrslieb itself is an enormous chunk of warpstone that continues to circle the world as a second moon, spreading Chaos across the lands over which it passes. Because of this, you will see an increase in warpstone meteorites falling upon your world.

On these ill-omened nights, Morrslieb’s sickly green light bathes the land and dark magic gathers in invisible pools of stagnant evil. Its influence can corrupt flesh, mutate the unborn and inspire madness and murder. The veil between this world and the next is thin at these times and many people may experience strange and prophetic dreams.
objects.title: Morrslieb (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
Now, the Greentide that appears in your starting world aren’t the Orks of 40k, but rather the Orcs of Warhammer Fantasy. While Fantasy Greenskins are similar in appearance and behavior — and retain their fungus-based biology — there are some key differences:

First, they have no access to advanced technology, or indeed the fine motor control required to craft any. Instead, they rely on crude and primitive weapons typically crafted for them by Goblins.

Second, instead of psychic powers the Greenskins of Warhammer Fantasy use a magic unique to them known as Waaagh! Magic, the arcane practice and tradition utilised by the shamans of the Orcs through the Lore of the Big Waagh! and Goblins through the Lore of the Little Waagh! through the use of the magical Waaagh!-energy generated by all Greenskins. This forms the gestalt, mental spirit-realm called the "Great Green" that all Orcs and Goblins share with each other and Gork and Mork.

Third, they don’t grow as large as their 40k-counterparts. In exchange however the Goblins are far more cunning and dangerous than the 40k-Gretchin.

The Orcs can be roughly divided into three categories: regular Orcs, Savage Orcs who eschew the use of metal in favor of implements of bone and flint, as well as Black Orcs, who are more intelligent and disciplined than their kinsfolk, their skins being a darker shade of green.

Goblins are smaller and weaker than Orcs, typically individually smaller and weaker than a human, but far crueler and more cunning, fond of poisons, traps, and ambushes. They can be found alongside Orcs as well as by themselves, often either riding wolves  or gathering in deep forests alongside gargantuan spiders.
Beneath the earth, Night Goblins dig ramshackle networks of tunnels and breed countless varieties of squigs, including beasts larger than elephants. Most at home in the mountains, they are a constant threat to any who attempt to mine for resources.

Finally, there are the Hobgoblins, the largest and strongest of the Goblin-breeds. Shunned by the other greenskins for their excessive treachery, Hobgoblins gather in hordes and scour large plains on their specially bred giant wolf mounts, forming roaming Khanates that threaten all unfortunate enough to cross their path.
objects.title: Greentide (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
It seems that the Vermintide and their deity, the Great Horned Rat, have burrowed their way into your world and established a strong presence. The Skaven are a race of intelligent and cunning ratmen who possess their own society, complete with a caste system, language, and unique technology. They are an extremely prolific race, capable of rapidly reproducing from a few hundred to tens of thousands in just a few weeks.

The Skaven are organized into clans, each with its own specialties. For example, Clan Skryre is known for its Warlock Engineers; Clan Pestilens is famous for its fanatical Plague Monks; Clan Eshin specializes in Assassin Adepts; and Clan Moulder is recognized for its mutated war beasts. These four clans form the core of the Skaven Under-Empire.

Although their presence remains largely unknown, it can certainly be felt. Signs include mysterious disappearances, bells ringing 13 times, an increase in rats and other pests, and the moon exhibiting a strange green glow. The Vermintide is here, so be prepared.

Additionally, a peculiar green-glowing mineral has begun to appear in the world, vanishing just as mysteriously as it emerged.
objects.title: Vermintide (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
Something stirs in the depths of the forests. Animals grow and mutate into monstrous forms. People traversing the wilderness go missing. Hateful eyes stare from the forests towards the towns and cities. The wild hordes of the Beastmen have arrived.

Visually hybrids between muscular humans and animals and having little social structure beyond Might makes Right, the dominant breeds of Beastmen are the Gors and Minotaurs, humanoids with the heads of goats and bulls and cloven legs. The only thing truly uniting the Beastmen is their shared hatred of civilization in all its forms, and their burning desire to bring it to ruin. Prone to attacking any human they find in the wilderness or encroaching upon their domain, logging operations will be frequent targets. Though normally found in small herds due to the limitations of how big a group hunting and foraging alone can sustain, powerful leaders known as Beastlords will with startling regularity gather huge warherds around themselves to wage war against towns and cities.

These armies are supported by a menagerie of monstrous beasts that the Cloven Ones herd to war with them out of the forests' depths, ranging from boars the size of draft-horses to abominations like the Jabberslythe whose appearance alone can horrify lesser minds into madness. Bray-Shamans wield fell magics both offensively as well as to protect the Beastmen from the works of man, rendering weapons less effective the more advanced they are. Among the largest warherds one can occasionally spot colossal Beastmen-mutations like the Cygors and Ghorgons, towering tall as trees and easily able to smash walls and buildings as well as flip vehicles.

The mutating effects are not limited to animals alone, as couples living on the edges or even surrounded by forests will occasionally give birth to a Beastman instead of a human. Driven by an instinctive deep sense of shame these parents will typically head deep into the forest and abandon their child there. And though miraculously the parents almost always make the journey into and out of the woods unmolested, equally miraculously the child is almost always found by the Beastmen within hours, the new Gave taken and raised as another warrior braying to bring down the world of man.
objects.title: Warherds (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
An ancient burial pyramid has emerged somewhere in your starting world. This monumental structure is inhabited by one of the Tomb Kings and their long-dead legions, who have lain dormant within their crypts for thousands of years. For each selection a single Tomb appears in your starting world containing at least five to ten thousand soldiers. You may decide which dynasties the Tomb Kings belong to but if you take all ten one of them will be ruled by Settra the Imperishable. Luckily for you Nagash wont be one of these Kings, unless you decide otherwise.

The armies of the Tomb Kings are vast and unrelenting. Once mortal men, they now march as legions of skeletal warriors, striding to war at the command of their mummified rulers. Among their ranks ride undead horsemen and charioteers, their gilded war machines and constructs thundering across the sands.

Supporting these legions are the Liche Priests of Nehekhara, sorcerers who wield the necromantic secrets of eternal unlife. They perform ancient rituals to draw mortal souls from the Realm of Souls, binding them once more into corporeal forms or mighty constructs shaped in the likeness of monsters and the ancient gods of Nehekhara.
objects.title: Tomb Kings (Warhammer: Fantasy)

objects.text:
Woe is you, for the Dark Gods' attention has been drawn to your world. An extensive and extremely competent group of cultists has formed within the cracks of society, and they are determined to summon their dread masters into realspace. By creating weakness in the barrier between realities, they plan to start summoning fell creatures of the Warp into realspace. If not stopped, they will eventually create a stable Warp Rift via a continuous and grand sorcerous ritual. This will entail the Warp itself spilling into reality, letting them bring through even Greater Daemons by breaching the veil altogether. After some point, however, it will not even require this ritual to remain open, becoming self-sustaining and requiring additional effort to close.

This will immediately corrupt the world, as daemons will begin pouring through the crack in reality, able to be summoned much more easily through the confluence between dimensions. It will also bend the laws of the Materium, spawning strange psychic phenomena and anomalies, or assault the minds of mortals with maddening visions. Any mortal forces will have to deal with an onslaught of daemonic legions, and the confusing mess that is the Warp. This will only worsen with time, as the Warp Rift will grow to encompass the entire planet. Eventually, as it becomes saturated with Warp energies and populated by daemons, it will be transformed into a hellish Daemon World.

After this point, there will essentially be no salvation, as the planet will be drawn partially into the Warp and forever be lost, now a playground for the servants of the Dark Gods. Due to their nature, these worlds are nearly impossible to cleanse or destroy, as they operate on a completely different set of metaphysical laws.
objects.title: Warp Rift (Warhammer: 40k)

objects.text:
The world is no longer limited to a single realm. Instead, your realm is one of countless mortal realms within the Myriad Worlds, above which lie higher realms inhabited by increasingly powerful cultivators, immortals, races, sects, empires, and civilizations. Every realm possesses its own laws, treasures, opportunities, and dangers, with the cycle of cultivation repeating itself on an ever greater scale.

Ascending to a higher realm does not bring peace or safety, only stronger enemies and greater challenges. Heavenly Tribulations become increasingly more dangerous, with higher realms presenting great dangers and opportunities. The higher you ascend, the greater the disparity in power becomes. Entire lower worlds may be reduced to collateral damage by conflicts between higher realm cultivators. Simply being born in the wrong realm or world may see you wiped out alongside it by the misstep of one.

In place of a generic setting, you may instead choose a specific Xianxia setting featuring higher realms. By default, you begin in one of the mortal realms, which will generally remain safe from the higher realms for at least a period of time unless something occurs to attract the attention of those above.
objects.title: Myriad Worlds (Xianxia)

objects.text: Long ago in Ancient Egypt, people dueled each other not with sword or bow, but with their Ka, spiritual beings from a parallel dimension summoned through the use of their Ba, spiritual energy, to fuel their existence. These spirits ranged from minor spirits weaker than a human child to literal gods capable of sundering nations, and they served their summoners loyally until the secrets of their existence were lost to time and tragedy. Throughout history, small groups and individuals rediscovered this method and used it for various purposes until the modern day, when someone found an alternative method to summon them: Children's Card Games! ...Yes, really. Through studying ruins in Egypt (or in lost Atlantis, or near the Nazca Lines in Peru, turns out a lot of ancient civilizations have similar secrets), they figured out how to bind Monster Spirits to alternative mediums for people to summon, and realized that playing cards was the perfect such medium. Less than two decades later, Duel Monsters became an international sensation, with tournaments fought between both casual and professional duelists happening everywhere, and even schools made just to teach the game, possibly encouraged by the spirits and magic of the cards themselves, and definitely encouraged by eccentric billionaires who somehow make mass producible portable hologram tech and decide to use it to spice up said card game. Though a fun game to play, especially as the magic of the cards and the foresight of the company or companies behind Duel Monsters specifically prevent things like First Turn Kill or other unfun meta strategies from being easily achieved by literally everybody, there are downsides to this art being revived. Duel Monsters themselves are sapient beings, and some are not remotely benevolent and will have goals they wish to pursue that threaten the world. In addition, various artifacts and sealed beings may be released in response to or by taking advantage of the growing presence of the game. The Millenium Items, seven powerful Egyptian Artifacts have been scattered, the one behind the fall of Atlantis is reawakening, groups like the Shadow Riders and Dark Signers seek to reawaken ancient evils, others seek to control the world through things like the Light of Destruction or other means, and others still are coming out of the woodwork. However, where evil rises, so does good. Somewhere, someone awakens an ancient Pharaoh sealed in the Millenium Puzzle and begins to teach them kindness. Elsewhere, the Crimson Dragon, one of the strongest Gods among Monster Spirits, marks six Crimson Signers to fight their Dark counterparts. One Duelist begins to tap into the Gentle Darkness to fight the Light of Destruction. More and more, good begins to fight back against evil, but even so, it is not guaranteed to win. However, by believing in the Heart of the Cards, anything is possible. Good luck.
objects.title: Get Your Game On (Yu-Gi-Oh!)

objects.text:
Rather than Duel Spirits being mythically bound to a Children's Card Game that limited their power, the knowledge of summoning them in the ancient ways was instead spread around the globe. Within a handful of years, someone figured out a method by which literally anyone could summon their Ka and even those of others too, and thus everyone, even children, now has the power of Duel Spirits on their side. In addition, knowledge on how to use the Ba, aka a person's spiritual energy or lifeforce, to fuel Spells or lay mystical Traps was discovered not long after and spread, adding more tools to their repertoire.

This world is much more dangerous, as now fights frequently have a real risk of death, and people overall are hardened in response. For example, in Canon Yu-Gi-Oh this could mean that Yugi has had to kill more than one of his opponents, and his rivalry with Kaiba was even more violent before they somehow stumbled their way into a pseudo-friendship, with Duelist Kingdom being more akin to a death game. Meanwhile, in 5Ds, the battle between the Signers Crimson and Dark was far more devastating, with tens of thousands dying, entire districts leveled, and ending with Yusei burning Rex Goodwin to ashes with Stardust Dragon as an example of how bad things can get. Basically, think of this world as operating on Shonen Battle logic rather than game logic.

In addition, with spirits no longer bound to a card game and physically manifested, their sapience is now common knowledge, with many spirits being important members of various organizations or acting as heroes or villains, some even summoning themselves through various methods to act in the world. Some even form relationships with humans, spawning a number of hybrids, some of which may have abilities or appearances reminiscent of various mythological beings.

Overall, the world is much crazier and more dangerous compared to canon. Good luck.
objects.title: Duel Monsters Unleashed (Yu-Gi-Oh!)

addons.text: Robohopps is no longer alone in her advanced technology body, including a few upgrades to herself and a lot of the police force. As opposed to another corporation that took over police, ZPC now is just genuinely looking to make the city safer than ever. Before, Robohopps could hit with 9500 newtons of force and hit a personal top speed of 200 mph, along with tanking 50 pounds of dynamite. Now, she can hit with legitimately enough force to destroy whole smaller buildings with a run up and punch, hit the speed of sound and beyond and function as if she were walking, and tank about 3 kilotons of TNT blowing up at ground zero. Along with this, Robohopps has now been joined by 4 more animal units similarly converted, although more around Robohopps previous level of capability. Robohopps has also been granted unimpeded access to the ZPD databases, as well as given her own personal AI that can guide her, console her, AND just overall be a help for her. The Zoocycle has now become the Neocruiser, a modified Police car with no driver seat that allows Judy to more physically integrate with it. The Car is armed with high-velocity specially made Rubber bullets, taser rounds, and PLENTY of other technology. On a personal level, Judy now has a much more balanced mental state thanks to her AI. Thanks to her, Zootopia has also increased about 40% in size due to the low crime rate promoting growth in size.
addons.title: Zootopia Police Force Neo (Zootopia)

objects.text: Officer Judy Hopps has been in some kind of horrible accident: a car crash, a bomb accident, a fall... something has left her body in a barely functionable state. ZCP, or Zootopia Consumer Products, a company meant to function as a technology provider for all districts of the city, both civilian and police force, has had a surplus of money and slight controversy to go with it. They have decided to rebuild Judy Hopps with their state of the art technology, relabeling her publicly as Robohopp. Privately, Judy is a bit weary mentally. While she can remember her family and 273 siblings, she couldn't tell you a single one of their names despite having other memories. She remembers the generalization rather than specifics. In spite of that, she now has access to a criminal database that can be pulled up with a single thought, and cross referenced with other benefits with just a couple more thoughts. Besides this, she has a host of other benefits. Before, she had to use smarts to win against predator sized animals. Now, she can indeed brute force them with her mechanical components. She can run at 200 miles per hour, punch with a whopping 9500 newtons of force without holding back, and could have 50 pounds of dynamite go off in her face, and she could walk away with minimal damage. Her sensors are able to see in all spectrums of light, X-ray, and more. And finally, she is equipped with the "Zoocycle", a motorcycle that can go twice as fast as her with even better handling, AND only she can turn it on and off with her tail acting as the ignition. Still, despite all of this, Judy is more reserved. She spends less time with friends, and more time at the station due to her worry about how people who knew her views her. It's as if she's a new person, and will likely be very emotionally unstable.
objects.title: Robohopps (Zootopia)

rows.title: Alternate Earth Modifiers
rows.titleText: Modifiers that add elements of Alternate Earths to a setting, and/or change elements of an Alternate Earth Setting

objects.text: Powers in your world are gained through more stranger circumstances. Exposure to Gamma rays from an experimental bomb, falling into a vat of acid, having your intrinsic field removed and being torn to pieces and instantly vaporised, etc. This doesn’t change the source of the powers, simply adapting the trigger to fit. Powers are also slightly adjusted, if not in appearance then in mechanics, so as to thematically match their new trigger better.
objects.title: Comic Origin

objects.text: Every person on Earth Bet has their level of beauty increased noticeably, becoming close to comic book-levels of attractiveness. People that would normally be considered "ugly" now have average levels of appearance, average-looking people are now quite attractive, and so on.
objects.title: Comic Book Pretty

addons.text: Now not only are people and powers pretty, but everything is beautiful. From nature, to people to even the powers here, everything is gorgeous to look at. The entire world is taken to a new level of appeal, where even the steam from your morning cup of coffee can be a small work of art. It's as if everything is hand drawn to the highest standard.
addons.title: It's a Beautiful World We Have

objects.text:
All powers look absolutely stunning in use, captivating onlookers with their breathtaking visual effects. Conjured fireballs blaze with mesmerizing, intricate patterns of flame that dance and flicker like living entities, their colors shifting from deep crimson to brilliant gold. Tinkertech creations gleam with a sleek, futuristic design, illuminated by pulsating neon lights and shimmering surfaces that reflect the environment in dazzling ways. In combat, these visually stunning powers turn battles into awe-inspiring displays of artistry. Explosions burst forth in a symphony of colors, protective barriers shimmer like ethereal shields, and healing abilities manifest as cascades of golden light that envelop and rejuvenate. 

Powers specifically designed to look good are boosted to an entirely new level.
objects.title: VFX On

objects.text: Parahumans and powered individuals now have additional powers worth 10% of your total SP spent on powers per time chosen up to 50% (with each time chosen having a limit of 20 SP up to 100sp at 5 picks). These extra powers cannot be Keystone, Paragon or Ascension powers. The points this modifier gives do not count towards the % of your total. Be aware this will massively power creep your chosen setting and make it much more dangerous based on number of times chosen.
objects.title: Varied Parahumans

objects.text:
Choose any power you purchased that costs 5 SP or less and this will be a natural ability every human in this setting possesses. This can be used to grant additional upgrades/fusions to a power, up to the cap of SP each power can give. Powers that are a result of a fusion have their requirement's SP budget combined.

You can have this be a retroactive change with humanity having always had this ability, or they can suddenly develop it upon your arrival. You can choose whether humans throughout the entire local multiverse possess the ability, whether they are or become aware that you are the reason for their powers, whether if there is an explanation for the ability or not, and if there is a reason you can choose what it is or leave it up entirely to chance, 

You can choose for their versions to be weaker than your own, with certain weaknesses and/or restrictions, to come with stipulations and/or side effects, to manifest different expressions of a power, have each person develop differently from one another or all the same or some kind of mix of the previous options, or you can choose to leave it entirely up to chance, although you’ll never be unhappy about the result.
objects.title: Powered World

objects.text: Each purchase of this modifier lets you share 1 more innate ability with humanity. This can be used to grant additional upgrades/fusions to a power, up to the cap of SP each power can give. Powers that are a result of a fusion have their requirement's SP budget combined. You can choose to have the abilities you share with them mix in some manner, either working as a single power with multiple functions, have them be entirely separate powers, take pieces and parts of different powers to create a power, have each person mix them separately or the same or you can choose to leave it entirely up to chance, although you’ll never be unhappy about the result.
objects.title: Multi Powered World

objects.text: Each purchase of this modifier increases the SP cap of the powers you can grant humanity by 5 SP.
objects.title: World of Supers

objects.text: You can choose any requirements that people must meet for any powers you grant with them through the Powered World modifiers. If you grant more than one power, you can choose different powers to have different requirements, some to have no requirements while others do, or just blanket requirements for all powers, anything between the previous options, or some kind of mix. You can also leave it entirely up to chance, although you’ll never be unhappy about the result.
objects.title: Not All Men Are Equal

objects.text: One of your powers is now an ability that every single powered individual in the verse has and can develop. For example, if you chose a Brute power, every single powered individual would have a superhuman physique and could develop it further. You can choose if this starts at the same level as your ability or starts off weaker. With either option, powered individuals can train the ability and gradually increase its strength.
objects.title: Power Communism

objects.text:
Choose any number of Objects of Power you purchased that costs 5 SP or less. Those Objects of Power are now something anyone in this world can purchase if they know where to look and can afford it. These Objects of Power will be equivalent to a limited run series, meaning there’s only a handful of them worldwide with limited means of producing more. 

The versions of those Objects of Power available in this world may have variations in their design and capabilities so they aren’t exact copies of your version or each other, but they will generally still be as capable as your version. Besides that any number of the Objects of Power available in this world can have the same Power Tweaks and Arbitrary Restrictions you may have placed on your own version.

This modifier only makes Objects of Power available to the world, not any additional powers and abilities that might be included in an Object of Power’s description that aren’t innate to the item in question. Using Klironomia as an example while the various different models of Klironomia could be available in this world, they wouldn’t include a physiology upgrade equivalent to the Age of Gods requiring some other work around to make them safe for general use.
objects.title: Esoteric Shopping

objects.text: Each additional purchase of this modifier increases the SP cost of the Objects of Power that can be shared by 5 SP.
objects.title: Mail Order Excalibur

objects.text: Each purchase of this modifier makes your selected Objects of Power more common. At 10 purchases they’re something that can be found in basically any store for only a few dollars. You can choose for different Objects of Power to have different levels of availability.
objects.title: Mass Production Excalibur

objects.text:
Choose any number of Skills you have purchased that cost 5 CP or less. Now, every person in the setting possesses an innate talent in these Skills. This talent accelerates their learning, allowing them to reach the level of the most outstanding master in these disciplines who has ever existed in this world. After that, their progress will depend solely on their own natural talent and effort.

Alternatively, you can make it so that every person is born with knowledge of the chosen Skills at the level of higher education or suddenly acquires this knowledge upon your arrival in the world.

You can choose whether these Skills are individually fitted to each person’s own understanding or if they are simply dry knowledge that people may or may not comprehend.

You can also determine whether this change occurs as a natural phenomenon, a part of human evolution, or the result of an unknown force. Additionally, you can decide whether people are aware of the source of their talent or simply take it for granted.
objects.title: Skilled World

objects.text: Each purchase of this modifier increases the number of Skills you can grant to humanity by 5 CP.
objects.title: Many-Skilled World

objects.text:
Each purchase of this modifier, in addition to the Skills you have granted, grants every person in setting a special accelerated learning talent equivalent to 5 CP.

This talent functions as a temporary pool that individuals unconsciously allocate to any skills, significantly enhancing their learning speed in those areas. As long as the total skill acquisition remains within the allocated CP, they will learn their chosen skills at an accelerated rate. However, once their accumulated skill and knowledge reach this CP limit, the talent fades, and further growth depends entirely on personal effort.

With this, people can rapidly master new skills and intuitively grasp complex science areas. However, each individual determines how to apply their learning and talent, meaning they may not always make the most efficient use of this resource.
objects.title: Polymathic World

objects.text: You can now choose Powers / OoPs / Skills that you haven't purchased in place of ones you did for the selected modifiers. So you can make everyone else a Kitsune with Powered World even if you aren't one, or make everyone talented at languages with Polyglot using Skilled World even if you purchased no Languages. This does not empower you in any way. You won't be one of the people who inexplicably has Magik or become talented at Parkour, and if you want Excalibur, Esoteric Shopping isn't going to give you one of the very few copies of it in the world.
objects.title: Unpurchased Empowerment
Simply Empowered
objects.text: Upon purchasing this modifier, 1/100000 people will gain between 1-5 random Tier 0 powers. People with more than the minimum number of powers are increasingly rarer, with those with 5 powers only being 1% of the empowered population. Each additional purchase increases the number of people empowered by a factor of ten, so the second purchase would empower 1/10000 people while the sixth would give everyone random Tier 0 powers. You will not be one of those empowered by this modifier no matter what. Note: You may choose if this happens upon insertion or if it's retroactive, and if the latter how long ago it happened. How these powers interact with preexisting power systems may vary.

objects.title: More Simple Powers
objects.text: Each purchase increases the number of powers the empowered can gain. The first purchase makes it 2-10, the second 3-15, and so on. At the maximum of nine purchases, they gain 10-50 Tier 0 powers. Those with a higher numbers of powers get progressively rarer, with the number of people with 50 powers being only 1/10000 of those empowered.

objects.title: Not So Simple Powers
objects.text: If someone has the requirements for it, they can gain a Tier 0 upgrade in place of a normal Tier 0 power, with no limit on how many they can potentially have in place of normal Tier 0's should they meet the requirements. For example, if you have 7 purchases of More Simple Powers, then someone might get Malachite Cells.

Choose one self-targeting Perk that costs 5 points or less, with Perks that cost both SP and CP using the combined total, so a Perk that costs 5 SP and 10 CP would count as 15 points. Everyone in this setting now has a copy of that Perk, with all that that entails. For every additional time you purchase this, you gain an additional 5 points to spend on Perks to give to everyone, and may choose any combination of Perks to grant so long as they add up to the total Points. Please note that this can rapidly get out of hand, and certain Perks (such as Blank) suddenly being thrust onto everyone may lead to certain forces acting out in response. Certain Perks being granted could result in certain powers (especially those granted by Shards) adjusting themselves to still be relevant. For example, if Trumped the Trump is chosen, power nullifiers might shift to become even more effective against external power supplies to try to 'drain' a power dry rather than nullify it directly. If you possess Power Tweak, Arbitrary Limitations, or both you may alter the Perks granted; maybe everyone starts with weaker versions of the Perks and need to 'train' them up, maybe everyone has variations of the base Perk so one person with Blank is immune to Precognition but weak to Sherlock Holmes style powers while another is immune to Sherlock Holmes style powers but Precogs see them just fine, or Perks are not absolute meaning a strong enough power could punch through Mental Barrier to Master someone anyway, or even Perk strength correlates directly with power strength such that the average civilian has limited power resistance with Manton Protected while someone on the level of an Entity would be nearly immune to almost all possible powers. You may freely decide if this is limited to just the base setting (Earth Bet for Worm, the Milky Way for Mass Effect, etc.), the entire setting (alternate Earths (+ Aleph, Gimel, Shin, etc.) for Worm, + the Andromeda Galaxy for Mass Effect, etc.) the entire universe, or even the entire Multiverse. You may also decide if people from outside this range also get a copy of the Perk the moment they enter it (alien visitors, sliders, jumpers, isekaiers, dimensional refugees, etc.). You may decide if these Perks suddenly showed up upon your insertion or if they retroactively appeared earlier. If so, you may decide when they first appeared, such as last week, or if they have been a thing for as long as intelligent life has been. Note that this will affect the culture and history of the world, though by default changes will tend to follow the path of least resistance so the world is still mostly recognizable, though you can override this to make more extensive historic changes if you want. You may also decide in an explanation for them is real, like a blessing by a god, the interference of sufficiently advanced alien space bats, the wishes/dreams of the populace warping reality, or something wierder like the local hacker accidentally activating cheat mode in the 11 dimensional supercomputer simulating the multiverse, a prank by the ROB who sent to this universe in the first place, or none at all leaving even omniscient observers confused as to where they come from. You may grant Perks that you haven't Purchased to everyone, but note that this modifier will not grant any such Perks to you no matter what, even if normally you would, as a reincarnated native or dimensional traveller, receive a copy, not even through intermediaries like someone with (Striker/Trump) Perk trying to share their Perk with you. If you want a Perk for yourself, go buy it in the Perks section. Note: By default this only affects people aka sophonts, not animals, plants, or robots lacking self awareness or complex thought. 'Intelligent' animals like Courage the Cowardly Dog or 'Warrior Cats' Cats and sapient AI / androids / robots like Dragon, 2B, or Claptrap count as people. Note: Perks granted by this modifier are treated as a completely separate phenomena from all powers, so even a Shardless Trump cannot directly affect them.
objects.title: Universal Perks

objects.text: Choose one self-targeting Drawback that grants 5 points or less, with Drawbacks that grant both SP and CP using the combined total, so a Drawback that grants 5 SP and 10 CP would count as 15 points. Everyone in this setting now has a copy of that Drawback, with all that that entails. For every additional time you purchase this, you gain an additional 5 points to spend on Drawbacks to give to everyone, and may choose any combination of Drawbacks to grant so long as they add up to the total Points. Please note that this can rapidly get out of hand, and certain Drawbacks (such as Human Killing Ghost or Kill Order) suddenly being thrust onto everyone may lead to the complete collapse of civilization. Certain Drawbacks being granted could result in certain powers (especially those granted by Shards) adjusting themselves to still be relevant. For example, if Major Disability (Blindness) is chosen, any powers that require eye contact or line of sight may adjust themselves to use other vectors to account for their wielder suddenly being blind. Any Drawbacks that are variable such as Major Disability or Conscious Geas may either have your specific variation chosen to apply universally (such as 'Blindness' or 'Don't eat meat') or be left to chance (so one person becomes blind while another loses an arm, and one person is forced to be vegan while another must try to kill some random person they never heard of).
