You may freely decide if this is limited to just the base setting (Earth Bet for Worm, Milky Way for Mass Effect, etc.), the entire setting (alternate Earths (+ Aleph, Gimel, Shin, etc.) for Worm, + the Andromeda Galaxy for Mass Effect, etc.), the entire universe, or even the entire Multiverse. You may also decide if people from outside this range also get a copy of the Perk the moment they enter it (alien visitors, sliders, jumpers, isekaiers, dimensional refugees, etc.). Note that if that’s the case your setting may become a very unpopular destination. You may decide if these Drawbacks suddenly showed up upon your insertion or if they retroactively appeared earlier. If so, you may decide when they first appeared, such as last week, or if they have been a thing for as long as intelligent life has been. Note that this will affect the culture and history of the world, though by default changes will tend to follow the path of least resistance so the world is still mostly recognizable, though you can override this to make more extensive historic changes if you want. You may also decide if an explanation for them is real, like a curse by a god, an experiment by sufficiently advanced alien space bats, the fears/nightmares of the populace warping reality, or something wierder like a virus affecting the 11 dimensional supercomputer simulating the multiverse, a cruel prank by the ROB who sent you to this universe in the first place, or none at all leaving even omniscient observers confused as to where they come from. You also may only grant Drawbacks you possess. No forcing the Conscious Geas (Obey me absolutely) onto everyone unless you also have that Geas. Note: By default this only affects people aka sophonts, not animals, plants, or robots lacking self awareness or complex thought. 'Intelligent' animals like Courage the Cowardly Dog or 'Warrior Cats' Cats and sapient AI / androids / robots like Dragon, 2B, or Claptrap count as people. Note: Drawbacks and powers are considered separate phenomena, so even Shardless Trumps can't affect them.
objects.title: Universal Drawbacks

objects.text: You can now set conditions for who can gain any Perk(s) or Drawback(s) you selected. This can be any arbitrary condition you can think of so long as at least one in a million people fit the criterion at insertion. If later on it becomes impossible for one in a million to meet it, such as only parahumans having a Perk but you successfully depowered everyone, some new condition for that Perk / Drawback will be created that a similar number of people meet, though it will tend to be related to the old one in some way, such as only people who could have had powers if they were still a thing or people who are superhuman cyborgs. Examples include but are not limited to: gender, age range, nationality, religion, only parahumans, only Shakers, must have died and been resuscitated 5 or more minutes later, must have killed someone or something stronger than them only using martial arts, must have suffered sufficient mental trauma, must have experienced a sufficiently strong feeling of achievement or enlightenment, be the seventh child of a seventh child, must be named [insert name here], only members of certain lineages, must have completed a certain ritual or trial, must be the leader of at least a thousand people, or it's completely random but with a [insert number here]% chance of anyone getting it. You can set up specific unique conditions for every single Perk / Drawback, even ones that are mutually exclusive with other Perks / Drawbacks like "any one person is only able to hold either this Perk or that Perk", have some be available for everyone while some aren't, or even have multiple unique conditions one must meet before receiving a specific Perk or Drawback, though again, at least one in a million individuals must be able to meet all of said conditions for any given Perk or Drawback.
objects.title: Not So Universal Afterall

objects.text:
Everyone with supernatural powers, no matter the origin, now possesses some kind of arbitrary weakness. What this weakness is can vary between individuals, but this weakness is strong enough and debilitating enough that exposure can effectively nullify whatever advantages their power grants them if exposed to enough of it. It can be anything, from exposure to bright lights, to certain frequencies of sound, exposure to certain chemicals, a debilitating phobia of some animal or imagery, to even certain types of powers like a Tinker or 'Science!' type cape who gets debilitating headaches in the presence of 'magic' type capes.

This weakness is generally at least mildly irritating or painful to the person in question when exposed and gets outright debilitating or crippling if exposed during active power use. Always on/passive powers that lack an off switch have weaknesses that are somewhere in between those two levels of severity, though more powerful abilities are paired with stronger (albeit not more common) weaknesses. Canon examples include Shadow Stalker's weakness to electrical currents in Worm, The Overseer's weakness to water in the Eastrail 177 series, Superman's weakness to Kryptonite in DC, Devil Fruit user's weakness to water and Seaprism Stone in One Piece, and Mad Pierrot's phobia of cats in Cowboy Bebop.

Non-unique powers that anyone can learn also possess weaknesses, but they are less debilitating and more just something that nullifies the power, and the weakness itself also wouldn't be unique. For example, in One Piece a Devil Fruit user would have an additional weakness appropriate to their power like a darkness Logia having a weakness to bright light, but all Haki users would have a weakness to some substance that just weakens their Haki's effects while leaving them physically fine, while in Fairy Tail mages would have some material that breaks their spells on contact.
objects.title: Everyone Hates Kryptonite

objects.text: Everyone with powers aka supernatural abilities now have some kind of disability to go with it. Generally, this disability can be anything, whether thematically appropriate to the power they possess or not is up to you, so long as the disability severly impacts everyday life while still leaving the power itself usable. This means that while someone with the power of enhanced eyesight could be deaf or paraplegic, they wouldn't be blind, though someone with clairvoyance could be blind since their power doesn't need functioning eyes. This disability can be physical (total blindness, missing limbs/organs, muscular atrophy, an alergy to sunlight, Atrial/Ventricular Septal Defects, etc.), mental/neuralogical (face blindness, low functioning autism, extreme OCD, a phobia of bugs to the point of panic attacks or fainting, Intermittent Explosive Disorder, severe memory retention issues, etc.), or even supernatural if the setting has it (fractured soul that leads to loss of emotions and lack of motiviation, lack of manton protections meaning telekinetics can mess with your organs by accident, broken mana core meaning you are in constant danger of either mana poisoning from absorbing too much or mana starvations from inability to hold magical energy, an inability to suppress your presense causing you to be vulnurable to spiritual predators, etc.). You can decide if these disabilities were caused by the powers themselves, or if only disabled people can have powers (this CYOA is not liable if this leads to people deliberately self harming in an attempt to gain powers). Either way, so long as they possess powers anyone with these disabilities will find them uncurable via natural or supernatural means. This does not mean they can't be treated to an extant, so someone who lacks arms can still get advanced prosthetics for example, but if someone with a hole in their heart got a heart transplant, their new heart would spontaneously develop an identical hole within the hour, and someone with memory loss would be immune to a memory refreshing spell.
objects.title: Super (Dis)Abilities

objects.text: Parahumans will only start appearing when you appear on Earth Bet.
objects.title: Modern

objects.text:
Things are a bit different than you remember them. Maybe the names are misspelled, or everyone's wearing the wrong costume or a bunch of other subtle but weird things. 
If you didn't exist things would play out about the same story-wise, but it'll probably throw you for a loop if you still remember how things were supposed to go.
objects.title: Off-Kilter

objects.text:
Things are definitely different from how you remember them. Maybe characters are dead where they should be alive, or a few key people got the wrong powers or some other changes of equal importance. 
If you remember canon, that knowledge is nearly useless now, but on the bright side if you didn't that doesn't matter as much.
objects.title: Off the Rails

addons.text: Unpowered Counterparts can now exist for characters whose appearance does not fully comply with human biology but are still visually human aside from unusual coloration.
addons.title: Colorful Crowd

addons.text: Unpowered Counterparts can now exist for characters with anthropomorphic features so long as they are still humanoid.
addons.title: Wild Encounters

addons.text: Any Counterparts that happen to undergo an Awakening will gain powers similar to those their Media Original hold, scaled down to the maximum given by Mass Awakening's chosen Tier.
addons.title: Shout-Out

addons.text: Any Counterparts that happen to undergo a Trigger will gain powers similar to those their Media Original hold, altered slightly to fit the rules of how shards work and scaled down to the maximum given by Second Wave Parahumans's chosen Tier.
addons.title: Shard Variant

addons.text: Any counterparts in this world may have powers similar to their original selves, but warped and altered to work through the native power systems of the world, and scaled down to the maximum given by Native Awakenings tier.
addons.title: Native Variant

objects.text:
Some of the normally faceless background-characters now seem oddly familiar. Turn on the TV and see star-reporter Lois Lane interviewing Colorado Senator Steven Armstrong. Officers Gibbs and DiNozzo are pulling over drivers for speeding. The most competent doctor working at Brockton General Hospital is a rather sarcastic man walking with a cane named Gregory House. Lou, owner of the nightclub Lux in the better part of town, looks just like Tom Ellis. In Brockton's Asian District one can find the Urahara Store and the Ichiraku Ramen Stand.

These are not dimensional refugees, simply regular non-powered people living their lives whose names, appearance, and, if one bothers to investigate it, parts of their backstory might feel familiar. Only characters whose appearance is fully human can have local counterparts.
objects.title: Huh, isn't that...

objects.text:
Now, on top of having some random familiar faces running around, you may have an entire cast of fully human characters included from a chosen setting. The selection of characters will be random, but the main cast will be included, and you may also name a few of them to make sure they are included. Just like in the perquisite of this modifier, the characters are mundane native versions heavily resembling their original counterparts.

The add-ons of “Huh, isn't that...” also apply here, which will allow for non-humans to be added, or to have an adjusted native variant of their original powers and such.

By selecting this modifier a second time, you may include a dozen settings and selecting a third time allows you to add as many as you want.
objects.title: Expy Galore

objects.text:
Choosing this option will make it so that any Setting Changes and Continuity Modifiers will be delayed until a future point in time within the setting that you choose to go to.

You can purchase this option up to three times; the first purchase will be 5 years, second purchase will be 10, and the final option for 20 years in total.

You can make preparations for  whatever hellscape you decided the world should suffer because you wanted some fun. 😀 

You can decide how the changes will be implemented near the end of the delay. Whether they occur one after the other or if by the last year they slowly start appearing making minor changes to the world, just go wild and enjoy your new prep time!
objects.title: Delayed Change

objects.text:
Hey pal, don't you just hate it when you see a neat location and think it'd be a nice place to stay for a bit but those superpowered Nazis got you down in the dumps and putting a damper on your vacation? 

Or maybe the heroes themselves aren't all that heroic and maybe should've never been granted those powers in the first place, well boy howdy do I have the option for you!

You are now one of the only superpowered being on the planet that you now reside on. If you picked an AU of Earth Bet you will go to a timeline where parahumans simply never came to light, because ol' Scion sat on a remote island the entire time. He sat there for decades without continuing the cycle, super sad that his GF crashed into a star and died; which also destroyed all her shards. 

Going to other settings will have their timelines accommodate, but that doesn't mean that you're all in the clear.

Sad Boy Scion is still going to cause Gold Morning once he's gotten over his depression, in maybe 30 to 40 years. 

Which means that its your problem to deal with, I hope you gave yourself a strong powerset because there will be *no one* there to help you. Unless you have a way to empower people and make preparations, otherwise you are going to have a horrible time being essentially the only one who can do something to stop him.

Oh! And this also includes any other setting changes you might have added; if monsters awaken then humanity is getting mauled with small groups only holding out, if its hell on earth then everyone is disgusting without powers, and if the Beasts of Entropy come then there will no Blessed coming (I hope you like fighting for days).
objects.title: One Of A Kind

objects.text:
Rather than powers having retroactively never existed, this modifier makes it so they did exist... until the instant you showed up. Upon your insertion, all powers in the setting are permanently disabled. Parahumans are disconnected from their shards, sorcerers stop producing cursed energy, quirks are erased, mages can no longer activate spells, etc.

Expect chaos to ensue as society has to adapt to the new status quo. Many former heroes and villains are left in despair as they feel practically crippled compared to what they used to be capable of. Governments desperately try to compensate for their lost defenders while parts of them simultaneously begin to retaliate against those who once were immune to their control. Meanwhile people are left fighting over pieces of leftover Super / Hyper / Magi / Tinkertech or empowered items that are now irreplaceable. Needless to say, should you have powers, you will get ALL the attention from every single faction, for good and for ill.

In addition, this only affects empowered humans and human adjacent / equivalent life (aliens, demihumans, etc.). Nonhuman supernatural beings whether canon or introduced by modifiers remain, as do various cosmic / divine forces which now have no one to stop them. Monsters, cursed spirits, beasts of entropy, entities, demonic invaders and more, with any that passively or actively empowered humans who could have fought back now no longer doing so. In a world that now lacks the defenders they so heavily relied on, you better hope whatever powers you purchased are enough to fight them off, because they now lack even whatever mundane forces they could have developed in place of powers that no longer exist.
objects.title: Twilight of Powers

objects.text:
You can alter the other AU modifiers in various ways, as long as you stick to some of the themes of the original modifier you can alter what the modifier actively changes.  

This could allow you to swap the targets of New Gods from the Quadrumvirate to the Undersiders, change Amalgam so that characters actually get split apart or some get split and others merged, change it so that Human Endbringers instead apply to pets, swap the Gotta Catch Em All’s Pokémon for Digimon, etc. 

Modifiers can also be focused, or the benefits taken in pieces, such as taking Old Empire’s technology & humanities power at its Old Empire modifier’s scale but leaving the scope of the empire itself at the galactic scale. 

You can take something like High School Worm x Worm and start removing the benefits you’d rather not include, such as the anime near-guaranteed good guys win ending, or perhaps the sex change included for most canon characters, while still retaining any of the other benefits that you do want to keep. 

Likewise, benefits can also be focused on, such as rewriting True Gods to remove Eidolon, Alexandria, and Hero and naming Legend the sole beneficiary as an extremely powerful amalgamation, or simply having his own brand of powers at a similar enough scale. 

The modifiers can also become more singular or have greater overall requirements, such as converting the Brute, Martial Artist, and the Boy Who Lifted into upgrades solely for Taylor Herbert, or perhaps solely Cauldron Capes, or have the VFX On modifier only apply to heroic parahumans or select individuals, etc. 

You can take Old Empire and convert the entirety of that humanities power into a single Shardless tinker on an otherwise normal Earth Bet, convert the Lost in Time modifier so that rather than people being dislocated in time and altering the timeline, it changes so that Parahumans have existed on Earth for a much greater period, and more. 

Alongside this, you can also alter the fundamentals of the world and its structure itself. From swapping which countries are the superpower, maybe Uganda has the same world status that America normally would while America is closer to what Italy would be considered. This also can be used to alter facets of reality itself, from the cosmology of the world such as turning it into a boundless flat world, or the afterlife by establishing or verifying one rewriting the rules of the current ones, or even removing it entirely. 

Benefits and challenges can be downgraded, reallocated, modified, swapped, amplified in a negative or positive direction, and otherwise altered in any way as long as it somewhat sticks to the theme in some manner.
objects.title: Editorial Edition

objects.text:
The various major components of your selected setting have been split apart and spread across the local multiverse. Necessitating at least a basic form of multiverse travel in order to visit these components.

Using Worm as an example, maybe Scion is in one world, Brockton Bay another, and organizations like the Yangban in a third.

Given the nature of the multiverse certain dimensions might have any combination of these components play out in them at the same time so maybe one world is basically an exact copy of canon Earth Bet in most aspects except for dimensionally unique existences like The Warrior and Endbringers.

For crossover settings you can choose for this to apply to the crossover itself and have your selected settings be whole, just as separate worlds across the local multiverse cluster. Though you can also further split up the components of those settings across the multiverse.

With crossovers you can choose for underlying mechanics such as power systems to remain connected.

Your selected location will have a major impact in determining which component of the setting you arrive at.
objects.title: Setting Fission

objects.text:
Purchasing this modifier ensures that any media your powers, companions, or objects of power (OOP) come from no longer exist in the world. The media they originate from may have simply never existed in this world, and if the media is too central to be removed, it will instead be replaced with a knock-off that somehow gets everything about your items wrong. This could involve inventing new weaknesses that don't apply to you or requiring an entirely different power source. As a result, no matter what you are, you will be something this world has never experienced before.

The effects of this Continuity Modifier can also be extended to your home universe.
objects.title: Original Content Only

objects.text: Now you no longer need to have purchased something for its media to cease existing. You may choose any number of content from any type of media—books, songs, movies, TV shows, games, or others—and be guaranteed that it has never existed, and will never exist in your starting setting, unless you create it yourself. If a particular piece of media is too central to be removed entirely, it will instead be replaced with a knockoff version.
objects.title: Your Choice of Content

objects.text:
Humanity begins their journey as blank slates—purely human in form at birth, untouched by the influence of diet. But as they grow, the things they consume begin to shape them. 

A child who regularly eats chicken might begin to sprout feathers by adolescence, their nose hardening into the beginnings of a beak. A diet heavy in lamb could lead to woolen fur and horizontal pupils. Those who consume mostly fish may find their legs fusing into scaled tails, struggling on land without developing the corresponding gills to survive underwater. Those devoted to fruits and vegetables slowly green over, developing leaf-like hair or bark-textured skin, some even gaining limited photosynthetic abilities.

Eating something once or twice, or even every few months, does nothing. The transformation only comes from sustained habits—those foods consumed every other day, week in and week out. 

Few adults look entirely human; instead, they’re mosaics of features drawn from every creature they’ve ever tasted. This doesn’t just affect appearance—traits include strengths, weaknesses, and even instincts of the consumed animals. A person who’s eaten too much predator meat may find themselves prone to aggression or territorial behavior. Someone who favors rabbit might become skittish, fast—but also perpetually anxious.

In this society, a perfectly human adult—smooth skin, with minimal mutated features, no bestial quirks—stands out as a deeply disturbing anomaly. Such a person can only exist if they regularly consumed one kind of meat: other humans. Most will get arrested or killed just by existing.
objects.title: You Are What You Eat

objects.text:
The setting becomes weaker to the point where most people with powers are street-level in strength on average. This also lowers the general scale of enemies or supernatural disasters, which typically won’t exceed city-level strength. This includes threats from super science as well. This doesn’t set a strict maximum power level, but instead reduces the average across the board, minimising large jumps in strength. 

This does not override any other drawbacks or choices that introduce more powerful beings or enemies. Lastly, you can optionally have it affect you and your build if you want.
objects.title: Street Level

objects.text: Whatever objects or powers you bought in this CYOA can now retroactively be inserted in place of their counterparts—if there are any—in the world you are heading to, taking their place in history. If you Drop In, then—to an outside observer—it may look like objects suddenly teleported straight to you, and powers have switched their wielder. If you reincarnate, objects may have had their history altered to have somehow found their way to you before your awakening, or your incarnation may have been born with the powers you purchased here. The specifics are completely up to you and can be decided on a case-by-case basis or, alternatively, left to be sorted out according to your subconscious desires. While this will not change your objects and abilities in any way, if their counterparts had something in the world narratively tied to them, those ties will remain.
objects.title: The Original

objects.text:
You can choose to make it so that the setting you are going into isn't the original, but rather one where the theories about the story that were later proven wrong were correct.

For example, you could make the Endbringers multiversal antibodies against parahumans, Coil’s power the ability to control a person's fate by making a deal with them, Jack Slash the secret creator of the Siberian who got his power by making a deal with his Passenger, Scion a time-travelling future version of Legend, and Theo Anders the one who destroys the world after triggering with an overwhelming power.
objects.title: It’s Obvious!

objects.text:
Another individual has been dropped into the world you’re entering. Unfortunately they used to be a fan of the fictional presentation of that world. Depending on that world’s circumstances this may cause them considerable distress.

This individual is guaranteed to have some power or skill, but the form this takes will vary from world to world. In DC they might be a Kryptonian, or possess a Quirk, etcetera. Similarly, you have no control over their personality, attitude or the powers they will receive.
objects.title: Good Heavens! Would You Look At The Time!

objects.text: The individual dropped into your world is no mere "fan", but a superfan of the highest calibre. They possess an eidetic memory and somehow know everything about the setting, including obscure knowledge that could only be gleaned from detailed interviews with the creators of the world itself. They are immune to any memetic hazards or negative consequences resulting from this. Their power is also guaranteed to make them strong enough to be considered a true powerhouse of the setting. They might be a stable Alpha psyker, a 4th-Generation Kindred, or a 20th-level wizard, depending on the world, and could become even stronger with time and effort.
objects.title: Transported To Another World, But It Turned Out It Was My Favourite Setting, And I Became The Strongest!?

addons.text:
The time-limit of ten years has been removed, letting you place the starting-point for your chosen options far earlier. Though the further back you place the starting-point relative to your insertion-point, the further along in the rollout you'll start in, with a decade or two being the absolute limit of time you have until the full effects are reached.

Now, with The Last Civilization in the Universe instead of stars being mere legends humanity has watched the stars wink out for generations, with the light of the last star still shining for a few more years even though its source has long since been snuffed out.
Instead of String Theory, the Moonshot was now caused thousands of years ago by an asteroid, and humanity is long accustomed to keeping an eye out for the occasional free-floating fragment falling to Earth.
The Mobs of World Curse, instead of appearing with your arrival, have plagued humanity since the days our ancestors starting building the first structures.
And The New Ice Age has slowly begun chilling the planet since the time of Columbus.

No matter what option or options selected, humanity is well-accustomed to the change and has long since adapted to it as best they can.
addons.title: Glacial Rollout

addons.text:
In this better world, you now have a chance to mitigate the options chosen. You can't prevent them, events still having been set in motion long before your arrival, but with enough effort you might be able to limit the damage somewhat, and with years and decades of effort perhaps one day even begin reversing the damage.

Perhaps you can find the cause for your world becoming a Desert World and remove it, or simply use your own powers and technology to counteract the effects, reducing the average temperature of the colder regions to a more tolerable 20°C (68°F) instead of 45°C.
If you have Transformed Ocean's Ancient Domain, you may be able to fight back, driving the ancient sea-dwellers back into the depths and preventing them from barring humanity from the seas.

Though be aware, just because it is possible does not mean it is easy, and you only have so much time before it is simply too late to prevent the worst. Good luck, you'll need it.
addons.title: An Actual Chance

objects.text:
Many World Modifiers and Different World-options change the world either instantly, rapidly, or retroactively. Now you can select any number of these options, and their effects will instead appear more gradually over the course of up to ten years. You cannot prevent the coming of your chosen options, as the rollout will have begun long before your insertion, with the absolute earliest point you can be begin at being the halfway point between the first traces of your options appearing and the option reaching full power. Basically if you choose the rollout to take ten years, the rollout will have started at least five years before your arrival.

Making options rollouts means that instead of Stone Age instantly shutting off all technology, it will now begin with a just few devices here and there breaking down before the process accelerates until eventually all technology becomes useless.
If you select Gotta Catch Em All, instead of Pokémon having coexisted with humanity since ages ago, now they only have only begun to appear recently, with rumors of them being a biotinker's work having escaped into the wild swirling about.
With The Alien Invaders, humanity has engaged in numerous skirmishes with scout-elements of the aliens for years, getting a measure of their tactics and technology, before their main-forces arrive and the true war begins.

On the flipside, options that otherwise would reach back further are now recent changes, with Competitive Society for example Cape-culture would actually start out much like canon, with corporate sponsorships being a very recent trend that's quickly sweeping across the world and reshaping the previous culture of heroes and villains.

The ultimate result remains unchanged, your chosen options eventually reaching their full effect, but now you, and humanity as a whole, have a bit more time to gradually adjust instead of being thrown right into the deep end.
objects.title: Gradual Rollout

objects.text: Every option selected in settings, excluding those under Alternate Earths and Original Settings, will alter not only the world you start on but also all worlds within the local multiverse.
objects.title: Multiversal Impact

objects.text: Now every time you enter another world you can redo the entire settings section as well as any world directed drawbacks. Your total SP and CP must remain above zero for this to work.
objects.title: Settings Redo

addons.text:
Rather than another area in your world with a higher power level, the levels of power now exist in parallel and the Shroud is multi-layered. Reaching a certain level of power starts peeling back the Shroud on the next layer, and disguising your actions to the layer below. 

The power of the Shroud to alter space, time, dimensions, destiny, causality, and/or more is further increased in order for it to keep the power layers separate. Conflicts in higher layers will have the tendency to 'miss' the lower layers, pretty much no matter how destructive they are, even if a continent-destroying fight takes place in a populated city. In order to bypass this, one must be able to bypass the Shroud entirely... and there's no telling how many layers it could possibly have.

Those with clearsight can only see one layer above themselves.
addons.title: Recursive Wells

objects.text:
You know that trope where you spend a while in one part of the setting, getting familiar with the power scale and seeing who the strongest guys are, and then suddenly you learn that there’s another area outside that place where the strongest guys look like chumps doing parlour tricks? Your world now follows that trope.

The normal setting is intact, but there’s another place you can travel to on another continent, planet, dimension, etc, where the power level is dramatically skewed so that even weak mooks from there would be considered top-tier threats in the normal world while the strongest normal characters are “just okay” by their standards. Of course, the rewards in the new area are commensurate with the risk. If you can make it there you’ll have access to materials, technology, and levels of your world’s power system beyond the wildest dreams of anyone in the old world.

The existence of this extra-strength new world may or may not be common knowledge to regular people. The path between the two areas is open to anyone capable of traversing it and goes both ways, so it’s practically inevitable that there will be crossover between them sooner or later.
objects.title: Big Fish in a Small Pond

addons.text: Instead of being fully replaced, the original cast still exists, though now as side characters that exists in the background. In a world where Spiderzuku exists, Peter Parker or Miles Morales might be unpowered neighbors who Izuku helps from time to time. Or in a world where Columbo is working on the Kira case, L could be one of the many officers working under him. You get the picture.
addons.title: They're Still Here!

addons.text: Turns out, there are parallel worlds where your cast changes happened the other way around. So for example, if Taylor as Goku exists, so does Goku as Taylor. This add-on will make it so that it is possible for this alternate swap to be isekaid here or the other way around. It's like looking into a mirror, but weirder!
addons.title: Cast Reunion

addons.text: With this choice, instead of merging with different characters from the same setting, the characters merge with the ones you chose to replace them with. A quick example would be Omniman replaced with Homelander will now instead be one entity, with combined backstory, traits, and abilities. Basically, just like how the original Amalgam Comics used to work.
addons.title: We Are One

objects.text:
Izuku? Who's Izuku? Don't you mean Shirou Midoriya?

With this choice, your setting's cast gets replaced by another setting's sets of characters. It's a crossover based role swap, where you can get scenarios like say, Columbo taking the place of L from Death Note, or Taylor taking the role of Spiderman, etc.

The characters retain their personality from their initial universe, though of course, playing way different lives could change a person. But their change in personality would also have a butterfly effect on how the canon storyline would of course go. So you can potentially be rather strategic with your recasting, after all, maybe certain people would be just right for the job? Note that you don't have to pick just one fanbase, you can mix and match. You also don't have to change the entire cast and may only pick one or a few more to be replaced. How will this affect the story? You'll see.

If you select this with a normal Earth, you can use this to instead, replace important people with a different cast. Imagine, if you will, Winnie the Pooh as the President? Or The Joker as the Pope? Etc etc.

Happy fancasting!
objects.title: Castswap

objects.text: This modifier allows you to add non-canon content to the setting you drop into. For example, in the world of Naruto, it can retroactively and logically integrate things like items, people, and locations from movies, games, and anime filler into the established timeline. You, of course, have the final say on what content is included.
objects.title: Filler Up

objects.text: The world you're going to is a bit sillier than you remember. Rather than going to the media itself, you’re going to an abridged version where everything is mixed up and exaggerated for comedy. To raise some possibilities: Jack Slash doesn't have powers, he just runs up to people, slashes them, runs back, and then gaslights them about it. Sophia Hess randomly infodumps about Animal Planet. Taylor Hebert repeatedly gets really into how attractive she finds women but still insists she's straight. This and more is just the tip of the iceberg. In general, every fandom joke there is has been thrown in, plus some original ones too, and from there the plot has spiraled into something loosely following the beats of the original while being altogether sillier. While the world will likely be more fun to be in, the actual threat level of the setting won't change, and it's going to be a lot less predictable.
objects.title: Worm Abridged

objects.text:
For some reason or another, the mightiest beings in the setting have turned their attention away from meddling with the world. This could have happened for a variety of reasons, such as a gentleman’s agreement between deities, boredom that comes with eternity, or a duty that can’t be ignored. The cause will fit seamlessly into whatever setting you apply it to.

The greatest entities in the setting have become largely inactive when it comes to interacting with the world. In general, this makes higher-powered beings less active and more reclusive. This will not fundamentally change any existing beings, but they will take action far less often in most affairs.

This does not prevent them from doing anything they would normally do. They will still act according to their own reasons and desires. However, the chances of them acting directly or heavily interfering with the world at large are greatly reduced. Garnering their active interference becomes more difficult, and they will often rely on intermediaries or use more subtle methods.

This does not prevent world-ending scenarios such as Scion’s eventual rampage, but it would significantly reduce his interest and activity unless he is heavily provoked.

This affects the highest echelon of beings in whatever world you enter. It scales relative to the strength of the world, so if the strongest being is a cosmic entity or someone powerful enough to destroy towns, it will always adjust to match that scale.
objects.title: A Step Back

objects.text:
By taking this mod you’ll find that everyone from canon Worm to be about 10 years older, and that the events and scenarios have been adjusted to match. For example Taylor Hebert is 25 instead of 15 on January 3rd, 2011. 

Alternatively you can be selective about who is older instead of having this apply to everyone. Maybe while Taylor is a young adult, Emma could still be a teenager like canon Worm for example. Though then you’d have to work out how an adult Taylor would trigger from being bullied by a teen. For example, maybe adult Taylor works at Winslow instead of triggering in college like she might’ve if she and Emma were the same age.

If you chose the twin reincarnation method, and chose for your twin to be older, then you will be aged to match.
objects.title: College AU

objects.text:
It's said that certain people have odd benign growths in their brains, but no one knows what they do. But some people with it who undergo a specific trigger event find themselves in a virtual world when they sleep. With special powers unique to them. In the real world they are nothing, in the Dreamworld they are Parahumans. It's an odd trend that good sleep products are quite expensive.

If you have powers, you can access this Dreamworld through sleeping.

(Essentially this means that there are no Parahumans.)
objects.title: Dreamers

objects.text:
If only dreams could stay as that, dreams.

Somehow, everybody with an access to the Dreamworld now can unknowingly or even knowingly manifest this world in their head. Soon, reports of strange happenings begins spreading across your world, as Dreams and the Waking begin clashing into one another. Until one day, this shall start to be the norm.

You are one of these Dreamers, able to slowly manifest your dreams into reality as much as everyone with Parahuman abilities (or the equivalent of) can. Whether or not you try to stop the encroachment of dreams is up to you. 

How this will affect your chosen world heavily depends. In a more grounded (relatively) world such as Parahumans, it means everything starts out mundane before things go out of wack. In a much stranger world like One Piece, stuff that aren't expected to be within the setting will manifestm. Dreams are not known for their realism afterall.

Now sleep dear, it's a long night ahead."
objects.title: The Dream Made Manifest

objects.text:
Each additional setting you have chosen has been applied over each other. This has resulted in each character becoming a hybrid between themselves and one from the other setting. These amalgamated people are a combination of their constituent histories, powers and experiences.

These can be rather unpredictable, but always pair up characters from each setting rather than multiple from a single setting. Such as Khep-El the last daughter of Bryckton, or Roronoa Wallis, the swordsmaster of the Brockton Islands. 

While the people merging are unpredictable, the power of the mixed form will be the average of both constituent parts or otherwise channeled through them in such a way that both parts have equal input. For instance, Peter Uzumaki might well have a giant spider spirit caged inside him, but this would still have the same effects as the original fox.

You may choose whether this amalgamation also applies to you, and whether with merge it applies to you, and your merge partner/s independently.
objects.title: Amalgam

addons.text: Superpowers? Parahumans? Endbringers? Magic Space Whales that travel across the universe causing untold destruction? Of course they’re real. You made them after all. Except they’re only as real as you want them to be. The world is still the same as normal, the worlds are still games as normal, the only difference is you. The difference between the real world and the virtual one might as well not exist for you, allowing you to retain your powers/perks/skills and anything else your purchase here out into the real world. You can choose any part of your build to work as it normally would have without this modifier, i.e. buying the Inheritable perk allows you to retroactively give your family your abilities in the real world as normal, Altered History allows you to alter your character inserts real world history etc. This also extends to things such as Alternate Continuity modifiers, companions, etc. Your personal life perks/items/skills affects your normal life as well as your avatar, unless you would wish otherwise in some manner. You can choose others to have this applied to as well, such as allowing your companions to have true powers and abilities like your own.
addons.title: Cheat Code

objects.text:
Superpowers? Parahumans? Endbringers? Magic Space Whales that travel across the universe, causing untold destruction? Of course, they’re not real. 

The world you’re going to is now almost as mundane as your own; instead, the only real difference is that they have managed to make huge strides in the advancement of VR and AR technology. 

Their VR technology has progressed to perfectly create true virtual worlds and can take you into them entirely, capable of accurately replicating sensations. This is similar, although more advanced, to the technology of SAO. 

Instead of going to another world entirely, the world you are going to is one of the many VR games on the market. Endbringers are boss battles to defeat; Scion is the final boss in a SAO theme scaling level boss battle; Skitter is a relative noob who is freakishly good at min-maxing, etc. More important and integral parts of the story are AI-NPCs made for the game. Their personalities and characters are as realistic as any human. 

The build you’re making here is for your online avatar instead of you; the Powers, Perks, Items, and the like are all attributes of your online avatar instead of you. You have no true powers, although you can retain any non-supernatural personal life items or perks for both your online life and real life (Coinage, Cosmetic Shapeshift, etc). 

You can buy more games (Alternate Worlds), Mods for your games (Modifiers), and there are even Mods on the market that can allow you to combine games (Crossover/Fusion Worlds). However, you’re going to have to pay for them as normal. Other modifiers you've chosen can also be counted as modifiers for your game, allowing you to remove or read them as you wish. 

There is also a general VR world where people can meet, hang out, and do thousands of other activities.

As all the games work on a similar engine, if you possess homecoming, you have a unique code that can import your character between worlds, allowing you to retain your abilities between games. 

This naturally removes any of the real dangers of these worlds, as they are now a game.
objects.title: Worm: Game of The Year Edition

objects.text: The world is not as you know it; something has fundamentally changed. Perhaps your expected Harry Potter adventure is now a romantic comedy, or maybe Cyberpunk is a murder mystery. What matters is that the world has undergone a fundamental shift from your expectations, rendering all your meta-knowledge unreliable; in fact, relying on assumptions based on it might even hinder you.
objects.title: Genre Shift

addons.text:
No longer are the voices in your head sourced from those you kill, instead they are sourced from the same internet which hosted the Discord server. The voices can perceive anything you do and know you can hear them. 

They still can’t do anything but speak, but they can be very loud if enough of them are speaking at the same time. The number of voices in your head can fluctuate, ranging from hundreds to thousands or even tens of thousands, although the number will never drop below 100. The number of voices usually correlates to whatever you’re doing, with more impressive and entertaining actions drawing more voices. 

If you entertain them, you'll find they do have a habit of wanting you to succeed, but can be extremely unhelpful at times even when trying to help. They also have a habit of referencing nuggets of meta information they shouldn't know, so if you sift through the nonsense and memes and manage to decipher the meaning behind what they say you may learn some things.
addons.title: The Voices

objects.text: ”Day after Day they pour forth Speech; Night after Night they reveal Knowledge.” In the 1st Phase, all of the computers and phones on Earth-Bet are given an archive of message logs from a Discord server that focuses on discussing and joking about fictional worlds. This Archive cannot be deleted/censored from any device. This server contains meta-knowledge of Worm, but only speaks of it sometimes, along with other fictional settings, often in the form of jokes or terms that (to the people of Earth-Bet) are nonsensical or carry little relevance. Many ignore it, some read a little of it, but only a handful of people attempt to decode each term, and dive deeper into the archive. The oldest messages date back to 4 years before the most recent message. With all the knowledge, theories, and the conclusions that they have drawn to, some of the that handful will attempt to join Cauldron (should they somehow figure out that it exists), others will head to the Protectorate, some will find other groups to sell their information to, but none of it will be even close to 100% accurate. Any information gained and/or inferred from the moment the server is leaked, until 2 months pass, will be closer to 30-40% accurate. Thus, misinformation being abundant about the future will end up making things worse for the world in many small and inconvenient ways. Thinkers will be unable to discern important information in the first month, not getting much feedback from their powers beyond what is irrelevant, and that some of this information pertains to events that take place in Earth-Bet. Until the end of the 2nd Phase, which begins after the 2nd week, nothing good or bad will occur as a result of the information inferred from the server. For example, Saint, even if he receives information confirming that the users in the server knew of Dragon’s nature and the Dragonslayers, would not activate the Iron Maiden Program and kill Dragon. After the first month passes and the second month begins, the interim between the 2nd and 3rd Phases begins. Accuracy slowly begins to rise, Thinkers receive more from their observations, with increasingly important facts and finer details coming to light. Nicknames and common names are finally given faces, but none of it truly makes much sense, even then. Nothing good or bad happens in the grand scheme of things, but minor inconveniences, conflicts, and events start popping up as a result of more accurate information. Now, the world figuratively waits in bated breath and heightened tension for the peak of this memetic madness, and the unraveling of this mystery. Eventually, the 3rd Phase will begin after the third month begins. A moderately-sized collection of 100% accurate information, specializing in plot relevant events or people, such as Cauldron, Coil’s Civilian Identity/Power, Eidolon being the reason why the Endbringers are active, the nature and meaning of “Gold Morning”, and Dragon being an AI, along with her origin, will come to be revealed to the eyes of the public. Chaos will likely ensue, and tension between some factions/groups, minor or major, will escalate in response. This is not a full play-by-play of the story, but a number of broad strokes, with the occasional deep dive, that is being released. It's just that all that it contains ends up being 100% accurate. Note: Pictures, GIFs, Videos, Music, and other such media that doesn't already exist in the world will not be able to work in the initial phases, resulting in many embed failures, but will be able to work a month after the server is leaked. If it is related to Worm, however, then they will not work properly until after the phase where 100% accurate information is given comes to pass. For maximum understanding, of course. (If you pick this option on an Alternate Earth, then changes will be made to suit your world properly in place of Earth-Bet and knowledge of Worm.)
objects.title: Discordant Emergence

objects.text: Rumours, lies, and half-truths are now coming to life, a twisted reflection of reality that slowly infects the world through the Collective Unconscious of Humanity. As more and more people believe in something, it will become real, uncaring if those things contradict the natural laws of reality. This strange phenomenon will only happen if the majority of people believe it to be true. The effects of this bizarre warping can also be localised to certain areas/pockets of people, making a strange new ecosystem where myths and beliefs exist alongside the people who brought them to life. While many of these effects can be dangerous since the vast majority of humanity has the will to live and survive deeply ingrained inside them, there won't be any world-ending catastrophe unless there is a global collective desire to end it all. Most people will not notice these effects even if something were to change right in front of their eyes, accepting it like it had always existed this way. Others who are disconnected from the larger Collective Unconscious or those who have a strong sense of self, will, or desire will find a strange sense of the Mandela effect, which will slowly boil over until they start to see this phenomenon.
objects.title: Truth. Lies. What's The Difference?!

objects.text: Does your favorite verse have a shitty reboot, prequel, or show that everybody pretends doesn't exist? Now, you can remove it from canon, as if those events never existed. Want to go to the MCU? You could remove the Time Variance Authority, the Eternals, Shang Chi, etc. This can also prevent future events from occurring. For example, if you choose this modifier and head to Star Wars: A New Hope, the events of episodes 7-9 would never happen if you wish. You can choose the way this modifier acts: maybe Korra was never born, Luke established a competent Jedi academy, time travel was always impossible, etc.
objects.title: Rey? Who?

addons.text:
Instead of being limited to only 3 lives, you now have infinite! Hooray! 

That... Also means your brain is gonna get real traumatized. Whoops.

Instead of going from Green to Yellow to Red, your mark instead goes from a bright Green before slowly losing color the more you die, turning Grey. 

You still cannot attack people directly when fully Green, but it gets easier as you lose color. You get meaner, you start to care less when you cause pain. And soon, your soul goes Gray.

The paranoia grows with each subsequent death, until you will fear everyone around you. The only way to regain color in your soul is to take the life of someone else.

Hmm? What happens when your soul goes fully grey? Um? <i>Checks notes<i> Don't think about that. We <b>totally<b> thought of that before adding this glorious new feature. <small>Just gunna pretend no one asked that...<small>

But at that point, could you even still be saved? Especially with how much people fear you?

What? I said something about free therapy. Um no I didn't? What do you mean you have records? They are clearly forged.

So uh, please, stop dying.
addons.title: The Cost of Eternity

objects.text:
Everyone is now born with 3 Lives, meaning they can die at least 3 times before "truly" dying. How many lives folks have is seen through a heart-shaped tattoo on their wrist, which changes color depending on how many lives they've lost (Green if none, Yellow if one, and Red if two). 

You can regain life either via a person willingly giving you one of their lives, or if you take it from them through murder. Should you be revived via outside means, you only get 1 new life (meaning you'll always start at Red post revival). You cannot exceed 3 lives.

How many lives you still have seems to have an effect mentally. Greens seem to have a mental block that prevents them from directly physically attacking people unless it's for self-defense. There are loopholes for this, but stuff like punching somebody or directly hurting them with your powers is a no-go. 

This limit is lifted on Yellows, who can now directly attack people, but they now start to get plagued by creeping paranoia. 

This is worse with Reds, who are now so paranoid that a lot are driven to murder just to shut up the thoughts that say everybody is out to get them. 

This has some interesting effects on society, with Reds and Yellows being seen as potentially dangerous while Greens are coddled heavily, even if being Green does not necessarily mean well intentioned, and neither does being Red mean willing to kill. 

Interestingly, this makes a lot of Parahumans Yellows.

There are ways to lose more than one life in one fell swoop. If your injuries are severe enough (like getting blown to pieces) or through enough aging, you could lose your lives even if you're at Green. 

This choice also has the potential to affect the timeline of your setting, with some dead characters potentially only losing a life instead of permanently dying. How this affects Canon is up to you.
objects.title: Hardcore, With A Twist!

objects.text: "God is a 12 year old girl, and we're living in a weird Sherlock College AU." The world you're in had changed. Certain common tropes found in Fanfiction had become the norm. You may see some characters suddenly becoming Coffee Shop owners, unrequited love of any form suddenly causing people to cough out flowers, a strange scarcity of beds, etc. The changes are surprisingly subtle, besides the characters being slightly out of character, the plot of whichever world you have chosen will not fully diverge. You can only choose which tropes you wish to blacklist from happening, otherwise, how it affects this world is random. Why is this happening? Well, it turns out, you spawned in a fanfic of the very CYOA choices you made, and too bad, you're not the author. You're simply a character here, so do expect these tropes to start happening to you as well. At the very least, you seem aware of this, and can simply go against what the author seems to be trying to do. Whether or not this has consequences depends on the author, though normally, the author isn't inherently malicious. Canon? What Canon? You must navigate this different yet still mostly similar world. Will you thrive or will you die like men?
objects.title: There is Only One Bed?!

objects.text:
The boundary separating fiction and reality has worn thin, just enough to let a lot of somethings to seep through. Fictional characters have basically appeared in the real world. Except it’s not the famous characters, but the lesser, smaller characters in the internet, the “OCs”, brought to life by imagination and confined to stories never meant to escape their creators’ notebooks or fanfiction archives. 

These characters will generally be confused for a short period after appearing, believing they are still in their original world. They will however quickly become aware that their lives, their memories, their pain were all crafted by someone else, often for entertainment. Most are consumed by the need to find their author—some driven by curiosity, others by grief, and some by wrath. What happens next depends entirely on how cruel or kind their creator was. Did the author break them again and again for the sake of a better plot? Did they ever give them peace? In many cases, their author does not survive the event.

Once that confrontation ends, they tend to pick up the threads of their former goals, repurposing their narrative momentum into the real world. And they’re not to be underestimated. They retain everything they were written with: supernatural powers, unique skills, cursed weapons, metaphysical knowledge, or stranger abilities. Their numbers are staggering, with enough to match 5 to 10% of the global human population. Millions worldwide, each with their own background, history, and goals.
objects.title: Author’s Wake

objects.text:
Sort of a counterpart to "Rey? Who?", have you ever had a piece of media where you see some concept art of it and think "Damn, they should've kept that"?

Well with this choice, you get to turn these dropped ideas into Canon! Whether you wish for that damn Wish star to be a human looking boy, have Nami from One Piece keep her initial mechanical arm design, or if for some godforsaken reason you want to revert Movie Sonic to his original pre-redesign look, then here ya go!
objects.title: What Could've Been

addons.text: When you take this alongside Gamer System, this makes it so that everybody gets access to their own version of this very same power, including whatever add-ons you have taken in Gamer System. This is both a good and a bad thing. The disadvantage is obvious as it is no longer a power only you could wield, but, you may also gain the benefit of walkthroughs in regards to certain quests due to other people also trying to get the hang of this ability. You're no longer special, but maybe that could be worth it?
addons.title: Not So Solo Leveling

addons.text:
The UI System instead becomes like a Fighting Game, with everyone having the same mental controls per given task. This makes doing things as easy as visualizing yourself clicking a few buttons, thus, changing how people approach things that requires any skill. Schools will be thought on how to execute combos to maximize one's potential. It becomes important for most folks to hone their reflexes first and foremost. And to put it simply, this ability becomes accessible to everybody, and they really mean everybody.

Maybe with the help of everyone around you, mastering this ability becomes much easier, especially with the existence of folks learning the art of the wombo combo before you even arrive. Life is a series of kicks to the noggin, can you parry your way into victory?
addons.title: EVO for Everyone

addons.text: Everyone also gets a body like that of a video game character, which works well with this UI as everything is now monitored through it. Your HP, the status effects you've incurred, etc, are all seen in your UI system. Be sure to keep that in mind, as the world is truly running on video game logic now.
addons.title: The Player Characters

objects.text:
Everybody in the entire world gets a UI system that helps with people's day to day life. It could be original to your world, or it could be based on any game. Either way, people have that now, including its benefits.

Depending on the chosen UI, people can have its extra storage system, though it is limited to the default storage size (unless expanded by other means, so Backpacks for example might still be useful). Abilities in powered setting could be put in quick spell slots for easy use. In RPG UIs, you can also look at stats that approximate numbers based on your skills.

Once more, it all depends on the UI you chose. Do keep in mind that everyone has this though, and opening your UI makes them visible to others as well. So be careful when using them. Keep in mind, this might affect how people interact when you have piles of windows in front of you. So, this might affect the world much more than one may think.

Life is a game, and now everyone can play it.
objects.title: Universal UI

objects.text:
Add a genre to the world you're about to be entering. This genre will become one of the main genres of the setting, taking a prominent role equal to the original main genres. Note that this new genre doesn't replace or invalidate any original genres, but is merely added to them. You can decide which genre it is, but have no control over how it integrates itself into the setting.

Adding Tragedy to Harry Potter could result in heroic sacrifices becoming more common and victories more costly, making the antagonists act even crueler, or just in the main-cast now having extremely depressing backstories that shaped them into far more jaded people. Adding Comedy to Star Wars could result in slapstick-esque situations happening frequently or people just throwing around very funny zingers all the time. Adding Scifi to Pokémon could result in trainers relying more on futuristic gadgets, or turn the different gym-towns they head for to into planets that the trainers travel to in personal spaceships, taking the Journey from the road to the stars.

The world is still recognizable, and your knowledge of the series will still be useful, but depending on what genre you choose your knowledge can range from “mostly accurate” to “applicable in only the broadest sense and possibly even detrimental if applied beyond that”.

You may select this option multiple times to add up to three new main genres.
objects.title: Additional Genre

objects.text:
A counterpart to Additional Genre, you are now able to remove at most 3 specific genres from a given work. And like with Additional Genre, how this may affect your work isn't something you can fully foresee. This is actually best used alongside Additional Genre for finer control, but it could also be used without it, leading to interesting results.

A couple of quick examples could be removing Fantasy from Harry Potter, making the adventure something mostly explained through rather mundane semi scifi means, or removing SciFi from Star Wars which may result in it becoming a Western turned War Film later down the line. Once again, do be careful in regards to how it will affect your setting as how it would end up integrating is outside of your control.

Finally, how accurate your setting is to the original work depends on you. It could range from still "mostly accurate" to "not really". So do keep that in mind.
objects.title: Minus Genre

objects.text:
Whoever is in charge of balance in your world has clearly given up, because people are just doing shit now.

Whatever the scale of the conflict in the setting is, the power levels involved will be inflated to be way out of scale with it. If you’re going to a world where the stakes revolve around high school sports then those high schoolers will be summoning demons on the field and telekinetically obliterating buildings just to score a point. In a world with actual superheroes there will probably be supervillains summoning the true form of Azathoth to rob a bank and heroes going faster than light and reversing time to prevent Candy Stealer Man’s great-grandparents from meeting. Heck, maybe some of the stronger characters will reach out of their animation to crumple up the frame of the storyboard with their enemy in it.

People will not notice anything weird about all the chicanery going on and will treat the new status quo as normal and proportionally valid. If you question why a pop idol is attacking their rival with an orbital laser you should expect weird looks for asking such a stupid question. The stakes of the main conflict itself will remain the same as the original, only the collateral around it will change. Opposing teams might be literally killing each other on the football field, but the number one concern is still whether the underdog team can break their school’s losing streak and bring home the trophy.
objects.title: Ref! REF! Ref DO Something!

objects.text:
As if something were working behind the scenes to ensure balance, events will somehow conspire to ensure that whenever characters interact they will somehow be able to compete roughly relative to each other. Even if one character is normally vastly above what the other can deal with, the weaker will either find themselves inexplicably more effective than they were before, temporarily gain access to some new asset which will allow them to punch above their usual weight class, or end up in situations which play to their unique strengths and traits to make them an effectual ally or enemy.

This won’t completely eliminate power differences, so the character who was vastly more powerful before will still maintain a comfortable combat superiority to the other, but it will ensure that the situation doesn’t become “Captain Omnipotent and Acquaintances.”

There can be some level of flexibility to this, so a regular human running into a galaxy destroying space-god probably still won’t be able to be a threat to them, but they may have the chance to somehow be useful to them or avoid being crushed.
objects.title: Crossover Logic

objects.text: Rather than having your other Continuity Modifiers be an inherent part of the fabric of reality you can have them be the result of a single source. This source can be anything; a creature, object, virus, weather pattern, or whatever else you can think of. It could even be you. If a living thing is the source then you may decide whether they’re uncontrollably causing the change or if they have the power to manipulate and selectively impose it. For example, you can make it so that Musical Worm! and Just Dance! are being caused by a supernatural entity using its powers to make people sing and dance like they’re in a musical, New Gods is the result of a strange meteor which amplifies the power of those who find it, or a radioactive storm is mutating life to cause Bizarre Ecology.
objects.title: Locus of Chaos

objects.text:
With this choice, your setting is actually not a world at all, but is instead, a TTRPG game played by you and the characters. This could mean we could have the Undersiders being characters from a Weaverdice campaign, or the Straw Hats being player characters in a really long and fucked up Dungeons and Dragons campaign, etc. 

Who their players are may be based on the character they are playing. These players could be original characters, or different characters from entirely different settings. That is for you to decide. 

This also means that the character you build shall now be a character for this TTRPG. This makes you a player alongside them. Do expect some stereotypical player behavior, and the general chicanery that one may expect in any long running roleplaying campaign.

After all, it was once said that if Lord of the Rings was a DND game, it would've been a really really dumb.

What the TTRPG is exactly may also depend on you. It could be any of the well known ones like DND, Pathfinder, or World of Darkness. Maybe you could go for niche ones like FATE or Gurps. Or maybe you'd prefer to keep this story system-agnostic and make up your own TTRPG as you go? You could even potentially use this for crossovers, with one universe being a game played by the characters of one of your settings. You could be real meta with this, the possibilities are pretty endless.

Do have fun with this game you've set up, game master. Now, pick your dice, and roll.
objects.title: It's Time to Roll

objects.text:
While the world of your setting remains mostly the same, the conflict is just a tad bit more... Exaggerated. 

People and the characters specifically seem to take almost everything in the worse way possible. Heightened emotions and wacky decisions permeate this universe. The poor are just comically destitute, and the rich are rolling in gold. No relationship is healthy. Everybody for some reason seems to be on the risk of dying but is rarely ever actually killed off. This whole world is just much more melodramatic yet nobody sees that as weird, it is all played completely straight, and you happen to be wrapped up in all of this.

Essentially, this turns your world into a Telenovela. Complete with hammy acting, over complicated love triangle plot lines, and hilariously evil in laws. The actual plot or stakes of your setting doesn't at all change, people just act way more over the top and tropey for soap operas.
objects.title: Telenovela Life

objects.text: Songs that the Hyades shall sing, Where flap the tatters of the King, Must die unheard in Dim Carcosa. Within the hushed whispers of your realm, lies a play. Or was it a book? A painting? A game? A story..? Regardless, an influence spreads amongst the weary little heads of the unknowing masses. It starts with a subtle shift amongst the people. The artists and the privileged. A rise in hedonism at the cost of basic values. A slow descent into the nihilistic pursuit of decadence. And finally, a singular thought, believed to be the absolute truth, spreads onto those who's eyes behold the dreaded Yellow Sign. "Nothing matters, for none of us are real." A forbidden truth has been unleashed, like a virus leaving chaos in its wake. A pandemic of pandemonium, driving people into mass hysteria. Cults begin to form, worshiping the enigmatic figure behind the curtain. A following that believes that the truth is freedom. That we are mere actors in a play, and what a wonderful performance are we doing. You can try to stop it, you can delay the slow spread of gold. You can try to destroy its source, but it shall emerge once more, in a new form, in a new thing of beauty. You can only delay the inevitable call of our true masters. Whether it be tomorrow or a million years from now, it is a fearful thing. You cannot fully destroy a concept, the very essence of our humanity. So why not embrace it? In a world that's seemingly already doomed, why not live to your fullest? The claws of our entropic demise shall forever close in on us. There is more to life than our would be end. Go forth and see things in all its beauty, or leave, and find beauty elsewhere. The world is as wide as you wish to see. Whatever you do at the crossroads, keep moving forward. Or something like that. (I was never really good at endings)
objects.title: The Call of Carcossa

objects.text:
Pick a character from your setting, any character. Upon doing so, your setting shall be contacted by a civilization consisting of nothing but clones of this character. Whether it be through actual cloning or through multiversal shenanigans, this civilization's shape and intentions are based specifically on which character you picked. This is also the basis on whether or not said civilization is even stable to maintain itself as not all folks could get along with themselves ironically enough.

Once again, depending on the person chosen, this civilization could be hostile or not. Maybe the introduction could be public, so that everyone knows about it, or it could instead be secretive, only told to your world's leaders. They could be allies or enemies. Where they even come from, whether they already exist in your planet or they contacted your people through an interdimensional portal is up to you. Even their tech and power level is dependent on the person this entire country is made out of. Is this a contact for negotiation or invasion? It'll be dependent on your overall choice.

They say no man is an island, this character took it as a challenge.
objects.title: Country of One

objects.text: Within your setting, there's always some sort of threat(s) which puts the lives of many people at risk, one that brings great calamity in their wake. It could be something like the Endbringers in Parahumans, or a particularly terrible pirate in One Piece, either way, the world is left quaking in their wrath. And as all seemed lost... Thankfully, something had occurred which gave people hope. A spark in the darkness has been found, as several people started awakening as Chosen Ones. The ones empowered to protect the world. There is always 7 Chosen, each awakening with a new ability, or in the cases where they already have powers, gain a new one which works incredibly well with their initial arsenal. These chosen gain marks on their bodies which signifies their status. They then feel compelled to find one another before going out to destroy whatever it is that's threatening this world. This is regardless of the chosen's character, as their mark burns whenever they go against what they are chosen to do. Thus, if any of the chosen want to be freed, they must save the world, or die trying. Once the mission is complete, the chosen lose their marks and their blessed powers. How this system works is unknown as it seems supernatural in nature, either way, society begins to shift around this cycle of Chosens vs Villains. Whenever a huge threat emerges, it is to be expected that heroes will rise. Some places even begin molding people, expecting them to become chosen ones ready to bring hope to their world as those that came before them. Now is such a cycle. You could choose to either be one of these chosen or not, who the chosen are is also random depending on your chosen setting. Should you choose to be one of them, expect to be rewarded if you survive whatever task is given to you. Always remember, you are meant to win.
objects.title: The Chosen Seven

objects.text:
There is a hitch in the supposed road to victory for the chosen of this cycle. For strangely, unlike in any cycle before them, there was an Eighth chosen. While this is already suspicious enough, all eight chosen seem to possess a verifiable mark as well as blessed powers as expected of heroes such as them, making it almost impossible to see whether or not this is some sort of glitch in the chosen one system, or if there is a traitor amongst the party.

And soon, the answer shall be revealed.

Indeed, the eighth is a traitor, betraying the party and putting the quest in jeopardy. How they are marked and how they gained their powers is all part of their master's plot. Who that is and what their motives are, you don't know. That is... Unless the traitor is instead... You?

Why you would choose to do that and where your loyalties lie shall be up to you. Either way, the actions of the traitor, regardless of who they are, shall set the group back by a lot. For the first time, there seems to be a huge chance that whatever the threat may be, they might end up winning. How the world handles this and how the party may proceed, it'll depend on them.

The world is left darker now that the sacred cycle has been jeopardized. Will you stand by as the world tethers in the brink of potential annihilation?
objects.title: Among Us Chosen

objects.text:
For whatever reason all humans are resistant to master powers. The more strong willed or mentally disciplined a person the more resistant they are, to the point that a sufficiently gutsy hero type could shrug off the effects of even the most powerful masters. Meaning most master powers that affect other people are best used as momentary distractions instead of being relied upon in a fight, since other capes tend to have strong personalities.

Even if someone is definitely one hundred percent mind controlled and mentally rewired, reminding them of things they care about, or provoking them emotionally can help their original personality fight for control and recover.

This doesn’t really help the average civilian all that much, but at least you can rest assured that genuine hero types, or anyone with a strong personality can go into battle against powerful masters and probably come out the other side ok.
objects.title: I Know The Real You Is Still In There!

objects.text:
The world is ending.

Mankind has been or will be pushed to the brink of survival by in universe events or by your choices in this CYOA; And the hundred and ninety five countries, despite all odds, have banded together to create Project Hail Mary. 

It is the desperate gamble by a race out of time. This project will take a very select few on a suicide mission to deep into the cosmos to either find a solution to mankind's woes, set up a colony far beyond the light of sol or act as a memorial for the species, should none of the other options be feasible.

The chances of salvation are extremely slim but will never be impossible. If you wish, you may join on this expedition and you will be remembered as one of mankind's greatest heroes.

In practice, this option gives any apocalypse setting a potential golden future, in which mankind survives the disasters it has endured.
objects.title: A Hail Mary

objects.text:
Any sort of item that is well loved enough (be it a toy, a tool, a cloth, etc) and then abandoned, there is a chance that that item will end up developing sapience.

After a bit of existential crisis, these trashed items will proceed to feel the urge to try to find their former owners once more. Their intentions are almost always non hostile, as they only wish to be reunited with those whom treasured them. What happens next depends on what has since happened to their owners or how the owner reacts to them returning. For a hostile owner or a departed one might cause these creatures to lash out, but an owner who accepts them back with open arms shall earn a loyal companion.

Now, what's special about these creatures is how much they take after their owners, not only in personality, but in abilities. This is especially dangerous in powered settings, as items will develop similar or even copies of their owner's powers depending on the power system. This can range from a rogue trash gaining Skitter powers, or a particularly dastardly villain having a loyal companion with their same insane fire power. Their strength is well known enough that they are feared, with certain organizations being formed in order to maintain order in a world where a beloved pen could cause mass destruction.

Maybe you may gain a loyal companion or your own? Or maybe you yourself are a discarded treasure? Whatever it may be, the choice is yours.
objects.title: A Well Loved Friend
One Timeline All Along
objects.text:
With this choice, simple Easter Eggs, cameos, or even a character sharing the same actor are now deemed canonical hints to the fact that these clearly separate properties are in fact actually part of a singular timeline.
