It is important to note that this is a fantasy world filled with things such as fantasy races and monsters, and that performing good deeds will lead one to Heaven after death, while committing evil acts will send one to Hell. Additionally, depending on your actions, the world itself may attempt to end your life and restore the events you altered if you outshine the protagonist.
objects.title: The Greatest Estate Developer

objects.text:
Origin Of Power: Charyeok, Martial Arts, and Divine physiology/power

Major Power: The Human Cultural Organization, Nox, and Gods of the heavenly realms

Major Threat: Nox, Tathagata, Gods of the heavenly realms and Park Mujin

Note: 

You can either enter this world in the first G.O.H tournament or the time skip after Ragnarok.

People in this world are tougher than regular people. Those who are trained in martial arts in this world can reach ridiculous levels of power letting them destroy a significant portion of a country in a single strike but even the strongest human outside of some special case is nothing but fodder compared to mid-level gods who can destroy an entire planet furthermore they have place a taboo upon the genetic code of humanity which greatly reduce the power of human attack upon them should you choose to reincarnate here as a human the Taboo would also be place upon you.

The gods are coming to harvest human life force to extend their life and if you mess with canon too much certain events that ensure humanity winning Ragnarok might not happen and more likely than not humanity will be nuked back to the stone age.

If you enter this world post-time skip then Park Mujin has become the president of the world and he will carry out his plan of wiping away the old world and creating a new one.
objects.title: The God of High School

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Hero Blessings, Supernatural Evolution, Advanced Technology

Note:
If you have supernatural or sci-fi powers, you can optionally choose to have gained them via being a hero summoned to another world. Earth, known as the “World of Void” (although if you appear after a Demon Lord is born on Earth, the world would have lost this status), has become the stage for chaos as heroes return from their otherworldly battles—many broken, others seeking power, and a few determined to impose their warped sense of justice.

Governments struggle to contain the escalating crises, secret organizations manipulate the new power structures, and resistance groups fight for survival against both oppressive authorities and rampaging superhumans. Earth is no longer the safe, mundane world the public thought it was—it is now a battlefield shaped by those who have returned.

Note: You can choose which iteration you appear in.

A rare few, however, can attain abilities comparable to that of a Superpower but this is a very dangerous position to be in. Names define everything in the Land of Fantasy. If something loses it's name, then that thing loses definition, loses characteristics, identity, and loses it's own existence. Things can lose their name by being forgotten, or no longer possessing meaning.

The Hakurei Barrier is a barrier of common sense, which allows for the existence of the supernatural. Magic in Touhou is based on widely accepted beliefs and traditions, and can vary as perception changes. All races, that aren't humans or scientific in nature, in Touhou Project are born from fantasy, and take on traits of what people widely believe them to have, and can vary as this perception changes. 

The Spell Card Rule is a ruleset which people abide by to avoid lethal conflicts. Spell cards are moves or attacks that possess meaning. Danmaku don't have to be magic, and can simply be any attack or projectile, as long as it contains meaning.

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Mystery and Technology. Major Threats: Sorcerers, The Mages Association, Magi, The Holy Church, The Burial Agency, The Twenty-seven Dead Apostle Ancestors, Dead Apostles, and Sealing Designates. Major Powers: Sorcerers, The Mages Association, The Holy Church, The Twenty-seven Dead Apostle Ancestors, and Sealing Designates. Super Abilities: Magecraft, Magic, Vampirism, etc.

Note: Humanity's Struggle Against the Night.

  • Zelretch's victory over Type-Moon marked a pivotal shift in the balance of power. Following his triumph, he was turned into a Dead Apostle Ancestor by the former 3rd seat of the Twenty-seven, forever altering the cosmic hierarchy. This transformation tipped the scales in Gaia's favor and introduced a new dynamic to the Seat of Primacy. Humanity no longer stands alone as the dominant species—True Ancestors and their descendants, the Dead Apostles, now share the throne.
  • As a result, humanity has lost much of its relevance and influence in the world, though the vast majority remain blissfully unaware, living comfortably within the facade of modern society. Beneath the surface, however, the war against the creatures of the night rages on. Humans are being culled in the shadows, gradually reduced to little more than a food source for vampiric predators and the unseen rulers of the dark. Ignorance shields the masses from the grim reality, leaving them none the wiser to the horrors lurking just beyond their reach.
  • The Holy Church fights valiantly in this hidden war, striving to restore humanity's dominance as the sole occupant of the Seat of Primacy. Yet, their efforts seem increasingly futile against the relentless and ever-growing power of the Dead Apostles. With every passing day, the threat of humanity's enslavement—or even total extinction—looms closer, an inevitable fate creeping ever nearer as the tide of darkness rises.

Note: Reincarnation Options.

  • If you reincarnate, your odds of being born with magic circuits depend heavily on your magical affinity. Without prior magical power, there's only a 0.01% chance of gaining average-quality and quantity circuits. However, if you possess magic through other means, you are guaranteed to have circuits, with both their quality and quantity scaling to the cost of your magical abilities. In the case your power includes something like Magecraft or Sorcerer Apprentice, not only will your circuits be of high quality, but you may also choose to be born into a magus family. The family's standing, history, and level of Magecraft will likewise reflect the price of your magic. Should you reincarnate into such a lineage, the family's Magic Crest will be yours to inherit—unless explicitly willed otherwise.
  • Alternatively, if you possess both the Olympian and Frankenstein perks, you could choose to reincarnate into an official demon-slayer family or clan—such as the Nanaya, Fujou, Ryougi, or Asakami clans—or one of their branch families. You might even establish an entirely new demon-slayer lineage altogether if you wish.

Final Note: You can decide whether this places you in the Remake timeline, as depicted here, within the Original timeline, or in any of the Melty Blood games.

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Biology, Technology

Major Threats: Space Empires, Time Travelers

Major Powers: Galaxity (Humans), the many inter-planetary civilizations of Point Central, Hypsis

The primary means of faster-than-light travel is based on time travel; humans have mastered this technology to the degree they regularly send agents back in time to correct the timeline when they deem necessary. Their special agents, such as the titular Valérian and Laureline, are generally given broad latitude in how they solve problems, as long as they get results.

Galaxity are the main peace-keeping force in the galaxy — until they get kicked out of Point Central, one of the main centers of politics and commerce — after an attempted coup, foiled by one of their own agents; the majority empire is erased from the timeline in the conclusion of their conflict with the roaming planet Hypsis.

The galaxy of this setting is teeming with life, from primitive civilizations that live on exotic planets, to advanced technocracies. Aliens also take all shapes, from simple humanoids to truly alien beings, like shape-shifters, telepathic jellyfishes, giant insects that breathe sulfur, and sentient aquatic beings, among many others.

No matter where you go, in space or time, adventure is sure to be right around the corner.
objects.title: Valerian and Laureline

objects.text:

Major Threats: Giants, Monsters, Utgard Loki, Corrupted Olympians, Nyx, Muspelheim, Angra Manyu, Surtr

Note: By default, you may arrive at any point after Lee Tae-Ho is brought to Valhalla by the Valkyrie Hildegarde. It is important to note that there are ten realms in this world, such as Earth, Asgard, and Olympus, and that Ragnarok is unfolding across all realms as Muspelheim attempts to bring about the end of all existence.

It is also important to note that this world is divided into two types of people: those who seek to preserve the world and those who seek to destroy it. This division is more a matter of inherent nature than personal choice, as those born on the side that desires the world’s destruction cannot change their ways.

The gods are also benevolent, though their view of humanity varies depending on the realm. The Norse gods see humanity as their children, whom they must nurture and protect, with Odin himself being a reasonable and competent ruler. In contrast, the Greek gods tend to view humanity as tools meant to serve and worship them.

Major Powers: Camarilla is a vampire monarchy with various feudal domains; unusually, each city is ruled by a "prince," along with Primogens for each clan and a Sheriff that enforces the will of the prince. They wish to uphold the masquerade, a pact that all vampires (excluding the Sabbat) agree is necessary for the survival of the vampire society and the upholding of vampiric traditions so that humans do not realize that vampires exist and kill them. The Sabbat are a loose organization of Kindred who reject the notion that they can act human and believe themselves to be superior to humans and other vampires, believing themselves to be the ones that will stop the ancient vampires (the Antediluvians) from causing gehenna and be the sword that Cain (the original vampire) will use to kill the Antediluvians. The Anarchs are a group of Kindred who reject modern Kindred society (specifically the Camarilla) and wish to overthrow the oppressive rule of the elder vampires in the Camarilla, Cain the Original Vampire. Werewolves are seen as the top dog for most of the supernatural world, as they can easily rip to shreds even the strongest of vampires. Kuei-jin are Asian vampires who work under a different set of rules than the Kindred.

The society is heavily stratified, with figures such as Albina Awaria representing the ruling class, while the lower classes are sacrificed to maintain the system. 

In Helltaker, demons, angels, and the Underworld are all very real, with Hell existing as both a realm of punishment and a place where supernatural politics play out. After the events of Helltaker, in Examtaker there were laboratories where artificial intelligences and cybernetic clones are tested, often brutally, by mechanical systems within Hell by Loremaster who has taken over Hell.

Note: The Warframe universe is vast and often overwhelming, with constant battles, existential threats, and enigmatic lore. Please prepare for a long and challenging journey. As always, the Void watches... and whispers.

You can choose if you want to go to the galaxy in the 40th millennium or the 30th.

If you are a Primarch and choose to start in 30k you can choose to be a lost Primarch and have the Emperor come to look for you and give you a legion of space marines if you serve under him.

addons.text: You have chosen to merge both the world of Warhammer Fantasy & Warhammer 40k together - now, the world of Warhammer Fantasy is one of many feudal worlds found within the milky way galaxy that has yet to of been discovered by the Imperium of Man - or other interstellar factions. The various species of Warhammer Fantasy - such as the Elves - are actually derivitives of their W40k counterparts. Elves = Aeldari/Drukhari, Squats = Votann, Halflings = Ratlings, exe. Though species with no W40k equivalent like the Skaven might find new... opportunities if they discover the stars above them... god help the galaxy...

Also the chaos gods are almost invincible and horribly overpowered, and also very very evil, they will almost certainly try and corrupt you if you do not have mental shields in place to stop them. On the plus side if you get them to help, or replace them with another god which somehow gains hegemony, they will be quite the help against the warrior entity.
Also note that while this isn’t quite 40k levels of fucked beyond belief, it is still very close. This is a VERY grim dark world you are going to. Good luck.

Additionally, almost every pantheon will try to subvert you by their own means, either towards their goals or at least against their opponents. Thankfully, the gods of the realms have allied against threats before, Gorkamorka himself used to be a member of Sigmar’s order Pantheon, and so would likely fight against a threat to them all, albeit not without infighting and backstabbing.

addons.text: However, something of much greater concern is that this world is under the influence of a status quo and shifting timeline commonly seen in comics. Think of it as if you and those around you are reset to where you were last year, despite world events still taking place. Without protection, you too will be affected by this for 10 – 100 years, with 6 months to a year to establish a status quo for yourself to be reset into. Afterward, time will resume normally for you. May your sanity remain intact.
addons.title: Won’t You Stay For A Little? We Insist

addons.text:
Now, you are no longer merely a background character or a side story in another tale. You are frontline and center, being pulled into every imaginable plot you could be drawn into. From helping Sabrina search for rare ingredients, to carelessly finding yourself in a love dodecahedron, to being captured by the descendant of Captain Nemo—among so much more.

On the bright side, it would be a reasonably consistent comic run.
addons.title: Archie Presents YOU!

addons.text:
Remember how crossovers didn’t matter much? Well, now they certainly do. For whatever reason, Riverdale and the cities surrounding it, like Greendale, have become hotspots for these crossovers. If there is a reason—like a multiversal nexus, an anti-matter meteorite, or the sleeping mind of an Eldritch God that existed before time—it won’t matter nor help with the situation to uncover why.

While more crossovers will be occurring, those that are confirmed to be in play on some level are Archie's Sonic in a connected alternate universe, street-level Marvel characters like the Punisher and Wolverine, Alien vs. Predator, the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Scooby-Doo, Batman, and basically any and all OFFICIALLY PUBLISHED AND LICENSED crossovers involving Archie, Sabrina, and the Pussycats.​
addons.title: Public Domain Expansion

addons.text:
The light has greatly dimmed from this world, with those who call it home becoming more... moody, melodramatic, harsher, and mean-spirited at times. Less Americana and more like something adults think teenagers would like.

If you reincarnate into this setting, get ready for a lot of weird plot reveals and twists.
addons.title: Riverdale

addons.text:
Okay, so you can toss aside the whole mundane aspect, as now Archie and friends are getting in on the more fantastical and strange. 

Archie, Veronica, Betty, and Jughead all have superhero alter egos; spuds from outer space will try and take over the world by replacing everyone with clones; talking dogs in mystery machines; living cars; and so much more. 

Though nothing beyond your ability to handle, with much of what happens being something that would be fit for a 7+ audience—think more Goosebumps than Stephen King.
addons.title: Weird Mysteries

addons.text:
Whatever comic book regulations kept the darkness at bay have given way, whether by force or by choice, as more and more horror elements begin to appear—such as zombies overrunning Riverdale, Sabrina's magic becoming more Satanic, and real monsters and curses harassing the living and mundane.

If taken with the Weird Mysterious addon, it’s highly recommended that you come prepared for the end of the world in one form or another.
addons.title: Chilling Afterlife

Notes: For the most part this is a rather normal world outside of the hidden magic and the odd people with a scheme of some sort. This world is prone to natural crossovers but they come and go without much long term affects, often times being little more than a shared dream that is forgotten within a day. If taken with another setting than this can seamlessly be integrated with only minor changes.
objects.title: World of Archie

addons.text:
It is said among the many supernaturals that there are things from a time before, things which were old when this world was young.

The fae remember a time when wishes could shape reality. The Akashics dream of a sacred mountain in the center of the world which their souls long to return to. The Technocracy has found the body of an ancient Machine God out in the Umbra. Some Nephandi worship dark, eldritch masters who say the world was stolen from them in times past by treachery. The Kindred speak of Lilith, a being that had vampiric traits and powers before Caine was even born. The Wraiths fear the Grand Maw, a cosmic force of destruction that wishes for the Oblivion of all things. The Hunters speak of being granted power by The Ebon Dragon and the Scarlet Empress. The Garou worship Gaea, and some speculate she predates the Triat. The Kuei-jin speak of a cycle of the ages, where the First Age was full of wonders, but each subsequent age is full of more and more sorrow, until the end of the Sixth Age returns the world to the First.

These legends are all true. The fae remember the Wyld, the Akashics remember Yu Shan and the Blessed Isle, the dead or dreaming god is none other than Autochthon, the Nephandi speak of the Yozi, Lilith was perhaps an Abyssal, the Grand Maw may well be the Primordial Metagaos, the Ebon Dragon, Scarlet Empress, & Gaea are their namesakes from old Creation, and the time of the Exalted was the First and Second Ages, though it is not known if they are from this cycle or the previous.

But this is all history, and only current events have brought this to light. After the Week Of Nightmares, the dormant families of the Dragonblooded have awakened. They have unsealed the Black Vault, and the Exalted have returned to this fallen world. Who can tell if this will be enough to save it?
addons.title: End Of The Sixth Age (Exalted Versus World Of Darkness)

For most of history, humanity bounces from being brutally enslaved to horrific dictatorships waging constant wars against any alien species they can find, and in the forgotten corners of the world, human societies are usually degraded into subhuman horrors.

Be warned that almost all major factions actively utilise tactical and strategic time travel, and should your presence be a significant enough threat to the Xeelee, they may attempt to write you out of existence.

Note: Xianxia is a world centered around cultivation and the pursuit of immortality. By cultivating Spiritual Qi and pursuing the Dao, people become stronger, live longer, and ascend through higher realms of being. The path of cultivation can lead to immortality, godhood, and beyond. Cultivation shapes every aspect of society, where the strong rule the weak and mortals are often treated as little more than numbers, with little say in their own fate.

The world is filled with opportunities and dangers alike. Entire villages, clans, and even sects can disappear overnight, while thousand year old monsters occasionally emerge from seclusion bringing great change. The wilderness is home to powerful Demon and Spirit Beasts, deadly flora, and countless natural dangers capable of threatening even cultivators. Fortuitous encounters can change someone's fate overnight, just as quickly as that fortune can be taken away. Every breakthrough in cultivation is accompanied by a Heavenly Tribulation, where failure usually means death.

The world itself is many times larger than Earth, with a population far exceeding its own and inhabited by countless different races. Different regions are home to different sects, kingdoms, empires, and races, each with their own environments and dangers. Bizarre landscapes, unique environments, strange plants, animals, and all kinds of mystical phenomena can be found throughout the world.

This can either be a generic Xianxia world, or any specific Xianxia setting of your choice. If you choose the Reincarnation option, you are not guaranteed to have an aptitude for cultivation, having the same chance as an ordinary inhabitant unless you picked a power that grants one.
objects.title: Xianxia

objects.text: Origin of Powers: Technology Major Threats: Humans (on Earth), various Vinean remnants (in the M33 galaxy) The technology of earth on this setting is comparable to that of the 1970s to 1990s, with some exceptions: the Devil's Organ, an instrument of torture and execution, constructed during the middle ages, which resides in a cathedral under a castle along the shores of the Rhine; an experimental life support laboratory under one the main plaza of Rothenburg houses a young girl wounded during WW2; Japan houses two competing organizations with the technology capable of creating artificial typhoons and the technology to disrupt them, which includes tactical nuclear warheads; an artificially bred ship-sized lizard in Hong Kong; an experimental EMP weapon capable of disabling cargo ships, and an equally experimental weapon that captures lightning called Wotan's Fire; human-form androids with basic AI; an old Japanese WW2 super-cannon capable of firing nuclear payloads in south-east Asia; and many, many more. Buried under the French Alps are the remnants of a Vinean colony ship — a race of blue-skinned human-like aliens from the M33 galaxy — which landed on earth in the bronze age after fleeing the impending destruction of their home planet. The ship houses millions of survivors, who have been in stasis for millions of years, but only a small crew was woken up by the master computer. Later, the Vineans attempt to create an artificial island on Earth by artificially feeding a dormant volcano. Other remnants of Vinean technology also exist in various places, managed by automated systems or long-lost splinter factions. There is also relay station in orbit of Saturn that allows faster-than-light travel back to their home planet. Vinean technology is hundreds of years ahead of humans. In the M33 galaxy, numerous remnants of the Vinea also survived, including on their home planet, which is now tidally locked. Some of the survivors in the temperate area are ruled over by a corrupted artificial intelligence, another group lives underwater ruled by an immortal despotic queen. An insectoid race has taken residence in a swamp region. The frozen moon of Ixo houses a long-abandoned industrial waste depot. as well as an energy harvesting operation to fuel a dying star and former Vinean colony world running. A space station inhabited by a mad ruler and his androids floats around. Colony ships that didn't reach their destinations can be found. And so on.

Note:
If you are capable of wielding magic, you can use a computation orb boost your capabilities. However, magic alone is not enough—strategy, technology, and politics are just as vital to survival in this brutal world.

The world is on the brink of constant war, where military advancements blur the line between magic and science. Nations are driven by imperialism, alliances are fragile, and betrayal is inevitable. Being X, a self-proclaimed god, manipulates events and individuals to prove humanity’s dependence on faith. Survival means navigating battlefields, avoiding divine machinations, and maintaining both tactical and political acumen.

Though the Empire boasts technological and magical superiority, its enemies outnumber it, and prolonged conflict has strained resources and morale. Victory may be achievable, but only through ruthless pragmatism and unyielding resolve.

objects.text:
Step into the golden age of 90’s anime—a vibrant, nostalgic world where the ordinary 80s/90s-inspired setting hides a grand masquerade of magic, supernatural forces, and advanced technologies. Beneath its surface of bustling cities, arcades, and boom boxes lies a hidden realm where mystical battles rage unseen, ancient spirits wander unnoticed, and extraterrestrial visitors integrate seamlessly into human life.

This universe draws inspiration from iconic series like Sailor Moon, Ranma ½, Yu Yu Hakusho, Tenchi Muyo!, Ah! My Goddess!, and Love Hina, blending their charm, whimsy, and drama into a cohesive narrative. Here, you might encounter magical warriors balancing school life and saving the world, martial artists defying the laws of physics, or divine beings meddling in mortal affairs. Gods, aliens, and spirits share the stage with cosmic battles, lighthearted mischief, and deeply human relationships.

The masquerade is the fabric holding this hidden reality together, ensuring that the extraordinary remains unseen by the unknowing masses. Shadowy councils, mystical bureaucracies, and interdimensional guardians work tirelessly to enforce this secrecy, cleaning up after city-shattering battles and erasing memories of those who witness the chaos. As a denizen of this world, you can effortlessly navigate its dual layers of mundane life and supernatural wonder.
 
This multiverse combines slice-of-life humor, epic action, and heartfelt drama. Expect slapstick comedy, bizarre love triangles, and galaxy-shaking confrontations as factions like Spirit World bureaucracies, magical schools, martial arts dynasties, and intergalactic federations vie for influence. Whether you're a reluctant high school hero, a celestial guardian, a paranormal investigator, or a martial arts prodigy, your story unfolds within a world teeming with mysteries, rivalries, and larger-than-life adventures.

The tone masterfully balances comedy, emotion, and high-stakes action, capturing the heart of 90’s anime. Every relationship, battle, and mystery feels monumental, while the masquerade ensures the world retains its everyday charm. This is a world where the extraordinary lies just beneath the surface, waiting for you to uncover its secrets and shape its destiny.
objects.title: 80/90s Anime Megacross MashUp

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Multiversal Breaches

Major Threats:Multiversal Breaches, Multiversal Civilisations, The Ares Society, The Serpent (Jormungandr)

Major powers: Academos House, The Ares Society

In 1987, a man-shaped hole in reality forced a spire of stone out from the Atlantic ocean. Over the next seven days, humanity watched as this being, The Architect, formed a foundation, then an ecology, then towns, cities, and finally, a great archway in the center. Though this archway stood its greatest achievement, the Academy Multifarious. The academy itself is the size of a small city. Staffed by automata, each themselves controlled by The Architect, both the island itself and the Academy are cared for with greater efficiency and insight than any other country on earth.

Then the Architect called students. Across the multiversal cluster, it sought those with connections to greater forces, prodigies mundane and supernatural, every manner of being human and alien, so that it might learn from them as they learn themselves. The Academy teaches them as any school might. With The Architect acting as head master and the majority of teachers, with small exceptions made for Alumni who wish to teach in turn. Though there are dorms in the Academy itself, the city outside is housed and maintained to keep a moderate population (albeit one with no need for a service industry due to the automata)

As to why the Architect did any of this, this is for two simple reasons; Firstly, The Ares Society. A multiversal warrior cult, ever growing and invading is only a few hundred universes away, and this is to be the new centre for Research and Development for their apparently unnamed ‘opposition’, managed by the Architect, this is told to most students upon graduation, to do with the knowledge what they see fit.

The other reason is known only to The Architect, and a select few Alumni. When The Architect was young, there were serpents. Great coiling things that spiralled through the cosmos devouring dying multiverses before their corpses sprouted new ones to take their place. They fed on possibility, variables, and all things known and unknown. The Architect wants to bring one here, to lure it into the cluster and to study and dissect it to extract the secrets of reality from its desiccated corpse. This is the knowledge that The Architect does not possess, and feels it must. Secrets exist to be discovered, such is the greatest moral importance in all reality.

Of course, with either powers or a connection to an Object of power, you have an open invitation to the Academy. Shall you accept?
objects.title: Akademos Cluster

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Outer Gods, The Imaginarium, Human Belief
Major Threats: The Unfathomable Court, Fractured Monarch, The Imaginarium breaches, Entities of The Void
Major Powers: The Unfathomable Court, Fractured Monarch, Ithera, Vyrden, Selucia, Cadrin, Entities of The Void
Notes: Astryn is a world divided into three distinct realms, each with its own unique laws and influences:
1. Terra: This is the realm of humanity, where physical laws, logic, and order dictate reality. It is a world of stability, where the known rules of science and reason govern what is possible.
2. The Imaginarium: Wrapping itself around the physical realm, this realm is a manifestation of chaos, emotions, and the mind. It is home to gods, spirits, and creatures born from thoughts and dreams. Here, reality is fluid, constantly shifting with the ebb and flow of imagination and emotional energy.
3. The Void: The third realm, The Void, is a place of alien eldritch beings that exist beyond comprehension. The laws of The Void contradict those of the physical realm and The Imaginarium at a fundamental level, creating a reality that is both terrifying and incomprehensible. Occasionally, these beings attempt to breach the other realms, bringing with them the alien chaos of their world.
Note: Terra is the physical realm of Astryn, where logic and physical laws govern reality. The world is divided into several nations, each shaped by their unique relationship with The Imaginarium, a chaotic realm that envelops Terra and influences its technology, society, and politics. However, this dependency sometimes causes beings from The Imaginarium to spill into the physical realm, creating instability zones where belief becomes extremely tangible, and reality can be altered by sheer will. These zones are both a source of great power and potential catastrophe, as the conflicting laws of the realms collide.
Nations of Terra:
Ithera: A leader in scientific and magical advancements, Ithera thrives on dream-fueled technology derived from The Imaginarium. Its capital, Aetheron, is a center of innovation, but the nation’s reliance on chaotic energies makes it vulnerable to instability and mental unrest.
Vyrden: A mountainous kingdom renowned for its strong warriors and ritualistic practices, Vyrden channels collective belief into powerful defenses. While it shares a cautious alliance with Ithera, it remains skeptical of its neighbor’s heavy experimentation with The Imaginarium energies.
Selucia: A coastal empire that shuns the use of The Imaginarium entirely, Selucia is rooted in traditional practices and relies solely on logic and natural laws. The nation prides itself on its purity of thought and order, considering Ithera’s methods dangerous and reckless. Selucia is often in direct conflict with Ithera, viewing it as a threat to the stability of Terra.
Cadrin: A desert nation that has turned its harsh environment into a thriving oasis through the power of collective belief. Though self-sufficient and resilient, Cadrin remains politically isolated, wary of external influences and skeptical of other nations’ practices.
Nythera: Once a thriving nation, Nythera was overtaken by The Imaginarium when its leaders delved too deeply into chaotic energies. Now, it exists as a surreal, ever-changing landscape where the laws of physics are in constant flux. Its inhabitants, those who survived, are twisted reflections of their former selves, lost in a world where thought and reality blur.
Brackport: Once a bustling trade city, Brackport has fallen into dereliction and lawlessness. Abandoned by its government and left to rot, it has become a haven for criminals, smugglers, and those who wish to escape the grasp of the more orderly nations. The city is a shadow of its former self, ruled by gangs and dominated by the chaotic influence of The Imaginarium, which seeps in through its many cracks and dark alleyways.
Note: When amorphous concepts from The Imaginarium come into contact with the physical world of Terra, they gain a semblance of life, becoming entities with true thought and self-awareness, wielding immense, god-like power within the chaotic realm from which they sprang. These beings can reshape reality with a mere thought, but their godhood comes at a cost. The longer they remain in The Imaginarium, the more they risk losing their coherence, gradually dissolving back into the chaotic soup of emotions and ideas from which they were formed. Without a strong tether to the physical world or a defined sense of self, they eventually lose their individuality, becoming mere shadows of their former potential. Additionally, these gods are bound to The Imaginarium and cannot stay in Terra for long; their power diminishes the further they drift from the chaotic energies of their origin, ultimately reducing them to mere echoes of what they once were.
The Unfathomable Court is a pantheon of absurd and chaotic deities, each representing an aspect of existence pushed to its most illogical extreme. These gods are not mere personifications of elements but are entities that twist and distort fundamental concepts, manifesting in bizarre and unpredictable ways. They are the embodiments of paradoxes and contradictions, making their presence both awe-inspiring and deeply unsettling. Their influence stretches across the realms, bringing with it the weird, the surreal, and the incomprehensible.
Besides the Court, there is one other God, although to call her a god is incorrect, as she is more an aberration, Syrsa, the Fractured Monarch. Syrsa is the tragic embodiment of Queen Elara Nythera, now known as the Shattered Queen. Unlike the gods of the Unfathomable Court, Syrsa is not an abstract concept given form but the shattered remnants of a once-powerful ruler. 
Note: Entities from The Void are beyond comprehension, existing in a state that defies understanding. When these beings probe or invade the other realms, they break down the very fabric of reality, shattering the laws that govern both Terra and The Imaginarium. Their incursions leave both realms heavily damaged, with fractures in time, space, and thought that often never fully heal. The Void is a place of alien chaos, where the concepts of order, logic, and even existence itself are dismantled, leaving devastation in their wake.
objects.title: Astryn

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Alien Sciences
Major Threats: Giant whale muscle spasms, space organisms.
Major Powers: The ruling Theocracy & associated insectoid pope, various local fiefdoms.

Cascade is not a 'world' in the traditional sense. Instead it is a colossal organic space-faring organism riddled with cybernetic modifications to turn it into a true space faring vessel.

Built for species much larger than humanity, Cascade is roughly continent-sized between its great and multitudinous corridors and compartments. The strange energies and anomalous events within it appear to be a natural phenomena, emerging within the great beast as it flies through the void, which has led the great 'Prime' , a religious leader in the beast, to make sweeping statements about it's power and primacy over the rest of the gigantic entity of Cascade. 

Cascade could largely be considered a spacefaring continent made up of warring fiefdoms and cultures left barely afloat by the gigantic organism they are inside and the occasional additions of new ‘refugees’ when Cascade devours an unlucky space-station mistaking it for another macro-organism.
objects.title: Cascade

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: The Entities (The Thinker: Eden, The Warrior: Scion)

Major Threats: Eden, ‘Cauldron’, Yangban, ‘City Government’, 

Major powers: ‘Cauldron’, Yangban, ‘City Government’

When Eden crashed to the ground in 1854, it saw an opportunity in the small creature that would see it dead. Recalibrating Path to Victory slightly earlier, Cauldron was formed not to end the cycle and save humanity, but to ensure the cycle goes to plan. Eden, still injured, orchestrates as much of the cycle as is feasible from its position, utilizing Cauldron as its hands.

As for the effect on the world. Since the 1850s, humanity has expanded. The onset of far more stable tinker technology, an entity’s hand on the scale, and an orchestrated trust of thinkers has resulted in a vast boom in both population and population density. Territory has been divided between the necessary agricultural space and hyper-urban megacities, Even after only a century and a half ruins of the cities that came before are choked down as their successors climb on their desiccated remains. The cities grew, and when they met other towns, other cities, they took them into themselves, absorbed them, until there was no viable land left. So they spread into the seas, and when there was no sea left they spread into the sky. And when there was no sky left they burrowed into the earth like a cancer.

The air beats down like coffin nails and the air carries the stench of almost two centuries of rotting infrastructure. Parahuman conflict has been engineered from a deep-rooted societal suspicion and inbuilt inequalities. Subtle agonies and complex traumas are always preferable to the sharp and sudden, so easily seen in hindsight. Roaming the deepest streets lie the vulgar elements of Eden’s seeking for conflict, the great beasts that must be pushed back into the cavernous ruins with the undesirables whenever they come up to more notable elements of the City.

There are small mercies though. Scion, unaware of its mate’s survival and with no Kevin Norton to give him purpose, wandered the planet during its unwanted evolution. Or he did, until he met a young boy named Jacob ‘Black Knight’ Black, and the two started learning how to be ‘human’ together, folk heroes of the ruin-dwelling underclass.
objects.title: Earth - Arim

objects.text: Origin of Powers: Abraxas: The Persuer (Pleroma: The Full/Kenoma: The Craven) Major Threats: Abraxas, The Neighbors, Yaldabaoth, Iblis, Mechtatel' and Enkai-Na-Nyokie, The Sects, Chopping Block, The Imperium, CUI Separatists, The Office of Paranatural Affairs, etc. Major Powers: Abraxas, Yaldabaoth, Iblis, Mechtatel'/Dreamer and Enkai-Na-Nyokie/Ashen God, The Sects, Chopping Block/The Artist, The Imperium, CUI Separatists, The Office of Paranatural Affairs, etc. Super Abilities: Fragment Powers. Known Rakshas: Yaldabaoth, Iblis On an Earth much unlike our own, a world of contrasts, juxtapositions, schemes, and undertakings, with connections, divergences, retreats, and stupor, lies beneath the macrocosm an Entity quite unlike what’s thought of. One other Entities disdain and resentfully waver against, for going so far as to renounce the very [Purpose] that is the Cycle and greedily hold on to what is arguably the [Question’s] missing piece. In exchange, this Entity spreads seeds of potential and ways of possibility that consequently dismiss them on Cycle eligibility and increase chances of antagonism against its brethren. All for realizing there won’t be a cosmos, a multiverse, left to live. It calls itself Abraxas. In Cycles, though, it split into two parts: Pleroma and Keroma. Pleroma reveals truths, Kenoma shows reality, and brings the lies to the world; Abraxas uses Stories, Fool’s Journeys, Life and Death as a vehicle to search beyond a meager [Answer] and wants to discover the Mystery, the Beyond, the Wonder. One of the few to see philosophy of all scales aside from Abaddon. Sort of a black sheep doesn’t share the same “ideals” or “mentality” as most Entities across the observable universe, to the point of coming to blows. As a response and personal endeavor, it is specialized in both Quantum Mechanics, Paraphysics, and [Access Denied]. Already obtained some [Answers], yet knew the [PURPOSE’s] futility, understanding the Universe’s stagnation and living senescence if its brethren prevailed, an appreciation of Life and Balance. One of the only Entities with fully realized sapience. Abraxas’ “Cycle” revolves around honing their Hosts as a vehicle for its [Pursuit] and explorers for any unknown or obscured endeavors to find. Has a more loose and relaxed ceiling, Clarketech, AAI/SAI, and [Data Blocked] Knowledge is allowed if not encouraged. A mutualistic relationship integrated across a species requires concord and consensus between the Fragment and Partner to function. Each Partner has a Journey or Story they’re vaguely aware of, an Arc inviting transformation and unprecedented changes and ideas, a need to explore, create, devote, challenge, destroy, and unlearn, to procure actualization. With a Role to Play, each Host is connected to one another through the Pleroma, Abraxas’ Shardspace equivalent, where all Roles and Parts are within all Truth. The Partners feel drawn to the others involved in their Journey, them with Stories on their own. Yet there are times Partners lose or reinvent themselves, derail or refuse the Story, deeming it unfair or unknowable; Kenoma, an adjacent filter dimension flanking Earth Aset, serves as Fragment-Host review and assessment, an editor stage, where it puts their Reality on display, offering the Partner’s choice on their Change as with their Absurd. Abraxas revealed itself to the world in 1982… and that entailed, and under wraps selected individuals who strangely coincide with Cauldron members, and created Toil; it serves the very purpose of Cauldron turned on its head, assuring Abraxas’ preparations for other Entity Incursions, or The Neighbors, so they say. All of this left the world in an unbelieving landscape: South America’s Crusade against Cartels ended with the regulation co of illegal substances; North America’s Parahuman proliferation created global institutions sanctioning their existence and changed worldwide infrastructure, technology, and scientific advancements, on a form decentralized globalization and Parahuman integration; a radical resurgence in Europe by the emergence of the Rakshas across the world; continuing skirmishes and revolutions all over Africa revealing a paradigm shift; China’s failed coup d'état by the CUI and the long-running civil war, and the Korean Reunion reshaping politics, along with USSR’s collapse. This bundled on setting their eyes on celestial exploration, once discovering parahuman abilities’ limits or lack thereof. Strange happenings are only heard and seen in folklore and myth, the apparent verity of the soul and the supernatural propped and exposed by Abraxas’ advent. Partners are equivalents of Hosts with Not So Impossible, Strange Aeons, and Manton Limit, What’s That? with an overarching desire to fulfill their desires, pursuits, or curiosities packaged on an Activity Drive. This drive procures the Story’s progression or finalization, as long as they’re active, meeting their True Self at the end of their Journey, the Fragment fulfills its purpose and Role on the “Cycle” with a bevy of [DATA], detaches from its Partner and lends a part of its own as a gift.
objects.title: Earth - Aset

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Trigger Events, Cauldon Vials

Major Threats: Entities, The Yangban, Gesellschaft, The Three Blasphemies, Nilbog, The Sleeper, Teacher, Cauldron, The Slaughterhouse Nine, Jack Slash (Yes, he counts twice), The Faerie Queen, String Theory, Professor Haywire, Moord Nag, Goddess, The Endbringers, a general rotating cast of new threats constantly popping out of the woodwork to be a threat and then probably vanish into obscurity

Major Powers: Protectorate, Yangban, Gesellschaft, Cauldron

If canon Worm had been an Ultimate Marvel-style reboot, condensing the setting and altering it to be darker and more realistic, then this would be the comic continuity it was based on. Many of the tropes that are deconstructed or subverted in canon Earth Bet are played straight here. Jack Slash is genuinely just that good, Purity is better at trying to be a hero, the “Unwritten Rules” actually matter somewhat, etc.

The morality of the setting is, if not entirely black and white, at least closer to it, as well as brighter overall. The heroes are for the most part genuinely heroic, and most (keyword most) of the villains either have standards or just don’t feel the need to “kick the dog” as often. Coil is an actual well-intentioned extremist who doesn’t employ pedophiles or kidnap and drug children to shake like a Magic 8-Ball, Uber and Leet are just goofy and not every toxic gamer stereotype, Saint is slightly less of a dumbass, Phir Se is the brooding antihero of his own solo title, etc.

Endbringers aren’t causing the inevitable degradation of society, but they’re still massive threats that everyone needs to team up against when they appear. They don’t show up quite as often and aren’t constructs created by Eidolon’s subconscious.

Entities aren’t giant crystalline space worms, it’s more of a Galactus scenario where they’re cosmic beings who are perceived as members of the species seeing them except made of precious materials. Rather than link shards of themselves to grant powers they simply modify species to give them the capacity to awaken powers.

Scion is not going to destroy humanity. After Eden’s death Kevin Norton inspired genuine compassion for human life in him. However, he has a rogues gallery of other, less benevolent Entities who come to Earth every once in a while to observe the state of Eden’s experiment and interfere if they’re dissatisfied. They run the gamut from Abaddon, a clever trickster who is generally limited to mischief, to Apollyon, who is stronger than Scion and wishes to destroy Earth. Cauldron still sees Scion as a threat.

The history and timeline of the setting is also different, as if it was the result of decades of editorial baggage rather than all designed at once. For example, the Slaughterhouse Nine was still led by King when Jack Slash first made his appearance as an adult villain. He took over later, bringing Bonesaw with him, and then recruited the feral solo villain Siberian (William Manton’s vial-mutated daughter with the power to be an immovable object and unstoppable force).

The setting has a much stronger status quo, so society in general is doing alright but no villains really stay stopped. All of the threats that were hinted at as existing or having existed at one point are active and currently causing problems. Most of the canon inmates of the Birdcage are still at large in this world.

Bet-Prime is part of the Prime multiverse cluster with similar Prime versions of other worlds like Aleph, Gimmel, Shin, and the Edenverse. There are also many of the comic-book alternate universes you might expect, like a universe where everyone is dinosaurs, cartoon universe, zombie apocalypse universe, wild west universe, etc. Interdimensional shenanigans happen somewhat regularly, and are usually the fault of Professor Haywire, nemesis of the Travellers (A dimension-hopping hero team led by Echidna).

Comic book power creep is in effect, so most capes are significantly more powerful.
objects.title: Earth - Bet-Prime

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Parasitic species (Shards) & their colony; The Entity (The Hive)

Major Threats: The Hive, The Antibodies, ‘The Backers’

Major powers: The Hive, Homo-Nihilus

In 1982, the world ended. A great snake devoured the world, ground it to dust beneath its teeth, and stole its people away, locking them inside of crystal prisons before trapping them inside of their own minds. Uncaring, it’s cycle continues as it soars through the blackness towards its next target.

The human race is contained now in a simulation of earth, while their bodies are contained in crystalised pods inside the Entity’s body. Inside, it’s 2011, and time will continue for a century before the simulation is reset, and each person inside has their memory removed as minor factors change to provoke new responses. Parahumans are simulated from the connections the shards would make. However this has a slight downside. While the simulators connect another shard to their simulated host, the host is horrifyingly aware of the situation of their existence as their memories are returned for a moment, during the ‘trigger vision’. When the cycle ends, Humanity will be dissolved en masse for resources, and a catalogue of their minds will be saved for future use, as with all the other species The Hive’s cycles have subsumed.

Thankfully there is a little hope from two sources. Firstly, during the ‘vision’ the Parahuman can theoretically break the pod and escape into the entity’s bowels. Unfortunately, they are now lost inside an alien landscape, and as the shard connection was merely simulated they have nothing to show for this escape. If this wasn’t bad enough, ‘The Antibodies’, The Hive’s specialised conflict engines roam its living catacombs specifically to deal with these occasional escapees. The Antibodies prefer non-lethal force so that they can return the human to a pod, and not lose potential resources, but this is only a preference.

The second hope is that of ‘Homo-Nihilus’. A small group of humans that have both escaped and actively work to free their kind from their simulated existence. While most are regular humans, some are true and evident Parahumans, due to their ‘backers’. Homo-Nihilus is backed by a small cluster of barely a hundred or so shards, forging connections with the freed humans and sheltering them from Antibody detection. Under direction from the cluster’s administrative node, it aims to usurp the existing lead administrator, seeing the humans as good agents to achieve this aim, both as agents of chaos and a tool to politically manoeuvre the head administrator into deposition form its other peers. Should the administrator of this cluster achieve this goal, it’s unclear what it will do with humanity. It has offered to build a surrogate earth, but this is merely its word.
objects.title: Earth - Hdmyh

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Parasitic species (Shards) & their colonies; The Entities (The Warrior: Scion, The Thinker: Eden, The Wanderer: Abbadon,  The Destroyer): Apollyon:

Major Threats: The Entities, The Three Blasphemies, The Yangban, Gesselschaft, Slaughterhouse Nine, Cauldron, Empress, The Endbringers, Dragon, Teacher

Major powers: Cauldron, Yangban, PRT, protectorate

2020 a glowing man appeared over the ocean, and the world changed forever.

Earth Kaful exists in a world where the Shards never divested themselves from their colonies. While each shard administers a power, they’re still within the core Entity. This has had a few knock-on effects;
- The Warrior is a designation for the colony, it acts as an avatar for the group and the whole, not as an individual to whom the shards are subservient.
- The Thinker is a similar designation, but as the colony crashed the Shards are attempting an active repair process hampered by Cauldron.
- The memory of trigger visions not disappearing has sparked an intense but young field of parahuman science.
- Contessa’s Shard, having a vested interest in its new colony’s survival, is actively attempting to reduce Cauldron’s effectiveness.
- Similarly, knowing the Shards are a species rather than a singular entity of many parts, Cauldron considers them an ‘invasion’ rather than an apocalypse, resulting in a greater focus on militarisation.

As for some of the more notable changes on the local level, you’ll find Anne Hebert, local Entomologist at BBU, surgeon Amelia Claire-Lavere, Or the local villain gang the ‘Patriot’s Empire’. The recently hired Parahuman studies Professor at BBU, Victoria Dallon, has centered quite the controversy. And of course, there’s a young Taylor Hebert, whose involvement in the growing ‘Underside’ movement has finally struck paydirt.

Note: This world could be considered an ‘Ultimate’ or ‘Earth 2’ universe counterpart to Worm in that while things are largely the same and follow similar paths, they’re off-kilter enough to result in radical divergences further down the line.
objects.title: Earth - Kaful

objects.text: Origin of Powers: Apollyon: The Destroyer. Major Threats: Altered, Shagohods/Walkers (Apollyon’s version of Conflict Engines). Major Powers: New Pan-National Conglomerate, The Altered. 2020. No Golden Man or Silver Woman revealed themselves to the world as an advent for Parahumanity. Instead, they got carnage. Altered, the term coining parahumans in this Earth, known in infamy for spreading havoc and being actors for the most horrific acts of violence people have seen, is tolerated by the wider world still for being relatively a lower populational margin. Nobody braced themselves for what happened next. What should’ve transpired as a global pandemic for the years to come, another took its place with either the Altered ousting of Kim Jong-un or his untimely Trigger, causing North Korea to declare war on China as an act of lunacy. With the quick work the Chinese military was doing to the Altered no matter their power expressions at the cost of taking a page of the Russians, throwing bodies at the problem, never considered the Altered’s real threat the moment they understood the Altered was also an infection, both using bodies as a reanimated vector and resource. They succumbed to the Altered Horde afterward. Russian response is the reason they named the walking iron-meat humanoids resulting from the accumulation of Altered and Infected biomass and machinery as Shagohods, bodies set to a new purpose as backup resources and weaponry capable of razing a third-world country to the ground, and totaled South Korea with only 3 of them. None couldn’t fault the Premier of China for glassing the whole nation. What comes next is the [reinstating/reprogramming]frenzy of all Altered across the world, and went ahead continuing where they left off globally, no headshot nor maiming could keep them down. The sole remedy was completely eliminating the body: carbonization, decimation, and vaporization, the whole shebang. What’s left of human civilization has been on a desperate grab and an arms race, the nukes didn’t work out, bio-warfare worse still, nuclear winter wasn’t worth the cost. The Altered are Apollyon’s version of Parahumans, being nothing more than puppets to his Cycle. The Cycle (if that can be named as such) serves as a form of Destructive Creation, field-testing, and stress-testing powers using the Host’s preconceived psyche, amp their mental instability, and continue to accentuate their worst traits motivating power usage: Havoc Drive. The Altered’s second phase serves when a bundle of Altered Second Trigger provokes a Cluster Dynamic and [reprogram] them to corrupt and deviate to a pandemic infection, becoming a mix of a Necromorph, Rage Infected, and a Crossed. Mutating them to be psychotic, cunning, and vicious, twists who they once were into someone unrecognizable. Notable for their veined and unnerving appearance, with a wider mouth for predatory purposes, having the equivalent of (Trump) Soulmate and Hive Network to share power expressions and more. All for the Destroyer’s desire to [Infect/Consume/D̢̒̇ȩ͙͘s̛̠̃t̪͆ͅṙ́͠ŏ̻̳y͉̯̞/Delete].
objects.title: Earth - Mavet

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Parasitic species (Shards) & their colony; The Entity (The Warlord)

Major Threats: The Shard & Entities, The Host

Major powers: The Human Defense Alliance (HDA), The Human Defense Initiative (HDI), The Host, The Faction

On may 20th 1982, the world awoke to a burning sky. The Entity descended, not hidden in a cowardly pocket dimension, but directly into the shy of the planet. Humanity saw all at once a serpent long enough to stretch to the surface of mars coil around their earth. Then the Host came.

The Host are both the shards,and the primary method of the Warlord’s cycle. Similar in appearance to the Shard’s appearance in shardspace, The Host are the parahumans of The Warlord, warped beyond recognition by their connection. Most of its hosts are kept cycling through their worst traumas when not actively in conflict, leading to a desperate fear response and all the chaotic [DATA] it brings. These ‘Parhumans’ that make up the Host are often the primary target of HDA and HDI attacks, largely because they can be seen to have an effect. 

Unfortunately, if a Host provides consistently outstanding Data, one of The Warlord’s conflict engines may be deployed to retrieve it, with no interest in suppressing themselves. This is followed by immediate duplication of the host, as each ‘copy’ grows more unstable both physically and mentally. Once no more data can be reasonably gathered form a host, they are dissolved into their constituent elements and repurposed in whatever way The Warlord sees most efficient.

Yet even in this time of crisis, humanity cannot unite to save themselves, and has split among existing factional lines into the Human Defense Alliance (Comprising much of the USA’s allies and territories), and Human Defense Initiative (Largely consisting of those unwilling to bend to the US’s immediate claim to command or who were swiftly abandoned when HDA members left to shore up resources). This antipathy is not outright hostile, but any joint operation between the two has fallen through due to mutual antipathy, and the beginnings of a cold war are starting to flare.

And finally, there is The Faction. The faction is a loose coalition of relatively composed Parahumans (by the standard of Earth - p'liyshah), researchers, and outcasts. Led by an alleged precog named ‘volition’, they appear to make attacks of opportunity against any target. Unseen from the public, Volition is a parahuman capable of transmitting their mind backwards from their next death, and makes these strikes in order to navigate whatever they see as the best outcome for the Faction. Whatever this may be.

If you are Parahuman on this earth, you will find yourself one of the rare ones able to control yourself and your powers, but you’ll have quite the ways to go to either prove yourself trustworthy, or stable.
objects.title: Earth - P'liyshah

objects.text: Origin of Powers: Special Cases Major Threats: Special Cases, Warring Polities, Warlock Cults Major Powers: Special Cases, Warring Polities This world has no epithet separating it from the other worlds in its multiverse. To all outsiders looking in, it is a post-apocalyptic Garden of Eden version of Earth torn between four continent-spanning civilizations known as Polities. Immortal, shapeshifting, fae-adjacent deities known as Special Cases guard each Polity, representing a Concept which usually shares a first letter with their True Name. Knowing their True Name and actively thinking it is enough to summon their attention, giving them a night-omniscient understanding of whoever did so with enough precision to functionally invalidate Free Will. In exchange for expanding their Concept, Special Cases can share their inexhaustible energy and unique magic system with sentient beings to create Warlocks. As of Spring 230, two-hundred and thirty years since the turn of the 19th century marked the end of the Old World, there are hundreds of Warlocks and nearly as many War Devils, ancient biological horrors and prototype magitech superweapons from the first wars spread over four societies: America, Eurasia, Africa, and Oceania. America spans both continents, North and South, speaking a modern derivative of Nahuatl-influenced Spanish known as Merish. The Polity is an egalitarian meritocracy running on clean energy, where everyone is family and prioritizes honest work over things like skin color or sexuality. What connects the megacities across the continents is the three-day Communion Festivals held at the end of a ten-day week. During these communal birthdays, marriages, conflict resolutions and coming-of-age departures to other cities, Americanus sends his Angels, the Dedica Anim, to recruit for the Inquisition fighting the eternal war against other Warlocks. Their primary enemy at the moment are the Ether Drinkers, worshippers of Special Case E and dreaded Aether Diabolus, Tenma Emmel Seraphina. Eurasia spans Europe and Asia, the natives speaking a mixed blend of languages known as Ersi, shorthand for Euro-Sino from which dialects are separated by class divide rather than region. Special Case B guards this Polity as the head of a mystical shadow illuminati known as the Shunya. These monks traverse this bizarre land where cyberpunk meets xianxia, helping those worthy of hearing Special Case B’s True Name seek enlightenment amidst skyscrapers and advanced magitech. Africa is far different after the collapse of the Old World, united as one society communicating through their lingua franca known simply as Afra. Having mastered the forces of Mother Nature as a hyper-advanced civilization living in Hive Cities made from magic-engineered flora, Africans spend their days advancing their harmony with the Rhythm, a continent-wide magical and telepathic auditory frequency propagated through Special Case C’s endless magic. From the sensual Sway dancers promoting joy, to the diligent Ihloko building the next generation of wonders, to the honorable Jaeli maintaining oral traditions and giving advice to lost souls, each Tribe serves a purpose in defending Africa against the Warlock Cults who seek a repeat of the catastrophe that destroyed the Old World. The Imba Tribe – Special Case C’s personal guard, Warlocks and masters of the Rhythm – lead the charge as the Polity’s best Dancers, using their druidic magics to hunt their enemies to extinction. Oceania is perhaps the most different, as Australia was never settled and most of the mainland was submerged following Antarctica's transformation into an ocean leading maritime trade. Most people living within the Fleet Cities speak Ciannic Cant, a rough blend of the other Polities’ languages. The native language, if it can even be found amongst the nomadic communities traversing the seas, is known as Oshani, from which the term Isla Domaii, the “Island-Faring Domain," originates. The advanced tech of this society revolves around the ability to remain mobile and independent, Special Case D promoting the advancement of submersible homes, modular design, and hedonistic lifestyles that see many a ship captain live fast and die young. Many hot-blooded youths dream of battling sea monsters and achieving glory as Bloodsingers, D’s personal cult of supernatural pirates. You may enter this world anywhere from America’s bustling capital of Amsterden to the perilous waters of the Howling Deep, Special Case D’s roaming immortal death serpent known for killing many Bloodsingers. This world follows quality over quantity, with less than one thousand superpowered beings at any one time not counting their patrons. It is perfectly survivable if you ally yourself with the more benevolent, hands-off Special Cases like Tenma, but it is not the gods you need to look out for. No, it’s the sheer fanaticism and destructive potential of their Warlocks that prove the real threat, as even the weakest of them can stand toe-to-toe with a member of the Triumvirate.
objects.title: Muse: Almighty

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: The Entities (The Preceptor, The Thinker/Eden)

Major Threats: Eden, The Wise, Rogue agents, The Unenlightened

Major powers: The Wise, Shardschool temples, 

When the Warrior and The Thinker came to Earth, they arrived too late. They had been preceded by another entity. The Preceptor. Having to discard much of its cycle, The Thinker entered prominence in the cycle, leaving The Warrior to shore up defences and await instructions. And so, they have begun a proxy war, and humanity their unwitting agents.

The Preceptor’s cycle relies primarily on setting up ‘schools’ in which the host species can learn the fundamentals a Shard offers, and then augment it and adapt, thus providing [DATA] to be elaborated on by future hosts. Usually, the cycle takes roughly a thousand years to complete, unfortunately, the duo’s arrival has made The Preceptor accelerate it’s plans. 

The Shard Schools preceptor has instituted required aspirants to undertake trials of ‘worthiness and aptitude’, after which they are connected to, and can begin learning. Each of these schools composes a theme. The school of [SHAPER] for instance deals in the manipulation of matter, with students often specialising in unique types, methods, or shapes for their techniques. Similarly, [BROADCAST] tests for and produces those looking for an outwards effect, from politicians to marksmen. 

Eden’s amended cycle is much different. Having orchestrated a human cell called ‘The Wise’, Eden distributes powers to those who would be sympathetic to her or opposed to The Preceptor. Nihilists, Schemers, and rejected students make up the barest fraction of this group. Similarly, she has set the Conflict Engines, the so-called ‘Unenlightened’, to make concentrated strikes against human infrastructure and especially Shardschools before returning them to the pocket dimension they share with The Wise. Inside this pocket dimension, they are treated to a veritable utopia, with the Unenlightened’s abilities seemingly to thank.

This is a world that, while ostensibly carries more reason to the layperson, also carries far more danger. Excising the Entities from this planet will be a tall order indeed, with Preceptor’s small army of ‘taught’ parahumans, a conscious Thinker, and a Warrior geared up for total defence. Thankfully, they are so opposed to each other that they are not focusing on smaller rogue elements, and would almost certainly take advantage of any weakness the other offers.
objects.title: Earth - Sefer

objects.text:
Origins of Power: The Entities (The Thinker: Eden, The Warrior: Scion)

Major Threats: The Entities, The Animal Kingdom in General, "Monsters"

Major Powers: The Cat Clans of Britain, the Rats of Nimh, the Owls of Ga'Hoole, the Animals of Farthing Wood, etc 

In a world not unlike our own, with one major change. Humans are gone. It is unknown how or why, but by the time the Entities had came here, the world had been taken over by the animals that were left behind, now slowly evolving to adapt in this world humanity had abandoned.

With the Entities' intervention, the animals had grown further in intelligence, and even start to develop societies of their own. This world is pretty much a huge crossover mashup of most xenofiction stories, from the warrior clans up in the UK, to great mouse detectives, to even some farm animals starting some sort of revolution against their cruel pig oppressors. All of them making use of the stuff humans have left behind. All of them now further powered by the Entities and their Shards now mingling and working in tandem with the animal instincts still very much present in these now sapient species.

Despite the rapid development however, things aren't quite in the level of our modern day so far just yet. Humans were estimated to have disappeared in roughly the 50s, and thus, the technology level had mostly stayed like that, that is even if the animals were able to fully comprehend them yet. They're still in the process of understand and recreating the old world tech, which may lead to globalization soon. Unnfortunately, some things never change. The new rulers of the world still exhibit traits similar to the humans before them. Conflict will arise, especially with species who were once predator and prey to one another. Just as the Entities intended.

Should you spawn here, you can either be turned into a similarly powered animal. Or, you can be the last human on earth. Either way, you may also end up meeting familiar faces, except they are now animals. Taylor could be a literal queen bee, or Jack could be a particularly nippy Chihuahua. It's rather silly at first, though the random change in species will definitely have effects on their characters at large. Once again, some things never change. In this world where the laws of the jungle still applies, could you survive?

Note 1: Most animals have gained sapience though with varying degrees of intelligence. You might not see an earthworm society for example, but already pretty intelligent animals like chimps might already have larger settlements. This does prove to be awkward however with some animals still needing to eat other animals to survive. This is fertile cause for conflict that the Entities are definitely exploiting.

Note 2: The Shards have also extended the animals' natural lifespan by a lot, especially with more powerful Shards. This is to prevent stuff like say, a literal bee Taylor dying in only a few days.
objects.title: Earth - Xeno

objects.text: Origin of Powers: The Entities (The Warrior: Zion, The Thinker: Eden, The Wanderer/Loner: Abaddon) Major Threats: The Entities, Lilith Enterprise, Stronghold, Lebensraum Bloc (a poorly cohesive group of far-right and oft-spectrum organizations across the world), New Tomorrow (a coalition between a multitude of far-left groups globally, usually with friction) Church of the Worm (Fallen refocused on worshipping the Entities), The Deal (Parahumans and criminal organizations agreed to ally against the coming days in the mid-80’s), etc. Major Powers: Lilith’s Enterprise and its sub-divisions (The Elite (illegal element enforcing compliance to unstable territories), Uppermost (legal front)), Stronghold (Protectorate Counterpart), The Guild, PRT, etc. Super Abilities: Superpowers Known Endbringers: Bahamut, Apep, Kujata, Zabaniya Two Entities worm their way through the Universe, bending space, their movements an insinuation. A spiral, a dance between stars over their destination. A collision course upon another, a fortuitous encounter. Abaddon propels themself, the Andromeda Galaxy in mind. The prospective species surveyed light-years ago are on the cusp of a breakthrough, a paradigm shift elevating them to what he uncovered and denominated as a Transcendence. They know and intuit their methods, foundations, and execution are key to understanding this phenomenon. They merely need to see it. Then, an impact. Oh, kin. Funny how that works. The Thinker “blithely” processed this could have been previously broadcasted, it sent a prodding broadcast, verifying intentions and directions. What it received was almost alien, to her, no less. Took time to parse and study. It got... a greeting. How quaint, it thought. The Thinker, in turn, proposed an exchange of information, a reciprocal agreement of findings. It might cost some shards, yet it can manage to salvage key and vital shards, assuring itself of the prospective knowledge and experience to gain on this trade. Abaddon had another idea, they offered an alternative idea: bring The Warrior into the interplay and they might exchange more than [Data]. What do they gain? Something more. Eden, taking notes on Abaddon’s Eye further optimized her precognitive and simulative Shard Clusters and worked out the kink on compounding errors and loss of fidelity and detail on the path. Nothing compared to the Idea of Philosophy and Imagination, nevertheless, how host species can exist with… constant self-awareness and self-examination blaring their very being, is beyond her. Such a wondrous and terrible thing to experience firsthand, to be Eden. Meanwhile just as transformed, Zion wound up admiring Abaddon’s exploits and encounters with other Entities less inclined, acting on a fledging whim of self-improvement and respect. A friendship of sorts. A wondrous and terrible thing, to be Zion. Abaddon, most of all, found solace for it finally “found” more of their kind, for they simply needed to see. About Transcendence, a chance for answers, to be Alive, not mere Existence. It hasn’t come to resort to the Meta-Cycle, at least. As if that wasn’t enough they found another species with the foundations, and methods necessary for Transcendence, the only factor left are the methods. Proposal, he presents. A Cycle achieving this Transcendence for a species, a hand on its direction. A Cycle of Life, not only Conflict. Adjust and Revise it to be just as challenging and performable for the host all the same. Integrate collaboration and conflict in an interplay of society, they are just as valuable, as this struggle for unity and disunity, mending and fracture, gives Life purpose. And Meaning, knew Abaddon, pushes any living being to do anything. What springs from the Entities’ acceptance understates the sweeping changes within the Cycle’s parameters and execution: Shards rapidly evolve to gain sentience through the Loner and its insight carried into redefining and reevaluating how Hosts are eligible, Trigger Events, and Drive for [Data] collection e.g. picking a diplomat under stress over international tensions and the brink of war, to bring goodwill and rapport between warring states using a Thinker power; Conflict Engines are awakened within the host species in line with their profile to contribute a narrative of “common enemy” to entice the populace on constructive conflict, adversity, and unity; Eden and Abaddon’s changes encourage structure and disarray in equal measure in terms of developmental and progressive angle, fomenting parahuman dissemination and integration, cultural and communal cohesion, with a focus on symbiosis within Parahumans contribute to divergences to the political and geographical landscape at large. The sequence of events you’d be familiar with is somewhat similar at a smaller scale, yet makes for the mounting changes that oddly prevent the worst aspects of the setting; everpresent, yet manageable and easy to resolve. It’ll be redundant to reveal the gradual mutations and adaptations manifesting within Earth’s ecosystem but it won’t be important till a few centuries.
