objects.text: Origin of Powers: Digestion of the Devourer's Flesh Major Threats: Sudden Shifting Biomes, Cannibalistic Beasts, and Other ambitious Ascendants Major Powers: The San Kuwari Union, The Disseereia Federation, The Holy Quai-Rrhiv Empire, and the Katerberg Duchy Congratulations, you have alerted Addie. A creature of incalculable size and equally insatiable appetite, this "Addie" is the name given to a member of a species of multiverse parasites. Its origins unknown, it is capable of latching on to entire universes and sucking out their nutrients. Doing so keeps it from dying of entropy, with the stuff sucked in being portaled in for digestion. Once inside, you cannot escape, this creature being a black hole of sorts on a multiversal scale, capable of keeping entire worlds, let alone universe hoppers, inside. This does not mean it is actively malicious, however, as a lot of folks found themselves accepting their perpetual stay here. You are one of these isekaid victims, an Ascendant. "Us Ascendants are the crushed remains of our dead homeworlds." Said one Ascendant. What that means is you are the culmination of the data of your home universe, with everything and everybody now existing within you in a personal world where you are a God. The choice of who becomes the Eaten Universe's Ascendant is random. Addie had graciously reforged your body, and now you must fuel it. How? Well, you simply survive. While you exist, your Addie-given body "digests" the data within you, using up the resources of your inner world to keep you alive. You must refuel yourself through struggling with other Ascendants, for when you devour another Ascendant's flesh, you gain their resources. You assimilate their world into your own, your inner world grows stronger, and with it, your powers. This conflict refines the data in you until it returns to Addie, and the cycle begins anew. You will awaken within the planet Hearth, a hollow planet with gravity magically tied to its walls, allowing people to walk around it. The core serves as the "sun", with it dimming at night. The planet's biomes also tend to suddenly shift, making its inhabitants adapt to its chaotic environment. There are other planets with people too, but until you pierce through the planet's walls, there isn't any known successful contact with those outside. There are 4 main superpowers in Hearth, each with massive influence on the planet at large. Each has powerful Ascendants vying for Planetary Godhood, where they have fueled themselves enough that their abilities extend across the globe. They are: - San Kuwari, the largest kingdom and a trade hub, claims to be accepting, though it has a habit of colonizing neighboring kingdoms. - Disseereia, a cutthroat capitalistic cyberpunk hellscape and currently the only democratic superpower. - Quai-Rrhiv, a theocratic martial state known for its demonic mercenaries and prison slave labor industry. - And Katerberg, a separatist nation from San-Kuwari, favoring isolationism on a moving warship. All in all, should you choose to reincarnate here, you are donating your world to be another of Addie's many meals. Your resources may exist forevermore within it; whatever you do with that is up to you. Note: Should you pick other worlds, they will also be considered assimilated into Addie. So crossover is possible, just not multiversal travel. Assimilated worlds shall have elements of them appearing in Addie, like flora and fauna, to even what's left of man-made structures. Note 2: You can bring people within your inner world outside, but at the cost of some of your power, as you are giving them a chunk of your world. Note 3: While Addie would normally try not to feed on universes with folks stronger than it, if a particularly strong person finds themselves in Addie, their power shall be nerfed or sometimes stripped.
objects.title: The Hearth of Adversity

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Black Code
Major Threats: Black Code ‘Demons’, Alien species, Breaking down technologies
Major Powers: The Menagerie, The Trau (Formerly)

In the 1680s the Trau, a spacefaring empire so advanced they had begun altering the laws of physics around them to facilitate their empire, came to earth. Over the course of a month a total of two hundred and fifty two humans were stolen from what would be the modern day Britain, Ethiopia, and India seeking an ‘assured genetic diversity’. 

These peoples were then trafficked to the ‘Menagerie’, The Trau’s bespoke mixture of anthropological mass research station and zoo. As generally monstrous as it was, it remained at least consistent. That was until back on the Trau homeworld they attempted to alter aspects of the Black Code related to their own species. In an instant every member of it disappeared in an instant not just on the world but across their empire. 

To all the species aboard the Menagerie however, it meant something all together different. To the humans whose grandparents had fought in ‘glorious revolutions’ and revolts, and had ever had an annoying tendency to enter the vents and circuit breakers; to the Kazekh whose energy-based forms could easily move through degrading facilities, to the Tralepidi to whom their queen remained quite literally immovable, It was a new dawn.

[-]

Today the Menagerie has some… peculiarities. Much of the technology still works, but is in the process of breaking down, maintained by the precarious mix of a priest class that doesn’t understand how they work and a slowly dying tiny Kazekh cohort trying to manage an oncoming crisis. 

The recreational cloning machine never turned off, producing humans (or rather one specific human) in batches. They’ve developed a culture of their own and remain rather violent whenever a Kazekh suggests deactivating their producer. In some places in the Menagerie 90% of the occupancy can be the same woman. 


The “Priesthood” of the Menagerie could better be described as 30 micro-religions in a trenchcoat sharing rituals of how to affect the Black-code none of them truly understand. Some temples are martial, some are technical, and none can even begin to understand the others.

It’s a multi-species station supplying a small empire made from the deprecated stations around the station and the planet they were built around. While they expand they continue to grow, having assembled themselves into a senate almost entirely through accident and passed down myth of the ‘Glorious Revolution’

And through it all, Earth moves on regardless none the wiser. It has just turned 1975.
objects.title: The Menagerie of Trau

Major Powers: 
- Fewiq: Too many smaller nations to count both above the Ic’awn islands floating in the sky, and beneath them still in the oceans.
- Studio: The Studio University of the Unnatural Arts, The Society for Recreational Criminal Acts (SRARC)
- Vardea: The Kankeri empire, Vrynite Conclave

- Rhondure: Khelmegi tribal alliance, The Holy Zevlade Dominion, The Phoenix Empire of Kagana, The Tiger Empire of Kagana, The Rabbit Empire of Kagana
- Oberlisk: Dormins Machinis, Htarex Academy
- Farcek: The One True Psychic Domain of Drascio, The One True Psychic Domain of Rhessus, The One True Psychic Domain of Beelchaj, The Worker’s Collectiver of Pjorne (ECP)
- Tserin: The Chili Under-Trade Empire

Notes:
The world of Vaniterra is a mobius strip world circling a mystical ‘conflux’ at its center, acting as a sun of sorts. The edge is marked by a mystical fog that dissolves organic matter on contact, leaving the populous to move between the continents sequentially unless they take the nest of tunnels in between both sides of the strip, currently occupied largely by Tserin scouts along major trade routes. 

It notably features duplicates of its population across its face on each continent. Brilliant Kankeri inventor Victor Hyde on Vardea is fundamentally the same person as Studo’s Symbiont Master professor of the same name. The environment has shaped them separately, but they are all reflected from the same light through the prism of the Confluence, Vanitera’s sun.

These continents are: 

- Fewiq: A continent archipelago of hundreds of small nations broken up by a large sea, with half of them launched and sustained in the sky. Patrolled by great forces of creation named Boundaries given to extreme destruction and creation at their whim. 
- Studio: A Necromantic academiarchy where all the people of the land are dead, and have nothing better to do than learn and entertain themselves in equal measure, largely focusing on their existing necromancy and Symbiotics.
- Vardea: a continent nearly conquered by the Crab-like Kankeri before their head god was killed on contact with the outer-being Mal Vryn. Now the empire has collapsed and the successor states are warring while the imperial core eats itself alive.
- Sanguinis: A violent megalopolis with a culture around Coming of Age Through Violence. Unless you have undergone trauma physical or mental, you are a child to the Sanguine. Similarly, Powers and non-replicable magic is deserving of pity, for the gods decided you needed a handicap to be on equal footing with your peers.
- Rhondure: a segment where the mobius strip connects suspended over a sea of starlight, containing three great orbs menaced by true dragons and cosmic monsters braving the Aurora sea.
- Obelisk: ruptured by constant time-breaks sending its peoples and cultures across it’s history, this has left it’s contemporary location with two main factions, the Htarex, who warp their bodies like clay, and the Torpids (Dormins Machinis) with mastery over the technological sciences.
- Farcek: Four nations locked in an endless psychic war over a conduit allowing one to enter the Conflux and speak with the Heirs of the Creator.
- Tserin: the world-spanning trade network-turned religious empire centred around the worship of the great Eel ‘Alpha Iota’.

Note: if you manage to make enough of a mess of the world, the Pantheon of Cosmic Doubt may take notice. If you’re lucky they may remove you, if not they may ask you to join them.

Note: When Nechane: Architect of What Is Not, that which lies between Art and Artifice, the space between the stars and the void between thought. Cogito Ergo Non Sum; He that Thinks, Therefore It Is Not, created Vaniterra, it was intended to adapt and warp to outside influences, but also to attract and entrap the influences that would impact on it so Nechane could study them later. Good luck.
objects.title: Vaniterra

objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Star-Seeds & Ancient archeotech
Major Threats: Derelict star programs, Voidhall caste structure
Major Powers: the Great Houses & associated dynasties

Millions of years ago, a great empire of two peoples spread out into the stars. When the universe was hot and things were young, they created great void cities in the depths of nothingness as things expanded. When they died, fading from the universe's eye, their structures and ruins were left unattended, the only evidence they had ever been.

Then, a small cluster of people, many of whom were aboard their ship for a 'deep sleep' colonisation, crashed into the underside of the city. Unable to repair their craft, they were forced to begin living in the Voidhall, among its dead machines and articles, and couldn't leave when they began to reawaken.

Today, the Voidhall has become a strict caste system fueled by the legacy of the star people, the Astrum and Stella Populi. Their 'star seeds' have infected few of the city's members, but the strength, prestige and recognition of the remaining digital infrastructure has given those 'Star decencents' primacy and privilege not afforded to the 'hosts' they once lived among.

Voidhall is the platonic ideal of a feudal hell. Dilemmas of distribution and supply are replaced with a need for technological maintenance, and the arbitrary control of violent means is made a very real power inequality due to the diminishing ‘humanity’ of the Stella and Astrum Populi. 

Note: It is worth noting that the population of Voidhall includes no humans, the colonists were a kind of radially symmetrical terrestrial isopod more akin to  profoundly aberrant four foot tall pillbugs than the human baseline.
objects.title: Voidhall

objects.text:
Origin of power: Cosmic radiation, magic, advanced technology

Major threat: The cripple god sunken beneath the sea, the beast of calamity

Major powers: Metahuman warlords

At the dawn of 2050, a prismatic comet tore across the night sky, blazing with every color of the rainbow. Its path was wild and unpredictable—a celestial anomaly with a mind of its own. It circled the Earth seven times in seven days, a glowing omen above a world blissfully unaware of the cataclysm to come.

Then, it shattered.

Fragments rained down across the globe, the largest crashing into the heart of the Pacific Ocean—an impact that would irreversibly alter the fate of the world.

But this was no ordinary comet, it was a dying god.

As it descended, the comet bathed the Earth in waves of cosmic radiation, releasing a mystical essence that warped reality itself. The transformation it brought was both wondrous and horrifying.

Around the world, those exposed to the exotic energy—human and animal alike—began to mutate, developing extraordinary, often terrifying powers. Forgotten rituals and ancient superstitions surged back into relevance, revealed not only as real but as potent beyond imagination.

The rise of superhuman abilities shattered the world’s fragile order. Governments lost their monopoly on violence. Law and structure crumbled. Chaos spread like wildfire. Civilization collapsed, replaced by a brutal new world where power reigned supreme. Mighty metahumans seized territory, carving out miniature kingdoms and warring endlessly for dominance. Ordinary people—powerless and unprotected—became an oppressed underclass, often reduced to collateral damage in metahuman conflicts.

Only those who were fortunate and brilliant enough to learn magic or master super-science had any hope of rising above their station. But such knowledge was rare and jealously guarded by powerful mage clans and technocrats, who ruled with cold efficiency, hoarding secrets to maintain dominion over the masses.

To make matters worse, mutated wildlife, especially those near the comet or its fragments, transformed into monstrous creatures. International shipping and trade came to a halt, plunging the global economy into a deep recession from which it has yet to recover, even decades later.

And then came the Beasts of Calamity.

Titanic kaiju, these monstrous entities fed on the divine remnants of the wounded god, growing larger, stronger, and more apocalyptic with every fragment consumed. They were less living beings than elemental forces, walking disasters driven by insatiable hunger.  

Whenever they ventured into human lands in search of more godly essence, only the strongest mages or metahumans could hope to stand against them. If none rose to the challenge, destruction was inevitable. When two Beasts of Calamity clashed, it was expected that the local geological and ecological system would be entirely reshaped by the time their battle ended.

Meanwhile, deep beneath the ocean’s surface, the fallen god struggles against numerous beasts of calamity who ravenously wish to devour it whole. When it bones are picked clean by the beast, they would eventually turn their claw and fang toward each other and eventually the rest of the world. Multiple special interest groups have attempted to build a blockade around the comet crash site to contain them as well as try to harvest any fragment of divinity for their own use with varying degrees of success so far.

Welcome to the Age of Warlords. May you have the strength to conquer or the wisdom to kneel, Because in this world, only power determines who will thrive and who will be crushed into stepping stones for others.

Note: Due to prolonged exposure to exotic energy, people in this world are significantly tougher than ordinary humans. Even non-powered individuals, with enough training, can shatter real-world records threefold.

Roughly 1 in 20 people develop powers. Of those:

99.99% possess powers equivalent to 5–10 SP.

The top 0.009% are considered high-tier, with 15–20 SP.

The elite 0.00099% possess 15–25 SP.

The near-mythical 0.00001% wield 25–35 SP.

With the global population being only 3 billion, there are an estimated 150 million metahumans. Wildlife, besides their mutated biology, also possess power, though thankfully at lower rates than humans. At least 300 Beasts of Calamity are known to roam the wilderness, with more likely yet undiscovered.

If you choose to reincarnate here, these are your odds—your chances of gaining power and how strong that power might be.
objects.title: Warlord: The Domination
The Empyrean Galaxy
objects.text:
Origin of Powers: Psionic Evolution, Internal Psionic Energy, Ambient Galactic Psionic Fields

Major Threats: Rival Great Powers, Psionic Masters, Ancient Weapons, Expansionist States, Proxy Wars, Uncharted Regions

Major Powers: The Great Civilizations of the Empyrean Galaxy and numerous independent interstellar powers

Super Abilities: Psionics

The Empyrean Galaxy is an ancient and heavily populated galaxy divided between numerous advanced interstellar civilizations. Curiously, many of these societies bear striking similarities to cultures and mythologies found on Earth, despite humanity itself never having existed here. Their languages, customs, aesthetics, personal names and even species often resemble peoples or beings associated with Greek, Norse, Egyptian, Celtic, Indian, Chinese, Japanese, Indigenous American and other mythological traditions. The reasons for these similarities are uncertain.

Many of these civilizations developed separately for thousands of years before increasingly coming into contact with one another, creating a galaxy where wildly different cultures, governments and technological traditions now compete, cooperate and influence each other. Some are enormous states controlling vast regions of space, while others remain smaller powers, isolated worlds or wandering societies.
Different civilizations have developed radically different philosophies and methods for cultivating these abilities. Consequently, their greatest psionics are rarely identical in capability, with legendary individuals often becoming exceptionally powerful within particular disciplines rather than universally mastering every possible psychic ability.

The modern Empyrean Galaxy exists in an uneasy balance between its greatest powers. Open warfare between them risks devastation on an enormous scale, encouraging espionage, political maneuvering, proxy conflicts, exploration and competition for influence instead. Beyond their established territories remain countless unexplored systems, forgotten ruins, independent civilizations and remnants of older ages, leaving much of the galaxy's history and future unwritten.

objects.text: Taylor eventually joined the Chicago Wards after things went downhill in Brockton Bay. Most of Wildbow's Pre-Gold Morning predictions took place while Taylor was a member of the Chicago Wards. The Chicago Protectorate is run by Myrddin, a powerful and versatile Parahuman.
objects.title: Chicago

objects.text: Leviathan attacked Newfoundland in the early 2000s. It's found at the east coast of Canada.
objects.title: Newfoundland

objects.text: North America is a big place, you might want to be elsewhere in North America. Choose any location on the East Coast of North America that isn't within the borders of Brockton Bay or Boston. This includes Greenland, Central America, and any island between the Americas and Europe.
objects.title: (East Coast) North America

objects.text: North America is a big place, you might want to be elsewhere in North America. Choose any location between the East and West coasts of North America that isn't within the borders of Chicago.
objects.title: (Central) North America

objects.text: North America is a big place, you might want to be elsewhere in North America. Choose any location on the West Coast of North America.
objects.title: (West Coast) North America

objects.text: Europe isn't nearly as well off as it is on your Earth, but it isn't nearly as bad as Africa is. Choose any location in Northern Europe (ie. Finland, Sweden) you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Northern Europe

objects.text: Choose any location in Western Europe (e.g., Britain or Germany), and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Western Europe

objects.text: Proximity to Sleeper and the Blasphemies makes Eastern Europe decisively unsafe. Choose any location within it (ie. Poland, Russia), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Eastern Europe

objects.text: Home to Leviathan's most impressive attack, in 1998 at the landlocked Madrid. Choose any location within Southern Europe (ie. Italy, Spain), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Southern Europe

objects.text: Canberra, Australia was attacked by the Endbringer known as the Simurgh or Ziz during the early months of 2011. Choose any location in Australia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Australia

objects.text: New Zealand may not have been known to have been attacked by any Endbringers in canon. Regardless, you can choose any location within New Zealand, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: New Zealand

objects.text: Choose any location within the Polynesian Islands, including Hawaii and Easter Island, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Polynesia

objects.text: Choose any location within the Melanesia region of Oceania, including Fiji and Papua New Guinea, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Melanesia

objects.text: Choose any location within the Micronesia region, including Guam and Kiribati, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Micronesia

objects.text: Choose any location in the western portion of South America such as Colombia, Ecuador, or Perú, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Western South America

objects.text: Choose any location in Eastern South America (ie. Brazil), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Eastern South America

objects.text: Choose any location in Southern South America (i.e. Chile, Argentina), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Southern South America

objects.text: You'll find yourself in Kyushu, where Leviathan attacked Japan on the November of 1999. I wouldn't suggest going there any later that that, it's completely flooded.
objects.title: Kyushu

objects.text: Home to Behemoth's first attack in Iran, Choose any location in Western Asia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: West Asia

objects.text: China is home to the brainwashed military Cape team known as the Yàngbǎn. Japan, as of November 3rd, 1999 is completely flooded. In July of 2011, Choose any location in East Asia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: East Asia

objects.text: Russia is home to Sleeper, the most mysterious of the S-Class Threats. Choose any location in North Asia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: North Asia

objects.text: Choose any location in Central Asia (i.e. Pakistan, Kazakhstan), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Central Asia

objects.text: Behemoth will attack New Delhi in India. Choose any location in South Asia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: South Asia

objects.text: Choose any location in Southeast Asia (Ie. Malaysia, Thailand), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Southeast Asia

objects.text: Africa is full of warlords and home to Ash Beast, one of the S-Class Threats. Choose any location in North Africa (ie. Algeria, Egypt), you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: North Africa

objects.text: Choose any location in East Africa, such as Ethiopia or Madagascar, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: East Africa

objects.text: Choose any location in West Africa, such as Nigeria or Ghana, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: West Africa

objects.text: Choose any location in Central Africa, such as Chad or Angolia, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Central Africa

objects.text: Choose any location in South Africa, such as Botswana or the Republic of South Africa, and you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: South Africa

objects.text: Choose any location in Antarctica or the North Pole, you'll find yourself there.
objects.title: Antarctica

objects.text: Choose any location that is quarantined at the time of your arrival. This can be a Simurgh Containment Zone, Ellisburg, Eagleton, Flint, Freedom, etc.
objects.title: Containment Zone

objects.text: You'll find yourself at a containment camp you fit the criteria for. Whether this is a Gesellschaft (Neo-Nazi) Containment Camp or a CUI Containment Camp for brainwashing Parahumans into being loyal Chinese pawns is up to whether you fit the criteria and chance.
objects.title: Containment Camp

objects.text: You'll find yourself at a location that Behemoth made uninhabitable during one of his attacks prior to 2011. If you're not in Earth Bet, you're at some other area that is too radioactive to be safe for humans to be.
objects.title: Radioactive Wasteland

objects.text: You find yourself trapped within the confines of the Baumann Parahuman Containment Center. It is not designed to allow prisoners to leave after they have been imprisoned within it. Because prisoners are only meant to enter the prison, prisoners are loaded onto an elevator with limited oxygen.
objects.title: Birdcage

objects.text: You find yourself on an island far from civilization and rich with any kind of resource you need to create a base. It comes with a complimentary volcano, rich underground and is a long-lasting place with various animals and fruits. It even has an abandoned ruined shack with various damaged tools inside.
objects.title: Personal Island

objects.text: You find yourself in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean with no islands within hundreds of miles at minimum.
objects.title: Ocean

objects.text: You find yourself in the middle of the Pacific Ocean on a single lone barren island. There are no trees or food. It's just a rocky island with no life.
objects.title: Barren Island

objects.text: You find yourself in the Amazon Rainforest completely lost.
objects.title: Forest

objects.text: You find yourself in a random Underwater Cave with limited oxygen and completely lost.
objects.title: Underwater Cave

objects.text:
‘Whoops’

It seems you’ve been transported high into the sky and will immediately begin falling to earth. I hope you brought a good book, it will take you two and a half minutes to hit the ground without any aide.
objects.title: 30,000-40,000 ft in the air.

objects.text: You appear in the middle of an active conflict. This could be a raging warzone, gladiatorial arena, chaotic street skirmish or any other location featuring fierce ongoing fighting.
objects.title: Battlefield

objects.text: You appear inside a locked holding cell within a jail, dungeon or any other facility designed for imprisonment such as a mad scientist's quarantine chamber, ship's brig or military black site.
objects.title: Prison

objects.text: You arrive in an abandoned structure of your choice. There might be squatters in the ruins that could be hostile or friendly as well as other hazards.
objects.title: Ruins

objects.text: You arrive near a notable place in the wilderness of your choice. There may or may not be civilization nearby, but you will have to survive and find your way there.
objects.title: Natural Landmark

objects.text:
You appear at, or nearby, the location of the most historically or narratively significant event within the setting occurring around the time of your arrival. The setting’s fate may hinge upon what happens here and the course of events can be dramatically altered, for better or worse.

If there are multiple feasible options when you arrive, you may choose between them.
objects.title: Canonical Crossroads

objects.text: You appear at the scene of an ongoing serious violent crime, such as first-degree murder, kidnapping or armed robbery. Be aware that the perpetrators may not want to leave any potential witnesses alive. Alternatively, you can be the victim instead, with the crime occurring right after you arrive.
objects.title: Active Crime Scene

objects.text: You find yourself on the bright side of the Moon.
objects.title: Moon

objects.text: You find yourself inside the center of the Sun.
objects.title: Sun

objects.text: You find yourself stranded on Mars.
objects.title: Mars

objects.text: You find yourself stranded on a random asteroid in the Asteroid Belt.
objects.title: Asteroid Belt

objects.text: You find yourself floating in space, orbiting Earth like a satellite.
objects.title: Orbiting Earth

objects.text: You find yourself floating in space, far far from Earth. Right outside the Solar System.
objects.title: Outside the Solar System

objects.text: You find yourself floating in space, at the edge of the milky way.
objects.title: Edge of The Galaxy

objects.text: You find yourself randomly in the Universe, somewhere with a different Entity doing a Cycle on an alien planet that is not Earth. Or anywhere near it.
objects.title: Wrong Planet

objects.text: You find yourself in a black hole at the center of the galaxy.
objects.title: Blackhole

objects.text: You find yourself in one of the random alternate universes. You're also floating in space. There is nothing around you, no planets or even any landmarks. You're completely lost.
objects.title: A Random Universe

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Aleph. It is a world that diverged paths from the time of Scion's first appearance. This world has variations of everyone born before said appearance (about 30 years before the start of Worm), though anyone born after will not have a duplicate in Earth Bet. This Earth still has capes. However, they're much weaker than the ones on Earth Bet. Endbringers also do not exist here.
objects.title: Earth Aleph

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Shin. Earth Shin is an alternate reality that featured villains operating like terrorist cells, destabilizing society to make people dependent on superhumans to get energy, food and safety. Basically put, a world with superhumans that had no superheroes. Takeover on a global level, with non-superhumans as second class citizens. This is also where Goddess resides.
objects.title: Earth Shin

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Gimel. This is an alternate Earth which seemed to have diverged from other human occupied earths roughly five thousand years ago. Due to this, it’s an empty world populated by wild animals and fauna.
objects.title: Earth Gimel

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Cheit. This is an alternate Earth unified under a culturally stagnant theocracy, ruled by strict religious orthodoxy. Parahumans exist but they hide themselves in positions of civilian power rather than overt heroism.
objects.title: Earth Cheit

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Nun, a sparsely populated world with multiple isolated settlements. Most of the population resides in the largest settlement, which is centered around the portal to Earth Gimel. Depending on when you arrive, the planet will be dominated by villains.
objects.title: Earth Nun

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Earth Eden. This is an alternate Earth where Eden crash-landed, tearing holes to Contessa's World and Doctor Mother's World. This world featured a number of monsters created by Eden's impact.
objects.title: Earth Eden

objects.text: This is the Earth where Khepri was exiled to after Scion’s death and where Contessa ultimately shot her. You appear on the same forested hillside where Khepri was lying when Contessa confronted and executed her.
objects.title: Khepri Exile Earth

rows.title: Location
rows.titleText:
Where were you reborn/transported?
Do not take a location here if it contradicts your location in the next section. Unless otherwise stated within your chosen options, you can choose the specifics of your locations within the parameters of your choices.

(If you have Home from Item section, you can choose to appear somewhere in there. This counts with Secret Lair, Tinkertech Base, or Company)

rows.title: Locations (Available to Non-Earths)
rows.titleText:
Where were you reborn/transported?
Do not take a location here that contradicts your location in the above section. Unless otherwise stated within your chosen options, you can choose the specifics of your locations within the parameters of your choices.

objects.text: You don't get to choose your starting location. You appear somewhere not particularly dangerous.
objects.title: Lost

objects.text: You don't get to choose your starting location. You appear somewhere actively dangerous to you, it could be because of the environment like a desert or mountain top, or because the locals are hostile to you.
objects.title: Lost (Perilous)

objects.text: You appear somewhere that is safe for the time being, though not necessarily for long. You don't get to choose the specifics.
objects.title: Safe Space

objects.text: You appear in a capital city of your choice in your chosen setting.
objects.title: Capital City

objects.text: You appear in any city of your choice in your chosen setting.
objects.title: City

objects.text: You appear in or near a school of your choice in your setting.
objects.title: School

objects.text: You appear inside the base of people who will assume you to be an enemy.
objects.title: Intruder Alert

objects.text: If the Main Character of the setting has a house, you appear right outside of it, or, if you want, inside of it. If they don't have a house, you appear in their resting space, even if that's just a camp or hotel room.
objects.title: Main Character's House

objects.text: You appear before the setting's Main Character. They will be fully clothed and decent when this happens.
objects.title: Main Character's Face

objects.text: If the Main Antagonist of the setting has a base of operations, you appear right outside of it, or, if you want, inside of it. If they don't have one, you appear in their resting space, even if that's just a camp or hotel room.
objects.title: Main Antagonist's Lair

objects.text: You appear before the setting's Main Antagonist. They will be fully clothed and decent when this happens.
objects.title: Main Antagonist's Face

objects.text: You appear right outside of, or, if you want, inside of the house of a named character of your choice who is not considered a major protagonist or antagonist of the story. If they don't have a house, you appear in their resting space, even if that's just a camp or hotel room.
objects.title: Side Character's House

objects.text: You appear before a named character of your choice who is not considered a major protagonist or antagonist of the story. They will be fully clothed and decent when this happens.
objects.title: Side Character's Face

objects.text:
You appear right outside of, or, if you want, inside of the house of a character of your own creation who could reasonably exist in the setting. You may also decide whether they have a house, or if you appear in another resting space such, as a camp or hotel room.

You may decide what powers and backstory this character has, but they may not be particularly powerful or absurd by the setting’s standards. You may also not have a prior relationship with this character.
objects.title: Original Character's House

objects.text:
You appear before a character of your own creation who could reasonably exist in the setting. They will be fully clothed and decent when this happens.

You may decide what powers and backstory this character has, but they may not be particularly powerful or absurd by the setting’s standards. You may also not have a prior relationship with this character.
objects.title: Original Character's Face

objects.text: You appear before someone who will believe your story if you tell the truth and will be an, at the very least, good ally. You can still push them away, even if you don't do it intentionally.
objects.title: Ally

objects.text:
‘Whoops’

It seems you’ve been transported high into the sky and will immediately begin falling to the ground. I hope you brought a good book, it will take you about two and a half minutes to hit the surface without any aide.
objects.title: 30,000-40,000 ft in the air.

objects.text: You appear in the middle of an active conflict. This could be a raging warzone, gladiatorial arena, chaotic street skirmish or any other location featuring fierce ongoing fighting.
objects.title: Battlefield

objects.text: You appear inside a locked holding cell within a jail, dungeon or any other facility designed for imprisonment such as a mad scientist's quarantine chamber, ship's brig or military black site.
objects.title: Prison

objects.text:
You appear at, or nearby, the location of the most historically or narratively significant event within the setting occurring around the time of your arrival. The setting’s fate may hinge upon what happens here and the course of events can be dramatically altered, for better or worse.

If there are multiple feasible options when you arrive, you may choose between them.
objects.title: Canonical Crossroads

objects.text: You arrive near a notable place in the wilderness of your choice. There may or may not be civilization nearby, but you will have to survive and find your way there.
objects.title: Natural Landmark

objects.text: You arrive in an abandoned structure of your choice. There might be squatters in the ruins that could be hostile or friendly as well as other hazards.
objects.title: Ruins

objects.text: You appear at the scene of an ongoing serious violent crime, such as first-degree murder, kidnapping or armed robbery. Be aware that the perpetrators may not want to leave any potential witnesses alive. Alternatively, you can be the victim instead, with the crime occurring right after you arrive.
objects.title: Active Crime Scene

objects.text: You start on a planet of your choice that isn’t Earth. Will be very lonely in a universe without widespread alien life and/or space travel. If the planet doesn’t have a breathable atmosphere, then you’d better come with your own space suit and habitat.
objects.title: Alien Planet

objects.text: You appear inside SCP-3008-1, a.k.a the 'Infinite IKEA'. This is an unending space resembling that of an IKEA Store with escape being extremely difficult. You may stumble across one of the makeshift communities trapped in here but whatever you do, avoid the ‘Staff’.
objects.title: SCP-3008-1

objects.text: You appear at the heart of an XK-Class End-of-the-World Scenario—either face-to-face with its source or deep within its most dangerous zone. This could be any XK-Class SCP event, from When Day Breaks to SCP-3002. Alternatively, you may choose a random or original XK-Class Scenario. Regardless of the scenario, you will always start in an area that is extraordinarily dangerous.
objects.title: XK-Class Scenario

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within the continent of Westeros, south of the Wall. This encompasses regions such as the North, the Vale of Arryn, the Reach and Dorne as well as nearby isles like the Iron Islands.
objects.title: The Seven Kingdoms

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice north of the Wall, outside the Seven Kingdoms. This includes regions such as the Thenn, Frostfangs and Lands of Always Winter. This is a cold, harsh and inhospitable place, containing savage beasts, Wildlings and... Others.
objects.title: Beyond the Wall

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within the territory controlled by the nine city-states situated west of the Dothraki Sea. This encompasses Braavos, Pentos, Lys, Volantis etc as well as areas like the Stepstones, Disputed Lands and the Rhoyne.
objects.title: The Free Cities

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice east of the Free Cities. This includes the vast Dothraki Sea, the city-states of Slaver's Bay, the opulent trade hub of Qarth and beyond, all the way to the Golden Empire of Yi Ti and the mysterious Shadow Lands.
objects.title: Eastern Essos

objects.text:
You appear within the Valyrian Peninsula, a nightmarish landscape of fire and ruin due to the Doom. The land is covered by active volcanoes and the sea itself boils and smokes. 

Few who enter ever return and many believe the region to be inhabited by ‘demons’ and unspeakable horrors, suspected by some to be the remnants of Valyrian experiments with blood magic.
objects.title: Valyrian Peninsula

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within the Summer Isles. Compared to Westeros or Essos, this large archipelago of islands is a peaceful and almost idyllic location with a tropical climate and vibrant culture.
objects.title: Summer Isles

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Blue Wind Empire. It is one of the seven nations of the Profound Sky Continent. It is home to Yun Che and some major characters. Historically, it has been the weakest nation; it is remote, has few resources and the peak strength of cultivators is the middle of Emperor Profound Realm.
objects.title: Blue Wind Empire

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Azure Cloud Continent. This continent is about five million kilometers away from the Profound Sky Continent and the Illusory Demon Realm. The combined profound cultivation of Azure Cloud Continent is slightly weaker than the Illusory Demon Realm. The three strongest sects within the Azure Cloud Continent were the Heaven Thwarting Sect, Seven Stars Divine Palace, and Soaring Celestial Sword Sect. Ninth level of the Sovereign Profound Realm was the highest level achieved by the three sect masters of the strongest sects.
objects.title: Azure Cloud Continent

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Illusory Demon Realm. It is one of the three continents of the Blue Pole Star. It has a population of roughly seventy billion. A large percentage of its population consists of demons. It is currently being ruled by the Demon Emperor Family with Empress Huan Caiyi.
objects.title: Illusory Demon Realm

objects.text: You appear in the Magus Bazaar, the magical trading hub of New York City, somewhere where no-one is observing.
objects.title: Magus Bazaar (American Dragon)

objects.text: You begin on the Isle of Draco, a meeting place of the Dragon Council, and the site of the annual dragon summit. You’ll appear somewhere unobserved, though I hope you have a way out of here.
objects.title: The Isle of Draco (American Dragon)

objects.text: You appear outside Canal Street Electronics, home to Luong Lao Shi a former World Dragon, and the training ground for his grandson Jake, the American Dragon.
objects.title: Canal Street Electronics (American Dragon)

objects.text: You appear in the Nomadic City, Chernobog.
objects.title: Chernobog Nomadic City

objects.text: You appear in the Nomadic City, Lungmen.
objects.title: Lungmen Nomadic City

objects.text: You appear on the Rhodes Island Landship
objects.title: Rhodes Island Landship

objects.text:
Yokosuka City is currently the biggest naval base in Japan. Japanese National Maritime Institute of Technology, where Gunzou Chihaya is currently studying, as well as Osakabe Mansion, the birthplace of Design Children, are located here.

You can appear in any publicly available space.
objects.title: Yokosuka City

objects.text:
One of the dry docks in Yokosuka port, where the Fleet of Fog submarine I-401 is stored.

Upon your arrival, should you wish, I-401 will awaken and choose you as her captain instead of Gunzou.
objects.title: Warehouse 51

objects.text:
You appear on the deck of the Fleet of Fog Vessel of your choice.

Good Luck.
objects.title: All Hands on Deck

objects.text: You start somewhere on the grounds of Fowl Manor, somewhere no-one is looking.
objects.title: Fowl Manor (Artemis Fowl)

objects.text: You appear in Haven, the underground sanctuary for the magical community, somewhere no-one is watching.
objects.title: Haven (Artemis Fowl)

objects.text: You appear on the island of Hybras, an island cast out of time into Limbo thousands of years ago, and inhabited by Demons. I hope you have a way out of here.
objects.title: Hybras (Artemis Fowl)

objects.text: You will arrive in any of the 3 walls of Paradis. Humankind there is generally empathetic, although that gets lessened the closer to the center you get. You cannot decide exactly where in the wall you choose that you land.
objects.title: Walls of Humanity

objects.text: You land on the island known as Paradis, but outside the walls. Titans number by the hundred as they are prisoners dumped there by Marley. Finally, the island is roughly the size of Madagascar, but you can choose where on the island to spawn besides inside the walls or on top
objects.title: Paradis

objects.text: You may appear anywhere on the continent of Marley. Being the size of Africa, it has fought off more advanced societies with Titans alone. Although, they can be intolerant for those they suspect of being Eldians.
objects.title: Marley

objects.text: You appear in the Spirit World. Good luck escaping.
objects.title: Spirit World

objects.text: You appear in a Naval Base of any country of your choice. You can choose to be the Admiral appointed to that base, some personal needed on it or a Ship Girl if you have the power.
objects.title: Naval Base

objects.text: You appear on any of the Siren's constructs, be it land, bases, caches or something similar of your choice. Take care, because even leftovers and abandoned places have active security systems.
objects.title: Siren Water's

objects.text:
You now appear on a Timeline where a Collab happened, from Kizuna AI conquering the World, Console Wars being fought on Shipgirls Frames, Hololive Mad Universe happening on the background, and more. 

Good Luck.
objects.title: Collab Special

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the city of San Fransokyo, a high-tech urban environment where most superhuman activity is the result of cutting-edge science and robotics. Local danger exists in the form of rogue tech users, but the city maintains law and order with strong institutions and emerging heroes.
objects.title: San Fransokyo

objects.text: You appear on Akuma Island, a remote, off-grid former military testing site now abandoned and overrun with decommissioned weapons, unstable tech, and mutated experimental organisms. The island is rarely monitored and often used as a hideout by fugitives and rogue scientists.
objects.title: Akuma Island

objects.text: You appear within the unstable dimensional space known as the Void, a collapsed interdimensional transit zone created by the malfunctioning Silent Sparrow portal. There is no gravity, no breathable atmosphere, and no conventional terrain—only drifting debris, scattered technology, and total isolation. Survival requires advanced tech, life-support systems, or robotic assistance. Escape is impossible without an external portal activation.
objects.title: The Void

objects.text: You appear in Karakura Town, a hotbed of spiritual activity in the human world, albeit a well-protected one.
objects.title: Karakura Town

objects.text: You appear in Soul Society, within the Seireitei. The Shinigami will likely treat you as an intruder upon arrival. Be prepared to have to fight your way out.
objects.title: Seireitei

objects.text: You appear in Hueco Mundo, the realm of the Hollows. Good luck with that.
objects.title: Hueco Mundo
Refugee Center
objects.text: A fenced compound whose above-ground area is large enough to house at least a couple of dozen or so survivors. The majority of its population is housed below, however, and they are no longer accepting any additions. This is still a somewhat safe haven and a place to rest and trade, though it's unlikely they will truly endure the cataclysm.

objects.title: Exodii Castle
objects.text: A fortress constructed out of metal and wires, this is the primary home of the Exodii node who have travelled to this Earth in search of resources and technology. Every single one is a cybernetically enhanced human, with enough robotic walkers and automatic defences to keep them safe, for now. They will sell cybernetic implants to survivors who come across them, though only if they prove they are trustworthy.

objects.title: Hub 01
objects.text: An underground lab which survived the Cataclysm mostly intact thanks to the efforts of its AI, which gained sapience during the portal storms and provided instructions during this brief window. They do not allow outsiders to enter, but are willing to provide work and trade to capable survivors. A mercenary bar has also sprung up just across from it, within an unused building.
This is the place where everyone starts their journey to fame, here are those who have from 1 to 10,000 Followers.
objects.title: District 13: City of Beginning

objects.text: This is the place where the most famous personalities live, those whose followers are over 50 Million. Here live such important personas as Youth and Elder.
objects.title: District 1: Heaven

objects.text: This is where most of the 72 live, as well as those who don't want to be part of the Cyberspace created by MAGA.
objects.title: Deep Web

objects.text: You appear at the site of an alien ship crash. The area is littered with advanced alien technology, strange biological materials, and remnants of battles. Powerful alien forces often revisit the site to recover lost tech.
objects.title: Alien Ship Crash Site

objects.text: You find yourself inside the infamous Turbo Granny’s Tunnel, a dark, twisting passage that serves as the domain of the notorious yokai, Turbo Granny. Turbo Granny herself prowls the tunnel. If you are a man and you get caught by her, she will try to take your “wiener” as part of her twisted sense of humor and vengeance. She will then curse and possess you.
objects.title: Turbo Granny’s Tunnel

objects.text: You appear on a floor in the dungeon. Roll a 1d20, that's what floor you're on. You cannot teleport out of the dungeon or to another floor for the first 100 hours of your time in DanMachi.
objects.title: Dungeon 1-20

objects.text: You appear on a floor in the dungeon. Roll a 1d20, add a 20 to that and that's what floor you're on. You cannot teleport out of the dungeon or to another floor for the first 100 hours of your time in DanMachi.
objects.title: Dungeon 21-40

objects.text: You appear on a floor in the dungeon. Roll a 1d20, add a 40 to that and that's what floor you're on. You cannot teleport out of the dungeon or to another floor for the first 100 hours of your time in DanMachi.
objects.title: Dungeon 41-60

objects.text: You appear on a floor in the dungeon. Roll a 1d20, add a 60 to that and that's what floor you're on. You cannot teleport out of the dungeon or to another floor for the first 100 hours of your time in DanMachi.
objects.title: Dungeon 61-80

objects.text: You appear on a floor in the dungeon. Roll a 1d20, add an 80 to that and that's what floor you're on. You cannot teleport out of the dungeon or to another floor for the first 100 hours of your time in DanMachi.
objects.title: Dungeon 81-100

objects.text: You appear in an isolated, cursed area saturated with spiritual energy and malevolent intent. The location varies but is always sealed off by the overwhelming power of a yokai or vengeful spirit. You cannot leave until the yokai has been dealt with, either by confrontation, appeasement, or exorcism.
objects.title: Major Haunted Location

objects.text: You appear at the Awamiya Shrine, the home and workplace of Touko Awamiya, a renowned exorcist and grandmother of the cursed spirit medium, Keitaro Gentoga. The shrine is a sprawling, ancient compound filled with spiritual artifacts, blessed exorcism tools, and countless sealed cursed dolls. The sealed dolls are the shrine’s most notorious feature, each containing a vengeful spirit trapped by the Awamiya family over generations. These spirits, though bound, are far from dormant—occasionally attempting to break free, causing an ever-present tension. The shrine also houses powerful exorcism tools, each imbued with blessings that make them highly effective against curses and spirits.
objects.title: Awamiya Shrine

objects.text: You appear at the grand shrine of Taisai Seikun. The shrine radiates the overwhelming presence of Taisai Seikun, an evil divine god whose mastery of onmyodo and connection to the Hashoshin grants him dominion over the fortunes of cardinal directions. Taisai Seikun will immediately takes an interest in you.
objects.title: Taisai Seikun’s Shrine

objects.text:
You start in Gotham city.
This place might legitimately have either 1000 curses or the attention of Despair of the endless. Either way, this is perhaps the worst major city I've ever seen. Expect any stay to be unpleasant.
objects.title: Gotham

objects.text:
You start in Blüdhaven, while costumed crime in Blüdhaven is generally non existent when compared to other places in DC, the sheer amount of other criminal activity more than makes up for it, to the point that even Gothamites have adopted a saying. 
 
"Hey, at least it's not Blüdhaven."
objects.title: Blüdhaven

objects.text:
You start in Metropolis.
This place is the polar opposite of Gotham, the city of tomorrow is bustling with life, opportunity, and safety, with small-level crime being practically non-existent due to the fact that all you need to do is yell for help and Superman arrives to help you out.
objects.title: Metropolis

objects.text: You’ll find yourself in the hidden Gorilla City, ruled by King Solovar. They don’t take kindly to humans here, so I hope you have a plan…
objects.title: Gorilla City

objects.text: You start in Smallville the home of Superman or at least where he was raised. Strange occurrences happen and people are miraculously saved by a mysterious hero that's only a blur.
objects.title: Smallville

objects.text: You appear on Paradise Island, the idyllic home of the Amazons. This magical island nation is the birthplace of Wonder Woman and is inhabited solely by women. The Amazons are an insular people who are proud of their way of life and wary of outside influence.
objects.title: Themyscira

objects.text: You appear in the Justice League Watchtower, a highly advanced satellite orbiting Earth and serving as the League’s home base. You will likely be detected immediately and detained shortly after.
objects.title: Justice League Watchtower

objects.text: You begin at the very heart of android innovation—CyberLife’s towering corporate headquarters in downtown Detroit. Sterile, futuristic, and fortified, it’s the safest place an android or tech-aligned individual can be. Access to cutting-edge tech, internal AI networks, and key personnel grants opportunities few places can match. However, eyes are always watching, and your presence will eventually raise questions—especially if you aren’t supposed to be there.
objects.title: CyberLife Tower

objects.text: You wake up in one of the crumbling outskirts that later become a haven for deviant androids. These neighborhoods are lawless, abandoned by the state, and rife with black market cybernetics, scavenged android parts, and hostile survivors—both human and synthetic. Danger is constant, but so is freedom. From here, you can join the uprising, reshape the city’s future, or disappear into the chaos.
objects.title: The Slums of New Jericho

objects.text: You arrive at the DPD precinct in central Detroit, a nerve center of law enforcement during one of the most volatile periods in modern history. You’ll be under constant scrutiny, but you’ll also have access to critical intel, police androids like RK800, and frontline insights into the growing deviant crisis.
objects.title: Detroit Police Department HQ

objects.text: A tightly controlled surveillance city. Corporate influence, covert police forces, and constant monitoring define daily life. Augmentations are regulated, restricted, and politically sensitive.
objects.title: Golem City

objects.text: A tightly controlled surveillance city. Corporate influence, covert police forces, and constant monitoring define daily life. Augmentations are regulated, restricted, and politically sensitive.
objects.title: Prague

objects.text: Corporate headquarters, private security, and heavy surveillance. Augmentations are common but closely monitored. Power flows through companies, contracts, and access control.
objects.title: Detroit

objects.text: You appear somewhere deep underground in the Deep Roads. Good luck finding your way to the surface and look out for Darkspawn and other creatures.
objects.title: The Deep Roads

objects.text: You arrive somewhere in the nation of Ferelden, a European-inspired realm located in southeast Thedas. Depending on your date of arrival, you may be arriving in the middle of a Blight. At least a certain Grey Warden is trying to stop it...
objects.title: Ferelden

objects.text: You have landed anywhere you desire on this lush, green planet. The natives are kindhearted, and this planet is known for Dragon Balls, wish granting orbs.
objects.title: Namek

objects.text: A planet with only 3 known inhabitants. You have been placed in a "safe" spot on the edge of the planetoid, but you better have a way of getting out of there before a certain purple cat wakes up and sees an intruder.
objects.title: Beerus' Planet

objects.text: You have arrived on the Lookout, on the edge of it, but facing towards the magnificent building. 2 people at a time usually occupy this location: The guardian of Earth, and their assistant Popo.
objects.title: Kami's Lookout

objects.text: Known as the City of Doors, Sigil is a neutral city and the self-proclaimed center of the multiverse. A major hub for interplanar travel and trade, the city contains multiple portals to every single plane, and is indirectly governed by the mysterious Lady of Pain to prevent deities and other powerful outsiders from affecting it. She generally lets people within its bounds do as they like as long as they avoid her wrath.
objects.title: Sigil

objects.text: You may arrive anywhere within the Sword Coast, the default location for most adventures in the Forgotten Realms. This includes the famous cities of Waterdeep, Baldur's Gate and Neverwinter, as well as many other places of greater and lesser importance. While civilised areas are generally safe, it's wilds are still full of threats.
objects.title: Sword Coast

objects.text: You arrive in the Underdark, a place of caverns and cave systems that stretches beneath the earth. Its dangers are many and its comforts few, as within are a dangerous assortment of man-eating creatures, and even its "civilised" races are brutal compared to surface-dwellers. You may choose to arrive anywhere from Menzoberranzan to Mantel Dereth, or simply appear somewhere random within it's twisting tunnels.
objects.title: Underdark

objects.text: You arrive anywhere within the six major or twelve minor elemental planes in the Great Wheel cosmology model, usually referred to as the Inner Planes. The danger of these planes varies wildly, and they generally follow exotic physical laws compared to the Prime Material Plane, but there are locations where extraplanar travellers are welcome. You can choose to arrive anywhere inside these planes, from the City of Brass to the Citadel of Ten Thousand Pearls or deep within the Sevenfold Mazework.
objects.title: Elemental Planes

objects.text: The Outer Planes of D&D are infinite dimensions organized by alignment: Law, Chaos, Good & Evil. These are exotic locales compared to the Prime Material Plane, and often inherently dangerous to mortals, even if they may be beautiful on the surface. You may choose to enter anywhere from the peaks of Mount Celestia to the deepest layers of the Abyss.
objects.title: Outer Planes

objects.text: The home of the Githyanki, planar travellers, astral dragons and more, the Astral Plane is most often traversed by means of the Astral Projection spell, but it is technically habitable by mortals. Here, distance and time lose meaning, as it is a barren place of other-dimensional nothingness extending in all directions. As such, where you arrive matters little, but you can exit via portals to other planes if you can find them.
objects.title: Astral Plane

objects.text: You arrive anywhere on Earth's surface. While the ocean plants still provide oxygen, the air is chock full of dust particles, heating the planet to an unbearable degree. Life here is all but extinct sans whatever self-sustaining shelter that may still function, and a regular human would die in a few days, either from the heat or from the dust.
objects.title: On the Surface

objects.text: You arrive at Upsilon Site. Responsible for powering the whole PATHOS-II complex, is also where Simon, the game protagonist, will “awaken”. Be aware the Construct is active here, and will turn hostile if it sees you.
objects.title: Upsilon Site

objects.text: You arrive at Tau Site. It is closely located near the Phi Site, home to the Omega Space Gun, and between the two is the Alpha Site, where the WAU is located. Most importantly, Tau is the location of Sarah Lindwall, the last human alive, and the ARK, a satellite running the copied minds of the PATHOS-II personnel.
objects.title: Tau Site

objects.text: The land which hides the sin of Queen Marika, and is home to Messmer's Legion; Bayle the Dread; and Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame. The Land of Shadow is also the site for Miquella's planned ascension to godhood, and he will not take too kindly to your interruption.
objects.title: Land of Shadow

objects.text: An abandoned chapel near castle Stormveil. If you choose, you may take the spot of Melina's chosen Tarnished. Also a hotspot of activity for both Mohgwyn Palace and Godrick the Grafted.
objects.title: Chapel of Anticipation

objects.text: A land plagued by Scarlet Rot after the battle between Malenia the Severed and General Radahn. If you can survive the festering rot, swarms of monsters, and hostile humans, you may challenge the fallen General during the Radahn festival. Caelid is also home to countless historical ruins, churches, and catacombs which contain a variety of ancient knowledge, sorceries, and loot. Some other notable locations include Redmane Castle; the Cathedral of Dragon Communion; Sellia, Town of Sorcery; and the Divine Tower of Caelid.
objects.title: Caelid

objects.text: You appear in the irradiated and crumbling ruins of Tokyo-1, also known as Old Tokyo
objects.title: Tokyo-1

objects.text: You appear in the new Capital of Japan, Tokyo-2
objects.title: Tokyo-2

addons.text:
You now either take the place of Shinji Ikari, or are another pilot candidate alongside him.

Whether you are a member of the Ikari family, a distant relative, or just a promising pilot candidate, you appear in the city of Atami while JSSDF tries to halt the attack of the Third Angel, Sakiel. In a few minutes, Misato will arrive to take you to Tokyo-3.

If you replace Shinji, EVA-01 will accept you as its pilot, but if you are not related to Yui, EVA-01 might not be inclined to go out of its way to protect you in critical situations as it did for Shinji.

If you are another pilot entirely, there will be a new EVA waiting for you.
addons.title: Get In The Robot

objects.text: Located above the massive subterranean cavity known as the Geofront, you appear in Tokyo-3, with its retractable buildings.
objects.title: Tokyo-3

objects.text: You appear inside or right outside a guild building—not just of any ordinary random guild, but one with at least one S-Rank Mage.
objects.title: Guild Building

objects.text: You arrive anywhere in the state of New California, including the outskirts of the Mojave Wasteland. Due to the relative togetherness and presence of the NCR, this is considered one of the safer areas of the post-apocalypse.
objects.title: New California

objects.text: You arrive in the Commonwealth, the corpse of the Massachusetts Commonwealth. Things are more civilized here, and the most dangerous area is known as the Glowing Sea to the southwest, with Far Harbor being an unknown distance up the coast.
objects.title: The Commonwealth

objects.text: You arrive in the ruins of DC and the surrounding area known as the Capital Wasteland. Super Mutants reign heavily over the West and East, from Vault 87 and the DC ruins respectively. The presence of the Enclave as well also makes northern travel a little risky
objects.title: Capital Wasteland

objects.text:
You appear inside the Tristanian Academy of Magic, where young nobles from Tristain and, in some cases, neighbouring countries, study magic.

If you wish, you can take the place of Saito and be summoned by Louise as her familiar.
objects.title: Tristanian Academy of Magic

objects.text: You arrive at the Chaldea Security Organization as a Master candidate, Servant, staff, or other at your discretion.
objects.title: Chaldea

objects.text: You appear inside of a Singularity of your choice. If you are a Servant, you can choose to be summoned either by Chaldea Masters or you can be summoned by the Holy Grail or whoever is manipulating it, otherwise, you can be a "normal" human of the era.
objects.title: Singularity

objects.text: You appear inside of a Lostbelt of your choice. If you are a Servant, you can choose to be summoned either by Chaldea Masters or you can be summoned by the Holy Grail or whoever is manipulating it, otherwise, you can be a "normal" human of the era.
objects.title: Lostbelt

objects.text: The city where the Holy Grail War takes place every 60 years. Has 3 leylines converging on the local temple, so a good place for any aspiring magi to ply their craft.
objects.title: Fuyuki City

objects.text: The Clocktower in London, a good place for any magi to learn and develop their mysteries. But if they catch a whiff of any unique or unreplicable powers, you are likely to gain a sealing designation and either spend the rest of your life on the run from the magi community, or as a lab experiment for some of the most demented people around.
objects.title: The Clocktower

objects.text: You appear in Shang Mu. Either within or outside of City Hall, or the Battlesphere.
objects.title: Shang Mu

objects.text: You appear in Shang Tu. Either within or outside of the Magister’s Royal Palace.
objects.title: Shang Tu

objects.text: You appear in Shuigang. Either within or outside of Prince Dail’s Palace.
objects.title: Shuigang

objects.text: You appear before Truth. He will take something from you. I suggest you prepare something to trade ahead of time. If you can regrow your limbs, Truth is not going to think of them as valuable, but if you can create substitutes, like prosthetics, that's fine.
objects.title: Truth

objects.text: You arrive at the amusement park known as the Gold Saucer, specifically the terminal station. Plenty of activities to be done, and even money and prizes to be won!
objects.title: Gold Saucer

objects.text: You will appear in Midgar, although you cannot choose the precise spot, only the sector. Midgar is a very split city in quality between the upper half and the lower half.
objects.title: Midgar

objects.text: You arrive in a town on the southeastern islands known as Mideel. It is a town known for hotsprings and being very close to the Lifestream.
objects.title: Mideel

objects.text: You appear in one of the seven nations of your choosing.
objects.title: Seven Nations

objects.text: You appear in the Abyss, time in the Abyss is different from the outside world, 3 months in here is 3 days in the outside world.
objects.title: Abyss

objects.text: You appear in Celestia. You will be confronted by the Unknown God, possibly attacked by her.
objects.title: Celestia

objects.text: You appear within the grand halls of Olympus, a realm high above the mortal plane and home to the Olympian gods. This divine mountain is adorned with gleaming temples, flowing ambrosial rivers, and radiant skies that never darken. Here, gods plot, feast, and govern the fates of mortals and immortals alike. Beware, for every step you take draws the gaze of powerful beings who may see you as an ally, an amusement, or a threat.
objects.title: Olympus

objects.text: You arrive at the gates of the Underworld, a shadowy and ominous realm ruled by the god Hades. The air is heavy with despair as the River Styx winds its way through a barren landscape filled with the cries of the dead. From the judgment of souls in the Fields of Asphodel to the torment of Tartarus and the solace of Elysium, this is a place where fate is final. Navigate this realm carefully, as even the dead must tread lightly under the watchful eyes of the Underworld’s ruler and his monstrous guardians.
objects.title: Hades

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Midgard, the realm of mortals in Norse mythology. A rugged land of sprawling forests, icy tundras, and small, scattered villages, it is a world teetering on the brink of chaos. Midgard is home to humanity, but it also harbors dangerous creatures and agents of the gods who weave their schemes among mortals. The realm is both protected and threatened by the World Tree, Yggdrasil, which connects it to the other Norse realms. Survival here depends on strength, resourcefulness, and knowledge of the gods’ ongoing machinations.
objects.title: Midgard

objects.text: You will spawn in, or around the Mystery Shack. This roadside attraction is slightly more than what it seems, given the mutli-dimensional portal underneath the basement.
objects.title: Mystery Shack

objects.text: You will land directly in the Blind Eye society's headquarters in the Gravity Falls museum. If you are unlucky enough to be caught and registered, people will ALWAYS be wiped of your presence if they see you again.
objects.title: Society Of The Blind Eye

objects.text: You appear somewhere you want in Diagon Alley, at the place where nobody is looking. It can be right behind the Leaky Cauldron in a small, walled courtyard, or near Gringotts, or even inside Knockturn Alley.
objects.title: Diagon Alley

objects.text: You appear somewhere you want in Hogsmeade Village, the only all-wizarding village in Britain. Hogwarts and train station are not far from this location.
objects.title: Hogsmeade

objects.text: You appear at King's Cross Station, at the place where nobody is looking. You appear on the muggle side of the station.
objects.title: King's Cross Station

objects.text: You appear somewhere inside Forbidden Forest. You don't choose your location there. But be careful - this forest is full of secrets and fraught with dangers for an unprepared muggle or wizard.
objects.title: Forbidden Forest

objects.text: You appear in a random empty cell inside Azkaban. It is a fortress on an island in the middle of the North Sea that is working as a jail for Dark Wizards and guarded by soul sucking monsters - Dementors. I hope you know what are you doing here.
objects.title: Azkaban

objects.text: You appear somewhere you want in Kuoh Town. It is a location in the Human World currently governed by Rias Gremory and Sona Sitri. It is the home to Hyoudou Issei and some major characters. Despite the fact that this territory belongs de jure to the Devils, it is also inhabited by several independent families of youkais and mages. This city is very often visited by stray devils, stray exorcists and almost-stray fallen angels, which can kill you for no reason at all. Be wary of random dates out of nowhere, especially if you have Sacred Gear. Also be aware that there may be devil bodyguard operatives and spies of other factions hiding somewhere in the city. Satans' siblings are a tasty morsel.
objects.title: Kuoh Town

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Underworld. You don't choose your exact location, but it be relatively safe for a while. The Underworld, also known as the Netherworld, is a separate dimension connected to the Earth. This is the home of the Devils and Fallen Angels, and by extension the Gods of Hell. Its size is roughly the same size as the Human world, but with a much larger landmass, as there are no oceans just lakes. Realm of the Dead, Purgatory, Limbo, Malebolge and Cocytus Domains are also located here.
objects.title: The Underworld

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Heavens. You don't choose your exact location, but it be relatively safe, but not for long. Christian Heaven is the home of Angels and a place sitting above the clouds with a bright white ceiling high overhead. It is guarded by a large gate and has a white stone path and stone buildings, which appear to be floating. Heaven is divided into seven regions, or "Heavens". Archangel Michael rules over Heaven at the moment.
objects.title: Heaven

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Dimensional Gap, an endless void with no direction or time, and place of iridescent colors. It is the birthplace of the Infinite Dragon God and is now home of the Dragon God of Dreams. You don't choose your exact location and it is a very dangerous place with many different realms, as it is the location that lies between the different worlds of Highschool DxD. Nothing can survive within the Dimensional Gap without some type protection, as without it, anyone can die within a matter of seconds after being exposed to the "nothingness" within the Dimensional Gap.
objects.title: Dimensional Gap

objects.text: You have found yourself inside St. Freya High, a school for Valkyries and a sanctuary for victims of the Honkai, run by Theresa Apocalypse.
objects.title: St. Freya

objects.text: You have arrived at the epicenter of a city stuck by an Honkai Eruption in both Eras. A place that kick-started the story and events later on in both their respective Eras.
objects.title: Nagazora

objects.text: You are now inside the main base of World Serpent, a secretive organization that seeks to destroy the Honkai through any means possible.
objects.title: World Serpent

objects.text: You arrive within one of the many bases operated by Fire Moth—the organization almost founded by, and final refuge of, the Flamechasers. The exact facility you manifest in depends on the era of your arrival, as the group evolves significantly across its history. In the Current Era this base is little more than a ruin closely monitored by World Serpent, but selecting an earlier Scenario like Prequel allows you to directly appear in the Previous Era when Fire Moth was active. If you're an insert, your sudden appearance will not be welcomed with open arms. Fire Moth’s personnel are accustomed to treating anything originating from beyond their reality as an immediate Honkai threat. Expect suspicion at best and armed hostility at worst. Earning their trust will require proof that you are not another aberration sent by the Honkai.
objects.title: Fire Moth Base

objects.text: You arrive somewhere within the Sundom of the Carja. This can be anywhere from the capital city Meridian to all the way to the Daunt.
objects.title: The Sundom

objects.text: You arrive somewhere within the land of the Nora Tribe. They aren't kind to strangers so be wary if you are one, lest they discover and try to hunt you down.
objects.title: Nora Lands

objects.text: You are west of the Daunt, the end of the Carja Sundom and into the territory of the Tenakth, a fierce clan of warrior tribes. These lands have been plagued by the red blight for years now.
objects.title: Forbidden West

objects.text: You have landed on Whale Island. It is relatively uninhabited with 2 (or one, depending on the time of arrival) children on the whole island besides the adults. It is filled with Fauna though.
objects.title: Whale Island

objects.text: You have arrived outside of the Heavens Arena in the Republic of Padokea. This 991-meter building is the fourth tallest in the known world, and is filled to the brim with up to 4000 fighters that you can earn money by fighting and elevating up each floor.
objects.title: Heavens Arena

objects.text: The City of Yorknew is a very dangerous place underneath the surface. Black Market deals, and shady auctions means a lot of dangerous material gets moved through, even if it's one of the most populated cities.
objects.title: Yorknew City

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Hyper Dimension, this is the main dimension of the Hyperdimension Neptunia series.
objects.title: Hyper Dimension

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Ultra Dimension, an alternate Gamindustri that resembles the Hyper Dimension but in 1989. Time in the Ultra Dimension is different, one year in the Ultra Dimension is equal to a day in the Hyper Dimension.
objects.title: Ultra Dimension

objects.text: You find yourself in the Super Dimension, specifically in the world of Hyperdimension Neptunia, or its remakes, Hyperdimension Neptunia Re;Birth1 or Neptunia re★Verse.
objects.title: Super Dimension

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Zero Dimension, a corrupted and destroyed version of Gamindustri with four Dark CPUs roaming the barren place. There are no humans left in this dimension.
objects.title: Zero Dimension

objects.text: You appear in an alternate Dimension not mentioned before. This includes spin-offs and crossovers such as the merged world of Neptunia x SENRAN KAGURA and Super Neptunia RPG 2D world. This does not include the worlds Neptunia has collaborated with. Only strange alternate dimensions of Gamindustri.
objects.title: Alternate Dimension

objects.text: You appear in a major human-controlled city, such as within the Analeit Kingdom or a similar nation. This is one of the safer environments available: guards, laws, guilds, healers, and infrastructure exist. You can train, learn magic, become an adventurer, or live relatively normally. That said, corruption, religious control, noble politics, and hidden power struggles are everywhere. Strong individuals are quickly noticed, and being noticed in this world is never truly safe.
objects.title: Human Kingdom City

objects.text: You appear inside a city under the Demon Lord’s rule. Monsters, demons, and powerful commanders walk openly. Strength is respected, weakness is exploited. Survival is harder, but opportunity is greater. You may gain access to forbidden knowledge, rare races, or protection if you prove useful. Fail to prove your worth, and you may simply disappear without anyone caring.
objects.title: Demon Territory City

objects.text:
You appear somewhere within the Great Elroe Labyrinth, with no control over the exact floor. This is one of the most lethal locations in the entire setting. Powerful monsters, constant hunger, environmental hazards, and nonstop combat define everyday existence. Survival for more than a few hours is unlikely without preparation.

However, for those who endure, growth is extreme. Levels skyrocket, rare skills become attainable, evolutions occur faster, and power can be gained here that would take decades elsewhere. Survive too long, and you will inevitably attract attention—from rulers, monsters, or entities far beyond the labyrinth.
objects.title: The Great Elroe Labyrinth

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the Kingdom of Altar, the land of knights. It seems similar to the era of knights and magic. Altar is governed by a feudal monarchy with the current acting queen being Altimia A Altar.
objects.title: Kingdom of Altar

objects.text: You appear anywhere on Mars. You can choose to appear within a certain Mars Base consisting of a single survivor.
objects.title: Mars
