objects.text: You find yourself standing within a facility housing zeroth stage Embryos. It is a heavily guarded location and you will be immediately attacked by all the Control AIs.
objects.title: Embryo Storage System

objects.text: You find yourself within a highly secure spatially warped prison housing some of the strongest Masters found in Infinite Dendrogram.
objects.title: Gaol

objects.text: You appear in a Naval Base of any country of your choice. You can choose to be the Admiral appointed to that base, some personal needed on it or a Ship Girl if you have the power.
objects.title: Naval Base

objects.text: You appear in a Princess Hold of your choice. Unless you are a Abyssal yourself, you will be considered Hostile, a Trophy or a Meal.
objects.title: Princess Hold

objects.text: You appear on the Bottom of the Ocean, you can choose for it to be filled with Abyssal Corruption. Unless you are a Ship Girl turning in a Abyssal or a Submarine Abyssal, you will most likely die.
objects.title: Bottom of the Ocean

objects.text: You appear somewhere on the quaint little star-shaped world of Popstar, what would be an idyllic and peaceful place, if not for the seemingly-random villains and other troublemakers that try to muscle in on the place what seems like every few months. You can pick any particular location to start in, from the rolling fields of Dream Land, to the Great Cave deep underground, to even the kingdom of Floralia high up in the sky.
objects.title: Planet Popstar

objects.text: You appear somewhere on the world of Halcandra, the home of the dragon Landia and a treasure trove of ancient tech and artifacts. While there isn't much here outside of volcanic crags and still-working mechanical complexes, this place is peaceful compared to the constant conflicts of Popstar, so as long as you don't try to take the Master Crown from Landia you're free to just live off the land. Note that this world is isolated in a different realm than the rest of the setting, so if you want to visit Popstar or somewhere else, you'll have to take a trip through Another Dimension.
objects.title: Planet Halcandra

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the uncreatively-named Another Dimension, a space-like realm usually devoid of anything but Doomers, strange winged creatures that are attracted to high concentrations of energy. Occasionally, you'll stumble across warped versions of areas from dimensions that AD borders, or strange shifting areas made of yellow-and-purple "terrain", of which either can potentially have rifts leading back into other realms.
objects.title: Another Dimension

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the New World, a parallel universe on the "other side" of Another Dimension from Kirby's homeworld. Aside from the ever-present Beast Pack and Fecto Forgo sealed deep inside Lab Discovera, this place is chock-full of the ruins of an ancient human-like civilization that had a fairly modern level of tech, barring any oddities hidden away in the Lab. This place has an extremely distorted flow of time compared to Kirby's dimension, with just a few seconds in his world translating to entire months here, so if you can fight off Forgo's influence and stand biding your time for extreme lengths, you could potentially get a lot done in-between incidents on Popstar.
objects.title: The New World

objects.text: You appear before a goddess who will grant you a cheat item or boon equal in strength to a power that costs 15-20 SP. Upon selecting a boon, you will be sent to Axel, Town of Beginners. (You may choose the goddess as your boon)
objects.title: Goddess

objects.text: The Valley of Peace is a lush, picturesque region surrounded by towering mountains, serving as the heart of Kung Fu in ancient China. It is home to the Jade Palace, the Furious Five, and the legendary Dragon Warrior. Despite its peaceful name, the Valley has witnessed intense battles against some of the most powerful villains in history.
objects.title: Valley of Peace

objects.text: Gongmen City is an ancient and influential metropolis by the sea, once protected by the formidable Kung Fu Council. Known for its beauty, culture, and innovation, it was also the birthplace of Lord Shen—a cunning peacock noble who sought to replace kung fu with mechanized warfare.
objects.title: Gongmen City

objects.text: The Spirit Realm is an ethereal plane where the souls of the departed, including great masters and malevolent forces, continue to exist. It is a world of raw energy, ancient knowledge, and unpredictable power. While travelers may uncover profound truths or harness supernatural strength, the Spirit Realm is not meant for the living. Prolonged presence here can disorient, corrupt, or even consume mortal beings who are unprepared or unworthy.
objects.title: Spirit Realm

objects.text: You appear inside one of the Temples or Shrines in the Zelda universe, one that exists and is accessible during your chosen time period.
objects.title: Dungeon

objects.text:
You appear in the Fool’s Dream. You are not a real person, but only a composite figment of the combined imagination of the Fool and the Celestial Worthy of Heaven and Earth. 

You have at most 7 years to escape this dream and somehow become a "real" person in the waking world; otherwise, you will inevitably cease to exist when the Fool awakens from his slumber. 

This dream has the presence of multiple other Great Old Ones and Outer Deities, most of which wish to delay the waking of the Fool. Additionally, to make things worse, all Beyonder powers are weakened to around sequence 7.
objects.title: Fool’s Dream,

objects.text: You appear on the homeworld of the Incubators
objects.title: Incubation

objects.text: You appear inside the Labyrinth of the Mirror Witch, a dangerous place full of mannequins that can replicate the appearance and abilities of those inside. It is a place that can connect across time, space, and alternate timelines. It can even connect to alternate Multiverses such as Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha.
objects.title: Mirror Witch Labyrinth

objects.text: You appear underground inside the secret base of the Wings of Magius. Inside this protected base you will find where they keep Eve.
objects.title: Hotel Fendthope

objects.text: You appear in The Capital of Mid Childa.
objects.title: Mid Childa

objects.text: You appear in the City of Uminari in Japan, where the Main Cast Resides.
objects.title: Uminari City

objects.text: You appear on a random planet somewhere within TSAB Space.
objects.title: Random Planet

objects.text: You appear in the capital of Ancient Belka.
objects.title: Ancient Belkan Capital

objects.text: You appear on a Magic School, be as a Student, One of the Staff or a Intruder. You can choose what one but will get judged depending on your role there.
objects.title: Magic School

objects.text: You appear on the Tendai Buddhist Temple located on top of a small hill at Fuchuu City and is approximately twenty kilometers west of the centre of Tokyo. This place trains people in ninjutsu and traditional shinobi magic. You better not be sneaking trough it uninvited.
objects.title: Kyuuchouji Temple

objects.text: You appear on one of the worlds seen within your Marvel universe.
objects.title: Alien World

objects.text: You appear outside the main offices of The Daily Bugle. Welcome to the city that never sleeps with its near-constant combination of gang crime, supervillain attacks, alien invasions, extra-dimensional shenanigans and sky-high rent prices. At least S.H.I.E.L.D. and numerous superheroes live nearby to help out.
objects.title: New York City

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within the hidden nation of Wakanda. This highly advanced, isolationist African kingdom is renowned for its prosperity due to its vast Vibranium deposits. It is led and protected by the Black Panther, a figure empowered by the sacred Heart-Shaped Herb found only in Wakanda.
objects.title: Wakanda

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within the secluded eastern european nation of Latveria. From the capital of Doomstadt to its borders, the country is ruled with an iron fist by Doctor Doom. Under his reign, Latveria thrives with a strong economy, advanced military and high standards of education, welfare and technology, albeit at the price of absolute obedience.
objects.title: Latveria

objects.text: You appear in the Presidium at the heart of the Citadel, a massive, almost 45 km long ancient space megastructure that acts as the main hub of governance and diplomacy for the entire galaxy.
objects.title: The Citadel

objects.text: You appear within space controlled by the Reapers.
objects.title: Reaped

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Oborozuka, the city where most of the series takes place. Despite the relatively high traffic from the Otherworld, this city has reached a status quo.
objects.title: Oborozuka

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Otherworld, where most supernatural beings originate and reside. This world is an incredibly large world that contains godly domains, afterlives, and other supernatural realms, alongside a largely medieval human society. Most of the world is involved in the ongoing conflict of the Chaos Faction and Harmony Faction over the worship of and obedience to gods in varying degrees, though the conflict has been calming down for a while and a balance has been reached.
objects.title: Otherworld

objects.text: You appear on Skull Island, home of Kong and quite a wide variety of dangerous wildlife. At least the local humans are friendly.
objects.title: Skull Island

objects.text: You appear within the Hollow Earth. Quite the dangerous place, due to being the home of the Titans and other large creatures.
objects.title: Hollow Earth

objects.text: You appear on I-Island, an artificial moving island for scientists and researchers to work together peacefully.
objects.title: I-Island

objects.text: The Everfree Forest is a chaotic place. Plants grow wild, the species are dangerous and often imbued with magical abilities, and many ruins hold secrets that are better to remain unknown. You will drop at least a full-day march away from any civilized settlement.
objects.title: Everfree Forest

objects.text: Rather than appearing in Equestria, you appear near the statue-portal on the human world side. You will be affected by the mirror magic if you try to cross it, though this can be remedied with some powers or perks. The portal will also be open for three days from the moment you arrive.
objects.title: Canterlot High

objects.text: You appear within a mile or inside one of the Hidden Villages.
objects.title: Hidden Village

objects.text: You appear on the moon of Ylum, home of Nexus. Given the sheer number of people escaping violent regimes to the moon you’re unlikely to draw attention immediately.
objects.title: Ylum

objects.text: You appear within Web Space, a capitalist oligarchy containing Earth among hundreds of other planets. Planets in Web space vary in safety greatly, ranging from near-uninhabited garden worlds to tyrannical slave states paying the Web their dues.
objects.title: The Web

objects.text: You appear within Sov Space, a Soviet Communist oligarchy containing hundreds of planets. These worlds are run under an administrative authority with complete control over the economic and social law of the world where it does not conflict with the law of higher authorities.
objects.title: Sov Space

objects.text: You appear inside the Black Hole, a domain ruled by a Psychic god that wants to force personal development, albeit by trapping people within its domain for months as they undergo its trials before escaping.
objects.title: Inside the Black Hole

objects.text: You arrive at the area that is highly infested by Machine Lifeform, better do something quick about it.
objects.title: Mechanized

objects.text: You arrived at one of the Resistance Camps, congratulations you are safe! For now.
objects.title: Resistance for Humanity

objects.text: You arrived at a random location on Earth, animals have mutated and become dangerous for squishy humans, and the sea itself has been polluted by Machine's waste. Good luck trying to survive!
objects.title: Wildlife

objects.text: You arrived at the Bunker, the main base of YoRHa, in space. Good luck getting out of there, maybe the Commander can be convinced to let you leave? And oh, the Machine has eyes in there too! So… good luck!
objects.title: Glory to Mankind!

objects.text: You arrived at the area that was infested by insane Emil's clones. Good luck, you will need it.
objects.title: Emil's Despair

objects.text: You arrived at a random location on Earth that is safe and has no hostility towards you. Do note while it is safe, there's no food or consumable water around the area.
objects.title: Safe, for now

objects.text: You can appear in any publically available space in Suwahara City. This place will soon become the stage for the second Transmutation of Gold—an immense arcane ritual to raise Reinhard to Godhood—in preparations for which all members of LDO will gather.
objects.title: Suwahara City

objects.text: This location moves your starting date. You appear in a remote German farming village during the mid-18th century, where Rusalka Schwagerin just got imprisoned on accusation of witchcraft and is soon to be subjected to horrific abuse. Soon, Mercurius himself would pay a visit, freeing Rusalka and teaching her magecraft.
objects.title: Birthplace of Malleus Maleficarum

objects.text: You appear inside the Twilight Beach, an area separated from all of space and time. At least you will have company, as the soul of the nascent Goddess Marie also resides here.
objects.title: Twilight Beach

objects.text: You appear inside the golden castle Gladsheimr. If your soul isn't ripped out and consumed the moment you arrive, the strongest members of the Longinus Dreizehn Orden, along with Reinhard, and even Mercurius currently reside here. Good luck.
objects.title: Walhalla Calling

objects.text: You appear on an Island, not on the Grand Line or Red Line.
objects.title: Great Blue

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the Grand Line (Not the Red Line).
objects.title: Grand Line

objects.text: You appear somewhere on the Red Line.
objects.title: Red Line

objects.text: Foosha Village is a small village on Dawn Island east of the Goa Kingdom. Windmills, houses, a bar, and meat store inhabit this town, along with its claim to fame for both the Hero of the Marine's Garp, and his grandson the Emperor of the Sea Luffy.
objects.title: Foosha Village

objects.text: Located in Paradis, this city is quite a hub for activity. It is known for the best Shipwrights in the world, and its yearly tidal wave. It is also home to Cutty Flam, otherwise known as Franky, depending on arrival.
objects.title: Water 7

objects.text: This island is in the New World and the mecca of scientists and inventors everywhere occupied by Dr. Vegapunk. However, as he works for the World Government, you will have to be careful how you arrive here.
objects.title: Egghead

objects.text: You have arrived at the most dangerous jail of the One Piece World, Impel Down. Made up of 5 levels, or rather 6 unofficially, this jail caters to different levels of bounty. The higher the number, the lower you go. You can choose to spawn in any location in any level in the prison, including level 5.5
objects.title: Impel Down

objects.text: You find yourself in Toronto, Canada in 2014. A city with many magical forces and threats. Should you use magic within the city, you might need to give an explanation before the City Council and it's Lord Conquest, an encounter that might not be in your favor.
objects.title: Toronto

objects.text: The Realm for Fae of all kinds, that trick, beguile and glamour the truth, until the lie becomes substantial enough to be indistinguishable. In this realm you’ll be hard-pressed to find any friends, as its inhabitants are more likely to lead you into cutthroat deals, places and talks that will see you losing pieces of yourself to them. Be it body parts, things like the ability to give thanks or apologize or even your name and the connections associated with it.
objects.title: Faerie Courts

objects.text: You've fallen into the Abyss, also known as hell, you'll need more than just wit to escape from here, this is the place where you become what you eat while slowly losing your sense of Self and there are plenty of Bogeyman willing to eat you. Its entire purpose is to break down whatever falls in, yet by nourishing yourself with the things found within, your connection to it grows in turn, a connection that might just drag you back into it, even if you manage to escape.
objects.title: The Abyss

objects.text: Roll 1d7, the rolled number is your initial arrival location, Zones are structured like the colors of the rainbow. Each has a large number of dangers and an equal number of opportunities.
objects.title: Color Zones

objects.text: You arrive in The Abyss, an extremely dangerous place filled with an incredibly large number of powerful races, immortals, transcendents, where humanity is the weakest race.
objects.title: The Abyss World

objects.text:
You appear somewhere in Heaven, the blissful afterlife inhabited by angels.

Whenever a human dies and is deemed worthy enough to enter, they come here and become Winner Angels.
objects.title: Heaven

objects.text: You appear somewhere in Hell, the miserable afterlife inhabited by demons. It is divided into seven rings named after the Seven Deadly Sins, and you can appear in any of them except the Pride Ring.
objects.title: Hell

objects.text:
You appear somewhere in Hell’s Pride Ring. This ring is notable for being the only place in Hell where sinners, human-turned-demons, are confined to, making it overpopulated and chaotic.

Depending on when you arrive, the area may be under attack by Exorcists from Heaven, who cull the population once every year.
objects.title: Pride Ring

objects.text: You come before the face of God, the bloodthirsty creator who, for the sake of entertainment, created countless worlds and made them suffer.
objects.title: Faced To God

objects.text: You end up in the bowels of Mount Massive Asylum after the Walrider’s escape and subsequent uprising and slaughter of the Variants. If you prefer, you can appear at the spark in Whistleblower, or the event’s climax in Outlast 1.
objects.title: Mount Massive

objects.text:
You appear in the rotting home of the Testament of New Ezekiel, a remote settlement in the Havasupai Indian Reservation in Northern Arizona, which served as a secret testing ground for the Murkoff Corporation in terms of mind control and modification using microwave broadcasts, turning those in its vicinity increasingly incensed and unhinged in their zealotry, back then, just before Outlast 2’s events.

Alternatively, you can appear years before to be one of the unlucky reagents for Murkoff’s project LATHE when they used Mount Sinyala as one of their many experiments to develop and concoct forms of brainwashing and indoctrination on the eve of the Cold War.
objects.title: Temple Gate/Sinyala Facility

objects.text:
You're not in the New World, you’re still on Earth. Specifically, one of the last semi-habitable urban sectors, shielded beneath a failing corporate arcology dome. The air is breathable, just barely, and food comes in pill form. Surveillance drones buzz overhead, and megacorp recruiters are always watching. 

Outside the dome? A dead, poisoned wasteland where only the desperate roam. Still, if you manage to survive long enough in this broken world and find the right games… you just might get isekaied yourself.
objects.title: Dystopian Earth

objects.text:
You don’t start in the New World, you start as an NPC in one of the Nine Realms of Yggdrasil, the legendary DMMO-RPG. You're a glitch in the system: unscripted, untracked, and not truly under developer control. This makes you immune to typical NPC restrictions. The devs might ignore you, watch you for fun, or work against you if you become too disruptive, although the latter is unlikely.

However, as an NPC, you lack the resurrection, leveling, and system protections Players enjoy. Worse, you're stuck living through one cataclysmic "Game Event" after another, and death means permanent deletion. Lastly, the game itself only lasted for 12 years before being shutdown for good. If you fail to get a World Item or somehow escape the world before the shutdown, you will die with it. Good luck.
objects.title: Yggdrasil

objects.text: You appear directly on the 9th floor of Nazarick. Good luck!
objects.title: Nazarick

objects.text:
You appear somewhere within the Re-Estize Kingdom, a failed state suffering from near-constant political disorder and civil unrest, having been plagued by inept nobles since its founding.

The kingdom fight in annual skirmishes with the Baharuth Empire.
objects.title: Re-Estize Kingdom

objects.text:
You appear somewhere within the Baharuth Empire, one of the strongest nations on the continent. It used to be a feudal state, similar to the Re-Estize Kingdom until the current Emperor established an absolute monarchy by purging much of the nobility.

The standard of living and literacy rate is fairly high by medieval standards, and the empire highly values magic.

The empire fight in annual skirmishes with the Re-Estize Kingdom.
objects.title: Baharuth Empire

objects.text: Massive military bases housing the Jaeger Program, where pilots are trained, Jaegers are repaired, and missions are coordinated. The most well-known is the Hong Kong Shatterdome, the last operational stronghold of the Pan Pacific Defense Corps before the final mission to close the Breach.
objects.title: Shatterdome

objects.text: The home dimension of the Precursors, located beyond the Breach. Little is known about this alien world aside from the fact that it serves as the command center for the Kaiju invasion. Those who enter rarely return, as it is filled with an unknown number of Precursors and possibly even stronger threats that have yet to emerge.
objects.title: The Anteverse

objects.text:
You arrive somewhere on the planet Earth. It’s relatively normal. If you arrived pre-Scratch  just pay no attention to the universe’s cancer or the meteors about to destroy it.

If you arrived Post-Scratch then It’s mostly normal up until 2011 wherein it will be conquered by ‘Fish Hitler’ who renders humanity near extinction. 

Earth C was finally made by winning a session. It’s a relatively good place to live as long as you’re not in the black hole timeline with the fascist life goddess.
objects.title: Earth A/B/C (Homestuck)

objects.text:
You arrive on the planet of Alternia, the relatively savage home to the Trolls where they dump their young to cull each other before taking the survivors to join the empire.

Alternatively if you arrive pre-Scratch you can choose to arrive on Beforus instead.
objects.title: Alternia (Homestuck)

objects.text: You arrive on the world of Prospit which in turn orbits Skaia within the Sburb session. It’s a relatively safe place to live but it is about to enter a war they know they will lose. Despite their reverence for the frog.
objects.title: Prospit (Homestuck)

objects.text: You arrive on the world of Derse which in turn orbits Skaia within the Sburb session. It’s a quite unsafe place to live but is almost certain to win the oncoming war without outside interference. Despite their hatred of the frog
objects.title: Derse (Homestuck)

objects.text: You appear inside the barrier of Camp Halfblood.
objects.title: Camp Halfblood

objects.text: You appear within New Rome.
objects.title: New Rome

objects.text: You appear on Olympus
objects.title: Gods Above

objects.text: You appear within the Labyrinth.
objects.title: Should I take a left... or my other left?

objects.text: You appear within the Underworld
objects.title: Underworld

objects.text: You appear within Tartarus. You cannot teleport out.
objects.title: Tartarus

objects.text: You appear right before a Primordial Deity.
objects.title: Primordial

objects.text: You appear within the River Styx.
objects.title: River Styx

objects.text: You arrive in a safe, discrete location in a core world of the Persean Sector of your choice. Note that “safe” is relative in some of those worlds, and safe passage may be trickier to arrange.
objects.title: Core World

objects.text: You arrive on a habitable planet in an outer system of the Persean Sector. While the planet is guaranteed to have a breathable atmosphere and some source of food, it doesn't mean that it is safe, be it from the wildlife, the climate or pirates.
objects.title: Outer System

objects.text: You appear in some other dimension within the Pokemon universe, such as the Distortion World, Ultra Space, etc.
objects.title: Kill the human!

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice within Night City. This sprawling megalopolis encompasses areas such as the corporate City Centre, the South City District, Pacifica, Santo Domingo and Westbrook. Here, everyone is in a constant struggle for survival and success, whether an edgerunner, corpo, nomad, scav, cyberpsycho or otherwise.
objects.title: Night City

objects.text:
Located in the US state of California, Angel Grove is a city most well known regarding the Power Rangers and for half a decade was the main battleground for the first Power Ranger teams of the Earth's modern era with monster attacks and invasions being semi regular to the point a lot of residence took the risk in boarding a Space Colony to get away from the monster attacks. That didn't help as they were still tormented by monster attacks only now it was in space!

Decent chance you will get into some fight with an alien or a monster within an hour of your arrival here.​
objects.title: Angel Grove

objects.text: You appear in one of the outer gates in the lower world. This can be any of the communities from 5-digit to 7-digit.
objects.title: 5-Digit to 7-Digit Outer Gates

objects.text: You appear in one of the universes in the Outer World.
objects.title: Outer Worlds

objects.text: You appear in the outer gates of the upper world, where god's reside in their true forms, which are dangerous to be around.
objects.title: 3-Digit Outer Gates

objects.text: You appear inside the Law of Cycles. A place where Magical Girls go when they die or fall into despair.
objects.title: Law of Cycles

objects.text: You appear in any publically available space inside Academy City, a landlocked sovereign city-state just west of Tokyo. It is a home of espers and the most advanced technology, being 30 years ahead of the rest of the world.
objects.title: Academy City

objects.text:
Located in School District 7 of Academy City, this building serves as the main base of operations for the general superintendent, Aliester Crowley.

Do note that it lacks any entry or exit point, requiring teleportation abilities to get in or out.
objects.title: The Windowless Building

objects.text: You appear somewhere inside the superstructure and body of the Iterator Five Pebbles.
objects.title: Five Pebbles Superstructure

objects.text: You appear somewhere inside the superstructure and body of the Iterator Looks to the Moon.
objects.title: Looks to the Moon Superstructure

objects.text: You appear at Journey's End, a large Orb Tree where a Slugcat colony lives.
objects.title: Journey's End

objects.text: You end up stranded in Martinaise, ground-zero of Disco Elysium’s events and forthcoming troubles befalling its World at large… giving rise to The Return.
objects.title: Martinaise

objects.text: Welcome to the intergalactic arcade that has thousands of games ranging from various arcade games, shooters, simple VR games like Virtual Rick-ality to fully-immersive ones like Roy: A Life Well Lived.
objects.title: Blips and Chitz

objects.text: The dimension Rick and Morty will escape to after abandoning their Prime dimension, it will remain intact even though there will be many disasters to come.
objects.title: Dimension C-131

objects.text: Rick and Morty primarily plays within the Central Finite Curve, a defined portion of the multiverse within which Rick is the smartest man alive. You’ll instead appear in a random, but relatively safe dimension within the Omniverse, it will be a much more normal dimension, though the galaxy will have just as many if not more shenanigans afoot as it no longer has a limited intelligence cap.
objects.title: Omniverse

objects.text:
You’re on Earth but in a random location. This is Rifts Earth, a scarred planet where the Great Cataclysm tore open dimensional rifts, saturating the world with ley lines and unstable magic. The Coalition States enforce their rule with brutal militarism, the Federation of Magic rallies sorcerers and creatures of legend, and Atlantis thrives on slavery and conquest.

The world is a perpetual warzone. Xiticix swarms spread like locusts, Vampire Intelligences reign in Mexico, alien gods walk among mortals, and the Minion War spills onto the planet from other dimensions. Safe havens exist only in theory — even Lazlo and New Lazlo live under constant threat. Earth is the ultimate crossroads of the Megaverse, and that makes it the ultimate battlefield.
objects.title: Somewhere in Earth

objects.text:
You find yourself not on Earth, but on one of the countless alien worlds tied into the same universe. These planets range from near-utopias of advanced alien civilizations to hellscapes crawling with demon lords, insectoid swarms, or interdimensional conquerors. You might stumble into a technologically advanced alien empire, a tribal wilderness, or a resource-rich world ripe for exploitation.

Don’t expect to understand the rules here. Alien laws, alien gods, alien biology — survival may hinge on navigating cultures and physics that don’t even resemble Earth’s. And when the rifts open here, things only get stranger.
objects.title: Somewhere Not in Earth

objects.text:
Instead of another planet on this universe, you’ve stepped into an entirely different dimension — one of the infinite pocket realms, planes, or universes tied into the Megaverse. Some resemble warped reflections of Earth, others are dreamlike expanses of impossible landscapes, and others are simply battlefields where gods and cosmic intelligences clash endlessly.

These realms can bend reality itself. Magic, time, and even causality may not behave as you expect. Some are ruled by singular entities — alien intelligences, demonic overlords, or ascended sorcerers — and many demand servitude or worship from those unlucky enough to appear within. Your existence here may not even be acknowledged as real.
objects.title: Somewhere Not Even in This Reality

objects.text:
Not all solar systems have planets in the golden-lock zone: where the planet is close enough to their sun to have liquid water on their surface. On the colder side, this planet was able to be partially terraformed. It has a breathable atmosphere, an ecosystem on the deep oceans where water is found in liquid form… and that's it.

Warmth is a rare commodity here, and so is fertile soil. Winter can last for more than half the year, and the temperature can fall to -80°c on its harshest days.

You may be able to find small communities here, that through sheer will, perseverance, and maybe some technological innovation, managed to survive in this frozen wasteland.
objects.title: Ice World

objects.text: You wake up in an escape pod hurtling from an exploding ship towards a random uninhabited location on a nearby rimworld. Your companions, items and Objects of Power are also in escape pods that will land nearby.
objects.title: Escape Pods

objects.text: Patch is a small island to the west of Vale. It is also the location of Signal Academy, a primary combat school for teenage students before attending a Huntsman Academy. The Island of Patch is a relatively safe place, although it is large enough to contain forest infested with weaker Grimm. Such as Beowolves and Ursai.
objects.title: The Island of Patch

objects.text: You appear in a Huntsman Academy of your choice. Huntsman Academies are institutions in Remnant founded by the King of Vale after the Great War and are dedicated to training Huntsmen and Huntresses, warriors whose task it is to defend the Kingdoms from the Grimm. The Academies and their staff also play a significant role in organizing the defense of the Kingdoms.
objects.title: Huntsman Academy

objects.text: You appear in the Grimmlands, possibly even in Salem's castle. If you specifically want to appear in Salem's castle, you can, but even if you don't want to, there is a chance you will.
objects.title: Grimmlands

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the city of Stilwater. You can choose where you appear, or leave it up to chance. If left to chance, the location you land will be at the very least be safe for the next hour.
objects.title: Stilwater

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the city of New Hades, a city of Hell. You can choose where you appear, or leave it up to chance. If left to chance, the location you land will be at the very least be safe for the next hour.
objects.title: New Hades

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the city of Steelport. You can choose where you appear, or leave it up to chance. If left to chance, the location you land will be at the very least be safe for the next hour.
objects.title: Steelport

objects.text: You appear in "The City" one of the few last bastions left in the Waking World and the largest city of it, the industrial, military, and administrative heart of humanity located in Asia. This Megacity holds 1/10 of all of the remaining humans on Earth. You'll find yourself in the heart of the city proper.
objects.title: Northern Quadrant Siege Capital "The City"

objects.text:
It appears you've found yourself in "The Outskirts". It's the place where the undesirable are left to rot. The Megacities can only sustain so many human lives, so around twenty percent of the city population is offloaded to the outskirts to slowly rot away and die, out of the sight and out of mind of the rest of humanity.

Be wary of everything here, for human lives are of the same worth as bugs, the air is acrid and toxic, conditions inhumane, and the people live short and miserable lives.
objects.title: The Outskirts

objects.text:
The Dream Realm is a treacherous and dangerous place to be in, but it seems that you've found yourself in one of the more perilous places in it. Monsters lurk behind every corner here. Common are creatures that could tear down a man with a single swipe with nary a thought, but there lurk monsters and beasts of such unholy magnitude that just their mere presence could fell cities and fortresses by being near them. It is best not to meander and always be on the move for these reasons alone. Swimming then is even more ill-advised, for what lurks beneath the surface of that inky abyss is not what humans can survive.

You may choose to arrive at any region of the forgotten shore, including the dark city, the only human settlement in it. Do know that there is no way out unless you find a Gate to return to the Waking World.
objects.title: Forgotten Shore

objects.text: Green Hill Zone, one of the safest places in the world when Eggman isn't screwing around. Home of Sonic the hedgehog.
objects.title: Green Hill

objects.text: You have landed on any of the 5 Starfall Islands. The defenses of the Island and the structure itself are quite powerful, able to defeat those without a power at least close to the Chaos Emeralds, if seen as a threat.
objects.title: Starfall Island

objects.text: You have landed inside the Space Colony ARK. Depending on your chosen time, it could be VERY abandoned, or occupied by chaos creatures. Regardless, you will have to look for a way down to the planet.
objects.title: Space Colony ARK

objects.text: You have arrived on Earth and thankfully, depending on the time period at least, you will be welcomed with open arms by the Federation. It is also considered one of the safest places in the Quadrants.
objects.title: Earth

objects.text: The pleasure planet, Risa. You have arrived here, and as long as you cause no trouble, you will find yourself in a dream vacation world.
objects.title: Risa

objects.text: You have landed somewhere in the Gamma Quadrant of the Galaxy. You will likely be hunted by the power known as the Dominion, which with its advanced technology, Shapeshifting leadership, AND its hellbound and determined Jem'Hadar soldiers, will be VERY difficult to avoid.
objects.title: Gamma Quadrant

objects.text: A peaceful town in Los Angeles, California.
objects.title: Echo Creek

objects.text: A medieval land divided into several kingdoms ruled by kings and queens of various species.
objects.title: Mewni

objects.text: A sub-level kingdom inhabited by demons, dead beings, and a multitude of other creatures, escaping it will be a lengthy endeavor.
objects.title: Underworld

objects.text: You appear within a mile of the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. You can appear inside the Temple if you want instead.
objects.title: A Disturbance in the Force

objects.text: You appear in a random location capable of supporting human life in the Core or Colonies regions of the galaxy.
objects.title: The Core

objects.text: You appear in a random location capable of supporting human life in the Inner Rim, Expansion Region, or Mid Rim regions of the galaxy.
objects.title: Mid Rim

objects.text: You appear in a random location capable of supporting human life in the Outer Rim, Hutt Space, or Wild Space regions of the galaxy.
objects.title: Outer Rim

objects.text: You appear in a random location capable of supporting human life in the Unknown Regions of the galaxy.
objects.title: Unknown Regions

objects.text:
Your starting date is moved to 3645 BBY. You start on one of the initial planets of one of 8 classes of the Star Wars: The Old Republic MMO.

You can assume the role—getting the necessary knowledge, history, and equipment—of one of the classes of your choice. If you can wield the Force, you may be either Jedi or Sith, starting on the worlds Tython or Korriban, respectively; if you can't—then you may assume the role of Imperial Agent, Bounty Hunter, Smuggler, or Republic Trooper. Imperial classes start on the world Hutta, and republic ones start on Ord-Mantell.
objects.title: Starting Planet

objects.text: You appear near Cheyenne Mountain complex, located a fairly short distance outside of Colorado Springs. This military installation houses the Stargate.
objects.title: Cheyenne Mountain

objects.text: You appear on the world of Abydos, which is under the domain of Supreme System Lord Ra, and is mainly used to mine naquadah for him.
objects.title: Abydos

objects.text: You appear on the world of Delmak, a highly industrialised planet controlled by the Goa'uld Sokar, who is well known for his cruel and sadistic nature.
objects.title: Delmak

objects.text: You arrive 5900 years ago on Earth. Pink Diamond has just been shattered by the Crystal Gems, the Rebellion has begun.
objects.title: Rose’s Rebellion

objects.text: You arrive after the main plot has been dealt with, including the movie. There’s not much more to fight, peace has been established, things are improving across the galaxy, and what threats remain are more nuisances than dangers.
objects.title: Future

objects.text: You arrive on Homeworld. Good news: Without a Gem the machines there won’t detect you. Bad news: Once gems notice you’re there, they’ll hunt you down. If you’re organic they’ll likely just kill you, if not they’ll try to find out what you are, most likely destroying you in the process.
objects.title: Homeworld

objects.text:
You manifest within a video game of your choice. If you possess a power or perk that simulates or forces your body into existence, the Cardinal System will recognize and treat you as a Player, akin to how it handled the Mental Health Counseling Programs 01 and 02. In this case, you'll have all the abilities and privileges of a Player, such as interacting with the environment, respawning, and using in-game menus.

If you do not possess such powers or perks, you will instead gain the designation of an NPC (Non-Player Character). As an NPC, your role is integrated into the game world, allowing you to interact with other players, affect quests, and possibly influence the game’s story. However, you won’t have access to typical Player functions like respawning or manipulating the game interface.

Abilities or Powers used inside the Game will make Cardinal try to categorize them and create skill's based on what was show, such a revival power becoming a automatic skill.
objects.title: Inside a Video Game

objects.text: You appear on the Real World, in a city of your choice.
objects.title: Physical World

objects.text: You appear at any location of your choice in the Central World, the first world Veldanava created and the one where he decided to live in. It is noted to be incredibly strong and resilient due to the Holy Relics created for that very purpose. This creates the conditions necessary to survive beings and events that would normally be enough to destroy entire worlds, such as the presence of four True Dragons in one universe or a fight between Milim Nava and Guy Crimson. Furthermore, many people and objects from other universes are noted to appear here for one reason or another.
objects.title: Magical Continent

objects.text: You appear in the Heavenly Star Palace, the very place Veldanava himself first awoke from after lowering himself from omnipotence. Fenn, a True Giant that never reformed his violent nature, is sealed inside and can potentially notice you. To leave, you must go through the Heaven Tower, which is guarded by the Demon Lord Dagruel. Attempting to do so would likely invite his attention and draw questions about how you were even inside in the first place.
objects.title: Heavenly Star Palace

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Otherworld. This universe is home to the invasive Aggressor races and the Spooky Palace, where Ivaragé is sealed away. Those inside live on dense concentrations of magicules resembling planets scattered throughout the expansive void as there is no gravity otherwise. Due to its anomalous location in the multiverse, natural portals can form connecting to other universes, which the Aggressor races exploit to conquer them.
objects.title: Otherworld

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Elemental Realm, a Spiritual World where elementals form. As a Spiritual World, it contains no physical matter, meaning material bodies can't exist without proper precautions. To leave, you must either get summoned elsewhere or go through the Dwelling of the Elementals, a labyrinth guarded by the Demon Lord Ramiris. Attempting to do so could draw her attention and may raise questions if she notices any anomalies.
objects.title: Elemental Realm

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Daemon Realm, a Spiritual World where daemons form. As a Spiritual World, it contains no physical matter, meaning material bodies can't exist without proper precautions. It is a chaotic place where daemons often fight each other without physical laws otherwise restricting them. At the bottom of this realm lies the Abyss, generating "minus energy" that reacts destructively to anything that exists. The realm is accessible through Hell Gates, portals connected to other universes, which are generally guarded by Primordial Daemons.
objects.title: Daemon Realm

objects.text: You appear either in or just outside Vought Tower, the main headquarters of Vought International and The Seven. You may choose which floor you appear on although be aware that they don't take kindly to trespassers.
objects.title: Vought Tower

objects.text: You appear in one of the cells in Sage Grove Centre, a secret facility controlled by Vought International that conducts illegal experiments on captive patients by administering Compound V in order to refine the formula.
objects.title: Sage Grove Centre

objects.text: A lone lamp post in the middle of the wilderness, and a short distance away from the Wardrobe entrance to Narnia.
objects.title: The Lamp Post of the Lantern Wastes

objects.text: The capital and seat of government of Narnia, a large castle on the coast of the Eastern Ocean.
objects.title: Cair Paravel

objects.text: A great slab of rock on four pillars in the heart of the Narnian mainland. the Lion Aslan has either been sacrificed here, or one day will be sacrificed here depending on your choices.
objects.title: The Stone Table

objects.text: You appear in Eden, home to the Constellation of Absolute  Good, there is also a Scribe of Heaven Metatron owner of the Wall that Divides Good and Evil.
objects.title: Edem

objects.text: You appear in the 73rd Demon Realm without the Demon King, Jang Hayoung, the owner of the Wall of Impossible Communication, is here.
objects.title: 73rd Demon Realm

objects.text: You appear in one of the Small Islands in Reincarnation Island, here are Yoo Hoosung master of Kyrgios Rodgraim and Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, also Guardian of Shambhala Buddha owner of the Wall of Samsara. Only Physical Powers work here.
objects.title: Reincarnation Island

objects.text: You are outside the scenarios, don't choose if you do not have the power to protect yourself. No, really don’t choose it,  you’ll be “Forgotten”
objects.title: Out of Scenarios

objects.text: You appear at some point in Tamriel that was a waypoint in one of the games.
objects.title: Waypoint

objects.text: You arrive in the habitable world from the start of the game. Like the game, it orbits a gas giant, and the sun possesses three other rocky planets orbiting it. There will be no Dark Fog presence right away, though your actions may attract their attention.
objects.title: Starting System

objects.text: You arrive in a habitable world, with a moderate Dark Fog presence. While your appearance on the planet isn't enough to catch their attention, their sensors are always working to catch anything irregular.
objects.title: Dark Fog Occupied System

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the town of Gravesfield, localized in the Human Realm.
objects.title: Gravesfield

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the Boiling Isles, localized in the Demon Realm.
objects.title: The Boiling Isles

objects.text: Upon taking this, you will appear at the Grace Field House, or you can choose to appear at one of the three other Premium Farms: Glory Bell, Grand Valley, and Goodwill Ridge. Some say ignorance is bliss. Here, you have the option to live a short but happy life with your fellow orphans.
objects.title: Premium Farms

objects.text: Why? Why would you willingly choose this? If you feel masochistic enough to pick this, expect to be placed in one of the hundreds of factory farms in the Demon realm. The conditions? Horrible! Here, you will be kept in squalid conditions, all for the purpose of becoming a cheap meal. Escape will be extremely difficult. If you choose reincarnation, you will keep your original intelligence and won't become a brain-dead husk like the rest.
objects.title: Factory Farms

objects.text: Once a safe haven for escapee children, now a secret hunting ground. You have willingly chosen to appear here; prepare to be in constant life-threatening danger if you don't have powers. Good luck.
objects.title: Goldy Pond

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the duchy of Toussaint. You can choose where you appear, from the throne room in the middle of Beaulcair, to the very outskirts of the dutchy, or leave it up to random chance. If left to chance, the location you land will be at the very least be safe for the next hour.
objects.title: Toussaint

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the free city of Novigrad. You can choose where you appear, from the middle of Grand Temple of  Eternal Flame to its slums. If left to chance, the location you land will be at the very be least safe for the next hour.
objects.title: Novigrad

objects.text: You appear just on front of Anteiku’s door, a safe haven for ghouls in need residing in 20th Ward in Tokyo. If you’re a Ghoul with a telling confirmation of both your species and current plight, they’ll have no qualms about lending a hand and offering you a place to settle.
objects.title: Anteiku

objects.text: You end around the CCG’s Main HQ, the organization specialized on prosecuting, containing and eliminating Ghouls for the security of the Japan’s populace. If you’re a Ghoul (and Investigators take notice of it the moment you purposefully make a show of it), they’ll have a duty to take care of you, so unless you’re as foolhardy as Kaneki, best of you to look as unassuming as possible and get the hell out of dodge.
objects.title: CCG Main Office

objects.text: The village is a modest settlement where most of the humans in Gensokyo reside, preserving traditional customs and trades. It serves as a sanctuary from the hostile, yokai-filled wilderness and relies on shrine maidens and guardians for protection. Some yokai have integrated into the village and coexist with the humans.
objects.title: Human Village

objects.text: A large Western-style mansion located near a lake in Gensokyo. It is home to two mischievous and deadly vampire sisters, and it is maintained by their maid and staff who inhabit the mansion.
objects.title: Scarlet Devil Mansion

objects.text: The borders of Gensokyo blur here, resulting in "outsiders" being pulled in. It draws in criminals, the spiteful, the lonely, the depressed and offering a second chance to those contemplating suicide to turn back and re-enter the real world. However, it is also used as a hunting ground for yokai.
objects.title: Road of Reconsideration

objects.text: You appear in a random location on the planet Cybertron. The locals may not take kindly to organic life, and there may not be a breathable atmosphere, but this location will otherwise be safe.
objects.title: Cybertron

objects.text: You're now placed in Souya City, a locale within the Tokyo Metropolitan Area and the primary setting of the Remake's events. If you lack any special abilities, it is strongly advised for you to leave while you still have the can—lest you become yet another unfortunate statistic in the city's dark and dangerous landscape.
objects.title: Souya

objects.text:
Well, you've found yourself in quite a quaint little town, haven't you? Nestled on the outskirts of the Kantō region, this mysterious place serves as the backdrop for the original Tsukihime and Melty Blood timelines.

It also holds a deeper history, being the sleepy town where Aoko Aozaki and Touko Aozaki spent their childhood under their family's influence. As the Second Owners, the Aozaki family also oversees the magical underpinnings of the area. Most notably, this is the same setting for the events of Mahoutsukai no Yoru (Witch on the Holy Night).
objects.title: Misaki Town

objects.text: You've found yourself in front of the gates of the Tohno Mansion in either timeline, a place that holds many dark secrets and mysteries. Beware of what you're looking for here.
objects.title: Tohno Mansion

objects.text: You appear on Mt. Ebott.
objects.title: Mt. Ebott

objects.text: You appear at the bottom of the hole leading into Mt. Ebott. You cannot teleport out of the Underground until the Barrier is destroyed.
objects.title: Underground

objects.text: You appear in Wellston Private High School. Wellston is one of the most prestigious and competitive schools, and filled to the brim with elite-tiers and high-tiers. The social hierarchy is practiced tirelessly here.
objects.title: Wellston Private High School

objects.text: You appear in New Bostin. New Bostin is a town that consists of many low-tiers and mid-tiers, with elite-tiers being hard to find. It's also where John was born. You can choose where to appear, with notable locations being New Bostin High/Middle School and the New Bostin Park.
objects.title: New Bostin

objects.text: A random planet inhabited by humans in some form, this could be a paradise world inhabited by humans with knowledge of technology to a feudal world to a death world were humanity is barely clinging to life.
objects.title: Random Inhabited Planet

objects.text:
Alright, you asked for this.
This is a death world, extremely unsuited for human habitation, but still colonized for god knows what reason. Perhaps the planets fauna and flora have evolved to be super predators or perhaps the world is entirely frozen or there is an active and warring population of chaos or Orks. Either way this planet is a hell on earth.
objects.title: Death World

objects.text:
...Why? Why would you do this to yourself?
The Immaterium, most commonly known as the Warp, is an alternate dimension of psychic energy that exists alongside the material universe, where thoughts and emotions become reality and the very landscape itself is ever-changing. On top of that, it is also home to the four Chaos Gods, their legions of Daemons, and God only knows what else.
objects.title: The Warp

objects.text: A very pleasant happy world with plenty of resources and likely a high level of technology. There are not any major wars or disasters and people live their lives generally in peace and happiness. Although given the universe this isnt likely to last.
objects.title: Paradise World

objects.text:
A world much like our own in less technologically advanced times.
A world without any advanced technology beyond maybe a few poorly understood 'relics'.
objects.title: Feudal World

objects.text: A sprawling, wretched underbelly of crime and gang warfare, the underhives of the Imperium's Hive Worlds can be almost as deadly as the surface of Death Worlds; life here is brutal, short and painful. Danger is everywhere, from industrial waste runoff, to rampant violence, mutant gangs, genestealer or heretic cults and hunts from nobles. Be thankful the air is  at least breathable down here. Usually. You arrive in an underhive of your choice.
objects.title: Underhive

objects.text: Halo Stars is the name given to the ancient formation of stars that encircles the outer edge of the galaxy. These are characterized by mystery and danger, and are largely unexplored, with many unknown dangers lurking within. Believed to be the oldest stars in existence, you can arrive at any point within them, from the infamous Ghoul Stars to the Koronus Expanse.
objects.title: Halo Stars

objects.text: You start in any city within the Empire of Man. This is a horribly superstitious and prejudiced place, so try not to stand out for the wrong reasons.
objects.title: The Empire

objects.text: You can start anywhere within the Old World.
objects.title: The Old World

objects.text:
You can start anywhere within the New World.
This means you have to deal with hostile dinosaur people to the south, and the world's most evil slaver society to the north. Have fun.
objects.title: The New World

objects.text: Orks… Orks everywhere. You are in the heart of Ork territory, there are Orks and Goblins as far as the eye can see. This is horrible. On the plus side you are not likely to ever want for a fight, if you care about that sort of thing.
objects.title: The Badlands

objects.text:
You start in Norsca, Kislev or in the chaos wastelands. Pro tip, for the love of all that's good don’t start in the chaos wastelands.
It's cold, there's no food, everything is being corrupted by chaos and everyone is hostile, and that's just Norsca. Start here if you are a real pro gamer.
objects.title: The North

objects.text: You have found yourself in Sigmar's home realm of Azyr. As Sigmar's home it enjoys fast response from his Stormcast, and most incursions are quick and brutal affairs.
objects.title: Azyr, Realm of Heaven

objects.text: An evershifting primal monstrosity, Ghur's own landscape is eating itslef much like the unending chain of predation within it. The Ghurish heartlands are savage and difficult to survive, but largely unorganised and uncoordinated
objects.title: Ghur, Realm of Beasts

objects.text: Home to Nagash, the realm of death is full of innumerable afterlives and wastelands, ech feeding their great undead mastwe who holds total dominion over the realm. After the Necroquake, the borders of Shyish are relatively stable, while it's center drags more and more of reality into the endless sea of souls beneath.
objects.title: Shyish, Realm of Death

objects.text: The deepest bowels of Substructure 17, The Mass which has been resting at the bottom of the Superstructure will spot you, and will most likely want to eat you. If you make it to the Breakroom, you might be able to obtain an Experimental Upgrade from the HES Experimental Upgrade Console there.
objects.title: Substructure 17 - Deep Storage (White Knuckle)

objects.text: The mid point of Substructure 17's Understructure, sealing the large door located here can block The Mass for some time. There is an HES Upgrade Console here, you might be able to obtain an Upgrade from it.
objects.title: Substructure 17 - Lockdown (White Knuckle)

objects.text: The final room of Substructure 17's Underworks, there's a Roach Bazaar here and an elevator that can take you up to the entrance of Habitation Yellow, the Forlorn Gateway. There is a HES Upgrade Console inside, you might be able to obtain an Upgrade from it.
objects.title: Substructure 17 - Ascent (White Knuckle)

objects.text: The beginning of the inter-structure transit line between Substructure 17 and Substructure 3. Rho Cultists used the power of two artifacts to seal Periphery Delta from this location, you can take one of them, though doing so will draw The Broker's attention.
objects.title: Substructure 17 - Evacuation (White Knuckle)

objects.text: The entrance to Substructure 3, you might be able to obtain an Upgrade from the HES Upgrade Console here. Substructure 3 is The Nest of The Mother, she is trapped here by a containment field, freeing her will break The Pact, but you may earn her favor.
objects.title: Substructure 3 - Symbiosis (White Knuckle)

objects.text: A hidden prison complex inside Substructure 10, the way out requires a fuel cell, luckily there's one nearby. Unluckily it only to another door, one which need three new fuel cells to open, the only remaining ones are in Organism Zeta.
objects.title: Substructure 10 - Old Ward (White Knuckle)

objects.text: The bottom level of Cooling Shaft X within Substructure 12. In an effort to drive off The Mass Cooling Shaft X is being flooding with K-Coolant, an anomalous liquid with supercooling properties.
objects.title: Substructure 12 - Frigid Facility (White Knuckle)

objects.text: You appear somewhere along the Rhine Front, the most crucial and blood-soaked battlefield of the Empire’s war against the Republic. This location includes war-torn trenches, forward operating bases, and highly contested skies. Survive the constant artillery barrages, mage combat, and ambushes while navigating imperial military bureaucracy.
objects.title: The Rhine Front

objects.text: You appear in Berun, the heart of the Empire, far from the chaos of the frontlines. If you are a civilian, you can live a relatively peaceful life amidst the bustling markets, grand architecture, and lively culture. However, the war’s shadow looms large—rationing, propaganda, and the risk of conscription are ever-present. If you’re careful, you might avoid direct involvement in the war, but staying neutral in a militaristic society may bring its own challenges.
objects.title: Imperial Capital – Berun

objects.text: You appear at a classified Unified States facility, a hub of cutting-edge magical and technological research. This is where advanced weapons, experimental computation orbs, and magic devices are developed. It’s also home to Dr. Schugel, the eccentric scientist blessed (or cursed) by Being X. The facility is heavily secured, with constant surveillance and the threat of sabotage by enemy spies.
objects.title: Unified States Research Facility

objects.text: You appear anywhere in the center of the city of Zootopia. It holds both City Hall and the Zootopia Police Department's Precinct One at the heart of the city.
objects.title: Savanah Central

objects.text: You appear 211 miles away from Zootopia in the place known as Bunnyborrow. Despite the name, animals besides bunnies live there even if the majority IS Bunnies.
objects.title: Bunnyborrow

objects.text: You appear in any of the other 4 districts of your choice: Rainforest District, Tundratown, Sahara Square, and Little Rodentia (Prepare to be the relative size of a Kaiju in the last one.)
objects.title: Anywhere Else In Zootopia

objects.text: You’re arriving in Ixia, a beautiful plane filled with Demon-esque peoples. South Ixia has been annexed as the 52nd state of the United States of America, though North Ixia is still a battleground in the process of annexation.
objects.title: Ixia (Deadlock)

objects.text: You’re arriving in the luxurious and high-class Baroness Hotel. Located on Broadway in the Cursed Apple, New York; It contains numerous luxuries such as egyptian cotton sheets, bottomless mimosas, spa days and more. Though you don’t have a reservation yourself it is quite a safe and calm place. That said, do try to stay aware of the nascent god acting as The Doorman of the hotel, he may enjoy his job but the trespassing is unfortunate.
objects.title: The Baroness Hotel (Deadlock)

objects.text: You’re entering the most famous illicit fight club in New York, The Bear Pit. A place of many varied bloodsports and gambling. Unfortunately you’re an unknown and likely strange person appearing inside without passing the bouncers in a place where if people aren’t armed they don’t need to be.
objects.title: The Bear Pit (Deadlock)

objects.text: You find yourself somewhere on academy grounds, be that inside a class room or even the Headmaster's office. While these areas are usually safe, an unexplaned presnece may be... stressful.
objects.title: Academy Grounds

objects.text: The island of Akademos itself is inhabited by the ocupants of the academy and ther family, much like a university villiage on much grander scale. similarly, it's almost garenteed to be relatively safe.
objects.title: Outer Academy island

objects.text: A Lawless city, home to many criminals and gangs.
objects.title: Brackport

objects.text: A city that has been overtaken by The Imaginarium. Survivors have been warped by the energies within the area. The Shattered Goddess resides within the heart of this city, her reflection roaming it freely.
objects.title: Nythera

objects.text: A chaotic landscape that is actively hostile to anything from the physical world, breaking it down into pure energy. This realm is a constant flux with the rules of its reality being nonexistent.
objects.title: Imaginarium

objects.text: Existence outside the two realms, a hostile place where the rules of reality reject the reality of the other two realms. Be careful when coming here.
objects.title: The Void

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the subliminal space of MR, the backrooms of reality. A place that stores knowledge of the changes within reality. Often adding new worlds and people into its catalog. You can use it to traverse the omniverse, even without Homecoming. However, you won’t be able to go back without some kind of teleportation power.
objects.title: Mer'ge Requ'Ests

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Sym-tan Animated TV Show story, the main continuity and otherwise known as the First Timeline. This timeline follows events of canon and the sequel Magical Girl Ärztinnen. This universe is oftentimes in danger that threatens all of reality.
objects.title: ☆Sym-tan☆ Animated Verse (First Timeline)

objects.text:
You appear somewhere in the closed F̷͍̐i̷͆̏f̶͂͑t̷͘͠h̶̃̑ Timeline. Formerly a simple variant Timeline, it has long since been twisted by The Incarnation of Evil, F̷͍̐i̷͆̏f̶͂͑t̷͘͠h̶̃̑. It is now an infinitly shifting labyrinth of non-euclidean space and endless sub-dimensions, a place where unfinished stories go to die. The countless souls trapped within are forever tormented by fragments of F̷͍̐i̷͆̏f̶͂͑t̷͘͠h̶̃̑ and former friends twisted into monsters by it.

The Time Gate leading to this Timeline is closed, meaning traversal out of it is nigh-impossible. You either fight to survive or die trying. Be warned, for when the monsters find you, so too will F̷͍̐i̷͆̏f̶͂͑t̷͘͠h̶̃̑.
objects.title: F̷͍̐i̷͆̏f̶͂͑t̷͘͠h̶̃̑ Timeline

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the hidden corner of The World of The Goddess's Creation. A place where The Goddess's gaze exists, you find yourself lost there. Perhaps due to all the Magical Girls, it is a very chaotic place. It is not a very good place to hide.
objects.title: Furthest Corner in The World of The Goddess's Creation

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Verse not mentioned. From the forgotten timeline of Azathoth to the other places not mentioned. This includes but is not limited to all the alternate timelines such as the Second, Third, and Sixth. But you can even appear in the Abyss.
objects.title: Other

objects.text: The impeiral core of the Kankeri empire is a stable place reaping the benefits of it's centuries of exploiting the rest of the continent. unfortunately it was not designed for human body plans, in favour of the crustacean, but at least it's safe.
objects.title: Vardea - The Imperial Core of Chae

objects.text: The Tunnels within the world of Vaniterra house the great merchant empire of Tserin, appearing within the tunnels places you at least on track to the capital, as all roads lead there (and in the path of numerous trade carrivans), but be wary of the less hospitable inhabitants.
objects.title: The Tunnels of Tserin

objects.text: The matriarchy of Sanguinis holds the befeathered Ornithi in something aproaching a species-wide pity. much like how they regard powers themselves, due to the Ornathi tendancy to be born in a variety of shapes dependant largely on the mother's caloric intake. You'll find yourself starting in one of their slums. the only major danger comes form Sanguinis's violent culture and the economic weakness of the area, but aside fromt hat the communities tends to be tight knit and relatively welcoming, if cautious.
objects.title: Sanguinis - Ornithi Slum

objects.text:
You appear inside one of the eusocial human hives somewhere in the universe. Depending on the timeline, it can be a Roman hive, one of the lost colonies, or even the Coalition's Olympus Mons Archive.

Do try to hold your breath.
objects.title: Coalescence

objects.text:
You appear inside configuration space, the atemporal and acausal space where every single moment in the universe is represented as a grain of sand. Stay out of the ocean of entropy, and do try not to lose yourself.

Do note that if you start here, unless you have powers to mitigate this, you will be a pure disembodied consciousness, as no physical matter can exist in the configuration space.
objects.title: Configuration Space

objects.text:
You appear inside the stolen Xeelee Nightfighter some light-years away from the Bolder's Ring.

As it is the site of the Xeelee's most prized project, you have little time before you are detected. Good luck figuring out the controls.
objects.title: The Ring's Construction Site

objects.text: You arrive at the site of the Gozenjiai tournament. Optionally, you can be registered as a representative of an unknown clan and compete for leadership of the expedition or simply join it as another member.
objects.title: Gozenjiai

objects.text:
This is the home of Yatsukahagi and the destination of the Eastern Expedition. Appearing here prevents you from contracting the curse of narcissism inherent in almost every other inhabitant of Mahamara.

You will not be considered hostile unless you try to confront the Yatsukahagi themselves.
objects.title: Land of Edo

objects.text: You appear somewhere on the western side of Ashihara no Nakatsukuni, the territory ruled by samurai and a figurehead emperor. This is the home country of the clans that take part in the Eastern Expedition.
objects.title: Western side of Shinshuu

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Outskirts, a desolate and merciless place filled with the rejects of The City, monsters that defy description, and ruins of history long-forgotten. As a dumping zone for things that are unwelcome in The City, you can find things like rogue AI, inhuman beasts, or simply those unfortunate enough to be left out or excised here. If you wander around enough, there's the possibility of discovering small human settlements like Cloud Town, and if you go beyond the Outskirts, you may even chance upon an encounter with entities "well beyond the grasp of human cognition".
objects.title: The Outskirts

objects.text:
You appear in The Library, the EGO of the former Lobotomy Corporation AI Angela. This place is noted for being nigh-impossible to reach depending on where in the timeline you land. Depending on when you arrive, you may have to deal with Angela before she mellowed out coming to investigate your uninvited presence, or a former Grade 1 Fixer, a previous Color Fixer once known as 'the strongest', and a former Arbiter of The Head.

If you end up here early enough, you may potentially end up replacing Roland as a Patron Librarian.
objects.title: The Library

objects.text: You appear somewhere in the Ruins, a vast underground area beneath The City that houses incredibly valuable relics and unique and dangerous creatures not found anywhere else. Known as a deep deep place where no one treads carelessly, you might have a hard time finding your way to the surface.
objects.title: The Ruins

objects.text:
Instead of beginning in a mortal realm, you begin in a random middle realm or one of your choice. A middle realm exists between the mortal and higher realms, where Spiritual Qi is far denser, cultivation is more prosperous, and even ordinary people commonly possess some level of cultivation from birth.

Resources and opportunities are far greater than those found in the mortal realms, but so too are the dangers. Cultivation progresses more quickly, and cultivators many realms beyond those of the mortal world are commonplace, making it a far harsher place to survive. Additionally, contact with the higher realms is far more frequent, with their influence regularly reaching the middle realms.
objects.title: Middle Realm

objects.text: You arrive within the Dark City itself. Confined inside the Webway, Commorragh is the largest city-state in the galaxy, though in reality it is more a series of satellite realms and cities linked by myriad portals and hidden pathways; its dimensions would be considered impossible if they could be read by conventional means, and its population is greater than that of whole star systems. You may choose to arrive anywhere from the slums of Sec Maegra to the beating heart of the city.
objects.title: Commorragh

objects.text: You arrive somewhere in T'au space, a collection of some of the most genuinely hospitable planets within civilized space for its inhabitants, being even more so than Imperial Pleasure Worlds, at least for ordinary civilians. Citizens here live under the laws of the Greater Good and their Ethereal masters. This covers anywhere from the core Sept Worlds to the fringe colonies of the Farsight Enclaves.
objects.title: T'au Space

objects.text: You arrive within the homes of the Leagues of Votann and many Greenskin empires, alongside any xenos hardy enough to survive here. The galactic core is a place of constant flux and peril, bounded by the unstable circumnuclear disc, and at its centre lies the supermassive black hole that constitutes the true gravitational heart of the galaxy. While rich in resources and stellar bounties, its comparative density spawns a wide variety of cosmic anomalies and dangers birthed from the clashing of fundamental forces. Your exact location within it is up to you, whether in a specific League's territory or on a random planet.
objects.title: Galactic Core

objects.text: You arrive within an Asuryani Craftworld of your choice, a marvel of psychic and mundane engineering built to ferry the last remnants of the Eldar race across the stellar sea. These are all generally paradisaical and utopian by human standards, being safe from all dangers. Every single one contains an Infinity Circuit to immortalize even the souls of the fallen.
objects.title: Craftworld

objects.text: A massive tear in reality, where the laws of space and time hold little, if any, sway. Here, the Warp has near-total supremacy over the Materium, and the forces of Chaos hold dominion. The barriers of realspace are thin here, so the summoning of daemons and corruption is easily done, resulting in many infernal lords ruling over countless daemon worlds. This only becomes worse the closer one gets to its center, making this the closest thing to literal hell in the galaxy. You arrive in a location of your choosing within its bounds.
objects.title: Eye of Terror

objects.text:
You appear in Europe... or rather, what little remains of it. 

Following the arrival of the Queen and the Second Summer of Love in 1989, the entire western Eurasian landmass up to and including Moscow was effectively annihilated, along with everyone living there.

You can choose to appear nearly anywhere in what was once Europe, but there’s not much left beyond open water and the fragments of desolate, shattered countries. Eliza Hellbound, an Atomic Superpower empowered by Hell, also resides at the impact's centre.
objects.title: Broken Europe

objects.text: You find yourself in Tet’s home, a giant King Chess Piece where the ten covenants were established. For all that it is called his home, Tet is rarely here. Without your own way to leave, you may be in for a long wait.
objects.title: King Chess Piece (No Game No Life)

objects.text: You find yourself in Elkia, the last kingdom of Immanity. It seems they’re trying to decide their next ruler, it could be you if you play your cards right.
objects.title: Kingdom of Elkia (No Game No Life)

objects.text: You appear somewhere within the Eastern Union. By default this will be its capital Kannagari City.
objects.title: The Eastern Union (No Game No Life)

objects.text: You find yourself somewhere within the Kingdom of Euchronia. By default, you’ll find yourself in the capital Grand Trad, though you can choose anywhere else in the Kingdom if you wish.
objects.title: Kingdom of Euchronia (Metaphor: ReFantazio)

objects.text: You find yourself in the Principality of Oceana, by default its capital Port Brilehaven. You can choose to start anywhere else within the Principality if you wish.
objects.title: Principality of Oceana (Metaphor: ReFantazio)

objects.text: The Principality of Montario is where you’ll end up. By default you’ll find yourself in its capital Altabury Heights, though you can choose to start anywhere else within the Principality if you wish.
objects.title: Principality of Montario (Metaphor: ReFantazio)

rows.titleText: Do you need some more points to get what you want? Trade all you like.

rows.title: (Entity) Network Conversion
rows.titleText: Network Capacity is your primary resource as an Entity, but it can be converted to and from other resources if needed. You may use these conversions at any time.
